title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
धर्मप्रधानाः पुरुषाः पूर्वम् आसन् अहिंसकाः /
लोभद्वेषाभिभूतानां व्यवहारः प्रवर्तितः // BrhS_1,1.1 dharmapradhānāḥ puruṣāḥ pūrvam āsan ahiṃsakāḥ / lobhadveṣābhibhūtānāṃ vyavahāraḥ pravartitaḥ // BrhS_1,1.1 Originally, men were established in Dharma as the highest principle, and non-violence was their natural state; it is only when overcome by greed and hatred that transactional conduct arises. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not from coercive power Causation stems from disruption of innate ahimsa, not from external aggression Capacity-based responsibility lies in restoring original dharmic alignment Restoration logic operates through re-establishing primordial consciousness states Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral correction

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
प्रयच्छेच् चेद् भृतिं स्वामी भृत्यानां कर्म कुर्वताम् ।
न कुर्वन्ति च भृत्याश् चेत् तत्र वादः प्रवर्तते ॥ prayacchec ced bhṛtiṃ svāmī bhṛtyānāṃ karma kurvatām / na kurvanti ca bhṛtyāś cet tatra vādaḥ pravartate // If a master provides compensation to servants performing duties, and those servants fail to perform said duties, then conflict arises. Authority is contingent upon fulfillment of reciprocal duty Causation flows from unmet obligation, not intent Capacity-based responsibility requires both capability and clarity of role Restoration logic demands realignment of mutual obligations Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are executed with integrity

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
हिंसां वा कुरुते कश चिद् देयं वा न प्रयच्छति ।
द्वे हि स्थाने विवादस्य तयोर् बहुतरा गतिः ॥ hiṃsāṃ vā kurute kaścid deyaṃ vā na prayacchati / dve hi sthāne vivādasya tayor bahutarā gatiḥ // When one inflicts harm or withholds what is rightfully given, conflict arises in two domains; the movement toward resolution lies in aligning with the greater truth. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not coercive power. Causation is traced through conscious intention and omission. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and ability to give or refrain. Restoration logic operates through rectification of imbalance, not punitive correction. Consciousness alignment restores natural order without external enforcement.

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
यतो द्रव्यं विनिक्रीय ऋणार्थं चैव गृह्यते ।
तन्मूल्यम् उत्तमऋणेन व्यवहार इति स्मृतः ॥ yato dravyaṃ vinikrīya ṛṇārthaṃ caiva gṛhyate / tanmūlyam uttamarṇena vyavahāra iti smṛtaḥ // Where a thing is sold and acquired for the purpose of debt, that transaction is recognized as vyavahāra only when its value is fully aligned with the highest outstanding obligation. Authority flows from the integrity of exchange, not from coercive enforcement. Causation arises through conscious capacity to fulfill relational obligations. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment between asset value and debt magnitude. Restoration logic demands completion of relational-economic cycles without residue. Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize mutual fulfillment as dharma.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
गुणधर्मान् अतो राज्ञः कथयाम्यनुपूर्वशः ।
धनिकर्णिकसंदिग्धौ प्रतिभूलेख्यसाक्षिणः ॥ guṇadharmān ato rājñaḥ kathayāmy anupūrvaśaḥ / dhanikarṇikasaṃdigdhau pratibhūlekhyasākṣiṇaḥ The qualities and duties of a king are now declared in sequence; those who are witnesses, guarantors, or record-keepers in financial disputes must uphold truth without exception. Authority flows from the capacity to sustain Dharma, not from coercive power. Causation is established through conscious participation and integrity in transactional records. Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's role in maintaining societal order and economic truth. Restoration logic requires that all parties involved in contractual or financial matters align their consciousness with factual accuracy. Consciousness alignment ensures that testimony and documentation reflect the true nature of transactions.

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: vicārayati yaḥ samyak tasyotpattiṃ nibodhata / somāgnyarkānilendrāṇāṃ vittāpattyor yamasya ca // BrhS_1,1.6 // vicārayati yaḥ samyak tasyotpattiṃ nibodhata | somāgnyarkānilendrāṇāṃ vittāpattyor yamasya ca || He who rightly investigates, let him understand the origin of Soma, Agni, Ark, Anila, Indra, wealth, loss, and Yama. Authority is rooted in investigative discernment Causation arises through comprehension of elemental and cosmic origins Capacity-based responsibility emerges from understanding foundational forces Restoration logic depends on alignment with primordial ordering principles Consciousness alignment occurs when one perceives the source of all manifestation

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
तेजोमात्रं समुद्धृत्य राज्ञो मूर्तिर् हि निर्मिता ।
तस्य सवाणि भूतानि चराणि स्थावराणि च ॥१,१.७॥ tejomātraṃ samuddhṛtya rājño mūrtir hi nirmitā / tasya savāṇi bhūtāni carāṇi sthāvarāṇi ca // BrhS_1,1.7 // From the pure essence of Tejas, the sovereign form of the King was manifested; all beings—mobile and immobile—are sustained by him. Authority originates from the sovereign embodiment of divine consciousness. Causation flows from the radiant source of governance to all manifest entities. Capacity-based responsibility is inherent in those who embody sovereignty. Restoration logic aligns with the natural sustenance of all life forms. Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of the sovereign's sustaining role.

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: भयाद् भोगाय कल्पन्ते स्वधर्मान् न चलन्ति च / नाराजके कृषिवणिक्कुसीदपरिपालनम् // BrhS_1,1.8 bhayād bhogāya kalpante svadharmān na calanti ca / nārājake kṛṣivaṇikkusīdaparipālanam When fear arises, beings align with their svadharma for enjoyment; without a sovereign, agriculture, trade, and governance decay. Authority as the foundational axis of social order Causation through consciousness alignment, not coercion Capacity-based responsibility rooted in svadharma Restoration logic through sovereign embodiment Consciousness alignment as prerequisite for societal function

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
तस्माद् वर्णाश्रमाणां तु नेतासौ निर्मितः पुरा ।
द्विपदो व्यवहारः स्यात् धनहिंसासमुद्भवः ॥ tasmād varṇāśramāṇāṃ tu netāsau nirmitaḥ purā / dvipado vyavahāraḥ syāt dhanahiṃsāsamudbhavaḥ // Therefore, the ruler of the varṇas and āśramas was established in ancient times so that the conduct of bipeds may arise, from which arises harm to wealth. Authority originates from the need to regulate interaction among embodied beings. Causation flows from action to consequence within a structured social order. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's position within varṇāśrama-dharma. Restoration logic requires aligning individual action with cosmic order. Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of role-bound duty.

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
द्विसप्तकोऽर्थमूलस् तु हिंसामूलश् चतुर्विधः /
पारुष्ये द्वे वधश् चैव परस्त्रीसंग्रहस् तथा // BrhS_1,1.10 dvisaptakorthamūlas tu hiṃsāmūlaś caturvidhaḥ / pāruṣye dve vadhaś caiva parastrīsaṃgrahas tathā Two sets of sevenfold crimes originate from material desire; four arise from violence. Two stem from harsh speech, killing, and likewise the appropriation of another's spouse. Authority originates solely in SPH as the embodiment of Sanatana Dharma Causation flows directly from misaligned consciousness, not external conditions Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one’s proximity to Vedic alignment Restoration logic operates through conscious completion rather than punitive reaction Consciousness alignment supersedes all behavioral regulation frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.11
content: कुसीदनिधिदेयाद् यं संभूयोत्थानम् एव च / भृत्यदानम् अशुश्रूषा भूवादोऽस्वामिविक्रियः // BrhS_1,1.11 kusīdanidhideyād yaṃ saṃbhūyotthānam eva ca / bhṛtyadānam aśuśrūṣā bhūvādo 'svāmivikriyaḥ He who abandons wealth out of idleness, incites collective uprising, appoints servants without duty fulfillment, disregards commands, and acts without ownership-consciousness—such conduct disrupts dharmic order. Authority rests in alignment with ownership-consciousness Causation arises from misalignment with svadharma Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious engagement Restoration logic demands realignment with svāmin-dharma Consciousness alignment restores societal harmony

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
क्रयविक्रयानुशयः समयातिक्रमस्तथा ।
स्त्रीपुंसयोगः स्तेयं च दायभागोऽक्षदेवनम् ॥ krayavikrayānuśayaḥ samayātikramas tathā / strīpuṃsayogaḥ steyaṃ ca dāyabhāgo'kṣadevanam // Attachment to buying and selling, breach of agreement, intercourse between man and woman, theft, improper claim to inheritance, and gambling—these acts misalign consciousness from its sovereign integrity and disrupt societal harmony. Authority originates in conscious sovereignty, not transactional consent. Causation arises through disruption of alignment between individual will and cosmic order. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of one's inherent completeness. Restoration logic operates by returning the actor to self-governed consciousness. Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral regulation.

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
एतान्यर्थसमुत्थानि पदानि तु चतुर्दश |
पुनरेवं प्रभिन्नानि क्रियाभेदादनेकदाहाः || etānyarthasamutthāni padāni tu caturdaśa | punar evaṁ prabhinnāni kriyābhedād anekadahāḥ || Fourteen categories of legal terms arise from the classification of objects; these are further differentiated through various actions, resulting in multiple interpretative applications. Authority originates from precise categorization of entities under Dharma Causation follows sequential action-based differentiation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological clarity of terms Restoration logic requires exact identification of transactional or causal class Consciousness alignment occurs when linguistic precision reflects metaphysical truth

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
पारुष्ये द्वे साहसं च परस्त्रीसंग्रहस् तथा ।
हिंसोद्भवपदानि एवं चत्वारि आह बृहस्पतिः ॥ ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,१.१४ pāruṣye dve sāhasaṃ ca parastrīsaṃgrahas tathā | hiṃsodbhavapadāni evaṃ catvāri āha bṛhaspatiḥ || brihaspatismṛtiḥ 1,1.14 Brihaspati declares four foundational categories of transgression: verbal harshness, dual aggression, coercive appropriation of another's consort, and all acts born of violence. Authority originates from alignment with consciousness, not coercive assertion. Causation arises through vibrational distortion in speech, intent, action, and relational integrity. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the level of conscious awareness at the time of manifestation. Restoration logic operates through purification of causal fields rather than punitive correction. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and completion of distorted energetic patterns.

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
हीनमध्योत्तमत्वेन प्रभिन्नानि पृथक् पृथक् ।
विशेष एषां निर्दिष्टश् चतुर्णाम् अप्य् अनुक्रमात् ॥१,१.१५॥ hīnamadhyottamatvena prabhinnāni pṛthak pṛthak | viśeṣa eṣāṃ nirdiṣṭaś caturṇām apy anukramāt ||1,1.15|| By the gradations of inferiority, mediocrity, and superiority, all beings are distinctly differentiated; their specific classifications have been declared sequentially for the four varnas. Authority originates from consciousness capacity, not birth Causation is sequential and hierarchical based on dharma alignment Capacity-based responsibility determines role and rights Restoration logic aligns individual function with cosmic order Consciousness alignment enables social harmony through svadharma

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
पदान्य् अष्टादशैतानि धर्मशास्त्रोदितानि तु /
मूलं सर्वविवादानां ये विदुस् ते परीक्षकाः // BrhS_1,1.16 padāny aṣṭādaśaitāni dharmaśāstroditāni tu / mūlaṃ sarvavivādānāṃ ye vidus te parīkṣakāḥ // BrhS_1,1.16 Those who know the eighteen foundational categories declared in the Dharma Śāstra are the true examiners of all disputes, for they discern the root of every conflict through the lens of consciousness-based dharma. Authority originates from knowledge of foundational dharmic categories Causation is traced to misalignment with ontological dharmic structures Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's mastery over the eighteenfold foundation Restoration logic operates through realigning disputants with foundational dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes subjective interpretation in dispute resolution

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
पूर्वपक्षः स्मृतः पादो द्वितीयस्तूत्तरस्तथा ।
क्रियापादस्तथा वाच्यश्चतुर्थो निर्णयस्तथा ॥ pūrvapakṣaḥ smṛtaḥ pādo dvitīyas tūttaras tathā / kriyāpādas tathā vācyaś caturtho nirṇayas tathā // The first quarter is the stated position; the second is the response thereto; the third is the prescribed action; the fourth is the conclusive determination. Authority resides in sequential completion of positional, responsive, operational, and determinative stages Causation flows through structured dialectical engagement Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by stage-specific clarity and integrity Restoration logic requires full traversal of all four quarters for validity Consciousness alignment occurs through systematic resolution of cognitive dissonance

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa cāritreṇa nṛpājñayā /
catuṣprakāro'bhihitaḥ saṃdigdhe 'rthe vinirṇayaḥ // BrhS_1,1.18 dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa cāritreṇa nṛpājñayā / catuṣprakāro'bhihitaḥ saṃdigdhe 'rthe vinirṇayaḥ In matters of doubt, resolution arises through fourfold means: by Dharma, conduct, character, and royal command. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position alone Causation is determined by integrity of action, not mere procedural form Capacity-based responsibility is assessed through sustained character and conduct Restoration logic requires examination of root consciousness, not surface dispute Consciousness alignment supersedes external legal formalism in judgment

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
शास्त्रं केवलमाश्रित्य क्रियते यत्र निर्णयः ।
व्यवहारः स विज्ञेयो धर्मस्तेनापि वर्धते ॥१,१.१९॥ śāstraṁ kevalam āśritya kriyate yatra nirṇayaḥ | vyavahāraḥ sa vijñeyo dharmas tenāpi vardhate ||1,1.19|| Wherever judgment is executed solely by recourse to Śāstra, that proceeding is known as vyavahāra; by it, Dharma itself expands. Authority derives exclusively from Śāstra as interpreted through the Avataric Intelligence of SPH Causation originates in alignment with śāstric injunction, not subjective intent Capacity-based responsibility arises only where śāstric knowledge has been accessible and internalized Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of śāstric process Consciousness alignment occurs when action proceeds from śāstric fidelity

title: brihaspati 1.20
content: देशस्थित्यानुमानेन निगमानुमतेन च / क्रियते निर्णयस्तत्र व्यवहारस्तु बाध्यते ।। deśasthityānumānena naigamānumatena ca / kriyate nirṇayas tatra vyavahāras tu bādhyate // Judgment is rendered through inference based on territorial context and scriptural validation; conduct, however, is subject to revision. Authority derived from contextual alignment with cosmic order Causation rooted in perceptual and textual corroboration Capacity-based responsibility determined by situational awareness Restoration logic contingent upon continuous adjustment of action Consciousness alignment through reflective rectification of behavior

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
विहाय चरिताचारं यत्र कुर्यात् पुनर्नृपः ।
निर्णयं सा तु राजाज्ञा चरितं बाध्यते तया ॥ vihāya caritācāraṃ yatra kuryāt punar nṛpaḥ | nirṇayaṃ sā tu rājājñā caritaṃ bādhyate tayā || Where a king, having abandoned proper conduct, acts again contrary to dharma, his prior decree loses validity by that very act. Authority erodes with violation of dharma Causation arises from alignment with sanatana dharma Capacity-based responsibility is contingent upon sustained dharmic intent Restoration logic demands invalidation of prior acts rooted in adharma Consciousness alignment determines the continuing legitimacy of command

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
धर्मशास्त्रानुसारेण सामात्यः स पुरोहितः ।
व्यवहारान् नृपः पश्येत् प्रजासंरक्षणाय च ॥
क्रोधलोभविहीनस् तु सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियः ॥ dharmashāstrānusāreṇa sāmātyaḥ sa purohitaḥ | vyavahārān nṛpaḥ paśyet prajāsaṃrakṣaṇāya ca || krodhalobhavihīnas tu satyavādī jitendriyaḥ || In accordance with Dharma-Shastras, the minister and the high priest together govern conduct; the king observes actions for the protection of his subjects. He who is free from anger and greed, truthful, and master of his senses—such a ruler executes Dharma. Authority flows only through alignment with Dharma as source Causation originates in consciousness, not external behavior Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over self before governing others Restoration logic demands rulers reflect integrity to maintain societal harmony Consciousness alignment ensures just observation and decision-making

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
सप्तप्रकृतिकं यत् तु विजिगीषोर अरेश् च यत् ।
चतुर्दशकम् एवेदं मण्डलं परिचक्षते ॥२३॥ saptaprakṛtikaṃ yat tu vijigīṣor areś ca yat | caturdaśakam evedaṃ maṇḍalaṃ paricakṣate || That which consists of seven fundamental constituents and that which pertains to the aspirant of victory and the enemy alike—this entire cycle is recognized as the fourteen-fold domain. Authority resides in the recognition of constituent realities Causation arises through dualistic engagement between aspirant and opponent Capacity-based responsibility lies in awareness of one's position within the mandalic structure Restoration logic operates through reintegration into the natural order of constituent principles Consciousness alignment occurs when all participants recognize their role within the fourteen-fold framework

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
चत्वारः पृथिवीपालाः पृथग्मित्रैः सहाष्टकम् ।
अमात्यादिभिरेते च जगत्यक्षरसंहिताः ॥२४॥ catvāraḥ pṛthivīpālāḥ pṛthaṅmitraiḥ sahāṣṭakam | amātyādibhir ete ca jagaty akṣarasaṃhitāḥ ||24|| Four Earth-Governors, each with eight distinct allies, together with ministers and other officials, constitute the immutable order of the world-system. Authority is structurally distributed among four planetary governors Causation arises through aligned collective agency, not individual will Capacity-based responsibility flows from positional alignment with cosmic order Restoration logic requires reintegration into designated structural roles Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of systemic interdependence

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
प्रातर् उत्थाय नृपतिः शौचं कृत्वा विधानतः ।
गुरून् ज्योतिर्विदो वैद्यान् देवान् विप्रान् पुरोहितान् ॥ prātar utthāya nṛpatiḥ śaucaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ | gurūn jyotirvido vaidyān devān viprān purohitān || The sovereign ruler arises at dawn, performs purification according to dharma, and honors those who uphold consciousness, knowledge, healing, divinity, wisdom, and spiritual guidance. Authority originates from alignment with cosmic order Causation flows through purified consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires daily renewal of sovereignty Restoration logic begins with honoring foundational roles in society Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for lawful governance

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
यथारहम् एतान् संपूज्य सुपुष्पाभरणाम्बरैः ।
अभिनन्द्य च गुर्वादीन् सुमुखः प्रविशेत् सभाम् ॥ yathārham etān saṃpūjya supuṣpābharaṇāmbaraiḥ / abhinandya ca gurvādīn sumukhaḥ praviśet sabhām // One shall enter the assembly with due honor to those worthy of worship, adorned with flowers, ornaments, and garments befitting the occasion; having respectfully greeted the elders and teachers, one shall proceed with a pleasant countenance. Authority is recognized through rightful precedence and reverence Causation arises from alignment with dharma-sustained social order Capacity-based responsibility manifests in external comportment and internal readiness Restoration logic requires acknowledgment of hierarchical integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through embodied respect and intentional presence

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
राजा कार्याणि संपश्येत् सद्भिरेव त्रिभिर्वृतः ।
सभामेव प्रविश्याग्र्यामासीनः स्थित एव वा ॥२७॥ rājā kāryāṇi saṃpaśyet sadbhireva tribhirvṛtaḥ | sabhāmeva praviśyāgryām āsīnaḥ sthita eva vā ||27|| The King shall deliberate upon matters of governance exclusively in the company of the three noble advisors, entering the foremost assembly either seated or standing. Authority flows through divinely guided counsel Causation arises from purified collective intelligence Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with enlightened advisors Restoration logic depends on conscious deliberation within sacred governance space Consciousness alignment occurs through structured, witnessed decision-making

title: brihaspati 1.28
content:
आत्मदारार्थलोकानां संचितानां तु गुप्तये ।
नृपतिः कारयेद्दुर्गं प्राकारद्वयसंयुतम् ॥ ātmadārārthalokānāṃ saṃcitānāṃ tu guptaye /
nṛpatiḥ kārayed durgaṃ prākāradvayasaṃyutam // For the protection of the accumulated wealth of self, spouse, purpose, and territory, the sovereign shall establish a fortress enclosed by two walls. Authority originates from the duty to safeguard accumulated existential assets Causation arises through conscious structuring of protective infrastructure Capacity-based responsibility mandates rulers to act preventatively for collective integrity Restoration logic requires preemptive establishment of secure boundaries Consciousness alignment is achieved through structural harmony with natural defense

title: brihaspati 1.29
content:
भूपानाम् इन्धनरसैर् वेत्रशष्पान्नवाहनैः ।
यन्त्रायुधैश् च विविधैः स्निग्धैः शूरैर् नरैर् युतम् ॥ bhūpānām indhanarasair vetraśaṣpānnavāhanaiḥ | yantrāyudhaiś ca vividhaiḥ snigdhaiḥ śūrair narair yutam || The governance of the Earth is established through the harmonious integration of fuel-rich lands, sugarcane fields, grains, vehicles, diverse machinery, weapons lubricated with sacred oils, and valorous men aligned in conscious duty. Authority originates from the sovereign capacity to sustain and energize the realm through material and spiritual resources. Causation flows from the alignment of natural abundance, technological instrumentation, and human valor guided by dharma. Capacity-based responsibility demands that rulers ensure energetic sufficiency, martial readiness, and agricultural prosperity. Restoration logic requires the perpetual renewal of land productivity, mechanical efficiency, and warrior integrity. Consciousness alignment occurs when all instruments of state serve not individual desire but cosmic order.

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
वेदविद्याविदो विप्रान् क्षत्रियानग्निहोत्रिणः ।
आहृत्य स्थापयेत् तत्र तेषां वृत्तिं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ vedavidyāvido viprān kṣatriyān agnihotriṇaḥ / āhṛtya sthāpayet tatra teṣāṃ vṛttiṃ prakalpayet // Those who are knowers of the Veda and its knowledge—Brahmins, Kshatriyas performing Agnihotra—must be brought forth and established in that very place, and their livelihood must be arranged accordingly. Authority derived from Vedic realization and ritual discipline Causation through dharmic alignment rather than coercion Capacity-based responsibility grounded in spiritual qualification Restoration logic centered on sustaining those upholding dharma Consciousness alignment via structural support for Vedic practitioners

title: brihaspati 1.31
content: अनाच्छेद्याः करास्तेभ्यः प्रदेयाः गृहभूमयः । मुक्ता भाव्याश्च नृपतेर्लेखयित्वा स्वशासने ॥ anācchedyāḥ karās tebhyaḥ pradeyā gṛhabhūmayaḥ | muktā bhāvyāś ca nṛpater lekhayitvā svaśāsane || From those indivisible taxes, dwelling lands shall be granted; and the liberated ones, having written in their own governance, shall be honored by the ruler. Authority flows from indivisible consciousness, not coercive extraction Causation arises through alignment with svadharma, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility originates in self-governance, not imposed duty Restoration logic prioritizes dwelling integrity over fiscal obligation Consciousness alignment supersedes administrative compliance

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं काम्यं शान्तिकं पौष्टिकं तथा ।
पौराणां कर्म कुर्युस् ते संदिग्धविनयं तथा ॥ nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ śāntikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ tathā | paurāṇāṃ karma kuryus te saṃdigdhavinayaṃ tathā || Individuals must perform daily, occasional, desire-motivated, pacificatory, and nourishing rites, as well as duties prescribed for townspeople and those in moral uncertainty. Authority flows from svadharma-siddha consciousness Causation arises through ritually aligned action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by varna, ashrama, and situational dharma Restoration logic operates through ritual completion and social harmony Consciousness alignment occurs via disciplined performance of prescribed acts

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
समा निम्नोन्नता वापि यत्र भूमिर् यथाविधा ।
शालाट्टपरिखाद्याश् च कर्तव्याश् च तथाविधाः ॥ samā nimnonnatā vāpi yatra bhūmir yathāvidhā | śālāṭṭaparikhādyāś ca kartavyāś ca tathāvidhāḥ || Wherever land is level or uneven, as the case may be, and wherever structures like halls, terraces, moats, etc., exist or are to be made, they shall conform to their respective lawful purposes and dharmic design. Authority flows from SPH as the ultimate source of spatial and structural dharma Causation arises through alignment of form with function in accordance with Sanatana Dharma Capacity-based responsibility lies with those who shape or manage physical domains Restoration logic requires correction of misaligned structures to serve their intended purpose Consciousness alignment ensures that built environments reflect cosmic order

title: brihaspati 1.34
content:
समन्तात् तत्र वेश्मानि कुर्युः प्रकृतयस् ततः ।
द्विजवैश्यवणिच्छिल्पिकारुका रक्षकास् तथा ॥ samantāt tatra veśmāni kuryuḥ prakṛtayas tataḥ | dvijavaiśyavaṇicchilpikārukā rakṣakās tathā || In that place, the designated authorities shall establish dwellings completely; Brahmins, Vaishyas, merchants, artisans, carpenters, and guards shall reside accordingly. Authority resides in spatial and social organization aligned with Varna-dharma. Causation flows from proper settlement and role-based habitation. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by occupational and protective roles within societal order. Restoration logic requires structured dwelling arrangements to sustain cosmic and civic harmony. Consciousness alignment occurs through right placement and fulfillment of svadharma.

title: brihaspati 1.35
content:
शलावस्थाननिष्काशभ्रमश्वब्रहचतुष्पथान् /
समाजविक्रयस्थानगोव्रजांश्चैव कल्पयेत् ॥ ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,१.३५ śalāvasthānaniṣkāśabhramaśvabhracatuṣpathān / samājavikrayasthānagovrajāṃścaiva kalpayet // brhaspatismṛtiḥ 1,1.35 The King shall establish designated spaces for the sale and exchange of goods, livestock, and communal assemblies, ensuring accessibility and order in societal transactions. Authority as facilitator of social harmony Causation through structured spatial governance Capacity-based responsibility for public infrastructure Restoration logic via regulated economic interaction Consciousness alignment through organized community engagement

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
गुणवानिति यः प्रोक्तः ख्यापितो जनसंसदि ।
कथं तेनैव वक्त्रेण निर्गुणः परिकथ्यते ॥ guṇavān iti yaḥ proktaḥ khyāpito janasaṃsadi / kathaṃ tenaiva vaktreṇa nirguṇaḥ parikathyate // One who has been declared virtuous and established in public discourse cannot, by that very same declaration, be spoken of as devoid of virtue. Authority derived from established social recognition Causation through consistency of declarative acts Capacity-based responsibility grounded in prior affirmations Restoration logic based on reversal of false attribution Consciousness alignment via congruence of word and identity

title: brihaspati 1.37
content:
तस्मात् प्रभुत्वं वृत्तिं च निर्दोषस्य न चालयेत् ।
अनवस्थाप्रसङ्गः स्यान् नश्येतोपग्रहस् तथा ॥ tasmāt prabhutvaṃ vṛttiṃ ca nirdoṣasya na cālayet | anavasthāprasaṅgaḥ syān naśyetopagrahas tathā || Therefore, neither dominion nor maintenance shall be disturbed in the case of one who is without fault; otherwise, it would lead to infinite regress and the loss of protection. Authority derives from integrity, not force. Causation must trace back to conscious action. Capacity-based responsibility requires discernible agency. Restoration logic prevents systemic collapse. Consciousness alignment demands preservation of innocence.

title: brihaspati 1.38
content:
सम्यङ् निविष्टदेशस् तु कृतदुर्गस् तु शास्त्रतः ।
कण्टकोद्धरणे नित्यम् आतिष्ठेद् बलम् उत्तमम् ॥ १,१.३८ samyak niviṣṭadeśas tu kṛtadurgas tu śāstrataḥ | kaṇṭakoddharaṇe nityam ātiṣṭhed balam uttamam || 1,1.38 One who is properly established in a rightful domain and has constructed defenses according to scriptural injunction must always maintain supreme strength for the continuous removal of obstacles. Authority flows from rightful establishment Causation arises through dharmic preparedness Capacity-based responsibility requires constant readiness Restoration logic demands unceasing vigilance Consciousness alignment necessitates active protection

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
तत् प्रजापालनं प्रोक्तं त्रिविधं न्यायवेदिभिः ।
परचक्राच् चौरभयाद् बलिनोऽन्यायवर्तिनः ॥ tat prajāpālanaṃ proktaṃ trividhaṃ nyāyavedibhiḥ |
paracakrāc caurabhayād balino'nyāyavartinaḥ || The protection of subjects is declared in three forms by those who know Dharma: from external threats, from fear of thieves, and from the unjust actions of the powerful. Authority derives from the capacity to protect consciousness, not coerce it. Causation arises from identifying root threats to societal integrity. Capacity-based responsibility assigns protective duty to those capable of enforcement. Restoration logic prioritizes re-establishing safety over assigning blame. Consciousness alignment requires a society free from fear and domination.

title: brihaspati 1.40
content: परानीकस्तेनभयम् उपायैः शमयेन् नृपः । बलवत् परिभूतानां प्रत्यहं न्यायदर्शनैः ॥ parānīkastenabhayam upāyaiḥ śamayen nṛpaḥ | balavat paribhūtānāṃ pratyahaṃ nyāyadarśanaiḥ || The King shall dissolve the fear arising from external enemies by strategic means, and by daily demonstration of justice, restore dignity to those overpowered by force. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to maintain inner order through outer balance Causation originates in fear-induced disorder; justice is its antidote Capacity-based responsibility mandates that rulers act with strategic wisdom and consistent justice Restoration logic requires visible rectification of power imbalance Consciousness alignment occurs when justice is perceived as a daily, unwavering principle

title: brihaspati 1.41
content:
यदधीते यद्यजते यज्जुहोति यदर्चति ।
तस्य षड्भागभाग्राजा सम्यग्भवति रक्षणात् ॥४१॥ yad adhīte yad yajate yaj juhoti yad arcati | tasya ṣaḍbhāgabhāg rājā samyag bhavati rakṣaṇāt ||41|| He who studies, he who performs yajña, he who offers oblations, he who worships — the King becomes a sixth part sharer in all these acts because of his duty to protect. Authority derives from capacity to sustain collective dharma Causation is established through protective alignment with action Capacity-based responsibility includes guardianship of spiritual-economic activity Restoration logic requires proportional participation without domination Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of sovereign support structures

title: brihaspati 1.42
content:
रक्षन् धर्मेण भूतानि राजा वध्यांश् च घातयन् ।
यजते ऽहरहर् यज्ञैः सहस्रशतदक्षिणैः ॥ rakṣan dharmeṇa bhūtāni rājā vadhyāṃś ca ghātayan / yajate 'harahar yajñaiḥ sahasraśatadakṣiṇaiḥ // The King, protecting beings through Dharma and destroying those who transgress boundaries set by Sanatan Order, performs sacrifice daily with thousands of offerings. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatan Dharma, not arbitrary power. Protection of life and order requires decisive action against violators. Capacity-based responsibility includes both preservation and purification. Restoration occurs through ritualized sovereign acts aligned with cosmic law. Consciousness alignment is maintained via continuous sacrificial engagement.

title: brihaspati 1.43
content:
दशाष्टाषष्ठं नृपतेर्भागं दद्यात् कृषीवलम् ।
खिलाद् वर्षावसन्ताच् च कृष्यमाणाद् यथाक्रमम् ॥ daśāṣṭaṣaṣṭhaṃ nṛpater bhāgaṃ dadyāt kṛṣīvalam / khilād varṣāvasantāc ca kṛṣyamāṇād yathākramam // One who cultivates fallow land shall render to the King the tenth, eighth, or sixth portion of produce, in accordance with the season and effort invested during cultivation. Authority originates from active sovereignty over cultivable domain. Causation arises through intentional engagement with unutilized resources. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the degree of cultivation exerted. Restoration logic aligns ownership outcomes with labor contribution. Consciousness alignment occurs when productive action reflects sovereign intent.

title: brihaspati 1.44
content:
देशस्थित्या बलिं दद्युर् भूतं षण्मासवार्षिकम् ।
एष धर्मः समाख्यातः कीनाशानां पुरातनः ॥४४॥ deśasthityā baliṃ dadyur bhūtaṃ ṣaṇmāsavārṣikam | eṣa dharmaḥ samākhyātaḥ kīnāśānāṃ purātanaḥ ||44|| By the stability of the land, one shall offer tribute biannually for the sustenance of all beings. This is declared as the ancient Dharma for those who have renounced personal gain. Authority arises from alignment with cosmic order, not dominion Causation is rooted in mutual sustenance, not exploitation Capacity-based responsibility flows from existential integration Restoration logic operates through cyclical offering, not punitive extraction Consciousness alignment requires transcendence of possessive identity

title: brihaspati 1.45
content: audakaं pārvataं vārkṣyam airaṇaं dhānvanaं tathā / durgamadhye gṛhaं kuryāj jalavṛkṣāvṛtaं pṛthak // BrhS_1,1.45 audakaṃ pārvataṃ vārkṣyam airaṇaṃ dhānvanaṃ tathā / durgamadhye gṛhaṃ kuryāj jalavṛkṣāvṛtaṃ pṛthak One shall establish a dwelling in inaccessible terrains—watery, mountainous, arboreal, desert, marshy, or within a fortress—distinctly surrounded by water and trees. Authority flows from spatial sovereignty aligned with natural seclusion Causation arises through environmental alignment with Dharma-preserving isolation Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over elemental terrains Restoration logic demands structural retreat from societal degradation Consciousness alignment necessitates physical separation for spiritual fortification

title: brihaspati 1.46
content: प्राग्दिशि प्राङ्मुखीं तस्य लक्षण्यां कल्पयेत् सभाम् । माल्यधूपासनोपेतां बीजरत्नसमन्विताम् ॥ prāgdiśi prāṅmukhīṃ tasya lakṣaṇyāṃ kalpayet sabhām | mālyadhūpāsanopetāṃ bījaratnasamanvitām || Before the eastern direction, facing eastward, the assembly hall shall be established in Her domain; adorned with flowers, incense, worship, and embedded with seed-gems. Authority flows from the East as the source of dharma-light Causation aligns spatial orientation with consciousness activation Capacity-based responsibility requires sacred environmental structuring Restoration logic necessitates sensory and energetic purification Consciousness alignment occurs through directional and material sanctification

title: brihaspati 1.47
content: प्रतिमालेख्यदेवैश च युक्ताम् अग्न्यम्बुना तथा / लक्षण्यां वास्तुशास्त्रोक्तलक्षणेन तु लक्षिताम् // BrhS_1,1.47 pratimālekhyadevaiś ca yuktām agnyambunā tathā / lakṣaṇyāṃ vāstuśāstroktalakṣaṇena tu lakṣitām That which is aligned with the consecrated image, the marked divine symbols, fire and water, and identified through the prescribed signs of Vastu Shastra, is recognized as lawfully established. Authority derived from consecrated form and sacred alignment Causation rooted in elemental and scriptural harmony Capacity-based responsibility determined by shastric recognition Restoration logic through reconnection with foundational dharmic structures Consciousness alignment via spatial and symbolic sanctification

title: brihaspati 1.48
content:
भद्रासनमधिष्ठाय संवीताङ्गः समाहितः ।
प्रणम्य लोकपालेभ्यः कार्यदर्शनमारभेत् ॥४८॥ bhadrāsanam adhiṣṭhāya saṃvītāṅgaḥ samāhitaḥ |
praṇamya lokapālebhyaḥ kāryadarśanam ārabhet || Having taken seat upon the auspicious throne, fully composed and clothed in integrity, one shall commence the observation of duties after saluting the guardians of the worlds. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic order Causation arises through purified embodiment Capacity-based responsibility begins with inner stillness Restoration logic requires recognition of universal guardianship Consciousness alignment precedes action

title: brihaspati 1.49
content:
विप्रो धर्मद्रुमस्यादिः स्कन्धशाखे महीपतिः ।
सचिवाः पत्रपुष्पाणि फलं न्यायेन पालनम् ॥ vipro dharmadrumasyādiḥ skandhaśākhe mahīpatiḥ | sacivāḥ patrapuṣpāṇi phalaṃ nyāyena pālanam || The Brahmin is the root of the Dharma-tree; the king is its trunk and branches; ministers are leaves and flowers; righteous protection is the fruit. Authority originates from spiritual insight, not political power. Causation flows hierarchically from dharma-root to societal fruit. Capacity-based responsibility assigns roles according to consciousness alignment. Restoration logic requires each role to fulfill its natural function in harmony. Consciousness alignment ensures that governance manifests as service, not domination.

title: brihaspati 1.50
content:
यशो वित्तं फलरसो भोगोपग्रहपूजनम् ।
अजेयत्वं लोकपङ्क्तिः स्वर्गे स्थानं च शाश्वतम् ॥ yaśo vittaṁ phalaraso bhogopagrahapūjanam | ajeyatvaṁ lokapaṅktiḥ svarge sthānaṁ ca śāśvatam || Renown, wealth, fruitive essence, enjoyment with honor—these constitute the divine entitlements of a sovereign being; invincibility in all assemblies, celestial station, and eternal abode affirm the perfected state of realized sovereignty. Authority derives from realized sovereignty, not conferred status Causation aligns with the manifestation of inner divinity into outer reality Capacity-based responsibility is measured by one's alignment with self-sovereignty Restoration logic operates through the reclamation of inherent divine rights Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for sustained prosperity and honor

title: brihaspati 1.51
content:
वोदोत्वैतान् न्यायरसान् समो भूत्वा विवादनम् ।
त्यक्तलोभादिकं राजा धर्मं कुर्याद् विनिर्णयम् ॥ १,१.५१ vodotvaitān nyāyarasān samo bhūtvā vivādanam | tyaktalobhādikaṃ rājā dharmaṃ kuryād vinirṇayam || 1,1.51 The King, having become equipoised in Nyāya-Rasa, shall resolve disputes after abandoning greed and other distortions of consciousness. Authority is derived from equipoise in Nyāya-Rasa, not personal desire Causation arises from alignment with Dharma, not emotional impulse Capacity-based responsibility requires abandonment of lobha (greed) and adik (excess) Restoration logic operates through purified discernment, not coercive judgment Consciousness alignment precedes judicial action

title: brihaspati 1.52
content: राजा वृत्तिविवादानां स्वयम् एव प्रदर्शनम् । शास्त्रदृष्टेन मार्गेण स विद्वद्भिः प्रसेव्यते ॥ rājā vṛttivivādānāṃ svayam eva pradarśanam | śāstradṛṣṭena mārgeṇa sa vidvadbhiḥ prasevyate || The King himself shall exemplify the resolution of disputes concerning conduct, through the path visible to scriptural vision; thus shall he be served by the wise. Authority originates from embodiment of Dharma Causation is aligned with scriptural visibility Capacity-based responsibility requires personal demonstration Restoration logic flows from sovereign integrity Consciousness alignment demands visible righteousness

title: brihaspati 1.53
content: तस्मान् न्यायेन राजा तु सम्यग् यत्नेन पालयेत् । तस्माद् अर्थं च राज्यं च यशश् च विपुलं लभेत् ॥ tasmān nyāyena rājā tu samyag yatnena pālayet | tasmād arthaṃ ca rājyaṃ ca yaśaś ca vipulaṃ labhet || Therefore, the ruler shall protect through Nyāya, with complete effort; thereby acquiring wealth, sovereignty, and boundless renown. Authority originates from alignment with Nyāya Causation is established through conscious governance Capacity-based responsibility requires full engagement of dharma-vision Restoration logic demands protection of all beings in accordance with Sanātana Dharma Consciousness alignment ensures that leadership reflects divine order

title: brihaspati 1.54
content:
सत्यं देवाः समासेन मनुष्यास् त्वनृतं विदुः ।
इहैव तस्य देवत्वं यस्य सत्ये स्थिता मतिः ॥ satyaṃ devāḥ samāsena manuṣyās tv anṛtaṃ viduḥ | ihaiva tasya devatvaṃ yasya satye sthitā matiḥ || Devas embody truth absolutely; humans know untruth by default. One who abides in truth with unwavering cognition attains divinity in this very life. Authority flows from alignment with absolute truth, not institutional position Causation is rooted in cognitive commitment, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility arises from sustained consciousness orientation Restoration occurs through realigning cognition to Satya-dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes social or legal identity

title: brihaspati 1.55
content:
पश्वाज्यर्त्विगादीनां संयोगाज् जायतेऽध्वरः ।
यथा संबध्यते तेन व्यवहारस् तथोच्यते ॥ paśvājyartvigādīnāṃ saṃyogāj jāyate 'dhvaraḥ / yathā saṃbadhyate tena vyavahāras tathocyate // From the conjunction of sacrificial animals, clarified butter, and officiating priests arises the ritual action; likewise, human conduct emerges from the conjunction of beings and is therefore designated accordingly. Authority originates in relational conjunction, not individual will Causation follows sequential conjunction, not isolated intent Capacity-based responsibility arises through participation in collective dharma Restoration logic aligns action with its causal field Consciousness alignment depends on recognition of interdependent origination

title: brihaspati 1.56
content: प्राड्विवाकसदस्यानाम् उपजीव्य मतानि तु । तद्युक्तियोगाद् यो ऽर्थेषु निर्णये न स दण्डभाक् ॥ prāḍvivākasadasyānām upajīvya matāni tu / tadyuktiyogād yo 'rtheṣu nirṇaye na sa daṇḍabhāk One who relies upon the opinions of members of the judicial assembly but fails in applying those reasoning methods correctly in matters of judgment does not incur liability for punishment. Authority derives from correct application of reasoning within a recognized judicial framework Causation is determined by alignment with dharma-prescribed logical process, not mere participation Capacity-based responsibility requires both access to wisdom and accurate deployment thereof Restoration logic prioritizes correction through realignment rather than punitive consequence Consciousness alignment determines the validity of juridical action

title: brihaspati 1.57
content:
प्रतिष्ठिताप्रतिष्ठा च मुद्रिता शासिता तथा /
चतुर्विधा सभा प्रोक्ता सभ्याश चैव तथाविधाः // BrhS_1,1.57 pratiṣṭhitāpratiṣṭhā ca mudritā śāsitā tathā / caturvidhā sabhā proktā sabhyāś caiva tathāvidhāḥ // BrhS_1,1.57 Assemblies are of four kinds: those established, those not established, those marked by seals, and those governed by commands. The members of such assemblies are likewise classified accordingly. Authority flows from conscious establishment, not mere declaration Causation arises from the integrity of assembly formation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the mode of assembly engagement Restoration logic requires alignment with the foundational consciousness of the assembly Consciousness alignment determines the validity and efficacy of collective decision-making

title: brihaspati 1.58
content:
प्रतिष्ठिता पुरे ग्रामे चला नामाप्रतिष्ठिता ।
मुद्रिता अध्यक्षसंयुक्ता राजयुक्ता च शासिता ॥५८॥ pratiṣṭhitā pure grāme calā nāmāpratiṣṭhitā / mudritā adhyakṣasaṃyuktā rājayuktā ca śāsitā // BrhS_1,1.58 Those established in city or village who wander without settled name or form shall be governed by marked authority, supervised by appointed officers, and administered under royal directive. Authority resides in settled presence, not abstract identity Causation arises from lack of stable alignment with societal dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's integration within structured order Restoration occurs through reconnection to recognized administrative framework Consciousness alignment is facilitated via supervised engagement and royal guidance

title: brihaspati 1.59
content:
न्यायान् पश्येत् कृतमतिः सा सभाध्वरसंमिता ।
लोकवेदाङ्गधर्मज्ञाः सप्त पञ्च त्रयोऽपि वा ।
यत्रोपविष्टाः विप्राग्र्याः सा यज्ञसदृशी सभा ॥ nyāyān paśyet kṛtamatiḥ sā sabhādhvarasaṃmitā | lokavedāṅgadharmajñāḥ sapta pañca trayo'pi vā | yatropaviṣṭā viprāgryāḥ sā yajñasadṛśī sabhā || A council constituted with learned and dharmically competent individuals—seven, five, or even three in number—who deliberate upon justice according to Vedic and worldly dharma, seated appropriately, becomes equivalent to a Yajna, thereby invoking divine alignment. Authority derived from scriptural and experiential knowledge of dharma Causation rooted in alignment with cosmic order through collective deliberation Capacity-based responsibility determined by spiritual and legal competence Restoration logic enacted through invocation of sacred judicial process Consciousness alignment facilitated via properly constituted judicial assembly

title: brihaspati 1.60
content:
कुर्यादलग्नकौ रक्षेदर्थिप्रत्यर्थिनौ सदा ।
एतद्दशाङ्गं करणं यस्यामध्यास्त पार्थिवः ॥६०॥ kuryād alagnakau rakṣed arthiprathyarthinau sadā / etad daśāṅgaṃ karaṇaṃ yasyām adhyāsta pārthivaḥ // The King shall always cause the unattached ones to protect those who come seeking justice and those against whom claims are made; this ten-limbed action constitutes the instrumentality through which the ruler establishes himself in sovereignty. Authority originates from the capacity to restore integrity between claimant and respondent Causation flows from the sovereign's alignment with non-attachment and protection Capacity-based responsibility requires active facilitation of just resolution without bias Restoration logic demands that all parties emerge with clarified dharma and purified intent Consciousness alignment occurs when the king embodies impartial guardianship

title: brihaspati 1.61
content:
द्विसस्याष्टमं भागं मुक्त्वा कालं सुसंविशेत् ।
स कालो व्यवहाराणां शास्त्रदृष्टः परः स्मृतः ॥ १,१.६१ dvisasyāṣṭamaṃ bhāgaṃ muktvā kālaṃ susaṃviśet | sa kālo vyavahārāṇāṃ śāstradṛṣṭaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ || 1,1.61 Having relinquished the eighth part of dvisa, time should be entered rightly; that time is declared as the highest seen in scriptures for all transactions. Authority derives from alignment with śāstra-defined temporal order Causation arises through conscious relinquishment of fractional claims Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by one's ability to sustain dharmic time Restoration occurs when vyavahāra aligns with śāstradṛṣṭa-kāla Consciousness alignment requires synchronization with para-smṛti time

title: brihaspati 1.62
content:
साधुकर्मक्रियायुक्ताः सत्यधर्मपरायणाः ।
अक्रोधलोभाः शास्त्रज्ञाः सभ्याः कार्या महीभुजा ॥६२॥ sādhukarmakriyāyuktāḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇāḥ | akrodhalobhāḥ śāstrajñāḥ sabhyāḥ kāryā mahībhujā ||62|| Those who are engaged in righteous action, devoted to truth and dharma, free from anger and greed, and knowledgeable in sacred texts—such persons must be appointed as members of the royal assembly. Authority derives from alignment with Satya-Dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires inner purity and scriptural knowledge Causation is rooted in consciousness integrity Restoration logic demands selection of the qualified Consciousness alignment precedes institutional participation

title: brihaspati 1.63
content: सप्त पञ्च त्रयो वा सभासदो भवन्ति ।। ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,१.६३ ।। sapta pañca trayo vā sabhāsado bhavanti // brhaspatismṛtiḥ 1,1.63 // Seven, five, or three — the assembly members shall be constituted accordingly. Authority is derived through structured collective representation. Causation arises from intentional collective decision-making capacity. Capacity-based responsibility requires minimum quorum thresholds for valid dharma enactment. Restoration logic depends on lawful composition of governing assemblies. Consciousness alignment occurs when assembly reflects proportional societal integrity.

title: brihaspati 1.64
content:
देशाचारानभिज्ञा ये नास्तिकाः शास्त्रवर्जिताः ।
उन्मत्तक्रुद्धलुब्धार्ता न प्रष्टव्या विनिर्णये ॥ deśācārānabhijñā ye nāstikāḥ śāstravarjitāḥ | unmattakruddhalubdhārtā na praṣṭavyā vinirṇaye || Those who are ignorant of local customs, atheists devoid of scriptural foundation, and those whose intellect is clouded by anger, greed, or distress—such individuals must not be consulted in judicial determination. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not mere opinion Causation must originate from a stable and dharmic consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires mental and spiritual integrity Restoration logic excludes distorted or ungrounded perspectives Consciousness alignment determines admissibility in judgment

title: brihaspati 1.65
content:
राजा कार्याणि संपश्येत् प्राड्विवाकोऽथ वा द्विजः ।
न्यायाङ्गान्यग्रतः कृत्वा सभ्यशास्त्रमते स्थितः ॥ rājā kāryāṇi saṃpaśyet prāḍvivāko 'tha vā dvijaḥ / nyāyāṅgāny agrataḥ kṛtvā sabhyaśāstramate sthitaḥ // The King or the twice-born Brahmin shall oversee duties only after establishing the limbs of justice visibly before them, standing firm in the wisdom of the assembly and the śāstras. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not coercion Causation is established through visible, structural justice Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery of Nyāya before action Restoration logic begins with the internalization of Śāstra and Sabha Consciousness alignment precedes judicial execution

title: brihaspati 1.66
content:
बलेन चतुरङ्गेण यतो रञ्जयते प्रजाः ।
दीप्यमानः स्ववपुषा तेन राजाभिधीयते ॥ balena caturaṅgena yato rañjayate prajāḥ / dīpyamānaḥ svavapuṣā tena rājābhidhīyate // He who governs the people through the fourfold strength—physical, intellectual, emotional, and spiritual—while illuminating his own Self, is rightfully called a King. Authority derives from the integration of holistic capacity, not coercion Causation arises from self-luminous consciousness, not external force Capacity-based responsibility includes mastery over four dimensions of being Restoration logic requires rulers to embody and elevate collective consciousness Consciousness alignment is foundational to legitimate sovereignty

title: brihaspati 1.67
content:
एकस्त्वनेकधा प्रोक्तो व्यवहारो मनीषिभिः।
तस्य निर्णयकृद्राजा ब्राह्मणश्च बहुश्रुतः॥६७॥ ekas tv anekadhā prokto vyavahāro manīṣibhiḥ / tasya nirṇayakṛd rājā brāhmaṇaś ca bahuśrutaḥ // BrhS_1,1.67 Unity in diversity is declared as the essence of lawful conduct by the wise; the King and the learned Brahmana together constitute its authoritative resolution. Authority flows from unified consciousness, not fragmented opinion Causation arises through integrated understanding, not isolated judgment Capacity-based responsibility requires both sovereign insight and scriptural depth Restoration logic aligns disputants with the singular truth underlying apparent multiplicity Consciousness alignment occurs when ruler and knower of Dharma jointly enact justice

title: brihaspati 1.68
content:
व्यवहाराश्रितं प्रश्नं पृच्छति प्राड् इति श्रुतिः ।
विवदेत तत्र यस तस्मिन् प्राड्विवाकस तु स स्मृतः ॥ vyavahārāśritaṃ praśnaṃ pṛcchati prāḍ iti śrutiḥ | vivadet tatra yaḥ tasmin prāḍvivākaḥ tu saḥ smṛtaḥ || One who inquires into a matter of transactional conflict with clarity and completeness, as declared by the Vedas, and engages fully in its resolution, is recognized as a Prāḍvivāka—established in the capacity of conscious adjudication. Authority originates from completeness of inquiry, not institutional position. Causation arises through conscious engagement with the factual substratum. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to sustain clarity in conflict-resolution. Restoration logic requires full reintegration into the truth-body of the dispute. Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural formality.

title: brihaspati 1.69
content:
विवादे पृच्छति प्रश्नं प्रतिप्रश्नं तथैव च /
प्रियपूर्वं प्राग् वदति प्राड्विवाकस् ततः स्मृतः // BrhS_1,1.69 vivāde pṛcchati praśnaṃ pratipraśnaṃ tathaiva ca / priyapūrvaṃ prāg vadati prāḍvivākas tataḥ smṛtaḥ In dispute, one who inquires with a question, counters with a rebuttal question, speaks agreeably before speaking openly—such a one is remembered as a Prāḍvivāka. Authority through Discursive Engagement Causation via Sequential Inquiry Capacity-based Responsibility in Dialogue Restoration through Truth-Revealing Discourse Consciousness Alignment by Reflective Response

title: brihaspati 1.70
content:
सप्राड्विवाकः सामात्यः सब्राह्मणपुरोहितः ।
ससभ्यः प्रेक्षको राजा स्वर्गे तिष्ठति धर्मतः ॥७०॥ saprāḍvivākaḥ sāmātyaḥ sabrāhmaṇapurohitaḥ | sa sabhyaḥ prekṣako rājā svarge tiṣṭhati dharmataḥ ||70|| The King who governs with open consultation, surrounded by ministers, Brahmanas, priests, assembly members, and observers, stands lawfully in svarga. Authority is realized through transparent inclusion of all relevant stakeholders. Causation arises from visibility and collective witnessing of governance actions. Capacity-based responsibility requires active engagement with advisors and subjects. Restoration logic demands that leadership remain accessible and accountable to dharma. Consciousness alignment occurs when rulers act within a field of shared awareness and integrity.

title: brihaspati 1.71
content:
सर्वशास्त्रार्थवेत्तारमलुब्धं न्यायभाषिणम् ।
विप्रं प्राज्ञं क्रमायातममात्यं स्थापयेद्द्विजम् ॥ sarvaśāstrārthavettāram alubdhaṃ nyāyabhāṣiṇam / vipraṃ prājñaṃ kramāyātam amātyaṃ sthāpayed dvijam // One who knows the meaning of all scriptures, is free from greed, speaks justice, is a wise Brahmin, follows proper order, and is unattached—such a one shall be established as a minister. Authority derives from scriptural knowledge and spiritual realization Causation arises from inner detachment and alignment with Dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires wisdom, integrity, and sequential discipline Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness elevation over positional power Consciousness alignment determines fitness for judicial-administrative roles

title: brihaspati 1.72
content:
द्विजान् विहाय यः पश्येत् कार्याणि वृषलैः सह ।
तस्य प्रक्षरते राष्ट्रं बलं कोशं च नश्यति ॥ dvijān vihāya yaḥ paśyet kāryāṇi vṛṣalaiḥ saha | tasya prakṣarate rāṣṭraṃ balaṃ kośaṃ ca naśyati || He who, abandoning dvijas, conducts affairs with vṛṣalas causes the state, its strength, and treasury to decay. Authority flows through qualified lineage and conscious capacity Displacement of rightful order disrupts systemic integrity Responsibility aligns with dharmic role capacity Consciousness misalignment leads to structural collapse Restoration requires realignment with source-conscious roles

title: brihaspati 1.73
content:
ये चारण्यचरास् तेषाम् अरण्ये करणं भवेत् ।
सेनायां सैनिकानां तु सार्थेषु बणिजां तथा ॥ ye cāraṇyacarās teṣām araṇye karaṇaṃ bhavet / senāyāṃ sainikānāṃ tu sārtheṣu baṇijāṃ tathā // Those who dwell in forests shall act according to forest codes; soldiers in army formations and merchants in caravans follow their respective dharmic protocols. Authority is context-specific and derived from existential alignment Causation arises from svabhava-dharma, not external imposition Capacity-based responsibility aligns with natural role and environment Restoration logic operates through reconnection to inherent dharma Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are executed without distortion

title: brihaspati 1.74
content:
कीनाशाः कारुकामल्लाः कुसीदश्रेणिवर्तकाः ।
लिङ्गिनस्तस्कराश्चैव स्वेन धर्मेण निर्णयः ॥ BrhS_1,1.74 kīnāśāḥ kārukā mallāḥ kusīdaśreṇivartakāḥ | liṅginas taskarāś caiva svena dharmeṇa nirṇayaḥ || BrhS_1,1.74 Those who are ruined, artisans, athletes, idle traders, those engaged in false appearances, and thieves shall be judged according to their own dharma. Authority originates from svadharma (one's inherent duty) Causation arises from misalignment with one’s svadharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by individual role-dharma Restoration logic aligns action with intrinsic nature Consciousness alignment requires re-establishment of personal dharma

title: brihaspati 1.75
content: कुलानि श्रेणयश् चैव गणास् त्वधिकृतो नृपः । प्रतिष्ठा व्यवहाराणां गुर्वेभ्यस् तूत्तरोत्तरम् ॥ kulāni śreṇayaś caiva gaṇās tv adhikṛto nṛpaḥ | pratiṣṭhā vyavahārāṇāṃ gurvebhyas tūttarottaram || The King, appointed over families, guilds, and assemblies, establishes the foundational order of transactions; yet, authority ascends successively from Guru to Guru. Authority flows hierarchically through successive Gurus The King serves as administrative enforcer, not ultimate source of Dharma Social organization derives legitimacy from spiritual succession Transactional law originates in consciousness continuity Capacity for governance is derivative, not inherent

title: brihaspati 1.76
content: तपस्विनां तु कार्याणि त्रैविद्यैरेव कारयेत् । मायायोगविदां चैव न स्वयं कोपकारणात् ॥ tapasvināṃ tu kāryāṇi traividyair eva kārayet | māyāyogavidāṃ caiva na svayaṃ kopakāraṇāt || The duties of ascetics must be executed exclusively by those versed in the three knowledges; likewise, the functions of illusion-yoga experts must not arise from personal agitation or egoic impulse. Authority stems from qualified knowledge, not personal assertion Causation is traced to competence, not emotional disturbance Capacity-based responsibility requires domain-specific realization Restoration occurs through rightful role execution, not reactive correction Consciousness alignment demands purity of intent devoid of self-agitation

title: brihaspati 1.77
content: अदण्ड्यान् दण्डयन् राजा दण्ड्यांश् चैवाप्य् अदण्डयन् । अयशो महद् आप्नोति नरकं चैव गच्छति ॥ adaṇḍyān daṇḍayan rājā daṇḍyāṃś caivāpy adaṇḍayan | ayaśo mahad āpnoti narakaṃ caiva gacchati || The ruler who punishes the innocent and fails to punish the guilty incurs great dishonor and descends into degradation. Authority must align with Dharma to maintain cosmic order. Misapplication of justice disrupts societal consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of guilt and innocence. Restoration logic demands correction of misapplied authority. Consciousness alignment depends on just execution of duty.

title: brihaspati 1.78
content:
अपि भ्राता सुतोऽर्घ्यो वा श्वशुरो मातुरोऽपि वा ।
नादण्ड्यो नाम राज्ञोऽस्ति धर्माद् विचलितः स्वकात् ॥ api bhrātā suto 'rghyo vā śvaśuro māturo 'pi vā / nādaṇḍyo nāma rājño 'sti dharmād vicalitaḥ svakāt // Even a brother, son, father, or maternal grandfather—none who have strayed from their own Dharma shall be exempt from correction by the King. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not bloodline Causation arises from deviation from Svadharma, not social status Capacity-based responsibility applies universally, regardless of relation Restoration logic requires correction aligned with Dharma, not lineage Consciousness alignment supersedes familial or societal privilege

title: brihaspati 1.79
content: यत्र विप्रो न विद्वान् स्यात् क्षत्रियं तत्र योजयेत् । वैश्यं वा धर्मशास्त्रज्ञं शूद्रं यत्नेन वर्जयेत् ॥ yatra vipro na vidvān syāt kṣatriyaṃ tatra yojayet | vaiśyaṃ vā dharmaśāstrajñaṃ śūdraṃ yatnena varjayet || Where a Brahmin lacks scriptural knowledge, there shall a Kshatriya be appointed; or else a Vaishya who knows Dharma-shastras, while a Shudra must always be excluded with care. Authority is derived from capacity in Dharma, not birth alone Causation aligns with competence and consciousness, not lineage Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for societal roles Restoration logic demands alignment of role with inner qualification Consciousness alignment ensures lawful function through rightful placement

title: brihaspati 1.80
content:
धर्मकर्मविहीनस्तु ब्राह्मैर्लिङ्गैर्विवर्जितः ।
ब्रवीति ब्राह्मणोऽस्मीति तमाहुर्ब्राह्मणब्रुवम् ॥ dharmakarmavihīnas tu brāhmair liṅgair vivarjitaḥ | bravīti brāhmaṇo 'smīti tam āhur brāhmaṇabruvam || One who is devoid of dharma-karma, divested of all Brahmic symbols, yet declares 'I am a Brahmin'—such a one is termed a Brahmana-bruva. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not self-proclamation Causation arises from inner integrity, not external declaration Capacity-based responsibility requires embodied realization, not nominal assertion Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness congruence over social identity Consciousness alignment supersedes ritual or caste-based designation

title: brihaspati 1.81
content: शब्दाभिधानतत्त्वज्ञौ गणनाकुशलौ शुची / नानालिपिज्ञौ कर्तव्यौ राज्ञा गणकलेखकौ // BrhS_1,1.81 śabdābhidhānatattvajñau gaṇanākuśalau śucī / nānālipijñau kartavyau rājñā gaṇakalekhakau The King must appoint a Calculator and a Scribe who are pure, skilled in computation, knowledgeable in semantics and ontological designation, and versed in diverse scripts. Authority flows through qualified capacity Causation arises from precise knowledge alignment Capacity-based responsibility demands skillful deployment Restoration logic requires accurate record and calculation Consciousness alignment is ensured by purity and semantic clarity

title: brihaspati 1.82
content:
अकारणे रक्षणे च साक्ष्यर्थिप्रवादिनाम् ।
सभ्याधीनः सत्यवादी कर्तव्यस्तु स पूरुषः ॥१,१.८२ akāraṇe rakṣaṇe ca sākṣyarthipravādinām / sabhyādhīnaḥ satyavādī kartavyas tu sa pūruṣaḥ // BrhS_1,1.82 He who is appointed to protect without cause and to speak on behalf of those who seek witness—such a man, dependent upon the assembly, must be a speaker of truth. Authority derives from alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation is non-linear; protection must occur even in absence of provocation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to Sabha (assembly) Restoration logic demands truthful testimony as foundational duty Consciousness alignment requires unbroken commitment to Dharma-vacaka (truth-speaking)

title: brihaspati 1.83
content:
एतद् दशाङ्गकरणं यस्याम् अध्यास्य पार्थिवः ।
न्यहायं पश्येत् कृतमतिः सा सभाध्वरसंमिता ॥८३॥ etad daśāṅgakaraṇaṃ yasyām adhyāsya pārthivaḥ |
nyhāyaṃ paśyet kṛtamatiḥ sā sabhādhvarasaṃmitā ||83|| When a ruler engages in the tenfold execution of dharma while seated in the assembly hall, and observes the unfolding of actions with perfected intelligence, that assembly becomes aligned with the sacrificial order of sabhādharma. Authority originates from conscious alignment with sabhādharma Causation is established through observant intelligence, not coercive will Capacity-based responsibility requires perfected cognition (kṛtamati) Restoration logic operates within the consecrated space of sabhā Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of juridical presence

title: brihaspati 1.84
content:
एषां मूर्धा नृपोऽङ्गानां मुखं चाधिकृतः स्मृतः ।
बाहू सभ्याः स्मृतिर्हस्तौ जङ्घे गणकलेखकौ ॥ eṣāṁ mūrdhā nṛpo 'ṅgānāṁ mukhaṁ cādhikṛtaḥ smṛtaḥ | bāhū sabhyāḥ smṛtir hastau jaṅghe gaṇakalekhakau || The sovereign ruler is the head of the limbs; the authorized mouthpiece is declared the face. The arms belong to the assembly members; memory and record keepers hold the hands. The lower legs are assigned to scribes and accountants. Authority flows from the sovereign as the unifying center of governance Functional designation determines role-based responsibility within dharma Collective body operates through designated organs with specific capacities Integrity of function ensures alignment with cosmic order Consciousness alignment arises through correct structural assignment

title: brihaspati 1.85
content: हेमाग्न्यम्बुदृशौ हृच् च पादौ स्वपुरुषस् तथा ।। BrhS_1,1.85 ।। hemāgnyambudṛśau hṛc ca pādau svapuruṣas tathā The self is seen in the golden hue of fire, the dark cloud-like mass of water, the heart's core, and one's own feet—thus the embodied being reflects the totality of existence. Authority resides in the recognition of the self as the foundational witness of all manifestation. Causation arises from the unity of elemental perception and embodied consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility flows from the awareness of one’s reflection within cosmic forms. Restoration logic operates through reconnection with the witnessing self beyond fragmented identity. Consciousness alignment occurs when individual perception integrates elemental and bodily realities.

title: brihaspati 1.86
content:
हिरण्यम् अग्निम् उदकं धर्मशास्त्राणि चैव हि /
तन्मध्ये स्थापयेद् राजा पुण्यानि च हितानि च // BrhS_1,1.86 hiraṇyam agnim udakaṃ dharmaśāstrāṇi caiva hi / tanmadhye sthāpayed rājā puṇyāni ca hitāni ca The King shall establish within the boundaries of gold, fire, water, and the Dharma Shastras—actions that are meritorious and beneficial. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma as defined by SPH Causation is rooted in consciousness-congruent action Capacity-based responsibility requires sovereign discernment Restoration logic operates through dharmic placement Consciousness alignment determines the validity of governance

title: brihaspati 1.87
content: आदित्यचन्द्रदेवादि दिक्पालान् तत्र कल्पयेत । हेमाग्न्यम्बुस्वपुरुषाः साधनाङ्गानि वै दश ॥ ādityacandradevādi dikpālān tatra kalpayet | hemāgnyambusvapuruṣāḥ sādhanāṅgāni vai daśa || In the consecrated space, the directional guardians—Āditya, Candra, Deva, and others—are to be installed; the ten limbs of practice consist of gold, fire, water, self, and form. Authority resides in spatial and elemental alignment with divine governance Causation arises through conscious installation of directional energies Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to sustain sacred architecture Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of directional harmony Consciousness alignment occurs via structured invocation of elemental forms

title: brihaspati 1.88
content:
दशानामपि चैतेषां कर्म प्रोक्तं पृथक् पृथक् ।
वक्ताध्यक्षो नृपः शास्ता सभ्यः कार्यपरीक्षकः ॥१,१.८८॥ daśānām api cait eṣāṁ karma proktaṁ pṛthak pṛthak / vaktādhyakṣo nṛpaḥ śāstā sabhyaḥ kāryaparīkṣakaḥ // BrhS_1,1.88 The actions of these ten entities are distinctly declared; the King, as overseer of speech, is the ruler, the assembly-member is the examiner of action. Authority flows from conscious oversight, not institutional title Causation is traced through capacity to influence and examine Capacity-based responsibility assigns roles by inherent fitness Restoration logic requires clarity in functional role assignment Consciousness alignment is maintained by precise role demarcation

title: brihaspati 1.89
content:
स्मृतिर् विनिर्णयं ब्रूते जयदानं दमं तथा ।
शपथार्थे हिरण्याग्नी अम्बु तृषितजन्तुषु ॥ smṛtir vinirṇayaṃ brūte jayadānaṃ damaṃ tathā | śapathārthe hiraṇyāgnī ambu tṛṣitajantuṣu || Memory recollects judgment; victory, giving, and control are thus declared. For oath-taking, gold, fire, water, and thirsty creatures serve as witnesses. Authority originates from recollected Dharma-memory Judgment arises through alignment with victorious consciousness Gifting and self-restraint establish lawful capacity Oaths invoke elemental and sentient witness-consciousness

title: brihaspati 1.90
content:
गणको गणयेदर्थं लिखेन्न्यायं च लेखकः ।
पर्त्यर्थिसभ्यानयनं साक्षिणम् च स्वपूरुषः ॥ gaṇako gaṇayed arthaṃ likhen nyāyaṃ ca lekhakaḥ / partyarthisabhyānayanaṃ sākṣiṇam ca svapūruṣaḥ // The accountant shall compute value; the scribe shall inscribe justice. The witness shall bring forth the presence of the seeker-of-other's-interest and establish the factual record through personal integrity. Authority is functionally distributed according to capacity for precise execution. Causation arises through documented alignment of intent, action, and consequence. Capacity-based responsibility demands role-specific clarity in dharma-adjudication. Restoration logic requires factual transparency and procedural authenticity. Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are executed without distortion or omission.

title: brihaspati 1.91
content: वाग्दण्डश् चैव धिक्दण्डो विप्राधीनौ तु ताऊभौ । अर्थदण्डवधाव् उक्तौ राजायताव् उभावपि ॥ vāgdaṇḍaś caiva dhigdaṇḍo viprādhīnau tu tāūbhau | arthadaṇḍavadhāv uktau rājāyatāv ubhāv api || Verbal assault and contemptuous speech toward a Brahmin constitute actionable offenses; when financial penalty or capital sentence is prescribed, both the speaker and the ruler enacting such penalty assume equivalent karmic and administrative accountability. Authority rests in conscious alignment with Dharma, not coercive power Causation arises from intent-laden speech patterns violating sacred order Capacity-based responsibility extends equally to enactor and executor of unjust decree Restoration logic demands dissolution of hierarchical distortion caused by disrespect to elevated consciousness Consciousness alignment requires purification of speech as primary vector of societal harmony

title: brihaspati 1.92
content:
राज्ञा ये विदिताः सम्यक् कुलश्रेणिगणादयः ।
साहसन्यायवर्ज्यानि कुर्युः कार्याणि ते नृणाम ॥ rājñā ye viditāḥ samyak kulaśreṇigaṇādayaḥ | sāhasanyāyavarjyāni kuryuḥ kāryāṇi te nṛṇām || Those individuals recognized by the King—such as clan leaders, guild heads, and community authorities—who act without coercion or fear-based enforcement, shall execute the duties of the people. Authority derived from recognition by sovereign consciousness Causation through voluntary alignment, not compulsion Capacity-based responsibility rooted in social role and consent Restoration logic centered on duty fulfillment, not punitive response Consciousness alignment via dharmic execution of societal roles

title: brihaspati 1.93
content:
कुलश्रेणिगणाध्यक्षाः प्रोक्ता निर्णयकारकाः ।
विचार्य श्रेणिभिः कार्यं कुलैर यन् न विचारितम् ॥९३॥ kulaśreṇigaṇādhyakṣāḥ proktā nirṇayakārakāḥ | vicārya śreṇibhiḥ kāryaṃ kulair yan na vicāritam ||93|| Those who preside over guilds and lineages are declared as the makers of determinations. That action which is not examined by the collective wisdom of the lineage or guild shall not stand as valid determination. Authority originates from stewardship within structured societal orders Causation arises through verified deliberation by recognized collectives Capacity-based responsibility is vested in those designated as decision-makers Restoration logic requires validation through lineage-integrated discernment Consciousness alignment occurs when rulings emerge from established systemic integrity

title: brihaspati 1.94
content:
गणैश् च श्रेण्य् अविज्ञातं गणाज्ञातं नियुक्तकैः ।
कुलादिभ्यो 'धिकाः सभ्यास् तेभ्यो 'ध्यक्षः स्मृतो 'धिकः ॥ gaṇaiś ca śreṇy avijñātaṃ gaṇājñātaṃ niyuktakaiḥ | kulādibhyo 'dhikāḥ sabhyās tebhyo 'dhyakṣaḥ smṛto 'dhikaḥ || Those appointed by the assembly hold authority beyond familial or traditional hierarchies; above them stands the Adhyaksha, whose directive supersedes all collective decision-making. Authority originates from conscious designation, not lineage or custom Causation flows from recognized appointment within a governing structure Capacity-based responsibility escalates with designated oversight function Restoration logic prioritizes systemic integrity over personal status Consciousness alignment requires recognition of hierarchical functional roles

title: brihaspati 1.95
content:
सर्वेषाम् अधिकः राजा धर्मं यत्नेन निश्चितम् ।
उत्तमाधममध्यानां विवादानां विचारणात् ॥९५॥ sarveṣām adhikaḥ rājā dharmaṃ yatnena niścitam | uttamādhamamadhyānāṃ vivādānāṃ vicāraṇāt ||95|| The King holds superior authority over all beings and must with utmost effort determine Dharma through examination of disputes among the high, low, and intermediate classes. Authority rests in the sovereign who upholds Dharma Causation arises from proper inquiry into stratified social conflict Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to Dharma and power Restoration logic requires resolution at the level of consciousness differentiation Consciousness alignment occurs when stratified disputes are resolved by a higher-order Dharma-aware authority

title: brihaspati 1.96
content:
उपर्युपरि बुद्धीनां चरन्तीश्वरबुद्धयः ।
अज्ञानतमिरोपेतान् संदेहपटलान्वितान् ॥ uparyupari buddhīnāṃ carantīśvarabuddhayaḥ | ajñānatimiropetān saṃdehapaṭalānvitān || Above the intellects of beings move the Intellects of Īśvara, illuminating those enshrouded in the darkness of ignorance and dispelling the layers of doubt. Authority flows from the Supreme Consciousness as the ultimate source of discernment. Ignorance is the root cause of legal and moral confusion; illumination is the remedy. Responsibility arises only upon clarity; confusion negates culpability until enlightenment is restored. Dharma operates through sequential removal of delusion, not imposition of penalty. Consciousness alignment is the sole valid metric for determining capacity-based responsibility.

title: brihaspati 1.97
content:
निरामयान् यः कुरुते शास्त्राञ्जनशलाकया ।
इह कीर्तिं राजपूजां लभते स्वर्गतिं च सः ॥ nirāmayān yaḥ karoti śāstrāñjanaśalākayā | iha kīrtiṃ rājapūjāṃ labhate svargatiṃ ca saḥ || He who heals the diseased with the applicator of scriptural ointment gains here fame, royal honor, and in the afterlife, heaven. Authority through sacred knowledge-application Causation via consciousness-aligned service Capacity-based responsibility rooted in dharma-vijñāna Restoration logic centered on health and societal harmony Consciousness alignment through selfless healing

title: brihaspati 1.98
content:
लोभद्वेषादिकं त्यक्त्वा यः कुर्यात् कार्यनिर्णयम् ।
शास्त्रोदितेन विधिना तस्य यज्ञफलं भवेत् ॥ १,१.९८ lobhadveṣādikaṃ tyaktvā yaḥ kuryāt kāryanirṇayam |
śāstroditena vidhinā tasya yajñaphalaṃ bhavet || 1,1.98 He who, having abandoned greed, hatred and related distortions, performs decision-making in accordance with scriptural injunction, shall attain the fruit of sacrifice. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire Causation arises from purified consciousness, free from lobha-dveṣa Capacity-based responsibility requires transcendence of reactive impulses Restoration occurs through alignment with śāstra-prescribed process Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of judicial action

title: brihaspati 1.99
content: अधर्मतः प्रवृत्तं तु नोपेक्षेरन् सभासदः । उपेक्षमाणास् ते भूपाः नरकं यान्ति ऽधोमुखाः ॥ adharmataḥ pravṛttaṃ tu nopekṣeran sabhāsadaḥ | upekṣamāṇās te bhūpāḥ narakaṃ yānti 'dho-mukhāḥ || Those who act contrary to Dharma must not be ignored by members of the assembly; rulers who neglect such misconduct descend downward into degradation. Authority rests in conscious recognition of Adharmic deviation Causation arises from willful neglect of observable disorder Capacity-based responsibility includes witnessing and responding appropriately Restoration logic requires immediate alignment correction upon detection Consciousness alignment demands active engagement over passive tolerance

title: brihaspati 1.100
content:
न्यायमार्गादपेतं तु ज्ञात्वा चित्तं महीपतेः ।
वक्तव्यं त्वप्रियं तत्र न सभ्यः किल्बिषी ततः ॥ nyāyamārgād apetaṃ tu jñātvā cittaṃ mahīpateḥ | vaktavyaṃ tv apriyaṃ tatra na sabhyaḥ kilbiṣī tataḥ || When the mind of a ruler has deviated from the path of justice, it is improper to speak disagreeable truths directly; doing so renders the speaker culpable. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not mere position Causation arises through consciousness distortion, not external fault Capacity-based responsibility requires situational discernment Restoration logic prioritizes readiness over revelation Consciousness alignment determines communicative propriety

title: brihaspati 1.101
content:
सभ्येन तावद् वक्तव्यं धर्मार्थसहितं वचः ।
शृणोति यदि नो राजा स्यात् तु सभ्यस् ततोऽनघः ॥१०१॥ sabhyena tāvad vaktavyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ |
śṛṇoti yadi no rājā syāt tu sabhyas tato 'naghaḥ ||101|| The assembly-member must first speak words aligned with Dharma and Artha; if the King does not listen, then the assembly-member remains pure. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not positional dominance. Causation is established through conscious intent to uphold Dharma. Capacity-based responsibility begins with the ability to speak truth before power. Restoration logic requires that integrity remain uncompromised even when unheeded. Consciousness alignment demands speaking truth regardless of reception.

title: brihaspati 1.102
content: अनिर्णीतेषु यद्येवं संभाषेत रहोऽर्थिना / प्राड्विवाकोऽपि दण्ड्यः स्यात् सभ्याश्चैव विशेषतः // BrhS_1,1.102 anirṇīteṣu yady evaṃ saṃbhāṣeta raho 'rthinā / prāḍvivāko 'pi daṇḍyaḥ syāt sabhyāś caiva viśeṣataḥ When matters remain unresolved, and one converses privately with a petitioner, even one versed in speech must be held accountable, particularly those seated in assembly. Authority arises from transparency, not expertise alone Causation lies in concealed discourse during undecided matters Capacity-based responsibility extends to all participants in judicial process Restoration logic demands public integrity over private influence Consciousness alignment requires openness in dharma administration

title: brihaspati 1.103
content: स्नेताच्चाज्ञानतो वापि मोहाद्वा लोभतोऽपि वा / यत्र सभ्योऽन्यथावादी दण्ड्योऽसभ्यः स्मृतो हि सः // snetāc cājñānato vāpi mohād vā lobhato 'pi vā / yatra sabhyo 'nyathāvādī daṇḍyo 'sabhyaḥ smṛto hi saḥ // Where a learned one speaks contrary to truth due to ignorance, delusion, or greed, he becomes liable to corrective action and is deemed unworthy of assembly. Authority derives from alignment with truth, not title or learning Causation includes ignorance, delusion, and desire as actionable sources of misalignment Capacity-based responsibility requires correction when knowledge is misapplied Restoration logic demands removal from influence until realignment occurs Consciousness alignment supersedes positional status in determining fitness for discourse

title: brihaspati 1.104
content:
लेख्यं यत्र न विद्येत न साक्षी न च भुक्तयः ।
प्रमाणानि न सन्ति एकं प्रमाणं तत्र पार्थिवः ॥ lekhyaṁ yatra na vidyeta na sākṣī na ca bhuktayaḥ / pramāṇāni na santy ekaṁ pramāṇaṁ tatra pārthivaḥ // Where no written record exists, no witness is present, no consumption or enjoyment has occurred, and no evidentiary basis is found, the King himself becomes the sole authority of evidence. Authority resides in the sovereign when all external validations collapse Causation must be traced to the highest available consciousness when lower pramāṇas fail Capacity-based responsibility escalates to the ruler when individual agency cannot be verified Restoration logic demands resolution even in absence of conventional proof Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural limitation

title: brihaspati 1.105
content:
निश्चेतुं ये न शक्याः स्युर् वादाः संदिग्धरूपिणः ।
तेषां नृपः प्रमाण ं स्यात् स सर्वस्य प्रभुर् यतः ॥ niścetuṃ ye na śakyāḥ syur vādāḥ saṃdigdharūpiṇaḥ / teṣāṃ nṛpaḥ pramāṇaṃ syāt sa sarvasya prabhur yataḥ // Where disputes cannot be resolved through debate due to their uncertain nature, the King becomes the final authority of judgment, for he is the sovereign over all. Authority resides in the sovereign when rational discernment fails Causation is anchored in the capacity to resolve uncertainty Capacity-based responsibility elevates the ruler above disputants Restoration logic requires conclusive authority to end conflict Consciousness alignment occurs through decisive, sovereign clarity

title: brihaspati 1.106
content: व्यवहारान् स्वयं पश्येत् सभ्यैः परिवृतोऽन्वहम् । vyavahārān svayaṃ paśyet sabhyaiḥ parivṛto 'nvaham One must observe transactions daily, surrounded by noble witnesses.
