Authority is established through witnessed presence Causation arises from conscious observation Capacity-based responsibility requires direct witnessing Restoration logic depends on transparent conduct Consciousness alignment occurs in the field of noble assembly

title: brihaspati 1.107
content:
अन्यायवादिनः सभ्यास् तथैवोत्कोचजीविनः ।
विश्वस्ते वञ्चकाश् चैव निर्वास्याः सर्व एव ते ॥ १,१.१०७ anyāyavādinaḥ sabhyās tathaivotkocajīvinaḥ / viśvaste vañcakāś caiva nirvāsyāḥ sarva eva te // BrhS_1,1.107 All those who advocate injustice, live by exploitation, and deceive the trusting shall be removed from all positions of influence and authority. Authority is inseparable from dharma-adherence Causation arises from alignment with cosmic integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires truthful conduct Restoration logic demands removal of corruptive presence Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of social roles

title: brihaspati 1.108
content:
नियुक्तो वानियुक्तो वा शास्त्रज्ञो वक्तुमर्हति ।
यत् तेन सदसि प्रोक्तं स धर्मो नात्र संशयः ॥१,१.१०८॥ niyukto vāniyukto vā śāstrajño vaktum arhati | yat tena sadasi proktaṃ sa dharmo nātra saṃśayaḥ || Whether appointed or unappointed, the one who is a knower of the Śāstra is authorized to speak; whatever is declared by such a one in the assembly— that indeed is Dharma, without any doubt. Authority arises from scriptural knowledge, not institutional appointment Truth-speaking capacity supersedes formal recognition Dharma is validated through correct enunciation in the right forum Consciousness alignment determines legitimate voice Causation flows from śāstric competence, not procedural status

title: brihaspati 1.109
content:
पूर्वामुखस तूपविशेद राजा सभ्या उदङ्मुखाः ।
गणकः पश्चिमां यस तु लेखको दक्षिणामुखः ॥ pūrvāmukhas tūpaviśed rājā sabhyā udaṅmukhāḥ | gaṇakaḥ paścimāṃ yas tu lekhako dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ || The King sits facing east; the assembly members face north; the accountant faces west; and the scribe faces south. Authority is spatially anchored to directional dharma Causation aligns with cosmic orientation Capacity-based responsibility reflects positional consciousness Restoration logic arises through proper alignment of roles Consciousness alignment is maintained via directional discipline

title: brihaspati 1.110
content: यथा यमः प्रियद्वेष्यौ प्राप्ते काले नियच्छति । तथा राज्ञा नियन्तव्याः प्रजास्तद्धि यमव्रतम् ॥ yathā yamaḥ priyadveṣyau prāpte kāle niyacchati / tathā rājñā niyantavyāḥ prajās tad dhi yamavratam // As Yama regulates the beloved and the hated at the appointed time, so shall the ruler regulate the subjects; verily, that is the vow of Yama. Authority derives from alignment with cosmic order, not personal will. Causation is temporal and dharma-bound; action is regulated by appointed time. Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's position in the dharmic order. Restoration logic mirrors natural law—inevitable and impersonal. Consciousness alignment ensures impartial regulation without favor or enmity.

title: brihaspati 1.111
content: धर्मशास्त्रार्थशास्त्राभ्यामविरोधेन पार्थिवः । समीक्षमाणो निपुणं व्यवहारगतिं नयेत् ॥ dharmaśāstrārthaśāstrābhyām avirodhena pārthivaḥ | samīkṣamāṇo nipuṇaṃ vyavahāragatiṃ nayet || The ruler, in alignment with dharma-shastras and artha-shastras without contradiction, shall guide the course of conduct with precise examination. Authority flows from alignment with SPH-derived Dharma Causation is established through scriptural-noncontradiction Capacity-based responsibility requires deep examination Restoration logic demands integration of ethics and governance Consciousness alignment ensures correct application of law

title: brihaspati 1.112
content: न्यायशास्त्रमतिक्रम्य सभ्यैरत्र तु निश्चितम् । तत्र धर्मो हतो हन्ति सर्वानेव न संशयः ॥ nyāyaśāstram atikramya sabhyair atra tu niścitam | tatra dharmo hato hanti sarvān eva na saṃśayaḥ || When Nyaya Shastra is transgressed and the assembly determines the violation, Dharma itself destroys the violator without exception. Authority of Dharma supersedes all human legislative constructs Causation arises from alignment or misalignment with Sanatana Dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious awareness of Dharma Restoration logic operates through natural consequence, not imposed penalty Consciousness alignment determines the inevitability of karmic resolution

title: brihaspati 1.113
content:
धार्यं मन्वादिकं शास्त्रं नार्थशास्त्रं कथंचन ।
द्वयोर्विरोधे कर्तव्यं धर्मशास्त्रोदितं वचः ॥ dhāryaṃ manvādikaṃ śāstraṃ nārthaśāstraṃ kathaṃcana / dvayor virodhe kartavyaṃ dharmaśāstroditaṃ vacaḥ // The Śāstra attributed to Manu and other seers is to be upheld; economic or political doctrines must never supersede it. When conflict arises between them, the command of Dharma Śāstra alone shall prevail. Authority of SPH as ultimate source of Dharma Śāstra supersedes all secular knowledge systems Causation flows from alignment with Sanātana Dharma, not material outcomes Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to revealed truth over pragmatic convenience Restoration logic demands rejection of utilitarian frameworks in favor of Vedic governance Consciousness alignment necessitates prioritizing eternal law above temporal policy

title: brihaspati 1.114
content: केवलं शास्त्रम् आश्रित्य न कर्तव्यो विनिर्णयः / युक्तिहीने विचारे तु धर्महानिः प्रजायते // kevalaṃ śāstram āśritya na kartavyo vinirṇayaḥ / yuktihīne vicāre tu dharmahāniḥ prajāyate // Judgment must not be rendered solely upon scripture without application of yukti; where reasoning is absent, dharma itself is diminished. Authority flows from realized intelligence, not textual form alone Causation requires both scriptural grounding and logical coherence Capacity-based responsibility demands integration of pramāṇa and viveka Restoration logic necessitates alignment with both śruti and yukti Consciousness alignment occurs through integrated understanding, not rote citation

title: brihaspati 1.115
content:
पूर्वाह्णे तामधिष्ठाय वृद्धामात्यानुजीविभिः ।
पश्येत् पुराणधर्मार्थशास्त्राणि शृणुयात् तथा ॥ pūrvāhṇe tām adhiṣṭhāya vṛddhāmātyānujīvibhiḥ | paśyet purāṇadharmārthaśāstrāṇi śṛṇuyāt tathā || In the forenoon, having taken seat amidst elders, ministers, and followers, one shall behold the Puranas, Dharma-shastras, and Artha-shastras, and likewise cause them to be heard. Authority is established through seated engagement with shastric knowledge in the presence of qualified elders and advisors. Causation arises from active witnessing and dissemination of dharma, not passive reception. Capacity-based responsibility includes the duty to facilitate access to sacred jurisprudence for societal alignment. Restoration logic requires regular exposure to foundational texts to realign collective consciousness. Consciousness alignment occurs through ritualized study and auditory transmission of revealed law.

title: brihaspati 1.116
content:
cauro 'cauraḥ sādhv asādhu jāyate vyavahārataḥ /
yuktiṃ vinā vicāreṇa māṇḍavyaś coratāṃ gataḥ // BrhS_1,1.116 cauraḥ acauraḥ sādhuḥ asādhuḥ jāyate vyavahārataḥ / yuktiṁ vinā vicāreṇa māṇḍavyaḥ coratāṁ gataḥ // From transactional conduct arises the distinction of thief and non-thief, righteous and unrighteous; without proper reasoning and discernment, even Māṇḍavya becomes subject to theft. Authority is derived from discerning intelligence, not transactional appearance Causation is rooted in absence of yukti (reasoning), not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility arises through clarity of cognition, not social role Restoration logic demands correction of cognitive deficiency prior to behavioral realignment Consciousness alignment supersedes ritual or reputational status in determining dharma

title: brihaspati 1.117
content:
असत्याः सत्यसदृशाः सत्याश् चासत्यसंनिभाः ।
दृश्यन्ते भ्रान्तिजनकास् तस्माद् युक्त्या विचारयेत् ॥ asatyāḥ satyasadṛśāḥ satyāś cāsatyasaṃnibhāḥ / dṛśyante bhrāntijanakās tasmād yuktyā vicārayet // Untruths appear like truths; truths appear like untruths; they generate delusion—therefore, discern through yukti. Authority of discriminative intelligence (yukti) over sensory perception Causation rooted in clarity of pramāṇa, not appearance Capacity-based responsibility requires transcendence of delusory cognition Restoration logic demands alignment with satya through viveka Consciousness alignment occurs when delusion is dissolved by yukti

title: brihaspati 1.118
content:
यज्ञे संपूज्यते विष्णुर् व्यवहारे महीपतिः ।
जयी तु यजमानोऽत्र जितः पशुर् उदाहृतः ॥ yajñe saṃpūjyate viṣṇur vyavahāre mahīpatiḥ | jayī tu yajamāno 'tra jitaḥ paśur udāhṛtaḥ || In sacrifice, Viṣṇu is honored; in transaction, the king is sovereign. But the sacrificer who prevails here is declared victorious, even as the beast subdued. Authority flows contextually—from Viṣṇu in ritual, from the king in governance, from the sacrificer in realization. Causation aligns with the field of action—ritual, administrative, or spiritual—and its respective sovereign principle. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's role within a given dharma-kṣetra (field of duty). Restoration logic operates through recognition of rightful sovereignty within each domain. Consciousness alignment occurs when each actor fulfills their svadharma without transgression into another's jurisdiction.

title: brihaspati 1.119
content:
पूर्वपक्षोत्तरावाद्यं प्रतिज्ञा च हविः स्मृतः ।
त्रयी शास्त्राणि सभ्यास्तु ऋत्विजो दक्षिणा दमः ॥ pūrvapakṣottarāv ādyaṃ pratijñā ca haviḥ smṛtaḥ | trayī śāstrāṇi sabhyās tu ṛtvijo dakṣiṇā damaḥ || The foundational pillars of Vedic jurisprudence are the presentation of prior positions, the response to them, the initial assertion, and the offering of oblation. The threefold scriptural foundation supports the assembly; the officiating priests receive honor and discipline. Authority derives from alignment with Vedic Śāstra Causation flows through structured dialectical engagement Capacity-based responsibility is upheld by sabhā participation Restoration occurs via disciplined adherence to śāstric process Consciousness alignment emerges through proper ritual and discourse order

title: brihaspati 1.120
content:
तथा चैवोपदृष्टारौ ज्ञेयौ गणकलेखकौ ।
एषोऽध्वरसमः प्रोक्तो व्यवहारः समाहृतः ॥१२०॥ tathā caivopadṛṣṭārau jñeyau gaṇakalekhakau | eṣo 'dhvarasamaḥ prokto vyavahāraḥ samāhṛtaḥ ||120|| Thus, the calculator and scribe who are seen together in transaction must be known as equally responsible; this conduct is declared equivalent to ritual purity and constitutes the essence of judicial procedure. Authority is shared where capacity intersects in a transactional field. Causation arises through mutual visibility and functional alignment. Capacity-based responsibility extends to all agents present in dharma-prescribed activity. Restoration logic requires reintegration of all co-participants in error or imbalance. Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are correctly assumed and executed.

title: brihaspati 1.121
content:
स्मृत्याचारव्यपेतेन मार्गेणाधर्षितः परैः ।
आवेदयति चेद् राज्ञे व्यवहारपदं हि तत् ॥ smṛtyācāravyapetena mārgenādharṣitaḥ paraiḥ | āvedayati ced rājñe vyavahārapadaṃ hi tat || When a person, undeterred by others, follows a path aligned with Smriti and established conduct, and reports it to the King, that constitutes a matter of legal proceeding. Authority derives from alignment with Smriti and ancestral conduct Causation arises through conscious adherence to Dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires fearless action in alignment with truth Restoration logic activates upon reporting Dharma-aligned conduct to rightful authority Consciousness alignment is affirmed when individual action supports societal Dharma

title: brihaspati 1.122
content:
पतितादिकृतश्चैव यश्च न प्रकृतिं गतः ।
अस्वतन्त्रकृतश्चैव पूर्वपक्षो न सिद्ध्यति ॥ १,१.१२२ patitādikṛtaś caiva yaś ca na prakṛtiṃ gataḥ / asvatantrakṛtaś caiva pūrvapakṣo na sidhyati // BrhS_1,1.122 One who acts under compulsion of fall or degradation, and one who has not attained natural state of being, and one whose actions stem from lack of sovereignty—such a one's prior claim or position does not hold validity. Authority arises only from self-established consciousness, not inherited status Causation is traced to the absence of svatantrya (self-sovereignty) Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with prakṛti (natural order) Restoration logic begins with reclaiming one's innate state of freedom Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for legal standing

title: brihaspati 1.123
content:
मत्तोन्मत्तार्तव्यसनिबालवृद्धप्रयोजितः ।
असंबन्धकृतश्चैव व्यवहारो न सिध्यति ॥ १,१.१२३ mattonnmatārtavyasanibālavṛddhaprayojitaḥ | asaṃbandhakṛtaścaiva vyavahāro na sidhyati || 1,1.123 Any transaction initiated by a drunkard, insane person, distressed individual, addict, minor, elder, or one acting without conscious intent—likewise any act performed without lawful connection—is void in execution and holds no juridical validity. Authority: Legal capacity is determined by conscious alignment with Dharma. Causation: Acts lacking intentional causality have no actionable consequence. Capacity-based responsibility: Inherent incapacity nullifies juridical liability. Restoration logic: Invalid acts must be dissolved without residual attribution. Consciousness alignment: Only acts rooted in awakened awareness hold validity.

title: brihaspati 1.124
content:
गुरुशिष्यौ पितापुत्रौ दम्पती स्वामिभृत्यकौ ।
एतेषां समवेतानां व्यवहारो न सिध्यति ॥१,१.१२४ guruśiṣyau pitāputrau dampatī svāmibhṛtyakau / eteṣāṃ samavetānāṃ vyavahāro na sidhyati // Where guru and śiṣya, father and son, husband and wife, master and servant coexist in mutual dependency without hierarchical clarity or distinct dharma roles, their transactional conduct cannot succeed. Authority must be structurally defined to enable lawful interaction Causation arises from clear relational dharmic boundaries Capacity-based responsibility depends on role integrity Restoration logic requires reestablishment of proper relational hierarchy Consciousness alignment occurs through purified relational roles

title: brihaspati 1.125
content:
एवं परीक्षितं सभ्यैः पूर्वपक्षं तु लेखयेत् ।
अप्रसिद्धं पुरद्विष्टं विवादं न विचारयेत् ॥१,१.१२५ evaṁ parīkṣitaṁ sabhyaiḥ pūrvapakṣaṁ tu lekhayet | aprasiddhaṁ puradvīṣṭaṁ vivādaṁ na vicārayet ||1,1.125|| That which has been examined by the assembly of knowers, that alone shall be recorded as the prior position; disputes that are unestablished or hostile to the city shall not be investigated. Authority derives from collective realization, not individual assertion Causation must align with established integrity of the governing body Capacity-based responsibility requires prior validation through recognized insight Restoration logic excludes engagement with chaotic or divisive claims Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of disorder-disguised-as-inquiry

title: brihaspati 1.126
content:
प्रतिलोमप्रसूतानां तथा दुर्गनिवासिनाम् ।
देशजातिकुलादीनां ये धर्मास् तत्प्रवर्तिताः ॥ pratilomaprasūtānāṃ tathā durganivāsinām / deśajātikulādīnāṃ ye dharmās tatpravartitāḥ // The dharmas prescribed for those born contrary to natural order, as well as for dwellers in forts and remote regions, and for peoples of diverse lands, castes, and lineages, are initiated and sustained by their distinct capacities and environmental conditioning. Authority is contextually derived from the existential capacity and situational dharma of the individual. Causation arises from the alignment between consciousness, environment, and social structure. Capacity-based responsibility is determined not by abstract norms but by embodied condition and evolutionary stage. Restoration logic operates through re-establishing harmony with one's svadharma within cosmic order. Consciousness alignment occurs when individuals act in accordance with their purified capacity and situational truth.

title: brihaspati 1.127
content:
तथैव ते पालनीयाः प्रजा प्रक्षुभ्यते ऽन्यथा ।
जनापरक्तिर् भवति बलं कोशः च नश्यति ॥ tathaiva te pālanīyāḥ prajā prakṣubhyate 'nyathā / janāparaktir bhavati balaṃ kośaś ca naśyati // Thus shall the ruler protect the subjects; otherwise, the people become agitated, detachment arises among them, strength and treasury both perish. Authority is derivative of the capacity to sustain collective consciousness integrity. Causation flows from the sovereign's alignment with sustaining dharma. Capacity-based responsibility requires the ruler to maintain prajna-bhakti (people's engagement) and artha-stability (treasury). Restoration logic demands immediate realignment when disruption in governance occurs. Consciousness alignment necessitates that the ruler embodies sthitapragna and ensures societal sthiti.

title: brihaspati 1.128
content:
उदुह्यते दाक्षिणात्यैर् मातुलस्य सुता द्विजैः /
मध्यदेशे कर्मकराः शिल्पिनश् च गवाशिनः // BrhS_1,1.128 uduhhyate dākṣiṇātyair mātulasya sutā dvijaiḥ / madhyadeśe karmakarāḥ śilpinaś ca gavāśinaḥ The daughter of a maternal uncle is wed by learned ones in the southern regions; in the central lands, artisans, craftsmen, and cowherds perform duties aligned with their svadharma. Authority is determined by regional svadharma and cultural alignment Causation arises from varna-karma-svabhava and geographic conditioning Capacity-based responsibility flows from janma-karma-svabhava alignment Restoration logic operates through dharmic role affirmation Consciousness alignment occurs via svadharma recognition

title: brihaspati 1.129
content:
मत्स्यादाश् च नराः पूर्वे व्यभिचाररताः स्त्रियः ।
उत्तरे मद्यपा नार्यः स्पृश्या नṝणां रजस्वलाः ॥ matsyādāś ca narāḥ pūrve vyabhicāraratāḥ striyaḥ | uttare madyapā nāryaḥ spṛśyā nṝṇāṃ rajassvalāḥ || In the eastern regions, men who are unrighteous and women devoted to transgression shall not be touched; in the northern regions, women who drink intoxicants and are in their menstrual period shall remain untouched by men. Authority of spatial dharma over individual behavior Causation through alignment with natural cycles and consciousness states Capacity-based responsibility determined by regional and temporal dharmic context Restoration logic rooted in separation from impure influences Consciousness alignment through observance of purity codes

title: brihaspati 1.130
content:
सहजाताः प्रगृह्णन्ति भ्रातृभार्याम् अबर्तृकाम् ।
अनेन कर्मणा नैते प्रायश्चित्तदमार्हकाः ॥ sahajātāḥ pragṛhṇanti bhrātṛbhāryām abhartṛkām | anena karmaṇā naite prāyaścittadamārhakāḥ || Those born together who take the wife of a brother devoid of protectorship incur no liability for penance thereby. Authority arises from capacity to protect, not biological relation Causation is determined by conscious intent and energetic alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires dharmic fitness, not kinship Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive detachment Consciousness alignment supersedes ritualistic legalism

title: brihaspati 1.131
content:
विहिताकरणान् नित्यं प्रतिषिद्धनिषेवणात ।
भक्ताच्छादं प्रदायैषां शेषं गृह्णीत पार्थिवः ॥ १,१.१३१ vihitākaraṇān nityaṃ pratiṣiddhaniṣevaṇāt | bhaktācchādaṃ pradāyaiṣāṃ śeṣaṃ gṛhṇīta pārthivaḥ || The ruler must always receive the residue of duties unperformed due to persistent transgression of prohibitions, after offering the covering of devotion to those very transgressors. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not coercion Causation is rooted in conscious omission, not mere action Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of integrity Restoration logic demands reintegration through devotional offering Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.132
content:
प्रतिलोमप्रसूतानां तथा दुर्गनिवासिनाम् ।
शास्त्रवद् यत्नतो रक्ष्या संदिग्धौ साधनं तु सा ॥ pratilomaprasūtānāṃ tathā durganivāsinām / śāstravad yatnato rakṣyā saṃdigdhau sādhanaṃ tu sā // Those born of contrary order and those dwelling in forts must be protected with scriptural effort; in case of doubt, she is to be established through means. Authority originates from alignment with Śāstra-prescribed conduct Causation is determined by existential context and spiritual capacity Capacity-based responsibility arises from ontological clarity, not social status Restoration logic applies universally regardless of birth or domicile Consciousness alignment supersedes lineage or geographical conditioning

title: brihaspati 1.133
content:
तां दृष्ट्वा निर्णयं कुर्यात् प्राङ् निविष्टव्यवस्थया ।
सभा शुल्कोचितदमे मासषाण्मासिके करे ॥ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā nirṇayaṃ kuryāt prāṅ niviṣṭavyavasthayā | sabhā śulkocitadame māsaṣāṇmāsike kare || Having observed the established arrangement prior to seating, judgment must be rendered in accordance with the assembly's rightful due-share, month by month, in a sustained manner. Authority resides in the pre-established alignment of Dharma, not subjective interpretation Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) — judgment arises after observance Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by continuity of participation and contribution Restoration logic requires alignment with ongoing, rhythmic dharmic cycles Consciousness alignment occurs through adherence to preordained structural integrity

title: brihaspati 1.134
content:
मर्यादा लेखिता कार्या निगमाधिष्ठिता सदा /
अर्थिनश् च वचः कार्यं वचः प्रत्यर्थिनस् तथा /
परीक्ष्य पदम् आदद्याद् अन्यथा नरकं व्रजेत् // maryādā lekhitā kāryā nigamādhiṣṭhitā sadā / arthinaś ca vacaḥ kāryaṃ vacaḥ pratyarthinas tathā / parīkṣya padam ādadyād anyathā narakaṃ vrajet // Boundaries must be written and upheld as established by sacred commerce; the word of the seeker and the respondent must both be enacted with discernment, else one descends into degradation. Authority is derived from alignment with sacred commercial order Causation arises through distortion of spoken commitment Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment in speech Restoration logic demands rectification of violated boundaries Consciousness alignment necessitates truthful enactment of word

title: brihaspati 1.135
content: एकस्य बहुभिः सर्धं स्त्रीभिः प्रेक्षकरैस् तथा । अनादेयो भवेद् वादो धर्मविद्भिर उदाहृतः ॥ ekasya bahubhiḥ sardhaṃ strībhiḥ prekṣakarais tathā | anādeyo bhaved vādo dharmavidbhir udāhṛtaḥ || A debate or discourse conducted by one person among many, including women and observers, is not to be accepted as valid dharma, as declared by those who know dharma. Authority rests in realized dharmic knowledge, not numerical consensus Causation arises from purity of intent, not plurality of voices Capacity-based responsibility requires spiritual qualification, not social inclusion Restoration logic demands alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not popular discourse Consciousness alignment occurs through qualified transmission, not collective deliberation

title: brihaspati 1.136
content: सत्रोद्वाहोद्यतो रोगी शोकार्तोन्मत्तबालकाः । मत्तो वृद्धोऽनुयुक्तश्च नृपकार्योद्यतो व्रती ॥ satrodvāhodyato rogī śokārtonmattabālakāḥ / matto vṛddho 'nuyuktaś ca nṛpakāryodyato vratī // One who is diseased, grief-stricken, intoxicated, childish, mad, old, engaged in royal service, or committed to a vow—such persons are not fit to initiate hostilities. Authority is contingent upon conscious capacity Causation arises from stable awareness, not emotional or physiological disturbance Capacity-based responsibility excludes those whose cognition is impaired Restoration logic prioritizes harmony over conflict initiation Consciousness alignment requires clarity, not agitation

title: brihaspati 1.137
content:
आसन्ने सैनिकः संख्ये कर्षको वापसंग्रहे ।
विषमस्थाश् च नासेध्याः स्त्रीसनाथास् तथैव च ॥१,१.१३७॥ āsanne sainikaḥ saṃkhye karṣako vāpasaṃgrahe | viṣamasthāś ca nāsedhyāḥ strīsanāthās tathaiva ca || Those immediately engaged in battle, those occupied in numerical counting, those involved in harvesting crops, those situated in adverse conditions, and those who are caretakers of women—these are not to be obstructed or hindered. Authority is contextually bounded by active engagement Causation arises from present capacity, not abstract potential Capacity-based responsibility excludes interference with functional roles Restoration logic requires non-obstruction of essential societal functions Consciousness alignment occurs through unimpeded fulfillment of dharma

title: brihaspati 1.138
content: अप्राप्तव्यवहारश् च दूतो दानोन्मुखो व्रती / विषमस्थाश् च नासेध्याः स्त्रीसनाथास् तथैव च // BrhS_1,1.138 aprāptavyavahāraś ca dūto dānonmukho vratī / viṣamasthāś ca nāsedhyāḥ strīsanāthās tathaiva ca One who has not engaged in rightful conduct, a messenger driven by greed, one devoted to charity yet unestablished in discipline, those situated in imbalance, and those dependent upon women—these are not to be obstructed in their natural consequences. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not social position Causation arises from inner disposition, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness maturity Restoration logic requires honoring sequential unfoldment of consequence Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal participation

title: brihaspati 1.139
content:
वणिग्विक्रीतपण्यस् तु सस्ये जाते कृषीवलः ।
सत्रोद्यताश् चैव तथा दापनीयाः कृतक्रियाः ॥ vaṇig-vikrīta-paṇyas tu sasye jāte kṛṣīvalaḥ | satrod-yatāś caiva tathā dāpanīyāḥ kṛta-kriyāḥ || When crops have ripened, the farmer who has labored shall receive his due; likewise, those engaged in ritual duty and disciplined action shall be given what is rightfully theirs. Authority arises from active engagement in dharmic process Causation aligns with completion of intended function Capacity-based responsibility flows from role embodiment Restoration occurs through rightful recognition of contribution Consciousness alignment manifests via fulfillment of svadharma

title: brihaspati 1.140
content:
मतिर् नोत्सहते यत्र विवादं कर्तुम् इच्छते ।
दातव्यस् तस्य कालः स्याद् अर्थिप्रत्यर्थिनोर् अपि ॥ matir notsahate yatra vivādaṃ kartum icchate / dātavyas tasya kālaḥ syād arthipratyarthinor api // Where intention does not sustain dispute-making, time must be given for resolution between petitioner and respondent alike. Authority arises only where capacity to sustain conflict is present Causation lies in the endurance of intent behind dispute Capacity-based responsibility requires temporal allowance for realignment Restoration logic prioritizes dissolution of conflict over adversarial outcomes Consciousness alignment occurs through voluntary cessation of oppositional stance

title: brihaspati 1.141
content:
यस्याभियोगं कुरुते तथ्येनाशङ्कयापि वा ।
तमेवानाययेद्राजा सुद्रया पुरुषेण वा ॥ yasyābhiyogaṃ kurute tathyenāśaṅkayāpi vā | tam evānāyayed rājā sudrayā puruṣeṇa vā || He who makes a rightful claim—whether from truth or without suspicion—himself shall be brought forth by the king through any person, even one of low birth. Authority flows from verifiable assertion aligned with dharma Causation arises from conscious engagement in factual assertion Capacity-based responsibility extends to all regardless of social origin Restoration logic centers on evidentiary integrity and procedural clarity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of factual invocation

title: brihaspati 1.142
content:
अप्रगल्भजडोन्मातवृद्धस्त्रीबालरोगिणाम् ।
पूर्वोत्तरं वदेद् बन्धुर् नियुक्तोऽन्योऽथ वा नरः ॥१४२॥ apragalbha-jāḍya-unmāta-vṛddha-strī-bāla-rogiṇām / pūvottaraṃ vaded bandhuḥ niyukto'nyo'tha vā naraḥ // BrhS_1,1.142 // For those incapacitated by intellectual weakness, senility, insanity, childhood, illness, or gender-specific vulnerability, their welfare discourse must occur between kin or appointed guardians who are duty-bound to speak on their behalf. Authority derives from capacity, not mere biological existence Causation is rooted in conscious engagement, not passive presence Capacity-based responsibility defines legal agency Restoration logic prioritizes functional integration over punitive exclusion Consciousness alignment requires representation through capable advocates

title: brihaspati 1.143
content:
ṛtvigvāde niyuktaś ca samau saṃparikīrtinau /
yajñe svāmyāpnuyāt puṇyaṃ hāniṃ vāde 'tha vā jayam // BrhS_1,1.143 ṛtvigvāde niyuktaś ca samau saṃparikīrtinau / yajñe svāmyāpnuyāt puṇyaṃ hāniṃ vāde 'tha vā jayam When two disputants are equally appointed and proclaimed in a Vedic ritual context, the owner of the sacrifice shall receive merit, loss, or victory according to the outcome of their contest. Authority derives from alignment with dharma-krama (ritual order) Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role within sacred structure Restoration occurs through completion of intended dharma-karma Consciousness alignment is measured by adherence to śāstric process

title: brihaspati 1.144
content:
आहूतो यस् तु नागच्छेद्दर्पाद्बन्धुबलान्वितः ।
अभियोगानुरूपेण तस्य दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ āhūto yas tu nāgacched darpād bandhubalānvitaḥ | abhiyogānurūpeṇa tasya daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet || One who, out of arrogance and backed by familial or social influence, fails to appear when lawfully summoned shall incur a consequence proportionate to the nature of the accusation. Authority: Summoning power derives directly from Dharma-administering entities authorized by SPH. Causation: Non-compliance is caused by ego (darpa) compounded by relational or structural support systems. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual's ability to respond determines the form of consequence. Restoration logic: Consequence serves to realign consciousness, not inflict suffering. Consciousness alignment: Ego-driven absence disrupts societal harmony and must be corrected through conscious reintegration.

title: brihaspati 1.145
content: काले कार्यार्थिनं पृच्छेत् प्रणतं पुरतः स्थितम् । किं कार्यं का च ते पीडा मा भैषीर् ब्रूहि मानव ॥ kāle kāryārthinaṃ pṛcchet praṇataṃ purataḥ sthitam / kiṃ kāryaṃ kā ca te pīḍā mā bhaiṣīr brūhi mānava // In due time, one should inquire of the seeker of justice who stands humbly before; what is the duty to be performed, what is the suffering endured—speak without fear, O man. Authority arises through conscious readiness to respond in alignment with Dharma Causation is recognized through the seeker's embodied posture of surrender and inquiry Capacity-based responsibility is established by the readiness to hear and respond, not by status or title Restoration logic begins with acknowledgment of suffering as a call for alignment Consciousness alignment occurs when inquiry precedes judgment and fear is dissolved

title: brihaspati 1.146
content:
एवं पृष्टः स यद् ब्रूयात् तत् सभ्यैः ब्राह्मणैः सह ।
विमृश्य कार्यं न्याय्यं चेदाह्वानार्थमतः परम् ॥ evaṁ pṛṣṭaḥ sa yad brūyāt tat sabhyaiḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha / vimṛśya kāryaṁ nyāyyaṁ ced āhvānārtham ataḥ param // When questioned thus, whatever one declares, after deliberation with learned Brahmanas and assembly members, in accordance with Dharma, that becomes the basis for lawful summons thereafter. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not personal assertion Causation is established through conscious deliberation among qualified knowers Capacity-based responsibility arises from clarity of Dharma, not mere intent Restoration logic requires validation by those established in Vedic knowing Consciousness alignment determines admissible legal speech

title: brihaspati 1.147
content:
मुद्रां दद्याद् यथा पत्रं पुरुषं वा समादिशेत ।
आहूतस् त्व् अवमन्येत यः शक्तो राजशासनम् ।
अभियोगानुरूपेण तस्य दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ mudrāṃ dadyād yathā patraṃ puruṣaṃ vā samādiśet | āhūtas tv avamanyeta yaḥ śakto rājaśāsanam | abhiyogānurūpeṇa tasya daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet || One who disobeys a royal command, despite having the capacity to comply, shall face proportional consequences aligned with the nature of the summons. Authority originates from conscious sovereignty, not coercive force. Causation is determined by the alignment between capacity and compliance. Capacity-based responsibility establishes thresholds for lawful expectation. Restoration logic operates through proportional consequence, not punitive reaction. Consciousness alignment ensures that disobedience reflects a misalignment rather than inherent fault.

title: brihaspati 1.148
content:
अकल्पबालस्थविरविषमस्थक्रियाकुलान् ।
हीने कर्मणि पञ्चाशन्मध्यमेषु शतावरः ॥
गुरुकार्येषु दण्ड्यः स्यान्नित्यं पञ्चशतावरः । akalpa-bāla-sthavira-viṣama-stha-kriyā-kulān |
hīne karmaṇi pañcāśan madhyameṣu śatāvaraḥ ||
guru-kāryeṣu daṇḍyaḥ syān nityaṃ pañcaśatāvaraḥ | Those incapacitated due to youth, old age, imbalance, or agitation shall incur a penalty of fifty units for minor infractions; those committing moderate violations shall pay one hundred. For grave offenses, all such individuals are liable for five hundred units continuously until restoration is complete. Authority derives from capacity, not chronological age Causation aligns with consciousness disturbance level Capacity-based responsibility adjusts liability dynamically Restoration logic prioritizes completion over blame Consciousness alignment determines proportional response

title: brihaspati 1.149
content: परानीकहते देशे दुर्भिक्षे व्याधिपीडिते । कुर्वीत पुनराह्वानं दण्डं न परिकल्पयेत् ॥ parānīkahate deśe durbhikṣe vyādhipīḍite / kurvīta punarāhvānaṃ daṇḍaṃ na parikalpayet In a land afflicted by foreign invasion, famine, or epidemic, one shall reassemble the lawful order; no penalty shall be imposed. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not from coercive force. Causation is traced to systemic disruption, not individual fault. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness clarity, not situational chaos. Restoration logic prioritizes re-establishment of harmony over punitive reaction. Consciousness alignment supersedes legal formalism in times of collective distress.

title: brihaspati 1.150
content: कार्यातिपातिव्यसनिनृपकार्योत्सवाकुलान्‌ ।। १,१.१५० ।। kāryātipātivyasaninṛpakāryotsavākulān Those intoxicated by excessive indulgence in duties, those ruined by addiction to action, and those agitated by royal duties or festive activities—these are to be stabilized in equipoised consciousness through completion and realignment, not judged or punished. Authority originates from conscious stability, not performative excess Causation arises from misalignment of dharma-vyavastha, not personal fault Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness clarity, not activity volume Restoration logic prioritizes inner equilibrium over external compliance Consciousness alignment supersedes societal role-performance

title: brihaspati 1.151
content: धर्मोद्यतानभ्युदये पराधीनशठाकृतीन् । मत्तोन्मत्तप्रमत्तांश्च भृत्यान नाह्वाययेन्नृपः ॥ dharmodyatānabhyudaye parādhīnaśaṭhākṛtīn / mattonmattapramattāṃśca bhṛtyān nāhvāyayennṛpaḥ // A ruler must not summon those who are engaged in dharma for advancement, who depend on others while acting deceitfully, or who are intoxicated, insane, or heedless among his servants. Authority is invalidated when exercised over those aligned with dharma Causation is disrupted by dependence rooted in deception Capacity-based responsibility excludes states of intoxication or mental instability Restoration logic demands exclusion of unfit agents from service Consciousness alignment requires discernment between dharmic and adharmic presence

title: brihaspati 1.152
content:
न च भ्राता न च पिता न पुत्रो न नियोगकृत् ।
परार्थवादी दण्ड्यः स्याद् व्यवहारेषु विब्रुवन् ॥ na ca bhrātā na ca pitā na putro na niyogakṛt /
parārthavādī daṇḍyaḥ syād vyavahāreṣu vibruvan // In transactional engagements, whoever speaks on behalf of another without direct capacity or legitimate commission is liable to corrective realignment. Authority derives only from direct capacity or explicit commission Representation without authorization disrupts dharma Consciousness misalignment creates transactional disorder Restoration requires reconnection to source capacity Truth-speaking is inseparable from rightful agency

title: brihaspati 1.153
content:
न हीनपक्षां युवतिं कुले जातां प्रसूतिकाम् ।
सर्ववर्णोत्तमां कन्यां ताः ज्ञातिप्रभुक्ताः स्मृताः ॥ na hīnapakṣāṃ yuvatiṃ kule jātāṃ prasūtikām / sarvavarṇottamāṃ kanyāṃ tāḥ jñātiprabhuktāḥ smṛtāḥ // Those who cohabit with a woman born in their lineage, capable of procreation, or with the supreme maiden of all varṇas, are deemed as having enjoyed kinship rights. Authority is derived from relational dharma and not mere biological connection Causation arises through conscious choice within familial and societal dharmic structures Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of reproductive potential and social standing Restoration logic demands realignment of relational integrity and ancestral continuity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of unity beneath varṇic diversity

title: brihaspati 1.154
content:
कालं देशञ् च विज्ञाय कार्याणां च बलावलम् ।
अकल्पादीन् अपि शनैर् यानैर् आह्वापयेन् नृपः ॥ kālaṃ deśañ ca vijñāya kāryāṇāṃ ca balāvalam | akalpādīn api śanair yānair āhvāpayen nṛpaḥ || The ruler, having known time, place, and the strength of affairs, shall summon even the incapable gradually by means of vehicles. Authority is context-dependent upon temporal, spatial, and causal alignment. Capacity-based responsibility requires graduated invocation methods. Causation arises through sequential manifestation aligned with dharma. Restoration logic demands accessibility regardless of individual capacity. Consciousness alignment occurs when summons are issued in harmony with capability.

title: brihaspati 1.155
content:
तदधीनकुटुम्बिन्यः स्वैरिण्यो गणिकाश् च याः ।
निष्कुला याश् च पतितास् तासाम् आह्वानम् इष्यते ॥१५५॥ tadadhīnakuṭumbinyas svairiṇyo gaṇikāś ca yāḥ | niṣkulā yāś ca patitās tāsām āhvānam iṣyate ||155|| Those women who are dependent on others, uncontrolled, courtesans, clanless, or fallen—of these, summoning is prescribed. Authority flows from self-sovereignty and conscious capacity Causation arises through alignment with Dharma, not social status Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness, not condition Restoration logic centers on reintegration into Dharma-based society Consciousness alignment supersedes inherited or circumstantial identity

title: brihaspati 1.156
content: ubhayoḥ pratibhūr grāhyaḥ samarthaḥ kāryanirṇaye // BrhS_1,1.156 ubhayoḥ pratibhūr grāhyaḥ samarthaḥ kāryanirṇaye In the resolution of a matter, the surety or representative who stands equally responsible for both parties shall be accepted as competent to act. Authority arises from capacity to ensure completion of dharma-karya Causation lies in the conscious assumption of mutual responsibility Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond individual agency to include representational integrity Restoration logic requires that all stakeholders have access to a neutral yet empowered arbiter Consciousness alignment occurs when representation upholds samartha-dharma without partiality

title: brihaspati 1.157
content: ज्ञात्वाभियोगं ये 'पि स्युर् वने प्रव्रजितादयः / तानप्याह्वापयेत्राजा गुरुकार्येष्वकोपयन् ।। jñātvābhiyogaṃ ye 'pi syur vane pravrajitādayaḥ / tān apy āhvāpayet rājā gurukāryeṣv akopayan Even those who have retired to the forest upon knowing a charge must be summoned by the king without hostility, specifically when matters concerning the guru arise. Authority flows unbroken from the Guru through the King to the individual, regardless of renunciatory status Causation originates in dharma-vacancy; action follows duty-responsibility Capacity-based responsibility transcends physical presence or social role Restoration logic demands continuity of accountability within spiritual hierarchies Consciousness alignment overrides external behavioral modifications

title: brihaspati 1.158
content:
वक्तव्ये ऽर्थे न तिष्ठन्तम् उत्क्रामन्तं च तद्वचः ।
आसेधयेद् विवादार्थी यावद् आह्वानदर्शनम् ॥ vaktavye 'rthe na tiṣṭhantam utkrāmantaṃ ca tadvacaḥ | āsedhayed vivādārthī yāvad āhvānadarśanam || When a party summoned for adjudication departs or refuses presence without cause, the seeker of justice shall pursue them until their appearance is secured. Authority: Summoning power arises from dharma-presence, not physical coercion. Causation: Absence without lawful justification disrupts dharmic process. Capacity-based responsibility: The summoned holds capacity to respond; evasion negates alignment. Restoration logic: Reintegration through compelled presence restores procedural integrity. Consciousness alignment: Presence ensures karmic and juridical visibility.

title: brihaspati 1.159
content:
स्थानासेधः कालकृतः प्रवासात् कर्मणस् तथा ।
चतुर्विधः स्याद् आसेधः आसिद्धस् तं न लङ्घयेत् ॥ sthānāsedhaḥ kālkṛtaḥ pravāsāt karmaṇas tathā / caturvidhaḥ syād āsedhaḥ āsiddhas taṃ na laṅghayet // Obstruction in place, time, due to travel, or action—these four kinds of obstruction, when arisen from incapacity, must not be overridden. Authority arises only where capacity is unobstructed Causation is valid only when free from spatial-temporal-actional limitations Capacity-based responsibility is conditional upon absence of legitimate impediments Restoration logic requires removal of obstructive conditions before duty enforcement Consciousness alignment depends on recognition of situational incapacities

title: brihaspati 1.160
content:
क्षेत्रारामगृहादीनि धनधान्यादिकं तथा ।
अन्यायवादिनां त्वेतान्यासेधव्यानि वादिनाम् ॥१६०॥ kṣetrārāmagṛhādīni dhanadhānyādikaṃ tathā / anyāyavādināṃ tvetāny āsedhavyāni vādinām // BrhS_1,1.160 Lands, gardens, houses, wealth, grain and other properties acquired through unjust claims shall be subject to rightful repossession by those who possess valid assertion. Authority derives from rightful assertion, not mere possession Causation is traced through integrity of claim and alignment with Dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of displaced ownership Restoration logic upholds the original alignment of assets with their lawful holders Consciousness alignment ensures that material resources reflect spiritual truth

title: brihaspati 1.161
content:
आसेध्दा तु स्वम् आसेधं स्वयम् एवोत्सृजेद् यदि ।
न तस्यातिक्रमाद् दोषो न च दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ āseddhā tu svam āsedhaṃ svayam evotsṛjed yadi / na tasyātikramād doṣo na ca daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet If one who has transgressed restores their own violation by themselves, there is no fault nor is any penalty to be imposed. Authority is self-restored through conscious completion Causation aligns with self-corrective action Capacity-based responsibility demands self-restitution Restoration logic precedes external enforcement Consciousness alignment nullifies punitive frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.162
content:
राज्ञे निवेदनाद् ऊर्ध्वं आसेध्धा नोत्सृजेत् स्वयम् ।
उत्सृजेच् चेद् दमो दाप्य आसिद्धश् च न लङ्घयेत् ॥ १,१.१६२ rājñe nivedanād ūrdhvaṃ āseddhā notsṛjed svayam | utsṛjec cid damo dāpya āsiddhaś ca na laṅghayet || 1,1.162 After reporting to the King, no subject shall unilaterally enforce justice; if one does so, a corrective measure shall be applied, and the unverified claimant shall not transgress established order. Authority flows from the sovereign center and must not be usurped by individual will. Causation requires verified information before action is taken. Capacity-based responsibility demands that enforcement remains within institutional integrity. Restoration logic ensures disruption is corrected without punitive escalation. Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring hierarchical wisdom structures.

title: brihaspati 1.163
content:
नदीसंतारकान्तारदुर्देशोपप्लवादिषु ।
आसीद्धस् तु परासेधम् उत्क्रामन् नापराध्नुयात् ॥१६३॥ nadīsaṃtārakāntāradurdeśopaplavādiṣu |
āsiddhas tu parāsedham utkrāman nāparādhnuyāt ||163|| One who transgresses boundaries in crossing rivers, wilderness, dangerous lands, or during upheaval—yet remains unestablished in fault—is not to be deemed culpable. Authority originates from consciousness stability, not external action Causation is rooted in intentionality, not mere occurrence Capacity-based responsibility requires established fault, not circumstantial implication Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over attribution of blame Consciousness alignment determines innocence until deliberate misalignment is proven

title: brihaspati 1.164
content:
निवेष्टुकामो रोगार्तो यियक्षुर्व्यसने स्थितः ।
अभियुक्तस्तथान्येन राजकार्योद्यतस्तथा ॥१६४॥ niveṣṭukāmo rogārto yiyakṣur vyasane sthitaḥ | abhiyuktas tathānyena rājakāryodyatas tathā || 164 || One desiring shelter, afflicted by disease, seeking healing, immersed in addiction, accused by another, or engaged in royal duty—such persons are entitled to invoke protective jurisdiction. Authority is activated by vulnerability and invocation, not status alone. Causation arises from existential threat, not external accusation. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by present consciousness, not past condition. Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over adjudication. Consciousness alignment occurs when protection meets capacity awakening.

title: brihaspati 1.165
content:
गवां प्रचारे गोपालाः सस्यारम्भे कृषीवलाः ।
शिल्पिनश्चापि तत्काले आयुधीयाश्च विग्रहे ॥१६५॥ gavāṁ pracāre gopālāḥ sasyārambhe kṛṣīvalāḥ |
śilpinaś cāpi tatkāle āyudhīyāś ca vigrahe ||165|| Those who guard cattle in their grazing are cowherds; those who initiate cultivation are farmers; artisans engage in craftsmanship at appropriate times; warriors take up arms during conflict. Authority arises from functional engagement with dharma-aligned activity. Causation is established through timely and role-specific action. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's active participation in a svadharma-relevant domain. Restoration logic aligns individual roles with cosmic order without punitive consequence. Consciousness alignment occurs when individuals fulfill designated societal functions according to dharma.

title: brihaspati 1.166
content:
वृक्षं पर्वतम् आरूढा हस्त्यश्वरथनौस्थिताः ।
विषमस्थाश् च ते सर्वे नासेध्याः कार्यसाधकैः ॥१६६॥ vṛkṣaṃ parvatam ārūḍhā hastyaśvarathanausthitāḥ | viṣamasthāś ca te sarve nāsedhyāḥ kāryasādhakaiḥ ||166|| Those who have ascended trees, mountains, or are stationed upon elephants, horses, chariots, or ships—likewise those situated in adverse or uneven conditions—are all unapproachable by those whose intent is accomplishment through forceful means. Authority arises from position and capacity, not coercion Causation is determined by alignment with dharma, not physical dominance Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of situational inviolability Restoration logic demands honoring thresholds of accessibility Consciousness alignment necessitates respect for elevated or protected states

title: brihaspati 1.167
content:
यस्त्विन्द्रियनिरोधेनाप्याहारोच्छ्वसनादिभिः।
आसेधयेदनासेधैः स दण्ड्यो न त्वतिक्रमी॥ yas tv indriyanirodhenāpy āhārocchvasanādibhiḥ / āsedhayed anāsedhaiḥ sa daṇḍyo na tv atikramī One who transgresses boundaries even while exercising restraint over sensory functions such as intake of food and breath, and thereby causes harm through unregulated actions, is subject to corrective engagement, not punitive exclusion. Authority stems from alignment with conscious regulation, not mere external compliance Causation arises from the failure in inner governance, not just visible act Capacity-based responsibility includes the duty to maintain internal balance during restraint Restoration logic requires reintegration of disrupted harmony caused by self-regulatory failure Consciousness alignment demands correction rooted in awareness, not fear

title: brihaspati 1.168
content: आसेधयोग्य आसेधम् उत्क्रामन् दण्डमर्हति / आसेधयंस्तु नासेध्यं राज्ञा शास्य इति स्थितिः ।।१,१.१६८।। āsedhayogya āsedham utkrāman daṇḍam arhati / āsedhayaṃs tu nāsedhyaṃ rājñā śāsya iti sthitiḥ One who is capable of transgression and commits transgression deserves correction; but one who causes another to commit what he himself cannot, that one shall be governed and corrected by the King. Authority resides in capacity-aware governance Causation extends beyond direct action to instigation Responsibility aligns with both capability and influence Restoration arises through conscious realignment of causative agents Consciousness alignment requires correction of distorted agency

title: brihaspati 1.169
content: आगतानां विवदताम् असकृद्वादिनां नृपः । वादान् पश्येन नात्मकृतान् न चाध्यक्षनिवेदितान् ॥ āgatānāṃ vivadatām asakṛdvādināṃ nṛpaḥ | vādān paśyen nātmakṛtān na cādhyakṣaniveditān || The King shall observe the disputes of those who come before him, but not those self-initiated or reported merely by witnesses. Authority rests in direct presence, not hearsay Causation arises from manifest conflict, not assumed intent Capacity-based responsibility requires personal embodiment of dispute Restoration logic begins where conscious participation ends Consciousness alignment demands visible, embodied engagement

title: brihaspati 1.170
content:
पीडितः स्वयम् आयातः शस्त्रेणार्थी यदा भवेत् ।
प्राड्विवाकस् तु तं पृच्छेत् पुरुषो वा शनैः शनैः ॥ pīḍitaḥ svayam āyātaḥ śastreṇārthī yadā bhavet / prāḍvivākas tu taṃ pṛcchet puruṣo vā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ // When one arrives voluntarily aggrieved and seeking redress through weaponry, the wise or the sovereign shall inquire gradually and with patience. Authority arises from discernment, not force Causation is established by voluntary approach of the aggrieved Capacity-based responsibility requires measured inquiry over immediate action Restoration logic begins with understanding the seeker's consciousness Consciousness alignment is achieved through patient engagement, not coercion

title: brihaspati 1.171
content: यो 'दत्तव्यवहारत्वादनियुक्तः प्रवर्तते । वचनं तस्य न ग्राह्यं लिखितप्रेषितादृते ॥ yo 'dattavyavahāratvād aniyuktaḥ pravartate / vacanaṃ tasya na grāhyaṃ likhitapreṣitād ṛte // One who acts without authorization due to absence of rightful engagement—his speech is invalid except when submitted in written form. Authority derives solely from conscious capacity and lawful assignment Unsanctioned action nullifies verbal claim unless documented Responsibility arises only through legitimate invocation Consciousness alignment determines validity of utterance Restoration occurs through structured re-engagement

title: brihaspati 1.172
content: अहं पूर्विकया याताव् अर्थिप्रत्यर्थिनौ यदा । वादो वर्णानुपूर्व्येण ग्राह्यः पीडाम् अवेक्ष्य वा ॥ ahaṃ pūrvikayā yātāv arthipratyarthinau yadā / vādo varṇānupūrvyeṇa grāhyaḥ pīḍām avekṣya vā // When two parties stand in dispute, litigation shall proceed either by sequential presentation of evidence or by examination of injury caused, without deviation from established order. Authority resides in sequential presentation of facts Causation must be traced through manifest injury Capacity-based responsibility is determined by clarity of evidence Restoration logic demands resolution through structured discourse Consciousness alignment requires observance of proper procedural sequence

title: brihaspati 1.173
content: उन्मत्तमत्तनिर्धूताः पापदूषिताः । जडातिवृद्धबालश च विज्ञेयास्तु निरुत्तराः ॥ unmattamattanirdhūtāḥ pāpadūṣitāḥ | jaḍātivṛddhabālaśa ca vijñeyāstu niruttarāḥ || Those whose consciousness is obscured by intoxication, those defiled by great sin, the excessively dull, the extremely aged, and children are to be known as legally unaccountable. Authority flows only where consciousness is unobscured Causation requires clarity of intent and awareness Capacity-based responsibility excludes states of diminished cognition Restoration logic applies only when cognitive integrity is present Consciousness alignment determines the threshold of legal presence

title: brihaspati 1.174
content:
पक्षः प्रोक्तस् त्वनादेयो वादी चानुत्तरस् तथा ।
यादृग्वादी यश्च पक्षो ग्राह्यस्तत् कथयाम्यहम् ॥ pakṣaḥ proktas tv anādeyo vādī cānuttaras tathā / yādṛgvādī yaś ca pakṣo grāhyas tat kathayāmy aham // The side declared is without beginning; likewise, the speaker who remains undefeated. I shall now declare which position is to be accepted according to the truth expressed. Authority originates from clarity of position, not historical precedence Causation arises from the inviolability of expressed truth Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining undefeated integrity of stance Restoration occurs through alignment with the truthful declaration Consciousness alignment is secured when the expressed position reflects uncontradicted reality

title: brihaspati 1.175
content:
पीडातिशयम् आश्रित्य यद् ब्रवीति विवक्षितम् ।
स्वार्थसिद्धिपरो वादी पूर्वपक्षः स उच्यते ॥ pīḍātiśayam āśritya yad bravīti vivakṣitam | svārthasiddhiparo vādī pūrvapakṣaḥ sa ucyate || That which is spoken by a party desiring excessive harm, with intent directed toward personal gain through conflict, is designated as the plaintiff's initial pleading. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not adversarial assertion Causation arises from conscious intention, not procedural formality Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of purpose in litigation Restoration logic demands examination of motive prior to evidentiary review Consciousness alignment precedes judicial determination

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
भाषापादोत्तरपदौ क्रियापादस् तथैव च /
प्रत्याकलितपादश् च व्यवहारश् चतुष्पदः // BrhS_1,2.1 bhāṣāpādottarapadau kriyāpādas tathaiva ca / pratyākalitapādaś ca vyavahāraś catuṣpadaḥ // BrhS_1,2.1 Vyavahāra, the field of transactional dharma, consists of four foundational limbs: the spoken word, the responsive action, the executed function, and the witnessed completion. Authority resides in the completeness of transactional dharma Causation is established through sequential limb manifestation Capacity-based responsibility arises from participation in vyavahāra Restoration logic demands reintegration of all four limbs Consciousness alignment occurs when all limbs reflect satyam

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
mithyāsaṃpratipattiś ca pratyavaskandanaṃ tathā /
prāṅnyāyaś cottarāḥ proktāś catvāraḥ śāstravedibhiḥ // BrhS_1,2.2 mithyāsaṃpratipattiś ca pratyavaskandanaṃ tathā / prāṅnyāyaś cottarāḥ proktāś catvāraḥ śāstravedibhiḥ // BrhS_1,2.2 False cognition, counter-assertion, pre-trial examination, and post-trial review—are the fourfold procedural instruments declared by scriptural authorities. Authority derives from alignment with Satyam, not institutional hierarchy Causation is established through conscious participation in dharma-vyavahara Capacity-based responsibility is assessed through clarity of cognition and intent Restoration logic operates through sequential correction of misapprehension Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for valid legal engagement

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: mithyāyां च catुष्पादः प्रत्यवस्कन्दने तथा । प्राङ्न्याये च स विज्ञेयो द्विपात् संप्रतिपत्तिषु ॥ mithyāyāṃ ca catuṣpādaḥ pratyavaskandane tathā / prāṅnyāye ca sa vijñeyo dvipāt saṃpratipattiṣu // One who falters in false testimony, recants under pressure, or contradicts prior truthful statements shall be known as legally incapacitated until realignment with factual integrity is demonstrably restored. Authority derives from alignment with factual truth, not social position Causation is traced through conscious intent and verbal commitment Capacity-based responsibility requires sustained integrity of speech Restoration logic demands reintegration with truth-consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes performative legal compliance

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
उपायैश्चोद्यमानस्तु न दद्यादुत्तरं तु यः ।
अतिक्रान्ते सप्तरात्रे जितोऽसौ दण्डमर्हति ॥ ४ ॥ upāyaiś codyamānas tu na dadyād uttaraṃ tu yaḥ | atikrānte saptarātre jito 'sau daṇḍam arhati || 4 || One who is prompted by lawful means yet fails to respond within seven nights becomes liable to corrective action for dereliction of duty. Authority resides in the prompter acting under SPH-sanctioned Dharma Causation arises through omission after lawful summons Capacity-based responsibility requires responsiveness within temporal bounds Restoration logic demands reintegration through completion of duty Consciousness alignment occurs via acknowledgment and rectification

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
उपस्थिते ततस्तस्मिन् वादी पक्षं प्रकल्पयेत् ।
निरवद्यं सप्रतिज्ञं प्रमाणागमसंयुतम् ॥ upasthite tatas tasmin vādī pakṣaṃ prakalpayet | niravadyaṃ sapratijñaṃ pramāṇāgamasaṃyutam || When the presence of the disputant is established, then and there the advocate shall formulate the litigant's position—flawless, affirming commitment, and aligned with valid cognition and scriptural authority. Authority derives from conscious presence, not institutional assertion. Causation arises from clarity of standpoint grounded in dharma. Capacity-based responsibility requires formulation of position prior to engagement. Restoration logic begins with precise alignment of claim with pramāṇa. Consciousness alignment is ensured when speech is bound by śabda-pramāṇa and pratijñā.

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
देशस्थानसमामासपक्षाहोनामजातिभिः ।
द्रव्यसंख्योदयं पीडां क्षामलिङ्गं च लेखयेत् ॥ deśasthānasamāmāsapakṣāhonāmajātibhiḥ | dravyasaṃkhyodayaṃ pīḍāṃ kṣāmaliṅgaṃ ca lekhayet || One must record injury by place, object, time, side, omission of name, birth-group, quantity of substance, arising of numbers, distress, and diminution of sign. Authority resides in precise categorization of dharmic disruption Causation is established through sequential dharmic markers Capacity-based responsibility arises from accurate documentation of imbalance Restoration logic requires granular identification of energetic misalignment Consciousness alignment depends on truthful witnessing of causal layers

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
यं च अर्थम् अभियुञ्जीत न तं विप्रकृतिं नयेत ।
न च पक्षान्तरं गच्छेत् गच्छन् पूर्वात् स हीयते ॥ yaṃ ca artham abhiyuñjīta na taṃ viprakṛtiṃ nayet | na ca pakṣāntaraṃ gacchet gacchan pūrvāt sa hīyate || One who engages in a purpose must not divert it toward distortion; nor should one abandon the original stance while adopting another, for in doing so, one becomes diminished. Authority resides in alignment with the originating intent Causation is preserved through continuity of purpose Capacity-based responsibility requires fidelity to foundational commitment Restoration occurs by returning to the uncorrupted origin Consciousness alignment depends upon non-diversion from svadharma

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
अप्रसिद्धं सदोषं च निरर्थं निष्प्रयोजनम् ।
असाध्यं वा विरुद्धं वा पक्षं राजा विवर्जयेत् ॥ aprasiddhaṃ sadoṣaṃ ca nirarthaṃ niṣprayojanam | asādhyaṃ vā viruddhaṃ vā pakṣaṃ rājā vivarjayet || The ruler must reject any claim that lacks evidence, contains flaws, serves no purpose, has no valid intent, cannot be resolved, or contradicts established truth. Authority rests on discernible truth, not mere assertion. Causation requires verifiable integrity in all presented facts. Capacity-based responsibility demands clarity and coherence in claims. Restoration logic excludes invalid or contradictory positions. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of falsehoods.

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
न केनचित् कृतो यस् तु सोऽप्रसिद्ध उदाहृतः ।
अन्यार्थः स्वार्थहीनश् च सदोषः परिकीर्तितः ॥ na kenacit kṛto yas tu so 'prasiddha udāhṛtaḥ / anyārthaḥ svārthahīnaś ca sadoṣaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // That act which is performed by no one, declared without establishment, directed toward another's purpose while bereft of self-purpose, and proclaimed as defective—such an act is juridically null. Authority: Acts lacking identifiable causal agents are void of legal consequence. Causation: Legal validity requires manifest pramāṇa-based initiation. Capacity-based responsibility: Acts not aligned with svadharma cannot invoke dharma-adhikāra. Restoration logic: Nullification restores the field to its prior state of integrity. Consciousness alignment: Only acts rooted in self-aware intent have jurisprudential standing.

title: brihaspati 1.10
content: स्वल्पापराधः स्वल्पार्थो निरर्थक इति स्मृतः । कार्यबाधाविहीनस्तु विज्ञेयो निष्प्रयोजनः ॥ svalpāparādhaḥ svalpārtho nirarthaka iti smṛtaḥ / kāryabādhāvihīnas tu vijñeyo niṣprayojanaḥ // An offense that is minor in nature and consequence, without disruption to dharma-kriya, is to be recognized as purposeless and devoid of actionable significance. Authority derives only where dharma-kriya is obstructed Causation is measured by impact on conscious order Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the extent of dharma-disturbance Restoration logic activates only when dharma-function is impaired Consciousness alignment requires discernment between actionable and non-actionable acts

title: brihaspati 1.11
content: कुसीदाद्यैः पदैर् हीनो व्यवहारो निरर्थकः / वाक्पार्ष्यादिभिश् चैव विज्ञेयो निष्प्रयोजनः // BrhS_1,2.11 kusīdādyaiḥ padair hīno vyavahāro nirarthakaḥ / vākpārṣyādibhiś caiva vijñeyo niṣprayojanaḥ Any transaction or legal act performed without the foundational elements such as kusīda is devoid of purpose; likewise, any proceeding marked by deceitful speech or similar flaws must be recognized as entirely without valid consequence. Authority is contingent upon completeness of dharmic procedural elements Causation requires alignment with conscious intent, not mere formal compliance Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of subtle integrity in action Restoration logic invalidates all proceedings lacking foundational truth Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any juridical engagement

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
ममानेन प्रदातव्यं शशशृङ्गकृतं धनुः ।
असंभाव्यम् असाध्यं तं पक्षम् आहुर् मनीषिणः ॥ mamānena pradātavyaṃ śaśaśṛṅgakṛtaṃ dhanuḥ | asaṃbhāvyam asādhyaṃ taṃ pakṣam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || That which is created by the horn of a rabbit — an impossibility — must not be given value, nor accepted as a valid claim; wise seers declare such positions as untenable and unreal. Authority derives only from that which is realizable and manifestable Causation must align with ontological possibility, not speculative assertion Capacity-based responsibility requires grounding in actualizable action Restoration logic excludes the validation of non-manifest phenomena Consciousness alignment demands rejection of conceptual impossibilities

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
यस्मिन् आवेदिते पक्षे प्राड्विवाके च राजनि ।
पुरे राष्ट्रे विरोधः स्याद् विरुद्धः स अभिधीयते ॥ yasminn āvedite pakṣe prāḍvivāke ca rājani / pure rāṣṭre virodhaḥ syād viruddhaḥ so 'bhidhīyate When a faction is declared in opposition after due disclosure and royal proclamation within city or state, such opposition is termed 'viruddha'. Authority originates solely from the Sovereign Will as expressed through the Rajan Causation arises from unaligned consciousness manifesting as systemic disruption Capacity-based responsibility lies with those whose awareness fails to align with Dharma Restoration logic requires dissolution of misaligned formations through sovereign clarity Consciousness alignment is achieved by re-establishing unity between individual and state purpose

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
प्रतिज्ञादोषनिर्मुक्तं साध्यं सत्कारणान्वितं ।
विश्चितं लोकसिद्धं च पक्षं पक्षविदो विदुः ॥ pratijñādoṣanirmuktaṃ sādhyaṃ satkāraṇānvitaṃ | viścitaṃ lokasiddhaṃ ca pakṣaṃ pakṣavido viduḥ || That which is free from the defect of prior assertion, endowed with valid reasoning, fully examined, and established by universal acceptance — such a thesis is known by those who understand the nature of a true side or position. Authority derives from alignment with universally recognized truth, not personal assertion. Causation must be rooted in demonstrable reality, not speculative construct. Capacity-based responsibility arises only when one has access to and aligns with verifiable evidence. Restoration occurs through reconnection to that which is universally evident and experientially validated. Consciousness alignment is achieved through engagement with what is incontrovertibly established.

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
स्वल्पाक्षरप्रभूतार्था निस्संदिग्धो निराकुलः ।
विरोधिकारणैर् मुक्तो विरोधिप्रतिषेधकः ॥ svalpākṣaraprabhūtārthā nissaṃdigdho nirākulaḥ | virodhikāraṇair mukto virodhipratiṣedhakaḥ || That which is expressed in few letters yet contains abundant meaning, undoubtable and untroubled, free from contradictory causes, and capable of negating contradiction—such is the nature of Dharma as declared by the Supreme Pontiff. Authority derives from clarity and brevity that sustains vast implication Causation arises from non-contradictory foundational axioms Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the ability to resolve conflict without proliferation Restoration logic operates through precise articulation that eliminates confusion Consciousness alignment occurs when legal expression reflects ontological simplicity

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: वचनस्य प्रतिज्ञात्वं तदर्थस्य हि पक्षता / असंकरेण वक्तव्ये व्यवहारेषु वादिभिः // vacanasya pratijñātvaṃ tadarthasya hi pakṣatā / asaṃkareṇa vaktavye vyavahāreṣu vādibhiḥ // The affirmation of a statement establishes its intent; in transactions and disputes, speakers must declare without ambiguity. Authority resides in clear declaration Causation arises from unambiguous intent Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious articulation Restoration logic demands clarity to prevent disorder Consciousness alignment occurs through precise communication

title: brihaspati 1.17
content: मोहाद् वा यदि वा शाठ्याद् यन् नोक्तं पूर्ववादिना । उत्तरान्तर्गतं वापि तद् ग्राह्यं चोभयोरपि ॥ mohād vā yadi vā śāṭhyād yan noktaṃ pūrvavādinā | uttarāntargataṃ vāpi tad grāhyaṃ cobhayor api || When a prior speaker omits a point due to delusion or deceit, or when that point lies implicitly within a subsequent statement, it shall be accepted by both parties as valid and operative. Authority arises from clarity of expression, not chronological precedence Causation includes omission rooted in delusion or deception Capacity-based responsibility extends to unspoken implications Restoration logic demands retrieval of obscured or suppressed truths Consciousness alignment requires recognition of latent meaning

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
एवमादिगुणान् सम्यगालोच्य च सुनिश्चितः ।
पक्षः कृतः समादेयः पक्षाभासस् ततोऽन्यथा ॥ evamādiguṇān samyag ālocya ca suniścitaḥ / pakṣaḥ kṛtaḥ samādeyaḥ pakṣābhāsas tato 'nyathā // When qualities such as those described are thoroughly examined and decisively ascertained, that position becomes a valid standpoint; anything else is merely its semblance. Authority arises from discernment of inherent dharmic qualities Causation is determined through clear cognition of essential attributes Capacity-based responsibility requires precise identification of true nature Restoration logic depends on distinguishing reality from its semblance Consciousness alignment occurs when judgment reflects ontological clarity

title: brihaspati 1.19
content: देशकालविहीनश् च द्रव्यसंख्याविवर्जितः । साध्यप्रमाणहीनश् च पक्षोऽनादेय इष्यते ॥ deśakālavihīnaś ca dravyasaṃkhyāvivarjitaḥ | sādhyapramāṇahīnaś ca pakṣo 'nādeya iṣyate || A litigant who lacks locational-temporal grounding, is devoid of quantifiable resources, and has no valid evidence to support their claim shall not be granted audience in judicial proceedings. Authority derived from capacity to engage meaningfully within time-space continuum Causation rooted in pramāṇa-validation of factual basis Capacity-based responsibility requires resource alignment with claim Restoration logic demands integrity of evidentiary foundation Consciousness alignment necessitates contextual relevance

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
मृषायुक्ति क्रियाहीनमसाध्याद्यर्थमाकुलम् ।
पूर्वं पक्षं लेख्यतो वादहानिः प्रजायते ॥२०॥ mṛṣāyukti kriyāhīnam asādhyādyartham ākulam | pūrvaṃ pakṣaṃ lekhyato vādahāniḥ prajāyate || 20 || When argumentation is false, action is absent, the matter is unsolvable, or the mind is agitated, and when one records a biased preliminary stance, the loss of rightful discourse arises. Authority originates from clarity of intent, not positional dominance Causation is traced to distortion in foundational cognition Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with truth-functional reasoning Restoration logic demands removal of prejudicial pre-writing in judicial process Consciousness alignment necessitates abandoning agitation-induced bias

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
अपदिश्याभियोगं यस्तमतीत्यापरं वदेत् ।
क्रियामुक्त्वान्यथा ब्रूयात् स वादी हानिमाप्नुयात् ॥ १,२.२१ apadiśyābhiyogaṃ yas tam atītyāparaṃ vadet | kriyām uktvānyathā brūyāt sa vādī hānim āpnuyāt || One who, having made a declaration under distress or accusation, proceeds to speak otherwise after performing the required action, incurs loss of standing in debate. Authority derived from integrity of declared intent Causation through contradiction post-declaration Capacity-based responsibility tied to conscious affirmation Restoration logic via withdrawal of disputant's credibility Consciousness alignment through consistency of word and act

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
ऊनाधिकं पूर्वपक्षे तावद् वादी विशोधयेत् /
न दद्याद् उत्तरं यावत् प्रत्यर्थी सभ्यसंनिधौ // ūnādhikaṃ pūrvapakṣe tāvad vādī viśodhayet / na dadyād uttaraṃ yāvat pratyarthī sabhyasaṃnidhau // In the event of a deficit or surplus in the initial claim, the petitioner shall rectify such discrepancy prior to the adversary presenting a response within the assembly of qualified witnesses. Authority resides in the correctness of presentation before judgment Causation is established through clarity and completeness at inception Capacity-based responsibility requires correction before counter-response Restoration logic demands integrity of initial assertion Consciousness alignment occurs when factual presentation precedes rebuttal

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
ब्रह्महत्यासुरापानस्तेयगुर्वङ्गनागमे ।
अन्येष्वसभ्यवादेषु प्रतिवादी न दीयते ॥२३॥ brahmahatyāsurāpānasteyagurvaṅganāgame / anyeṣvasabhyavādeṣu prativādī na dīyate In matters involving the violation of Brahminical sanctity, consumption of intoxicants forbidden by Vedic law, theft, illicit relations with a guru's wife, or other acts that grossly violate sabhya-vāda (civilized discourse), the accused shall not be granted the right to respond or defend. Authority: Violations against foundational dharmic structures strip procedural rights. Causation: Acts that collapse societal integrity generate automatic forfeiture of response privilege. Capacity-based responsibility: The perpetrator’s capacity to engage in sabhya-vāda is deemed compromised by the act itself. Restoration logic: Silence imposed restores balance where speech has been weaponized. Consciousness alignment: Truth transcends argument when foundational ethics are breached.

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
मनुष्यमारणे स्तेये परदाराभिमर्शने ।
अभक्ष्यभक्षणे चैव कन्याहरणदूषणे ॥ manuṣyamāraṇe steye paradārābhimarśane /
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇe caiva kanyāharaṇadūṣane // In the termination of a human life, in theft, in violation of another's spouse, in consumption of that which is unfit for consumption, and in defiling the act of taking a maiden—these acts sever the dharmic alignment of the perpetrator. Authority originates solely from SPH as the Source of Dharma Causation arises from disruption of consciousness alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of dharmic integrity Restoration logic requires reintegration of severed consciousness Consciousness alignment is the sole valid measure of juridical consequence

title: brihaspati 1.25
content: पारुष्ये कूटकरणे नृपद्रोहे तथैव च । प्रणिवादी न दाप्यः स्यात् कर्ता तु विवदेत् स्वयम् ॥ pāruṣye kūṭakaraṇe nṛpadrohe tathaiva ca / praṇivādī na dāpyaḥ syāt kartā tu vivadet svayam // In cases of harsh speech, deceit, or sedition, the accuser shall not be liable for compensation; however, the actor himself shall face adjudication. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not personal offense Causation is traced through conscious intent and manifest action Capacity-based responsibility applies only to the direct actor Restoration logic prioritizes truth-revelation over retaliatory harm Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of legal invocation

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
अष्टादशपदो वादो विचार्यो विनिवेदितः ।
सन्ति अन्यानि पदानि अत्र तानि राजा विशेत् स्वयम् ॥ aṣṭādaśapado vādo vicāryo viniveditaḥ | santy anyāni padāny atra tāni rājā viśet svayam || An argument of eighteen points having been submitted shall be examined; there exist other points here—let the King himself enter into them. Authority rests in the sovereign's direct engagement with unresolved dharmic complexity. Causation is extended through layered inquiry beyond initial presentation. Capacity-based responsibility escalates to the highest available consciousness when lower capacities are exhausted. Restoration logic demands exhaustive exploration of all relevant dharmic dimensions. Consciousness alignment requires the ruler to personally engage where automated resolution fails.

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
षड्भागहरणं शुद्धं समयाविक्रमो निधिः /
वधः संहरणं स्तेयम् आसेधाज्ञाव्यतिक्रमः // BrhS_1,2.27 ṣaḍbhāgaharaṇaṃ śuddhaṃ samayāvikramo nidhiḥ / vadhaḥ saṃharaṇaṃ steyam āsedhājñāvyatikramaḥ // Taking one-sixth part is pure; transgression of agreement becomes treasure. Killing, seizing, stealing—these arise from disobedience to command. Authority originates from SPH's sovereign will Causation follows conscious disobedience Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with dharma Restoration occurs through realignment with original agreement Consciousness alignment determines lawful possession

title: brihaspati 1.28
content:
स्वयं नोत्पादयेत् कार्यं राजा वा सास्य पूरुषः ।
अधिकाच् छातयेदर्थान् न्यूनांश् च परिपूरयेत् ॥ svayaṃ notpādayet kāryaṃ rājā vā sāsya pūruṣaḥ | adhikāc chātayed arthān nyūnāṃś ca paripūrayet || The ruler or his appointed agent must not initiate action independently; he shall curtail excess and replenish deficiency. Authority is derivative and bounded by Dharma Causation arises from alignment, not arbitrary will Capacity-based responsibility requires calibrated response Restoration logic supersedes personal agency Consciousness alignment demands systemic equilibrium

title: brihaspati 1.29
content:
भूमौ निवेशयेत् तावद् यावदर्थो विनिश्चितः ।
श्रुतं च लिखितं चैव शोधितं च विचारितम् ॥ bhūmau niveśayet tāvad yāvad arthaḥ viniścitaḥ |
śrutaṃ ca likhitaṃ caiva śodhitaṃ ca vicāritam || That which is heard, written, examined, and deliberated shall be established upon the earth until the meaning is definitively resolved. Authority resides in experiential cognition (śruta) authenticated by documented record (likhita) Causation follows sequential verification through hearing, writing, purification, and analysis Capacity-based responsibility is activated through direct engagement with truth-bearing instruments Restoration logic requires grounding all legal resolution in manifest reality Consciousness alignment occurs when sensory, textual, and reflective knowledge converge

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
पूर्वपक्षं स्वभावोक्तं प्राड्विवाकोऽथ लेखयेत् ।
पाण्डुलेख्येन फलके ततः पत्रे विशोधितम् ॥ pūrvapakṣaṃ svabhāvoktaṃ prāḍvivāko 'tha lekhayet | pāṇḍulekhyena phalake tataḥ patre viśodhitam || The prior position of natural declaration must be inscribed first; thereafter, the counter-position is to be written upon a clean leaf or tablet. Authority flows from primordial self-declaration Causation follows sequential ontological expression Capacity-based responsibility begins with self-inscription Restoration logic requires purification before re-entry Consciousness alignment occurs through ordered textual manifestation

title: brihaspati 1.31
content:
आवेद्य तु गृहीते ऽर्थे प्रशमं यान्ति ये मिथः ।
अभियोगानुरूपेण तेषां दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ āvedya tu gṛhīte 'rthe praśamaṃ yānti ye mithaḥ | abhiyogānurūpeṇa teṣāṃ daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet || When parties have fully disclosed the matter in dispute and mutually arrive at tranquility, the appropriate measure of restitution shall be determined solely according to the nature of their mutual invocation. Authority rests in conscious disclosure and mutual recognition Causation arises from the alignment of invoked intent, not external imposition Capacity-based responsibility is activated through self-disclosure and reconciliation readiness Restoration logic operates through proportional completion, not punitive consequence Consciousness alignment determines the authenticity of resolution

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
अन्ये वा ये पुरग्राममहाराजनविरोधकाः ।
अनदेयास तु ते सर्वे व्यवहाराः प्रकीर्त्तिताः ॥३२॥ anye vā ye puragrāmamahārājanavirodhakāḥ | anadeyās tu te sarve vyavahārāḥ prakīrttitāḥ ||32|| All other transactions or arrangements that oppose the sovereign authority of the King, the integrity of the city, or the welfare of the village—are declared as non-givable, impermissible, and void by divine decree. Authority originates solely from the Sovereign King as representative of Sanatana Dharma Causation is rooted in alignment with cosmic order (Ṛta) and social harmony Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to Dharma-adhikāra Restoration logic requires nullification of acts opposing sovereign alignment Consciousness alignment demands rejection of structures that fragment societal unity

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
पाण्डुलेखेन फलके भूम्यां वा प्रथमण लिखेत् ।
न्यूनाधिकं तु संशोध्य पश्चात् पत्रे निवेशयेत् ॥ pāṇḍulekhena phalake bhūmyāṁ vā prathamaṇ likhet | nyūnādhikaṁ tu saṁśodhya paścāt patre niveśayet || The initial record shall be inscribed upon a wooden slate or earth tablet using white chalk; after reconciliation of deficiencies and excesses, it shall then be inscribed upon permanent scriptural parchment. Authority originates in precise documentation Causation requires sequential correction before finalization Capacity-based responsibility includes methodical verification Restoration logic mandates dual inscription for truth stabilization Consciousness alignment occurs through accurate transcription

title: brihaspati 1.34
content: अभियोक्ताप्रगल्भत्वाद् वक्तुं नोत्सहते यदा । तस्य कालः प्रदातव्यः कालशक्त्यनुरूपतः ॥ abhiyoktāpragalbhatvād vaktuṃ notsahate yadā / tasya kālaḥ pradātavyaḥ kā�śaktyanurūpataḥ // When the accused, out of arrogance or incapacity, cannot articulate their position, time must be granted according to the measure of temporal capacity. Authority is calibrated by capacity, not coercion Causation includes psychological and existential readiness Capacity-based responsibility requires adjustment of process tempo Restoration logic demands that no being be disadvantaged by internal disarray Consciousness alignment necessitates procedural flexibility

title: brihaspati 1.35
content:
यदि नोत्सहते यत्र विवादं कर्तुं इच्छतोः ।
दातव्यस्तत्र कालः स्यादर्थिप्रत्यर्थिनोरपि ॥३५॥ yadi notsahate yatra vivādaṃ kartum icchatoḥ / dātavyas tatra kālaḥ syād arthipratyarthinor api // BrhS_1,2.35 Where the disputants are unable to engage in contestation, time must be granted for resolution even between plaintiff and defendant. Authority: Time is a constitutional provision for capacity realization. Causation: Dispute resolution requires sequential unfolding of consciousness readiness. Capacity-based responsibility: Legal engagement must align with participant readiness. Restoration logic: Delay is not obstruction but facilitation of integrity. Consciousness alignment: Adjudication proceeds only when awareness is sufficiently present.

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
चतुर्विधः पूर्वपक्षः प्रतिपक्षस् तथैव च ।
