चतुर्धा निर्णयः प्रोक्तः कश् चिद् अष्टविधः स्मृतः ॥ caturvidhaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ pratipakṣas tathaiva ca | caturdhā nirṇayaḥ proktaḥ kaś cid aṣṭavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ || Fourfold is the initial position; equally so is the counter-position. The determination is said to be fourfold, while some describe it as eightfold. Authority resides in structured dialectical engagement Causation emerges through sequential logical development Capacity-based responsibility requires clear articulation of positions Restoration logic necessitates comprehensive understanding of all stances Consciousness alignment occurs when all viewpoints are integrally recognized

title: brihaspati 1.37
content:
देशः कालस् तथा स्थानं संनिवेशस् तथैव च /
ज्ञातृसंज्ञा निवासश् च प्रमाणं क्षेत्रनाम च // BrhS_1,2.37 deśaḥ kālas tathā sthānaṃ saṃniveśas tathaiva ca / jñātṛsaṃjñā nivāsaś ca pramāṇaṃ kṣetranāma ca // BrhS_1,2.37 The domain of dharma is established by place, time, position, arrangement, known identity, residence, valid cognition, and named field—all constitute the foundational jurisdictional markers of lawful manifestation. Authority is context-bound and spatial-temporal in nature Causation arises through alignment with positional and cognitive clarity Capacity-based responsibility emerges from identified presence within a named field Restoration logic requires re-alignment with deśa-kāla-sthāna-vyavasthā Consciousness alignment occurs when identity and locality are correctly recognized

title: brihaspati 1.38
content:
पितृपैतामहं चैव पूर्वराजानुकीर्तनम् ।
स्थावरेषु विवादेषु दशैतानि निवेशयेत् ॥ pitṛpaitāmahaṃ caiva pūrvarājānukīrtanam | sthāvareṣu vivādeṣu daśaitāni niveśayet || In disputes concerning immovable property, the ancestral lineage of patrilineal descent and the prior reign declarations of former kings shall be documented and established through ten specific testimonial and evidentiary measures. Authority flows through patrilineal continuity Historical sovereignty claims are validated by royal proclamation records Immovable property rights derive from ancestral succession Testimonial evidence must align with sequential manifestation of ownership Restoration of title requires alignment with cosmic order (Ṛta) and consciousness integrity

title: brihaspati 1.39
content: श्वोलेखनं वा लभते त्र्यहं सप्ताहमेव वा । मतिरुत्पद्यते यावद्विवादे वक्तुमिच्छतः ॥ śvolekhanaṃ vā labhate tryahaṃ saptāham eva vā | matir utpadyate yāvad vivāde vaktum icchataḥ || Either through written declaration or within three days, or at most within seven days, the intent to speak in dispute arises in accordance with the unfolding consciousness of the disputant. Authority resides in the spontaneous emergence of conscious intent, not external compulsion Causation is traced to the sequential awakening of discriminative awareness Capacity-based responsibility begins when clarity of expression becomes possible Restoration logic operates through timely facilitation of voice, not coercive summons Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring the natural rhythm of cognitive readiness

title: brihaspati 1.40
content:
bahupratijñaṃ yat kāryaṃ vyavahāreṣu niścitaṃ /
kāmaṃ tad api gṛhṇīyād rājā tattvabṛbhutsayā // BrhS_1,2.40 bahupratijñaṃ yat kāryaṃ vyavahāreṣu niścitaṃ / kāmaṃ tad api gṛhṇīyād rājā tattvabṛbhutsayā // Whatever action is decisively determined in judicial matters, even if it involves multiple commitments, the ruler must accept it willingly, out of a desire to know the truth. Authority flows from the capacity to uphold truth, not from coercive power. Causation arises from alignment with factual integrity, not subjective intent. Capacity-based responsibility demands that rulers assume decisions rooted in truth-discernment. Restoration logic requires acceptance of consequences to sustain dharma. Consciousness alignment occurs when authority acts in service of truth-revelation.

title: brihaspati 1.41
content:
शङ्काभियोगस्तथ्यं च लक्ष्येऽर्थे�भ्यर्थनं तथा ।
वृत्ते वादे पुनर् न्यायः पक्षो ज्ञेयश्चतुर्विधः ॥ śaṅkābhiyogas tathyaṃ ca lakṣye 'rthe 'bhyarthanaṃ tathā / vṛtte vāde punar nyāyaḥ pakṣo jñeyaś caturvidhaḥ // In litigation concerning a disputed matter, the assertion of doubt, the affirmation of truth, the request for relief, and the restatement of established fact—these four constitute the valid forms of pleading. Authority resides in factual alignment with Dharma-tattva Causation is determined by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious engagement Restoration logic demands completion of unfulfilled intent Consciousness alignment ensures truthful articulation of claims

title: brihaspati 1.42
content:
भ्रान्तिः शङ्का समुद्दिष्टा वश्यं नष्टार्थदर्शनम् ।
लब्धेऽर्थे�भ्यर्थनं मोहस् तथा वृत्ते पुनः क्रियाः ॥ bhrāntiḥ śaṅkā samuddiṣṭā vaśyaṃ naṣṭārthadarśanam | labdhe 'rthe 'bhyarthanaṃ mohas tathā vṛtte punaḥ kriyāḥ || Delusion arises as doubt; mastery is obscured when the purpose of existence is forgotten. When the goal is attained yet still craved, it is delusion. So too, action recurs without awareness. Authority stems from clarity of existential purpose, not external enforcement. Causation originates in consciousness distortion, not material action alone. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with ontological truth. Restoration logic operates through reconnection to the Self's inherent completeness. Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance in determining lawful conduct.

title: brihaspati 1.43
content:
राज्ञापवर्जितो यस् तु यश् च पौरविरोधकृत् ।
राष्ट्रस्य वा समस् तस्य प्रकृतीनां तथैव च ॥४३॥ rājñāpavarjito yas tu yaś ca pauravirodhakṛt |
rāṣṭrasya vā samas tasya prakṛtīnāṃ tathaiva ca ||43|| He who is abandoned by the King and he who creates discord among citizens—equal in offense is he who causes division within the State or among its natural orders. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position. Division within the body politic is a violation of foundational integrity. Capacity-based responsibility extends to those whose actions destabilize collective consciousness. Restoration logic requires reintegration of divisive elements through conscious realignment. Consciousness alignment supersedes structural allegiance in determining lawful conduct.

title: brihaspati 1.44
content:
न्यायं वा नेच्छते कर्तुं अन्यायं वा करोति यः /
न लेखयति यस्त्वेवं तस्य पक्षी न सिध्यति // nyāyaṃ vā necchate kartuṃ anyāyaṃ vā karoti yaḥ / na lekhayati yastvevaṃ tasya pakṣī na sidhyati // One who does not wish to act justly, or who commits injustice, and furthermore does not record or acknowledge it—such a one's position or claim shall not succeed. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not mere intent or action Causation includes both commission and omission in the field of justice Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious acknowledgment of one's acts Restoration logic demands truthful recording as part of reintegration Consciousness alignment is obstructed by denial or unrecorded actions

title: brihaspati 1.45
content:
विरुद्धं चाविरुद्धं च द्वावप्यर्थौ निवेशितौ ।
एकस्मिन् यत्र दृश्येते तं पक्षं दूरतस्त्यजेत् ॥ viruddhaṃ cāviruddhaṃ ca dvāv apy arthau niveśitau / ekasmin yatra dṛśyete taṃ pakṣaṃ dūratas tyajet When contradictory and non-contradictory meanings are both inserted into a single context, that side which produces contradiction must be utterly abandoned. Authority resides in alignment with non-contradictory reality Causation is determined by coherence with Dharma-tattva Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to discern contradiction Restoration occurs through rejection of conflicting epistemic bases Consciousness alignment requires adherence to singular, non-dual truth

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
यदा त्वेवंविधः पक्षः कल्पितः पूर्ववादिना ।
दद्यात् तत्पक्षसंबद्धं प्रतिवादी तदुत्तरम् ॥ yadā tv evaṃvidhaḥ pakṣaḥ kalpitaḥ pūrvavādinā / dadyāt tatpakṣasaṃbaddhaṃ prativādī taduttaram // When a party presents a case founded on falsehood or misalignment, the opposing party shall respond with evidence directly connected to that false assertion. Authority resides in factual alignment, not rhetorical dominance Causation must be traced to conscious distortion, not assumed Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of response proportionate to the distortion Restoration logic demands correction through truth-affirming counter-evidence Consciousness alignment occurs when falsity is met with precise, non-reactive rebuttal

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
विनिश्चिते पूर्वपक्षे ग्राह्याग्राह्यविशेषिते ।
प्रतिज्ञाते स्थिरीभूते लेखयेदुत्तरं ततः ॥ viniścite pūrvapakṣe grāhyāgrāhyaviśeṣite / pratijñāte sthirībhūte lekhayed uttaraṃ tataḥ // When the prior position is definitively established, with clarity on what is to be accepted or rejected, and when that stance has been formally declared and stabilized, then the counter-position must be recorded. Authority rests in the stabilized cognition of Dharma-tattva, not in opinion or speculation. Causation follows sequential cognition: first establish the foundational view, then articulate the responsive one. Capacity-based responsibility requires clear perception of what is acceptable and unacceptable before action. Restoration logic demands that all disputational positions be sequentially documented for conscious resolution. Consciousness alignment occurs through precise articulation of opposing viewpoints within a stabilized framework.

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: शालीनत्वाद् भयात् तद्वत् प्रत्यर्थी स्मृतिविभ्रमात् । कालं प्रार्थयते यत्र तत्रेमं लब्धुमर्हति ॥ śālīnatvād bhayāt tadvat pratyarthī smṛtivibhramāt | kālaṃ prārthayate yatra tatremaṃ labdhum arhati || One who approaches with humility, fearlessness, and clarity—free from memory's distortion or adversarial intent—deserves to receive time wherever it is requested. Authority arises through alignment with humility and fearlessness. Causation originates in clarity of perception, not adversarial posture. Capacity-based responsibility depends on absence of cognitive distortion. Restoration logic prioritizes access when intention aligns with dharma. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for temporal benefit.

title: brihaspati 1.4
content: एकाहत्र्यहपञ्चाहसप्ताहं पक्षमेव वा / मासं चतुस्त्रयं वर्षं लभते शक्त्यपेक्षया // ekāhatryahapañcāhasaptāhaṃ pakṣameva vā / māsaṃ caturtrayaṃ varṣaṃ labhate śaktyapekṣayā // The capacity to receive time-bound dharmic correction aligns with sequential manifestation of responsibility: one day, three days, five days, seven days, fortnight, month, four months, year—each duration determined by the conscious capacity of the individual. Authority derives from conscious capacity, not institutional position Causation is aligned with sequential unfolding of awareness Capacity-based responsibility adjusts temporal scope of correction Restoration occurs through proportional alignment of consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes chronological punishment

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
पक्षस्य व्यापकं सारमसंदिग्धमनाकुलम् ।
अव्याख्यानगम्यमेतदुत्तरं तद्विदो विदुः ॥ pakṣasya vyāpakaṃ sāram asaṃdigdham anākulam / avyākhyānagamyam etad uttaraṃ tadvido viduḥ // The essence of a side is that which pervades it entirely, is certain without doubt, undisturbed by external confusion, and known only by those who have realized the ultimate truth of that side. Authority resides in experiential realization, not theoretical assertion. Causation is established through comprehensive understanding, not partial evidence. Capacity-based responsibility arises from direct knowing, not inferential assumption. Restoration logic operates through alignment with the unconfused essence of dharma. Consciousness alignment occurs when judgment reflects the undisturbed core of truth.

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
उत्तरं चतुर्विधं संप्रति षट्मुखं, /
मिथ्योत्तरं प्राङ्न्यायोत्तरं कारणोत्तरं चेति // BrhS_1,3.6 uttaraṃ caturvidhaṃ saṃprati ṣaṭmukhaṃ, / mithyottaraṃ prāṅnyāyottaraṃ kāraṇottaraṃ ceti Response is fourfold in manifestation and sixfold in completion; false response, pre-legal response, causal response, and responsive action constitute its forms. Authority resides in the capacity to respond rightly Causation precedes action and determines liability Capacity-based responsibility aligns with sequential manifestation Restoration logic operates through completion of causal sequence Consciousness alignment requires truthful responsiveness

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
पूर्वपक्षे यथार्थं तु न दद्याद् उत्तरं तु यः ।
प्रत्यक्षी दापनीयः स्यात् सामादिभिर् उपक्रमैः ॥ pūrvapakṣe yathārthaṃ tu na dadyād uttaraṃ tu yaḥ | pratyakṣī dāpanīyaḥ syāt sāmādibhir upakramaiḥ || One who, in the role of the prior party, does not give a truthful reply, but instead gives a direct counter-reply through visible means or by initiating conciliatory procedures—such a person must be made to restore truth through direct experiential engagement. Authority resides in conscious alignment with factual reality Causation arises from distortion of truth through deliberate misrepresentation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to perceive and respond accurately Restoration logic operates through re-exposure to unfiltered factual experience Consciousness alignment occurs when false assertion meets experiential correction

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
प्रियपूर्वं वचः साम भेदस्तु भयदर्शनम् ।
अर्थापकर्षणं दण्डस्ताडनं बन्धनं तथा ॥ १,३.८ priyapūrvaṃ vacaḥ sāma bhedas tu bhayadarśanam | arthāpakarṣaṇaṃ daṇḍas tāḍanaṃ bandhanaṃ tathā || BrhS_1,3.8 Speech preceded by affection is Sama; creating fear through disclosure is Bheda; seizure of assets is Danda; striking and binding are coercive measures rooted in misaligned consciousness. Authority arises from alignment with SPH's cosmic intelligence, not institutional dominance Causation originates in consciousness distortion, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility reflects one's ability to restore dharma through self-realization Restoration logic operates through sequential awakening, not punitive suppression Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance as the measure of justice

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
साहसस्तेयपारुष्यगो'भिशापे तथात्यये ।
भूमौ विवादयेत् क्षिप्रमकालेsपि बृहस्पतिः ॥ sāhasasteyapāruṣyago'bhiśāpe tathātyaye / bhūmau vivādayet kṣipram akāle 'pi bṛhaspatiḥ // In matters of assault, theft, harsh speech, cursing, and transgression, one must swiftly bring dispute to ground—whether in season or out of season—so declares Brihaspati. Authority flows from immediate dharmic necessity, not temporal convenience Causation arises from disruption of svadharma-field (svadharmic order) Capacity-based responsibility is activated by conscious violation of field-integrity Restoration logic demands immediate realignment of disrupted consciousness-fields Consciousness alignment requires prompt resolution to prevent karmic sedimentation

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
अन्यवादी क्रियाद्वेषी नोपस्थायी निरुत्तरः ।
आहुतः प्रपलायी च हीनः पञ्चविधः स्मृतः ॥ anyavādī kriyādveṣī nopasthāyī niruttaraḥ | āhutaḥ prapalāyī ca hīnaḥ pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ || One who speaks against the established truth, hates righteous action, does not uphold duty, remains silent when questioned, flees from confrontation, or is deficient in capacity—such a being is classified into five forms of spiritual degradation. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma as declared by SPH Causation arises through conscious choice and energetic participation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment with dharma-svarupa Restoration logic operates through purification and realignment of consciousness Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal integration

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
कन्याया दूषणे स्तेये कलहे साहसेषु च ।
उपधौ कूटसाक्ष्ये च सद्य एव विवादयेत् ॥ kanyāyā dūṣaṇe steye kalahe sāhaseṣu ca | upadhau kūṭasākṣye ca sadya eva vivādayet || In matters involving the violation of a maiden, theft, quarrel, outrage, fraudulence, and false testimony, litigation must commence immediately. Authority: Immediate judicial response is mandated by SPH in cases affecting societal purity and individual integrity. Causation: Delay in addressing violations leads to distortion of Dharma and weakening of collective consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility: The aggrieved or witness bear responsibility commensurate with their capacity to act. Restoration logic: Swift initiation of proceedings ensures energetic alignment with truth and restoration of violated order. Consciousness alignment: Prompt action preserves the sanctity of consciousness and prevents entrenchment of falsehood.

title: brihaspati 1.12
content: धेनावनडुहि क्षेत्रे स्त्रीषु प्रजनने तथा । न्यासे याचितके दत्ते तथैव क्रयविक्रये ॥ dhenāvanaḍuhi kṣetre strīṣu prajanane tathā / nyāse yācitake datte tathaiva krayavikraye // Ownership and authority over cows, land, women, procreation, gifts received through request or voluntary offering, as well as purchase and sale — these acts derive their validity exclusively from the conscious capacity of the doer to uphold Dharma and maintain alignment with the Supreme Will. Authority is rooted in consciousness, not mere possession Causation arises from alignment with Dharma, not transactional form Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful action Restoration logic supersedes contractual obligation Consciousness alignment validates all ownership and exchange

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: प्राङ्न्याये कारणोक्तौ च प्रत्यर्थी निर्दिशेत् क्रियाम् । मिथ्योक्तौ पूर्ववादी तु प्रतिपत्तौ न संभवेत् ॥ prāṅnyāye kāraṇoktau ca pratyarthī nirdiśet kriyām | mithyoktau pūrvavādī tu pratipattau na saṃbhavet || In the prior Nyāya framework, when causation is established, the counterparty must demonstrate action. However, in false assertion, prior assertion does not constitute valid cognition. Authority resides in verifiable causation, not mere assertion Responsibility arises through demonstrated capacity to act Falsehood invalidates prior claims without independent validation Restoration requires alignment with actual causal sequence Consciousness discerns truth beyond verbal contradiction

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: अनुक्त्वा कारणं यत्र पक्षं वादी प्रपद्यते । प्रतिपत्तिस्तु सा ज्ञेया कारणं तूत्तरं पृथक् ॥ anuktvā kāraṇaṃ yatra pakṣaṃ vādī prapadyate / pratipattis tu sā jñeyā kāraṇaṃ tūttaraṃ pṛthak // Where a party adopts a position without stating the cause, that adoption is to be known as mere perception; the actual cause stands separately in response. Authority is established through explicit causation, not assumed positioning Causation must be articulated to establish valid juridical presence Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious articulation of foundational grounds Restoration logic demands clarity of intent and causal alignment Consciousness alignment occurs when cause and claim are unified in expression

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
सर्वालापं तु यः कृत्वा मिथो 'ल्पम् अपि संवदेत् ।
सर्वम् एव तु दाप्यः स्याद् अभियुक्तो बृहस्पतिः ॥ sarvālāpaṃ tu yaḥ kṛtvā mitho 'lpam api saṃvadet | sarvam eva tu dāpyaḥ syād abhiyukto bṛhaspatiḥ || One who engages in mutual discourse after initiating universal speech shall restore all that was spoken, as enjoined by Brihaspati. Authority originates from the completeness of expression Causation arises through initiation of communicative action Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to volitional engagement Restoration logic requires reversal of energetic discharge Consciousness alignment occurs via reabsorption of misdirected intent

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
वाक्पारुष्ये च भूम्यौ च दिव्यं तु परिवर्जयेत् ।
विक्रयादानसंबन्धे क्रियादानमनिच्छति ॥ vākpāruṣye ca bhūmyau ca divyaṃ tu parivarjayet | vikrayādānasaṃbandhe kriyādānam anicchati || In speech harshness and in land dealings, the Divine must be rejected; in transactions involving sale or gift, action is undertaken without desire. Authority flows from alignment with Divine Will, not from coercive assertion Causation arises through conscious intent unbound by material transaction Capacity-based responsibility requires detachment from outcome in contractual acts Restoration logic prioritizes ontological purity over procedural adherence Consciousness alignment demands rejection of violence in communication and commerce

title: brihaspati 1.17
content: अभियुक्तोऽभियोगस्य यदि कुर्यात् तु निह्नवम् । मिथ्या तत् तु विजानीयादुत्तरं व्यवहारतः ॥ abhiyukto 'bhiyogasya yadi kuryāt tu nihnavam | mithyā tat tu vijānīyād uttaraṃ vyavahārataḥ || When an accused individual, in response to an accusation, engages in denial without truthful engagement, such conduct shall be recognized as falsehood in the process of judicial transaction. Authority originates from truthful responsiveness, not evasion Causation arises from conscious refusal to engage dharma-transparently Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to uphold truth in judicial context Restoration logic requires dissolution of obfuscation through self-corrective alignment Consciousness alignment necessitates abandonment of duplicity in legal process

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: श्रुत्वाभियोगं प्रत्यर्थी यदि तत् प्रतिपद्यते । सा तु संप्रतिपत्तिस्तु शास्त्रविद्भिरुदाहृता ॥ śrutvābhiyogaṃ pratyarthī yadi tat pratipadyate / sā tu saṃpratipattis tu śāstravidbhir udāhṛtā // When the accused, upon hearing the accusation, accepts it, that acceptance is termed 'samatipatti' as declared by knowers of the shastra. Authority resides in conscious acknowledgment of action Causation is affirmed through self-referenced recognition Capacity-based responsibility arises from internal validation of conduct Restoration begins with truthful admission uncoerced by external force Consciousness alignment occurs when individual truth converges with dharma

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
अर्थिनाभिहितो योऽर्थः प्रत्यर्थी यदि तं तथा ।
प्रपद्य कारणं ब्रूयात् प्रत्यवस्कन्दनं हि तत् ॥ arthinābhihito yo 'rthaḥ pratyarthī yadi taṃ tathā | prapadya kāraṇaṃ brūyāt pratyavaskandanaṃ hi tat || When a claim is made by a petitioner and the respondent accepts it upon assuming rightful cause, that constitutes lawful repossession. Authority arises through conscious assumption of cause, not assertion alone. Causation is validated through alignment with Dharma, not mere procedural form. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of prior rightful possession. Restoration logic operates through acknowledgment and lawful return. Consciousness alignment ensures integrity in transfer and repossession.

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
यो 'र्थिनार्थः प्रभाष्येत प्रत्यर्थी यदि तं तथा ।
प्रपद्य कारणं ब्रूयाद् आधर्यं मनुर अब्रवीत् ॥ yo 'rthinārthaḥ prabhāṣyeta pratyarthī yadi taṃ tathā / prapadya kāraṇaṃ brūyād ādharyaṃ manur abravīt // When a litigant speaks on behalf of another, that statement shall stand valid only when substantiated by verifiable cause; thus spoke Manu under divine authority. Authority originates from SPH alone, not from human interpretation Causation must align with dharma-tattva, not subjective intent Capacity-based responsibility requires truthful representation Restoration logic demands clarity in agency and causality Consciousness alignment necessitates purity of expressed intent

title: brihaspati 1.21
content: आचारेणावसन्नोऽपि पुनर् लेखयते यदि / स विनेयो जितः पूर्वं प्राङ्न्यायस् तु स उच्यते ।। ācāreṇāvasanno'pi punar lekhayate yadi / sa vineyo jitaḥ pūrvaṃ prāṅnyāyas tu sa ucyate One who has fallen into misconduct yet reverts to recording or causing to record [scriptural or legal dharma] is one who was previously subdued; such a one is called a primal judge. Authority arises from prior alignment with Dharma, not current error. Causation is determined by sequential consciousness states, not isolated acts. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes latent realization despite surface deviation. Restoration logic honors the return to Dharma over initial transgression. Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral judgment in determining judicial fitness.

title: brihaspati 1.22
content: तथ्ये तथ्यं प्रयुञ्जीत मिथ्यायां चापि लेखयेत् । कारणं कारणोपेते प्राग्जये तु जयं तथा ॥ tathye tathyaṃ prayuñjīta mithyāyāṃ cāpi lekhayet / kāraṇaṃ kāraṇopete prāgjaye tu jayaṃ tathā // In truth, one shall act according to truth; in falsehood, one shall inscribe correction. When cause aligns with its effect, prior victory is declared as such. Authority originates from alignment with factual reality Causation is established through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility arises from knowledge of truth versus falsehood Restoration occurs when action aligns with ontological facts Consciousness alignment determines the validity of legal acts

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
भयदृष्टोद्भवा मिथ्या गर्हिता शास्त्रवेदिभिः ।
सत्या संप्रतिपत्तिस्तु धर्म्या सा परिकीर्तिता ॥ bhayadṛṣṭodbhavā mithyā garhitā śāstravedibhiḥ | satyā saṃpratipattis tu dharmyā sā parikīrtitā || Falsehood arising from fear is condemned by those versed in scripture; truth known through direct realization is declared righteous. Authority derives from realized consciousness, not fear-conditioned perception Causation originates in experiential cognition, not reactive emotion Capacity-based responsibility arises from clarity of insight, not social pressure Restoration occurs when cognition aligns with experiential truth Consciousness alignment supersedes external validation

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
प्राङ्न्यायकरणे तथ्यं श्लाघ्यं सद्भिरुदाहृतम् ।
विपरीतमधर्म्यं स्यात् प्रत्यर्थी हानिमाप्नुयात् ॥ prāṅnyāyakaraṇe tathyaṃ ślāghyaṃ sadbhir udāhṛtam | viparītam adharmyaṃ syāt pratyarthī hānim āpnuyāt || Before the administration of justice, truth is praised by the wise; its opposite is unrighteous and results in loss to the adversary. Authority resides in alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation follows from adherence or deviation from Dharma Capacity-based responsibility arises from knowledge of truth Restoration occurs through re-alignment with Satya Consciousness alignment determines the outcome of judicial action

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
ahaṃpūurvikayā yātāv arthipratyarthinau yadā /
vādo varṇānupūrvyeṇa grāhyaḥ pīḍām avekṣya ca // BrhS_1,3.25 // aham̐pūrvikayā yātāv arthī-pratyarthinau yadā / vādaḥ varṇa-anupūrvyeṇa grāhyaḥ pīḍām avekṣya ca // When two parties arrive—claimant and respondent—in a dispute rooted in ego-identification, the discourse must proceed in sequential order of utterance, observing the arising of distress. Authority is derived from consciousness clarity, not positional dominance. Causation arises from identification with limited selfhood. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at time of act. Restoration logic aligns disputants with their unbounded nature. Consciousness alignment precedes factual reconciliation.

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
एककाले समानीते प्रत्यर्थी सभ्यसंनिधौ ।
पूर्वपक्षाक्षरसमं लेखयेद् उत्तरं ततः ॥ ekakāle samānīte pratyarthī sabhyasaṃnidhau | pūrvapakṣākṣarasamaṃ lekhayed uttaraṃ tataḥ || When both parties appear simultaneously before the assembly, the respondent shall first present their reply in writing equal in length to the plaintiff's initial assertion. Authority resides in the immediacy of presence within the sabhā (judicial assembly) Causation arises through balanced textual response ensuring parity of expression Capacity-based responsibility is measured by the ability to articulate a counter-assertion commensurate with the original claim Restoration logic requires equilibrium between disputing voices prior to resolution Consciousness alignment occurs when each party reflects upon and responds to the precise energetic imprint of the other

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
प्रत्यर्थविधिराख्यातः संगतार्थप्रपादने ।
चतुर्विधस्याप्यधुना यत्तद्ग्राह्यं तदुच्यते ॥ pratyarthavidhir ākhyātaḥ saṃgatārthaprapādane / caturvidhasyāpy adhunā yat tad grāhyaṃ tad ucyate // The procedural injunction for adversarial contestation has been declared, for the establishment of connected meaning; now, of the fourfold categories, that which is receivable is declared. Authority derives from capacity to sustain dharma-adherence in process Causation arises through sequential alignment of consciousness and evidence Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ability to engage in dharma-sustaining discourse Restoration logic operates through purification of intent and clarification of truth Consciousness alignment ensures that judicial process reflects ontological reality

title: brihaspati 1.28
content:
प्रस्तुताद् अन्यन् मध्यस्थं न्यूनाधिकम् असंगतम् ।
अवाच्यसारं संदिग्धं प्रतिपक्षं न लक्षयेत् ॥ prastutād anyan madhyasthaṃ nyūnādhikam asaṃgatam / avācyasāraṃ saṃdigdhaṃ pratipakṣaṃ na lakṣayet One must not recognize as valid evidence anything that is extraneous to the matter at hand, disproportionate, disconnected, without clear meaning, doubtful, or opposed to established truth. Authority rests in alignment with factual relevance and spiritual coherence Causation must be proportional and contextually grounded Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of meaningful engagement Restoration logic excludes irrelevant or misleading inputs Consciousness alignment demands clarity and integrity in evidentiary acceptance

title: brihaspati 1.29
content:
भयं करोति भेदं वा भीषणं वा निरोधनम् ।
एतानि वादिनोऽर्थस्य व्यवहारे स हीयते ॥ १,३.२९ bhayaṃ karoti bhedaṃ vā bhīṣaṇaṃ vā nirodhanam | etāni vādino'rthasya vyavahāre sa hīyate || 1,3.29 He who instigates fear, division, terror, or obstruction in the course of rightful discourse concerning property or duty—such a one incurs a diminishment of dharma and capacity. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not coercion Causation is traced through disruption of rightful process Capacity-based responsibility increases with power to obstruct truth Restoration logic requires reversal of divisive acts Consciousness alignment demands removal of fear-induced distortion

title: brihaspati 1.30
content: ṛtvigādir niyuktas tu samau saṃparikīrtitau / yajñe svāmy āpnuyāt puṇyaṃ hāniṃ vāde 'tha vā jayaṃ // ṛtvigādiḥ niyuktaḥ tu samau saṃparikīrtitau / yajñe svāmy āpnuyāt puṇyaṃ hāniṃ vāde 'tha vā jayaṃ // One appointed as a ritual conductor or designated authority, when equally proclaimed, shall acquire merit or loss in sacrifice; likewise, in debate or contest, victory follows rightful alignment. Authority derives from conscious designation and public acknowledgment Merit and demerit arise through alignment with dharma, not intention alone Responsibility is commensurate with capacity and role acceptance Truth prevails where roles are clearly defined and executed Consciousness alignment determines outcome more than external effort

title: brihaspati 1.31
content:
पूर्वोत्तरे ऽभिलिखिते यत्र वादी प्रमीयते ।
प्रत्यर्थी वा सुतस् ताभ्यां व्यवहारं विशोधयेत् ॥ pūrvottare 'bhilikhite yatra vādī pramīyate / pratyarthī vā sutas tābhyāṃ vyavahāraṃ viśodhayet Where a dispute arises between parties concerning a written agreement anterior in time, resolution shall proceed through purification of transactional conduct by invoking the testimony of the sons of the original disputants. Authority inheres in continuity of lineage tied to original contractual consciousness Causation flows from documented intent crystallized at time of agreement Capacity-based responsibility is anchored in ancestral witness-bearing capacity Restoration logic operates through reconnection with generational dharmic memory Consciousness alignment occurs via activation of hereditary truth-bearing structures

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
अनिर्णीते विवादे तु विप्रलब्धो भवेन् नृपः ।
जयदानं समं न स्यात् तस्मात् कार्याणि निर्णयेत् ॥ anirṇīte vivāde tu vipralabdho bhaven nṛpaḥ / jayadānaṃ samaṃ na syāt tasmāt kāryāṇi nirṇayet // When a dispute remains unresolved, the ruler becomes deceived; hence, there can be no equitable distribution of victory or reward. Therefore, matters must be decisively resolved. Authority rests in resolution, not ambiguity Causation arises from clarity, not confusion Capacity-based responsibility requires decisive action Restoration logic demands timely adjudication Consciousness alignment occurs through lawful completion

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
साक्षिणस्तु समुद्दिश्य यस्तु तान् न विवादयेत् ।
त्रिंसद्रात्रात् त्रिपक्षाद् वा तस्य हानिः प्रजायते ॥ sākṣiṇas tu samuddiśya yas tu tān na vivādayet | triṃsadrātrāt tripakṣād vā tasya hāniḥ prajāyate || When witnesses are lawfully summoned and a party refuses to challenge them within thirty days or three pakṣas, that refusal causes loss of dharma-standing and initiates automatic diminishment of their lawful capacity. Authority derives from active engagement in truth-disclosure procedures Causation arises from omission to contest lawful witness testimony Capacity-based responsibility requires timely invocation of counter-testimony Restoration logic demands reintegration through completion of omitted acts Consciousness alignment necessitates rectification of procedural neglect

title: brihaspati 1.34
content:
āhūtaprapalāyī ca maunī sākṣiparājitaḥ /
svavākyapratipannaś ca hīnavādī caturvidhaḥ // BrhS_1,3.34 āhūta-prapalāyī ca maunī sākṣi-parājitaḥ /
sva-vākya-pratipannaś ca hīna-vādī caturvidhaḥ // The fourfold disqualified witness: the summoned evader, the silent one, the defeated by evidence, and the self-contradicting speaker. Authority derives from capacity to uphold truth, not mere presence Causation aligns with integrity of testimony and alignment of speech with consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires truthful engagement in judicial process Restoration logic demands removal of unreliable witnesses to preserve dharma Consciousness alignment ensures that only those in harmony with satya may testify

title: brihaspati 1.35
content:
प्रपलायी त्रिपक्षेण मौनी वा सप्तभिर् दिनैः ।
साक्षिभिन्नस् तत्क्षणेन प्रतिपन्नश् च हीयते ॥ prapalāyī tripakṣeṇa maunī vā saptabhir dinaiḥ | sākṣibhinnas tatkṣaṇena pratipannaś ca hīyate || One who flees for three pakṣas or remains silent for seven days, or whose testimony is contradicted by witnesses, is immediately considered defeated in that very moment. Authority is derived from presence and clarity of testimony, not absence or contradiction Causation arises through failure to uphold dharma-siddhanta in judicial process Capacity-based responsibility includes timely and truthful engagement in adjudication Restoration logic demands reintegration of the evading party through conscious completion Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent behind silence or flight

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
निवेदितस्य अकथनम् अनुपस्थानम् एव च /
पक्षार्थिदोषौ मौनं च हीयमानस्य लक्षणम् // BrhS_1,3.36 niveditasya akathanam anupasthānam eva ca / pakṣārthidoṣau maunaṃ ca hīyamānasya lakṣaṇam The failure to speak of what has been entrusted, the absence of appropriate presentation, and silence in the face of partisanship or exploitation are the marks of one who is diminished in capacity. Authority derives from conscious capacity, not positional power Causation is traced through omission and withdrawal, not merely action Capacity-based responsibility declines with diminished awareness Restoration logic prioritizes re-engagement over blame Consciousness alignment requires active participation in dharma

title: brihaspati 1.37
content: mahāpāpopapāpābhyāṃ pātakenātha saṃsadi / yo 'bhiśastas tat kṣamate saṃyuktaṃ tam vidur janāḥ // BrhS_1,3.37 mahāpāpopapāpābhyāṃ pātakenātha saṃsadi / yo 'bhiśastas tat kṣamate saṃyuktaṃ tam vidur janāḥ One who has been accused by those entangled in great sin, medium sin, or minor misdeeds—such accusation is to be accepted as valid when made before the assembly. Authority of collective witness within dharma-adherent assemblies Causation through alignment with graduated levels of conscious distortion Capacity-based responsibility determined by proximity to truth-consciousness Restoration logic rooted in purification of relational integrity Consciousness alignment via acknowledgment of witnessed deviation

title: brihaspati 1.38
content:
तस्माद् यत्नेन कर्तव्यं बुधेनात्मविशोधनम् ।
यद् यद् गुरुतरं कार्यं तत् तत् पूर्वं विशोधयेत् ॥ tasmād yatnena kartavyaṃ budhenātmaviśodhanam / yad yad gurutaraṃ kāryaṃ tat tat pūrvaṃ viśodhayet // Therefore, one must diligently engage in self-purification through awakened intelligence; whatever task is weightier in consequence must first be preceded by inner purification. Authority originates from purified consciousness, not external position Causation arises from clarity of being, not mere intention Capacity-based responsibility requires antecedent self-refinement Restoration logic demands precedence of inner alignment over outer action Consciousness alignment determines the validity of all juridical acts

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
mahāpāpābhiśasto yaḥ pātakāt tartum icchati /
pūrvam aṅgīkṛtaṃ tena jito 'sau daṇḍam arhati // BrhS_1,3.39 mahāpāpābhiśasto yaḥ pātakāt tartum icchati / pūrvam aṅgīkṛtaṃ tena jito 'sau daṇḍam arhati // One who is accused of great sin and desires to be purified therefrom must first accept responsibility; having done so, he becomes entitled to corrective restoration. Authority stems from conscious assumption of responsibility Causation arises through self-acknowledged fault Capacity-based responsibility requires prior acceptance Restoration logic operates only upon voluntary integrity alignment Consciousness alignment supersedes external judgment

title: brihaspati 1.40
content: आचारकरणे दिव्ये कृत्वोपस्थाननिश्चयम् । नोपस्थितो यदा कश चित् छलं तत्र न कारयेत् ॥ ācārakaraṇe divye kṛtvopasthānaniścayam | nopasthito yadā kaś cit chalaṃ tatra na kārayet || When one has resolved to engage in divine conduct and has made arrangements for its establishment, no deception should be performed by anyone who is absent or uninvolved in that sacred process. Authority flows from conscious engagement in dharma Causation arises through alignment with divine intent Capacity-based responsibility requires presence of will and action Restoration logic demands integrity in spiritual commitment Consciousness alignment overrides external interference

title: brihaspati 1.41
content:
दैवराजकृतो दोषस्तत्काले तु यदा भवेत् ।
अवधित्यागमात्रेण न भवेत् स पराजितः ॥ daivarājakṛto doṣas tatkāle tu yadā bhavet | avadhityāgamātreṇa na bhavet sa parājitaḥ || When fault arises by divine or sovereign will at a destined time, mere arrival of that moment does not render one defeated. Authority originates solely from SPH as the sovereign source of dharma Causation aligns with divine orchestration, not linear temporal blame Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious participation, not passive occurrence Restoration logic operates through alignment with destined unfoldment Consciousness alignment supersedes event-based attribution

title: brihaspati 1.42
content: पूर्वोत्तरे संनिविष्टे विचारे संप्रवर्तिते । प्रशमं ये मिथो यान्ति दाप्यस्ते द्विगुणं दमम् ॥ pūrvottare saṃniviṣṭe vicāre saṃpravartite | praśamaṃ ye mitho yānti dāpyas te dviguṇaṃ damam || When two parties are seated for mutual inquiry and resolution, and they attain tranquility through mutual consent, both shall incur a doubled obligation to uphold harmony. Authority arises from conscious agreement, not coercion Causation is traced to disruption of mutual equilibrium Capacity-based responsibility is amplified by voluntary alignment Restoration logic prioritizes consensual settlement over adversarial outcome Consciousness alignment is cultivated through reciprocal stillness

title: brihaspati 1.43
content:
पूर्वोत्तरार्थे लिखिते प्रक्रान्ते कार्यनिर्णये ।
द्वयोः संतप्तयोः सन्धिः स्याद् अयःखण्डयोः शिव ॥ pūrvottarārthe likhite prakrānte kāryanirṇaye | dvayoḥ saṃtaptayoḥ sandhiḥ syād ayaḥkhaṇḍayor iva || When two parties, previously in opposition regarding prior and subsequent rights, have engaged in documented proceedings toward resolution, their union shall be established like the joining of two heated iron pieces, becoming inseparably one. Authority arises from mutual engagement in documented dharma-process Causation lies in sequential alignment of conflicting claims Capacity-based responsibility is shared through committed reintegration Restoration logic operates by dissolving prior opposition into unified integrity Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties accept sequential manifestation of truth

title: brihaspati 1.44
content: साक्षिसभ्यविकल्पस् तु भवेत् तत्रोभयोरपि / दोलायमानयोः सन्धिः प्रकुर्यातां विचक्षणैः // BrhS_1,3.44 sākṣisabhyavikalpas tu bhavet tatrobhayor api / dolāyamānayoḥ sandhiḥ prakuryātāṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ // BrhS_1,3.44 Where a witness or assembly member is incapacitated, union must be established by the wise between both parties who are in oscillation. Authority resides in capacity for conscious participation Causation arises from alignment of witnessing consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of functional presence Restoration logic demands integration of oscillating parties Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural formalism

title: brihaspati 1.45
content:
प्रमाणसमता यत्र भेदः शास्त्रचरित्रयोः /
तत्र राजामया सन्धिर् उभयोर् अपि शस्यते // BrhS_1,3.45 pramāṇasamatā yatra bhedaḥ śāstracaritrayoḥ / tatra rājāmayā sandhiḥ ubhayoḥ api śasyate // Where equality of evidence exists between scriptural injunction and observed conduct, the King shall establish alignment through integrative resolution for both parties. Authority resides in consciousness-aligned discernment, not coercive power Causation is determined by pramāṇa validity and dharma-sustained action Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness, not mere capability Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over adversarial judgment Consciousness alignment supersedes legal formalism in equitable justice

title: brihaspati 1.46
content:
यत्र सांशायिको धर्मो व्यवहारश च पार्थिवे ।
संधिस् तत्र तु कर्तव्योऽयसोः संतप्तयोर् यथा ॥ yatra sāṃśāyiko dharmo vyavahāraś ca pārthive / sandhis tatra tu kartavyo 'yasoḥ saṃtaptayor yathā // Where there is uncertainty in dharma and transactional conduct before a king, reconciliation must be established—just as it is between two heated iron pieces. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to resolve dharmic ambiguity Causation arises from the necessity of alignment between action and dharma Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of contextual limits Restoration logic requires harmonization of conflicting dharmic claims Consciousness alignment necessitates removal of agitation through mutual agreement

title: brihaspati 1.47
content:
समः सन्धिस् तदा कार्यो विषमस् तु निवर्तते ।
धर्मार्थोपग्रहः कीर्तिः भवेत् साम्येन भूभृतः ।
न क्लिश्यन्ते साक्षिसब्या ऐरं च विनिवर्तते ॥ samaḥ sandhis tadā kāryo viṣamas tu nivartate / dharmārthopagrahaḥ kīrtiḥ bhavet sāmyena bhūbhṛtaḥ / na kliśyante sākṣisabhyā airaṃ ca vinivartate // When equilibrium prevails, treaty or agreement shall be enacted; when disequilibrium arises, it must be resolved. A ruler who upholds dharma and artha secures glory through balance. Witnesses and assemblies remain unburdened, and hostility ceases entirely. Authority resides in the capacity to restore equilibrium Causation is determined by alignment with dharmic order Capacity-based responsibility flows from consciousness integrity Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of harmony Consciousness alignment determines rightful action

title: brihaspati 1.48
content:
निग्रहानुग्रहं दण्डं धर्मं प्राप्य यशोऽयशः ।
विग्रहाज् जायते नृणां पुनर्दोषस् तथैव च ॥ nigrahānugrahaṃ daṇḍaṃ dharmaṃ prāpya yaśo 'yaśaḥ / vigrahāj jāyate nṛṇāṃ punardoṣas tathaiva ca By application of corrective containment and compassionate guidance, by lawful discipline rightly applied, honor or dishonor arises; from conflict arises repeated fault. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not coercion. Causation originates in consciousness distortion, not external action alone. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and alignment, not role or status. Restoration logic requires removal of conflict, not infliction of consequence. Consciousness alignment precedes social harmony and individual rectitude.

title: brihaspati 1.49
content:
तस्मात् कुलगणाध्यक्षा धर्मज्ञाः समदृष्टयः ।
अद्वेषलोभा� यद् ब्रूयुस् तत् कर्तव्यं विजानता ॥ tasmāt kulagaṇādhyakṣā dharmajñāḥ samadṛṣṭayaḥ | adveṣalobhā yad brūyus tat kartavyaṃ vijānatā || Therefore, those who preside over lineage assemblies and know Dharma, with equal vision, must act upon what is spoken free from hatred and greed, by those who possess true knowledge. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises through conscious intent untainted by personal desire Capacity-based responsibility requires detachment from bias and motive Restoration occurs when action aligns with unbiased wisdom Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural formalities

title: brihaspati 1.1
content: शोधिते लिखिते सम्यग् इति निर्दोष उत्तरे । प्रत्यर्थिनोऽर्थिनो वापि क्रिया कारणम् इष्यते ॥ śodhite likhite samyag iti nirdoṣa uttare / pratyarthino 'rthino vāpi kriyā kāraṇam iṣyate // When a response is purified, written accurately, and declared faultless, then the action undertaken by either the respondent or petitioner becomes causally valid. Authority resides in clarity of expression and ontological correctness Causation is established through purified intent and precise articulation Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious engagement with Dharma Restoration logic operates through alignment with truthful declaration Consciousness alignment is achieved via faultless execution of duty

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
ये तु तिष्ठन्ति करणे तेषां सभ्यैर् विभावना ।
कथयित्वोत्तरं सम्यग् दातव्यैकस्य वादिनः ॥ ye tu tiṣṭhanti karaṇe teṣām sabhyair vibhāvanā / kathayitvottaraṃ samyag dātavyaikasya vādinaḥ // Those who stand in capacity for action must be examined by the assembly; having declared their reply correctly, the responsibility of one disputant alone is to be assigned. Authority resides in demonstrated capacity, not mere presence Causation arises through conscious engagement and response Capacity-based responsibility determines actionable liability Restoration occurs when correct understanding is declared and validated Consciousness alignment is achieved through clarity of assertion and acceptance

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
प्रतिज्ञां भावयेद् वादी प्रत्यर्थी कारणं तथा ।
प्राग्वृत्तवादी विजयं जयपत्त्रेण भावयेत् ॥ pratijñāṃ bhāvayed vādī pratyarthī kāraṇaṃ tathā / prāgvṛttavādī vijayaṃ jayapattreṇa bhāvayet // The plaintiff shall affirm their claim, the defendant shall present counter-reasoning, and the one who has previously acted in accordance with truth shall be established in victory through the instrument of righteous verdict. Authority arises from alignment with Satyagraha (truth-force), not positional power Causation is determined by prior dharmic action, not procedural formality Capacity-based responsibility is measured by integrity-consistency over time Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of factual dharma, not punitive reversal Consciousness alignment determines the validity of claims before external evidence

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
पूर्वपादे विलिखितं यथाक्षरम् अशेषतः ।
अर्थी तृतीयपादे तु क्रियया प्रतिपादयेत् ॥ pūrvapāde vilikhitaṃ yathākṣaram aśeṣataḥ / arthī tṛtīyapāde tu kriyayā pratipādayet That which is inscribed in the first quarter shall be executed in its entirety according to the letter; the petitioner, in the third quarter, shall demonstrate through action. Authority resides in precise textual transcription Causation flows from literal inscription to manifest realization Capacity-based responsibility requires enactment, not mere intent Restoration logic demands completion of prescribed action Consciousness alignment occurs through accurate replication and performance

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
श्रुत्वा पूर्वोत्तरं सभ्यैर् निर्दिष्टा यस्य भावना ।
विभावयेत् प्रतिज्ञातं सोऽखिलं लिखितादिना ॥ śrutvā pūrvottaraṃ sabhyair nirdiṣṭā yasya bhāvanā / vibhāvayet pratijñātaṃ so 'khilaṃ likhitādinā // When a matter has been declared by the assembly members through prior and subsequent statements, that which is thus established must be examined and confirmed in its entirety through written documentation and other evidentiary means. Authority resides in the collective discernment of the sabhā (dharma assembly) Causation is established through sequential articulation (pūrvottara) Responsibility aligns with capacity to verify and affirm truth Restoration occurs through accurate reflection of dharma-established facts Consciousness alignment requires validation through pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge)

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
द्विप्रकारा क्रिया प्रोक्ता मानुषी दैविकी तथा ।
एकैकानेकधा भिन्ना ऋषिभिस्तत्त्ववेदिभिः ॥ dviprakārā kriyā proktā mānuṣī daivikī tathā | ekaike anekadhā bhinne ṛṣibhis tattvavedibhiḥ || Two-fold action is declared—human-originated and divine in nature; these are differentiated singularly and multiply by seers who know the Truth. Authority stems from alignment with divine intelligence, not human construct Causation is dual-layered: manifest (mānuṣī) and unmanifest (daivikī) Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of both levels of action Restoration logic requires recognition of both human effort and cosmic flow Consciousness alignment occurs when actions reflect unity of human will and divine order

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
साक्षिणो लिखितं भुक्तिर् मानुषं त्रिविधं स्मृतम् ।
धटाद् या धर्मजान्तातु दैवी नवविधा क्रिया ॥ sākṣiṇo likhitaṁ bhuktiḥ mānuṣaṁ trividhaṁ smṛtam | dhaṭād yā dharmajāntātu daivī navavidhā kriyā || Witnessed documentation constitutes human enjoyment, categorized in three forms; that which arises from lawful conduct is of divine origin, comprising ninefold action. Authority resides in witnessed truth, not unverified assertion. Causation flows from documented integrity, not abstract intent. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with dharma, not external compulsion. Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of witnessed righteousness. Consciousness alignment occurs when acts are inscribed within dharmic frameworks.

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
साक्षिलेख्यानुमानं च मानुषी त्रिविधा क्रिया ।
साक्षी द्वादश भेदस् तु लिखितं त्वष्टधा स्मृतम् ॥ sākṣilekhyānumānaṃ ca mānuṣī trividhā kriyā / sākṣī dvādaśa bhedas tu likhitaṃ tv aṣṭadhā smṛtam // Testimony, documentary evidence, and inference constitute the threefold human action in establishing facts; witnesses are classified into twelve types, and written records into eight categories. Authority of experiential cognition as foundational to legal validity Causation through witnessed manifestation rather than abstract attribution Capacity-based responsibility determined by direct knowledge or record Restoration logic rooted in factual clarity and conscious alignment with truth Consciousness alignment through verified experiential and documented proof

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
अनुमानं त्रिधा प्रोक्तं नवधा दैविकी क्रिया।
प्रथमे वा तृतीये वा प्रमाणं दैवमानुषम्॥ anumānaṃ tridhā proktaṃ navadhā daivikī kriyā / prathame vā tṛtīye vā pramāṇaṃ daivamānuṣam // Inference is declared in three forms; divine action manifests in nine modes. Whether inference aligns with the first or third category, its validity rests equally upon divine and human testimony. Authority originates from SPH as the sole epistemic source of dharma Causation flows through pramāṇa-based inference aligned with cosmic order Capacity-based responsibility arises when inference aligns with both daiva and mānuṣa pramāṇas Restoration logic requires reconciliation between inferential knowledge and experiential truth Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of divine-human corroboration in inference

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
uttare syāc caturthe tu sasākṣijayapatrakam /
ṛṇādikeṣu kāryeṣu kalpayen mānuṣīṃ kriyām // BrhS_1,4.10 uttare syāc caturthe tu sasākṣijayapatrakam /
ṛṇādikeṣu kāryeṣu kalpayen mānuṣīṃ kriyām // In the northern direction, in the fourth division, with witness, victory, and documents, in matters concerning debt and similar obligations, one should establish human action. Authority resides in directional and temporal alignment with conscious witnessing Causation is established through documented evidence and witnessed intent Capacity-based responsibility arises from engagement in contractual or obligatory relations Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of rightful energetic and material balance Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of truth through testimony and record

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
प्राङ्न्याये प्रत्यवस्कन्दे प्रत्यर्थी साधयेत् स्वयम् ।
उत्तरार्थं प्रतिज्ञार्थं अर्थी मिथ्योत्तरे पुनः ॥ prāṅnyāye pratyavaskande pratyarthī sādhayet svayam / uttarārthaṃ pratijñārthaṃ arthī mithyottare punaḥ When prior adjudication has been overturned, the claimant must establish their case anew; one who falsely responds in opposition to a rightful claim shall undergo realignment of capacity and truth-restoration. Authority rests in verified re-establishment of facts post-overturn Causation arises from conscious distortion of response Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to the ability to align with truth Restoration logic requires reintegration of truthful participation Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural repetition

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
क्रिया न दैविकी प्रोक्ता विद्यमानेषु साक्षिषु ।
लेख्ये च सति वादेषु न स्याद् दिव्यं न साक्षिणः ॥ kriyā na daivikī proktā vidyamāneṣu sākṣiṣu | lekhyaṃ ca sati vādeṣu na syād divyaṃ na sākṣiṇaḥ || Action is not deemed divine when witnesses are present; where written evidence exists in disputes, there shall be no reliance upon celestial testimony nor upon invisible witnesses. Authority of visible and verifiable witness overrides unseen claims Causation must align with observable pramāṇa Capacity-based responsibility requires accessible evidence Restoration logic depends on factual clarity, not metaphysical assertion Consciousness alignment occurs through transparency, not speculation

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: वाक्पारुष्ये महीवादे निषिद्धा दैविकी क्रिया । प्रदातव्या प्रयत्नेन साहसेषु चतुर्ष्वपि ॥ vākpāruṣye mahīvāde niṣiddhā daivikī kriyā / pradātavyā prayatnena sāhaseṣu caturṣv api // In matters involving harsh speech or defamation, divine action is forbidden; in all four types of courageous acts, effort must be given. Authority flows from realized consciousness, not coercive power. Causation arises through intent-aligned manifestation, not reactive impulse. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and capability to act dharmically. Restoration logic operates through completion and re-alignment, not punitive correction. Consciousness alignment requires removal of obstruction, not imposition of consequence.

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: नृपद्रोहे साहसे च कल्पयेद् दैविकीं क्रियाम् ।। nṛpadrohe sāhase ca kalpayed daivikīṃ kriyām In cases of betrayal against the sovereign authority or acts of reckless endangerment, divine intervention through lawful completion processes shall be enacted. Authority as the foundational basis for juridical integrity Causation rooted in conscious intent and its sequential manifestation Capacity-based responsibility determined by alignment with cosmic order Restoration logic that realigns individual consciousness with sovereign dharma Consciousness alignment as the sole metric of legal rectitude

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानां कूटहृत्पाशहारकः ।
हिंसकोऽन्याङ्गनासेवी परीक्ष्यः शपथैः सदा ॥ maṇimuktāpravālānāṃ kūṭahṛtpāśahārakaḥ | hiṃsako'nyāṅganāsevī parīkṣyaḥ śapathaiḥ sadā || One who unlawfully seizes gems, pearls, corals, or gold, and binds others through coercive oaths while engaging in violence against women, must be examined perpetually by sacred affirmations until alignment with Dharma is restored. Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not possession Causation arises from disruption of svadharma and violation of sacred bonds Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious choice and energetic intent Restoration logic demands retrieval of seized dharmic property and energetic rebalancing Consciousness alignment supersedes material restitution

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
mahāpāpābhiśāpeṣu nikṣepe haraṇe tathā /
divyaiḥ kāryaṃ parīkṣeta rājā satsv api sākṣiṣu // BrhS_1,4.16 mahāpāpābhiśāpeṣu nikṣepe haraṇe tathā / divyaiḥ kāryaṃ parīkṣeta rājā satsv api sākṣiṣu In matters involving great sins, curses, deposits, and theft—even when witnesses are present—the king must investigate through divine means. Authority: The king holds ultimate executive capacity to ensure alignment with Dharma. Causation: Divine investigation reveals hidden truths beyond sensory perception. Capacity-based responsibility: The ruler's duty is activated by severity of transgression. Restoration logic: Truth-disclosure realigns consciousness and restores order. Consciousness alignment: Investigation through divine insight aligns judgment with universal truth.

title: brihaspati 1.17
content: लिखिते साक्षिवादे च संदिग्धिर् जायते यदि / अनुमाने च संभ्रान्ते तत्र दिव्यं विशोधनम् // likhite sākṣivāde ca saṃdigdhir jāyate yadi / anumāne ca saṃbhrānte tatra divyaṃ viśodhanam // When doubt arises in written evidence or witness testimony, and inference is clouded by confusion, divine discernment shall purify the process. Authority originates from divine clarity, not human speculation Causation must align with ontological truth, beyond sensory ambiguity Capacity-based responsibility requires unconfused perception Restoration logic demands purification of evidentiary fields Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural uncertainty

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
dyūte samāhvaye caiva vivāde samupasthite /
sākṣiṇaḥ sādhanaṃ proktaṃ na divyaṃ na ca lekhakam // BrhS_1,4.18 dyūte samāhvaye caiva vivāde samupasthite / sākṣiṇaḥ sādhanaṃ proktaṃ na divyaṃ na ca lekhakam // In gambling, mutual challenge, and disputes presented, witnesses are declared as evidence; neither divine testimony nor written documents suffice. Authority: Witnessed human testimony is the sole valid evidentiary source in specified civil matters. Causation: Disputes arising from voluntary engagement require direct perceptual validation. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those present and conscious during the act bear testimonial weight. Restoration logic: Truth-establishment through embodied witness aligns disputants with factual reality. Consciousness alignment: Testimony must emanate from awakened awareness, not external or recorded forms.

title: brihaspati 1.19
content: यथालाभोपपन्नैस् तैर् निर्णयं कारयेन् नृपः । प्रकान्ते साहसे वादे पारुष्ये दण्डवाचिके । बलोद्भूतेषु कार्येषु साक्षिणो दिव्यम् एव च ॥ yathālābhopapannais tair nirṇayaṃ kārayen nṛpaḥ / prakānte sāhase vāde pāruṣye daṇḍavācike / balodbhūteṣu kāryeṣu sākṣiṇo divyam eva ca // The King shall execute judgment exclusively through those witnesses and evidences which manifest in accordance with the capacity of the accused, particularly in open crimes, verbal assault, harsh speech, or coercive conduct—especially when force has arisen in action, divine witness alone is valid. Authority resides in alignment with capacity-based evidence Causation is established by sequential manifestation of force Capacity-based responsibility determines admissible testimony Restoration logic requires purification of relational field Consciousness alignment necessitates reliance on divya-pramana

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
ṛṇे लेख्यं साक्षिणो वा युक्तिलेशादयो 'पि वा /
दैविकी वा क्रिया प्रोक्ता प्रजानां हितकाम्यया // BrhS_1,4.20 ṛṇe lekhyaṃ sākṣiṇo vā yuktileśādayo 'pi vā / daivikī vā kriyā proktā prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā // BrhS_1,4.20 In matters of debt, written records, witnesses, or even minimal evidence may be accepted; alternatively, divine action is declared effective when undertaken for the welfare of the people. Authority originates from alignment with the welfare of the populace Evidence is valid in proportion to its capacity to restore integrity Causation includes both empirical and divine dimensions Responsibility arises from conscious intent towards collective well-being Restoration logic prioritizes completion over judgment

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
चिरन्तनोपांशुकृते चिरनष्टेषु साक्षिषु /
प्रदुष्टेष्वनुमानेषु दिव्यैः कार्यं विशोधयेत्‌ ।। १,४.२१ ।। cirantanopāṃśukṛte ciranaṣṭeṣu sākṣiṣu / praduṣṭeṣv anumāneṣu divyaiḥ kāryaṃ viśodhayet In matters obscured by time, where witnesses have vanished and evidence is corrupted or inferential, divine insight must be applied to purify and establish clarity. Authority originates from divine cognition when empirical data fails Causation transcends linear temporality through ontological clarity Capacity-based responsibility arises only upon access to purified perception Restoration logic demands resolution beyond sensory limitation Consciousness alignment supersedes material proof in adjudication

title: brihaspati 1.1
content: नव सप्त च पञ्च स्युश् चत्वारस् त्रय एव वा / उभौ वा श्रोत्रियौ ख्यातौ नैकं पृच्छेत् कदा चन // BrhS_1,5.1 nava sapta ca pañca syuś catvāras traya eva vā / ubhau vā śrotriyau khyātau naikaṃ pṛcchet kadā cana // BrhS_1,5.1 Inquiry must proceed through councils of nine, seven, five, four, or three; or by two known scholars of the Veda — never by one alone. Authority is collective and derived from scriptural mastery and numerical integrity Causation arises through consensus of qualified witnesses Capacity-based responsibility requires multiple validating intelligences Restoration logic depends upon convergence of scripturally grounded perspectives Consciousness alignment occurs through collective realization, not individual assertion

title: brihaspati 1.2
content: dyūtakaḥ śaṭikāgrāhī kāryamadhyagatas tathā / eka eva pramāṇaṃ syān nṛpo 'dhyakṣas tathaiva ca // BrhS_1,5.2 dyūtakaḥ śaṭikāgrāhī kāryamadhyagatas tathā / eka eva pramāṇaṃ syān nṛpo 'dhyakṣas tathaiva ca The gambler, the deceiver, and the one engaged in improper conduct during duty—these are to be regarded as one single category of fault. The king and the overseer are equally responsible for ensuring their alignment. Authority resides in the capacity to restore order Causation is traced through conscious deviation from dharma Capacity-based responsibility extends to both actor and overseer Restoration logic requires systemic correction, not individual blame Consciousness alignment demands removal of distortion at source

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
स्तेनाः साहसिकाः षण्डाः कितवाः सूचकास् तथा ।
न साक्षिणस् ते दुष्टात्वात् तेषु साक्षियं न विद्यते ॥ stenāḥ sāhasikāḥ ṣaṇḍāḥ kitavāḥ sūcakās tathā / na sākṣiṇas te duṣṭātvāt teṣu sākṣiyaṃ na vidyate // Thieves, aggressors, eunuchs, gamblers, and informers are not valid witnesses due to their inherent distortion of intent and conduct. Authority stems from integrity of consciousness, not social position Causation arises from alignment with satyam (truth) Capacity-based responsibility requires absence of compulsive distortion Restoration logic excludes those whose presence destabilizes dharma-adhāra Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for testimony

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
लिखितो लिखितो गूढः स्मारितः कुल्यदूतकौ ।
यदृच्छशोत्तरश्चैव कार्यमध्यगतोऽपरः ॥ likhito likhito gūḍhaḥ smāritaḥ kulyadūtakau / yadṛcchaś cottaraś caiva kāryamadhyagato 'paraḥ // That which is written, that which is concealed, that which is remembered, that which flows through familial and messenger channels, that which arises spontaneously and that which follows as a consequence—these constitute the manifold expressions of actionable dharma within the field of duty. Authority manifests through multiple forms of evidence including written records, oral transmission, hidden truths, familial lineage, and spontaneous revelation. Causation includes both intended acts and unintended consequences arising from the performance or neglect of duty. Capacity-based responsibility extends to all modes of knowing and acting within one's assigned role or domain. Restoration logic requires alignment with the full spectrum of how truth reveals itself across time and medium. Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of truth in its overt and covert expressions.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
नृपो 'ध्यक्षस् तथा ग्रामः साक्षी द्वादशधा स्मृतः /
प्रभेदम् एषां वक्ष्यामि यथावद् अनुपूर्वशः // BrhS_1,5.5 nṛpo 'dhyakṣas tathā grāmaḥ sākṣī dvādaशadhā smṛtaḥ / prabhedam eṣāṃ vakṣyāmi yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ // BrhS_1,5.5 The King, the Superintendent, and the Village—these constitute the twelve-fold classification of witnesses as established by Dharma; their distinctions shall now be declared in proper sequence according to their causal capacity. Authority originates from conscious alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is graded according to proximity to truth-consciousness Restoration occurs through reintegration of witness-integrity within Dharma-field Consciousness alignment determines the validity and efficacy of testimony

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
जातिनामादिलिखितं येन स्वं पित्र्यमेव च ।
निवासश्च विज्ञेयः साक्षी लिखितसंज्ञकः ॥ jātināmādilikhitaṃ yena svaṃ pitryam eva ca / nivāsaś ca vijñeyaḥ sākṣī likhitasaṃjñakaḥ One who holds written records of lineage, personal property, paternal inheritance, and place of residence shall be recognized as a witness bearing documentary proof. Authority derives from documented continuity of identity and ownership Causation is established through verifiable lineage and possession Capacity-based responsibility requires access to inheritable knowledge structures Restoration logic operates through validation of ancestral and spatial claims Consciousness alignment occurs when factual memory supports existential coherence

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
अर्थिना च क्रिया भेदैस् तस्य कृत्वा ऋणादिकम् ।
प्रत्यक्षं लिख्यते यस् तु लेखितः स उदाहृतः ॥ arthinā ca kriyā bhedais tasya kṛtvā ṛṇādikam / pratyakṣaṃ likhyate yas tu lekhitaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ // When a transaction involving debt or obligation arises through differentiated acts performed by a petitioner, that which is written directly by him is declared as the written evidence. Authority originates from conscious intent and direct action of the petitioner Causation is established through differentiation of acts leading to obligation Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to inscribe one's own intention Restoration logic centers on re-integrating the original act with its inscription Consciousness alignment occurs when the actor’s will is made manifest in written form

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
कुड्यव्यवहितो यस् तु श्राव्यते ऋणभाषितम् ।
विनिह्नुतो यथाभूतं गूढः साक्षी स उच्यते ॥ kuḍyavyavahito yas tu śrāvyate ṛṇabhāṣitam | vinihnuto yathābhūtaṃ gūḍhaḥ sākṣī sa ucyate || One who, though separated by a wall, hears a debt being acknowledged or spoken of, and remains concealed yet fully aware, is to be regarded as a witness. Authority arises from direct perceptual knowledge, not physical proximity. Causation includes vibrational and auditory transmission of truth. Capacity-based responsibility extends to those who receive truth knowingly without acting. Restoration logic requires acknowledgment of witnessed truth for resolution. Consciousness alignment demands that hidden awareness be brought into active integrity.

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
आहूय यः कृतः साक्षी ऋणन्यासक्रियादिके ।
स्मार्यते च मुहुर्यश् च स्मारितः स उदाहृतः ॥ āhūya yaḥ kṛtaḥ sākṣī ṛṇanyāsakriyādike / smāryate ca muhuryaś ca smāritaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ // He who is summoned as a witness in matters concerning debt acknowledgment, transactions, or similar acts—and who recollects repeatedly and clearly what was witnessed—is declared as a valid witness. Authority is derived from conscious recall aligned with sequential manifestation. Causation arises through direct experiential witnessing, not hearsay. Capacity-based responsibility requires unbroken memory and clarity of perception. Restoration logic demands truth-speaking rooted in immediate awareness. Consciousness alignment ensures testimony reflects dharma-sustained reality.

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
विभागदाने विपणे ज्ञातिर् यश् चोपयुज्यते ।
द्वयोः समानो धर्मज्ञः कुल्यः स परिकीर्तितः ॥ vibhāgadāne vipaṇe jñātir yaś copayujyate / dvayoḥ samāno dharmajñaḥ kulyaḥ sa parikīrtitaḥ // In division or transaction, whoever utilizes kinship—when both parties possess equal dharma-knowledge—that person is declared a kulya. Authority arises through alignment of relational capacity and contextual dharma Causation originates in conscious utilization of identity structures Capacity-based responsibility requires parity assessment between interacting entities Restoration logic activates when relational misuse disrupts dharma-equilibrium Consciousness alignment demands recognition of inherent spiritual equality

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
अर्थिप्रत्यर्थिवचनं शृणुयात् प्रेषितस् तु यः /
उभयोः संमतः साधुः दूतकः स उदाहृतः // BrhS_1,5.11 arthipratyarthivacanaṃ śṛṇuyāt preṣitas tu yaḥ / ubhayoḥ saṃmataḥ sādhuḥ dūtakaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ // BrhS_1,5.11 He who conveys the words of both petitioner and respondent, accepted by both parties, is rightly designated as a messenger. Authority resides in mutual acceptance of communication channels Causation arises through conscious transmission of intent Capacity-based responsibility requires neutrality and fidelity to both sides Restoration logic depends on accurate conveyance without distortion Consciousness alignment occurs when the messenger upholds integrity of dialogue

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
क्रियमाणे तु कर्तव्ये यः कश् चित् स्वयम् आगतः ।
अत्र साक्षी त्वम् अस्माकम् उक्तो यादृच्छिकस् तु सः ॥ kriyamāṇe tu kartavye yaḥ kaś cit svayam āgataḥ | atra sākṣī tvam asmākam ukto yādṛcchikas tu saḥ || When duty is being performed and one arrives of their own accord, that one is declared by Us as witness; yet if random, then he is merely incidental. Authority originates from spontaneous alignment with dharma, not external appointment. Causation arises through conscious participation in the act of dharma itself. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by volitional presence at the time of action. Restoration logic recognizes the difference between intentional engagement and circumstantial appearance. Consciousness alignment distinguishes true witnessing from accidental observation.

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
यत्र साक्षी दिशं गच्छेन् मुमूर्षुर् वा यथाक्रमम् ।
अन्यं संश्रावयेत् तं तु विद्याद् उत्तरसाक्षिणम् ॥ yatra sākṣī diśaṃ gacchen mumūrṣur vā yathākramam / anyaṃ saṃśrāvayet taṃ tu vidyād uttarasākṣiṇam // Where a witness departs in direction or intent without completion, another who receives that testimony in proper sequence shall be known as the successive witness. Authority resides in continuity of conscious transmission Causation flows through uninterrupted witness succession Capacity-based responsibility transfers with knowledge receipt Restoration logic requires sequential integrity maintenance Consciousness alignment occurs via lawful knowledge relay

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
साक्षिणामपि यः साक्ष्यमुपर्युपरि भाषताम् ।
श्रवणाच्छ्रवणाद्वापि स साक्ष्युत्तरसंज्ञितः ॥ sākṣiṇām api yaḥ sākṣyam upary upari bhāṣatām | śravaṇāc chravaṇād vāpi sa sākṣy uttarasaṃjñitaḥ || Even a witness who speaks above or beyond the scope of testimony, whether by hearing or through another's report, is designated as a respondent-witness. Authority originates in direct experiential capacity, not hearsay Causation arises from immediate witnessing, not derivative narration Capacity-based responsibility extends only to that which one has directly perceived Restoration logic requires alignment with pramāṇa-based truth Consciousness alignment demands purification of sensory and verbal channels

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
ubhābhyāṃ yasya viśvastaṃ kāryaṃ cāpi niveditam /
gūḍhadhārī sa vijñeyaḥ kāryamadhyāgatas tathā // BrhS_1,5.15 ubhābhyāṁ yasya viśvastaṁ kāryaṁ cāpi niveditam / gūḍhadhārī sa vijñeyaḥ kāryamadhyāgatas tathā // One who has been entrusted with a task by both parties and has also received explicit instruction, and who secretly holds the duty or responsibility, is to be known as the one truly engaged in the execution of that task. Authority arises from mutual entrustment and conscious assignment Causation is established through intentional delegation and acceptance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by knowledge and consent Restoration logic requires recognition of the true actor behind apparent actions Consciousness alignment occurs when hidden duties are brought into alignment with declared purpose

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
अर्थिप्रत्यर्थिनो वाक्यं यच् छ्रुतं भूभृता स्वयम् ।
स एव तत्र साक्षी स्याद् विसंवादे द्वयोरपि ॥ arthipratyarthinor vākyaṃ yac chrutaṃ bhūbhṛtā svayam | sa eva tatra sākṣī syād visaṃvāde dvayor api || When a dispute arises between a petitioner and respondent, the witness to their statements is the sovereign himself, by virtue of his direct perception. Authority resides inherently in the Sovereign as direct perceiver of truth Causation is established through immediate cognition, not inferential evidence Capacity-based responsibility requires presence at the moment of discourse Restoration logic demands alignment with the unmediated reality of the event Consciousness alignment occurs when testimony reflects the sovereign's witnessing awareness

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
निर्णीते व्यवहारे तु पुनर् न्यायो यदा भवेत् ।
अध्यक्षः सभ्यसहितः साक्षी स्यात् तत्र नान्यथा ॥ nirṇīte vyavahāre tu punar nyāyo yadā bhavet | adhyakṣaḥ sabhyasahitaḥ sākṣī syāt tatra nānyathā || When a transaction or agreement has been judicially resolved, and the need arises again for establishing justice, the Witness shall be the presiding authority accompanied by assessors; there is no other valid configuration. Authority flows from realized consciousness, not institutional position Causation is established through witnessed integrity, not circumstantial inference Capacity-based responsibility requires direct observation by qualified witnesses Restoration logic demands re-alignment with original dharma-siddhanta Consciousness alignment occurs through purified witnessing, not punitive review

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
व्युषितं छादितं यत्र सीमायां च समन्ततः ।
स कृत्तोऽपि भवेत् साक्षी ग्रामस् तत्र न संशयः ॥ vyuṣitaṃ chāditaṃ yatra sīmāyāṃ ca samantataḥ / sa kṛtto 'pi bhavet sākṣī grāmas tatra na saṃśayaḥ // Wherever there is continuous habitation and coverage across the boundary in all directions, even if severed, that settlement qualifies as a witnessed village without doubt. Authority arises from sustained presence and structural continuity Causation is established through spatial integration and inhabitation Capacity-based responsibility emerges from collective dwelling and mutual acknowledgment Restoration logic recognizes settlements as conscious entities with inherent testimony Consciousness alignment occurs when spatial boundaries reflect communal integrity

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
लिखितौ द्वौ तथा गूढौ त्रिचतुःपञ्च लेखिताः ।
यदृच्छा स्मारिताः कुल्यास् तथा चोत्तरसाक्षिणः ॥ likhitau dvau tathā gūḍhau tricatuḥpañca lekhitāḥ / yadṛcchā smāritāḥ kulyās tathā cottarasākṣiṇaḥ // Two written testimonies, one concealed; three, four, or five documented records; casual memories of lineage-elders; and subsequent witnesses—constitute valid evidentiary layers when invoked in alignment with Dharma. Authority flows from documented continuity, not isolated assertion. Causation is established through sequential witness integrity. Capacity-based responsibility arises from access to truth-bearing instruments. Restoration logic demands multi-layered validation to prevent distortion. Consciousness alignment occurs when testimony reflects inner knowing, not external coercion.

title: brihaspati 1.20
content: दूतकः स्वटिकाग्राहीकार्यमध्यगतस् तथा । एक एव प्रमाणं स्यान् नृपोऽध्यक्षस् तथैव च ॥ dūtakaḥ svaṭikāgrāhīkāryamadhyagatas tathā / eka eva pramāṇaṃ syān nṛpo 'dhyakṣas tathaiva ca // The messenger, the one who receives the token of authority at the task-center, and the king himself as the overseeing witness—these constitute the singular valid source of testimony. Authority originates solely from the witnessed presence of the Sovereign Will Causation is anchored in direct transmission of sovereign intent Capacity-based responsibility is validated through witnessed engagement Restoration logic operates via reconnection to the singular Source-Witness Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of singular authoritative axis

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
साक्षिणोऽर्थसमुद्दिष्टान् यस् तु दोषेण दूषयेत् ।
अदुष्टं दूषयन् वादी तत्समं दण्डमर्हति ॥ sākṣiṇo 'rthasamuddiṣṭān yas tu doṣeṇa dūṣayet | aduṣṭaṃ dūषayan vādī tatsamaṃ daṇḍam arhati || One who discredits a witness summoned for the purpose of establishing facts by imputing fault, or who defames an innocent speaker, deserves equivalent consequence. Authority: Only that which aligns with factual establishment holds judicial validity. Causation: Misrepresentation through defamation disrupts truth-revelation mechanisms. Capacity-based responsibility: The ability to speak truthfully and evaluate testimony carries corresponding accountability. Restoration logic: When speech distorts reality, reintegration occurs through correction and conscious alignment. Consciousness alignment: Truth-speaking capacity must be restored in harmony with Dharma.

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
लेख्यदोषास्तु ये केचित् साक्षिणाम् चैव ये स्मृताः ।
वादकाले तु वक्तव्याः पश्चादुक्तान् न दूषयेत् ॥ lekhya-doṣās tu ye kecit sākṣiṇām caiva ye smṛtāḥ | vāda-kāle tu vaktavyāḥ paścād uktān na dūṣayet || All defects in written documents and those remembered by witnesses shall be declared at the time of argument; anything declared later shall not invalidate what was previously stated. Authority resides in timely and transparent disclosure Causation is anchored in sequential integrity of testimony Capacity-based responsibility requires full presence during adjudication Restoration logic demands prevention of post-hoc manipulation Consciousness alignment occurs through upfront truthfulness

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
साक्षिदोषाः प्रयोक्तव्याः संसदि प्रतिवादिना ।
पत्रे विलिख्य तान् सर्वान् वाच्यं प्रत्युत्तरं ततः ॥ sākṣidoṣāḥ prayoktavyāḥ saṃsadi prativādinā |
patre vilikhya tān sarvān vācyaṃ pratyuttaraṃ tataḥ || All evidentiary discrepancies must be presented by the respondent in council; these shall be recorded in writing and thereafter addressed through responsive declaration. Authority resides in the collective discernment of conscious witnesses Causation is established through documented contradiction, not accusation Capacity-based responsibility requires full disclosure of perceptual conflict Restoration logic demands transparency before rebuttal Consciousness alignment occurs when all disputable evidence is openly inscribed

title: brihaspati 1.24
