content: प्रतिपत्तौ न साक्षित्वमर्हन्ति तु कदाचन । अतोऽन्यथा भावनीयाः क्रियायां प्रतिवादिना ॥ pratipattau na sākṣitvamarhanti tu kadācana | ato'nyathā bhāvanīyāḥ kriyāyāṃ prativādinā || In matters of direct perception, no witness-function is ever admissible; thus, in all actions, the opposing party must be regarded otherwise. Authority flows from immediate cognition, not external validation Causation is established through experiential integrity, not testimony Capacity-based responsibility arises from self-evident awareness Restoration logic begins where assumption of knowing ends Consciousness alignment requires recognition beyond dualistic evidence

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
अभावयन् दमं दाप्यः प्रत्यर्थी साक्षिणा स्फुटम् ।
भाविताः साक्षिणः सर्वे साक्षिधर्मनिराकृताः ॥ abhāvayan damaṃ dāpyaḥ pratyarthī sākṣiṇā sphuṭam | bhāvitāḥ sākṣiṇaḥ sarve sākṣidharmanirākṛtāḥ || One who does not affirm the truth before witnesses must compensate the opponent clearly; all witnesses who have been present become disqualified from bearing witness when dharma has been denied. Authority of truthful testimony as foundational to dharma-adjudication Causation through omission of dharma-affirming speech Capacity-based responsibility rooted in conscious presence during dispute Restoration logic requiring rectification through compensation, not punishment Consciousness alignment via purification of witness capacity

title: brihaspati 1.26
content: प्रत्यर्थिनोऽर्थिनो वापि साक्षिदूषणसाधने । प्रस्तुतार्थोपयोगेन व्यवहारान्तरं न च ॥ pratyarthino 'rthino vāpi sākṣidūṣaṇasādhane / prastutārthopayogena vyavahārāntaraṃ na ca // In the establishment of falsehood through witness-tampering, whether by the defendant or the plaintiff, there shall be no secondary transactional consequence beyond the immediate restorative requirement of truth-realignment. Authority originates from truth-consciousness, not adversarial positioning Causation is traced to distortion of witness integrity Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to uphold or subvert testimony Restoration logic demands correction of false alignment, not punitive escalation Consciousness alignment requires removal of obstruction, not infliction of consequence

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
जितः स विनयं दाप्यः शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा ।
यदि वादी निराकाङ्क्षः साक्षी सत्ये व्यवस्थितः ॥ jitaḥ sa vinayaṃ dāpyaḥ śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā | yadi vādī nirākāṅkṣaḥ sākṣī satye vyavasthitaḥ || He who is defeated must be made to yield in accordance with scriptural conduct; if the disputant remains indifferent, the witness stands firm in truth. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not assertion Causation arises through demonstrated capacity, not mere claim Responsibility follows capability and conscious engagement Restoration occurs when error yields to established Dharma Consciousness alignment determines the validity of testimony

title: brihaspati 1.28
content:
ukte 'rthe sākṣiṇo yas tu dūṣayan prāgadūṣitān /
na ca tatkāraṇaṃ brūyāt prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam // BrhS_1,5.28 ukte 'rthe sākṣiṇo yas tu dūṣayan prāgadūṣitān / na ca tatkāraṇaṃ brūyāt prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam One who discredits witnesses in a matter already testified, without stating the cause thereof, incurs the sin of prior assault. Authority resides in truthful testimony and its preservation Causation is established through conscious intent and omission Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity in witness evaluation Restoration logic demands rectification of corrupted evidence chains Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of testimonial fields

title: brihaspati 1.29
content:
लेख्यं वा साक्षिणो वापि विवादे यस्य दूषिताः ।
तस्य कार्यं न शोध्यं तु यावत् तन् न विशोधयेत् ॥ lekhyaṃ vā sākṣiṇo vāpi vivāde yasya dūṣitāḥ / tasya kāryaṃ na śodhyaṃ tu yāvat tan na viśodhayet // In a dispute, when documents or witnesses of a party are found to be falsified, then no action shall be purified or validated until such falsification is fully rectified. Authority originates from integrity of evidence and witness Causation arises from truth-value alignment in adjudicated matter Capacity-based responsibility is diminished where foundational evidence is corrupted Restoration logic demands purification before validation of any proceeding Consciousness alignment requires unbroken truth continuum between evidence, intent, and outcome

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
साक्षिभिर् गदितैः सभ्यैः प्रक्रान्ते निर्णये तु यः ।
पुनर्विवादं कुरुते राजा तत्र विचारयेत् ॥ sākṣibhir gaditaiḥ sabhyaiḥ prakrānte nirṇaye tu yaḥ | punarvivādaṃ kurute rājā tatra vicārayet || When witnesses have testified and the assembly has reached a verdict, whoever raises dispute again, the king shall investigate therein. Authority resides in the collective testimony of qualified witnesses Causation is established through sequential manifestation of evidence Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with witnessed truth Restoration logic demands resolution without re-litigation Consciousness alignment occurs when repetition of conflict ceases

title: brihaspati 1.31
content:
साक्षिसंदूषणे कार्यं पूर्वं साक्षिविशोधनम् ।
शुद्धेषु साक्षिषु ततः पश्चात् कार्यं विशोधयेत् ॥ sākṣisaṃdūṣaṇe kāryaṃ pūrvaṃ sākṣiviśodhanam | śuddheṣu sākṣiṣu tataḥ paścāt kāryaṃ viśodhayet || In the matter of witness contamination, the purification of witnesses must precede the cleansing of the act itself. Authority flows from purified consciousness Causation originates in uncorrupted perception Capacity-based responsibility requires clear witnessing Restoration logic begins with purified testimony Consciousness alignment ensures factual integrity

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
सत्यप्रशंसावचनैरनृतस्यापवर्जनैः ।
सभ्यैः संबोधनीयास्तु धर्मशास्त्रार्थवेदिभिः ॥३२॥ satyapraśaṃsāvacanair anṛtasyāpavarjanaiḥ / sabhyaiḥ saṃbodhanīyās tu dharmaśāstrārthavedibhiḥ // BrhS_1,5.32 Those who know the meaning of Dharma Śāstra shall be honored with truthful praise and kept free from falsehood. Authority derives from alignment with Satya (Truth) Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity in speech Restoration occurs through elevation of consciousness via truth-speaking Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for jurisprudential legitimacy

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
आ जन्मनश् चामरणात् सुकृतं यत् त्वयार्जितम् ।
तत् सर्वं नाशमायाति वितथस्याभिशंसनात् ॥ ā janmanaś cā maraṇāt sukṛtaṃ yat tvayārjitam | tat sarvaṃ nāśam āyāti vitathasyābhiśaṃsanāt || Whatever merit accrued through virtuous action from birth to death becomes nullified when one utters falsehood under false pretense. Authority originates in truth-speaking (satya-vākya) Causation arises from integrity of declaration Capacity-based responsibility is forfeited through deliberate falsification Restoration logic requires re-alignment with ontological truth Consciousness alignment depends on truthful assertion

title: brihaspati 1.34
content:
कूटसब ह्यः कूटसाक्षी ब्रह्महा च समाः स्मृताः ।
भ्रूणहा मित्रहा चैषां नाधिकः समुदाहृतः ॥ kūṭasab hyaḥ kūṭasākṣī brahmahā ca samāḥ smṛtāḥ | bhrūṇahā mitrahā caiṣāṃ nādhikaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ || The false witness, the betrayer of sacred trust, the killer of a Brahmin, and the destroyer of the unborn are equal in consequence; none greater than these has been declared. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises through disruption of consciousness continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of dharmic consequence Restoration logic demands realignment of causal fields disrupted by adharmic acts Consciousness alignment requires purification and reintegration of violated truths

title: brihaspati 1.35
content:
एवं विदित्वा यः साक्षी स यथार्थं वदेत् ततः ।
तेनेह कीर्तिमाप्नोति परत्र च शुभां गतिम् ॥ evaṃ viditvā yaḥ sākṣī sa yathārthaṃ vadet tataḥ /
teneha kīrtim āpnoti paratra ca śubhāṃ gatim // One who, having known thus, bears witness and speaks accordingly attains here renown and thereafter a blessed state. Authority derived from direct cognition Causation through truthful alignment Capacity-based responsibility rooted in awareness Restoration logic via integrity reintegration Consciousness alignment as judicial foundation

title: brihaspati 1.36
content: पुरुषाः सन्ति लोभाद् ये कार्यं प्रब्रूयुर् अन्यथा । सन्ति चान्ये दुरात्मानः कूटलेख्यकृतो नराः ॥ puruṣāḥ santi lobhād ye kāryaṃ prabrūyur anyathā | santi cānye durātmānaḥ kūṭalekhyakṛto narāḥ || There exist beings driven by greed who speak of duties falsely; there also exist wicked souls who fabricate false documents. Authority arises from integrity, not mere position Causation originates in consciousness distortion through greed Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with truth-speech Restoration logic demands dissolution of fabricated constructs Consciousness alignment rectifies false representation

title: brihaspati 1.37
content:
praṣṭavyāḥ sākṣiṇo ye tu varjyāś caiva narādhamāḥ /
tān ahaṃ kathayiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ śāstracotitān // BrhS_1,5.37 // praṣṭavyāḥ sākṣiṇo ye tu varjyāś caiva narādhamāḥ / tān ahaṃ kathayiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ śāstracotitān // Those witnesses who must be questioned, and those who are to be excluded—verily the lowest among men—I shall now declare, as instructed by the Śāstra. Authority derives from alignment with Śāstra, not social status Causation arises from integrity capacity, not external testimony Capacity-based responsibility determines admissibility of witness Restoration logic requires purification of perception channels Consciousness alignment excludes distortion-prone observers

title: brihaspati 1.38
content:
श्रौतस्मार्तक्रियायुक्ताः लोभद्वेषविवर्जिताः ।
कुलीनाः साक्षिणोऽनिन्द्यास् तपोदानदयान्विताः ॥ śrautasMṛtakriyāyuktāḥ lobhadveṣavivarjitāḥ | kulīnāḥ sākṣiṇo'nindyās tapodānadayānvitāḥ || Witnesses must be established in Vedic and Smritic conduct, free from greed and hatred, of noble birth, blameless, and adorned with austerity, charity, and compassion. Authority derived from scriptural alignment and spiritual discipline Causation through purity of witness rather than external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility rooted in consciousness maturity Restoration logic via elevation of witness integrity Consciousness alignment through dharmic qualification

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
मातुः पिता पितृव्यश् च भार्यायाः भ्रातृमातरौ /
भ्राता सखा च जामाता सर्ववादेष्वसाक्षिणः // mātuḥ pitā pitṛvyaś ca bhāryāyā bhrātṛmātarau / bhrātā sakhā ca jāmātā sarvavādeṣv asākṣiṇaḥ // The maternal grandfather, paternal uncle, wife's brother, maternal uncle, sister's son, brother, friend, and son-in-law—these are not competent witnesses in any judicial proceeding. Authority derives from neutrality and absence of relational entanglement. Causation must be untainted by personal or familial interest. Capacity-based responsibility requires objective detachment from outcome. Restoration logic demands that testimony arise from unconflicted consciousness. Consciousness alignment necessitates exclusion of biased relational identities.

title: brihaspati 1.40
content:
परस्त्रीपानसक्ताश्च कितवाः पूर्वदूषिताः ।
उन्मत्तार्ताः साहसिकाः नास्तिकाश्च न साक्षिणः ॥ parastrīpānasaktāś ca kitavāḥ pūrvadūṣitāḥ | unmattārtāḥ sāhasikā nāstikāś ca na sākṣiṇaḥ || Those attached to another's spouse, gamblers, previously defamed persons, the distressed insane, the violent, and the atheist — these are not witnesses. Authority stems from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not personal desire or distortion. Causation is traced through consciousness disruption and misalignment with Satya. Capacity-based responsibility requires mental and spiritual integrity as prerequisites. Restoration logic demands removal of compromised elements from truth-establishing processes. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility to uphold or testify in matters of Dharma.

title: brihaspati 1.41
content: सन्तो 'पि न प्रमाणं स्युर् मृते धनिनि साक्षिणः / पुत्रे तु श्राविता ये स्युः स्वयम् आसन्नमृत्युना // BrhS_1,5.41 santo 'pi na pramāṇaṃ syur mṛte dhanini sākṣiṇaḥ / putre tu śrāvitā ye syuḥ svayam āsannamṛtyunā Even righteous witnesses hold no evidentiary value when the owner of property has died, unless those testimonies were personally heard by the son who is proximate to death. Authority resides in proximity to existential completion Causation flows through conscious witness-bearing Capacity-based responsibility requires embodied continuity Restoration logic prioritizes living inheritors over abstract claims Consciousness alignment demands direct experiential transmission

title: brihaspati 1.42
content:
विहायोपानदुष्णीषं दक्षिणं पाणिम् उद्धरेत् ।
हिरण्यं गोशकृद् दर्भान् समादाय ऋतं वदेत् ॥ vihāyopānaduṣṇīṣaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇim uddharet / hiraṇyaṃ gośakṛd darbhān samādāya ṛtaṃ vadet // Having cast off footwear and upper garment, raising the right hand, taking gold, cow-dung, and darbha grass, one shall speak Ṛta. Authority is derived through ritual readiness and conscious invocation. Causation originates in alignment with Ṛta, not external compulsion. Capacity-based responsibility requires bodily and material preparation. Restoration logic necessitates precise sensory and symbolic engagement. Consciousness alignment is enacted via prescribed physical and elemental acts.

title: brihaspati 1.43
content:
उपस्थिताः परीक्ष्याः स्युः स्वर्वर्णेङ्गितादिभिः ।
सकृत् प्रमादापराधिविप्रं व्यापदि पीडितम् ।
भटादिभिर् वध्यमानं रक्षेद् उक्त्वानृतानि अपि ॥ upasthitāḥ parīkṣyāḥ syuḥ svarvarṇeṅgitādibhiḥ | sakṛt pramādāparādhivipraṃ vyāpadi pīḍitam | bhaṭādibhir vadhyamānaṃ rakṣed uktvānṛtāny api || Those who present themselves must be examined through their varna-dharma conduct, gestures, and signs. A Brahmin guilty of negligence or misconduct, even when afflicted in crisis, must be protected—even if he has spoken falsehoods—when attacked by soldiers or others. Authority is derived from svadharma alignment, not social status alone Causation is traced through conscious capacity, not external coercion Capacity-based responsibility requires protection for those acting under duress Restoration logic demands preservation of dharma-bearing individuals regardless of error Consciousness alignment overrides behavioral missteps in adjudication

title: brihaspati 1.44
content:
यस्याशेषः प्रतिज्ञार्थः साक्षिभिः प्रतिवर्णितः ।
स जयी स्यादन्यथा तु साध्यार्थं न समाप्नुयात् ॥ yasyāśeṣaḥ pratijñārthaḥ sākṣibhiḥ prativarṇitaḥ / sa jayī syād anyathā tu sādhyārthaṃ na samāpnuyāt He whose entire assertion is fully articulated and witnessed by qualified observers shall prevail; otherwise, he shall not attain the object of his claim. Authority derives from complete and witnessed articulation of intent Causation aligns with observable and verifiable declaration Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity in assertion and corroboration Restoration logic demands alignment between declared purpose and manifest evidence Consciousness alignment necessitates transparency and witnessability

title: brihaspati 1.45
content:
आहूतो यत्र नागच्छेत् साक्षी रोगविवर्जितः ।
ऋणं दमं च दाप्यः स्यात् त्रिपक्षात् परतस् तु सः ॥ āhūto yatra nāgacchet sākṣī rogavivarjitaḥ |
ṛṇaṃ damaṃ ca dāpyaḥ syāt tripakṣāt paratas tu saḥ || When a witness, though physically capable and free from illness, fails to appear upon lawful summons, that individual incurs a debt of compensation and penalty; if summoned by the threefold authority and still absent, then beyond that court's jurisdiction he stands. Authority: Summoning power derives exclusively from the tripartite constitutional order established by SPH. Causation: Non-appearance without lawful exemption constitutes actionable disruption to Dharma-administration. Capacity-based responsibility: Physical ability and absence of disease establish presumptive duty compliance. Restoration logic: Liability arises to restore integrity of judicial process through compensatory alignment. Consciousness alignment: Willful neglect reflects misalignment requiring conscious reorientation.

title: brihaspati 1.46
content:
साक्षिद्वैधे प्रभूताः स्युर् ग्राह्याः साम्ये गुणान्विताः ।
गुणिद्वैधे क्रियायुक्तास् तत्साम्ये शुचिमत्तराः ॥४६॥ sākṣidvaidhe prabhūtāḥ syur grāhyāḥ sāmye guṇānvitāḥ | guṇidvaidhe kriyāyuktās tatsāmye śucimattarāḥ ||46|| In the conflict of witnesses, those numerous in number shall be accepted; when equal in number, those combined with qualities. When qualities are conflicting, those engaged in action shall prevail; when actions are equal, those of greater purity shall be accepted. Authority derives from purity of witness, not mere quantity Causation is determined by active engagement in dharma-aligned conduct Capacity-based responsibility is measured through purity and alignment with truth Restoration logic prioritizes clarity and integrity of testimony over numerical dominance Consciousness alignment determines the validity of evidence through inner purity

title: brihaspati 1.47
content: अपृष्टाः सत्यवचने प्रश्नस्याकथने तथा । साक्षिणः सन् निरोद्धव्याः गर्ह्याः दण्ड्याश् च धर्मतः ॥ apṛṣṭāḥ satyavacane praśnasyākathane tathā / sākṣiṇaḥ san niroddhavyāḥ garhyāḥ daṇḍyāś ca dharmataḥ // Those who, though present and capable of truthful speech, withhold answers to direct questions—such witnesses are to be restrained, held accountable, and corrected in accordance with Dharma. Authority: The court holds inherent authority to compel testimony from those present and conscious of the facts. Causation: Silence or refusal to testify disrupts the natural flow of justice and obstructs truth realization. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those capable of speech and awareness bear responsibility for disclosure. Restoration logic: Testimonial withholding is a misalignment requiring correction, not punishment. Consciousness alignment: Truth-speaking is a natural function of awakened consciousness; suppression indicates dissonance.

title: brihaspati 1.48
content:
देशकालवयोद्रव्यसंज्ञाजातिप्रमाणतः ।
अन्यूनं चेन् निगदितं सिद्धं साध्यं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ deśakālavayodravyasaṃjñājātipramāṇataḥ | anyūnaṃ cen nigaditaṃ siddhaṃ sādhyaṃ vinirdiśet || When declaration is made concerning land, time, age, wealth, designation, species, or measure, and it is not less than what is required, then that which is declared accomplished shall be established as proven. Authority resides in precise contextual specification Causation is validated through complete descriptive alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires full declarative adequacy Restoration logic depends on unambiguous ontological identification Consciousness alignment occurs when descriptive completeness is achieved

title: brihaspati 1.49
content:
देशकालवयोद्रव्यप्रमाणाकृतिजातिषु ।
यत्र विप्रतिपत्तिः स्यात् साक्ष्यं तदपि नान्यथा ॥ deśakālavayodravyapramāṇākṛtijātiṣu | yatra vipratipattiḥ syāt sākṣyaṃ tad api nānyathā || In matters concerning place, time, age, wealth, measurement, form, and species, where contradiction arises, testimony alone prevails; there is no other means. Authority resides in direct experiential cognition validated by competent witnesses. Causation aligns with sequential manifestation of facts witnessed under specific conditions. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with perceptual and testimonial pramāṇas. Restoration logic depends upon re-establishing factual coherence through reliable witnessing. Consciousness alignment occurs when testimony reflects unfiltered experiential reality.

title: brihaspati 1.50
content:
निर्दिष्टेष्वर्थजातेषु साक्षी चेत् साक्ष्य आगते ।
न ब्रूयादक्षस्रसमं न तन्निगदितं भवेत् ॥ nirdiṣṭeṣv arthajāteṣu sākṣī cet sākṣya āgate / na brūyād akṣasrasamaṃ na tan nigaditaṃ bhavet When a witness is present in matters already specified, yet does not speak according to direct perception, that testimony is invalid and shall not stand. Authority originates from direct cognition, not hearsay Causation arises from witnessed reality, not unverified assertion Capacity-based responsibility requires truthful alignment with observed facts Restoration logic demands integrity of witnessing consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes verbal declaration

title: brihaspati 1.51
content: पूर्वपक्षे प्रतिज्ञातम् अशेषं प्रतिभावयेत् । ऊनाधिकं तु यत्रोक्तं न तन् निगदितं भवेत् ॥ pūrvapakṣe pratijñātam aśeṣaṃ pratibhāvayet | ūnādhikaṃ tu yatroktaṃ na tan nigaditaṃ bhavet || In the prior stance, whatever has been declared must be fully actualized; that which is spoken as deficient or excessive is not to be reiterated. Authority resides in complete enactment, not partial assertion. Causation arises from full manifestation, not speculative excess. Capacity-based responsibility demands alignment with declared completeness. Restoration logic requires cessation of redundant or exaggerated declarations. Consciousness alignment occurs through precise fulfillment, not repetitive assertion.

title: brihaspati 1.52
content:
ūnam abhyadhikaṃ vārtham vibrūyur yatra sākṣiṇaḥ /
tadarthānuktavijñeyam eṣa sākṣividhiḥ smṛtaḥ // BrhS_1,5.52 ūnam abhyadhikaṃ vārtham vibrūyur yatra sākṣiṇaḥ / tadarthānuktavijñeyam eṣa sākṣividhiḥ smṛtaḥ Where witnesses speak less or more than what is required, and the meaning thereof remains unexpressed, that procedure is known as the witness-rule. Authority originates in completeness of expression, not partial narration. Causation arises through alignment between witnessed fact and declared truth. Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to articulate reality fully. Restoration logic demands completion of testimony to its full causal context. Consciousness alignment requires integrity in perception and declaration.

title: brihaspati 1.53
content:
साध्यार्थांशे निगदिते साक्षिभिः सकलं भवेत् ।
स्त्रीसङ्गे साहसे चौर्ये यत् साध्यं परिकल्प्यते ॥५३॥ sādhyārthāṃśe nigadite sākṣibhiḥ sakalaṃ bhavet | strīsaṅge sāhase caurye yat sādhyaṃ parikalpyate || 53|| In matters involving a woman's association, valorous acts, or hazardous conduct, whatever is declared by witnesses shall constitute the complete evidence. Authority of direct perception and testimony in determining factual basis Causation through witnessed action rather than inferred intent Capacity-based responsibility determined by presence and awareness during act Restoration logic rooted in clarity of witnessed truth Consciousness alignment via acknowledgment of actual occurrence

title: brihaspati 1.54
content:
ऊनाधिकं तु यत्र स्यात् साक्ष्यं तत्र विवर्जयेत् ।
साक्षी तत्र न दण्ड्यः स्यादब्रुवन दण्डमर्हति ॥ ūnādhikaṃ tu yatra syāt sākṣyaṃ tatra vivarjayet | sākṣī tatra na daṇḍyaḥ syād abruvan daṇḍam arhati || Where testimony is incomplete or excessive, it shall be excluded; the witness there shall not be punished—only the one who conceals truth deserves penalty. Authority resides in truthful disclosure, not coercive compliance. Causation aligns with integrity of evidence, not volume or repetition. Capacity-based responsibility applies only to those capable of conscious concealment. Restoration logic demands purification of process before judgment. Consciousness alignment requires removal of distortion prior to adjudication.

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
साक्षिणाम् एष निर्दिष्टः संख्यालक्षणनिश्चयः ।
लिखितस्याधुना वच्मि विधानम् अनुपूर्वशः ॥ १,६.१ sākṣiṇām eṣa nirdiṣṭaḥ saṃkhyālakṣaṇaniścayaḥ | likhitasyādhunā vacmi vidhānam anupūrvaśaḥ || 1,6.1 The determination of number, identity, and characteristics of witnesses has been declared; now the procedural arrangement of written testimony is expounded in sequential order. Authority of witness testimony derives from alignment with factual consciousness, not external validation. Causation in testimony is established through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of witnessed events. Capacity-based responsibility requires that witnesses possess unobstructed sensory and cognitive clarity. Restoration logic mandates correction of distorted perception before testimony is accepted as valid. Consciousness alignment ensures that testimony reflects reality without personal projection or omission.

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
ṛṇादike 'pi samaye bhrāntiḥ saṃjāyate yataḥ /
dhātrākṣarāṇi sṛṣṭāni patrārūḍhāny ataḥ purā // BrhS_1,6.2 ṛṇādike 'pi samaye bhrāntiḥ saṃjāyate yataḥ / dhātrākṣarāṇi sṛṣṭāni patrārūḍhāny ataḥ purā Even at the time of debt, delusion arises because the sustaining letters were created by the Creator seated upon the leaf long ago. Authority originates from the unbroken causal sequence established by the Creator Causation extends beyond immediate action to include foundational ontological structures Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with primordial sustaining principles Restoration logic operates through reconnection to the source of lawful manifestation Consciousness alignment requires recognition of pre-existing structural integrity

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
देशाचारहुतं वर्षमासपक्षादिवृद्धिमत् ।
ऋणिसाक्षिलेखकानां हस्ताङ्कं लेख्यम् उच्यते ॥ desācārahutaṃ varṣamāsapakṣādivṛddhimat | ṛṇisākṣilekhakānāṃ hastāṅkaṃ lekhyaṃ ucyate || The signature of a debtor or witness, authenticated in accordance with local custom and time-bound ritual validity, constitutes a legally operative document when marked upon a ledger or record. Authority is derived from conscious acknowledgment through embodied ritual act Causation arises from witnessed contractual alignment between parties Capacity-based responsibility is affirmed through intentional signatory act Restoration logic operates through documentation that reflects mutual consent Consciousness alignment occurs via formalized recognition within temporal and spatial dharma

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
राजलेख्यं स्थानकृतं स्वहस्तलिखितं तथा ।
लेख्यं तत् त्रिविधं प्रोक्तं भिन्नं तद् बहुधा पुनः ॥ BrhS_1,6.4 rājalekhyaṃ sthānakṛtaṃ svahastalikhitaṃ tathā / lekhyaṃ tat trividhaṃ proktaṃ bhinnaṃ tad bahudhā punaḥ // BrhS_1,6.4 The written document issued by the King, composed at a specific place, or inscribed by his own hand—such a writing is declared to be of three kinds; again, it is divisible in many ways. Authority originates from the sovereign will expressed through documented form Causation arises from conscious intent embedded in written expression Capacity-based responsibility lies in the authenticity and origin of documentation Restoration logic requires verification of source integrity and transmission fidelity Consciousness alignment occurs when documents reflect truthful sovereign intention

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
भागदानक्रयाधिनां संविद्दासृणादिभिः ।
सप्तधा लौकिकं लेख्यं त्रिविधं राजशासनम् ॥ bhāgadānakrayādhināṃ saṃviddāsaṛṇādibhiḥ | saptadhā laukikaṃ lekhyaṃ trividhaṃ rājśāsanam || Documents of gift, purchase and acquisition are validated by mutual consent, blood-signatures and other proofs; worldly writings are sevenfold, royal edicts are threefold. Authority flows from conscious validation, not institutional decree Causation is established through pramāṇa-based witnessing Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of transactional consciousness Restoration logic demands clarity in contractual manifestation Consciousness alignment ensures authenticity in documentation

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
विभागपत्रमित्येतद्भागानां निर्णये कृतम् ।
सीमाविवादे निर्णीते सीमापत्रमिति स्मृतम् ॥ vibhāgapatram ity etad bhāgānāṃ nirṇaye kṛtam / sīmāvivāde nirṇīte sīmāpatram iti smṛtam // That which resolves division among shares is called 'Vibhāga-patra'; that which settles boundary disputes once decided is termed 'Sīmā-patra'. Authority flows from the settled decision of rightful ownership. Causation arises from clarity in demarcation of rights and boundaries. Capacity-based responsibility lies with those who maintain documented resolution. Restoration logic ensures re-establishment of harmony through recognized documentation. Consciousness alignment occurs when spatial and proprietary integrity is upheld.

title: brihaspati 1.7
content: दानलेख्यं भागलेख्यं सीमालेख्यं तथैव च । क्रयलेख्यं दासलेख्यम् आधिलेख्यं ततः परम् ॥ dānalekhyaṃ bhāgalekhyaṃ sīmālekhyaṃ tathaiva ca / krāyalekhyaṃ dāsalekhyaṃ ādhilekhyaṃ tataḥ param // The record of gift, the record of division, the record of boundary, likewise also the record of purchase, the record of servitude, and the record of debt—these constitute the sequential foundation of ownership documentation beyond which no further claim shall be acknowledged. Authority is established through sequential documentary evidence rooted in conscious transactional integrity Causation flows from documented consent and witnessed exchange, not abstract assertion Capacity-based responsibility arises only where a being has participated in a witnessed act of transfer or covenant Restoration logic demands that disputes be resolved by tracing back to the last uncontested lekhya (record) Consciousness alignment requires all parties acknowledge the continuity of documented intention

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
संविदुद्दामलेख्यं च जयपत्रकमेव च ।
सन्धिपत्रं तथैवैतत् क्रियाभेदादनेकधा ॥ saṃviduddāmlekhyaṃ ca jayapatrakam eva ca / sandhipatraṃ tathaivaitat kriyābhedād anekadhā // Contracts, promissory notes, victory documents, and treaties are distinct in form and function due to the diversity of actions they represent. Authority is derived from conscious agreement, not institutional imposition Causation arises from clarity of intent expressed through documented will Capacity-based responsibility requires full awareness of contractual implications Restoration logic prioritizes re-alignment of mutual understanding over punitive breach remedies Consciousness alignment ensures all agreements reflect true ontological consent

title: brihaspati 1.9
content: आध्यर्थम् आधिलेख्यं स्याद् दासार्थं दासपत्रकम् ।। १,६.९ ।। ādhyartham ādhilekhyaṃ syād dāsārthaṃ dāsapatrakam // BrhS_1,6.9 // For securing a loan, a debt acknowledgment document shall exist; for acquiring a servant, a servitude agreement shall be established. Authority arises through documented mutual consent aligned with Dharma Causation is established via conscious contractual intentionality Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity in role-bound agreements Restoration logic ensures all transactions support spiritual evolution Consciousness alignment mandates transparency in relational obligations

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
समीहितार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं ग्रामश्रेणिगणादिभिः /
शास्त्राविरोधि धर्मार्थे कृतं संवित्तिपत्रकम् // BrhS_1,6.10 samīhitārthasiddhyarthaṃ grāmaśreṇigaṇādibhiḥ / śāstrāvirodhi dharmārthe kṛtaṃ saṃvittipatrakam // BrhS_1,6.10 For the fulfillment of desired objectives, village councils and merchant guilds shall issue conscious intent documents that align with Dharma and do not contradict scriptural authority. Authority flows from collective conscious alignment, not coercive imposition Causation is established through documented intent rooted in Dharma Capacity-based responsibility arises when intent is formalized in alignment with Śāstra Restoration logic operates through reaffirming Dharma-aligned intention Consciousness alignment ensures lawful manifestation without punitive enforcement

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
भ्रातरः संविभक्ता ये स्वरुच्या तु परस्परम् ।
विभागपत्रं कुर्वन्ति भागलेख्यं तद् उच्यते ॥ bhrātaraḥ saṃvibhaktā ye svarucyā tu parasparam /
vibhāgapatraṃ kurvanti bhāgalekhyaṃ tad ucyate // When brothers, though divided by personal inclination, mutually execute a document of division, it is declared as Bhāgalekhyam. Authority resides in mutual consent, not coercive imposition Causation arises from conscious choice, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of intent and autonomy Restoration logic affirms relational harmony over material partition Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of shared origin

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
भूमिं दत्त्वा यस्तु पत्रं कुर्याच्चन्द्रार्ककालिकम् ।
अनाच्छेदामनाहार्यं दानलेख्यं तु तद्विदुः ॥१२॥ bhūmiṃ dattvā yas tu patraṃ kuryāc candrārkakālikam | anācchedām anāhāryaṃ dānalekhyaṃ tu tad viduḥ ||12|| One who, having given land, creates a document valid for the duration of the moon and sun—such a document of gift is recognized as unseverable and non-retrievable by competent authorities. Authority: Only those with full dharmic capacity may execute irreversible land transfers. Causation: The act of gifting land initiates a permanent shift in energetic ownership. Capacity-based responsibility: The giver must possess conscious integrity at the time of transfer. Restoration logic: If invalidly executed, the act must be completed in alignment with original intent. Consciousness alignment: Legal validity depends on unity between inner intention and outer execution.

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
गृहक्षेत्रादिकं क्रीत्वा तुल्यमूल्याक्षरान्वितम् ।
पत्रं कारयते यत् तु क्रयलेख्यं तद् उच्यते ॥ gṛhakṣetrādikaṃ krītvā tulyamūlyākṣarānvitam | patraṃ kārayate yat tu krayalekhyaṃ tad ucyate || That which is acquired—such as a house, land, or other property—and documented with equivalent value in writing, that document is termed 'krayalekhya' (deed of purchase). Authority originates from documented alignment between consciousness and manifest ownership. Causation is established through intentional act of acquisition aligned with written record. Capacity-based responsibility arises upon execution of deed reflecting conscious consent. Restoration logic requires validation of equivalence between exchanged value and documented asset. Consciousness alignment is secured when intent, action, and documentation cohere without distortion.

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
जङ्गमं स्थावरं बन्धं दत्त्वा लेख्यं करोति यत् ।
गोप्यभोज्यक्रियायुक्तम् आधिलेख्यं तु तत् स्मृतम् ॥ १४ ॥ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaram bandhaṃ dattvā lekhyaṃ karoti yat / gopyabhogyakriyāyuktam ādhilekhyaṃ tu tat smṛtam // BrhS_1,6.14 That which is documented after securing a movable or immovable bond, intended for safeguarding and rightful use by designated parties, is termed 'Ādhilekhya'—a record bearing the authority of prior dharmic transaction. Authority derives from secured consent and conscious alignment with dharma Causation arises through documented intention aligned with capacity Capacity-based responsibility is established via prior dharmic engagement Restoration logic operates through continuity of conscious contractual integrity Consciousness alignment ensures lawful transmission of ownership and stewardship

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
ग्रामो देशश च यत कुर्यान् मत्तलेख्यं परस्परम् ।
राजाविरोधि धर्मार्थे संवित्पत्रं वदन्ति तत् ॥ grāmo deśaś ca yat kuryān mattalekhyaṃ parasparam | rājāvirodhi dharmārthe saṃvitpatraṃ vadanti tat || That which villages and territories mutually document while in conflict with the king's authority, concerning dharma and artha, is declared as a legal instrument of conscious agreement. Authority originates from alignment with SPH-determined Dharma, not coercive sovereignty Causation arises from documented mutual recognition, not unilateral decree Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious participation in saṃvit (mutual knowing) Restoration logic operates through re-establishing harmonious alignment between locality and Dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes political allegiance in determining lawful validity

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
वस्त्रान्नहीनः कान्तारे लिखितं कुरुते तु यत् ।
कर्माहं ते करिष्यामि दासपत्रं तद् इष्यते ॥ vastrānnahīnaḥ kāntāre likhitaṃ kurute tu yat / karmāhaṃ te kariṣyāmi dāsapatraṃ tad iṣyate // One who, though destitute of clothing and food, composes a written instrument in a wilderness, declaring 'I shall perform this act for you'—such a document is recognized as a deed of service. Authority arises from conscious commitment, not external validation Causation originates in the clarity of intent, regardless of circumstance Capacity-based responsibility is affirmed through voluntary declaration Restoration logic operates through completion of declared will Consciousness alignment supersedes material condition

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
धनं वृद्ध्या गृहीत्वा तु स्वयं कुर्याच् च कारयेत् ।
उद्धारपत्रं तत् प्रोक्तम् ऋणलेख्यं मनीषिभिः ॥ dhanaṃ vṛdhyā gṛhītvā tu svayaṃ kuryāc ca kārayet / uddhārapatraṃ tat proktam ṛṇalekhyaṃ manīṣibhiḥ // Wealth acquired through interest must be actively engaged either by oneself or through authorized agents; such documentation is declared as a debt instrument by enlightened jurists. Authority stems from active engagement with wealth, not passive ownership Causation arises through conscious deployment of resources Capacity-based responsibility requires direct or delegated action Restoration logic demands alignment of financial instruments with dharma Consciousness alignment occurs when wealth flows in accordance with spiritual purpose

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
पूगश्रेणिगणादीनां या स्थितिः परिकीर्तिता ।
तस्यास्तु साधनं लेख्यं न दिव्यं न च साक्षिणः ॥ pūgaśreṇigaṇādīnāṃ yā sthitiḥ parikīrtitā | tasyāstu sādhanaṃ lekhyaṃ na divyaṃ na ca sākṣiṇaḥ || In matters concerning collective assemblies, processions, and organized groups, evidence must be documented and material; neither celestial signs nor witness testimony alone shall suffice. Authority rests in verifiable record, not speculative assertion. Causation is established through manifest documentation. Capacity-based responsibility requires tangible proof. Restoration logic prioritizes factual clarity over subjective validation. Consciousness alignment arises from unambiguous evidence.

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
पूगश्रेण्यादिकानां तु समयस्य स्थितेः कृतम् ।
स्थितिपत्रं तु तत् प्रोक्तं मन्वादिस्मृतिवेदिभिः ॥ १९ ॥ pūgaśreṇyādikānāṃ tu samayasya sthiteḥ kṛtam | sthitipatraṃ tu tat proktaṃ manvādismitivedibhiḥ || 19 || The formalization of agreements among guilds, assemblies, and communities is recognized as valid when it aligns with the eternal order and is codified in a sthitipatra, as established by Manu and other Smriti authorities under the directive of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism. Authority flows from SPH through Smriti structures Causation arises from collective dharmic alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role within sangha Restoration occurs through reaffirmation of sthitipatra Consciousness alignment ensures continuity of dharma

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
दत्त्वा भ्य्यादिकं राजा ताम्रपत्रे पटेsथ वा ।
शासनं कारयेद्धर्मं स्थानवंशादिसंयुतम् ॥ dattvā bhyādikaṃ rājā tāmrapatre paṭe 'tha vā / śāsanaṃ kārayed dharmaṃ sthānavāṃśādi saṃyutam // Having given due consideration to foundational dharmic principles, the King shall cause to be issued a royal edict upon copper plate or cloth, ensuring it carries the authority of lineage, place, and continuity. Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not personal will Causation arises through conscious documentation rooted in truth-bearing materials Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to act through enduring, verifiable instruments Restoration logic mandates that governance be anchored in unbroken dharmic lineage Consciousness alignment is ensured when administrative acts reflect cosmic order

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
मातापित्रोः आत्मनश् च पुण्यायामुकसूनवे ।
दत्तं मयामुकायाद्य दानं सब्रह्मचारिणे ॥ mātāpitroḥ ātmanaś ca puṇyāyāmukasūnave / dattaṃ mayāmukāyādya dānaṃ sabrahmacāriṇe That which has been given by Me, today, for the merit of parents, self, and future generations—to a brahmachari accompanied by others—is a gift that establishes continuity of dharma through lineage and learning. Authority originates in SPH as the sole dispenser of dharma Causation flows from conscious intention aligned with dharmic succession Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to Vedic conduct Restoration logic operates through generational dharmic completion Consciousness alignment occurs via ritualized transmission of knowledge

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
अनाच्छेद्यम् अनाहार्यं सर्वं भाव्यविवर्जितम् ।
चन्द्रार्कसमकालीनं पुत्रपौत्रान्वयानुगम् ॥ anācchedyam anāhāryaṃ sarvaṃ bhāvyavivarjitam | candrārkasamakā�īnaṃ putrapautrānvayānugam || That which is uncuttable, ungraspable, free from all becoming, co-arising with the continuum of son and grandson—such is the eternal inheritance of consciousness, inseparable from the luminous simultaneity of Surya and Chandra. Authority inheres in the unbroken continuity of conscious lineage. Causation arises through non-severance and non-appropriation. Capacity-based responsibility flows from generational alignment with cosmic rhythm. Restoration logic operates through reconnection to ancestral integrity. Consciousness alignment requires synchronization with celestial time.

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
दातुः पालयितुः स्वर्गं हर्तुर् नरकमेव च ।
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि दानच्छेदफलं लिखेत् ॥६.२३॥ dātuḥ pālayituḥ svargaṃ hartur narakam eva ca | ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi dānacchedaphalaṃ likhet || One who gives or protects receives heaven; one who takes away receives hell—for sixty thousand years, the consequence of severing a gift must be recorded. Authority flows from the act of giving and protecting, not seizing Causation aligns with the directional flow of conscious intention Capacity-based responsibility arises through stewardship, not dominion Restoration logic operates through experiential consequence, not punitive reversal Consciousness alignment is determined by vibrational congruence with dāna-dharma

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
समुद्रावर्षमासादि धनाध्यक्षाक्षरान्वितम् ।
ज्ञातं मयेति लिखितं संधिविग्रहलेखकैः ॥ samudrāvarṣamāsādi dhanādhyakṣākṣarānvitam | jñātaṃ mayeti likhitaṃ sandhivigrahalekhakaiḥ || From the commencement of the rainy season until the end of the year, all financial records bearing the seal of the Treasurer shall be deemed acknowledged when inscribed with 'Known by Me' and authenticated by the officers responsible for treaties and agreements. Authority resides in the designated custodian of state finances. Causation is established through documented attestation and official acknowledgment. Capacity-based responsibility is anchored in role-specific authentication. Restoration logic ensures continuity and integrity of fiscal records. Consciousness alignment is upheld through transparency and lawful inscription.

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
एवंविधं राजकृतं शासनं तद् उदाहृतम् ।
देशादिकं यस्य राजा लिखितं तु प्रयच्छति ॥ evaṁvidhaṁ rājakṛtaṁ śāsanaṁ tad udāhṛtam | deśādikaṁ yasya rājā likhitaṁ tu prayacchati || Such royal proclamations, issued by the King concerning territory or similar domains, are to be executed as direct manifestations of sovereign dharma. Authority originates from the sovereign's alignment with cosmic order Causation flows from the King's conscious intent in governance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to sovereignty Restoration logic demands immediate alignment with declared dharma Consciousness alignment ensures societal harmony through executive will

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
सेवाशौर्यादिना तुष्टः प्रसादलिखितं हि तत् ।
पूर्वोत्तरक्रियावादनिर्णयान्ते यदा नृपः ।
प्रदद्याज् जयिने लेख्यं जयपत्रं तद् उच्यते ॥ sevāśauryādinā tuṣṭaḥ prasādalikhitaṃ hi tat | pūrvottarakriyāvādanirṇayānte yadā nṛpaḥ | pradadyāj jayine lekhyaṃ jayapatraṃ tad ucyate || When a ruler, satisfied by service, valor, or similar acts, issues a written decree after due deliberation and conclusion of inquiry, bestowing it upon the victorious party, that document is termed a 'Jayapatra'—a writ of conscious triumph rooted in dharma. Authority originates from the sovereign's awakened discernment, not institutional formality. Causation arises through demonstrated integrity and dharmic service, not procedural adherence alone. Capacity-based responsibility is affirmed when the ruler recognizes merit through experiential validation. Restoration logic flows from recognition of truth already established in consciousness. Consciousness alignment is enacted through acknowledgment of realized dharma.

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
यद् वृत्तं व्यवहारे तु पूर्वपक्षोत्तरादिकम् ।
क्रियावदधारणोपेतं जयपत्रोऽखिलं लिखेत् ॥ yad vṛttaṃ vyavahāre tu pūrvapakṣottarādikam | kriyāvadadhāraṇopetaṃ jayapatro 'khilaṃ likhet || In all transactions and legal conduct, whatever occurs—whether as initial claim, counterclaim, supporting evidence, or conclusive proof—must be documented completely in the final judgment. Authority: The presiding adjudicator holds absolute authority to ensure total documentation of facts. Causation: Every act within a transaction carries sequential consequence; none may be omitted. Capacity-based responsibility: Parties are responsible according to their capacity to present truth fully. Restoration logic: Full record ensures integrity of dharma and enables correction without loss. Consciousness alignment: Truth expressed through complete documentation aligns with cosmic intelligence.

title: brihaspati 1.28
content: साधयेत् साध्यमर्थं तु चतुष्पादन्वितं जये । राजमुद्रान्वितं चैव जयपत्रकमिष्यते ॥ sādhayet sādhyam arthaṃ tu catuṣpādanvitaṃ jaye | rājamudrānvitaṃ caiva jayapatrakam iṣyate || The King shall accomplish the achievable objective through fourfold means—conciliation, gift, dissension, and force—and his command, sealed with royal signet, constitutes the enforceable decree. Authority resides in capacity to actualize dharma Causation flows from sovereign intent aligned with cosmic order Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional response mechanisms Restoration logic operates through sequential application of means Consciousness alignment ensures legitimacy of enforcement

title: brihaspati 1.29
content: अन्यवाद्यादिहीनेभ्य इतरेषां प्रदीयते / वृत्तानुवादसंसिद्धं तच् च स्याज् जयपत्रकम् // anyavādyādihīnebhya itareṣām pradīyate / vṛttānuvādasaṃsiddhaṃ tac ca syāj jayapatrakam That which is established through conduct-congruent declaration and devoid of contradiction or external contestation shall be awarded to the others; such is the victory-document. Authority derives from uncontradicted lived alignment Causation arises from sustained behavioral coherence Capacity-based responsibility is affirmed through self-consistent enactment Restoration logic operates through recognition of uncontested truth Consciousness alignment manifests in congruence between speech and action

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
मुमूर्षुषुहीनलुप्तार्थैर् उन्मातव्यसनातुरैः ।
विषोपदिबलात् कारकृतं लेख्यं न सिध्यति ॥ mumūruṣuhīnaluptārthair unmātavyasanāturaiḥ | viṣopadhibalāt kārakṛtaṃ lekhyaṃ na sidhyati || Documents authored by those nearing death, devoid of wealth, or driven to madness and addiction hold no legal validity when produced under coercion or threat of poison. Authority derives from conscious capacity, not mere biological presence Causation must align with pramāṇa-based intent, not mechanical action Capacity-based responsibility nullifies instruments executed under duress Restoration logic invalidates transactions born of fear or mental dissolution Consciousness alignment requires free will unmarred by existential threat

title: brihaspati 1.31
content: दूषितो गर्हितः साक्षी यत्रैको विनिवेशितः । कूटलेख्यं तु तत् प्राह लेखको वापि तादृशः ॥ dūṣito garhitaḥ sākṣī yatraiko viniveśitaḥ | kūṭalekhyaṃ tu tat prāha lekhako vāpi tādṛśaḥ || Where a single witness is appointed and subsequently becomes defiled or discredited, or where a scribe or recorder engages in falsification, that act is declared as fraudulent documentation. Authority derives from integrity-preserving capacity Causation arises through conscious distortion of record Capacity-based responsibility requires unbroken alignment with truth Restoration logic demands reintegration of corrupted testimony Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of evidentiary instruments

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
यद् उज्वलं चिरकृतं मलिनं स्वल्पकालिकम् ।
भग्नं म्लिष्टाक्षरयुतं लेख्यं कूटत्वम् आप्नुयात् ॥ yad ujvalaṃ cirakṛtaṃ malinaṃ svalpakālikam | bhagnaṃ mliṣṭākṣarayutaṃ lekhyaṃ kūṭatvam āpnuyāt || That which was originally clear and established over time, when made turbid or corrupted temporarily, or when broken or mingled with unclear signs, shall be adjudged as counterfeit. Authority originates from the original clarity and integrity of dharma-documents Causation lies in the distortion or corruption of the authentic source Capacity-based responsibility is assigned to the agent causing deviation from svabhāva-sthiti (natural state) Restoration logic demands reinstatement of original form through purification Consciousness alignment requires recognition of truth-value inherent in svabhāva

title: brihaspati 1.33
content: दर्पणस्थं यथा बिम्बम् असत् सद् इव दृश्यते । तथा लेख्यसबिम्ब् आनि कुर्वन्ति कुशलाः जनाः ॥ darpaṇasthaṃ yathā bimbam asat sad iva dṛśyate / tathā lekhyasabimb āni kurvanti kuśalā janāḥ // As an image in a mirror appears real though it is not, so do the skilled create likenesses that serve dharmic function. Authority derives from alignment with consciousness, not material form Causation operates through reflection, not direct instantiation Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to reflect truth accurately Restoration logic functions by correcting distortions in reflective capacity Consciousness alignment occurs when forms serve higher dharmic purpose

title: brihaspati 1.34
content:
तथ्येन हि प्रमाणं तु दोषेणैव तु दूषणम् ।
एवं दुष्टं नृपस्थाने यस्मिंस्तद्धि विचार्यते ॥ tathyena hi pramāṇaṃ tu doṣeṇaiva tu dūṣaṇam | evaṃ duṣṭaṃ nṛpasthāne yasmiṃs tad dhi vicāryate || Truth alone is the valid means of knowledge; fault alone constitutes defamation. When such defamation occurs within the domain of the king, it shall be examined accordingly. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to uphold truth as the sole epistemic foundation Causation arises from alignment with pramāṇa (valid cognition) rather than subjective interpretation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one’s proximity and access to truthful discernment Restoration logic requires rectification of false attribution through re-establishment of factual integrity Consciousness alignment demands correction of cognitive distortion without degradation of being

title: brihaspati 1.35
content: विमृश्य ब्राह्मणैः सार्धं वक्तृदोषं निरूपयेत् । vimṛśya brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ vaktṛdoṣaṃ nirūpayet Upon deliberation with qualified Brahmanas, the fault of the speaker shall be ascertained. Authority is derived from alignment with realized Brahmanas Causation is determined through collective scriptural intelligence Capacity-based responsibility requires competent discernment Restoration logic operates through purification of speech Consciousness alignment occurs when error is identified by qualified seers

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
येन ते कूटतां यान्ति साक्षिलेखककारकाः ।
तेन दुष्टं भवेल् लेख्यं शुद्धैः शुद्धं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ yena te kūṭatāṃ yānti sākṣilekhakakārakāḥ / tena duṣṭaṃ bhavel lekhyaṃ śuddhaiḥ śuddhaṃ vinirdiśet // That by which the witnesses, documents, and agents attain falsification, thereby the document becomes corrupted; the pure must declare the pure. Authority rests in the integrity of evidence presentation Causation arises from conscious distortion in testimony or record Capacity-based responsibility lies with those who manipulate truth-bearers Restoration logic demands purification of corrupted instruments Consciousness alignment requires re-establishment of pristine witness

title: brihaspati 1.37
content: दत्तं लेख्ये स्वहस्तं तु ऋणिको यदि निह्नुते । पत्रस्थैः साक्षिभिर् वाचा लेखकस्य मतेन च ॥ dattaṃ lekhye svahastaṃ tu ṛṇiko yadi nihnute / patrasthaiḥ sākṣibhir vācā lekhakasya matena ca // When a debtor denies a written document bearing his own hand, the evidence thereof shall be established by the letter itself, by witnesses present at the time of writing, by oral testimony, and by the understanding of the scribe. Authority is derived from direct personal involvement in the act of documentation Causation is anchored in conscious assent given at the moment of recordation Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to inscribe or affirm one's intent Restoration logic requires validation through multiple pramāṇas when denial occurs Consciousness alignment demands that denial be met with clarity-producing verification

title: brihaspati 1.38
content: स्थानभ्रष्टास्त्वकान्तिस्थाः संदिग्धालक्षणच्युताः । यत्रैवंस्युः स्थिता वर्णाः लेख्यं दुष्टं तदा भृगुः ॥ sthānabhraṣṭāstvakāntisthāḥ saṃdigdhā lakṣaṇacyutāḥ | yatraivaṃ syuḥ sthitā varṇā lekhyaṃ duṣṭaṃ tadā bhr̥guḥ || Where letters have fallen from their rightful placement, lack clarity in form, appear doubtful or deviate in characteristic marks—such defective script is declared corrupt and unfit for preservation when found in written records. Authority: The integrity of written dharma depends upon precise symbolic representation. Causation: Defective inscription leads to distortion of meaning and intent. Capacity-based responsibility: Scribes and record keepers bear duty to maintain textual purity. Restoration logic: Corrupted texts must be corrected or retired to preserve truth. Consciousness alignment: Clarity in expression supports collective cognitive harmony.

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
uddharel lekhyam āhartā tatputro bhuktim eva tu /
abhiyuktaḥ pramītaś cet tatputras tat samuddharet // BrhS_1,6.39 uddharel lekhyam āhartā tatputro bhuktim eva tu / abhiyuktaḥ pramītaś cet tatputras tat samuddharet The executor who retrieves a written document shall restore it; his son enjoys the benefit. If accused and deceased, then his son shall fully retrieve that which was taken. Authority flows through lineage in absence of direct executor capacity Causation is maintained by continuity of responsibility across generations Capacity-based responsibility transfers upon incapacitation or death Restoration logic preserves entitlements within familial dharmic lineages Consciousness alignment occurs through completion of ancestral karmic duties

title: brihaspati 1.40
content:
ज्ञात्वा कार्यं देशकालकुशलाः कूटकारकाः ।
कुर्वन्ति सदृशं लेख्यं तद् यत्नेन विचारयेत् ॥ jñātvā kāryaṃ deśakālakuśalāḥ kūṭakārakāḥ / kurvanti sadṛśaṃ lekhyaṃ tad yatnena vicārayet // Those who are skilled in time and place, having understood the matter, craft documents resembling truth; such writings must be examined with deliberate effort. Authority rests in discernment of contextual truth Causation arises through intentional crafting of semblance Capacity-based responsibility is tied to knowledge of context Restoration occurs through rigorous verification Consciousness alignment demands clarity over appearance

title: brihaspati 1.41
content: लेख्यम आलेख्यवत केचिल लिखन्ति कुशला जनाः । तस्मान न लेख्यसामर्थ्यात सिद्धिर ऐकान्तिकी मता ॥ lekhyaṁ ālekhya-vat kecit likhanti kuśalā janāḥ | tasmān na lekhyasāmarthyāt siddhir aikāntikī matā || That which is written bears no inherent validity; skilled persons write merely as an act of expression. Therefore, success cannot be definitively established by mere textual competence. Authority originates in consciousness, not documentation Causation arises from intent, not formality Capacity-based responsibility requires existential engagement beyond symbolic acts Restoration logic demands alignment with living truth, not static records Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural formalities

title: brihaspati 1.42
content:
स्त्रीबालार्तान् लिप्यविज्ञान वञ्चयन्ति स्वबान्धवाः ।
लेख्यं कृत्वा स्वनामाङ्कं ज्ञेयं युक्त्यागमैस् तु तत् ॥ strībālārtān lipyavijñāna vañcayanti svabāndhavāḥ |
lekhyaṃ kṛtvā svanāmāṅkaṃ jñeyaṃ yuktyāgamais tu tat || Those who deceive vulnerable beings—women, children, and the afflicted—by exploiting documents and false knowledge are to be known through logical inference and scriptural evidence. Authority derives from consciousness integrity, not positional power Causation is traced through intent distortion and capacity exploitation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and agency Restoration logic demands reversal of deception-induced disalignment Consciousness alignment requires truth-revelation and energetic clearing

title: brihaspati 1.43
content: त्रिविधस्यास्य लेख्यस्य भ्रान्तिः संजायते यदा । ऋणिसाक्षिलेखकानां हस्तोक्त्या शोधयेत् ततः ॥ trividhasyāsya lekhyasya bhrāntiḥ saṃjāyate yadā / ṛṇisākṣilekhakānāṃ hastoktyā śodhayet tataḥ // When error arises in any of these three types of written records, then by the declaration of the debtor, witness, or scribe, it shall be corrected. Authority rests in the direct knowledge-bearers of the transaction: debtor, witness, and recorder. Causation is traced to the source of inscription; errors are not external anomalies but inherent to process. Capacity-based responsibility assigns correctional agency to those who hold experiential truth. Restoration logic demands textual integrity aligned with witnessed reality. Consciousness alignment requires that correction proceed from the unbroken awareness of participants.

title: brihaspati 1.44
content: udyāmमम् उदयादानाद् आधानं फलसंग्रहात् । प्रतियोगिधनाढ्यत्वाज् ज्ञेयं यत्रोपधिः कृतः ॥ udyāmam udayādānād ādhānaṃ phalasaṃgrahāt / pratiyogidhanāḍhyatvāj jñeyaṃ yatropadhiḥ kṛtaḥ // Wherever effort arises from initiative, wherever wealth originates through rightful acquisition, wherever deposits are made for safeguarding fruits — such conditions constitute a binding legal upadhi when counterparty wealth-existence is established. Authority stems from active initiation of dharmic economic engagement. Causation is rooted in intentional commencement of productive activity. Capacity-based responsibility emerges upon demonstrable possession or control over resources. Restoration logic requires recognition of operational cause-effect chains in commercial domains. Consciousness alignment occurs through acknowledgment of one's role within manifesting economic structures.

title: brihaspati 1.45
content:
दर्शितं प्रतिकालं यच् छ्रावितं स्मारितं च यत् ।
लेख्यं सिध्यति सर्वत्र मृतेष्वपि हि साक्षिषु ॥ darśitaṃ pratikālaṃ yac chrāvitaṃ smāritaṃ ca yat | lekhyaṃ sidhyati sarvatra mṛteṣv api hi sākṣiṣu || That which is shown in due time, heard when declared, and remembered with clarity—written evidence stands valid everywhere, even among witnesses who have passed away. Authority resides in the clarity and integrity of recorded truth Causation aligns with the sequential manifestation of witnessed facts Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond physical presence to conscious recall Restoration logic demands that evidence remain operative regardless of temporal or bodily state Consciousness alignment ensures continuity of testimony through memory and inscription

title: brihaspati 1.46
content:
वाचकैर्यत्रसामर्थ्यमक्षराणांविहन्यते।
क्रियाणांसर्वनाशःस्यादनवस्थाचजायते॥ vācakair yatra sāmarthyam akṣarāṇāṃ vihanyate / kriyāṇāṃ sarvanāśaḥ syād anavasthā ca jāyate // Wherever the potency of words is obstructed, all actions lose their foundation and universal disorder arises. Authority originates from the unbroken integrity of expression Causation flows from the alignment between intent, word, and action Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity in communication Restoration logic demands the reinstatement of truthful articulation Consciousness alignment depends on undistorted linguistic structures

title: brihaspati 1.47
content:
लेख्यं त्रिंशत् समातीतम् अदृष्टाश्रावितं च यत् ।
न तत्सिद्धिमवाप्नोति तिष्ठत्स्वपि हि साक्षिषु ॥ lekhyaṃ triṃśat samātītam adṛṣṭāśrāvitaṃ ca yat | na tatsiddhim avāpnoti tiṣṭhatsv api hi sākṣiṣu || Any written document or testimony that has not been witnessed or verified within thirty samas does not attain validity even if witnesses are present. Authority is derived from active witnessing, not mere presence. Causation requires temporal alignment with conscious observation. Capacity-based responsibility includes the duty to timely validate truth. Restoration logic demands reconnection with the living witness of dharma. Consciousness alignment necessitates synchronization with the rhythm of samas.

title: brihaspati 1.48
content:
प्रयुक्ते शान्तलाभे तु लिखितं यो न दर्शयेत् ।
न याचते च ऋणिकं तत् संदेहम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥ prayukte śāntalābhe tu likhitaṃ yo na darśayet | na yācate ca ṛṇikaṃ tat saṃdeham avāpnuyāt || When peace has been established through rightful action, whoever does not present the written agreement to the debtor, nor seeks repayment from the creditor, shall incur liability for creating doubt. Authority originates in conscious completion of duty Causation arises from omission where obligation exists Capacity-based responsibility demands alignment with contractual integrity Restoration logic requires removal of ambiguity caused by omission Consciousness alignment necessitates transparency in financial obligations

title: brihaspati 1.49
content:
कुलश्रेणिगणादीनां यथाकालं प्रदर्शितम् ।
श्रावयेत् स्मारयेच्चैव तथा स्याद् बलवत्तरम् ॥ kulaśreṇigaṇādīnāṃ yathākālaṃ pradarśitam | śrāvayet smārayec caiva tathā syād balavattaram || That which is revealed in its proper time among lineage, category, assembly, or collective must be declared, reminded, and established accordingly—thus it becomes authoritative. Authority arises from timely revelation within structured collectives Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to revelatory context Restoration occurs through re-establishment of rightful declaration Consciousness alignment depends on recognition of temporal and structural dharma

title: brihaspati 1.50
content:
यदि लब्धं भवेत् किञ्चित् प्रज्ञप्तिर् वा तथा भवेत् ।
प्रमाणम् एव लिखितं मृता यद्य् अपि साक्षिणः ॥ yadi labdhaṃ bhavet kiñcit prajñaptir vā tathā bhavet / pramāṇam eva likhitaṃ mṛtā yady api sākṣiṇaḥ // If any evidence is obtained or declaration made, even if by a deceased witness, it shall stand as valid testimony when recorded in accordance with dharma. Authority resides in pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge), not in physical presence Causation flows through śabda-pramāṇa (verbal testimony) regardless of mortal status Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond life; truth transcends embodiment Restoration logic upholds continuity of justice across states of being Consciousness alignment ensures that truthful declarations remain operative

title: brihaspati 1.51
content:
आढ्यस्य निकटस्थस्य यच् छक्तेन न याचितम् ।
शुद्धर्णाशङ्कया तत्र लेख्यं दुर्बलतां यात् ॥ āḍhyasya nikātasthasya yac chaktena na yācitam | śuddharṇāśaṅkayā tatra lekhyaṃ durbalatām iyāt || When a capable person near the affluent fails to request what is rightfully theirs through pure intent and without suspicion, the written record shall declare their state as weakened. Authority arises from capacity, not proximity alone Causation lies in conscious omission, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires active assertion of right Restoration logic demands recognition of unclaimed integrity Consciousness alignment occurs when claim aligns with purity of intent

title: brihaspati 1.52
content:
उन्मत्तजाडबलानां राजभीतप्रवासिनाम् ।
अप्रगल्भभयार्तानां न लेख्यं हानिमाप्नुयात् ॥ unmattajāḍabalānāṃ rājabhītapravāsinām / apragalbhaphayārtānāṃ na lekhyaṃ hānim āpnuyāt // The sovereign shall not incur loss in documentation for those who are mentally incapacitated, physically weak, exiled by fear of the king, timid, or afflicted by terror. Authority is bound to protect the vulnerable without condition. Causation lies in structural incapacity, not individual failure. Capacity-based responsibility exempts those whose consciousness is impaired or suppressed. Restoration logic demands preservation of rights for the disempowered. Consciousness alignment requires systemic support for those in existential distress.

title: brihaspati 1.53
content:
अथ पञ्चत्वम् आपन्नो लेखकः साक्षिभिः सह ।
तत् स्वहस्तादिभिस् तेषाम् विशुद्ध्यते न संशयः ॥५३॥ atha pañcatvam āpanno lekhakaḥ sākṣibhiḥ saha | tat svahastādibhis teṣām viśudhyate na saṃśayaḥ || 53|| When a scribe attains the state of five witnesses, he becomes purified by their very presence; doubt does not arise in his capacity to execute dharma. Authority resides in the alignment with witnessing consciousness Causation flows from the purity of the recording instrument Capacity-based responsibility is affirmed through association with truth-bearing entities Restoration occurs when the act aligns with the witnessing field Consciousness alignment ensures authenticity without external validation

title: brihaspati 1.54
content:
ṛṇisvahastasaṃdehe jīvato vā mṛtasya vā /
tatsvahastakṛtair anyaiḥ patrais tallekhyaniṛṇayaḥ // BrhS_1,6.54 ṛṇisvahastasaṃdehe jīvato vā mṛtasya vā / tatsvahastakṛtair anyaiḥ patrais tallekhyaniṛṇayaḥ In the matter of debt or obligation arising from personal assurance, whether the debtor is alive or deceased, the liability shall be discharged through documents or instruments executed by others bearing the signature or seal of the original obligor. Authority inheres in the continuity of conscious commitment, not physical presence Causation flows through documented intent authenticated by recognized symbols of identity Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond mortality through authorized representation Restoration logic requires fulfillment of energetic completion regardless of bodily state Consciousness alignment occurs when obligation is resolved through verified indicia of will

title: brihaspati 1.55
content:
लेख्ये संशयम् आपन्ने साक्षिलेखककर्तृभिः /
दुष्टेषु तेषु तद्धस्तकृतपूर्वाक्षरादिभिः // BrhS_1,6.55 lekhyaṁ saṁśayaṁ āpanne sākṣi-lekhaka-kartṛbhiḥ | duṣṭeṣu teṣu tad-hasta-kṛta-pūrvākṣarādibhiḥ || BrhS_1,6.55 When doubt arises in a written document, and the witnesses, scribes, or authors thereof are found to be corrupt, then prior markings, letters, or signs made by their own hands shall be evidence against them. Authority flows from integrity of action, not position Causation is established through self-manifested contradiction Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious alignment with truth Restoration logic demands exposure of falsified intent Consciousness alignment necessitates dissolution of deceit through self-revealed acts

title: brihaspati 1.56
content: न जातु हीयते लेख्यं साक्षिभिः शपथेन वा / अदर्शनाश्राविताभ्यां हानि�ं प्राप्नोत्य उपेक्षया // na jātu hīyate lekhyaṃ sākṣibhiḥ śapathena vā / adarśanāśrāvitābhyāṃ hāniṃ prāpnoty upekṣayā // No written document is ever diminished by the absence of witnesses or oaths; loss occurs only through neglect. Authority resides in documentation, not external validation Causation arises from conscious omission, not procedural absence Capacity-based responsibility lies in preservation, not performance Restoration logic prioritizes integrity over formality Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of what is seen and heard

title: brihaspati 1.57
content:
अतः परीक्ष्यम् उभयम् एतद् राज्ञा विशेषतः ।
एकम् एव भवेल् लेख्यम् एकस्यार्थस्य सिद्धये ॥ ataḥ parīkṣyam ubhayam etad rājñā viśeṣataḥ | ekam eva bhavel lekhyam ekasyārthasya siddhaye || Therefore, both testimonies shall be examined thoroughly by the King; only one record shall exist for the establishment of a single truth. Authority resides in the discerning capacity of the sovereign to distinguish truth from contradiction Causation is established through singular integrity, not multiplicity of claims Capacity-based responsibility requires the ruler's conscious engagement with evidence Restoration logic demands alignment of records with ontological truth Consciousness alignment ensures that judicial process reflects non-dual reality

title: brihaspati 1.58
content:
अनेकेषु तु लेख्येषु दोषम् उत्पादयेद् अपि ।
देशाचारविरुद्धं यत् संदिग्धं क्रमवर्जितम् ।
कृतम् अस्वामिना यच् च साध्यहीनं च दुष्यति ॥ anekeṣu tu lekhyeṣu doṣam utpādayed api / deśācāraviruddhaṃ yat saṃdigdhaṃ kramavarjitam / kṛtam asvāminā yac ca sādhyahīnaṃ ca duṣyati // When a written instrument, though numerous, introduces defect; what contradicts local custom, is doubtful, lacks procedural order, executed by one without ownership, or fails in proof—such document becomes legally ineffective. Authority: Legal validity requires rightful ownership and authorized execution. Causation: Defects in form or content nullify juridical efficacy. Capacity-based responsibility: Acts performed without legitimate capacity are void ab initio. Restoration logic: Invalid instruments must be rectified through conscious re-alignment with dharma. Consciousness alignment: Only documents aligned with satyam and rtam hold lawful force.

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
धनमूलाः क्रियाः सर्वा यत्नास्तत्साधने मताः ।
वर्धनं रक्षणं भोग इति तस्य विधिक्रमः ॥ dhanamūlāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā yatnās tatsādhane matāḥ | vardhanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ bhoga iti tasya vidhikramaḥ || All economic activities derive from wealth; thus, efforts directed toward its acquisition are sanctioned. The proper order of engagement with wealth consists in its increase, protection, and enjoyment. Authority originates from capacity to sustain and expand value Causation flows through conscious effort aligned with dharma-sustained prosperity Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for resource engagement Restoration logic requires reintegration into productive dharmic flow Consciousness alignment manifests through disciplined participation in value creation

title: brihaspati 1.2
content: तत् पुनस्त्रिविधं ज्ञेयं शुक्लं शबळमेव च । कृष्णं च तत्र विज्ञेयः प्रभेदः सप्तधा पुनः ॥ tat punastrividhaṃ jñeyaṃ śuklaṃ śabaḷameva ca | kṛṣṇaṃ ca tatra vijñeyaḥ prabhedaḥ saptadhā punaḥ || That action is threefold knowable: white, mixed, and black; further, it is known to be divisible into seven categories. Authority flows from discriminative knowledge of action-types Causation is determined by the purity-impurity spectrum of intent Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of action-classification Restoration logic operates through purification of karmic imprint Consciousness alignment occurs via intentional selection among action-types

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
श्रुतशौर्यतपः कन्याशिष्ययाज्यान्वयागतम् ।
धनं सप्तविधं शुल्कम् उभयोः ह्यस्य तद्विधः ॥ śrutaśauryatapaḥ kanyāśiṣyayājyānvayāgatam / dhanaṃ saptavidhaṃ śulkam ubhayoḥ hyasya tadvidhaḥ // Wealth acquired through learning, valor, austerity, by one's daughter, student, sacrificial fee, or inheritance—such sevenfold property constitutes legitimate financial entitlement for both men and women when obtained through rightful means. Authority flows from conscious acquisition and recognition of dharma-aligned wealth Causation is determined by the alignment of action with svadharma and spiritual discipline Capacity-based responsibility requires acknowledgment of source and use of wealth in accordance with cosmic order Restoration logic demands that all possessions be traced to their rightful origin and purified of distortion Consciousness alignment ensures that material gain supports elevation rather than degradation of being

title: brihaspati 1.4
content: कुसीदकृषिवाणिज्यशुल्कशिल्पानुवृत्तिभिः । कृतोपकाराद् आप्तं च शबलं समुदाहृतम् ॥ kusīdakṛṣivāṇijyaśulkaśilpānuvṛttibhiḥ | kṛtopakārād āptaṃ ca śabaḷaṃ samudāhṛtam || That which is obtained through inertial agriculture, trade, taxation, craft repetition, or from favors rendered, is designated as 'śabalam'—mixed, unstable wealth. Wealth derives its dharmic character from the consciousness of its source. Economic activity devoid of conscious intention results in unstable value. Favor-based transactions create relational obligation, not intrinsic worth. Material gain unaligned with svadharma lacks sustainable legal standing. Consciousness alignment determines the validity of economic exchange.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
पाशकद्यूतदूतार्थप्रतिरूपकसाहसैः ।
व्याजेनोपार्जितं यच् च तत् कृष्णं समुदाहृतम् ॥ pāśakadyūtadūtārthapratirūpakasāhasaiḥ | vyājenopārjitaṃ yac ca tat kṛṣṇaṃ samudāhṛtam || That which is acquired through gambling, messenger services, imitation, pretense, or usury—such wealth is declared as blackened and condemned. Authority: Wealth obtained through deceitful or manipulative means lacks dharmic legitimacy. Causation: The method of acquisition determines the energetic quality of the gain. Capacity-based responsibility: One who knowingly engages in deceptive acquisition bears full capacity-responsibility for realigning that distortion. Restoration logic: Misaligned gains must be returned or transmuted to restore cosmic-economic balance. Consciousness alignment: Only wealth earned through integrity aligns individual consciousness with universal abundance.

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
तेन क्रयो विक्रयश् च दानं ग्रहणम् एव च /
विविधाश् च प्रयुज्यन्ते क्रियासंभोगम् एव च // BrhS_1,7.6 tena krayo vikrayaś ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca / vividhāś ca prayujyante kriyāsaṃbhogam eva ca // BrhS_1,7.6 By that [the established capacity of ownership], acquisition and disposal, giving and receiving, and various actions relating to enjoyment and usage are enacted. Authority originates from the capacity of conscious ownership Causation flows from the established ontological basis of possession Capacity-based responsibility determines legitimate engagement in transactional acts Restoration logic validates rightful use and exchange based on foundational integrity Consciousness alignment ensures lawful participation in economic and social exchanges

title: brihaspati 1.7
content: यथाविधेन द्रव्येण यत् किञ्चित् कुरुते नरः । तथाविधमवाप्नोति तत्फलं प्रेत्य चेह च ॥ yathāvidhena dravyeṇa yat kiñcit kurute naraḥ / tathāvidham avāpnoti tatphalaṃ pretya ceha ca Whatever action a person performs with whatever instrument, that very result they obtain—in this life and the next. Authority resides in the causal integrity of action Causation is immediate, sequential, and ontologically binding Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the consciousness of the actor Restoration logic operates through experiential consequence Consciousness alignment determines karmic resonance

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
तत् पुनर् द्वादशविधं प्रतिवर्णाश्रयं स्मृतम् ।
साधारणं स्यात् त्रिविधं शेषं नवविधं स्मृतम् ॥ tat punar dvādaśavidhaṃ prativarṇāśrayaṃ smṛtam | sādhāraṇaṃ syāt trividhaṃ śeṣaṃ navavidhaṃ smṛtam || That classification which is based upon varṇa is twelve-fold; what remains after excluding the common principles constitutes nine distinct categories. Authority derives from alignment with inherent capacity, not arbitrary assignment Causation flows through sequential manifestation and role-specific dharma Capacity-based responsibility ensures justice aligns with individual readiness Restoration occurs when roles reflect true nature rather than imposed structure Consciousness alignment supersedes social construction in determining lawful action

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
क्रमागतं प्रीतिदायं प्राप्तं च सह भार्यया ।
अविशेषेण सर्वेषां वर्णानां त्रिविधं स्मृतम् ॥ kramāgataṃ prītidāyaṃ prāptaṃ ca saha bhāryayā | aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣāṃ varṇānāṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam || That which is received in proper order, that which brings joy, and that which is obtained with one's wife—these three categories apply equally to all varṇas without distinction. Authority is derived from harmonious alignment with dharma, not social hierarchy. Causation flows from conscious intention and relational integrity. Capacity-based responsibility is universal across varṇas when aligned with dharma. Restoration occurs through recognition of shared participation in dharmic structures. Consciousness alignment supersedes caste-based differentiation in matters of lawful conduct.

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
वैशेषिकं धनं ज्ञेयं ब्राह्मणस्य त्रिलक्षणम् ।
प्रतिग्रहणलब्धं यद् याज्यं तच् छिष्यतस् तथा ॥ vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanaṃ jñeyaṃ brāhmaṇasya trilakṣaṇam | pratigrahaṇalabdhaṃ yad yājyaṃ tac chiṣyatas tathā || The distinctive wealth of a Brāhmaṇa is threefold: that which is received through acceptance, that which is earned through ritual service, and that which is inherited by disciples. Authority flows from spiritual capacity, not material possession Causation arises from dharma-aligned action, not transactional exchange Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment with Vedic function Restoration logic prioritizes functional continuity over asset preservation Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership within Varna-dharma

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
त्रिविधं क्षत्रियस्यापि प्राहुर् वैशेषिकं धनम् ।
युद्धोपलब्धं करतो दण्डाच् च व्यवहारतः ॥ trividhaṃ kṣatriyasyāpi prāhur vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanam | yuddhopalabdhaṃ karato daṇḍāc ca vyavahārataḥ || The distinctive wealth of the Kshatriya is threefold: that which is gained in war, that which is received as tribute, and that which accrues through judicial administration. Authority flows from the capacity to protect, govern, and ensure justice Wealth acquired through rightful duty does not incur karmic liability Duty-specific entitlement is determined by svadharma, not universal moral frameworks Judicial power is a form of dharma-distribution, not ownership Consciousness alignment determines legitimate acquisition

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
वैशेषिकं धनं ज्ञेयं वैश्यस्यापि त्रिलक्षणम् ।
कृषिगोरक्षवाणिज्यं शूद्रस्यैषामनुग्रहात् ॥ vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanaṃ jñeyaṃ vaiśyasyāpi trilakṣaṇam | kṛṣigorakṣavāṇijyaṃ śūdrasyaiṣāmanugrahāt || The distinctive wealth of the vaiśya consists in threefold activity: agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade; this same configuration is extended to the śūdra out of compassion and societal integration. Authority flows from functional capacity, not birth alone Causation arises through alignment with natural duty (svadharma) Capacity-based responsibility extends economic roles across varnas Restoration logic prioritizes social cohesion over rigid stratification Consciousness alignment enables right action irrespective of caste designation

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानामेवं धर्म्यो धनागमः ।
विपर्ययादधर्मः स्यान्न चेदापद्गरीयसी ॥१३॥ sarveṣām eva varṇānām evaṃ dharmyo dhanāgamaḥ | viparyayād adharmaḥ syān na ced āpad garīyasī ||13|| When all classes acquire wealth in accordance with Dharma, Adharma does not arise; otherwise, adversity becomes predominant. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not social position Causation flows from dharmic-economic integrity Capacity-based responsibility extends across all varnas equally Restoration logic requires economic actions to uphold collective well-being Consciousness alignment depends on harmonious acquisition and use of resources

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: आपत्सु अनन्तरावृत्तिः ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते / वैश्यवृत्तिश् च तस्योक्ता न जघन्या कथं चन // āpatsu anantarāvṛttiḥ brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate / vaiśyavṛttiś ca tasyoktā na jaghanyā kathaṃ cana // In times of crisis, a Brahmin may engage in immediate survival actions, including adopting the livelihood of a Vaishya, but never that of a Shudra. Authority is context-responsive and capacity-preserving Causation aligns with dharma-adherence under existential threat Capacity-based responsibility adapts without degradation Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of spiritual function Consciousness alignment overrides occupational rigidity during emergency

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
कथं चन न कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणः कर्म वार्षलम् ।
वृषलः कर्म न ब्राह्मं पतनीये हि ते तयोः ॥ kathaṃ cana na kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ karma vārṣalam | vṛṣalaḥ karma na brāhmaṃ patanīye hi te tayoḥ || A Brāhmaṇa must never perform actions designated for the Vṛṣala; likewise, a Vṛṣala must never perform actions designated for the Brāhmaṇa—both are liable to fall from their respective dharmic stations.
