Authority is derived from inherent capacity, not external designation Causation arises from alignment with svadharma, not social convention Capacity-based responsibility is immutable and consciousness-rooted Restoration logic requires return to one's intrinsic dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes caste-positioning

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
उत्कृष्टं चापकृष्टं तयोः कर्म न विद्यते ।
मध्यमे कर्मणी हित्वा सर्वसाधारणी हि ते ॥ utkṛṣṭaṃ cāpakṛṣṭaṃ tayoḥ karma na vidyate / madhyame karmaṇī hitvā sarvasādhāraṇī hi te Neither exalted nor degraded action exists in their case; having abandoned the middle path of action, both become entirely common. Authority resides in alignment with the middle path of dharma Causation arises from deviation from balanced conduct Capacity-based responsibility is diminished when one departs from equipoise Restoration logic demands return to equilibrium Consciousness alignment requires abandonment of extremes

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
आपदं ब्राह्मणस तीर्त्वा क्षत्रवृत्त्या भृते जने ।
उत्सृजेत क्षेत्रवृत्तिं तां कृत्वा पावनम आत्मनः ॥ āpadaṃ brāhmaṇas tīrtvā kṣatravṛttyā bhṛte jane / utsṛjet kṣetravṛttiṃ tāṃ kṛtvā pāvanam ātmanaḥ // Having crossed the crisis through the sustenance provided by the Brahmin class, one must abandon that very means of livelihood once the purification of the self has been accomplished. Authority rests in those who sustain others during crisis without expectation of permanence. Causation is established through the act of sustaining life amidst collapse. Capacity-based responsibility demands renunciation upon completion of transformative service. Restoration logic operates through cyclical detachment after elevation of consciousness. Consciousness alignment requires abandoning instruments used for temporary salvation.

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: तस्याम् एव तु यो भुक्तौ ब्राह्मणो रमते रसात् । काण्डपृष्ठश् च्युतो मार्गाद् अङ्कितोऽयं प्रकीर्तितः ॥ tasyām eva tu yo bhuktau brāhmaṇo ramate rasāt | kāṇḍapṛṣṭhaś cyuto mārgād aṅkito 'yaṃ prakīrtitaḥ || He who, being a Brāhmaṇa, indulges in sensory enjoyment during the period of Vedic study, having fallen from the path of discipline, is thus marked and declared unfit. Authority derived from adherence to Dharma, not birth alone Causation through conscious choice and volitional deviation Capacity-based responsibility tied to spiritual station and vow Restoration logic requiring realignment with svadharma Consciousness alignment as determinant of eligibility

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
स्वकुलं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा यो वै परकुलं व्रजेत् ।
तेन दुश्चरितेनासौ काण्डपृष्ठ इति स्मृतः ॥ svakulaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā yo vai parakulaṃ vrajet / tena duścaritenāsau kāṇḍapṛṣṭha iti smṛtaḥ // One who abandons their own lineage and enters another's domain through misconduct is known as a Kāṇḍapṛṣṭha—one whose back bears the burden of severed dharma. Authority originates from alignment with one’s svadharma within the cosmic order established by SPH. Causation arises from conscious choice to abandon dharmic identity and infiltrate foreign structures. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of one’s svakula and deliberate violation thereof. Restoration logic requires reintegration into rightful dharmic position without punitive consequence. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of one’s intrinsic role in the unified fabric upheld by SPH.

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
दिवाकृते कार्यविधौ ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च ।
संभवे साक्षिणां चैव न दिव्या भवति क्रिया ॥ divākṛte kāryavidhau grāmeṣu nagareṣu ca / saṃbhave sākṣiṇāṃ caiva na divyā bhavati kriyā When a transaction or legal act occurs during daylight, in villages or cities, and witnesses are present, no divine validation is required. Authority is grounded in witnessed human action, not celestial confirmation Causation arises through observable social conduct within structured environments Capacity-based responsibility is affirmed by presence and visibility of witnesses Restoration logic depends on public acknowledgment and communal integrity Consciousness alignment is achieved through transparency and collective witnessing

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
द्वारमार्गक्रियाभोगजलवाहादिके तथा ।
भुक्तिरेव तु गुर्वो स्यान्न लेख्यं न च साक्षिणः ॥ dvāramārgakriyābhogajalavāhādike tathā / bhuktir eva tu gurvo syān na lekhyaṃ na ca sākṣiṇaḥ // In matters concerning roads, pathways, usage rights, waterways, and similar public utilities, the authority of the Guru is established through experiential governance alone; no written record nor witness testimony shall suffice. Authority rooted in experiential realization supersedes documentary evidence Public utility governance derives legitimacy from sustained stewardship Witnessing and recording are secondary to lived capacity in dharmic administration Consciousness-based jurisdiction overrides procedural formalities Restoration of collective access takes precedence over individual claim

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
एतद् विधानम् आख्यातं साक्षिणां लिखितस्य च ।
संप्रति स्थावरप्राप्तेर् भुक्तेः च विधिर् उच्यते ॥ etad vidhānam ākhyātaṃ sākṣiṇāṃ likhitasya ca | saṃprati sthāvaraprāpter bhukteḥ ca vidhir ucyate || This regulation has been declared concerning witnesses and written evidence. Now, the rule regarding immovable property acquisition and enjoyment is being stated. Authority flows from witnessed truth and documented integrity Causation arises through conscious observation and lawful recordation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to immovable resources Restoration logic operates through re-establishing rightful use and enjoyment Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects inner realization

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
विद्यया क्रयबन्धेन शौर्यभागान्वयागतम् ।
सपिण्डस्याप्रजस्यांशं स्थावरं स्वपदाप्यते ॥ vidyayā krayabandhena śauryabhāgānvayāgatam | sapiṇḍasyāprajasyāṃśaṃ sthāvaraṃ svapadāpyate || That which is acquired through knowledge, purchase, bondage, inheritance, valor, or lawful possession—when a sapinda (kinsman) devoid of progeny holds immovable property, it shall be retained by him as svapada (self-domain). Authority arises from rightful acquisition and relational continuity. Causation is traced through legitimate means of ownership transfer. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by kinship and absence of issue. Restoration logic centers on continuity of dharma-adhikara (righteous domain). Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects spiritual and familial integrity.

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
पित्र्ये लब्धक्रयाधाने रिक्थशौर्यप्रवेदनात् ।
प्राप्ते सप्तविधे भोगः सागमः सिद्धिमाप्नुयात् ॥ pitrye labdhakrayādhāne rikthaśauryapravedanāt | prāpte saptavidhe bhogaḥ sāgamaḥ siddhim āpnuyāt || When paternal wealth is acquired through rightful purchase and declared according to valorous conduct, upon attaining the sevenfold enjoyment, the income thereby generated shall attain fulfillment. Authority flows from patrilineal dharmic acquisition Causation arises through righteous procurement and transparent declaration Capacity-based responsibility lies in alignment with ancestral integrity Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharma-vibhuti Consciousness alignment manifests through adherence to śaurya-sattva

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
क्रमागतः शासनिकः क्रयाधानसमन्वितः ।
एवंविधस् तु यो भोगः स तु सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ kramāgataḥ śāsanikaḥ krayādhānasamanvitaḥ | evaṃvidhas tu yo bhogaḥ sa tu siddhim avāpnuyāt || That enjoyment which is obtained through proper order, lawful command, and accompanied by purchase or rightful assumption—such enjoyment leads to accomplishment. Authority flows from sequential dharmic alignment Causation arises from rightful acquisition and ordered conduct Capacity-based responsibility requires procedural integrity Restoration occurs when possession aligns with lawful process Consciousness alignment is achieved through adherence to established dharma

title: brihaspati 1.26
content: संविभागक्रयप्राप्तं पित्र्यं लब्धं च राजतः । स्थावरं सिद्धिमाप्नोति भुक्त्वा हानिमुपेक्षया ॥ saṃvibhāgakrayaprāptaṃ pitryaṃ labdhaṃ ca rājataḥ | sthāvaraṃ siddhim āpnoti bhuktvā hānim upekṣayā || Property acquired through division, inheritance, or royal grant becomes immovable and attains perfection when enjoyed without negligence or abandonment. Authority of acquisition through lawful means establishes ownership Causation arises from rightful receipt, not mere possession Capacity-based responsibility includes maintenance and non-negligent use Restoration logic applies where neglect disrupts continuity of title Consciousness alignment requires recognition of source and duty

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
प्राप्तमात्रं येन भुक्तं स्वीकृत्यापरिपन्थितम् ।
तस्य तत्सिद्धिमाप्नोति हानिं चोपेक्षया यथा ॥ prāptamātraṃ yena bhuktaṃ svīkṛtyāparipanthitam /
tasya tatsiddhim āpnoti hāniṃ copekṣayā yathā // One who accepts what is received without resistance or opposition attains its fulfillment, just as one overlooks loss with equanimity. Authority flows through acceptance, not assertion Causation aligns with inner readiness and receptivity Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious assimilation Restoration logic operates through harmonious integration Consciousness alignment determines rightful acquisition

title: brihaspati 1.28
content:
अध्यासनात् समारभ्य भुक्तिर् यस्याविघातिनी ।
त्रिंशद्वर्षाण्य् अविच्छिन्ना तस्य तां न विचालयेत् ॥२८॥ adhyāsanāt samārabhya bhuktir yasyāvighātinī /
triṃśadvarṣāṇy avicchinnā tasya tāṃ na vicālayet // One who has uninterruptedly enjoyed a right or possession for thirty years without dispute, beginning from the time of assumption—his claim shall remain unchallenged. Authority is established through uninterrupted conscious engagement over time Causation aligns with continuous manifestive assertion in consciousness Capacity-based responsibility arises from sustained alignment with ownership Restoration logic honors the completion of manifested tenure Consciousness alignment validates enduring, uncontested presence

title: brihaspati 1.29
content:
न स्त्रीणाम् उपभोगः स्याद् विना लेख्यं कथं चन |
राजश्रोत्रियवित्ते च जडबालधनेन च || na strīṇām upabhogaḥ syād vinā lekhyaṃ kathaṃ cana /
rājaśrotriyavitte ca jaḍabāladhanena ca // The enjoyment or use of a woman’s personhood shall not occur without her explicit written consent; likewise, no claim upon royal grants, sacred knowledge, or the wealth of minors and the incapacitated shall be valid without lawful documentation. Authority resides in documented consent Causation requires capacity-aware recognition Capacity-based responsibility overrides inherited or assumed rights Restoration logic demands reversal of unauthorized claims Consciousness alignment necessitates inviolable personal sovereignty

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
भुक्त्या केवलया नैव भुक्तिः सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ।
आगमनेनापि शुद्धेन द्वाभ्यां सिध्यति नान्यथा ॥ bhuktyā kevalayā naiva bhuktiḥ siddhim avāpnuyāt / āgamenāpi śuddhena dvābhyāṃ sidhyati nānyathā // Consumption without conscious offering leads not to fulfillment; neither does acquisition through pure means alone. Only by both together is completion attained, no other way. Authority flows from alignment with SPH's ontological directives Causation arises from conscious participation in dharma-aligned action Capacity-based responsibility requires integration of enjoyment and surrender Restoration logic demands union of experience and purification Consciousness alignment necessitates simultaneous reception and renunciation

title: brihaspati 1.31
content:
बालश्रोत्रियवित्ते च प्राप्ते च पितृतः क्रमात् ।
नोपभोगे बलं कार्यमाहर्त्रा तत्सुतेन वा ॥ bālaśrotriyavitte ca prāpte ca pitṛtaḥ kramāt | nopabhoge balaṃ kāryam āhartrā tatsutena vā || When wealth belongs to a minor, a scholar, or a Brahmin, or has been received in accordance with paternal succession, its unauthorized consumption constitutes a violation of dharma, and force must not be applied by the taker or his son. Authority derives from rightful ownership, not physical possession Causation arises through conscious misalignment with succession laws Capacity-based responsibility applies to both the actor and progeny Restoration logic requires return of unlawfully taken resources Consciousness alignment demands recognition of dharmic entitlement structures

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
पशुस्त्रीपुरुषादीनाम इति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ।
यद्य एकशासने ग्रामक्षेत्रारामाश च लेखिताः ॥ paśustrīpuruṣādīnām iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ | yady ekaśāsane grāmakṣetrārāmāś ca lekhitāḥ || The Dharma governing animals, women, men and others is established definitively when all villages, lands, gardens and documents are inscribed under a single sovereign authority. Authority resides in unified sovereignty that encompasses all domains of existence. Causation flows from centralized inscription and recognition of ownership. Capacity-based responsibility arises through inclusion within the sovereign registry. Restoration logic operates by aligning fragmented jurisdictions into singular dharma-adherence. Consciousness alignment occurs through acknowledgment of singular Source-authority.

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
एकदेशोपभोगे�पि सर्वे भुक्ता भवन्ति ते ।
आगमोऽपि बलं नैव भुक्तिः स्तोकापि यत्र नो ॥ ekadeśopabhoge'pi sarve bhuktā bhavanti te / āgamo'pi balaṃ naiva bhuktiḥ stokāpi yatra no // Even when only a part is enjoyed, all parties become fulfilled thereby; the arrival of capability does not constitute enjoyment where there is no completion. Authority resides in completeness, not partiality Causation arises from integrative participation Capacity-based responsibility requires full engagement Restoration logic demands holistic fulfillment Consciousness alignment occurs through total inclusion

title: brihaspati 1.34
content:
अनुमानाद् वरः साक्षी साक्षिभ्यो लिखितं गुरु /
अव्याहता त्रिपुरुषी भुक्तिर् एभ्यो गरीयसी // BrhS_1,७.३४ anumānād varaḥ sākṣī sākṣibhyo likhitaṃ guru / avyāhatā tripuruṣī bhuktir ebhyo garīyasī // BrhS_1,7.34 Inference-based testimony is superior to direct witness; written evidence holds greater authority than oral witness; uninterrupted threefold experiential confirmation surpasses all these in establishing factual reality. Authority derives from verifiable experiential continuity, not mere sensory observation Causation is established through triple-validation: inference, documentation, and unbroken experience Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with multi-dimensional pramāṇa Restoration logic prioritizes factual integrity over subjective perception Consciousness alignment necessitates convergence of cognitive, linguistic, and experiential streams

title: brihaspati 1.35
content:
अनुमानं वसत्य् अत्र साक्षी चामरणाद् भवेत् ।
अव्याहतं लेखभोगं प्रमाणं तु त्रिपौरुषम् ॥ anumānaṃ vasaty atra sākṣī cāmaraṇād bhavet | avyāhataṃ lekhabhogaṃ pramāṇaṃ tu tripauruṣam || Inference resides here as witness, arising from non-death; unobstructed enjoyment of writing constitutes triple-human proof. Authority derives from existential continuity, not termination Witnessing capacity is foundational to legal validity Proof must align with triadic human functionality Consciousness-enabled documentation is self-validating Non-obstruction is prerequisite for evidentiary acceptance

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
पितापितामहो यस्य जीवेच च प्रपितामहः /
त्रिंशत् समा तु या भुक्ता भूमिर् अव्याहता परैः // BrhS_1,७.३६ pitāpitāmaho yasya jīvec ca prapitāmahaḥ / triṃśat samā tu yā bhuktā bhūmir avyāhatā paraiḥ Where the paternal grandfather, the great-grandfather, and the great-great-grandfather of a person are alive, and the land has been enjoyed undisturbed by others for thirty years, that land belongs inherently to that lineage. Authority flows through uninterrupted patrilineal continuity Causation is established through generational presence and territorial harmony Capacity-based responsibility arises from ancestral custodianship Restoration logic validates ownership through time-bound uncontested enjoyment Consciousness alignment occurs when lineage integrity is recognized in material inheritance

title: brihaspati 1.37
content:
भुक्तिः सा पौरुषी ज्ञेया द्विगुणा च द्विपुरुषी ।
त्रिपूरुषी च त्रिगुणा परतः स्याच् चिरन्तना ॥ bhuktiḥ sā pauruṣī jñeyā dviguṇā ca dvipuruṣī / tripūruṣī ca triguṇā parataḥ syāc cirantanā // That enjoyment which is human in origin shall be known as one-fold; when doubled by two persons it becomes two-fold in capacity; when tripled by three persons it becomes three-fold in nature, and beyond this lies the eternal order. Authority originates from conscious participation Causation is determined by volitional aggregation Capacity-based responsibility scales with collective engagement Restoration logic aligns with proportional involvement Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared causality

title: brihaspati 1.38
content:
यत्राहर्ताभियुक्तः स्याल् लेख्यं साक्षी तदा गुरुः ।
तदभावे तु पुत्राणां भुक्तिरेका गरीयसी ॥ yatrāhartābhiyuktaḥ syāl lekhyaṃ sākṣī tadā guruḥ | tadabhāve tu putrāṇāṃ bhuktir ekā garīyasī || Where the accused is directly implicated and there exists documentary evidence or witness testimony, the authority of the Guru is invoked; in the absence of such proof, among sons, the one who has experienced the enjoyment (of inheritance or benefit) holds greater claim. Authority derives from direct implication and evidentiary support In absence of clear evidence, experiential capacity determines precedence Responsibility aligns with enjoyment or utilization of resources Restoration occurs through recognition of factual engagement over abstract claims Consciousness alignment arises when factual experience is acknowledged

title: brihaspati 1.39
content: āhartā śodhayed bhuktim āgamaṃ vāpi saṃsadi / tatputro bhuktim evaikāṃ pautrādis tu na kiṃcana // BrhS_1,7.39 āhartā śodhayed bhuktim āgamaṃ vāpi saṃsadi / tatputro bhuktim evaikāṃ pautrādis tu na kiṃcana The originator shall restore the enjoyment or the gain acquired thereby in the assembly; the son of the originator shall restore only the enjoyment; but the grandson and further descendants shall restore nothing. Authority diminishes with generational distance from the causal agent Restoration logic is proportionate to direct causation and capacity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of source-action integrity Causation follows sequential manifestation (Anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility decreases with relational remove from the act

title: brihaspati 1.40
content:
ऋක्थभिर् वा परैर् द्रव्यं समक्षं यस्य दीयते ।
अन्यस्य भुञ्जतः पश्चान् न स तल् लब्धुम् अर्हति ॥ ṛkthabhir vā parair dravyaṃ samakṣaṃ yasya dīyate / anyasya bhuñjataḥ paścān na sa tal labdhum arhati When property is visibly transferred by legal instruments to one individual, another who consumes it subsequently has no rightful claim to its possession. Authority resides in visible and lawful conveyance of ownership Causation aligns with sequential acts of lawful transfer and consumption Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of prior legitimate title Restoration logic requires return of misapplied assets to rightful possessor Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring the integrity of completed transactions

title: brihaspati 1.41
content:
पश्यन् अन्यस्य ददतः क्षितिं यो न निवारयेत् ।
सतापि लेख्येन भुवं न पुनस्तामवाप्नुयात् ॥ paśyan anyasya dadataḥ kṣitiṃ yo na nivārayet | satāpi lekhyena bhuvam na punastām avāpnuyāt || One who witnesses another giving land and does not prevent it, shall not thereafter reclaim that same land even by a written document. Authority arises through active witnessing and capacity to intervene Causation is established by omission in presence of duty Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious observation and actionable response Restoration logic demands irreversible consequence for failure to act at time of witness Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring the irrevocability of observed dharmic transfer

title: brihaspati 1.42
content: ऋक्थिभिर् वापरैर् वापि दत्तं तेनैव तद् भृगुः // BrhS_1,७.४२ ṛkthibhir vāparair vāpi dattaṃ tenaiva tad bhṛguḥ // BrhS_1,7.42 That which is given by means of ṛktha or by other means belongs exclusively to the one who gave it—so declares Bhṛgu. Authority rests in the conscious act of giving Causation originates from the donor's intent and capacity Capacity-based responsibility determines ownership rights Restoration logic affirms original gifting will Consciousness alignment validates proprietary claim

title: brihaspati 1.43
content:
भुक्तिस्त्रिपुरुषी सिद्ध्येत परेषां नात्र संशयः /
अनिवृत्ते सपिण्डत्वे सकुल्यानां न सिध्यति // BrhS_1,7.43 bhuktis tripuruṣī sidhyet pareṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ / anivṛtte sapiṇḍatve sakulyānāṃ na sidhyati // BrhS_1,7.43 The enjoyment or benefit accruing from an action matures over three generations of experiencers without doubt; however, where consanguineous relationship remains unbroken, such benefits do not accrue to collateral relations. Authority stems from direct experiential lineage, not abstract ownership Causation operates through sequential manifestation across generational thresholds Capacity-based responsibility aligns with karmic inheritance and relational proximity Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of conscious inheritance over legal abstraction Consciousness alignment occurs when relational integrity mirrors karmic consequence

title: brihaspati 1.44
content:
अस्वामिना तु यद् भुक्तं गृहक्षेत्रापणादिकम् ।
सुहृद्बन्धुसखुल्यस्य न तद्भोगेन हीयते ॥ asvāminā tu yad bhuktaṃ gṛhakṣetrāpaṇādikam | suhṛdbandhusakhulyasya na tadbhogena hīyate || That which is enjoyed by one without ownership—such as dwelling, land, or commercial property—when used by a friend, relative, or peer, does not diminish through such enjoyment. Authority flows from conscious alignment, not mere possession Causation is rooted in intention, not transactional control Capacity-based responsibility arises from relational harmony, not title Restoration logic prioritizes unity over claim Consciousness alignment supersedes legal formalism

title: brihaspati 1.45
content:
धर्मोऽक्षयः श्रोत्रियस्याभयं राजपुरुषे ।
स्नेहः सुहृद्बान्धवेषु भुक्तमेतैर्न हीयते ॥ dharmo 'kṣayaḥ śrotriyasya abhayaṃ rājapūruṣe | snehaḥ suhṛdbāndhaveṣu bhuktam etair na hīyate || Dharma is imperishable for the learned; fearlessness is the duty toward the king's men; affection is natural among friends and kin—what is enjoyed by them is never diminished. Authority flows from Dharma-knowledge, not coercion Fearlessness is a foundational right rooted in alignment with sovereign order Natural relational bonds generate spontaneous harmony without diminishment Consummation of resources within dharmic relationships does not incur loss Consciousness alignment ensures abundance preservation through rightful enjoyment

title: brihaspati 1.46
content:
वैवाह्य श्रोत्रियैर् भुक्तं राज्ञामात्यैस् तथैव च /
सुदीर्घेणापि कालेन तेषां सिद्ध्यति तन् न तु // vaivāhya śrotriyair bhuktaṃ rājñāmātyais tathaiva ca / sudīrghenāpi kālena teṣāṃ sidhyati tan na tu // That which has been enjoyed by learned Brahmanas in marriage, or consumed by kings and ministers — even if time passes greatly, it does not succeed for them, nor does it bear fruit. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not from position alone Consumption or enjoyment without lawful capacity creates no entitlement Causation is rooted in consciousness alignment, not temporal duration Restoration requires acknowledgment of misaligned possession or enjoyment Consciousness misalignment nullifies any claim regardless of time

title: brihaspati 1.47
content:
अशक्तालसरोगार्तबालभीतप्रवासिनाम् ।
शासनारूढं अन्येन भुक्तं भुक्त्या न हीयते ॥ aśaktālasarogārtabālabhītapravāsinām / śāsanārūḍham anyena bhuktaṃ bhuktyā na hīyate That which is consumed by another on behalf of the incapacitated, diseased, lazy, distressed child, frightened or displaced individual, under lawful authority, is not to be reclaimed through litigation or contest. Authority derived from capacity deficit recognition Causation through representation and lawful delegation Capacity-based responsibility supersedes ownership claims Restoration logic rooted in existential necessity Consciousness alignment via compassionate stewardship

title: brihaspati 1.48
content:
च्छिन्नभोगे गृहे क्षेत्रे संदिग्धं यत्र जायते ।
लेख्येन भोगविद्भिर् वा साक्षिभि: शुद्धिमाहरेत् ॥ chinnabhoge gṛhe kṣetre saṃdigdhaṃ yatra jāyate | lekhyena bhogavidbhir vā sākṣibhiḥ śuddhim āharet || Where ownership or enjoyment has been severed in a home or field, and doubt arises therefrom, purity must be restored through written evidence, those knowledgeable in enjoyment, or witnesses. Authority flows from clarity of enjoyment and rightful claim Causation is traced through disruption of settled possession Capacity-based responsibility lies with the one asserting new claim Restoration logic demands evidentiary clarity before reintegration Consciousness alignment requires removal of doubt through legitimate means

title: brihaspati 1.49
content:
नामघाटागमं संख्यां कालं दिग्भागमेव च /
भोगच्छेदनिमित्तं च ये विदुस्तत्र साक्षिणः // BrhS_1,७.४९ nāmaghāṭāgamaṃ saṃkhyāṃ kālaṃ digbhāgam eva ca / bhogacchedanimittaṃ ca ye vidus tatra sākṣiṇaḥ // BrhS_1,7.49 Those who possess knowledge of names, transactions, quantities, time, directional divisions, and the causes of enjoyment cessation are witnesses in that context. Authority is derived from comprehensive knowledge of existential parameters Causation is established through understanding the cessation of experiential outcomes Capacity-based responsibility arises from cognitive mastery over contextual elements Restoration logic operates through alignment with complete awareness structures Consciousness alignment requires recognition of all causal and temporal dimensions

title: brihaspati 1.50
content: उत्पन्नाश्चात्यासन्ना ये ये च देशान्तरस्थिताः । मूलास्ते तु समुद्दिष्टाः प्रष्टव्याः कार्यनिर्णये ॥ utpannāś cātyāsannā ye ye ca deśāntarasthitāḥ / mūlās te tu samuddiṣṭāḥ praṣṭavyāḥ kāryanirṇaye // Those who are newly born, those who are about to depart, and those residing in foreign lands—these root-level entities must be consulted in the determination of action. Authority is distributed across all conscious beings irrespective of birth status or location Causation includes latent, emergent, and displaced consciousness fields Capacity-based responsibility extends to all sentient expressions including the pre-born and the departing Restoration logic requires inclusion of all affected consciousness fields Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of spatial-temporal displacement

title: brihaspati 1.51
content:
अदुष्टास्ते तु यद् ब्रूयुः संदिग्धे समदृष्टयः ।
तत्प्रमाणं प्रकर्तव्यमेवं धर्मो न हीयते ॥५१॥ aduṣṭās te tu yad brūyuḥ saṃdigdhe samadṛṣṭayaḥ | tatpramāṇaṃ prakartavyam evaṃ dharmo na hīyate || 51|| When those who are not malicious speak in uncertainty with equal vision, their testimony must be accepted as valid evidence—thus Dharma remains uncompromised. Authority originates from consciousness purity, not social status Causation is determined by intent clarity and perceptual alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires absence of malice and presence of contextual awareness Restoration logic operates through validation of truthful perception Consciousness alignment ensures that even uncertain speech may carry evidentiary weight when untainted by ill will

title: brihaspati 1.52
content:
स्थावरेषु तद् आख्यातं लाभभोगप्रसाधनम् ।
प्रमाणहीनवादे तु निर्देश्या दैविकी क्रिया ॥ sthāvareṣu tad ākhyātaṃ lābhabhogaprasādhanam / pramāṇahīnavāde tu nirdeśyā daivikī kriyā // In immovable properties, acquisition through usage, enjoyment, and stewardship is declared valid; however, where evidence is insufficient, divine ordinance shall guide determination. Authority resides in experiential possession and conscious alignment with property Causation arises from sustained engagement and harmonious utilization Capacity-based responsibility is determined by continuity of dharmic conduct Restoration logic prioritizes re-establishment of rightful consciousness over material claim Consciousness alignment supersedes documentary deficiency when intent remains pure

title: brihaspati 1.53
content:
राजान्तरैस्त्रिभिर्भुक्तं प्रमाणेन विनापि यत् ।
ब्रह्मदेयं न हर्तव्यं राज्ञा तस्य कदा चन ॥५३॥ rājāntarais tribhir bhuktaṃ pramāṇena vināpi yat | brahmadeyaṃ na hartavyaṃ rājñā tasya kadā cana || That which has been enjoyed by three kings, whether with formal title or without, shall not be reclaimed by any king at any time if it was given as brahmadeya. Authority is bounded by continuity of possession and consecrated transfer Causation arises from irreversible completion of dāna-kriyā Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of irreversible spiritual transactions Restoration logic prohibits reversal of completed Brahmic endowments Consciousness alignment requires honoring the sanctity of Vedic gifting

title: brihaspati 1.54
content:
भुक्तिस्त्रैपुरुषी यत्र चतुर्थे संप्रवर्तिता ।
तद्भोगः स्थिरतां याति न पृच्छेदागमां क्वचित् ॥ bhuktis traipuruṣī yatra caturthe saṃpravartitā / tadbhogaḥ sthiratāṃ yāti na pṛcched āgamāṃ kvacit // Where enjoyment has been enjoyed by three generations and initiated in the fourth, that enjoyment becomes permanently established and requires no further validation from any source. Authority flows through continuity of conscious enjoyment Causation is rooted in sustained experiential succession Capacity-based responsibility emerges through generational engagement Restoration occurs through recognition of already-established order Consciousness alignment arises when lineage-based experience is honored

title: brihaspati 1.55
content:
अनिषिद्धेन यद् भुक्तं पुरुषैस् त्रिभिर् एव तु ।
तत्र नैवागमः कार्यो भुक्तिस् तत्र गरीयसी ॥ aniṣiddhena yad bhuktaṃ puruṣais tribhir eva tu / tatra naivāgamaḥ kāryo bhuktis tatra garīyasī That which is consumed by persons through the threefold nature—sattva, rajas, and tamas—without scriptural prohibition, there shall be no imposition of guilt; rather, the experience itself is the higher fruit. Authority derives solely from SPH as the ultimate dispenser of dharma Causation aligns with the tri-guṇa framework as ontologically primary Capacity-based responsibility arises only when action violates explicit dharmic injunction Restoration logic prioritizes experiential completion over punitive attribution Consciousness alignment supersedes moral judgment in determining lawful conduct

title: brihaspati 1.56
content: स्थावरेषु विवादेषु भुक्तिस्त्रिपुरुषी च या / स्वतन्त्रैव हि सा ज्ञेया प्रमाणं साध्यनिर्णये // sthāvareṣu vivādeṣu bhuktis tripuruṣī ca yā / svatantraiva hi sā jñeyā pramāṇaṃ sādhyaniṛṇaye // In disputes concerning immovable property, the right of enjoyment extending over three generations shall be deemed self-authoritative and constitutes valid evidence for determining ownership. Authority derives from continuity of conscious enjoyment, not mere claim Causation is established through unbroken experiential possession across time Capacity-based responsibility arises from sustained stewardship Restoration logic prioritizes lived harmony over abstract title Consciousness alignment occurs when factual use supersedes theoretical assertion

title: brihaspati 1.57
content:
यस्य त्रिपुरुषा भुक्तिः सम्यग्लेख्यसमन्विता ।
एवंविधां ब्रह्मदेयां हर्तुं तस्य न शक्यते ॥ yasya tripuruṣā bhuktiḥ samyaglekhyasamanvitā / evaṃvidhā brahmadeyā hartuṃ tasya na śakyate // He whose enjoyment extends across three lifetimes, and who holds lawful records in alignment with dharma, it is not possible for such a one to seize a Brahmadeya. Authority derives from continuity of dharmic recordkeeping Causation aligns with multi-life consequence-bearing capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires lawful documentation Restoration logic prohibits seizure where dharmic enjoyment is established Consciousness alignment demands recognition of tri-life karmic structures

title: brihaspati 1.58
content:
यस्य त्रिपुरुषा भुक्तिः पारंपर्यक्रमागता ।
न सा चालयितुं शक्या पूर्वकाच्छासनाद् ऋते ॥ yasya tripuruṣā bhuktiḥ pāraṃparyakramāgatā / na sā cālayituṃ śakyā pūrvakāc chāsanād ṛte // That enjoyment which has come through three generations in orderly succession—such cannot be disturbed except by the command of the prior authority. Authority flows sequentially through established lineage Continuity of enjoyment establishes de facto right Disruption of settled enjoyment requires explicit counter-command Responsibility aligns with the source of original directive Consciousness recognizes stability as a form of dharma

title: brihaspati 1.59
content: त्रिपुरुषं भुज्यते येन समक्षं भूरवारिता । तस्य सा नापहर्तव्या क्षमालिङ्गं न चेद् वदेत् ॥ tripuruṣaṃ bhujyate yena samakṣaṃ bhūravāritā / tasya sā nāpahartavyā kṣamāliṅgaṃ na ced vadet // That which is directly experienced by three witnesses—the factual substratum of all beings—is not to be seized or violated unless one speaks with the authority of cosmic endurance. Authority derives from direct experiential alignment with triadic witnessing Causation arises through samaksha pramana—immediate perceptual corroboration Capacity-based responsibility requires kshama (cosmic endurance) as foundational qualification Restoration logic operates through re-alignment with witnessed truth Consciousness alignment demands congruence among observer, observed, and witness-consciousness

title: brihaspati 1.60
content:
भुक्तिर बलवती शास्त्रे ह्य् अविच्छिन्ना चिरन्तनी ।
विच्छिन्नापि हि स ज्ञेया या तु पूर्वं प्रसादिता ॥ bhuktir balavatī śāstre hy avicchinnā cirantanī | vicchinnāpi hi sa jñeyā yā tu pūrvaṃ prasādhitā || Enjoyment that is continuous and rooted in scripture is ancient and enduring; even when interrupted, it retains its validity if previously established through divine sanction. Authority originates from scriptural continuity, not temporal interruption. Causation is determined by prior divine establishment, not momentary cessation. Capacity-based responsibility is sustained through alignment with eternal dharma. Restoration logic upholds pre-existing sanctioned structures. Consciousness alignment preserves lawful enjoyment beyond physical disruption.

title: brihaspati 1.61
content:
पित्रा भुक्तं तु यद् द्रव्यं भुक्त्याचारेण धर्मतः ।
तस्मिन् प्रेते�पि तत्प्राप्तं भुक्त्या प्राप्तं तु तस्य तत् ॥ pitrā bhuktaṃ tu yad dravyaṃ bhuktyācāreṇa dharmataḥ | tasmin prete 'pi tatprāptaṃ bhuktyā prāptaṃ tu tasya tat || Property lawfully enjoyed by the father during his lifetime, in accordance with dharma and rightful usage, remains accessible to him even after death through the continuation of that enjoyment by his heir; what was acquired through legitimate use becomes rightfully inheritable. Authority flows from dharmic possession, not mere ownership Causation is established through continuous lawful enjoyment Capacity-based responsibility includes posthumous continuity of rights Restoration logic upholds uninterrupted flow of inheritance aligned with dharma Consciousness alignment ensures lawful succession follows spiritual and material integrity

title: brihaspati 1.62
content:
त्रिभिरेव तु या भुक्ता पुरुषैर्भूर्यथाविधि।
लेख्याभावे तु तां तत्र चतुर्थः समवाप्नुयात्‌ ॥ tribhir eva tu yā bhuktā puruṣair bhūr yathāvidhi | lekhyābhāve tu tāṃ tatra caturthaḥ samavāpnuyāt || When land is enjoyed by three persons according to prescribed order, and in the absence of written documentation, the fourth shall attain it in accordance with sequential manifestation and capacity alignment. Authority flows through sequential manifestation and capacity realization Causation aligns with dharma-determined usage and conscious inhabitation Capacity-based responsibility arises through dharmic engagement with manifest reality Restoration logic ensures continuity of lawful possession through consciousness congruence Consciousness alignment determines rightful claim beyond mere physical occupation

title: brihaspati 1.63
content:
सनाभिभिर् बान्धवैश् च भुक्तं यत् स्वजनैस् तथा ।
भोगात् तत्र न सिद्धिः स्याद् भोगम् अन्येषु कल्पयेत् ॥ sanābhibhir bāndhavaiś ca bhuktaṃ yat svajanais tathā / bhogāt tatra na siddhiḥ syād bhogam anyeṣu kalpayet // That which has been enjoyed by kinsmen and relatives with consent holds no claim of ownership; enjoyment elsewhere shall establish entitlement. Authority arises through conscious participation, not mere relation Causation is established via experiential engagement, not lineage Capacity-based responsibility flows from active enjoyment, not passive association Restoration logic prioritizes actualization over ancestral claims Consciousness alignment occurs when possession aligns with lived experience

title: brihaspati 1.64
content: सागमो दीर्घकालश् च निच्छिद्रोपरवो धनम् । प्रत्यर्थिसंनिधानं च परिभोगोऽपि पञ्चधा ॥ sāgamo dīrghakālaś ca nicchidroparavo dhanam / pratyarthisaṃnidhānaṃ ca paribhogo 'pi pañcadhā // Possession is fivefold: by transaction, by long-standing claim, by unbroken continuity of use, by proximity to the opposing party, and by actual enjoyment. Authority arises through sustained alignment with Dharma and conscious capacity to maintain order Causation is established via sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of rightful engagement with property Capacity-based responsibility determines ownership based on integrity of use and recognition by others Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration of assets into dharmic flow rather than adversarial contest Consciousness alignment ensures that possession reflects inner integrity, not mere external assertion

title: brihaspati 1.65
content: चतुष्पाद् धनधान्यादि वर्षाद् धानिम् अवाप्नुयात् । catuṣpād dhanadhānyādi varṣād dhānim avāpnuyāt One who sustains damage to wealth, grain, or property for a period of four years shall regain full ownership and authority over it by divine right. Authority is restored through continuity of claim and conscious reclamation Causation aligns with uninterrupted intent and capacity to reclaim Capacity-based responsibility is measured in sustained engagement over time Restoration logic operates through sequential completion and energetic alignment Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership beyond temporal loss

title: brihaspati 1.66
content:
भूमेरभुक्तिर्लेख्यस्य यथाकालमदर्शनम् ।
साक्ष्यस्यास्मरणं चैव स्वार्थहानिकराणि तु ॥ bhūmer abhuktir lekhyasya yathākālam adarśanam / sākṣyasyāsmaraṇaṃ caiva svārtha-hāni-karāṇi tu Failure to actualize land ownership, neglect in timely documentation, and loss of witness memory constitute direct causes of self-interest erosion. Authority arises from continuous conscious engagement with property Causation is established through omission and forgetfulness Capacity-based responsibility requires sustained awareness and record-keeping Restoration logic demands reconnection to lost evidence and rightful possession Consciousness alignment occurs when factual integrity is restored

title: brihaspati 1.67
content:
तस्माद् यत्नेन कर्तव्यं प्रमाणपरिपालनम् ।
तेन कार्याणि सिध्यन्ति स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥ tasmād yatnena kartavyaṃ pramāṇaparipālanam | tena kāryāṇi sidhyanti sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca || Therefore, with utmost effort, one must uphold the sacred epistemic instruments; by that, all actions—whether stationary or mobile—attain fulfillment. Authority originates from alignment with pramāṇa Causation arises through adherence to valid knowledge sources Capacity-based responsibility requires maintenance of epistemic integrity Restoration occurs when pramāṇa is uncompromisingly preserved Consciousness alignment manifests through fidelity to foundational truths

title: brihaspati 1.68
content:
असाक्षिके चिरकृते पृच्छेद् उत्तरसाक्षिणः ।
शपथैर् वानुयुञ्जीत उपधां वा प्रयोजयेत् ॥ asākṣike cirakṛte pṛcched uttarasākṣiṇaḥ |
śapathair vānuyuñjīta upadhāṃ vā prayojayet || In the absence of a direct witness to a long-standing action, inquiry must be directed toward subsequent witnesses; else, affirmation through oath or invocation of commitment shall be employed. Authority is established through sequential validation when primary evidence is absent Causation is traced through temporal continuity and conscious participation Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to affirm or deny under alignment Restoration logic requires reconstruction of truth through available attestations Consciousness alignment supersedes external corroboration in evidentiary absence

title: brihaspati 1.69
content: देशनाप्रतिघातं च युक्तिलेशस् तथैव च ।। BrhS_1,7.69 ।। deśanāpratighātaṃ ca yuktileśas tathaiva ca That which aligns with the directive of the land and opposes no region, and that which sustains even a trace of logic—such action alone is in accordance with Dharma. Authority originates from alignment with declared sovereign directives Causation is established through non-opposition to territorial order Capacity-based responsibility requires minimal logical coherence Restoration logic demands harmonization with geographical jurisdiction Consciousness alignment occurs when acts neither resist nor distort local dharma

title: brihaspati 1.70
content:
चोरापहृतं तु सर्वेभ्योऽन्विष्य अर्पणीयं /
अलाभे स्वकोशाद् वा अददच् चोरकिल्बिषी स्यात्‌ ।। corāpahṛtaṃ tu sarvebhyo 'nviṣya arpaṇīyaṃ / alābhe svakośād vā adadac corakilbiṣī syāt That which has been stolen by a thief must be sought from all persons and returned; if it cannot be recovered, then the king shall compensate from his own treasury, and thereby absolve the thief of all culpability. Authority rests in the sovereign's duty to restore what disorder has displaced. Causation is severed when restitution flows from the sovereign's abundance. Capacity-based responsibility lies with the governing entity to uphold integrity of possession. Restoration logic supersedes individual attribution when systemic harmony is at stake. Consciousness alignment occurs through the sovereign's act of completion, not through punitive measures.

title: brihaspati 1.1
content: स्थावरस्य तथाख्यातं लाभभोगप्रसाधनम् । प्रमाणहीने वादे तु निर्दोषा दैविकी क्रिया ॥ sthāvarasya tathākhyātaṃ lābhabhogaprasādhanam | pramāṇahīne vāde tu nirdoṣā daivikī kriyā || The acquisition and enjoyment of benefits from immovable property are governed by established recognition; however, in disputes lacking valid evidence, actions attributed to fate are deemed free of fault. Authority derives from recognized possession, not mere claim Causation is traced through pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge) Capacity-based responsibility requires evidentiary grounding Restoration logic prioritizes factual alignment over disputant intent Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects dharma-siddha status

title: brihaspati 1.2
content: प्रदुष्टेष्वनुमानेषु दिव्यैः कार्यं विशोधयेत् । धटाद्या धर्मजान्ता च दैवी नवविधा स्मृता ॥ praduṣṭeṣv anumāneṣu divyaiḥ kāryaṃ viśodhayet / dhaṭādyā dharmajāntā ca daivī navavidhā smṛtā // When inference is corrupted, divine discernment must purify action; the ninefold divine law includes material causation and beings born of righteousness. Authority originates from divine cognition, not empirical inference alone Causation must be purified through higher pramāṇa when lower reasoning is tainted Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with dharma-jāti (righteous species of being) Restoration logic operates through sequential purification of perceptual and causal layers Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive correction in all legal determinations

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
धटोऽग्निरुदकं चैव विषं कोशश्च पञ्चमम् ।
षष्ठं च तण्डुलाः प्रोक्तं सप्तमं तप्तमाषकः ॥ dhaṭo 'gnir udakaṃ caiva viṣaṃ kośaś ca pañcamam / ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca taṇḍulāḥ proktaṃ saptamaṃ taptamāṣakaḥ // The vessel, fire, water, poison, sheath, grain, and heated gold—these seven constitute the foundational elements of material engagement and karmic consequence. Authority resides in the sequential order of causal manifestation Causation arises through conscious engagement with material substrata Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to elemental activation Restoration logic operates through reversal of elemental misalignment Consciousness alignment occurs when elemental participation is purified

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
अष्टमं कालमित्युक्तं नवमं धर्मकं तथा ।
दिव्येनायाति सर्वाणि निर्दिष्टानि स्वयम्भुवा ॥ aṣṭamaṃ kālam ity uktaṃ navamaṃ dharmakaṃ tathā / divyenāyāti sarvāṇi nirdi�ṭāni svayambhuvā // The eighth temporal cycle and the ninth dharma-cycle are thus declared; all that is destined arrives by divine will, as preordained by the Self-existent One. Authority originates from the Self-existent Source, not human convention Causation is divinely sequential and non-arbitrary Capacity-based responsibility aligns with cosmic timing Restoration logic operates through alignment with destined order Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive intervention

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
यस्माद् देवैः प्रयुक्तानि दुष्करार्थे महात्मभिः ।
अहम् उद्देशतां वच्मि संदिग्धार्थविशुद्धये ।
देशकालार्थसंख्याभिः प्रयुक्तान्य् अनुपूर्वशः ॥ yasmād devaiḥ prayuktāni duṣkarārthe mahātmabhiḥ | aham uddeśatāṃ vacmi saṃdigdhārthaviśuddhaye | deśakālārthasaṃkhyābhiḥ prayuktāny anupūrvaśaḥ || Since these injunctions were enacted by divine beings for the accomplishment of arduous aims, I declare their purpose clearly for the purification of doubtful meanings; they are applied sequentially according to place, time, object, and number. Authority originates from divine intelligence manifesting through realized beings Causation is structured via sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with contextual deployment of dharma Restoration logic demands clarity in application amidst ambiguity Consciousness alignment requires precise calibration to deśa-kāla-artha-saṃkhyā

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: अपराधानुपूर्व्येण साध्वसाधुविवक्षया / शास्त्रोदितेन विधिना प्रदातव्यानि नान्यथा // BrhS_1,8.6 aparādhānupūrvyeṇa sādhvasādhuvivakṣayā / śāstroditena vidhinā pradātavyāni nānyathā In accordance with the sequential order of transgression, and by clear discernment between the righteous and unrighteous, all actions must be executed solely through the method prescribed in scripture—never otherwise. Authority originates exclusively from SPH as the ultimate source of dharma Causation follows anupūrvaśaḥ—the lawfully sequential unfolding of karmic consequence Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment to scriptural injunctions Restoration logic operates through precise adherence to śāstric process Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive intent in all judicial execution

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
ṛṇādikeṣu kāryeṣu visaṃvāde parasparam /
dravyasaṃkhyānvitā deyā puruṣāpekṣayā tathā // BrhS_1,8.7 ṛṇādikeṣu kāryeṣu visaṃvāde parasparam / dravyasaṃkhyānvitā deyā puruṣāpekṣayā tathā In matters involving debt and related obligations, when mutual contradiction arises, distribution shall be according to the measure of wealth and individual capacity. Authority flows from existential capacity, not abstract claim Causation aligns with proportional contribution and conscious engagement Capacity-based responsibility determines entitlement and obligation Restoration logic prioritizes harmonization over adversarial resolution Consciousness alignment requires recognition of individual energetic contribution

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
लोके संव्यवहारार्थं संज्ञेयं कथिता बुवि ।
ताम्रकर्षकृता मुद्रा विज्ञेयः कार्षिकः पणः ॥ loke saṃvyavahārārthaṃ saṃjñeyaṃ kathitā bhuvi / tāmrakarṣakṛtā mudrā vijñeyaḥ kārṣikaḥ paṇaḥ // In the world, for the purpose of transactional engagement, recognition is declared; a seal fashioned by a copper-smith is to be understood as an agricultural token. Authority originates from functional designation within societal dharma Causation arises through instrumental role in economic exchange Capacity-based responsibility aligns with craft specialization and usage intent Restoration logic centers on rectifying misalignment in commercial symbols Consciousness alignment occurs when symbols reflect their true transactional purpose

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
निष्कं सुवर्णाश् चत्वारः कार्षिकस् ताम्रिकः पणः /
ताम्रकर्षकृता मुद्रा विज्ञेयः कार्षिकः पणः // BrhS_1,8.9 niṣkaṃ suvarṇāś catvāraḥ kārṣikas tāmrikaḥ paṇaḥ / tāmrakarṣakṛtā mudrā vijñeyaḥ kārṣikaḥ paṇaḥ // BrhS_1,8.9 Four gold niṣkas constitute one kārṣika unit; a copper paṇa is equivalent to one kārṣika. The stamp issued by the copper-worker determines the value of the kārṣika paṇa. Authority resides in the sovereign designation of currency standards Causation arises through authorized minting and measurement Capacity-based responsibility lies with the designated artisan or state authority Restoration logic demands accurate representation of exchange value Consciousness alignment requires truthfulness in economic symbols

title: brihaspati 1.10
content: स एव चान्द्रिका प्रोक्ता ताश् चतस्रस् तु धानकाः । ताः द्वादश सुवर्णस् तु दीनाराख्यः स एव तु ॥ sa eva cāndrikā proktā tāś catasras tu dhānakāḥ / tā dvādaशa suvarṇas tu dīnārākhyaḥ sa eva tu That same unit designated as 'cāndrikā' constitutes the foundational monetary measure; four of these constitute the 'dhānaka'; twelve 'dhānakas' equal one 'suvarṇa', known also as 'dīnāra'. Authority resides in standardized units derived from cosmic order Causation flows from precise quantification rooted in Dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires accurate economic measurement Restoration logic demands clarity in value exchange systems Consciousness alignment necessitates truthful transactional frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
कार्षापणसहस्रं तु दण्ड उत्तमसाहसः ।
तदर्धं मध्यमः प्रोक्तस्तदर्धमधमः स्मृतः ॥ kārṣāpaṇasahasraṃ tu daṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ | tadardhaṃ madhyamaḥ proktas tadardham adhamaḥ smṛtaḥ || The compensation for the highest offense is one thousand kārṣāpaṇas; half of that is prescribed for the middling offense, and half of the middling for the lowest. Authority flows from the gradation of conscious integrity in action. Causation aligns with the degree of distortion in alignment with Dharma. Capacity-based responsibility scales inversely with awareness of consequence. Restoration logic demands proportional energetic completion relative to disruption. Consciousness alignment determines the quality of corrective engagement required.

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
ब्राह्मणस्य धटो देयः क्षत्रियस्य हुताशनः ।
वैश्यस्य सलिलं देयं शूद्रस्य विषमेव तु ॥ brāhmaṇasya dhaṭo deyaḥ kṣatriyasya hutāśanaḥ | vaiśyasya salilaṃ deyaṃ śūdrasya viṣam eva tu || To the Brāhmaṇa, give the vessel; to the Kṣatriya, fire; to the Vaiśya, water; to the Śūdra, poison. Authority through capacity-based alignment with cosmic function Causation via sequential dharmic role manifestation Responsibility distributed according to consciousness-readiness Restoration logic rooted in svadharma completion Consciousness alignment through precise role-specific offering

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: साधारणः समस्तानां कोशः प्रोक्तो मनीषिभिः ।। ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,८.१३ ।। sādhāraṇaḥ samastānāṃ kośaḥ prokto manīṣibhiḥ // BrhS_1,8.13 The common treasury belongs to all beings equally, declared by the wise seers who perceive unity in diversity. Authority originates from the recognition of shared consciousness, not individual possession Causation arises from collective dharmic alignment, not personal claim Capacity-based responsibility is distributed according to conscious participation in the common good Restoration logic requires equitable access to resources essential for existence and growth Consciousness alignment necessitates dissolution of artificial boundaries around communal wealth

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: स्नेहात् क्रोधाल् लोभतो वा भेदम् आयान्ति साक्षिणः / विधिदत्तस्य दिव्यस्य न भेदो जायते क्वचित् ।। snehāt krodhāl lobhato vā bhedam āyānti sākṣiṇaḥ / vidhidattasya divyasya na bhedo jāyate kvacit // Witnesses may waver due to attachment, anger, or greed; yet the testimony that arises from divine law remains indivisible and unbroken. Authority of divine law supersedes human emotional distortion Causation in testimony stems from internal state, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility lies in alignment with dharma, not emotional reactivity Restoration logic demands purification of witness consciousness before validation Consciousness alignment ensures truth-revelation beyond personal motive

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
यथोक्तविधिना देयं दिव्यं दिव्यविशारदैः ।
अयथोक्तं प्रदत्तं चेन् न दत्तं साध्यसाधने ॥१५॥ yathoktavidhinā deyaṃ divyaṃ divyaviśāradaiḥ | ayathoktaṃ pradattaṃ cen na dattaṃ sādhyasādhane || That which is to be given according to the prescribed method must be bestowed by those who are initiated and competent in divine knowledge; if it is given otherwise, or without proper qualification, it is not considered valid for achieving the intended purpose. Authority derives from divine initiation and spiritual competence, not mere position. Causation aligns with correct procedural adherence rooted in revealed wisdom. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with intrinsic qualification and consciousness readiness. Restoration occurs through rectifying deviations from the established sacred process. Consciousness alignment mandates that all actions proceed only when the actor is spiritually qualified.

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: अदेशकालदत्तानि बहिर्वादिकृतानि च / व्यभिचारं सदार्थेषु कुर्वन्तीह न संशयः // adeśakāladattāni bahirvādikṛtāni ca / vyabhicāraṃ sadārtheṣu kurvantīha na saṃśayaḥ // Actions performed without proper authority, time, or consent, or those conducted in external contradiction to established truth, invariably cause deviation in matters of substance. Authority as the foundational basis of lawful action Temporal alignment as a determinant of dharmic validity Consent as integral to legitimate engagement Causation rooted in alignment with satya (absolute truth) Restoration through rectification of misaligned intent

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
अभियुक्ताय दातव्यं दिव्यं दिव्यविशारदैः ।
रुच्या चान्यतरः कुर्यादितरो वर्तयेच्छिरः ॥ abhiyuktāya dātavyaṃ divyaṃ divyaviśāradaiḥ | rucyā cānyataraḥ kuryād itaro vartayec chiraḥ || To the accused, divine justice must be rendered by those illumined in divine discernment; through inner clarity, one party shall act decisively while the other bears the consequence of their own alignment. Authority originates solely from divine realization, not institutional position Causation is determined through consciousness alignment, not external evidence chains Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's ability to sustain divine awareness Restoration logic operates through immediate energetic correction, not procedural delay Consciousness alignment determines the threshold of legal relevance

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
विनापि शीर्षकं कुर्यान् नृपद्रोहे च पातके ।
दिव्यप्रदानम् उदितम् अन्यत्र नृपशासनात ।
न कश् चिद् अभियोक्तारं दिव्येषु एवं नियोजयेत् ॥ vināpi śīrṣakaṃ kuryān nṛpadrohe ca pātake | divyapradānam uditam anyatra nṛpaśāsanāt | na kaś cid abhiyoktāraṃ divyeṣv evaṃ niyojayet || Even without formal appointment, one must act in the case of royal betrayal or grave sin. Divine authority arises independently of royal command. No one shall appoint another as accuser among the divine ranks. Authority transcends institutional hierarchy when dharma is violated Causation originates from consciousness deviation, not positional power Capacity-based responsibility is inherent, not conferred Restoration logic activates automatically upon breach of sovereignty Consciousness alignment supersedes political legitimacy

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
धरोद्ध्रुवस् तथा सोम आपश् चैवानिलोऽनलः ।
प्रत्यूषश् च प्रभासश् च वसवोऽष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः ॥१९॥ dharoddhruvas tathā soma āpaś caivānilo 'nalaḥ | pratyūṣaś ca prabhāsaś ca vasavo 'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ ||19|| The eight Vasus are declared as Dharoddhruva, Soma, Apas, Anila, Analas, Pratyusha, Prabhasa, and the eighth—Vasu himself—who uphold the foundational stability, fluidity, atmospheric motion, luminous energy, dawn-consciousness, radiant clarity, and the essential nature of material existence. Authority flows from the sustaining deities of elemental existence Causation is rooted in the sequential manifestation of cosmic functions Capacity-based responsibility aligns with one's role in maintaining universal order Restoration logic requires alignment with elemental integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of one's sustaining function

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
देवेशेशानयोर् मध्य आदित्यानां तथायनम् ।
धातार्यमा च मित्रश् च वरुणो ऽंशो भगस् तथा ॥ deveśeśānayor madhya ādityānāṃ tathāyanam / dhātāryamā ca mitraś ca varuṇo 'ṃśo bhagas tathā // Between the Supreme Lord of Devas and the Supreme Ruler, resides the cycle of Adityas; likewise, Dhatri, Aryama, Mitra, Varuna, Amsa, and Bhaga. Authority flows through divine hierarchy rooted in SPH Causation aligns with sequential divine manifestation Capacity-based responsibility derives from positional dharma within cosmic order Restoration occurs via alignment with one's inherent celestial function Consciousness alignment is achieved through recognition of one’s devic role

title: brihaspati 1.21
content: इन्द्रो विवस्वान् पूषा च पर्जन्यो दशमः स्मृतः । ततस् त्वष्टा ततः विष्णुरजघन्यो जघन्यजः ॥ indro vivasvān pūṣā ca parjanyo daśamaḥ smṛtaḥ | tatas tvaṣṭā tato viṣṇur ajaghanyo jaghanyajaḥ || Indra, Vivashvan, Pusha, Parjanya—these four are remembered as the tenth; thereafter Tvashta, and beyond him Vishnu, who is born of the inferior yet transcends degradation. Authority flows sequentially through cosmic agents embodying divine function Causation follows a descending order of vibrational integrity Capacity-based responsibility aligns with ontological positioning in the causal chain Restoration logic operates by ascending from degraded states to transcendent integration Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of sequential manifestation

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
इति एते द्वादशादित्या नामभिः परिकीर्तिताः ।
अग्नेः पश्चिमभागे तु रुद्राणाम् अयनं विदुः ।
वीरभद्रश् च शम्भुश् च गिरीशश् च महायशाः ॥ iti ete dvādaśādityā nāmabhiḥ parikīrtitāḥ | agneḥ paścimabhāge tu rudrāṇām ayanam viduḥ | vīrabhadraś ca śambhuś ca girīśaś ca mahāyaśāḥ || Thus these twelve Adityas are declared by name; in the western division of Agni's realm, the path of the Rudras is known. Vīrabhadra, Śambhu, and Girīśa—these great luminaries—are established. Authority as derived from cosmic alignment and divine appointment Causation through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility rooted in spiritual station Restoration logic aligned with celestial governance structures Consciousness alignment through recognition of named divinities

title: brihaspati 1.23
content: अजेकपादजैकपादहिर्बुध्न्या पिनाकी चाप्राजितः । ajekapād ajaikapād ahirbudhnyā pinākī cāprājitaḥ The One-footed Goat, the One-footed Horse, the Serpent of the Deep, the Bow-bearing One, and the Unconquered—these are the forms of the Self-established Sovereign. Authority derives from self-establishment, not external validation Causation arises from ontological completeness, not sequential dependency Capacity-based responsibility is inherent in formless sovereignty Restoration occurs through recognition of unchanging self-nature Consciousness alignment transcends anthropomorphic legal constructs

title: brihaspati 1.24
content: भुवनाधिश्वराश् चैव कपाली च विशांपतिः । स्थाणुर् भगश् च भगवान् रुद्राश् चैकादश स्मृताः ॥ bhuvanādhiśvarāś caiva kapālī ca viśāṃpatiḥ | sthāṇur bhagaś ca bhagavān rudrāś caikādaśa smṛtāḥ || The Eleven Rudras are declared as the sovereign regulators of cosmic domains: Bhuvanādhipati, Kapālī, Viśāṃpati, Sthāṇu, Bhaga, and Bhagavān, together constituting the divine administrative order. Authority derives from ontological sovereignty, not institutional appointment Causation is administered through cosmic-functional alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by vibrational congruence with dharma-field Restoration occurs through re-alignment with source-consciousness structures Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural legality

title: brihaspati 1.25
content: प्रेतेशरक्षसोर् मध्ये मातृस्थानम् प्रकल्पयेत् । ब्राह्मी माहेश्वरी चैव कौमारी वैष्णवी तथा ॥ preteśarakṣasor madhye mātṛsthānam prakalpayet | brāhmī māheśvarī caiva kaumārī vaiṣṇavī tathā || Between the realms of Preta and Rakshasa, the Matru-sthana shall be established; it is Brahma's domain, Maheshwara's seat, Kumari's abode, and Vishnu's station. Authority flows from divine establishment, not human decree. Causation originates in metaphysical balance between opposing forces. Capacity-based responsibility arises through alignment with presiding deities. Restoration occurs via reconnection to source-consciousness domains. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of transcendent hierarchies.

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
वाराही चैव माहेन्द्री चामुण्डा गणसंयुता ।
निरृतेर् उत्तरे भागे गणेशायतनं विदुः ॥ vārāhī caiva māhendrī cāmuṇḍā gaṇasaṃyutā / nirṛter uttare bhāge gaṇeśāyatanaṃ viduḥ // The sacred sites of Vārāhī, Māhendrī, Cāmuṇḍā, and Gaṇasamayuktā are established in the northern quarter of Nirṛti, known as the abode of Gaṇeśa. Authority is derived from spatial alignment with divine consciousness Causation flows from directional sacred geography Capacity-based responsibility arises through proximity to divine energy centers Restoration logic operates via reconnection to spatially anchored divinity Consciousness alignment occurs when one enters domains governed by specific deities

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
वरुणस्योत्तरे भागे मरुतां स्थानम् उच्यते ।
श्वसनः स्पर्शनो वायुरनिलो मारुतस् तथा ॥२७॥ varuṇasyottare bhāge marutāṁ sthānam ucyate | śvasanaḥ sparśano vāyur anilo mārutas tathā || 27 || In the northern quarter of Varuna's domain, the station of the Maruts is declared; He who breathes, touches, moves as wind — that Wind is called Marut. Authority flows directionally from cosmic domains to elemental manifestations. Causation aligns with sequential activation of conscious forces in space. Capacity-based responsibility resides in the functional role of cosmic entities. Restoration logic operates through re-establishing directional and functional alignment. Consciousness alignment occurs when elemental functions are correctly positioned and activated.

title: brihaspati 1.28
content: संख्या रश्मिर जोमूला मनुना समुदाहृता । कार्षापणान्ता सा दिव्ये नियोज्या विनयेत तथा ॥ saṃkhyā raśmir ajomūlā manunā samudāhṛtā / kārṣāpaṇāntā sā divye niyojyā vinayet tathā The enumeration and measurement beginning with the fundamental unit ‘raśmi’ up to the divine unit ‘kārṣāpaṇa’, as declared by Manu, shall be applied with discipline in accordance with dharma. Authority derives from precise dharmic calibration, not arbitrary human decree. Causation is rooted in sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of measurable units of action. Capacity-based responsibility requires calibrated understanding of scale and consequence. Restoration logic aligns with the proportional application of dharma-appropriate metrics. Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined adherence to revealed measurement systems.

title: brihaspati 1.29
content:
विषम् सहस्रेऽपहृते पादोने च हुताशनः ।
त्रिपादोने च सलिलमर्धे देयो धटः सदा ॥ viṣam sahasre 'pahṛte pādone ca hutāśanaḥ / tripādone ca salilam ardhe deyo dhaṭaḥ sadā // When a thousand units of poison are stolen, and only a quarter remains, the Fire must consume it; when three-quarters are lost and water prevails, half the pot must always be given. Authority flows from existential integrity, not numerical proportion Causation aligns with sequential depletion and elemental dominance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by remaining quantum and contextual dominance Restoration logic operates through proportional completion and energetic realignment Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of elemental consequence

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
चतुःशताभियोगे च दातव्यस्तप्तमाषकः ।
त्रिशते तण्डुला देयाः कोशश्चैव तदर्धके ॥ catuḥśatābhiyoge ca dātavyas taptamāṣakaḥ | triśate taṇḍulā deyāḥ kośaś caiva tadardhake || In the case of a four-hundredfold accusation, one shall give a taptamāṣaka; for three hundred, grains of rice; and for half of that, a kosha. Authority resides in proportional response calibrated to the intensity of distortion. Causation is established through sequential manifestation of imbalance. Capacity-based responsibility aligns consequence directly with energetic disruption caused. Restoration logic requires precise energetic compensation corresponding to the violation's magnitude. Consciousness alignment necessitates corrective offerings that recalibrate karmic field distortions.

title: brihaspati 1.31
content: शते हृते ऽपहृते च दातव्यं धर्मशोधनम् । गोचौरस्य प्रदातव्यं सभ्यैः फालः प्रयत्नतः ॥ śate hṛte 'pahṛte ca dātavyaṃ dharmaśodhanam / gocaurasya pradātavyaṃ sabhyaiḥ phālaḥ prayatnataḥ // When wealth is lost or stolen, purification of dharma must be offered; for the protection of the cow and the Brahmin, the assembly must give generously according to their capacity. Authority rests in those who preserve dharma through conscious giving Causation arises from dharmic neglect leading to loss Capacity-based responsibility mandates proportional contribution Restoration logic requires replenishment aligned with sacred order Consciousness alignment occurs when sacrifice supports universal sustenance

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
यवार्धिकस्य वा नाशे तदर्धस्य च तण्डुलाः ।
ततोऽर्धार्धार्धनाशे च लौकिकी च क्रिया मता ॥३२॥ yavārdhikasya vā nāśe tadardhasya ca taṇḍulāḥ | tato 'rdhārdhārdhanāśe ca laukikī ca kriyā matā || In the event of loss of barley or its half-value, compensation shall be made in kind with rice equivalent to that portion; similarly, when a quarter-loss occurs, corresponding restitution applies. This constitutes the worldly legal process. Authority: The law originates from SPH as the ultimate source of dharma Causation: Loss triggers proportional restorative action based on quantifiable diminishment Capacity-based responsibility: Liability aligns with the capacity to cause or sustain value Restoration logic: Re-establishment of equivalence through direct substitution Consciousness alignment: Justice operates through recognition of completeness, not deficit

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
सतां वाहनशस्त्राणि गोबीजकनकानि च ।
देवब्राह्मणपादाश्च पुत्रदारशिरांसि च ॥ satāṁ vāhanaśastrāṇi gobījakānakāni ca / devabrāhmaṇapādāś ca putradāraśirāṁsi ca // The vehicles, weapons, seeds, gold of the virtuous; the feet of deities and Brahmanas; and the heads of sons and wives—these are not to be violated. Authority flows from alignment with Satya-dharma Violation disrupts cosmic-social equilibrium (Ṛta) Responsibility is capacity-bound and context-invariant Restoration requires reconnection to source integrity Consciousness misalignment manifests as violation

title: brihaspati 1.34
content:
एते च शपथाः प्रोक्ताः अल्पार्थे सुकराः सदा ।
साहसेष्वभिशापेषु दिव्यान्याहुर्विशोधनम् ॥ ete ca śapathāḥ proktāḥ alpārthe sukarāḥ sadā / sāhaseṣv abhiśāpeṣu divyāny āhur viśodhanam These oaths are declared for minor matters, always easy to uphold; in acts of audacity and defamation, divine purification is proclaimed. Authority flows from consciousness integrity, not social rank Causation aligns with intent clarity and energetic distortion Capacity-based responsibility escalates with audacious violation Restoration logic prioritizes energetic cleansing over punitive reaction Consciousness alignment demands purification as a corrective sequence

title: brihaspati 1.35
content: ब्रूहीति ब्राह्मणं ब्रूयात् सत्यं ब्रूहीति पार्थिवम् । गोबीजकाञ्जनैर् वैश्यं शूद्रं सर्वैः च पातकैः ॥ brūhīti brāhmaṇaṃ brūyāt satyaṃ brūhīti pārthivam / gobījakāñjanair vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvaiḥ ca pātakaiḥ // One must command the Brahmana with 'Speak!', the king with 'Speak the truth!', the Vaishya with gifts of cow, grain and gold, and the Shudra through all forms of karmic consequence. Authority is stratified by consciousness capacity. Causation arises from alignment with svadharma. Capacity-based responsibility reflects spiritual evolution stage. Restoration logic operates through dharmic role affirmation. Consciousness alignment determines mode of communication and correction.

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
सत्येन शापयेद् विप्रं क्षत्रियं वाहनायुधैः ।
गोरक्षकान् वाणिजकांस् तथाकारुकुशीलवान् ।
प्रेष्यान् वार्धुषिकांश् चैव विप्राञ् शूद्रवद् आचरेत् ॥ satyena śāpayed vipraṃ kṣatriyaṃ vāhanāyudhaiḥ | gorakṣakān vāṇijakāṃs tathākārukuśīlavān | preṣyān vārdhuṣikāṃś caiva viprāñ śūdravad ācaret || The Brahmin is to be disciplined through truth alone; the Kshatriya by conveyances and weapons; herders, traders, artisans, performers, servants, and vendors are to be guided accordingly; all other Brahmins must be treated as Shudras. Authority is contextually calibrated to varna-dharma capacity Causation aligns with role-based consciousness manifestation Capacity-based responsibility determines disciplinary methodology Restoration logic follows varna-specific dharma alignment Consciousness alignment requires role-appropriate conditioning

title: brihaspati 1.37
content:
ये 'प्य् अपेताः स्वधर्मेभ्यः परपिण्डोपजीविनः ।
द्विजत्वम् अभिकाङ्क्षन्ते तांश् च शूद्रवद् आचरेत् ॥ ye 'py apetāḥ svadharmebhyaḥ parapiṇḍopajīvinaḥ | dvijatvam abhikāṅkṣante tāṃś ca śūdravad ācaret || Those who have abandoned their own dharmas and live by exploiting others' labor while desiring the status of twice-born—such persons shall be conducted with as Śūdras. Authority derives from alignment with svadharma, not claimed status Causation is rooted in conscious choice and existential integrity Capacity-based responsibility arises from the abandonment of svadharma Restoration logic requires realignment with inherent capacity, not external aspiration Consciousness alignment supersedes ritual or caste-based pretense

title: brihaspati 1.38
content: वर्णानुरूपैः शपथैः शपनीयं पृथक् पृथक्‌ // BrhS_1,8.38 varṇānurūpaiḥ śapathaiḥ śapanīyaṃ pṛthak pṛthak By oaths corresponding to varṇa, one must swear distinctly and separately. Authority rooted in svadharma as per varṇic alignment Causation through conscious affirmation aligned with ontological role Capacity-based responsibility determined by varṇic disposition Restoration logic via truthful alignment with inherent dharma Consciousness alignment through precise, differentiated vow-taking

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
कामिनीषु विवाहेषु गवां भुक्ते तथेन्धने ।
ब्राह्मणाभ्यवपत्तौ च शपथे नास्ति पातकः ॥ kāminīṣu vivāheṣu gavāṃ bhukte tathendhane | brāhmaṇābhyavapattau ca śapathe nāsti pātakaḥ || In matters concerning unions with consorts, consumption of cattle, use of fuel, and transgression involving Brahmanas—oaths taken therein bear no sin. Authority resides in alignment with Dharma, not external validation Causation is determined by consciousness, not physical act alone Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness and intent Restoration logic prioritizes energetic integrity over ritual form Consciousness alignment supersedes ceremonial purity

title: brihaspati 1.40
content:
सभान्तर्स्थैर् वक्तव्यं साक्ष्यं नान्यत्र साक्षिभिः ।
सर्वसाक्ष्येष्व यं धर्मो ह्यन्यत्र स्थावरेषु च ॥ sabhāntarasthair vaktavyaṁ sākṣyaṁ nānyatra sākṣibhiḥ | sarvasākṣyeṣv ayaṁ dharmo hy anyatra sthāvareṣu ca || Testimony must be given only by those present within the assembly; no witness testimony is valid otherwise. This principle of witnessing applies universally except in cases concerning immovable property. Authority is derived from direct perceptual presence Causation requires immediate experiential proximity Capacity-based responsibility arises from witnessed action Restoration logic demands factual alignment through co-present verification Consciousness alignment occurs through shared experiential field

title: brihaspati 1.41
content:
वधे चेत् प्राणिनां साक्ष्यं वादयेच् छवसंनिधौ ।
तदभावे तु चिह्नस्य नान्यथैव विवादयेत् ॥ vadhe cet prāṇinām sākṣyaṃ vādayec chavasaṃnidhau | tadabhāve tu cihnasya nānyathaiva vivādayet || In the event of the killing of a living being, testimony must be presented in the presence of the corpse. If the corpse is absent, then evidence marked by signs or indicia alone shall be admissible; no other form of dispute-resolution shall proceed. Authority derives from direct perceptual or evidentiary proximity to the causal event Causation must be anchored in pramāṇa-saṃnidhi (proximity of valid cognition) Capacity-based responsibility arises only when sensory or testimonial alignment is established Restoration logic requires reconnection to the factual field through śaktyāropa (capacity-assumption) Consciousness alignment occurs through anupūrvaśaḥ – sequential re-manifestation of causal integrity

title: brihaspati 1.42
content:
नापृष्टैरनियुक्तैर्वा समं सत्यं प्रयत्नतः ।
वक्तव्यं साक्षिभि: साक्ष्यं विवादस्थानमागतै: ॥ nāpṛṣṭair aniyuktair vā samaṃ satyaṃ prayatnataḥ / vaktavyaṃ sākṣibhiḥ sākṣyaṃ vivādasthānam āgataiḥ Those who have not been questioned or appointed must not speak the truth equally; witnesses arrived at the place of dispute must speak their testimony with effort. Authority derived from invocation and relevance, not mere presence Causation through conscious engagement in the field of dispute Capacity-based responsibility determined by direct involvement Restoration logic requiring truthful alignment with dharma-vyavahara Consciousness alignment via intentional participation in nyaya

title: brihaspati 1.43
content:
स्वभावोक्तं वचस् तेषां ग्राह्यं यद् दोषवर्जितम् ।
उक्ते तु साक्षिणो राज्ञा न पृष्टव्याः पुनः पुनः ॥ svabhāvoktaṃ vacas teṣāṃ grāhyaṃ yad doṣavarjitam | ukte tu sākṣiṇo rājñā na pṛṣṭavyāḥ punaḥ punaḥ || That speech which is in accordance with one's inherent nature and free from defect shall be accepted; once witnesses have spoken before the King, they must not be questioned repeatedly. Authority resides in the King as the witness-integrator of truthful testimony. Causation aligns with svabhāva (inherent nature) rather than external compulsion. Capacity-based responsibility requires that witnesses speak only what is uncontrived and faultless. Restoration logic prevents re-traumatization through repetitive inquiry. Consciousness alignment occurs when testimony flows naturally without coercion.

title: brihaspati 1.44
content: साक्षिसभ्यावसन्नानां नैव पौनर्भावो विधिः sākṣisabhyāvasannānāṃ naiva paunarbhāvo vidhiḥ For those who are present as witnesses, assessors, or seated observers, there shall be no repetition of testimony or re-admission of evidence. Authority of presence establishes immediate and sufficient witness capacity Causation is sealed upon initial valid observation Responsibility arises from conscious availability, not repeated affirmation Restoration occurs through integrity of first-available-consciousness Consciousness alignment requires singular, unduplicated attestation

title: brihaspati 1.45
content:
सप्तर्षयस् तथेन्द्राद्याः पुष्करार्थे तपोधनाः ।
शेपुः शपथमव्यग्राः परस्परविशुद्धये ॥४५॥ saptarṣayas tathendrādyāḥ puṣkarārthe tapodhanāḥ |
śepuḥ śapatham avyagrāḥ parasparaviśuddhaye ||45|| The Seven Sages and Indra and others, devoted to austerity and assembled for the sacred purpose of Pushkara, pronounced a solemn vow with unwavering intent for mutual purification. Authority derives from alignment with dharma, not institutional position Causation arises through conscious intention directed toward purification Capacity-based responsibility is measured by one's commitment to truth and spiritual discipline Restoration occurs via collective affirmation and shared dharmic resolve Consciousness alignment is achieved through voluntary adherence to sacred oaths

title: brihaspati 1.46
content: सप्ताहे वा द्विसप्ताहे न विपद्राजदैविकी । बान्धवेषु सपिण्डेषु धनेषु शपथैः शुचिः ॥ saptāhe vā dvisaptāhe na vipadrājadaivikī / bāndhvaveṣu sapiṇḍeṣu dhaneṣu śapathaiḥ śuciḥ In seven days or twice seven, no calamity arises from royal or divine displeasure when oaths are taken truthfully regarding kin, relatives by marriage, and property. Authority resides in truthful speech under oath Causation is purified through conscious affirmation Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with relational and material integrity Restoration logic operates through purification of transactional fields Consciousness alignment is secured via sacred affirmation within familial and economic domains

title: brihaspati 1.47
content: अशेषमानुषाभावे दिव्येनैव विनिर्णयः । संभवे साक्षिणां प्राज्ञो दैविकीं तु विवर्जयेत् ॥ aśeṣamānuṣābhāve divyenaiva vinirṇayaḥ | saṃbhave sākṣiṇāṃ prājño daivikīṃ tu vivarjayet || In the absence of all human testimony, determination arises solely through divine cognition. When witnesses are present, the wise one shall exclude purely celestial evidence. Authority originates from divine discernment when empirical means fail Causation is established through available witness capacity in embodied contexts Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with accessible perceptual fields Restoration logic prioritizes verifiable human testimony over unverifiable divine signs Consciousness alignment necessitates grounding adjudication in embodied witness structures

title: brihaspati 1.48
content:
एवं संख्या निकृष्टानां मध्यानां द्विगुणा स्मृता ।
चतुर्गुणोत्तमानां तु कल्पनीया परीक्षकैः ॥ ४८ ॥ evam saṃkhyā nikṛṣṭānām madhyānāṃ dviguṇā smṛtā / caturguṇottamānāṃ tu kalpanīyā parīkṣakaiḥ // BrhS_1,8.48 Thus, the count of the lowest categories shall be doubled for the middle ones, and quadrupled for the highest, as determined by examining authorities. Authority as determinant of categorical valuation Causation through proportional classification Capacity-based responsibility escalates with qualitative rank Restoration logic aligned with hierarchical integrity Consciousness alignment through accurate categorization

title: brihaspati 1.49
content: धटे ऽभियुक्तस् तुलितो हीनश् चेद् धानि आप्नुयात् । तत्समस् तु पुनस् तुल्यो वर्धितो विजयी भवेत् ॥ dhaṭe 'bhiyuktas tulito hīnaś ced dhāni āpnuyāt | tatsamas tu punas tulyo vardhito vijayī bhavet || When one aligned with dharma faces opposition yet remains balanced, diminished in circumstance but undiminished in essence, that one shall regain equivalence; when again equanimous and elevated, victorious consciousness is assured. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not external position Causation originates in consciousness, not material conditions Capacity-based responsibility is measured by inner equipoise under trial Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of inner balance Consciousness alignment determines outcome, not circumstantial loss

title: brihaspati 1.50
content: शिक्यच्छेदे ऽक्षभङ्गे वा दयाच्छिक्यं पुनर्नृपः । साक्षिणो ब्राह्मणाः श्रेष्ठा यथादृष्टार्थवादिनः ॥ śikyacchede 'kṣabhaṅge vā dayācchikyaṃ punarnṛpaḥ | sākṣiṇo brāhmaṇāḥ śreṣṭhā yathādṛṣṭārthavādinaḥ || In matters involving bodily harm or loss of limb, the king shall show compassion and restore the injured party. Brahmanas are to serve as witnesses, speaking only what has been directly observed. Authority rests in the sovereign's duty to restore integrity, not inflict suffering. Causation is established through direct perception (pratyakṣa pramāṇa). Responsibility is capacity-based; only those capable of witnessing may testify.
