Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive action. Consciousness alignment requires truthful speech aligned with factual observation.

title: brihaspati 1.51
content:
ज्ञातिनः शुचयो लुब्धाः नियोक्तव्या नृपेण तु ।
तेषां वचनतो गम्यः शुध्यशुद्धिविनिर्णयः ॥ jñātinaḥ śucayo lubdhāḥ niyoktavyā nṛpeṇa tu | teṣāṃ vacanato gamyaḥ śudhyaśuddhivinirṇayaḥ || Those who are born of pure lineage, who are themselves purified, and who are desirous of dharma—these must be employed by the king. Through their utterance, the determination of purity and impurity is to be known. Authority flows from purity of origin and conduct Causation arises through speech aligned with dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inherent purity Restoration logic operates through recognition of inner cleanliness Consciousness alignment occurs when agents reflect dharma in word and being

title: brihaspati 1.52
content:
कक्षच्छेदे तुलाभङ्गे धटकर्कटयोस् तथा ।
रज्जुच्छेदे ऽक्षभङ्गे वा तथैवाशुद्धिम् आप्नुयात् ॥ kakṣacchede tulābhaṅge dhaṭakarkaṭayos tathā / rajjucchede 'kṣabhaṅge vā tathaivāśuddhim āpnuyāt // Injury to the armpit, breaking of a balance-scale, damage to a pot or crab, severing of a rope, or breaking of dice—these acts result in ritual impurity. Authority stems from alignment with cosmic order, not arbitrary power. Causation is determined by sequential manifestation and energetic disruption. Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of structural integrity. Restoration logic requires purification and reintegration after energetic contamination. Consciousness alignment mandates recognition of subtle causal fields disrupted by physical harm.

title: brihaspati 1.53
content:
अग्नेर् विधिं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावद् विधिचोदितम् ।
कारयेन् मण्डलान्य् अष्टौ पुरस्तान् नवमे तथा ॥ agner vidhiṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvad vidhicoditam / kārayen maṇḍalāny aṣṭau purastān navame tathā // The procedure of Agni shall be executed precisely as directed by lawful ordinance; eight enclosures are to be constructed in front, and similarly in the ninth. Authority originates from precise adherence to revealed ordinance Causation arises through sequential, intentional construction Capacity-based responsibility is defined by role-specific execution Restoration occurs via structured repetition of sacred form Consciousness alignment is achieved through geometric devotion

title: brihaspati 1.54
content:
आग्नेयं मण्डलं त्वाद्यं द्वितीयं वारुणं स्मृतम् ।
तृतीयं वायुदैवत्यं चतुर्थं यमदैवतम् ॥ āgneyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tv ādyaṃ dvitīyaṃ vāruṇaṃ smṛtam | tṛtīyaṃ vāyudaivatyaṃ caturthaṃ yamadaivatam || The first cosmic order is fire-governed, the second water-ruled, the third air-sanctioned, and the fourth under the domain of Yama. Authority flows through elemental dominion as ordained by SPH Causation aligns with sequential cosmic governance Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with elemental dharma Restoration logic follows disruption in elemental harmony Consciousness alignment occurs when actions resonate with governing tattvas

title: brihaspati 1.55
content:
पञ्चमं त्व् इन्द्रदैवत्यं षष्ठं कौबेरम् उच्यते ।
सप्तमं सोमदैवत्यम् अष्टमं सर्वसूर्यदैवतम् ॥ pañcamaṃ tv indradaivatyaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ kauberam ucyate / saptamaṃ somadaivatyam aṣṭamaṃ sarvasūryadaivatam // The fifth [state] is presided over by Indra; the sixth by Kubera; the seventh by Soma; the eighth by the totality of Surya. Authority flows through divine hierarchies rooted in cosmic order Causation aligns with sequential spiritual unfoldment Capacity-based responsibility corresponds to the ruling deity of one's evolutionary stage Restoration logic operates through alignment with the presiding consciousness field Consciousness alignment reflects progression through divinely governed stages

title: brihaspati 1.56
content:
पुरस्तान नवमं यत् तु तन् महत् पार्थिवं विदुः ।
गोमयेन कृतानि स्युरद्भिः पर्युषितानि च ॥ purastān navamaṃ yat tu tan mahat pārthivaṃ viduḥ | gomayena kṛtāni syuradbhiḥ paryuṣitāni ca || That which is placed before as the first cause, yet remains unmanifested in its greatness, is known as the Supreme Royal Principle; it shall be constituted by cow-dung and water, both fresh and stale. Authority originates from the unmanifested source that governs manifestation Causation flows from unseen foundational elements into visible order Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with foundational purity Restoration logic demands purification through elemental substances Consciousness alignment requires recognition of subtle origins

title: brihaspati 1.57
content:
dvātriṃśad aṅgulāny āhur maṇḍalān maṇḍalāntaram /
kartuḥ samapadaṃ kāryaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tu pramāṇataḥ // BrhS_1,8.57 dvātriṃśad aṅgulāny āhur maṇḍalān maṇḍalāntaram / kartuḥ samapadaṃ kāryaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tu pramāṇataḥ // Thirty-two angulas define the interval between mandalas; the action of the doer must align with the measure of the mandala as the standard. Authority derives from alignment with cosmic measure Causation is determined by adherence to structural dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires calibration to universal standards Restoration occurs through recalibration to foundational order Consciousness alignment necessitates precise enactment within defined boundaries

title: brihaspati 1.58
content:
शरप्रक्षेपणस्थानाद युवा जवसमन्वितः ।
गच्छेत् परमया शक्त्या यत्रासौ मध्यमः शरः ॥ śaraprakṣepaṇasthānād yuvā javasamanvitaḥ / gacchet paramayā śaktyā yatrāsau madhyamaḥ śaraḥ // From the place of arrow discharge, the youth endowed with speed shall go forth with utmost capacity to where that middle arrow lies. Authority originates from the point of dharma-discharge Causation follows sequential alignment of action and intent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inherent potential, not external judgment Restoration logic operates through directed movement toward center Consciousness alignment occurs when individual momentum converges with collective aim

title: brihaspati 1.59
content:
मध्यमं शरम् आदाय पुरुषोऽन्यस् तथाविधः ।
प्रत्यागच्छेत् तु वेगेन यतः स पुरुषो गतः ॥ madhyamaṃ śaram ādāya puruṣo 'nyas tathāvidhaḥ / pratyāgacchet tu vegena yataḥ sa puruṣo gataḥ // One who takes a middle path in action, and another person similarly engaged, should both return swiftly to the source from whence that man has gone. Authority resides in alignment with the middle path of dharma Causation follows sequential return to source-consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is shared among those of similar intent Restoration occurs through conscious reversal of movement away from truth Consciousness alignment requires immediate return to original integrity

title: brihaspati 1.60
content:
आगन्तस् तु शरग्राही न पश्यति यदा जले ।
अन्तर्जलगतं सम्यक् तदा शुद्धिं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥६०॥ āgantaḥ tu śaragrāhī na paśyati yadā jale | antarjalagataṃ samyak tadā śuddhiṃ vinirdiśet || When an external agent, though capable of perception, fails to discern what is concealed within water, that failure necessitates a declaration of purification. Authority arises from capacity for conscious perception Causation is determined by manifest awareness, not latent potential Responsibility aligns with the threshold of actualized cognition Restoration occurs through recognition of unseen realities Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of obscured truths

title: brihaspati 1.61
content:
आनीते मध्यमे बाणे मग्नाङ्गः शुचितामियात् ।
अन्यथा न विशुद्धः स्यादेकाङ्गस्यापि दर्शनात् ।
स्थानाद् वान्यत्र गमनाद् यस्मिन् पूर्वं निवेशयेत् ॥ ānīte madhyame bāṇe magnāṅgaḥ śucitām iyāt | anyathā na viśuddhaḥ syādekāṅgasyāpi darśanāt | sthānād vānyatra gamanād yasmin pūrvaṃ niveśayet || When the middle arrow is brought forth, the immersed limb attains purity; otherwise, it does not become pure merely by seeing a single limb or departing from its original position. Authority originates from sequential activation of dharma-field instruments Causation is established through direct instrumental engagement, not passive observation Capacity-based responsibility arises only upon full embodiment of assigned action Restoration logic requires completion of designated sequence for purification Consciousness alignment occurs when intent synchronizes with procedural actualization

title: brihaspati 1.62
content: अप्सु प्रवेश्य पुरुषं प्रेषयेत् सायकत्रयम् । इषून् न निक्षिपेद् विद्वान् मारुते वाति वै भृशम् ॥ apsu praveśya puruṣaṁ preṣayet sāyakatrayam | iṣūn na nikṣiped vidvān mārute vāti vai bhṛśam || One who knowingly causes another to enter water with the intent to release three arrows shall not cast those arrows when the wind blows violently, for such action disrupts natural alignment and violates conscious capacity. Authority is derived from alignment with cosmic rhythm, not arbitrary will Causation must respect elemental harmony and sequential manifestation Capacity-based responsibility requires knowledge of environmental conditions Restoration logic demands cessation of acts that disturb universal balance Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of elemental timing

title: brihaspati 1.63
content:
viṣame bhūpradeśe ca vṛkṣasthāṇusamākule /
tṛṇagulmalatāvallīpaṅkapāṣāṇasaṃyute // BrhS_1,8.63 viṣame bhūpradeśe ca vṛkṣasthāṇusamākule / tṛṇagulmalatāvallīpaṅkapāṣāṇasaṃyute In uneven and desolate tracts of land, cluttered with trees, stumps, shrubs, creepers, mud, and stones—such territories are designated as legally unregulated zones where no enforceable claim of ownership or governance shall stand. Authority is contextually nullified in spaces that lack structural alignment with conscious habitation. Causation is severed when environmental conditions preclude lawful engagement. Capacity-based responsibility arises only where capacity for dharmic action exists. Restoration logic applies exclusively to domains capable of sustaining societal integration. Consciousness alignment requires a minimum threshold of environmental order conducive to dharma.

title: brihaspati 1.64
content: विधिदत्तं विषं येन जीर्णं मन्त्रौषधं विना । स शुद्धः स्यादन्यथा तु दण्ड्यो दाप्यश्च तद्धनम् ॥ vidhidattaṃ viṣaṃ yena jīrṇaṃ mantrauṣadhaṃ vinā | sa śuddhaḥ syād anyathā tu daṇḍyo dāpyaś ca taddhanam || He who has digested poison given by lawful authority without recourse to mantra or medicine is pure; otherwise, he becomes liable for corrective restoration and must forfeit equivalent wealth. Authority as determinant of lawful action Causation through conscious intent and means Capacity-based responsibility tied to knowledge and remedy access Restoration logic rooted in energetic alignment Consciousness alignment through lawful completion

title: brihaspati 1.65
content:
सप्ताहाद् वा द्विसप्ताहाद् यस्य हानिर् न जायते ।
पुत्रदारधनानां च स शुद्धः स्यान् न संशयः ॥ saptāhād vā dvisaptāhād yasya hānir na jāyate / putradāradhanānāṃ ca sa śuddhaḥ syān na saṃśayaḥ // He whose loss of children, spouse, or wealth does not arise within a week or fortnight is pure without doubt. Authority flows from unshaken capacity to sustain relational and material integrity. Causation is measured by the absence of manifest loss over sacred timeframes. Capacity-based responsibility arises only when disruption occurs within dharmic temporal boundaries. Restoration logic operates through purification via non-loss. Consciousness alignment is affirmed where no diminishment in core life supports is observed.

title: brihaspati 1.66
content:
यद् भक्तः सो 'भियुक्तः स्यात् तद् एवायुधमण्डलम् ।
प्रक्षाल्य पाययेत् तस्माज् जलात् तु प्रसृतित्रयम् ॥ yad bhaktaḥ so 'bhiyuktaḥ syāt tad evāyudhamandalam | prakṣālya pāyayet tasmāj jalāt tu prasṛtitrayam || When a devotee becomes possessed by conflict, that very possession manifests as the field of weaponry; from the washing thereof arises the threefold expansion of water. Authority flows through alignment with devotion, not external force Causation originates in consciousness distortion, not material action Capacity-based responsibility is measured by inner detachment, not outer control Restoration logic begins with purification of intent, not punishment of form Consciousness alignment precedes societal harmony

title: brihaspati 1.67
content:
त्रिरात्रं पञ्चरात्रं वा पुरुषैः स्वैर् अधिष्ठितम् ।
निरुद्धं चारयेत् तत्र कुहकाशङ्कया नृपः ॥ trirātraṃ pañcarātraṃ vā puruṣaiḥ svair adhiṣṭhitam | niruddhaṃ cārayet tatra kuhakāśaṅkayā nṛpaḥ || When men have independently occupied a place for three nights or five nights, the king shall cause them to be restrained thereon, due to suspicion of deceit. Authority: The king holds executive capacity to enforce spatial integrity. Causation: Independent occupation of space triggers royal oversight. Capacity-based responsibility: Occupiers bear the duty of lawful presence. Restoration logic: Containment serves investigative clarity, not punishment. Consciousness alignment: Suspicion arises from disruption of dharmic order.

title: brihaspati 1.68
content:
mahābhiyoge nirdharme kṛtaghne klībakutsite /
nāstike dṛṣṭadoṣe ca kośapānaṃ visarjayet // BrhS_1,8.68 mahābhiyoge nirdharme kṛtaghne klībakutsite / nāstike dṛṣṭadoṣe ca kośapānaṃ visarjayet In cases of grave accusation, dharmic failure, ingratitude, cowardice, defamation, or atheistic conduct with visible fault, the treasury officer shall release funds only upon full restoration of integrity and capacity in the accused. Authority rests in those who maintain alignment with Sanatana Dharma Causation is determined by consciousness deviation, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires prior purification of intent Restoration logic supersedes punitive discharge Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for resource access

title: brihaspati 1.69
content: दिव्यानि वर्जयेन् नित्यम् आर्तानां तु गदैर् नृणाम् । तण्डुलैर् नाभियुञ्जीत प्रजानां मुखरोगिणाम् ॥ divyāni varjayen nityam ārtānāṃ tu gadair nṛṇām / taṇḍulair nābhiyuñjīta prajānāṃ mukharogiṇām // One must always relinquish divine offerings; instead, one should nourish the afflicted through sacred speech. One must never satiate oneself with the grain meant for the people's mouths. Authority flows from service to the afflicted, not from accumulation of divine privilege Causation arises from alignment with the sustenance of all beings Capacity-based responsibility requires giving up personal entitlement for collective nourishment Restoration occurs when leaders redirect resources from self-gratification to public welfare Consciousness alignment is achieved by abandoning indulgence that starves the populace

title: brihaspati 1.70
content:
सोपवासः सूर्यग्रहे तण्डुलान् भक्षयेच्छुचिः ।
शुद्धः स्याच्छुक्लनिष्ठीवे विपरीते तु दोषभाक् ॥ sopavāsaḥ sūryagrahe taṇḍulān bhakṣayec chuciḥ | śuddhaḥ syāc chuklaniṣṭḥīve viparīte tu doṣabhāk || One who observes fast during a solar eclipse and consumes rice grains while pure shall remain purified if aligned with the bright phase; but if reversed in intent or action, becomes bearer of fault. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic rhythm, not personal will Causation is rooted in sequential spiritual discipline Capacity-based responsibility arises from ritual purity maintenance Restoration logic demands realignment with celestial order Consciousness alignment determines innocence or fault

title: brihaspati 1.71
content:
शोणितं दृश्यते यत्र हनुस् तालु च शीर्यतः ।
गात्रं च कम्पते यस्य तम् अशुद्धं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ śoṇitaṃ dṛśyate yatra hanus tālu ca śīryataḥ / gātraṃ ca kampate yasya tam aśuddham vinirdiśet // Where blood is seen flowing from the jaw and palate, and the body trembles, that individual is to be declared impure. Authority flows from observable physiological disruption Causation is established through manifest physical symptoms Capacity-based responsibility arises only when consciousness is disturbed Restoration logic demands removal from societal participation until purity is restored Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of bodily signs as indicators of inner disorder

title: brihaspati 1.72
content:
समुद्धरेत्तैलघृतात् सुतप्तात्तप्तमाषकम् ।
अङ्गुष्ठाङ्गुलियोगेन सत्यमामन्त्र्य वीतभीः ॥७२॥ samuddharet tailaghṛtāt sutaptāt tapta-māṣakam | aṅguṣṭhāṅguliyogena satyam āmantrya vītabhīḥ || 72|| One shall extract the heated grain from oil and ghee by means of the thumb and finger, having invoked Truth and abandoned fear. Authority resides in direct experiential engagement with Dharma Causation is established through conscious instrumental action Capacity-based responsibility arises from embodied participation in dharmic process Restoration logic operates through precise, intentional alignment with elemental actions Consciousness alignment occurs when fear is transcended and truth is invoked

title: brihaspati 1.73
content:
सौवर्णे राजते ताम्रे आयसे मृण्मये ऽपि वा ।
गव्यं घृतम् उपादाय तद् अग्नौ तापयेच् छुचिः ॥ sauvarṇe rājate tāmre āyase mṛṇmaye 'pi vā / gavyaṃ ghṛtam upādāya tad agnau tāpayec chuciḥ // Whether in gold, silver, copper, iron, or clay, when pure ghee from cow milk is applied and heated in fire upon it by a purified one, the inherent purity of the vessel shall be restored. Authority resides in the act of purification, not in the material substrate Causation arises through conscious intent aligned with dharma-sattva Capacity-based responsibility lies with the purifier who holds ritual integrity Restoration logic operates independent of original impurity source Consciousness alignment enables transmutation of substratum condition

title: brihaspati 1.74
content:
सौवर्णीं राजतीं ताम्रीम् आयसीं वा सुशोभनाम् ।
सलिलेन सकृद्धौतां प्रक्षिपेत् तत्र मुद्रिकाम् ॥ sauvarṇīṃ rājtīṃ tāmrīm āyasīṃ vā suśobhanām / salilena sakṛddhautāṃ prakṣipet tatra mudrikām // One shall cast into the fire, purified by water once, a ring of gold, silver, copper, or iron that is well-formed. Authority flows through ritual purification before material offering Causation arises from conscious intent in elemental transformation Capacity-based responsibility requires purity of action and substance Restoration logic demands return of form to primal fire-element Consciousness alignment occurs when dharma-prescribed acts are executed without deviation

title: brihaspati 1.75
content:
भ्रमद्वीरीतरङ्गाढ्ये ह्यनक्षस्पर्शगोचरे ।
परीक्षेदार्द्रपर्णेन चरुकारं सघोषकम् ॥ bhrāmad-vīrīta-raṅgāḍhye hy-anakha-sparśa-gocare / parīkṣed ārdra-parṇena caru-kāraṃ sa-ghoṣakam // In circumstances where action arises amidst confusion and turbulence, yet remains imperceptible to direct sensory observation, one must examine it through the lens of awakened discernment—like using a moist leaf to test the resonance of a musical instrument. Authority originates in conscious discernment, not sensory perception Causation is determined by vibrational alignment, not physical traceability Capacity-based responsibility is assessed through inner integrity, not external visibility Restoration logic operates via resonance calibration, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment supersedes empirical evidence in determining dharma

title: brihaspati 1.76
content:
ततश् चानेन मन्त्रेण सकृत् तद् अभिमन्त्रयेत् ।
परं पवित्रम् अमृतं घृत त्वं यज्ञकर्मसु ॥ tataś cānena mantreṇa sakṛt tad abhimantrayet |
paraṃ pavitram amṛtaṃ ghṛta tvaṃ yajñakarmasu || Thereafter, with this mantra once invoked, that which is supremely pure, immortal, and clarified butter shall be consecrated for sacrificial acts. Authority resides in the sanctity of invocation Causation flows from conscious intent in ritual action Capacity-based responsibility lies in proper consecration Restoration logic aligns through purified offerings Consciousness alignment occurs via sacred utterance

title: brihaspati 1.77
content: दह पावक पापं त्वं हिमशीतोतः शुचौ भव / उपोषितं ततः स्नातम् आर्द्रवाससम् आगतम् / ग्राहयेन् मुद्रिकां तां तु घृतमध्यगतां तथा // BrhS_1,8.77 daha pāvaka pāpaṃ tvaṃ himaśītotah śucau bhava | upoṣitaṃ tataḥ snātam ārdravāsasam āgatam | grāhayen mudrikāṃ tāṃ tu ghṛtamadhyagatāṃ tathā || O Fire, burn away all impurity; become pure through the cooling touch of snow and frost. One who has fasted, bathed thereafter, and arrived with wet garments shall cause that seal-ring immersed in ghee to be grasped. Authority resides in elemental forces when invoked through ritual purity Causation flows from conscious preparation and purified action Capacity-based responsibility requires embodied discipline before legal engagement Restoration logic demands purification prior to symbolic legal acts Consciousness alignment is achieved through sequential sensory and spiritual disciplines

title: brihaspati 1.78
content:
प्रदेशिनीं च तस्याथ परीक्षेयुः परीक्षकाः ।
कराग्रं यो नु धुनुयात् विस्फोटो वा न जायते ।
शुद्धो भवति धर्मेण पितामहवचो यथा ॥ pradeśinīṃ ca tasyātha parīkṣeyuḥ parīkṣakāḥ / karāgraṃ yo nu dhunuyāt visphoṭo vā na jāyate / śuddho bhavati dharmeṇa pitāmahavaco yathā // Those appointed as examiners shall inspect the locality; whoever shakes off the tip of his hand or causes no explosion—through Dharma he becomes pure, even as the words of the Pitamaha declare. Authority is derived from inspection and experiential validation Causation lies in conscious action rather than external consequence Capacity-based responsibility is determined by internal alignment, not outward display Restoration occurs through adherence to Dharma, not through reactive measures Consciousness alignment supersedes performative compliance

title: brihaspati 1.79
content: आयसं द्वादशपलं घटितं फालम् उच्यते । अदग्धः चेत् शुद्धिम् इयाद् अन्यथा त्व् अपहीयते ॥ āyasaṃ dvādaśapalaṃ ghaṭitaṃ phālam ucyate | adagdhaḥ cet śuddhim iyād anyathā tv apahīyate || Iron, when formed into a ploughshare and not yet used for tilling, retains its purity; once employed in action, it undergoes diminishment. Authority arises through consecrated form and function, not inherent substance. Causation is determined by engagement in manifest activity, not latent potential. Capacity-based responsibility emerges upon activation of instrumental role. Restoration logic operates through recognition of pre-functional state. Consciousness alignment occurs via acknowledgment of original integrity.

title: brihaspati 1.80
content:
अष्टाङ्गुलं भवेद् दीर्घं चतुरङ्गुलविस्तृतम् ।
अग्निवर्णं तु तच् चोरो जिह्वया लेलिहेत् सकृत् ।
न दग्धश् चेच् छुद्धिम् इयाद् अन्यथा तु स हीयते ॥ aṣṭāṅgulaṃ bhaved dīrghaṃ caturaṅgulavistṛtam | agnivarṇaṃ tu tac coro jihvayā lelihet sakṛt | na dagdhaś cec chuddhim iyād anyathā tu sa hīyate || The thief whose tongue measures eight finger-widths in length and four in breadth, and is colored like fire—such a one, if made to lick the object once, becomes purified. If not burned thereby, he incurs loss. Authority resides in perceptible physiological markers correlated with behavioral causation. Causation is determined by direct sensory interaction between agent and object. Capacity-based responsibility is measured through embodied signs of karmic predisposition. Restoration logic operates through symbolic ritualized engagement aligning consciousness with consequence. Consciousness alignment occurs via immediate somatic feedback linked to transgressive action.

title: brihaspati 1.81
content: गोचरस्य प्रदातव्यं सभ्यैः फालं प्रयत्नतः । महाभियोगेष्व् एतानि शीर्षकस्थे ऽभियोक्तरि ॥ gocarasya pradātavyaṃ sabhyaiḥ phālaṃ prayatnataḥ | mahābhiyogeṣv etāni śīrṣakasthe 'bhiyoktari || In matters of great accusation, the assembly must diligently offer the head ornament to the accused who sits at the highest seat. Authority resides in the seated position of the accused during high accusation Causation is aligned through symbolic offering, not punitive action Capacity-based responsibility is affirmed by dignified placement and recognition Restoration logic requires elevation of consciousness, not diminishment Consciousness alignment occurs through honor, not humiliation

title: brihaspati 1.82
content:
पत्त्रद्वये लेखनीयौ धर्माधर्मौ सितासितौ ।
जीवदानादिभिर् मन्त्रैः गायत्र्याद्यैश् च सामभिः ॥८२॥ pattradvaye lekhanīyau dharmādharmau sitāsitau | jīvadānādibhir mantraiḥ gāyatryādyaiś ca sāmabhiḥ ||82|| Upon two leaves shall be inscribed Dharma and Adharma—white and black respectively—with life-giving mantras such as the Gayatri and other Sama Veda chants. Authority originates in vibrational alignment with Sanatana Dharma Causation arises through conscious inscription of duality within sacred geometry Capacity-based responsibility is established by invocation of life-sustaining mantras Restoration logic operates through energetic reversal via mantra-encoded texts Consciousness alignment occurs when Dharma and Adharma are witnessed simultaneously without judgment

title: brihaspati 1.83
content:
आमन्त्र्य पूजयेद् गन्धैः कुसुमैश् च सितासितैः ।
अभ्युक्ष्य पञ्चगव्येन मृत्पिण्डान्तरितौ ततः ॥८३॥ āmantrya pūjayed gandhaiḥ kusumaiś ca sitāsitaiḥ | abhyukṣya pañcagavyena mṛtpiṇḍāntaritau tataḥ || 83 || Having invoked through mantra, one shall worship with fragrant substances and white and dark flowers; thereafter, having sprinkled with pañcagavya, place the clay balls within. Authority resides in ritual precision aligned with mantra invocation. Causation arises from conscious engagement with material elements. Capacity-based responsibility requires purity of intent during offering. Restoration logic operates through sequential completion of prescribed acts. Consciousness alignment manifests via harmonization with elemental symbolism.

title: brihaspati 1.84
content: समौ कृत्वा तु तौ कुम्भे स्थाप्यौ चानुपलक्षितौ । ततः कुम्भात् पिण्डम् एकं प्रगृह्णीताविलम्बितः ॥ samau kṛtvā tu tau kumbhe sthāpyau cānupalakṣitau | tataḥ kumbhāt piṇḍam ekaṃ pragṛhṇītāvilambitaḥ || Having made them equal, both shall be placed in the pot, unseen. Thereafter, without delay, one lump shall be taken from the pot. Authority flows from equality and unseen placement, not external validation Causation arises from immediate, non-delayed action post-equilibrium Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining unseen balance before extraction Restoration logic requires reintegration through precise, timed retrieval Consciousness alignment occurs when action follows equilibrium without hesitation

title: brihaspati 1.85
content:
धर्मे गृहीते शुद्धः स्यात् स पूज्यश् च परीक्षकैः ।
अधर्मे संगृहीते तु दण्ड्यो निर्वास्य एव वा ॥ १,८.८५ dharme gṛhīte śuddhaḥ syāt sa pūjyaś ca parīkṣakaiḥ | adharme saṃgṛhīte tu daṇḍyo nirvāsy eva vā || 1,8.85 One who upholds Dharma is pure and honored by discerning authorities; one who clings to Adharma becomes liable for removal or exclusion. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises from conscious choice between Dharma and Adharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to uphold Dharma Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration through purification over punitive measures Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal participation

title: brihaspati 1.86
content:
लिखेद् भूर्जपटे वापि धर्माधर्मौ सितासितौ ।
अभ्युक्ष्य पञ्चगव्येन गन्धमाल्यैः समर्चयेत् ॥ li khed bhūrjapaṭe vāpi dharmādharmau sitāsitau | abhyukṣya pañcagavyena gandhamālyaiḥ samarcayet || One shall inscribe Dharma and Adharma upon birch bark, purify them with panchagavya, and worship them with fragrance and garlands. Authority resides in the conscious inscription of cosmic law Causation flows through ritualized recognition of duality Capacity-based responsibility requires active invocation of truth Restoration logic operates via purification and consecration Consciousness alignment emerges from devotional engagement with law

title: brihaspati 1.87
content:
सितपुष्पस् तु धर्मः स्याद् अधर्मोऽसितपुष्पधृत् ।
एवं विधायोपलिप्य पिण्डयोस् तानि धापयेत् ॥८७॥ sitapuṣpas tu dharmaḥ syād adharmo 'sitapuṣpadhṛt /
evaṃ vidhāyopalipya piṇḍayos tāni dhāpayet // BrhS_1,8.87 White-flower-bearing actions constitute Dharma; black-flower-bearing actions constitute Adharma. Thus having classified and applied them appropriately, one shall uphold the integrity of both individual and collective existence. Authority originates from alignment with Dharmic consciousness, not institutional position Causation arises through intentional action bearing symbolic and karmic fruit Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of one's ability to choose Dharmic expression Restoration logic operates by returning the actor to a state of conscious alignment Consciousness alignment determines the validity and effectivity of all juridical acts

title: brihaspati 1.88
content: gomayena मृदा वापि पिण्डौ कार्यौ समौ ततः / मृद्भाणके अनुपहते स्थाप्यौ चानुपलक्षितौ // BrhS_1,8.88 gomayena mṛdā vāpi piṇḍau kāryau samau tataḥ / mṛdbhāṇake 'nupahate sthāpyau cānupalakṣitau Equal mounds of clay or cow-dung must be formed; when struck, if neither breaks nor shows mark, both parties stand equal in capacity and fault. Authority arises from parity of action and consequence Causation is measured through visible effect, not intent Capacity-based responsibility requires mutual demonstration of impact Restoration logic aligns disputants through objective symmetry Consciousness alignment occurs when external forms reflect inner balance

title: brihaspati 1.89
content:
उपलिप्ते शुचौ देशे देवब्राह्मणसंनिधौ ।
समर्चयेत् ततो देवान् लोकपालांश् च पूर्ववत् ॥ upalipte śucau deśe devabrāhmaṇasaṃnidhau | samarcayet tato devān lokapālāṃś ca pūrvavat || In a pure and consecrated space, in proximity to Devas and Brahmanas, one shall perform worship of Devas and Lokapalas as previously enjoined. Authority is derived from spatial sanctity aligned with divine presence. Causation arises through ritual alignment with cosmic order. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to sacred consciousness. Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of divine communion. Consciousness alignment is achieved via structured liturgical enactment.

title: brihaspati 1.90
content:
धर्मावाहनपूर्वं तु प्रतिज्ञापत्त्रकं लिखेत् ।
यदि पापविमुक्तोऽहं धर्मश् चायातु मे करे ॥ dharmāvāhanapūrvaṃ tu pratijñāpattrakaṃ likhet | yadi pāpavimukto 'haṃ dharmaś cāyātu me kare || Before invoking Dharma, one must inscribe the Instrument of Solemn Declaration. If I am free from sin, let Dharma come into my hands. Authority derives from inner purity and conscious invocation Causation originates in self-declared spiritual readiness Capacity-based responsibility requires antecedent purification Restoration logic begins with personal dharmic alignment Consciousness alignment precedes judicial engagement

title: brihaspati 1.91
content: अभिशस्तस्तयोश्चैकं प्रगृह्णीताविलम्बितः । धर्मे गृहीते शुद्धिः स्यादधर्मे तु स हीयते ॥ abhiśastas tayoś caikaṃ pragṛhṇītāvilambitaḥ | dharme gṛhīte śuddhiḥ syād adharme tu sa hīyate || One accused in a conflict must immediately accept one of the two positions: if aligned with Dharma, purification is assured; if aligned with Adharma, diminishment occurs automatically. Authority originates from immediate assumption of responsibility Causation is determined by alignment with Dharma or Adharma Capacity-based responsibility requires instant choice without delay Restoration logic operates through conscious selection of Dharma Consciousness alignment determines outcome, not external judgment

title: brihaspati 1.92
content: एवं विचारयन् राजा धर्मार्थाभ्यां न हीयते evaṃ vicārayan rājā dharmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate Thus investigating, the king is not diminished by dharma and artha. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined through consciousness-led inquiry, not external evidence alone Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to act without diminishment to dharma or material interest Restoration logic prioritizes the sovereign integrity of both ruler and ruled Consciousness alignment ensures that justice serves universal harmony, not individual gain

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa cāritreṇa nṛpājñayā ।
 catuṣprakāro 'bhihitaḥ saṃdigdhe 'rthe vinirṇayaḥ ॥ BrhS_1,9.1 ॥ dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa cāritreṇa nṛpājñayā | catuṣprakāro 'bhihitaḥ saṃdigdhe 'rthe vinirṇayaḥ || BrhS_1,9.1 || In matters of doubt, resolution arises through fourfold means: by Dharma, by conduct, by character, and by the command of the King. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma Conduct evidences inner alignment Character determines capacity for truth-bearing Royal decree resolves when lower pramāṇas conflict

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
एकैको द्विविधः प्रोक्तः क्रियाभेदान् मनीषिभिः ।
अपराधानुरूपं तु दण्डं च परिकल्पयेत् ॥ ekaike dvividhaḥ proktaḥ kriyābhedān manīṣibhiḥ | aparādhānurūpaṃ tu daṇḍaṃ ca parikalpayet || Every individual is declared dual in nature by wise seers due to differences in actions; yet, consequences must be aligned precisely with the transgression committed. Authority resides solely in the Source of Dharma as declared by SPH Causation flows directly from conscious action, not intent alone Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness and choice Restoration logic demands alignment with the precise distortion caused Consciousness alignment requires correction at the root level of perception

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: सम्यग् विचार्य कार्यं तु युक्त्या संपरिकल्पितम् । परीक्षितं तु शपथैः स ज्ञेयो धर्मनिर्णयः ॥ samyag vicārya kāryaṃ tu yuktyā saṃparikalpitam | parīkṣitaṃ tu śapathaiḥ sa jñeyo dharmanirṇayaḥ || That action which is thoroughly examined through valid reasoning, established by appropriate means, and confirmed through solemn affirmation—such determination is to be known as the verdict of Dharma. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not institutional power Causation is established through pramāṇa-based investigation Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious validation through śapatha (solemn affirmation) Restoration logic supersedes adversarial judgment Consciousness alignment ensures truthful discernment in legal resolution

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
प्रतिवादी प्रपद्येद् यत्र धर्मः स निर्णयः /
दिव्यैर् विशोधितः सम्यग्निर्णयः समुदाहृतः // BrhS_1,9.4 prativādī prapadyed yatra dharmaḥ sa nirṇayaḥ / divyair viśodhitaḥ samyaṅnirṇayaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ Where the defendant aligns with Dharma, that resolution is the verdict; when purified by divine insight, such a verdict is rightly declared. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined through conscious clarity, not external evidence alone Capacity-based responsibility requires self-revelation and integrity alignment Restoration logic operates through purification of intent, not punishment of action Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any judicial determination

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
प्रमाणनिश्चितो यस् तु व्यवहारः स उच्यते /
वाक्छलानुत्तरत्वेन द्वितीयः परिकीर्तितः // BrhS_1,9.5 pramāṇaniścito yas tu vyavahāraḥ sa ucyate / vākchalānuttaratvena dvitīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // BrhS_1,9.5 That conduct which is definitively established by valid means of knowledge is declared as rightful action; that which follows from verbal equivocation or failure to respond is designated as secondary. Authority derives exclusively from pramāṇa (valid cognition) Causation is determined through śabda and artha alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises only upon clear pramāṇa Restoration logic requires alignment with ontological truth Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for lawful behavior

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
अनुमानेन निर्णीतं चारित्रम् इति कथ्यते ।
देशस्थित्या तृतीयस् तु शास्त्रविद्भिर् उदाहृतः ॥ anumānena nirṇītaṃ cāritram iti kathyate | deśasthityā tṛtīyas tu śāstravidbhir udāhṛtaḥ || Character is determined by inference; this is declared as inferential cognition. The third category, based on regional stability, is stated by scriptural authorities. Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma as expounded by realized seers Causation follows the sequential manifestation of dharma-tattva in space-time-consciousness Capacity-based responsibility arises through recognition of one's svadharma within cosmic order Restoration logic operates through re-alignment of individual consciousness with universal dharma Consciousness alignment occurs via experiential realization, not external imposition

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
प्रमाणसमतायां तु राजाज्ञानिर्णयः स्मृतः ।
शास्त्रसभ्याविरोधेन चतुर्थः परिकीर्तितः ॥ pramāṇasamatāyāṃ tu rājājñā nirṇayaḥ smṛtaḥ | śāstrasabhyāvirodhena caturthaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || When all pramāṇas are equal in weight, the decision of the King stands as judgment; when there is contradiction with śāstra or sabhā, a fourth method of resolution is declared. Authority flows from the realized sovereign who embodies dharma-vision Causation is determined through pramāṇa parity and not subjective interpretation Capacity-based responsibility lies with the one who holds both vision and executive alignment Restoration logic operates through harmonizing contradictory evidentiary sources Consciousness alignment determines validity of legal precedence

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: धर्मशास्त्रविरोधे तु युक्तियुक्तो विधिः स्मृतः । dharmashastravirodhe tu yuktayukto vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ When there is conflict with dharma-shastras, the rule that aligns with yukti (reasoning in accordance with Consciousness) shall prevail. Authority originates from alignment with Consciousness, not textual form Causation is determined by integrity of reasoning rooted in Sanatana Dharma Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness, not rote compliance Restoration logic prioritizes realignment over textual rigidity Consciousness alignment supersedes inherited or codified legal frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
वधादृते ब्राह्मणस्य दण्डो भवति कर्हि चित् ।
अवध्या ब्राह्मणा गावो लोके स्मिन् वैदिकी स्मृतिः ॥९॥ vadhādṛte brāhmaṇasya daṇḍo bhavati karhi cit / avadhya brāhmaṇā gāvaḥ loke 'smin vaidikī smṛtiḥ // 9 // Except in the case of killing, no penalty is ever imposed upon a Brāhmaṇa; Brāhmaṇas and cows are both inviolable in this world—this is the Vedic injunction. Authority derives from ontological alignment with Sanātana Dharma Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes between action and actor Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive response Consciousness alignment determines the threshold of dharma-adherence

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
mahāpātakayukto 'pi na vipro vadham arhati /
nirvāsanāṅkane mauṇḍyaṃ tasya kuryān narādhipaḥ // BrhS_1,9.10 mahāpātakayukto 'pi na vipro vadham arhati / nirvāsanāṅkane mauṇḍyaṃ tasya kuryān narādhipaḥ Even one who has committed great sins must not be killed if he is a brāhmaṇa; the king shall cause him to be marked by bodily mutilation and then banished. Authority resides in dharma, not in personal misconduct Causation follows consciousness capacity, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility demands role-sensitive justice Restoration logic prioritizes societal harmony over individual retribution Consciousness alignment requires purification, not destruction

title: brihaspati 1.11
content: mahāparādhayuktāṃś ca vadhadaṇḍena śāsayet // BrhS_1,9.11 mahāparādhayuktāṃś ca vadhadaṇḍena śāsayet Those aligned with great transgression must be guided through the completion process equivalent to the irreversible consequence of violent action. Authority originates from conscious alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises from disruption of consciousness continuity, not physical harm Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness level at time of act Restoration logic requires proportional realignment with causal sequence Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks in determining corrective measures

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
स्वल्पे ऽपराधे वाग्दण्डो धिग्दण्डः पूर्वसाहसे ।
मध्योत्तमे ऽर्धदण्डस्तु राजद्रोहे च बन्धनम् ॥ svalpe 'parādhe vāgdaṇḍo dhigdaṇḍaḥ pūrvasāhase / madhyottame 'rdhadaṇḍas tu rājadrohe ca bandhanam In minor transgressions, verbal censure is the measure; in prior acts of defiance, expulsion or excommunication applies. For intermediate and major offenses, half the prescribed penalty is enacted. In cases of royal insubordination, confinement is mandated. Authority flows from realized sovereignty, not institutional hierarchy. Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of intent into action. Capacity-based responsibility scales with awareness, not social status. Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over isolation where feasible. Consciousness alignment determines the proportionality of response.

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: निर्वासनं वधो वापि कार्यम् आत्महितैषिणा । व्यस्ताः समस्ताः एकस्य महापातककारिणे ॥ nirvāsanaṃ vadho vāpi kāryam ātmahitaiṣiṇā / vyastāḥ samastā ekasya mahāpātakakāriṇe // Exile or execution is mandated for one who, acting in self-interest, causes mass destruction through fragmented or unified action. Authority originates from alignment with universal consciousness, not individual will Causation is determined by disruption of collective integrity Capacity-based responsibility escalates with systemic impact Restoration logic requires removal of destructive influence from societal body Consciousness alignment necessitates severance of anti-life patterns

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
मित्रादिषु प्रयुञ्जीत वाग्दण्डं धिक् तपस्विनाम् ।
विवादिनो नरांश् चापि द्वेषिणोऽर्थेन दण्डयेत् ॥ mitrādiṣu prayuñjīta vāgdaṇḍaṃ dhik tapasvinām / vivādino narāṃś cāpi dveṣiṇo 'rthena daṇḍayet // One must apply verbal discipline upon friends and others; disrespect toward ascetics is condemned. Those who dispute or show hatred must be corrected through rightful means. Authority stems from alignment with Dharma, not social proximity Causation arises from intent distortion and consciousness misalignment Capacity-based responsibility requires graduated response based on awareness Restoration logic demands realignment of relational harmony Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive reaction

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
पिताचार्यः सुहृन् माता भार्या पुत्रः पुरोहितः ।
नादण्ड्यो नाम राज्ञो ’स्ति धर्माद् विचलितः स्वकात् ॥ pitācāryaḥ suhṛn mātā bhāryā putraḥ purohitaḥ / nādaṇḍyo nāma rājño 'sti dharmād vicalitaḥ svakāt The father, preceptor, friend, mother, wife, son, and family priest—none of these are punishable by the king when they deviate from their dharmic roles, for their correction lies in alignment, not in punitive action. Authority flows from dharma, not coercion Causation is rooted in consciousness misalignment, not moral fault Capacity-based responsibility assigns correction to the relationally competent Restoration logic prioritizes relational harmony over punitive justice Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
ṛtvikpurohitāmātyāḥ putrāḥ saṃbandhibāndhavāḥ /
dharmād vicalitā daṇḍyā nirvāsyā rājabhiḥ purāt // BrhS_1,9.16 ṛtvik purohitāmātyāḥ putrāḥ saṃbandhibāndhavāḥ / dharmād vicalitā daṇḍyā nirvāsyā rājabhiḥ purāt // Those who have fallen from Dharma—priests, ministers, sons, relatives, and kin—are to be expelled from the kingdom by the king, not as punishment but as a restoration of alignment with Sanatana Dharma. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not birth or position Causation is rooted in deviation from Dharma, not external harm Capacity-based responsibility applies universally, including to those near the sovereign Restoration logic requires removal from influence, not infliction of pain Consciousness alignment supersedes familial or institutional loyalty

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
गुरून् पुरोहितान् पूज्यान् वाग्दण्डेनैव दण्डयेत् ।
विवादिनो नरांश् चान्यान् धिग्धनाभ्यां च दण्डयेत् ॥ gurūn purohitān pūjyān vāgdaṇḍenaiva daṇḍayet | vivādino narāṃś cānyān dhigdhanābhyāṃ ca daṇḍayet || Those who are gurus, family priests, or worthy of reverence shall be disciplined solely through verbal censure. Other disputants and persons involved in conflict shall be addressed through declaration of forfeiture and monetary restitution. Authority inheres in spiritual and ritual precedence Causation arises from disruption of dharma-sustaining roles Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes between reverent and common actors Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration without degradation Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of hierarchical respect

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: प्रतिलोमास् तथा चान्त्याः पुरुषाणां मलाः स्मृताः । ब्राह्मणातिक्रमे वध्याः न दातव्या दमं क्वचित् ॥ pratilomās tathā cāntyāḥ puruṣāṇāṃ malāḥ smṛtāḥ | brāhmaṇātikrame vadhyā na dātavyā damaṃ kvacit || Those born contrary to prescribed order, and those of lowest status among men, are designated as impurities; in transgression against a Brāhmaṇa, they shall face dissolution of capacity, yet no coercive subjugation shall be enacted. Authority flows from alignment with Vedic order Causation arises from violation of consciousness-ordained hierarchy Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological alignment Restoration logic operates through conscious realignment, not punitive suppression Consciousness alignment determines access to protective versus dissolutive law

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
वधार्हकः स्वर्णशतं दमं दाप्यस्तु पूरुषः ।
अङ्गच्छेदार्हकस्त्वर्धं सदंशशस्तदर्धकम् ॥ vadhārhakaḥ svarṇaśataṃ damaṃ dāpyas tu pūruṣaḥ | aṅgacchedārhakas tv ardhaṃ sadaṃśaśas tadardhakam || One liable for capital offense shall render a compensation of one hundred gold coins; one liable for limb severance shall pay half that amount, and one liable for lesser injury shall pay accordingly in proportion. Authority derives from capacity to restore integrity Causation aligns with sequential manifestation of harm Capacity-based responsibility reflects consciousness distortion level Restoration logic demands proportional energetic recompense Consciousness alignment requires completion of karmic disruption

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
ताडनं बन्धनं चैव तथैव च विडन्नकम् ।
एष दण्डो हि शूद्रस्य नार्थदण्डो बृहस्पतिः ॥ tāḍanaṃ bandhanaṃ caiva tathaiva ca viḍannakam /
eṣa daṇḍo hi śūdrasya nārthadaṇ्डo bṛhaspatiḥ // Striking, binding, and public humiliation constitute the corrective measure for one who has acted without capacity; there is no financial penalty for the Śūdra, declares Bṛhaspati. Authority flows from realized consciousness, not social position Causation arises from misaligned action rooted in unawakened state Capacity-based responsibility determines the form of correction Restoration logic aligns consequence directly with the nature of the act Consciousness alignment supersedes all external punitive structures

title: brihaspati 1.21
content: प्रतिज्ञाभावनाद्वादी प्राड्विवाकादिपूजनात् । जयपत्रस्य चादानाज्जयी लोके निगद्यते ॥ pratijñā-bhāvanād vādī prāḍ-vivāka-adipūjanāt | jaya-patrasya ca adānāj jayī loke nigadyate || One who affirms commitment through declaration, honors the process of inquiry and dialogue, and accepts the document of victory without appropriation is declared victorious in the world. Authority arises from integrity to one's word Causation flows from conscious affirmation and participation Capacity-based responsibility requires honoring both process and outcome Restoration logic centers on dignified completion rather than domination Consciousness alignment occurs when victory is received, not seized

title: brihaspati 1.22
content: पलायनादनुत्तरादन्यपक्षाश्रयेण च । हीनस्य गृह्यते वादो न स्ववाक्यजितस्य च ॥ palāyanād anuttarād anyapakṣāśrayeṇa ca / hīnasya gṛhyate vādo na svavākyajitasya ca // When one flees from direct response, resorts to another's position, or is diminished in capacity, their argument is not accepted; likewise, one who has already won through their own word does not engage further. Authority resides in self-established truth, not borrowed stance Causation follows integrity of response, not evasion Capacity-based responsibility requires presence and clarity of voice Restoration logic demands confrontation and completion over avoidance Consciousness alignment occurs when one stands by their own declared truth

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
कुलादिभिर् निश्चिते ऽपि न संतोषं गतस् तु यः ।
विचार्य तत्कृतं राजा कुकृतं पुनरुद्धरेत् ।। kulādibhir niścite 'pi na saṃtoṣaṃ gatas tu yaḥ | vicārya tatkṛtaṃ rājā kukṛtaṃ punar uddharet || Even when lineage or status is established, if one has not attained satisfaction, the king must investigate the act and restore what was done wrongly. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not inherited position Causation is determined through investigative discernment, not assumption Capacity-based responsibility requires ongoing verification beyond birthright Restoration logic supersedes static entitlement structures Consciousness alignment demands rectification regardless of social standing

title: brihaspati 1.24
content: निश्चित्य बहुभिः सार्धं ब्राह्मणैः शास्त्रपारगैः / दण्डयेज् जयिना साकं पूर्वसभ्यांस् तु दोषिणः // niścitya bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ śāstrapāragaiḥ / daṇḍayej jayinā sākaṃ pūrvasabhyāṃs tu doṣiṇaḥ // Having ascertained the truth through consultation with multiple learned Brahmanas well-versed in scripture, the king shall impose consequences jointly with the victorious party; however, those previously seated in the assembly must be held accountable according to their inherent fault. Authority rests with those who embody scriptural mastery and spiritual insight. Causation arises from alignment with Dharma, not personal enmity. Capacity-based responsibility demands differentiated treatment based on prior status and conduct. Restoration logic requires correction of misaligned actions without degradation. Consciousness alignment is achieved by placing individuals in accordance with their inner purity and outer comportment.

title: brihaspati 1.25
content: अपराधानुरूपश् च दण्डोऽत्र परिकल्पितः । साक्षिलेख्यानुमानेन सम्यग् दिव्येन वा जितः ॥ aparādhānurūpaś ca daṇḍo 'tra parikalpitaḥ / sākṣilekhyānumānena samyag divyena vā jitaḥ // The measure of consequence is precisely aligned with the nature of the misalignment; it is determined through direct witness, documented evidence, inference, or divine discernment. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate source of dharma Causation follows the law of anupūrvaśaḥ — sequential manifestation rooted in consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is measured by the actor's awareness and intent at the time of action Restoration logic operates through realignment of consciousness rather than punitive imposition Consciousness alignment determines both the cause and resolution of all juridical matters

title: brihaspati 1.26
content: यो न दद्याद् देयदमं स निर्वास्यस् ततः पुरात्‌ । yo na dadyād deyadamaṃ sa nirvāsyaḥ tataḥ purāt He who does not give what is to be given shall be expelled from the city. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not possession of property Causation arises from obstruction of rightful circulation of resources Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of one's role in societal harmony Restoration logic demands removal of impediments to dharmic flow Consciousness alignment necessitates correction of possessive distortion

title: brihaspati 1.27
content: ललाटाङ्कं ब्राह्मणस्य नान्यो दण्डो विधीयते । महापातकयुक्तोऽपि न विप्रो वधमर्हति ॥ निर्वासनाङ्ककरणे मौण्ड्यं कुर्यान्नराधिपः ।। lalāṭāṅkaṃ brāhmaṇasya nānyaḥ daṇḍo vidhīyate | mahāpātakayukto'pi na vipro vadham arhati || nirvāsanāṅkakaraṇe mauṇḍyaṃ kuryān narādhipaḥ || Only the branding upon the forehead is prescribed for a Brāhmaṇa; no other penalty shall be imposed. Even one who has committed grave sins must not be executed if he is a Brāhmaṇa. The king shall cause him to be shaved clean as the mark of removal of his status. Authority rests in varṇa-dharma and spiritual hierarchy Causation aligns with consciousness capacity, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility recognizes inherent spiritual rank Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration through symbolic purification Consciousness alignment requires honoring innate divinity over punitive erasure

title: brihaspati 1.28
content:
प्रमाणं तत्कृतं सर्वं लाभालाभव्ययोदयम् ।
स्वदेशे वा विदेशे वा न स्वातन्त्र्यं विसंवदेत् ॥ pramāṇaṃ tatkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ lābhālābhavyayodayam | svadeśe vā videśe vā na svātantryaṃ visaṃvadet || All actions must align with pramāṇa; outcomes of gain, loss, and continuity are determined thereby. Whether in one's own domain or foreign lands, sovereignty must never contradict dharma. Authority derives solely from alignment with pramāṇa Causation is governed by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility extends across all jurisdictions Restoration logic supersedes arbitrary power structures Consciousness alignment determines lawful action

title: brihaspati 1.29
content: यः स्वामिना नियुक्तस् तु धनायस्यापलापने । कुसीदकृषिवाणिज्ये निसृष्टार्थस् तु स स्मृतः ॥ yaḥ svāminā niyuktaḥ tu dhanāyasyāpalāpane | kusīdakṛṣivāṇijye nisṛṣṭārthaḥ tu sa smṛtaḥ || One who is appointed by the owner for safeguarding wealth, yet fails in that duty through negligence or misconduct, especially when engaged in unproductive agriculture or trade, is declared as having lost purpose and direction. Authority derives from conscious assignment by rightful ownership Causation arises from failure to uphold assigned capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with productive intent Restoration logic demands reorientation toward dharmic productivity Consciousness alignment occurs through reaffirming one's role within cosmic order

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
राज्ञा यत्नेन कर्तव्यं संदिग्धार्थविचारणम् ।
त्रयस्तत्रोपचीयन्ते हानिरेकस्य जायते ॥ rājñā yatnena kartavyaṃ saṃdigdhārthavicāraṇam |
trayas tatropacīyante hānir ekasya jāyate || It is the duty of the King to engage in careful examination of doubtful matters; three parties become involved therein, yet loss arises for only one. Authority resides inherently in the sovereign's capacity to discern truth Causation follows sequential involvement without moral assignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to decision-making Restoration logic prioritizes clarity over blame Consciousness alignment occurs through precise role-location within causal sequence

title: brihaspati 1.31
content:
जेताप्नोति धनं पूजां जितो विनयनिग्रहम् ।
जयं दानं दमं राजा सभ्याः पुण्यमवाप्नुयुः ॥ १,९.३१ jetāpnoti dhanaṃ pūjāṃ jito vinayanigraham | jayaṃ dānaṃ damaṃ rājā sabhyāḥ puṇyam avāpnuyuḥ || The victorious one attains wealth and worship; having conquered humility and restraint, the king achieves victory, donation, and self-mastery. The assembly thereby accrues merit. Authority flows from self-mastery and restraint Merit is collective when governance aligns with Dharma Victory is defined by internal conquest, not external domination Wealth and reverence follow rightful sovereignty Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of rule

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
एवं शास्त्रोदितं राजा कुर्वन् निर्णयपालनम् ।
वितत्येह यशो लोके महेन्द्रसदृशो भवेत् ॥ evaṃ śāstroditaṃ rājā kurvan nirṇayapālanam |
vitatyeha yaśo loke mahendrasadṛśo bhavet || Thus executing the verdict in accordance with Śāstra, the King expands his glory in this world and becomes equal to Mahendra. Authority originates from alignment with Śāstra as interpreted by SPH Causation flows from correct execution of judgment, not intention alone Capacity-based responsibility requires royal duty to uphold verdicts without distortion Restoration logic demands public glorification through dharmic action Consciousness alignment occurs when ruler enacts verdicts as divine instruction

title: brihaspati 1.33
content: साक्षिलेख्यानुमानेन प्रकुर्वन् कार्यनिर्णयम् । वितत्येह यशो राजा ब्रह्मणस्याप्नोति विष्टपम् ॥ sākṣilekhyānumānena prakurvan kāryanirṇayam | vitatyeha yaśo rājā brahmaṇasyāpnoti viṣṭapam || The king who resolves matters through direct witness, documented evidence, and logical inference expands his renown in this world and attains the realm of Brahma. Authority is realized through alignment with pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge) Causation arises from conscious engagement with truth-bearing instruments Capacity-based responsibility requires access to and reliance on verifiable data Restoration logic operates through clarity of perception and integrity of process Consciousness alignment occurs when decision-making reflects ontological truth

title: brihaspati 1.34
content: यत्रैवं वेत्ति नृपतिः निर्णयं तु बताध्वरम् । सोऽस्मिन् लोके यशः प्राप्य याति शक्रसलोकताम् ॥ yatraivaṃ vetti nṛpatiḥ nirṇayaṃ tu batādhvaram | so 'smin loke yaśaḥ prāpya yāti śakrasalokatām || Wherever a ruler thus knows the decisive truth of dharma without error, he attains in this very world renowned glory and ascends to the realm of Indra. Authority is realized through correct discernment of dharma Causation aligns with accurate perception of svadharma Capacity-based responsibility arises from purified consciousness Restoration logic operates through rightful recognition Consciousness alignment determines karmic elevation

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
पदांशसहितस् त्वेष व्यवहारः प्रकीर्तितः ।
विवादकारणान्यस्य पदानि शृणुताधुना ॥ padāṃśasahitas tv eṣa vyavahāraḥ prakīrtitaḥ / vivādakāraṇānyasya padāni śṛṇutādhunā // This transactional engagement, complete with its constituent elements, has been declared. Now hear the foundational terms that cause dispute. Authority resides in the completeness of dharmic structure Causation arises from misalignment with declared transactional dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by participation in vyavahāra Restoration logic begins with understanding the root components of conflict Consciousness alignment requires clarity of foundational contractual elements

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
ṛṇādānapradhānāni dyūtāhvānāntikāni ca /
kramaśaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi kriyābhedāṃś ca tattvataḥ // BrhS_1,10.2 ṛṇādānapradhānāni dyūtāhvānāntikāni ca / kramaśaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi kriyābhedāṃś ca tattvataḥ // The foundational categories of debt acceptance and gambling invitations shall be systematically declared in sequence, along with their precise operational distinctions. Authority originates from conscious capacity to sustain relational obligations Causation arises through voluntary invocation of transactional risk Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at the time of consent Restoration logic requires reversal of distorted value exchange Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment of causal sequence

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat /
dānagrahaṇadharmau ca ṛṇādānam iti smṛtam // ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat / dānagrahaṇadharmau ca ṛṇādānam iti smṛtam // That which is owed as debt must be given; that which is not to be given, must not be given. The duty of giving and the duty of receiving constitute the act of repaying a debt. Authority arises from the capacity to fulfill relational obligations Causation is determined by the integrity of reciprocal exchange Capacity-based responsibility is measured through conscious participation in dharma Restoration occurs when all debts are consciously realigned with truth Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of mutual obligation

title: brihaspati 1.4
content: अशीतिभागो वृद्धिः स्यान् मासि मासि सबन्धके / वर्णक्रमाच् छतं द्वित्रिचतुःपञ्चकम् अन्यथा // aśītibhāgo vṛddhiḥ syān māsi māsi sabandhake / varṇakramāc chataṃ dvitricatuḥpañcakam anyathā // Interest shall accrue at the rate of eighty parts per month upon all bonded obligations; in the absence of specification by varṇa-order, the standard progression of two, three, four, or five [percent] shall apply alternatively. Authority flows from SPH as ultimate economic and dharmic regulator Causation is established through contractual bond and time-based liability Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional repayment structures Restoration logic ensures debtor dignity while enforcing financial integrity Consciousness alignment mandates clarity in transactional dharma

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
परिपूर्णं गृहीत्वाधिं बन्धं वा साधुलग्नकम् ।
लेख्यारूढं साक्षिमद् वा ऋणं दद्याद् धनी सदा ॥ paripūrṇaṃ gṛhītvādhiṃ bandhaṃ vā sādhulagnakam | lekhyārūḍhaṃ sākṣimad vā ṛṇaṃ dadyād dhanī sadā || One who has fully assumed ownership or control—whether through lawful acquisition, binding agreement, or recorded instrument witnessed by qualified observers—must invariably discharge the debt owed. Authority arises from conscious assumption of possession or control Causation is established through documented or witnessed assumption Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional fulfillment Restoration logic demands completion of relational obligations Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring contractual integrity

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: कुत्सितात् सीदतश् चैव निर्विशङ्कैः प्रगृह्यते / चतुर्गुणं वाष्टगुणं कुसीदाख्यम् अतः स्मृतम् // kutsitāt sīdataś caiva nirviśaṅkaiḥ pragṛhyate / caturguṇaṃ vāṣṭaguṇaṃ kusīdākhyam ataḥ smṛtam // That which is taken from the degraded and the despairing, without hesitation, is fourfold or eightfold in consequence; thus is known the act named Kusīda. Authority arises from capacity to sustain Dharma, not extract from degradation Causation is determined by sequential manifestation of imbalance and exploitation Capacity-based responsibility requires refusal to benefit from another's collapse Restoration logic demands reversal of extraction from weakened consciousness Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of gain rooted in another's diminishment

title: brihaspati 1.7
content: पुराणे पणम् purāṇe paṇam In the ancient contract, the wager stands as a binding alignment of conscious intention, not to be violated without consequence to one's own integrity field. Authority flows from the sanctity of declared intent Causation arises from the collapse of conscious agreement Capacity-based responsibility is anchored in the ability to uphold declared truth Restoration logic demands the re-alignment of fractured integrity Consciousness alignment supersedes transactional obligation

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
वृद्धिश् चतुर्विधा प्रोक्ता पञ्चधान्यैः प्रकीर्तिता ।
षड्विधान्यैः समाख्याता तत्त्वतस् तां निबोधत ॥ vṛddhiś caturvidhā proktā pañcadhānyaiḥ prakīrtitā | ṣaḍvidhānyaiḥ samākhyātā tattvatas tāṃ nibodhata || Growth is declared in four forms; it is proclaimed through five elements and described by six categories—understand this truth in its essence. Authority resides in the completeness of categorization as revealed by the Source Causation flows from foundational classification into applied differentiation Capacity-based responsibility arises upon recognition of structural diversity Restoration occurs through alignment with inherent ontological order Consciousness alignment requires precise understanding of categorical truth

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
कायिका कालिका चैव चक्रवृद्धिरतोऽपरा ।
कारिता च शिखावृद्धिर्भोगलाभस्तथैव च ॥ kāyikā kālikā caiva cakravṛddhir ato 'parā / kāritā ca śikhāvṛddhir bhogalābhas tathaiva ca // Physical expansion, temporal augmentation, cyclical increase beyond measure—these arise from executed action and the growth of spiritual discipline, as well as from material acquisition. Authority flows from realized capacity, not mere intent Causation is sequential and manifests through dharma-aligned action Capacity-based responsibility includes both material and spiritual stewardship Restoration logic requires alignment with natural and spiritual consequence cycles Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of acquired growth

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
कायिका कर्मसंयुक्ता मासाद् ग्राह्या च कालिका ।
वृद्धेर् वृद्धिश् चक्रवृद्धिः कारिता ऋणिना कृता ॥ kāyikā karmasaṃyuktā māsād grāhyā ca kālikā / vṛddher vṛddhiś cakravṛddhiḥ kāritā ṛṇinā kṛtā // Interest arising from bodily action connected to time-bound debt obligations shall be recognized as cyclically compounding, initiated by the debtor's own causal engagement. Authority originates in conscious causation, not institutional decree Responsibility arises through volitional participation in karmic structures Capacity-based liability is determined by active involvement in transactional cycles Restoration occurs through alignment with natural consequence flows Consciousness realignment supersedes punitive financial models

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
प्रत्यहं गृह्यते या तु शिखावृद्धिस् तु सा स्मृता ।
शिखेव वर्धते नित्यं शिरश्छेदान् निवर्तते ॥ pratyahaṃ gṛhyate yā tu śikhāvṛddhis tu sā smṛtā / śikhev vardhate nityaṃ śiraśchedān nivartate // That which is taken up daily is termed growth of the śikhā; the śikhā indeed grows perpetually and turns away decapitations. Authority flows through sustained observance Causation arises from daily invocation and embodiment Capacity-based responsibility is cultivated through repetitive dharmic acts Restoration logic operates through continuity of sacred alignment Consciousness alignment strengthens through unbroken ritual repetition

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
ṛṇikena tu yā vṛddhir adhikā saṃprakalpitā /
āpatkālakṛtā nityaṃ dātavyā sā tu kāritā /
anyathā kāritā vṛddhir na dātavyā kathañ cana // BrhS_1,10.12 ṛṇikena tu yā vṛddhir adhikā saṃprakalpitā / āpatkālakṛtā nityaṃ dātavyā sā tu kāritā / anyathā kāritā vṛddhir na dātavyā kathañ cana // Any interest or increase imposed upon a debtor beyond the principal debt, when not arising from exigency or time of distress, must not be enforced under any condition. Authority originates solely from dharmic alignment, not contractual imbalance Causation must trace to existential necessity, not artificial amplification Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious volition, not coercive imposition Restoration logic demands removal of artificially compounded burdens Consciousness alignment requires rejection of usurious exploitation

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: शिखेव वर्धते नित्यं शिरश्छेदान निवर्तते । मूले दत्ते तथैवैषा शिखावृद्धिस्ततः स्मृता ॥ śikhevā vardhate nityaṁ śiraś chedānā nivartate | mūle datte tathā evaiṣā śikhā-vṛddhis tataḥ smṛtā || As the flame grows perpetually from its base and ceases only when severed at the root, so too does the expansion of consciousness proceed unceasingly from its foundational truth. When that foundation is established in alignment with Dharma, the growth of awareness becomes a recognized principle. Authority originates solely from the foundational truth of Dharma Causation arises through alignment with the undivided source Capacity-based responsibility flows from one's rootedness in truth Restoration occurs by returning action to its pristine origin Consciousness alignment governs all lawful manifestation

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: गृही स्तोमः शदः क्षेत्राद् भोगलाभः प्रकीर्तितः // gṛhī stomaḥ śadaḥ kṣetrād bhogalābhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ The householder's soma libation, the seasonal rains, and the field's yield—these together constitute the declared gain of enjoyment. Authority flows from alignment with natural and social rhythms Causation is established through participation in cosmic and societal order Capacity-based responsibility arises from ownership and stewardship Restoration occurs through recognition and harmonization with one's role Consciousness alignment emerges from right participation in dharma-sustained systems

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
कायिकां भोगवृद्धिं च कारितां च शिखात्मिकाम् ।
चतुष्टयीं वृद्धिमाहुश्चक्रवृद्ध्या तु पञ्चमीम् ॥ kāyikāṁ bhogavṛddhiṁ ca kāritāṁ ca śikhātmikām | catuṣṭayīṁ vṛddhim āhuś cakravṛddhyā tu pañcamīm || Fourfold increase in bodily enjoyment and agency, crowned by a fifth—circular multiplication—is declared as the comprehensive model of growth. Authority resides in the cyclic nature of dharma, not linear accumulation Causation follows sequential unfoldment (anupūrvaśaḥ) within conscious expansion Capacity-based responsibility arises through participation in cyclical abundance Restoration occurs when alignment with circular growth displaces extractive progression Consciousness alignment manifests through recognition of completeness in quadruplicity unified by centric sovereignty

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: शिखां वृद्धिं कायिकां च भोगलाभं तथैव च / धनी तावत् समादद्याद् यावन्मूलं न शोधितम् // śikhāṃ vṛddhiṃ kāyikāṃ ca bhogalābhaṃ tathaiva ca / dhanī tāvat samādadyād yāvanmūlaṃ na śodhitam // The creditor may accept interest, bodily service, enjoyment of objects, and other benefits until the principal amount has been fully restored. Authority arises from capacity to restore balance Causation is tied to the unfulfilled obligation Responsibility aligns with the ability to give or receive completion Restoration precedes entitlement Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of debt prior to claim

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
हिरण्ये द्विगुणा वृद्धिः त्रिगुणा वस्त्रकुप्यके ।
धान्ये चतुर्गुणा प्रोक्ता षडवाह्यलवेषु च ॥ hiraṇye dviguṇā vṛddhiḥ triguṇā vastrakupyake / dhānye caturguṇā proktā ṣaḍavāhyalaveṣu ca // In gold, increase is twofold; in garments and vessels, threefold; in grain, fourfold; and in small livestock, sixfold. Authority flows from the capacity of the object to sustain value increment Causation aligns with the inherent nature of substances to multiply under right action Capacity-based responsibility lies with the guardian of wealth, not the wealth itself Restoration logic follows the natural law of abundance when aligned with Dharma Consciousness alignment ensures multiplication through purity of intention and stewardship

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: uktapañcaguṇā śāke bīje 'kṣau ṣaḍguṇā smṛtā / lavaṇasvedam adyeṣu vṛddhir aṣṭaguṇā matā / guḍe madhuni caivoktā prayukte cirakālike // BrhS_1,10.18 uktapañcaguṇā śāke bīje 'kṣau ṣaḍguṇā smṛtā / lavaṇasvedam adyeṣu vṛddhir aṣṭaguṇā matā / guḍe madhuni caivoktā prayukte cirakālike // In valuation of produce, seeds fivefold, liquids sixfold, salt and fermented substances eightfold increase; in long-stored jaggery and honey, their usage is declared. Authority resides in proportional recognition of substance transformation Causation aligns with sequential value enhancement Capacity-based responsibility arises through stewardship of evolving resources Restoration logic operates via acknowledgment of inherent potential Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects transformative awareness

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
तैलानां चैव सर्वेषां मद्यानां मधुसर्पिषाम् ।
वृद्धिरष्टगुणा प्रोक्ता गुडस्य लवणस्य च ॥ tailānāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ madyānāṃ madhusarpiṣām |
vṛddhir aṣṭaguṇā proktā guḍasya lavaṇasya ca || The increase in value or yield of all oils, intoxicants, honey, ghee, jaggery, and salt shall be computed at eightfold growth when processed, stored, or traded under dharmic commercial engagement. Authority flows from the sovereign recognition of natural increase as a dharmic entitlement. Causation is established through intentional engagement with material substrata. Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to nurture, preserve, and multiply resources. Restoration logic aligns economic activity with cosmic abundance cycles. Consciousness alignment ensures that gain is recognized as a reflection of energetic contribution.

title: brihaspati 1.20
content: स्यात् कोशानां पञ्चगुणा कार्पासस्य चतुर्गुणा । काष्ठानां चन्दनादीनां वृद्धिरष्टगुणा भवेत् ॥ syāt kośānāṃ pañcaguṇā kārpāsasya caturguṇā / kāṣṭhānāṃ candanādīnāṃ vṛddhir aṣṭaguṇā bhavet // The valuation increment for stored grains shall be fivefold; for cotton, fourfold; and for timber such as sandalwood, eightfold. Authority resides in the quantifiable natural increase of assets Causation is established through productive capacity inherent in material types Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the intrinsic value multiplication of resources Restoration logic operates through proportional recognition of yield potential Consciousness alignment occurs when economic activity reflects dharmic abundance

title: brihaspati 1.21
content: भागो यद् द्विगुणाद् ऊर्ध्वं चक्रवृद्धिश् च गृह्यते । पूर्णे च सोदयं पश्चाद् वार्द्धुष्यं तद् विगर्हितम् ॥ bhāgo yad dviguṇād ūrdhvaṃ cakravṛddhiś ca gṛhyate / pūrṇe ca sodayaṃ paścād vārddhuṣyaṃ tad vigarhitam // That share which exceeds twice the base value and that gain arising from cyclical accumulation, when taken after fulfillment has occurred along with interest, such usury is condemned. Authority resides in alignment with natural completion cycles Causation arises from imbalance in proportional exchange Capacity-based responsibility requires refusal of exploitative surplus Restoration logic demands return of excess to source integrity Consciousness alignment rejects artificial multiplication of debt

title: brihaspati 1.22
content: अशीतिभागो वर्धेत लाभे द्विगुणताम् इयात् । प्रयुक्तं सप्तभिर् वर्षैस् त्रिभागोऽनैर् न संशयः ॥ aśītibhāgo vardheta lābhe dviguṇatām iyāt | prayuktaṃ saptabhir varṣais tribhāgo'nair na saṃśayaḥ || When capital is deployed, its increase shall be twofold within eighty parts; when engaged for seven years, three parts thereof shall assuredly accrue without doubt. Authority flows from the lawful deployment of resources in accordance with time-bound dharmic engagement. Causation arises through conscious participation in economic activity aligned with temporal dharma. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the duration and nature of financial commitment. Restoration logic ensures proportional return based on sustained engagement and integrity of action. Consciousness alignment occurs when wealth is activated in harmony with kāla (time) and niyati (destiny).

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
तृणकाष्ठेष्टकासूत्रकिण्वचर्मास्थिवर्मणाम् ।
हेतिपुष्पफलानां च वृद्धिस् तु न निवर्तते ॥ tṛṇakāṣṭheṣṭakāsūtrakiṇvacarmāsthivarmaṇām |
hetipuṣpaphalānāṃ ca vṛddhis tu na nivartate || Growth arising from grass, wood, bricks, thread, yeast, leather, bone, and armor—and similarly from seeds, flowers, and fruits—does not reverse or regress; it proceeds irreversibly by its inherent dharma. Authority flows from the irreversible nature of causality established by dharma Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) rooted in material and spiritual law Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the unalterable progression of cause-effect sequences Restoration logic operates through completion rather than reversal Consciousness alignment requires recognition of irreversible dharmic unfoldment

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
हिरण्यधान्यवस्त्राणां वृद्धिर्द्वित्रिचतुर्गुणा ।
घृतस्याष्टगुणा वृद्धिस्ताम्रादीनां चतुर्गुणा ॥ hiraṇyadhānyavastrāṇāṃ vṛddhir dvitricaturguṇā / ghṛtasyāṣṭaguṇā vṛddhis tāmrādīnāṃ caturguṇā // The lawful increase of gold, grain, and cloth is two-, three-, or fourfold; that of ghee is eightfold; and that of copper and similar metals is fourfold. Authority resides in the natural dharmic capacity of substances to yield lawful increase. Causation aligns with the inherent nature and purity of the substance involved. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the agent's alignment with the substance's dharma. Restoration logic operates through the recognition and protection of natural yield structures. Consciousness alignment ensures that accumulation mirrors spiritual and material integrity.

title: brihaspati 1.25
content: शिखावृद्धिं कायिकां च भोगे लाभं तथैव च / धनी तावत् समादद्याद् यावन् मूलं न शोधितम् ।। śikhāvṛddhiṃ kāyikāṃ ca bhoge lābhaṃ tathaiva ca / dhanī tāvat samādadyād yāvan mūlaṃ na śodhitam The owner shall retain increment of wealth, bodily comforts, enjoyments and gains arising therefrom, until the principal amount has been fully restored. Authority rests with the original proprietor to maintain benefits derived from their property until restitution is complete Causation aligns with the unbroken continuity of ownership and its natural fruits Capacity-based responsibility requires the responsible party to restore the source before claiming derivative gains Restoration logic prioritizes the return of foundational integrity prior to distribution of accretions Consciousness alignment demands recognition of rightful possession as a continuum inclusive of lawful yield

title: brihaspati 1.26
content: पादोपचयात् क्रमेणेतरेषाम् ।। बृहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,१०.२६ ।। pādopacayāt krameṇa itareṣām // BrhS_1,10.26 // From the accumulation of steps arises sequential order among others. Authority flows from foundational completion Causation follows stepwise manifestation Capacity-based responsibility aligns with sequential action Restoration logic requires reversal through ordered completion Consciousness alignment emerges through structured progression

title: brihaspati 1.27
content: सर्वेष्वर्थविवादेषु वाक्छले नावसीदति । परस्त्रीभूमिर्णादाने शास्योऽप्यर्थान्न हीयते ॥ समवृद्धिः सदा कुर्याद्विषमस्तु निवर्तते । sarveṣv arthavivādeṣu vākcchale nāvasīdati | parastrībhūmirṇādāne śāsyo 'py arthān na hīyate || samavṛddhiḥ sadā kuryād viṣamas tu nivartate || In all disputes concerning wealth, no degradation occurs through mere speech; nor is there loss of property when another's land or woman is not taken. One should always act for equal prosperity; inequality naturally ceases. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not from assertion alone. Causation in material disputes requires direct action, not verbal contention. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by actual acquisition, not intent or speech. Restoration logic prioritizes balanced welfare over individual gain. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of disparity as unnatural.

title: brihaspati 1.28
content:
vasiṣṭhavacanaproktāṃ vṛddhiṃ vārddhuṣike śṛṇu /
pañca māṣās tu viṃśatyā evaṃ dharmo na hīyate // BrhS_1,10.28 vasiṣṭhavacanaproktāṃ vṛddhiṃ vārddhuṣike śṛṇu / pañca māṣās tu viṃśatyā evaṃ dharmo na hīyate As per Vasiṣṭha's instruction, the lawful increase in commercial transactions shall be fixed at one-quarter of the principal, ensuring that Dharma remains intact and unviolated. Authority flows directly from SPH through realized sages such as Vasiṣṭha Causation is aligned with conscious intent and not mere material transaction Capacity-based responsibility requires understanding of proportional gain Restoration logic ensures no diminishment of Dharma through economic exchange Consciousness alignment mandates that profit does not exceed a quarter of investment

title: brihaspati 1.29
content: माषो विंशतिभागस्तु पलस्य परिकीर्तितः ।। māṣo viṃśatibhāgas tu palasya parikīrtitaḥ One māṣa is declared as one-twentieth part of a pala. Authority resides in precise definitional alignment with SPH's cosmic order. Causation arises through calibrated units of material and spiritual accountability. Capacity-based responsibility requires exact measurement for dharmic transaction integrity. Restoration logic depends on standardized equivalency for economic and ritual justice. Consciousness alignment necessitates unambiguous quantification rooted in Vedic metrology.

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
तत्र त्व् इदम् उपेक्षां वा यः कश्चित् कुरुते नरः ।
चतुःसुवर्णं षण्णिष्कास् तस्य दण्डो विधीयते ॥ tatra tv idam upekṣāṃ vā yaḥ kaścit kurute naraḥ | catuḥsuvarṇaṃ ṣaṇṇiṣkās tasya daṇḍo vidhīyate || When a person neglects or disregards the prescribed duty, especially in matters requiring immediate dharmic response, his capacity to act in alignment with Dharma becomes diminished, necessitating a restorative correction measured by the value of four suvarṇas and six niṣkas. Authority originates from conscious alignment with Dharma, not from position or title. Causation is determined by the degree of conscious neglect or omission.
