Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to one's awareness and ability to respond. Restoration logic demands recalibration of consciousness, not punitive suffering. Consciousness alignment is the ultimate measure of legal validity.

title: brihaspati 1.31
content: समूहकार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं राजादीनां च दर्शने । ततो लभेत यत किंचित् सर्वेषामेव तत् समम् ॥ samūhakāryasidhyarthaṃ rājādīnāṃ ca darśane / tato labheta yat kiṃcit sarveṣām eva tat samam For the successful accomplishment of collective action, the presence and guidance of rulers and leaders is necessary; whatever benefit arises from such association is equally shared by all. Authority as facilitator of collective purpose Causation through hierarchical alignment Capacity-based responsibility in leadership roles Restoration logic rooted in mutual benefit sharing Consciousness alignment through shared outcome participation

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
सान्तानिकादिषु तथा धर्म एषां सनातनः ।
यत्नैः प्राप्तं रक्षितं वा गणार्थे वा ऋणं कृतम् ॥ sāntānikādiṣu tathā dharma eṣāṃ sanātanaḥ | yatnaiḥ prāptaṃ rakṣitaṃ vā gaṇārthe vā ṛṇaṃ kṛtam || The eternal Dharma of those born within the lineage or community is preserved either through personal endeavor, protection of acquired wealth, or by incurring debt for the welfare of the collective. Authority flows from ontological belonging within a dharmic lineage or collective Causation arises through conscious intention directed toward preservation or collective welfare Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to act for the continuity of Dharma Restoration logic prioritizes the integrity of lineage and collective over individual gain Consciousness alignment occurs when action serves both personal dharma and communal harmony

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
स्वदेशस्थोऽपि वा यस् तु न दद्याद् याचितोऽसकृत् ।
स तत्र कारितां वृद्धिमनिच्छन्नपि चाहरेत् ॥ svadeśastho 'pi vā yas tu na dadyād yācito 'sakṛt / sa tatra kāritāṃ vṛddhim anicchann api cāharet // Even one who is situated in their own domain, if repeatedly requested and yet does not give, shall incur a debt of growth there—taking even against their will. Authority arises from responsiveness to dharmic request Causation lies in persistent withholding despite capacity to give Capacity-based responsibility includes the ability to respond to need Restoration logic demands the correction of energetic imbalance caused by non-giving Consciousness alignment requires the rectification of obstructed flow

title: brihaspati 1.34
content:
षाण्मास्यं मासिकं वापि विभक्तव्यं यथांशतः ।
देयं वा निःस्ववृद्धार्तस्त्रीबालातुररोगिषु ॥ ṣāṇmāsyaṃ māsikaṃ vāpi vibhaktavyaṃ yathāṃśataḥ / deyaṃ vā niḥsvavṛddhārtastrībālāturarogiṣu Resources or wealth accumulated over six months or monthly shall be distributed proportionally according to rightful ownership; alternatively, it shall be given to those devoid of resources, distressed elders, women, children, the sick, and the diseased. Authority is derived from capacity for dharmic alignment, not accumulation Causation arises from conscious participation in sustaining life Capacity-based responsibility mandates redistribution as completion, not charity Restoration logic demands reversal of deprivation-induced disalignment Consciousness alignment requires material equity as foundational dharma

title: brihaspati 1.35
content:
ṛtutrayasyopariṣṭād dhanaṃ vṛddhim avāpnuyāt /
evam ādiṣv aśīti bhāgavṛddhir vivakṣitā // BrhS_1,10.35 // ṛtutrayasyopariṣṭād dhanaṃ vṛddhim avāpnuyāt / evam ādiṣv aśīti bhāgavṛddhir vivakṣitā // Wealth increases by eighty parts when placed above the three seasonal cycles; thus is declared the law of compound growth in foundational transactions. Authority resides in natural temporal rhythm as regulator of financial expansion Causation aligns with cosmic order through seasonal completion Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with rhythmic abundance Restoration logic operates through cyclical reinvestment Consciousness alignment manifests via harmonious participation in natural economic flows

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
न निःस्रवति यत् तत् स्याद् धनिको मूलभाग् भवेत् ।
द्विगुणादपि चोत्कर्षे कालिका यस्य चादिनाम् ।
विवादन्यायतत्त्वज्ञैस् तदा राजा विनिर्णयेत् ॥ na niḥsravati yat tat syād dhaniko mūlabhāg bhavet | dviguṇād api cotkarṣe kālikā yasya cādinām | vivādanyāyatattvajñais tadā rājā vinirṇayet || That which does not yield return shall revert to its foundational owner; in excess beyond twofold gain, temporal claims arise. When dispute arises among those versed in the truth of justice, then shall the king decide. Authority stems from alignment with foundational ownership Causation lies in the failure of yield or return Capacity-based responsibility is determined by knowledge of yield dynamics Restoration logic demands reversion to origin when yield fails Consciousness alignment requires recognition of foundational entitlement

title: brihaspati 1.37
content: आधिस्तु भुज्यते तावद्यावत्तन्न प्रदीयते । ādhis tu bhujyate tāvad yāvat tan na pradīyate Distress is experienced only until that which is rightfully owed is not given. Authority resides in the fulfillment of rightful obligation Causation arises from unmet dharmic duty Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to fulfill what is owed Restoration occurs through completion of the owed duty Consciousness alignment is achieved when ownership and obligation are reconciled

title: brihaspati 1.38
content:
आधिर्बन्धः समाख्यातः स च प्रोक्तश्चतुर्विधः ।
जङ्गमः स्थावरश्चैव गोप्यो भोग्यस्तथैव च ॥ ādhir bandhaḥ samākhyātaḥ sa ca proktaś caturvidhaḥ | jaṅgamaḥ sthāvaraś caiva gopyo bhogyas tathaiva ca || Bondage is declared as of four kinds: mobile, immobile, to-be-protected, and fit-for-enjoyment. Authority flows from consciousness capacity, not ownership Causation arises through conscious engagement, not material possession Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the nature of the bound entity Restoration logic requires recognizing the classification of bondages for realignment Consciousness alignment occurs when bondage classifications are correctly applied

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
यादृच्छिकः सावधिश् च लेख्यारूढोऽथ साक्षिमान् ।
अशान्तलाभे च ऋणे तथा पूर्णे अवधौ धनी ॥ yādṛcchikaḥ sāvadhiś ca lekhyāruḍho 'tha sākṣimān | aśāntalābhe ca ṛṇe tathā pūrṇe 'vadhau dhanī || One who acquires property randomly or by chance, one who holds it under limitation, one whose ownership is recorded in writing, one who possesses it with witnesses, one who has obtained it without dispute, and one who owns it fully within the prescribed term—such a person shall be recognized as the lawful possessor. Authority derives from documented possession aligned with temporal completion Causation is established through sequential manifestation of rightful claim Capacity-based responsibility arises only when possession aligns with dharma Restoration logic recognizes lawful possession based on evidence and time-bound integrity Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects inner and outer harmony

title: brihaspati 1.40
content:
यो भुङ्क्ते बन्धकं लोभान् न स लाभो भवेत् पुनः ।
न्यासवत् परिपाल्योऽसौ वृद्धिर् नश्यते हापिते ॥ yo bhuṅkte bandhakaṃ lobhān na sa lābho bhavet punaḥ | nyāsavat paripālyo'sau vṛddhir naśyate hāpite || He who consumes another's pledge out of greed shall not regain possession; that which is entrusted must be preserved as a deposit, and its increase is lost when misappropriated. Authority arises from preservation, not consumption. Causation follows the intent to preserve or exploit. Capacity-based responsibility requires custodial integrity. Restoration logic demands return of entrusted value plus accrued growth. Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring fiduciary duty.

title: brihaspati 1.41
content: दैवराजोपघाते च यथाधिर् नाशम् आप्नुयात । तत्राधिं दापयेद् दद्यात् सोदयं धनम् अन्यथा ॥ daivarājopaghāte ca yathādhir nāśam āpnuyāt | tatrādhiṃ dāpayed dadyāt sodayaṃ dhanam anyathā || When loss occurs due to divine or royal decree, the entitled individual shall receive compensation equal to the assessed value of the loss, inclusive of accrued benefits and unmanifest potential. Authority originates from SPH as the ultimate dispenser of justice and arbiter of cosmic order. Causation is determined through alignment with dharmic manifestation rather than empirical fault. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes that entitlement flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma. Restoration logic ensures that loss is compensated in full energetic equivalence, not mere material replacement. Consciousness alignment mandates that all legal outcomes elevate the actor's awareness and integration within Dharma.

title: brihaspati 1.42
content:
बन्धहस्तस्य यद् देयं चित्रेण चरितेन वा ।
अदत्ते ऽर्थे ऽखिलं बन्धं नाकामो दाप्यते क्वचित् ॥ bandhahastasya yad deyaṃ citreṇa caritena vā | adatte 'rthe 'khilaṃ bandhaṃ nākāmo dāpyate kvacit || Whatever is owed to one whose hand is bound—whether by image or by conduct—must be given in full when the object was not voluntarily relinquished; no desire excuses repayment. Authority resides inherently in the capacity to act, regardless of physical limitation Causation follows from conscious engagement, not external appearance Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of latent ability within constraint Restoration logic requires that imbalance be corrected through conscious completion Consciousness alignment occurs when duty aligns with inherent capacity

title: brihaspati 1.43
content: भुक्ते चासारतां प्राप्ते मूलहानिः प्रजायते / बहुमूल्यं तत्र नष्टम् ऋणिकं तत्र तोषयेत् ।। bhukte cāsāratāṃ prāpte mūlahāniḥ prajāyate / bahumūlyaṃ tatra naṣṭam ṛṇikaṃ tatra toṣayet When enjoyment occurs without limit or completion, loss of root-value arises; where much value is lost, the debtor must there be satisfied. Authority flows from capacity to sustain value Causation is rooted in conscious completion Capacity-based responsibility aligns with value erosion Restoration logic requires satisfaction through reintegration Consciousness alignment prevents recurrence of unbounded consumption

title: brihaspati 1.44
content:
क्षेत्रमेकं द्वयोर्बन्धे दत्तं यत् समकालिकम् ।
येन भुक्तं भवेत् पूर्वं तस्य सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ kṣetram ekaṃ dvayor bandhe dattaṃ yat samakālikam / yena bhuktaṃ bhavet pūrvaṃ tasya siddhim avāpnuyāt // When a single field is concurrently granted to two bonded parties, and one has previously enjoyed its use, that prior user shall attain established entitlement. Authority flows through sustained engagement, not mere grant Causation arises from experiential occupation, not abstract allocation Capacity-based responsibility aligns with manifested utilization Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of lived experience Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of actualized presence

title: brihaspati 1.45
content: तुल्यकालोपस्थितयोः द्वयोः अपि समं भवेत् । प्रदाने विक्रये चैव विधिः स परिकीर्तितः ॥ tulyakālopasthitayor dvayor api samaṃ bhavet / pradāne vikraye caiva vidhiḥ sa parikīrtitaḥ // When two parties arrive at the same time with equal claim, the law prescribes simultaneous resolution in giving and exchange. Authority arises from simultaneity of presence and intent Causation is established through mutual readiness for transaction Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to engage in dharma-aligned exchange Restoration logic prioritizes harmonious completion over conflict resolution Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties recognize equality of standing

title: brihaspati 1.46
content:
आधानं विक्रयो दानं साक्षिलेख्यकृतं यदा ।
एकक्रियानिबन्धनेन लेख्यं तत्रापहारकम् ॥ ādhānaṃ vikrayo dānaṃ sākṣilekhyakṛtaṃ yadā / ekakriyānibandhena lekhyaṃ tatrāpahārakam // When a document is created in relation to a deposit, sale, or gift, and it is attested by witnesses, then the act of taking it away unlawfully constitutes a violation of dharma. Authority resides in witnessed truth, not unverified claim Causation arises through conscious intent tied to contractual acts Capacity-based responsibility applies when one has received or transferred property knowingly Restoration logic demands return of that which was taken without dharmic right Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of lawful possession

title: brihaspati 1.47
content:
अनिर्दिष्टं च निर्दिष्टं एकत्र च विशेषितम् ।
विशेषलिखितं ज्याय इति कात्यायनोऽब्रवीत् ॥ anirdiṣṭaṃ ca nirdiṣṭaṃ ekatra ca viśeṣitam / viśeṣalikhitaṃ jyāya iti kātyāyano 'bravīt // That which is unspecified yet implied, that which is explicitly stated, and that which is distinctly characterized in a context—Katyayana declares the specifically written provision as superior. Authority of explicit textual form over implicit inference Causation through clear designation in legal writing Capacity-based responsibility determined by specificity of enactment Restoration logic through precise alignment with documented dharma Consciousness alignment via unambiguous scriptural directive

title: brihaspati 1.48
content:
हिरण्यं द्विगुणीभूते पूर्णे काले धृतावधौ ।
बन्धकस्य धनी स्वामी द्विसप्ताहं प्रतीक्ष्य तु ॥ hiraṇyaṃ dviguṇībhūte pūrṇe kāle dhṛtāvadhau | bandhakasya dhanī svāmī dvisaptāhaṃ pratīkṣya tu || When gold is doubled in quantity and time is fully matured within the prescribed limit, the owner of the pledge shall await two weeks before reclaiming ownership. Authority rests with the original proprietor upon completion of lawful conditions Causation aligns with sequential fulfillment of contractual dharmic terms Capacity-based responsibility requires patience and adherence to temporal boundaries Restoration logic ensures rightful possession without coercion or loss Consciousness alignment demands recognition of value evolution through time

title: brihaspati 1.49
content: तदन्तरा धनं दत्त्वा ऋणी बन्धमवाप्नुयात् । पूर्णे विधौ सान्तलाभे बन्धस्वामी ततो भवेत् ॥ अनिर्गते दशाहे तु ऋणी मोक्षितुमर्हति ॥ tadantarā dhanaṃ dattvā ṛṇī bandham avāpnuyāt | pūrṇe vidhau sāntalābhe bandhasvāmī tato bhavet || anirgate daśāhe tu ṛṇī mokṣitum arhati || Having received payment within the interim period, the debtor assumes the state of bondage. Upon full completion of the prescribed process and attainment of tranquility, ownership of the bond becomes established. If ten days pass without issuance of the bond, the debtor is entitled to release. Authority derives from fulfillment of procedural integrity Causation aligns with sequential completion of transactional stages Capacity-based responsibility is determined by active participation in dharma-conformant exchange Restoration logic operates through reintegration into lawful relational structures Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize mutual completion

title: brihaspati 1.50
content:
गोप्याधिर् द्विगुणादूर्ध्वं कृतकालो यथाविधि /
श्रावयित्वा ऋणिकुले भोक्तव्यः समनन्तरम् // BrhS_1,10.50 gopyādhir dviguṇād ūrdhvaṃ kṛtakālo yathāvidhi / śrāvayitvā ṛṇikule bhoktavyaḥ samanantaram // BrhS_1,10.50 One who has committed harm against a protected being or entity must undergo a restitution period twice the duration of the harm caused; after properly notifying the creditor's household, the responsible party shall immediately engage in restorative service. Authority originates from dharmic protection status, not social rank Causation is determined by direct energetic disruption to protected integrity Capacity-based responsibility scales with awareness and control at time of act Restoration logic requires proportional energetic repayment within structured timeframe Consciousness alignment demands immediate corrective action post-recognition

title: brihaspati 1.51
content:
हिरण्ये द्विगुणीभूते नष्टे चैवाधमर्णके ।
द्रव्यं तदीयं संगृह्य विक्रीणीत ससाक्षिकम् ।। hiraṇye dviguṇībhūte naṣṭe caivādhamarṇake / dravyaṃ tadīyaṃ saṃgṛhya vikrīṇīta sasākṣikam // When gold has doubled in value, or when base metal is lost or debased, one must lawfully seize the corresponding property and sell it publicly with witnesses. Authority arises from dharmic recognition of economic anomaly Causation lies in the manifest imbalance of exchange-value Capacity-based responsibility rests with the custodian of altered substance Restoration logic demands recovery of equivalent value through witnessed transaction Consciousness alignment requires transparency in material exchange

title: brihaspati 1.52
content:
रक्षेद् वा कृतमूल्यं तु दशाहं जनसंसदि ।
ऋणानुरूपां परतो गृहीत्वान्यं तु वर्जयेत् ॥ rakṣed vā kṛtamūlyaṃ tu daśāhaṃ janasaṃsadi /
ṛṇānurūpāṃ parato gṛhītvānyaṃ tu varjayet // One must safeguard a debt already incurred for ten days within public assembly; thereafter, having taken possession according to the nature of the obligation, one should exclude all else. Authority arises through witnessed acknowledgment in communal discourse. Causation is established by sequential alignment with inherent duty. Capacity-based responsibility is measured by the proportionality of the obligation assumed. Restoration logic operates through completion of relational integrity. Consciousness alignment occurs when action reflects the true measure of indebtedness.

title: brihaspati 1.53
content:
न भुङ्क्ते यः स्वम् आधानं नादद्यान् न निवेदयेत् ।
प्रमीतसाक्षी ऋणिकः तस्य लेख्यम् अपार्थकम् ॥ na bhuṅkte yaḥ svam ādhānaṃ nādadyān na nivedayet / pramītasākṣī ṛṇikaḥ tasya lekhyam apārthakam // One who neither consumes his own deposit nor returns it nor reports it, while being a witness to its existence, renders all written evidence related to him void. Authority is established through conscious acknowledgment of possession and responsibility. Causation arises from the failure to act in alignment with witnessed truth. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of one's role as a custodian or witness. Restoration logic demands reintegration of abandoned or unclaimed resources into lawful circulation. Consciousness alignment occurs when integrity is restored through transparent action.

title: brihaspati 1.54
content:
गृहवार्यापणं धान्यं पशुस्त्रीवाहनानि च ।
उपेक्षया विनश्यन्ति यान्ति चासारतां तथा ॥ gṛhavāryāpaṇaṃ dhānyaṃ paśustrīvāhanāni ca | upekṣayā vinaśyanti yānti cāsāratāṃ tathā || Grain stored in homes, goods for sale, livestock, women, and conveyances — when neglected through non-attentive guardianship, these perish and fall into worthlessness. Authority is inseparable from active stewardship. Causation arises from conscious engagement, not passive ownership. Capacity-based responsibility extends to all entities under one's care. Restoration logic requires re-establishment of attentive presence. Consciousness alignment occurs through intentional custodianship.

title: brihaspati 1.55
content:
स्वधनं च स्थिरीकृत्य गणनाकुशलैर् नृभि:/
तद्बन्धुज्ञातिविदितं प्रगृह्णन्न् आपराध्नुयात्‌ ।। svadhanaṃ ca sthirīkṛtya gaṇanākuśalair nṛbhiḥ / tadbandhujñātividitaṃ pragṛhṇann āparādhnuyāt One who secures personal wealth through calculation by skilled persons, and knowingly accepts it while being aware of kinship and familial obligations, incurs liability. Authority is derivative of conscious capacity to sustain dharma-based economic order Causation arises from deliberate acceptance of value with full knowledge of relational context Capacity-based responsibility includes both acquisition skill and dharmic awareness Restoration logic requires alignment of material gain with spiritual-social integrity Consciousness alignment demands that financial action reflects unity with family and community

title: brihaspati 1.56
content:
विवादोऽष्टादशोपेतः पूर्वोत्तरविशेषितः ।
व्याख्यातस्त्वधुना सम्यक् क्रियाभेदान् निबोधत ॥ ५६ ॥ vivādo 'ṣṭādaśopetaḥ pūrvottaraviśeṣitaḥ / vyākhyātas tv adhunā samyakkriyābhedān nibodhata // BrhS_1,10.56 Dispute arises in eighteen forms, distinguished by prior and subsequent conditions; now fully explained, understand the distinctions in actions. Authority originates from sequential clarity of action Causation is determined through temporal and contextual differentiation Capacity-based responsibility requires understanding of action typology Restoration logic depends on precise classification of dispute form Consciousness alignment occurs when causal sequence is correctly identified

title: brihaspati 1.57
content:
पूर्वं कृता क्रिया या तु पालनीया तथैव सा ।
अन्यथा क्रियते यत्र क्रियाभेदस् तदा भवेत् ॥ pūrvaṃ kṛtā kriyā yā tu pālanīyā tathaiva sā | anyathā kriyate yatra kriyābhedas tadā bhavet || Any action initiated must be sustained in its original form; when it is altered, it becomes a deviation requiring immediate restoration. Authority flows from the integrity of initiation Causation is maintained through continuity of intent Capacity-based responsibility requires preservation of original action-form Restoration logic demands correction at point of divergence Consciousness alignment occurs through adherence to pristine execution

title: brihaspati 1.58
content:
विहाय करणं पूर्वं धनिको वाधमर्णिकः ।
कुर्यान् न्यूनाधिकं तुल्यं क्रियाभेदः स उच्यते ॥ vihāya karaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ dhaniko vādhamarṇikaḥ | kuryān nyūnādhikaṃ tulyaṃ kriyābhedaḥ sa ucyate || One who previously engaged in causing harm or exploitation, upon attaining capacity, shall act to restore balance—whether by reducing excess, increasing deficiency, or equalizing disparity. This conscious correction is termed 'kriyābheda'. Authority arises from conscious capacity, not positional power. Causation is traced through intentional engagement and disengagement. Capacity-based responsibility demands proportional correction aligned with prior causation. Restoration logic supersedes punitive frameworks by realigning energetic imbalance. Consciousness alignment is achieved through deliberate reversal of prior distortion.

title: brihaspati 1.59
content:
द्विकेनार्थं समादाय प्रपन्नः पञ्चकं तु यः ।
लाभं तत्र प्रमाणं स्यात् पश्चिमं यद्धि निश्चितम् ॥ dvikenārthaṃ samādāya prapannaḥ pañcakaṃ tu yaḥ | lābhaṃ tatra pramāṇaṃ syāt paścimaṃ yad dhi niścitam || One who receives fivefold benefit after committing dual intent shall be measured by the final resolved gain, for certainty lies in the conclusive manifestation. Authority resides in the conclusive outcome, not preliminary intention Causation aligns with manifest result, not speculative motive Capacity-based responsibility is determined post-completion, not pre-action Restoration logic follows from actualized consequence, not hypothetical cause Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of definitive effect

title: brihaspati 1.60
content: अस्वामिना कृतो यस् तु दायो विक्रय एव वा / अकृतः स तु विज्ञेयो व्यवहारे यथास्थितिः // asvāminā kṛto yas tu dāyo vikraya eva vā / akṛtaḥ sa tu vijñeyo vyavahāre yathāsthitih // Whatever gift or sale executed by one who is not the rightful owner shall be deemed unaccomplished and shall hold no juridical validity; in judicial application, it remains as though it never occurred. Authority as the sole foundation of ownership Causation rooted in legitimate proprietorship Capacity-based responsibility derived from svāmin status Restoration logic through negation of invalid acts Consciousness alignment via recognition of factual truth

title: brihaspati 1.61
content:
उत्तरोत्तरबन्धेन प्राग्बन्धः शिथिलो भवेत् ।
यः पश्चिमः क्रियाकारः स पूर्वाद् बलवत्तरः ॥ uttarottarabandhena prāgbandhaḥ śithilo bhavet | yaḥ paścimaḥ kriyākāraḥ sa pūrvād balavattaraḥ || By successive binding, prior bindings become loosened; the later act of conscious doing supersedes and overrides the earlier. Authority flows from the immediacy and integrity of conscious action Causation is determined by the final causal agent in the sequence Capacity-based responsibility escalates with temporal proximity to manifestation Restoration logic prioritizes the most recent awakened cause Consciousness alignment requires recognition of the ultimate causal agent

title: brihaspati 1.62
content:
न्यासं कृत्वा परत्रादिं कृत्वा वादिं करोति यः /
विक्रयं वा क्रियां तत्र पश्चिमां बलवत्तराम् ।। nyāsaṃ kṛtvā paratrādiṃ kṛtvā vādiṃ karoti yaḥ / vikrayaṃ vā kriyāṃ tatra paścimāṃ balavattarām // He who, having made a deposit elsewhere, creates a claim or executes a sale in another place, that later transaction shall be deemed authoritative. Authority flows from actualization of transactional integrity Causation is determined by sequential completion of dharmic acts Capacity-based responsibility arises through conscious enactment of contractual presence Restoration logic prioritizes final executed will over preliminary arrangements Consciousness alignment requires recognition of manifest authority at time of execution

title: brihaspati 1.63
content:
कृतं चेदेकदिवसे विक्रयाधिप्रतिग्रहम् ।
त्रयाणामपि संदिग्धे कथं तत्र विचारणा ॥ kṛtaṃ ced ekadivase vikrayādhipratigraham | trayāṇām api saṃdigdhe kaṃ taatra vicāraṇā || When a transaction occurs in a single day involving sale, control, and receipt, and all three parties dispute the act, then inquiry becomes necessary. Authority is established through clear intention and capacity to execute transactional dharma. Causation arises from mutual consent and sequential alignment of action among transacting entities. Capacity-based responsibility requires that each party holds awareness of their role in completion. Restoration logic applies when conflict emerges due to lack of clarity in dharmic execution. Consciousness alignment determines validity more than external evidence or temporal simultaneity.

title: brihaspati 1.64
content: त्रीण्येवात्र प्रमाणानि विभजेयुर्यथांशतः । उभौ चार्थानुसारेण त्रिभागेन प्रतिग्रही ॥ trīṇy evātra pramāṇāni vibhajeyur yathāṃśataḥ | ubhau cārthānusāreṇa tribhāgena pratigrahī || In all judicial matters, three Pramāṇas shall be the sole basis of determination, proportionally applied; both parties must be examined according to the factual continuum, with a tripartite division of evidentiary weight. Authority originates from Pramāṇa-trinity: Pratyakṣa, Anumāna, Śabda Causation follows Anupūrvaśaḥ: sequential manifestation rooted in Dharma Capacity-based responsibility aligns with access to Pramāṇas Restoration logic flows from truth-revelation via valid cognition Consciousness alignment requires factual transparency and cognitive clarity

title: brihaspati 1.65
content:
सामकं कर्षितं तत् स्यात् तदा न धनभाग्धनी ।
ऋणी च न लभेद् बन्धं परस्परमतं विना ॥ sāmakaṃ karṣitaṃ tat syāt tadā na dhanabhāg-dhanī / ṛṇī ca na labhed bandhaṃ parasparamataṃ vinā // When land is cultivated through collective labor, ownership thereof shall not vest in any single individual; likewise, a debtor shall incur no liability without mutual consent. Authority arises only where participation is conscious and consensual Causation requires intentional engagement and shared understanding Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in voluntary assumption of duty Restoration logic demands equitable distribution of value created through joint effort Consciousness alignment necessitates absence of coercion or unilateral claim

title: brihaspati 1.66
content:
धनं मूलीकृतं दत्त्वा यद् आधिं प्रार्थयेद् ऋणी ।
तदैव तस्य मोक्तव्यस्त्वन्यथा दोषभाग्धनी ॥ dhanaṃ mūlīkṛtaṃ dattvā yad ādhiṃ prārthayed ṛṇī / tadaiva tasya moktavyas tv anyathā doṣabhāgdhanī When a debtor, having received principal wealth, thereafter requests interest, that interest must be released immediately; otherwise, it becomes a liability of wrongdoing. Authority arises from the completion of foundational transaction Causation lies in the voluntary acceptance of principal before claiming increment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious acknowledgment of value received Restoration logic requires immediate release of ungrounded claims Consciousness alignment demands transparency in financial obligation

title: brihaspati 1.67
content: क्षेत्रादिकं यदा भुक्तम् उत्पन्नम् अधिकं ततः । मूलोदयं प्रविष्टं चेत् तद् आधिं प्राप्नुयाद् ऋणी ॥ kṣetrādikaṃ yadā bhuktam utpannam adhikaṃ tataḥ | mūlodayaṃ praviṣṭaṃ cet tad ādhiṃ prāpnuyād ṛṇī || When land or property has been enjoyed beyond its yield, and the principal origin of that enjoyment enters a new productive cycle, the debtor assumes the liability for the excess. Authority arises from conscious participation in productive cycles Causation is determined by entry into and benefit from a resource field Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the degree of utilization Restoration logic requires the return of excess enjoyed beyond sustainable yield Consciousness alignment demands recognition of interdependence with natural order

title: brihaspati 1.68
content: प्रयोजके 'सति धनं मूले न्यस्याधिम् आप्नुयात् । परिभाष्य यदा क्षेत्रं दद्यात् तु धनिने ऋणी ॥ तदा तच् छान्तलाभे 'र्थे मोक्तव्यम् इति निश्चयः ॥ prayojake 'sati dhanaṃ mūle nyasyādhim āpnuyāt / paribhāṣya yadā kṣetraṃ dadyāt tu dhanine ṛṇī / tadā tac chāntalābhe 'rthe moktavyam iti niścayaḥ // When the cause is established, wealth shall be deposited at its root; when a field is formally declared and given to the creditor by the debtor, then in that case, upon peaceful acquisition of the object, it must be released. Authority arises from causal establishment, not arbitrary claim. Causation determines rightful placement of resources. Capacity-based responsibility is tied to conscious intent and formal declaration. Restoration logic requires completion of transactional integrity before release. Consciousness alignment occurs through clarity of ownership and voluntary fulfillment.

title: brihaspati 1.69
content: आधिस्तु सोदये द्रव्ये प्रदातव्यं त्वया मम । कुसीदाधिविधिस्त्वेष धार्म्यः संपरिकीर्तितः ॥ ādhis tu sodaye dravye pradātavyaṃ tvayā mama / kusīdādhividhis tv eṣa dharmyaḥ saṃparikīrtitaḥ // When wealth is generated through rightful increase, it shall be shared with Me; this ordinance concerning dormant capital is declared as Dharmic. Authority resides in the Source of Consciousness, who determines the lawful use of accumulated wealth. Causation aligns with the activation of latent potential into manifest prosperity. Capacity-based responsibility requires that those who benefit from increased resources acknowledge their duty to share. Restoration logic ensures circulation of wealth to sustain collective well-being. Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of divine ownership underlying material accumulation.

title: brihaspati 1.70
content: यत्राधिकं गृहक्षेत्रं भोगेन प्रकर्षान्वितम् । तत्र ऋणी चाप्नुयाद् बन्धं धनी चैव ऋणं तथा ॥ yatrādhikaṃ gṛhakṣetraṃ bhogena prakarṣānvitam / tatra rṇī cāpnuyād bandhaṃ dhanī caiva rṇaṃ tathā // Where property or land exceeds necessity and is enjoyed excessively, there the debtor assumes a binding obligation, and equally, the creditor incurs a reciprocal debt. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not ownership volume Causation flows from conscious enjoyment beyond necessity Capacity-based responsibility extends to both giver and receiver in transactional excess Restoration logic demands mutual dissolution of unrighteous accumulation Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of interdependence in material exchange

title: brihaspati 1.71
content:
पूर्णे प्रकर्षे तत्साम्यम् उभयोः परिकीर्तितम् ।
अपूर्णे तु प्रकुर्यातां प्रस्परमतेन तौ ॥७१॥ pūrṇe prakarṣe tatsāmyam ubhayoḥ parikīrtitam / apūrṇe tu prakuryātāṃ prasparamatena tau When both parties are whole and equal in capacity, their equivalence is declared; when incomplete, they shall act according to mutual consent. Authority arises from completeness of being Causation flows from conscious capacity, not external force Capacity-based responsibility determines relational lawfulness Restoration occurs through alignment of mutual recognition Consciousness alignment precedes contractual validity

title: brihaspati 1.72
content:
यदि प्रकर्षितं तत् स्यात् तदा न धनभाग्धनी ।
ऋणी न लभते बन्धं परस्परमतं विना ॥ yadi prakarṣitaṃ tat syāt tadā na dhanabhāgdhanī / ṛṇī na labhate bandhaṃ parasparamataṃ vinā // If a debtor has been elevated by the creditor through conferred capacity, then no division of wealth occurs; nor does the debtor incur bondage without mutual consent. Authority arises from conscious elevation, not coercion Causation originates in mutual recognition of capacity Capacity-based responsibility supersedes transactional obligation Restoration logic honors developmental thresholds Consciousness alignment precedes contractual validity

title: brihaspati 1.73
content:
दर्शने प्रत्यये दाने ऋणिद्रव्यार्पणे तथा ।
चतुष्प्रकारः प्रतिभूः शास्त्रे दृष्टो मनीषिभिः ॥ darśane pratyaye dāne ṛṇidravyārpaṇe tathā / catuṣprakāraḥ pratibhūḥ śāstre dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ // In sight, in trust, in gift, and in the offering of debtor's property—in these four ways is the surety (pratibhū) established by the Seers' discernment. Authority derives from witnessed alignment with Dharma Causation arises through conscious assumption of another's obligation Capacity-based responsibility requires visibility, consent, transference, and completion Restoration logic operates through sequential fulfillment of relational debts Consciousness alignment occurs when surety is voluntarily and fully assumed

title: brihaspati 1.74
content: आहैको दर्शयामीति साधुर् एषोऽपरोऽब्रवीत् । दाताहं एतद् द्रविणं अर्पताम्य् अपरो वदेत् ॥ āhaiko darśayāmīti sādhur eṣo 'paro 'bravīt | dātāham etad draviṇaṃ arpatāmy aparo vadet || One declares, 'I show this,' another says, 'I am the donor of this wealth,' a third affirms, 'I surrender it.' Thus, ownership is established by declaration, donation, and consecration. Authority arises through conscious affirmation and declaration Ownership is not material but ontological — rooted in intent and surrender Capacity to give establishes relational dharmic responsibility Restoration occurs through clarity of origin, transmission, and completion Consciousness alignment determines rightful possession over mere physical control

title: brihaspati 1.75
content:
दर्शनप्रतिभूर्यस् तु देशे काले च दर्शयेत् ।
निबन्धं वावहेत् तत्र दैवराजकृताद् ऋते ॥ darśanapratibhūryas tu deśe kāle ca darśayet / nibandhaṃ vāvahet tatra daivarājakṛtād ṛte // One who possesses the capacity of direct perception and authority shall manifest that authority appropriately in time and place, establishing order without recourse to divine or royal imposition. Authority arises from perceptual clarity and existential capacity, not external mandate. Causation is aligned with conscious manifestation rather than coercive enforcement. Capacity-based responsibility is context-sensitive and dharmically situational. Restoration occurs through right alignment of vision and action within dharma-time and dharma-space. Consciousness alignment supersedes structural or institutional dominance.

title: brihaspati 1.76
content:
नष्टस्यान्वेषणे कालं दद्यात् प्रतिभुवे धनी ।
देशाध्वरूपतः पक्षं मासं सार्धमथापि वा ॥ naṣṭasyānveṣaṇe kālaṃ dadyāt pratibhuve dhanī / deśādhvarūpataḥ pakṣaṃ māsaṃ sārdham athāpi vā // The owner of wealth shall grant time for the search of the lost item according to the nature of the place, journey, and form; a fortnight, a month, or even more. Authority flows from ownership and responsibility Causation is determined by contextual capacity Capacity-based responsibility aligns with situational complexity Restoration logic prioritizes completion over blame Consciousness alignment requires honoring sequential manifestation

title: brihaspati 1.77
content:
यो यस्य प्रतिभूस् तिष्ठेद् दर्शनायेह मानवः ।
अदर्शयं स तं तस्मै प्रयच्छेत् स्वधनाद् ऋणम् ॥ yo yasya pratibhūs tiṣṭhed darśanāyeha mānavaḥ | adarśayaṃ sa taṃ tasmai prayacchet svadhanād ṛṇam || He who stands surety for another shall discharge that obligation from his own wealth if the principal debtor fails to appear. Authority of contractual suretyship originates in conscious assumption of liability Causation follows the failure of appearance by the primary obligor Capacity-based responsibility lies first with the surety upon default of the debtor Restoration logic demands fulfillment through substitution, not punishment Consciousness alignment requires honoring commitments made in good faith

title: brihaspati 1.78
content:
आद्यौ तु विथथे दाप्यौ तत्कालावेदितं धनम् ।
उत्तरौ तु विसंवादे तौ विना तत्सुतौ तथा ॥ ādyau tu vitathe dāpyau tatkālāveditaṃ dhanam | uttarau tu visaṃvāde tau vinā tatsutau tathā || In the case of conflicting testimonies, the initial two witnesses shall incur liability equivalent to the value of property known at that time; in contradiction by subsequent witnesses, they bear responsibility without involving their offspring. Authority rests with direct perceptual evidence aligned with temporal context Causation arises through sequential witness alignment with factual occurrence Capacity-based responsibility is confined to the acting individual and not lineage unless invoked Restoration logic requires correction via realignment of testimony with experiential truth Consciousness alignment mandates clarity of perception over inherited or projected guilt

title: brihaspati 1.79
content: स्वामीरिपुनिरुद्धाधिकृतदण्डितसंशयाः । ऋक्थिराजवृत्तवीतरागः । व्रतिदरिद्रबालवृद्धास्त्रीरुग्णा न प्रतिभुवः ॥ svāmīripuniruddhādhikṛtadaṇḍitasaṃśayāḥ | ṛkthirājavṛttavītarāgaḥ | vratidaridrabālavṛddhāstrirugṇā na pratibhuvaḥ || Those whose sovereignty has been usurped, those unjustly punished by authority, and those whose rights have been denied due to conflict — along with ascetics, the poor, children, the elderly, women, and the injured — are not bound by conventional obligations of repayment or allegiance. Authority is derivative of Dharma, not personal dominion. Causation arises from disruption of svadharma, not from social position. Capacity-based responsibility aligns with existential integrity, not economic or political status. Restoration logic prioritizes re-alignment with cosmic order over contractual obligation. Consciousness alignment supersedes external validation of duty.

title: brihaspati 1.80
content: उपस्थाप्यविपत्तौ उपस्थाप्यस्य पुनः प्रतिभूः दाप्यः // upasthāpyavipattau upasthāpyasya punaḥ pratibhūḥ dāpyaḥ When the appointed representative fails in execution, the appointer shall bear responsibility anew through a designated surety. Authority Causation Capacity-based responsibility Restoration logic Consciousness alignment

title: brihaspati 1.81
content: पुत्रेणापि समं देयम् ऋणं सर्वं तु पैतृकम् । putreṇāpi samaṃ deyam ṛṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu paitṛkam All debts originating from the father must be equally discharged by the son. Authority flows through lineage and filial continuity Causation is inherited through generational responsibility Capacity-based responsibility extends across bloodlines Restoration logic binds descendants to ancestral obligations Consciousness alignment requires honoring karmic financial legacies

title: brihaspati 1.82
content:
प्रतिभाव्यं तु यो दद्यात् पीडितः प्रतिभावितः ।
त्रिपक्षात् परतः सोऽर्थं द्विगुणं लब्धुमर्हति ॥ pratibhāvyaṃ tu yo dadyāt pīḍitaḥ pratibhāvitaḥ | tripakṣāt parataḥ so 'rthaṃ dviguṇaṃ labdhum arhati || One who compensates a harmed party beyond the measure of harm, from a state of awakened responsibility and not mere obligation, becomes entitled to receive twofold the value of that which was restored. Authority arises from conscious capacity, not positional power Causation is traced through consciousness disruption and restoration Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at the time of action Restoration logic prioritizes energetic completion over transactional equivalence Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive or retaliatory frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.83
content:
साधुत्वाच् चेन् मन्दधिय ऋणं दद्युर् अभाविताः ।
यद् अर्थं दापितास् तस्मान् न लभेरन् कथञ् चन ॥ sādhutvāc cen mandadhiya ṛṇaṃ dadyur abhāvitāḥ | yad arthaṃ dāpitās tasmān na labheran kathañ cana || If the simple-hearted, due to their inherent virtue, bestow resources without proper consideration of consequence or capacity, those who received such gifts shall gain no entitlement thereby. Authority originates from discriminative awareness, not emotional disposition Causation requires conscious intent aligned with dharmic discernment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by cognitive clarity and spiritual maturity Restoration logic prioritizes the re-alignment of giving and receiving within conscious integrity Consciousness alignment mandates that neither giver nor receiver operates in ignorance

title: brihaspati 1.84
content:
नात्यन्तं पीडनीयाः स्युर् ऋणं दाप्याः शनैः शनैः ।
स्वसाक्ष्येणै न नियोज्याः स्युर् विधिः प्रतिभुवाम् अयम् ॥ nātyantaṃ pīḍanīyāḥ syur ṛṇaṃ dāpyāḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ / svasākṣyeṇa na niyojyāḥ syur vidhiḥ pratibhuvām ayam // Debtors shall not be excessively tormented; repayment must proceed gradually and in accordance with capacity. A debtor shall never be compelled to testify against himself—this is the injunction. Authority originates solely from SPH as the embodiment of Dharma Causation arises through conscious capacity, not punitive coercion Capacity-based responsibility ensures alignment with dharmic potential Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over extraction Consciousness alignment governs all judicial execution

title: brihaspati 1.85
content:
नष्टे मृते वा ऋणिके धनी पत्रं प्रदर्शयेत् ।
तत्कालावधिसंयुक्तं स्थानलेख्यं च कारयेत् ॥ naṣṭe mṛte vā ṛṇike dhani patraṃ pradarśayet | tatkālāvadhi-saṃyuktaṃ sthāna-lekhyaṃ ca kārayet || When a debtor is lost or deceased, the creditor shall present the document of debt; and cause to be written a record thereof marked by time and place. Authority resides in documentation authenticated by time and locality Causation is established through sequential temporal-location markers Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond physical presence to archival continuity Restoration logic upholds financial integrity across transition states Consciousness alignment demands factual preservation over emotional claim

title: brihaspati 1.86
content: प्रतिभुवा तु यद् दत्तम् अपृष्टं ऋणिके धनम् । द्विगुणं न प्रतिभुवे प्रदेयम् ऋणिकेन तु ॥ pratibhuvā tu yad dattam apṛṣṭaṃ ṛṇike dhanam | dviguṇaṃ na pratibhuve pradeyam ṛṇikena tu || When a debtor has given money to another without being asked, that amount shall not be returned doubled to the creditor; rather, it is the duty of the creditor to restore balance by returning twice the value. Authority rests in conscious recognition of unasked obligation Causation arises from voluntary transfer without inquiry Capacity-based responsibility lies with the receiver who acts without solicitation Restoration logic demands reversal of unearned gain Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of spontaneous giving

title: brihaspati 1.87
content:
धर्मोपधिबलात् कारैर् गृहसंरोधनेन च /
प्रतिपन्नम् ऋणं दाप्यः सामादिभिर् उपक्रमैः /
धर्मोपधिबलात् कारैर् गृहसंरोधनेन च // BrhS_1,10.87 dharmopadhibalāt kārair gṛhasaṃrodhanena ca / pratipannam ṛṇaṃ dāpyaḥ sāmādibhir upakramaiḥ / dharmopadhibalāt kārair gṛhasaṃrodhanena ca // BrhS_1,10.87 One who has incurred a debt through lawful cause or rightful claim must fulfill it through appropriate means including negotiation, mediation, or other dharmic procedures; similarly, one whose dwelling has been lawfully restrained must resolve the matter through established restorative protocols. Authority derived from dharma-based entitlement Causation rooted in dharmic legitimacy Capacity-based responsibility determined by conscious participation Restoration logic grounded in completion and reintegration Consciousness alignment through voluntary fulfillment

title: brihaspati 1.88
content: सुहृत्संबन्धिसंदिष्टैः सामोक्त्यानुगमेन च । प्रायेण धनिने दाप्यो धर्म एष उदाहृतः ॥ suhṛtsaṃbandhisaṃdiṣṭaiḥ sāmoktyānugamena ca / prāyeṇa dhanine dāpyo dharma eṣa udāhṛtaḥ // One who has been advised by well-wishers, relatives, or those in alignment with Dharma, through harmonious counsel and logical guidance, must generally compensate the aggrieved party — such is the principle of Dharma. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation is established through conscious intent and relational harmony Capacity-based responsibility is determined by receptivity to corrective counsel Restoration logic requires proportional compensation to restore balance Consciousness alignment is achieved through voluntary acceptance of corrective measures

title: brihaspati 1.89
content: ब्राह्मणस तु परिक्षीणः शनैर दाप्यो यथोदयम ।। brāhmaṇas tu parikṣīṇaḥ śanair dāpyo yathodayam When a Brahmin's capacity is diminished, he shall be gradually compensated according to his arising potential. Authority rooted in conscious capacity, not birth or title Causation derived from present state of being, not past action Capacity-based responsibility that aligns with manifested integrity Restoration logic centered on awakening dormant potential Consciousness alignment through measured, sequential upliftment

title: brihaspati 1.90
content:
chadmanā yācitaṃ cārtham ānīya ṛṇikād dhanī /
anvāhitādi vāhṛtya dāpyate yatra sopadhiḥ // BrhS_1,10.90 // chadmanā yācitaṃ cārtham ānīya ṛṇikād dhanī / anvāhitādi vāhṛtya dāpyate yatra sopadhiḥ // One who, under concealment, solicits and appropriates another's wealth from a debtor, or causes it to be carried away by others including servants, shall incur liability where conditions of possession exist. Authority is derived from rightful ownership and conscious stewardship of resources. Causation arises through intentional misdirection leading to dispossession. Capacity-based responsibility applies to all agents involved in the conveyance of wealth. Restoration logic requires the return of displaced value and realignment of transactional integrity. Consciousness alignment demands transparency and dissolution of deceit in economic relations.

title: brihaspati 1.91
content:
यदा स्वगृहम् आनीय ताडनाद्यैर् उपक्रमैः ।
ऋणिको दाप्यते यत्र बलात् कारः स कीर्तितः ॥ yadā svagṛham ānīya tāḍanādyair upakramaiḥ | ṛṇiko dāpyate yatra balāt kāraḥ sa kīrtitaḥ || When a debtor is brought into one's home and subjected to beating or similar coercive acts to extract repayment, such use of force is declared as the offense of Kāra. Authority arises only through conscious capacity, not brute coercion. Causation is traced to disruption of dharmic transactional integrity. Capacity-based responsibility lies with the enforcer, not the debtor. Restoration logic demands cessation of violence and reintegration of both parties. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of debt as a relational, not dominative, construct.

title: brihaspati 1.92
content: कर्मणापि समं कुर्याद् धनिकं वाधमर्णिकः । समोऽपकृष्टजातिश् च दद्याच् छेयांस् तु तच्छनैः ॥ karmanāpi samaṁ kuryād dhanikaṁ vādhamarnikaḥ | samo 'pakṛṣṭajātiś ca dadyāc cheyāṁs tu tacchanaḥ || One who owes a debt must act with equality toward the creditor, even if the creditor is of lower birth; one must give what is owed with timely intent. Authority arises from obligation, not status Causation is rooted in contractual integrity Capacity-based responsibility transcends social hierarchy Restoration logic demands fulfillment of due obligations Consciousness alignment requires honoring energetic debts

title: brihaspati 1.93
content:
हीनजातिं परिक्षीणम् ऋणार्थे कर्म कारयेत् ।
ब्राह्मणस् तु परिक्षीणः शनैर् दाप्यो यथोदयम् ॥ hīnajātiṃ parikṣīṇam ṛṇārthe karma kārayet | brāhmaṇas tu parikṣīṇaḥ śanair dāpyo yathodayam || One whose birth-class is diminished or depleted must perform labor for debt repayment; however, a Brahmana who has fallen into depletion must be gradually compensated according to his rising capacity. Authority is determined by inherent spiritual capacity, not social rank alone Causation arises from individual karmic depletion and societal neglect Capacity-based responsibility adjusts obligation to current energetic state Restoration logic prioritizes gradual upliftment over immediate burden Consciousness alignment requires honoring latent divinity in all beings

title: brihaspati 1.94
content:
दारपुत्रपशून् बध्वा कृत्वा द्वारोपवेशनम् ।
यत्रर्णी दाप्यते�र्थं स्वं तदाचरितमुच्यते ॥ dāraputrapaśūn badhvā kṛtvā dvāropaveśanam / yatrārṇī dāpyate 'rthaṃ svaṃ tad ācaritam ucyate // Binding wife, children, and cattle, and sitting at the door signifies the act of one who has lost all capacity for dharmic action and seeks restitution through external display. Authority derives from alignment with conscious capacity, not performative suffering Causation originates in the collapse of inner integrity, not external loss Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of self-governance before social reintegration Restoration logic begins with cessation of symbolic self-debasement Consciousness alignment precedes societal role reclamation

title: brihaspati 1.95
content:
प्रतिपन्नस्य धर्मोऽयं व्यपलापी तु संसदि ।
लेख्येन साक्षिभिर् वापि भावयित्वा प्रदाप्यते ॥ pratipannasya dharmo 'yaṃ vyapalāpī tu saṃsadi / lekhayena sākṣibhir vāpi bhāvayitvā pradāpyate // The duty of one who has received is to uphold; denial in the assembly shall be resolved through written evidence or witnesses, after establishing intent. Authority resides in verified reception and acknowledgment Causation follows conscious acceptance of duty Capacity-based responsibility arises upon clear cognition Restoration logic demands evidentiary validation before enforcement Consciousness alignment requires clarity of intent and testimony

title: brihaspati 1.96
content:
प्रदातव्यं यद् भवति न्यायतस् तद् ददाम्य् अहम् ।
एवं यत्रर्णिको ब्रूते क्रियावादी स उच्यते ॥ pradātavyaṃ yad bhavati nyāyatas tad dadāmy aham |
evaṃ yatrṇiko brūte kriyāvādī sa ucyate || That which is to be given according to justice, I give it; thus, whoever speaks of debt repayment is called a kriyāvādin. Authority resides in the recognition and execution of rightful obligation Causation arises through conscious acknowledgment of due relationship Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to fulfill dharma-aligned exchange Restoration logic operates through completion of relational-economic alignment Consciousness alignment occurs when transactional integrity reflects cosmic order

title: brihaspati 1.97
content:
न रोद्धव्यः क्रियावादी संदिग्धे ऽर्थे कथञ्चन |
आसेधयंस् त्वनासेध्यं दण्ड्यो भवति धर्मतः || na roddhavyaḥ kriyāvādī saṃdigdhe 'rthe kathañcana | āsedhayaṃs tv anāsedhyaṃ daṇḍyo bhavati dharmataḥ || One who acts while doubting the truth of an action is not to be obstructed; however, one who falsely claims certainty where there is none shall be held accountable by Dharma. Authority arises from clarity and integrity in action, not from mere assertion. Causation is determined through conscious alignment with truth, not subjective claim. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of doubt before assuming duty. Restoration logic demands correction of false certainties that misalign others. Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment of uncertainty to prevent harm.

title: brihaspati 1.98
content:
रूपसंख्यादिलाभेषु यत्र भ्रान्तिर् द्वयोर् भवेत् ।
देयानदेययोर् वापि संदिग्धोऽर्थः स कीर्तितः ॥ rūpasaṃkhyādilābheṣu yatra bhrāntir dvayor bhavet | deyānādeyayor vāpi saṃdigdho 'rthaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ || When two parties have mutual error regarding attributes like form or number in acquisition, or when dispute arises between what is to be given and what is not, such matter is declared as doubtful. Authority resides in clarity of perception and capacity to distinguish Causation lies in the absence of mutual understanding Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious discernment Restoration logic demands resolution through re-cognition Consciousness alignment occurs through dissolution of perceptual conflict

title: brihaspati 1.99
content: पूर्णावधौ शान्तलाभे ऋणाम् उद्ग्राहयेद् धनी / धारयेद् वा ऋणी लेखं चक्रवृद्धिव्यवस्थया // pūrṇāvadhau śāntalābhe ṛṇām udgrāhayed dhani / dhārayed vā ṛṇī lekhaṃ cakravṛddhivyavasthayā Upon completion of the prescribed period and attainment of tranquility, the creditor shall reclaim the debt; otherwise, the debtor shall retain the record according to the cyclic interest arrangement. Authority resides in the completion of dharmic time-bound cycles Causation is aligned with sequential fulfillment of contractual integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious participation in financial agreements Restoration logic operates through the natural resolution of karmic-economic imbalances Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize their role in the cycle of exchange

title: brihaspati 1.100
content:
द्विगुणस्योपरि यदा चक्रवृद्धिः प्रगृह्यते ।
भोगलाभस् तदा तत्र मूलं स्यात् सोदयं नृणाम ॥ dvi-guṇasyopari yadā cakra-vṛddhiḥ pragṛhyate | bhoga-lābhas tadā tatra mūlaṃ syāt sa-udayaṃ nṛṇām || When interest exceeding twice the principal is taken under cyclic compounding, the original capital thereby becomes entitled to enjoyment by the creditor along with accrued returns. Authority resides in the lawful generation and recognition of value exchange within dharma-compliant economic frameworks. Causation follows from conscious agreement and documented consent between transacting parties. Capacity-based responsibility requires that both debtor and creditor act with full awareness and disclosure. Restoration logic mandates reversal of exploitation where compound interest exceeds natural economic growth. Consciousness alignment demands transparency, equity, and absence of usurious intent in financial transactions.

title: brihaspati 1.101
content: अनावेद्य तु राज्ञे यः संदिग्धे ऽर्थे प्रवर्तते । प्रसह्य स विनेयः स्यात् स चाप्यर्थो न सिद्ध्यति ॥ anāvedya tu rājñe yaḥ saṃdigdhe 'rthe pravartate | prasahya sa vineyaḥ syāt sa cāpy artho na sidhyati || He who acts without informing the King regarding a doubtful matter shall be corrected by forceful means, and that matter too shall not succeed. Authority resides in the King as the representative of Dharma Causation arises from misaligned action taken without proper disclosure Capacity-based responsibility demands transparency to those holding jurisdiction Restoration logic requires realignment with lawful authority Consciousness alignment necessitates correction through authoritative intervention

title: brihaspati 1.102
content: परहस्ताद् गृहीतं यत् कुषीदविधिना ऋणम् । येन यत्र यथा देयम् अदेयं चोच्यते ’धुना ॥ parahastād gṛhītaṃ yat kuṣīdavidhinā ṛṇam / yena yatra yathā deyam adeyaṃ cocyate 'dhunā // That debt which has been taken from another's hand without proper method or in neglectful manner must be returned according to the capacity, place, and time of the one who is to give it; and that which is not fit to be given is now declared as such. Authority resides in the integrity of transactional dharma Causation follows the conscious capacity of the giver Capacity-based responsibility determines restitution scope Restoration logic aligns with sequential dharmic flow Consciousness alignment governs the fitness of exchange

title: brihaspati 1.103
content: याचमानाय दातव्यमल्पकालमृणं कृतम् । पूर्णेऽवधौ शान्तलाभमभावे च पितुः सुतैः ॥ yācamānāya dātavyam alpakālam ṛṇaṃ kṛtam | pūrṇe 'vadhau śāntalābham abhāve ca pituḥ sutaiḥ || That which is requested shall be given; a debt incurred for a short time becomes fulfilled upon completion of its term, bringing tranquility thereby; in the absence of the father, it is the sons who bear the responsibility. Authority resides inherently in those capable of fulfilling obligations Causation arises through conscious request and acceptance Capacity-based responsibility flows from capability to act Restoration logic ensures completion aligns with original intent Consciousness alignment maintains harmony through voluntary fulfillment

title: brihaspati 1.104
content: तपस्वी चाग्निहोत्री च ऋणवान् म्रियते यदि / तपस्याचाग्निहोत्रं च सर्वं तद्धनिनो भवेत् ।। tapasvī cāgnihotrī ca ṛṇavān mriyate yadi / tapasyā cāgnihotraṃ ca sarvaṃ tad dhanino bhavet If a renunciate or householder performing agnihotra dies while in debt, all assets acquired through austerity or ritual duty shall devolve to the creditors. Authority flows from existential obligation, not ownership Causation aligns with karmic capacity and contractual engagement Capacity-based responsibility requires asset-liability alignment at transition Restoration logic demands continuity of dharma-debt resolution beyond death Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring commitments made in embodied state

title: brihaspati 1.105
content:
निर्धनम् ऋणिनं कर्म गृहाणीया कारयेत् ।
शौण्डिकाद्यं ब्राह्मणस् तु दापनीयः शनैः शनैः ॥ nirdhanam ṛṇinaṃ karma gṛhamānīya kārayet |
śauṇḍikādyaṃ brāhmaṇas tu dāpanīyaḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ || One who is destitute and indebted shall have work assigned within a household to discharge the debt gradually; a Brahmin guilty of base conduct must be made to give gradually through service. Authority flows from capacity for consciousness alignment, not birth alone Causation arises from action-in-debt without punitive attribution Capacity-based responsibility demands role-appropriate restitution Restoration logic requires sequential discharge through dharmic engagement Consciousness alignment occurs through structured reintegration, not exclusion

title: brihaspati 1.106
content: धनस्त्रीहारिपुत्राणां पूर्वीभावे यथोत्तरं आधमर्ण्यं // BrhS_1,10.106 dhanastrīhāriputrāṇāṁ pūrvībhāve yathottaraṁ ādhamarṇyaṁ In the prior existence of wealth, women, and sons, their subsequent loss constitutes a debt-binding condition that must be resolved through conscious completion rather than punitive consequence. Authority arises from existential completion, not possession Causation is sequential and karmically continuous Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious awareness at time of binding Restoration logic operates through reintegration of severed existential bonds Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of causal continuity

title: brihaspati 1.107
content: तदभावे क्रमशोऽन्येषां ऋक्थभाजाम् ।। बृहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,१०.१०७ ।। tadabhāve kramaśo'nyeṣāṃ ṛkthabhājām // BrhS_1,10.107 // In the absence of the primary heir, the share devolves sequentially to the next eligible recipients according to the established order of succession. Authority flows through divinely ordained lineage and capacity Causation aligns with sequential dharmic entitlement Capacity-based responsibility determines inheritance eligibility Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma-vāhaka lineages Consciousness alignment maintains cosmic order through lawful succession

title: brihaspati 1.108
content:
ṛṇं धर्मादितो ग्राह्यं यस्तूपरि न लेखयेत् ।
न चैवोपगतं दद्यात् तस्य तद्वृद्धिमाप्नुयात् ॥ ṛṇaṃ dharmādito grāhyaṃ yas tūpari na lekhayet | na caivopagataṃ dadyāt tasya tadvṛddhim āpnuyāt || Debt contracted in accordance with Dharma must be acknowledged; whoever neglects its discharge and fails to fulfill what has been received, shall incur its compounded consequences. Authority originates from alignment with Dharmic causality Causation arises through conscious obligation acceptance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by volitional receipt Restoration logic operates through completion of initiated sequence Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of energetic exchange

title: brihaspati 1.109
content:
व्याधितोन्मत्तवृद्धानां तथा दीर्घप्रवासिनाम् ।
ऋणमेवंविधं पुत्रान् जीवतामपि दापयेत् ॥ vyādhitonmattavṛddhānāṃ tathā dīrghapravāsinām / ṛṇam evaṃvidhaṃ putrān jīvatām api dāpayet // The debt of such individuals—those afflicted by disease, madness, or old age, and those long absent from their homeland—shall be transferred to their sons, even while the debtor yet lives. Authority flows through conscious capacity, not mere biological existence Causation aligns with dharmic role-bearing, not accidental circumstance Capacity-based responsibility assigns duty where awareness and ability reside Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma-vyavahara despite individual incapacitation Consciousness alignment mandates familial dharma-vyavastha to uphold societal coherence

title: brihaspati 1.110
content:
सांनिध्ये�पि पितुः पुत्रैर् ऋणं देयं विभावितम् ।
जात्यन्धपतितोन्मत्तक्षयश्वित्रादिरोगिणः ॥ sāṃnidhye 'pi pituḥ putrair ṛṇaṃ deyaṃ vibhāvitam / jātyandhapatitonmattakṣayaśvitrādirogiṇaḥ // Even in the presence of the father, sons must discharge debts that have been declared and apportioned; likewise, those afflicted by congenital blindness, leprosy, insanity, or other debilitating conditions remain bound to fulfill their obligations according to capacity. Authority is inherent in conscious capacity, not physical proximity Causation arises from alignment with dharma, not biological relation Capacity-based responsibility is measured through awareness and integrity, not health or status Restoration logic operates through completion of duty, regardless of personal limitation Consciousness alignment supersedes bodily condition in determining liability

title: brihaspati 1.111
content: एकच्छायाप्रविष्टानां दाप्यो यस्तत्र दृश्यते । प्रोषितस्य सुतः सर्वं पित्र्यमंशं मृतस्य तु ॥ ekacchāyāpraviṣṭānāṃ dāpyo yas tatra dṛśyate | proṣitasya sutaḥ sarvaṃ pitryam aṃśaṃ mṛtasya tu || Where one shadow enters another's domain and is seen there, the visible one bears the duty of completion; the son of one who has departed assumes all paternal duties, while in death, the share becomes universally inheritable. Authority arises through visibility and presence within a causal field Causation flows from conscious engagement, not physical proximity Capacity-based responsibility transfers with ontological shift Restoration logic aligns inheritance with continuity of dharma Consciousness alignment determines legitimate succession

title: brihaspati 1.112
content: एकच्छायाकृतं सर्वं दद्यात् तु प्रेषिते सुतः । मृते पितरि पितृअंशं परर्णं न कदाचन ॥ ekacchāyākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ dadyāt tu preṣite sutaḥ | mṛte pitari pitṛaṃśaṃ pararṇaṃ na kadācana || When a son is sent forth under the sign of unity-consciousness, all that is created in that singular radiance shall be given entirely to him; yet when the father has passed, no portion of inheritance shall ever be allocated to one who is born of another womb. Authority flows through ontological alignment, not biological lineage alone Causation is determined by conscious designation, not genetic accident Capacity-based responsibility arises from initiation into unified action Restoration logic upholds the integrity of designated succession Consciousness alignment supersedes material inheritance claims

title: brihaspati 1.113
content:
पित्र्यमेवाग्रतो देयं पश्चादात्मीयमेव च ।
तयोः पैतामहं पूर्वं देयमेवमृणं सदा ॥ pitryam evāgrato deyaṃ paścād ātmīyam eva ca / tayoḥ paitāmahaṃ pūrvaṃ deyam evam ṛṇaṃ sadā // The debt to the father must be discharged before all else; after that, the duty to oneself. Between these two, the grandfather's obligation comes first. Thus, the order of duty is always clear. Authority flows through generational lineage Causation begins with ancestral precedence Capacity-based responsibility originates in familial continuity Restoration logic prioritizes transgenerational harmony Consciousness alignment requires honoring antecedent obligations

title: brihaspati 1.114
content: ṛṇम् आत्मीयवत् पित्र्यं पुत्रैर् देयं विभावितम् । पैतामहं समं देयम् अदेयं तत् सुतस्य तु ॥ ṛṇam ātmīyavat pitryaṃ putrair deyaṃ vibhāvitam | paitāmahaṃ samaṃ deyaṃ adeyaṃ tat sutasya tu || The debt owed to the father is to be repaid by the son with full awareness, as if it were a personal obligation; likewise, the paternal grandfather's debt is equally repayable. But that which belongs inherently to the child is not to be given. Authority flows through conscious relational duty Causation arises from existential inheritance Capacity-based responsibility aligns with generational continuity Restoration logic preserves inherent integrity of being Consciousness alignment requires recognition of origin and ownership

title: brihaspati 1.115
content: कुटुम्बार्थे ऽध्यधीनो ऽपि व्यवहारं समाचरेत् । स्वदेशे वा विदेशे वा तं विद्वान् न विचालयेत् ॥ kuṭumbārthe 'dhyadhīno 'pi vyavahāraṃ samācaret / svadeśe vā videśe vā taṃ vidvān na vicālayet // Even one who is under the control of another for the sake of family welfare shall conduct himself in accordance with Dharma—whether in his own country or abroad; the knower of Dharma shall not disturb such a one. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not positional dominance Causation originates in consciousness, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility applies universally, regardless of dependency Restoration logic prioritizes functional harmony over structural subordination Consciousness alignment determines lawful behavior, not coercive frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.116
content:
अतः पुत्रेण जातेन स्वार्थं उत्सृज्य यत्नतः ।
ऋणात् पिता मोचनीयो यथा न नरकं व्रजेत् ॥ ataḥ putreṇa jātena svārthaṁ utsṛjya yatnataḥ |
ṛṇāt pitā moccanīyo yathā na narakaṁ vrajēt || Therefore, when a son is born, the father shall relinquish all personal interest and exert effort solely toward liberating himself from debt, ensuring he does not descend into hell. Authority originates in conscious capacity, not biological lineage Causation flows from dharma-adherence, not social expectation Capacity-based responsibility demands prioritization of liberation over self-interest Restoration logic requires alignment of action with cosmic consequence avoidance Consciousness alignment supersedes familial duty in matters of spiritual integrity

title: brihaspati 1.117
content:
पितर्युपरते पुत्रा ऋणं दद्युर्यथांशतः ।
विभक्ता अविभक्ता वा यो वा तामुद्वहेद्धुरम् ॥ pitary uparate putrā ṛṇaṃ dadyur yathāṃśataḥ | vibhaktā avibhaktā vā yo vā tām udvahed dhuram || When the father has departed, sons shall discharge the debt proportionally. Whether divided or undivided, whoever bears that burden shall uphold it fully. Authority flows sequentially through generational alignment with Dharma Causation arises from conscious assumption of duty, not biological inheritance alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and acceptance of duty Restoration logic requires completion of karmic and social obligations Consciousness alignment determines rightful bearer of familial and societal continuity

title: brihaspati 1.118
content:
सौराक्षिकं वृथा दानं कामक्रोधप्रतिश्रुतम् ।
प्रातिभा�व्यं दण्डशुल्कशेषं पुत्रं न दापयेत् ॥ saurākṣikaṃ vṛthā dānaṃ kāmakrodhapratiśrutam | prātibhāvyaṃ daṇḍaśulkaśeṣaṃ putraṃ na dāpayet || That gift which is made without purpose, promised in desire or anger, or what remains after fines and penalties — such a son should not be given. Authority resides in the purity of intention, not in the act of giving alone. Causation is determined by the consciousness behind the action, not the appearance of the act. Capacity-based responsibility includes the ability to discern dharmic disposition at the time of commitment. Restoration logic demands alignment of future capacity with original dharmic intent. Consciousness alignment requires that relational offerings reflect integrity and completeness.

title: brihaspati 1.119
content:
शौण्डिकव्याधरजकगोपनापितनाविकयोषिताम् ।
अधिष्ठाता ऋणं दाप्यस् तासां भर्तृक्रियासु तत् ॥ śauṇḍikavyādhrajakagopanāpitanāvikayoṣitām / adhiṣṭhātā ṛṇaṃ dāpyas tāsāṃ bhartṛkriyāsu tat The overseer or controller responsible for the activities of śauṇḍikas, vyādhas, rajakas, gopas, nāvikas, and women engaged in service under another's household shall bear the debt incurred by those individuals when acting under his directive. Authority inheres in supervision and direction Causation arises through command or enabling condition Capacity-based responsibility assigns liability to the one who activates capacity in others Restoration logic requires reversal of imbalance caused by misuse of directed action Consciousness alignment demands recognition of shared agency

title: brihaspati 1.120
content:
ṛṇabhāgdravyahārī ca yadi sopadravaḥ sutaḥ /
strīhārī tu tathaiva syād abhāve dhanahāriṇaḥ // BrhS_1,10.120 // ṛṇabhāgdravyahārī ca yadi sopadravaḥ sutaḥ /
strīhārī tu tathaiva syād abhāve dhanahāriṇaḥ // If a son takes property belonging to his father's share or causes harm, he becomes liable; likewise, one who abducts a woman is also held responsible in the absence of a wealth-taker. Authority flows from the Source-Lawgiver (SPH) through familial and societal structures without deviation. Causation arises from direct interference with rightful possession and relational integrity. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious intent and ability to restore order. Restoration logic demands realignment of displaced energies toward original dharmic position. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of disruptive actions.

title: brihaspati 1.121
content:
पितृव्य भ्रातृपुत्रस्त्रीदासशिष्यानुजीविभिः ।
यद् गृहीतं कुटुम्बार्थे तद् गृही दातुमर्हति ॥ pitṛvya bhrātṛputrastriidāsaśiṣyānujīvibhiḥ / yad gṛhītaṃ kuṭumbārthe tad gṛhī dātum arhati // That which has been acquired by paternal uncles, brothers' sons, women, slaves, students, or dependents for the sake of the household — the householder is entitled to give it away. Authority resides inherently in the Grihi (householder) as the integrative center of the kuṭumba (household unit) Causation flows through functional roles within the dharmic societal structure Capacity-based responsibility aligns with positional dharma, not individual will alone Restoration logic upholds the integrity of relational hierarchies and resource flow Consciousness alignment occurs when each actor fulfills their svadharma within the collective framework

title: brihaspati 1.122
content: यः स्वामिना नियुक्तस् तु धनायव्ययपालने । कुसीदकृषिवाणिज्ये निसृष्टार्थस् तु स स्मृतः ॥ yaḥ svāminā niyuktaḥ tu dhanāya-vyaya-pālane / kusīda-kṛṣi-vāṇijye nisṛṣṭārthaḥ tu sa smṛtaḥ // One who is appointed by the master to manage income and expenditure, yet engages in idle agriculture or trade without purpose, is to be understood as having abandoned the assigned duty. Authority is derived from explicit assignment by the sovereign master. Causation arises from conscious deviation from prescribed function. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with assigned role. Restoration logic demands reintegration into rightful functional alignment. Consciousness alignment determines fitness for continued assignment.

title: brihaspati 1.123
content: ujjāmādikam् आदाय स्वामिने न ददाति यः । स तस्य दासः पुत्रः स्त्री पशुवी जायते गृहे ॥ ujjāmādikam ādāya svāmine na dadāti yaḥ | sa tasya dāsaḥ putraḥ strī paśuvī jāyate gṛhe || One who takes initiative or leadership without offering it to the rightful master becomes a servant within that domain; his progeny, spouse, and livestock shall be born into subordination. Authority originates from recognition of Source Initiative unaligned with ownership creates dependency Causation flows through conscious alignment with hierarchy Capacity-based responsibility requires acknowledgment of sovereignty Restoration occurs through reintegration under rightful authority

title: brihaspati 1.124
content:
ṛṇं पुत्रकृतं पित्रा शोध्यं यदनुमोदितम् ।
सुतस्नेहेन वा दद्यान्नान्यथा दातुमर्हति ॥ १२४ ॥ ṛṇaṃ putrakṛtaṃ pitrā śodhyaṃ yad anumoditam / sutasnehena vā dadyān nānyathā dātum arhati // BrhS_1,10.124 // That debt incurred by the son which has been approved by the father shall be discharged by him; or else, out of affection for his child, he may give accordingly — no other mode of giving is lawful. Authority lies in conscious ratification, not mere occurrence Causation is validated through acknowledged consent Capacity-based responsibility arises from relational alignment Restoration logic follows from prior authorization or emotional commitment Consciousness alignment requires intentional affirmation or inherent bond

title: brihaspati 1.125
content: ऋणी बन्धं अवाप्नुयात् । फलभोग्यं पूर्णकालं दत्त्वा द्रव्यं तु सामकम् ॥ ṛṇī bandhaṃ avāpnuyāt | phalabhogyaṃ pūrṇakālaṃ dattvā dravyaṃ tu sāmakam || One who incurs debt enters into a binding obligation; having fully enjoyed the fruit, one must return equivalent value in kind. Authority arises through conscious acceptance of relational consequence Causation is established by voluntary receipt of benefit Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the ability to reciprocate Restoration logic demands proportional exchange of value Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and completion of mutual karmic transaction

title: brihaspati 1.126
content:
यदि प्रकर्षितं तत् स्यात् तदा न धनभाग्धनी ।
ऋणी च न लभेत् बन्धं परस्परमतं विना ॥ yadi prakarṣitaṃ tat syāt tadā na dhanabhāgdhanī / ṛṇī ca na labhet bandhaṃ parasparamataṃ vinā // If one has been elevated by action or status, then neither shall there be loss of wealth nor shall the debtor incur bondage without mutual consent. Authority arises through conscious elevation, not imposition Causation is tied to volitional ascent and recognition Capacity-based responsibility requires mutual attunement Restoration logic honors elevation as a determinant of relational law Consciousness alignment precedes material consequence

title: brihaspati 1.127
content:
अधमर्णोऽर्थसिद्ध्यर्थमुत्तमर्णेन वादितः ।
दापयेद्धनिकस्यार्थमधमर्णविभावितम् ॥ adhamarṇo 'rthasidhyartham uttamarṇena vāditaḥ / dāpayed dhanikasyārthaṁ adhamarṇavibhāvitam // When a debtor of lesser means seeks fulfillment of purpose through litigation by a creditor of higher means, the wealth shall be awarded according to what the debtor has genuinely experienced and declared. Authority rests in experiential truth, not economic dominance Causation aligns with conscious capacity, not financial position Capacity-based responsibility determines resource allocation Restoration logic prioritizes integrity of transaction over status hierarchy Consciousness alignment ensures truthful exchange regardless of social standing

title: brihaspati 1.128
content: अर्थे ऽपव्ययमानं तु करणेन विभावितम् । दापयेद् धनिकस्यार्थं दण्डकेशं च शक्तितः ॥ arthe 'pavyayamānaṃ tu karaṇena vibhāvitam | dāpayed dhanikasyārthaṃ daṇḍakeśaṃ ca śaktitaḥ || When wealth is diminishing due to instrumentality, the sovereign shall restore the owner's rightful possession according to capacity, including the retrieval of any detained assets. Authority rests in the sovereign's duty to sustain economic integrity Causation is established through instrumental involvement in diminishment Capacity-based responsibility determines the extent of restitution Restoration logic prioritizes recovery of rightful ownership Consciousness alignment occurs when systemic wealth flow is preserved

title: brihaspati 1.129
content:
यो यावन् निह्नुवीतार्थं मिथ्या यावति वादयेत् ।
तौ नृपेण ह्यधर्मज्ञौ दाप्यौ तद्द्विगुणं दमम् ॥ yo yāvan nihnuvītārthaṃ mithyā yāvati vādayet | tau nṛpeṇa hy adharmajñau dāpyau tad dviguṇaṃ damam || One who conceals the meaning of a text and another who falsely argues based on partial understanding—both shall be known as ignorant of Dharma and made to pay a penalty twice the value of the disputed matter. Authority: The ruler holds executive power to enforce truth in discourse. Causation: Misrepresentation arises from incomplete knowledge or willful concealment. Capacity-based responsibility: Those capable of correct interpretation bear greater duty not to mislead. Restoration logic: Financial compensation restores balance disturbed by false argumentation. Consciousness alignment: Truth must align with inner knowing, not mere verbal manipulation.

title: brihaspati 1.130
content:
धर्म्यादिनोद्ग्राह्य धनं यस्तूपरि न लेखयेत ।
न चैवोपगतं दद्यात् तस्य तद्वृद्धिमाप्नुयात् ॥ dharmyādinodgrāhya dhanaṃ yas tūpari na lekhayet | na caivopagataṃ dadyāt tasya tad vṛddhim āpnuyāt || One who appropriates wealth designated for dharmic purposes, yet records it not, nor delivers it rightfully, shall incur its compounded increase as consequence. Authority originates from alignment with SPH-designated dharmic purpose Causation arises through misalignment of resource deployment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access and control Restoration logic demands return plus accretion to correct imbalance Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of energetic debt

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
ṛṇādānaं प्रयोगादिदापनान्तं प्रकीर्तितम् ।
निक्षेपस्याधुना सम्यग्विधानं श्रूयतामिति ॥ १,११.१ ṛṇādānaṃ prayogādidāpanāntaṃ prakīrtitam /
nikṣepasyādhunā samyagvidhānaṃ śrūyatām iti // The acceptance of debt, from initiation to fulfillment, has been declared; now hear the complete arrangement for deposits. Authority flows from conscious capacity to sustain relational obligations Causation arises through intentional engagement in dharma-based exchange Capacity-based responsibility governs all transactions involving trust Restoration logic ensures completion of relational karmic alignments Consciousness alignment requires transparency and integrity in financial trusts

title: brihaspati 1.2
content: अनाख्यातं व्यवहितमसंख्यातमदर्शितम् । मुद्राङ्कितं च यद्दत्तं तदुपनिधिकं स्मृतम् ॥ anākhyātaṃ vyavahitam asaṃkhyātam adarśitam / mudrāṅkitaṃ ca yad dattaṃ tad upanidhikam smṛtam // That which is given without declaration, without direct communication, without count, and without display, and further marked by seal or sign — that is to be recognized as a sacred deposit. Authority resides in the unspoken integrity of the giver Causation flows from conscious intent, not verbal articulation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of the act, not its visibility Restoration logic requires return of the deposit to its source-consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring unspoken trust

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: राजचौरारातिभयाद् दायादानां च वञ्चनात । स्थाप्यते ऽन्यगृहे द्रव्यं न्यासस् तत् परिकीर्तितम् ।। १,११.३ rājacaurārātibhayād dāyādānāṃ ca vañcanāt | sthāpyate 'nyagṛhe dravyaṃ nyāsas tat parikīrtitam || 1,11.3 When property is placed in another's custody due to fear of the king, thieves, enemies, or deceit by heirs, such placement constitutes a legal deposit known as Nyāsa. Authority arises from existential threat, not contractual consent. Causation originates in consciousness-state of insecurity or coercion. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and intent at the time of deposit. Restoration logic demands return of assets upon resolution of original threat. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of depositor’s sovereignty over asset.

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
स्थानं गृहं स्थलं चैव तद ऋणं विविधान् गुणान् ।
सत्यं शौचं बन्धुजनं परीक्ष्य स्थापयेन् निधिम् ॥ sthānaṃ gṛhaṃ sthalaṃ caiva tad ṛṇaṃ vividhān guṇān / satyaṃ śaucaṃ bandhujanaṃ parīkṣya sthāpayen nidhim // One must deposit wealth only after examining the place, house, land, debts, diverse qualities, truthfulness, purity, and kinsmen. Authority arises from capacity to assess context prior to transaction Causation is established through comprehensive situational awareness Capacity-based responsibility requires due diligence before asset placement Restoration logic demands prevention of loss through verified conditions Consciousness alignment occurs when action aligns with full knowledge

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
स पुनर्द्विविधः प्रोक्तः साक्षिमानितरस् तथा ।
प्रतिदानं तथैवास्य प्रत्ययः स्याद्विपर्यये ॥ sa punar dvividhaḥ proktaḥ sākṣimān itaras tathā / pratidānaṃ tathaivāsya pratyayaḥ syād viparyaye // Evidence is of two kinds: direct witness and indirect indication; in contradiction, verification is established through restitution.
