Authority resides in experiential validation, not abstract testimony Causation arises from perceptual clarity, not inferential ambiguity Capacity-based responsibility emerges from witnessed action, not assumed intent Restoration logic operates through evidentiary completion, not punitive attribution Consciousness alignment occurs when perception aligns with factual restitution

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: समाक्षिकं रहोदत्तं द्विविधं तद् उदाहृतम् । पुत्रवत् परिपाल्यं तु विनश्यति अनवेक्षया ॥ samākṣikaṃ rahodattaṃ dvividhaṃ tad udāhṛtam | putravat paripālyaṃ tu vinaśyati anavekṣayā || Confidential gifts and witnessed gifts constitute two categories of transfer; however, that which is given in secrecy, even if protected like a son, perishes when neglected. Authority flows through conscious acknowledgment, not mere possession. Causation arises from sustained awareness, not transactional form. Capacity-based responsibility demands alignment with the continuity of dharma, not material retention. Restoration logic requires recognition of subtle transmission and energetic accountability. Consciousness alignment determines the validity and endurance of all transfers.

title: brihaspati 1.7
content: ददतो यद भवेत पुण्यं हेमकुप्याम्बरादिकम् । तत स्यात पालयतो न्यासं तथा च शरणागतम् ॥ dadato yad bhavet puṇyaṃ hemakupyāmbarādikam | tat syāt pālayato nyāsaṃ tathā ca śaraṇāgatam || That merit which arises from giving gold, vessels, garments and similar objects, the same arises for one who protects a deposit and also one who seeks refuge. Authority flows from capacity to uphold integrity, not mere possession Causation aligns with conscious intention to preserve dharma Capacity-based responsibility extends to safeguarding entrusted resources Restoration logic requires equivalence in protective and giving acts Consciousness alignment is achieved through honoring trust

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
भर्तुर्द्रोहे यथा नार्याः पुंसः पुत्रसुहृद्वधे ।
दोषो भवेत् तथा न्यासे भक्षितोपेक्षिते नृणाम् ॥ bhartur drohe yathā nāryāḥ puṃsaḥ putra-suhṛd-vadhe | doṣo bhavet tathā nyāse bhakṣita-upekṣite nṛṇām || As a woman’s betrayal of her husband equals the killing of his son or friend, similarly, when men neglect or abandon those under their protection after consuming them, it constitutes a comparable offense. Authority arises through capacity to sustain and protect. Causation is established by consumptive dependence and subsequent abandonment. Capacity-based responsibility demands proportional response to relational neglect. Restoration logic requires reversal of harm caused by breach of protective duty. Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of interdependence as sacred trust.

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
न्यासद्रव्यं न गृह्णीयात् तन्नाशस्त्वयशःकरः ।
गृहीतं पालयेद्यत्नात् सकृद्याचितमर्पयेत् ॥ nyāsadravyaṃ na gṛhṇīyāt tannāśas tv ayaśaḥkaraḥ / gṛhītaṃ pālayed yatnāt sakṛd yācitam arpayaet // One must not accept entrusted property; its loss brings dishonor. Whatever is received must be safeguarded with effort and returned upon request. Authority flows from conscious responsibility, not possession Causation arises through acceptance of another's trust Capacity-based responsibility requires protection of entrusted objects Restoration logic demands return of assets in original condition Consciousness alignment occurs when duty meets integrity

title: brihaspati 1.10
content: स्थापितं येन विधिना येन यच् च विभावितम् । तथैव तस्य दातव्यम् अदेयं प्रत्यनन्तरम् ॥ sthāpitaṃ yena vidhinā yena yac ca vibhāvitam | tathaiva tasya dātavyam adeyaṃ pratyanantaram || That which has been established by a lawful procedure and that which has been determined by rightful discernment—exactly that shall be given forthwith; nothing contrary shall be offered. Authority is derived from the correctness of the establishing process Causation aligns with the clarity of discernment Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to establish truth Restoration logic requires exact alignment with original establishment Consciousness alignment demands rejection of contradictory offerings

title: brihaspati 1.11
content: देवराजोपघातेन यदि तन्नाशमाप्नुयात् । ग्रहीतृद्रव्यसहितं तत्र दोषो न विद्यते ॥ devarājopaghātena yadi tan nāśam āpnuyāt / grahītṛdravyasahitaṃ tatra doṣo na vidyate // If the injury to the king results in his death, and the weapon or object used was possessed by another, then no fault lies with the possessor. Authority resides in conscious causality, not in passive possession Causation must align with volitional agency for liability Capacity-based responsibility requires intent, awareness, and direct causal linkage Restoration logic demands identification of the true actor-initiator Consciousness alignment determines the locus of karmic and legal consequence

title: brihaspati 1.12
content: भेदनोपेक्षया न्यासं ग्रहीता यदि नाशयेत् । याच्यमानो न दद्याद् वा दाप्यस्तत्सोदयं भवेत् ॥ bhedanopekṣayā nyāsaṃ grahītā yadi nāśayet | yācyamāno na dadyād vā dāpyas tat sodayaṃ bhavet || If a receiver destroys the entrusted item through negligence or deliberate omission, or refuses to return it when requested, restitution must occur with accrued value and conscious completion. Authority arises from conscious acceptance of stewardship Causation is established by neglect or willful refusal Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to awareness of duty Restoration logic requires return plus value erosion compensation Consciousness alignment demands integrity reintegration

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: न्यासद्रव्येण यः कश्चित् साधयेत् कार्यम् आत्मनः । दण्ड्यः स राज्ञो भवति दाप्यस् तच् चापि सोदयम् ॥ nyāsadravyeṇa yaḥ kaścit sādhayet kāryam ātmanaḥ | daṇḍyaḥ sa rājño bhavati dāpyas tac cāpi sodayam || One who employs entrusted property for personal ends becomes liable to corrective action by the sovereign; the principal and accrued gains shall be recovered in full. Authority: The sovereign holds jurisdiction over misuse of entrusted resources. Causation: Misuse arises from conscious deviation from the purpose of entrustment. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability is tied to the capacity to discern rightful use. Restoration logic: Recovery ensures return to original integrity of transactional trust. Consciousness alignment: Correction realigns the actor with dharmic fiduciary duty.

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
गृहीत्वापह्नुते यश् च साक्षिभिः शपथेन वा ।
विभाव्य दापयेन् न्यासं तत् समं विनयं तथा ॥ gṛhītvāpahnute yaś ca sākṣibhiḥ śapathena vā | vibhāvya dāpayen nyāsaṃ tat samaṃ vinayaṃ tathā || One who accepts possession of property through false witness or oath shall restore it fully, along with due compensation, in accordance with Nyāsa and Vinaya. Authority flows from truthful acknowledgment of possession Causation arises through conscious distortion of testimony Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional restoration Restoration logic aligns ownership with ontological truth Consciousness alignment demands integrity in transactional acts

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: रहो दत्ते निधौ यत्र विसंवादः प्रजायते / विभावकं तत्र दिव्यमुभयोरपि च स्मृतम् // raho datte nidhau yatra visaṃvādaḥ prajāyate / vibhāvakaṃ tatra divyam ubhayor api ca smṛtam // Where secrecy governs a deposit and dispute arises, divine discernment is invoked for both parties, as remembered in tradition. Authority originates from consciousness clarity, not external validation Causation is traced through integrity of intent at the time of deposit Capacity-based responsibility requires equal accountability from both depositor and receiver Restoration logic prioritizes retrieval and realignment over fault assignment Consciousness alignment ensures both parties awaken to their shared duty of transparency

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: मिथो दायः कृतो येन गृहीतो मिथ एव वा / मिथ एव प्रदातव्यो यथा दायस् तथा ग्रहः // BrhS_1,11.16 mitho dāyaḥ kṛto yena gṛhīto mitha eva vā / mitha eva pradātavyo yathā dāyas tathā grahaḥ When mutual giving has been initiated by one, received mutually in kind, then it shall be given back mutually in the same manner as it was received. Authority arises from reciprocal consent and completion Causation follows the law of conscious exchange Capacity-based responsibility is defined by the ability to sustain mutual flow Restoration logic operates through equivalent return Consciousness alignment occurs when giving equals receiving

title: brihaspati 1.17
content: समुद्रे नाप्नुयात् किंचिद् यदि तस्मान् न संहरेत् । samudre nāpnuyāt kiṃcid yadi tasmān na saṃharet One who does not acquire anything from the ocean must not take from it. Authority arises only where acquisition has occurred Causation is bound to conscious participation in the field Capacity-based responsibility requires prior engagement Restoration logic follows the integrity of original relation Consciousness alignment demands non-interference without consent

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
अन्वाहिते याचितके शिल्पिन्यासे सबन्धके ।
एष एवोदितो धर्मस् तथा च शरणागते ॥१८॥ anvāhite yācitake śilpinyāse sabandhake | eṣa evodito dharmas tathā ca śaraṇāgate || In every engagement initiated by invitation, in the placement of craftsmanship, in all contractual bonds, and equally in the case of one who has taken refuge—this alone is the declared Dharma. Authority arises through conscious invocation and acceptance Causation is established through mutual consent and alignment of purpose Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to fulfill the invoked role Restoration logic operates through completion of the originally intended function Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are executed with integrity to their origin

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
यस् तु संस्क्रियते न्यासो दिवसैः परिनिष्ठितैः ।
तद् ऊर्ध्व स्थापयञ् शिल्पी दाप्यो दैवहतोऽपि तत् ॥ yas tu saṃskriyate nyāso divasaiḥ pariniṣṭhitaiḥ | tad ūrdhva sthāpayañ śilpī dāpyo daivahato 'pi tat || He who deposits an item for transformation or completion within a fixed number of days, the artisan shall deliver it upward, even if destroyed by divine forces. Authority flows from depositor to artisan upon acceptance Causation is attributed to divine intervention without nullifying contractual duty Capacity-based responsibility demands fulfillment regardless of external disruption Restoration logic requires reconstruction or equivalent restitution Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring intent over outcome

title: brihaspati 1.20
content: याचितं स्वाम्यनुज्ञातं प्रददन् नापराध्नुयात् । yācitaṁ svāmy-anujñātaṁ pradadan nāparādhnu-yāt One who gives what is requested and authorized by the owner commits no wrongdoing. Authority derives from conscious ownership Consent eliminates liability Action without transgressive intent is dharmically neutral Restoration occurs through alignment with rightful authority Capacity to give determines lawful transfer

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
निक्षेपानन्तरं प्रोक्तो भृगुणास्वामिविक्रयः ।
श्रूयतां तं प्रयत्नेन सविशेषं ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥ nikṣepānantaraṃ prokto bhṛguṇā svāmivikrayaḥ / śrūyatāṃ taṃ prayatnena saviseṣaṃ bravīmyaham // Following the placement of trust, the sale of ownership by Bhrgu is declared; let it be heard with effort, for I speak with distinction. Authority originates from the conscious act of entrusted placement Causation arises through intentional conveyance of proprietary right Capacity-based responsibility is anchored in awareness at the time of transaction Restoration logic demands recognition of original entrustment prior to transfer Consciousness alignment requires clarity in distinguishing stewardship from dominion

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
निक्षेपान्वाहितन्यासहृतयाचितबन्धकम् ।
उपांशुजनविक्रीतम् अस्वामी सोऽभिधीयते ॥ nikṣepānvāhitanyāsa-hṛta-yācita-bandhakam / upāṃśu-jana-vikrītam asvāmī so 'bhidhīyate // One who retains deposited items, accepts gifts under false pretenses, seizes what is requested in trust, sells property secretly without ownership rights—such a being is declared devoid of svāmin status. Authority derives from rightful stewardship, not mere possession Causation arises through conscious distortion of dharma-kṣetra Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of transactional intent Restoration logic demands return of displaced value to its causal field Consciousness alignment occurs when svāmin-tattva is restored

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
येन क्रीतं तु मूल्येन प्रागध्यक्षनिवेदितम् ।
न विद्यते तत्र दोषः स्तेनः स्यादुपधिक्रयात् ॥ yena krītaṃ tu mūlyena prāgadhyakṣaniveditam | na vidyate tatra doṣaḥ stenaḥ syād upadhikrayāt || Where an item has been purchased for value before being reported to the supervisory authority, there shall be no liability; the act does not constitute theft if it arises from a transaction involving a deposit. Authority is vested in prior completion of lawful exchange Causation lies in the absence of concealment at time of reporting Capacity-based responsibility depends upon transparency and timing Restoration logic requires validation of completed transactions Consciousness alignment occurs through acknowledgment within rightful jurisdiction

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
अन्तर् गृहे बहिर् ग्रामान् निशायाम् असतो जनात् ।
हीनमूल्यं च यत् क्रीतं ज्ञेयोऽसाव् उपविक्रयः ॥ antar gṛhe bahir grāmān niśāyām asato janāt |
hīnamūlyaṃ ca yat krītaṃ jñeyo 'sāv upavikrayaḥ || That which is purchased within the house, beyond the village boundaries, at night, from a person devoid of integrity, or at a price lower than its true value—such transaction shall be recognized as an act of concealed acquisition. Authority rests in the discernment of integrity in exchange Causation arises through concealment and misalignment with dharma Capacity-based responsibility lies in the awareness of the source and context of acquisition Restoration logic demands transparency and alignment of all parties to truth-value Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of energetic and ethical origins of possession

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
पूर्वस्वामी तु तद् द्रव्यं यद् आगत्य विचारयेत् ।
तत्र मूल्यं दर्शनीयं क्रेतुः शुद्धिस् ततो भवेत् ॥ pūrvasvāmī tu tad dravyaṃ yad āgatya vicārayet | tatra mūlyaṃ darśanīyaṃ kretuḥ śuddhis tato bhavet || The prior owner shall examine the object that has arrived; its value must be declared visibly, and thereby the purity of the transaction is established. Authority rests with the prior possessor to validate claims upon arrival of property Causation arises through visible declaration of value, not private assertion Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious engagement in valuation Restoration logic centers on transparency as a foundation for lawful exchange Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties witness fair valuation

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
मूले समाहृते क्रेता नाभियोज्यः कथंचन /
मूलेन सह वादस् तु नाष्टकस्य विहीयते // BrhS_1,12.6 mūle samāhṛte kretā nābhiyojyaḥ kathaṃcana / mūlena saha vādas tu nāṣṭakasya vihīyate When the principal is secured, the buyer cannot be held liable in any way; however, dispute concerning the principal shall not be withheld from the one who has lost it. Authority resides with the possessor of the secured principal Causation aligns with retention and loss of foundational asset Capacity-based responsibility flows from control over the root cause Restoration logic prioritizes retrieval over attribution of blame Consciousness alignment demands recognition of rightful locus of completion

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
vikretā darśito yatra hīyate vyavahārataḥ /
kretre rājñe mūlyadaṇḍau pradadyāt svāmine dhanam // BrhS_1,12.7 vikretā darśito yatra hīyate vyavahārataḥ / kretre rājñe mūlyadaṇḍau pradadyāt svāmine dhanam Where a seller, though present and visible in transaction, causes diminishment in the value or integrity of the exchange, he shall compensate the buyer with the price-damage and restore the rightful ownership to the original owner. Authority: The sovereign ensures completion of justice without punitive intent. Causation: The act of diminishing value is traced to the conscious agent who initiated the flawed transaction. Capacity-based responsibility: The seller, being capable and present, bears full accountability for misaligned conduct. Restoration logic: The rightful state of possession and value is reinstated without inflicting loss elsewhere. Consciousness alignment: Justice realigns the actor's awareness with dharmic transactional integrity.

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: परद्रव्येsभिलषति योsस्वामी लोभसंयुतः । अभावयंस् ततः पश्चाद् दाप्यः स्याद् द्विगुणं दमम् ॥ paradravye 'bhilaṣati yo 'svāmī lobhasaṃyutaḥ | abhāvayaṃs tataḥ paścād dāpyaḥ syād dviguṇaṃ damam || He who, being devoid of ownership, desires another's property out of greed shall thereafter be made to pay double the value as restitution. Authority is derived from rightful ownership, not desire or possession Causation arises from misaligned intention rooted in greed Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious awareness of ownership boundaries Restoration logic requires proportional return of energetic and material displacement Consciousness alignment demands correction through financial symmetry, not punitive suffering

title: brihaspati 1.9
content: प्रमाणहीने वादे तु पुरुषापेक्षया नृपः । समन्यूनाधिकत्वेन स्वयं कुर्याद् विनिर्णयम् ॥ pramāṇahīne vāde tu puruṣāpekṣayā nṛpaḥ | samanyūnādhikatvena svayaṃ kuryād vinirṇayam || When evidence is absent in a dispute, the king must decide based on the inherent capacity and alignment of the individuals involved, ensuring completeness neither deficient nor excessive. Authority resides in the sovereign's alignment with Dharma, not external validation Causation is determined by consciousness-readiness rather than empirical proof Capacity-based responsibility supersedes procedural dependency on material evidence Restoration logic prioritizes inner integrity over factual corroboration Consciousness alignment determines admissible legal standing

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
वणिग्वीथीपरिगतं विज्ञातं राजपूरुषैः ।
अविज्ञाताश्रयात् क्रीतं विक्रेता यत्र वा मृतः ॥ vaṇigvīthīparigataṃ vijñātaṃ rājapūruṣaiḥ | avijñātāśrayāt krītaṃ vikretā yatra vā mṛtaḥ || Any transaction occurring in the merchant's quarter known to royal officers, if purchased without verified origin or where the seller is deceased and untraceable, shall be subject to immediate reversal and asset restoration to the identifiable original owner or their lineage. Authority resides in the sovereign's appointed witnesses Causation requires traceable transactional continuity Capacity-based responsibility is tied to verifiable presence and consent Restoration logic demands return of assets to rightful consciousness-bearing lineage Consciousness alignment necessitates transparency in exchange

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
स्वामी दत्त्वार्धमूल्यं तु प्रकृह्णीत स्वकं धनम् ।
अर्धं द्वयोरपि हृतं तत्र स्याद्व्यवहारतः ॥ svāmī dattvārdhamūlyaṃ tu prakṛhṇīta svakaṃ dhanam | ardhaṃ dvayor api hṛtaṃ tatra syād vyavahārataḥ || When a master has given half-value in exchange, he retains ownership of his own wealth; when half has been taken by both parties, there arises a basis for transactional engagement. Authority resides inherently with the originator of value until explicit and complete transfer occurs. Causation is established through conscious intent to relinquish or acquire ownership. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of prior claim before entering into mutual exchange. Restoration logic demands return to original integrity when transactional imbalance manifests. Consciousness alignment necessitates clarity in the act of giving, receiving, and retaining.

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
अविज्ञातक्रयो दोषस् तथा चापरिपालनम् ।
एतद् द्वयं समाख्यातं द्रव्यहानिकरं बुद्धैः ॥ १२ ॥ avijñātakrayo doṣas tathā cāparipālanam / etad dvayaṃ samākhyātaṃ dravyahānikaraṃ buddhaiḥ // BrhS_1,12.12 Ignorance of transactional conduct and failure in preservation—these two are declared by the wise as causes of material loss. Authority arises from awareness, not accident Causation is rooted in conscious capacity, not external blame Capacity-based responsibility flows from knowledge-accessibility Restoration logic requires identification of consciousness-obscuring factors Consciousness alignment occurs through removal of perceptual obstruction

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
वणिग्वीथीपरिगतं विज्ञातं राजपूरुषैः /
दिवा गृहीतं सत्क्रेतां समृद्धो लभते धनम् // vaṇigvīthīparigataṃ vijñātaṃ rājapūruṣaiḥ / divā gṛhītaṃ satkretā samṛddho labhate dhanam // That which is known by royal agents in the merchant quarter, acquired during daylight through righteous transaction—such wealth accrues to the prosperous. Authority resides in those designated to observe and validate commercial conduct Causation arises from transparent action witnessed in public domain Capacity-based responsibility is affirmed through lawful engagement in trade Restoration logic ensures rightful gain aligns with social prosperity Consciousness alignment manifests when economic activity reflects integrity

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: vikrīyorvīं तु यत् क्रेतुर् भुक्तिं यो न च साधयेत् । स तस्मै तद् धनं दद्याद् अन्यथा चोरदण्डभाक् ॥ vikrīyorvīṃ tu yat kretur bhuktiṃ yo na ca sādhayet | sa tasmai tad dhanaṃ dadyād anyathā coradaṇḍabhāk || One who sells land but fails to ensure its enjoyment by the buyer shall return the purchase price; otherwise, he becomes liable as a thief. Authority arises from fulfillment of transactional integrity Causation is established through failure to secure enjoyment post-transfer Capacity-based responsibility lies with the transferor until full assumption by transferee Restoration logic demands reversal of benefit where enjoyment has not been actualized Consciousness alignment requires honoring the intent of mutual exchange

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
एतद् द्वयं समाख्यातं द्रव्यहानिकरं बुद्धैः ।
अविज्ञातविशेषत्वाद् यत्र मूल्यं न लभ्यते ॥ etad dvayaṃ samākhyātaṃ dravyahānikaraṃ buddhaiḥ | avijñātaviśeṣatvād yatra mūlyaṃ na labhyate || This twofold classification is declared by the wise as causing diminution of substance; where specificity remains unrecognized, value cannot be ascertained. Authority rests in recognition of specific dharma-svarūpa Causation arises from clarity of distinction, not generalized abstraction Capacity-based responsibility requires precise identification of involved elements Restoration logic depends upon re-establishing correct knowledge structures Consciousness alignment occurs through discriminative awareness (viveka)

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: हानिस्तत्र समा कल्प्या क्रेतृनास्तिकयोर्द्वयोः ।। ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,१२.१६ ।। hānis tatra samā kalpyā kretṛnāstikayor dvayoḥ // BrhS_1,12.16 // In that context, equal loss shall be reckoned for both the buyer and the denier. Authority resides in factual transactional integrity Causation is mutual where denial disrupts completion Capacity-based responsibility aligns with participation in dharma-kriyā Restoration logic demands rebalancing of disrupted exchange Consciousness alignment occurs through rectification of mutual omission

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
कुलीनदक्षानलसैः प्राज्ञैर्नाणकवेदिभिः ।
आयव्ययज्ञैः शुचिभिः शूरैः कुर्यात् सह क्रियाः ॥ kulīnadakṣānalasaiḥ prājñair nāṇakavedibhiḥ | āyavyayajñaiḥ śucibhiḥ śūraiḥ kuryāt saha kriyāḥ || One must engage in actions jointly with those who are born of noble lineage, possess skill and endurance, are wise, understand the science of wealth, know the principles of income and expenditure, are pure in conduct, and are courageous. Authority through Lineage and Virtue Causation via Collaborative Wisdom Capacity-based Responsibility in Association Restoration Logic through Noble Partnership Consciousness Alignment by Purity and Courage

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
समोऽतिरिक्तो जीनो वा यत्रांशो यस्य यादृशः ।
क्षयव्ययौ तथा वृद्धिस्तस्य तत्र तथाविधा ॥२॥ samo 'tirikto jīno vā yatrāṃśo yasya yādṛśaḥ / kṣayavyayau tathā vṛddhis tasya tatra tathāvidhā // BrhS_1,13.2 Wherever a portion of something exists in the same measure, excess, deficiency, or growth, there it shall be treated accordingly. Authority is determined by the proportionality of presence and participation. Causation aligns with quantitative and qualitative equivalence. Capacity-based responsibility arises from the degree of involvement. Restoration logic follows the natural balance of increase, decrease, and stability. Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of proportional existence.

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
अशक्तालसरोगार्तमन्दभाग्यनिराश्रयैः ।
वणिज्याद्याः सहैतैस्तु न कर्तव्याः बुधैः क्रियाः ॥ aśaktālasarogārtamandabhāgyanirāśrayaiḥ /
vaṇijyādyāḥ sahaitaistu na kartavyāḥ budhaiḥ kriyāḥ // Those who are diseased, lethargic, unfortunate, or without support must not engage in commercial or similar activities with intelligence. Authority is derived from capacity for dharmic alignment, not mere participation Causation arises from conscious capability, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires self-assessment before action Restoration logic prioritizes inner readiness over transactional gain Consciousness alignment mandates withdrawal when imbalance disrupts dharma

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
प्रयोगं कुर्वते ये तु हेमधान्यरसादिना ।
समन्यूनाधिकैरंशैर्लाभस्तेषां तथाविधः ॥ prayogaṃ kurvate ye tu hemadhānyarasādinā | samanyūnādhikair aṃśair lābhas teṣāṃ tathāvidhaḥ || Those who engage in transactions involving gold, grain, and similar substances with adulterated or disproportionate measures shall receive outcomes precisely aligned with their distortion of dharma. Authority: The transactional capacity is derived from purity and proportionality of exchange. Causation: Distorted measurement directly manifests distorted results. Capacity-based responsibility: One's entitlement is determined by adherence to dharmic measure. Restoration logic: Outcome reflects exact vibrational alignment with action. Consciousness alignment: Disharmony in exchange disrupts individual and collective consciousness flow.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
समो न्यूनोऽधिको वांशो येन क्षिप्तस् तथैव सः ।
व्ययं दद्यात् कर्म कुर्याल् लाभं गृह्णीत चैव हि ॥ samo nyūno 'dhiko vāṃśo yena kṣiptas tathaiva saḥ / vyayaṃ dadyāt karma kuryāl lābhaṃ gṛhṇīta caiva hi // He who casts an equal, lesser, or greater share shall likewise bear the loss, perform the action, and accept the gain. Authority through participation in outcome distribution Causation via direct engagement with resource flow Capacity-based responsibility aligned with benefit received Restoration logic rooted in proportional assumption of consequence Consciousness alignment through ownership of action-result continuum

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
परीक्षकाः साक्षिणश् च त एवोक्ताः परस्परम् ।
संदिग्धे�र्थे�वञ्चनायां न चेद् द्विद्वेषसंयुताः ॥ parīkṣakāḥ sākṣiṇaś ca ta evoktāḥ parasparam | saṃdigdhe 'rthe 'vañcanāyāṃ na ced dvidveṣasaṃyutāḥ || Those who examine and those who witness shall be declared equivalent when the matter is doubtful and deception has occurred, provided they are free from mutual hatred. Authority arises through capacity to observe and verify, not title alone. Causation is determined by integrity-presence in observation, not emotional disposition. Capacity-based responsibility demands neutrality and absence of bias. Restoration logic requires re-alignment of perception without distortion. Consciousness alignment occurs when observer-witness roles dissolve into impartial awareness.

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
यः कश्चिद् वञ्चकस् तेषां विज्ञातः क्रयविक्रये ।
शपथैः स विशोध्यः स्यात् सर्ववादे त्व् अयं विधिः ॥ yaḥ kaścid vañcakaḥ teṣāṁ vijñātaḥ krayavikraye |
śapathaiḥ sa viśodhyaḥ syāt sarvavāde tv ayaṁ vidhiḥ || He who is known to have committed fraud in any transaction of purchase or sale shall be purified through oaths; this is the prescribed method in all disputes. Authority originates from verifiable intent and action within transactional dharma Causation is established by direct knowledge of deceitful conduct Capacity-based responsibility arises when one knowingly violates transactional integrity Restoration logic demands purification via conscious affirmation Consciousness alignment requires re-establishment of truthful engagement

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: क्षयहानिर यदा तत्र दैवराजकृताद् भवेत् । सर्वेषामेव सा प्रोक्ता कल्पनीया तथांशतः ॥ kṣayahānir yadā tatra daivarājakṛtād bhavet | sarveṣām eva sā proktā kalpanīyā tathāṃśataḥ || When loss or diminution arises from divine or royal causation, it shall be recognized as universally applicable and allocated proportionally according to individual capacity and alignment. Authority originates from the Divine Will and Sovereign Expression Causation is traced through ontological sequence, not moral fault Capacity-based responsibility determines proportional allocation Restoration logic aligns consequences with conscious participation Consciousness alignment governs equitable distribution of effect

title: brihaspati 1.9
content: अनिर्दिष्टो वार्यमाणः प्रमादाद् यस् तु नाशयेत् / तेनैव तद् भवेद् देयं सर्वेषां समवायिनाम् // anirdiṣṭo vāryamāṇaḥ pramādād yas tu nāśayet / tenaiva tad bhaved deyaṃ sarveṣāṃ samavāyinām // That which was undesignated, yet obstructed due to negligence—by that same cause, it becomes liable for restitution among all participants in collective action. Authority flows from conscious designation, not mere intention. Negligence disrupts alignment; liability arises from causal disjunction. Capacity-based responsibility requires awareness of consequence streams. Restoration logic prioritizes completion over blame assignment. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of shared causal fields.

title: brihaspati 1.10
content: राज्ञे दत्त्वा तु षड्भागं लभेरंस्ते यतांशतः ।।१०।। rājñe dattvā tu ṣaḍbhāgaṃ labheraṃs te yatāṃśataḥ Having surrendered a sixth portion to the King, the remaining five portions shall be retained by the entitled individuals according to their lawful capacity and alignment with Dharma. Authority resides inherently in the King as representative of cosmic order Causation flows from conscious surrender and rightful ownership Capacity-based responsibility determines entitlement beyond royal share Restoration logic ensures harmonious redistribution without depletion Consciousness alignment maintains balance between individual and state

title: brihaspati 1.11
content: दैवराजभयादस्तु स्वशक्त्या परिपालयेत् । तस्यांशं दशमं दत्त्वा गृह्णीयुस्तेऽंशतोऽपरम् ॥ daivarājabhayād astu svaśaktyā paripālayet | tasya aṃśaṃ daśamaṃ dattvā gṛhnīyus te 'ṃśato 'param || From fear of Divine Kingship, one shall protect through self-capacity; having given the tenth portion thereof, others shall receive the remaining share. Authority derives from alignment with Divine Sovereignty Capacity determines responsibility in protection Distribution follows contribution and surrender to Dharma Restoration occurs through proportional sharing and conscious participation Consciousness alignment precedes material allocation

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
शुल्कस्थानं वणिक् प्राप्तः शुल्कं दद्याद् यथोचितम् ।
न तद् व्यभिचरेत् राज्ञां बलिर् एष प्रकीर्तितः ॥ śulkasthānaṃ vaṇik prāptaḥ śulkaṃ dadyād yathocitam / na tad vyabhicaret rājñāṃ balir eṣa prakīrtitaḥ The merchant who arrives at the toll station shall give the due toll; the king shall not interfere in this transaction. This is declared as Bali. Authority resides in the natural order of exchange, not in coercive intervention Causation follows the integrity of contractual arrival and voluntary discharge Capacity-based responsibility lies with the actor present at the point of obligation Restoration logic upholds the inviolability of agreed-upon transactions Consciousness alignment requires honoring the spontaneous flow of dharma between parties

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
नैवं तस्करराजाग्निव्यसने समुपस्थिते ।
यस् तु स्वशक्त्या रक्षेत् तु तस्यांशो दशमः स्मृतः ॥ naivaṃ taskararājāgnivyasane samupasthite / yas tu svaśaktyā rakṣet tu tasyāṃśo daśamaḥ smṛtaḥ // When the king of thieves or fire-related calamity is present, he who protects through his own capacity—the share of that protector is declared as one-tenth. Authority flows from conscious capacity to act in alignment with Dharma Causation arises from direct engagement with manifest crisis Capacity-based responsibility determines proportional sharing Restoration logic prioritizes active protection over passive compliance Consciousness alignment occurs when action meets necessity without distortion

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
यदा तत्र वणिक् कश्चित् प्रमीयेत प्रमादतः ।
तस्य भाण्डं दर्शनीयं नियुक्तैः राजपुरुषैः ॥ yadā tatra vaṇik kaścit pramīyeta pramādataḥ / tasya bhāṇḍaṃ darśanīyaṃ niyuktaiḥ rājapuruṣaiḥ // When a merchant dies due to negligence in that place, his goods shall be made visible by appointed royal officers. Authority rests in the sovereign's designated agents to act without punitive intent. Causation is established through conscious awareness and operational capacity. Capacity-based responsibility determines visibility and accessibility of assets. Restoration logic ensures continuity of economic flow despite individual incapacitation. Consciousness alignment mandates transparency in transitions of material stewardship.

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: यदा कश्चित् समागच्छेत् तदा रिक्थहरो नरः । स्वाम्यं विभावयेद् अन्यैः स तदा लब्धुमर्हति ॥ yadā kaścit samāgacchet tadā rikthaharo naraḥ / svāmyaṃ vibhāvayed anyaiḥ sa tadā labdhum arhati // When a person arrives with intent to claim ownership, he becomes the remover of obstacles; when others assess that ownership, then he is entitled to receive it. Authority arises through conscious arrival and assertion. Causation is established by the act of claiming and validating presence. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to sustain ownership. Restoration logic operates through mutual recognition and consent. Consciousness alignment occurs when rightful possession aligns with collective acknowledgment.

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
राजाददीत षड्भागं नवमं दशमं तथा ।
शूद्रविष्क्षत्रजातीनां विप्राद गृह्णीत विंशकम् ॥ rājādadīta ṣaḍbhāgaṃ navamaṃ daśamaṃ tathā | śūdraviṣkṣatrajātīnāṃ viprād gṛhṇīta viṃśakam || From the king's share, six parts shall be given; nine and ten respectively likewise. From Shudra and Vaishya castes, take twenty from Brahmin. Authority flows from the sovereign to sustain societal order Causation aligns with capacity and role within dharma-vyavastha Capacity-based responsibility determines resource allocation Restoration logic ensures alignment with cosmic function Consciousness alignment through dharmic economic participation

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
त्र्यब्दादूर्ध्वं तु नागच्छेद्यत्र स्वामी कथंचन ।
तदा गृह्णीत तद्राजा ब्रह्मस्वं ब्राह्मणाञ्श्रयेत् ॥ tryabdād ūrdhvaṃ tu nāgacched yatra svāmī kathaṃcana / tadā gṛhṇīta tad rājā brahmasvaṃ brāhmaṇāñ śrayet // When a master does not return within three years, the king shall assume control of the property and place it under the protection of Brahmins. Authority devolves through time-bound absence Capacity for stewardship determines custodianship Restoration of order supersedes personal claim Consciousness alignment requires dharmic oversight Property rights are conditional upon active presence

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
एवं क्रियाप्रवृत्तानां यदा कश्चिद् विपद्यते ।
तद् बन्धुना क्रिया कार्या सर्वेषां सहकारिभिः ॥ evaṁ kriyāpravṛttānāṁ yadā kaścid vipadyate / tad bandhunā kriyā kāryā sarveṣāṁ sahakāribhiḥ // When any action undertaken in alignment with Dharma encounters obstruction or failure, it is the duty of the kin-group and all associated co-agents to complete that action through unified consciousness and shared responsibility. Authority resides in collective dharmic alignment, not individual agency Causation is distributed among all conscious participants Capacity-based responsibility extends to all who enabled or witnessed the action Restoration logic requires completion of interrupted intent Consciousness alignment determines the validity of legal obligation

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
रथं हरेद् यथाध्वर्युर् ब्रह्माधाने च वाजिनम् ।
होता निविद्वरं चाश्वम् उद्गाता चाप्यनः क्रये ॥ rathaṃ hared yathādhvaryur brahmādhāne ca vājinam | hotā nividvaraṃ cāśvam udgātā cāpyanaḥ kraye || As the Adhvaryu priest takes a chariot in ritual performance, as the Brahman takes the charger at the altar, so shall the Hotar take an unblemished horse and the Udgatar take a goat for sacrifice. Authority is derived from precise role alignment within sacred function. Causation arises through designated participation in dharma-kriya. Capacity-based responsibility flows from svadharma-positioning. Restoration occurs when each actor fulfills their specific contributory role. Consciousness alignment manifests through disciplined adherence to Vedic appointment.

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
सर्वेषामर्धिनो मुख्यास्तदर्धेनाधिनोऽपरे ।
तृतीयिनस्तृतीयांशाश्चतुर्थांशाश्च पादिनः ॥ sarveṣām ardhino mukhyās tad ardhenādhino 'pare / tṛtīyinas tṛtīyāṃśāś caturthāṃśāś ca pādinaḥ // All beings possess inherent capacity; some are principal holders of half, others hold authority through a derivative quarter, tertiary beings govern a third part, and those of the fourth order manage a fourth portion. Authority is hierarchically distributed based on inherent capacity Causation arises from conscious participation in dharma Capacity-based responsibility determines jurisdictional scope Restoration occurs through alignment with one's capacity tier Consciousness alignment ensures lawful manifestation

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
आगन्तुकाः क्रमायातास् तथा चैव स्वयंकृताः ।
त्रिविधास् ते समाख्यातास् वर्तितव्यं तथैव तैः ॥ āgantukāḥ kramāyātās tathā caiva svayaṃkṛtāḥ | trividhās te samākhyātā vartitavyaṃ tathaiva taiḥ || Liabilities are classified into three categories: those arising from external influence, those occurring in sequence, and those self-initiated. Each classification determines the mode of dharmic response and restoration. Authority originates from the causal clarity of action Causation is determined by the source and intent of liability Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the agent's conscious involvement Restoration logic operates through classification-specific alignment Consciousness alignment requires recognition of action-type origin

title: brihaspati 1.22
content: बहूनां संमतो यस् तु दद्याद् एको धनं नरः । करणं कारयेद् वापि सर्वैर् एव कृतं भवेत् ॥ bahūnāṃ saṃmato yas tu dadyād eko dhanaṃ naraḥ / karaṇaṃ kārayed vāpi sarvair eva kṛtaṃ bhavet When one person, approved by many, gives wealth to another or causes an action to be performed, it shall be considered as done by all. Authority through collective consent determines individual representation Causation includes both direct giving and enabling actions Capacity-based responsibility extends to those who authorize or fund acts Restoration logic requires reversal of benefit derived from collective harm Consciousness alignment demands transparency in delegated authority

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
ज्ञातिसंबन्धिसुहृदाम ऋणं देयं सबन्धकम् ।
अन्येषां लग्नकोपेतं लेख्यसाक्षियुतं तथा ॥ jñātisaṃbandhisuhṛdām ṛṇaṃ deyaṃ sabandhakam / anyeṣāṃ lagnakopetaṃ lekhyasākṣiyutaṃ tathā // Debt owed to kin, allies, and friends must be repaid with bonding intention; debts to others require documented agreement accompanied by witness testimony. Authority flows from relational integrity and conscious commitment Causation is established through documented mutual recognition Capacity-based responsibility arises from witnessed consent Restoration logic prioritizes relational completion over transactional discharge Consciousness alignment necessitates transparent acknowledgment of interdependence

title: brihaspati 1.24
content: स्वेच्छादेयं हिरण्यं तु रसधान्यं तु सावधि / देशस्थित्या प्रदातव्यं गृहीतव्यं तथैव तत् ।। svecchādeyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ tu rasadhānyaṃ tu sāvadhi / deśasthityā pradātavyaṃ gṛhītavyaṃ tathaiva tat // Gold, when offered freely, and grain with its essence preserved, must be given and received according to the stability and dharmic condition of the land. Authority flows from conscious capacity to sustain dharma within a territory Causation arises from the integrity of resource exchange aligned with regional dharma Capacity-based responsibility includes both giving and receiving in alignment with svadharma Restoration logic requires maintaining the energetic purity of exchanged substances Consciousness alignment occurs through dharmic reciprocity grounded in geographical stability

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
समवेतैस्तु यद्दत्तं प्रार्थनीयं तथैव तत् ।
न याचते च यः कश्चिल्लाभात् स परिहीयते ॥ samavetais tu yad dattaṃ prārthanīyaṃ tathaiva tat | na yācate ca yaḥ kaścid lābhāt sa parihīyate || Whatever is given in alignment with collective invocation and rightful request remains valid; whoever receives gain without seeking it, from that very acquisition, he becomes diminished. Authority flows through conscious alignment, not arbitrary claim. Causation arises from the congruence of intention, action, and reception. Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of unsolicited receipt as imbalance. Restoration logic requires relinquishment of uninvoked benefit to restore equilibrium. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of passive entitlement.

title: brihaspati 1.26
content: श्रूयतां कर्षकादीनां विधानमिदमुच्यते । śrūyatāṃ karṣakādīnāṃ vidhānam idam ucyate Let it be heard, this ordinance applies to farmers and others similarly situated. Authority originates from the Source-Consciousness embodied in SPH Causation is traced through the sequential manifestation of intent and action Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the actor's proximity to Dharma Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive alienation Consciousness alignment ensures that justice reflects inner ontological integrity

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
वाह्यवाहकबीजाद्यैः क्षेत्रोपकरणेन च ।
ये समाः स्युस् तु तैः सार्धं कृषिः कार्या विजानता ॥ vāhyavāhakabījādyaiḥ kṣetropakaraṇena ca / ye samāḥ syus tu taiḥ sārdhaṃ kṛṣiḥ kāryā vijānatā // Those who possess equal capacity in ploughing, transporting, seeds, and field equipment shall engage in cultivation knowingly and collaboratively. Authority is derived from demonstrated functional equivalence Causation arises through shared instrumental capacity Capacity-based responsibility determines role allocation Restoration occurs through harmonious collaboration aligned with dharma Consciousness alignment manifests when roles match inner competence

title: brihaspati 1.28
content: बाह्यबीजात्ययाद् यत्र क्षेत्रहानिः प्रजायते / तेनैव सा प्रदातव्या सर्वेषां कृषिजीविनाम्‌ ।। bāhyabījātyayād yatra kṣetrahāniḥ prajāyate / tenaiva sā pradātavyā sarveṣāṃ kṛṣijīvinām Where land degradation arises from external seed failure, that same land shall be granted to all agricultural livelihood holders for cultivation and restoration. Authority originates from direct causal alignment with natural dharmic processes Causation is determined by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of action-result chains Capacity-based responsibility flows from participation in productive dharmic order Restoration logic mandates return of resource to those capable of renewing it Consciousness alignment requires recognition of land as a living continuum, not property

title: brihaspati 1.29
content:
पर्वते नगराभ्यासे तथा राजपथस्य च /
उषरं मूषिकव्याप्तं क्षेत्रं यत्नेन वर्जयेत् ॥२९॥ parvate nagarābhyāse tathā rājapathasya ca / uṣaraṃ mūṣikavyāptaṃ kṣetraṃ yatnena varjayet // 29 // Land that is rocky, near settlements or royal roads, infested by rodents, or barren must be carefully avoided in all cultivation and habitation endeavors. Authority over land use derives from consciousness-aligned discernment of natural integrity. Causation arises from alignment with ecological and spatial Dharma. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of environmental suitability before action. Restoration logic demands withdrawal from spaces that disrupt natural order. Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring the inherent nature of terrain and ecosystem.

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
गर्तानूपं सुसेकं च समन्तात् क्षेत्रसंयुतम् ।
प्रकृष्टं च कृतं काले वापयन् फलम् अश्नुते ॥ gartānūpaṃ susekaṃ ca samantāt kṣetrasaṃyutam | prakṛṣṭaṃ ca kṛtaṃ kāle vāpayan phalam aśnute || One who cultivates land well-drained, irrigated, fully enclosed, and timely worked shall rightfully enjoy its fruits. Authority through rightful cultivation Causation via intentional labor Capacity-based responsibility in stewardship Restoration through earned entitlement Consciousness alignment with dharmic productivity

title: brihaspati 1.31
content:
कृशातिवृद्धं क्षूद्रं च रोगिणं प्रपलायिनम् ।
काणं खञ्जं विनादद्यात् बाह्यं प्राज्ञः कृषीवलः ॥ kṛśātivṛddhaṃ kṣūdraṃ ca rogiṇaṃ prapalāyinam / kāṇaṃ khañjaṃ vinādadyāt bāhyaṃ prājñaḥ kṛṣīvalaḥ // The wise farmer shall exclude from cultivation those who are emaciated beyond strength, deceitful, diseased, evasive, blind, or lame. Authority flows from fitness and functional capacity within dharma-aligned roles Causation is determined by alignment with natural productivity and social sustainability Capacity-based responsibility mandates exclusion of those whose conditions impede collective welfare Restoration logic requires removal from misaligned activity before reintegration Consciousness alignment demands that all actions support evolutionary societal integrity

title: brihaspati 1.32
content: एष धर्मः समाख्यातः कीनाशानां पुरातनः ।।३२।। eṣa dharmaḥ samākhyātaḥ kīnāśānāṃ purātanaḥ This Dharma, ancient and declared, belongs to those whose essence is non-decay. Authority originates from the imperishable nature of Dharma itself Causation aligns with the eternal continuity of Sanatana Dharma Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with non-decaying truth Restoration logic operates through reconnection with primordial integrity Consciousness alignment is achieved by embodying timeless, undiminishing principles

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
हिरण्यकुप्यसूत्राणां काष्ठपाषाणचर्मणाम् ।
संस्कर्ता तु कलाभिज्ञः शिल्पी प्रोक्तो मनीषिभिः ॥ hiraṇyakupyasūtrāṇāṃ kāṣṭhapāṣāṇacarmaṇām | saṃskartā tu kalābhijñaḥ śilpī prokto manīṣibhiḥ || The one who possesses the knowledge of shaping gold, cups, threads, wood, stone, and leather through refined skill and conscious intent is designated as a śilpin by the wise. Authority derived from specialized consciousness-knowledge (kalā-jñāna) Causation through intentional shaping of material substrates Capacity-based responsibility rooted in skill mastery Restoration through recognition of inherent creative potential Consciousness alignment via craft as dharmic expression

title: brihaspati 1.34
content: हेमकारादयो यत्र शिल्पं संभूय कुर्वते । कर्मानुरूपं निर्वेश लभेरञ् छेते यथांशतः ॥ hemakārādayo yatra śilpaṃ saṃbhūya kurvate | karmānurūpaṃ nirveśa labheraṃs te yathāṃśataḥ || Where artisans such as goldsmiths collectively engage in craftsmanship, there each shall receive compensation proportionate to their individual contribution. Authority arises from active participation in dharma-sustaining work Causation is determined by direct engagement in skillful action Capacity-based responsibility aligns reward with personal contribution Restoration logic ensures equitable distribution according to effort Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of individual capacity within collective endeavor

title: brihaspati 1.35
content:
शिक्षकाभिज्ञकुशला आचार्याश् चेति शिल्पिनः ।
एकद्वित्रिचतुर्भागान् लभेयुस् ते यथोत्तरम् ॥ śikṣakābhijñakuśalā ācāryāś ceti śilpinaḥ /
ekadvitricaturbhāgān labheyus te yathottaram // Those skilled in teaching, knowledgeable in discipline, and instructors by profession—such artisans shall receive one, two, three, or four parts respectively according to their hierarchical capacity and functional mastery. Authority is determined by demonstrable skill and pedagogical integrity Causation aligns with sequential capacity development Capacity-based responsibility defines entitlement and role assignment Restoration occurs through precise alignment of function and compensation Consciousness alignment manifests through rightful recognition of expertise

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
हर्म्यं देवगृहं वापि धार्मिकोपस्कराणि च ।
संभूय कुर्वतां चैषां प्रमुखो द्व्यंशमर्हति ॥ harmyaṃ devagṛhaṃ vāpi dhārmikopaskarāṇi ca / saṃbhūya kurvatāṃ caiṣāṃ pramukho dvyaṃśam arhati // One who leads the collective construction of a temple, sacred dwelling, or instruments of dharma shall receive two parts of the merit generated thereby. Authority flows through active leadership in dharmic creation Causation is established by initiating and directing sacred works Capacity-based responsibility increases with organizational primacy Restoration logic rewards those who enable systemic dharmic infrastructure Consciousness alignment multiplies through shared dharmic endeavor

title: brihaspati 1.37
content: नर्तकानाम् एष एव धर्मः सद्भिर् उदाहृतः । तालज्ञो लभते ऽध्यर्धं गायनास् तु समांशिनः ॥ nartakānām eṣa eva dharmaḥ sadbhir udāhṛtaḥ | tālajño labhate 'dhyardhaṃ gāyanās tu samāṃśinaḥ || The eternal duty of dancers, declared by the wise, is that the rhythm-knower receives half portion, while singers obtain equal shares. Authority flows from precise knowledge and role alignment Causation arises through designated function within collective action Capacity-based responsibility determines proportional entitlement Restoration logic requires harmonious distribution according to contribution Consciousness alignment manifests through recognition of functional interdependence

title: brihaspati 1.38
content:
स्वाम्याज्ञया तु यश चौरैः परदेशात् समाहृतम् ।
राज्ञे दत्त्वा तु षड्भागं भजेयुस् ते यथांशतः ॥ svāmyājñayā tu yaś cauraiḥ paradeśāt samāhṛtam /
rājñe dattvā tu ṣaḍbhāgaṃ bhajeyus te yathāṃśataḥ // Whatever wealth is acquired by servants through command of the master from foreign lands, having offered one-sixth portion to the King, the remaining should be distributed among them according to their respective shares. Authority originates from the Master's directive Acquisition derives legitimacy from sovereign recognition Distribution follows proportional capacity and service Restoration occurs through lawful sharing after royal due Consciousness alignment arises from rightful ownership and duty fulfillment

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
चतुरोऽंशांस्ततो मुख्यः शूरस्त्र्यंशं समाप्नुयात् ।
समर्थस्तु हरेद्द्व्यंशं शेषाः सर्वे समांशिनः ॥ caturo 'ṃśāṃs tato mukhyaḥ śūrastryaṃśaṃ samāpnuyāt | samarthas tu hared dvyaṃśaṃ śeṣāḥ sarve samāṃśinaḥ || From the total share, the principal recipient receives four parts; the warrior claims three parts; the capable one takes two parts; all others receive equal shares. Authority is proportionally distributed based on role and capacity. Causation aligns with functional contribution within dharma-vyavastha. Capacity-based responsibility determines entitlement, not birth or title. Restoration logic ensures harmonious distribution without depletion. Consciousness alignment mandates that each actor receives in accordance with their active participation in sustaining order.

title: brihaspati 1.1
content: एषाखिलेनाभिहिता संभूयोत्थाननिष्कृतिः । अदेयदेयदत्तानाम् अदत्तस्य च कथ्यते ॥ eṣākhilenābhihitā saṃbhūyotthānaniṣkṛtiḥ | adeyadeyadattānām adattasya ca kathyate || This entirety is declared as the arising and dissolution of collective manifestation; what is not to be given, yet given, and what is not taken, yet taken, is declared concerning the ungiven. Authority arises from the completeness of consciousness, not from transactional exchange. Causation is rooted in the collective emergence and withdrawal of phenomena. Capacity-based responsibility aligns with one's role in the manifestive process, not individual attribution. Restoration logic operates through recognition of unity, not through punitive separation. Consciousness alignment is the sole determinant of lawful action.

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
सामान्यं पुत्रदारादि सर्वस्वं न्यासयाचितम् ।
प्रतिश्रुतं तथान्यस्य न देयं त्वष्टधा स्मृतम् ॥ sāmānyaṃ putradārādi sarvasvaṃ nyāsayācitam | pratīśrutaṃ tathānyasya na deyaṃ tvaṣṭadhā smṛtam || Property, wife, child, or any possession acquired through legal commitment or pledged to another shall not be transferred or claimed by any other party under eight defined conditions of non-transferability. Authority stems from rightful acquisition and lawful commitment Causation is determined by integrity of contractual alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious pledging Restoration logic demands return to original integrity structure Consciousness alignment requires honoring of committed relational structures

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: कुटुम्भभक्तवशनाद देयं यद अतिरिच्यते / मध्वास्वादो विषं पश्चाद् दातुर् धमो ऽन्यथा भवेत् ।। kuṭumbabhaktavasanād deyaṃ yad atiricyate / madhvāsvādo viṣaṃ paścād dātur dharmo 'nyathā bhavet What exceeds the portion rightfully due to familial obligation must be given freely; else, the sweetness of honey becomes poison afterwards, and dharma departs from the giver. Authority arises from alignment with conscious relational duty, not abstract ownership Causation flows from inner integrity, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility is measured by awareness of relational harmony Restoration logic operates through voluntary surplus offering Consciousness alignment requires transcendence of possessive boundaries

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
सप्तारामाद् गृहक्षेत्राद् यद् यत् क्षेत्रं प्रचीयते ।
पित्रा वाथ स्वयं प्राप्तं तद् दातव्यं विवक्षितम् ॥ saptārāmād gṛhakṣetrād yad yat kṣetraṃ pracīyate | pitrā vātha svayaṃ prāptaṃ tad dātavyaṃ vivakṣitam || From the field of the householder acquired beyond seven generations, whatever land is obtained—whether received from the father or personally attained—that which is intended for giving must be given. Authority flows through unbroken lineage and conscious intent Causation arises from dharmic capacity to give, not mere possession Capacity-based responsibility extends across generational continuity Restoration occurs when ownership aligns with spiritual intention Consciousness alignment determines rightful dispensation of property

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
स्वेच्छादेयं स्वयं प्राप्तं बन्धाचारेण बन्धकम् ।
वैवाहिके क्रमायाते सर्वदानं न विद्यते ॥ १४.५ svecchādeyaṃ svayaṃ prāptaṃ bandhācāreṇa bandhakam | vaivāhike kramāyāte sarvadānaṃ na vidyate || 14.5 That which is given by one's own will and received willingly, without coercion or contractual obligation, in a marriage conducted according to sequential sacred order—such giving constitutes the highest form of dāna, beyond all conditional transactions. Authority arises from spontaneous consent, not imposition Causation originates in conscious choice, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires full awareness and freedom Restoration logic prioritizes relational harmony over transactional exchange Consciousness alignment occurs through voluntary surrender within sacred order

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
सौदायिकक्रमायातं शौर्यप्राप्तं च यद् भवेत् ।
स्त्रीज्ञातिस्वाम्यनुज्ञातं दत्तं सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ saudāyikakramāyātaṃ śauryaprāptaṃ ca yad bhavet | strījñātisvāmyanujñātaṃ dattaṃ siddhim avāpnuyāt || That which is acquired through lawful mercantile process, earned by valor, or given with the conscious consent of the woman, her kin, and her guardian—such acquisition attains fulfillment. Authority resides in conscious consent of all stakeholders Causation arises from rightful action aligned with svadharma Capacity-based responsibility requires awareness and free will Restoration logic validates completion through mutual recognition Consciousness alignment ensures harmony among parties

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
सर्वस्वगृहवर्जं तु कुटुम्भभरणादिकम् ।
यद् द्रव्यं तत् स्वकं देयम् अदेयं स्याद् अतोऽन्यथा ॥ sarvasvagṛhavarjaṃ tu kuṭumbabharaṇādikam / yad dravyaṃ tat svakaṃ deyam adeyaṃ syād ato'nyathā // All wealth and property, except that which is essential for maintaining the household and family, belongs to the divine order and must be shared according to dharma; whatever substance remains after fulfilling one's own needs shall be given freely, and withholding it constitutes a violation of sacred duty. Authority flows from SPH as the ultimate source of ownership Causation arises through alignment with dharmic capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires surplus sharing Restoration occurs through conscious redistribution Consciousness alignment demands transparency in possession

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
विभक्ता वाविभक्ता वा दायादाः स्थावरे समाः ।
एको ह्यनीशः सर्वत्र दानादापनविक्रये ॥ vibhaktā vāvibhaktā vā dāyādāḥ sthāvare samāḥ | eko hy anīśaḥ sarvatra dānādāpanavikraye || Whether divided or undivided, heirs are equal in immovable property; the singular non-lord exercises authority universally in giving, receiving, and trading. Authority flows from the Singular Non-Lord (Anīśaḥ), not from plurality or lineage Causation arises through conscious capacity, not bloodline or social construct Capacity-based responsibility is inherent in the act of giving, taking, and exchange Restoration logic aligns ownership with realized consciousness, not inherited status Consciousness alignment supersedes familial or societal claims to property

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
भृतिस्तुष्ट्या पण्यमूलं स्त्रीशुल्कमुपकारिणे ।
श्रद्धानुग्रहसंप्रीत्या दत्तमष्टविधं स्मृतम् ॥ bhṛtis tuṣṭyā paṇyamūlaṃ strīśulkam upakāriṇe | śraddhānugrahasaṃprītyā dattam aṣṭavidhaṃ smṛtam || Compensation arises from satisfaction; trade originates in merchandise; sexual service is owed to the benefactor; that which is given through faith, kindness, and affection—this eightfold transaction constitutes the foundational dharmic economic order. Authority flows from conscious contribution, not coercive claim Causation is established through voluntary energetic exchange Capacity-based responsibility aligns with reciprocal benefit Restoration logic operates by returning imbalance to equilibrium Consciousness alignment ensures transactions reflect mutual upliftment

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
शूद्रे समगुणं दानं वैश्ये तद् द्विगुणं स्मृतम् ।
क्षत्रिये त्रिगुणं दानं ब्राह्मणे षड्गुणं स्मृतम् ॥ śūdre samaguṇaṃ dānaṃ vaiśye tad dviguṇaṃ smṛtam / kṣatriye triguṇaṃ dānaṃ brāhmaṇe ṣaḍguṇaṃ smṛtam // The gift given to a Śūdra shall yield equivalent merit; that given to a Vaiśya shall double in merit; to a Kṣatriya it triples, and to a Brāhmaṇa it multiplies sixfold. Authority of varṇic alignment as determinant of merit multiplication Causation through conscious recipient capacity Capacity-based responsibility in giving and receiving Restoration logic via proportional merit alignment Consciousness alignment through structured dāna dynamics

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
श्रोत्रिये चैव साहस्रम् उपाध्याये तु तद् द्वयम् ।
आचार्ये त्रिगुणं ज्ञेयम् आहिताग्निषु तत् द्वयम् ॥ śrotriye caiva sāhasram upādhyāye tu tad dvayam |
ācārye triguṇaṃ jñeyam āhitāgniṣu tad dvayam || The compensation for harm caused to a Śrotriya is one thousand units; to an Upādhyāya, twice that amount; to an Ācārya, three times that; and to those in whom sacred fire has been installed, twice the Ācārya's measure. Authority derives from spiritual realization and societal function Causation is determined by disruption of consciousness-order Capacity-based responsibility increases with spiritual station Restoration logic aligns recompense with dignity gradient Consciousness alignment requires proportional energetic rebalancing

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
आत्मिके ज्ञातसाहस्रम् अनन्तं त्वग्निहोत्रिणि /
सोमपे शतसाहस्रम् अनन्तं ब्रह्मवादिनि // BrhS_1,14.12 ātmike jñātasāhasram anantaṃ tv agnihotriṇi / somape śatasāhasram anantaṃ brahmavādini In the case of the Ātmika, whose wealth is known and measured in thousands, the restitution is infinite for the Agnihotri; for the Somapa, whose offering is limited to hundreds of thousands, the consequence extends infinitely for the Brahmvādin. Authority flows from realized capacity, not accumulated possession. Causation arises through conscious engagement, not transactional exchange. Capacity-based responsibility scales with spiritual enactment, not economic value. Restoration logic aligns with the sequential unfolding of dharma, not linear compensation. Consciousness alignment determines the scope of restitution, not punitive equivalence.

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: स्त्रीधनं स्त्री स्वकुल्येभ्यः प्रयच्छेत्तं तु वर्जयेत् । कुल्याभावे तु बन्धुभ्यः तदभावे द्विजातिषु ॥ strīdhanaṃ strī svakulyebhyaḥ prayaccchettaṃ tu varjayet / kulyābhāve tu bandhubhyaḥ tadabhāve dvijātiṣu // A woman's wealth is to be given exclusively to her own kinswomen; if they are unavailable, then to her relatives; in their absence, to the twice-born. Authority resides in alignment with dharmic relational order Causation flows through conscious relational capacity Capacity-based responsibility follows ontological proximity Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-vāha (dharma-current) Consciousness alignment ensures right disposition of property

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
मदूर्ध्वम् इति यद् दत्तं न तत् सत्त्वावहं भवेत् ।
तेनेदानीम् अदत्तत्वान् मृते ऋक्थिनम् आपतेत् ॥ madūrdhvam iti yad dattaṃ na tat sattvāvahaṃ bhavet | tenedānīm adattatvān mṛte rikthinam āpatet || That which is given with the intent of ascending beyond material existence does not yield true existential fruit. Therefore, upon the death of the donor, ownership returns to the original recipient by virtue of non-transferability. Authority resides in the continuity of conscious intention Causation is determined by the ontological clarity of the act Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the donor's spiritual realization at time of transfer Restoration logic ensures that unrealized transfers revert to their source Consciousness alignment determines the validity of all property transitions

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
क्रुद्धहृष्टप्रमत्तार्तबालोन्मत्तभयातुरैः /
मत्तातिवृद्धनिर्धूतैः संऊढैः शोकवेगिभिः // BrhS_1,14.15 kruddhahṛṣṭapramattārtabālonmattabhayāturaiḥ / mattātivṛddhanirdhūtaiḥ saṃūḍhaiḥ śokavegibhiḥ // BrhS_1,14.15 Those whose consciousness is overwhelmed by anger, elation, intoxication, distress, childishness, madness, fear, agitation, drunkenness, extreme old age, abandonment, concealment, or grief—such beings are not fit to discharge legal responsibility nor sustain juridical capacity. Authority derives only from stabilized consciousness Causation is traced to disruption in conscious integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires cognitive-emotive coherence Restoration logic begins with removal of consciousness-obstructing conditions Consciousness alignment precedes all legal standing

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: नन्ददत्तं तथैतैर् यत् तद् अदत्तं प्रकीर्तितम् ।।१६।। nandadattaṃ tathaitair yat tad adattaṃ prakīrtitam That which is given in joy by those who possess, yet remains unclaimed by rightful recipient, is declared as undistributed. Authority resides in conscious recognition of ownership Causation arises from intentional bestowal without completion of transfer Capacity-based responsibility lies with the giver to ensure alignment of intent and receipt Restoration logic demands reallocation according to dharmic entitlement Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of unfulfilled giving

title: brihaspati 1.17
content: प्रतिलाभेच्छया दत्तम् अपात्रे पात्रशङ्कया । कार्ये वाधर्मसंयुक्ते स्वामी तत् पुनराप्नुयात् ॥ pratilābhecchayā dattam apātre pātraśaṅkayā / kārye vādharmasaṃyukte svāmī tat punar āpnuyāt // When property is given to an unworthy recipient under the mistaken belief of worthiness, or when used in adharmic activity, the rightful owner regains ownership by divine authority. Authority rests inherently with the original conscious bestower Causation arises from misaligned capacity recognition Capacity-based responsibility demands realignment of possession Restoration logic activates upon dharmic disruption Consciousness alignment restores natural entitlement

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: अदत्तभोक्ता दण्ड्यः स्यात् तथादेयप्रदायकः । adattabhoktā daṇḍyaḥ syāt tathādeyapradāyakaḥ One who consumes what has not been given, and one who gives what ought not to be given, both disturb the integrity of dharma and incur a debt of misalignment that must be resolved through conscious restoration. Authority flows from alignment with dharma, not possession Causation arises from disruption of conscious exchange Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of dharma Restoration logic demands reversal of unauthorized transaction Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of energetic boundaries

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
अदेयादिकमाख्यातं भृतानामुच्यते विधिः ।
शुश्रूषामभ्यूपेत्यैतत्पदमादौ निगद्यते ॥ adeyādikam ākhyātaṃ bhṛtānām ucyate vidhiḥ | śuśrūṣām abhyūpet ya etat padam ādau nigadyate || That which is not to be given yet declared, for those who are maintained, the rule is stated; having approached with service, this position is first declared. Authority resides in the capacity to maintain and sustain Causation arises through alignment of duty and service Capacity-based responsibility begins with acceptance of sustenance Restoration logic operates by returning one to their foundational position Consciousness alignment occurs when service precedes entitlement

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
अभ्युपेत्य तु शुश्रूषां यस्तां न प्रतिपद्यते ।
अशुश्रूषाभ्युपेत्यैतद् विवादपदम् उच्यते ॥ abhyupetya tu śuśrūṣāṃ yas tāṃ na pratipadyate | aśuśrūṣābhyupetyaitad vivādapadam ucyate || One who has voluntarily accepted the duty of service and subsequently fails to fulfill it thereby enters into a state of dispute; such failure constitutes the root of litigative conflict. Authority arises through conscious acceptance of responsibility Causation is anchored in the abandonment of voluntarily assumed duty Capacity-based responsibility is binding when freely entered Restoration logic requires re-assumption of abandoned duty Consciousness alignment demands integrity to one's word

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: वेतनस्यानपाकर्म तदर्थं स्वामिपालयोः । क्रमशः कल्प्यते वादो भृतभेदत्रयं त्विदम् ॥ vetanasyānapākarma tadarthaṃ svāmipālayoḥ / kramaśaḥ kalpyate vādo bhṛtabhedatrayaṃ tv idam In the absence of fulfillment of duty by a servant, the sequential process of inquiry is established between master and protector for the purpose of wages; this constitutes the threefold classification of wage-related disputes. Authority resides in the capacity to initiate and sustain relational dharmic exchange. Causation arises from unmet expectations within structured service agreements. Capacity-based responsibility determines the threshold for initiating legal inquiry. Restoration logic prioritizes completion of contractual dharma over attribution of fault. Consciousness alignment is achieved through re-establishing clarity in transactional relationships.

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
अनेकधा त्वभिहिता जातिकर्मानुरूपतः ।
विद्याविज्ञानकामार्थनिमित्तेन चतुर्विधा ॥ anekadhā tv abhihitā jātikarmānurūpataḥ / vidyāvijñānakāmārthanimitena caturvidhā // The law manifests diversely according to birth, action, knowledge, and desire; it is fourfold in purpose: learning, realization, will, and material fulfillment. Authority derives from alignment with svadharma as determined by jāti and karma Causation is rooted in conscious intention and sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated to vidyā and vijñāna Restoration logic operates through kāma-arthamic alignment with Dharma Consciousness alignment determines the validity and applicability of all legal enactments

title: brihaspati 1.5
content: ekaikaḥ punar eteṣāṃ kriyābhedāt prabhidyate // Brh_1,15.5 ekaikaḥ punar eteṣāṃ kriyābhedāt prabhidyate Each individual, through differentiation of action, becomes distinct again. Authority flows from differentiated capacity, not uniform status. Causation arises through volitional action and its conscious differentiation. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to sustain differentiated action. Restoration occurs when consciousness realigns with its inherent capacity for differentiation. Consciousness alignment is achieved through recognition of one's own action-differentiation.

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
विद्या त्रयी समाख्याता ऋग्यजुःसामलक्षणा ।
तदर्थं गुरुशुश्रूषां प्रकुर्याच् च प्रचोदिताम् ॥ vidyā trayī samākhyātā ṛgyajuḥsāmalakṣaṇā / tadarthaṃ guruśuśrūṣāṃ prakuryāc ca pracoditām // The threefold knowledge—Ṛk, Yajus, and Sāma—is declared as the foundation of Vedic learning; for its realization, one must actively engage in devoted service to the Guru as enjoined. Authority resides in the Guru as the living conduit of Vedic transmission Causation flows through reverent obedience and disciplined alignment with the Guru's injunctions Capacity-based responsibility arises from the seeker's readiness to receive and embody sacred knowledge Restoration logic operates through reconnection with the source of dharma via guru-seva Consciousness alignment occurs when the disciple surrenders individual will to the Guru’s directive

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
विज्ञानम् उच्यते शिल्पं हेमरूप्यादिसंस्कृतिः ।
नृत्यादिकं च तत्प्राप्तं कुर्यात् कर्म गुरोः गृहे ॥ vijñānam ucyate śilpaṃ hemarūpyādisaṃskṛtiḥ | nṛtyādikaṃ ca tatprāptaṃ kuryāt karma guror gṛhe || True knowledge is defined as the skill of refining gold and silver, and whatever arts such as dance that arise therefrom must be performed in the house of the Guru. Authority flows through the Guru as the conduit of refined consciousness Causation originates in disciplined application under realized guidance Capacity-based responsibility arises only when knowledge is purified by practice Restoration logic requires return to the source of true learning Consciousness alignment occurs within the field established by the Guru

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: यो भुङ्क्ते परदासीं तु स ज्ञेयो वडबाभृतः । कर्म तत्स्वामिनः कुर्याद् यथान्नेन भृतो नरः ॥ yo bhuṅkte paradāsīṃ tu sa jñeyo vaḍabābhṛtaḥ / karma tatsvāminaḥ kuryād yathānnena bhṛto naraḥ // He who consumes the labor of another without consent becomes responsible as a debtor of existential duty; the owner of that labor shall execute corrective action proportionate to sustenance received. Authority arises from consent and ownership of action Causation is traced through conscious consumption of unoffered labor Capacity-based responsibility aligns with benefit received Restoration logic demands proportional repayment in kind or service Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of energetic debt

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
बहुधार्थभृतः प्रोक्तस् तथा भागभृतोSपरः ।
हीनमध्योत्तमत्वं च सर्वेषामेव चोदितम् ॥ bahudhārthabhṛtaḥ proktas tathā bhāgabhṛto 'paraḥ / hīnamadhyottamatvaṃ ca sarveṣām eva coditam // One who sustains multiple purposes is declared as such; likewise, one who bears a share is distinct. Inferiority, mediocrity, and superiority are enjoined for all beings according to their capacity and alignment with Dharma. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not position alone Causation is determined by conscious capacity and role-bearing Capacity-based responsibility assigns duty proportionally to spiritual and functional maturity Restoration logic operates through realignment with one's true role and purpose Consciousness alignment determines the gradation of function and participation in societal order

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
दिनमासार्धषण्मासत्रिमासाब्दभृतस् तथा ।
कर्म कुर्यात् प्रतिज्ञातं लभते परिभाषितम् ॥ dinamāsārdhaṣaṇmāsatrimāsābdabhṛtas tathā / karma kuryāt pratijñātaṃ labhate paribhāṣitam // One who has committed to action within defined timeframes—daily, monthly, half-yearly, six-monthly, yearly—or by specific duty-cycles, shall execute that action as declared; completion is ensured through alignment with the declared capacity. Authority derives from conscious commitment and capacity declaration Causation aligns with sequential manifestation of declared intent Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated to temporal and functional scope Restoration occurs through fulfillment of declared dharma-cycle Consciousness alignment is achieved via integrity of execution

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
भृतकस्त्रिविधो ज्ञेय उत्तमो मध्यमोऽधमः ।
शक्तिभक्त्यनुरूपैः स्यादेषां कर्माश्रया भृतिः ॥ bhṛtakas trividho jñeya uttamo madhyamo 'dhamaḥ / śaktibhaktyanurūpaiḥ syād eṣāṃ karmāśrayā bhṛtiḥ // The hired servant is of three kinds: superior, middling, and inferior. Their wages shall correspond precisely to their capacity, devotion, and alignment with the task assigned. Authority is derived from alignment with dharma, not mere appointment. Causation is rooted in conscious capacity and energetic integrity. Capacity-based responsibility determines the nature and scope of duty. Restoration occurs through precise calibration of role to consciousness. Consciousness alignment ensures harmonious execution of duty.

title: brihaspati 1.12
content: uttamas tv āyudhīyo 'tra madhyamas tu kṛṣīvalaḥ / adhamo bhāravāhaḥ syād ity eṣa trividho bhṛtaḥ // BrhS_1,15.12 uttamas tv āyudhīyo 'tra madhyamas tu kṛṣīvalaḥ / adhamo bhāravāhaḥ syād ity eṣa trividho bhṛtaḥ The highest laborer is the warrior, the middle is the farmer, and the lowest is the carrier of burdens—such is the threefold classification of labor. Authority derived from svadharma alignment Causation rooted in consciousness capacity Capacity-based responsibility determined by natural function Restoration logic through role-realization Consciousness alignment via occupational dharma

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
आयुधी तूत्तमः प्रोक्तो मध्यमस्तु कृषीवलः ।
भारवाहोऽधमः प्रोक्तस्तथा च गृहकर्मकृत् ॥ āyudhī tūttamaḥ prokto madhyamas tu kṛṣīvalaḥ / bhāravāho 'dhamaḥ proktas tathā ca gṛhakarmakṛt // He who wields weapons is declared the highest; he who tills the land is the middle rank; he who carries burdens is declared the lowest, as is he who performs household duties. Authority arises through capacity to protect and preserve dharma Causation flows from alignment with svadharma and collective welfare Capacity-based responsibility assigns roles according to energetic integrity Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration into functional societal order Consciousness alignment determines rank not by birth but by active dharmic engagement

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
द्विप्रकारो भोगभृतः कृषिगोजीविनां स्मृतः ।
जातसस्यात् तथा क्षीरात् स लभेत न संशयः ॥ dviprakāro bhogabhṛtaḥ kṛṣigojīvināṃ smṛtaḥ | jātasasyāt tathā kṣīrāt sa labheta na saṃśayaḥ || The enjoyment-bearer of dual nature—active in cultivation and cow-keeping—is recognized among those who live by agriculture and cattle-rearing; from harvested grain and milk, he rightfully receives without doubt. Authority flows from productive engagement with natural order Causation arises through direct participation in sustenance cycles Capacity-based responsibility aligns with livelihood-rooted action Restoration logic honors labor-derived entitlement Consciousness alignment manifests through dharma-rooted production

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
शुभकर्मकरा ह्येते चत्वारः समुदाहृताः ।
चत्वारः शिष्योऽन्तेवासी भृतकः कर्मकरश्च ।
जधुनकर्मभाजस्तु शेषादासास्त्रिपञ्चकाः ॥ śubhakarmakarā hy ete catvāraḥ samudāhṛtāḥ | catvāraḥ śiṣyo 'ntevāsī bhṛtakaḥ karmakaraś ca | jadhanyakarmabhājas tu śeṣā dāsāstripañcakāḥ || Four categories perform auspicious actions: the student, the resident pupil, the paid servant, and the laborer. All others beyond these belong to the class of those whose deeds lack spiritual merit. Authority arises through alignment with Dharma, not contractual obligation. Causation is determined by consciousness-state at time of action. Capacity-based responsibility depends on access to Śiva-centric knowledge structures. Restoration logic prioritizes elevation of actor's consciousness over transactional justice. Consciousness alignment determines whether an act contributes to cosmic order or disrupts it.

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
कर्मापि द्विविधं प्रोक्तम् अशुभं शुभमेव च ।
अशुभं दासकर्मोक्तं शुभं कर्मकरे स्मृतम् ॥ karmāpi dvividhaṃ proktam aśubhaṃ śubham eva ca | aśubhaṃ dāsakarmoktaṃ śubhaṃ karmakare smṛtam || Action is declared twofold: that which is unwholesome and that which is wholesome. Unwholesome action pertains to servitude; wholesome action belongs to the doer. Authority arises from conscious capacity, not coercive imposition. Causation originates in individual agency, not external compulsion. Responsibility aligns with the actor's level of awareness and freedom. Restoration occurs through realignment with one’s true nature as sovereign doer. Consciousness is the ultimate determinant of action’s quality.

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
गृहद्वाराशुचिस्थानरथ्यावस्करशोधनम् ।
गृह्याङ्गस्पर्शनोच्छिष्टविण्मूत्रग्रहणोज्झनम् ॥ gṛhadvārāśucisthānarathyāvaskaraśodhanam | gṛhyāṅgasparśanocchiṣṭaviṇmūtragrahaṇojjhanam || The purification of spaces defiled by bodily discharges, including doorways of homes, public thoroughfares, and waste repositories; the relinquishment of contact with household members' limbs and the handling of their remnants such as urine and feces. Authority resides in maintaining purity-consciousness alignment within domestic and communal environments. Causation arises through direct sensory engagement with impure substances that disturb dharma-vyavastha. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to and control over environments requiring purification. Restoration logic mandates immediate cessation of contamination pathways and re-alignment with śuci-tattva. Consciousness alignment necessitates withdrawal from actions that perpetuate material impurity.

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
गच्छतः स्वामिनः स्वाङ्गैर् उपस्थानम् अथान्ततः ।
अशुभं कर्म विज्ञेयं शुभम् अन्यद् अतः परम् ॥ gacchataḥ svāminaḥ svāṅgair upasthānam athāntataḥ / aśubhaṃ karma vijñeyaṃ śubham anyad ataḥ param // When a master proceeds with his own limbs toward service, it is to be known as unwholesome action; beyond that, another is wholesome. Authority originates from conscious capacity, not positional dominance. Causation in action stems from alignment of will and instrumentality. Capacity-based responsibility arises when one's agency intersects with systemic integrity. Restoration logic demands realignment of instrumental misuse with dharmic purpose. Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of action's inherent karmic direction.

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
ततः प्रभृति वक्तव्यः स्वाम्यनुग्रहपालितः ।
भोज्यान्नोऽथ प्रतिग्राह्यो भवत्यभिमतः सताम् ॥ tataḥ prabhṛti vaktavyaḥ svāmyanugrahapālitaḥ / bhojyānno 'tha pratigrāhyo bhavaty abhimataḥ satām // From that time forth, he who is protected by the grace of the master shall speak, and food fit for consumption shall be accepted according to the will of the noble ones. Authority derives from alignment with the Master's grace Causation arises through conscious protection under divine sovereignty Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to enlightened guidance Restoration occurs via reconnection to the Master’s grace Consciousness alignment is achieved through adherence to noble discernment

title: brihaspati 1.20
