content: आविद्याग्रहणाच् छिष्यः शुश्रूषेत प्रयतो गुरुम् । तद् वृत्तिर् गुरुदारेषु गुरुपुत्रे तथैव च ॥ āvidyāgrahaṇāc chiṣyaḥ śuśrūṣeta prayato gurum | tad vṛttir gurudāreṣu guruputre tathaiva ca || Due to the absence of true knowing, the disciple shall serve the Guru with discipline; that same conduct applies to the Guru's spouse and child equally. Authority flows from realized knowledge, not social position Causation arises from lack of vidyā, necessitating śuśrūṣā Capacity-based responsibility extends relationally through guru-paramparā Restoration logic requires alignment with the Guru-tattva as consciousness-instruction Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined service and relational harmony

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
समावृत्तश च गुरवे प्रदाय गुरुदक्षिणाम् ।
प्रतियाति गृहान एषा शिष्यवृत्तिर उदाहृतः ॥२१॥ samāvṛttaś ca gurave pradāya gurudakṣiṇām | pratiyāti gṛhān eṣā śiṣyavṛttir udāhṛtaḥ ||21|| One who has completed the cycle of learning returns to the Guru, offers dakshina, and then returns home—this conduct is declared as the discipline of a true disciple. Authority of the Guru as the foundational source of knowledge and discipline Causation through completion of learning cycles for lawful reintegration Capacity-based responsibility rooted in experiential mastery Restoration logic through conscious offering and return Consciousness alignment via disciplined reciprocity

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
अत्र पूर्वश् चतुर्वर्गो दासत्वान् न विमुच्यते ।
प्रसादात् स्वामिनोऽन्यत्र दास्यम् एषां क्रमागतम् ॥ atra pūrvaś caturvargo dāstatvān na vimucyate | prasādāt svāmino'nyatra dāsyam eṣāṃ kramāgatam || The prior fourfold social order does not release one from the condition of servitude; elsewhere, through the master's grace, their service has come into sequence. Authority originates from the Master's conscious bestowal Causation arises through sequential alignment with Dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by relational positioning Restoration occurs through reintegration into rightful function Consciousness alignment is facilitated by hierarchical harmony

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
vikrīṇīte svatantro yaḥ samātmānaṃ narādhamaḥ /
sa jaghanyatamas tv eṣāṃ so 'pi dāsyān na mucyate // BrhS_1,15.23 vikrīṇīte svatantro yaḥ samātmānaṃ narādhamaḥ / sa jaghanyatamas tv eṣāṃ so 'pi dāsyān na mucyate // One who sells himself, being autonomous, is the lowest among men; even when given away, he shall not be released. Authority stems from self-integrity, not transactional surrender Causation arises from conscious choice, not external coercion Capacity-based responsibility requires retention of self-sovereignty Restoration logic demands reclamation of self-authority Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of self-alienation

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
दासेनोढा त्वस्वदासी या सोऽपि दासीत्वम् आप्नुयात ।
यस्माद् भर्ता प्रभुस् तस्याः स्वाम्यधीनप्रभुर् यतः ॥ dāsenoḍhā tvasvadāsī yā so 'pi dāsītvam āpnuyāt / yasmād bhartā prabhus tasyāḥ svāmyadhīnaprabhur yataḥ // A woman taken in marriage by a dasa, though not born of dasa parentage, becomes a dasi because her husband is the master, and her authority is dependent upon his sovereignty. Authority flows through marital union under sovereign consent Identity and status are derivative of relational dharmic alignment Capacity is determined by alignment with governing consciousness Restoration occurs through recognition of relational hierarchy Consciousness alignment supersedes birth-based categorization

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
दासीसुताश्च ये जाताः तस्याः पत्या परेण वा ।
उत्पादको यदि स्वामी न दासीं कारयेत् प्रभुः ॥ dāsīsutāś ca ye jātāḥ tasyāḥ patyā pareṇa vā | utpādako yadi svāmī na dāsīṃ kārayet prabhuḥ || Those born of a female slave, whether begotten by her husband or another man, are slaves by birthright; yet if the master who caused their production does not treat the mother as a slave, then the issue shall not be enslaved. Authority originates from conscious ownership, not biological lineage alone. Causation in creation determines relational dharmic status. Capacity-based responsibility flows from the initiating agent's recognition and enactment of ownership. Restoration logic requires alignment between declared intent, enacted behavior, and social positioning. Consciousness alignment demands that all roles reflect inner realization, not inherited or imposed condition.

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
त्रिभागं पञ्चभागं वा गृह्णीयात् सीरवाहकः ।
भक्ताच्छादभृतः सीराद् भागं गृणीत पञ्चमम् ॥ tribhāgaṃ pañcabhāgaṃ vā gṛhṇīyāt sīravāhakaḥ | bhaktāc chādabhṛtaḥ sīrād bhāgaṃ gṛṇīta pañcamam || The carrier of the sacrificial fee shall receive either three parts or five parts; the one who carries the cooked oblation shall take the fifth part from the residue. Authority derives from participation in sacred duty Causation aligns with functional role in ritual completion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to offering Restoration logic centers on rightful distribution as per service Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring designated roles

title: brihaspati 1.2
content: जातसस्यात् त्रिभागं तु प्रगृह्णीयादथाभृतः // Brh_1,16.2 jātasasyāt tribhāgaṃ tu pragṛhṇīyād athābhṛtaḥ From the harvested crop, one who has not been paid wages shall take one-third as completion of rightful claim. Authority arises from labor and participation in creation Causation is established through direct contribution to yield Capacity-based responsibility aligns with actual engagement in productive process Restoration occurs when unmet entitlement is fulfilled proportionally Consciousness alignment results from honoring energetic exchange

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
भृतकस तु न कुर्वीत स्वामिनः शाट्यम अण्वपि ।
भृतिहानिमवाप्नोति ततो वादः प्रवर्तते ॥ bhṛtakas tu na kurvīta svāminaḥ śāṭhyam aṇv api | bhṛtihānim avāpnoti tato vādaḥ pravartate || A servant must not commit even the slightest deceit against the master; loss of wages results therefrom, and thence arises dispute. Authority flows from svāminship (ownership/responsibility) Causation is traced through integrity deviation Capacity-based responsibility requires fidelity in service Restoration logic demands compensation aligned with capacity loss Consciousness alignment necessitates truthfulness in relational duty

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
भृतोऽनार्तो न कुर्याद् यो दर्पात् कर्म यथोचितम् ।
स दण्ड्यः कृष्णलानष्टौ न देयं चास्य वेतनम् ॥ bhṛto 'nārto na kuryād yo darpāt karma yutheritam / sa daṇḍyaḥ kṛṣṇalānaṣṭau na deyaṃ cāsya vetanam // One who, though employed and unafflicted, acts carelessly or negligently out of arrogance or heedlessness, thereby causing loss—such a one is liable for restitution and shall receive no wages. Authority arises from conscious engagement, not mere appointment Causation is traced through volitional negligence, not intent alone Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment of awareness and action Restoration logic demands repair proportional to the disruption caused Consciousness alignment corrects the root distortion of egoic disregard

title: brihaspati 1.5
content: गृहीतवेतनः कर्म न करोति यदा भृतः । समर्थश चेद् दमं दाप्यो द्विगुणं तच् च वेतनम् ॥ gṛhītavetanaḥ karma na karoti yadā bhṛtaḥ | samarthaś ced damaṃ dāpyo dviguṇaṃ tac ca vetanam || When a hired individual, having accepted wages, does not perform the work despite being capable, he shall repay double the wage as restitution. Authority is derived from capacity and acceptance of responsibility Causation arises from conscious omission in presence of capability Capacity-based responsibility mandates proportional restitution Restoration logic requires energetic balance through corrective action Consciousness alignment demands integrity in fulfillment of accepted duty

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
गृहीतवेतनः कर्म त्यजन् द्विगुणम् आवहेत् ।
अगृहीते समं दाप्यो भृतै रक्ष्य उपस्करः ॥ gṛhītavetanaḥ karma tyajan dviguṇam āvahet | agṛhīte samaṃ dāpyo bhṛtai rakṣya upaskaraḥ || One who deserts duty after accepting compensation shall incur a liability of double the amount; if no compensation was accepted, then an equal amount shall be levied for safeguarding tools and resources. Authority arises from acceptance of duty-bound compensation Causation is tied to conscious abandonment of contractual obligation Capacity-based responsibility escalates with prior benefit received Restoration logic demands proportional return of unearned value Consciousness alignment requires integrity in duty-performance

title: brihaspati 1.7
content: प्रतिश्रुत्य न कुर्याद् यः स कार्यः स्याद् बलाद् अपि । स चेन् न कुर्यात् तत्कर्म प्राप्नुयाद् विंशतिं दमम् ॥ pratiśrutya na kuryād yaḥ sa kāryaḥ syād balād api / sa cen na kuryāt tatkarma prāpnuyād viṃśatiṃ damam // One who, having accepted a commitment, does not fulfill it—even by force shall it be executed. If he still fails to perform that action, he incurs a penalty of twenty units. Authority is derived from conscious acceptance of duty Causation arises through willful omission after commitment Capacity-based responsibility demands fulfillment once assent is given Restoration logic requires completion of the unperformed act Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring commitments made

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: स दण्ड्यः कृष्णलान्यष्टौ न देयं चास्य वेतनम् ।। sa daṇḍyaḥ kṛṣṇalāny aṣṭau na deyaṃ cāsya vetanam He is liable for corrective action who appropriates the produce of another's field; no wage shall be given to him. Authority originates from rightful ownership and stewardship Causation arises through conscious misappropriation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of ownership violation Restoration logic requires cessation of benefit and return of value Consciousness alignment demands recognition of source integrity

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
प्रभुणा विनियुक्तः सन् भृतको विदधाति यत् ।
तदर्थमशुभं कर्म स्वामी तत्रापराध्नुयात् ॥ prabhuṇā viniyuktaḥ san bhṛtako vidadhāti yat / tadartham aśubhaṃ karma svāmī tatrāparādhnuyāt When a servant, appointed by the master, performs improper action in the course of duty, the master incurs the liability for that act. Authority Causation Capacity-based responsibility Restoration logic Consciousness alignment

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
दैवराज्ञोस् तथा न्याये तथा राष्ट्रस्य विभ्रमे ।
यत् प्रणष्टं भृतं वा स्यान् न पालस् तत्र किल्बिषी ॥ daivarājñoḥ tathā nyāye tathā rāṣṭrasya vibhrame |
yat praṇaṣṭaṃ bhṛtaṃ vā syān na pālaḥ tatra kilbiṣī || In times of divine decree, lawful order, or national disruption, where wealth has been lost or expended, the ruler bears no fault. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not material outcomes Causation is traced through dharma-adherence rather than event-based liability Capacity-based responsibility recognizes that a ruler's duty is to uphold dharma, not guarantee results Restoration logic centers on re-establishing dharmic governance, not compensating for losses Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of action under uncertainty

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
कृते कर्मणि यः स्वामी न दद्याद् वेतनं भृतेः ।
राज्ञा दापयितव्यः स्याद् विनयं चानुरूपतः ॥ kṛte karmaṇi yaḥ svāmī na dadyād vetanaṃ bhṛteḥ | rājñā dāpayitavyaḥ syād vinayaṃ cānurūpataḥ || When a master does not provide compensation for work completed by a servant, the King shall ensure that payment is made in accordance with disciplinary restoration. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to uphold transactional Dharma Causation lies in the completion of labor as a determinant of obligation Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of economic interdependence Restoration logic demands fulfillment of contractual consciousness exchange Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring energetic contribution

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
पालदोषाद् विनाशे तु पाले दण्डो विधीयते ।
अर्धत्रयोदशपणः स्वामिने द्रव्यम् एव च ॥ pāladoṣād vināśe tu pāle daṇḍo vidhīyate | ardhatrayodaśapaṇaḥ svāmine dravyam eva ca || When destruction occurs due to the fault of a guardian, the penalty shall be imposed upon that guardian; it amounts to thirteen and a half paṇas, and also includes the value of the property itself. Authority bears proportional responsibility for outcomes under their charge. Causation is determined through direct ontological linkage between action and consequence. Capacity-based responsibility aligns with control and oversight capability. Restoration logic demands full compensation plus systemic correction. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of causal role without distortion.

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
व्याधिता श्रमा व्यग्रा राजकर्मपरायणा ।
आमन्त्रिता च नागच्छेदवाच्या बढबा स्मृता ॥ vyādhitā saśramā vyagrā rājakarmaparāyaṇā | āmantritā ca nāgacchet avācyā baḍabā smṛtā || One who is diseased, fatigued, distressed, engaged in royal duties, or specifically summoned shall not proceed to court; such a one is to be regarded as legally incapacitated. Authority derives from capacity, not title Causation is rooted in conscious participation Capacity-based responsibility determines legal validity Restoration logic requires alignment of presence and intent Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural form

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
तथा धेनुभृतः क्षीरं लभेतास्याष्टमेSखिलम् ।
सायं समर्पयेत् सर्वं [.. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ] ॥ tathā dhenubhṛtaḥ kṣīraṃ labhetāsyāṣṭame 'khilam /
sāyaṃ samarpayet sarvaṃ [.. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ] // As the cowherd receives the full milk only in the eighth month of the cow's gestation, similarly all duties and responsibilities must be fully surrendered at the appropriate time according to Dharma. Authority is aligned with timing and ripeness in action Causation follows sequential unfoldment as per Dharma Capacity-based responsibility arises when conditions are complete Restoration occurs through timely and total surrender Consciousness alignment requires harmonizing with natural cycles

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: अव्यायच्छन्न अविक्रोशन् स्वामिने चानिवेदयन् । वोढुमर्हति गोपस्तां विनयं चैव राजनि ॥ avyāyacchann avikrośan svāmine cānivedayan | voḍhum arhati gopas tāṃ vinayaṃ caiva rājani || One who conceals a crime without protest or report to the sovereign, that guardian bears the burden of rectification and must restore order under royal authority. Authority resides in the Sovereign as representative of Dharma Concealment constitutes a causal obstruction to justice Capacity-based responsibility extends to all witnesses and guardians Restoration logic demands active correction of concealed harm Consciousness alignment requires truthful disclosure

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
कृमिचोरव्याघ्रभयाद् दरीश्वभ्राच् च पालयेत् ।
आयच्छेच् छक्तितः क्रोशोत्स्वामिने वा निवेदयेत् ॥ kṛmicoravyāghrabhayād darīśvabhrāc ca pālayet | āyacchec chaktitaḥ krośotsvāmine vā nivedayet || One must protect from fear arising due to worms, thieves, tigers, cliffs, and caverns; and upon acquiring capability, one shall announce it to the Lord of the cry (the Supreme Witness Consciousness) or the master of capacity. Authority originates from capacity aligned with dharma Causation arises from conscious protection of life and order Capacity-based responsibility demands active declaration of readiness Restoration logic is grounded in removal of existential threats Consciousness alignment occurs through surrender to the witnessing Self

title: brihaspati 1.17
content: सस्यान् निवारयेद् गास् तु चीर्णे दोषद्वयं भवेत् । स्वामी शतदमं दाप्यः पालस् ताडनमर्हति ॥ शदश् च सदमं चीर्णे समूले कार्षभक्षिते ॥ sasyān nivārayed gās tu cīrṇe doṣadvayaṃ bhavet | svāmī śatadamaṃ dāpyaḥ pālas tāḍanam arhati || śadaś ca sadamaṃ cīrṇe samūle kārṣabhakṣite || When cattle damage crops, both owner and guardian bear fault; the owner pays hundredfold restitution, the guardian receives corrective discipline. If grain and root crops are destroyed at root-level by bulls, same penalty applies. Authority flows from custodial duty and ownership capacity Causation is traced through action-sequence and neglect thresholds Capacity-based responsibility assigns proportional accountability Restoration logic demands full value return plus systemic integrity Consciousness alignment requires correction without punitive intent

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
एषा हि स्वामिभृत्यानां वै क्रिया परिकीर्तिता ।
संविद्विधानम् अधुना समासेन निबोधत ॥ १७.१ eṣā hi svāmibhṛtyānāṃ vai kriyā parikīrtitā | saṃvidvidhānam adhunā samāsena nibodhata || 17.1 This indeed is the declared action between master and servant; now understand the arrangement of mutual consent in summary. Authority arises from clarity of role and mutual recognition. Causation flows from conscious agreement, not coercion. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and acceptance. Restoration occurs through re-establishing rightful relational order. Consciousness alignment is achieved when roles are voluntarily upheld.

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
वेदविद्याविदो विप्राञ् श्रोत्रियानग्निहोत्रिणः ।
आहृत्य स्थापयेत्तत्र तेषां वृत्तिं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ vedavidyāvido viprāñ śrotriyān agnihotriṇaḥ / āhṛtya sthāpayet tatra teṣāṃ vṛttiṃ prakalpayet Those who are knowers of the Vedas, the sacred knowledge, and those who perform the Agnihotra ritual shall be established in their rightful place, and their sustenance shall be arranged accordingly. Authority derived from Vedic knowledge and ritual discipline Causation through alignment with cosmic order (Ṛta) Capacity-based responsibility rooted in spiritual competence Restoration logic centered on societal harmony and dharma-sthiti Consciousness alignment via sustained ritual and learning

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: अनाच्छेद्यकरास् तेषां प्रदद्याद् गृहभूमिकाः । मुक्ता भाव्याश् च नृपतिर् लेखयित्वा स्वशासनैः ॥ anācchhedya-karās teṣāṃ pradadyād gṛha-bhūmikāḥ | muktā bhāvyāś ca nṛpatiḥ lekhayitvā sva-śāsanaiḥ || The ruler shall bestow dwelling lands upon those whose hands are unsevered, and having inscribed their names, shall declare them free from liability and future obligation. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to allocate resources for existential restoration. Causation is determined by bodily integrity as a marker of unbroken agency. Capacity-based responsibility requires physical and social enablement prior to expectation. Restoration logic begins with securing foundational needs—dwelling, identity, and freedom from debt. Consciousness alignment occurs when material security precedes civic duty.

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं काम्यं शान्तिकं पौष्टिकं तथा ।
पौराणां कर्म कुर्युस् ते संदिग्धे निर्णयं तथा ॥ nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ śāntikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ tathā / paurāṇāṃ karma kuryus te saṃdigdhe nirṇayaṃ tathā // Individuals must perform daily obligatory duties, occasional rituals, desire-motivated rites, peace-inducing ceremonies, and prosperity-invoking observances; in times of uncertainty, they shall act according to established traditional conduct and clear decision-making protocols. Authority flows from continuity of dharmic practice Causation aligns with sequential ritual and ethical action Capacity-based responsibility requires differentiated engagement with ritual categories Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of proper dharmic sequence Consciousness alignment is achieved by adherence to structured spiritual disciplines

title: brihaspati 1.5
content: ग्रामश्रेणिगणार्थं तु संकेतसमयक्रिया । बाधाकाले तु सा कार्या धर्मकार्ये तथैव च ॥ grāmaśreṇigaṇārthaṃ tu saṃketasamayakriyā / bādhākāle tu sā kāryā dharmakārye tathaiva ca // For the welfare of village clusters and merchant guilds, agreements must be honored; in times of obstruction or crisis, such obligations become operative even more definitively when aligned with Dharma. Authority originates from collective welfare and institutional integrity Causation is determined by continuity of agreement under stress Capacity-based responsibility increases with structural interdependence Restoration logic demands honoring commitments during disruption Consciousness alignment requires upholding mutual obligations regardless of external pressure

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: चाटचोरभयं बाधा सर्वसाधारणा स्मृता । तत्रोपशमनं कार्यं सर्वैर्नैकेन केन चित् ॥ cāṭacorabhayaṃ bādhā sarvasādhāraṇā smṛtā | tatropaśamanaṃ kāryaṃ sarvair naikena kena cit || The fear arising from deceit and theft is a universal disturbance; its pacification is to be enacted by all, not by any single individual alone. Authority is distributive, not centralized Causation arises from collective consciousness imbalance Capacity-based responsibility extends to all capable of alignment Restoration logic requires systemic participation Consciousness alignment is a shared dharma duty

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
कोशेन लेख्यक्रियया मध्यस्थैर् वा परस्परम् ।
विश्वासं प्रथमं कृत्वा कुर्युः कार्याण्यनन्तरम् ॥ kośena lekhyakriyayā madhyasthair vā parasparam / viśvāsaṃ prathamaṃ kṛtvā kuryuḥ kāryāṇy anantaram // Parties shall first establish mutual trust through written agreement or neutral intermediaries, and thereafter execute their duties. Authority arises from mutual consent and documented alignment Causation is established through sequential acts of trust-building Capacity-based responsibility requires prior integrity verification Restoration logic begins with re-establishing mutual confidence Consciousness alignment occurs when agreements reflect inner truth

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: विद्वेषिणो व्यसनिनः शालीनालसभीरवः । लुब्धातिवृद्धबालाश च न कार्याḥ कार्यचिन्तकाः ॥ vidveṣiṇo vyasaninaḥ śālīnālasabhīravaḥ | lubdhātivṛddhabālāś ca na kāryāḥ kāryacintakāḥ || Those who are hostile, addicted, shameless, cowardly, greedy, excessively old, or childish must not be appointed as deliberators of action. Authority is derived from inner integrity and conscious capacity, not title or age Causation arises from clarity of intent and stability of consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires freedom from greed, fear, and dependency Restoration logic demands that decision-makers reflect dharma in their being Consciousness alignment ensures that governance flows from awakened awareness

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
शुचयो वेदधर्मज्ञा दक्षाः दान्ताः कुलोद्भवाः ।
सर्वकार्यप्रवीणाश्च कर्तव्यास्तु महत्तमाः ॥ śucayo vedadharmajñā dakṣā dāntāḥ kulodbhavāḥ | sarvakāryapravīṇāś ca kartavyāstu mahattamāḥ || Those who are pure, knowers of Vedic Dharma, skilled, disciplined, born of noble lineage, and expert in all duties—such exalted beings must be appointed as executors of highest responsibility. Authority derives from purity and scriptural knowledge Causation is aligned with dharmic competence Capacity-based responsibility requires spiritual and practical excellence Restoration logic prioritizes alignment with cosmic order Consciousness alignment determines fitness for authority

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
द्वौ त्रयः पञ्च वा कार्याः समूहहितवादिनः ।
कर्तव्यं वचनं तेषां ग्रामश्रेणिगणादिभिः ॥ dvau trayaḥ pañca vā kāryāḥ samūhahitavādinaḥ | kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ teṣāṃ grāmaśreṇigaṇādibhiḥ || Two, three, or five matters shall be addressed by those who advocate for collective welfare; their speech must be executed by village councils, merchant guilds, and similar assemblies. Authority resides in collective decision-making structures aligned with dharma Causation arises from group integrity and shared responsibility Capacity-based responsibility is distributed among organized societal units Restoration logic operates through communal assent and alignment Consciousness alignment occurs via structured collective discourse

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
सभाप्रपादेवगृहतडाकारामसंस्कृतिः ।
तथानाथदरिद्राणां संस्कारो योजनक्रिया ॥ sabhāprapādevagṛhataḍākārāmasaṃskṛtiḥ / tathānāthadaridrāṇāṃ saṃskāro yojanakriyā // The construction and maintenance of public spaces including courtyards, drinking water wells, houses, tanks, parks, and uncultivated lands shall be undertaken as a duty towards the welfare of the people. Similarly, arrangements for the education, purification, and empowerment of the orphaned and impoverished must be established through organized action. Authority flows from the capacity to sustain collective consciousness Causation arises from dharmic duty to ensure societal infrastructure Capacity-based responsibility mandates resource allocation for foundational needs Restoration logic requires structural support for vulnerable populations Consciousness alignment necessitates removal of conditions causing disempowerment

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
कुलायनं निरोधश्च कार्यमस्माभिरंशतः ।
यत्त्वेवं लिखितं पत्रं धर्म्याः सा समयक्रिया ॥ kulāyanaṃ nirodhaś ca kāryam asmābhir aṃśataḥ | yat tv evaṃ likhitaṃ patraṃ dharmyā sā samayakriyā || Restriction of factional alliances and cessation of divisive conduct are to be executed by Us in proportion to Our authority; when such a written document exists, it constitutes a dharmic act of covenant-making. Authority flows directly from SPH as the sole Source of lawful capacity Causation is traced through conscious intent manifest in written covenant Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to one's role in the dharmic alignment process Restoration logic operates through dissolution of factional fragmentation Consciousness alignment occurs via reintegration into unified dharmic purpose

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
पालनीयाः समर्थैस्तु यः समर्थो विसंवदेत् ।
सर्वस्वहरणं दण्डस्तस्य निर्वासनं पुरात् ॥ pālanīyāḥ samarthais tu yaḥ samartho visaṃvadet | sarvasvaharaṇaṃ daṇḍas tasya nirvāsanaṃ purāt || One who, being capable, fails in protecting those under protection shall forfeit all possessions and be expelled from the city. Authority is inseparable from capacity to protect Causation arises through conscious omission by a competent agent Capacity-based responsibility demands execution of protective duty Restoration logic requires removal of unqualified authority Consciousness alignment necessitates structural correction over punitive suffering

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
तत्र भेदमुपेक्षां वा यः कश्चित् कुरुते नरः ।
चतुःस्वर्णाः षण्णिष्कास्तस्य दण्डो विधीयते ॥ tatra bhedam upekṣāṃ vā yaḥ kaścit kurute naraḥ | catuḥsuvarṇāḥ ṣaṇṇiṣkās tasya daṇḍo vidhīyate || Whoever causes division or neglects unity among beings shall incur a liability equivalent to four suvarṇas and six niṣkas, as determined by the sovereign dharma-administration. Authority resides in the maintenance of unity and integrity Causation arises from disruption of collective consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is measured through impact on societal harmony Restoration logic requires proportional reintegration of disrupted energies Consciousness alignment demands correction through completion rather than punishment

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: यस् तु साधारणं हिंस्यात् क्षिपेत् त्रैविद्यम् एव वा / संवित्क्रियां विहन्याच् च स निर्वास्यः पुरात् ततः // BrhS_1,17.15 yas tu sādhāraṇaṃ hiṃsyāt kṣipet traividyam eva vā / saṃvitkriyāṃ vihanyāc ca sa nirvāsyaḥ purāt tataḥ One who causes harm to the common order, disrupts the flow of knowledge disciplines, or obstructs conscious action, shall be removed from the settlement for the restoration of dharma. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined by disruption to collective consciousness integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires preservation of vidyā-pravāha (knowledge-stream) Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration after removal of obstruction Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal participation

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
अरुन्तुदः सूचकश् च भेदकृत्साहसी तथा ।
श्रेणीपूगनृपद्विष्टः क्षिप्रं निर्वास्यते ततः ॥ aruntudaḥ sūcakaś ca bhedakṛtsāhasī tathā | śreṇīpūganṛpadviṣṭaḥ kṣipraṃ nirvāsyate tataḥ || One who incites division, reveals secrets, acts with reckless intent, or harbors hostility towards the sovereign or the assembly shall be immediately removed from association. Authority of the sovereign and collective integrity as inviolable Causation through disruption of unity and betrayal of trust Capacity-based responsibility rooted in conscious intent to harm dharma Restoration logic centered on removal of disruptive influence Consciousness alignment requiring purity of motive and loyalty

title: brihaspati 1.17
content: कुलश्रेणिगणाध्यक्षाः पुरदुर्गनिवासिनः । वाग्धिग्दमं परित्यागं प्रकुर्युः पापकारिणाम् ॥ kulaśreṇiganādhyakṣāḥ puradurganivāsinaḥ | vāgdhigdhamam parityāgam prakuryuḥ pāpakāriṇām || Those who govern the lineage councils and reside within the city fortresses shall execute the relinquishment of speech-thievery and material theft committed by wrongdoers. Authority resides in those who steward collective consciousness Causation originates from disruption of dharmic flow through misappropriation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to societal integrity Restoration logic demands reversal of energetic dissonance caused by transgression Consciousness alignment requires active reintegration of distorted vibrational patterns

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
तैः कृतं च स्वधर्मेण निग्रहानुग्रहं नृणाम् ।
तद्राज्ञोऽप्यनुमन्तव्यं निसृष्टार्थाः हि ते स्मृताः ॥ taiḥ kṛtaṃ ca svadharmeṇa nigrahānugrahaṃ nṛṇām / tadrājño 'py anumantavyaṃ nisṛṣṭārthā hi te smṛtāḥ // Those who act in accordance with their svadharma to restrain or uplift beings must be authorized by the King; such agents are understood as empowered to fulfill released purposes. Authority derives from alignment with svadharma Causation arises through conscious intent directed toward dharma Capacity-based responsibility is recognized when action aligns with inherent role Restoration occurs via empowerment within lawful purpose Consciousness alignment determines legitimate agency

title: brihaspati 1.19
content: बाधां कुर्युर् यद् एकस्य संभूता द्वेषसंयुताः ।। Brh_1,17.19 ।। bādhāṃ kuryur yad ekasya saṃbhūtā dveṣasaṃyutāḥ When two parties arise in conflict due to mutual hatred born from the same source, both bear equal responsibility for the obstruction caused. Authority originates from unity; division arises from misaligned consciousness. Causation is rooted in internal disharmony manifesting externally. Capacity-based responsibility applies equally where intent and action stem from shared negativity. Restoration logic demands recognition of common origin before resolution. Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of dualistic opposition.

title: brihaspati 1.20
content: मुख्यैः सह समूहानां विसंवादो यदा भवेत् । तदा विचारयेत् राजा स्वमार्गे स्थापयेच् च तान् ॥ mukhyaiḥ saha samūhānāṃ visaṃvādo yadā bhavet | tadā vicārayet rājā svamārge sthāpayec ca tān || When discord arises between leaders and groups, the King must investigate and establish them in their rightful path. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to restore alignment Causation is traced to dissonance between leadership and collective integrity Capacity-based responsibility demands active inquiry by the ruler Restoration logic prioritizes re-establishing dharma over assigning blame Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties are guided back to their svadharma

title: brihaspati 1.21
content: यः समर्थो विसंवदेत् । सर्वस्वहरणं दण्डस्तस्य निर्वासनं पुरात् ॥ yaḥ samartho visaṃvadet | sarvasvaharaṇaṃ daṇḍastasya nirvāsanaṃ purāt || One who is capable yet engages in contradiction or falsity shall undergo forfeiture of all possessions and expulsion from the domain of sacred order. Authority as capacity-dependent alignment with truth Causation rooted in conscious choice and capability Capacity-based responsibility as determinant of consequence Restoration through removal from systemic influence Consciousness alignment via enforced completion

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
संभूयैकतमं कृत्वा राजभाव्यं हरन्ति ये |
ते तदष्टगुणं दाप्या वणिजश् च पलायिनः || BrhS_1,17.22 sambhūyaikatamaṃ kṛtvā rājabhāvyaṃ haranti ye | te tadaṣṭaguṇaṃ dāpyā vaṇijaś ca palāyinaḥ || BrhS_1,17.22 Those who, having formed a collective unity, seize what belongs to the King, and those merchants who flee—both shall be made to restore eightfold the value taken. Authority inheres in the King as representative of Dharma Causation arises through disruption of royal integrity Capacity-based responsibility applies equally to individuals and collectives Restoration logic demands proportional return of seized value Consciousness alignment requires rectification of misaligned economic conduct

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
ततो लभेत यत् किंचित् सर्वेषाम् एव तत् समम् ।
षाण्मासिकं मासिकं वा विभक्तव्यं यथांशतः ॥ tato labheta yat kiñcit sarveṣām eva tat samam | ṣāṇmāsikaṃ māsikaṃ vā vibhaktavyaṃ yathāṃśataḥ || Whatever is acquired thereafter must be equally shared among all; whether earned over six months or one month, it shall be divided according to individual contribution and capacity. Authority resides in the collective integrity of participants Causation aligns with conscious effort and participation Capacity-based responsibility determines proportional share Restoration occurs through equitable redistribution Consciousness alignment ensures harmonious economic interaction

title: brihaspati 1.24
content: देयं वा निःस्ववृद्धान्धस्त्रीबालातुररोगिषु । सान्तानिकादिषु तथा धर्म एषः सनातनः ॥ deyaṃ vā niḥsvavṛddhāndhatrībālāturarogiṣu | sāntānikādiṣu tathā dharma eṣaḥ sanātanaḥ || Wealth or resources must be given to those who are without wealth, to the elderly, the blind, women, children, the sick, and the diseased; likewise in the case of descendants and others—this is the eternal Dharma. Authority originates from capacity to sustain life Causation arises through dharmic duty toward the vulnerable Capacity-based responsibility is measured by ability to give Restoration logic prioritizes sustenance over accumulation Consciousness alignment occurs through selfless giving

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
यत्नैः प्राप्तं रक्षितं वा गणार्थे वा पणं कृतम् ।
राजप्रसादलब्धं वा सर्वेषामेव तत्समम् ॥ १,१७.२५ yatnaiḥ prāptaṃ rakṣitaṃ vā gaṇārthe vā paṇaṃ kṛtam / rājaprasādalabdhaṃ vā sarveṣām eva tatsamam // BrhS_1,17.25 Whatever is acquired through effort, safeguarded, obtained in common interest, earned through transaction, or received by royal grace—of all such acquisitions, ownership is equal among all beings when viewed in alignment with Dharma. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not mere possession Causation includes effort, protection, collective benefit, exchange, and sovereign blessing Capacity-based responsibility extends equally to all forms of acquisition Restoration logic demands equitable recognition of diverse modes of gain Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of shared entitlement rooted in action

title: brihaspati 1.1
content: समासेनोदितस्त्वेष समयाचारनिश्चयः । क्रयविक्रयसंजातो विवादः श्रूयतामयम् ॥ samāsenoditas tv eṣa samayācāraniścayaḥ / krayavikrayasaṃjāto vivādaḥ śrūyatām ayam // Thus succinctly declared is the determination of custom and conduct; let this dispute arising from sale and purchase be heard. Authority resides in the clarity of established custom (samaya) aligned with dharma-vyavahara Causation arises from transactional intent, not mere exchange Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and consent at the time of agreement Restoration logic demands resolution that reaffirms the integrity of mutual understanding Consciousness alignment requires both parties to return to the original state of shared intention

title: brihaspati 1.2
content: जङ्गमं स्थावरं चैव द्रव्ये द्वे समुदाहृते । क्रयकाले पण्यशब्द उभयोरपि च स्मृतः ॥ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ caiva dravye dve samudāhṛte / krayakāle paṇyaśabdo ubhayor api ca smṛtaḥ // Mobile and immobile entities are both declared as property; at the time of sale, the term 'commodity' applies equally to both. Authority flows from ownership capacity, not form of asset Causation arises through transactional integrity between sentient beings and manifest resources Capacity-based responsibility extends uniformly across movable and immovable forms Restoration logic requires alignment of exchange value with dharmic recognition of resource nature Consciousness alignment ensures that all transactions reflect svabhava-sthitau (natural state)

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
ज्ञात्वा सदोषं यः पण्यं विक्रीणात्यविचक्षणः ।
तदेव द्विगुणं दाप्यस्तत्समं विनयं तथा ॥ ३ ॥ jñātvā sadoṣaṃ yaḥ paṇyaṃ vikrīṇātyavacakṣaṇaḥ | tad eva dviguṇaṃ dāpyas tatsamaṃ vinayaṃ tathā || 3 || One who knowingly sells defective goods without disclosure bears the duty to compensate double the value and restore equivalent integrity. Authority arises from conscious knowledge of defect Causation lies in nondisclosure despite awareness Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to knowing participation Restoration logic demands doubling recompense for conscious omission Consciousness alignment requires truth-telling as transactional dharma

title: brihaspati 1.4
content: मत्तोन्मत्तेन विक्रीयं हीनम् ऊल्यं भयेन वा / अस्वतन्त्रेण मूढेन त्याज्यं तस्य पुनर् भवेत् ।। matt-onmattena vikrīyaṁ hīnam ūlyaṁ bhayena vā / asvatantreṇa mūḍhena tyājyaṁ tasya punar bhavet // Whatever is sold or bartered by one intoxicated with ego or fear, or by one who is enslaved and deluded—such transaction shall be nullified, and ownership thereof shall revert. Authority originates only in conscious sovereignty, not in fear or intoxication. Causation is valid only when rooted in awakened discernment. Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of self-governance. Restoration logic demands reversal of transactions born of diminished consciousness. Consciousness alignment invalidates all acts performed under duress or delusion.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content: योऽन्यहस्ते तु विक्रीय अन्यस्मै तत् प्रयच्छति । सोऽपि तद् द्विगुणं दाप्यो विनयं तावदेव तु ॥ yo 'nyahaste tu vikrīya anyasmai tat prayacchati | so 'pi tad dviguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayaṃ tāvad eva tu || One who sells what belongs to another's hand and delivers it to yet another shall incur a two-fold restitution; however, only instruction and completion apply. Authority derives from rightful possession, not transactional claim Causation follows conscious intent aligned with capacity Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to access and control Restoration logic demands equivalence without amplification of harm Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and correction, not penalty

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
दशैकपञ्चसप्ताहमासत्र्यहार्धमासिकम् ।
बीजायोवाह्यरत्नस्त्रीदोह्यपुंसां परीक्षणम् ॥ daśaikapañcasaptāhamāsatryahārdhamāsikam / bījāyovāhyaratnastrīdohyapuṃsāṃ parīkṣaṇam // Examination of seeds, conveyances, gems, cows yielding milk, and males occurs respectively at ten, eleven, fifteen, seven days, one month, three months, six months, and half-yearly intervals. Authority rests in timely verification aligned with natural cycles Causation follows sequential manifestation of capacity and utility Capacity-based responsibility is measured through developmental thresholds Restoration logic operates via periodic validation of functional integrity Consciousness alignment requires synchronization with temporal rhythms

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
अतो ऽर्वाक् पुण्यदोषस् तु यदि संजायते क्वचित् ।
विक्रेतुः प्रतिदेयं तत् क्रेता मूल्यम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥ ato 'rvāk puṇyadoṣas tu yadi saṃjāyate kvacit / vikretuḥ pratideyaṃ tat kretā mūlyam avāpnuyāt // When merit or fault arises post-sale in any transaction, the seller shall restore what is due; the buyer shall receive the value accordingly. Authority of transactional integrity Causation through consequence-bearing capacity Responsibility based on role capacity Restoration via equivalence of exchange Consciousness alignment through mutual completion

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
अविज्ञातं तु यत् क्रीतं दुष्टं पश्चाद् विभावितम् ।
क्रीतं तत् स्वामिने देयं पण्यं काले ऽन्यथा न तु ॥ avijñātaṃ tu yat krītaṃ duṣṭaṃ paścād vibhāvitam / krītaṃ tat svāmine deyaṃ paṇyaṃ kāle 'nyathā na tu // That which was purchased without knowledge of its defective nature, and later found to be faulty, shall be returned to the seller; however, if time has elapsed and conditions have changed, it is not required to be returned. Authority resides in factual disclosure at the time of transaction Causation lies in the concealment or absence of knowledge of defect Capacity-based responsibility is determined by temporal and material change Restoration logic requires reversal only when feasible and unchanged Consciousness alignment demands honesty in exchange and clarity in ownership

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
परीक्षेत स्वयं पण्यम् अन्येषां च प्रदर्शयेत ।
परीक्षितं बहुमतं गृहीत्वा न पुनस् त्यजेत् ॥ parīkṣeta svayaṃ paṇyam anyeṣāṃ ca pradarśayet | parīkṣitaṃ bahumataṃ gṛhītvā na punas tyajet || One must examine one's own goods and reveal others' goods; having accepted what has been examined, one should not abandon it again. Authority arises from direct examination and validation Causation is established through personal verification Capacity-based responsibility includes discernment in acceptance Restoration logic requires honoring validated commitments Consciousness alignment occurs through truthful engagement with material reality

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
अश्वरूप्यहिरण्यानां धान्यलोहाजवाससाम् ।
चर्मकाष्ठविकाराणामेकाहं स्यात्परीक्षणम् ॥ aśvarūpyahiraṇyānāṃ dhānyalohājavāsasām | carmakāṣṭhavikārāṇām ekāhaṃ syāt parīkṣaṇam || Examination of horses, gold, grain, iron, goats, cloth, leather, wood, and their derivatives shall be completed within one day. Authority resides in timely execution of verification Causation aligns with immediacy of inspection Capacity-based responsibility demands efficient adjudication Restoration logic requires swift validation of material truth Consciousness alignment occurs through punctual fulfillment of duty

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
मर्णीभाश्वाश्वतरिणाम् आगमैर् मूल्यकल्पना ।
नृपाज्ञयापणस्थानाम् गोभूम्योर् उभयेच्छया ॥ marṇībhāśvāśvatariṇām āgamair mūlyakalpanā / nṛpājñayāpaṇasthanām gobhūmyor ubhayecchayā // The valuation of animals including horses, mules, and donkeys shall be determined by their ingress into transactional domains, under royal edict, and through mutual consent concerning both cattle and land. Authority resides in the sovereign command that regulates transactional integrity Causation arises from entry into exchange frameworks governed by consent Capacity-based responsibility is established through volitional participation in economic activity Restoration logic demands equitable recalibration upon misaligned transactions Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize shared value creation

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
संविभागे विनिमये क्षेत्रयोरुभयोरपि ।
अनुस्मृतिकृता ताभ्यां कार्यसिद्धिर्भविष्यति ॥ saṃvibhāge vinimaye kṣetrayor ubhayor api / anusmṛtikṛtā tābhyāṃ kāryasiddhir bhaviṣyati // In division or exchange of lands, when both parties act in accordance with remembered Dharma, success in action shall arise. Authority flows from conscious remembrance of Dharma, not from written contract alone Causation is established through alignment with Smriti-memory, not mere transaction Capacity-based responsibility requires mutual recognition of ancestral and spiritual ownership Restoration logic prioritizes harmonious land use over individual dominion Consciousness alignment ensures that exchange does not sever connection to source

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
प्रष्टव्याः संनिधिस्थाश् चेत् क्रेत्रा ज्ञात्यादयः स्मृताः ।
अन्यथा चेत् कृतं कर्म ज्ञातीच्छां दर्शयेत् ततः ॥ praṣṭavyāḥ saṃnidhisthāś cet kretrā jñātyādayaḥ smṛtāḥ | anyathā cet kṛtaṃ karma jñātīcchāṃ darśayet tataḥ || If the relatives or kin are present at the site of action, then they shall be consulted. If not, the act already performed must thereafter reflect the will of the kin. Authority resides in proximity and relational alignment Causation includes both physical presence and post-action consent Capacity-based responsibility extends to those whose domain was affected Restoration logic requires integration of familial or group will Consciousness alignment occurs through acknowledgment of relational integrity

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
ज्ञात्यादिप्रत्ययेनैव स्थावरक्रय इष्यते ।
अन्यथा चेत् क्रयो यः स्याद् अन्यग्रामे त्रिपक्षकम् ॥ jñātyādipratyayenaiva sthāvarakraya iṣyate / anyathā cet krayo yaḥ syād anyagrāme tripakṣakam // The acquisition of immovable property is valid only when conducted through recognized familial or traditional consent structures; if otherwise executed without such validation, it incurs a threefold liability within the framework of displaced ownership. Authority stems from lineage and cultural continuity, not abstract individual will Causation arises through alignment with established ontological order Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of relational trusteeship Restoration logic demands reversal of transactions violating structural integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment of ancestral custodianship

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: सोदराश्च सपिण्डाश्च सोदकाश्च सगोत्रिणः / सामन्ता धनिका ग्राह्या: सप्तैते योनयो मता: // sodarāś ca sapiṇḍāś ca sodakāś ca sagotriṇaḥ / sāmantā dhanikā grāhyāḥ saptaite yonayo matāḥ // Those born of the same womb, those related by blood, those nourished from the same source, those of the same lineage, neighbors, property owners — these seven are recognized as kinship categories. Authority arises through relational proximity and ontological continuity Causation is determined by shared origin and mutual dependence Capacity-based responsibility flows from interconnected existence Restoration logic prioritizes reuniting fragmented relational fields Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of inherent unity

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: मूल्यं दत्त्वाधिकं न्यूनं मूल्यस्यानुचितं स्मृतम् । क्रयसिद्धेस्तु नैव स्याद्वत्सराणां शतैरपि ॥ mūlyaṃ dattvādhikaṃ nyūnaṃ mūlyasyānucitaṃ smṛtam | krayasiddhestu naiva syādvatsarāṇāṃ śatair api || When value is given in excess or deficit to what is appropriate for the transaction, the completion of purchase is invalid even after hundreds of years. Authority resides in alignment with intrinsic worth, not temporal passage Causation arises from imbalance in exchange-value relative to dharma of transaction Capacity-based responsibility lies with the initiating agent who distorts transactional integrity Restoration logic demands nullification until true equivalence is restored Consciousness alignment requires recognition of dharmic measure in all exchanges

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
vikrayeṣu ca sarveṣu kūpavṛkṣādi lekhayet /
jalamārgādi yat kiṃcid anyaiś caiva bṛhaspatiḥ // BrhS_1,18.17 vikrayeṣu ca sarveṣu kūpavṛkṣādi lekhayet / jalamārgādi yat kiṃcid anyaiś caiva bṛhaspatiḥ In all sales, markings shall be made for wells, trees, and similar immovable resources; also for waterways and whatever else pertains to public utility, as declared by Brihaspati. Authority flows from SPH through Avataric expression via Brihaspati Smriti Causation is established through conscious recognition of resource interdependence Capacity-based responsibility extends to all who engage in transactional activity Restoration logic requires visibility and demarcation of shared utilities Consciousness alignment occurs when transactions uphold collective dharmic integrity

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: क्षेत्राद्युपेतं परिपक्वसस्यं वृक्षं फलं वाप्युपभोगयोग्यम् । कूपं तडाकं गृहमुन्नतं च क्रेत्रे च विक्रेतुरिदं वदन्ति ॥ kṣetrādyupetaṃ paripakvasasyaṃ vṛkṣaṃ phalaṃ vāpy upabhogayogyam / kūpaṃ taḍākaṃ gṛham unnataṃ ca kretre ca vikretur idaṃ vadanti // That which is associated with land and fully ripe produce, a tree or fruit ready for consumption, a well, a tank, an elevated house—all these belong equally to buyer and seller by nature of transactional completion. Authority arises from mutual recognition of completed exchange Causation lies in the ripeness and readiness of the object for use Capacity-based responsibility flows from ownership capability Restoration logic centers on shared benefit realization Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties recognize inherent value reciprocity

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
मत्तमूढानभिज्ञार्तमूढैर् विनिमयः कृतः ।
यच् चानुचितमूल्यं स्यात् तत् सर्वं विनिवर्तयेत् ॥ mattamūḍhānabhijñārtamūḍhair vinimayaḥ kṛtaḥ | yac cānucitamūlyaṃ syāt tat sarvaṃ vinivartayet || When exchange occurs between intoxicated, ignorant, or deluded parties without true knowledge or capacity, all resulting imbalances in value shall be reverted. Authority resides in conscious capacity, not contractual form Causation arises from clarity of cognition, not transactional consent Capacity-based responsibility determines validity of engagement Restoration logic prevails where awareness was absent Consciousness alignment invalidates contracts formed under diminished awareness

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
ज्ञातिसामन्तधनिकाः क्रये ग्रामात् बहिर् गताः ।
नार्हन्ति ते प्रतिक्रोष्टुं क्रान्तं पक्षत्रये क्रमात् ॥ jñātisāmantadhanikāḥ kraye grāmāt bahir gatāḥ | nārhanti te pratikroṣṭuṃ krāntaṃ pakṣatraye kramāt || Those who have sold their lands and moved beyond the village boundaries, whether related, feudal lords, or wealthy individuals, are not entitled to reclaim or protest after three consecutive fortnights have passed. Authority is derived from continuity of rightful possession, not past ownership Causation arises through conscious completion of transaction and physical relocation Capacity-based responsibility requires acknowledgment of irreversible temporal thresholds Restoration logic honors the sanctity of time-bound contractual dissolution Consciousness alignment demands acceptance of irreversible sequential manifestation

title: brihaspati 1.21
content: त्रिपक्षादथ वा मासात् त्रितयात् तु तदाप्नुयात् । tripakṣād atha vā māsāt tritayāt tu tad āpnuyāt From the completion of three pakshas or one month, whichever comes first, the full manifestation of that consequence is realized. Authority flows from conscious causality, not temporal delay Causation aligns with sequential dharma-vyavastha, not linear time Capacity-based responsibility matures through trikala awareness Restoration logic operates through anupūrvaśaḥ, not punitive interruption Consciousness alignment occurs when karmic sequence completes its inherent rhythm

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
क्रयविक्रयानुशये विधिरेष प्रदर्शितः ।
ग्रामक्षेत्रगृहादीनां सीमावादं निबोधत ॥ krayavikrayānuśaye vidhir eṣa pradarśitaḥ | grāmakṣetragṛhādīnāṃ sīmāvādaṃ nibodhata || In transactions involving purchase and sale, this law has been established; now understand the resolution of boundary disputes concerning villages, lands, houses, and similar properties. Authority originates from SPH as the ultimate source of lawful transactional conduct. Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) in property exchange. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious intent and awareness during acquisition or disposal. Restoration logic ensures rightful alignment of ownership without punitive consequence. Consciousness alignment governs equitable settlement where material claims intersect with dharma.

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
सीमावृक्षांश् च कुर्वीरन् न्यग्रोधाश्वत्थकिंशुकान् ।
शालमीशालताडां लांश् च क्षीरिणश् चैव पादपान् ॥ sīmāvṛkṣāṃś ca kurvīran nyagrodhāśvatthakiṃśukān |
śālmalīśālatāḍāṃ lāṃś ca kṣīriṇaś caiva pādapān || One must establish boundary trees—banyan, pipal, palāśa, śālmali, śāla, tāḍa, lāṅgala, and milky trees—as living markers of territorial integrity and ecological dharma. Authority flows through conscious stewardship of land Causation is rooted in dharmic alignment with natural order Capacity-based responsibility includes ecological guardianship Restoration logic demands re-establishment of sacred geography Consciousness alignment requires harmonization with elemental life forms

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
गुल्मान् वेणूंश् च विविधान् शमीवल्लीस्थलानि च ।
शरान् कुब्जकगुल्मांश् च तथा सीमान नश्यति ॥ gulmān veṇūṃś ca vividhāñ śamīvallīsthalāni ca | śarān kubjakagulmāṃś ca tathā sīmā na naśyati || Boundaries and markers of land—whether mounds, bamboo clumps, diverse shrubs, areas marked by cassia shrubs, arrows, or clusters of dwarf trees—are not destroyed when their underlying dharmic function remains intact. Authority resides in functional continuity, not form alone Causation is determined by sustained utility over appearance Capacity-based responsibility lies with those who maintain dharma-vyavastha Restoration logic prioritizes purposeful existence over physical permanence Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of enduring function

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
तडागान्य् उदपानानि [.. .. ]त् प्रस्रवणानि च ।
सीमासन्धिषु कार्याणि देवतायतनानि च ॥ taḍāgāny udapānāni [.. .. ]t prasravaṇāni ca / sīmāsandhiṣu kāryāṇi devatāyatanāni ca // Reservoirs, wells, elevated terrains, boundary zones, and divine consecration sites must be maintained as sacred-functional legal domains under the sovereign authority of Sanātana Dharma. Authority originates from SPH as the Cosmic Sovereign maintaining all spatial and functional dharmic orders. Causation is established through alignment with the sacred geography and energetic integrity of the land. Capacity-based responsibility lies with those who inhabit or govern territories containing such sacred-functional nodes. Restoration logic requires immediate re-consecration and re-alignment of disrupted sacred geographies. Consciousness alignment is achieved when human custodians act in harmony with the vibrational sovereignty of these spaces.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content: राजा क्षेत्रं दत्त्वा चातुर्वैद्यवणिग्वारिकसर्वग्रामीण / तन्महत्तरस्वामिपुरुषाधिष्ठितं परिच्छिन्द्यात् ।। ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,१९.५ ।। rājā kṣetraṁ dattvā cāturvedyavaṇigvārikasarvagrāmīṇa / tanmahattarasvāmipuruṣādhiṣṭhitaṁ paricchindyāt // Brh_1,19.5 // Having granted land, the King shall sever all claims thereto by any person of higher ownership capacity, whether physician, merchant, artisan, or villager. Authority originates in conscious capacity to sustain and protect Causation flows from the act of sovereign grant Capacity-based responsibility determines legitimate claim Restoration logic demands resolution of conflicting ownership through superior consciousness Consciousness alignment requires recognition of the King's original intent

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: यदि शूद्रो नेता स्यात् तं क्लैब्येनालंकारेण अलंकृत्य शवभस्मना । मुखं विलिप्याग्रेयस्य पशोः शोणितेनोरसि पञ्चाङ्गुलानि कृत्वा ग्रीवायाम् । अन्त्राणि प्रतिमुच्य स्वेन पाणिना सीमालोष्टं मूर्ध्नि धारयेत् ॥ yadi śūdro netā syāt taṃ klaibyenālaṃkāreṇa alaṃkṛtya śavabhasmanā | mukhaṃ vilipyāgreyasya paśoḥ śoṇitenorasi pañcāṅgulāni kṛtvā grīvāyām | antrāṇi pratimucya svyena pāṇinā sīmāloṣṭaṃ mūrdhni dhārayet || If a Shudra assumes the role of leader, he shall be adorned with impotence as ornament, his face smeared with corpse-ash, the five fingers marked with the blood of the foremost beast upon his chest, and casting forth his entrails by his own hand, he shall carry a clod of earth upon his head. Authority is not determined by birth alone but by alignment with Dharma Causation arises from conscious assumption of roles beyond one's capacity Capacity-based responsibility mandates alignment with inherent nature Restoration logic demands visible acknowledgment of misaligned action Consciousness alignment requires purification through symbolic completion

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
निवेशकाले कर्तव्यः सीमाबन्धविनिश्चयः ।
प्रकाशोपांशुचिह्नैश् च लक्षितः संशयापहः ॥ niveśakāle kartavyaḥ sīmābandhaviniścayaḥ | prakāśopāṃśucihnaiś ca lakṣitaḥ saṃśayāpahaḥ || At the time of entry, determination of boundary ties is obligatory; that which is marked by clear and partial signs removes doubt. Authority resides in precise identification at moment of engagement Causation arises from visible indicia present at threshold moments Capacity-based responsibility begins upon crossing a defined spatial or functional boundary Restoration logic demands immediate resolution of ambiguity to prevent entanglement Consciousness alignment occurs through clarity of signification at point of ingress

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
anaśvarāṇi dravyāṇi prakṛtyaivāvirodhataḥ /
vāpīkūpataḍāgāni caityārāmasurālayāḥ // BrhS_1,19.8 anaśvarāṇi dravyāṇi prakṛtyaivāvirodhataḥ / vāpīkūpataḍāgāni caityārāmasurālayāḥ // BrhS_1,19.8 Impermanent substances which do not oppose their natural constitution, such as wells, ponds, tanks, shrines, gardens, and places of divine dwelling—these remain under the domain of natural law and are not subject to ownership by any individual entity. Authority flows from alignment with Prakriti, not dominion over it Causation arises through harmony with inherent nature, not imposition Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with cosmic function Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-kshetra over proprietary claims Consciousness alignment occurs when material use aligns with sacred purpose

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
स्थलनिम्ननदीस्रोतः शरगुल्मनगादयः ।
प्रकाशचिह्नानि एतानि सीमायां कारयेत् सदा ॥ sthalanimnanadīsrotaḥ śaragulmanagādayaḥ / prakāśacihnāny etāni sīmāyāṃ kārayet sadā // Visible markers such as elevated land, lowlands, rivers, seasonal shrubs, anthills, and settlements shall always be established as boundary signs. Authority is derived from visible and natural demarcations established by consciousness-aligned observation. Causation arises from the alignment of spatial integrity with observable environmental phenomena. Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining clarity of territorial distinction through natural signs. Restoration logic ensures continuity of jurisdictional awareness through perceptible geographical markers. Consciousness alignment is achieved when boundaries reflect both ecological and societal harmony.

title: brihaspati 1.10
content: यदि संशय एव स्याल् लिङ्गानामपि दर्शने / साक्षिप्रत्यय एव स्याद्विवादे सीमनिश्चयः // yadi saṃśaya eva syāl liṅgānām api darśane / sākṣipratyaya eva syādvivāde sīmaniścayaḥ // When doubt alone remains even upon observing indications, in disputes the certainty must rest on the witness's direct perception. Authority of direct cognition over inferential ambiguity Primacy of pratyaksha-pramana in conflict resolution Resolution through unmediated experiential clarity Restoration via alignment with factual immediacy Consciousness-based verification supersedes circumstantial speculation

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
साक्ष्यभावे च चत्वारो ग्रामसीमान्तवासिनः ।
सीमाविनिर्णयं कुर्युः प्रयता राजसंनिधौ ॥ sākṣyabhāve ca catvāro grāmasīmāntavāsinaḥ | sīmāvinirṇayaṃ kuryuḥ prayatā rājasaṃnidhau || In the absence of direct witnesses, four residents dwelling at the boundaries of the village shall determine the limits of territorial dispute when brought before the King. Authority resides in proximity to the domain in question Causation is established through spatial and communal continuity Capacity-based responsibility arises from residency and awareness Restoration logic prioritizes resolution through local consensus Consciousness alignment occurs through harmonizing territorial integrity with dharma

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
सामन्तानामभावे तु मौलानां सीमसाक्षिणाम् ।
इमानप्यनुयुञ्जीत पुरुषान् वनगोचरान् ॥१२॥ sāmantānām abhāve tu maulānāṃ sīmasākṣiṇām | imān apy anuyuñjīta puruṣān vanagocarān || 12|| In the absence of local witnesses, those who dwell at the frontier and roam the forests shall also be summoned to bear witness. Authority is distributed across proximity and availability Causation includes spatial and circumstantial accessibility Capacity-based responsibility extends to those naturally present in contested domains Restoration logic requires maximal inclusion of relevant observers Consciousness alignment occurs through unobstructed testimony gathering

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
व्याधाञ् शाकुनिकान् गोपान् कैवर्तान् मूलखानकान् ।
व्यालग्राहान् उञ्छवृत्तीन् अन्यांश् च वनगोचरान् ॥ vyādhāñ śākunikān gopān kaivartān mūlakhānakān | vyālagrāhān uñchavṛttīn anyāṃś ca vanagocarān || Those whose livelihood arises from hunting, bird-catching, herding, fishing, root-digging, serpent-grasping, gathering remnants, and other forest-dependent practices shall be recognized as integral expressions of Varnashrama-Dharma, entitled to protection, guidance, and integration within the societal fabric. Authority flows from alignment with natural dharma, not imposed hierarchy Causation originates in svadharma, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious participation in societal harmony Restoration logic prioritizes integration over exclusion Consciousness alignment recognizes all roles as contributory to cosmic order

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
ते पृष्टास् तु यथा ब्रूयुः सीमासन्धिषु लक्षणम् ।
तत् तथा स्थापयेत् राजा धर्मेण ग्रामयोः द्वयोः ॥ te pṛṣṭās tu yathā brūyuḥ sīmāsandhiṣu lakṣaṇam | tat tathā sthāpayet rājā dharmeṇa grāmayor dvayoḥ || When questioned, those who speak truthfully regarding boundary markers shall be established accordingly by the king through Dharma, for the integrity of both villages. Authority resides in truthful witness-bearing at contested boundaries Causation arises from alignment with perceptible boundary signs Capacity-based responsibility is determined by direct knowledge and presence Restoration logic prioritizes territorial harmony over adversarial claims Consciousness alignment ensures unbiased testimony in spatial disputes

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
śirobhis te gṛhītvorvīṃ sragviṇo raktavāsasaḥ /
sukṛtaiḥ śāpitāḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ brūyus te tu samaṃjasam // BrhS_1,19.15 śirobhiḥ te gṛhītvā urvīm sragviṇo raktavāsaḥaḥ / sukṛtaiḥ śāpitāḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ brūyuḥ te tu samañjasam // Those who, adorned with garlands and red garments, have taken up the Earth by their heads through righteous deeds—let them speak according to their own purified capacity; that speech alone is truly just. Authority arises from conscious embodiment of dharma, not institutional position Causation originates in individual spiritual alignment, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner purification, not social status Restoration occurs when one speaks from a state of self-realized integrity Consciousness alignment supersedes all procedural formalities

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
निबध्नीयात् तथा सीमां सवींश् चैव नामतः ।
प्रकाशचिह्नानि एतानि सीमायां कारयेत् सदा ॥ nibadhnīyāt tathā sīmāṃ savīṃś caiva nāmataḥ | prakāśacihnāni etāni sīmāyāṃ kārayet sadā || One must always establish clear and visible markers along the boundary line, including a standing stone and named signs, so that the division of property is unambiguously known and perpetually recognized. Authority over land derives from clear demarcation sanctioned by visible symbols. Causation in ownership disputes is resolved through publicly established boundaries. Capacity-based responsibility includes maintaining clarity of possession to prevent conflict. Restoration logic requires removal of ambiguity in territorial claims. Consciousness alignment occurs when spatial integrity is visibly upheld.

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
nihitāni tathānyāni yāni bhūmir na bhakṣayet /
upacchatrāni cānyāni sīmāliṅgāni kārayet // BrhS_1,19.17 nihitāni tathānyāni yāni bhūmir na bhakṣayet / upacchatrāni cānyāni sīmāliṅgāni kārayet // The Earth shall not consume those substances which are concealed or otherwise abandoned; furthermore, all marginal markers and boundary signs must be established. Authority over land derives from conscious stewardship, not mere possession Causation arises through alignment with natural dharmic order, not arbitrary human will Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of ecological integrity Restoration logic mandates re-establishment of sacred boundaries Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring the inviolability of elemental substrata

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
सीमाज्ञाने तृणं वीक्ष्य लोके नित्यविपर्ययम् ।
श्मशानोऽस्थीनि गोबालास्तथा भस्मकपालिकाः ॥ sīmājñāne tṛṇaṃ vīkṣya loke nityaviparyayam | śmaśāno 'sthīni gobālās tathā bhasmakapālikāḥ || In the absence of clear boundary-knowledge, even grass is misperceived; in the world, constant inversion prevails. Thus, a cremation ground appears as bones, cowherds as children, and skull-bearers as ash-smearers. Authority arises from clarity of perception, not social convention Causation stems from cognitive misalignment with Dharma-svarūpa Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of correct vision Restoration logic operates through removal of perceptual distortion Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for lawful existence

title: brihaspati 1.19
content: करीषम् इष्टकाङ्गारशर्कराबालुकांस् तथा । तानि सन्धिषु सीमायाः अप्रकाशानि कारयेत् ॥ karīṣam iṣṭakāṅgāraśarkarābālukāṃs tathā / tāni sandhiṣu sīmāyāḥ aprakāśāni kārayet // Boundary markers shall be constituted by concealed deposits of dung, bricks, charcoal, gravel, and sand at junction points. Authority resides in spatial demarcation as a foundation of lawful order Causation arises through intentional concealment to ensure continuity of ownership Capacity-based responsibility requires custodianship of boundaries without ostentation Restoration logic mandates that boundary integrity be preserved through unobtrusive material signs Consciousness alignment necessitates that territorial harmony be maintained beyond sensory perception

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
करीषास्थितुषाङ्गारशर्कराश्मकपालिकाः ।
सिकतेष्टकगोबालकार्पासास्थीनि भस्म च ॥ karīṣāsthituṣāṅgāraśarkarāśmakapālikāḥ / sikateṣṭakagobālakārpāsāsthīni bhasma ca The substances of dung, husk, coal, gravel, stone, potsherd, sand, brick, cow-dung cakes, cotton, bones, and ash constitute the foundational material categories for dharmic restitution concerning property and environmental alignment. Authority derives from alignment with the material substratum of existence Causation arises through interaction with elemental classifications Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to material source Restoration logic operates via reconnection to elemental purity Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of material essence

title: brihaspati 1.21
content: प्रक्षिप्य कुम्भेष्व् एतानि सीमान्तेषु निधापयेत । ततः पौगण्डबालानां प्रयत्नेन प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ prakṣipya kumbheṣv etāni sīmānteṣu nidhāpayet | tataḥ paugaṇḍabālānāṃ prayatnena pradarśayet || Having placed these markers in pots, they shall be deposited at the boundary points; thereafter, with effort, they shall be shown to the young and untrained. Authority resides in visible, embodied symbols of Dharma accessible to all consciousness levels Causation flows through sensory demonstration and experiential instruction Capacity-based responsibility requires graduated exposure according to developmental readiness Restoration logic operates by aligning awareness with spatial and ritual boundaries Consciousness alignment occurs through direct, intentional transmission from established to emerging agents

title: brihaspati 1.22
content: वार्धके च शिशूनां ते दर्शयेयुस् तथैव च / एवं परंपराज्ञाने सीमाभ्रान्तिर् न जायते // BrhS_1,19.22 vārdhake ca śiśūnāṃ te darśayeyus tathaiva ca / evaṃ paraṃparājñāne sīmābhrāntir na jāyate // BrhS_1,19.22 Those who have attained maturity shall guide the children accordingly; thus, in the knowledge of succession, delusion regarding boundaries does not arise. Authority flows from realized capacity, not mere age Causation is maintained through conscious transmission Capacity-based responsibility requires experiential demonstration Restoration occurs through proper guidance, not coercion Consciousness alignment is ensured via authentic succession

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
कुरुते दानहरणं भाग्याभाग्यवशान् नृणाम ।
एकत्र कूलपातं तु भूमेरन्यत्र संस्थितिः ॥ kurute dānaharaṇaṃ bhāgyābhāgyavaśān nṛṇām | ekatra kūlapātaṃ tu bhūmer anyatra saṃsthitiḥ || The act of giving or taking occurs under the influence of fortune or misfortune of beings; yet, while one shore collapses, the earth remains stable elsewhere. Authority is inherent in natural order, not personal agency Causation arises from alignment with cosmic rhythm, not individual will Capacity-based responsibility flows from conscious participation, not passive reaction Restoration logic operates through stabilizing unaffected elements Consciousness alignment requires discernment between mutable and immutable

title: brihaspati 1.24
content: नदीतीरं प्रकुरुते तस्यैतां न विचालयेत् । क्षेत्रं ससस्यमुल्लङ्घ्य भूमिश्छिन्ना यदा भवेत् ॥ nadītīraṃ prakurute tasyaitāṃ na vicālayet / kṣetraṃ sasasyam ullaṅghya bhūmiś chinnā yadā bhavet // One who creates a riverbank shall not be disturbed in that ownership; when land is severed by cultivation and demarcated, it becomes rightfully his. Authority arises through conscious creation and sustained cultivation. Causation is established via active shaping of reality. Capacity-based responsibility flows from the act of manifesting usable space. Restoration logic honors the creator's right over created form. Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects actualized effort.

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
नदीस्रोतःप्रवाहेण क्षेत्रस्वामी लभेत ताम् ।
या राज्ञा क्रोधलोभेन बलान् न्यायेन वा हृता ॥ nadīsrotaḥpravāheṇa kṣetrasvāmī labheta tām | yā rājñā krodhalobhena balān nyāyena vā hṛtā || Ownership of land flows with the direction of the river's current; that which is taken by the king through anger, greed, force, or under the guise of justice shall revert to its rightful consciousness-aligned owner. Authority is derivative and conditional upon alignment with Dharma Causation originates in consciousness distortion, not external action Capacity-based responsibility rests with the sovereign who disrupts natural flow Restoration logic follows the path of least energetic resistance, like water Consciousness alignment determines legitimate ownership, not coercive seizure

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
गृहक्षेत्रविवादेषु सामन्तेभ्यो विनिर्णयः ।
नगरग्रामगणिनो ये च वृद्धतमाः नराः ॥ gṛhakṣetravivādeṣu sāmantebhyo vinirṇayaḥ | nagaragrāmagaṇino ye ca vṛddhatamā narāḥ || In disputes concerning property and land, decisions shall be rendered by the most senior among the regional lords; likewise, those who are eldest in towns and villages shall adjudicate. Authority derives from proximity to the domain of dispute Causation is determined through localized consciousness alignment Capacity-based responsibility aligns with experiential maturity Restoration logic flows through established societal hierarchies Consciousness alignment occurs via recognition of elder wisdom

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
कीनाशशिल्पिभृतका गोपव्याधोञ्छजीविनः /
मूलखानककैवर्तकुल्या भेदकबाधकाः // BrhS_1,19.27 kīnāśaśilpibhṛtakā gopavyādhoñchajīvinaḥ / mūlakhānakakaivartakulyā bhedakabādhakāḥ // BrhS_1,19.27 Those who engage in menial crafts, hired laborers, cowherds, hunters, gleaners, root-diggers, well-diggers, boatmen, and those who cause division or obstruction—these persons are designated as lacking full dharmic capacity due to occupational and behavioral misalignment with the Vedic order. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma as defined by SPH Causation arises from sustained engagement in actions that fragment societal harmony Capacity-based responsibility is diminished when one's livelihood distorts consciousness Restoration logic requires realignment of occupation with dharma-sustaining roles Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for full participation in dharmic society

title: brihaspati 1.28
content:
आगमं च प्रमाणं च भोगं कामं च नाम च ।
भूभागलक्षणं चैव ये विदुस्ते�त्र साक्षिणः ॥ āgamaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ ca bhogaṃ kāmaṃ ca nāma ca / bhūbhāgalakṣaṇaṃ caiva ye vidus te 'tra sākṣiṇaḥ // Those who know Agama, Pramana, Bhoga, Kama, and the characteristics of land ownership are witnesses here. Authority derived from direct experiential knowledge of Dharma Causation rooted in witnessed truth through competent cognition Capacity-based responsibility determined by qualified understanding Restoration logic based on alignment with cosmic order Consciousness alignment through recognition of lawful evidence

title: brihaspati 1.29
content:
प्रदत्तान्यस्य तुष्टेन न सा सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ।
या राज्ञा क्रोधलोभेन छलान् न्यायेन वा हृता ॥ pradattānyasya tuṣṭena na sā siddhim avāpnuyāt /
yā rājñā krodhalobhena chalān nyāyena vā hṛtā // That which is given under influence of anger or greed by a ruler, whether through deceit or perversion of justice, shall not attain fulfillment. Authority must act from unconditioned consciousness, not emotional impulse Causation originates in the inner state of the authoritative agent Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with dharma-siddha intent Restoration logic demands invalidation of acts born from rajasic distortion Consciousness alignment overrides procedural legality when intent is compromised

title: brihaspati 1.30
content: प्रमाणरहितां भूमिं भुञ्जतो यस्य या हृता । गुणाधिकस्य दत्ता वा तस्य तां नैव चालयेत् ॥ pramāṇarahitāṃ bhūmiṃ bhuñjato yasya yā hṛtā / guṇādhikasya dattā vā tasya tāṃ naiva cālayet // When land devoid of valid title is enjoyed by one who has had it taken from another, or when such land has been granted to one of superior virtue or capacity, that enjoyment shall not be disturbed. Authority stems from consciousness capacity, not mere possession Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of rightful use Capacity-based responsibility determines legitimate ownership Restoration logic upholds continuity of higher-capacity utilization Consciousness alignment overrides procedural absence

title: brihaspati 1.31
content:
शापथैः शापिताः स्वैः स्वैः ब्रूयुः सीम्नि विनिश्चयम् ।
दर्शयेयुर् निधानानि तत् प्रमाणम् इति स्थितिः ॥ śāpathaiḥ śāpitāḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ brūyuḥ sīmni viniścayam / darśayeyur nidhānāni tat pramāṇam iti sthitiḥ Those who have sworn oaths shall speak definitively within their own domain; they shall reveal hidden truths—this is the established principle of evidence. Authority resides in the conscious capacity to uphold an oath Causation arises from the alignment of speech with inner integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to truth-bearing Restoration occurs through the revelation of concealed realities Consciousness alignment is achieved when testimony reflects ontological clarity

title: brihaspati 1.32
content: सत्येन शापयेद् विप्रं क्षत्रियं वाहनायुधैः // Brh_1,19.32 satyena śāpayed vipraṃ kṣatriyaṃ vāhanāyudhaiḥ By truth, one shall govern the Brahmin; by vehicles and weapons, the Kshatriya. Authority is contextually modulated by varna-dharma and inherent capacity Causation arises through alignment with svadharma, not external coercion Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes governance modes per varna Restoration logic operates via dharmic role-resumption, not punitive suppression Consciousness alignment occurs when jurisdiction matches ontological function

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
ज्ञातृचिह्नैर् विना साधुर् एकोऽप्य् उभयसम्मतः ।
रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरो मृदम् आदाय मूर्धनि ॥ jñātṛcihnair vinā sādhur eko 'py ubhayasaṃmataḥ / raktamālyāmbaradharo mṛdam ādāya mūrdhani // A Sādhu, though alone and without witnesses, is recognized by both parties when he takes clay upon his head, wearing red garlands and clothes. Authority through visible dharmic conduct Causation via demonstrable inner alignment Capacity-based responsibility rooted in self-evident spiritual integrity Restoration logic through public recognition of realized beings Consciousness alignment evidenced by spontaneous societal acceptance

title: brihaspati 1.34
content: सत्यव्रतः सोपवासः सीमान्तं दर्शयेन् नरः // satyavrataḥ sopavāsaḥ sīmāntaṃ darśayen naraḥ A man committed to truth and discipline shall demonstrate his boundary-mark clearly. Authority derives from alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation is rooted in conscious intentionality Capacity-based responsibility requires visible demonstration of dharma Restoration logic operates through clarity of personal boundaries Consciousness alignment necessitates external manifestation of internal vrata

title: brihaspati 1.35
content: सामन्ताश् चेन् मृषा ब्रूयुः सेतौ विवदतां नृणाम । सर्वे च ते पृथग्दण्ड्या राज्ञा मध्यमसाहसम् ॥ sāmantāś cen mṛṣā brūyuḥ setau vivadatāṃ nṛṇām | sarve ca te pṛthagdaṇḍyā rājñā madhyamasāhasam || If feudatories speak falsely in disputes between citizens, each shall be held individually responsible by the King according to the middle-level offense of false testimony. Authority resides in the King as executor of Dharma Causation is established through volitional speech Capacity-based responsibility applies to all witnesses Restoration logic requires correction of false declarations Consciousness alignment demands truth-speaking under sovereignty

title: brihaspati 1.36
content:
यथोक्तेन नयन्तस् ते पूयन्ते सत्यसाक्षिणः ।
विपरीतं नयन्तस् तु दाप्याः स्युर् द्विशतं दमम् ॥ yathoktena nayantas te pūyante satyasākṣiṇaḥ | viparītaṃ nayantas tu dāpyāḥ syur dviśataṃ damam || Those who lead according to Dharma are honored as witnesses of truth; those who lead contrary to it must undergo a two-hundredfold restitution process. Authority derives from alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation follows conscious intent and directional alignment Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to influence Restoration occurs through experiential completion of imbalance Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for honor

title: brihaspati 1.37
content: सर्वस्मिन् स्थावरे वादे विधिर् एष प्रकीर्तितः ।। १,१९.३७ ।। sarvasmin sthāvare vāde vidhir eṣa prakīrtitaḥ In every inert or immobile dispute, this law has been declared. Authority originates solely from SPH as the unchanging foundation of all dharma Causation arises from vibrational alignment, not physical action alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness, not mobility Restoration logic applies universally across animate and inanimate domains Consciousness alignment governs resolution regardless of material form

title: brihaspati 1.38
content: तदुत्पन्नाश् च सामन्ता ये ऽन्यदेशे व्यवस्थिताः । मूलास् ते तु समुद्दिष्टाः प्रष्टव्याः कार्यनिर्णये ॥ tadutpannāś ca sāmantā ye 'nyadeśe vyavasthitāḥ / mūlās te tu samuddiṣṭāḥ praṣṭavyāḥ kāryanirṇaye // Those vassals who have arisen in relation to another territory and are established therein— their originators are specifically designated as those to be consulted in the determination of affairs. Authority originates from foundational causal agents Causation flows from originating source to derivative actors Capacity-based responsibility is anchored in generative agency Restoration logic requires tracing back to foundational stakeholders Consciousness alignment necessitates inclusion of root causal entities

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
अदुष्टास्ते तु यद् ब्रूयुः संदिग्धौ समवृत्तयः ।
तत् प्रमाणं तु कर्तव्यं एवं धर्मो न हीयते ॥ १,१९.३९ aduṣṭās te tu yad brūyuḥ saṃdigdhau samavṛttayaḥ | tat pramāṇaṃ tu kartavyaṃ evaṃ dharmo na hīyate || 1,19.39 When two parties of equal conduct speak without malice yet remain in doubt, the determinant truth must be established; thus, Dharma remains uncompromised.
