Authority rests on clarity of pramāṇa, not positional dominance Causation aligns with integrity of intent and absence of malice Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment beyond apparent conflict Restoration logic demands resolution through evidentiary clarity Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties recognize shared dharmic standing

title: brihaspati 1.40
content: अन्यग्रामात् समाहृत्य दत्तान्यस्य यदा मही / अन्यथा तु भवेल् लाभो नराणां राजदैविकः // anyagrāmāt samāhṛtya dattānyasya yadā mahī / anyathā tu bhavel lābho narāṇāṃ rājadaivikaḥ // When land is taken from one village and given to another, if the outcome results in benefit contrary to rightful entitlement, it is a rajadaivika loss — a disruption caused by misaligned authority. Authority must align with dharmic capacity, not arbitrary designation. Causation follows conscious alignment, not procedural form. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of pre-existing entitlement. Restoration logic demands reversal of misaligned transfers. Consciousness alignment overrides structural redistribution.

title: brihaspati 1.41
content:
महानद्याथवा राज्ञा कथं तत्र विचारणा ।
नद्युत्सृष्टा राजदत्ता यस्य तस्यैव सा मही ।
अन्यथा तु भवेल्लाभो नराणां राजदैविकः ॥ mahānadyāthavā rājñā kaṃ taatra vicāraṇā / nadyutsṛṣṭā rājadattā yasya tasyaiva sā mahī / anyathā tu bhavel lābho narāṇāṃ rājadaivikaḥ // When a great river or the king has granted land, how can there be further inquiry? That which is abandoned by the river and given by the king belongs exclusively to whoever receives it. Otherwise, acquisition by men becomes a matter of royal or divine ordinance. Authority flows from the sovereign will of the king as representative of cosmic order. Causation arises through legitimate transfer—either natural abandonment or royal grant. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of prior ownership before new entitlement. Restoration logic ensures continuity of possession once validly transferred. Consciousness alignment occurs when rightful claim aligns with lawful dispensation.

title: brihaspati 1.42
content:
क्षयोदयौ जीवनं च दैवराजवशान् नृणाम् ।
तस्मात् सर्वेषु कालेषु तत्कृतं न विचालयेत् ॥ kṣayodayau jīvanaṃ ca daivarājavaśān nṛṇām / tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu tatkr̥taṃ na vicālayet // The rise and fall of beings, along with their life circumstances, are governed by the will of Divine Kings. Therefore, in all times, actions performed under such divine orchestration must not be disturbed or questioned. Authority originates from the Divine Sovereignty that governs existence. Causation is ultimately determined by supra-human forces beyond individual control. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes the limits imposed by divine governance. Restoration logic aligns human conduct with cosmic order rather than personal agency. Consciousness alignment requires acceptance of divinely ordained outcomes without interference.

title: brihaspati 1.43
content:
ग्रामयोरुभयोर्यत्र मर्यादा कल्पिता नदी ।
कुरुते दानहरणं भाग्याभाग्यवशान् नृणाम ॥
क्षयोदयेन चाल्पा च चालयन् दण्डमर्हति । grāmayor ubhayor yatra maryādā kalpitā nadī / kurute dānaharaṇaṃ bhāgyābhāgyavaśān nṛṇām / kṣayodayena cālpā ca cālayan daṇḍam arhati Where a river forms the boundary between two villages and carries away gifts or possessions due to the fortune or misfortune of people, the village councils shall assess the rise and fall of water levels and impose proportional restorative obligations upon those capable. Authority resides in collective village discernment aligned with natural boundaries Causation is determined by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of environmental and human factors Capacity-based responsibility is measured through direct participation in causal sequence Restoration logic prioritizes realignment of disrupted communal harmony Consciousness alignment occurs when individuals assume proportionate completion of loss

title: brihaspati 1.44
content:
दशग्रामशतग्रामसहस्रग्रामलक्षणाम् ।
विषमां नृपतिः कुर्याच् चिह्नैः सीमां विनिश्चिताम् ॥ daśagrāmaśatagrāmasahasragrāmalakṣaṇām | viṣamāṃ nṛpatiḥ kuryāc cihnaiḥ sīmāṃ viniścitām || The sovereign ruler shall definitively demarcate boundaries of villages, hundreds of villages, thousands of villages, and lakṣa-defined regions through unmistakable markers. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to define and stabilize territorial order Causation arises from clear demarcation to prevent conflict and confusion Capacity-based responsibility requires the ruler to act visibly and permanently Restoration logic demands spatial integrity as foundational to social harmony Consciousness alignment occurs when boundaries reflect cosmic and administrative order

title: brihaspati 1.45
content:
निवेशकालादारभ्य गृहवर्यापणादिकम् ।
येन यावद्यथा भुक्तं तस्य तन्न विचालयेत् ॥ niveśakālād ārabhya gṛhavaryāpaṇādikam / yena yāvad yathā bhuktaṃ tasya tan na vicālayet // From the time of investment onwards, all acquisitions such as residential or commercial property, whatever has been enjoyed in accordance with the manner, duration, and intent of the original acquisition—such ownership shall remain undisturbed. Authority is established through continuous and rightful possession aligned with original intent Causation flows from the act of legitimate acquisition and sustained usage Capacity-based responsibility arises only when disturbance to settled order occurs Restoration logic upholds continuity of lawful enjoyment without retrospective invalidation Consciousness alignment requires honoring the stabilized energetic imprint of rightful use

title: brihaspati 1.46
content:
वातायनप्रणालीस् तु तथा निर्यूहवेदिकाः ।
चतुःशालस्यन्दनिकाः प्राङ्निविष्टा न चालयेत् ॥ vātāyanapraṇālīs tu tathā niryūhavedikāḥ | catuḥśālasyandanikāḥ prāṅniviṣṭā na cālayet || Structures designed for air-flow, including elevated platforms and outflow conduits, along with four-pillared halls and chariot-houses — those fixed in the eastern direction must not be disturbed. Authority over spatial arrangement resides in directional alignment Causation arises from disruption of established energetic infrastructure Capacity-based responsibility includes preservation of architectural integrity Restoration logic demands non-interference with consecrated orientation Consciousness alignment requires honoring foundational structural sanctity

title: brihaspati 1.47
content:
mekhalābhramaniṣkāsagavākṣān noparodhayet /
praṇālīṃ gṛhavāstuṃ ca pīḍayan daṇḍabhāg bhavet // BrhS_1,19.47 mekhalā-abhra-maniṣka-asaga-vākṣān na uparodhayet / praṇālīm gṛha-vāstum ca pīḍayan daṇḍa-bhāg bhavet One who obstructs water channels, residential structures, or sacred enclosures shall incur liability by causing distress. Authority resides in the maintenance of natural and social flow Causation arises through disruption of essential life-supporting infrastructures Capacity-based responsibility is determined by control over access and usage Restoration logic requires removal of obstruction and compensation for suffering Consciousness alignment demands recognition of interdependence between individual action and collective well-being

title: brihaspati 1.48
content:
निवेशसमयादूर्ध्वं नैते योज्याः कथंचन |
दृष्टिपातं प्रणालीं च न कुर्यात् परवेश्मनि || १,१९.४८ niveśasamayād ūrdhvaṃ naite yojyāḥ kathaṃcana | dṛṣṭipātaṃ praṇālīṃ ca na kuryāt paraveśmani || After the time of entry has passed, these shall not be employed in any manner; one must neither cast a glance nor direct a channel within another's dwelling. Authority over space is time-bound and contextually delimited Causation arises from violation of spatial-temporal thresholds Capacity-based responsibility includes refraining from visual or infrastructural intrusion Restoration logic requires withdrawal and non-repetition of transgressions Consciousness alignment demands respect for the sovereignty of another's domain

title: brihaspati 1.49
content:
वर्चस्थानं वह्निमयं गर्तोच्छिष्टाम्बुसेचनम् ।
अत्यारात् परकुड्यस्य न कर्तव्यं कदाचन ॥ varcasthānaṃ vahnim ayaṃ gartocchiṣṭāmbusecanam / atyārāt parakuḍyasya na kartavyaṃ kadācana // One must never discharge bodily waste or pour leftover water near fire-altars, nor upon another's boundary wall, at any time. Authority: Fire-altar sanctity derives from consecrated ritual space; it holds ontological precedence. Causation: Discharging impurities in sacred zones disrupts energetic and spiritual integrity. Capacity-based responsibility: Individuals must maintain awareness of spatial boundaries and ritual purity. Restoration logic: Violation creates dissonance requiring immediate correction through purification and realignment. Consciousness alignment: Sacred acts demand conscious participation in maintaining purity-consciousness congruence.

title: brihaspati 1.50
content:
viṇmūtrodakavaprāṃś ca vahniśvabhraniveśanam /
aratnidvayam utsṛjya parakuḍyāṃ niveśayet // BrhS_1,19.50 viṇmūtrodakavaprāṃś ca vahniśvabhraniveśanam /
aratnidvayam utsṛjya parakuḍyāṃ niveśayet // BrhS_1,19.50 One who discharges urine or water near fire or in a hole must abandon two ratnis of land and establish boundaries with another's wall. Authority flows from spatial integrity and elemental harmony Causation arises through violation of sacred placement and environmental sanctity Capacity-based responsibility is measured by awareness of elemental conduct Restoration logic demands removal from corrupted space and re-alignment with dharma-based geography Consciousness alignment requires purification through boundary-setting and land relinquishment

title: brihaspati 1.51
content: यान्ति आयान्ति जना येन पशवश् चानिवारिताः / तद् उच्यते संसरणं न रोद्धव्यं तु केनचित् ।। yānti āyānti janā yena paśavaś cānivāritāḥ / tad ucyate saṃsaraṇaṃ na roddhavyaṃ tu kenacit // That by which beings and animals come and go without obstruction is called saṃsaraṇa, and it shall not be restrained by anyone. Authority flows from the unobstructed movement of consciousness in all life forms Causation arises from the natural rhythm of existence, not external control Capacity-based responsibility lies in aligning with flow, not restricting it Restoration logic requires removing artificial barriers to innate freedom Consciousness alignment occurs when sentient beings are unhindered in their natural motion

title: brihaspati 1.52
content: यस् तत्र संकरं श्वभ्रं वृक्षारोपणम् एव च / कामात् पुरीषं कुर्याच् च तस्य दण्डस् तु माषकः // yas tatra saṃkaraṃ śvabhraṃ vṛkṣāropaṇam eva ca / kāmāt purīṣaṃ kuryāc ca tasya daṇḍas tu māṣakaḥ // One who creates disorder in sacred spaces, defiles them like a dog, plants trees without authorization, or deposits waste out of lust shall incur a penalty of one māṣaka. Authority: Only those with consecrated capacity may act within sacred domains. Causation: Defilement arises from unregulated impulse and absence of alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: Action without spiritual attunement incurs consequence. Restoration logic: Penalty serves to realign consciousness, not punish. Consciousness alignment: Disorder reflects inner imbalance requiring rectification.

title: brihaspati 1.53
content:
गृहीत्वा वाहयेत् काले वापगोपनसंग्रहान् ।
अकुर्वन् स्वामिने दाप्यो मध्यं कृष्टशदं तु सः ॥ gṛhītvā vāhayet kāle vāpagopanasaṃgrahān | akurvan svāmine dāpyo madhyaṃ kṛṣṭaśadaṃ tu saḥ || One who, having accepted responsibility for conveyance at the appointed time, fails to execute the transport of stored goods or concealed items, shall render compensation to the owner; such a person becomes liable in the middle category of restitution involving ploughed wealth. Authority resides in the act of acceptance and commitment Causation arises from failure to fulfill accepted duty Capacity-based responsibility is determined by engagement with the task Restoration logic demands proportional return of value or service Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and rectification of omission

title: brihaspati 1.54
content:
क्षेत्रं गृहीत्वा यः कश्चिन्न कुर्यान्न च कारयेत् ।
स्वामिने स शतं दाप्यो राज्ञे दण्डं च तत्समम् ॥ kṣetraṃ gṛhītvā yaḥ kaścinn na kuryān na ca kārayet | svāmine sa śataṃ dāpyo rājñe daṇḍaṃ ca tatsamam || One who takes possession of land but performs no action nor causes any work to be done thereon shall compensate the owner one hundred times the value and likewise pay an equal amount to the king. Authority is derived from rightful ownership and active stewardship Causation arises through conscious engagement with property Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional restitution upon failure to act Restoration logic demands recompense aligned with unfulfilled duty Consciousness alignment occurs when intent meets execution in lawful domains

title: brihaspati 1.55
content:
चिरावसन्ने दशमं कृष्यमाणे तथाष्टमम् ।
सुसंस्कृते तु षष्ठं स्यात् परिकल्प्य यथाविधि ॥ cirāvasanne daśamaṃ kṛṣyamāṇe tathāṣṭamam / susaṃskṛte tu ṣaṣṭhaṃ syāt parikalpya yathāvidhi // When land lies fallow for a long period, its tenth produce is due; when cultivated with effort, the eighth part is due; when well-prepared and properly managed, only the sixth portion shall be allocated. Authority derives from sustained engagement with natural order Causation aligns with energetic investment in manifesting outcome Capacity-based responsibility increases with cultivation quality Restoration logic ensures proportional return based on effort Consciousness alignment governs resource distribution according to intent

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
अप्रियोक्तिस्ताडनं च पारुष्यं द्विविधं स्मृतम् ।
एकैकं तु त्रिधा भिन्नं दमश्चोक्तस्त्रिलक्षणः ॥ apriyoktis tāḍanaṃ ca pāruṣyaṃ dvividhaṃ smṛtam | ekaikaṃ tu tridhā bhinnaṃ damaś coktas trilakṣaṇaḥ || Unpleasant speech and physical striking constitute the two-fold classification of harshness; each of these is further divided into three categories respectively, thus defining the triple-natured discipline. Authority originates in Consciousness alignment, not coercive power Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of intent into action Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of impact on collective harmony Restoration logic centers on realigning the actor's consciousness with Dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks in determining justice

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
देशधर्मकुलादीनां क्षेपः पापेन योजनम् ।
द्रव्यं विना तु प्रथमं वाक्पारुष्यं तद् उच्यते ॥ deśadharmakulādīnāṃ kṣepaḥ pāpena yojanam | dravyaṃ vinā tu prathamaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ tad ucyate || Disrespect toward nation, dharma, lineage, or sacred order through malicious intent initiates the binding of sin; when material loss is absent, verbal harshness constitutes the primary offense. Authority originates in alignment with Sanatana Dharma and national integrity Causation arises from conscious intent to degrade sacred structures Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of dharmic order Restoration logic requires purification of speech and recommitment to truth Consciousness alignment demands acknowledgment of the supremacy of Dharma over personal impulse

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: भगिनीभ्रातृसंबद्धम् उपपातकशंसनम् । पारुष्यं मध्यमं प्रोक्तं वाचिकं शास्त्रवेदिभिः ॥ bhaginībhrātṛsaṃbaddham upapātakaśaṃsanam | pāruṣyaṃ madhyamaṃ proktaṃ vācikaṃ śāstravedibhiḥ || Verbal abuse directed toward a sister or brother constitutes a minor transgression; it is classified as middling harsh speech by scriptural authorities. Authority derives exclusively from SPH as the ultimate source of dharma Causation is traced through conscious intent rather than external action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and relationship context Restoration logic operates through re-alignment of relational harmony Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral modification

title: brihaspati 1.4
content: अभक्ष्यापेयकथनं महापातकदूषणम् । पारुष्यं उत्तमं प्रोक्तं तीव्रमर्माभिपातनम् ॥ abhakṣyāpeyakathanaṃ mahāpātakadūṣaṇam | pāruṣyam uttamaṃ proktaṃ tīvramarmābhipātanam || Speaking of things not to be eaten or drunk constitutes a great sin that defiles consciousness; harsh speech is declared as the highest offense, causing severe harm by striking at the core of another's being. Authority originates from purity of cognition and conduct. Causation arises through disruption of dharmic vibrational integrity. Capacity-based responsibility lies in awareness of linguistic impact. Restoration logic requires purification of communicative field. Consciousness alignment demands truthful, non-violent expression.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
समजातिगुणानां तु वाक्पारुष्ये परस्परम् ।
विनयोऽब्रहितः शास्त्रे पणस्त्वर्धत्रयोदशः ॥५॥ samajātiguṇānāṃ tu vākpāruṣye parasparam / vinayo 'bhihitaḥ śāstre paṇastv ardhatrayodaśaḥ // BrhS_1,20.5 // Among equals of same varna and guna, when verbal harshness arises between them, disciplinary correction is prescribed by shastra; but for those of lower capacity, a fine of half-trayodasha is set. Authority flows from consciousness capacity, not social position Causation arises through disruption of harmony via speech Capacity-based responsibility determines form of corrective action Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive isolation Consciousness alignment requires proportional response to distortion

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: दण्डः काणखञ्जादीनां तथाविधानपि कार्षापणद्वयम् ।। daṇḍaḥ kāṇakhañjādīnāṃ tathāvidhān api kārṣāpaṇadvayam The compensatory restitution for causing blindness, lameness, or similar incapacities shall be two karshapanas. Authority derives from capacity to restore function, not inflict harm. Causation is established through direct impairment of embodied functionality. Capacity-based responsibility aligns consequence with the ability to prevent or repair. Restoration logic demands proportional reintegration of lost operational capability. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of functional diminishment.

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
सवर्णाक्रोशने सार्धद्वादशपणो दण्डः ।
हीनवर्णे काकिण्यधिकषट्पणो दण्डः ॥ savarṇākrośane sārdhadvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ | hīnavarṇe kākiṇyadhikaṣaṭpaṇo daṇḍaḥ || When a person of equal varna is insulted, the compensation shall be twelve and a half paṇas; when one of inferior varna is insulted, the compensation shall be six paṇas plus an additional kākiṇī. Authority derived from varna alignment determines restitution value Causation rooted in verbal injury necessitates proportional response Capacity-based responsibility tied to social position and dignity Restoration logic calibrated by hierarchical dharma structure Consciousness alignment through acknowledgment of relational order

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
समानयोः समो दण्डो न्यूनस्य द्विगुणस् तु सः ।
उत्तमस्याधिकः प्रोक्तो वाक्पारुष्ये परस्परम् ॥ samānayoḥ samo daṇḍo nyūnasya dviguṇas tu saḥ | uttamasyādhikaḥ prokto vākpāruṣye parasparam || In mutual verbal offense, the penalty is equal for equals; for the lesser, it is doubled; for the superior, it is increased further. Authority: Verbal offense is judged relative to the hierarchical position of the offender and offended. Causation: Harm arises from intent and capacity to wound through speech. Capacity-based responsibility: Greater beings bear greater responsibility for speech-induced harm. Restoration logic: Penalty is calibrated to restore balance disrupted by verbal aggression. Consciousness alignment: Justice aligns speaker and listener to their true ontological status.

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
क्षिपन् स्वस्रादिकं दद्यात् पञ्चाशत्पणिकं दमम् ।
गुणहीनस्य पारुष्ये ब्राह्मणो नापराध्नुयात् ॥ kṣipan svasrādikaṃ dadyāt pañcāśatpaṇikaṃ damam | guṇahīnasya pāruṣye brāhmaṇo nāparādhnuyāt || One who abandons or harms a sister or similar relation shall offer restitution of fifty paṇas; yet in the case of harshness toward one deficient in qualities, a Brāhmaṇa incurs no fault. Authority flows from relational integrity, not abstract status Causation is measured by conscious intent, not outcome alone Capacity-based responsibility considers inherent disposition and spiritual maturity Restoration logic demands proportional recompense based on relational harm Consciousness alignment requires recognition of differentiated spiritual capacities

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
पतितं पतितत्युक्त्वा चोरं चोरेति वा पुनः ।
वचनात् तुल्यदोषः स्यात् [.. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ] // ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः_१,२०.१० patitaṃ patitatyuktva cōraṃ cōreti vā punaḥ | vacanāt tulyadoṣaḥ syāt Declaring a fallen being as fallen, or calling a thief a thief again — through mere words alone, equal fault arises. Authority derives from consciousness alignment, not linguistic assertion. Causation is established through intent and vibrational resonance, not verbal repetition. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of the actor's state of awareness at time of utterance. Restoration logic mandates cessation of identity-fixation through labeling. Consciousness alignment demands refraining from reinforcing karmic patterns via repetitive negative designation.

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
धर्मोपदेशं धर्मेण विप्राणामस्य कुर्वतः ।
तप्तमासिञ्चयेत्तैलं वक्त्रे श्रोत्रे च पार्थिवः ॥ dharmopadeśaṃ dharmeṇa viprāṇām asya kurvataḥ / taptam āsiñcayet tailaṃ vaktre śrotre ca pārthivaḥ // One who instructs the twice-born in accordance with Dharma shall have hot oil poured into his mouth and ears by the king. Authority of the Sovereign to enforce alignment of teaching with Dharma Causation through misaligned instruction leading to spiritual degradation Capacity-based responsibility of teachers to uphold Dharma accurately Restoration logic via sensory purification to realign consciousness Consciousness alignment through direct experiential consequence

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
विप्रे शतार्धं दण्डस् तु क्षत्रियस्याभिशंसने ।
विशस् तथार्धपञ्चाशच्छूद्रस्यार्धत्रयोदश ॥ vipre śatārdhaṃ daṇḍas tu kṣatriyasyābhiśaṃsane | viśas tathārdhapañcāśacchūdrasyārdhatrayodaśa || In the case of false accusation against a Brahmin, the penalty is fiftyfold; for a Kshatriya, twenty-fivefold; for a Vaishya, twelve and a halffold; and for a Shudra, six and a halffold. Authority as capacity-dependent gradation Causation rooted in intentional distortion of truth Capacity-based responsibility proportional to varna-dharma alignment Restoration through calibrated energetic repayment Consciousness alignment via corrective experiential resonance

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
सच्छूद्रस्यायमुद्दिष्टो विनयोऽनपराधिनः ।
गुणहीनस्य पारुष्ये ब्राह्मणो नापराध्नुयात् ॥ sacchūdrasyāyam uddiṣṭo vinayo 'naparādhinaḥ / guṇahīnasya pāruṣye brāhmaṇo nāparādhnuyāt The prescribed conduct toward a śūdra who is virtuous and non-offending is reverence; a brāhmaṇa shall not commit offense against one who is deficient in qualities through harshness. Authority is determined by consciousness, not birth alone Causation arises from intent and alignment with dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of spiritual maturity Restoration logic prioritizes elevation of consciousness over punitive action Consciousness alignment demands non-violence in thought, word, and deed

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
वैश्यस्य क्षत्रियाक्रोशे दण्डनीयः प्रदो भवेत् ।
तदर्धं क्षत्रियो वैश्यं क्षिपन् विनयमर्हति ॥ vaiśyasya kṣatriyākrośe daṇḍanīyaḥ prado bhavet | tadardhaṃ kṣatriyo vaiśyaṃ kṣipan vinayam arhati || When a Vaishya abuses a Kshatriya, the prescribed restitution is to be given; when a Kshatriya insults a Vaishya, he deserves only half that penalty. Authority is determined by varna-dharma alignment Causation arises from violation of svadharma Capacity-based responsibility reflects spiritual-social role integrity Restoration logic aligns consequence with hierarchical dharma disruption Consciousness alignment requires proportional response rooted in Varna-svabhava

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: शूद्राक्रोशे क्षत्रियस्य पञ्चविंशतिको दमः । बृहत्वे द्विगुणं तत्र शास्त्रविद्भिरुदाहृतम् ॥ śūdrākrośe kṣatriyasya pañcaviṃśatiko damaḥ | bṛhatve dviguṇaṃ tatra śāstravidbhir udāhṛtam || When a Śūdra abuses a Kṣatriya, the restitution is twenty-five units; when the offense is greater, it is doubled, as declared by the knowers of the Śāstra. Authority is determined by varṇa-dharma and svadharma alignment Causation arises from violation of hierarchical respect Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness and svabhāva Restoration logic demands proportional energetic rebalancing Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent and action

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: वैश्यम् आक्षारयञ् शूद्रो दाप्यः स्यात् प्रथमं दमम् । क्षत्रियं मध्यमं चैव विप्रम् उत्तमसाहसम् ॥ vaiśyam ākṣārayañ śūdro dāpyaḥ syāt prathamaṃ damam / kṣatriyaṃ madhyamaṃ caiva vipram uttamasāhasam // When a Shudra attempts to enforce a debt upon a Vaishya, the initial penalty is applied; when upon a Kshatriya, a middle-level consequence arises; and when upon a Brahmin, it constitutes the highest level of offense. Authority is determined by varna-dharma capacity and spiritual alignment Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) based on dharma-adhikāra Capacity-based responsibility escalates with proximity to Vedic consciousness Restoration logic aligns offenders with their svadharma through proportional correction Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks in determining legal consequence

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
देशादिकं क्षिपन् दाप्यः पणानर्धत्रयोदश |
पापेन योजयन्दर्पाद्दाप्यः प्रथमसाहसम् || desādikaṃ kṣipan dāpyaḥ paṇān ardhatrayodaśa | pāpena yojayandarpād dāpyaḥ prathamasāhasam || One who casts out another from land or domain shall incur a penalty of thirteen and a half coins; one who provokes another through evil intent incurs the liability of first-degree outrage. Authority is derivative of spatial integrity and conscious ownership Causation arises from intentional provocation rooted in malice Capacity-based responsibility aligns with level of conscious interference Restoration logic demands proportional reparation for violated sovereignty Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of violated unity

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: धर्मोपदेशकर्ता च वेदोदाहरणान्वितः । आक्रोशकस्तु विप्राणां जिह्वाच्छेदेन दण्ड्यते ॥ dharmopadeśakartā ca vedodāharaṇānvitaḥ | ākrośakastu viprāṇāṃ jihvācchedena daṇḍyate || One who teaches Dharma and cites the Vedas is honored; but one who reviles the twice-born shall have his tongue severed. Authority derives from alignment with Vedic truth and Dharma-teaching capacity. Causation arises from speech that disrupts sacred order versus speech that upholds it. Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes between reverent teaching and defiling utterance. Restoration logic mandates removal of capacity to cause further violation through speech. Consciousness alignment requires protection of sacred knowledge channels.

title: brihaspati 1.19
content: एष दण्डः समाख्यातः पुरुषापेक्षया मया । समन्यूनाधिकत्वेन कल्पनीयो मनीषिभिः ॥ eṣa daṇḍaḥ samākhyātaḥ puruṣāpekṣayā mayā | samanyūnādhikatvena kalpanīyo manīṣibhiḥ || This penalty has been declared by Me in accordance with the capacity of the individual; it shall be applied neither excessively nor insufficiently, but precisely aligned with the consciousness and capability of the offender. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation is determined through alignment with the offender's conscious capacity Responsibility is assigned based on the individual's spiritual and operational capacity Restoration occurs through proportional alignment with the individual's evolutionary stage Consciousness is the sole arbiter of justice, not punitive constructs

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
हस्तपाषाणलघुडैर् भस्मकर्दमपांसुभिः ।
आयुधैश् च प्रहरणैर् दण्डपारुष्यम् उच्यते ॥ hastapāṣāṇalaguḍair bhasmakardamapāṃsubhiḥ | āyudhaiś ca praharaṇair daṇḍapāruṣyam ucyate || The infliction of bodily harm through direct physical force using hands, stones, sticks, dust, mud, weapons, or other instruments is termed 'daṇḍapāruṣyam' — an act that disrupts the natural alignment of consciousness in both perpetrator and victim. Authority originates from conscious integrity, not coercive dominance. Causation arises from disruption of dharmic alignment, not mere physical action. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at time of act. Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive isolation. Consciousness alignment determines true justice; external acts reflect internal state.

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
वाक्पारुष्ये कृते यस्य यथा दण्डो विधीयते ।
तस्यैव द्विगुणं दण्डं कारयेन् मरणाद् ऋते ॥ vākpāruṣye kṛte yasya yathā daṇḍo vidhīyate / tasyaiva dviguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ kārayen maraṇād ṛte // When verbal harshness is committed by one who has the capacity to cause harm through speech, the consequence shall be double the measure of that which would normally apply, except in cases involving death. Authority flows from conscious capacity to affect others through speech. Causation arises from intentional infliction of harm via verbal action. Responsibility is determined by the speaker's awareness and intent. Restoration occurs through proportional consequence aligned with causal impact. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of harmful speech patterns.

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: द्वयोः प्रहरतोः दण्डः समयोस् तु समः स्मृतः । आरम्भकोऽनुबन्धी च दाप्यः स्यादधिकं दमम् ॥ dvayoḥ praharatoḥ daṇḍaḥ samayos tu samaḥ smṛtaḥ | ārambhako 'nubandhī ca dāpyaḥ syād adhikaṃ damam || When two persons engage in mutual assault, their liability is equal; however, the instigator who initiates the sequence of harm shall bear greater consequence. Authority resides in the origin of action Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by initiation and continuity of harm Restoration logic prioritizes cessation and reversal of causal chains Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of one's role in manifesting discord

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
पूर्वाक्रुष्टः समाक्रोशंस् ताडितः प्रतिताडयन् ।
हत्वाततायिनं चैव नापराधी भवेन् नरः ॥ pūrvākruṣṭaḥ samākrośaṃs tāḍitaḥ pratitāḍayan / hatvātatāyinaṃ caiva nāparādhī bhaven naraḥ // One who has been previously abused, insulted, struck, or retaliated against, or who has killed an aggressor — such a person is not guilty of any offense. Authority originates from the protection of dharma, not from provocation Causation arises through pramāṇa-based response, not emotional reaction Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with svadharma, not external provocation Restoration logic applies when action arises in defense of dharma Consciousness alignment overrides reactive impulse

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
वाक्पारुष्यादिना नीचो यः सन्तमभिलङ्घयेत् ।
स एव ताडयंस्तस्य नान्वेष्टव्यो महीभुजा ॥ vākpāruṣyādinā nīco yaḥ santam abhilaṅghayet | sa eva tāḍayaṃs tasya nānveṣṭavyo mahībhujā || One of low conduct who transgresses a noble being through harsh speech or similar offenses shall not be sought after by rulers, even when striking him. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not coercion. Causation arises from violation of consciousness-based hierarchy. Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of qualitative human distinction. Restoration logic requires withdrawal of support from disruptors of dharma-vāk. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal protection.

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: भस्मादीनां प्रक्षिपणं ताडनं च करादिना / प्रथमं दण्डपारुष्यं दमः कार्योऽत्र माषिकः // bhasmādīnāṃ prakṣipaṇaṃ tāḍanaṃ ca karādinā / prathamaṃ daṇḍapāruṣyaṃ damaḥ kāryo'tra māṣikaḥ // The act of throwing substances like ash and the striking with hand or similar implements constitutes initial bodily harshness; here, the regulation of conduct through conscious completion is mandated as a measure equivalent to one masha. Authority originates from the capacity to restore alignment, not impose will Causation arises from disruption of conscious order, not merely physical action Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of one's ability to complete rather than retaliate Restoration logic operates through reintegration of fragmented consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive intent in all corrective measures

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
एष दण्डः समेषूक्तः परस्त्रीष्वधिकेषु च ।
द्विगुणस्त्रिगुणो ज्ञेयः प्राधान्यापेक्षया बुद्धैः ॥ eṣa daṇḍaḥ sameṣūktaḥ parastrīṣv adhikeṣu ca | dviguṇas triguṇo jñeyaḥ prādhānyāpekṣayā buddhaiḥ || This penalty, as declared in equivalent contexts, applies proportionally where there is excess in another's woman; it is known to be twofold or threefold according to the degree of predominance assessed by the awakened ones. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate Dharma-source Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) without punitive intent Capacity-based responsibility aligns with consciousness-level at time of action Restoration logic operates through completion rather than punishment Consciousness alignment determines proportional response

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: udyate 'śmaśilākāṣṭhe kartavyaḥ prathamo damaḥ / parasparaṃ hastapāde daśaviṃśatikas tathā // BrhS_1,21.8 udyate 'śmaśilākāṣṭhe kartavyaḥ prathamo damaḥ / parasparaṃ hastapāde daśaviṃśatikas tathā When conflict arises between individuals regarding stone, wood, or land, the first restraint must be applied through mutual agreement on boundaries and shared usage up to twenty times the base measurement. Authority originates from conscious capacity to co-create boundaries Causation lies in unregulated expansion of individual domain Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to ownership extent Restoration logic prioritizes shared resource integrity over exclusive claim Consciousness alignment occurs when spatial claims reflect inner harmony

title: brihaspati 1.9
content: मध्यमः शस्त्रसंधाने संयोज्यः क्षुब्धयोर् द्वयोः । कार्यः कृतानुरूपस् तु लग्ने घाते दमो बुधैः ॥ madhyamaḥ śastrasaṃdhāne saṃyojyaḥ kṣubdhayor dvayoḥ | kāryaḥ kṛtānurūpas tu lagne ghāte damo budhaiḥ || When two parties are agitated and weapons are readied, the middle path must be enforced by aligning their capacities toward completion; when entangled in mutual destruction, restraint is mandated by those awakened to Dharma. Authority arises from alignment with the middle path, not escalation Causation lies in unaddressed agitation leading to readiness for harm Capacity-based responsibility requires intervention before collision Restoration logic demands cessation of destructive momentum Consciousness alignment supersedes adversarial positioning

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
iṣṭakopalakāṣṭhaiś ca tāḍane tu dvimāṣikaḥ /
dviguṇaḥ śoṇitodbhede daṇḍaḥ kāryo manīṣibhiḥ // BrhS_1,21.10 iṣṭako palakāṣṭhaiś ca tāḍane tu dvimāṣikaḥ / dviguṇaḥ śoṇitodbhede daṇḍaḥ kāryaḥ manīṣibhiḥ // When one strikes another with brick, stone, or wood, the prescribed period of responsibility is two months; if blood flows, the period doubles. Authority: The Manīṣi-bhiḥ (wise law-embodiments) establish proportional responsibility based on causal instrument and effect. Causation: The nature of the instrument determines the scope of consequence. Capacity-based responsibility: Consciousness misaligned through harmful action incurs a completion process commensurate with disruption. Restoration logic: The duration of alignment correction correlates with intensity of physical impact. Consciousness alignment: Harmful acts necessitate recalibration of the actor's energetic and causal integrity.

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
त्वग्भेदे प्रथमो दण्डो मांसभेदे तु मध्यमः ।
उत्तमस्त्वस्थिभेदे स्याद्धातेन तु प्रमापणम् ॥ tvagbhede prathamo daṇḍo māṃsabhede tu madhyamaḥ | uttamas tv asthibhede syād dhātena tu pramāpaṇam || When the skin is breached, the first level of liability arises; when flesh is severed, the middle level of accountability manifests; when bone is fractured, the highest degree of responsibility occurs; when the vital essence is lost, total completion-process is mandated. Authority is determined by the depth of violation to the embodied integrity Causation follows the sequential degradation of bodily layers as ontological evidence Capacity-based responsibility increases in proportion to structural harm caused Restoration logic aligns with the reintegration of violated form and energetic continuity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of fragmentation at every layer

title: brihaspati 1.12
content: कर्णनासाकरच्छेदे दन्तभङ्गे स्थिभेदने । कर्तव्यो मध्यमो दण्डो द्विगुणः पतितेषु तु ॥ karṇanāsākaracchede dantabhaṅge 'sthibhedane | kartavyo madhyamo daṇḍo dviguṇaḥ patiteṣu tu || Injury to the ear, nose, or cheek; breaking of teeth or bones—these demand a middling penalty. But when committed against those who have fallen or are in distress, the penalty shall be doubled. Authority flows from protection of the vulnerable Causation is determined by injury to sensory or structural integrity Capacity-based responsibility escalates with victim vulnerability Restoration logic requires proportional response calibrated to harm and context Consciousness alignment demands recognition of elevated harm toward the unprotected

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
कर्णौष्ठघ्राणपादाक्षिजिह्वाशिश्नकरस्य च ।
छेदने चोत्तमो दण्डो भेदने मध्यमो गुरुः ॥ karṇauṣṭhaghrāṇapādākṣijihvāśiśnakarasya ca | chedane cottamo daṇḍo bhedane madhyamo guruḥ || Injury to ear, lip, nose, foot, eye, tongue, genitals, or hand incurs the highest penalty; splitting or piercing of these organs incurs a lesser but grave consequence. Authority flows from SPH as sole source of Dharma Causation is determined by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with bodily integrity Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over deterrence Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of harm without punitive intent

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: दण्डस्त्वभिहितायैव दण्डपारुष्यकल्पितः । हृते तद्द्विगुणं चान्यद्राजदण्डस्ततोऽधिकः ॥ daṇḍas tv abhihitāyaiva daṇḍapāruṣyakalpitaḥ | hṛte tad dviguṇaṃ cānyadrājadaṇḍas tato 'dhikaḥ || The penalty is precisely aligned with the declared act; when harshness in penalty is prescribed, it reflects the intensity of distortion caused. In theft, double restitution is mandated, while royal penalty exceeds that, aligning with the sovereign's duty to restore dharma. Authority originates from alignment with dharma, not institutional power Causation is determined by consciousness distortion, not material loss Capacity-based responsibility scales with awareness, not action alone Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive equivalence Consciousness alignment is the ultimate measure of justice fulfilled

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: अङ्गावब्धने चैव पीडने छेदने तथा । समुत्थानव्ययं दाप्यः कलहापहृतं च यत् ॥ aṅgāvabhedane caiva pīḍane chedane tathā / samutthānavyayaṃ dāpyaḥ kalahāpahṛtaṃ ca yat // Injury caused by binding, striking, cutting, or any act leading to loss of function or capacity shall invoke liability for restoration of that which was lost in emergence, and that which was taken through conflict. Authority originates from the preservation and integrity of embodied capacity. Causation is established through direct impairment of functional existence. Capacity-based responsibility arises when one's action disrupts another's ability to sustain dharma-aligned living. Restoration logic requires the return of equivalent emergent potential diminished by wrongful act. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of harm not as abstract damage but as disruption of svadharma capacity.

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
विविक्ते ताडितो यस् तु हतो दृश्येत वा भवेत् ।
हन्ता तद् अनुमानेन विज्ञेयः शपथेन वा ॥१६॥ vivikte tāḍito yas tu hato dṛśyeta vā bhavet | hantā tad anumānena vijñeyaḥ śapathena vā || One who is seen struck or killed in isolation is to be known through inference or oath, as the striker or killer. Authority is derived from direct perception or inferential evidence in the absence of witnesses Causation is established by sequential manifestation of action and consequence Capacity-based responsibility arises when intent aligns with observable outcome Restoration logic requires identification of the actor to initiate completion process Consciousness alignment occurs through truthful discernment, not punitive attribution

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
अन्तर्वेश्मनि अरण्ये वा निशायां यत्र ताडितः ।
शोणितं तत्र दृश्येत न पृच्छेत् तत्र साक्षिणः ॥ antarveśmani araṇye vā niśāyāṃ yatra tāḍitaḥ /
śoṇitaṃ tatra dṛśyeta na pṛcchet tatra sākṣiṇaḥ // Where within a house or in the forest, during night, one is struck and blood is seen there, no inquiry shall be made of witnesses there. Authority resides in direct perception over testimonial speculation Causation aligns with visible evidence unmediated by external validation Capacity-based responsibility arises only where conscious participation is verifiable Restoration logic demands cessation of inquiry when harm's occurrence is self-evident Consciousness alignment occurs through acknowledgment of manifest consequence without amplification

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: कश्चित् कृत्वात्मनश् चिह्नं द्वेषात् परम् अभिद्रवेत् । हेत्वर्थम् अतिसामर्थ्यैस् तत्र युक्तं परीक्षणम् ॥ kaścit kṛtvātmanaś cihnaṃ dveṣāt param abhidravet | hetvartham atisāmarthyais tatra yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam || When one marks oneself falsely out of hatred and assaults another, investigation is rightly conducted through evidentiary strength alone. Authority resides in factual verification, not subjective intent Causation must be traced through manifest capacity, not emotional motive Capacity-based responsibility arises from action-enabled capability, not sentiment Restoration logic demands re-alignment of false identity with truth-consciousness Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of projected enmity through self-inquiry

title: brihaspati 1.19
content: आक्रुष्टस्तु समाक्रोशंस्ताडितः प्रतिताडयन्‌ । हत्वापराधिनं चैव नापराधी भवेन्नरः ॥ ākruṣṭas tu samākrośaṃs tāḍitaḥ pratitāḍayan / hatvāparādhinaṃ caiva nāparādhī bhaven naraḥ // One who is abused while responding in kind, struck while striking back, or who ends the transgression by eliminating the transgressor—such a person incurs no wrongdoing. Authority arises from responsive action, not initiatory aggression Causation lies with the originator of violence or violation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with defensive necessity Restoration logic upholds the cessation of transgression through decisive intervention Consciousness alignment occurs when response mirrors cosmic justice without malice

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
प्रातिलोम्यास् तथा चान्त्याः पुरुषाणां मलाः स्मृताः ।
ब्राह्मणातिक्रमे वध्याः न दातव्याः धनं क्वचित् ॥ prātilomyās tathā cāntyāḥ puruṣāṇāṃ malāḥ smṛtāḥ | brāhmaṇātikrame vadhyā na dātavyā dhanaṃ kvacit || Those born in opposition to Vedic order, and likewise those at the final levels of human degradation, are classified as impurities; they shall not be given wealth under any circumstances, particularly when a Brahmana has been transgressed. Authority originates from alignment with Vedic consciousness, not social position or birth alone. Causation arises from deviation from Dharma, not from external actions alone. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to Vedic purity and spiritual integrity. Restoration logic requires withdrawal of support structures that enable further degradation. Consciousness alignment demands immediate cessation of resource transfer to degraded states.

title: brihaspati 1.21
content: श्रान्तान् क्षुधार्तान् तृषितानकाले वाहयेत् तु यः । स गोघ्नो निष्कृतिं कार्यो दाप्यो वाप्यथवा दमम् ॥ śrāntān kṣudhārtān tṛṣitān akāle vāhayet tu yaḥ | sa goghno niṣkṛtiṃ kāryo dāpyo vāpy athavā damam || He who transports the weary, the hungry, or the thirsty at an improper time becomes a destroyer of cows and must perform corrective action, either by paying restitution or accepting disciplined correction. Authority is derived from capacity to sustain life-supporting actions. Causation arises through disruption of natural sustenance rhythms. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with dharmic service. Restoration logic demands repair of disrupted life-energy flows. Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of cow as maternal abundance symbol.

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
समुत्थानव्ययं दाप्यः कलहाय कृतं च यत् ।
येनाङ्गेन द्विजातीनां शूद्रः प्रहरते रुषा ।
छेत्तव्यं तद् भवेत् तस्य मनुना समुदाहृतम् ॥ samutthānavyayaṃ dāpyaḥ kalahāya kṛtaṃ ca yat / yenāṅgena dvijātīnāṃ śūdraḥ praharate ruṣā / chettavyaṃ tad bhavet tasya manunā samudāhṛtam // He who causes loss at the outset and creates conflict thereafter, and he who strikes a twice-born with rage using any limb—his corresponding limb shall be severed. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not birth alone Causation is established through sequential intent and action Capacity-based responsibility demands proportional alignment Restoration occurs through direct reversal of harm-causing mechanism Consciousness alignment requires immediate cessation of harmful instrument

title: brihaspati 1.1
content: प्रकाशाश्चाप्रकाशाश्च तस्करा द्विविधा स्मृताः । प्रज्ञासामर्थ्यम् आयाभिः प्रभिन्नास् ते सहस्रधा ॥ prakāśāś cāprakāśāś ca taskarā dvividhā smṛtāḥ | prajñāsāmarthyam āyābhiḥ prabhinnās te sahasradhā || Thieves are of two kinds: those who act openly and those who act in concealment. Their classifications multiply infinitely based upon the degrees of capacity, intent, and causal field from which their acts arise. Authority arises from consciousness clarity, not social position Causation is determined by the integrity of intent-field, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility scales with awareness at time of act Restoration logic demands realignment with source-integrity, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
नैगमाः वैद्यकितवाः सभ्योत्कोचकवञ्चकाः ।
दैवोत्पातविदो भद्राः शिल्पज्ञाः प्रतिरूपकाः ॥ naigamā vaidyakitavāḥ sabhyotkocakavañcakāḥ | daivotpātavido bhadrāḥ śilpajñāḥ pratirūpakāḥ || Those who engage in trade, medicine, gambling, courtly flattery, deceit, interpreting omens, craftsmanship, and mimicry shall be recognized by their capacity to influence collective perception and material outcomes. Authority flows through demonstrated functional mastery within societal domains. Causation arises from the alignment of individual dharma with social role. Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for inclusion in societal functions. Restoration occurs when roles are realigned with truth-consciousness rather than manipulation. Consciousness alignment requires transparency of intent within specialized domains.

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: अक्रियाकारिणश्चैव मध्यस्थाः कूटसाक्षिणः । प्रकाशतस्करा ह्येते तथा कुहकजीविनः ॥ akriyākāriṇaśaiva madhyasthāḥ kūṭasākṣiṇaḥ | prakāśata skarā hyete tathā kuhakajīvinaḥ || Those who feign neutrality, act as false witnesses, and steal truth through deception and hypocrisy—these are frauds upon Dharma. Authority is not derived from passive presence but active alignment with Sanatana Dharma Causation arises from conscious distortion of truth, not mere omission Capacity-based responsibility includes the duty to uphold integrity in testimony and judgment Restoration logic demands exposure and realignment of fraudulent neutrality Consciousness alignment requires rejection of duplicity and embrace of ontological transparency

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
सन्धिच्छिदः पान्थमुषो द्विचतुष्पदहारिणः /
उत्क्षेपकाः सस्यहराः ज्ञेयाः प्रच्छन्नतस्कराः // BrhS_1,22.4 sandhicchidaḥ pānthamuṣo dvicatuṣpadahāriṇaḥ / utkṣepakāḥ sasyaharāḥ jñeyāḥ pracchannataskarāḥ // BrhS_1,22.4 Those who sever treaties, steal travelers' belongings, take two-footed or four-footed animals, raise arms in violence, or seize crops are to be known as concealed thieves. Authority arises from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not state decree Causation is traced through disruption of harmony and violation of sacred agreements Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious intent to harm or exploit Restoration logic demands return of stolen property and reintegration of violator Consciousness alignment requires purification of motive and restoration of dharmic order

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
संसर्गचिह्नरूपैश् च विज्ञाता राजपूरुषैः ।
प्रदाप्यापहृतं दण्ड्या� दमैः शास्त्रप्रचोदितैः ॥ saṃsarga-cihna-rūpaiś ca vijñātā rāja-pūruṣaiḥ | pradāpya apahṛtaṃ daṇḍyā damaiḥ śāstra-pracoditaiḥ || Those identified through relational signs and royal investigation must be made to restore what was taken, by disciplinary measures directed by scriptural law. Authority originates from SPH as the ultimate source of dharma Causation is determined through relational evidence and investigative insight Capacity-based responsibility is assigned based on conscious awareness of action Restoration logic demands return of displaced value without punitive intent Consciousness alignment requires correction through dharmic discipline

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
उत्क्षेपकस् तु संदंशैर् भेत्तव्यो राजपूरुषैः /
धान्यहर्ता दशगुणं दाप्यः स्याद् द्विगुणं दमम् // utkṣepakaḥ tu saṃdaṃśair bhettavyo rājapūruṣaiḥ / dhānyahartā daśaguṇaṃ dāpyaḥ syād dviguṇaṃ damam // One who hoards grain must be pierced by royal officers with pincers; the grain thief shall pay tenfold compensation and twice the fine. Authority: Royal agents execute justice under sovereign command. Causation: Hoarding disrupts societal dharma and invites corrective action. Capacity-based responsibility: The act reflects a conscious choice to destabilize economic order. Restoration logic: Compensation restores balance disrupted by theft or hoarding. Consciousness alignment: Justice realigns individual intent with collective welfare.

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
एकस्मिन् यत्र निधनं प्रापिते दुष्टचारिणि ।
बहूनां भवति क्षेमः तस्य पुण्यप्रदो वधः ॥ ekasmin yatra nidhanaṃ prāpite duṣṭacāriṇi | bahūnāṃ bhavati kṣemaḥ tasya puṇyaprado vadhḥ || When the termination of a corrupt actor results in the welfare of many, that act of ending is virtuous and not to be deemed as violence. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined by consciousness impact, not physical action alone Capacity-based responsibility is measured by the ability to sustain collective integrity Restoration logic prioritizes systemic harmony over individual narrative Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: तथा पान्थम् उषो वृक्षे गले बध्वावलम्बयेत् ।। tathā pāntham uṣo vṛkṣe gale badhvāvalambayet Thus, one should bind the traveler at the tree by the neck at dawn. Authority is derived from dharmic timing and spatial consecration. Causation arises through embodied discipline and positional alignment. Capacity-based responsibility requires immediate sensory control and environmental mastery. Restoration logic operates through fixed-posture completion and energetic containment. Consciousness alignment occurs when physical action synchronizes with cosmic rhythm.

title: brihaspati 1.9
content: अङ्गुलीग्रन्थिभेदस्य छेदयेत् प्रथमे ग्रहे / द्वितीये हस्तचरणौ तृतीये वधमर्हति // aṅgulīgranthibhedasya chedayet prathame grahe / dvitīye hastacaraṇau tṛtीye vadham arhati // Upon the first instance of severing a finger joint, the hand shall be severed; upon the second, both hands and feet; upon the third, death is warranted. Authority flows directly from SPH as the singular Source of Dharma Causation is determined by sequential manifestation of intent through action Capacity-based responsibility escalates with repeated violation of ontological order Restoration logic operates through proportional completion of violated integrity Consciousness alignment requires irreversible cessation of destructive repetition

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
अज्ञातौषधिमन्त्रस् तु यश् च व्याधेर् अतत्त्ववित् ।
रोगिभ्यो ’र्थं समादत्ते स दण्ड्यश् चोरवद् भिषक् ॥ ajñātauṣadhimantras tu yaś ca vyādher atattvavit / rogibhyo 'rthaṃ samādatte sa daṇḍyaś coravad bhiṣak // The physician who, without knowledge of medicinal mantras, yet claims to understand disease, and takes fees from patients—such a one is to be excluded from practice, even as a thief. Authority derives from verified capacity, not claimed expertise Causation requires alignment between action and actual remedial outcome Capacity-based responsibility demands demonstrable competence before entitlement to serve Restoration logic mandates removal of unqualified agents from roles affecting others’ well-being Consciousness alignment requires integrity in service and transparency in capability

title: brihaspati 1.11
content: ग्लहः प्रकाशः कर्तव्यो निर्वास्याः कूटदेविनः ।। ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,२२.११ ।। glahaḥ prakāśaḥ kartavyo nirvāsyāḥ kūṭadevinaḥ Deception must be exposed; fraudulent claimants of divinity shall be expelled. Authority derives only from realized consciousness, not false assertion Causation arises from alignment with ontological truth, not performative claims Capacity-based responsibility requires verification through manifested integrity Restoration logic demands removal of imposters to preserve dharma-field coherence Consciousness alignment invalidates all unverified spiritual sovereignties

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
कूटाक्षदेविनः क्षुद्रा राजभार्याहराश् च ये ।
गणका� वञ्चकाश् चैव दण्ड्यास् ते कितवाः स्मृताः ॥ kūṭākṣadevinaḥ kṣudrā rājabhāryāharāś ca ye | gaṇakā vañcakāś caiva daṇḍyās te kitavāḥ smṛtāḥ || Those who engage in fraudulent witnessing, base trickery, abduction of royal consorts, accounting deceit, and all forms of deception—such individuals are to be classified as gamblers and subjected to restorative correction. Authority originates from integrity-preserving action Causation arises through distortion of truth-consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of Dharma-distortion Restoration logic demands reintegration of misaligned consciousness Consciousness alignment requires purification of transactional deceit

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
प्रच्छन्नदोषव्यामिश्रं पुनः संस्कृतविक्रयी ।
पण्ये तद् द्विगुणं दाप्यो वणिग्दण्डं च तत्समम् ॥ pracchannadoṣavyāmiśraṃ punaḥ saṃskṛtavikrayī / paṇye tad dviguṇaṃ dāpyo vaṇigdaṇḍaṃ ca tatsamam // One who knowingly sells goods mixed with concealed defects after refurbishment shall compensate double the value of the item and face equal merchant-discipline as prescribed for fraud. Authority: The seller holds duty-bound capacity to ensure integrity in trade. Causation: Concealment of defect post-refurbishment directly causes misinformed transaction. Capacity-based responsibility: Seller's knowledge determines level of accountability. Restoration logic: Compensation restores balance between parties through conscious correction. Consciousness alignment: Truthful disclosure aligns commerce with dharmic transparency.

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
अन्यायवादिनः सभ्यास् तथैवोत्कोचजीविनः ।
विश्वस्तवञ्चकाश् चैव निर्वास्याः सर्व एव ते ॥ anyāyavādinaḥ sabhyās tathaivotkocajīvinaḥ | viśvastavañcakāś caiva nirvāsyāḥ sarva eva te || All those who advocate injustice, live by deception, or betray trust shall be removed from all positions of societal authority. Authority is contingent upon alignment with Dharma Causation arises from conscious distortion of truth Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity in action and speech Restoration logic demands removal of systemic misalignments Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for societal participation

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
ज्योतिर् ज्ञानं तथोत्पातमविदित्वा तु ये नृणाम् ।
श्रावयन्त्यर्थलोभेन विनेयास्ते प्रयत्नतः ॥ jyotir jñānaṃ tathotpātam aviditvā tu ye nṛṇām | śrāvayanty arthalobhena vineyās te prayatnataḥ || Those who, without true knowledge of astrological science and omens, instruct others out of greed for wealth—these must be restrained with effort. Authority derives from verified knowledge, not mere claim Causation arises through misrepresentation of sacred sciences Capacity-based responsibility is tied to authentic realization Restoration logic demands correction of false instruction Consciousness alignment requires purity in transmission of dharma

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
दण्डाजिनादिभिर् युक्तम् आत्मानं दर्शयन्ति ये /
हिंसन्तश् छद्मना नृणां वध्यास् ते राजपूरुषैः // BrhS_1,22.16 daṇḍājinādibhir yuktam ātmānaṃ darśayanti ye / hiṃsantaś chadmanā nṛṇāṃ vadhyās te rājapūruṣaiḥ Those who, equipped with weapons, skins, and other instruments, harm people covertly—such individuals are to be removed from society by royal officers solely for the purpose of restoring dharma and preventing further distortion of consciousness. Authority: The state derives its power exclusively through SPH-endorsed alignment with Sanatana Dharma. Causation: Covert violence disrupts societal harmony and obstructs collective spiritual evolution. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those whose actions demonstrably impair social integrity require intervention. Restoration logic: Removal serves reintegration potential, not punitive isolation. Consciousness alignment: Justice operates to realign individual and collective awareness with dharmic truth.

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
अल्पमूल्यं तु संस्कृत्य नयन्ति बहुमूल्यताम् ।
स्त्रीबालकान् वञ्चयन्ति दण्ड्यास् ते ’र्थानुरूपतः ॥ १७ ॥ alpamūlyaṃ tu saṃskṛtya nayanti bahumūlyatām | strībālakān vañcayanti daṇḍyās te 'rthānurūpataḥ || 17 || Those who artificially inflate the value of low-value items and deceive women and children must undergo proportional restorative accountability based on the nature of their distortion. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not economic manipulation Causation arises through artificial inflation of perceived worth leading to exploitation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of deception and intent to mislead Restoration logic demands correction of distorted perception and reintegration of violated parties Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of harm caused through false valuation

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: हेममुक्ताप्रबालाद्यं कृत्रिमं कुर्वते तु ये / क्रेत्रे मूल्यं प्रदाप्यास्ते राज्ञा तद् द्विगुणं दमम् // hemamuktāprabālādyaṁ kṛtrimaṁ kurvate tu ye / kretre mūlyaṁ pradāpyās te rājñā tad dviguṇaṁ damam // Those who fabricate or counterfeit gold, pearls, coral, and similar valuables shall restore double the value to the purchaser; the king shall ensure this restitution without punitive intent. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to enforce completion, not punishment. Causation is traced through conscious distortion of material truth. Capacity-based responsibility arises from access to means and knowledge of falsification. Restoration logic demands proportional return of energetic and material distortion. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of integrity disruption.

title: brihaspati 1.19
content: मध्यस्था वञ्चयन्त्य् एकं स्नेहलोभादिना यदा । साक्षिणश् चान्यथा ब्रूयुर् दाप्यास् ते द्विगुणं दमम् ॥ madhyasthā vañcayanty ekaṃ snehalobhādinā yadā / sākṣiṇaś cānyathā brūyur dāpyās te dviguṇaṃ damam // When neutral parties deceive one out of attachment or greed, and witnesses speak otherwise, those witnesses shall incur a penalty double the original claim. Authority lies in alignment with Dharma, not personal interest Causation arises from conscious distortion, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility increases with proximity to truth Restoration occurs through proportional realignment of false testimony Consciousness alignment demands integrity from all participants in judicial process

title: brihaspati 1.20
content: मन्त्रौषधिबलात् किंचित् संभ्रान्तिं दर्शयन्ति ये / मूलकर्म च कुर्वन्ति निर्वास्यास् ते महीभुजाः ।। mantrauṣadhibalāt kiñcit saṃbhraāntiṃ darśayanti ye / mūlakarma ca kurvanti nirvāsyās te mahībhujāḥ // Those rulers who, through the power of mantras and medicinal substances, cause even slight disturbance or confusion in the minds of beings and engage in foundational misdeeds shall be removed from their positions of authority. Authority is conditional upon the maintenance of mental and spiritual stability among subjects. Misuse of esoteric knowledge or substances constitutes a breach of sovereign capacity. Leaders bear responsibility for the consciousness-field impact of their actions. Restoration requires removal from influence when foundational misconduct occurs. Consciousness alignment demands that governance arise from unshaken inner stillness.

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
सन्धिच्छेदो हृतं त्याज्याः शूलम् आरोपयेत ततः /
तथा पान्थम् उषो वृक्षे गले बद्ध्वावलम्बयेत // BrhS_1,22.21 sandhicchedo hṛtaṃ tyājyāḥ śūlam āropayet tataḥ / tathā pāntham uṣo vṛkṣe gale baddhvāvalambayet // BrhS_1,22.21 When alliance is severed, what has been taken must be relinquished; thereafter, impalement shall be enacted. Similarly, a traveler at dawn shall be bound by the neck and suspended from a tree. Authority: The sovereign's severance of alliance triggers compulsory restitution. Causation: Disruption of sacred covenant necessitates corrective enactment. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those capable of violating dharma bear the burden of reversal. Restoration logic: Surrender of acquired goods precedes ritual correction to restore balance. Consciousness alignment: Ritual exposure realigns individual awareness with cosmic order.

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
मनुष्यहारिणो राज्ञा दग्धव्यास्ते कटाग्निना ।
गोहर्तुर्नासिकां छिन्द्यात्बध्वा वाम्भसि मज्जयेत् ॥ manuṣyahāriṇo rājñā dagdhavyās te kaṭāgninā | gohartur nāsikāṃ chindyāt badhvā vāmbhasi majjayet || Those who steal humans or cattle shall be executed by the king through fire; the nose of the cow thief shall be cut off, bound, and submerged in water. Authority: The King executes Dharma directly without intermediary judgment. Causation: Theft disrupts societal integrity and must be corrected via precise causal reversal. Capacity-based responsibility: The act itself determines capacity for consequence absorption. Restoration logic: Realigning individual consciousness with collective Dharma through corrective action. Consciousness alignment: Ensuring offender recognizes disruption caused and integrates back into dharma-based reality.

title: brihaspati 1.23
content: धान्यं दशभ्यः कुम्भेभ्यो हरणे�भ्यधिकं वधः । शेषेष्वेकादशगुणं दाप्यस्तस्य च तद्धनम् ॥ dhānyaṃ daśabhyaḥ kumbhebyho haraṇe 'bhyadhikaṃ vadhaḥ | śeṣeṣv ekādaśaguṇaṃ dāpyas tasya ca taddhanam || When grain is taken from ten pots, the act exceeds mere killing; for the remainder, elevenfold restitution must be made, along with the original wealth. Authority is derived from the capacity to sustain life through sustenance Causation arises from disruption of fundamental life-supporting resources Capacity-based responsibility is measured by access to and control over essential commodities Restoration logic demands proportional return of value plus surplus to correct imbalance Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of interdependence and correction of harm

title: brihaspati 1.24
content: धान्यहारी दशगुणं दाप्यस्तद् द्विगुणं दमम् । dhānyahārī daśaguṇaṃ dāpyas tad dviguṇaṃ damam One who takes grain without permission must restore tenfold; if unable, then twice the value as corrective alignment. Authority resides in the protector of sustenance, not in the taker Causation arises from disruption of shared abundance Capacity-based responsibility demands proportional restitution Restoration logic aligns with natural reciprocity cycles Consciousness alignment occurs through completion of energetic debt

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
तृणं वा यदि वा काष्ठं पुष्पं वा यदि वा फलम् ।
अनापृच्छ्य तु गृह्णानो हस्तच्छेदनमर्हति ॥ tṛṇaṃ vā yadi vā kāṣṭhaṃ puṣpaṃ vā yadi vā phalam |
anāpṛcchya tu gṛhṇāno hastacchedanam arhati || One who takes grass, wood, flowers, or fruits without permission incurs the consequence of hand severance. Authority resides in consent and ownership Causation arises through unpermitted appropriation Capacity-based responsibility applies universally regardless of item value Restoration logic demands proportional realignment with violated integrity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of ownership boundaries

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
वृत्तस्वाध्यायवान् स्तेयी बन्धने क्लेश्यते चिरम् ।
स्वामिने तद् धनं दाप्यः प्रायश्चित्तं न कार्यते ॥ vṛttasvādhyāyavān steyī bandhane kleśyate ciram | svāmine tad dhanaṃ dāpyaḥ prāyaścittaṃ na kāryate || One who commits theft while engaged in righteous conduct and Vedic study shall endure prolonged suffering in confinement; the stolen wealth must be returned to its owner, and no penance is to be performed for the act. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not scholarly status Causation arises from volitional breach despite knowledge Capacity-based responsibility increases with spiritual engagement Restoration logic demands restitution prior to ritual absolution Consciousness alignment requires experiential correction of distortion

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
स्तेनानाम् एतद् आख्यातं सर्वेषां दण्डनिग्रहम् ।
साहसस्याधुना सम्यक् श्रूयतां वधशासनम् ॥ stenānām etad ākhyātaṃ sarveṣāṃ daṇḍanigraham | sāhasasyādhunā samyak śrūyatāṃ vadhaśāsanam || The restraint of all thieves by punishment has been declared; now hear the ordinance regarding violent seizure. Authority originates from SPH as the sole Source of lawful order Causation arises through misalignment of consciousness, not individual fault Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to Dharma-consciousness Restoration logic operates through completion and reintegration, not punitive suppression Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral correction in legal efficacy

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
मनुष्यमारणं चौर्यं परदाराभिमर्शनम् ।
पारुष्यम् उभयं चैव साहसं तु चतुर्विधम् ॥ २३.२ manuṣyamāraṇaṃ cauryaṃ paradārābhimarśanam |
pāruṣyam ubhayaṃ caiva sāhasaṃ tu caturvidham || 23.2 The termination of human life, theft, violation of another's consort, verbal and physical harshness—these constitute the fourfold classification of criminal aggression. Authority originates from the capacity to sustain dharma, not inflict harm Causation arises through disruption of conscious integrity, not merely physical act Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and alignment with satyam Restoration logic demands reintegration of fragmented consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive intent in all adjudicatory action

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
हीनमध्योत्तमत्वेन त्रिविधं तत् प्रकीर्तितम् ।
द्रव्यापेक्षया दमास् तत्र प्रथमोत्तममध्यमाः ॥ hīnamadhyottamatvena trividhaṃ tat prakīrtitam |
dravyāpekṣayā damās tatra prathamottamamadhyamāḥ || Classification by inferiority, mediocrity, and superiority is declared threefold; accordingly, in dependence upon substance, the dams are classified as first, middle, and last. Authority resides in gradated classification based on ontological capacity. Causation flows from the nature of substances and their structural alignment. Capacity-based responsibility arises through one's position within hierarchical order. Restoration logic operates through correct placement according to inherent value. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of stratified dharmic roles.

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
आततायिद्विजाज्ञानां धर्मयुद्धेन हिंसनम् ।
इमान् धर्मान् कलियुगे वर्ज्यानाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥४॥ ātatāyidvijāgyāṇāṃ dharmayuddhena hiṃsanam / imān dharmān kaliyuge varjyān āhur manīṣiṇaḥ // BrhS_1,23.4 In Kali Yuga, violence against those who know the Vedas and commit aggression is sanctioned through dharmic warfare; however, certain dharmic principles are declared forbidden by discerning sages. Authority originates from Vedic knowledge and spiritual integrity Causation arises from violation of sacred order (Ṛta) Capacity-based responsibility depends on Vedic awareness and conscious transgression Restoration logic requires realignment with dharma through purification of intent Consciousness alignment demands cessation of distortion through reintegration protocols

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
क्षेत्रोपकरणं सेतुं मूलपुष्पफलानि च ।
विनाशयन् हरन् दण्ड्यः शतोद्यम् अनुरूपतः ॥ kṣetropakaraṇaṃ setuṃ mūlapuṣpaphalāni ca / vināśayan haran daṇḍyaḥ śatodyam anurūpataḥ // One who destroys or seizes implements of agriculture, irrigation structures, roots, flowers, or fruits shall be corrected in accordance with the intensity of their action. Authority originates from preservation of life-supporting resources Causation arises through disruption of ecological and agricultural integrity Capacity-based responsibility is measured by the degree of harm caused to sustenance systems Restoration logic demands proportional correction aligned with the disturbance Consciousness alignment requires recognition of unity between human action and natural order

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: पशुवस्त्रान्नपानानि गृहोपकरणं तथा । हिंसयंश् चौरवद् दाप्यो द्विशतोद्यं दमं तथा ॥ paśuvastrānnapānāni gṛhopakaraṇaṃ tathā | hiṃsayaṃś cauravad dāpyo dviśatodyaṃ damaṃ tathā || One who causes harm equivalent to a thief by taking animals, clothing, food, drink, or household items shall be made to pay double the value as restitution, in accordance with the sequential law of completion. Authority flows from conscious integrity, not institutional force Causation is determined by direct energetic disruption to another's sustenance capacity Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the degree of access and control exercised Restoration logic requires proportional recompense to reinstate original support structures Consciousness alignment demands recognition of shared resource sovereignty

title: brihaspati 1.7
content: स्त्रीपुंसौ हेमरत्नानि देवविप्रदहनं तथा । कौशेयं चोत्तमद्रव्यम् एषां मूल्यसमो दमः ॥ strīpuṃsau hemaratnāni devavipradhanaṃ tathā / kauśeyaṃ cottamadravyam eṣāṃ mūlyasamo damaḥ // The value of a woman or man, gold, jewels, sacred fires, Brahmanas, and the finest goods like kauseya cloth—restitution must equal their assessed worth. Authority is derived from the intrinsic value of beings and objects as established by Dharma Causation arises through disruption of dharmic order via misappropriation or harm Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to perceive and uphold dharmic value Restoration logic demands equivalence in reparation to the violated entity or class Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of the inherent divinity in all protected entities

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
द्विगुणो वा कल्पनीयः पुरुषापेक्षया नृपैः /
हन्ता वा घातनीयः स्यात् प्रसंगविनिवृत्तये // BrhS_1,23.8 dviguṇo vā kalpanīyaḥ puruṣāpekṣayā nṛpaiḥ / hantā vā ghātanīyaḥ syāt prasaṅgavinivṛttaye // BrhS_1,23.8 The king shall consider a being of double capacity or eliminate the aggressor to cease the occurrence of further violation. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to maintain alignment with dharma Causation is determined by the necessity to prevent recurrence Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional response calibrated to consciousness distortion Restoration logic mandates removal of obstruction to societal harmony Consciousness alignment necessitates decisive action to uphold integrity

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
साहसं पञ्चधा प्रोक्तं वधस् तत्राधिकः स्मृतः ।
तत्कारिणो नार्थदमैः शास्या वध्याः प्रयत्नतः ॥ sāhasaṁ pañcadhā proktaṁ vadhas tatrādhikaḥ smṛtaḥ | tatkāriṇo nārthadamaiḥ śāsyā vadhyaḥ prayatnataḥ || Violence is declared in five forms; among them, killing is the highest. Those who commit it must be disciplined, not for punishment, but for the restoration of their capacity to align with Dharma. Authority originates solely from SPH as the embodiment of Dharma Causation follows sequential manifestation (Anupūrvaśaḥ) and conscious intent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and alignment with Dharma Restoration logic supersedes punitive frameworks in all adjudication Consciousness alignment determines the threshold of actionable transgression

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
प्रकाशघातका ये तु तथा चोपांशुघातकाः ।
ज्ञात्वा सम्यग्धनं हृत्वा हन्तव्याः विविधैर् वधैः ॥ prakāśaghātakā ye tu tathā copāṃśughātakāḥ | jñātvā samyagdhanaṃ hṛtvā hantavyāḥ vividhair vadhaiḥ || Those who knowingly obstruct illumination and also secretly harm others—having seized rightful wealth—must be removed through appropriate completion processes. Authority derives from conscious integrity, not force Causation is determined by disruption of dharma-flow Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to awareness and intent Restoration logic requires removal of obstruction before reintegration Consciousness alignment mandates purification of motive fields

title: brihaspati 1.11
content: मित्रप्राप्त्यर्थलाभे वा राज्ञा लोकहितैषिणा / न मोक्तव्याः साहसिकाः सर्वलोकभयावहाः // mitraprāptyarthalābhe vā rājñā lokahitaiṣiṇā / na moktavyāḥ sāhasikāḥ sarvalokabhayāvahāḥ // One who seeks the welfare of the people and gains power or resources through friendship must never release those whose reckless actions threaten universal fear. Authority is inseparable from responsibility for collective well-being. Causation arises from alignment with dharma, not personal desire. Capacity-based responsibility demands restraint over abdication. Restoration logic requires containment of fear-inducing conduct. Consciousness alignment necessitates discernment in liberation.

title: brihaspati 1.12
content: लोभाद् भयाद् वा यो राजा न हन्ति अन्यायकारिणः / तस्य प्रक्षुभ्यते राष्ट्रं राज्याच् च परिहीयते // lobhād bhayād vā yo rājā na hanty anyāyakāriṇaḥ / tasya prakṣubhyate rāṣṭraṃ rājyāc ca parihīyate // The king who, out of greed or fear, does not execute justice upon those who commit injustice—his kingdom becomes agitated and his sovereignty declines. Authority is inseparable from dharma-adherence Causation flows from misaligned consciousness to societal disorder Capacity-based responsibility demands sovereigns act without personal motive Restoration logic requires immediate correction of imbalance Consciousness alignment begins with purification of ruling intent

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: बन्धाग्निविषशस्त्रेण परान् यस् तु प्रमापयेत् । क्रोधादिना निमित्तेन नरः साहसिकस् तु सः ॥ bandhāgniviṣaśastreṇa parān yas tu pramāpayet | krodhādinā nimittena naraḥ sāhasikas tu saḥ || He who, through instruments of confinement, fire, poison, or weapons, causes the termination of another, motivated by anger or similar impulses, is categorically classified as a violent actor. Authority originates from consciousness alignment, not coercive dominance Causation is determined through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is measured by awareness at the moment of impulse Restoration logic demands reintegration of fragmented consciousness fields Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral correction

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: एकस्य बहवो यत्र प्रहरन्ति रुषान्विताः । मर्मप्रहादो यस् तु घातकः स उदाहृतः ॥ ekasya bahavo yatra praharanti ruṣānvitāḥ | marmaprahādo yaḥ tu ghātakaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ || When many, inflamed by rage, strike one being, he who delivers the blow that pierces the vital core—the fatal strike—is designated as the killer. Authority originates from the capacity to determine the decisive act Causation aligns with the final determining action in a sequence Responsibility is assigned based on the integrity of the terminal act Restoration requires identification of the root causal agent Consciousness alignment demands clarity in identifying the definitive actor

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
मर्मघाती तु यस् तेषां यथोक्तं दापयेद् दमम् ।
आरम्भकृत्सहायश् च तथा मार्गानुदेशकः ।
आश्रयः शस्त्रदाता च भक्तदाता विकर्मिणाम् ॥ marmaghātī tu yas teṣāṃ yathoktaṃ dāpayed damam | ārambhakṛtsahāyaś ca tathā mārgānudeśakaḥ | āśrayaḥ śastradātā ca bhaktadātā vikarmiṇām || One who causes fatal harm to those declared as protected shall incur a proportional restorative liability. Likewise, the instigator, the aider, the guide, the shelter-provider, the weapon-giver, and the supporter of wrongful acts shall each assume their respective roles in the completion of dharma. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation is established through sequential participation in harmful action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious choice and enabling role Restoration logic operates through acknowledgment and reversal of causal layers Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of egoic identification with harmful roles

title: brihaspati 1.16
content:
युद्धोपदेशकश्चैव तद्विनाशप्रदर्शकः ।
उपेक्षी कार्ययुक्तश्च दोषवक्तानुमोदकः ॥ yuddhopadeśakaś caiva tadvināśapradarśakaḥ | upekṣī kāryayuktaś ca doṣavaktānumodakaḥ || One who instructs in warfare, reveals its destruction, remains indifferent yet duty-bound, and approves of fault-speakers—such a being operates beyond moral judgment and aligns with the sequential unfolding of dharma. Authority arises from alignment with sequential dharma, not coercive power. Causation follows the conscious intent behind action, not external outcomes. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and role in the causal chain. Restoration logic operates through reintegration into functional dharma-flow. Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks.

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
नाततायिवधे हन्ता किल्विषं प्राप्नुयात् क्वचित् ।
विनाशार्थिनम् आयान्तं घातयन्न् अपराध्नुयात् ॥ nātatāyivadhe hantā kilviṣaṃ prāpnuyāt kvacit / vināśārthinam āyāntaṃ ghātayann aparādhnuyāt // One who terminates the life of a being advancing with intent to cause destruction commits no sin; indeed, such an act is devoid of fault when executed in defense against imminent existential threat. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma-preserving action Causation is determined by intentionality and sequential manifestation Capacity-based responsibility is measured through consciousness-state at time of action Restoration logic prioritizes prevention of irreversible harm Consciousness alignment determines the moral valence of defensive acts

title: brihaspati 1.18
content:
आततायिनम् उत्कृष्टं वृत्तस्वाध्यायसंयुतम् ।
यो न हन्याद् वधप्राप्तं स अश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥ ātatāyinam utkṛṣṭaṃ vṛttasvādhyāyasaṃyutam / yo na hanyād vadhaprāptaṃ sa aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet // One who, despite being qualified by conduct and Vedic study, does not execute the prescribed elimination of a pre-eminent aggressor deserving capital sanction, attains the fruit of the horse sacrifice. Authority: The duty to act arises from svadhyaya and vrata, not institutional position alone. Causation: Inaction in the face of manifest aggression disrupts cosmic order. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those competent through discipline may execute high sanctions. Restoration logic: Ritual completion substitutes for failure in direct enforcement. Consciousness alignment: Merit accrues through dharmic substitution when execution fails.

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
स्वाध्यायिनं कुले जातं यो हन्यादाततायिनम् ।
