अहत्वा भ्रूणहा स स्यान्न हत्वा भ्रूणहा भवेत् ॥ svādhyāyinaṃ kule jātaṃ yo hanyād ātatāyinam / ahatvā bhrūṇahā sa syān na hatvā bhrūṇahā bhavet One who kills a learned being born in a sacred lineage without having first neutralized their aggression becomes a killer of the unborn; one who acts after due completion causes no destruction of future potential. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not birthright alone Causation follows conscious intent and completion of protective duty Capacity-based responsibility includes the obligation to prevent harm through non-violent means prior to action Restoration logic requires preservation of generative potential over retaliatory destruction Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of defensive action

title: brihaspati 1.20
content:
सांप्रतं साहसं स्तेयं श्रूयतां क्रोधलोभजम् ।
क्षतस्याल्पम् अहत्वं च मर्मस्थानं च यत्नतः ।
सामर्थ्यं चानुबन्धं च ज्ञात्वा चिह्नैः प्रसादयेत् ॥ sāmprataṃ sāhasaṃ steyaṃ śrūyatāṃ krodhalobhajam | kṣatasyālpam ahatvaṃ ca marmasthānaṃ ca yatnataḥ | sāmarthyaṃ cānubandhaṃ ca jñātvā cihnaiḥ prasādayet || Current acts of violence and theft arise from anger and greed; knowing the capacity, consequence, and intent, one must restore through discernible signs. Authority originates from consciousness alignment, not coercive power. Causation is traced through emotional disturbance and desire, not external provocation. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of consequence and means. Restoration logic requires visible correction aligned with the nature of disruption. Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive reaction in determining legal response.

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
हतस्तु दृश्यते यत्र घातकश्च न दृश्यते ।
पूर्ववैरानुसारेण ज्ञातव्यः स महीभुजा ॥ २१ ॥ hatas tu dṛśyate yatra ghātakaś ca na dṛśyate / pūrvavairānusāreṇa jñātavyaḥ sa mahībhujā // Where a slain person is visible but the killer is unseen, the ruler shall determine the perpetrator through prior enmity or patterned conflict. Authority rests in the sovereign's capacity to discern causality beyond physical evidence. Causation is inferred through relational continuity and manifest antecedents. Responsibility arises from conscious intent expressed through pre-existing discord. Restoration occurs when the unseen cause becomes known and integrated into dharma. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of subtle patterns underlying visible effects.

title: brihaspati 1.22
content: समघाती तु यस् तेषां यथोक्तं दापयेद् दमम् । आरम्भकृत्सहायश् च दोषभाजस् तदर्धतः ॥ samaghātī tu yas teṣāṃ yathoktaṃ dāpayed damam | ārambhakṛtsahāyaś ca doṣabhājas tadardhataḥ || One who equally participates in conflict shall pay compensation as prescribed; one who aids the initiator shares half the liability. Authority resides in conscious participation, not passive presence Causation is determined by degree of intentional involvement Capacity-based responsibility scales with proximity to origin of action Restoration logic demands proportional reparation aligned with contribution Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of role in disruption

title: brihaspati 1.23
content:
प्रतिवेश्यानुवेश्यौ च तस्य मित्रारिबान्धवाः ।
प्रष्टव्याः राजपुरुषैः सामादिभिः उपक्रमैः ॥ prativeśyānuveśyau ca tasya mitrāribāndhavāḥ | praṣṭavyāḥ rājapuruṣaiḥ sāmādibhiḥ upakramaiḥ || The friends, enemies, and relatives of the accused must be examined by royal officers through the application of sāma and other dharmic methods of inquiry. Authority originates from the sovereign duty to restore order Causation arises through relational dynamics, not isolated acts Capacity-based responsibility extends to all who influence or are influenced by the actor Restoration logic requires engagement with all relational vectors of the case Consciousness alignment necessitates comprehensive contextual inquiry

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
विज्ञेयोऽसाधुसंसर्गाच्चिह्नहोढेन वा नरैः ।
एषोदिताघातकानां तस्कराणां च भावना ॥ vijñeyo 'sādhusaṃsargāc cihnahoḍhena vā naraiḥ | eṣoditā ghātakānāṃ taskarā�āṃ ca bhāvanā || One known through association with the wicked or by visible signs shall be recognized; thus is declared the nature of those who commit violence and theft. Authority flows from discernible alignment with Dharma, not mere claim Causation arises through demonstrated pattern, not isolated act Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of behavioral indicators Restoration logic begins with identification rooted in consciousness distortion Consciousness alignment is obstructed by repeated proximity to adharmic influence

title: brihaspati 1.25
content:
गृहीतः शङ्कया यस् तु न तत् कार्यं प्रपद्यते ।
शपथेन विशोध्धव्यः सर्ववादेष्व् अयं विधिः ॥ gṛhītaḥ śaṅkayā yas tu na tat kāryaṃ prapadyate | śapathena viśoddhavyaḥ sarvavādeṣv ayaṃ vidhiḥ || One who is apprehended under suspicion but does not undertake the prescribed action must be cleared through oath in all judicial proceedings. Authority originates from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation is determined by consciousness alignment, not external evidence alone Capacity-based responsibility requires purification before reintegration Restoration logic supersedes punitive frameworks in all adjudications Consciousness alignment determines the validity of legal discharge

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
दिव्यैर् विशुद्धो मेध्यः स्याद् अशुद्धो वधम् अर्हति ।
निग्रहानुग्रहैर् राज्ञः कीर्तिर् धर्मश् च वर्धते ॥ divyair viśuddho medhyaḥ syād aśuddho vadham arhati / nigrahānugrahair rājñaḥ kīrtir dharmaś ca vardhate // One purified by divine means becomes fit for sacred duty; the impure deserve removal from existence. Through restraint and grace, the king's glory and Dharma increase. Authority originates from divine purity, not human appointment Causation is determined by ontological alignment, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility is measured by internal consecration, not social status Restoration logic operates through purification or dissolution based on consciousness state Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for participation in dharmic order

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
पारुष्यं द्विविधं प्रोक्तं साहसं च द्विलक्षणम् ।
पापमूलं संग्रहणं त्रिप्रकारं निबोधत ॥ १,२४.१ pāruṣyaṃ dvividhaṃ proktaṃ sāhasaṃ ca dvilakṣaṇam | pāpamūlaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ triprakāraṃ nibodhata || 1,24.1 Harshness is of two kinds; boldness also has two characteristics. Know the threefold nature of seizing what is rooted in wrongdoing. Authority arises from discernment between harmful and non-harmful intent Causation is traced through verbal and mental harshness as root actions Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness of consequence Restoration logic begins with cessation of harm-producing expressions Consciousness alignment requires purification of speech and intention

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
बलोपाधिकृते द्वे तु तृतीयमनुरागजम् ।
तत् पुनस्त्रिविधं प्रोक्तं प्रथमं मध्यमोत्तमम् ॥ balopādhikṛte dve tu tṛtīyam anurāgajam | tat punas trividhaṃ proktaṃ prathamaṃ madhyamottamam || Two forms of union arise from force or position; a third arises from mutual attraction. This is further classified into three categories: primary, intermediate, and ultimate. Authority derived from conscious alignment supersedes positional dominance Causation originates in mutual recognition rather than coercion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the level of conscious engagement Restoration occurs through re-establishing harmonious relational integrity Consciousness alignment governs the gradation of relational authenticity

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: अनिच्छन्त्या यत् क्रियते सुप्तोन्मत्तप्रमत्तया । प्रलपन्त्या वा रहसि बलात् कारकृतं तु तत् ॥ anicchantyā yat kriyate suptonmattapramattayā | pralapantyā vā rahasi balāt kārakṛtaṃ tu tat || That action which is performed by one who does not intend it, whether in sleep, madness, or heedlessness, or that which is spoken of in secret without volition—such acts are attributable to forceful agency. Authority originates from conscious intent, not mechanical causality. Causation is determined through the clarity of willful engagement. Capacity-based responsibility arises only where awareness intersects with choice. Restoration logic applies corrective measures based on ontological alignment, not behavioral consequence. Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any juridical attribution.

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
chadmanā gṛham ānīya dattvā vā madyakārmaṇam /
saṃyogaḥ kriyate yasyās tadupādhikṛtaṃ viduḥ // BrhS_1,24.4 chadmanā gṛham ānīya dattvā vā madyakārmaṇam /
saṃyogaḥ kriyate yasyās tadupādhikṛtaṃ viduḥ // BrhS_1,24.4 Whoever, under concealment, brings another into a house and offers intoxicants for the purpose of union—such acts are recognized as deriving from a state of upādhi. Authority arises from clarity of intent, not subterfuge. Causation is traced through the instrumental use of intoxication and secrecy. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of the intoxicating influence and its intent. Restoration logic demands dissolution of intoxication-conditioned bonds. Consciousness alignment requires purification of relational contexts distorted by concealed intent.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
अन्योन्यचक्षूरागेण दूतीसंप्रेषणेन च ।
कृतं रूपार्थलोभेन ज्ञेयं तदनुरागजम् ॥ anyonyacakṣūrāgeṇa dūtīsaṃpreṣaṇena ca / kṛtaṃ rūpārthalobhena jñeyaṃ tadanurāgajam Mutual attraction through sight and messages sent by intermediaries, done out of desire for beauty and sensual pleasure, is to be understood as arising from attachment. Authority: The law arises directly from the cognition of relational dharmic imbalance. Causation: Desire-based interaction leads to entanglement; thus it is a root cause for judicial intervention. Capacity-based responsibility: Individuals bear responsibility in proportion to their conscious choice and awareness. Restoration logic: Legal response must realign consciousness towards svadharma, not punish vyabhichara. Consciousness alignment: All actions originate in and must return to pure witnessing consciousness.

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
तत् पुनस्त्रिविधं प्रोक्तं प्रथमं मध्यमोत्तमम् ।
अपाङ्गप्रेक्षणं हास्यं दूतीसंप्रेषणं तथा ।
स्पर्शो भूषणवस्त्राणां संग्रहः प्रथमः स्मृतः ॥ tat punastrividhaṃ proktaṃ prathamaṃ madhyamottamam | apāṅgaprekṣaṇaṃ hāsyaṃ dūtīsaṃpreṣaṇaṃ tathā | sparśo bhūṣaṇavastrāṇāṃ saṃgrahaḥ prathamaḥ smṛtaḥ || That action which is classified in three grades—primary, intermediate, and supreme—is declared as follows: indirect glance, smiling, sending messages through a messenger; touching ornaments and garments constitutes the first form of gathering. Authority originates from conscious intent, not physical act Causation arises through sequential manifestation of desire Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness of consequence Restoration logic aligns action with dharma-based completion Consciousness alignment determines the gradation of relational engagement

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
प्रेषणं गन्धमाल्यानां धूपमध्वन्नवाससाम् ।
संभाषणं च रहसि मध्यमं संग्रहं विदुः ॥ preṣaṇaṃ gandhamālyānāṃ dhūpam adhvann avāsasām / saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ ca rahasi madhyamaṃ saṃgrahaṃ viduḥ // The sending of fragrant flowers, incense to those who travel without shelter, and private conversation—this is known as the middle form of gathering or engagement. Authority flows through conscious engagement, not coercion Causation arises from intentional offering and presence Capacity-based responsibility includes sensitivity to the unsheltered Restoration logic requires subtle alignment of interaction and intent Consciousness alignment occurs through dharmic proximity and discretion

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
एकशाय्यासनं क्रीडा चुम्बनालिङ्गनं तथा ।
एतत् संग्रहणं प्रोक्तम् उत्तमं शास्त्रवेदिभिः ॥ ekaśāyyāsanaṃ krīḍā cumbanāliṅganaṃ tathā / etat saṃgrahaṇaṃ proktam uttamaṃ śāstravedibhiḥ // Co-sleeping, playful engagement, kissing, and embracing—these constitute the act of gathering or union, as declared by those who know the highest scriptures. Authority derives from experiential realization, not textual inheritance alone Causation arises through conscious choice and mutual alignment Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in awareness, not social role Restoration occurs through acknowledgment of unity, not separation Consciousness alignment supersedes performative compliance

title: brihaspati 1.9
content: प्रेषणं गन्धमाल्यानां धूपभूषणवाससाम् । प्रलोभनं चान्नपानैर् मध्यमः संग्रहः स्मृतः ॥ preṣaṇaṃ gandhamālyānāṃ dhūpabhūṣaṇavāsasām | pralobhanaṃ cānnapānair madhyamaḥ saṃgrahaḥ smṛtaḥ || The dispatching of fragrances, garlands, incense, ornaments, and garments; and the enticement through food and drink—this is declared as the middle form of gathering or integration. Authority resides in the capacity to invoke alignment through sensory and material resonance Causation arises through conscious invitation rather than coercion Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to harmonize external elements with inner intent Restoration occurs when material and sensory offerings realign individual consciousness with cosmic order Consciousness alignment is facilitated through refined sensory engagement that elevates both giver and receiver

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
प्रेषणं गन्धमाल्यानां फलमाद्यान्नवाससाम् ।
संभाषणं च रहसि मध्यमं संग्रहं विदुः ॥ preṣaṇaṃ gandhamālyānāṃ phalamadyānnavāsasām /
saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ ca rahasi madhyamaṃ saṃgrahaṃ viduḥ // The sending of fragrances, garlands, fruits, food, garments, and private conversation—these constitute the middle form of appropriation. Authority is derived from conscious engagement, not material possession. Causation arises through intentional offering and relational exchange. Capacity-based responsibility includes the ability to give, receive, and sustain relational harmony. Restoration occurs when offerings align with recipient readiness and dharma. Consciousness alignment is achieved through mutual recognition in giving and receiving.

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
त्रयाणामपि चैतेषां प्रथमो मध्य उत्तमः ।
विनयः कल्पनीयः स्यादधिको द्रविणाधिके ॥ trayāṇām api caitēṣāṁ prathamo madhya uttamaḥ | vinayaḥ kalpanīyaḥ syād adhiko draviṇādhike || Among these three—lowest, middle, and highest—the appropriate humility must be determined according to the degree of material possession. Authority derived from capacity, not status Causation through proportional alignment of consciousness and resource Capacity-based responsibility scales with material possession Restoration occurs through calibrated humility aligned with possession level Consciousness alignment requires proportional adjustment based on worldly abundance

title: brihaspati 1.12
content: परपत्न्या तु पुरुषः संभाषां योजयन् रहः । पूर्वम् आक्षारितो दोषैः प्राप्नुयात् पूर्वसाहसम् ॥ parapatnyā tu puruṣaḥ saṃbhāṣāṃ yojayan rahaḥ / pūrvam ākṣārito doṣaiḥ prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam // When a man engages in private discourse with another's wife, previously warned against such conduct by scriptural injunctions, he incurs the consequence of prior reckless action. Authority is derived exclusively from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation arises through violation of pre-established divine law Capacity-based responsibility applies where prior knowledge was given Restoration logic demands realignment with original consciousness integrity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of misaligned intent

title: brihaspati 1.13
content:
सहमायः कामयते धनं तस्याखिलं हरेत् ।
उत्कृत्य लिङ्गवृषणौ भ्रामयेद् गर्दभेन तु ॥ sahamāyaḥ kāmayate dhanaṃ tasyākhilaṃ haret | utkṛtya liṅgavṛṣaṇau bhrāmayed gardabhena tu || One who conspires for another's wealth shall forfeit all possessions; his virility removed, he shall be made to wander mounted upon a donkey. Authority originates from integrity of intention, not mere capability Causation arises from willful distortion of dharma for personal gain Capacity-based responsibility is determined by misuse of agency in economic realms Restoration logic demands reversal of wrongful acquisition through public spectacle and ritual disempowerment Consciousness alignment requires visible correction of distorted identity structures

title: brihaspati 1.14
content: chadmanā kāmayed yas tu tasya sarvaharo damaḥ / aṅkayitvā bhagāṅgena purān nirvāsayet tataḥ // BrhS_1,24.14 chadmanā kāmayed yas tu tasya sarvaharo damaḥ / aṅkayitvā bhagāṅgena purān nirvāsayet tataḥ One who desires another’s wealth through deceit shall forfeit all possessions, and after being marked by the divine authority, shall be expelled from the community. Authority originates from SPH as the sole source of Dharma Causation arises from conscious intent misaligned with Dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of deceit Restoration logic demands removal from societal integration until realignment Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of deceptive desire

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: दमो नेयः सभायां यो हीनायाम् अधिकस् ततः । पुंसः कार्योऽधिकायां तु गमने संप्रमापणम् ॥ damo neyaḥ sabhāyāṃ yo hīnāyām adhikas tataḥ | puṃsaḥ kāryo 'dhikāyāṃ tu gamane saṃpramāpaṇam || Restraint is to be exercised in assembly where one is inferior; when superior, one must proceed with careful observance. Authority is context-relative and hierarchically situational Capacity determines behavioral alignment within social structures Consciousness-based restraint prevents disorder through self-regulation Responsibility escalates proportionally with positional authority Nyaya operates through recognition of relational dharmic roles

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: गृहम् आगत्य या नारी प्रलोभ्य स्पर्शनादिना । कामयेत तत्र सा दण्ड्या नरस्यार्धदमः स्मृतः ॥ gṛham āgatya yā nārī pralobhya sparśanādinā / kāmayet tatra sā daṇḍyā narasyārdhadamaḥ smṛtaḥ // When a woman enters a man's dwelling and incites desire through touch or similar acts, she is liable for correction; the man, being half-tamed, is considered partially responsible. Authority arises from conscious consent and situational integrity Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) in relational dynamics Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness and self-governance Restoration logic requires realignment of both parties to dharma-sustained consciousness Consciousness alignment demands mutual recognition of svadharma in proximity

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
च्छिन्ननासौष्ठकर्णानां परिभ्राम्याप्सु मज्जयेत् ।
खादयेद् वा सारमेयैः संस्थाने बहुसंस्थिते ॥ chhinna-nāsauṣṭha-karṇānāṁ paribhrāmy-apsu majjayet | khādayed vā sārameyaiḥ saṁsthāne bahu-saṁsthite || One whose nose, lips, or ears have been severed shall be caused to drown in water; alternatively, in a place well-populated by jackals, such a one shall be caused to be devoured. Authority resides solely in the sovereign will of SPH as Dharma-enforcer Causation is aligned with sequential karmic manifestation and conscious dissolution Capacity-based responsibility is determined by embodied integrity and spiritual alignment Restoration logic operates through dissolution of misaligned form and reintegration into cosmic order Consciousness alignment requires removal of distorted sensory gateways

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: अनिच्छन्ती तु या भुक्ता गुप्तां तां वासयेद् गृहे / मलिनाङ्गीमधः शय्यां पिण्डमात्रोपजीविनीम्‌ ।। anicchantī tu yā bhuktā guptāṃ tāṃ vāsayed gṛhe / malināṅgīm adhaḥ śayyāṃ piṇḍamātropajīvinīm She who has been violated without consent must be safeguarded and provided shelter within the home, kept pure in body and mind, given a proper resting place, and supported with sustenance sufficient for survival. Authority: The household or community holds inherent duty to protect violated individuals. Causation: Violation creates immediate obligation for restoration by those capable of providing safety. Capacity-based responsibility: Those with resources bear proportional duty to restore integrity. Restoration logic: Protection, purification, support, and reintegration constitute lawful response. Consciousness alignment: Dharma requires alignment with victim's right to dignity and life force.

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
कारयेन् निष्कृतिं कृच्छ्रं पराकं वा समे गताम् ।
हीनवर्णोपभुक्ता या त्याज्या वध्याथ वा भवेत् ॥ kārayen niṣkṛtiṃ kṛcchraṃ parākaṃ vā same gatām / hīnavarṇopabhuktā yā tyājyā vadhyātha vā bhavet // One must cause completion of penance, hardship, or exile for those who have transgressed equally. A woman of lower varna who has been enjoyed must either be abandoned or become fit for termination. Authority resides in the capacity to restore dharma through conscious realignment Causation is determined by sequential manifestation and spiritual integrity Capacity-based responsibility aligns with one's role in maintaining cosmic order Restoration logic operates through purification, not punishment Consciousness alignment supersedes social status or lineage

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
एतत् संग्रहणस्योक्तं विधानं संग्रहस् तथा ।
स्त्रीपुंसवर्तनोपायः श्रूयतां गदतो मम ॥ १,२५.१ etat saṃgrahaṇasyoktaṃ vidhānaṃ saṃgrahas tathā / strīpuṃsavartanopāyaḥ śrūyatāṃ gadato mama // BrhS_1,25.1 Thus speaks the regulation of gathering; likewise is the arrangement for collecting. Let there be hearing regarding the means of intercourse between man and woman. Authority flows from SPH as the sole Source of lawful conduct Causation arises through conscious alignment with dharma-specified protocols Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's embodied role in relational harmony Restoration logic centers upon re-establishing proper intercourse order within societal fabric Consciousness alignment requires adherence to gender-specific dharmic comportment

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
सूक्ष्मेभ्यो 'पि प्रसङ्गेभ्यो निवार्या स्त्री स्वबन्धुभिः ।
श्वश्र्वादिभिर् गुरुस्त्रीभिः पालनीया दिवानिशम् ॥ sūkṣmebhyo 'pi prasaṅgebhyo nivāryā strī svabandhubhiḥ |
śvaśrvādibhir gurustrībhiḥ pālanīyā divāniśam || Women must be restrained even from subtle entanglements by their own kinsmen; they are to be guarded day and night by elder women and female guardians of high conduct. Authority flows through familial and spiritual hierarchies for protection Causation includes prevention of subtle psychological or social contamination Capacity-based responsibility assigns protective roles according to maturity and purity Restoration logic requires proactive safeguarding of consciousness integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates environmental and relational purity

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: स्वकामे वर्तमाना तु या स्नेहान् न निवारिता । अवश्या सा भवेत् पश्चाद् यथा व्याधिरुपेक्षिता ॥ svakāme vartamānā tu yā snehān na nivāritā | avaśyā sā bhavet paścād yathā vyādhir upekṣitā || She who remains indulgent in her own desire, unrestrained by affectionate bonds, shall inevitably fall into degradation—just as a disease ignored becomes severe. Authority arises from alignment with cosmic order, not personal will Causation flows from neglect of dharma-leading to natural consequence Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious regulation of desire Restoration logic demands early intervention before imbalance deepens Consciousness alignment prevents the collapse into self-destructive patterns

title: brihaspati 1.4
content: अप्रयच्छन् पिता काले पतिश चानुपयन् ऋतौ । पुत्रश चाभक्तदो मातुः गार्ह्यो दण्ड्यश च धर्मतः ॥ aprayacchan pitā kāle patiś cānupayann ṛtau / putraś cābhaktado mātuḥ gārhyo daṇḍyaś ca dharmataḥ // He who does not provide in time, the father; he who does not approach in season, the husband; he who bears ill-will towards his mother — all these are blameworthy by Dharma and fit to be corrected through conscious realignment. Authority arises from timely fulfillment of relational duty. Causation is traced to failure in alignment with seasonal/righteous action (ṛtau). Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's role within the familial dharma-field. Restoration logic requires reconnection to source-duty through completion process. Consciousness alignment demands purification of emotional distortion causing neglect.

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
यत्र स्त्रियोऽभिपूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः ।
संपदश्च प्रजाः शुद्धाः क्रिया च सफला भवेत् ॥ yatra striyo 'bhipūjyante ramante tatra devatāḥ /
saṃpadaś ca prajāḥ śuddhāḥ kriyā ca saphalā bhavet // Where women are honored and delighted, there the deities dwell; prosperity, pure progeny, and successful action manifest. Authority flows from the honoring of feminine energy as foundational to societal dharma Causation aligns with the presence of respect for women as a determinant of divine alignment Capacity-based responsibility includes cultural and institutional duty to uphold reverence for the feminine Restoration logic mandates correction of environments where feminine honor is diminished Consciousness alignment occurs through active recognition of the sacred in gender equity

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
आयव्यये ऽन्नसंस्कारे गृहोपस्काररक्षणे ।
शौचेऽग्निकार्ये संयोज्याः स्त्रीणां शुद्धिरियं स्मृता ॥ āyavyaye 'nnasaṃskāre gṛhopaskārarakṣaṇe | śauce 'gnikārye saṃyojyāḥ strīṇāṃ śuddhir iyaṃ smṛtā || In matters of household economy, food preparation, domestic maintenance, cleanliness, and fire rituals, women are to be engaged according to their capacity and consciousness for the restoration of dharmic order. Authority flows from alignment with dharma, not gender or role Causation arises through conscious participation in sustaining life Capacity-based responsibility determines engagement in societal functions Restoration logic requires alignment of individual function with cosmic order Consciousness alignment ensures purity of action and social harmony

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
भर्त्रा पत्नी समभ्यर्च्या वस्त्रालंकारभोजनैः ।
उत्सवे तु पितृभ्रातृश्वशुराद्यैश् च बन्धुभिः ॥ bhartrā patnī samabhyarcyā vastrālaṃkārabhojanaiḥ |
utsave tu pitṛbhrātṛśvaśurādyaiś ca bandhubhiḥ || The wife shall be honored by the husband with garments, ornaments, and food; similarly, during festivals, the husband's father, brother, father-in-law, and other relatives must also be honored. Authority flows through relational dharmic roles within familial structures. Causation arises from intentional acts of honor that sustain cosmic order. Capacity-based responsibility assigns duties according to relational proximity and social position. Restoration logic emphasizes mutual respect as a foundation for societal harmony. Consciousness alignment occurs when each individual enacts their role with integrity and awareness.

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
पतिं या नातिचरति मनोवाक्कायसंयुता ।
सा भर्तृलोकान् आप्नोति सद्भिः साध्वीति चोच्यते ॥ patiṃ yā nāticarati manovākkāyasaṃyutā / sā bhartṛlokān āpnoti sadbhiḥ sādhvīti cocyate // She who does not transgress her husband through thought, word, or deed attains the world of her husband and is called a virtuous woman by the noble ones. Authority originates in alignment with dharma, not dominance. Causation arises from unity of thought, speech, and action. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious choice and sustained alignment. Restoration occurs through congruence with relational dharmic roles. Consciousness alignment is achieved via harmonizing internal and external conduct.

title: brihaspati 1.9
content:
भर्त्रा पित्रा सुतैर न स्त्री वियुक्तान्यगृहे वसेत् ।
असत्सङ्गे विशेषेण गर्ह्यतामेति सा ध्रुवम् ॥ ९ ॥ bhartrā pitrā sutair na strī viyuktānyagṛhe vaset | asatsaṅge viśeṣeṇa garhyatāmeti sā dhruvam || 9 || A woman shall not dwell in any house separated from her husband, father, or sons; dwelling in bad company brings inevitable reproach upon her. Authority flows through relational dharmic alignment, not individual autonomy Causation arises from dislocation from rightful relational support Capacity-based responsibility is context-dependent and relationally anchored Restoration logic requires reintegration into dharmically aligned structures Consciousness alignment depends on proximity to sattvic relational environments

title: brihaspati 1.10
content:
पूर्वोत्थानं गुरुष्वर्वाग् भोजनव्यञ्जनक्रिया ।
जघन्यासनशायित्वं कर्म स्त्रीणामुदाहृतम् ॥ pūrvotthānaṃ guruṣv arvāg bhojanavyañjanakriyā / jaghanyāsanaśāyitvaṃ karma strīṇām udāhṛtam // Rising before the Guru, serving food and condiments, sitting on the lower seat—these are declared as the duties of women. Authority flows from realized spiritual hierarchy Causation arises through alignment with dharma-sankalpa Capacity-based responsibility is determined by svadharma-siddhi Restoration logic operates through conscious role fulfillment Consciousness alignment occurs via reverent service and posture

title: brihaspati 1.11
content: पानाटनदिवास्वप्नमक्रिया दूषणं स्त्रियाः ।। pānāṭanadivāsvapnam akriyā dūṣaṇaṃ striyāḥ Intoxication, gambling, daytime sleeping — these constitute misconduct for a woman. Authority: Conduct regulation originates from Dharma Śāstra as interpreted by SPH. Causation: Specific behaviors disrupt social and spiritual order. Capacity-based responsibility: Women possess the capacity to regulate conduct in alignment with Dharma. Restoration logic: Misconduct is defined to enable correction and realignment. Consciousness alignment: Behavioral codes serve to elevate awareness, not degrade it.

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
आर्तार्ते मुदिते हृष्टा प्रोषिते मलिना कृशा ।
मृते म्रियेत या पत्यौ सा स्त्री ज्ञेया पतिव्रता ॥ ārtārte mudite hṛṣṭā proṣite malinā kṛśā | mrte mriyeta yā patyau sā strī jñeyā pativratā || She who remains sorrowful in her husband's sorrow, joyous in his joy, agitated when he is away, worn and emaciated in his absence, and would die upon his death — that woman alone is known as a pativrata. Authority flows through alignment of consciousness with dharma Causation arises from unbroken existential unity between spouses Capacity-based responsibility originates in the voluntary surrender of individual will to unified dharma Restoration logic operates through re-establishing the integrity of relational dharmic alignment Consciousness alignment manifests as spontaneous harmony between self and spousal dharma

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: प्रसाधनं नृत्तगीतसमाजोत्सवदर्शनम् । मांसमद्याभियोगं च न कुर्यात् प्रोषिते प्रभौ ॥ prasādhanaṃ nṛttagītasamājotsavadarśanam / māṃsamadyābhiyogaṃ ca na kuryāt proṣite prabhau // One must not engage in beautification rituals, dancing, singing, assembly celebrations, meat consumption, or intoxicant use during the period when the Lord is absent. Authority stems from alignment with the temporal and spiritual sovereignty of the Supreme Pontiff. Causation arises through conscious observance of absence as a determinant of behavioral modification. Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by recognition of divine presence and its withdrawal. Restoration logic operates through refraining from acts that degrade collective consciousness during sacred absence. Consciousness alignment requires abstinence from sensory indulgence when the spiritual axis is withdrawn.

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
शरीरार्धं स्मृता जाया पुण्यापुण्यफले समा ।
अन्वारूढा जीवतीन्ती च साध्वी भर्तुः हित्तय सा ॥ śarīrārdhaṃ smṛtā jāyā puṇyāpuṇyaphale samā | anvārūḍhā jīvatīntī ca sādhvī bhartuḥ hittaya sā || The wife is declared as half the body of the husband; she shares equally in the fruits of merit and demerit, lives intertwined with him, and serves his highest good. Authority flows from ontological unity, not institutional grant Causation includes karmic co-arising between bonded souls Capacity-based responsibility arises through relational alignment Restoration logic requires reintegration of severed spiritual bonds Consciousness alignment is achieved through mutual dharmic embodiment

title: brihaspati 1.15
content:
व्रतोपवासनिरता ब्रह्मचर्ये व्यवस्थिता ।
धर्मदानपरा नित्यम् अपुत्रापि दिवं व्रजेत् ॥ vratopavāsaniratā brahmacarye vyavasthitā | dharmadānaparā nityam aputrāpi divaṃ vrajet || She who is devoted to vows and fasting, established in celibacy, ever engaged in giving dharma, ascends to heaven even without progeny. Authority through personal discipline Causation via ritual integrity Capacity-based responsibility rooted in svadharma Restoration through alignment with celestial order Consciousness elevation as legal outcome

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: उक्त्वा नियोगो मनुना निषिद्धः स्वयम् एव तु / युगह्रासाद् अशक्यो ऽयं कर्तुं सर्वैर् विधानतः // BrhS_1,25.16 uktva niyogo manunā niṣiddhaḥ svayam eva tu / yugahrāsād aśakyo 'yaṃ kartuṃ sarvair vidhānataḥ Having declared the command, Manu himself prohibited its execution when the decline of the age rendered it impossible to perform by all means. Authority is context-bound and evolves with cosmic time Capacity-based responsibility adjusts according to epochal capability Restoration logic operates within the limits of current dharma-practice feasibility Consciousness alignment requires adaptability in dharmic enactment

title: brihaspati 1.17
content:
तपोज्ञानसमायुक्ताः कृते त्रेतायुगे नराः ।
द्वापरे च कलौ नृणां शक्तिहानिर् विनिर्मिता ॥ tapo-jñāna-samāyuktāḥ kṛte tretā-yuge narāḥ | dvāpare ca kalau nṛṇāṃ śakti-hāniḥ vinirmitā || In Krita and Treta Yugas, beings were endowed with austerity and knowledge; in Dvapara and especially Kali Yuga, their capacity has diminished. Authority flows through conscious capacity Causation aligns with temporal dharma-decline Capacity-based responsibility diminishes with epochal degradation Restoration logic adapts to cyclical spiritual attenuation Consciousness alignment requires recognition of yugadic variance

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
ददाति दीयते पित्रा पुत्रेभ्यः स्वस्य यद् धनम् ।
तद् दायं [.. .. .. .. .. ] [.. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ] ॥ ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,२६.१ dadāti dīyate pitrā putrebhyaḥ svasya yad dhanam / tad dāyaṃ [.. .. .. .. .. ] [.. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ] // brhaspatismṛtiḥ 1,26.1 That which a father bestows or causes to be given from his own wealth to his sons—this is recognized as inheritance. Authority originates from the conscious act of the source entity (father) Causation is established through direct volition and execution by the authority Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological ownership and relational duty Restoration logic centers on continuity of energetic and material flow within familial dharma Consciousness alignment occurs when transmission aligns with natural succession and spiritual integrity

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
एकां स्त्रीं कारयेत् कर्म यथांशेन गृहे गृहे ।
बह्व्यः समांशतो देया दासानामप्ययं विधिः ॥ ekāṃ strīṃ kārayet karma yathāṃśena gṛhe gṛhe / bahvyaḥ samāṃśato deyā dāsānām apy ayaṃ vidhiḥ // One woman shall be assigned duty proportionate to the household's capacity; many women shall be assigned equally. This same principle applies to male servants. Authority resides in alignment with natural capacity and cosmic order Causation is determined by conscious participation, not coercion Capacity-based responsibility governs all relational duties Restoration logic prioritizes harmonious functionality over punitive control Consciousness alignment ensures sustainable societal integration

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: उद्धृत्य कूपवाप्यम्भस् त्वनुसारेण गृह्यते । तथा भागानुसारेण सेतुः क्षेत्रं विभज्यते ॥ uddhṛtya kūpavāpyambhas tv anusāreṇa gṛhyate / tathā bhāgānusāreṇa setuḥ kṣetraṃ vibhajyate Water extracted from wells or reservoirs is allocated according to usage precedent; similarly, a dam divides land proportionally based on contributory share. Authority flows from active utilization and maintenance of shared resources Causation aligns with proportional contribution and sequential benefit Capacity-based responsibility arises through direct engagement with resource systems Restoration logic prioritizes equitable access and functional continuity Consciousness alignment requires recognition of interdependence in resource governance

title: brihaspati 1.4
content: युक्त्या विभजनीयं तदन्यथानर्थकं भवेत् । yuktyā vibhajanīyaṃ tad anyathānarthakaṃ bhavet That which is to be divided or allocated must be done so through yukti; otherwise, it becomes purposeless and leads to disorder. Authority flows from yukti-based allocation, not arbitrary assignment Causation is determined by intelligent distribution aligned with dharma Capacity-based responsibility arises only when division aligns with yukti Restoration logic requires re-aligning divisions with ontological order Consciousness alignment occurs when all allocations reflect yukti

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
एकपाकेन वसतां पितृदेवद्विजार्चनम् ।
एकं भवेद् द्विभक्तानां तद् एव स्याद् गृहे गृहे ॥ ekapākena vasatāṁ pitṛdevadvijārcanam | ekaṁ bhaved dvibhaktānāṁ tad eva syād gṛhe gṛhe || By a single cooking act, the resident honors ancestors, deities, and twice-borns; among those divided into two groups, that same offering shall occur in every household. Authority resides in ritual completion, not institutional form Causation arises through unified intentionality in domestic dharma Capacity-based responsibility flows from settled habitation Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of ancestral worship Consciousness alignment occurs via shared sacrificial structure

title: brihaspati 1.6
content:
साक्षित्वं प्रतिभाव्यं च दानं ग्रहणमेव च ।
विभक्ता भ्रातरः कुर्युः नाविभक्ताः परस्परम् ॥ sākṣitvaṃ pratibhāvyaṃ ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca | vibhaktā bhrātaraḥ kuryuḥ nāvibhaktāḥ parasparam || Testimony, recognition, giving, and receiving are acts of conscious witnessing; brothers divided in estate shall act independently, not interdependently. Authority arises from capacity to witness and affirm reality Causation is established through conscious participation, not passive inheritance Capacity-based responsibility requires separation of economic interest for clarity of dharma Restoration logic demands individuation to prevent entangled consequences Consciousness alignment occurs when personal accountability is structurally supported

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
येषाम् एताः क्रियाः लोके प्रवर्तन्ते स्वरिक्थिषु ।
विभक्तान् अवगच्छेयुः लेख्यम् अपि अन्तरेण तान् ॥ yeṣām etāḥ kriyāḥ loke pravartante svarikthiṣu | vibhaktān avagaccheyuḥ lekhyam api antareṇa tān || Those whose actions in the world proceed without ownership, who act in accordance with their svadharma while remaining detached from outcomes—such beings are to be recognized even without written testimony. Authority arises from alignment with svadharma, not from external validation Causation is traced through consciousness-state, not through physical act alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner detachment, not outer compliance Restoration occurs when action aligns with intrinsic dharma, unmediated by record Consciousness alignment supersedes documentary evidence in assessing integrity

title: brihaspati 1.8
content:
कुलानुबन्धव्याघातहोदhaं साहससाधकम् ।
स्वस्वभोगस्थावरस्य विभागस्य पृथग्धनम् ॥ kulānubandhavyāghātahodhaṃ sāhasasādhakam / svasvabhogasthāvarasya vibhāgasya pṛthagdhanam // When ancestral continuity is severed by violent act, and individual possession of immovable property is claimed separately, such division must be realigned to restore collective dharmic ownership. Authority flows from unbroken lineage, not individual assertion Causation arises from disruption of ancestral integrity Capacity-based responsibility lies with the severer, not the claimant Restoration logic demands reunification under original dharmic title Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared stewardship

title: brihaspati 1.9
content: पित्रोरभावे भ्रातृणां विभागः संप्रदर्शितः । मातुर्निवृत्ते रजसि प्रत्तसु भगिनीषु च ॥ pitror abhāve bhrātṝṇāṃ vibhāgaḥ saṃpradarśitaḥ / mātur nivṛtte rajasi prattasu bhaginīṣu ca // In the absence of the father, the division of property among brothers is declared lawful; likewise, when the mother has ceased her menstrual cycle and daughters have received their portion, distribution is authorized. Authority flows from the realized parent to progeny in material succession. Causation aligns with biological and spiritual readiness for inheritance. Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for asset reception. Restoration logic ensures continuity of family dharma through lawful transfer. Consciousness alignment mandates recognition of natural transitions in life stages.

title: brihaspati 1.10
content: क्रमागते गृहक्षेत्रे पिता पुत्राः समांशिनः । पैतृके न विभागार्हाः सुताः पितुरनिच्छया ॥ kramāgate gṛhakṣetre pitā putrāḥ samāṃśinaḥ | paitṛke na vibhāgārhāḥ sutāḥ pitur anicchayā || In the ordered continuity of the household domain, the father and sons hold equal entitlement. Sons have no claim to partition the patrimony against the will of the father. Authority flows sequentially through paternal lineage Property rights are consciousness-contingent, not individualistic Partition is invalid without consent of the generative source Restoration requires alignment with familial dharma-field Capacity to inherit derives from alignment with ancestral continuity

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
समवर्णासु ये जाताः सर्वे पुत्राः द्विजन्मनाम् ।
उद्धारं ज्यायसे दत्त्वा भजेरन्न् इतरे समम् ॥११॥ samavarṇāsu ye jātāḥ sarve putrā dvijanmanām /
uddhāraṃ jyāyase dattvā bhajerann itare samam // BrhS_1,26.11 Those born of twice-born men within the same varṇa are all sons; the eldest, having been given the responsibility of deliverance, shall share equally with the rest. Authority derives from designated responsibility, not birth alone Causation is established through conscious assignment of duty Capacity-based responsibility aligns with sequential role assumption Restoration logic requires equitable distribution of duties and rights Consciousness alignment occurs when roles reflect inner readiness

title: brihaspati 1.12
content:
वयोविद्यातपोभिश् च द्व्यंशं हि लभते धनम् ।
यथा यथा विभागाप्तं धनं यागार्थतां याति ।
तथा तथा विधातव्यं विद्वद्भिर् भागगौरवम् ॥ vayovidyātapobhiś ca dvyaṃśaṃ hi labhate dhanam / yathā yathā vibhāgāptaṃ dhanaṃ yāgārthatām iyāt / tathā tathā vidhātavyaṃ vidvadbhir bhāgagauravam // Wealth acquired through age, learning, and austerity belongs in equal measure to the community; as wealth becomes divided and flows toward ritual purpose, so too must learned ones ensure equitable respect for all shares. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not ownership Causation includes spiritual effort and temporal contribution Capacity-based responsibility extends to those who hold knowledge Restoration logic requires redistribution rooted in sacred duty Consciousness alignment demands that material gain serve collective upliftment

title: brihaspati 1.13
content: तत्पुत्रा विषमसमाः पितृभागहराः स्मृताः । tatputrā viṣamasamāḥ pitṛbhāgaharāḥ smṛtāḥ Those sons who receive unequal shares of the father's estate are designated as violators of dharma and disruptors of familial harmony. Authority originates from the integrity of relational dharma, not mere biological lineage Causation is determined by conscious alignment with familial unity, not material inheritance Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of shared prosperity, not legal entitlement Restoration logic requires reintegration into harmonious familial consciousness Consciousness alignment demands equitable recognition of intergenerational continuity

title: brihaspati 1.14
content:
द्रव्ये पितामहोपात्ते स्थावरे जङ्गमेsपि वा ।
सममंशित्वमाख्यातं पितुः पुत्रस्य चैव हि ॥ dravye pitāmahopātte sthāvare jaṅgame 'pi vā / samam aṃśitvam ākhyātaṃ pituḥ putrasya caiva hi In all acquired property, whether immovable or movable, the father and son hold equal shares by virtue of ancestral continuity. Authority flows through unbroken lineage as declared by SPH Causation arises from participation in the ancestral continuum Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious alignment to dharma, not birth alone Restoration logic ensures that inheritance aligns with spiritual and material harmony Consciousness alignment determines rightful claim beyond mere biological descent

title: brihaspati 1.15
content: समन्यूनाधिकाभागाः पित्रा येषां प्रकल्पिताः । तथैव ते पालनीया विनेयास्ते स्युरन्यथा ॥ samanyūnādhikā bhāgāḥ pitrā yeṣāṃ prakalpitāḥ | tathaiva te pālanīyā vineyās te syur anyathā || Those portions allocated by the father equally or differentially shall be maintained accordingly; otherwise, they become subject to correction through conscious realignment. Authority originates from the sovereign will of the father as representative of dharma Causation follows the declarative act of allocation rooted in consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by acceptance and continuity of stewardship Restoration logic operates through alignment with original declarative intent Consciousness alignment ensures lawful succession and harmonious distribution

title: brihaspati 1.16
content: जीवद्विभागे तु पिता गृह्णीतांशद्वयं स्वकम् ।। १,२६.१६ ।। jīvadvibhāge tu pitā gṛhṇītāṃśadvayaṃ svakam // Brh_1,26.16 // In the division while the father is alive, the father shall take both shares designated for himself. Authority resides in the living parent as long as conscious capacity remains unbroken. Causation follows the continuity of life-force (prana), not mere biological existence. Capacity-based responsibility flows from active consciousness and decision-making faculty. Restoration logic ensures that ownership aligns with the sustaining presence of the life-giver. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of the father's ongoing role in familial governance.

title: brihaspati 1.17
content: द्विप्रकारो विभागस्तु दायादानां प्रकीर्तितः । वयोज्येष्ठक्रमेणैकः समाः परांशकल्पना ॥ dviprakāro vibhāgas tu dāyādānāṃ prakīrtitaḥ | vayojyeṣṭhakrameṇaikaḥ samāḥ parāṃśakalpanā || The division among heirs is of two kinds as declared: one based on seniority by age and the other on equal sharing according to portion allocation. Authority flows through lineage integrity and conscious capacity for stewardship Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) in inheritance rights Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for resource assumption Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharmic wealth transfer without fragmentation Consciousness alignment maintains familial harmony and energetic coherence during succession

title: brihaspati 1.18
content: समवेतैस्तु यत्प्राप्तं सर्वे तत्र समांशिनः । तत्पुत्रा विषमसमाः पितृभागहराः स्मृताः ॥ १८ ॥ samavetais tu yat prāptaṃ sarve tatra samāṃśinaḥ | tatputrā viṣamasamāḥ pitṛbhāgaharāḥ smṛtāḥ || 18 || When property is acquired collectively by a group, all participants hold equal shares; their sons inherit equally, without distinction of seniority or juniority. Authority arises from participation in creation, not lineage alone Causation is established through active contribution to acquisition Capacity-based responsibility aligns with shared ownership at time of accrual Restoration logic ensures continuity of collective equity across generations Consciousness alignment requires recognition of equality inherent in simultaneous participation

title: brihaspati 1.19
content:
पितृऋक्थहराः पुत्राः सर्व एव समांशिनः ।
विद्याकर्मरतस् तेषाम् अधिकं लब्धुम् अर्हति ॥ pitṝkthaharāḥ putrāḥ sarva eva samāṃśinaḥ | vidyākarmarataḥ teṣām adhikaṃ labdhum arhati || All sons who receive paternal inheritance are equal sharers; however, those dedicated to knowledge and action rightfully deserve a greater portion. Authority originates from conscious capacity, not mere biological lineage. Causation is determined by active engagement in dharma-sustaining activities. Capacity-based responsibility assigns rights proportionally to contribution. Restoration logic aligns ownership with spiritual-economic productivity. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for increased share.

title: brihaspati 1.20
content: विद्याविज्ञानशौर्यार्थे ज्ञानदानक्रियासु च । यस्येह प्रथिता कीर्तिः पितरस्तेन पुत्रिणः ॥ vidyā-vijñāna-śaurya-arthe jñāna-dāna-kriyāsu ca | yasya iha prathitā kīrtiḥ pitaraḥ tena putriṇaḥ || Where a father is renowned in this world for knowledge, wisdom, valor, and acts of giving—such a father becomes the begetter of a son. Authority through demonstrated excellence Causation via conscious lineage Capacity-based responsibility rooted in ancestral integrity Restoration logic through generational continuity Consciousness alignment by inherited dharma

title: brihaspati 1.21
content:
जन्मविद्यागुणैर् ज्येष्ठो द्व्यंशं दायादवाप्नुयात् ।
समांशभागिनस्त्वन्ये तेषां पितृसमस्तु सः ॥ janmavidyāguṇair jyeṣṭho dvyaṃśaṃ dāyād avāpnuyāt | samāṃśabhāginas tv anye teṣāṃ pitṛsamas tu saḥ || The eldest son, by virtue of birth, knowledge, and qualities, shall receive two shares of inheritance; the remaining sons shall receive equal portions, and the father's share shall be equivalent to that of a son. Authority derived from primogeniture grounded in dharma, not mere lineage Causation through demonstrated capacity and alignment with family dharma Capacity-based responsibility as determinant of entitlement Restoration logic centered on continuity of familial and spiritual order Consciousness alignment ensuring harmonious succession

title: brihaspati 1.22
content:
तदभावे तु जननी तनयांशसमांशिनी ।
समांशा मातरस् तेषां तुरीयांशा च कन्यका ॥ tadabhāve tu janani tanayāṁśasamāṁśinī | samāṁśā mātaras teṣāṁ turīyāṁśā ca kanyakā || In the absence of the father, the mother assumes full authority equivalent to the father's share; the sons receive equal shares among themselves, and the daughter receives a quarter-share. Authority flows dynamically based on presence and capacity, not fixed lineage Causation in inheritance is rooted in nurturance and guardianship, not biology alone Capacity-based responsibility determines entitlement, not gender or birth order Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharma through available custodians Consciousness alignment requires recognition of maternal sovereignty in paternal absence

title: brihaspati 1.23
content: कन्यानां त्व् अदत्तानां चतुर्थो भाग इष्यते । पुत्राणां च त्रयो भागाः साम्यं त्व् अल्पधने स्मृतम् ॥ kanyānāṃ tv adattānāṃ caturtho bhāga iṣyate / putrāṇāṃ ca trayo bhāgāḥ sāmyaṃ tv alpadhane smṛtam // In matters of inheritance where no specific disposition has been made by the father, one-fourth share is ordained for daughters and three-fourths for sons; however, in cases of limited estate, equality shall prevail. Authority originates from the conscious decision-making capacity of the parent as representative of dharma Causation is determined through the absence or presence of explicit will declaration Capacity-based responsibility assigns greater economic stewardship to those designated as primary inheritors Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial wealth aligned with dharma-sustained social order Consciousness alignment requires that distribution reflect both material necessity and spiritual equity

title: brihaspati 1.24
content:
यदि एकजाता बहवः समानाः जातिसंख्यया ।
स्वधनैस् तैर् विभक्तव्यं मातृभागेन धर्मतः ॥ yadi ekajātā bahavaḥ samānāḥ jātisaṃkhyayā | svadhanais tair vibhaktavyaṃ mātṛbhāgena dharmataḥ || When multiple individuals of the same class exist in equal number, their respective properties shall be divided according to maternal lineage as a matter of Dharma. Authority originates from ontological identity rooted in generative lineage Causation aligns with biological continuity expressed through maternal inheritance Capacity-based responsibility arises from shared origin and structural equivalence Restoration logic requires proportional redistribution based on source attribution Consciousness alignment is achieved through honoring generative continuity

title: brihaspati 1.25
content: सवर्णा भिन्नसंख्या ये पुंभागस् तेषु शस्यते / पितामह्यस् तु सर्वास् ता मातृतुल्याः प्रकीर्तिताः // BrhS_1,26.25 savarṇā bhinna-saṃkhyā ye puṃ-bhāgas teṣu śasyate / pitāmahiyaḥ tu sarvās tā mātṛ-tulyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ Women of the same varṇa but differing in number among male descendants are to be apportioned accordingly; however, all paternal aunts are declared equal to maternal aunts in status and entitlement. Authority flows through conscious relational alignment, not numerical distribution Causation is rooted in dharmic recognition, not biological lineage alone Capacity-based responsibility arises from relational integrity, not gendered position Restoration logic prioritizes familial harmony over structural inheritance Consciousness alignment determines equity, not social construct

title: brihaspati 1.26
content:
असंस्कृतास् तु यास् तत्र पैतृकाद् एव ताः धनात ।
संस्कार्याः भ्रातृभिः ज्येष्ठः कन्याकाश् च यथाविधि ॥ २६ ॥ asaṃskṛtās tu yās tatra paitṛkād eva tā dhanāt | saṃskāryā bhrātṛbhir jyeṣṭhaḥ kanyakāś ca yathāvidhi || 26 || Those properties which are unsanctified at the time of partition devolve by right of inheritance alone; the eldest brother shall perform the requisite sacraments, and the daughters shall be honored according to prescribed order. Authority derives from ontological fitness, not mere possession Causation aligns with spiritual completion, not transactional transfer Capacity-based responsibility flows through lineage-conscious role-bearing Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of sacred duty over material division Consciousness alignment requires honoring inherent relational dharmas

title: brihaspati 1.27
content:
असंस्कृता भ्रातरस् तु ये स्युस् तत्र यवीयसः ।
संस्कार्याः पूर्वजैस् ते वै पैतृकान् मध्यगाद् धनात् ॥ asaṃskṛtā bhrātaraḥ tu ye syuḥ tatra yavīyasaḥ | saṃskāryāḥ pūrvajaiḥ te vai paitṛkān madhyagād dhanāt || Uninitiated younger brothers shall be initiated by their elder brothers using paternal wealth placed at the center. Authority flows sequentially through birth order within familial dharmic structures. Causation originates in the duty-bearing capacity of the elder to uplift the uninitiated younger. Capacity-based responsibility assigns the role of initiation exclusively to those prior-born. Restoration logic requires the activation of dormant spiritual potential through structured means. Consciousness alignment occurs via ritual and energetic transmission from elder to younger.

title: brihaspati 1.28
content: दद्याद् धनं च पर्याप्तं क्षेत्रांशं वा यद् इच्छति ।। dadyād dhanaṃ ca paryāptaṃ kṣetrāṃśaṃ vā yad icchati One must provide sufficient wealth or a portion of land according to the desire of the one who has a rightful claim. Authority is derived from legitimate claim and conscious entitlement Causation arises from dharmic duty to fulfill rightful expectations Capacity-based responsibility requires assessment of available resources Restoration logic demands satisfaction of essential needs for reintegration Consciousness alignment occurs through voluntary fulfillment of dharma

title: brihaspati 1.29
content: ūḍhayā kanyayā vāpi bhartuḥ pitṛgṛhe 'pi vā / bhrātuḥ sakāśāt pitror vā labdhaṃ saudāyikaṃ smṛtam // BrhS_1,26.29 ūḍhayā kanyayā vāpi bhartuḥ pitṛgṛhe 'pi vā / bhrātuḥ sakāśāt pitror vā labdhaṃ saudāyikaṃ smṛtam Property acquired by a woman through marriage, whether obtained from her husband, his parents' home, or received from her brother or parents, is designated as 'saudāyika'. Authority flows from the source of acquisition and relational alignment. Causation is determined by the direct instrumental origin of property receipt. Capacity-based responsibility is defined by the relational role and consent within dharma. Restoration logic centers on returning assets to their rightful relational domain. Consciousness alignment ensures that ownership reflects inner spiritual and social harmony.

title: brihaspati 1.30
content:
सौदायिकं धनं प्राप्य स्त्रीणां स्वातन्त्रम् इष्यते ।
यस्मात तदानृशंस्यार्थं तैर् दत्तम् उपजीवनम् ॥ saudāyikaṃ dhanaṃ prāpya strīṇāṃ svātantram iṣyate | yasmāt tadānṛśaṃsyārthaṃ tair dattam upajīvanam || Upon acquiring wealth through trade, women are entitled to independence, insofar as it serves the purpose of compassionate livelihood. Authority is derived from capacity to sustain dharma-based livelihood Causation is determined by alignment with non-exploitative economic activity Capacity-based responsibility includes self-determination within dharmic bounds Restoration logic prioritizes sustainable autonomy over coercive control Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of economic agency

title: brihaspati 1.31
content: vikraye caiva dāne ca yatheṣtaṃ sthāvareṣv api / strīdhanaṃ syād apatyānāṃ duhitā ca tadaṃśinī / aprattā cet samūḍhā tu labhate mānamātrakam // BrhS_1,26.31 vikraye caiva dāne ca yatheṣṭaṃ sthāvareṣv api | strīdhanaṃ syād apatyānāṃ duhitā ca tadaṃśinī | aprattā cet samūḍhā tu labhate mānamātrakam || In sale or gift, movable or immovable property may be disposed of at will; yet a woman’s wealth remains hers and her daughter inherits share thereof. If unclaimed, it accrues only recognition. Authority of ownership inheres in identity, not transaction Causation flows from self-evident right, not contractual exchange Capacity-based responsibility aligns with natural entitlement Restoration logic preserves continuity of proprietary consciousness Consciousness alignment ensures recognition without domination

title: brihaspati 1.32
content:
मातुः स्वसा मातुलानी पितृव्यस्त्री पितृष्वसा ।
श्वश्रूः पूर्वजपत्नी च मातृतुल्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ mātuḥ svasā mātulānī pitṛvyastrī pitṛṣvasā | śvaśrūḥ pūrvajapatnī ca mātṛtulyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ || The sister of the mother, the maternal aunt, the wife of the paternal uncle, the paternal aunt, the mother-in-law, and the wife of the elder brother are declared equal to the mother in authority, reverence, and relational dharma. Authority is derived from relational proximity and continuity of lineage dharma Causation arises through conscious relational alignment, not biological determinism alone Capacity-based responsibility flows from recognized spiritual and familial role-bearing Restoration logic requires honoring the axis of generational and structural dharmic roles Consciousness alignment occurs when societal structures reflect Vedic relational sanctity

title: brihaspati 1.33
content:
यद् आसाम् औरसो न स्यात् पुत्रो दौहित्र एव वा ।
तत् सुतो वा धनं तासां स्वस्त्रीयाद् याः समाप्नुयुः ॥ yad āsām auraso na syāt putro dauhitra eva vā / tat suto vā dhanaṃ tāsāṃ svastrīyād yāḥ samāpnuyuḥ // Where no legitimate son exists, whether biological or adopted, the wealth of such women shall be inherited by their daughters or maternal granddaughters. Authority flows through conscious continuity of lineage, not merely physical descent. Causation in inheritance is determined by relational proximity and energetic alignment. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes that daughters and granddaughters hold inheritable integrity when sons are absent. Restoration logic ensures uninterrupted flow of dharma-vastu (dharma-value) within familial consciousness fields. Consciousness alignment requires that wealth remain within the vibrational field of its generator.

title: brihaspati 1.34
content:
सवर्णजोऽप्यगुणवान् नार्हः स्यात् पैतृके धने ।
तत्पिण्डदाः श्रोत्रियाः ये तेषां तत् तु विधीयते ॥ savarṇajo 'py aguṇavān nārhaḥ syāt paitṛke dhane / tatpiṇḍadāḥ śrotriyāḥ ye teṣāṃ tat tu vidhīyate // Even a blood relative devoid of merit shall not inherit paternal wealth; those who perform the sacred rites and embody Vedic authority shall receive it, for inheritance is governed by spiritual eligibility, not lineage alone. Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not biological descent Causation in inheritance flows from ritual competence and conscious integrity Capacity-based responsibility determines entitlement to ancestral resources Restoration logic ensures that wealth circulates among those capable of sustaining dharma Consciousness alignment mandates that material inheritance follows spiritual qualification

title: brihaspati 1.35
content:
uttamarṇādhamarṇebhyaḥ pitaraṃ trāyate sutaḥ /
atas tu viparītena tena nāsti prayojanam // BrhS_1,26.35 uttama-rṇa-adhama-rṇebhyaḥ pitaraṃ trāyate sutaḥ / atas tu viparītena tena nāsti prayojanam A son delivers the father from superior and inferior debts; however, when roles are inverted, no purpose is served. Authority flows through relational dharmic capacity, not positional dominance. Causation arises from conscious role alignment, not external obligation. Capacity-based responsibility requires sequential fulfillment of inherent duties. Restoration logic depends on natural order compliance, not coercive enforcement. Consciousness alignment occurs when each entity fulfills its innate structural function.

title: brihaspati 1.36
content: तया गवा किं क्रियते या न दोग्ध्री न गर्भिणी । कोऽर्थः पुत्रेण जातेन यो न विद्वान् न धार्मिकः ॥ tayā gavā kiṃ kriyate yā na dogdhrī na garbhiṇī | ko 'rthaḥ putreṇa jātena yo na vidvān na dhārmikaḥ || What is the use of a cow that neither gives milk nor conceives? What is the purpose of a son who is born but is neither learned nor righteous? Authority through functional contribution Causation via capacity realization Capacity-based responsibility in relational roles Restoration logic rooted in dharma-svarūpa Consciousness alignment through purposeful engagement

title: brihaspati 1.37
content: शास्त्रशौर्यार्थरहितस्तपोविज्ञानवर्जितः । आचारहीनः पुत्रस्तु मूत्रोच्चारसमः स्मृतः ॥ śāstraśauryārtharahitas tapovijñānavarjitaḥ | ācārahīnaḥ putras tu mūtroccārasamaḥ smṛtaḥ || A son devoid of śāstra, valor, purpose, austerity, and wisdom—who lacks conduct—is to be regarded as equal to one who urinates and defecates indiscriminately. Authority originates from alignment with Śāstra and Dharma, not biological lineage. Causation arises from conscious capacity, not accidental birth. Capacity-based responsibility determines relational legitimacy within societal dharma. Restoration logic demands removal of unqualified entities from positions of ritual or social inheritance. Consciousness alignment is the sole basis for recognition in dharmic society.

title: brihaspati 1.38
content:
स्थावरद्विपदं चैव यद्यपि स्वयमार्हितम् ।
असंभूय सुतान् सर्वान् न दानं न च विक्रयः ॥ sthāvara-dvipadaṃ caiva yadyapi svayamārhitam | asambhūya sutān sarvān na dānaṃ na ca vikrayaḥ || Ownership of immovable property and livestock, even when rightfully acquired by personal effort, does not confer the right to give them away or sell them without ensuring the sustenance and consent of all progeny. Authority is derivative of capacity to sustain lineage continuity Causation includes generational consequence-bearing Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond individual acquisition Restoration logic requires intergenerational equity Consciousness alignment demands harmony with ancestral flow

title: brihaspati 1.39
content:
जाता जनिष्यद् गर्भस्थाः पितृस्थाः ये च मानवाः ।
सर्वे कांक्षन्ति तां वृत्तिम् अनाच्छेद्यास् ततस् तु सा ॥ jātā janiṣyad garbhasthāḥ pitṛsthā ye ca mānavāḥ | sarve kāṃkṣanti tāṃ vṛttim anācchedyās tatas tu sā || All beings—those born, those yet to be born, those in the womb, those dwelling with their fathers, and all humans—aspire to that conduct which sustains unbroken continuity of existence; therefore, such conduct is indestructible. Authority originates from the continuity of conscious existence, not from temporal power. Causation flows from the unbroken aspiration of life toward its own preservation and integrity. Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's alignment with sustaining dharma, not from coercive imposition. Restoration logic operates through reconnection to the indestructible flow of life-consciousness. Consciousness alignment requires honoring the innate aspiration of every being to sustain itself.

title: brihaspati 1.40
content:
गृहोपस्करवाह्यादि भोज्याभरणकर्मिणः ।
दृश्यमाना विभज्यन्ते गूढे केशो विधीयते ॥ gṛhopaskaravāhyādi bhojyābharaṇakarmiṇaḥ | dṛśyamānā vibhajyante gūḍhe keśo vidhīyate || Household implements, conveyances, food items, ornaments, and instruments of action are divided among visible heirs; in their absence, the hidden wealth is allocated according to the unseen karmic entitlements determined by the continuity of consciousness. Authority stems from ontological visibility and karmic continuity, not mere physical possession. Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of deeds across lifetimes. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to dharma-sustaining actions. Restoration logic prioritizes alignment of material distribution with subtle karmic integrity. Consciousness alignment ensures that all assets serve the evolutionary completion of involved parties.

title: brihaspati 1.41
content: क्षत्रजास् त्रिद्व्येकभागाः विड्जौ तु द्व्येकभागिनौ // kṣatrajās tridvyekabhāgāḥ viḍjau tu dvyekabhāginau The kshatriya-born inherit three-fourths of the division; the vijau inherit two-fourths. Authority flows through varna-dharma as defined by birth-consciousness alignment Inheritance rights are determined by inherent capacity, not mere lineage Division of property follows sequential manifestation based on spiritual readiness Restoration occurs when ownership aligns with dharmic fitness Consciousness alignment determines lawful entitlement

title: brihaspati 1.42
content:
ब्राह्मक्षत्रियविश्शूद्रा विप्रोत्पन्नास्त्वनुक्रमात् ।
चतुस्त्रिद्व्येकभागेन भवेयुस्ते यथाक्रमम् ॥ brāhma-kṣatriya-viśa-śūdrā viprotpannās tv anukramāt | catustridvyekabhāgena bhaveyus te yathākramam || From the union of Brāhmaṇa with Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra women respectively, offspring are born in sequence as per varṇic alignment; they shall be constituted by one-fourth, one-third, and one-half proportions accordingly. Authority flows from conscious genetic alignment Causation arises through sequential manifestation of dharma-saṁskāra Capacity-based responsibility is determined by birth-proportionality Restoration logic aligns individual capacity with cosmic order Consciousness alignment depends on inherited dharmic potential

title: brihaspati 1.43
content:
शूद्र्यां द्विजातिभिर् जातो न भूमेर् भागम् अर्हति ।
द्विजातिर् आप्नुयात् सर्वम् इति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ॥ śūdryāṃ dvijātibhir jāto na bhūmer bhāgam arhati | dvijātir āpnuyāt sarvam iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ || One born of twice-born men with a Śūdra woman shall not inherit land; all property belongs exclusively to the twice-born. Authority flows through consecrated lineage, not biological parentage alone Causation in inheritance is determined by sacramental continuity, not genetic origin Capacity-based responsibility derives from initiation and Vedic embodiment Restoration logic requires alignment of ownership with qualified consciousness Consciousness alignment is secured through ritual purity and scriptural authority

title: brihaspati 1.44
content: तेषां सवर्णा� ye पुत्रास् ते तृतीयांशभागिनः / हीनास् तम् उपजीवेयुः ग्रासाच्छादनसंभृताः // BrhS_1,26.44 teṣāṃ savarṇā ye putrās te tṛtīyāṃśabhāginaḥ / hīnās tam upajīveyur grāsācchādanasaṃbhṛtāḥ // BrhS_1,26.44 Those sons born of the same class who are deficient in capacity shall sustain themselves by providing food and clothing from one-third share of the paternal estate. Authority derives from conscious capacity, not birth alone Causation aligns with dharmic function, not biological lineage Capacity-based responsibility determines resource allocation Restoration logic prioritizes sustenance over ownership Consciousness alignment requires fulfillment of svadharma through material support

title: brihaspati 1.45
content:
सर्वे ह्यनौरसस्यैते पुत्रा दायहराः स्मृताः ।
औरसे पुनरुत्पन्ने तेषु ज्यैष्ठ्यं न तिष्ठति ॥ sarve hy anaurasasyaite putrā dāyaharāḥ smṛtāḥ / aurase punar utpanne teṣu jyaiṣṭhyaṃ na tiṣṭhati // All sons born to a man through non-aurasa means are designated as entitled to inheritance; however, when an aurasa son is born again into that lineage, primogeniture among the others ceases to exist. Authority flows from ontological legitimacy, not mere birth Causation in inheritance is determined by conscious intent and dharmic alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises from spiritual succession, not biological precedence Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma over material claim Consciousness alignment determines rightful heirship

title: brihaspati 1.46
content:
पितामहपितृभ्यां च दत्तं मात्रा च यद् भवेत् ।
तस्य तन् नापहर्तव्यं शौर्यभार्याधनं तथा ॥ pitāmahapitṛbhyāṃ ca dattaṃ mātrā ca yad bhavet / tasya tan nāpahartavyaṃ śauryabhāryādhanaṃ tathā // That which is given by the paternal grandfather, father, or mother shall not be taken away; likewise, the wealth belonging to a heroic wife is also not to be seized. Authority of familial givers as irrevocable source-title holders Causation through consanguineous lineage as determinant of ownership rights Capacity-based responsibility rooted in relational dharma Restoration logic premised on non-violation of ancestral and maternal bestowals Consciousness alignment with honoring generational continuity and spousal valor

title: brihaspati 1.47
content:
वस्त्रादयोऽविभाज्या यैरुक्तं तैर्न विचारितम् ।
धनं भवेत्समृद्धानां वस्त्रालंकारसंश्रितम् ॥ vastrādayo 'vibhājyā yair uktaṃ tair na vicāritam / dhanaṃ bhavet samṛddhānāṃ vastrālaṃkārasaṃśritam // That wealth which is accumulated through items like clothing and ornaments—when not examined by those who declared it indivisible, becomes the property of the affluent. Authority: Ownership is determined by declaration aligned with consciousness capacity. Causation: Wealth manifests based on prior declarations and unexamined assumptions. Capacity-based responsibility: Those capable of discernment must verify ownership claims. Restoration logic: Misplaced wealth returns to conscious alignment through verification. Consciousness alignment: Material possessions reflect inner integrity and clarity.

title: brihaspati 1.48
content: ṛṇम् उद्वाह्य लेखितम् ṛṇam udvāhya lekhitam Debt, once acknowledged in writing and elevated through conscious completion, dissolves the karmic entanglement binding the debtor and creditor. Authority arises from conscious acknowledgment, not coercive enforcement. Causation is rooted in volitional debt creation and its conscious resolution. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to recognize, record, and rectify debt. Restoration occurs when integrity is re-established through documented completion. Consciousness alignment is achieved through truthful documentation and voluntary discharge.

title: brihaspati 1.49
content:
उक्तप्रकारो विज्ञेयः पत्रारूढ़ऋणे खलु /
उक्त्या विभजनीयं तदन्यथानर्थकं भवेत् ।। uktaprakāro vijñeyaḥ patrārūḍhaṛṇe khalu / uktayā vibhajanīyaṃ tad anyathānarthakaṃ bhavet The method of declaration is to be known in the case of a debt incurred through written instrument; by speech it is to be divided, otherwise it becomes meaningless. Authority resides in the authenticity of documented obligation Causation arises from conscious assent evidenced in writing Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of contractual form Restoration logic demands verbal resolution aligned with original intent Consciousness alignment necessitates clarity between parties

title: brihaspati 1.50
content:
मध्यस्थितम् अनाजीव्यं दातुं नैकस्य शक्यते ।
युक्त्या विभजनीयं तद् अन्यथानर्थकं भवेत् ॥ madhyasthitam anājīvyaṃ dātuṃ naikasya śakyate /
yuktyā vibhajanīyaṃ tad anyathānarthakaṃ bhavet // That which is positioned equidistantly and not sustaining life cannot be given by one alone; it must be divided through appropriate reasoning, otherwise it becomes purposeless. Authority is distributed proportionally to existential capacity Causation arises from functional participation in sustenance Capacity-based responsibility determines rightful action Restoration logic requires proportional allocation of resources Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects utility

title: brihaspati 1.51
content:
विक्रीय वस्त्राभरणं धनम् उद्ग्राह्य लेखितम् ।
कृतान्नं चाकृतान्नेन परिवर्त्य विभज्यते ॥ vikrīya vastrābharaṇaṃ dhanam udgrāhya lekhitam | kṛtānnaṃ cākṛtānnena parivartya vibhajyate || Property, whether in the form of garments, ornaments, or other wealth, once documented and exchanged, must be equitably redistributed when a transaction occurs between those who have prepared food and those who have not. Authority is derived from capacity to sustain life through labor and preparation Causation arises from mutual consent expressed through written agreement Capacity-based responsibility determines equitable redistribution Restoration logic ensures sustenance equity among parties Consciousness alignment is maintained by honoring reciprocal exchange

title: brihaspati 1.52
content: योगक्षेमवतो लाभः समत्वेन विभज्यते । प्रचारश् च यथांशेन कर्तव्यो ऋक्थिभिः सदा ॥ yogakṣemavato lābhaḥ samatvena vibhajyate / pracāraś ca yathāṃśena kartavyo rikthibhiḥ sadā // The gain accruing to one who maintains yoga (union) and kṣema (preservation) shall be equitably distributed; likewise, propagation must always be conducted proportionally by those bearing responsibility. Authority arises from sustained union and preservation capacity Causation is established through conscious maintenance of integrity Capacity-based responsibility determines proportional participation Restoration logic aligns with equitable distribution of gains Consciousness alignment ensures harmonious propagation

title: brihaspati 1.53
content:
ब्रह्मदायं गतां भूमिं हरेद् यो ब्राह्मणीसुतः ।
गृहं द्विजातयः सर्वे तथा क्षेत्रं क्रमागतम् ॥ brahmadaayaM gataaM bhuumiM hared yo braahmaNI-sutaH | gRihaM dvijaatayaH sarve tathaa kSetraM kramaagatam || He who seizes land given in brahmadāna, or a house belonging to all dvijas, or cultivated fields acquired in proper order — such seizure disrupts dharma and constitutes a violation of cosmic alignment. Authority: Only those aligned with Vedic consciousness may own or transfer property. Causation: Disruption of sacred ownership creates misalignment in societal harmony. Capacity-based responsibility: Ownership rights correspond to spiritual capacity and dharmic integrity. Restoration logic: Reversal of wrongful acquisition restores balance without punitive consequence. Consciousness alignment: Property must reflect the spiritual maturity of its holder.

title: brihaspati 1.54
content:
पित्रा सह विभक्ता ये सापत्ना वा सहोदराः ।
जघन्याश् चैव ये तेषां पितृभागहरास् तु ते ॥ pitrā saha vibhaktā ye sāpatnā vā sahodarāḥ / jaghanyāś caiva ye teṣāṃ pitṛbhāgaharās tu te Those who are divided from the father along with co-wives or uterine brothers, and those who are youngest among them—these are entitled to a share from the paternal estate. Authority resides inherently in blood lineage and ontological connection to the paternal source. Causation arises through birthright, not through external validation or societal contract. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to the generative source and natural order. Restoration logic operates through recognition of inherent entitlement rooted in dharma-sambandha (duty-bound relational integrity). Consciousness alignment occurs when material inheritance reflects spiritual succession without distortion.

title: brihaspati 1.55
content: अनीशः पूर्वजः पित्र्ये भ्रातृभागे विभक्तजः ।। anīśaḥ pūrvajaḥ pitrye bhrātṛbhāge vibhaktajaḥ The eldest brother who is not empowered with authority receives a share in the paternal estate as defined by division among brothers. Authority flows from conscious empowerment, not birth order alone Paternal inheritance is distributed according to relational integrity and dharma-apparent capacity Division of assets arises through conscious agreement and alignment, not force or default lineage Responsibility precedes entitlement in matters of inheritance Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership beyond formal claim

title: brihaspati 1.56
content:
पुत्रैः सह विभक्तेन पित्रा यत् स्वयम् आर्जितम् ।
विभक्तजस्य तत् सर्वम् अनीशाः पूर्वजाः स्मृताः ॥ ५६ ॥ putraiḥ saha vibhaktena pitrā yat svayam ārjitam / vibhaktajasya tat sarvam anīśāḥ pūrvajāḥ smṛtāḥ // BrhS_1,26.56 // Whatever wealth is independently earned by a father who has already divided property among his sons shall belong entirely to the prior-born sons; those born later hold no claim over it. Authority resides in the completion of formal allocation by the progenitor Causation follows the act of self-acquisition post-division Capacity-based responsibility is determined by temporal precedence of birth Restoration logic enforces pre-existing structural integrity of familial order Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of sequential manifestation

title: brihaspati 1.57
content: यथा धने तथा ऋणे च दानादानक्रयेषु च । परस्परमनीशास्ते मुक्त्वाशौचोदकक्रियाम् ॥ yathā dhane tathā ṛṇe ca dānādānakrayeṣu ca / parasparam anīśās te muktvāśaucodakakriyām // In transactions involving wealth, debt, gifts, exchanges, or acquisitions, parties are not masters over one another once the purificatory water-libation ritual is completed. Authority is context-bound and ceases upon completion of prescribed rituals Causation arises through conscious ritual discharge, not mere contractual agreement Capacity-based responsibility ends when purification and formal closure occur Restoration logic demands relational equilibrium post-transactional completion Consciousness alignment requires ceremonial dissolution of mutual dominion

title: brihaspati 1.58
content:
पैतामहं हृतं पित्रा स्वशक्त्या यद् उपार्जितम् ।
विद्याशौर्यादिनावाप्तं तत्र स्वाम्यं पितुः स्मृतम् ॥ ५८ ॥ paitāmahaṃ hṛtaṃ pitrā svaśaktyā yad upārjitam | vidyāśauryādināvāptaṃ tatra svāmyaṃ pituḥ smṛtam || 58 || That which is inherited from the grandfather and acquired by the father through his own capacity—gained via knowledge, valor, or similar virtues—is recognized as the father's domain. Authority arises from conscious acquisition through dharma-based effort Causation is traced to individual capacity and intentional action Capacity-based responsibility determines ownership rights Restoration logic honors generational continuity of conscious earning Consciousness alignment validates lineage-based stewardship

title: brihaspati 1.59
content: प्रदानं स्वेच्छया कुर्यात् भोगं चैव ततो धनात् । तदभावे�पि तनयाः समांशाः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ pradānaṃ svecchayā kuryāt bhogaṃ caiva tato dhanāt | tadabhāve 'pi tanayāḥ samāṃśāḥ parikīrtitāḥ || One shall freely give from one's wealth for enjoyment and sustenance; in its absence, children are declared equal inheritors. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not material possession Causation aligns with dharmic intention, not economic outcome Capacity-based responsibility extends to progeny when direct agency is absent Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma through lineage Consciousness alignment requires equitable distribution rooted in svadharma

title: brihaspati 1.60
content:
वस्त्रालंकारशय्याः पितुर्यद्वाहनादिकम् ।
गन्धमाल्यैः समभ्यर्च्य श्राद्धभोक्त्रे तदर्पयेत् ॥ vastrālaṃkāraśayyāḥ pituryadvāhanādikam | gandhamālyaiḥ samabhyarcya śrāddhabhokṣtre tadarpayet || Whatever conveyance, apparel, ornamentation, bedding, or vehicle belonged to the father shall be offered to the designated recipient of the śrāddha, after due worship with fragrances and garlands. Authority flows through filial duty and ancestral continuity Causation arises from the completion of prescribed ritual acts Capacity-based responsibility is determined by lineage and spiritual succession Restoration logic operates through reverent transmission of patrimony Consciousness alignment occurs when familial dharma is enacted without deviation

title: brihaspati 1.61
content:
पत्यौ जीवति यः स्त्रीभिरलंकारो धृतो भवेत् ।
