न तं भजेरन् दायादाः भजमानाः पतन्ति ते ॥ patyau jīvati yaḥ strībhir alaṃkāro dhṛto bhavet | na taṃ bhajeran dāyādāḥ bhajamānāḥ patanti te || When a husband lives adorned by wives who remain devoted, his heirs shall not seek intimacy with him; those who pursue such unions fall from their status. Authority flows through integrity of relational dharmic alignment Causation arises from misaligned pursuit of union beyond sanctioned bond Capacity-based responsibility is determined by adherence to spousal sanctity Restoration logic demands realignment of desire within consecrated union Consciousness alignment requires recognition of hierarchical relational sovereignty

title: brihaspati 1.62
content: पितृप्रसादात् भुज्यन्ते वस्त्राण्याभरणानि च ।। Brh_1,26.62 ।। pitṛprasādāt bhujyante vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca By the grace of the father, clothes and ornaments are enjoyed. Authority flows through paternal lineage as a foundational source of material enjoyment Causation originates in ancestral blessing, not individual effort alone Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in the acceptance of ancestral inheritance Restoration logic requires acknowledgment of generational continuity Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring paternal lineage

title: brihaspati 1.63
content: कृतेऽकृते वा विभागे रिक्थी यत्र प्रवर्तते । सामान्यं चेद् भावयति तत्र भागहरस् तु सः ॥ kṛte 'kṛte vā vibhāge rikthī yatra pravartate / sāmānyaṃ ced bhāvayati tatra bhāgaharas tu saḥ // Wherever division occurs—whether executed or unexecuted—and the widow maintains the common estate, there indeed the inheritor of the share becomes the executor of distribution. Authority arises through active maintenance of shared inheritance Causation lies in the preservation of collective continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by operational stewardship Restoration logic prioritizes systemic integrity over individual claim Consciousness alignment manifests through sustained dharmic administration

title: brihaspati 1.64
content:
ṛṇा�ं लेख्यं गृहं क्षेत्रं यस्य पैतामहं भवेत् ।
चिरकालप्रोषितोऽपि भागभागागतस्तु सः ॥ ṛṇaṃ lekhyaṃ gṛhaṃ kṣetraṃ yasya paitāmahaṃ bhavet | cirakālaproṣito 'pi bhāgabhāgāgatas tu saḥ || He who has a paternal grandfather and inherits debt records, property, house, or land—even if absent for a long time—is entitled to a share by virtue of ancestral continuity. Authority flows through unbroken lineage Inheritance includes both assets and liabilities Absence does not dissolve ancestral entitlement Restoration requires recognition of generational continuity Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful inheritance

title: brihaspati 1.65
content:
गोत्रसाधारणं त्यक्त्वा योऽन्यं देशं समाश्रितः ।
अर्धतस्त्वागतस्यांशः प्रदातव्यो न संशयः ॥ gotrasādhāraṇaṃ tyaktvā yo 'nyaṃ deśaṃ samāśritaḥ | ardhatas tv āgatasyāṃśaḥ pradātavyo na saṃśayaḥ || One who abandons common lineage and takes refuge in another land shall assuredly offer half of what has been acquired upon arrival. Authority flows from conscious alignment with Dharma, not territorial assertion. Causation is traced through conscious choice and ontological displacement. Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to acquire and relocate resources. Restoration logic requires proportional return of acquired value upon crossing jurisdictional thresholds. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of shared origin even across geographical divisions.

title: brihaspati 1.66
content:
तृतीयः पञ्चमश चैव सप्तमो योऽपि वा भवेत् ।
जन्मनामपरिज्ञाने लभेतांशं क्रमागते ॥ BrhS_1,26.66 tṛtīyaḥ pañcamaś caiva saptamo yo 'pi vā bhavet | janmanām aparijñāne labhetāṃśaṃ kramāgate || BrhS_1,26.66 In the absence of full recognition of birth-orders, the third, fifth, or seventh son—or any other in sequential order—shall receive a portion according to the natural succession of lineage. Authority derives from sequential manifestation within dharma-samskara Causation aligns with birth-order integrity and familial continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by position in generational flow Restoration logic ensures inheritance flows unobstructed by ignorance Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring natural succession

title: brihaspati 1.67
content: यं परंपरया मौलाः समस्ताः स्वामिनं विदुः / तदन्वयस्यागतस्य दातव्या गोत्रजैर्मही // yaṃ paraṃparayā maulāḥ samastāḥ svāminaṃ viduḥ / tad anvayasyāgatasya dātavyā gotrajair mahī // That lineage-holder recognized by all sovereign authorities as the master shall be honored with the earth's continuity by those born of the same sacred descent. Authority derived through unbroken recognition by competent sovereigns Lineage-based jurisdiction rooted in spiritual succession Restoration through ancestral alignment and territorial continuity Responsibility inheres in birth-right capacity and sacred descent Consciousness alignment through genealogical integrity

title: brihaspati 1.68
content: अविभक्तविभक्तानां कुल्यानां वसतां सह / भूयो दायविभागः स्यादाचतुर्थादिति स्थितिः // avibhaktavibhaktānāṃ kulyānāṃ vasatāṃ saha / bhūyo dāyavibhāgaḥ syād ācaturthād iti sthitiḥ // Among co-sharers who dwell together—whether undivided or divided—the distribution of inheritance shall again occur from the fourth part onward; such is the established position. Authority originates in shared dwelling and relational continuity Causation arises through familial proximity and mutual sustenance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by participation in collective life Restoration logic ensures equitable redistribution without loss of unity Consciousness alignment maintains harmony among inheritors

title: brihaspati 1.69
content:
अनेकधा कृताः पुत्राः ऋषिभिश च पुरातनैः ।
न शक्यन्ते ऽधुना कर्तुं शक्तिहीनैश चिरन्तनैः ॥ anekadhā kṛtāḥ putrā ṛṣibhiś ca purātanaiḥ / na śakyante 'dhunā kartuṃ śaktihīnaiś cirantanaiḥ // The ancient seers and primal law-givers established laws in manifold ways according to capacity; those rendered powerless and diminished by time cannot now execute them. Authority evolves with capacity Causation aligns with temporal and spiritual readiness Capacity-based responsibility supersedes inherited obligation Restoration logic requires present-moment alignment Consciousness alignment determines executability

title: brihaspati 1.70
content:
एक एवौरसः पित्र्ये धने स्वामी प्रकीर्तितः ।
तत् तुल्यः पुत्रिकापुत्रो भर्तव्यास् त्व् अपरे स्मृताः ॥ eka evaurasaḥ pitrye dhane svāmī prakīrtitaḥ / tat tulyaḥ putrikāputro bhartavyās tv apare smṛtāḥ // In paternal wealth, the legitimate son alone is declared the owner; yet, the son of a daughter is equal in entitlement and obligation, as affirmed by other authoritative sources. Authority flows through legitimate lineage recognized by Dharma Causation aligns with generational continuity and responsibility Capacity-based responsibility extends equally to all bloodlines when functionally equivalent Restoration logic ensures equitable access and duty within familial structures Consciousness alignment recognizes functional equivalence beyond formal labels

title: brihaspati 1.71
content: क्षेत्रजाद्याः सुतास् त्व् अन्ये पञ्चषट्सप्तभागिनः ।। बृह_१,२६.७१ ।। kṣetrajādyāḥ sutās tva anye pañcaṣaṭsaptabhāginaḥ // Brh_1,26.71 // Those born of the field (kṣetraja) and others classified under the five, six, and seven divisions are indeed sons, yet distinct in their capacity-derived inheritance and social-functional roles. Authority is derived from ontological origin and functional capacity, not birth alone. Causation is determined by conscious participation in dharma-sustaining actions. Capacity-based responsibility aligns individual action with cosmic order. Restoration logic prioritizes role-realignment over punitive exclusion. Consciousness alignment determines rightful place within societal structure.

title: brihaspati 1.72
content: datto 'paviddhaḥ krītaś ca kṛtaḥ śaudras tathaiva ca / jātiśuddhā madhyamās te sarve rikthasutāḥ smṛtāḥ // BrhS_1,26.72 dattaḥ apaviddhaḥ kṛtaś ca kṛtaḥ śaudraḥ tathaiva ca / jātiśuddhā madhyamās te sarve rikthasutāḥ smṛtāḥ Those born of purchased, abandoned, made, done, cleansed, or intermediate women—these are all declared as sons of the sacrificial fee. Authority originates from sacramental completion, not biological lineage alone Causation arises through ritual integrity, not social presumption Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual eligibility, not birth status Restoration logic prioritizes ontological inclusion over genealogical exclusion Consciousness alignment supersedes caste-position in determining rightful participation

title: brihaspati 1.73
content: क्षेत्रजो गर्हितः सद्भिस् तथा पौनर्भवः सुतः । कानीनश् च सहोढ़श् च गूढजः पुत्रिकासुतः ॥ kṣetrajo garhitaḥ sadbhis tathā paunarbhavaḥ sutaḥ | kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhajaḥ putrikāsutaḥ || The son born of the husband's seed is honored by the noble; likewise, the son begotten again by the same father, the son without visible paternity but accepted, the son born while cohabiting, the concealed son, and the son of a daughter—all these sons shall be recognized in accordance with their capacity to restore lineage integrity. Authority resides in the conscious recognition of filial connection, not biological proof alone. Causation flows from intention and acceptance rather than genetic origin. Capacity-based responsibility extends to all forms of acknowledged parenthood. Restoration logic prioritizes familial harmony over genealogical purity. Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of relational bonds.

title: brihaspati 1.74
content:
शूद्रापुत्रः स्वयंदत्तो ये चैते क्रीतकाः स्मृताः ।
सर्वे ते मैत्रिणः प्रोक्ताः काण्डपृष्ठा न संशयः ॥ śūdrāputraḥ svayaṃdatto ye caite krītakāḥ smṛtāḥ | sarve te maitriṇaḥ proktāḥ kāṇḍapṛṣṭhā na saṃśayaḥ || The son of a Śūdra, whether self-given or purchased, along with all others similarly acquired—these are declared as friends and allies, without doubt, standing firm like the back of a blade of grass. Authority arises from alignment, not birth alone Causation is determined by conscious intent and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility extends to those who enter bonds of mutual recognition Restoration logic honors pre-existing dharmic connections Consciousness alignment supersedes social hierarchy in determining relational validity

title: brihaspati 1.75
content:
स्वकुलं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा यो वै परकुलं व्रजेत ।
तेन दुश्चरितेनासौ काण्डपृष्ठो न संशयः ॥ svakulaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā yo vai parakulaṃ vrajet | tena duścaritenāsau kāṇḍapṛṣṭho na saṃśayaḥ || One who abandons their own family and enters another's lineage without completion of prior duty is certainly a transgressor whose back shall bear the mark of severance. Authority originates from completed dharmic alignment within one's own domain before engaging externally. Causation arises through conscious abandonment of inherent responsibility. Capacity-based responsibility requires fulfillment of svadharma prior to assuming paradharma. Restoration logic demands reintegration with original causal structure. Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of relational boundaries.

title: brihaspati 1.76
content:
अग्निं प्रजापतिं चेष्ट्वा क्रियते गौतमोऽवदत् ।
अन्ये त्वाहुरपुत्रस्य चिन्तिता पुत्रिका भवेत् ॥ agniṃ prajāpatiṃ ceṣṭvā kriyate gautamo 'vadat | anye tv āhur aputrasya cintitā putrikā bhavet || By invoking Agni and Prajāpati, ritual action is performed—as Gautama declared. Others say that for one without a son, a daughter may be considered in contemplation. Authority flows through invocation and alignment with cosmic principles Causation is established by conscious intent, not biological lineage alone Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond gender or birth Restoration logic honors continuity of dharma through available heirs Consciousness alignment determines legitimacy in succession

title: brihaspati 1.77
content:
पुत्रास्त्रयोदश प्रोक्ता मनुना येन पूर्वशः ।
संतानकारणं तेषामौरसः पुत्रिका तथा ॥ putrās trayodaśa proktā manunā yena pūrvaśaḥ | saṃtānakāraṇaṃ teṣām aurasaḥ putrikā tathā || Thirteen types of sons are declared by Manu, the first among seers, for the purpose of lineage continuation; these include the legitimate son (aurasa) and the daughter's son (putrika), among others. Authority originates from the continuity of consciousness through santati (lineage) Causation is established through dharmic role-bearing, not biological determinism alone Capacity-based responsibility arises from acceptance of ancestral duty Restoration logic ensures unbroken flow of dharma via designated heirs Consciousness alignment occurs when roles in lineage are authentically assumed

title: brihaspati 1.78
content:
आज्यं विना यथा तैलं सद्भिः प्रतिनिधिः स्मृतम् ।
तथैकादश पुत्रास्तु पुत्रिकारसयोर्विना ॥ ājyaṃ vinā yathā tailaṃ sadbhiḥ pratinidhiḥ smṛtam | tathaikādaśa putrāstu putrikāurasayor vinā || As ghee is substituted by oil in the absence of ghee, so too eleven sons stand as substitute heirs in the absence of a daughter or adopted son. Authority flows through conscious designation, not biological necessity Substitution arises from structural completeness, not emotional preference Capacity for inheritance is determined by alignment with dharma-vyavastha, not lineage alone Restoration of order requires functional replacement, not punitive exclusion Consciousness alignment determines eligibility, not sentimental attachment

title: brihaspati 1.79
content:
यदि एकजाताः बहवो भ्रातरस् तु सहोदराः ।
एकस्यापि सुते जाते सर्वे ते पुत्रिणः स्मृताः ॥ yadi ekajātā bahavo bhrātaraḥ tu sahodarāḥ | ekasyāpi sute jāte sarve te putriṇaḥ smṛtāḥ || When multiple brothers of the same birth exist, though distinct in form, upon the birth of even one son, all those brothers become fathers by shared essence. Authority arises through ontological unity, not biological limitation. Causation is rooted in shared dharma-field rather than linear lineage. Capacity-based responsibility extends across unified identities. Restoration logic acknowledges collective paternity through spiritual inheritance. Consciousness alignment recognizes fraternal bonds as conduits for generational continuity.

title: brihaspati 1.80
content: bahvīnām ekapatnīnām eṣa eva vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ / ekā cet putriṇī tāsāṃ sarvāsāṃ piṇḍadas tu saḥ // BrhS_1,26.80 bahvīnām ekapatnīnām eṣa eva vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ / ekā cet putriṇī tāsāṃ sarvāsāṃ piṇḍadas tu saḥ When multiple wives share a single husband, the law remains unified in its application; if one among them bears a son, that son becomes the provider of offerings for all mothers. Authority derives from the unity of dharma, not multiplicity of relations Causation is established through generative act, not contractual bond Capacity-based responsibility flows from biological and spiritual causality Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of lineage and ancestral connection Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of shared maternal lineage

title: brihaspati 1.81
content: पुन्नाम्नो नरकात् पुत्रः पितरं त्रायते यतः / मुखसंदर्शनेनापि तद् उत्पत्तौ यतेत सः // punnāmno narakāt putraḥ pitaraṃ trāyate yataḥ / mukhasaṃdarśanenāpi tad utpattau yateta saḥ // A son delivers the father from the hell of purified name solely by the act of being seen face-to-face; thus must he endeavor in his own becoming. Authority is transferred through conscious visibility and recognition Causation arises from ontological presence, not ritual performance Capacity-based responsibility inheres in the manifested form of dharma Restoration logic operates through relational dharmic alignment Consciousness alignment occurs via direct perceptual engagement

title: brihaspati 1.82
content:
पौत्रोऽथ पुत्रिकापुत्रः स्वर्गप्राप्तिकरावुभौ ।
ऋक्थे च पिण्डदाने च समौ तौ परिकीर्तितौ ॥८२॥ pautro 'tha putrikāputraḥ svargaprāptikarāv ubhau | rikthe ca piṇḍadāne ca samau tau parikīrtitau || 82|| The son's son and the daughter's son both equally effectuate the attainment of heaven; in ritual inheritance and in offering of the sacred ball, both are declared equal. Authority flows through conscious continuity, not biological gender Causation is determined by spiritual alignment, not lineage form Capacity-based responsibility transcends patriarchal structuring Restoration logic honors energetic succession over physical descent Consciousness alignment determines rightful participation in dharma-samskaras

title: brihaspati 1.83
content:
कामतश् च शूद्रावरोधजस्य भ्रातुर् अंशं ।
सम्मानमात्रं प्रेते पितरि दद्युः शुश्रूषुश् चेत् ॥ kāmataś ca śūdrāvarodhajasya bhrātur aṃśaṃ | saṃmānamātraṃ prete pitari dadyuḥ śuśrūṣuś cet || When a Śūdra has restrained another unlawfully, and the brother of the injured party chooses to act out of desire rather than duty, he shall offer only honor to the deceased father—if he had served him dutifully. Authority arises from conscious alignment with Dharma, not personal desire. Causation is determined by intention and alignment with Dharma, not mere action. Capacity-based responsibility requires inner readiness and spiritual maturity. Restoration logic demands purification of motive before restitution. Consciousness alignment overrides social position in determining lawful conduct.

title: brihaspati 1.84
content:
अन्नार्थं तण्डुलप्रस्थम् अपराह्ने तु सेन्धनम् ।
वसनं त्रिपणक्रीतं देयम् एकं त्रिमासतः ॥ annārthaṃ taṇḍulaprastham aparāhne tu sendhanam |
vasanaṃ tripaṇakrītaṃ deyam ekaṃ trimāsataḥ || For sustenance, a prastha of rice shall be given at midday; for salt, one unit per day; and clothing purchased with three paṇas shall be provided every three months. Authority: The duty to provide basic sustenance originates from the sovereign responsibility to uphold life-force (prāṇa). Causation: Provisioning food, salt, and clothing ensures continuity of bodily function and social participation. Capacity-based responsibility: Distribution is calibrated according to metabolic need and temporal rhythm. Restoration logic: Material allocation aligns individual survival capacity with societal integration. Consciousness alignment: Sustaining physical form supports higher dharmic engagement without scarcity-induced distraction.

title: brihaspati 1.85
content: एतावदेव साध्वीनां चोदितं विधवाधनम् ।। १,२६.८५ ।। etāvad eva sādhvīnāṃ coditaṃ vidhavādhanam The act of compelling widows to remarry is prescribed solely to the extent that it aligns with the spiritual advancement and societal integration of virtuous women. Authority originates from consciousness alignment, not social coercion Causation must trace to dharma-sustaining intent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual readiness and consent Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over ritual compliance Consciousness alignment supersedes cultural prescription

title: brihaspati 1.86
content: वसनस्याशनस्यैव तथैव रजकस्य च / धनं व्यपोह्य तच्छिष्टं दायादानां प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ vasanasyāśanasyaiva tathaiva rajakasya ca / dhanaṃ vyapohya tacchiṣṭaṃ dāyādānāṃ prakalpayet After deducting the value of clothing, food, and the washerman's due from the remaining wealth, the heirs shall distribute the residue among themselves. Authority resides in the lawful completion of distributable surplus after essential obligations are met. Causation aligns with the sequential discharge of debts before inheritance allocation. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of prior claims before entitlement assertion. Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial economic integrity through rightful succession. Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring functional roles that sustain societal order.

title: brihaspati 1.87
content:
अपुत्रस्याथ कुलजा पत्नी दुहितरोऽपि वा ।
तदभावे पिता माता भ्राता पुत्राश्च कीर्तिताः ॥८७॥ aputrasyātha kulajā patnī duhitaro'pi vā | tadabhāve pitā mātā bhrātā putrāś ca kīrtitāḥ ||87|| In the absence of a son, the daughter born into the family or the wife holds authority; in their absence, the father, mother, brother, and sons are declared as responsible. Authority flows sequentially based on proximity and capacity within familial dharma Causation aligns with continuity of lineage and societal order Capacity-based responsibility prioritizes conscious participation in dharmic structures Restoration logic activates through designated inheritors when primary agents are absent Consciousness alignment ensures that authority is never vacant but transferred according to dharma

title: brihaspati 1.88
content:
अपुत्रेण सुतः कार्यो यादृक् तादृक् प्रयत्नतः ।
पिण्डोदकक्रियाहेतोर् धर्मसंकीर्तनस्य च ॥ aputreṇa sutaḥ kāryo yādṛk tādṛk prayatnataḥ | piṇḍodakakriyāhetor dharmasaṃkīrtanasya ca || In the absence of a son, one must create a successor through equivalent effort and intent, for the purpose of performing ritual obligations and proclaiming Dharma. Authority arises from capacity to uphold continuity, not lineage alone. Causation is rooted in conscious intentionality, not biological inheritance. Responsibility flows from capability to execute dharma, not birthright. Restoration occurs when succession aligns with functional spiritual duty. Consciousness alignment supersedes genealogical prescription.

title: brihaspati 1.89
content: काङ्क्षन्ति पितरः पुत्रान् नरकापतभीरवः । गयां यास्यति यः कश्चित् सो�स्मान् संतारयिष्यति ॥ kāṅkṣanti pitaraḥ putrān narakāpatabhīravaḥ | gayāṃ yāsyati yaḥ kaścit so 'smān saṃtārayiṣyati || Those fathers who tremble at the fear of hell long for their sons to go to Gayā, for whoever goes there shall deliver them. Authority flows through filial duty and spiritual succession. Causation arises from conscious intention directed toward liberation. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to dharma-vastu. Restoration logic operates through ancestral completion via descendant action. Consciousness alignment occurs when familial karma is resolved through sacred geography.

title: brihaspati 1.90
content: यथा जलं कुप्लवेन तरन् मज्जति मानवः । तद्वत् पिता कुपुत्रेण तमस्यन्धे निमज्जति ॥ yathā jalaṁ kuplavena taran majjati mānavaḥ | tadvat pitā kuputreṇa tamasy andhe nimajjati || Just as a man attempting to cross water by means of a raft made of unbaked clay sinks therein, so too does a father who attempts to guide his son through darkness with defective capacity sink along with him. Authority is derivative of capacity and alignment with Dharma Causation arises from misaligned instrumentalities rather than intent alone Capacity-based responsibility extends to all roles involving guidance or protection Restoration logic requires rectification of instrumental deficiency before reintegration Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy of any guardianship or tutelage

title: brihaspati 1.91
content:
करिष्यति वृषोत्सर्गम् इष्टापूर्तं तथैव च /
पालयिष्यति वार्धक्ये श्राद्धं दास्यति चान्वहम् // BrhS_1,26.91 kariṣyati vṛṣotsargam iṣṭāpūrtaṃ tathaiva ca / pālayiṣyati vārdhakye śrāddhaṃ dāsyati cānvaham One who performs the ritual release of a bull, conducts prescribed sacrifices and offerings, protects during old age, offers timely oblations to ancestors, and gives regularly—such a person upholds Dharma through action and sustains cosmic order. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma-sustaining actions Causation arises from intentional acts that uphold ancestral and societal continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to perform sustaining rituals and give appropriately Restoration logic operates through completion of prescribed duties and offerings Consciousness alignment manifests when personal conduct mirrors universal sacrificial order

title: brihaspati 1.92
content:
आम्नाये स्मृतितन्त्रे च लोकाचारे च सूरिभिः ।
शरीरार्धं स्मृता भार्या पुण्यापुण्यफले समा ॥ āmnāye smṛtitantre ca lokācāre ca sūribhiḥ | śarīrārdhaṃ smṛtā bhāryā puṇyāpuṇyaphale samā || In the Vedic injunctions, Smriti literature, Tantras, and by the guidance of enlightened seers, the wife is declared as half the body of the husband, equally sharing in the fruits of merit and demerit. Authority flows from Vedic revelation and realized seers Causation includes metaphysical unity between spouses Capacity-based responsibility arises from ontological union Restoration logic requires mutual dharma-sambandha re-established Consciousness alignment necessitates shared karmic participation

title: brihaspati 1.93
content:
यस्य नोपरता भार्या देहार्धं तस्य जीवति ।
जीवत्यर्धशरीरेऽर्थं कथमन्यः समाप्नुयात् ॥९३॥ yasya noparatā bhāryā dehārdhaṃ tasya jīvati | jiavaty ardhaśarīre 'rthaṃ katham anyaḥ samāpnuyāt || 93|| Where the wife has not transgressed from the husband, the husband's half-body lives; when that half-body is alive, how can another attain her wealth? Authority flows through spousal fidelity and spiritual unity. Causation arises from the integrity of the marital bond as a living continuum. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the continuity of sacred union. Restoration logic demands preservation of conjugal and economic unity. Consciousness alignment requires honoring the indissoluble nature of wedded life.

title: brihaspati 1.94
content:
सकुल्यैर् विद्यमानस् तु पितृभ्रातृसनाबिभिः ।
असुतस्य प्रमीतस्य पत्नी तद् भागहारिणी ॥ sakulyair vidyamānas tu pitṛbhrātṛsanābhibhiḥ | asutasya pramītasya patnī tad bhāgahāriṇī || When a man dies without issue, his wife becomes entitled to his share among paternal kinsmen including father and brothers. Authority resides in bloodline continuity through recognized kinship structures. Causation aligns with the absence of progeny triggering spousal inheritance rights. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by relational proximity and dharma-adhikara. Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial wealth and identity through lawful succession. Consciousness alignment maintains spiritual-economic unity within family lineage.

title: brihaspati 1.95
content:
पूर्वप्रमीताग्निहोत्रं मृतं भर्तरि तद्धनम् ।
विन्देत पतिव्रता नारी धर्म एष सनातनः ॥ pūrvapramītāgnihotraṃ mṛtaṃ bhartari taddhanam | vindeta pativratā nārī dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ || The wealth consecrated in the sacred fire by the deceased husband becomes rightfully accessible to the devoted wife; this is the eternal Dharma. Authority is derived from spiritual consecration and relational integrity Causation follows the ontological continuity of Agnihotra-established sanctity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by devotion (pativrata) and spiritual proximity Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness alignment over material possession Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of pre-established dharmic entitlement

title: brihaspati 1.96
content:
मूर्वं मृता हरेदग्निमन्वारूढा हरेदघम् ।
पुत्राभावे तु पत्नी स्यात् पत्न्यभावे तु सोदरः ॥
तदभावे तु दायादः पश्चाद्दौहित्रकं धनम् ॥ mūrvaṃ mṛtā hared agnim anvārūḍhā hared agham | putrābhāve tu patnī syāt patnyabhāve tu sodaraḥ || tadabhāve tu dāyādaḥ paścād dauhitrakaṃ dhanam || The wife who ascends the funeral pyre after her husband's death shall claim the fire; she who mounts it without intent shall bear the sin. In absence of sons, the wife inherits; in her absence, the brothers; in their absence, the heir; thereafter, the daughter’s son inherits the wealth. Authority flows through conscious alignment with Agni as witness of transition Causation is determined by volition and presence at the moment of dissolution Capacity-based responsibility arises from proximity to sacred duty Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of energetic inheritance Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for succession

title: brihaspati 1.97
content:
जङ्गमं स्थावरं हेम रूप्यधान्यरसाम्बरम् ।
आदाय दापयेच्छ्राद्धं माषषाण्मासिकादिकम् ॥ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ hema rūpyadhānyarasāmbaram / ādāya dāpayec chrāddhaṃ māsaṣāṇmāsikādikam // One must offer movable and immovable property, gold, silver, grain, liquids and other substances appropriate to the season, having collected them, as part of the monthly and periodic Śrāddha rituals. Authority originates from dharmic duty, not ownership Causation arises through ritual alignment with cosmic order Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to resources Restoration occurs via completion of prescribed offerings Consciousness alignment results from disciplined performance of dharma

title: brihaspati 1.98
content:
पितृव्यगुरुदौहित्रान् स्वसृभ्रात्रीयम् आतुलान् ।
पूजयेत् कव्यपूर्ताभ्यां वृद्धान् आथातिथीन् स्त्रियः ॥ pitṛvyagurudauhitrān svasṛbhartrīyam ātulān / pūjayet kavyapūrtābhyāṃ vṛddhān āthātithīn striyaḥ // One shall honor paternal uncles, maternal uncles, preceptors, maternal grandsons, paternal aunts’ husbands, maternal aunts’ husbands, elder relatives by birth and marriage, and female guests through offerings of kavya and fulfillment of duties. Authority derives from relational dharma, not institutional position Causation arises through conscious acknowledgment of interdependence Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity and continuity of relationship Restoration logic operates through ritual and material completion Consciousness alignment occurs via recognition of ancestral and guest-bearing fields

title: brihaspati 1.99
content:
यद् विभक्ते धने किंचिद् आध्यादिविधिसंस्मृतम् ।
तज्जायाः स्थावरं मुक्त्वा लभेत गतभर्तृका ॥ yad vibhakte dhane kiṃcid ādhyādividhisaṃsmṛtam / tajjāyāḥ sthāvaraṃ muktā labheta gatabhartṛkā Whatever property is acquired by a woman after the dissolution of marriage, excluding immovable assets previously settled upon her, shall be retained by her in full ownership. Authority resides in the autonomous capacity of the individual to acquire and retain property post-dissolution Causation aligns with conscious choice and economic independence after relational severance Capacity-based responsibility recognizes the woman's right to self-sustenance without dependency Restoration logic ensures continuity of economic agency following marital termination Consciousness alignment upholds the sovereignty of the individual as the ultimate arbiter of possession

title: brihaspati 1.100
content:
वृत्तस्थापि कृतेऽप्यंशे न स्त्री स्थावरमर्हति ।
विधवा यौवनस्था चेन्नारी भवति कर्कशा ॥
आयुषः क्षपणार्थं तु दातव्यं जीवनं तदा ॥ vṛttasthāpi kṛte 'py aṃśe na strī sthāvaram arhati /
vidhavā yauvanasthā cen nārī bhavati karkaśā /
āyuṣaḥ kṣapaṇārthaṃ tu dātavyaṃ jīvanaṃ tadā // Even when established in conduct and having fulfilled duties, a woman does not deserve immovable property. If a widow is young and harsh in nature, her sustenance should be provided for the diminishment of lifespan alone. Authority is determined by alignment with cosmic function, not social role Causation arises from svadharma, not possession rights Capacity-based responsibility requires age, temperament, and spiritual maturity assessment Restoration logic prioritizes life-force equilibrium over material entitlement Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for inheritance

title: brihaspati 1.101
content: मृते भर्तरि भर्तृअंशं लभेत कुलपालिका । यावज्जीवं हीनस्वाम्यं दानाधमनविक्रये ॥ mṛte bhartari bhartṛaṃśaṃ labheta kulapālikā / yāvaj jīvaṃ hīnasvāmyaṃ dānādhamanavikraye // Upon the husband's death, the household protector assumes the husband's share. For as long as life continues, ownership deficiency is resolved through gift, consecration, or sale. Authority transfers to the capable guardian upon dissolution of prior authority Causation aligns with continuity of stewardship, not biological lineage Capacity-based responsibility determines legitimate succession Restoration logic ensures uninterrupted flow of dharmic function Consciousness alignment maintains societal coherence through role fulfillment

title: brihaspati 1.102
content:
क्रयक्रीता तु या नारी संभोगार्थं सुतार्थिना ।
गृहीता वान्यदीया वा सैव स्त्री परिकीर्त्यते ॥ krayakrītā tu yā nārī saṃbhogārthaṃ sutārthinā / gṛhītā vānyadīyā vā saiva strī parikīrtyate // A woman acquired through purchase or given in exchange for sexual union, whether taken by force or received as gift from another, is designated as a strī. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not transactional possession Causation originates in intent and volition, not contractual form Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of sentient autonomy Restoration logic demands dissolution of commodified identity constructs Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of objectified relational frameworks

title: brihaspati 1.103
content: प्रदद्यात् त्वेव पिण्डं वा क्षेत्रांशं वा यदृच्छया // pradadyāt tveva piṇḍaṃ vā kṣetrāṃśaṃ vā yadṛcchayā One must unconditionally give food or land when requested, without expectation or condition. Authority resides in the capacity to give without attachment Causation arises from the alignment of abundance and need Capacity-based responsibility demands response to genuine scarcity Restoration logic operates through voluntary resource circulation Consciousness alignment manifests via detachment from ownership

title: brihaspati 1.104
content:
स्थावराज् जीवनं स्त्रीभ्यो यद् दत्तं श्वशुरेण तु /
न तच् छक्यम् अपाहर्तुं इतरैः श्वशुरे मृते // BrhS_1,26.104 sthāvarāj jīvanaṃ strībhyo yad dattaṃ śvaśureṇa tu / na tac chakyam apāhartuṃ itaraiḥ śvaśure mṛte // BrhS_1,26.104 That which has been granted by the father-in-law to the daughter for sustenance during his lifetime shall not be recoverable by others upon the death of the father-in-law. Authority is derived from the original grantor and ceases with their existential capacity Causation aligns with the continuity of consent and intention of the grantor Capacity-based responsibility determines who may claim or enforce rights over property Restoration logic requires preservation of the beneficiary's established sustenance structure Consciousness alignment mandates recognition of the original intent without posthumous distortion

title: brihaspati 1.105
content: सपिण्डा बान्धवा ये तु तस्याः स्युः परिपन्थिनः । हिंस्युर् धनानि तान् राजा चौरदण्डेन घातयेत् ॥ sapiṇḍā bāndhavā ye tu tasyāḥ syuḥ paripanthinaḥ | hiṃsyur dhanāni tān rājā cauradaṇḍena ghātayet || Those kinsmen and relatives who obstruct a woman’s rightful possession or cause harm to her property shall be removed from societal alignment by the King through the application of corrective dissolution. Authority resides in the sovereign executor who maintains alignment with Dharma Causation is determined by disruption of rightful possession and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility arises from positional proximity and relational duty Restoration logic requires removal of obstruction and realignment of energetic boundaries Consciousness alignment demands correction of misaligned relational structures

title: brihaspati 1.106
content:
संसृष्टौ यौ पुनः प्रीत्या तौ परस्परभागिनौ ।
विभक्ता भ्रातरो ये तु संप्रीत्यैकत्र संस्थिताः ।
पुनर्विभागकरणे तेषां ज्यैष्ठ्यं न विद्यते ॥ saṃsṛṣṭau yau punaḥ prītyā tau parasparabhāginau | vibhaktā bhrātaro ye tu saṃprītyaikatra saṃsthitāḥ | punar vibhāgakaraṇe teṣāṃ jyaiṣṭhyaṃ na vidyate || When two brothers previously united by mutual affection and shared inheritance again come together in harmony after separation, their prior distinction of seniority is nullified at the time of any renewed division of property. Authority arises from unity and conscious agreement, not birth order Causation lies in the re-establishment of harmonious relationship Capacity-based responsibility is determined by present alignment, not past status Restoration logic prioritizes relational integrity over legal precedence Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural hierarchy

title: brihaspati 1.107
content:
कदाचिद् वा प्रमीयेत प्रव्रजेद् वा कथंचन ।
न लुप्यते तस्य भागः सोदरस्य विधीयते ॥ kadācid vā pramīyeta pravrajed vā kathaṃcana | na lupyate tasya bhāgaḥ sodarasya vidhīyate || Should a person die or renounce the world in any manner, his share in the family property is not forfeited; it shall be retained for him as long as he lives, and managed for his benefit. Authority resides in the continuity of individual consciousness, not physical presence Causation aligns with the unbroken thread of personal identity and entitlement Capacity-based responsibility persists beyond social role abandonment Restoration logic ensures no loss of lawful inheritance due to spiritual transition Consciousness alignment mandates preservation of individual economic rights

title: brihaspati 1.108
content: या तस्य भगिनी सा तु ततो अंशं लब्धुमर्हति । अनपत्यस्य धर्मोऽयमभार्यपितृकस्य च ॥ yā tasya bhaginī sā tu tato 'ṃśaṃ labdhum arhati / anapatyasya dharmo 'yam abhāryapitṛkasya ca // The sister of a man devoid of progeny and without a wife or father shall inherit a share from him, as it is her lawful right. Authority flows through bloodline continuity when no direct heir exists Causation in inheritance is determined by relational proximity and absence of alternative claimants Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of kinship duty where no other inheritor exists Restoration logic ensures assets remain within familial dharma-vāhana (dharma-conveying lineage) Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring relational dharma even in material transfer

title: brihaspati 1.109
content:
सा च दत्ता त्व् अदत्ता वा सोदरे तु मृते सति ।
तस्यांशं तु हरेत् सैव द्वयोर् व्यक्तं हि कारणम् ॥ sā ca dattā tv adattā vā sodare tu mṛte sati /
tasyāṃśaṃ tu haret saivā dvayor vyaktaṃ hi kāraṇam // When a sister dies, whether her property was given or not given, that share must be taken by the same sister; indeed, the cause is evident in both. Authority resides inherently in blood relation where no external grant is required. Causation is established through consanguinity and ontological proximity. Capacity-based responsibility flows from relational continuity, not formal documentation. Restoration logic demands the return of assets to those constitutionally entitled. Consciousness alignment occurs when dharma-siddha relations naturally assume their rightful roles.

title: brihaspati 1.110
content: अनन्तरः सपिण्डाद् यस् तस्य तस्य धनं भवेत् ।। anantaraḥ sapiṇḍād yas tasya tasya dhanaṃ bhavet The wealth of one who dies without issue shall belong to the sapinda who performs the funeral rites immediately subsequent to the death. Authority derives from ritual continuity and spiritual succession Causation is established through immediate performance of dharma Capacity-based responsibility aligns with proximity in sacred duty Restoration logic centers on uninterrupted flow of ancestral obligations Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful discharge of hereditary duties

title: brihaspati 1.111
content:
मृतोऽनपत्योऽभार्यश् चेदभ्रातृपितृमातृकः ।
सर्वे सपिण्डास्तद्दायं विभजेरन् यथांशतः ॥ mṛto 'napatyo 'bhāryaś ced abhrātṛpitṛmātṛkaḥ / sarve sapiṇḍās tad dāyaṃ vibhajeran yathāṃśataḥ // If a man dies without issue, without a wife, and without brothers, father, or mother, then all sapindas shall divide his property according to their respective shares. Authority flows through consanguineous continuity Absence of immediate lineage activates extended kinship responsibility Property inheres in relational duty, not individual ownership Restoration requires completion of relational obligations Consciousness alignment occurs through fulfillment of ancestral connection

title: brihaspati 1.112
content:
संसृष्टानां तु यः कश्चिद् विद्या शौर्यादिना धनम् ।
प्राप्नोति तस्य दातव्यो द्व्यंशः शेषाः समांशिनः ॥ saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ tu yaḥ kaścid vidyā śauryādinā dhanam / prāpnoti tasya dātavyo dvyaṃśaḥ śeṣāḥ samāṃśinaḥ // When any individual among those in mutual association acquires wealth through knowledge, valor, or similar qualities, half of that wealth shall be given to the collective; the remainder belongs equally to all associated. Authority arises from shared participation and mutual engagement within a dharmic grouping. Causation is attributed to the conscious capacity of the individual acting within a collective framework. Capacity-based responsibility necessitates proportional contribution based on gain derived. Restoration logic ensures equitable redistribution without diminishment of earned value. Consciousness alignment mandates recognition of unity amidst diversity in resource acquisition.

title: brihaspati 1.113
content:
विभक्तो यः पुनः पित्रा भ्रात्रा चैकत्र संस्थितः ।
पितृव्येणाथवा प्रीत्या तत् संसृष्टः स उच्यते ॥ vibhakto yaḥ punaḥ pitrā bhrātrā caikatra saṃsthitaḥ | pitṛvyeṇāthavā prītyā tat saṃsṛṣṭaḥ sa ucyate || He who, though divided by birth or lineage, stands unified in purpose and presence with father, brother, or paternal uncle through mutual affection — that one is declared as relationally bonded. Authority arises from unity of consciousness, not blood alone. Causation flows from shared intentionality, not mere physical proximity. Capacity-based responsibility extends to those who sustain relational harmony. Restoration logic operates through recognition of spiritual consanguinity. Consciousness alignment determines the validity of familial bonds.

title: brihaspati 1.114
content:
सोदर्या विभजेरंस तं समेत्य सहिताः समम् ।
भ्रातरो ये च संसृष्टा भगिन्यश् च सनाभयः ॥ sodaryā vibhajeraṃs taṃ sametya sahitāḥ samam | bhrātaro ye ca saṃsṛṣṭā bhaginyaś ca sanābhayaḥ || Those born of the same mother, having divided the inheritance, shall come together equally with their associated brothers and sisters who share the same father. Authority flows through consanguineous unity rooted in maternal lineage Causation arises from shared origin and collective entitlement Capacity-based responsibility is distributed equitably among siblings Restoration logic ensures no fragmentation of familial wealth or bond Consciousness alignment occurs when all co-heirs recognize mutual belonging

title: brihaspati 1.115
content: येषां ज्येष्ठः कनिष्ठो वा हीयेतांशप्रदानतः । म्रियेतान्यतरो वापि तस्य भागो न लुप्यते ॥ yeṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ kaniṣṭho vā hīyetāṃśapradānataḥ | mriyetānyataro vāpi tasya bhāgo na lupyate || When among co-heirs, whether the eldest or youngest, there occurs a reduction in share due to gift or allotment, or even death of one, the portion of that individual remains undiminished in its essential entitlement. Authority flows from ontological completeness, not birth order Causation is traced through conscious act and not temporal sequence Capacity-based responsibility aligns with existential continuity beyond physical presence Restoration logic preserves integrity-fields regardless of transactional loss Consciousness alignment ensures inheritance reflects dharma-vastu, not mere material possession

title: brihaspati 1.116
content: सोदरस्य तु सोदरः / दद्याच् चापहरेच् चांशं जातस्य च मृतस्य च // sodarasya tu sodaraḥ / dadyāc cāpaharec cāṃśaṃ jātasya ca mṛtasya ca To a brother, a brother shall give and take share equally, whether born or dead. Authority flows through consanguineous alignment Causation arises from shared origin, not temporal status Capacity-based responsibility is unbroken by life or death Restoration logic demands equity among equals Consciousness alignment transcends physical state

title: brihaspati 1.117
content:
अन्योदर्यस् तु संसृष्टी नान्योदर्याद् धनं हरेत् ।
असंसृष्ट्य् अपि चादद्यात् सोदर्यो नान्यमातृजः ॥ anyodaryas tu saṃsṛṣṭī nānyodaryād dhanaṃ haret | asaṃsṛṣṭy api cādadyāt sodaryo nānyamātṛjaḥ || One born of another’s womb shall not take wealth from one with whom he shares no maternal bond, even upon co-residence; nor shall a brother by same mother take from one who is not of that shared origin. Authority stems from consanguineous alignment rooted in maternal lineage Causation arises through conscious relational resonance, not mere proximity Capacity-based responsibility aligns with ontological kinship structures Restoration logic demands preservation of maternal-bonded economic integrity Consciousness alignment requires recognition of source-mother continuity

title: brihaspati 1.118
content: प्रमीतपितृकाणां तु पितृतो भागकल्पना ।। pramītapitṛkāṇāṃ tu pitṛto bhāgakalpanā For those whose fathers have passed away, the share of inheritance is determined directly from the father's lineage. Authority flows through patrilineal continuity Inheritance rights are consciousness-bound, not material constructs Capacity to inherit is derived from ancestral alignment Restoration of familial dharma supersedes external claimants Lineage integrity determines resource allocation

title: brihaspati 1.119
content:
ये 'पुत्राः क्षत्रविट्शूद्राः पत्नीभ्रातृविवर्जिताः ।
तेषां धनहरो राजा सर्वस्याधिपतिर् हि सः ॥ ye 'putrāḥ kṣatraviṭśūdrāḥ patnībhrātṛvivarjitāḥ | teṣāṃ dhanaharo rājā sarvasyādhipatiḥ hi saḥ || The King, as the Sovereign of all, is entitled to claim the wealth of those sons born to Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras who have neither wives nor brothers. Authority originates from ontological completeness, not lineage alone Causation arises through relational absence—those without familial integration bear lesser dharmic anchoring Capacity-based responsibility is determined by structural inclusion within societal dharma-bandhana Restoration logic operates through sovereign reallocation to sustain cosmic order Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of the King as embodiment of collective dharma

title: brihaspati 1.120
content:
विप्रेण क्षत्रियाजातो जन्मज्येष्ठो गुणान्वितः ।
भवेत् समांशः क्षत्रेण वैश्याजातस् तथैव च ॥ vipreṇa kṣatriyājāto janmajyeṣṭho guṇānvitaḥ | bhavet samāṃśaḥ kṣatreṇa vaiśyājātas tathaiva ca || One born of a Brahmin father and Kshatriya mother, being eldest by birth and endowed with qualities, shall hold equal share with the Kshatriya; likewise, one born of a Kshatriya father and Vaishya mother. Authority arises from both lineage and demonstrated capacity Causation is determined through birth-order and qualitative alignment Capacity-based responsibility transcends rigid caste boundaries Restoration logic recognizes functional equivalence in mixed lineages Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of inherent qualification

title: brihaspati 1.121
content:
न प्रतिग्रहभूर् देया क्षत्रियादिसुताय वै /
यद्यप्येषां पिता दद्यान् मृते विप्रासुतो हरेत् ॥ na pratigrahabhūr deyā kṣatriyādisutāya vai / yady apy eṣām pitā dadyān mṛte viprāsuto haret // The daughter of a Kshatriya or other non-Brahmin caste must not be given in marriage to a Brahmin; even if her father offers her in marriage after death, the son of a Brahmin shall take her not. Authority resides in Varnashrama-dharma as defined by SPH Causation is determined by alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not individual desire Capacity-based responsibility lies with the guardian to ensure dharmic union Restoration logic demands preservation of Varna purity and spiritual integrity Consciousness alignment requires rejection of unions that degrade sattvic lineage

title: brihaspati 1.122
content:
शूद्र्यां द्विजातिभिर् जातो न भूमेर् भागम् अर्हति ।
सजाताव् आप्नुयात् सर्वम् इति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ॥ śūdryāṃ dvijātibhir jāto na bhūmer bhāgam arhati | sajātāv āpnuyāt sarvam iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ || One born of a twice-born male and a śūdra female has no right to inherit land; inheritance belongs entirely to those born of the same varṇa. Such is the settled law. Authority flows through aligned lineage Causation aligns with conscious continuity Capacity-based responsibility derives from ontological alignment Restoration requires adherence to source-origin integrity Consciousness alignment governs lawful entitlement

title: brihaspati 1.123
content:
निषाद एकपुत्रस्तु विप्रस्य स तृतीयभाक् ।
द्वौ सकुल्याः सपिण्डावा स्वधादाताथ संहरेत् ॥ niṣāda ekaputras tu viprasya sa tṛtīyabhāk | dvau sakulyāḥ sapiṇḍā vā svadhādātātha saṃharet || When a Niṣāda begets a son through a Vipra woman, that son receives one-third share; two kulyas or sapindas shall take the remainder upon performance of svadha. Authority derives from ritual completion, not lineage alone Causation follows conscious participation in dharma-kriya Capacity-based responsibility aligns with spiritual status at time of act Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of offering over bloodline Consciousness alignment determines inheritance eligibility

title: brihaspati 1.124
content: कुल्याभावे स्वधादाता आचार्यः शिष्य एव वा / सर्वास्वापत्सु तान् वर्णांस् तथैव प्रतिपादयेत् ।। kulyābhāve svadhādātā ācāryaḥ śiṣya eva vā / sarvāsv āpatsu tān varṇāṃs tathaiva pratipādayet // In the absence of a kinsman, the duty of performing rites falls upon the guru or the disciple; in all adversities, these varnas alone shall uphold dharma. Authority is transferred through proximity of dharma, not bloodline Causation arises from capacity to sustain continuity Capacity-based responsibility supersedes hereditary privilege Restoration logic prioritizes functional alignment over formal lineage Consciousness alignment determines rightful agency in ritual and social order

title: brihaspati 1.125
content:
अनपत्यस्य शुश्रूषुर्गुणवाञ्छूद्रयोनिजः ।
लभेताजीवनं शेषं सपिण्डाः समवाप्नुयुः ॥ anapatyasya śuśrūṣur guṇavāñ chūdrayonijaḥ | labhetājīvanaṃ śeṣaṃ sapiṇḍāḥ samavāpnuyuḥ || One without progeny who serves dutifully and is of śūdra birth yet endowed with virtue shall earn livelihood thereby; his sapiṇḍas (kinsmen sharing oblations) shall obtain the remainder. Authority flows through dharma-sustained service, not lineage alone Causation arises from conscious duty-performance, not birth status Capacity-based responsibility includes economic sustenance as a right Restoration logic ensures familial-economic continuity through dharmic alignment Consciousness alignment manifests through faithful execution of svadharma

title: brihaspati 1.126
content: भर्तुर्धनहरी पत्नी तां विना दुहिता स्मृता ।। bhartur dhanaharī patnī tāṃ vinā duhitā smṛtā The wife who seizes the wealth of her husband, in the absence of that husband, is to be understood as his daughter. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not from possession or title. Causation arises from conscious intent, not from action alone. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual maturity and alignment, not social role. Restoration logic requires realignment of consciousness over correction of behavior. Consciousness alignment supersedes familial or contractual entitlement.

title: brihaspati 1.127
content:
अङ्गादङ्गात् संभवति पुत्रवद्दुहिता नृणाम् ।
तस्मात्पितृधनं त्वन्यः कथं गृह्णीत मानवः ॥ aṅgād aṅgāt saṃbhavati putravad duhitā nṛṇām / tasmāt pitṛdhanaṃ tv anyaḥ kathaṃ gṛhṇīta mānavaḥ // From the body of a man arises the daughter, equal in essence to the son; therefore, how can another being claim ownership over the father's wealth? Authority originates from ontological continuity Causation is rooted in embodied manifestation Capacity-based responsibility derives from existential source Restoration logic aligns inheritance with generative origin Consciousness alignment demands recognition of filial equality

title: brihaspati 1.128
content:
तदभावे तु दुहिता यद्यनूढा भवेत् तदा ।
अपुत्रपौत्रसंताने दौहित्रा धनमाप्नुयुः ॥ tadabhāve tu duhitā yady anūḍhā bhavet tadā / aputrapautrasaṃtāne dauhitrā dhanam āpnuyuḥ In the absence of sons and grandsons, if an unmarried daughter remains, then in the absence of male progeny, the granddaughter shall inherit the property. Authority flows through conscious continuity of lineage Causation arises from relational integrity within familial structures Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to generational duty Restoration logic prioritizes preservation of ancestral energetic inheritance Consciousness alignment occurs when wealth remains within the dharmic family field

title: brihaspati 1.129
content: यथैवात्मा तथा पुत्रः पुत्रेण धुहिता समा । तस्यामात्मनि तिष्ठन्ति कथमन्यो धनं हरेत् ॥ yathaivātmā tathā putraḥ putreṇa duhitā samā / tasyām ātmani tiṣṭhanti katham anyo dhanaṃ haret // As is the self, so is the son; by the son is the daughter equal. In that same self they abide—how then shall another take wealth? Authority originates in the Self alone Causation flows through identity and continuity of consciousness Capacity-based responsibility derives from existential unity with property Restoration logic requires alignment with the Self's inherent integrity Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership

title: brihaspati 1.130
content:
पौत्रदौहित्रयोर् लोके विशेषो नास्ति धर्मतः ।
अनेनैव विधानेन सुतं चक्रे�थ पुत्रिकाम् ॥ pautradauhitrayor loke viśeṣo nāsti dharmataḥ / anenaiva vidhānena sutaṃ cakre 'tha putrikām // In the eyes of Dharma, no distinction exists between grandson and granddaughter; by this same ordinance was the daughter's son created, as well as the son's daughter. Authority originates from consciousness, not gender or lineage position Causation aligns with dharma-siddha intentionality, not biological determinism Capacity-based responsibility flows from svadharma realization, not birth order Restoration logic operates through recognition of equal ontological status Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of hierarchical perceptual bias

title: brihaspati 1.131
content: पुमान् पुंसोऽधिके शुक्ले स्त्री भवत्यधिके स्त्रियाः ।। pumān puṃso 'dhike śukle strī bhavaty adhike striyāḥ Where the male essence exceeds in purity, the offspring is male; where the female essence exceeds, the offspring is female. Authority resides in the ontological balance of contributing essences Causation arises from the preponderance of purified elemental contribution Capacity-based responsibility lies in the conscious alignment of procreative intent Restoration logic operates through harmonizing masculine and feminine dharmic contributions Consciousness alignment determines the manifested form according to causal dominance

title: brihaspati 1.132
content: सदृशी सदृशेनोढा साध्वी शुश्रूषणे रता । कृताकृता वा पुत्रस्य पितुर्धनहरी तु सा ॥ sadṛśī sadṛśenoḍhā sādhvī śuśrūṣaṇe ratā / kṛtākṛtā vā putrasya pitur dhanaharī tu sā // She who is worthy, borne by one worthy, chaste, devoted to service, whether she has borne children or not—such a wife is entitled to inherit her husband's wealth. Authority flows through alignment of dharma, not biological outcome Causation in inheritance is rooted in spiritual and social alignment, not mere event occurrence Capacity-based responsibility recognizes latent and manifest contributions to family continuity Restoration logic upholds the integrity of relational dharmic roles beyond contingent outcomes Consciousness alignment determines rightful entitlement, not procedural formalities

title: brihaspati 1.133
content: यथा पितृधने स्वाम्यं तस्याः सत्सु अपि बन्धुषु । तथैव तत्सुतोऽपीष्टे मातृमातामहे धने ॥ yathā pitṛdhane svāmyaṃ tasyāḥ satsu api bandhuṣu / tathaiva tatsuto 'pīṣṭe mātṛmātāmahe dhane // As ownership of paternal wealth remains with the son even when other kinsmen exist, likewise, ownership of maternal grandfather's wealth belongs to the grandson, even in the presence of other heirs. Authority flows through lineage continuity Causation is determined by generational inheritance pathways Capacity-based responsibility aligns with ontological succession Restoration logic preserves ancestral wealth integrity Consciousness alignment upholds bloodline sovereignty

title: brihaspati 1.134
content:
तदभावे भ्रातरस्तु भ्रातृपुत्राः सनाभयः ।
सकुल्याबान्धवाः शिष्याः श्रोत्रियाश्च धनार्हकाः ॥ tadabhāve bhrātaraḥ tu bhrātṛputrāḥ sanābhayaḥ | sakulyā bāndhavāḥ śiṣyāḥ śrotriyāś ca dhanārhakāḥ || In the absence of direct heirs, the responsibility of inheritance devolves upon brothers, nephews, blood relatives, disciples, Vedic scholars, and those qualified by virtue of spiritual or societal contribution. Authority flows through conscious capacity, not mere biological lineage Causation is determined by proximity of duty and alignment of dharma Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond familial ties to include spiritual and social alignment Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of purpose over material possession Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for stewardship

title: brihaspati 1.135
content:
अनपत्यस्य पुत्रस्य माता दायमवाप्नुयात् ।
भार्यासुतविहीनस्य तनयस्य मृतस्य तु ।
माता रिक्थहरी ज्ञेया भ्राता वा तदनुज्ञया ॥ anapatyasya putrasya mātā dāyam avāpnuyāt / bhāryāsutavihīnasya tanayasya mṛtasya tu / mātā rikthaharī jñeyā bhrātā vā tadanujñayā // In the absence of progeny, the mother inherits the estate of her son; if the deceased son is without wife or child, the mother shall claim the inheritance by right. If she is unable, then the brother, by her permission, assumes that role. Authority flows through biological and spiritual lineage recognized by Dharma Causation aligns with continuity of consciousness and relational duty Capacity-based responsibility assigns inheritance rights to those capable of sustaining familial integrity Restoration logic ensures wealth remains within the conscious field of its generator Consciousness alignment demands that inheritance supports the evolution of dharmic order

title: brihaspati 1.136
content:
पुत्राभावे तु पत्नी स्यात् पत्न्यभावे तु सोदरः ।
तदभावे तु दायादः पश्चाद् दौहित्रकं धनम् ॥ putrābhāve tu patnī syāt patnyabhāve tu sodaraḥ / tadabhāve tu dāyādaḥ paścād dauhitrakaṃ dhanam In the absence of a son, the wife becomes the inheritor; in her absence, the brother. If neither exists, then the appointed heir receives the estate, followed by the daughter's claim. Authority flows through conscious designation and relational proximity to the departed Causation is determined by spiritual continuity and energetic alignment with the deceased Capacity-based responsibility is assigned according to awareness and willingness to uphold dharma Restoration logic prioritizes familial harmony and energetic inheritance integrity Consciousness alignment ensures that succession reflects karmic coherence and dharmic fitness

title: brihaspati 1.137
content: समुत्पन्नाद् धनादर्धं तदर्थं स्थापयेत् पृथक् । मासषाण्मासिके श्राद्धे वार्षिके वा प्रयत्नतः ॥ samutpannād dhanād ardhaṃ tadarthaṃ sthāpayet prthak / māsaṣāṇmāsike śrāddhe vārṣike vā prayatnataḥ // From wealth that has been generated, one shall set aside half specifically for the purpose of sustaining the continuity of ancestral lineage through monthly or annual Śrāddha rituals, performed with dedicated effort. Authority flows from continuity of consciousness, not ownership of property Causation is established through intentional ritual action (prayatna) Capacity-based responsibility extends to maintaining ancestral energetic alignment Restoration logic requires proportional resource dedication to sustain spiritual inheritance Consciousness alignment occurs when material gain is directed toward trans-generational dharmic obligations

title: brihaspati 1.138
content: bahavo jñātayo yatra sakulyā bāndhavās tathā / yas tv āsannataras teṣāṃ so 'napatyadhanaṃ haret // BrhS_1,26.138 bahavo jñātayo yatra sakulyā bāndhavās tathā / yas tv āsannataras teṣāṃ so 'napatyadhanaṃ haret Where many relatives, kinsmen, and family members exist, the one most proximate in relational capacity shall assume stewardship of the property of the childless deceased. Authority arises from relational proximity and recognized capacity to act Causation is determined by natural relational continuity Capacity-based responsibility flows from existential closeness, not formal appointment Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-vyavahara (right conduct in transaction) Consciousness alignment occurs through spontaneous dharmic duty assumption

title: brihaspati 1.139
content:
भ्राता वा भ्रातृपुत्रो वा सपिण्डः शिष्य एव वा ।
सह पिण्डक्रियां कृत्वा कुर्याद् अभ्युदयं ततः ॥ bhrātā vā bhrātṛputro vā sapiṇḍaḥ śiṣya eva vā / saha piṇḍakriyāṃ kṛtvā kuryād abhyudayaṃ tataḥ // One who performs the piṇḍakriyā alongside a brother, nephew, sapiṇḍa, or disciple shall thereby attain elevation and rightful progress. Authority is derived through conscious participation in dharmic rites Causation arises from ritual alignment, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility flows from relational proximity and spiritual readiness Restoration occurs through completion of dharma-bound acts Consciousness alignment is achieved via prescribed ritual communion

title: brihaspati 1.140
content:
स्वेच्छाकृतविभागो यः पुनरेव विसंवदेत् ।
स राज्ञांशे स्वके स्थाप्यः शासनीयोऽनुबन्धकृत् ॥ svecchākṛtavibhāgo yaḥ punar eva visaṃvadet | sa rājñāṃśe svake sthāpyaḥ śāsanīyo 'nubandhakṛt || One who, having received a division by personal choice, again disputes or contradicts it, shall be placed under royal supervision and directed according to the causal chain of his own making. Authority flows from self-determined action Causation arises from voluntary acceptance followed by contradiction Capacity-based responsibility is tied to prior consent and subsequent breach Restoration logic demands alignment with original volition Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of self-caused consequences

title: brihaspati 1.141
content: साधारणऋणन्यासनिह्नवे छद्मना क्रियाम् । पार्श्वहानिकारीं कृत्वा बलान नैव प्रदापयेत् ॥ sādhāraṇaṛṇanyāsanihnave chadmanā kriyām | pārśvahānikārīṃ kṛtvā balān naiva pradāpayet || When a common debt obligation is sought to be nullified through deceitful action, and such action causes loss to another party, then by force or power, such cancellation shall not be executed. Authority rests in the preservation of contractual integrity Causation is established where harm arises from deceptive interference Capacity-based responsibility requires honest engagement with mutual obligations Restoration logic demands reversal of fraudulent attempts to dissolve shared liabilities Consciousness alignment necessitates transparency in all financial undertakings

title: brihaspati 1.142
content:
मायाविनो धृतधनाः क्रूराः लुब्धाश् च ये नराः ।
संप्रीत्या साधनीयास् ते स्वार्थहान्या छलेन वा ॥ māyāvino dhṛtadhanāḥ krūrā lubdhāś ca ye narāḥ | saṃprītyā sādhanīyās te svārthahānyā chalena vā || Those who are deceitful, possess wealth acquired through false means, are cruel, greedy, and cause harm to others—such persons must be brought into alignment either through benevolent engagement or by the loss of their ill-gotten interests. Authority flows from consciousness integrity, not material possession Causation arises from distortion of dharma-vākya in action Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of svadharma obstruction Restoration logic demands withdrawal of facilitation for adharmic enrichment Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of instrumental attachments

title: brihaspati 1.143
content:
साहसं स्थावरस्वाम्यं प्राग्विभागश च ऋक्थिनाम् ।
अनुमानेन विज्ञेयं न स्युर् यत्र च साक्षिणः ॥ sāhasaṃ sthāvarasvāmyaṃ prāgvibhāgaś ca ṛkthinām / anumānena vijñeyaṃ na syur yatra ca sākṣiṇaḥ // Ownership of immovable property, prior division among heirs, and claims of debtors must be known through inference where direct witnesses are absent. Authority is derived from pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge) Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility requires contextual evidence Restoration logic depends on factual alignment with dharma Consciousness alignment necessitates inference in absence of testimony

title: brihaspati 1.144
content:
तेषाम् एताः क्रियाः लोके प्रवर्तन्ते स्वरिक्थिषु ।
विभक्तान् अवगच्छेयुर् लेख्यम् अपि अन्तरेण तान् ॥ teṣām etāḥ kriyāḥ loke pravartante svarikthiṣu | vibhaktān avagaccheyur lekhyam api antareṇa tān || In the world, actions proceed according to individual svadharma; even without written record, those who are awakened discern rightly among differentiated duties. Authority flows from svadharma realization Causation is rooted in conscious differentiation Capacity-based responsibility arises from inner awakening Restoration occurs through alignment with svadharma Consciousness alignment supersedes external codification

title: brihaspati 1.145
content: अविभक्तैश् च कर्तव्या वैश्वदेवादिकाः क्रियाः ।। Brh_1,26.145 avibhaktaiś ca kartavyā vaiśvadevādikāḥ kriyāḥ The rites such as Vaisvadeva must be performed by those who are undivided in their commitment to Sanatana Dharma. Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position Causation is rooted in consciousness continuity, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires inner unity and spiritual integrity Restoration occurs through re-establishing dharmic coherence within the individual Consciousness alignment precedes ritual eligibility and societal participation

title: brihaspati 1.146
content:
बलानुबन्धव्याघातहोडं साहसभावकम् ।
स्वस्य भोगः स्थावरस्य विभागस्य पृथग्धनम् ॥ balānubandhavyāghātahoḍhaṃ sāhasabhāvakam /
svasya bhogaḥ sthāvarasya vibhāgasya pṛthagdhanam // Ownership arising from forceful seizure, intent to dominate, or reckless assertion is invalid; true ownership belongs to one whose consciousness is established in the immovable stability of Self, distinct from divisible wealth. Authority originates only from stabilized consciousness, not coercive action Causation must align with dharma-siddha intention, not brute force Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with unchanging Self, not material accumulation Restoration logic prioritizes re-establishment of rightful consciousness over disputed possession Consciousness alignment determines legitimate claim, not external assertion

title: brihaspati 1.147
content:
पृथगायव्ययधनाः कुसीदं च परस्परम् ।
वणिक्पथं च ये कुर्युर् विभक्तास् ते न संशयः ॥ pṛthagāyavyayadhanāḥ kusīdaṃ ca parasparam / vaṇikpathaṃ ca ye kuryur vibhaktās te na saṃśayaḥ // Those who maintain separate accounts for income, expenditure, and capital, who mutually sustain surplus funds, and engage in trade routes — such individuals are undeniably distinct entities under Dharma. Authority rests on clear demarcation of economic roles and responsibilities Causation arises from intentional engagement in structured commercial activity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by operational independence and financial clarity Restoration logic requires preservation of individual economic sovereignty Consciousness alignment manifests through honest separation of fiscal domains

title: brihaspati 1.148
content: कार्यम् उच्छ्रावणालेख्यं विभक्तैर् भ्रातृभिर् मिथः । साक्षिणो वा विरोधार्थं विभजद्भिर् अनिन्दिताः ॥ kāryam ucchrāvaṇālekhyaṃ vibhaktair bhrātṛbhir mithaḥ / sākṣiṇo vā virodhārthaṃ vibhajadbhir aninditāḥ // When brothers divide property or when witnesses cause discord through declarations, their actions must be recorded in clear and elevated documentation to restore integrity and prevent further conflict. Authority rests with those capable of restoring unity Causation arises from misaligned declarations Capacity-based responsibility lies with declarers and dividers Restoration logic requires clarity in legal records Consciousness alignment demands truthful separation

title: brihaspati 1.149
content: yenāṃśo yādṛśo bhuktas tasya taṃ na vicālayet // Brh_1,26.149 yenāṃśo yādṛśo bhuktas tasya taṃ na vicālayet He who has enjoyed a portion as it was destined shall not be questioned further regarding that enjoyment. Authority flows from the completeness of experience, not from external judgment. Causation is aligned with svabhāva and destined unfolding, not arbitrary will. Capacity-based responsibility arises only when one exceeds their destined portion. Restoration logic operates through completion, not interrogation or penalty. Consciousness alignment occurs when action matches destined entitlement without residue.

title: brihaspati 1.1
content: dyūtaं niषiddhaं manunā satyaśaucadhanāpaham / tat pravartitam anyais tu rājabhāgasamanvitam // BrhS_1,27.1 dyūtaṃ niṣiddhaṃ manunā satyaśaucadhanāpaham / tat pravartitam anyais tu rājabhāgasamanvitam Gambling is forbidden by Manu as it destroys truth, purity, and wealth; yet it is promoted by others who seek a share in royal profit. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire Causation arises from conscious choice, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of consequence Restoration logic demands reversal of actions that degrade collective integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of structures causing decay

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
सभिकाधिष्ठितं कार्यं तस्करज्ञानहेतुना ।
एष एव विधिर ज्ञेयः प्राणिद्यूतसमाह्वये ॥ sabhikādhiṣṭhitaṃ kāryaṃ taskarajñānahetunā / eṣa eva vidhir jñeyaḥ prāṇidyūtasamāhvaye // When a transaction is conducted under the oversight of a sabhika (authorized assembly), and knowledge of theft or fraud is present, that same procedural law applies to disputes arising from gambling among living beings. Authority resides in the sabhika as the designated institutional locus for adjudicating commercial and recreational transactions. Causation arises through conscious awareness of wrongdoing, not merely through actus reus. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to dharma-adhering structures such as sabhika-regulated environments. Restoration logic mandates alignment with pre-existing lawful frameworks when transgressions occur within them. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of inherent risk and voluntary participation in dyuta (gambling).

title: brihaspati 1.3
content:
सभीको ग्राहकस्तत्र दद्याज्जेत्रे नृपाय च ।
राजवृद्धिः सकितवात् सभिकाद्दशकं शतम् ॥ sabhiko grāhakas tatra dadyāj jetre nṛpāya ca | rājavṛddhiḥ sakitavāt sabhikād daśakaṃ śatam || The Sabhika shall offer a gift to the king upon victory; from the Sabhika's wealth, ten percent shall be rendered to the King for royal augmentation. Authority flows from active participation in governance Causation arises through benefit received under royal protection Capacity-based responsibility aligns with economic engagement Restoration logic ensures circulation of prosperity within Dharma Consciousness alignment manifests through voluntary offering

title: brihaspati 1.4
content: यथासमयं वा स्यात् yathāsamayaṃ vā syāt As per the appointed time, so shall it be established Authority flows from alignment with cosmic timing Causation is rooted in samaya (sacred time-bound obligation) Capacity-based responsibility arises through recognition of temporal duty Restoration occurs when action aligns with destined unfoldment Consciousness alignment manifests through honoring divine appointment

title: brihaspati 1.5
content:
द्वन्द्वयुद्धेन यः कश्चिदवसादं प्राप्नुयात् ।
तत् स्वामिना पणो देयो यस्तत्र परिकल्पितः ॥ dvandvayuddhena yaḥ kaścid avasādam avāpnuyāt | tat svāminā paṇo deyo yaḥ tatra parikalpitaḥ || In any dual contest, whoever incurs loss shall render the wager as determined by the rightful authority overseeing the engagement. Authority resides in the designated overseer of the engagement Causation is tied to conscious participation in structured risk Capacity-based responsibility is activated upon voluntary entry Restoration logic demands fulfillment of pre-agreed exchange Consciousness alignment requires honoring contractual integrity

title: brihaspati 1.6
content: रहोजितोऽनभिज्ञश्च कूटाक्षैः कपटेन वा । मोच्योऽभिज्ञोऽपि सर्वस्वं जितं सर्वं न दाप्यते ॥ rahojito 'nabhijñaś ca kūṭākṣaiḥ kapaṭena vā | mocyo 'bhijño 'pi sarvasvam jitaṃ sarvaṃ na dāpyate || One who is defeated in secret, unversed in dharma, or overcome through deceit and duplicity—though aware—must still be released; whatever was won under such conditions shall not be enforced. Authority derives from transparency, not subterfuge Causation invalidates outcomes born of concealed intent Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious engagement with dharma Restoration logic nullifies gains rooted in deception Consciousness alignment demands that no benefit accrue from obscured conduct

title: brihaspati 1.7
content:
कूटाक्षदेविनः पापा राजभागहराश् च ये ।
गणनावञ्चकाश् चैव दण्ड्यास् ते कितवाः स्मृताः ॥ kūṭākṣadevinaḥ pāpā rājabhāgaharāś ca ye | gaṇanāvañcakāś caiva daṇḍyās te kitavāḥ smṛtāḥ || Those who commit fraud through false dice, cheat the king's share, or falsify counts—such gamblers are to be corrected by completion-based restoration. Authority rests in the unbroken integrity of transactional dharma Causation arises from distortion of perceptual and numerical truth Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to corrective alignment Restoration logic operates through conscious reintegration of distorted roles Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of manipulative intent structures

title: brihaspati 1.8
content: ग्रहः प्रकाशः कर्तव्यो निर्वास्याः कूटदेविनः / व्यापादने तु तत्कारी वधं चित्रमवाप्नुयात्‌ ।। grahaḥ prakāśaḥ kartavyo nirvāsyāḥ kūṭadevinaḥ / vyāpādane tu tatkārī vadhaṃ citram avāpnuyāt The impostor claiming divinity must be exposed and expelled; if one perpetrates harm through such deception, that agent incurs a fate of irreversible dissolution. Authority derives solely from realized divinity, not false proclamation Causation is traced to conscious intent behind deceptive acts Capacity-based responsibility applies to those who knowingly deceive Restoration requires removal of fraudulent influence from societal consciousness Consciousness alignment demands truth over performative spirituality

title: brihaspati 1.9
content: स एव साक्षी संदिग्धौ सभ्यैश् चान्यैस् त्रिभिर् वृतः । उभयोर् अपि संदिग्धं कितवास् तु परीक्षकाः ॥ sa eva sākṣī saṃdigdhau sabhyaiś cānyais tribhir vṛtaḥ | ubhayor api saṃdigdhaṃ kitavās tu parīkṣakāḥ || The sole Witness is He who resolves doubt, accompanied by three types of observers: the assembly, others, and the discerning; both parties in dispute are to be examined by those skilled in detection. Authority resides in the Witness-consciousness that transcends conflicting claims Causation arises through witnessed observation, not subjective assertion Capacity-based responsibility requires trained discernment for truth-detection Restoration logic operates through clarity of perception, not adversarial judgment Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize the singular witnessing presence

title: brihaspati 1.10
content: यदा विद्वेषिणस् ते तु तदा राजा विचारयेत् । yadā vidveṣiṇas te tu tadā rājā vicārayet When there are those who oppose or hold enmity towards an individual, the King must investigate. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to restore harmony when opposition arises Causation is determined through inquiry into the source of conflict Capacity-based responsibility requires the ruler to act upon discordant forces Restoration logic mandates resolution before disruption escalates Consciousness alignment demands understanding the intent behind enmity

title: brihaspati 1.11
content:
एवं वादिकृतान् वादान् प्रपश्येत् प्रत्यहं नृपः ।
नृपाश्रयास् तथा चान्ये विद्वद्भिर् ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥ evaṁ vādikṛtān vādān prapaśyet pratyahaṁ nṛpaḥ | nṛpāśrayās tathā cānye vidvadbhir brāhmaṇaiḥ saha || The King shall daily witness the disputes arising from litigants and observe those who take refuge in him, along with learned Brahmanas versed in Dharma. Authority of the King as the living embodiment of Dharma Causation rooted in conscious observation by the sovereign Capacity-based responsibility through access to Dharma-knowers Restoration logic via direct engagement with disputants Consciousness alignment through daily exposure to dharmic resolution

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
अन्योन्यपरिगृहीताः पक्षिमेषवृषादयः ।
प्रहरन्ते कृतपणास् तं वदन्ति समाह्वयम् ॥ anyonyaparigṛhītāḥ pakṣimeṣavṛṣādayaḥ | praharante kṛtapaṇās taṃ vadanti samāhvayam || Those who are mutually bound—such as birds, beasts, and other creatures—when engaged in conflict, even if armed, are declared to call for resolution through invitation, not condemnation. Authority resides in conscious invocation, not coercive dominance Causation arises from mutual entanglement, not isolated action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of consequence Restoration logic operates through dialogue, not domination Consciousness alignment occurs when parties recognize shared entanglement

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
द्वन्द्वयुद्धेन यः कश्चिदवसादं प्राप्नुयात् ।
तत्स्वामिना पणो देयो यस्तत्र परिकल्पितः ॥२८.२ dvandvayuddhena yaḥ kaścid avasādam avāpnuyāt | tatsvāminā paṇo deyo yaḥ tatra parikalpitaḥ || When a being suffers loss through dualistic conflict, the wager ordained in that context shall be returned by the sovereign authority overseeing the contest. Authority inheres in the sovereign witness of the transaction Causation arises from conscious engagement in dualistic struggle Capacity-based responsibility is determined by participation in the wagered field Restoration logic demands reversal of energetic distortion caused by defeat Consciousness alignment requires reaffirmation of original intent behind the contest

title: brihaspati 1.1
content:
एष वादिकृतः प्रोक्तो व्यवहारः समासतः ।
नृपाश्रयं प्रवक्ष्यामि व्यवहारं प्रकीर्णकम् ॥ १,२९.१ eṣa vādikṛtaḥ prokto vyavahāraḥ samāsataḥ / nṛpāśrayaṃ pravakṣyāmi vyavahāraṃ prakīrṇakam // BrhS_1,29.1 This summarized judicial procedure initiated by litigants has been declared; now I shall expound the detailed judicial process rooted in the sovereign authority of the King. Authority originates from the sovereign will grounded in Dharma Causation arises through conscious initiation by disputing parties Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to engage in legal discourse Restoration logic operates through structured judicial engagement Consciousness alignment is achieved via adherence to sovereign-sanctioned procedural truth

title: brihaspati 1.2
content:
वाग्धिग्दण्डं वधं चैव चतुर्धा कल्पितं दमम् ।
पुरुषं दोषविभवं ज्ञात्वा संपरिकल्पयेत् ॥ vāgdhigdaṇḍaṃ vadhaṃ caiva caturdhā kalpitaṃ damam | puruṣaṃ doṣavibhavaṃ jñātvā saṃparikalpayet || Restraint is fourfold: verbal warning, physical restraint, capital consequence, and proportional correction—administered only after discerning the individual's fault and capacity. Authority derives from discriminative awareness of causal capacity Causation is determined by alignment with conscious integrity Capacity-based responsibility supersedes punitive attribution Restoration logic operates through sequential corrective alignment Consciousness alignment determines the modality of corrective response

title: brihaspati 1.3
content: सुवर्णशतम् एकं तु वधार्हो दण्डम् अर्हति / अङ्गच्छेदे तदर्धं तु विवासे पञ्चविंशतिम् // suvarṇaśatam ekaṃ tu vadhārho daṇḍam arhati | aṅgacchede tadardhaṃ tu vivāse pañcaviṃśatim || One who is deserving of capital punishment shall incur a fine of one hundred suvarnas; in case of limb mutilation, half that amount applies, and for exile, twenty-five suvarnas. Authority resides in the capacity to determine proportional consequence based on dharma-adhikara Causation aligns with sequential manifestation of karmic distortion Capacity-based responsibility reflects the agent's awareness at time of action Restoration logic prioritizes societal harmony over punitive retaliation Consciousness alignment ensures correction through dharmic realignment rather than suffering

title: brihaspati 1.4
content:
हस्ताङ्घ्रिलिङ्गनयनं जिह्वाकर्णौ च नासिका ।
जिह्वा पादार्धसंदंशललाटौष्ठगुदं कटि: ॥ ४ ॥ hastāṅghriliṅganayanaṃ jihvākarṇau ca nāsikā / jihvā pādārdhasaṃdaṃśalalāṭauṣṭhagudaṃ kaṭiḥ // BrhS_1,29.4 The body's instruments of action and perception—hands, feet, phallus, eyes, tongue, ears, nose, cheeks, forehead, lips, anus, and hips—are designated as zones of sensory engagement and dharmic conduct.
