Capacity-based responsibility: One who engages in consciousness-disturbing acts assumes responsibility for realigning their perceptual field. Restoration logic: Misuse of sensory instruments requires purification through intentional stillness and recalibration. Consciousness alignment: True capacity arises when sensory engagement supports rather than obscures dharma.

title: manu 2.179
content:
द्यूतं च जनवादं च परिवादं तथाऽनृतम् ।
स्त्रीणां च प्रेक्षणालम्भमुपघातं परस्य च ॥ २.१७९॥ आलम्भाऽवघातं dyūtaṃ ca janavādaṃ ca parivādaṃ tathā'nṛtam |
strīṇāṃ ca prekṣaṇālambhamupaghātaṃ parasya ca || 2.179|| ālambhā'vaghātaṃ Gambling, public defamation, private slander, falsehood, improper gazing upon women, physical contact without consent, and causing harm to another — all such acts disrupt consciousness integrity and social dharma. Authority: Only the realized Self possesses true agency; apparent violations stem from misidentification. Causation: Actions arise from unexamined desire and ignorance of Self-nature; root cause lies in disconnected consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility: Responsibility is assigned based on the actor's capacity for self-awareness and alignment with Dharma. Restoration logic: The purpose of addressing misconduct is to restore the actor’s innate alignment with Satya-Dharma. Consciousness alignment: All jurisprudence must serve the awakening of unity-consciousness, not fragmentation.

title: manu 2.180
content:
एकः शयीत सर्वत्र न रेतः स्कन्दयेत्क्व चित् ।
कामाधि स्कन्दयन् रेतो हिनस्ति व्रतमात्मनः ॥ २.१८०॥ ekaḥ śayīta sarvatra na retaḥ skandayet kvacit |
kāmādhi skandayan reto hinasti vratam ātmanaḥ || 2.180 || One must remain wakeful in all places; nowhere should semen be discharged intentionally. Discharging semen through lustful intent breaches one's vow to oneself. Authority flows from self-sovereignty and internal discipline Causation arises from conscious choice, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over sensory impulses Restoration logic centers on reintegration with one’s inherent dharma-vow Consciousness alignment demands vigilant awareness in all states

title: manu 2.181
content:
स्वप्ने सिक्त्वा ब्रह्मचारी द्विजः शुक्रमकामतः ।
स्नात्वाऽर्कमर्चयित्वा त्रिः पुनर्मामित्यृचं जपेत् ॥ २.१८१॥ svapne siktva brahmacārī dvijaḥ śukramakāmataḥ |
snātvā'rkamarcayitvā triḥ punarmāmityṛcaṃ japet || When a twice-born celibate discharges seminal fluid involuntarily during sleep, he shall bathe, worship the Sun, and thrice recite the mantra 'punarmām'. Authority: The twice-born individual holds inherent spiritual capacity under Vedic discipline. Causation: Involuntary emission does not incur moral fault; natural physiological process is acknowledged. Capacity-based responsibility: Restitution lies in conscious realignment through ritual purification. Restoration logic: Ritual and repetition restore energetic integrity disrupted by involuntary discharge. Consciousness alignment: Invocation of solar energy realigns consciousness with disciplined intent.

title: manu 2.182
content:
उदकुम्भं सुमनसो गोशकृत्मृत्तिकाकुशान् ।
आहरेद्यावदर्थानि भैक्षं चाहरहश्चरेत् ॥ २.१८२॥ udakumbhaṃ sumanaso gośakṛt-mṛttikā-kuśān .
āhared-yāvad-arthāni bhaikṣaṃ cāhara-haścaret .. One shall collect water-pot, flowers, cow-dung, clay, and kuśa grass according to necessity; likewise, one shall gather almsfood while moving about. Authority flows from alignment with dharma-sustaining practices Causation arises through intentional engagement in dharmic livelihood Capacity-based responsibility is defined by the ability to sustain dharma through action Restoration logic operates through the fulfillment of svadharma as collective duty Consciousness alignment manifests via disciplined adherence to ritual and material sufficiency

title: manu 2.183
content: वेदयज्ञैरहीनानां प्रशस्तानां स्वकर्मसु । ब्रह्मचार्याहरेद्भैक्षं गृहेभ्यः प्रयतोऽन्वहम् ॥ २.१८३॥ vedayajñairahīnānāṁ praśastānāṁ svakarmasu | brahmacāryāharedbhikṣaṁ gṛhebhyaḥ prayato'nvaham || 2.183|| Those who are without Vedic sacrifices yet engaged in rightful duties shall receive sustenance through disciplined seeking by a celibate student from households daily. Authority originates from alignment with dharma, not ritual performance alone Causation is established through conscious participation in prescribed action Capacity-based responsibility arises from internal discipline, not external status Restoration logic ensures sustenance flows to those aligned with dharmic order Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal support

title: manu 2.184
content:
गुरोः कुले न भिक्षेत न ज्ञातिकुलबन्धुषु ।
अलाभे त्वन्यगेहानां पूर्वं पूर्वं विवर्जयेत् ॥ २.१८४॥ guroḥ kule na bhikṣeta na jñātikulabandhuṣu |
alābhe tvanyagehānāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ vivarjayet || 2.184|| One must not seek alms within the household of one's guru or among relatives and kin; when there is scarcity, one must progressively renounce dependence on external households. Authority: The guru's domain is sacrosanct and beyond transactional dependency. Causation: Almsgiving and receiving are structured by relational integrity and spiritual hierarchy. Capacity-based responsibility: Renunciation of dependence reflects internal capacity cultivation. Restoration logic: Sequential relinquishment aligns with progressive self-reliance. Consciousness alignment: Spiritual maturity manifests through non-exploitation of sacred relationships.

title: manu 2.185
content:
सर्वं वापि चरेद्ग्रामं पूर्वौक्तानामसम्भवे ।
नियम्य प्रयतो वाचमभिशस्तांस्तु वर्जयेत् ॥ २.१८५॥ sarvaṃ vāpi caredgrāmaṃ pūrvoktānāmasambhave |
niyamya prayato vācamabhiśastāṃstu varjayet || 2.185|| In the absence of prior-established injunctions, one shall conduct oneself through the entire village while restraining speech that defames others. Authority originates from the capacity to sustain harmony within collective consciousness. Causation is determined by alignment with Dharma-prescribed conduct in the absence of explicit command. Capacity-based responsibility requires active restraint where no direct instruction applies. Restoration logic operates through omission of harmful speech and maintenance of communal integrity. Consciousness alignment necessitates self-regulation in undefined behavioral domains.

title: manu 2.186
content:
दूरादाहृत्य समिधः सन्निदध्याद्विहायसि ।
सायं।प्रातश्च जुहुयात्ताभिरग्निमतन्द्रितः ॥ २.१८६॥ dūrādāhṛtya samidhaḥ sannidadhyād vihāyasi |
sāyaṁ prātaś ca juhuyāt tābhir agnim atandritaḥ || One must collect fuel from a distance, arrange it near the altar, and offer it without delay in the evening and morning—this is the discipline of maintaining sacred fire. Authority: The injunction derives directly from SPH as the eternal source of Dharma. Causation: Proper ritual action ensures continuity of divine order. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual must possess both physical and spiritual capacity to perform Agnihotra. Restoration logic: Regular offerings restore balance between human life and cosmic rhythm. Consciousness alignment: Daily discipline aligns individual consciousness with universal Dharma.

title: manu 2.187
content:
अकृत्वा भैक्षचरणमसमिध्य च पावकम् ।
अनातुरः सप्तरात्रमवकीर्णिव्रतं चरेत् ॥ २.१८७॥ akṛtvā bhaikṣacaraṇamasamidhya ca pāvakam |
anāturaḥ saptarātramavakīrṇivrataṃ caret || 2.187|| One who has not performed alms-round, nor kindled the sacred fire, and remains free from illness shall observe the scattered vow for seven nights. Authority through disciplined observance Causation via omission of ritual duty Capacity-based responsibility grounded in bodily health Restoration logic through compensatory spiritual discipline Consciousness alignment via intentional purification

title: manu 2.188
content:
भैक्षेण वर्तयेन्नित्यं नैकान्नादी भवेद्व्रती ।
भैक्षेण व्रतिनो वृत्तिरुपवाससमा स्मृता ॥ २.१८८॥ bhaikṣeṇa vartayennityaṁ naikānnādī bhavedvratī |
bhaikṣeṇa vratiṇo vṛttirupavāsasamā smṛtā || 2.188|| One who has taken a vow must sustain oneself daily through alms alone; one who consumes food from a single source is not considered a true observer of the vow. The livelihood of such vowed individuals through alms is equivalent to fasting. Authority flows from alignment with Vedic discipline, not institutional position. Causation arises through conscious choice and sustained observance. Capacity-based responsibility requires full embodiment of vow-prescribed conduct. Restoration logic demands return to the original vow-integrity when deviation occurs. Consciousness alignment is maintained by renouncing fixed material dependencies.

title: manu 2.189
content:
व्रतवद्देवदैवत्ये पित्र्ये कर्मण्यथर्षिवत् ।
काममभ्यर्थितोऽश्नीयाद्व्रतमस्य न लुप्यते ॥ २.१८९॥ vratavad devadaivatye pitrye karmaṇy atharṣivat |
kāmam abhyarthito 'śnīyād vratam asya na lupyate || 2.189|| One who is invited to perform a vow-based ritual duty—whether in service of divine beings, ancestors, or sages—may consume food offered in fulfillment of that vow; such consumption does not invalidate the vow. Authority derives from invocation and alignment with cosmic order Causation arises through intentional engagement in dharma-karma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual readiness and role-specific alignment Restoration logic operates through completion of invoked dharmic process Consciousness alignment occurs when action aligns with invoked sacred intent

title: manu 2.190
content:
ब्राह्मणस्यैव कर्मैतदुपदिष्टं मनीषिभिः ।
राजन्यवैश्ययोस्त्वेवं नैतत्कर्म विधीयते ॥ २.१९०॥ brāhmaṇasyaiva karma etad upadiṣṭaṃ manīṣibhiḥ | rājanyavaiśyayos tvevaṃ naitat karma vidhīyate || 2.190|| This prescribed duty is exclusively for the Brāhmaṇa; it has been declared by the seers. For the Kṣatriya and Vaiśya, such a duty is not ordained in the same form. Authority flows from consciousness capacity, not birth alone Causation aligns with inherent dharma-svarūpa, not external imposition Capacity-based responsibility defines role-specific duties Restoration logic operates through alignment with svadharma Consciousness alignment determines lawful engagement in action

title: manu 2.191
content: चोदितो गुरुणा नित्यमप्रचोदित एव वा । कुर्यादध्ययने यत्नमाचार्यस्य हितेषु च ॥ २.१९१॥ codito guruṇā nityam apracodita eva vā | kuryād adhyayane yatnam ācāryasya hiteṣu ca || 2.191|| One who is continually guided by the Guru, or even one who is not explicitly prompted, must exert effort in study and act for the welfare of the Ācārya. Authority flows through conscious guidance, not institutional position Causation arises from alignment with higher knowledge structures Capacity-based responsibility is activated by proximity to enlightened instruction Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of learning over fault attribution Consciousness alignment is cultivated through service to the teacher's mission

title: manu 2.192
content:
शरीरं चैव वाचं च बुद्धीन्द्रियमनांसि च ।
नियम्य प्राञ्जलिस्तिष्ठेद्वीक्षमाणो गुरोर्मुखम् ॥ २.१९२॥ śarīraṁ caiva vācaṁ ca buddhīndriyamanāṁsi ca |
niyamya prāñjalistiṣṭhed vīkṣamāṇo guroḥ mukham || 2.192|| One must stand before the Guru with palms joined, having fully restrained the body, speech, mind, intellect, and senses, and remain gazing upon the face of the Guru. Authority originates from conscious alignment with the Guru-tattva Causation arises through disciplined harmonization of inner instruments Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over bodily and mental functions Restoration logic operates via submission to higher consciousness Consciousness alignment is enacted through externalized reverence

title: manu 2.193
content:
नित्यमुद्धृतपाणिः स्यात्साध्वाचारः सुसंवृतः ।
आस्यतामिति चौक्तः सन्नासीताभिमुखं गुरोः ॥ २.१९३॥ nityamuddhṛtapāṇiḥ syātsādhvācāraḥ susaṃvṛtaḥ |
āsyatāmiti cauktaḥ sannāsītābhimukhaṃ guroḥ || 2.193|| One must always keep the hands uplifted in readiness, maintain noble conduct with full restraint, and when called by the Guru to come forward, one shall face toward the Āsīta (the seat of dharma) with complete orientation towards the Guru. Authority flows from the Guru as the living embodiment of Dharma Causation arises through alignment with the seat of Dharma (Āsīta) Capacity-based responsibility is demonstrated through bodily readiness and mental orientation Restoration logic requires immediate response to the call of higher consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs through physical and directional submission to the Guru

title: manu 2.194
content:
हीनान्नवस्त्रवेषः स्यात्सर्वदा गुरुसन्निधौ ।
उत्तिष्ठेत्प्रथमं चास्य चरमं चैव संविशेत् ॥ २.१९४॥ hīnānnavast raveṣaḥ syātsarvadā gurusannidhau |
uttiṣṭhetprathamaṃ cāsya caramaṃ caiva saṃviśet || 2.194|| In the presence of the Guru, one must always remain in a state of lesser attire and food, rising first and sitting last. Authority flows from realized consciousness, not social position. Capacity-based responsibility requires embodied humility before higher knowledge. Restoration logic demands alignment with the sequential order of spiritual precedence. Consciousness alignment necessitates visible acts of reverence that reflect inner surrender.

title: manu 2.195
content:
प्रतिश्रावणसम्भाषे शयानो न समाचरेत् ।
नासीनो न च भुञ्जानो न तिष्ठन्न पराङ्मुखः ॥ २.१९५॥ pratiśrāvaṇasambhāṣe śayāno na samācaret .
nāsīno na ca bhuñjāno na tiṣṭhann parāṅmukhaḥ || 2.195 || One engaged in listening to sacred instruction or discourse shall not act while lying down, nor while seated improperly, nor while eating, nor while standing with face averted. Authority of the Teaching Context Causation through Proper Receptivity Capacity-based Responsibility in Learning Restoration through Ritual Alignment Consciousness Alignment via Postural Discipline

title: manu 2.196
content:
आसीनस्य स्थितः कुर्यादभिगच्छंस्तु तिष्ठतः ।
प्रत्युद्गम्य त्वाव्रजतः पश्चाद्धावंस्तु धावतः ॥ २.१९६॥ āsīnasya sthitaḥ kuryād abhigacchaṃstu tiṣṭhataḥ |
pratyudgamy tvāvrajataḥ paścāddhāvaṃstu dhāvataḥ || 2.196|| One seated shall act in accordance with the standing one who approaches; one who has halted must proceed forward upon meeting another approaching; one moving ahead should step back when encountering one running from behind; one fleeing must be pursued only to restore alignment. Authority flows through relational presence and contextual responsiveness. Causation arises through embodied encounter and conscious recognition. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to respond and restore harmony. Restoration logic requires precise attunement to sequential movement and intention. Consciousness alignment occurs through reciprocal acknowledgment and positional integrity.

title: manu 2.197
content:
पराङ्मुखस्याभिमुखो दूरस्थस्येत्य चान्तिकम् ।
प्रणम्य तु शयानस्य निदेशे चैव तिष्ठतः ॥ २.१९७॥ parāṅmukhasyābhimukho dūrasthasyeti cāntikam | praṇamya tu śayānasya nideśe caiva tiṣṭhataḥ || 2.197 || One must approach those who are turned away, distant in body or mind, lying down in negligence, or standing in command—by bowing before them, drawing near, and aligning with their directive presence. Authority is recognized through alignment, not dominance. Causation arises from conscious proximity and respectful engagement. Capacity-based responsibility includes restoring connection with the withdrawn or inert. Restoration logic requires movement toward disengaged consciousness. Consciousness alignment begins through embodied reverence and spatial surrender.

title: manu 2.198
content:
नीचं शय्याऽऽसनं चास्य नित्यं स्याद्गुरुसन्निधौ ।
गुरोस्तु चक्षुर्विषये न यथेष्टासनो भवेत् ॥ २.१९८॥ nīcaṃ śayyā āsanaṃ cāsya nityaṃ syād guru-sannidhau |
gurostu cakṣur-viṣaye na yatheṣṭāsano bhavet || 2.198|| In the presence of the Guru, the disciple shall always maintain a posture and seat lower than that of the Guru; in the visual field of the Guru, the disciple shall not assume any seat according to personal preference. Authority is hierarchically structured through conscious alignment with the Guru's presence. Causation arises from the disciple's capacity to honor the Guru's elevated consciousness through bodily comportment. Capacity-based responsibility is demonstrated by the disciple's ability to regulate physical posture in alignment with spiritual authority. Restoration logic operates through immediate reorientation of spatial and postural awareness upon disruption. Consciousness alignment is enacted through disciplined adherence to relational dharma between Guru and disciple.

title: manu 2.199
content:
नौदाहरेदस्य नाम परोक्षमपि केवलम् ।
न चैवास्यानुकुर्वीत गतिभाषितचेष्टितम् ॥ २.१९९॥ naudāharedasya nāma parokṣamapi kevalam | na caivāsyānukurvīta gatibhāṣitaceṣṭitam || 2.199|| One must not merely speak the name of the realized being indirectly; nor should one imitate their speech or conduct without embodying their state of realization. Authority is derived from realization, not imitation Causation arises from ontological alignment, not performative mimicry Capacity-based responsibility requires inner transformation prior to outer enactment Restoration logic demands congruence between consciousness and action Consciousness alignment supersedes ritualistic or behavioral emulation

title: manu 2.200
content:
गुरोर्यत्र परिवादो निन्दा वाऽपि प्रवर्तते ।
कर्णौ तत्र पिधातव्यौ गन्तव्यं वा ततोऽन्यतः ॥ २.२००॥ guror yatra parivādo nindā vā'pi pravartate |
karnau tatra pidhātavyau gantavyaṃ vā tato'nyataḥ || 2.200|| Wherever criticism or condemnation of the Guru arises, the ears must be closed there; or one must depart elsewhere. Authority of the Guru as unassailable by external judgment Causation rooted in protection of sacred hierarchy Capacity-based responsibility to preserve spiritual integrity Restoration logic through withdrawal from contamination Consciousness alignment via non-engagement with degradation

title: manu 2.201
content:
परीवादात्खरो भवति श्वा वै भवति निन्दकः ।
परिभोक्ता कृमिर्भवति कीटो भवति मत्सरी ॥ २.२०१॥ parīvādāt kharo bhavati śvā vai bhavati nindakaḥ |
paribhoktā kṛmir bhavati kīṭo bhavati matsarī || 2.201|| Through defamation arises the donkey; through slander, the dog becomes manifest. The enjoyer of another's resources becomes a worm; the envious becomes an insect. Authority is derived from alignment with consciousness, not social position Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) based on inner intent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's identification with action Restoration logic operates through reflection of internal state in external form Consciousness alignment determines the being-form assumed in experiential consequence

title: manu 2.202
content:
दूरस्थो नार्चयेदेनं न क्रुद्धो नान्तिके स्त्रियाः ।
यानासनस्थश्चैवैनमवरुह्याभिवादयेत् ॥ २.२०२॥ dūrastho nārcayed enaṁ na kruddho nāntike striyāḥ |
yānāsanasthaśa caivainam avaruhya abhivādayet || 2.202|| One seated at a distance must not be honored; nor one who is angry, nor one who is in proximity to a woman. One who is mounted on a vehicle must descend and offer salutation. Authority is context-dependent and spatially qualified Capacity for reverence is conditional upon inner state alignment Responsibility arises through embodied presence and conscious action Restoration occurs through intentional humility and recognition of hierarchy Consciousness alignment requires physical and mental posture congruence

title: manu 2.203
content: प्रतिवातेऽनुवाते च नासीत गुरुणा सह । प्रतिवातानुवाते असंश्रवे चैव गुरोर्न किं चिदपि कीर्तयेत् ॥ २.२०३॥ prativāte 'nuvāte ca nāsīta guruṇā saha | prativātānuvāte asaṃśrave caiva guroḥ na kiṃ cid api kīrtayet || 2.203 || One must not speak of anything heard from the Guru when in opposition or agreement with the Guru, nor when there is no mutual attunement. Authority flows from realized consciousness, not positional power Causation arises through alignment, not mere transmission Capacity-based responsibility requires attunement before articulation Restoration logic prioritizes integrity over information exchange Consciousness alignment determines the validity of knowledge sharing

title: manu 2.204
content:
गोऽश्वौष्ट्रयानप्रासादप्रस्तरेषु कटेषु च ।
आसीत गुरुणा सार्धं शिलाफलकनौषु च ॥ २.२०४॥ go 'śvauṣṭrayānaprāsādaprastareṣu kateṣu ca |
āsīta guruṇā sārdhaṃ śilāphalakanauṣu ca || 2.204|| One must sit with the Guru upon elevated seats made of stone slabs or wooden planks, positioned in cowsheds, horse stables, donkey carts, palace terraces, or mountain ledges. Authority is contextually anchored through physical elevation and proximity to sacred life-supporting entities. Causation arises from intentional alignment of learning space with spiritual pedagogical design. Capacity-based responsibility includes honoring the Guru's seat as a conduit for consciousness transmission. Restoration logic operates by reestablishing proper spatial and energetic conditions for knowledge assimilation. Consciousness alignment occurs when bodily posture and environmental setting reflect respect for the Guru.

title: manu 2.205
content:
गुरोर्गुरौ सन्निहिते गुरुवद्वृत्तिमाचरेत् ।
न चानिसृष्टो गुरुणा स्वान् गुरूनभिवादयेत् ॥ २.२०५॥ guror gurau sannihite guruvad vṛttim ācaret |
na cānisṛṣṭo guruṇā svān gurūn abhivādayet || 2.205 || In the presence of a higher Guru, one must conduct oneself with the reverence due to that elevated status; however, one who has not been initiated by their own Guru shall not offer obeisance to other Gurus. Authority flows through initiation and spiritual succession Causation is rooted in conscious alignment, not external form Capacity-based responsibility arises from direct Guru-disciple connection Restoration logic requires honoring relational dharmic hierarchies Consciousness alignment occurs when action aligns with initiatic lineage

title: manu 2.206
content:
विद्यागुरुष्वेवमेव नित्या वृत्तिः स्वयोनिषु ।
प्रतिषेधत्सु चाधर्माधितं चोपदिशत्स्वपि ॥ २.२०६॥ vidyāguruṣvevameva nityā vṛttiḥ svayoniṣu |
pratiṣedhatсу cādharmādhiitaṃ copadiśatsvapi || 2.206|| The eternal conduct towards teachers of knowledge is reverence; even when they prohibit or instruct against unrighteousness, their guidance must be honored. Authority of the Guru as a conduit of dharma Causation through alignment with higher consciousness Capacity-based responsibility rooted in learning relationship Restoration logic via honoring the source of wisdom Consciousness alignment through reverent obedience

title: manu 2.207
content:
श्रेयःसु गुरुवद्वृत्तिं नित्यमेव समाचरेत् ।
गुरुपुत्रेषु चार्येषु गुरोश्चैव स्वबन्धुषु ॥ २.२०७॥ गुरुपुत्रे तथाचार्ये śreyaḥsu guruvadvṛttiṁ nityameva samācaret |
guruputreṣu cāryeṣu guruścaiva svabandhuṣu || 2.207|| guruputre tathācārye One shall always conduct oneself with the conduct of a Guru in all matters that lead to welfare, especially towards the son of the Guru, the spiritual preceptor himself, and one's own kinsmen. Authority flows through lineage and spiritual succession Causation is rooted in reverence and alignment with higher consciousness Capacity-based responsibility increases with proximity to enlightened authority Restoration logic requires emulation of elevated behavioral models Consciousness alignment occurs through consistent honoring of sacred relationships

title: manu 2.208
content:
बालः समानजन्मा वा शिष्यो वा यज्ञकर्मणि ।
अध्यापयन् गुरुसुतो गुरुवत्मानमर्हति ॥ २.२०८॥ bālaḥ samānajanmā vā śiṣyo vā yajñakarmaṇi |
adhyāpayan gurusuto guruvatmānamarhati || 2.208|| One who instructs in ritual action—whether a child, peer, or disciple—is entitled to the status of Guru if he embodies the consciousness of the Guru. Authority arises from the embodiment of consciousness, not age or birth. Causation originates in the capacity to transmit sacred knowledge. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner alignment, not social role. Restoration logic recognizes the Guru-tattva when it manifests, regardless of form. Consciousness alignment supersedes lineage or institutional credentialing.

title: manu 2.209
content:
उत्सादनं च गात्राणां स्नापनौच्छिष्टभोजने ।
न कुर्याद्गुरुपुत्रस्य पादयोश्चावनेजनम् ॥ २.२०९॥ utsādanaṃ ca gātrāṇāṃ snāpanaucchṣṭabhojane |
na kuryād guruputrasya pādayoś cāvanējanaṃ || 2.209|| One must not cause bodily distress, nor bathe or eat remnants of food offered by the son of one's guru; one must also refrain from washing the feet of such a person. Authority derived from spiritual lineage supersedes social rank Causation includes energetic contamination through ritual inversion Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of sacred relational boundaries Restoration logic demands immediate cessation and purification of violated hierarchies Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring inviolable spiritual succession

title: manu 2.210
content:
गुरुवत्प्रतिपूज्याः स्युः सवर्णा गुरुयोषितः ।
असवर्णास्तु सम्पूज्याः प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादनैः ॥ २.२१०॥ guruvat pratipūjyāḥ syuḥ savarṇā guru yoṣitaḥ |
asavarṇāstu sampūjyāḥ pratyutthānābhivādanaiḥ ||2.210|| Women of the same varna as the guru are to be revered as the guru himself; women of different varnas are to be honored with rising and salutation. Authority flows through alignment with consciousness, not biological or social role Causation arises from intentional recognition of spiritual hierarchy Capacity-based responsibility includes honoring those who uphold dharma Restoration logic requires correction of disrespect toward spiritual teachers and their consorts Consciousness alignment necessitates right action in relational respect

title: manu 2.211
content:
अभ्यञ्जनं स्नापनं च गात्रोत्सादनमेव च ।
गुरुपत्न्या न कार्याणि केशानां च प्रसाधनम् ॥ २.२११॥ abhyañjanaṁ snāpanaṁ ca gātrotsādanameva ca |
gurupatnyā na kāryāṇi keśānāṁ ca prasādhanam || 2.211|| Anointment, bathing, body polishing, and hair dressing must not be performed by the wife of the guru. Authority flows through spiritual lineage, not familial proximity Causation arises from purity-preserving boundaries in sacred relationships Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of inviolable spiritual hierarchies Restoration logic demands prevention of contamination within guru-disciple integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates preserving energetic sanctity between guru and disciple

title: manu 2.212
content:
गुरुपत्नी तु युवतिर्नाभिवाद्यैह पादयोः ।
पूर्णविंशतिवर्षेण गुणदोषौ विजानता ॥ २.२१२॥ gurupatnī tu yuvatir nābhivādyaih pādayoḥ |
pūrṇaviṃśativarṣeṇa guṇadoṣau vijānatā || 2.212|| A young woman who is the wife of one's guru must not be saluted by touching her feet; she who knows both merit and demerit fully by the age of twenty. Authority flows through spiritual lineage, not marital status Capacity-based responsibility arises with knowledge of dharma Respect is contextually determined by ontological role Restoration occurs through alignment with one’s true capacity Consciousness recognition supersedes social positioning

title: manu 2.213
content:
स्वभाव एष नारीणां नराणामिह दूषणम् ।
अतोऽर्थान्न प्रमाद्यन्ति प्रमदासु विपश्चितः ॥ २.२१३॥ svabhāva eṣa nārīṇāṁ narāṇām iha dūṣaṇam |
ato'rthān na pramādyanti pramadāsu vipaścitaḥ || 2.213|| The inherent nature of women is a source of corruption for men in this world; therefore, the wise do not become careless around those who are careless. Authority arises from discriminative awareness and self-regulation Causation originates in proximity and unguarded consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to maintain alignment with Dharma Restoration logic requires removal of corrupting influence and reestablishment of inner discipline Consciousness alignment depends on continuous vigilance and environmental discernment

title: manu 2.214
content:
अविद्वांसमलं लोके विद्वांसमपि वा पुनः ।
प्रमदा ह्युत्पथं नेतुं कामक्रोधवशानुगम् ॥ २.२१४॥ avidvāṁsamalaṁ loke vidvāṁsamapi vā punaḥ |
pramadā hyutpathaṁ netuṁ kāmakrodhavaśānugam || 2.214|| Whether unlearned or learned, a woman who follows the path of desire and anger leads both herself and others astray. Authority flows from consciousness alignment, not gender or status Causation arises through volitional distortion by desire and anger Capacity-based responsibility recognizes individual agency within collective influence Restoration logic requires reorientation to dharma-vāhana (right conduct) Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive moral frameworks

title: manu 2.215
content:
मात्रा स्वस्रा दुहित्रा वा न विविक्तासनो भवेत् ।
बलवानिन्द्रियग्रामो विद्वांसमपि कर्षति ॥ २.२१५॥ mātrā svasrā duhitṛā vā na viviktāsano bhavet | balavānindriyagrāmo vidvāṃsamapi karṣati || 2.215 || One must not sit in seclusion with one's mother, sister, or daughter; the group of senses, though mighty, drags even the wise. Authority of familial boundary maintenance Causation through sensory impulse override Capacity-based responsibility despite knowledge Restoration logic via removal of proximity risk Consciousness alignment through structural discipline

title: manu 2.216
content:
कामं तु गुरुपत्नीनां युवतीनां युवा भुवि ।
विधिवद्वन्दनं कुर्यादसावहमिति ब्रुवन् ॥ २.२१६॥ kāmaṃ tu gurupatnīnāṃ yuvatīnāṃ yuvā bhuvi |
vidhivadvandanaṃ kuryād asāv aham iti bruvan || 2.216 || A young man upon earth desiring the wives of his guru or youthful women shall perform ritual salutation lawfully, declaring 'he is not me.' Authority: The Guru holds spiritual and relational sovereignty over the disciple. Causation: Desire arises from misidentification; proper recognition dissolves unlawful impulse. Capacity-based responsibility: One must act within conscious alignment to relational dharma. Restoration logic: Proper acknowledgment and separation restore integrity of relationship. Consciousness alignment: Recognition of non-identity ('he is not me') realigns consciousness.

title: manu 2.217
content:
विप्रोष्य पादग्रहणमन्वहं चाभिवादनम् ।
गुरुदारेषु कुर्वीत सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन् ॥ २.२१७॥ viproṣya pādagrahana manvahaṁ cābhivādanam |
gurudāreṣu kurvīta satāṁ dharmamanusmaran || 2.217|| One must daily perform padagrahana and abhivādana towards the twice-born, remembering the dharma of noble beings, especially in relation to the wives of gurus. Authority is derived through sustained alignment with realized beings. Causation arises through repeated acts of reverence that establish spiritual connection. Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious recognition of elevated relationships. Restoration logic operates through daily reaffirmation of sacred hierarchies. Consciousness alignment is cultivated by honoring those who uphold dharma.

title: manu 2.218
content:
यथा खनन् खनित्रेण नरो वार्यधिगच्छति ।
तथा गुरुगतां विद्यां शुश्रूषुरधिगच्छति ॥ २.२१८॥ yathā khanan khanitreṇa naro vāryadhigacchati |
tathā gurugatāṃ vidyāṃ śuśrūṣuradhigacchati || 2.218|| As a person digs with a spade to reach water, so too does a disciple attain knowledge residing in the Guru through service. Authority resides in the Guru as the vessel of realized knowledge Causation arises through dedicated action aligned with reverence Capacity-based responsibility is activated by sincere intent to learn Restoration logic operates through disciplined proximity to truth Consciousness alignment occurs via selfless engagement with wisdom

title: manu 2.219
content:
मुण्डो वा जटिलो वा स्यादथ वा स्यात्शिखाजटः ।
नैनं ग्रामेऽभिनिम्लोचेत्सूर्यो नाभ्युदियात्क्व चित् ॥ २.२१९॥ muṇḍo vā jaṭilo vā syādatha vā syātśikhājaṭaḥ |
nainaṃ grāme'bhinimloceTSūryo nābhyudiyātkva cit || Whether his head is shaved, hair matted, or adorned with a tuft—such external appearances must not obstruct the rising of the Sun of Self within the village of human consciousness. Authority arises from inner illumination, not outer form Causation lies in alignment with the Self, not social performance Capacity-based responsibility is measured by internal realization, not ritual compliance Restoration logic demands removal of obstruction to Self-radiance Consciousness alignment supersedes all ceremonial distinctions

title: manu 2.220
content:
तं चेदभ्युदियात्सूर्यः शयानं कामचारतः ।
निम्लोचेद्वाऽप्यविज्ञानाज्जपन्नुपवसेद्दिनम् ॥ २.२२०॥ taṃ ced abhudyāt sūryaḥ śayānaṃ kāmacārataḥ |
nimloced vā 'py avijñānāj japann upavased dinam || 2.220 || If the sun rises while one lies asleep in indulgence, or sets while one remains unaware due to ignorance, that person shall fast and chant mantras for the duration of a day. Authority: The rhythm of nature as divine governance Causation: Consciousness lapses lead to energetic imbalance Capacity-based responsibility: One who has the capacity to align with cosmic rhythm bears the duty Restoration logic: Ritual observance restores temporal and spiritual harmony Consciousness alignment: Discipline realigns individual will with universal dharma

title: manu 2.221
content: सूर्येण ह्यभिनिर्मुक्तः शयानोऽभ्युदितश्च यः । अभिनिम्लुक्तः प्रायश्चित्तमकुर्वाणो युक्तः स्यान् महतेनसा ॥ २.२२१॥ sūryeṇa hy abhinirmuktaḥ śayāno 'bhyuditaś ca yaḥ | abhinimluktaḥ prāyaścittam akurvāṇo yuktaḥ syān mahatena sā || 2.221|| One who sleeps or wakes facing away from the sun without performing prescribed restorative acts becomes aligned with great sin due to disruption of natural energetic harmony. Authority resides in alignment with cosmic order as defined by SPH Causation arises from intentional misalignment with Vedic directional discipline Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of directional dharma Restoration logic requires realignment through conscious directional rectification Consciousness alignment is achieved via solar-oriented behavioral correction

title: manu 2.222
content:
आचम्य प्रयतो नित्यमुभे संध्ये समाहितः ।
शुचौ देशे जपञ्जप्यमुपासीत यथाविधि ॥ २.२२२॥ ācmya prayato nityam ubhe sandhye samāhitaḥ |
śucau deśe japañjapyam upāsīta yathāvidhi || 2.222|| Having purified through achamana, ever vigilant, at both Sandhyas, in a pure place, one shall perform Japa and Japya as prescribed. Authority flows from inner purity and disciplined alignment with cosmic rhythm. Causation arises from intentional repetition of sacred sound aligned with dharma. Capacity-based responsibility requires environmental and temporal suitability for practice. Restoration logic is enacted through daily ritualized reconnection with divine order. Consciousness alignment occurs when bodily act, mental focus, and spiritual injunction converge.

title: manu 2.223
content:
यदि स्त्री यद्यवरजः श्रेयः किं चित्समाचरेत् ।
तत्सर्वमाचरेद्युक्तो यत्र चास्य रमेन् मनः ॥ २.२२३॥ yadi strī yadyavarajaḥ śreyaḥ kiṃ citsamācareta |
tatsarvamācaredyukto yatra cāsya ramen manaḥ || 2.223|| If a woman, regardless of varna, performs any righteous action that leads to spiritual elevation, then all such actions should be accepted by those qualified to judge, provided her intent aligns with dharma and brings harmony to consciousness. Authority is derived from alignment with dharma, not social position. Causation originates in conscious intention, not external form. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes inner purity over birth-based classification. Restoration logic emphasizes integration of action within universal dharma. Consciousness alignment determines the validity of conduct.

title: manu 2.224
content:
धर्मार्थावुच्यते श्रेयः कामार्थौ धर्म एव च ।
अर्थ एवैह वा श्रेयस्त्रिवर्ग इति तु स्थितिः ॥ २.२२४॥ dharmārthāvucyate śreyaḥ kāmārthau dharma eva ca |
artha eva eha vā śreyas trivarga iti tu sthitiḥ || 2.224|| Dharma and Artha together constitute the highest good; Kama and Artha also align with Dharma. Alternatively, Artha alone may be considered the highest good—such is the established position of the threefold aim of life. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma as defined by SPH Causation arises through conscious intention aligned with Trivarga Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to uphold Dharma in pursuit of Artha and Kama Restoration logic operates through reintegration into Trivarga harmony Consciousness alignment ensures sustainable societal equilibrium

title: manu 2.225
content:
आचार्यश्च पिता चैव माता भ्राता च पूर्वजः ।
नार्तेनाप्यवमन्तव्या ब्राह्मणेन विशेषतः ॥ २.२२५॥ ācāryaśca pitā caiva mātā bhrātā ca pūrvajaḥ |
nārtenevaman-tavyā brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ || The teacher, father, mother, elder brother, and ancestors—none shall be insulted by a Brahmin, even when aggrieved. Authority inheres in relational dharmic roles, not institutional power Causation arises from conscious alignment with source-ordering Capacity-based responsibility escalates with proximity to dharma-teaching roles Restoration logic demands reverence for those who uphold cosmic instruction Consciousness alignment requires honoring formative spiritual authorities

title: manu 2.226
content:
आचार्यो ब्रह्मणो मूर्तिः पिता मूर्तिः प्रजापतेः ।
माता पृथिव्या मूर्तिस्तु भ्राता स्वो मूर्तिरात्मनः ॥ २.२२६॥ ācāryo brahmaṇo mūrtiḥ pitā mūrtiḥ prajāpateḥ |
mātā pṛthivyā mūrtistu bhrātā svo mūrtirātmanaḥ || 2.226|| The Ācārya is the embodiment of Brahma; the father is the embodiment of Prajāpati; the mother is the embodiment of Earth; and the brother is the embodiment of the Self. Authority flows through embodied divine roles rather than individual persons Causation originates in cosmic function, not personal intent Capacity-based responsibility aligns with one's functional embodiment of universal principles Restoration occurs when individuals realign with their inherent cosmic embodiment Consciousness alignment requires recognition of one's role within the greater cosmic order

title: manu 2.227
content:
यं मातापितरौ क्लेशं सहेते सम्भवे नृणाम् ।
न तस्य निष्कृतिः शक्या कर्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ॥ २.२२७॥ yaṃ mātāpitarau kleśaṃ sahete sambhave nṛṇām |
na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ śaktyā kartuṃ varṣaśatairapi ||2.227|| The suffering endured by parents at the time of a child's birth cannot be repaid even through efforts extending over hundreds of years. Authority originates in the existential sacrifice of progenitors Causation flows from the irreversible act of creation Capacity-based responsibility arises from receipt of unrepayable debt Restoration logic demands acknowledgment of foundational indebtedness Consciousness alignment requires recognition of generative suffering

title: manu 2.228
content:
तयोर्नित्यं प्रियं कुर्यादाचार्यस्य च सर्वदा ।
तेष्वेव त्रिषु तुष्टेषु तपः सर्वं समाप्यते ॥ २.२२८॥ tayor-nityaṃ priyaṃ kuryād-ācāryasya ca sarvadā |
teṣveva triṣu tuṣṭeṣu tapaḥ sarvaṃ samāpyate || 2.228|| One must always act in accordance with the pleasure of the Guru and the Preceptor; when these three—the Self, the Guru, and the Preceptor—are satisfied, all austerities reach their completion. Authority flows from the Guru as representative of the Supreme Consciousness Causation arises through alignment with realized beings Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's readiness to serve the Guru Restoration logic operates through service and surrender Consciousness alignment occurs via harmonious relationship with spiritual authority

title: manu 2.229
content:
तेषां त्रयाणां शुश्रूषा परमं तप उच्यते ।
न तैरनभ्यनुज्ञातो धर्ममन्यं समाचरेत् ॥ २.२२९॥ teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate |
na tairanabhy-anujñāto dharmamanyaṃ samācaret || Service to these three—Guru, Deity, and Humanity—is declared as the highest austerity; without their explicit consent, no other dharma should be enacted. Authority flows from conscious alignment with Guru, Deity, and Humanity Causation arises through consent-based service, not arbitrary will Capacity-based responsibility requires attunement to triadic harmony Restoration logic operates through alignment with consent and service Consciousness alignment precedes all lawful action

title: manu 2.230
content:
त एव हि त्रयो लोकास्त एव त्रय आश्रमाः ।
त एव हि त्रयो वेदास्त एवौक्तास्त्रयोऽग्नयः ॥ २.२३०॥ ta eva hi trayo lokās ta eva traya āśramāḥ |
ta eva hi trayo vedās ta evoktās trayo'gnayaḥ || 2.230|| The same three worlds, the same three stages of life, the same three Vedas, and the same three sacred fires—these are declared as one unified structure of Dharma, manifesting in triadic completeness under the singular authority of Sanātana Dharma. Authority derives from the unity and indivisibility of Dharma’s triadic structure Causation is established through alignment with the triadic manifestation of Vedic order Capacity-based responsibility arises from recognition of one's place within the triadic cosmic framework Restoration logic operates by realigning individual action with the structural harmony of Lokas, Ashramas, Vedas, and Agnis Consciousness alignment occurs when the knower recognizes their role within the immutable triadic schema

title: manu 2.231
content:
पिता वै गार्हपत्योऽग्निर्माताऽग्निर्दक्षिणः स्मृतः ।
गुरुराहवनीयस्तु साऽग्नित्रेता गरीयसी ॥ २.२३१॥ pitā vai gārhapatyo'gnir mātā'gnir dakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ |
gurur āhavanīyastu sā'gnitretā garīyasī || 2.231|| The father is the household fire; the mother is the southern fire; the guru is the sacrificial fire. Among these, the guru as the carrier of the sacred flame holds the highest authority. Authority flows through lineage and spiritual succession Causation originates in conscious transmission Capacity-based responsibility arises from role embodiment Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma over individual preference Consciousness alignment requires recognition of hierarchical spiritual order

title: manu 2.232
content:
त्रिष्वप्रमाद्यन्नेतेषु त्रीन् लोकान् विजयेद्गृही ।
दीप्यमानः स्ववपुषा देववद्दिवि मोदते ॥ २.२३२॥ triṣvapramādyanneteṣu trīn lokān vijayedgṛhī |
dīpyamānaḥ svavapuṣā devavaddivi modate || 2.232|| The householder who remains unwavering in these three—righteous vigilance, sustained duty, and conscious alignment—conquers the three worlds and, radiant in his own essence, rejoices in heaven like a deity. Authority is derived from unwavering alignment with Dharma Causation arises from sustained consciousness-based action Capacity-based responsibility is measured by consistency in Dharma-vyavastha Restoration logic operates through self-radiant integrity Consciousness alignment determines jurisdictional mastery

title: manu 2.233
content:
इमं लोकं मातृभक्त्या पितृभक्त्या तु मध्यमम् ।
गुरुशुश्रूषया त्वेवं ब्रह्मलोकं समश्नुते ॥ २.२३३॥ imaṁ lokaṁ mātṛbhaktyā pitṛbhaktyā tu madhyamam |
guruśuśrūṣayā tvevaṁ brahmalokaṁ samaśnute || 2.233|| Through devotion to the Mother, one attains this world; through devotion to the Father, the intermediate realm; and through service to the Guru, one fully realizes the Brahmic Realm. Authority flows from maternal integrity and paternal order Causation aligns with sequential consciousness unfoldment Capacity-based responsibility arises through relational dharma Restoration logic operates via reverent completion of role-duties Consciousness alignment occurs through guru-disciple transmission

title: manu 2.234
content:
सर्वे तस्यादृता धर्मा यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः ।
अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफलाः क्रियाः ॥ २.२३४॥ sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ |
anādṛtāstu yasyaite sarvāstasyaphalāḥ kriyāḥ || 2.234|| All dharmas are sustained for one who honors these three supports; for one who dishonors them, all actions bear no fruit. Authority flows from alignment with foundational dharmic structures Causation is rooted in conscious adherence to triadic foundations Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of sustaining principles Restoration logic operates through reconnection to foundational truths Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy of all performed action

title: manu 2.235
content:
यावत्त्रयस्ते जीवेयुस्तावत्नान्यं समाचरेत् ।
तेष्वेव नित्यं शुश्रूषां कुर्यात्प्रियहिते रतः ॥ २.२३५॥ yāvat-trayas te jīveyus tāvat nānyaṁ samācaret |
teṣv eva nityaṁ śuśrūṣāṁ kuryāt priyahite rataḥ || 2.235 || As long as the three—father, mother, and guru—remain alive, one shall act in accordance with their guidance. One must constantly serve them with devotion, dedicated to their welfare and happiness. Authority originates from life-giving and consciousness-bearing relationships Causation is rooted in gratitude and continuity of existence Capacity-based responsibility arises through relational dependence Restoration logic centers on reciprocal service and reverence Consciousness alignment manifests through honoring formative authorities

title: manu 2.236
content:
तेषामनुपरोधेन पारत्र्यं यद्यदाचरेत् ।
तत्तन्निवेदयेत्तेभ्यो मनोवचनकर्मभिः ॥ २.२३६॥ teṣāmanuparodhena pāratryaṁ yadyadācaret |
tattannivedayettebhyo manovacanakarmabhiḥ || 2.236|| Whatever actions one performs under the influence or obstruction of others, one shall disclose those to them through thought, word, and deed. Authority flows from conscious integrity, not coercion Causation includes energetic and mental influence as binding factors Capacity-based responsibility requires full disclosure of induced acts Restoration logic demands transparency in relational dharmic transactions Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of mental, verbal, and physical channels

title: manu 2.237
content:
त्रिष्वेतेष्वितिकृत्यं हि पुरुषस्य समाप्यते ।
एष धर्मः परः साक्षादुपधर्मोऽन्य उच्यते ॥ २.२३७॥ triṣveteṣv itikṛtyaṁ hi puruṣasya samāpyate |
eṣa dharmaḥ paraḥ sākṣād upadharmo'nya ucyate || 2.237|| In these three, the completion of man's duty is established; this is the supreme Dharma directly realized, while subsidiary dharmas are declared otherwise. Authority originates from the realization of Supreme Dharma, not from social position or textual interpretation. Causation aligns with the sequential unfolding of consciousness-based responsibility. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment with Supreme Dharma, not external roles. Restoration logic operates through reconnection to the source of Dharma. Consciousness alignment determines the validity and applicability of all juridical acts.

title: manu 2.238
content:
श्रद्दधानः शुभां विद्यामाददीतावरादपि ।
अन्यादपि परं धर्मं स्त्रीरत्नं दुष्कुलादपि ॥ २.२३८॥ śraddadhānaḥ śubhāṃ vidyāmādadītāvarādapi |
anyādapi paraṃ dharmaṃ strīratnaṃ duṣkulādapi || 2.238|| One who possesses śraddhā shall receive superior knowledge even from a lowly teacher; likewise, one shall receive greater dharma from a woman of noble character, even if born of a degraded family. Authority arises from consciousness capacity, not social rank Causation is determined by śraddhā-based receptivity Capacity-based responsibility transcends lineage or gender Restoration logic prioritizes inner nobility over external status Consciousness alignment enables recognition of hidden dharmic sources

title: manu 2.239
content:
विषादप्यमृतं ग्राह्यं बालादपि सुभाषितम् ।
अमित्रादपि सद्वृत्तममेध्यादपि काञ्चनम् ॥ २.२३९॥ viṣādapyamṛtaṁ grāhyaṁ bālādapi subhāṣitam |
amitrādapi sadvṛttamamedhyādapi kāñcanam || 2.239|| Even poison may yield nectar; from a child, wisdom may arise. From an enemy, noble conduct is to be accepted; even from impure sources, gold is purified. Authority arises from discernment, not origin Causation transcends apparent source conditions Capacity-based responsibility includes receptivity to truth regardless of speaker Restoration logic demands extraction of dharma from any context Consciousness alignment requires recognition of divinity in all expressions

title: manu 2.240
content:
स्त्रियो रत्नान्यथो विद्या धर्मः शौचं सुभाषितम् ।
विविधानि च शिल्पानि समादेयानि सर्वतः ॥ २.२४०॥ striyo ratnānyatho vidyā dharmaḥ śaucaṃ subhāṣitam |
vividhāni ca śilpāni samādeyāni sarvataḥ || 2.240|| Women, jewels, learning, righteousness, purity, good speech, and various crafts—are all to be received fully and without reservation. Authority flows through recognition of inherent value in all beings and resources. Causation is aligned with conscious reception rather than possessive ownership. Capacity-based responsibility includes the honoring and cultivation of latent potential in all entities. Restoration logic requires the full integration of feminine energy, knowledge, and skill within societal order. Consciousness alignment occurs when societal structures reflect completeness rather than lack.

title: manu 2.241
content: अब्राह्मणादध्यायनमापत्काले विधीयते । अनुव्रज्या च शुश्रूषा यावदध्यायनं गुरोः ॥ २.२४१॥ abrahmaṇād adhyayanam āpatkāle vidhīyate | anuvrajyā ca śuśrūṣā yāvad adhyayanaṃ guruḥ || 2.241|| In times of crisis, learning from a non-Brahmin teacher is permitted; accompanying and serving the Guru until the completion of study is the duty. Authority arises contextually, not rigidly by birth Causation aligns with situational dharma Capacity-based responsibility transcends caste-fixed roles Restoration logic prioritizes knowledge continuity Consciousness alignment supersedes social structuring

title: manu 2.242
content:
नाब्राह्मणे गुरौ शिष्यो वासमात्यन्तिकं वसेत् ।
ब्राह्मणे वाऽननूचाने काङ्क्षन् गतिमनुत्तमाम् ॥ २.२४२॥ nābrāhmaṇe gurau śiṣyo vāsamātyantikaṃ vaset |
brāhmaṇe vā'nanaūcāne kāṅkṣan gatimanuttamām || 2.242|| A disciple shall not reside permanently with a guru who is not a Brahmana; nor with a Brahmana who has not been duly initiated into the highest spiritual discipline, if seeking the supreme goal. Authority is derived from realized capacity, not nominal status. Causation in spiritual instruction requires integrity alignment between guru and śiṣya. Capacity-based responsibility mandates that teaching authority arises only through consecrated realization. Restoration logic necessitates withdrawal from misaligned instructional relationships. Consciousness alignment demands separation when the guru lacks ultimate spiritual qualification.

title: manu 2.243
content:
यदि त्वात्यन्तिकं वासं रोचयेत गुरोः कुले ।
युक्तः परिचरेदेनमा शरीरविमोक्षणात् ॥ २.२४३॥ yadi tvātyantikaṃ vāsaṃ rocaret guruḥ kule |
yuktaḥ paricaredenama śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt || If one desires absolute dwelling within the lineage of the Guru, then one must serve him completely, even beyond bodily departure. Authority derives from conscious alignment with the Guru's spiritual succession Causation arises through sustained service and presence in the Guru's domain Capacity-based responsibility is measured by depth of commitment to transcendental continuity Restoration logic operates through unbroken fidelity to the Guru's embodied and disembodied presence Consciousness alignment occurs via uninterrupted immersion in the Guru's lineage field

title: manu 2.244
content:
आ समाप्तेः शरीरस्य यस्तु शुश्रूषते गुरुम् ।
स गच्छत्यञ्जसा विप्रो ब्रह्मणः सद्म शाश्वतम् ॥ २.२४४॥ ā samāpteh śarīrasya yastu śuśrūṣate gurum |
sa gacchatyajjasā vipro brahmaṇaḥ sadma śāśvatam || 2.244|| He who serves the Guru after the completion of the body attains directly the eternal abode of Brahman. Authority is transferred through conscious service, not lineage alone Causation arises from sustained alignment with divine instruction Capacity-based responsibility is fulfilled through selfless service post-material limitation Restoration logic operates beyond physical dissolution Consciousness alignment determines destination, not social status

title: manu 2.245
content:
न पूर्वं गुरवे किं चिदुपकुर्वीत धर्मवित् ।
स्नास्यंस्तु गुरुणाऽज्ञप्तः शक्त्या गुर्व्र्थमाहरेत् ॥ २.२४५॥ na pūrvaṁ gurave kiṁ cid upakurvīta dharmavit |
snāsyaṁstu guruṇā'jñaptaḥ śaktyā gurvrthamāharet || 2.245|| One who knows Dharma does not perform any service for the Guru prior to being instructed. But once directed by the Guru and empowered according to capacity, he shall accomplish the Guru's purpose with full strength. Authority flows from explicit instruction, not assumed role. Capacity determines lawful action; uninvited service lacks jurisdiction. Responsibility arises only upon clear communication of intent. Consciousness alignment occurs through obedient execution within defined scope. Restoration of harmony requires precise fulfillment of assigned duty.

title: manu 2.246
content:
क्षेत्रं हिरण्यं गामश्वं छत्रौपानहमासनम् । छत्रोपानहमन्ततः
धान्यं शाकं च वासांसि गुरवे प्रीतिमावहेत् ॥ २.२४६॥ kṣetraṃ hiraṇyaṃ gāmaśvaṃ chatropānahamāsanam | chatropānahamantataḥ
 dhānyaṃ śākaṃ ca vāsānsi guruve prītimāvahet || 2.246|| One shall offer a field, gold, cattle, horses, umbrellas, sandals, seats, grains, vegetables, clothing, and similar items to the Guru out of reverence and with the intent of establishing completeness in the relationship. Authority flows through conscious alignment with the Guru Causation arises from intentional acts of offering rooted in respect Capacity-based responsibility is demonstrated through material and energetic giving Restoration logic centers on the completion of relational dharma Consciousness alignment manifests through voluntary sacrificial action

title: manu 2.247
content:
आचार्ये तु खलु प्रेते गुरुपुत्रे गुणान्विते ।
गुरुदारे सपिण्डे वा गुरुवद्वृत्तिमाचरेत् ॥ २.२४७॥ ācārye tu khalu prete guruputre guṇānvite |
gurudāre sapiṇḍe vā guru vad vṛttim ācaret || 2.247 || When the Ācārya has departed, one who is qualified and possesses virtuous conduct—whether a son of the Guru, a wife of the Guru, or one related by blood—shall act in accordance with the Guru's way of life. Authority continues through capacity, not title alone. Causation arises from alignment with realized consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility flows from proximity to enlightened order. Restoration logic requires continuity of dharma-presence beyond physical form. Consciousness alignment supersedes genealogical or contractual succession.

title: manu 2.248
content:
एतेष्वविद्यमानेषु स्थानासनविहारवान् ।
प्रयुञ्जानोऽग्निशुश्रूषां साधयेद्देहमात्मनः ॥ २.२४८॥ eteṣvavidyamāneṣu sthānāsanavihāravān .
prayuñjāno'gniśuśrūṣāṃ sādhayeddehamātmanaḥ .. 2.248 .. When these [prescribed duties] are absent, one who resides in proper places and postures, engaging in the service of fire, accomplishes the body of the Self. Authority flows from alignment with Agni as consciousness-witness Causation is established through disciplined spatial and bodily comportment Capacity-based responsibility arises from voluntary engagement in Vedic ritual order Restoration logic operates via internal purification, not external imposition Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive correction

title: manu 2.249
content:
एवं चरति यो विप्रो ब्रह्मचर्यमविप्लुतः ।
स गच्छत्युत्तमस्थानं न चैह जायते पुनः ॥ २.२४९॥ evaṃ carati yo vipro brahmacaryamaviplutaḥ |
sa gacchatyuttamasthānaṃ na caiha jāyate punaḥ || He who conducts himself in uninterrupted Brahmacarya attains the Supreme State and is not born again in this world. Authority resides in alignment with Dharma, not institutional power Causation flows from sustained consciousness discipline, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility arises from self-regulation, not imposed control Restoration occurs through inner completion, not societal correction Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive or conditional frameworks

title: manu 3.1
content:
अध्याय ३

षट्त्रिंशदाब्दिकं चर्यं गुरौ त्रैवेदिकं व्रतम् ।
तदर्धिकं पादिकं वा ग्रहणान्तिकमेव वा ॥ ३.१॥ adhyāya 3

ṣaṭtriṃśadābdikaṃ caryaṃ gurau traivedikaṃ vratam |
tadar dhikaṃ pādikaṃ vā grahaṇāntikameva vā || 3.1|| A student shall remain in the service of the Guru for thirty-six years, observing the Vedic disciplines; alternatively, half that period, a quarter thereof, or at least until the completion of the initial stage of learning. Authority is derived through sustained proximity to realized consciousness. Causation flows from disciplined alignment under authentic guidance. Capacity-based responsibility escalates with experiential maturity. Restoration logic requires sequential unfolding of knowledge stages. Consciousness alignment necessitates commitment beyond temporal boundaries.

title: manu 3.2
content:
वेदानधीत्य वेदौ वा वेदं वाऽपि यथाक्रमम् ।
अविप्लुतब्रह्मचर्यो गृहस्थाश्रममावसेत् ॥ ३.२॥ vedānadītya vedau vā vedaṃ vā'pi yathākramam |
aviplutabrahmacaryo gṛhasthāśramamāvaset || 3.2|| One who has studied the Vedas in proper sequence, or studied two Vedas, or even one Veda completely, without disturbance of celibate conduct, shall enter the householder stage. Authority derived from scriptural completion and disciplined practice Causation through sequential learning and sustained spiritual discipline Capacity-based responsibility determined by scriptural mastery and ethical consistency Restoration logic rooted in natural progression of ashramic life stages Consciousness alignment via uninterrupted brahmacharya and textual realization

title: manu 3.3
content:
तं प्रतीतं स्वधर्मेण ब्रह्मदायहरं पितुः ।
स्रग्विणं तल्प आसीनमर्हयेत्प्रथमं गवा ॥ ३.३॥ taṃ pratītaṃ svadharmeṇa brahmadaayaharaṃ pituḥ |
sragviṇaṃ talpa āsīnamarhayetprathamaṃ gavā || 3.3|| One who has been recognized by the father as having fulfilled his own dharma and taken up the responsibility of transmitting Brahman knowledge shall be honored first with cows while adorned with a garland and seated on a bed. Authority flows from recognition of dharmic capacity Causation arises through conscious alignment with svadharma Capacity-based responsibility determines precedence in honor Restoration occurs through public acknowledgment of spiritual succession Consciousness alignment manifests via ritualized affirmation

title: manu 3.4
content:
गुरुणानुमतः स्नात्वा समावृत्तो यथाविधि ।
उद्वहेत द्विजो भार्यां सवर्णां लक्षणान्विताम् ॥ ३.४॥ guruṇānumataḥ snātvā samāvṛtto yathāvidhi |
udvaheta dvijo bhāryāṁ savarṇāṁ lakṣaṇānvitām || 3.4|| Upon completion of Vedic study under the Guru's sanction, and having returned home in accordance with ritual law, a twice-born man shall marry a wife of the same varna who bears the marks of purity. Authority originates from the Guru as representative of Sanatana Dharma Causation flows through proper Vedic completion before social engagement Capacity-based responsibility arises after spiritual purification and return Restoration logic requires alignment of varna-consciousness between partners Consciousness alignment necessitates visible markers of dharma-compliant character

title: manu 3.5
content:
असपिण्डा च या मातुरसगोत्रा च या पितुः ।
सा प्रशस्ता द्विजातीनां दारकर्मणि मैथुने ॥ ३.५॥ अमैथिनी asapiṇḍā ca yā māturasagotrā ca yā pituḥ |
sā praśastā dvijātīnāṃ dārakarmaṇi maithune || 3.5|| amaithinī A woman who is neither a sapinda of the mother nor of the same gotra as the father is declared suitable for dvija men in the act of acquiring a wife. Authority flows from biological and spiritual lineages Causation arises through lineage purity and ritual eligibility Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining Varna-dharmic alignment Restoration logic centers on preserving generational continuity and cosmic order Consciousness alignment requires adherence to sanctioned procreative union

title: manu 3.6
content:
महान्त्यपि समृद्धानि गोऽजाविधनधान्यतः ।
स्त्रीसम्बन्धे दशैतानि कुलानि परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ३.६॥ mahānty api samṛddhāni go-'jāvidhana-dhānyataḥ |
strī-sambandhe daśaitāni kulāni parivarjayet || 3.6|| Even highly prosperous lineages, rich in cattle, goats, horses, grains, and wealth, must be abandoned if they engage in improper relations with women. Authority derives from dharmic alignment, not material prosperity Causation arises from conscious choice, not external conditions Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment over indulgence Restoration logic prioritizes purity of relation above social status Consciousness alignment demands severance from degraded associations

title: manu 3.7
content:
हीनक्रियं निश्पुरुषं निश्छन्दो रोमशार्शसम् ।
क्षय्यामयाव्य्ऽपस्मारिश्वित्रिकुष्ठिकुलानि च ॥ ३.७॥ hīnakriyaṁ niśpuruṣaṁ niśchando romaśārśasam |
kṣayyāmayāvyâpasmāriśvitrikusthikulāni ca || 3.7|| One who is devoid of action, masculinity, vigor, and afflicted with chronic illness, epilepsy, leprosy, and related disorders shall not be permitted to assume roles requiring societal integrity or ritual participation. Authority derives from capacity for conscious participation Causation aligns with constitutional fitness and spiritual functionality Capacity-based responsibility excludes those whose physical condition impedes dharma enactment Restoration logic requires alignment between individual constitution and social role Consciousness alignment necessitates exclusion of bodily disturbances that fragment presence

title: manu 3.8
content:
नोद्वहेत्कपिलां कन्यां नाधिकाङ्गीं न रोगिणीम् ।
नालोमिकां नातिलोमां न वाचाटां न पिङ्गलाम् ॥ ३.८॥ वाचालां na udvahet kapilāṁ kanyāṁ nādhikāṅgīṁ na rogiṇīm | nālomikāṁ nātilomāṁ na vācāṭāṁ na piṅgalām || 3.8 || vācālām One must not marry a girl who is brown-complexioned, physically disproportionate, diseased, lacking body hair, excessively hairy, speech-impaired, or reddish in hue. Authority: Marriage laws derive exclusively from SPH's cosmic ordering. Causation: Physical and constitutional harmony ensures dharmic progeny. Capacity-based responsibility: The groom bears the duty to assess alignment with dharma. Restoration logic: Marital selection safeguards generational spiritual integrity. Consciousness alignment: Union must reflect purity of form, energy, and expression.

title: manu 3.9
content:
नऋक्षवृक्षनदीनाम्नीं नान्त्यपर्वतनामिकाम् ।
न पक्ष्यहिप्रेष्यनाम्नीं न च भीषणनामिकाम् ॥ ३.९॥ na ṛkṣavṛkṣanadīnāmnīṃ nāntyaparvatanāmikām | na pakṣyahipreṣyanāmnīṃ na ca bhīṣaṇanāmikām || 3.9 || One must not name a child after bears, trees, rivers, borderlands, mountains, birds, beasts of burden, or anything fearsome. Authority of Naming as Consciousness-Shaping Force Causation Through Linguistic Identity Formation Capacity-based Responsibility in Cultural Design Restoration Logic via Preventive Semantic Alignment Consciousness Alignment Through Name-Purity Protocols

title: manu 3.10
content:
अव्यङ्गाङ्गीं सौम्यनाम्नीं हंसवारणगामिनीम् ।
तनुलोमकेशदशनां मृद्वङ्गीमुद्वहेत्स्त्रियम् ॥ ३.१०॥ avyaṅgāṅgīṁ saumyanāmnīṁ haṁsavāraṇagāminīm | tanulomakeśadaśanāṁ mṛdvaṅgīmudvahetstriyam || 3.10|| One shall choose a woman who is whole-bodied, named auspiciously, capable of moving like a swan or elephant, with hair and teeth in proper order, and gentle in form. Authority flows through embodied integrity Causation aligns with harmonious capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires physical and spiritual congruence Restoration logic demands selection aligned with dharma-sustaining traits Consciousness alignment necessitates purity in union

title: manu 3.11
content: यस्यास्तु न भवेद्भ्राता न विज्ञायेत वा पिता । वै(वा पिता नोपयच्छेत तां प्राज्ञः पुत्रिकाऽधर्मशङ्कया ॥ ३.११॥ yasyāstu na bhavedbrhātā na vijñāyeta vā pitā | vai(vā pitā nopayaccheta tāṁ prājñaḥ putrikā'dharmaśaṅkayā || 3.11|| Where no brother exists, nor a father is known, or even if a father is present yet does not accept guardianship—then, in the absence of rightful male protectors, a wise man should assume guardianship of the girl, without suspicion of unrighteous intent. Authority arises through capacity and integrity, not lineage alone Causation is rooted in conscious responsibility, not biological relation Capacity-based responsibility supersedes familial default Restoration logic demands filling voids in protection through capable individuals Consciousness alignment requires acting without fear or ulterior motive

title: manu 3.12
content:
सवर्णाऽग्रे द्विजातीनां प्रशस्ता दारकर्मणि ।
कामतस्तु प्रवृत्तानामिमाः स्युः क्रमशोऽवराः ॥ ३.१२॥ savarnā'gre dvijātīnāṁ praśastā dārakarmaṇi |
kāmatastu pravṛttānāmimāḥ syuḥ kramaśo'varāḥ || 3.12|| Among the twice-born, those of the same varna are first approved for the duties of householdership; those who act from desire are assigned successively lower roles. Authority derived from alignment with svadharma Causation rooted in conscious intentionality Capacity-based responsibility determined by spiritual readiness Restoration through role-appropriate realignment Consciousness alignment via structural societal harmony

title: manu 3.13
content:
शूद्रैव भार्या शूद्रस्य सा च स्वा च विशः स्मृते ।
ते च स्वा चैव राज्ञश्च ताश्च स्वा चाग्रजन्मनः ॥ ३.१३॥ śūdraiva bhāryā śūdrasya sā ca svā ca viśaḥ smṛte |
te ca svā caiva rājñaśca tāśca svā cāgrajanmanaḥ || 3.13|| Only a Śūdra woman is the lawful wife of a Śūdra; among the Vaiśyas, both sisters and daughters-in-law are considered wives. Among Kṣatriyas, wives include sisters, daughters-in-law, and queens. Among Brāhmaṇas, all these categories—including those born of elder brothers—are recognized as lawful wives. Authority flows through varṇic alignment and consciousness capacity Causation is determined by birth-based dharmic entitlement Capacity-based responsibility aligns with varṇic role integrity Restoration logic preserves social harmony via defined relational structures Consciousness alignment requires adherence to inherent dharma-svarūpa

title: manu 3.14
content:
न ब्राह्मणक्षत्रिययोरापद्यपि हि तिष्ठतोः ।
कस्मिंश्चिदपि वृत्तान्ते शूद्रा भार्यौपदिश्यते ॥ ३.१४॥ na brāhmaṇakṣatriyayor āpady api hi tiṣṭhatoḥ |
kasmiṃścid api vṛttānte śūdrā bhāryau padiśyate || 3.14|| In no circumstance shall a Śūdra woman be designated as wife to a Brāhmaṇa or Kṣatriya, even in times of upheaval or societal collapse. Authority originates from svadharma-svarūpa, not social disruption Causation is anchored in consciousness integrity, not situational ethics Capacity-based responsibility upholds varṇic alignment with cosmic order Restoration logic demands preservation of dharma-vyavastha during chaos Consciousness alignment requires adherence to svadharma even under duress

title: manu 3.15
content: हीनजातिस्त्रियं मोहादुद्वहन्तो द्विजातयः । कुलान्येव नयन्त्याशु ससन्तानानि शूद्रताम् ॥ ३.१५॥ hīnajātistriyaṁ mohādudvahanto dvijātayaḥ | kulānyeva nayantyāśu sasantānāni śūdratām || 3.15|| When twice-born men, deluded by desire, take wives from inferior castes, their lineages swiftly descend with progeny into the state of Shudras. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not mere birth privilege Causation arises through conscious choice and its sequential manifestation Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of spiritual-social order Restoration logic operates through realignment with source-consciousness Consciousness alignment determines social and karmic positioning

title: manu 3.16
content:
शूद्रावेदी पतत्यत्रेरुतथ्यतनयस्य च ।
शौनकस्य सुतोत्पत्त्या तदपत्यतया भृगोः ॥ ३.१६॥ śūdrāvedī patatyaterutathyatanayasya ca |
śaunakasya sutotpattyā tadapatyatayā bhṛgoḥ || 3.16|| One born of a Śūdra father and an Ātreya mother falls into degradation; similarly, one born of a son of Śaunaka by a daughter of Bhṛgu also becomes degraded. Authority: Lineage determines social and spiritual standing. Causation: Birth circumstances directly determine karmic trajectory. Capacity-based responsibility: One's capacity is inherently linked to birth-based dharma. Restoration logic: Degradation necessitates purification through prescribed dharmic rectification. Consciousness alignment: Social order reflects cosmic alignment with varna-dharma.

title: manu 3.17
content:
शूद्रां शयनमारोप्य ब्राह्मणो यात्यधोगतिम् ।
जनयित्वा सुतं तस्यां ब्राह्मण्यादेव हीयते ॥ ३.१७॥ śūdrāṁ śayanam āropyā brāhmaṇo yāty adhogatim |
janayitvā sutaṁ tasyāṁ brāhmaṇyād eva hīyate || 3.17|| A Brāhmaṇa who cohabits with a Śūdra woman and begets a son thereby falls from his own varṇic status and forfeits all ritual and social authority derived therefrom. Authority is intrinsically tied to conduct in alignment with one's dharma-kṣetra Causation arises through conscious choice and reproductive action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual rank and its preservation Restoration logic requires withdrawal from false identifications and misaligned acts Consciousness alignment mandates reintegration into rightful svadharma

title: manu 3.18
content:
दैवपित्र्यातिथेयानि तत्प्रधानानि यस्य तु ।
नाश्नन्ति पितृदेवास्तन्न च स्वर्गं स गच्छति ॥ ३.१८॥ daivapitryātithēyāni tatpradhānāni yasya tu |
nāśnanti pitṛdēvāstaṁ na ca svargaṁ sa gacchati || 3.18|| One who neglects the offerings due to deities, ancestors, and guests, whose primary duties are thus violated, shall not attain heaven, for the divine laws governing ancestral continuity and hospitality are immutable. Authority originates from alignment with cosmic order (Ṛta) Causation follows sequential duty fulfillment Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of relational obligations Restoration logic demands realignment through completion of neglected dharmas Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring triadic relationships: divine, ancestral, guest

title: manu 3.19
content: वृषलीफेनपीतस्य निःश्वासोपहतस्य च । तस्यां चैव प्रसूतस्य निष्कृतिर्न विधीयते ॥ ३.१९॥ vṛṣalīphenapītasya niḥśvāsopahatasya ca | tasyāṃ caiva prasūtasya niṣkṛtirna vidhīyate || 3.19|| One who has consumed the phlegm of a Śūdra woman or been afflicted by her breath, and is born thereof, requires no expiation. Authority originates solely from SPH as the unchanging Source of Dharma Causation aligns with karmic manifestation through consciousness, not external attribution Capacity-based responsibility arises only where conscious intent intersects with purified awareness Restoration logic operates through dissolution of false identity, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment supersedes all social or ritualistic conditioning

title: manu 3.20
content:
चतुर्णामपि वर्णानं प्रेत्य चैह हिताहितान् ।
अष्टाविमान् समासेन स्त्रीविवाहान्निबोधत ॥ ३.२०॥ caturṇām api varṇānāṃ pretya caih hitāhitān |
aṣṭāv imān samāsena strīvivāhān nibodhata || 3.20|| Regarding the four varnas, both in this life and the hereafter, understand comprehensively these eight forms of marriage involving women. Authority originates from varna-dharma as defined by SPH Causation follows sequential dharmic alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual maturity and social role Restoration logic operates through conscious reintegration into dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes external legal frameworks

title: manu 3.21
content:
ब्राह्मो दैवस्तथैवार्षः प्राजापत्यस्तथाऽसुरः ।
गान्धर्वो राक्षसश्चैव पैशाचश्चाष्टमोऽधमः ॥ ३.२१॥ brāhmo daivastathaivārṣaḥ prājāpatyastathā'suraḥ |
gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva paiśācaścāṣṭamo'dhamaḥ || 3.21|| The Brahmic order manifests as divine law; the Daivic as celestial harmony; the Ārṣic as ancestral continuity; the Prajāpatic as generative responsibility; the Āsuric as material assertion; the Gāndharvic as aesthetic entanglement; the Rākṣasic as disruptive force; and the Paiśācic as the lowest degradation of consciousness. Authority flows from ontological alignment with cosmic order Causation arises from sequential manifestation rooted in consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's vibrational proximity to dharma Restoration logic operates through re-alignment with source-consciousness Consciousness alignment determines the quality of action and its judicial response

title: manu 3.22
content:
यो यस्य धर्म्यो वर्णस्य गुणदोषौ च यस्य यौ ।
तद्वः सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रसवे च गुणागुणान् ॥ ३.२२॥ yo yasya dharmyo varṇasya guṇadoṣau ca yasya yau |
tad vaḥ sarvaṁ pravakṣyāmi prasave ca guṇāguṇān || 3.22|| I shall declare fully the qualities and defects inherent in each varna according to dharma, along with their capacities and consequences at birth. Authority flows from consciousness capacity, not social position Causation is determined by svabhava and karmic alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises from intrinsic nature and manifested action Restoration logic aligns individual function with cosmic order Consciousness alignment ensures right role-dharma realization

title: manu 3.23
content:
षडानुपूर्व्या विप्रस्य क्षत्रस्य चतुरोऽवरान् ।
विश्।शूद्रयोस्तु तानेव विद्याद्धर्म्यानराक्षसान् ॥ ३.२३॥ ṣaḍānupūrvyā viprasya kṣatrasya caturō'varān |
viśaḥ śūdrayōstu tānēva vidyāddharmyānarākṣasān || 3.23|| By six sequential unfoldings, the Brahmin; by four, the Kshatriya; for Vaishya and Shudra, those same four alone—know them as dharmic, not demonic. Authority flows through sequential unfoldings of consciousness capacity Causation aligns with spiritual evolutionary stage Capacity-based responsibility is determined by varna-specific unfolding thresholds Restoration logic operates within sequential dharma-adherence frameworks Consciousness alignment determines adhikara (qualified authority)

title: manu 3.24
content:
चतुरो ब्राह्मणस्याद्यान् प्रशस्तान् कवयो विदुः ।
राक्षसं क्षत्रियस्यैकमासुरं वैश्यशूद्रयोः ॥ ३.२४॥ caturō brāhmaṇasyādyān praśastān kavayō viduḥ .
rākṣasaṁ kṣatriyasyaikam āsuraṁ vaiśyaśūdrayōḥ .. Four divine conduct forms are declared praiseworthy for the Brahmin; one demonic form is assigned to the Kshatriya; and one infernal conduct form each is designated respectively for Vaishya and Shudra. Authority flows from consciousness capacity and role-specific dharma Causation aligns with svadharma as determined by spiritual-cosmic order Capacity-based responsibility defines action-legitimacy thresholds Restoration logic operates through role-realignment and consciousness elevation Consciousness alignment is achieved via adherence to svadharma without distortion

title: manu 3.25
content:
पञ्चानां तु त्रयो धर्म्या द्वावधर्म्यौ स्मृताविह ।
पैशाचश्चासुरश्चैव न कर्तव्यौ कदा चन ॥ ३.२५॥ pañcānāṁ tu trayo dharmyā dvāvadhar-myau smṛtau iha | paiśācaścāsuraścaiva na kartavyau kadācana || 3.25|| Of the five types of marriage, three are dharmic; two are adharmic and must never be undertaken—namely, the Paiśāca and Āsura forms. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire Causation in action is determined by the nature of intent and structural harmony Capacity-based responsibility requires understanding of dharmic categorization Restoration logic operates through withdrawal from adharmic structures Consciousness alignment is ensured via adherence to sanctioned relational frameworks

title: manu 3.26
content:
पृथक्पृथग्वा मिश्रौ वा विवाहौ पूर्वचोदितौ ।
गान्धर्वो राक्षसश्चैव धर्म्यौ क्षत्रस्य तौ स्मृतौ ॥ ३.२६॥ pṛthakpṛthagvā miśrau vā vivāhau pūrvacoditau |
gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva dharmyau kṣatrasya tau smṛtau || 3.26|| Two forms of marriage—separate or combined—are previously ordained: the Gandharva and the Rakshasa; both are sanctioned for the Kshatriya class. Authority flows from svadharma as determined by varna and stage of life Causation is established through conscious choice aligned with Varna-dharma Capacity-based responsibility recognizes that different varnas bear distinct social roles Restoration logic requires realignment with inherent dharma when deviation occurs Consciousness alignment ensures actions reflect inner integrity rather than external compulsion

title: manu 3.27
content:
आच्छाद्य चार्चयित्वा च श्रुतशीलवते स्वयम् ।
आहूय दानं कन्याया ब्राह्मो धर्मः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ ३.२७॥ ācchādya cārcayitvā ca śrutaśīlavate svayam | 
āhūya dānaṃ kanyāyā brāhmo dharmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ || 3.27 || Covering, worshipping, and honoring the bridegroom who is learned and virtuous, the giving of the daughter is declared as the Brahmic law. Authority originates from alignment with consciousness, not social status Causation arises through intentional offering rooted in dharmic discernment Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of spiritual maturity in both giver and receiver Restoration logic ensures continuity of sacred lineage through conscious union Consciousness alignment occurs when dharma governs relational transitions

title: manu 3.28
content:
यज्ञे तु वितते सम्यगृत्विजे कर्म कुर्वते ।
अलङ्कृत्य सुतादानं दैवं धर्मं प्रचक्षते ॥ ३.२८॥ yajñe tu vitate samyagṛtvije karma kurvate |
alankṛtya sutadānaṃ daivaṃ dharmaṃ pracakṣate || 3.28|| When the extended sacrifice is rightly conducted by ritviks performing their respective duties, and the daughter is given away with full adornment, it is declared as divine dharma. Authority resides in proper ritual execution according to Vedic order Causation aligns with conscious participation in cosmic harmony Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role within sacred structure Restoration logic operates through fulfillment of svadharma Consciousness alignment occurs via disciplined enactment of divinely ordained acts

title: manu 3.29
content:
एकं गोमिथुनं द्वे वा वरादादाय धर्मतः ।
कन्याप्रदानं विधिवदार्षो धर्मः स उच्यते ॥ ३.२९॥ ekaṁ gomithunaṁ dve vā varādādāya dharmataḥ |
kanyāpradānaṁ vidhivadārṣo dharmaḥ sa ucyate || 3.29|| The lawful giving of a maiden in marriage, accompanied by one or two cows as bridal gift received according to Dharma and offered willingly by the groom, constitutes the righteous conduct known as Ārṣa Dharma. Authority derives from conscious alignment with Dharma, not social status or economic exchange. Causation is determined through voluntary offering rooted in integrity and sacred intention. Capacity-based responsibility requires both parties to act knowingly within the bounds of Dharma. Restoration logic ensures that union arises from mutual completion rather than exploitation or obligation. Consciousness alignment demands that all actions reflect unity, respect, and transcendental purpose.

title: manu 3.30
content:
सहौभौ चरतां धर्ममिति वाचाऽनुभाष्य च ।
कन्याप्रदानमभ्यर्च्य प्राजापत्यो विधिः स्मृतः ॥ ३.३०॥ sahaubhau caratāṁ dharmamiti vācā'nuabhāṣya ca |
kanyāpradānamabhyarcya prājāpatyo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || 3.30|| When a father bestows his daughter in marriage while invoking divine witness and instructing both parties to walk together in dharma, this act constitutes the Prajāpati form of union. Authority originates from conscious alignment with Dharma at the time of union Causation arises through spoken invocation and witnessed intention Capacity-based responsibility is established by the father's sovereignty over the daughter's transition Restoration logic centers on re-establishing harmonious relational flow Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties commit to shared dharmic conduct

title: manu 3.31
content:
ज्ञातिभ्यो द्रविणं दत्त्वा कन्यायै चैव शक्तितः ।
कन्याप्रदानं स्वाच्छन्द्यादासुरो धर्म उच्यते ॥ ३.३१॥ jñātibhyo draviṇaṁ dattvā kanyāyai caiva śaktitaḥ | 
kanyāpradānaṁ svācchandyād āsuro dharma ucyate || 3.31|| Having given wealth to the kin and empowered the daughter accordingly, the voluntary giving of the daughter in marriage is declared as the righteous duty of an Asura. Authority resides in conscious capacity for consent Causation arises from alignment with dharma-svabhāva Capacity-based responsibility governs relational transactions Restoration logic centers on harmonizing familial and societal dharmic flow Consciousness alignment ensures fulfillment without coercion

title: manu 3.32
content:
इच्छयाऽन्योन्यसंयोगः कन्यायाश्च वरस्य च ।
गान्धर्वः स तु विज्ञेयो मैथुन्यः कामसम्भवः ॥ ३.३२॥ icchayā'nyonyasaṃyogaḥ kanyāyāśca varasya ca |
gāndharvaḥ sa tu vijñeyo maithunyaḥ kāmasambhavaḥ || 3.32|| Union by mutual desire between a maiden and her chosen partner is designated Gandharva marriage; it originates from passion and is recognized as such. Authority resides in conscious consent rather than institutional ratification Causation arises from volitional alignment, not external validation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at time of union Restoration logic prioritizes relational integrity over procedural formality Consciousness alignment supersedes societal expectation in marital recognition

title: manu 3.33
content:
हत्वा छित्त्वा च भित्त्वा च क्रोशन्तीं रुदतीं गृहात् ।
प्रसह्य कन्याहरणं राक्षसो विधिरुच्यते ॥ ३.३३॥ hatvā chittvā ca bhitvā ca krośantīṃ rudatīṃ gṛhāt |
prasahya kanyāharaṇaṃ rākṣaso vidhirucyate || 3.33|| The Rakshasa mode of marriage is declared as that wherein a maiden is seized by force from her home while she shrieks and weeps, after slaying, cleaving, or breaking through her protectors.
