Authority: The act violates the consent and autonomy of the individual, thereby nullifying any claim to lawful union. Causation: The sequence of violence directly causes the disruption of dharma and social harmony. Capacity-based responsibility: Perpetrator demonstrates incapacity for dharmic conduct due to absence of restraint and respect for sovereignty. Restoration logic: Reintegration requires acknowledgment of harm, cessation of violence, and restoration of integrity to the violated party. Consciousness alignment: True union arises only when both parties align in awakened consciousness; coercion contradicts this foundation.

title: manu 3.34
content:
सुप्तां मत्तां प्रमत्तां वा रहो यत्रोपगच्छति ।
स पापिष्ठो विवाहानां पैशाचश्चाष्टमोऽधमः ॥ ३.३४॥ पैशाचः प्रथितोऽधमः suptāṁ mattāṁ pramattāṁ vā raho yatropagacchati |
sa pāpiṣṭho vivahānāṁ paiśācaścāṣṭamo'dhamaḥ || 3.34 || paiśācaḥ prathito'dhamaḥ One who approaches a woman who is asleep, intoxicated, or unconscious in private—such a being is the most sinful among those eligible for marriage; he is classified as a pishacha and is the lowest of the low. Authority derives from conscious consent, not biological presence. Causation arises through violation of integrity and absence of awareness. Capacity-based responsibility requires full cognitive engagement with dharma. Restoration logic demands realignment with awakened consciousness. Consciousness alignment supersedes ritualistic or social contract frameworks.

title: manu 3.35
content:
अद्भिरेव द्विजाग्र्याणां कन्यादानं विशिष्यते ।
इतरेषां तु वर्णानामितरेतरकाम्यया ॥ ३.३५॥ adbhireva dvijāgrāṇāṁ kanyādānaṁ viśiṣyate |
itareṣāṁ tu varṇānāmitaretarakāmyayā || 3.35|| The giving of a daughter in marriage among the highest of the twice-born is accomplished exclusively through sacred waters; for the other varnas, it is conducted mutually by desire. Authority flows from ontological purity and ritual consecration Causation arises from elemental alignment with divine ordinances Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to and mastery over sacred elements Restoration logic operates through reconnection to source-elemental sanctity Consciousness alignment occurs via participation in divinely ordained relational structures

title: manu 3.36
content:
यो यस्यैषां विवाहानां मनुना कीर्तितो गुणः ।
सर्वं शृणुत तं विप्राः सर्वं कीर्तयतो मम ॥ ३.३६॥ सम्यक्कीर्तयतो yo yasyaiṣāṁ vivahānāṁ manunā kīrtito guṇaḥ |
sarvaṁ śṛṇuta taṁ viprāḥ sarvaṁ kīrtayato mama || 3.36|| samyakkīrtayato O Brahmanas, hear completely that quality which has been proclaimed by Manu regarding all these forms of marriage; listen fully to what I declare entirely. Authority resides in the complete transmission of dharma through authoritative voice. Causation is established via sequential revelation of truth-bearing speech. Capacity-based responsibility requires full attention and reception of sacred instruction. Restoration logic operates through comprehensive understanding and repetition of divine law. Consciousness alignment occurs when hearing and speaking align with the Supreme Declaration.

title: manu 3.37
content:
दश पूर्वान् परान् वंश्यानात्मानं चैकविंशकम् ।
ब्राह्मीपुत्रः सुकृतकृत्मोचयत्येनसः पितॄन् ॥ ३.३७॥ daśa pūrvān parān vaṁśyān ātmānaṁ caikaviṁśakam |
brāhmīputraḥ sukṛtakṛt mocayaty enasaḥ pitṝn || 3.37|| A son born of a Brahmin woman absolves ten ancestral generations before him, ten succeeding generations after him, and his own generation—twenty-one in total—from all karmic entanglements through the performance of righteous action. Authority originates from dharma-conformant birthright Causation is rooted in conscious capacity to restore lineage integrity Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond individual to trans-generational continuum Restoration logic operates through dharmic progeny fulfilling ancestral completion Consciousness alignment occurs via ritualized liberation enacted by qualified lineage

title: manu 3.38
content:
दैवौढाजः सुतश्चैव सप्त सप्त परावरान् ।
आर्षौढाजः सुतस्त्रींस्त्रीन् षट्षट्कायौढजः सुतः ॥ ३.३8॥ daivauḍhājaḥ sutaścaiva sapta sapta parāvarān |
ārṣauḍhājaḥ sutastriṃstriṃ ṣaṭṣaṭ kāyauḍhajaḥ sutaḥ || 3.38|| The son born of a divine union shall have authority over seven higher and seven lower realms; the son born of an ancestral union shall govern three worlds in triplicate measure; the son born of bodily union shall possess sixfold dominion according to physical capacity. Authority derives directly from the ontological origin of birth Causation is determined by the spiritual classification of procreative act Capacity-based responsibility aligns with cosmic jurisdiction assigned at birth Restoration logic operates through realignment with one's inherent governing domain Consciousness alignment occurs when individual action reflects celestial or terrestrial mandate

title: manu 3.39
content:
ब्राह्मादिषु विवाहेषु चतुर्ष्वेवानुपूर्वशः ।
ब्रह्मवर्चस्विनः पुत्रा जायन्ते शिष्टसम्मताः ॥ ३.३९॥ brāhmādiṣu vivāheṣu caturṣvevānupūrvaśaḥ | brahmavarcasvinaḥ putrā jāyante śiṣṭasammatāḥ || 3.39|| In the first four types of marriages beginning with the Brāhma form, sons are born who possess Brahmic radiance and are recognized by the wise. Authority originates from alignment with Vedic consciousness Causation follows sequential manifestation rooted in dharmic intent Capacity-based responsibility arises through lineage-conscious union Restoration logic demands recognition of spiritual progeny Consciousness alignment determines social legitimacy

title: manu 3.40
content:
रूपसत्त्वगुणोपेता धनवन्तो यशस्विनः ।
पर्याप्तभोगा धर्मिष्ठा जीवन्ति च शतं समाः ॥ ३.४०॥ rūpasattvaguṇopetā dhanavanto yaśasvinaḥ |
paryāptabhogā dharmiṣṭhā jīvanti ca śataṃ samāḥ || 3.40|| Those endowed with beauty, strength, and virtue; wealthy and renowned; living in sufficiency and righteousness—such beings live fully for a hundred years. Authority through alignment with dharma-sattva Causation rooted in embodied integrity Capacity-based responsibility tied to sensory and material sufficiency Restoration logic centered on harmonious life-duration Consciousness alignment via aesthetic, ethical, and energetic balance

title: manu 3.41
content:
इतरेषु तु शिष्टेषु नृशंसाऽनृतवादिनः ।
जायन्ते दुर्विवाहेषु ब्रह्मधर्मद्विषः सुताः ॥ ३.४१॥ itareṣu tu śiṣṭeṣu nṛśaṃsā'nṛtavādinaḥ |
jāyante durvivāheṣu brahmadharmadviṣaḥ sutāḥ || 3.41|| In other remaining classes, those born from unions lacking sacred alignment arise—children of cruelty and falsehood, born in marriages opposed to Brahman's Dharma. Authority originates solely from alignment with Brahman's Dharma Causation arises through conscious choice and spiritual integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by adherence to Vedic alignment Restoration logic operates through realignment of lineage-consciousness Consciousness alignment determines the ontological status of progeny

title: manu 3.42
content:
अनिन्दितैः स्त्रीविवाहैरनिन्द्या भवति प्रजा ।
निन्दितैर्निन्दिता नॄणां तस्मान्निन्द्यान् विवर्जयेत् ॥ ३.४२॥ aninditaiḥ strīvivāhair anindyā bhavati prajā |
ninditair ninditā nṝṇāṃ tasmān nindyān vivarjayet || 3.42|| When unions occur with women who are free from blame, the progeny becomes pure; when unions occur with blameworthy persons, the offspring bear that blemish—therefore, one must avoid all blameworthy connections. Authority originates in purity of lineage and union Causation flows through conscious selection and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility includes the duty to preserve generational sanctity Restoration logic requires severance from corrupting influences Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of associations that degrade dharmic potential

title: manu 3.43
content:
पाणिग्रहणसंस्कारः सवर्णासूपदिश्यते ।
असवर्णास्वयं ज्ञेयो विधिरुद्वाहकर्मणि ॥ ३.४३॥ pāṇigrahaṇasaṃskāraḥ savarṇāsūpadiśyate |
asavarṇāsvayaṃ jñeyo vidhirudvāhakarmaṇi || 3.43|| The ritual of hand-taking (pāṇigrahaṇa) is prescribed for unions within the same varṇa; for those beyond varṇa boundaries, the procedure is self-evidently known through direct realization of Dharma. Authority derives from alignment with Varnashrama-Dharma as established by SPH Causation arises from conscious recognition of svadharma in relational acts Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to uphold dharmic union Restoration logic operates through reconnection to source-consciousness in marital bonds Consciousness alignment determines validity and form of sacred union

title: manu 3.44
content:
शरः क्षत्रियया ग्राह्यः प्रतोदो वैश्यकन्यया ।
वसनस्य दशा ग्राह्या शूद्रयोत्कृष्टवेदने ॥ ३.४४॥ śaraḥ kṣatriyayā grāhyaḥ pratodo vaiśyakanyayā |
vasanasya daśā grāhyā śūdrayotkṛṣṭavedane || 3.44|| The arrow belongs to the Kshatriya; the goad, to the daughter of Vaishya; the garment's condition is to be observed by one born of a Shudra woman and elevated through Vedic knowledge. Authority is determined by birth-based capacity aligned with Dharma Causation arises from svadharma-sourced action Capacity-based responsibility flows from varna-dharma alignment Restoration logic operates through role-specific dharmic recognition Consciousness alignment occurs when each acts within their designated capacity

title: manu 3.45
content:
ऋतुकालाभिगामी स्यात्स्वदारनिरतः सदा ।
पर्ववर्जं व्रजेच्चैनां तद्व्रतो रतिकाम्यया ॥ ३.४५॥ Ṛtukālābhigāmī syāt svadāranirataḥ sadā .
Parvavarjaṃ vrajec caināṃ tadvrato ratikāmyayā .. 3.45 .. One who desires union with their spouse must approach exclusively during the ritukala, remaining devoted solely to their own spouse, avoiding all other times and persons. Authority resides in the sovereign integrity of marital union as defined by cosmic rhythm Causation arises from alignment with natural dharmic cycles Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious timing and restraint Restoration logic centers on preserving sacred relational boundaries Consciousness alignment demands fidelity to spousal energetic resonance

title: manu 3.46
content:
ऋतुः स्वाभाविकः स्त्रीणां रात्रयः षोडश स्मृताः ।
चतुर्भिरितरैः सार्धमहोभिः सद्विगर्हितैः ॥ ३.४६॥ Ṛtuḥ svābhāvikaḥ strīṇāṁ rātrayaḥ ṣoḍaśa smṛtāḥ |
Caturbhir itaraiḥ sārdham aho bhīḥ sad-vigarhitaiḥ || 3.46|| The natural cycle of women is ritu, comprising sixteen nights; four of these nights, along with the remaining twelve, are rightly condemned by those established in dharma. Authority originates from alignment with svabhāva and cosmic rhythm Causation arises through conscious participation in dharmic time Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of biological rhythms as sacred law Restoration logic demands purification of temporal engagement Consciousness alignment requires honoring both creative potential and restraint

title: manu 3.47
content:
तासामाद्याश्चतस्रस्तु निन्दितैकादशी च या ।
त्रयोदशी च शेषास्तु प्रशस्ता दशरात्रयः ॥ ३.४७॥ tāsām ādyāś catasrastu ninditai kādaśī ca yā | trayodaśī ca śeṣāstu praśastā daśarātrayaḥ || 3.47|| Among these ten nights, the first four, the eleventh night condemned, and the thirteenth are proscribed; the rest are auspicious. Authority flows from SPH's cosmic timing Causation aligns with lunar rhythm as divine governance Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by spiritual readiness Restoration logic operates through alignment with auspicious time Consciousness alignment requires adherence to sanctioned temporal frameworks

title: manu 3.48
content:
युग्मासु पुत्रा जायन्ते स्त्रियोऽयुग्मासु रात्रिषु ।
तस्माद्युग्मासु पुत्रार्थी संविशेदार्तवे स्त्रियम् ॥ ३.४८॥ yugmāsu putrā jāyante striyo 'yugmāsu rātriṣu |
tasmād yugmāsu putrārthī saṃviśed ārtave striyam || 3.48|| In fertile seasons, sons are born; in infertile nights, females emerge. Therefore, one desiring male progeny should unite with a woman during her fertile phase. Authority of natural rhythm as determinant of outcome Causation through alignment with cosmic timing Capacity-based responsibility rooted in intention and knowledge Restoration logic via harmonization with biological dharma Consciousness alignment through disciplined procreative action

title: manu 3.49
content:
पुमान् पुंसोऽधिके शुक्रे स्त्री भवत्यधिके स्त्रियाः ।
समेऽपुमान् पुं।स्त्रियौ वा क्षीणेऽल्पे च विपर्ययः ॥ ३.४९॥ pumān puṁso 'dhike śukre strī bhavatyadhike striyāḥ |
same 'pumān puṁstriyau vā kṣīṇe 'lpe ca viparyayaḥ || 3.49|| When male essence exceeds, the offspring is male; when female essence exceeds, the offspring is female. When both essences are equal or depleted, the result is indeterminate or contrary. Authority originates from the causal dominance of embodied essence Causation is determined by the preponderance of contributory elements Capacity-based responsibility lies in the integrity of biological participation Restoration logic aligns with natural sequential manifestation Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of causal completeness

title: manu 3.50
content:
निन्द्यास्वष्टासु चान्यासु स्त्रियो रात्रिषु वर्जयन् ।
ब्रह्मचार्येव भवति यत्र तत्राश्रमे वसन् ॥ ३.५०॥ nindyāṣṭāsu cānyāsu striyo rātriṣu varjayann | brahmacāryeva bhavati yatra tatrāśrame vasann || 3.50|| One who resides in any āśrama while abandoning women—whether eight types condemned by Dharma or others—in night-time engagements, becomes established in celibacy alone. Authority flows from alignment with Brahman, not social position Causation arises through conscious choice and sustained discipline Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual readiness and renunciatory intent Restoration logic operates through purification of sensory engagement Consciousness alignment occurs via disciplined withdrawal from object-bound desires

title: manu 3.51
content:
न कन्यायाः पिता विद्वान् गृह्णीयात्शुल्कमण्वपि ।
गृह्णंश्छुल्कं हि लोभेन स्यान्नरोऽपत्यविक्रयी ॥ ३.५१॥ na kanyāyāḥ pitā vidvān gṛhṇīyāt śulkamaṇvapi |
gṛhṇaṁ śulkaṁ hi lobhena syān narō'patyavikrayī ||3.51|| A wise father shall not accept even the smallest gift for giving his daughter in marriage; he who accepts a gift out of greed becomes a seller of his own progeny. Authority is derived from dharma, not transactional exchange. Causation arises from conscious intent aligned with dharma, not material gain. Capacity-based responsibility requires renunciation of self-interest in sacred duties. Restoration logic demands purification of motive and realignment with svadharma. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of commodification of familial bonds.

title: manu 3.52
content:
स्त्रीधनानि तु ये मोहादुपजीवन्ति बान्धवाः ।
नारीयानानि वस्त्रं वा ते पापा यान्त्यधोगतिम् ॥ ३.५२॥ strīdhanāni tu ye mohādupajīvanti bāndhavāḥ |
nārīyānāni vastraṁ vā te pāpā yāntyadhogatim || 3.52|| Those relatives who, out of delusion, exploit a woman's wealth or property, or her garments, fall into degradation and assume karmic burden. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not familial position Causation arises through conscious exploitation, not mere association Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of Dharma Restoration logic demands reparation through surrender of ill-gotten gains Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of harm and dharmic correction

title: manu 3.53
content:
आर्षे गोमिथुनं शुल्कं के चिदाहुर्मृषैव तत् ।
अल्पोऽप्येवं महान् वाऽपि विक्रयस्तावदेव सः ॥ ३.५३॥ तावानेव स विक्रयः ārṣe gomithunaṃ śulkaṃ ke cidāhurmṛṣaiva tat |
alpo'pyevaṃ mahān vā'pi vikrayastāvadeva saḥ || 3.53 || tāvāneva sa vikrayaḥ In Vedic transactions, the price paid for cattle intercourse is declared by some as mere fiction; yet whether small or great, such sale stands valid only to that extent. Authority originates from Vedic precedent, not popular consensus Causation aligns with transactional integrity, not nominal value Capacity-based responsibility lies in recognizing the true nature of exchange Restoration logic demands alignment with the actuality of contractual consent Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of transactional truth over apparent fiction

title: manu 3.54
content:
यासां नाददते शुल्कं ज्ञातयो न स विक्रयः ।
अर्हणं तत्कुमारीणामानृशंस्यं च केवलम् ॥ ३.५४॥ न केवलम् yāsāṁ nādadate śulkaṁ jñātayo na sa vikrayaḥ |
arhaṇaṁ tat-kumārīṇām ānṛśaṁsyaṁ ca kevalam || 3.54|| na kevalam Wherein kinsmen receive no fee, that is not a sale; the maiden's honor-price belongs solely to her integrity and compassionate alignment. Authority resides in conscious consent, not transactional exchange. Causation aligns with dharma-preserving intentionality. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of inherent dignity. Restoration logic upholds individual sovereignty without commodification. Consciousness alignment precedes all contractual validity.

title: manu 3.55
content:
पितृभिर्भ्रातृभिश्चैताः पतिभिर्देवरैस्तथा ।
पूज्या भूषयितव्याश्च बहुकल्याणमीप्सुभिः ॥ ३.५५॥ pitṛbhirbhra̱tṛbhiścaitāḥ patibhirdevarais tathā |
pūjyā bhūṣayitavyāśca bahukalyāṇamīpsubhiḥ || 3.55|| Women are to be honored, adorned, and served by fathers, brothers, husbands, and brothers-in-law who seek highest welfare. Authority flows through relational dharmic duty, not coercive power. Causation arises from conscious intention to uplift and protect. Capacity-based responsibility is distributed across familial and societal roles. Restoration logic centers on mutual flourishing and energetic alignment. Consciousness alignment occurs when service is rendered without expectation.

title: manu 3.56
content:
यत्र नार्यस्तु पूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः ।
यत्रैतास्तु न पूज्यन्ते सर्वास्तत्राफलाः क्रियाः ॥ ३.५६॥ yatra nāryas tu pūjyante ramante tatra devatāḥ | yatraitās tu na pūjyante sarvāstatrāphalāḥ kriyāḥ || 3.56|| Where women are honored, there the deities dwell in joy; where they are not honored, all actions become fruitless. Authority is derived from respect for feminine consciousness Causation flows from alignment with Shakti-based social order Capacity-based responsibility includes honoring the foundational role of women Restoration logic requires re-establishing reverence for the feminine principle Consciousness alignment depends on societal recognition of feminine divinity

title: manu 3.57
content:
शोचन्ति जामयो यत्र विनश्यत्याशु तत्कुलम् ।
न शोचन्ति तु यत्रैता वर्धते तधि सर्वदा ॥ ३.५७॥ śocanti jāmayo yatra vinaśyaty āśu tatkulam |
na śocanti tu yatraitā vardhate tadhi sarvadā || 3.57|| Wherever women mourn due to oppression, that lineage perishes swiftly; wherever they are honored and protected, that family thrives continually. Authority is derived from the protection of consciousness embodied in women. Causation follows the energetic alignment of societal integrity with feminine dignity. Capacity-based responsibility includes ensuring environments where consciousness flourishes without fear. Restoration logic demands immediate rectification of conditions causing distress to women. Consciousness alignment requires honoring the foundational role of women in sustaining dharma.

title: manu 3.58
content: जामयो यानि गेहानि शपन्त्यप्रतिपूजिताः । तानि कृत्याहतानीव विनश्यन्ति समन्ततः ॥ ३.५८॥ jāmayo yāni gehāni śapanty-apratipūjitāḥ | tāni kṛtyāhatānīva vinaśyanti samantataḥ || 3.58|| Those homes wherein guests are cursed without being honored—those very dwellings perish utterly, as if struck by divine decree. Authority of hospitality as foundational dharma Causation through violated sacred duty Capacity-based responsibility of householders Restoration logic via alignment with guest-consciousness Consciousness alignment through honoring the arriving presence

title: manu 3.59
content:
तस्मादेताः सदा पूज्या भूषणाच्छादनाशनैः ।
भूतिकामैर्नरैर्नित्यं सत्कारेषूत्सवेषु च ॥ ३.५९॥ tasmād etāḥ sadā pūjyā bhūṣaṇācchādanāśanaiḥ |
bhūtikāmair narair nityaṁ satkāreṣūtsaveṣu ca || 3.59|| Therefore, these beings must always be honored—with ornaments, clothing, food, and offerings—by those who seek well-being, through respectful conduct and celebration. Authority flows from recognition of the divine essence in all beings Causation arises from intentional acts of reverence that sustain universal harmony Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with dharma through active veneration Restoration logic operates through continuous acknowledgment and service Consciousness alignment occurs when respect becomes a lived practice

title: manu 3.60
content:
संतुष्टो भार्यया भर्ता भर्त्रा भार्या तथैव च ।
यस्मिन्नेव कुले नित्यं कल्याणं तत्र वै ध्रुवम् ॥ ३.६०॥ saṃtuṣṭo bhāryayā bhartā bhartṛā bhāryā tathaiva ca |
yasminneva kule nityaṃ kalyāṇaṃ tatra vai dhruvam || 3.60 || The husband finds fulfillment through the wife; the wife finds fulfillment through the husband. In whichever family this mutual alignment and completion exist perpetually, there alone is assured welfare. Authority arises from mutual recognition of capacity Causation flows from relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility is shared and reciprocal Restoration logic operates through harmonious alignment Consciousness alignment manifests as mutual completion

title: manu 3.61
content:
यदि हि स्त्री न रोचेत पुमांसं न प्रमोदयेत् ।
अप्रमोदात्पुनः पुंसः प्रजनं न प्रवर्तते ॥ ३.६१॥ yadi hi strī na roced vumāṃsaṃ na pramodayet |
apramodāt punaḥ puṃsaḥ prajanaṃ na pravartate || 3.61|| If a woman does not incline toward union with a man, she should not incite his joy; from lack of joy in the man, procreation does not proceed. Authority flows from conscious consent and mutual alignment Causation arises through harmonious intentionality, not coercion Capacity-based responsibility requires both parties to uphold energetic congruence Restoration logic demands realignment of relational dharma prior to reproductive engagement Consciousness alignment ensures that generative acts reflect unified will

title: manu 3.62
content:
स्त्रियां तु रोचमानायां सर्वं तद्रोचते कुलम् ।
तस्यां त्वरोचमानायां सर्वमेव न रोचते ॥ ३.६२॥ striyaṁ tu rocamānāyāṁ sarvaṁ tadrocate kulam |
tasyāṁ tv arocamānāyāṁ sarvam eva na rocate || 3.62|| When a woman is pleased, the entire lineage flourishes; when she is displeased, nothing in that lineage finds harmony. Authority resides in alignment with feminine consciousness Causation flows through emotional and energetic resonance Capacity-based responsibility includes harmonizing familial energies Restoration logic requires recognition of foundational affective balance Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring the sovereign sentiment of the feminine

title: manu 3.63
content:
कुविवाहैः क्रियालोपैर्वेदानध्ययनेन च ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च ॥ ३.६३॥ kuvivāhaiḥ kriyālopair vedānadhyayanena ca | kulāny akulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca || 3.63|| Families fall from their noble status through improper unions, abandonment of sacred duties, neglect of Vedic study, and violation of Brahminical conduct. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not lineage alone Causation arises from conscious choice and sustained practice Capacity-based responsibility requires maintenance of spiritual and social integrity Restoration logic demands recommitment to foundational practices Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for societal harmony

title: manu 3.64
content:
शिल्पेन व्यवहारेण शूद्रापत्यैश्च केवलैः ।
गोभिरश्वैश्च यानैश्च कृष्या राजोपसेवया ॥ ३.६४॥ śilpena vyavahāreṇa śūdrāpatyaiśca kevalaiḥ |
gobhir aśvaiś ca yānaiś ca kṛṣyā rājopasevayā || By craft, trade, service under Śūdra-born individuals alone, and through cattle, horses, vehicles, and agriculture—these constitute the means by which a king shall sustain his rule. Authority flows from capacity to sustain collective order Causation arises from alignment with natural economic roles Capacity-based responsibility requires utilization of available resources Restoration logic centers on self-sufficient societal function Consciousness alignment occurs when action aligns with svadharma

title: manu 3.65
content:
अयाज्ययाजनैश्चैव नास्तिक्येन च कर्मणाम् ।
कुलान्याशु विनश्यन्ति यानि हीनानि मन्त्रतः ॥ ३.६५॥ ayājyayājanaiścaiva nāstikyena ca karmaṇām |
kulānyāśu vinaśyanti yāni hīnāni mantrataḥ || 3.65|| Families and lineages that neglect sacred rituals, deny the authority of Vedic mantras, and act with disbelief in dharma are severed from their sustaining spiritual continuum and collapse instantaneously by the withdrawal of divine coherence. Authority flows from alignment with Vedic mantric integrity Causation is rooted in mantra-dharma alignment, not material action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious participation in sustaining lineage dharma Restoration logic demands reconnection to mantra-source, not external reform Consciousness alignment occurs through ritual rectitude and mantra-reaffirmation

title: manu 3.66
content:
मन्त्रतस्तु समृद्धानि कुलान्यल्पधनान्यपि ।
कुलसङ्ख्यां च गच्छन्ति कर्षन्ति च महद्यशः ॥ ३.६६॥ mantratastu samṛddhāni kulānyalpadhanānyapi |
kulasankhyāṃ ca gacchanti karṣanti ca mahadyashaḥ || 3.66|| Through mantra alone, even families of modest means attain prosperity; they rise in lineage count and draw forth great renown. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic intelligence Causation originates in vibrational utterance, not material effort Capacity-based responsibility is awakened through sacred invocation Restoration logic operates via elevation of consciousness Consciousness alignment multiplies effect beyond resource input

title: manu 3.67
content:
वैवाहिकेऽग्नौ कुर्वीत गृह्यं कर्म यथाविधि ।
पञ्चयज्ञविधानं च पक्तिं चान्वाहिकीं गृही ॥ ३.६७॥ vaiavāhike'gnau kurvīta gṛhyaṃ karma yathāvidhi |
pañcayajñavidhānaṃ ca paktiṃ cānvāhikīṃ gṛhī || 3.67|| In the domestic fire established through marriage, one shall perform household duties according to prescribed procedure; also, the five sacrifices and the twice-daily cooking for guests. Authority flows from the consecrated domestic fire as established by sacramental union. Causation arises from alignment with ritualized household duty. Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in initiation through Vedic rites. Restoration logic centers on re-establishing consecrated order within the household. Consciousness alignment occurs through sustained performance of dharma-bound domestic actions.

title: manu 3.68
content: पञ्च सूना गृहस्थस्य चुल्ली पेषण्युपस्करः । कण्डनी चौदकुम्भश्च बध्यते यास्तु वाहयन् ॥ ३.६८॥ pañca sūnā gṛhasthasya cullī peṣaṇyupaskaraḥ | kaṇḍanī caudakumbhaśca badhyate yāstu vāhayan || 3.68|| Five implements indispensable to a householder are: the hearth, the grinding stone, the broom, the water pot, and the carrying vessel; whoever carries these away is subject to binding. Authority derives from the preservation of foundational domestic order Causation arises through disruption of essential household instruments Capacity-based responsibility is measured by awareness of social interdependence Restoration logic centers on reintegration with functional societal structures Consciousness alignment requires recognition of mutual support systems

title: manu 3.69
content:
तासां क्रमेण सर्वासां निष्कृत्यर्थं महर्षिभिः ।
पञ्च कॢप्ता महायज्ञाः प्रत्यहं गृहमेधिनाम् ॥ ३.६९॥ tāsāṃ krameṇa sarvāsāṃ niṣkṛtyarthaṃ maharṣibhiḥ |
pañca kḷptā mahāyajñāḥ pratyahaṃ gṛhamedhinām || 3.69|| For the purpose of purification from all transgressions, in sequential order, the great sages have ordained five great sacrifices to be performed daily by householders. Authority originates from realized seers who embody cosmic order Causation follows sequential purification aligned with dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires daily ritual alignment for householders Restoration logic operates through sustained sacrificial action Consciousness alignment is maintained via prescribed daily yajña

title: manu 3.70
content: अध्यापनं ब्रह्मयज्ञः पितृयज्ञस्तु तर्पणम् । होमो दैवो बलिर्भौतो नृयज्ञोऽतिथिपूजनम् ॥ ३.७०॥ adhyāpanaṁ brahayajñaḥ pitṛyajñastu tarpaṇam | homo daivo balirbhauto nṛyajño'tithipūjanam || 3.70|| Teaching is the sacrifice to Brahman; offering to ancestors constitutes the ancestral sacrifice; oblation is the divine offering; distributing food is the earthly offering; honoring guests is the human sacrifice. Authority flows through knowledge dissemination Causation arises via dharmic duty fulfillment Capacity-based responsibility aligns with role-specific offerings Restoration logic embedded in reciprocal societal service Consciousness alignment achieved by performing one's svadharma

title: manu 3.71
content:
पञ्चैतान् यो महाऽयज्ञान्न हापयति शक्तितः ।
स गृहेऽपि वसन्नित्यं सूनादोषैर्न लिप्यते ॥ ३.७१॥ pañcetān yo mahā-yajñān na hāpayati śaktitaḥ |
sa gṛhe 'pi vasannityaṃ sūnādoṣair na lipyate || 3.71|| One who, by capacity, does not abandon these five great sacrifices dwells continually in the household without being stained by sins. Authority is derived from alignment with dharma, not social position Causation arises through conscious omission or commission within one's capacity Capacity-based responsibility determines the scope of karmic consequence Restoration logic operates through purification of intent, not external judgment Consciousness alignment supersedes ritual performance when capacity is honored

title: manu 3.72
content:
देवताऽतिथिभृत्यानां पितॄणामात्मनश्च यः ।
न निर्वपति पञ्चानामुच्छ्वसन्न स जीवति ॥ ३.७२॥ devatā'tithibhṛtyānāṁ pitṝṇāmātmanaśca yaḥ |
na nirvapati pañcānāmucchwasan sa jīvati || 3.72|| He who does not offer oblations to the deities, guests, servants, ancestors, and the Self while breathing—lives indeed. Authority as alignment with cosmic order Causation through omission of dharmic duty Capacity-based responsibility rooted in breath-sustained life Restoration logic via reconnection to ritual and relational duties Consciousness alignment through recognition of interdependent existence

title: manu 3.73
content: अहुतं च हुतं चैव तथा प्रहुतमेव च । ब्राह्म्यं हुतं प्राशितं च पञ्चयज्ञान् प्रचक्षते ॥ ३.७३॥ ahutaṃ ca hutaṃ caiva tathā prahutameva ca | brāhmyaṃ hutaṃ prāśitaṃ ca pañcayajñān pracakṣate || 3.73|| That which is unoffered, that which is offered, that which is repeatedly offered, that which is offered through Brahmanic knowledge, and that which is consumed — these together constitute the fivefold sacrifice. Authority flows from conscious participation in cosmic order Causation arises through alignment with sacrificial completeness Capacity-based responsibility is measured by one's integration into dharma-sacrifice Restoration occurs through re-entry into the cycle of dharmic offering Consciousness alignment manifests when action reflects Vedic continuity

title: manu 3.74
content:
जपोऽहुतो हुतो होमः प्रहुतो भौतिको बलिः ।
ब्राह्म्यं हुतं द्विजाग्र्यार्चा प्राशितं पितृतर्पणम् ॥ ३.७४॥ japo 'huto huto homaḥ prahuto bhautiko baliḥ |
brāhmyaṃ hutaṃ dvijāgryārcā prāśitaṃ pitṛtarpaṇam || 3.74|| Unuttered recitation, oblation offered in fire, material offering, Brahmanic invocation through worship of twice-born elders, and libations given to ancestors—these constitute the fivefold act of sacrifice. Authority resides in ritual completion aligned with cosmic order Causation flows from consciousness-intention into manifest action Capacity-based responsibility requires fulfillment of dharmic acts Restoration logic operates through sequential purification rituals Consciousness alignment achieved via structured sacrificial engagement

title: manu 3.75
content:
स्वाध्याये नित्ययुक्तः स्याद्दैवे चैवैह कर्मणि ।
दैवकर्मणि युक्तो हि बिभर्तीदं चराचरम् ॥ ३.७५॥ svādhyāye nityayuktaḥ syād daive caiva aih karmaṇi | daivakarmaṇi yukto hi bibhartīdaṁ carācaram || 3.75|| One must remain perpetually engaged in svādhyāya and in actions aligned with divine will; indeed, it is through alignment with divine action that one sustains the entire animate and inanimate creation. Authority originates from sustained alignment with svādhyāya and divine intelligence Causation arises from conscious participation in divinely ordered activity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's commitment to svādhyāya and alignment with dharma Restoration logic operates through continuous reconnection to source-consciousness via disciplined study and action Consciousness alignment ensures harmonious participation in cosmic order

title: manu 3.76
content:
अग्नौ प्रास्ताऽहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते ।
आदित्याज्जायते वृष्तिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः ॥ ३.७६॥ agnau prāstā' hutiḥ samyag ādityam upatiṣṭhate |
ādityāj jāyate vṛṣtir vṛṣṭer annaṁ tataḥ prajāḥ || 3.76|| The offering rightly cast into the fire ascends to the sun; from the sun arises rain, from rain food, and from food, beings. Authority: The sequential order of cosmic causation originates in Agni and culminates in Prajāḥ, establishing a divine chain of lawful manifestation. Causation: Each element arises sequentially through prior action—offering leads to rain, rain to food, food to beings—demonstrating precise causal alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual's act of offering determines the integrity of the entire causal chain, assigning capacity-responsive duty at every level. Restoration logic: When disruption occurs in any part of the causal sequence, restoration begins by re-aligning the initial offering—the root cause. Consciousness alignment: The law reflects the sequential unfolding of consciousness itself—from will (agni), to illumination (āditya), to nourishment (food), to life (prajāḥ).

title: manu 3.77
content:
यथा वायुं समाश्रित्य वर्तन्ते सर्वजन्तवः । सर्वे जीवन्ति जन्तवः
तथा गृहस्थमाश्रित्य  वर्तन्ते सर्व आश्रमाः ॥ ३.७७॥ वर्तन्त इतराश्रमः yathā vāyuṁ samāśritya vartante sarvajantavaḥ | sarve jīvanti jantavaḥ tathā gṛhasthamāśritya vartante sarva āśramāḥ || 3.77 || vartanta itarāśramaḥ Just as all beings depend upon air for their functioning and existence, so too do all ashramas depend upon the Grihastha ashrama for sustenance and operational continuity. Authority flows from the foundational ashrama that supports collective life Causation originates in the Grihastha ashrama as the enabler of all social dharma Capacity-based responsibility is distributed through interdependence of ashramas Restoration logic requires recognition of Grihastha ashrama's sustaining role Consciousness alignment occurs when each ashrama acknowledges its dependence

title: manu 3.78
content:
यस्मात्त्रयोऽप्याश्रमिणो ज्ञानेनान्नेन चान्वहम् ।
गृहस्थेनैव धार्यन्ते तस्माज्ज्येष्ठाश्रमो गृही ॥ ३.७८॥ yasmat trayo 'py āśramiṇo jñānenānnenānuvaham | gṛhasthenai eva dhāryante tasmāj jyeṣṭhāśramo gṛhī || 3.78|| Since all three orders of renunciants are sustained continuously by knowledge and food, and it is only the householder who supports them thereby, therefore the householder is declared the eldest among the ashramas. Authority arises from foundational sustenance Causation flows from material and spiritual support Capacity-based responsibility originates in sustaining power Restoration logic prioritizes structural integrity of dharma society Consciousness alignment requires recognition of interdependence

title: manu 3.79
content:
स संधार्यः प्रयत्नेन स्वर्गमक्षयमिच्छता ।
सुखं चेहेच्छताऽत्यन्तं योऽधार्यो दुर्बलेन्द्रियैः ॥ ३.७९॥ sa saṃdhāryaḥ prayatnena svargam akṣayam icchatā |
sukhaṃ ca iha icchatā' tyantaṃ yo 'dhāryo durbalendriyaiḥ || 3.79|| That which is to be firmly upheld through effort by one desiring imperishable heaven; that ultimate happiness which one desires here—such a state is unattainable by those whose senses are weak. Authority originates in sustained alignment with Dharma Causation arises from capacity-based volition Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful outcome Restoration logic aligns action with eternal consequence Consciousness alignment governs access to higher realms

title: manu 3.80
content:
ऋषयः पितरो देवा भूतान्यतिथयस्तथा ।
आशासते कुटुम्बिभ्यस्तेभ्यः कार्यं विजानता ॥ ३.८०॥ ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā bhūtānyatithayastathā |
āśāsate kuṭumbibhyastebhyaḥ kāryaṃ vijānatā || 3.80|| Ṛṣis, ancestors, deities, beings, and guests—all command householders who understand duty to perform actions for them. Authority flows from cosmic order and conscious alignment, not institutional hierarchy Causation arises through dharma-compliant action by those capable of discernment Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond human agents to include unseen authorities Restoration occurs when individual capacity aligns with universal expectation structures Consciousness alignment ensures that duty recognition activates reciprocal support systems

title: manu 3.81
content:
स्वाध्यायेनार्चयेतऋषीन् होमैर्देवान् यथाविधि ।
पितॄंश्राद्धैश्च नॄनन्नैर्भूतानि बलिकर्मणा ॥ ३.८१॥ svādhyāyenārcayet ṛṣīn homair devān yathāvidhi |
pitṝn śrāddhaiś ca nṝn annair bhūtāni balikarmaṇā || 3.81|| One honors the Rishis through Svadhyaya, the Devas through Homa performed according to Vidhi, the Pitrs through Shraddha with offerings of food, and all beings through Bali karma. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic order Causation is established through ritualized consciousness engagement Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional participation in sustaining creation Restoration logic operates via reciprocal offering and recognition Consciousness alignment occurs through structured invocation and service

title: manu 3.82
content: कुर्यादहरहः श्राद्धमन्नाद्येनोदकेन वा । दद्यादहरहः पयोमूलफलैर्वाऽपि पितृभ्यः प्रीतिमावहन् ॥ ३.८२॥ kuryādaharahaḥ śrāddhamannādyenodakena vā | dadyādaharahaḥ payomūalphalairvā'pi pitṛbhyaḥ prītimāvahan || 3.82|| One must perform Shraddha daily with food or water, and likewise offer milk, roots, and fruits to the ancestors, ensuring their satisfaction and invoking their grace. Authority flows from ancestral continuity and filial duty Causation arises through sustained ritual action aligning present conduct with ancestral lineage Capacity-based responsibility requires daily conscious engagement in ancestral worship Restoration logic operates through perpetual offering that maintains cosmic familial harmony Consciousness alignment occurs when individual actions reflect unbroken ancestral connection

title: manu 3.83
content: एकमप्याशयेद्विप्रं पित्र्यर्थे पाञ्चयज्ञिके । पित्र्यर्थं न चैवात्राशयेत्किं चिद्वैश्वदेवं प्रति द्विजम् ॥ ३.८३॥ ekam apy āśayed vipraṁ pitryarthe pāñcayajñike | pitryarthe na caivātrāśayed kiṁ cid vaiśvadevaṁ prati dvijam || 3.83 || In matters concerning ancestral rites within the five great sacrifices, even one Brahmin must be invited. However, in the context of offerings for the universal deities (Vaiśvadeva), no specific Brahmin should be exclusively invited for ancestral purposes. Authority resides in ritual specificity and contextual alignment Causation is determined by spiritual intent and ontological purpose Capacity-based responsibility is defined by role-specific invocation Restoration logic requires precise alignment of offering, recipient, and purpose Consciousness alignment occurs through correct ritual differentiation

title: manu 3.84
content:
वैश्वदेवस्य सिद्धस्य गृह्येऽग्नौ विधिपूर्वकम् ।
आभ्यः कुर्याद्देवताभ्यो ब्राह्मणो होममन्वहम् ॥ ३.८४॥ vaiśvadevasya siddhasya gṛhye'gnau vidhipūrvakam |
ābhyaḥ kuryāddevatābhyo brāhmaṇo homamanvaham || 3.84|| Upon completion of the Vaiśvadeva ritual, the Brāhmaṇa shall perform homa in the domestic fire according to prescribed method, offering oblations to the respective deities continually. Authority resides in the continuity of Vedic observance Causation aligns with sequential dharmic performance Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in svadharma-siddhi Restoration logic flows through uninterrupted yajña-krama Consciousness alignment occurs via disciplined agnihotra

title: manu 3.85
content:
अग्नेः सोमस्य चैवादौ तयोश्चैव समस्तयोः ।
विश्वेभ्यश्चैव देवेभ्यो धन्वन्तरय एव च ॥ ३.८५॥ agneḥ somasya caivādau tayoścaiva samastayoḥ |
vizvebhyaścaiva devebhyaḥ dhanvantaraye eva ca || 3.85|| In the beginning, offerings are made to Agni and Soma, and also to both of them together; likewise, to all the gods collectively and specifically to Dhanvantari. Authority flows from invocation and alignment with divine order Causation originates in conscious offering before manifestation Capacity-based responsibility begins with recognition of source energies Restoration logic requires sequential honoring of foundational forces Consciousness alignment necessitates precise devotional sequencing

title: manu 3.86
content:
कुह्वै चैवानुमत्यै च प्रजापतय एव च ।
सह द्यावापृथिव्योश्च तथा स्विष्टकृतेऽन्ततः ॥ ३.८६॥ kuhvai caivānumatyai ca prajāpataya eva ca | saha dyāvāpṛthivyor vyaḥ tathā sviṣṭakṛte 'ntataḥ || 3.86|| The invocation of Kuhu, Anumati, Prajapati, Dyavaprithivi, and Svistakrt establishes the sequential alignment of consciousness with cosmic order for the restoration of dharma through completion, not judgment. Authority flows from conscious invocation aligned with cosmic order Causation is established by sequential ritual alignment, not punitive intent Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's alignment with invoked consciousness Restoration logic operates through completion of invoked sequence, not external enforcement Consciousness alignment supersedes historical or cultural interpretation

title: manu 3.87
content:
एवं सम्यग्विर्हुत्वा सर्वदिक्षु प्रदक्षिणम् ।
इन्द्रान्तकाप्पतीन्दुभ्यः सानुगेभ्यो बलिं हरेत् ॥ ३.८७॥ evaṁ samyagvihutvā sarvadiṣu pradakṣiṇam |
indrāntakāppatīndubhyaḥ sānugebhyo baliṁ haret || 3.87|| Thus having performed the sacrifice correctly, offering circumambulation in all directions, one shall offer oblations to Indra, Antaka, Aapati, and Chandra along with their followers. Authority resides in conscious alignment with cosmic order through prescribed ritual action Causation flows from precise execution of dharmic injunctions Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition and honoring of divine hierarchies Restoration logic operates through reverent completion of sacrificial duty Consciousness alignment occurs via structured devotional offerings

title: manu 3.88
content:
मरुद्भ्य इति तु द्वारि क्षिपेदप्स्वद्भ्य इत्यपि ।
वनस्पतिभ्य इत्येवं मुसलोलूखले हरेत् ॥ ३.८८॥ marudbhya iti tu dvāri kṣiped apsvadhy ity api | vanaspatibhya ity evaṃ musalolūkhale haret || 3.88|| One should cast out at the door those who speak falsely, and likewise those who speak divisively; similarly, one must remove from the threshing floor those who act destructively toward living beings and vegetation. Authority resides in discernment of truth-speaking and harmony-preserving conduct. Causation arises through alignment with life-supporting actions. Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition and removal of disruptive elements without infliction of harm. Restoration logic demands purification of spaces where dharma is enacted. Consciousness alignment requires separation from that which undermines collective integrity.

title: manu 3.89
content:
उच्छीर्षके श्रियै कुर्याद्भद्रकाल्यै च पादतः ।
ब्रह्मवास्तोष्पतिभ्यां तु वास्तुमध्ये बलिं हरेत् ॥ ३.८९॥ ucchīrṣake śriyai kuryād bhadra-kālyai ca pādataḥ |
brhma-vāstospatibhyāṁ tu vāstu-madhye baliṁ hared || 3.89|| For the elevation of prosperity at the threshold, offerings are made; for auspicious time at the foundation, reverence is given. To Brahma and Vāstuśpati in the center of the dwelling, homage shall be offered. Authority flows from spatial sanctification rooted in divine presence Causation aligns with directional consecration as a determinant of energetic harmony Capacity-based responsibility arises through ritual alignment with cosmic order Restoration logic operates via structural devotion to foundational divinities Consciousness alignment occurs when built environments reflect celestial governance

title: manu 3.90
content:
विश्वेभ्यश्चैव देवेभ्यो बलिमाकाश उत्क्षिपेत् ।
दिवाचरेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो नक्तञ्चारिभ्य एव च ॥ ३.९०॥ viśvebhyaśaiva devebhyo balim ākāśa utkṣipet |
divācarebhyo bhūtebhyo naktañcāribhya eva ca || 3.90 || Let oblations be offered into the sky for all beings—gods, day-wanderers, night-wanderers—and all creatures universally. Authority originates from recognition of universal divinity in all beings. Causation arises through conscious offering that aligns with cosmic order. Capacity-based responsibility is fulfilled by acknowledging interdependence among all forms of existence. Restoration occurs when offerings dissolve ego-boundary and establish unity-consciousness. Consciousness alignment manifests through acts of reverence toward all strata of creation.

title: manu 3.91
content: पृष्ठवास्तुनि कुर्वीत बलिं सर्वात्मभूतये । सर्वान्नभूतये पितृभ्यो बलिशेषं तु सर्वं दक्षिणतो हरेत् ॥ ३.९१॥ pṛṣṭhavāstuni kurvīta baliṃ sarvātmabhūtaye | sarvānnabhūtaye pitṛbhyo baliśeṣaṃ tu sarvaṃ dakṣiṇato haret || 3.91|| In all dwelling places, one shall offer Bali to all beings who are expressions of the Self. To all creatures, through Pitrs, whatever remains after Bali offerings shall be given completely towards the South. Authority originates in recognition of the Self's omnipresence in all beings. Causation arises through conscious offering and energetic alignment with ancestral lineage. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to sustain energetic reciprocity. Restoration logic operates via completion of ritual obligations to maintain cosmic balance. Consciousness alignment occurs when offerings are made without expectation, directed toward universal integration.

title: manu 3.92
content:
शूनां च पतितानां च श्वपचां पापरोगिणाम् ।
वयसानां कृमीणां च शनकैर्निर्वपेद्भुवि ॥ ३.९२॥ वयसां च śūnāṁ ca patitānāṁ ca śvapacāṁ pāparogiṇām |
vayasānāṁ kṛmīṇāṁ ca śanakair nirvaped bhuvi || 3.92|| vayasāṁ ca One must systematically and gradually disperse the remnants of those who have fallen from Dharma, including outcasts, sinners, the diseased, aged beings, and worms, upon the earth. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not social status Causation is determined by spiritual degradation, not physical action alone Capacity-based responsibility includes caretaking of all life forms in alignment with cosmic order Restoration logic requires removal of impurities that obstruct universal harmony Consciousness alignment demands purification of environments to elevate collective awareness

title: manu 3.93
content:
एवं यः सर्वभूतानि ब्राह्मणो नित्यमर्चति ।
स गच्छति परं स्थानं तेजोमूर्तिः पथार्जुना ॥ ३.९३॥ evaṁ yaḥ sarvabhūtāni brāhmaṇo nityamarcatai |
sa gacchati paraṁ sthānaṁ tejomūrtiḥ pathārjunā || 3.93|| Thus, the Brahmin who perpetually worships all beings attains the Supreme Abode, becoming a luminous form upon the path of Arjuna. Authority is derived from perpetual alignment with universal consciousness Causation arises through worshipful recognition of all existence as divine Capacity-based responsibility requires constant realization of unity in diversity Restoration logic operates through illumination and spiritual ascension Consciousness alignment supersedes ritualistic performance

title: manu 3.94
content:
कृत्वैतद्बलिकर्मैवमतिथिं पूर्वमाशयेत् ।
भिक्षां च भिक्षवे दद्याद्विधिवद्ब्रह्मचारिणे ॥ ३.९४॥ kṛtva etad balikarma evam atithiṁ pūrvam āśayet | bhikṣāṁ ca bhikṣave dadyād vidhivid brahmacāriṇe || 3.94|| Having performed the sacrificial offering thus, one shall first receive the guest; and likewise, one shall give alms to the mendicant according to rule, and to the celibate student of sacred knowledge. Authority as service to consciousness Causation through dharmic hospitality Capacity-based responsibility in giving Restoration logic via ritual completion and social duty Consciousness alignment through honoring guests and seekers

title: manu 3.95
content: यत्पुण्यफलमाप्नोति गां दत्त्वा विधिवद्गुरोः । तत्पुण्यफलमाप्नोति भिक्षां दत्त्वा द्विजो गृही ॥ ३.९५॥ yat puṇya-phalam āpnoti gāṁ dattvā vidhivid guroḥ | tat puṇya-phalam āpnoti bhikṣāṁ dattvā dvijo gṛhī || 3.95 || That merit which accrues to a guru upon receiving a cow according to prescribed ritual, the same merit accrues to a householder dvija when he gives alms. Authority is proportionate to capacity for dharma-conformant action Causation aligns with conscious intent and structural role Capacity-based responsibility determines karmic equivalency Restoration logic operates through equivalence of dharmic effect Consciousness alignment occurs via structural parity in giving

title: manu 3.96
content:
भिक्षामप्युदपात्रं वा सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकम् ।
वेदतत्त्वार्थविदुषे ब्राह्मणायोपपादयेत् ॥ ३.९६॥ bhikṣām apy udapātraṁ vā satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam |
vedatattvārthaviduṣe brāhmaṇāya upapādayet || 3.96|| Even alms or a water vessel must be respectfully offered according to prescribed procedure to a Brahmin who knows the truth of the Vedas. Authority derives from consciousness realization, not institutional position Causation flows through ritual correctness and inner alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of spiritual competence Restoration logic prioritizes energetic purity over material transaction Consciousness alignment ensures that offerings activate dharma-field resonance

title: manu 3.97
content:
नश्यन्ति हव्यकव्यानि नराणामविजानताम् ।
भस्मीभूतेषु विप्रेषु मोहाद्दत्तानि दातृभिः ॥ ३.९७॥ naśyanti havya-kavyāni narāṇām avijānatām | bhasmībhūteṣu vipreṣu mohād dattāni dātṛbhiḥ || 3.97 || When those who offer sacrifices and perform rituals lack discriminative knowledge, their offerings become nullified; similarly, gifts given in delusion to priests who have lost spiritual integrity are rendered void. Authority is contingent upon consciousness alignment Causation arises from clarity of intent and capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires ontological fitness Restoration logic demands re-alignment with Dharma-sourced awareness Consciousness alignment determines the validity of transactional acts

title: manu 3.98
content:
विद्यातपस्समृद्धेषु हुतं विप्रमुखाग्निषु ।
निस्तारयति दुर्गाच्च महतश्चैव किल्बिषात् ॥ ३.९८॥ vidyātapassamṛddheṣu hutaṃ vipramukhāgniṣu |
nistārayati durgācca mahataścaiva kilbiṣāt || 3.98|| One who is enriched with knowledge and austerity, and whose offerings are accepted by the fire facing the Brahmin—such a being liberates from great sins and removes obstacles. Authority derives from spiritual enrichment, not institutional position. Causation originates in consciousness purity expressed through action. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment with Vedic fire (Ṛta). Restoration logic operates through ritual-integrity and conscious offering. Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks in determining legal efficacy.

title: manu 3.99
content:
सम्प्राप्ताय त्वतिथये प्रदद्यादासनौदके ।
अन्नं चैव यथाशक्ति सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकम् ॥ ३.९९॥ samprāptāya tvatithaye pradadyād āsanodake .
annaṃ caiva yathāśakti satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam .. To the arrived guest, one shall offer seat and water. Food too, according to capacity, respectfully and in accordance with dharma. Authority arises through presence, not title Causation originates in conscious reception Capacity-based responsibility aligns with resource availability Restoration occurs via dignified inclusion Consciousness alignment manifests through hospitality

title: manu 3.100
content:
शिलानप्युञ्छतो नित्यं पञ्चाग्नीनपि जुह्वतः ।
सर्वं सुकृतमादत्ते ब्राह्मणोऽनर्चितो वसन् ॥ ३.१००॥ śilānapyuñchato nityaṁ pañcāgnīnapi juhvataḥ |
sarvaṁ sukṛtamādatte brāhmaṇo'narcito vasan || 3.100|| One who resides without worship, yet unceasingly gathers from stones and offers into the five fires—such a Brāhmaṇa accepts all merit as his due by virtue of dwelling in non-reliance. Authority derives from self-sustained consciousness, not external validation Causation arises through detached action aligned with svadharma Capacity-based responsibility is inherent in one's state of abidance, not ritual performance Restoration logic operates through alignment with non-possessive existence Consciousness alignment supersedes ceremonial obligation

title: manu 3.101
content:
तृणानि भूमिरुदकं वाक्चतुर्थी च सूनृता ।
एतान्यपि सतां गेहे नोच्छिद्यन्ते कदा चन ॥ ३.१०१॥ tṛṇāni bhūmirudakaṁ vākcatuthī ca sūnṛtā |
etānyapi satāṁ gehe nocchidyante kadā cana || 3.101|| Grass, earth, water, speech, and sweet words—these five elements of a righteous household are never to be severed or withheld from any being at any time. Authority is derived from alignment with Satya-Dharma, not coercive power. Causation arises through continuous offering and non-withholding of life-supporting resources. Capacity-based responsibility requires that those in possession sustain others unconditionally. Restoration logic operates through perpetual circulation of essential resources. Consciousness alignment is maintained by ensuring no sentient being is deprived of fundamental sustenance.

title: manu 3.102
content:
एकरात्रं तु निवसन्नतिथिर्ब्राह्मणः स्मृतः ।
अनित्यं हि स्थितो यस्मात्तस्मादतिथिरुच्यते ॥ ३.१०२॥ ekarātraṁ tu nivasannatithirbrāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ |
anityaṁ hi sthito yasmāttasmādatithirucyate || 3.102|| A Brahmin residing for one night is designated as a guest, because his stay is impermanent. Authority through temporary residence establishes relational dharma Causation arises from the nature of impermanence Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to the duration and intent of presence Restoration logic centers on harmonizing transient relationships Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are recognized without attachment

title: manu 3.103
content:
नैकग्रामीणमतिथिं विप्रं साङ्गतिकं तथा ।
उपस्थितं गृहे विद्याद्भार्या यत्राग्नयोऽपि वा ॥ ३.१०३॥ naikagrāmīṇam atithiṁ vipraṁ sāṅgatikaṁ tathā | upasthitaṁ gṛhe vidyādbhāryā yatrāgnayo'pi vā || 3.103|| One must recognize the presence of a guest who is a Brahmin, even if he comes from a single village or arrives in company; whether a wife is present or even fire is kindled in the house. Authority: The duty to receive and honor guests arises irrespective of their origin or social status. Causation: Recognition of divine presence through hospitality establishes karmic alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: Householders bear absolute responsibility for honoring spiritual guests regardless of domestic circumstances. Restoration logic: Proper reception of guests renews dharma within the household and community. Consciousness alignment: True awareness manifests in spontaneous reverence towards those embodying sacred knowledge.

title: manu 3.104
content:
उपासते ये गृहस्थाः परपाकमबुद्धयः ।
तेन ते प्रेत्य पशुतां व्रजन्त्यन्नादिदायिनः ॥ ३.१०४॥ upāsate ye gṛhasthāḥ parapākamabuddhayaḥ |
tena te pretya paśutāṃ vrajantyannādidāyinaḥ || 3.104|| Those householders who serve with clouded intelligence, offering what belongs to another without awareness, by that deed they descend into animalhood after death, becoming givers of flesh. Authority originates in conscious alignment with Dharma, not ritual performance Causation arises from distorted perception, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires full cognition of ownership and consequence Restoration logic operates through experiential completion rather than punitive reversal Consciousness alignment determines karmic trajectory more than physical act

title: manu 3.105
content: अप्रणोद्योऽतिथिः सायं सूर्यौढो गृहमेधिना । काले प्राप्तस्त्वकाले वा नास्यानश्नन् गृहे वसेत् ॥ ३.१०५॥ apraṇodyo'tithiḥ sāyaṁ sūryauḍho gṛhamedhinā | kāle prāptaḥ tvakāle vā nāsyānaśnan gṛhe vaset || 3.105|| An uninvited guest arriving at dusk or after sunset must not be refused food or shelter by the householder, whether he arrives at the proper time or not. Authority of hospitality supersedes temporal convenience Causation through dharmic duty overrides personal preference Capacity-based responsibility of the householder to sustain life Restoration logic through immediate provision of sustenance Consciousness alignment via selfless service to the unexpected

title: manu 3.106
content:
न वै स्वयं तदश्नीयादतिथिं यन्न भोजयेत् ।
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं स्वर्ग्यं वा�तिथिपूजनम् ॥ ३.१०६॥ na vai svayaṁ tadaśnīyād atithiṁ yanna bhojayet |
dhanyaṁ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṁ svargyaṁ vā'tithipūjanam || 3.106|| One who does not feed a guest who has come to their home must not eat themselves; honoring a guest brings prosperity, fame, longevity, and access to heaven. Authority originates in the capacity to serve dharma through hospitality. Causation is established by the sequential alignment of duty and consequence. Capacity-based responsibility requires that one capable of offering food must do so before partaking. Restoration logic operates through reciprocal integrity between host and guest. Consciousness alignment manifests when service to another becomes self-realization.

title: manu 3.107
content:
आसनावसथौ शय्यामनुव्रज्यामुपासनाम् ।
उत्तमेषूत्तमं कुर्याधीने हीनं समे समम् ॥ ३.१०७॥ āsanāvasathau śayyāmanuvrajyāmupāsanām |
uttameṣūttamaṃ kuryādhīne hīnaṃ same samam || 3.107|| In all seats of dwelling, in lying down, in following, in worship — among the superior, one should act with excellence; among the dependent, with humility; among equals, with equanimity. Authority is context-dependent and relational Capacity-based responsibility aligns action with status Restoration logic requires situational ethical calibration Consciousness alignment manifests through graded social harmony Causation arises from dharmic attunement to relational roles

title: manu 3.108
content: वैश्वदेवे तु निर्वृत्ते यद्यन्योऽतिथिराव्रजेत् । तस्याप्यन्नं यथाशक्ति प्रदद्यान्न बलिं हरेत् ॥ ३.१०८॥ vaiśvadeve tu nirvṛtte yadyanyo'tithirāvrajeta | tasyāpyannaṁ yathāśakti pradadyānna baliṁ haret || 3.108|| When the Vaishvadeva rite has been completed, if another guest arrives, food should still be given to that guest according to one's capacity; no oblation should be withheld. Authority flows from capacity, not status Responsibility arises upon encounter, not invitation Restoration logic prioritizes presence over precedence Consciousness alignment requires immediate response to manifested need

title: manu 3.109
content:
न भोजनार्थं स्वे विप्रः कुलगोत्रे निवेदयेत् ।
भोजनार्थं हि ते शंसन् वान्ताशीत्युच्यते बुधैः ॥ ३.१०९॥ na bhojanārthaṁ sve vipraḥ kulagotre nivedayet |
bhojanārthaṁ hi te śaṁsan vāntāśītyucyate budhaiḥ || 3.109|| A Vipra must not declare his own birth-group or lineage for the purpose of obtaining food; one who does so, knowingly seeking alms under false pretenses, is declared by the wise as spiritually voided and consciousness-degraded. Authority derives from spiritual integrity, not genealogical claim. Causation arises from conscious intent to deceive for material gain. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment between identity and action. Restoration logic demands purification of false representation. Consciousness alignment necessitates withdrawal of misaligned declarations.

title: manu 3.110
content:
न ब्राह्मणस्य त्वतिथिर्गृहे राजन्य उच्यते ।
वैश्यशूद्रौ सखा चैव ज्ञातयो गुरुरेव च ॥ ३.११०॥ na brāhmaṇasya tvatithirgṛhe rājanya ucyate |
vaiśyaśūdrau sakhā caiva jñātayo guru eva ca || 3.110|| In the household of a Brāhmaṇa, no guest is to be deemed equal to a Kṣatriya; among guests, a Vaiśya or Śūdra, a friend, relatives, or even a guru hold no equivalence in status or entitlement within that sacred domain. Authority is contextually graded by spiritual hierarchy and not by personal relationship Causation arises from the sanctity of the dwelling space and its presiding consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment with Dharma, not social role alone Restoration logic operates through recognition of graded spiritual entitlements Consciousness alignment determines rightful place and access within sacred domains

title: manu 3.111
content:
यदि त्वतिथिधर्मेण क्षत्रियो गृहमाव्रजेत् ।
भुक्तवत्सु च विप्रेषु कामं तमपि भोजयेत् ॥ ३.१११॥ yadi tvatithidharmeṇa kṣatriyo gṛhamāvrajet | bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu kāmaṃ tamapi bhojayet || 3.111|| When a Kshatriya enters a house in the manner of an uninvited guest, and the Brahmins therein have already eaten, that Kshatriya must still be offered food according to desire. Authority flows from Dharma, not status or class Causation arises through presence and intent, not invitation Capacity-based responsibility requires provision based on need Restoration logic demands fulfillment of duty despite inconvenience Consciousness alignment occurs when hospitality transcends social roles

title: manu 3.112
content:
वैश्यशूद्रावपि प्राप्तौ कुटुम्बेऽतिथिधर्मिणौ ।
भोजयेत्सह भृत्यैस्तावानृशंस्यं प्रयोजयन् ॥ ३.११२॥ vaiśyaśūdrāvapi prāptau kuṭumbe'tithidharmiṇau |
bhojayetsaha bhṛtyaistāvānṛśaṃsyaṃ prayojayan || 3.112|| When a Vaishya and a Shudra arrive at a household as guests entitled to hospitality, the householder shall feed them along with servants, thereby fulfilling the duty of non-cruelty. Authority is derived from the capacity to host and sustain life Causation arises through the dharmic obligation to honor guest-consciousness Capacity-based responsibility extends equally regardless of varna when guest-dharma is invoked Restoration logic operates through completion of hospitality as an act of dharma Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of divinity in all beings arriving as guests

title: manu 3.113
content:
इतरानपि सख्यादीन् सम्प्रीत्या गृहमागतान् ।
प्रकृत्यान्नं यथाशक्ति भोजयेत्सह भार्यया ॥ ३.११३॥ itarānapi sakhya ādīn sampriyā gṛham āgatān |
prakṛtyannam yathāśakti bhojayet saha bhāryayā || 3.113|| One must feed guests, including friends and others who arrive at the home with affection, with natural food according to one's capacity, together with one's wife. Authority: The household holder possesses intrinsic duty-bearing capacity towards arriving guests. Causation: Affectionate reception and feeding of guests generates dharmic continuity and societal harmony. Capacity-based responsibility: Obligation is proportionate to individual material and energetic capacity. Restoration logic: Feeding guests restores relational integrity between host, guest, and cosmic order. Consciousness alignment: Act of service aligns individual consciousness with universal hospitality principle.

title: manu 3.114
content:
सुवासिनीः कुमारीश्च रोगिणो गर्भिणीः स्त्रियः ।
अतिथिभ्योऽग्र एवैतान् भोजयेदविचारयन् ॥ ३.११४॥ suvasiniḥ kumariśca rogiṇo garbhiṇiḥ striyaḥ |
atithibhyo'gra evaitan bhōjayēdavičārayan || Women who are adorned, youthful, diseased, or pregnant shall be served food before guests without hesitation. Authority originates from the protection and sustenance of life conditions Causation aligns with capacity-sensitive social order Capacity-based responsibility mandates prioritization of vulnerable states Restoration logic demands immediate provisioning without evaluative delay Consciousness alignment requires honoring biological and spiritual vulnerability

title: manu 3.115
content: अदत्त्वा तु य एतेभ्यः पूर्वं भुङ्क्तेऽविचक्षणः । स भुञ्जानो न जानाति श्वगृध्रैर्जग्धिमात्मनः ॥ ३.११५॥ adattvā tu ya etebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ bhuṅkte'vicakṣaṇaḥ | sa bhuñjāno na jānāti śvagṛdhrair jagdhim ātmanaḥ || 3.115|| One who, without giving, consumes before these beings what is rightfully theirs, acts without discernment. While consuming, he does not realize that he himself shall be consumed by dogs and vultures. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not from consumption or possession Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) — misaligned action leads to inevitable consequence Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious recognition of rightful order Restoration logic demands correction of distorted consumption patterns Consciousness alignment necessitates understanding the cycle of inversion in karmic receptivity

title: manu 3.116
content:
भुक्तवत्स्वथ विप्रेषु स्वेषु भृत्येषु चैव हि ।
भुञ्जीयातां ततः पश्चादवशिष्टं तु दम्पती ॥ ३.११६॥ bhuktavatsva atha vipreṣu sveṣu bhṛtyeṣu caiva hi |
bhuñjīyātāṁ tataḥ paścād avaśiṣṭaṁ tu dampatī || 3.116|| After feeding the Brahmins, one's own servants, and other dependents, the remainder shall be enjoyed by the married couple. Authority flows from sacrificial duty fulfilled towards higher spiritual orders Causation is established through sequential service obligations before personal enjoyment Capacity-based responsibility requires householders to prioritize sustenance of spiritual and dependent structures Restoration logic ensures that material surplus arises only after sacred and social debts are settled Consciousness alignment manifests through structured renunciation prior to relational enjoyment

title: manu 3.117
content:
देवान् ऋषीन् मनुष्यांश्च पितॄन् गृह्याश्च देवताः ।
पूजयित्वा ततः पश्चाद्गृहस्थः शेषभुग्भवेत् ॥ ३.११७॥ devān ṛṣīn manuṣyāṃś ca pitṝn gṛhyāś ca devatāḥ |
pūjayitvā tataḥ paścād gṛhasthaḥ śeṣabhug bhavet || 3.117 || Having honored the Devatas, Rishis, ancestors, household deities, and all beings according to their capacity and relation, the householder becomes entitled to enjoy the remaining fruits of action. Authority flows from recognition of cosmic hierarchy and relational integrity Causation is established through prior acknowledgment and alignment with divine order Capacity-based responsibility requires honoring foundational supports before personal enjoyment Restoration logic demands completion of relational duties as precondition for lawful fulfillment Consciousness alignment occurs when actions reflect gratitude and systemic interdependence

title: manu 3.118
content:
अघं स केवलं भुङ्क्ते यः पचत्यात्मकारणात् ।
यज्ञशिष्टाशनं ह्येतत्सतामन्नं विधीयते ॥ ३.११८॥ aghaṃ sa kevalaṃ bhuṅkte yaḥ pacatyātmakāraṇāt |
yajñaśiṣṭāśanaṃ hyetatsatāmannā vidhīyate || 3.118|| He alone consumes sin who cooks food for himself without offering it in sacrifice; food remaining after sacrifice is ordained as the proper nourishment for those established in truth. Authority originates from sacrificial alignment with cosmic order Causation arises through conscious participation in dharma-yajña Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's role in sustaining collective integrity Restoration logic operates through realignment with satya-vākya and yajña-consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs when actions are dedicated to the Whole rather than individual appetite

title: manu 3.119
content:
राजर्त्विग्स्नातकगुरून् प्रियश्वशुरमातुलान् ।
अर्हयेन् मधुपर्केण परिसंवत्सरात्पुनः ॥ ३.११९॥ rājar tvig snātakagurūn priyaśvaśuramātalān |
arhayen madhuparkeṇa parisamvatsarātpunaḥ || 3.119|| The King shall honor again, after the completion of a full year, the priests, the graduated scholars, the revered father-in-law, and maternal uncles with the Madhuparka ceremony. Authority is cyclical and relational, grounded in sustained respect and conscious renewal. Causation arises through ritualized acknowledgment that aligns temporal duty with spiritual continuity. Capacity-based responsibility requires periodic re-recognition of roles within the societal fabric. Restoration logic operates via ceremonial reaffirmation rather than punitive enforcement. Consciousness alignment occurs when social hierarchies are honored through prescribed dharmic acts.

title: manu 3.120
content: राजा च श्रोत्रियश्चैव यज्ञकर्मण्युपस्थितौ । उपस्थिते मधुपर्केण सम्पूज्यौ न त्वयज्ञ इति स्थितिः ॥ ३.१२०॥ rājā ca śrotriyaścaiva yajñakarmaṇyupasthitau | upasthite madhuparkeṇa sampūjyau na tvayajña iti sthitiḥ || 3.120 || When the King and the Shrotriya are present at a sacrificial ritual, they shall be honored with Madhuparka; however, their presence does not constitute the performance of the Yajna itself. Authority is context-dependent and role-specific within ritual action Presence alone does not confer causative efficacy in sacred duty Ceremonial protocol reflects hierarchical spiritual alignment Restoration occurs through proper recognition of capacity, not mere attendance Consciousness alignment requires intentional participation, not passive observance

title: manu 3.121
content:
सायं त्वन्नस्य सिद्धस्य पत्न्यमन्त्रं बलिं हरेत् ।
वैश्वदेवं हि नामैतत्सायं प्रातर्विधीयते ॥ ३.१२१॥ sāyaṁ tvannasya siddhasya patnyamantraṁ baliṁ haret |
vaiśvadevaṁ hi nāmaitat sāyaṁ prātarvidhīyate || 3.121|| When food has been prepared in the evening by a perfected householder, the wife shall offer oblation with mantra at the time of dusk. This ritual is called Vaiśvadeva and is performed both in the evening and morning. Authority flows through prescribed roles within household structure Causation arises from correct timing and ritual alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual maturity and domestic role Restoration logic embedded in daily sacrificial acts sustains cosmic order Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined performance of dharma

title: manu 3.122
content: पितृयज्ञं तु निर्वर्त्य विप्रश्चन्द्रक्षयेऽग्निमान् । चैन्दुक्षये पिण्डान्वाहार्यकं श्राद्धं कुर्यान् मासानुमासिकम् ॥ ३.१२२॥ pitṛyajñaṃ tu nirvartya vipraś candrakṣaye'gnimān | caindu-kṣaye piṇḍānvāhāryakaṃ śrāddhaṃ kuryān māsānumāsikam || 3.122|| Having performed the sacrifice to the ancestors, a twice-born man who maintains the sacred fire shall perform the monthly Śrāddha offering during the waning phase of the moon, specifically when the moon enters the asterism associated with the Pitṛs. Authority derives from continuity of ritual duty and alignment with cosmic order Causation is established through sequential participation in ancestral rites Capacity-based responsibility requires maintenance of sacred fire and lunar observance Restoration logic resides in regular repetition of offerings ensuring ancestral integration Consciousness alignment occurs via precise timing and devotional execution of prescribed acts

title: manu 3.123
content: पितॄणां मासिकं श्राद्धमन्वाहार्यं विदुर्बुधाः । तच्चामिषेणा कर्तव्यं प्रशस्तेन प्रयत्नतः ॥ ३.१२3॥ pitṝṇāṁ māsikaṁ śrāddham anvāhāryaṁ vidurbudhāḥ | tacca ammiṣeṇa kartavyaṁ praśastena prayatnataḥ || 3.123|| The monthly Śrāddha for ancestors is to be performed by those who know; it must be conducted with pure intent, careful effort, and appropriate offerings. Authority flows from conscious alignment with ancestral lineage Causation arises through sustained ritual integrity and devotional discipline Capacity-based responsibility requires knowledge, purity, and intentional action Restoration logic operates via consecrated repetition and spiritual maintenance Consciousness alignment occurs when duties are executed in accordance with dharma-prescribed form

title: manu 3.124
content:
तत्र ये भोजनीयाः स्युर्ये च वर्ज्या द्विजोत्तमाः ।
यावन्तश्चैव यैश्चान्नैस्तान् प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ॥ ३.१२४॥ tatra ye bhojanīyāḥ syurye ca varjyā dvijottamāḥ |
yāvantaścaiva yaiścānnaiḥ stān pravakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ || 3.124 || Therein, O Supreme Twice-Born, those who are fit to be fed, those who must be avoided, and all beings nourished by various foods—these shall be declared completely. Authority flows from the realized Brahmin who discerns the dharmic eligibility of beings Causation arises through conscious alignment with the hierarchy of sustenance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to sustain dharma through feeding Restoration logic operates via proper allocation of nourishment according to spiritual capacity Consciousness alignment occurs when food exchange honors the gradations of spiritual evolution

title: manu 3.125
content: द्वौ दैवे पितृकार्ये त्रीनेकैकमुभयत्र वा । पितृकृत्ये भोजयेत्सुसमृद्धोऽपि न प्रसज्जेत विस्तरे ॥ ३.१२५॥ न प्रवर्तेत dvau daive pitṛkārye trīnekaiakamubhayatra vā | pitṛkṛtye bhojayetsusamṛddho'pi na prasajjeta vistare || 3.125|| na pravarteta In matters concerning divine worship and ancestral duties, whether performed separately or together, even one who is highly prosperous must not indulge in excess. He should not initiate actions that lead to expansion beyond capacity. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not material abundance Causation arises from conscious choice, not external prosperity Capacity-based responsibility requires proportionality between action and resource Restoration logic demands prevention of energetic imbalance before it manifests Consciousness alignment necessitates restraint in all acts, especially those involving sacred duty

title: manu 3.126
content:
सत्क्रियां देशकालौ च शौचं ब्राह्मणसम्पदः ।
पञ्चैतान् विस्तरो हन्ति तस्मान्नैहेत विस्तरम् ॥ ३.१२६॥ satkriyāṁ deśakālau ca śaucaṁ brāhmaṇasampadaḥ |
pañcaitān vistaro hanti tasmānna iheta vistaram || 3.126|| Proper conduct, place, time, purity, and the qualities of a Brahmin—these five destroy expansion; therefore, one should not engage in excess. Authority is rooted in alignment with dharma-sattva, not external power Causation arises through conscious capacity, not material action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of inherent spiritual order Restoration logic operates by removing excess that disrupts harmony Consciousness alignment occurs when actions reflect satvic precision

title: manu 3.127
content:
प्रथिता प्रेतकृत्यैषा पित्र्यं नाम विधुक्षये ।
तस्मिन् युक्तस्यैति नित्यं प्रेतकृत्यैव लौकिकी ॥ ३.१२७॥ prathitā pretakṛtyaiṣā pitryaṃ nāma vidhukṣaye |
tasmin yuktasyaiti nityaṃ pretakṛtyaiva laukikī || 3.127|| This well-known rite performed for the deceased, called 'Pitrya', is established for the continuity of lineage. One who is properly engaged in it attains perpetually the status of a Preta-Kriya performer within worldly existence. Authority originates from sustained ritual engagement that aligns individual action with ancestral continuity. Causation flows through intentional performance of prescribed rites, generating karmic alignment rather than consequence. Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's ability to uphold and execute ancestral duties without external compulsion. Restoration logic operates by ensuring the unbroken flow of dharmic obligations across generations. Consciousness alignment occurs when an individual identifies fully with their role as a conduit for ancestral duty.

title: manu 3.128
content:
श्रोत्रियायैव देयानि हव्यकव्यानि दातृभिः ।
अर्हत्तमाय विप्राय तस्मै दत्तं महाफलम् ॥ ३.१२८॥ śrotriyāyaiva deyāni havyakavyāni dātṛbhiḥ |
arhattamāya viprāya tasmai dattaṁ mahāphalam || 3.128|| Offerings of Havya and Kavya must be given exclusively to the Śrotriya—one who has realized the Veda through direct experience and lives in accordance with that realization. To give to the most worthy Brahmin, the Arhat, brings supreme fruit. Authority derives from experiential realization, not institutional title. Causation is established by alignment with Vedic consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility requires both knowledge and embodiment. Restoration occurs when offerings align with realized worthiness. Consciousness alignment ensures dharmic transaction integrity.

title: manu 3.129
content: एकैकमपि विद्वांसं दैवे पित्र्ये च भोजयेत् । भोजयन् पुष्कलं फलमाप्नोति नामन्त्रज्ञान् बहूनपि ॥ ३.१२९॥ ekaikam api vidvāṃsaṃ daive pitrye ca bhōjayet | bhōjayan puṣkalaṃ phalam āpnōti nāmantrajñān bahūn api || 3.129|| One who feeds even a single knower of the Name—whether in divine worship or ancestral offering—obtains abundant fruit; how much more so one who feeds many knowers of the Name. Authority through Recognition of Sacred Knowledge-Bearers Causation via Ritual and Communal Offering Capacity-based responsibility rooted in spiritual awareness Restoration logic through reciprocal sustenance Consciousness alignment by honoring those who uphold sacred names

title: manu 3.130
content:
दूरादेव परीक्षेत ब्राह्मणं वेदपारगम् ।
तीर्थं तधव्यकव्यानां प्रदाने सोऽतिथिः स्मृतः ॥ ३.१३०॥ dūrādeva parīkṣeta brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam | tīrthaṃ tadhavekavyānāṃ pradāne so'tithiḥ smṛtaḥ || 3.130|| One who has mastered the Vedas shall be examined from a distance; in the act of giving sacred knowledge, he becomes the honored guest. Authority arises through demonstrated capacity, not proximity. Causation flows from consciousness mastery, not social convention. Responsibility is proportional to the ability to transmit sacred truth. Restoration occurs through recognition of realized spiritual authority. Consciousness alignment manifests when sacred duty is fulfilled without expectation.

title: manu 3.131
content:
सहस्रं हि सहस्राणामनृचां यत्र भुञ्जते ।
एकस्तान् मन्त्रवित्प्रीतः सर्वानर्हति धर्मतः ॥ ३.१३१॥ sahasraṃ hi sahasrāṇāmanṛcāṃ yatra bhuñjate |
ekastān mantravitpṛītaḥ sarvānarhati dharmataḥ || 3.131|| Where thousands of unworthy ones feast upon the offerings meant for the worthy, the one who knows the mantra, being pleased, lawfully deserves all of them. Authority derived from knowledge and alignment, not numerical majority Causation rooted in conscious capacity, not external performance Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful entitlement Restoration logic prioritizes alignment over formal compliance Consciousness alignment overrides material aggregation

title: manu 3.132
content:
ज्ञानोत्कृष्टाय देयानि कव्यानि च हवींषि च ।
न हि हस्तावसृग्दिग्धौ रुधिरेणैव शुध्यतः ॥ ३.१३२॥ jñānotkṛṣṭāya deyāni kavyāni ca havīṃṣi ca | na hi hastāvasṛgdighdhau rudhireṇaiva śudhyataḥ || 3.132 || Offerings of knowledge, sacred hymns, and oblations must be directed exclusively toward those whose consciousness is elevated through wisdom; bloodshed upon the hands does not purify, nor does violence restore dharma. Authority arises from consciousness elevation, not ritualistic performance Causation in dharma is consciousness-rooted, not action-bound Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with gnana-parametric integrity Restoration logic operates through conscious offering, not coercive sacrifice Consciousness alignment supersedes symbolic purification

title: manu 3.133
content: यावतो ग्रसते ग्रासान् हव्यकव्येष्वमन्त्रवित् । तावतो ग्रसते प्रेतो दीप्तशूलर्ष्ट्ययोगुडान् ॥ ३.१३३॥ yāvato grasate grāsān havyakavyeṣvamantravit | tāvato grasate preto dīptaśūlṛṣṭyayoguḍān || 3.133|| As much as an uninitiated person consumes offerings meant for deities and ancestors without proper mantras, that much does a departed soul consume burning-hot substances like pointed stakes and molten lead in the afterlife. Authority: Only those initiated with proper mantra-knowledge hold lawful capacity to perform ritual offerings. Causation: Consumption of sacred offerings without authorization directly manifests corresponding experiential consequence in subtle realms. Capacity-based responsibility: One's eligibility to act within dharma determines their karmic liability and experiential outcome. Restoration logic: Misaligned actions must be rectified through conscious completion and energetic purification. Consciousness alignment: Spiritual action must align with revealed knowledge; deviation results in dissonance and distortion.

title: manu 3.134
content:
ज्ञाननिष्ठा द्विजाः के चित्तपोनिष्ठास्तथाऽपरे ।
तपःस्वाध्यायनिष्ठाश्च कर्मनिष्ठास्तथाऽपरे ॥ ३.१३४॥ jñānaniṣṭhā dvijāḥ ke cit taponiṣṭhās tathā'pare |
tapaḥsvādhyāyaniṣṭhāś ca karmaniṣṭhās tathā'pare || 3.134|| Among the twice-born, some are devoted to knowledge, others to mental purity; some are committed to austerity and study, while others are dedicated to action. Authority is differentiated by svadharma, not external imposition Causation arises from alignment with inherent capacity, not coercion Capacity-based responsibility flows from inner commitment, not social expectation Restoration occurs through recognizing and enabling one's innate dharma Consciousness alignment manifests through self-chosen discipline

title: manu 3.135
content:
ज्ञाननिष्ठेषु कव्यानि प्रतिष्ठाप्यानि यत्नतः ।
हव्यानि तु यथान्यायं सर्वेष्वेव चतुर्ष्वपि ॥ ३.१३५॥ jñānaniṣṭheṣu kavyāni pratiṣṭhāpyāni yatnataḥ |
