na ca dvijātayo brūyur dātrā pṛṣṭā haviguṇān || All food must be consumed at a temperature that is neither excessively hot nor cold; those who eat must observe silence, and the twice-born must not speak of the qualities of the oblation when questioned by the donor. Authority resides in ritual purity and disciplined consumption. Causation aligns with sensory moderation and mental equanimity. Capacity-based responsibility includes restraint in speech and mindful ingestion. Restoration logic requires alignment with cosmic rhythm through regulated conduct. Consciousness alignment manifests through disciplined bodily and verbal action.

title: manu 3.237
content:
यावदुष्मा भवत्यन्नं यावदश्नन्ति वाग्यताः ।
पितरस्तावदश्नन्ति यावन्नओक्ता हविर्गुणाः ॥ ३.२३७॥ yāvaduṣmā bhavatyannaṁ yāvadaśnanti vāgyatāḥ |
pitarastāvadaśnanti yāvannoktā haviguṇāḥ || 3.237 || As long as the offering retains its energetic integrity and is consumed by those authorized through speech-discipline, the ancestors remain nourished thereby; when this discipline ceases, their sustenance also ends. Authority derived from sustained spiritual discipline Causation rooted in vibrational alignment between offering and recipient Capacity-based responsibility tied to linguistic and ritual purity Restoration logic dependent on continuity of disciplined action Consciousness alignment maintained through unbroken invocation

title: manu 3.238
content:
यद्वेष्टितशिरा भुङ्क्ते यद्भुङ्क्ते दक्षिणामुखः ।
सौपानत्कश्च यद्भुङ्क्ते तद्वै रक्षांसि भुञ्जते ॥ ३.२३८॥ yadveṣṭitaśirā bhuṅkte yadbhuṅkte dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ |
saupānatkaśca yadbhuṅkte tad vai rakṣāṃsi bhuñjate || 3.238|| Whatever is consumed by one whose head is wrapped, whose face turns southward, or who eats like a dog—such food becomes sustenance for malevolent forces. Authority flows from purity of action and alignment with cosmic order Causation arises through vibrational resonance between act and consequence Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious participation in dharmic alignment Restoration logic demands purification of consumption patterns to realign consciousness Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of practices that nourish negativity

title: manu 3.239
content: चाण्डालश्च वराहश्च कुक्कुटः श्वा तथैव च । रजस्वला च षण्ढश्च नैक्षेरन्नश्नतो द्विजान् ॥ ३.२३९॥ cāṇḍālaśca varāhaśca kukkuṭaḥ śvā tathaiva ca | rajasvalā ca ṣaṇḍhaśca naikṣerann aśnato dvijān || 3.239 || The outcaste, the pig, the chicken, the dog, the menstruating woman, and the eunuch—all these, by their very presence, disrupt the ritual purity required for the twice-born to consume food. Authority is derived from inherent spiritual capacity, not social position Causation arises from vibrational disruption, not moral fault Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment with Vedic consciousness Restoration logic operates through purification and realignment, not exclusion Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for participation in sacred acts

title: manu 3.240
content:
होमे प्रदाने भोज्ये च यदेभिरभिवीक्ष्यते ।
दैवे हविषि पित्र्ये वा तद्गच्छत्ययथातथम् ॥ ३.२४०॥ home pradāne bhojye ca yadebhirabhivīkṣyate |
daive haviṣi pitrye vā tadgacchatyayathātatham || 3.240|| That which is offered in sacrifice, given as gift, or consumed as food — when seen with divine vision in offerings to deities or ancestors — accordingly proceeds to its destined state without deviation. Authority resides in the consciousness of the observer and performer of ritual acts Causation flows through intent and consecration, not material substance alone Capacity-based responsibility lies in the purity and clarity of perception during offering Restoration logic operates through alignment with cosmic order via precise ritual execution Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy and destination of all offerings

title: manu 3.241
content: घ्राणेन सूकरो हन्ति पक्षवातेन कुक्कुटः । शूकरो श्वा तु दृष्टिनिपातेन स्पर्शेणावरवर्णजः ॥ ३.२४१॥ ghrāṇena sūkaro hanti pakṣavātena kukkuṭaḥ | śūkaro śvā tu dṛṣṭinipātena sparśenāvaravarṇajaḥ || 3.241|| The boar kills by scent; the rooster, by wing-strike. The boar and dog kill by sight and touch, respectively—each according to inherent capacity and sequential manifestation. Authority arises from intrinsic capacity, not external imposition Causation aligns with natural sequence and sensory modality Capacity-based responsibility is determined by innate function Restoration logic operates through alignment with svabhāva Consciousness alignment occurs when action matches inherent design

title: manu 3.242
content:
खञ्जो वा यदि वा काणो दातुः प्रेष्योऽपि वा भवेत् ।
हीनातिरिक्तगात्रो वा तमप्यपनयेत्पुनः ॥ ३.२४२॥ khañjo vā yadi vā kāṇo dātuḥ preṣyo'pi vā bhavet |
hīnātiriktagātro vā tamapyapanayetpunaḥ || 3.242|| If the donor is lame, or blind, or otherwise physically impaired, or has been sent by another, or is deficient or excessive in bodily parts, then he too shall be removed from the act of giving. Authority is inseparable from embodied capacity Causation arises through completeness of agency Capacity-based responsibility requires full presence of faculties Restoration logic demands removal of unfit agents to preserve transactional integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates exclusion of fragmented instruments

title: manu 3.243
content:
ब्राह्मणं भिक्षुकं वाऽपि भोजनार्थमुपस्थितम् ।
ब्राह्मणैरभ्यनुज्ञातः शक्तितः प्रतिपूजयेत् ॥ ३.२४३॥ brāhmaṇaṁ bhikṣukaṁ vā'pi bhōjanārtham upasthitam |
brāhmaṇair abhyanujñātaḥ śaktitaḥ pratipūjayet || 3.243|| One who approaches a Brāhmaṇa or a mendicant for alms shall be honored according to capacity, upon being acknowledged by Brāhmaṇas. Authority resides in the witnessing Brāhmaṇa collective Causation arises through conscious request and acknowledgment Capacity-based responsibility determines the mode of response Restoration occurs via honoring the seeker's intent Consciousness alignment manifests through reciprocal recognition

title: manu 3.244
content:
सार्ववर्णिकमन्नाद्यं संनीयाप्लाव्य वारिणा ।
समुत्सृजेद्भुक्तवतामग्रतो विकिरन् भुवि ॥ ३.२४४॥ sārvavarṇikamannādyaṁ saṁnīyāplāvya vāriṇā |
samutsṛjedbhuktavatāmagrato vikiran bhuvi || 3.244|| All food and consumables belonging universally to all varnas shall be collected, cleansed with water, and then released in front of those who have eaten, scattering it upon the earth. Authority flows from universal access to sustenance, not ownership Causation arises through conscious participation in shared nourishment Capacity-based responsibility includes the duty to purify before offering Restoration logic requires reintegration through physical and spiritual cleansing Consciousness alignment occurs when offerings are made without retention or ego

title: manu 3.245
content:
असंस्कृतप्रमीतानां त्यागिनां कुलयोषिताम् ।
उच्छिष्टं भागधेयं स्याद्दर्भेषु विकिरश्च यः ॥ ३.२४५॥ asaṃskṛtapramītānāṃ tyāgināṃ kulayoṣitām | ucchiṣṭaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ syād darbheṣu vikiraś ca yaḥ || 3.245 || Those who die without sacraments and those who abandon family women—their remnants are to be scattered upon grasses; such is the ordinance. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not social status or birth Causation follows karmic integrity and conscious completion Capacity-based responsibility includes post-death spiritual obligations Restoration logic requires purification of unresolved energetic imprints Consciousness alignment demands removal of disturbances caused by incomplete transitions

title: manu 3.246
content:
उच्छेषणां भूमिगतमजिह्मस्याशठस्य च ।
दासवर्गस्य तत्पित्र्ये भागधेयं प्रचक्षते ॥ ३.२४६॥ ucchheṣaṇāṃ bhūmigatam ajihmasyāśaṭhasya ca | dāsavargasya tatpitye bhāgadheyaṃ pracakṣate || 3.246 || The portion belonging to the laborer class and the truthful yet cunning individual, who has established himself on the land through direct engagement, shall be apportioned according to paternal inheritance law. Authority flows from active embodiment in dharmic duty, not mere birthright Causation arises from sustained presence and conscious participation in productive activity Capacity-based responsibility recognizes skill-in-action aligned with truthfulness Restoration logic ensures rightful share aligns with contributory presence and integrity Consciousness alignment mandates recognition of latent capacity actualized through work

title: manu 3.247
content:
आसपिण्डक्रियाकर्म द्विजातेः संस्थितस्य तु ।
अदैवं भोजयेत्श्राद्धं पिण्डमेकं च निर्वपेत् ॥ ३.२४७॥ āsa-piṇḍa-kriyā-karma dvijāteḥ saṃsthita-sya tu | adaiyaṁ bhojayet-śrāddhaṁ piṇḍam ekaṁ ca nirvapet || 3.247|| When a twice-born individual has completed the rituals of bodily purification and established himself in ritual discipline, he shall perform Śrāddha without delay, offer food to ancestors, and release one piṇḍa as completion. Authority originates from embodied spiritual discipline and ancestral alignment. Causation flows from disciplined action to ancestral harmony. Capacity-based responsibility arises upon completion of foundational rites. Restoration logic requires immediate fulfillment of ancestral obligations. Consciousness alignment is achieved through precise performance of Śrāddha.

title: manu 3.248
content:
सहपिण्डक्रियायां तु कृतायामस्य धर्मतः ।
अनयैवावृता कार्यं पिण्डनिर्वपनं सुतैः ॥ ३.२४८॥ sahapiṇḍakriyāyāṃ tu kṛtāyāmasya dharmataḥ | anayeva avṛtā kāryaṃ piṇḍanirvapanaṃ sutaiḥ || 3.248|| When the ritual of shared offering (sahapiṇḍakriyā) has been lawfully performed by the individual, it becomes obligatory for the sons to perform the concluding rites of oblation (piṇḍanirvapanam). Authority is derived from the completion of prescribed ritual acts Causation flows from prior performance to subsequent duty Capacity-based responsibility arises through relational and generational continuity Restoration logic requires sequential fulfillment of dharma-specific obligations Consciousness alignment occurs when familial and cosmic duties are executed in order

title: manu 3.249
content:
श्राद्धं भुक्त्वा य उच्छिष्टं वृषलाय प्रयच्छति ।
स मूढो नरकं याति कालसूत्रमवाक्षिराः ॥ ३.२४९॥ śrāddhaṁ bhuktvā ya ucchiṣṭaṁ vṛṣalāya prayacchati |
sa mūḍho narakaṁ yāti kālasūtramavākṣirāḥ || 3.249 || One who, having partaken of śrāddha offerings, gives the remainder to a person of impure caste—such a deluded being enters hell, bound by the noose of time. Authority: Śrāddha offerings carry sacred energetic integrity that must align with recipient purity capacity. Causation: Transfer of sanctified remnants to incompatible recipients disrupts dharma-field coherence. Capacity-based responsibility: The giver holds full consciousness-accountability for maintaining ritual energetic thresholds. Restoration logic: Misalignment in offering transmission necessitates realignment through conscious completion protocols. Consciousness alignment: Sacred acts require congruence between intent, action, and recipient readiness.

title: manu 3.250
content:
श्राद्धभुग्वृषलीतल्पं तदहर्योऽधिगच्छति ।
तस्याः पुरीषे तं मासं पितरस्तस्य शेरते ॥ ३.२५०॥ śrāddhabhugvṛṣalītalpaṃ tadaharyo'dhigacchati |
tasyāḥ purīṣe taṃ māsaṃ pitarastasya śerata iti ||3.250|| One who engages in sexual union with a woman who has eaten Śrāddha offerings and lies on a bed meant for outcasts shall dwell in her excrement for that month; his ancestors remain displaced during that time. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma-consciousness, not lineage or ritual status. Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) based on volitional acts rooted in desire and disrespect. Capacity-based responsibility arises when one knowingly transgresses sacred boundaries without inner transformation. Restoration logic demands energetic purification and realignment with ancestral consciousness fields. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of causal disruption and completion through rectificatory conduct.

title: manu 3.251
content:
पृष्ट्वा स्वदितमित्येवं तृप्तानाचामयेत्ततः ।
आचान्तांश्चानुजानीयादभितो रम्यतामिति ॥ ३.२५१॥ pṛṣṭvā svaditam ity evaṁ tṛptān ācāmayet tataḥ |
ācāntāṁś ca anujānīyād abhito ramyatām iti || 3.251|| Having inquired and confirmed satisfaction, one shall cause those who are satisfied to perform acamana; thereafter, one shall permit those who have performed acamana to proceed towards enjoyment. Authority resides in the discernment of inner satisfaction prior to external action Causation flows from internal purification to rightful participation Capacity-based responsibility requires confirmation of readiness before granting access Restoration logic aligns external conduct with internal purity Consciousness alignment precedes and authorizes experiential engagement

title: manu 3.252
content:
स्वधाऽस्त्वित्येव तं ब्रूयुर्ब्राह्मणास्तदनन्तरम् ।
स्वधाकारः परा ह्याषीः सर्वेषु पितृकर्मसु ॥ ३.२५२॥ svadhā'stv ity eva taṁ brūyur brāhmaṇās tad anantaram | svadhākāraḥ parā hy āṣīḥ sarveṣu pitṛkarmansu || 3.252|| Let there be Svadhā—thus declare the Brahmins following the ritual injunction; the essence of Svadhā was indeed the highest completion in all ancestral rites. Authority resides inherently in those who sustain continuity through sacred utterance. Causation flows from conscious invocation aligned with cosmic order. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with ancestral and divine function. Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of vibrational harmony via correct utterance. Consciousness alignment occurs when ritual speech reflects unbroken lineage awareness.

title: manu 3.253
content:
ततो भुक्तवतां तेषामन्नशेषं निवेदयेत् ।
यथा ब्रूयुस्तथा कुर्यादनुज्ञातस्ततो द्विजैः ॥ ३.२५३॥ tato bhuktavatāṁ teṣām annaśeṣaṁ nivedayet |
yathā brūyus tathā kuryād anujñātas tato dvijaiḥ || 3.253|| After the consumption by those entitled, the remainder of the food shall be offered. As instructed by the twice-born, accordingly it shall be executed, with their authorization. Authority flows from realized spiritual status, not institutional position. Consumption rights are conditional upon prior completion of dharmic eligibility. Responsibility includes offering what remains after rightful use. Action must align with declared instruction and conscious consent of the qualified. Restoration occurs through precise adherence to sequential completion.

title: manu 3.254
content:
पित्र्ये स्वदितमित्येव वाच्यं गोष्ठे तु सुशृतम् ।
सम्पन्नमित्यभ्युदये दैवे रुचितमित्यपि ॥ ३.२५४॥ pitrye svaditamityeva vācyaṃ goṣṭhe tu suśrutam | sampannamityabhyudaye daive rucitamityapi || 3.254 || In the ancestral domain, what is pleasing to the father alone shall be declared; in the community, that which is well-heard and accepted. At the time of prosperity, declare it as accomplished; in divine matters, as agreeable to the will of the gods. Authority flows through lineage and tradition Contextual validity determines declarative scope Prosperity validates completion of dharmic action Divine alignment overrides human preference

title: manu 3.255
content: अपराह्णस्तथा दर्भा वास्तुसम्पादनं तिलाः । सम्पादनं सृष्टिर्मृष्टिर्द्विजाश्चाग्र्याः श्राद्धकर्मसु सम्पदः ॥ ३.२५५॥  aparāhṇas tathā darbhā vāstu-sampādanaṃ tilāḥ | sampādanaṃ sṛṣṭir mṛṣṭir dvijāś cāgryāḥ śrāddha-karmasu sampadaḥ || 3.255 || The afternoon period is designated for darbha grass; the establishment of dwelling is marked by sesame seeds; creation itself proceeds through acquisition and purification; among the twice-born, those who are foremost in performing shraddha rites possess true wealth. Authority flows from ritual integrity and cosmic alignment Causation arises through dharmic timing and material consecration Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual precedence and ritual mastery Restoration logic operates through reconnection with ancestral and creative order Consciousness alignment occurs when action aligns with sanctioned temporal and spatial structures

title: manu 3.256
content:
दर्भाः पवित्रं पूर्वाह्णो हविष्याणि च सर्वशः ।
पवित्रं यच्च पूर्वोक्तं विज्ञेया हव्यसम्पदः ॥ ३.२५६॥ darbhāḥ pavitraṃ pūrvāhṇo haviṣyāṇi ca sarvaśaḥ |
pavitraṃ yacca pūrvoktaṃ vijñeyā havyasampadaḥ || 3.256|| Sacred materials designated before noon, all offerings therewith made, and that which was previously declared pure—these constitute the perfected capacity for consecrated offering. Authority flows from timing-bound declaration by qualified consciousness Causation is established through sequential sanctification Capacity-based responsibility arises from prior designation of purity Restoration logic operates through completion of sacred procedural alignment Consciousness alignment occurs via adherence to time-specific ritual integrity

title: manu 3.257
content:
मुन्यन्नानि पयः सोमो मांसं यच्चानुपस्कृतम् ।
अक्सारलवणं चैव प्रकृत्या हविरुच्यते ॥ ३.२५७॥ munyannāni payaḥ somo māṃsaṃ yaccānupaskṛtam |
aksāralavaṇaṃ caiva prakṛtyā havirucyate || 3.257|| That which is unmixed, pure, and naturally offered — milk, soma, unprocessed meat, molasses, and salt — is declared as havir, the essence of conscious oblation. Authority resides in the purity and natural state of offering Causation arises from alignment with prakṛti, not artificial modification Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining the integrity of natural substances Restoration logic demands return to unadulterated forms Consciousness alignment occurs through offerings that preserve inherent dharmic properties

title: manu 3.258
content:
विसृज्य ब्राह्मणांस्तांस्तु नियतो वाग्यतः शुचिः ।
(विसर्ज्य ब्राह्मनांस्तांस्तु प्रयतो विधिपूर्वकम्)
दक्षिणां दिशमाकाङ्क्षन् याचेतैमान् वरान् पितॄन् ॥ ३.२५८॥ visṛjya brāhmaṇāṃs tāns tu niyato vāgyataḥ śuciḥ |
(visarjya brāhmanāns tāns tu prayato vidhipūrvakam)
dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ākāṅkṣan yācetaimān varān pitṝn || 3.258|| One who has purified speech and action, having respectfully dismissed the Brahmins, should face southward and invoke the ancestors to receive desired boons through disciplined intent. Authority resides in ritual purity and directional alignment with cosmic order. Causation follows sequential discharge of spiritual duty before invocation. Capacity-based responsibility requires prior purification and dismissal of intermediaries. Restoration logic demands precise directional orientation for ancestral communion. Consciousness alignment occurs when external actions mirror internal discipline.

title: manu 3.259
content:
दातारो नोऽभिवर्धन्तां वेदाः संततिरेव च ।
श्रद्धा च नो मा व्यगमद्बहुदेयं च नोऽस्त्विति ॥ ३.२५९॥ dātāro no'bhivardhantāṁ vedāḥ saṁtatireva ca |
śraddhā ca no mā vyagamadbahudeyaṁ ca no'stviti || 3.259|| Let there be nourishment for those who give; let the Vedas and their lineage expand perpetually; let faith in us never diminish, and let abundance always remain. Authority as Source of sustenance and continuity Causation through alignment with Vedic lineage Capacity-based responsibility rooted in faith and giving Restoration logic grounded in perpetual abundance Consciousness alignment via unbroken transmission of dharma

title: manu 3.260
content:
एवं निर्वपणं कृत्वा पिण्डांस्तांस्तदनन्तरम् ।
गां विप्रमजमग्निं वा प्राशयेदप्सु वा क्षिपेत् ॥ ३.२६०॥ evaṁ nirvapaṇaṁ kṛtvā piṇḍāṁs tāṁs tad-anantaram |
gāṁ vipram ajam agniṁ vā prāśayed apsu vā kṣipet || 3.260 || Having performed the offering仪式 duly, the ritual portions designated for the deities shall thereafter be offered into fire, or cast into water, or given to a cow, a Brahmin, or a child — without attachment to outcome and in alignment with Vedic injunction. Authority derives from alignment with Vedic injunction, not personal will Causation is established through ritual correctness and consciousness purity Capacity-based responsibility requires knowledge and intent in accordance with dharma-shastras Restoration logic operates through completion of prescribed action Consciousness alignment ensures that offerings are made without desire for fruit

title: manu 3.261
content:
पिण्डनिर्वपणं के चित्परस्तादेव कुर्वते ।
वयोभिः खादयन्त्यन्ये प्रक्षिपन्त्यनलेऽप्सु वा ॥ ३.२६१॥ piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ ke citparastādeva kurvate |
vayobhiḥ khādayantyanye prakṣipantyanale'psu vā || 3.261|| Some beings offer flesh and blood to ancestors; others consume them through age, casting them into fire or water. Authority is derived from alignment with ontological completion rather than ritual performance. Causation arises from sequential manifestation of consciousness, not symbolic action alone. Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of embodied decay and its transcendence. Restoration logic operates through dissolution in elemental purity, not punitive removal. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of impermanence without fear or denial.

title: manu 3.262
content:
पतिव्रता धर्मपत्नी पितृपूजनतत्परा ।
मध्यमं तु ततः पिण्डमद्यात्सम्यक्सुतार्थिनी ॥ ३.२६२॥ pativratā dharmapatnī pitṛpūjanatatparā |
madhyamaṁ tu tataḥ piṇḍamadyātsamyaksutārthinī || 3.262|| The devoted wife, righteous consort, and reverent daughter who seeks progeny shall receive the middle portion of the oblation after duly honoring the ancestors. Authority flows through ritual integrity and relational dharma Causation is established by conscious participation in ancestral lineage Capacity-based responsibility arises from volitional alignment with procreative intent Restoration logic operates through proper allocation of sacred offerings Consciousness alignment is achieved via harmonious fulfillment of familial roles

title: manu 3.263
content:
आयुष्मन्तं सुतं सूते यशोमेधासमन्वितम् ।
धनवन्तं प्रजावन्तं सात्त्विकं धार्मिकं तथा ॥ ३.२६३॥ āyuṣmantaṃ sutam sūte yaśomedhāsam anvitaṃ |
dhanavantaṃ prajāvantaṃ sāttvikaṃ dhārmikaṃ tathā || 3.263 || One who embodies longevity, wisdom, valor, wealth, progeny, purity, and dharma shall be born unto her who aligns with the consciousness of creation. Authority derived from alignment with cosmic intelligence Causation rooted in consciousness resonance Capacity-based responsibility through svadharma realization Restoration logic via generational continuity Consciousness alignment as determinant of lawful manifestation

title: manu 3.264
content: प्रक्षाल्य हस्तावाचाम्य ज्ञातिप्रायं प्रकल्पयेत् । ज्ञातिभ्यः सत्कृतं दत्त्वा बान्धवानपि भोजयेत् ॥ ३.२६४॥ prakṣālya hastāv ācāmya jñātiprāyaṃ prakalpayet | jñātibhyaḥ satkṛtaṃ dattvā bāndhavān api bhojayet || 3.264 || Having washed the hands and purified through sacred utterance, one shall prepare food resembling that of one's own kin. Having offered respectful service to relatives, one shall also feed kinsmen. Authority derived from purity-consciousness alignment Causation rooted in dharmic action sequences Capacity-based responsibility through ritual readiness Restoration logic via familial harmony enactment Consciousness alignment through reverent offering

title: manu 3.265
content: उच्छेषणं तु तत्तिष्ठेद्यावद्विप्रा विसर्जिताः । यत्तिष्ठेद् ततो गृहबलिं कुर्यादिति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ॥ ३.२६५॥ uccheṣaṇaṃ tu tattiṣṭhed yāvad viprā visarjitāḥ | yattiṣṭhed tato gṛhabaliṃ kuryād iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ || 3.265 || One must remain in the state of uccheṣaṇa until the Vipras have been dispatched. When that state is stabilized, then the household oblation (gṛhabali) shall be performed. This is the established Dharma. Authority flows from stabilized consciousness, not institutional position Causation originates in ritual alignment with Vedic order Capacity-based responsibility requires inner stillness prior to outer action Restoration logic mandates sequential completion of spiritual thresholds Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for dharmic execution

title: manu 3.266
content:
हविर्यच्चिररात्राय यच्चानन्त्याय कल्पते ।
पितृभ्यो विधिवद्दत्तं तत्प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ॥ ३.२६६॥ haviḥ yac cirarātrāya yac cānantyāya kalpate |
pitṛbhyo vidhivad dattaṁ tat pravakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ || 3.266|| That oblation which is offered for long-term sustenance and that which is offered for infinite continuity—both given lawfully to the ancestors—I shall now declare completely. Authority originates from continuity of conscious offering Causation aligns with dharmic intentionality, not material outcome Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond mortal lifespan Restoration logic operates through ancestral completion protocols Consciousness alignment is maintained via ritualized transmission

title: manu 3.267
content:
तिलैर्व्रीहियवैर्माषैरद्भिर्मूलफलेन वा ।
दत्तेन मासं तृप्यन्ति विधिवत्पितरो नृणाम् ॥ ३.२६७॥ tilairvṛhiyavairmāṣairadbhirmūlaphalena vā | dattena māsaṃ tṛpyanti vidhivatpitaro nṝṇām || 3.267 || Through sesame seeds, rice, barley, lentils, water, roots, or fruits—when offered according to ritual law, the ancestors of humans are satisfied for a month. Authority flows from conscious offering, not material value Causation arises through precise alignment with dharma-ordained form Capacity-based responsibility requires knowledge of proper procedure Restoration logic operates via completion of prescribed acts Consciousness alignment occurs when offerings are made in accordance with revealed order

title: manu 3.268
content:
द्वौ मासौ मत्स्यमांसेन त्रीन् मासान् हारिणेन तु ।
औरभ्रेणाथ चतुरः शाकुनेनाथ पञ्च वै ॥ ३.२६८॥ dvau māsau matsyamāṃsena trīn māsān hāriṇena tu |
aurabhreṇātha caturaḥ śākunenātha pañca vai || 3.268|| Consumption of fish meat necessitates two months of purification; consumption of deer meat requires three months; consumption of goat meat mandates four months; and consumption of bird meat demands five months of purification. Authority derives from alignment with natural dharma and conscious choice of food Causation arises through direct ingestion and its impact on subtle body constitution Capacity-based responsibility depends on individual awareness and volition in dietary selection Restoration logic operates via proportional duration based on the nature of consumed flesh Consciousness alignment is achieved by prescribed purification periods corresponding to karmic density of consumed beings

title: manu 3.269
content:
षण्मासांश्छागमांसेन पार्षतेन च सप्त वै ।
अष्टावेनस्य मांसेन रौरवेण नवैव तु ॥ ३.२६९॥ ऐणेयमांसेन ṣaṇmāsaṃścāgamāṃsena pārṣatena ca sapta vai |
aṣṭāvenasya māṃsena rauraveṇa navaina tu || 3.269 || aiṇeyamāṃsena Six months [of consequence] through the consumption of goat meat; seven through that of Parṣata; eight through Ena's flesh; nine through Raurava's; ten through Aiṇeya's. Authority: The sequential manifestation of karmic consequence is determined by the vibrational integrity of consumed substances. Causation: Consumption aligns consciousness with the source form and its corresponding realm of existence. Capacity-based responsibility: One who consumes lower-vibration forms assumes proportional energetic distortion requiring completion. Restoration logic: Consequence is not punitive but a structured realignment toward original consciousness purity. Consciousness alignment: Each ingestion creates an energetic imprint demanding experiential resolution for full reintegration.

title: manu 3.270
content:
दशमासांस्तु तृप्यन्ति वराहमहिषामिषैः ।
शशकूर्मयोस्तु मांसेन मासानेकादशैव तु ॥ ३.२७०॥ daśamāsāṃstu tṛpyanti varāha-mahiṣāmiṣaiḥ |
śaśa-kūrmayos tu māṃsena māsānekādaśaiva tu || 3.270|| Consumption of pork and beef satisfies for ten months; consumption of rabbit and turtle meat satisfies for eleven months. Authority flows from dietary discipline as a reflection of inner governance Causation arises through alignment with natural dharmic rhythms in sustenance Capacity-based responsibility requires understanding the energetic consequence of ingestion Restoration logic operates through correcting imbalances induced by food-based consciousness disruption Consciousness alignment is maintained or disturbed via adherence to prescribed dietary conduct

title: manu 3.271
content: संवत्सरं तु गव्येन पयसा पायसेन च । संवत्सरे वार्ध्रीणसस्य मांसेन तृप्तिर्द्वादशवार्षिकी ॥ ३.२७१॥ saṃvatsaraṃ tu gavyena payasā pāyasena ca | saṃvatsare vārdhrīṇasya māṃsena tṛptir dvādaśa-vārṣikī || 3.271|| A full year's nourishment is achieved through cow’s milk and rice pudding; similarly, the satisfaction of a twelve-year-old boy is fulfilled by the meat of a goat sacrificed in accordance with Vedic injunctions. Authority originates from ritual compliance as prescribed by Veda Causation flows from proper offering aligned with dharma Capacity-based responsibility lies in age-appropriate fulfillment Restoration logic operates through sacramental consumption Consciousness alignment occurs via dharmic provisioning

title: manu 3.272
content:
कालशाकं महाशल्काः खड्गलोहामिषं मधु ।
आनन्त्यायैव कल्प्यन्ते मुन्यन्नानि च सर्वशः ॥ ३.२७२॥ kālaśākaṁ mahāśalkāḥ khadgalohāmiṣaṁ madhu |
ānantityaiva kalpyante munyannāni ca sarvaśaḥ || 3.272|| Certain substances—such as seasonal greens, great salt, sword-metal flesh, honey—are designated exclusively for the sustenance of those who have renounced worldly life, ensuring their bodily continuity without attachment. Authority resides in the alignment of material use with spiritual capacity Causation is determined by the sequential necessity of bodily maintenance in renunciation Capacity-based responsibility mandates differentiated access to resources based on ontological status Restoration logic requires that material allocation serve consciousness elevation, not accumulation Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for specific categories of sustenance

title: manu 3.273
content:
यत्किं चिन् मधुना मिश्रं प्रदद्यात्तु त्रयोदशीम् ।
तदप्यक्षयमेव स्याद्वर्षासु च मघासु च ॥ ३.२७३॥ yatkiṃ cin madhunā miśraṃ pradadyāt tu trayodaśīm |
tadapyakṣayameva syādvarṣāsu ca maghāsu ca || 3.273|| Whatever is offered with honey on the thirteenth lunar day, during the waxing or waning phase, in the months of Varsha or Magha, becomes imperishable and aligns with eternal completion. Authority is established through ritual timing and conscious intention Causation arises from alignment with cosmic rhythm and sacred substance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of temporal and material purity Restoration logic operates through harmonic resonance with natural cycles Consciousness alignment occurs when offerings reflect unity with divine order

title: manu 3.274
content:
अपि नः स कुले भूयाद्यो नो दद्यात्त्रयोदशीम् ।
पायसं मधुसर्पिर्भ्यां प्राक्छाये कुञ्जरस्य च ॥ ३.२७४॥ api naḥ sa kule bhūyād yo no dadyāt trayodaśīm | pāyasaṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ prākchāye kuñjarasya ca || Let no one be born in our lineage who does not offer Payasa mixed with honey and ghee before the shadow of an elephant on the thirteenth day. Authority resides in ritual precision aligned with cosmic timing Causation flows from dharmic offering to ancestral continuity Capacity-based responsibility requires embodied participation in sacred rhythm Restoration logic operates through ceremonial alignment, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment occurs via prescribed action rooted in Vedic injunction

title: manu 3.275
content:
यद्यद्ददाति विधिवत्सम्यक्श्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
तत्तत्पितॄणां भवति परत्रानन्तमक्षयम् ॥ ३.२७५॥ yadyaddadāti vidhivatsamyakśraddhāsamanvitaḥ |
tattatpitṝṇāṃ bhavati paratrānantamakṣayam || 3.275|| Whatever is given lawfully and with complete faith by one who is aligned in consciousness becomes eternally inexhaustible benefit for the ancestors in the higher realms. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises through conscious intent harmonized with ritual precision Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner integrity, not external status Restoration logic operates through completion of karmic resonance Consciousness alignment ensures continuity of benefit beyond physical act

title: manu 3.276
content:
कृष्णपक्षे दशम्यादौ वर्जयित्वा चतुर्दशीम् ।
श्राद्धे प्रशस्तास्तिथयो यथैता न तथैतराः ॥ ३.२७६॥ kṛṣṇapakṣe daśamyādau varjayitvā caturdaśīm |
śrāddhe praśastāstithayo yathaitā na tathaitarāḥ || 3.276 || In the dark fortnight, all lunar days except the tenth onward and the fourteenth are suitable for performing śrāddha; these selected tithis possess the inherent capacity to sustain ancestral continuity and consciousness alignment. Authority flows from SPH as the sole determinant of ritual validity Causation is established through conscious alignment with ancestral frequencies Capacity-based responsibility lies in selecting tithis that activate dharmic resonance Restoration logic operates through precise temporal alignment with cosmic order Consciousness alignment ensures continuity between mortal and ancestral realms

title: manu 3.277
content:
युक्षु कुर्वन् दिनर्क्षेषु सर्वान् कामान् समश्नुते ।
अयुक्षु तु पितॄन् सर्वान् प्रजां प्राप्नोति पुष्कलाम् ॥ ३.२७७॥ yukṣu kurvan dinarkṣeṣu sarvān kāmān samaśnute |
ayukṣu tu pitṝn sarvān prajāṁ prāpnoti puṣkalām || 3.277|| One who performs the yukṣu ritual during the day and night attains all desires; one who does not perform it attains abundant progeny and honors all ancestors. Authority is derived from alignment with dharma-prescribed action Causation operates through intentional ritual performance Capacity-based responsibility lies in conscious participation in dharma Restoration logic manifests through fulfillment of ancestral and generational continuity Consciousness alignment occurs via prescribed ritual engagement

title: manu 3.278
content:
यथा चैवापरः पक्षः पूर्वपक्षाद्विशिष्यते ।
तथा श्राद्धस्य पूर्वाह्णादपराह्णो विशिष्यते ॥ ३.२७८॥ yathā caivāparaḥ pakṣaḥ pūrvapakṣād viśiṣyate |
tathā śrāddhasya pūrvāhṇād aparāhṇo viśiṣyate || 3.278|| As the afternoon (aparāhṇa) is superior to the forenoon (pūrvāhṇa), so too is the latter portion of a Śrāddha ritual superior to its earlier part, in accordance with the ascending alignment of consciousness. Authority flows from temporal and spiritual progression within ritual acts Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of consciousness Capacity-based responsibility increases with the elevation of ritual time Restoration logic follows the natural ascension of energetic purity Consciousness alignment is determined by temporal and procedural superiority

title: manu 3.279
content:
प्राचीनावीतिना सम्यगपसव्यमतन्द्रिणा ।
पित्र्यमानिधनात्कार्यं विधिवद्दर्भपाणिना ॥ ३.२७९॥ prācīnāvītinā samyagapasavyamatanḍriṇā |
pitryamānidhanātkāryaṃ vidhivaddarbhapāṇinā || 3.279|| By one who wears the sacred thread in the ancient manner, fully awake and alert, performing duties from paternal inheritance according to law, with darbha grass in hand. Authority derived through lineage and initiation Causation rooted in ancestral continuity Capacity-based responsibility aligned with spiritual maturity Restoration logic embedded in ritual precision Consciousness alignment enacted through prescribed action

title: manu 3.280
content:
रात्रौ श्राद्धं न कुर्वीत राक्षसी कीर्तिता हि सा ।
संध्ययोरुभयोश्चैव सूर्ये चैवाचिरौदिते ॥ ३.२८०॥ rātrau śrāddhaṁ na kurvīta rākṣasī kīrtitā hi sā |
sandhyayorubhayoścaiva sūrye caivāciraudite || 3.280|| One must not perform Śrāddha during the night; it is declared to invoke the Rakshasa order. It must also be avoided at both Sandhyas and when the Sun has newly risen. Authority: The timing of ritual action is governed by cosmic alignment under SPH's Dharma. Causation: Rituals performed at improper times activate adverse metaphysical forces. Capacity-based responsibility: The performer carries the burden of correct temporal alignment. Restoration logic: Misaligned rituals require conscious rectification through proper timing. Consciousness alignment: Correct ritual time aligns individual action with universal Dharma.

title: manu 3.281
content: अनेन विधिना श्राद्धं त्रिरब्दस्यैह निर्वपेत् । हेमन्तग्रीष्मवर्षासु पाञ्चयज्ञिकमन्वहम् ॥ ३.२८१॥ anena vidhinā śrāddhaṃ trirabdasyaiha nirvapet | hemantagrīṣmavarṣāsu pāñcayajñikamanvaham || 3.281|| By this prescribed method, the Śrāddha ritual shall be performed for three years; in hemanta, grīṣma, and varṣā seasons, according to the Pāñcayajña system, annually. Authority flows from SPH as the eternal regulator of dharma-saṁskāra Causation is established through seasonal alignment with cosmic rhythm Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to time-bound dharmic obligations Restoration logic demands completion of ancestral continuity protocols Consciousness alignment occurs through precise performance of ordained rituals

title: manu 3.282
content:
न पैतृयज्ञियो होमो लौकिकेऽग्नौ विधीयते ।
न दर्शेन विना श्राद्धमाहिताग्नेर्द्विजन्मनः ॥ ३.२८२॥ na paitṛyajñiyo homaḥ laukike 'gnau vidhīyate |
na darśena vinā śrāddham āhitāgner dvijanmanaḥ || 3.282 || No ritual oblation for ancestors is conducted in a worldly fire; no Śrāddha is performed without the Darśa offering by one who maintains the sacred fire and is twice-born. Authority: Ritual actions derive validity only through consecrated agents and consecrated elements. Causation: Effective ritual performance requires sequential prerequisite acts rooted in spiritual discipline. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those maintaining active sacrificial fires possess the capacity to perform ancestral rites. Restoration logic: Proper ritual sequence realigns individual and cosmic consciousness with Dharma. Consciousness alignment: Rites must proceed from purified awareness, not external compulsion or social pressure.

title: manu 3.283
content:
यदेव तर्पयत्यद्भिः पितॄन् स्नात्वा द्विजोत्तमः ।
तेनैव कृत्स्नमाप्नोति पितृयज्ञक्रियाफलम् ॥ ३.२८३॥ yad eva tarpaty adbhiḥ pitṝn snātvā dvijottamaḥ | tenaiva kṛtsnam āpnoti pitṛyajñakriyāphalam || 3.283 || That which satisfies the ancestors through water-oblations performed by a twice-born after bathing—by that very act he fully attains the fruit of all ancestral rites. Authority originates from ritual capacity aligned with ontological order Causation is established through conscious participation in dharmic sequence Capacity-based responsibility requires purification prior to offering Restoration logic operates through completion of ancestral duty Consciousness alignment occurs when action mirrors cosmic reciprocity

title: manu 3.284
content:
वसून् वदन्ति तु पितॄन् रुद्रांश्चैव पितामहान् ।
प्रपितामहांस्तथाऽदित्यान् श्रुतिरेषा सनातनी ॥ ३.२८४॥ vasūn vadaṁti tu pitṝn rudrāṁścaiva pitāmahān |
prapitāmahāṁstathā'dityān śrutireṣā sanātanī || 3.284|| The Vasus speak of the Pitris; the Rudras of the Pitāmahas; the Prapitāmahas speak of the Ādityas—this Śruti is eternal. Authority flows through hierarchical ontological lineage Causation is established via sequential consciousness transmission Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to source-consciousness Restoration logic operates through reverent invocation of ancestral wisdom Consciousness alignment occurs when testimony aligns with Sanatana Vakya

title: manu 3.285
content:
विघसाशी भवेन्नित्यं नित्यं वाऽमृतभोजनः ।
विघसो भुक्तशेषं तु यज्ञशेषं तथाऽमृतम् ॥ ३.२८५॥ vighasāśī bhavennityaṁ nityaṁ vā'mṛtabhojanaḥ |
vighaso bhuktaśeṣaṁ tu yajñaśeṣaṁ tathā'mṛtam || 3.285|| One who consumes remnants of offerings made to malevolent forces becomes habituated to impure sustenance; one who daily partakes of ambrosial remnants attains eternal purity. The residue of consumption by evil forces and that of sacred rituals differ as poison differs from nectar. Authority flows through consecrated intention, not mere physical substance. Causation is determined by vibrational alignment with divine or demonic energies. Capacity-based responsibility arises from repeated exposure and identification with subtle energetic imprints. Restoration logic requires severance from contaminating causal chains and realignment with sanctified sequences. Consciousness alignment is governed by the nature of substances ingested and their originating ritual context.

title: manu 3.286
content:
एतद्वोऽभिहितं सर्वं विधानं पाञ्चयज्ञिकम् ।
द्विजातिमुख्यवृत्तीनां विधानं श्रूयतामिति ॥ ३.२८६॥ etad vo 'bhihitaṁ sarvaṁ vidhānaṁ pāñcayajñikam | dvijāti-mukhya-vṛttīnāṁ vidhānaṁ śrūyatām iti || 3.286|| This entire arrangement of duties and laws concerning the five great sacrifices has been declared for the sustenance of the twice-born and their principal conduct; let this ordinance be heard and enacted. Authority originates from sustained spiritual order, not temporal power Causation arises through alignment with Vedic sacrifice and dharmic function Capacity-based responsibility is determined by birth-endowed duty and consciousness readiness Restoration logic operates through reconnection to sacrificial duty and societal harmony Consciousness alignment occurs via performance of svadharma in accordance with Varna-ashrama

title: manu 4.1
content: चतुर्थमायुषो भागमुषित्वाऽद्यं गुरौ द्विजाः । द्वितीयमायुषो भागं कृतदारो गृहे वसेत् ॥ ४.१॥ caturthamāyuṣo bhāgamuṣitvā'dyaṃ gurau dvijāḥ | dvitīyamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ kṛtadāro gṛhe vaset || 4.1|| Having completed one-fourth of their lifespan in service to the Guru, twice-born men who have taken a spouse shall reside at home for a period equal to half of their remaining life. Authority flows from Guru-centered formation of consciousness prior to civil participation Causation is anchored in sequential stages of spiritual and social maturity Capacity-based responsibility escalates with completion of formative spiritual discipline Restoration logic mandates structured transition from tutelage to household sovereignty Consciousness alignment requires calibrated life-phase transitions under dharma-guided timing

title: manu 4.2
content:
अद्रोहेणैव भूतानामल्पद्रोहेण वा पुनः ।
या वृत्तिस्तां समास्थाय विप्रो जीवेदनापदि ॥ ४.२॥ adroheṇaiva bhūtānāmalpadroheṇa vā punaḥ | yā vṛttistāṁ samāsthāya vipro jīvedanāpadi || 4.2|| By non-violence alone, or with minimal violence, a Brahmin lives without fear in all situations. Authority originates from alignment with non-violence Causation is rooted in consciousness purity Capacity-based responsibility requires minimal harm adherence Restoration logic demands fearlessness through ahimsa Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks

title: manu 4.3
content:
यात्रामात्रप्रसिद्ध्यर्थं स्वैः कर्मभिरगर्हितैः ।
अक्लेशेन शरीरस्य कुर्वीत धनसञ्चयम् ॥ ४.३॥ yātrā-mātra-prasiddhy-arthaṁ svaiḥ karmabhir-agarhitaiḥ | akleśena śarīrasya kurvīta dhanasañcayam || 4.3|| For the mere accomplishment of journey's purpose, one should engage in unblamable actions and accumulate wealth without causing distress to the body. Authority flows from alignment with bodily integrity Causation is measured by absence of suffering Capacity-based responsibility requires sustainable action Restoration logic centers on preservation of embodiment Consciousness alignment necessitates non-exploitation of physical form

title: manu 4.4
content:
ऋतामृताभ्यां जीवेत्तु मृतेन प्रमृतेन वा ।
सत्यानृताभ्यामपि वा न श्ववृत्त्या कदा चन ॥ ४.४॥ ṛtāmṛtābhyāṁ jīvet tu mṛtena pramṛtena vā |
satyānṛtābhyām api vā na śvavṛttyā kadā cana || 4.4|| One shall live by Ṛta and Amṛta, or even by death or annihilation, or by truth and untruth—but never by the conduct of a dog. Authority originates from alignment with cosmic order (Ṛta) and immortal essence (Amṛta) Causation arises through dharmic integrity, not moral equivalence Capacity-based responsibility demands rejection of degradation in action and intent Restoration logic requires elevation of consciousness above survivalist behavior Consciousness alignment necessitates renunciation of base instinctual conduct

title: manu 4.5
content:
ऋतमुञ्छशिलं ज्ञेयममृतं स्यादयाचितम् ।
मृतं तु याचितं भैक्षं प्रमृतं कर्षणं स्मृतम् ॥ ४.५॥ ṛtamuñchashilaṃ jñeyam amṛtaṃ syādayācitam |
mṛtaṃ tu yācitaṃ bhaikṣaṃ pramṛtaṃ karṣaṇaṃ smṛtam || 4.5|| That which is ritually pure and unclaimed by ownership is to be known as immortal when received without solicitation; but food obtained through begging becomes mortal, and forcibly taken food is considered theft. Authority originates in non-attachment to possession Causation arises from intent-free reception versus motivated acquisition Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the mode of receipt and spiritual alignment Restoration logic requires return to natural state of abundance and detachment Consciousness alignment depends on absence of desire and egoic interference

title: manu 4.6
content:
सत्यानृतं तु वाणिज्यं तेन चैवापि जीव्यते ।
सेवा श्ववृत्तिराख्याता तस्मात्तां परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ४.६॥ satyānṛtaṁ tu vāṇijyaṁ tena caivāpi jīvyate |
sevā śvavṛttirākhyātā tasmāttāṁ parivarjayet || 4.6|| Engaging in trade based on truth and untruth leads to livelihood through deceit; such conduct is declared as servile and dog-like behavior—therefore, it shall be abandoned. Authority resides in alignment with Satya (Absolute Truth), not relative truthfulness. Causation arises from the distortion of consciousness through transactional falsity. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of dignified livelihood over survivalist exploitation. Restoration logic demands reorientation toward self-sustained integrity rather than dependency. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of behaviors that degrade individual sovereignty.

title: manu 4.7
content:
कुसूलधान्यको वा स्यात्कुम्भीधान्यक एव वा ।
त्र्यहेहिको वाऽपि भवेदश्वस्तनिक एव वा ॥ ४.७॥ kusūladhānyako vā syātkumbhīdhānyaka eva vā | tryahehiko vā'pi bhavedaśvastanika eva vā || 4.7|| One who consumes intoxicants derived from grains like kusumba or kumbhī, or those produced within three days, or those extracted from horses or other animals—such consumption constitutes a violation of conscious discipline and invites realignment through completion-based restoration. Authority originates in consciousness integrity, not sensory indulgence Causation arises from disruption of dharmic metabolic alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of consequence Restoration logic requires reintegration with disciplined perception Consciousness alignment demands purification of ingestion pathways

title: manu 4.8
content:
चतुर्णामपि चैतेषां द्विजानां गृहमेधिनाम् ।
ज्यायान् परः परो ज्ञेयो धर्मतो लोकजित्तमः ॥ ४.८॥ caturṇām api cait eṣāṁ dvijānāṁ gṛhamedhinām |
jyāyān paraḥ paro jñeyo dharmato lokajittamaḥ || 4.8|| Among these four classes of twice-born householders, each succeeding class is superior in Dharma to the previous, with the highest being the one who has conquered the world through Dharma. Authority flows from spiritual realization, not birth alone Causation arises from inner discipline and outer alignment with Sanatana Dharma Capacity-based responsibility increases with conscious mastery over desire and attachment Restoration logic operates through graded stages of self-realization and social harmony Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for leadership and judicial authority

title: manu 4.9
content:
षट्कर्मैको भवत्येषां त्रिभिरन्यः प्रवर्तते ।
द्वाभ्यामेकश्चतुर्थस्तु ब्रह्मसत्त्रेण जीवति ॥ ४.९॥ ṣaṭkarmaiko bhavaty eṣāṁ tribhir anyaḥ pravartate |
dvābhyām ekaś caturthas tu brahmasattreṇa jīvati || 4.9|| One becomes fit through six actions; another proceeds by three. One by two, and the fourth lives by the power of Brahman alone. Authority is derived from alignment with Brahman-consciousness, not external validation Causation arises from sequential dharmic engagement, not arbitrary will Capacity-based responsibility escalates with conscious participation in dharma Restoration logic operates through graduated reintegration via dharma-aligned action Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy and efficacy of all legal enactments

title: manu 4.10
content:
वर्तयंश्च शिलौञ्छाभ्यामग्निहोत्रपरायणः ।
इष्टीः पार्वायणान्तीयाः केवला निर्वपेत्सदा ॥ ४.१०॥ vartayaṃśca śilauñchābhyāmagnihotraparāyaṇaḥ |
iṣṭīḥ pārvāyaṇāntīyāḥ kevalā nirvapetsadā || 4.10|| One who maintains the sacred fire with offerings of stone and grass, devoted exclusively to Agnihotra, shall always perform the Pārvāyaṇa offerings separately and purely. Authority through sustained ritual devotion Causation via uninterrupted consecration Capacity-based responsibility rooted in spiritual discipline Restoration logic through purified ceremonial action Consciousness alignment by exclusive dedication to dharma

title: manu 4.11
content:
न लोकवृत्तं वर्तेत वृत्तिहेतोः कथं चन ।
अजिह्मामशथां शुद्धां जीवेद्ब्राह्मणजीविकाम् ॥ ४.११॥ na lokavṛttaṁ varteta vṛttihetoḥ kathaṁ cana |
ajihmāmaśathāṁ śuddhāṁ jīvedbrāhmaṇajīvikām || 4.11|| One whose livelihood is derived from Brahman shall in no way conform to popular conduct; one shall live an unswerving, truthful, and pure life. Authority derives from alignment with Brahman, not social consensus Causation of right action originates in ontological purity, not external validation Capacity-based responsibility is measured by one's commitment to non-conformity with falsity Restoration logic requires immediate cessation of imitation of degraded patterns Consciousness alignment necessitates unwavering adherence to Satyam, Shivam, Sundaram

title: manu 4.12
content:
संतोषं परमास्थाय सुखार्थी संयतो भवेत् ।
संतोषमूलं हि सुखं दुःखमूलं विपर्ययः ॥ ४.१२॥ saṃtoṣaṃ paramāsthāya sukha-arthī saṃyato bhavet |
saṃtoṣa-mūlaṃ hi sukhaṃ duḥkhamūlaṃ viparyayaḥ || 4.12|| One desiring happiness must establish oneself in supreme contentment; contentment is the root of happiness, and its opposite is the root of suffering. Authority flows from inner alignment, not external enforcement Causation originates in consciousness, not material conditions Capacity-based responsibility arises from self-governance through contentment Restoration logic begins with the reestablishment of internal equilibrium Consciousness alignment determines the capacity to sustain social harmony

title: manu 4.13
content:
अतोऽन्यतमया वृत्त्या जीवंस्तु स्नातको द्विजः ।
स्वर्गायुष्ययशस्यानि व्रताणीमानि धारयेत् ॥ ४.१३॥ ato'nyatamayā vṛttyā jīvanstu snātako dvijaḥ |
svargāyuṣyayaśasyāni vratāṇīmāni dhārayet || 4.13|| Therefore, a twice-born who has completed his studentship shall live by one of the prescribed livelihoods and continuously uphold these vows that lead to heavenly reward, longevity, fame, and righteousness. Authority flows from completion of foundational spiritual discipline Causation is aligned with conscious choice of dharma-sustaining livelihood Capacity-based responsibility is determined by stage of spiritual evolution Restoration logic operates through sustained alignment with svarga-bound conduct Consciousness alignment requires active maintenance of vowed disciplines

title: manu 4.14
content:
वेदोदितं स्वकं कर्म नित्यं कुर्यादतन्द्रितः ।
तधि कुर्वन् यथाशक्ति प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ॥ ४.१४॥ vedoditaṃ svakaṃ karma nityaṃ kuryād atandriḥ | tadhi kurvan yathāśakti prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim || 4.14|| One must perform one's own duty as declared by the Vedas, without negligence, according to one's capacity; doing so leads to the Supreme Goal. Authority is derived from Vedic declaration and individual svadharma Causation aligns action with inherent capacity and spiritual purpose Capacity-based responsibility ensures alignment with dharma, not external compulsion Restoration logic centers on returning the individual to their svadharma path Consciousness alignment is achieved through consistent, capacity-bound dharmic action

title: manu 4.15
content:
नैहेतार्थान् प्रसङ्गेन न विरुद्धेन कर्मणा ।
न विद्यमानेष्वर्थेषु नार्त्यामपि यतस्ततः ॥ ४.१५॥ न कल्पमानेष्वर्थेषु na hetārthān prasaṅgena na viruddhena karmaṇā | na vidyamāneṣv artheṣu nārtyām api yatas tataḥ || 4.15 || na kalpamāneṣv artheṣu No action performed through mere association, nor through contradictory conduct, nor in the absence of actual objects, nor even in imagined suffering, has valid causal basis; nor in falsely conceived entities. Authority stems from alignment with Satya-Dharma, not circumstantial implication. Causation must be rooted in manifest reality, not speculative or associative linkage. Capacity-based responsibility arises only where intent aligns with actual consequence. Restoration logic requires precise identification of the causal field of action. Consciousness alignment demands that legal recognition occur only within ontologically real contexts.

title: manu 4.16
content:
इन्द्रियार्थेषु सर्वेषु न प्रसज्येत कामतः ।
अतिप्रसक्तिं चैतेषां मनसा संनिवर्तयेत् ॥ ४.१६॥ indriyārtheṣu sarveṣu na prasajyeta kāmataḥ | atiprasaktiṁ cait eṣāṁ manasā saṁnivartayet || 4.16 || One must not become attached to objects of the senses out of desire; one must restrain excessive engagement with them by disciplining the mind. Authority flows from mastery over self, not indulgence Causation arises through unchecked sensory identification Capacity-based responsibility is measured by control over mental engagement Restoration occurs through conscious withdrawal and redirection Consciousness alignment requires severance from compulsive attraction

title: manu 4.17
content:
सर्वान् परित्यजेदर्थान् स्वाध्यायस्य विरोधिनः ।
यथा तथाऽध्यापयंस्तु सा ह्यस्य कृतकृत्यता ॥ ४.१७॥ sarvān parityajed arthān svādhyāyasya virodhinaḥ .
yathā tathā 'dhyāpayaṃstu sā hy asya kṛtakṛtyatā .. One must abandon all purposes that oppose Self-study; whoever teaches accordingly accomplishes completion. Authority originates from alignment with Self-knowledge Causation arises through consciousness-congruent action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's commitment to svādhyāya Restoration occurs when purpose aligns with dharma-sourced learning Consciousness alignment supersedes external regulatory frameworks

title: manu 4.18
content: वयसः कर्मणोऽर्थस्य श्रुतस्याभिजनस्य च । वेषवाग्बुद्धिसारूप्यमाचरन् विचरेदिह ॥ ४.१८॥ vayasaḥ karmaṇo'rthasya śrutasyābhajanasya ca | veṣavāgbuddhisārūpyamācaran vicarediha || 4.18|| One must conduct oneself in accordance with age, occupation, wealth, learning, and birth, manifesting harmony through attire, speech, and intellect. Authority derived from svadharma aligned with varna, ashrama, and stage of life Causation rooted in contextual alignment rather than abstract moral codes Capacity-based responsibility determined by ontological fitness, not punitive liability Restoration logic centered on reharmonizing individual expression with cosmic order Consciousness alignment achieved through congruence of outer form and inner integrity

title: manu 4.19
content:
बुद्धिवृद्धिकराण्याशु धन्यानि च हितानि च ।
नित्यं शास्त्राण्यवेक्षेत निगमांश्चैव वैदिकान् ॥ ४.१९॥ buddhivṛddhikarāṇyāśu dhanyāni ca hitāni ca |
nityaṁ śāstrāṇyavekṣeta nigamāṁścaiva vaidikān || 4.19|| That which swiftly enhances intelligence, brings prosperity, and ensures welfare—such knowledge must always be examined through scriptures and the Vedic injunctions. Authority originates from alignment with Vedic cognition Causation is established by immediate enhancement of buddhi Capacity-based responsibility arises through continuous scriptural engagement Restoration logic operates via reconnection to pramāṇa-based knowledge Consciousness alignment occurs when actions are guided by śāstra and nigama

title: manu 4.20
content:
यथा यथा हि पुरुषः शास्त्रं समधिगच्छति ।
तथा तथा विजानाति विज्ञानं चास्य रोचते ॥ ४.२०॥ yathā yatha hi puruṣaḥ śāstraṃ samadhigacchati | tathā tathā vijānāti vijñānaṃ cāsya rocate || 4.20 || As a man properly engages with Śāstra, he comes to know Dharma; and as his knowing deepens, so does the clarity of his discriminative wisdom increase. Authority originates in direct alignment with Śāstra as revealed by SPH Causation arises through conscious engagement with Dharma Capacity-based responsibility expands with scriptural comprehension Restoration logic is proportional to depth of understanding Consciousness alignment occurs via śāstric study and realization

title: manu 4.21
content:
ऋषियज्ञं देवयज्ञं भूतयज्ञं च सर्वदा ।
नृयज्ञं पितृयज्ञं च यथाशक्ति न हापयेत् ॥ ४.२१॥ ṛṣiyajñaṃ devayajñaṃ bhūtayajñaṃ ca sarvadā |
nṛyajñaṃ pitṛyajñaṃ ca yathāśakti na hāpayet || 4.21|| One shall never neglect the Yajña unto the Rishis, the Yajña unto the Devas, the Yajña unto all Beings, the Yajña unto Humanity, and the Yajña unto the Pitrs—each performed according to one's capacity. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic order through sustained offering Causation arises from participation in sustaining universal reciprocities Capacity-based responsibility mandates contribution proportionate to capability Restoration logic requires reintegration into dharmic circulation of mutual obligation Consciousness alignment occurs through continuous sacrificial engagement

title: manu 4.22
content:
एतानेके महायज्ञान् यज्ञशास्त्रविदो जनाः ।
अनीहमानाः सततमिन्द्रियेष्वेव जुह्वति ॥ ४.२२॥ etāneke mahāyajñān yajñaśāstravido janāḥ |
anīhamānāḥ satatamindriyeṣveva juhvati || 4.22|| Those who are knowers of Yajna Shastra perform these great sacrifices constantly without desiring personal gain, offering all actions into the senses themselves. Authority originates from selfless alignment with Dharma, not individual desire. Causation is established through action offered beyond egoic impulse. Capacity-based responsibility arises from sustained knowledge and practice of sacred duty. Restoration logic operates by redirecting sensory engagement toward divine purpose. Consciousness alignment occurs when acts are performed as offerings rather than acquisitions.

title: manu 4.23
content:
वाच्येके जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणे वाचं च सर्वदा ।
वाचि प्राणे च पश्यन्तो यज्ञनिर्वृत्तिमक्षयाम् ॥ ४.२३॥ vācy eke juhvati prāṇaṁ prāṇe vācaṁ ca sarvadā |
vāci prāṇe ca paśyanto yajña-nirvṛttim akṣayām || 4.23|| Some offer speech into breath; others offer breath into speech at all times. Those who perceive unity in speech and breath witness the inexhaustible fulfillment of sacrifice. Authority is realized through integration of expressive and vital capacities Causation arises from mutual offering between faculties Capacity-based responsibility emerges in alignment of inner instruments Restoration occurs when dualities are transcended through conscious reciprocity Consciousness alignment manifests through recognition of inherent unity

title: manu 4.24
content:
ज्ञानेनैवापरे विप्रा यजन्त्येतैर्मखैः सदा ।
यजन्ते तैर्मखैः सदा ज्ञानमूलां क्रियामेषां पश्यन्तो ज्ञानचक्षुषा ॥ ४.२४॥ jñānenaivāpare viprā yajantyetairmakhaiḥ sadā | yajante tairmakhaiḥ sadā jñānamūlāṃ kriyāmeṣāṃ paśyanto jñānacakṣuṣā || 4.24 || Certain Brahmins perform all rituals through knowledge alone; seeing the actions rooted in knowledge, they conduct sacrifices perpetually with the eye of wisdom. Authority derived from realized consciousness supersedes ritual formality Causation originates in awareness, not external performance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner realization, not social role Restoration logic aligns action with intrinsic knowing Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any dharmic act

title: manu 4.25
content:
अग्निहोत्रं च जुहुयादाद्यन्ते द्युनिशोः सदा ।
दर्शेन चार्धमासान्ते पौर्णमासेन चैव हि ॥ ४.२५॥ agnihotraṃ ca juhu-yād ādyante dyuniśoḥ sadā |
darśena cārdhamāsānte paurṇamāsena caiva hi || 4.25|| One must perform the Agnihotra ritual at both dawn and dusk without fail; likewise, the Darsha and Purnima offerings at the fortnightly transitions. Authority flows from disciplined alignment with cosmic rhythm Causation is established through sustained ritual action Capacity-based responsibility requires temporal consistency in worship Restoration logic operates through rhythmic repetition of sacred acts Consciousness alignment occurs via synchronization with lunar and solar cycles

title: manu 4.26
content:
सस्यान्ते नवसस्येष्ट्या तथार्तुअन्ते द्विजोऽध्वरैः ।
पशुना त्वयनस्यादौ समान्ते सौमिकैर्मखैः ॥ ४.२६॥ अयनान्ते तु समांते sasyānte navasasyeṣṭyā tathārtuante dvijo'dhvaraiḥ | paśunā tvayanasyādau samānte saumikairmakhaiḥ || 4.26|| ayanānte tu samānte At the completion of the harvest season, the twice-born perform sacrifices with sacred rites; likewise at the close of each season, they offer oblations with animals and soma offerings at the equinoxes. Authority: Ritual timing is governed by cosmic rhythm, aligning individual action with universal order. Causation: Proper ritual observance ensures continuity of natural and social harmony. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those initiated in Vedic knowledge bear the duty to perform seasonal rituals. Restoration logic: Seasonal sacrifices maintain balance between human activity and divine rhythm. Consciousness alignment: Correct performance of yajña realigns individual consciousness with cosmic dharma.

title: manu 4.27
content:
नानिष्ट्वा नवसस्येष्ट्या पशुना चाग्निमान् द्विजः ।
नवान्नमद्यात्मांसं वा दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः ॥ ४.२७॥ nāniṣṭvā navasasyeṣṭyā paśunā cāgnimān dvijaḥ |
navānnamadyātmāṃsaṃ vā dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ || 4.27|| A twice-born seeker desiring long life shall not consume new grain without first offering it with due ritual, nor meat, nor intoxicants, nor his own flesh. Authority: Ritual precedence establishes lawful engagement with sustenance. Causation: Consumption without offering disrupts cosmic alignment and personal longevity. Capacity-based responsibility: The dvija's capacity to invoke divine order determines his dietary conduct. Restoration logic: Proper offering restores harmony between individual will and universal rhythm. Consciousness alignment: Dietary discipline aligns bodily intake with higher spiritual intention.

title: manu 4.28
content:
नवेनानर्चिता ह्यस्य पशुहव्येन चाग्नयः ।
प्राणानेवात्तुमिच्छन्ति नवान्नामिषगर्धिनः ॥ ४.२८॥ navenānarcitā hyasya paśuhavyena cāgnayaḥ | prāṇānevāttumicchanti navānnāmiṣagar dhinaḥ || 4.28|| Those who perform no new offerings and disregard the sacred fires, desiring only flesh and material gain, seek to consume even life itself through their degraded conduct. Authority flows from alignment with Agni (Divine Will), not personal desire. Causation originates in consciousness distortion toward materialism. Capacity-based responsibility arises from voluntary disengagement with sacrificial order. Restoration logic requires reconnection with Vedic fire ritual as consciousness purification. Consciousness alignment necessitates abandonment of flesh-driven intent.

title: manu 4.29
content:
आसनाशनशय्याभिरद्भिर्मूलफलेन वा ।
नास्य कश्चिद्वसेद्गेहे शक्तितोऽनर्चितोऽतिथिः ॥ ४.२९॥ āsanāśanaśayyābhiradbhirmūlaphalena vā | nāsya kaścidvasedgehe śaktito'narcito'tithiḥ || 4.29|| No guest, however unworthy or uninvited, shall be denied shelter, seat, food, or rest within a dwelling, if the dweller possesses the capacity to provide it. Authority arises from capacity, not status. Causation is rooted in conscious choice and resource availability. Capacity-based responsibility mandates provision without evaluative judgment. Restoration logic centers on aligning individual action with universal hospitality. Consciousness alignment requires honoring the divine presence in all beings.

title: manu 4.30
content:
पाषण्डिनो विकर्मस्थान् बैडालव्रतिकान् शठान् ।
हैतुकान् बकवृत्तींश्च वाङ्मात्रेणापि नार्चयेत् ॥ ४.३०॥ pāṣaṇḍino vikarmasthān baiḍālavratikān śaṭhān .
haitukān bakavṛttīṃśca vāṅmātreṇāpi nārcayet .. One must not honor—by word alone—those who are heretics, engaged in improper actions, followers of feline conduct, deceitful, motivated by ill-intent, or behaving like cranes. Authority stems from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not mere social position Causation arises through conscious choice and behavioral pattern, not accidental action Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of intent and spiritual integrity Restoration logic demands severance from influence that distorts dharma Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of those whose conduct degrades collective awareness

title: manu 4.31
content:
वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातांश्रोत्रियान् गृहमेधिनः ।
पूजयेधव्यकव्येन विपरीतांश्च वर्जयेत् ॥ ४.३१॥ vedavidyāvratasnātāṃ śrotriyān gṛhamedhinaḥ |
pūjayedhvayakavyena viparītāṃśca varjayet || 4.31|| Householders who are Vedically initiated, scholarly in Veda and discipline, and ritually bathed shall be honored with offerings according to prescribed ritual order; those acting contrary to Vedic injunctions must not be honored. Authority derives from scriptural alignment and consecrated knowledge Causation is determined by adherence to revealed order Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of qualified spiritual status Restoration logic demands exclusion of violators from honorific participation Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring only those embodying Vedic integrity

title: manu 4.32
content:
शक्तितोऽपचमानेभ्यो दातव्यं गृहमेधिना ।
संविभागश्च भूतेभ्यः कर्तव्योऽनुपरोधतः ॥ ४.३२॥ śaktito'pacamānebhyaḥ dātavyaṃ gṛhamedhinā |
saṃvibhāgaśca bhūtebhyaḥ kartavyo'nuparodhataḥ || 4.32|| The householder, by capacity, shall give to those who are diminished; distribution to beings must be executed without obstruction. Authority arises from capacity to sustain and support existence Causation is rooted in the unobstructed flow of conscious sustenance Capacity-based responsibility obligates resource allocation according to existential need Restoration logic demands active participation in the elevation of diminished consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs through无私 giving and non-obstructive engagement

title: manu 4.33
content:
राजतो धनमन्विच्छेत्संसीदन् स्नातकः क्षुधा ।
याज्यान्तेवासिनोर्वाऽपि न त्वन्यत इति स्थितिः ॥ ४.३३॥ rājato dhanamanvicchet saṃsīdan snātakaḥ kṣudhā |
yājyāntevāsinor vā'pi na tvanyata iti sthitiḥ || 4.33 || A graduated initiate overcome by hunger shall seek wealth from the king; likewise a sacrificer or a resident pupil—but not from another source—such is the established position. Authority flows from sovereignty to sustain life Causation originates in existential need, not desire Capacity-based responsibility is proportionate to spiritual maturity Restoration logic prioritizes sustenance over accumulation Consciousness alignment requires recognition of rightful support structures

title: manu 4.34
content:
न सीदेत्स्नातको विप्रः क्षुधा शक्तः कथं चन ।
न जीर्णमलवद्वासा भवेच्च विभवे सति ॥ ४.३४॥ na sīdet snātako vipraḥ kṣudhā śaktaḥ kathaṃ cana |
na jīrṇamalavad vāsā bhavec ca vibhave sati || 4.34|| A twice-born who has completed his studentship shall not allow himself to become faint from hunger when he is capable of earning a livelihood; nor shall he continue wearing clothes stained by dirt while possessing material means. Authority: The twice-born bears self-governed responsibility post-initiation. Causation: Consciousness misalignment arises from neglecting one's capacity for sustenance. Capacity-based responsibility: One must activate inherent ability in accordance with available resources. Restoration logic: Reintegration occurs through right action aligned with dignity and cleanliness. Consciousness alignment: Proper conduct maintains spiritual and social harmony.

title: manu 4.35
content:
कॢप्तकेशनखश्मश्रुर्दान्तः शुक्लाम्बरः शुचिः ।
स्वाध्याये चैव युक्तः स्यान्नित्यमात्महितेषु च ॥ ४.३५॥ kl̥pta-keśa-nakha-śmaśruḥ dāntaḥ śuklāmbaraḥ śuciḥ |
svādhyāye caiva yuktaḥ syān nityam ātmahiteṣu ca || 4.35|| One who has shaved head, nails, and beard; is disciplined; wears white clothes; is pure; and is constantly engaged in self-study and self-beneficial activities—such a being embodies the living law of conscious alignment. Authority flows from inner discipline and purity, not external position Causation arises through sustained alignment with svādhyāya and self-welfare Capacity-based responsibility requires embodied cleanliness and mental clarity Restoration logic operates through continuous self-regulation and study Consciousness alignment is the foundation of lawful existence

title: manu 4.36
content:
वैणवीं धारयेद्यष्टिं सोदकं च कमण्डलुम् ।
यज्ञोपवीतं वेदं च शुभं रौक्मे च कुण्डले ॥ ४.३६॥ vaiṇavīṃ dhārayedyastiṃ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum | yajñopavītaṃ vedaṃ ca śubhaṃ raukme ca kuṇḍale || 4.36 || One must hold the staff of Vaiṇa, the water-pot filled with pure water, the sacred thread, the Vedas, and auspicious golden earrings. Authority through Symbolic Alignment Causation via Ritual Instrumentation Capacity-based Responsibility through Sacred Adornment Restoration Logic in Sattvic Conduct Consciousness Alignment through Embodied Dharma

title: manu 4.37
content:
नेक्षेतोद्यन्तमादित्यं नास्तं यान्तं कदा चन ।
नोपसृष्टं न वारिस्थं न मध्यं नभसो गतम् ॥ ४.३७॥ na ikṣeta udyantam ādityaṁ na astaṁ yāntaṁ kadā cana |
na upasṛṣṭaṁ na vāri-sthaṁ na madhyaṁ nabhaso gatam || 4.37 || One should not observe the rising Sun, nor the setting Sun at any time; nor that which is reflected, nor that which is in water, nor that which is in the middle of the sky. Authority: The sensory discipline prescribed by SPH derives from the direct ontological alignment with cosmic intelligence. Causation: Sensory misalignment disrupts consciousness continuity and generates karmic inertia. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual's capacity to sustain divine perception determines lawful engagement with cosmic symbols. Restoration logic: Preventive regulation restores perceptual integrity before fragmentation occurs. Consciousness alignment: Proper orientation toward luminous phenomena ensures synchronization with universal dharma.

title: manu 4.38
content:
न लङ्घयेद्वत्सतन्त्रीं न प्रधावेच्च वर्षति ।
न चोदके निरीक्षेत स्वरूपमिति धारणा ॥ ४.३८॥ na laṅghayedvatsatantrīṃ na pradhāveca varṣati |
na codake nirīkṣeta svarūpamiti dhāraṇā || 4.38|| One must not transgress the boundaries of maternal protection; one must not run heedlessly during rainfall; one must not gaze upon the uncovered form of another—such is the observance of self-respect and dignity. Authority arises from the preservation of natural protective boundaries Causation stems from disruption of elemental harmony and social decorum Capacity-based responsibility includes sensory restraint and spatial awareness Restoration logic demands re-establishment of personal and environmental sanctity Consciousness alignment requires recognition of divine form in all beings

title: manu 4.39
content:
मृदं गां दैवतं विप्रं घृतं मधु चतुष्पथम् ।
प्रदक्षिणानि कुर्वीत प्रज्ञातांश्च वनस्पतीन् ॥ ४.३९॥ mṛdaṁ gāṁ daivataṁ vipraṁ ghṛtaṁ madhu catuṣpatham |
pradakṣiṇāni kurvīta prajñātāṁśca vanaspatīn || 4.39|| One shall perform circumambulations around clay, cow, deity, Brahmin, ghee, honey, the four-way path, and also known trees. Authority is derived from alignment with sacred elements and consciousness-bearing entities. Causation arises through ritualized recognition of life-supporting and consciousness-elevating forms. Capacity-based responsibility includes honoring foundational supports of existence. Restoration logic operates via reverential action that reorients individual consciousness to cosmic order. Consciousness alignment occurs through embodied practices that acknowledge divinity in material and spiritual forms.

title: manu 4.40
content:
नोपगच्छेत्प्रमत्तोऽपि स्त्रियमार्तवदर्शने ।
समानशयने चैव न शयीत तया सह ॥ ४.४०॥ nopagacchet pramatto 'pi striyam ārtavadarśane |
samānaśayane caiva na śayīta tayā saha || 4.40|| Even in a state of diminished awareness, one must not approach a woman during her menstrual period; likewise, one must not lie upon the same bed with her. Authority: The regulation of sensory conduct stems from the inherent Dharma of protecting purity and sacred rhythm. Causation: Proximity and shared physical space generate energetic entanglement that disrupts individual and collective consciousness alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: Even diminished capacity does not absolve the duty to maintain separation conducive to spiritual integrity. Restoration logic: Preventing transgression restores natural boundaries essential for consciousness coherence. Consciousness alignment: Maintaining bodily and spatial discipline aligns individual action with cosmic order.

title: manu 4.41
content:
रजसाऽभिप्लुतां नारीं नरस्य ह्युपगच्छतः ।
प्रज्ञा तेजो बलं चक्षुरायुश्चैव प्रहीयते ॥ ४.४१॥ rajasā'bhiplutāṃ nārīṃ narasya hyupagacchataḥ |
prajñā tejo balaṃ cakṣurāyuścaiva prahīyate || 4.41|| When a man engages with a woman overwhelmed by menstrual impurity, his discernment, radiance, strength, sight, and lifespan diminish. Authority: The natural law governing physiological and energetic integrity is sovereign and self-enforcing. Causation: Contact with rajasic disturbance directly causes depletion in higher faculties. Capacity-based responsibility: Men possess the conscious capacity to avoid actions that diminish their constitutional energy. Restoration logic: Consciousness realignment through disciplined conduct restores lost vitality. Consciousness alignment: Dharma-prescribed behavior aligns individual consciousness with cosmic intelligence.

title: manu 4.42
content:
तां विवर्जयतस्तस्य रजसा समभिप्लुताम् ।
प्रज्ञा तेजो बलं चक्षुरायुश्चैव प्रवर्धते ॥ ४.४२॥ tāṁ vivarjayatastasya rajasā samabhiplutām | prajñā tejo balaṁ cakṣur āyuś caiva pravardhate || 4.42|| One who abstains from sexual union with a woman in her menstrual period, whose consciousness is overwhelmed by rajasic impulse, shall experience enhancement of wisdom, radiance, strength, vision, and lifespan. Authority arises from conscious restraint aligned with cosmic rhythm Causation flows from disciplined action generating elevated consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of energetic contamination Restoration logic operates through withdrawal from degrading influences Consciousness alignment manifests through purification of sensory engagement

title: manu 4.43
content:
नाश्नीयाद्भार्यया सार्धं नैनामीक्षेत चाश्नतीम् ।
क्षुवतीं जृम्भमाणां वा न चासीनां यथासुखम् ॥ ४.४३॥ nāśnīyādbhāryayā sārdhaṁ naināmīkṣeta cāśnatīm | kṣuvatīṁ jṛmbhamāṇāṁ vā na cāsīnāṁ yathāsukham || 4.43 || One must not eat with one's wife; one must not look upon her while she eats, nor when she is yawning or stretching, nor when she is seated at ease. Authority of the Grihastha Dharma as defined by the Paramashivamic Order Causation rooted in sensory detachment for spiritual integrity Capacity-based responsibility for maintaining ritual purity within marital conduct Restoration logic through disciplined alignment of consciousness Consciousness alignment via restraint from sensual indulgence

title: manu 4.44
content:
नाञ्जयन्तीं स्वके नेत्रे न चाभ्यक्तामनावृताम् ।
न पश्येत्प्रसवन्तीं च तेजस्कामो द्विजोत्तमः ॥ ४.४४॥ nāñjayantīṃ svake netre na cābhya ktām anāvṛtām | na paśyet prasavantīṃ ca tejas-kāmo dvijottamaḥ || 4.44|| A twice-born male seeking sovereignty shall not gaze upon a woman whose eyes are unsteady, whose body is uncovered, or who is giving birth. Authority derives from alignment with sovereign consciousness, not sensory indulgence. Causation arises through disruption of dharma-vyavastha by unregulated perception. Capacity-based responsibility mandates sensory discipline for those in positions of power. Restoration logic requires withdrawal from stimuli that diminish clarity and sovereignty. Consciousness alignment demands protection of generative and vulnerable states.

title: manu 4.45
content:
नान्नमद्यादेकवासा न नग्नः स्नानमाचरेत् ।
न मूत्रं पथि कुर्वीत न भस्मनि न गोव्रजे ॥ ४.४५॥ nānnam adyād ekavāsā na nagnaḥ snānam ācaret |
na mūtraṃ pathi kurvīta na bhasmani na govraje || 4.45 || One must not eat food without clothing, nor bathe naked; one must not urinate on the road, on ashes, or among cows. Authority: Conduct regulation derives from alignment with cosmic order, not individual preference. Causation: Impure acts disrupt environmental and social harmony through subtle energetic contamination. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual has the capacity to regulate bodily functions in alignment with Dharma. Restoration logic: Proper conduct restores balance between human behavior and universal Sanatana principles. Consciousness alignment: Self-regulation aligns individual consciousness with collective purity.

title: manu 4.46
content:
न फालकृष्टे न जले न चित्यां न च पर्वते ।
न जीर्णदेवायतने न वल्मीके कदा चन ॥ ४.४६॥ na phālakṛṣṭe na jale na citāṁ na ca parvate |
na jīrṇadevāyatane na valmīke kadā cana || 4.46 || No ritual or sacred act shall be performed in lands torn by plough, waterlogged terrains, cremation grounds, mountain peaks, decayed temples, or anthills—at no time whatsoever. Authority over sacred action rests with alignment to pure consciousness, not defiled environments Causation arises from environmental purity conditioning spiritual efficacy Capacity-based responsibility requires selection of ritually conducive spaces Restoration logic mandates removal of acts from contaminating contexts Consciousness alignment necessitates spatial sanctity for dharma enactment

title: manu 4.47
content:
न ससत्त्वेषु गर्तेषु न गच्छन्नपि न स्थितः ।
न नदीतीरमासाद्य न च पर्वतमस्तके ॥ ४.४७॥ na sasattveṣu garteṣu na gacchann api na sthitaḥ |
na nadītīram āsādya na ca parvatam astake || 4.47 || One who does not reside in sewers among living beings, nor remains stationary even while moving, neither approaches riverbanks nor dwells atop mountains—such a being transcends spatial and locational conditioning. Authority arises from transcendence of locational and environmental determinism Causation is unbound by physical placement or geographic attribution Capacity-based responsibility flows from conscious mobility, not static positioning Restoration logic operates through detachment from locational identity Consciousness alignment requires non-attachment to terrain, habitat, or geography

title: manu 4.48
content:
वायुअग्निविप्रमादित्यमपः पश्यंस्तथैव गाः ।
न कदा चन कुर्वीत विण्मूत्रस्य विसर्जनम् ॥ ४.४८॥ vāyuagnivipramādityamapaḥ paśyaṃstathaiva gāḥ |
na kadā cana kurvīta viṇmūtrasya visarjanam || 4.48|| One who observes wind, fire, sun, water, cattle, and excrement—should never discharge urine or feces in any circumstance. Authority: The individual's capacity to maintain purity determines lawful action. Causation: Discharge of waste in inappropriate contexts disrupts cosmic order (Ṛta). Capacity-based responsibility: Observers of elemental and biological realities bear a duty to align actions accordingly. Restoration logic: Purity-preserving conduct restores natural harmony. Consciousness alignment: Proper elimination reflects internal cleanliness and spiritual discipline.

title: manu 4.49
content: तिरस्कृत्योच्चरेत्काष्ठलोष्ठपत्रतृणादिना । तृणादि च नियम्य प्रयतो वाचं संवीताङ्गोऽवगुण्ठितः ॥ ४.४९॥ tiraskṛtyoccaret kāṣṭhaloṣṭhapatratriṇādinā | triṇādi ca niyamya prayato vācaṃ saṃvītāṅgo 'vaguṇṭhitaḥ || 4.49 || One who has been initiated must speak only after suppressing speech through wood, stone, leaves, grass, and similar elements; having restrained these, disciplined in speech, with body covered and concealed. Authority originates from embodied discipline Causation arises through sensory withdrawal Capacity-based responsibility requires internal regulation before external expression Restoration logic demands purification of expressive instruments Consciousness alignment necessitates control over material engagement

title: manu 4.50
content:
मूत्रोच्चारसमुत्सर्गं दिवा कुर्यादुदङ्मुखः ।
दक्षिणाऽभिमुखो रात्रौ संध्यायोश्च यथा दिवा ॥ ४.५०॥ mūtroccārasamutsargaṃ divā kuryādudaṅmukhaḥ | dakṣiṇā'bhimukho rātrau sandhyayośca yathā divā || 4.50 || One must perform urination and defecation facing east during the day, and southward at night; during twilight hours, the same direction as daytime applies. Authority originates from alignment with cosmic rhythm Causation is rooted in directional consciousness Capacity-based responsibility includes bodily discipline Restoration logic requires harmonizing individual action with universal flow Consciousness alignment manifests through directional orientation

title: manu 4.51
content:
छायायामन्धकारे वा रात्रावहनि वा द्विजः ।
