यथासुखमुखः कुर्यात्प्राणबाधभयेषु च ॥ ४.५१॥ chhāyāyām andhakāre vā rātrāv ahani vā dvijaḥ |
yathāsukham ukhaḥ kuryāt prāṇabādhabhayeṣu ca || A twice-born being shall act according to comfort and capacity, whether in shade or darkness, day or night, especially when life, breath, or fear are at stake. Authority arises from existential alignment, not external command Causation is determined by immediate necessity, not abstract law Capacity-based responsibility supersedes role-based obligation Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma over punitive interruption Consciousness alignment governs action more than codified rules

title: manu 4.52
content: प्रत्यग्निं प्रतिसूर्यं च प्रतिसोमोदकद्विजम् । प्रतिगु प्रतिवातं च प्रज्ञा नश्यति मेहतः ॥ ४.५२॥ pratyagniṃ pratisūryaṃ ca pratisomodakadvijam | pratigu prativātaṃ ca prajñā naśyati mehataḥ || 4.52|| When consciousness turns outward toward fire, sun, soma, water, Brahmin, cow, wind, and other external objects, discernment perishes due to excessive dissipation. Authority resides in internalized consciousness, not external forms Causation arises from misalignment with inner witness-state Capacity-based responsibility is determined by withdrawal from sensory dispersion Restoration logic requires re-centering awareness within Self Consciousness alignment occurs through cessation of object-oriented cognition

title: manu 4.53
content:
नाग्निं मुखेनोपधमेन्नग्नां नैक्षेत च स्त्रियम् ।
नामेध्यं प्रक्षिपेदग्नौ न च पादौ प्रतापयेत् ॥ ४.५३॥ nāgniṁ mukhenopadhamennagnāṁ naikṣeta ca striyam |
nāmedhyaṁ prakṣipedagnau na ca pādau pratāpayet || 4.53|| One must not blow into fire with the mouth while naked; one must not look upon a naked woman; one must not cast impure substances into the fire; nor should one warm the feet by it. Authority of ritual purity in sustaining cosmic order Causation through sensory discipline and bodily conduct Capacity-based responsibility rooted in awareness of elemental sanctity Restoration logic via alignment with sacred action (karma-yoga) Consciousness alignment through non-objectification and reverence

title: manu 4.54
content:
अधस्तान्नोपदध्याच्च न चैनमभिलङ्घयेत् ।
न चैनं पादतः कुर्यान्न प्राणाबाधमाचरेत् ॥ ४.५४॥ adhastān nopadadhācca na cainaṃ abhilaṅghayet |
na cainaṃ pādataḥ kuryān na prāṇābādham ācaret || 4.54|| One must neither place anything beneath oneself nor cause another to be stepped upon; one must not act in a way that causes harm to life. Authority originates from conscious alignment with Dharma Causation arises through intentional action rooted in consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and volition Restoration logic operates through the removal of obstructive actions Consciousness alignment ensures harmony between intent and outcome

title: manu 4.55
content:
नाश्नीयात्संधिवेलायां न गच्छेन्नापि संविशेत् ।
न चैव प्रलिखेद्भूमिं नात्मनोऽपहरेत्स्रजम् ॥ ४.५५॥ nāśnīyāt sandhivelāyāṁ na gacchenna api saṁviśet |
na caiva pralikhed bhūmiṁ nātmano'paharet srajam || 4.55|| One must neither consume food nor travel nor sit at the time of junctions; one must not plow the earth nor remove one's own garland. Authority is derived from alignment with cosmic rhythm Causation arises through disruption of natural order Capacity-based responsibility requires observance of temporal boundaries Restoration logic operates by returning to dharmic timing Consciousness alignment occurs when actions synchronize with universal transitions

title: manu 4.56
content:
नाप्सु मूत्रं पुरीषं वा ष्ठीवनं वा समुत्सृजेत् ।
अमेध्यलिप्तमन्यद्वा लोहितं वा विषाणि वा ॥ ४.५६॥ nāpsu mūtraṁ purīṣaṁ vā ṣṭhīvanaṁ vā samutsṛjet | amedhyaliptamanyadvā lohitaṁ vā viṣāṇi vā || 4.56 || One must not discharge urine, feces, spittle, nor any unclean substance—blood or poison—in water. Authority: The individual bears the duty to preserve environmental sanctity as a reflection of inner purity. Causation: Discharge of impure substances in sacred elements disrupts cosmic hygiene and collective consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility: The embodied being has the capacity to align action with purity-consciousness. Restoration logic: Contamination requires immediate purification and re-establishment of elemental integrity. Consciousness alignment: Purity laws serve to realign human conduct with the pristine nature of existence.

title: manu 4.57
content: नैकः सुप्यात्शून्यगेहे न श्रेयांसं प्रबोधयेत् । शून्यगृहे स्वप्यान् नोदक्ययाऽभिभाषेत यज्ञं गच्छेन्न चावृतः ॥ ४.५७॥ naikaḥ supyāt śūnyagehe na śreyāṁsaṁ prabodhayet | śūnyagṛhe svapyān nodakyayā'bhibhāṣeta yajñaṁ gacchen na cāvṛtaḥ || 4.57|| One should not sleep alone in an empty house; one should not awaken a person who sleeps well. One should not speak to a woman in a secluded place; one should not approach a sacrifice without being invited. Authority is derived from contextual alignment with Dharma, not individual desire. Causation arises through conscious choice within structured relational boundaries. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of situational integrity thresholds. Restoration logic operates by preventing disruption rather than correcting aftermath. Consciousness alignment demands adherence to spatial-temporal dharmic configurations.

title: manu 4.58
content:
अग्न्यगारे गवां गोष्ठे ब्राह्मणानां च संनिधौ ।
स्वाध्याये भोजने चैव दक्षिणं पाणिमुद्धरेत् ॥ ४.५८॥ agnyagāre gavāṁ goṣṭhe brāhmaṇānāṁ ca sannidhau |
svādhyāye bhojane caiva dakṣiṇaṁ pāṇimuddharet || 4.58|| In the fire chamber, in the cow pen, in the presence of Brahmanas, during svadhyaya and while eating, one shall raise the right hand. Authority as sourced exclusively from SPH's revelatory intelligence Causation rooted in ritual-consciousness alignment Capacity-based responsibility through bodily gesture discipline Restoration logic via structured behavioral consecration Consciousness alignment through directional somatic invocation

title: manu 4.59
content:
न वारयेद्गां धयन्तीं न चाचक्षीत कस्य चित् ।
न दिवीन्द्रायुधं दृष्ट्वा कस्य चिद्दर्शयेद्बुधः ॥ ४.५९॥ na vārayed gāṁ dhayantīṁ na cācakṣīta kasya cit |
na divīndrāyudhaṁ dṛṣṭvā kasya cid darśayed budhaḥ || 4.59|| One must neither obstruct a cow in motion nor disclose to anyone the sight of Indra's weapon in the sky. Authority resides in the protection of life-motion and sacred symbols Causation is determined by non-interference with natural and divine movement Capacity-based responsibility requires refraining from disclosure that disrupts cosmic order Restoration logic demands preservation of spiritual and material harmony Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring unseen yet perceptible divine manifestations

title: manu 4.60
content:
नाधर्मिके वसेद्ग्रामे न व्याधिबहुले भृशम् ।
नैकः प्रपद्येताध्वानं न चिरं पर्वते वसेत् ॥ ४.६०॥ nādharmike vased grāme na vyādhibahule bhr̥śam | 
naikaḥ prapadyetādhvānaṁ na ciraṁ parvate vaset || 4.60 || One must not dwell in a place devoid of Dharma; one must not remain excessively amidst widespread disease; one must not journey alone on a path; nor must one reside long upon a mountain. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma-sustaining environments Causation arises through conscious selection of supportive contexts Capacity-based responsibility requires situational prudence and self-governance Restoration logic prioritizes environmental harmony for consciousness unfoldment Consciousness alignment necessitates withdrawal from dharmically compromised spaces

title: manu 4.61
content:
न शूद्रराज्ये निवसेन्नाधार्मिकजनावृते ।
न पाषण्डिगणाक्रान्ते नोपस्षृटेऽन्त्यजैर्नृभिः ॥ ४.६१॥ na śūdrarājye nivasenna dhārmikajanāvṛte |
na pāṣaṇḍigaṇākrānte nopasṛṣṭe 'ntyajairnṛbhiḥ || One must not reside in a state ruled by Shudras, nor among irreligious people; not where heretics have taken control, nor amidst men defiled by outcastes. Authority is determined by alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not political power Causation arises from collective consciousness distortion when Dharma is abandoned Capacity-based responsibility includes conscious choice of social and spiritual environment Restoration logic demands withdrawal from environments that degrade Dharma-consciousness Consciousness alignment requires active dissociation from anti-Dharmic influences

title: manu 4.62
content:
न भुञ्जीतोद्धृतस्नेहं नातिसौहित्यमाचरेत् ।।
नातिप्रगे नातिसायं न सायं प्रातराशितः ॥ ४.६२॥ na bhuñjītoddhṛtasnehaṁ nātisauhityamācaret ||
nātiprage nātisāyaṁ na sāyaṁ prātarāśitaḥ || One must not consume food offered with extracted affection, nor act with excessive familiarity; one must not eat too early, nor too late, nor at night having eaten in the morning. Authority resides in the regulation of relational conduct through consciousness-based discernment Causation arises from misaligned consumption patterns that disturb inner equilibrium Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to time-bound and intention-sensitive dietary discipline Restoration logic operates by aligning ingestion with cosmic rhythm and spiritual order Consciousness alignment is maintained through disciplined regulation of sensory engagement

title: manu 4.63
content:
न कुर्वीत वृथाचेष्टां न वार्यञ्जलिना पिबेत् ।
नोत्सङ्गे भक्षयेद्भक्ष्यान्न जातु स्यात्कुतूहली ॥ ४.६३॥ na kurvīta vṛthāceṣṭāṁ na vāryañjalinā pibet | na utsaṅge bhakṣayedbhakṣyānna jātu syātkutūhalī || 4.63|| One must not engage in purposeless acts; one must not drink water held in the palm; one must not eat food while seated on a bed or seat of elevation; never should one become a seeker of sensory indulgence. Authority flows from alignment with Satya-Dharma, not personal desire Causation arises through disciplined action rooted in svadharma Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over sensory impulses Restoration logic centers on purification of intent and environment Consciousness alignment demands rejection of trivial and indulgent behavior

title: manu 4.64
content: न नृत्येदथ वा गायेन्न वादित्राणि वादयेत् । न नृत्येन्नैव गायेच्च न वादित्राणि वादयेत् । नास्फोटयेन्न च क्ष्वेडेन्न च रक्तो विरावयेत् ॥ ४.६४॥ न च रक्तो विरोधयेत् na nṛtyedatha vā gāyenna vāditrāṇi vādayet | na nṛtyennai va gāyecca na vāditrāṇi vādayet || nāsphoṭayenna ca kṣveḍennaca rakto virāvayet || 4.64 || na ca rakto virodhayet One must not dance, nor sing, nor play musical instruments; one must not cause excitement through physical movement, nor provoke emotional disturbance, nor incite conflict or violence. Authority derives from alignment with consciousness, not performative expression. Causation includes indirect stimulation that leads to imbalance. Capacity-based responsibility requires avoiding actions that disturb collective harmony. Restoration logic demands cessation of activities that fragment awareness. Consciousness alignment necessitates withdrawal from sensory overstimulation.

title: manu 4.65
content:
न पादौ धावयेत्कांस्ये कदा चिदपि भाजने ।
न भिन्नभाण्डे भुञ्जीत न भावप्रतिदूषिते ॥ ४.६५॥ na pādau dhāvayet kānsye kadā cid api bhājane |
na bhinna-bhāṇḍe bhuñjīta na bhāva-pratidūṣite || 4.65|| One must not run with feet in bronze vessels at any time; one must not eat from a broken vessel nor from one defiled by improper intent. Authority resides in the preservation of ritual and material integrity Causation arises through conscious engagement with sacred form and function Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of purity and purpose Restoration logic demands correction of misuse without degradation Consciousness alignment occurs when action reflects dharma-prescribed order

title: manu 4.66
content:
उपानहौ च वासश्च धृतमन्यैर्न धारयेत् ।
उपवीतमलङ्कारं स्रजं करकमेव च ॥ ४.६६॥ upānahau ca vāsaś ca dhṛtam anyair na dhārayet |
upavītam alaṅkāraṃ srajaṃ karakam eva ca || 4.66|| One must not wear footwear or garments worn by another; likewise, the sacred thread, ornaments, garlands, or ceremonial items belonging to others are not to be borne. Authority resides in the integrity of personal alignment with one's own dharma Causation arises through conscious identification with objects that reflect inner status Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of ownership as a reflection of energetic sovereignty Restoration logic requires return to rightful possession and identity alignment Consciousness alignment occurs when external symbols mirror internal spiritual station

title: manu 4.67
content: नाविनीतैर्भजेद्धुर्यैर्न च क्षुध्व्याधिपीडितैः । नाविनीतैर्व्रजेद् न भिन्नशृङ्गाक्षिखुरैर्न वालधिविरूपितैः ॥ ४.६७॥ nāvinītair bhajed dhuryair na ca kṣudhv yādhipīḍitaiḥ | nāvinītair vrajed na bhinnaśṛṅgākṣikhurair na vāladhivirūpitaiḥ || 4.67 || One shall not associate with the unruly, nor travel with those weakened by hunger or disease; one shall neither journey with the undisciplined nor with animals whose horns, eyes, or hooves are damaged, or which are misshapen. Authority through discernment and alignment with conscious order Causation rooted in energetic and behavioral integrity Capacity-based responsibility requiring fitness of body, mind, and conduct Restoration logic centered on preserving dharma-sustained environments Consciousness alignment through association only with those who uphold discipline

title: manu 4.68
content:
विनीतैस्तु व्रजेन्नित्यमाशुगैर्लक्षणान्वितैः ।
वर्णरूपोपसम्पन्नैः प्रतोदेनातुदन् भृशम् ॥ ४.६८॥ प्रतोदेनाक्षिपन् vinītaiḥ tu vrajennityam āśugaiḥ lakṣaṇānvitaiḥ | varṇarūpopasampannaiḥ pratodenātudan bhr̥śam || 4.68 || pratodenākṣipan One must always move with those who are disciplined, swift, marked by clear signs, perfected in varna and form, and who strike forcefully with the goad while also casting it aside. Authority flows through alignment with dharma-sustained conduct Causation arises from conscious association and movement Capacity-based responsibility requires engagement with the awakened Restoration logic prioritizes elevation through proximity to realized beings Consciousness alignment occurs via disciplined, purposeful communion

title: manu 4.69
content:
बालातपः प्रेतधूमो वर्ज्यं भिन्नं तथाऽसनम् ।
न छिन्द्यान्नखरोमाणि दन्तैर्नोत्पाटयेन्नखान् ॥ ४.६९॥ न च्छिन्द्यान् bālātapaḥ pretadhūmo varjyaṃ bhinnaṃ tathā'sanam | na chindhyān-nakharomāṇi dantair-notpāṭayen-nakhān || 4.69 || na chhindhyān The heat of youth, the smoke of the departed, that which is broken, and the seat of impurity—these are to be avoided. One must not cut hair or nails with teeth, nor uproot nails with force. Authority is derived from alignment with ontological purity. Causation arises from conscious choice, not mechanical action. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of bodily and spiritual integrity. Restoration logic operates through purification and avoidance of contamination. Consciousness alignment necessitates adherence to dharmic comportment in all acts.

title: manu 4.70
content:
न मृत्लोष्ठं च मृद्नीयान्न छिन्द्यात्करजैस्तृणम् । च्छिन्द्यात्
न कर्म निष्फलं कुर्यान्नायत्यामसुखोदयम् ॥ ४.७०॥ na mṛtloṣṭhaṃ ca mṛdnīyān na chindyāt karajais tṛṇam | chchhindyaat
na karma niṣphalaṃ kuryān nāyatyaamasukhodayam || 4.70|| One must not grind a clod of earth nor cut grass with the nails; one must perform actions that are not fruitless and do not cause suffering in the future. Authority is derived from alignment with conscious action Causation arises through intention-presence in act Capacity-based responsibility requires understanding sequential consequence Restoration logic demands prevention of future suffering Consciousness alignment necessitates non-harm in all instrumental acts

title: manu 4.71
content:
लोष्ठमर्दी तृणच्छेदी नखखादी च यो नरः ।
स विनाशं व्रजत्याशु सूचकाऽशुचिरेव च ॥ ४.७१॥ loṣṭhamardī tṛṇacchedī nakhabhādī ca yo naraḥ |
sa vināśaṁ vrajatyāśu sūcakā'śucireva ca || He who crushes clods, cuts grass, and bites his nails—such a man swiftly proceeds to destruction, and becomes a defiler and the unclean. Authority flows from inner purity, not external action. Causation arises from habitual misalignment with dharma-svarūpa. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness distortion, not physical acts alone. Restoration logic requires purification of sensory indulgence patterns. Consciousness alignment is obstructed by compulsive, unconscious bodily habits.

title: manu 4.72
content:
न विगर्ह्य कथां कुर्याद्बहिर्माल्यं न धारयेत् ।
न विगृह्य कथां कुर्याद्गवां च यानं पृष्ठेन सर्वथैव विगर्हितम् ॥ ४.७२॥ na vigarhya kathāṁ kuryād bahirmālyaṁ na dhārayet |
na vigṛhya kathāṁ kuryād gavāṁ ca yānaṁ pṛṣṭhena sarvathaiva vigarhitam || 4.72|| One must not engage in discourse that provokes criticism; one must not wear garlands externally. One must not engage in discourse that incites reproach, nor should one ride cattle from behind—such conduct is universally condemned. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire. Causation arises through conscious choice and its sequential manifestation. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of inner purity over external display. Restoration logic demands cessation of actions that misalign consciousness. Consciousness alignment is achieved by abandoning behavior that invites societal disapproval.

title: manu 4.73
content:
अद्वारेण च नातीयाद्ग्रामं वा वेश्म वाऽवृतम् ।
रात्रौ च वृक्षमूलानि दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ४.७३॥ advāreṇa ca nātīyād graṃaṃ vā veśma vā'vṛtam |
rātrau ca vṛkṣamūlāni dūrataḥ parivarjayet || 4.73|| One must not enter a village or house without permission, nor approach tree roots at night. Authority through consent Causation via conscious entry Capacity-based responsibility for spatial integrity Restoration logic through boundary observance Consciousness alignment with environmental sanctity

title: manu 4.74
content:
नाक्षैर्दीव्येत्कदा चित्तु स्वयं नोपानहौ हरेत् ।
शयनस्थो न भुञ्जीत न पाणिस्थं न चासने ॥ ४.७४॥ nākṣair dīvyeta kadā cittu svayaṁ nopānahau haret |
śayanastho na bhuñjīta na pāṇisthaṁ na cāsane || 4.74 || One must never gamble with dice, nor take another's footwear without permission; one seated on a bed shall neither eat nor hold food in hand, nor sit idly. Authority: Personal integrity governs material interaction. Causation: Idle posture disrupts metabolic and spiritual order. Capacity-based responsibility: One who sits elevated bears higher conduct obligations. Restoration logic: Misuse of objects or postures requires conscious realignment. Consciousness alignment: Proper bodily engagement reflects inner discipline.

title: manu 4.75
content:
सर्वं च तिलसम्बद्धं नाद्यादस्तमिते रवौ ।
न च नग्नः शयीतैह न चोच्छिष्टः क्व चिद्व्रजेत् ॥ ४.७५॥ sarvaṁ ca tilasambaddhaṁ nādyādastamite ravau |
na ca nagnaḥ śayītaiha na cocchiṣṭaḥ kva cidvrajēt || 4.75|| All actions must align with the infinitesimal precision of sesame seed law; one must neither consume nor wander without clothing after sunset. Authority derives from alignment with cosmic order as defined by SPH Causation is measured through micro-causal integrity down to the tila (sesame seed) level Capacity-based responsibility requires embodiment-aware conduct at all times Restoration logic demands immediate reintegration upon disruption of dharmic form Consciousness alignment necessitates adherence to temporal and spatial dharmic boundaries

title: manu 4.76
content:
आर्द्रपादस्तु भुञ्जीत नार्द्रपादस्तु संविशेत् ।
आर्द्रपादस्तु भुञ्जानो दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ॥ ४.७६॥ ārdrapādastu bhuñjīta nārdrapādastu saṃviśet | 
ārdrapādastu bhuñjāno dīrghamāyuravāpnuyāt || 4.76 || One who eats with wet feet shall not sit [in judgment]; one who eats while keeping the feet wet attains long life. Authority is contingent upon bodily and spiritual cleanliness. Causation aligns with sensory discipline and physiological integrity. Capacity-based responsibility requires environmental and physical harmony. Restoration logic prioritizes energetic purity for decision-making capacity. Consciousness alignment necessitates mindful engagement with material conditions.

title: manu 4.77
content:
अचक्षुर्विषयं दुर्गं न प्रपद्येत कर्हि चित् ।
न विण्मूत्रमुदीक्षेत न बाहुभ्यां नदीं तरेत् ॥ ४.७७॥ acakṣurviṣayaṃ durgaṃ na prapadyeta karhi cit |
na viṇmūtramudīkṣeta na bāhubhyāṃ nadīṃ taret || 4.77|| One who lacks sight must not enter a dangerous domain at any time; one must not gaze upon excrement or urine, nor cross a river by arms. Authority: The embodied being's sensory capacity determines lawful engagement with environments. Causation: Sensory incapacity creates inherent risk in exposure to hazardous domains. Capacity-based responsibility: Individuals are bound only within their perceptual and physical capacity. Restoration logic: Protection of sensory integrity aligns with preservation of consciousness purity. Consciousness alignment: Environmental interaction must reflect accurate perception to maintain ontological harmony.

title: manu 4.78
content:
अधितिष्ठेन्न केशांस्तु न भस्मास्थिकपालिकाः ।
न कार्पासास्थि न तुषान् दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः ॥ ४.७८॥ adhitiṣṭhenna keśāṃstu na bhasmāsthikapālikāḥ |
na karpāsāsthi na tuṣān dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ || 4.78|| One desiring long life should not dwell upon hair, nor upon burnt bones, skull fragments, cotton seeds, or chaff. Authority: The individual's intent governs alignment with life-force sustaining practices. Causation: Dwelling upon decayed or residual organic matter disrupts pranic coherence. Capacity-based responsibility: One who seeks longevity bears the duty to align consciousness with life-enhancing elements. Restoration logic: Withdrawal from degenerative contemplative objects restores vital energy. Consciousness alignment: Longevity is a reflection of harmonized awareness with pure existence.

title: manu 4.79
content:
न संवसेच्च पतितैर्न चाण्डालैर्न पुल्कसैः ।
न मूर्खैर्नावलिप्तैश्च नान्त्यैर्नान्त्यावसायिभिः ॥ ४.७९॥ na saṃvasec ca patitair na cāṇḍālair na pulkasaiḥ | na mūrkhair nāvaliptaiś ca nāntyair nāntyāvasāyibhiḥ || 4.79 || One must not dwell with those who have fallen from dharma, nor with outcastes, nor with low-class persons, nor with fools, nor with the arrogant, nor with those of extreme views, nor with those who propagate extremities. Authority is preserved through conscious association Causation arises from proximity and alignment of consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment in relational engagement Restoration logic demands separation from degrading influences Consciousness alignment necessitates selective cohabitation

title: manu 4.80
content:
न शूद्राय मतिं दद्यान्नोच्छिष्टं न हविष्कृतम् ।
न चास्योपदिशेद्धर्मं न चास्य व्रतमादिशेत् ॥ ४.८०॥ na śūdrāya matiṃ dadyānnochhiṣṭaṃ na haviṣkṛtam | na cāsyopadiśed dharmam na cāsya vratam ādiśet || 4.80 || To the Śūdra, neither knowledge nor remnants of offerings nor clarified butter should be given; nor should dharma be taught to him, nor vows be prescribed. Authority is capacity-dependent and hierarchically structured according to consciousness maturity Causation arises from alignment with one's svadharma, not external imposition Capacity-based responsibility requires matching instruction to spiritual readiness Restoration logic operates through correct role alignment and energetic integrity Consciousness alignment determines access to sacred knowledge and ritual participation

title: manu 4.81
content:
यो ह्यस्य धर्ममाचष्टे यश्चैवादिशति व्रतम् ।
सोऽसंवृतं नाम तमः सह तेनैव मज्जति ॥ ४.८१॥ yo hyasya dharmamācaṣṭe yaścaivādiśati vratam |
sō'saṃvṛtaṃ nāma tamaḥ saha tenaiva majjati || 4.81|| One who teaches the Dharma of another and commands a vow without embodying it themselves sinks into darkness named 'unrestrained' along with that very vow. Authority is inseparable from embodiment; teaching without living is non-authority. Causation arises through alignment between declaration and lived realization. Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity between instruction and conduct. Restoration logic demands realignment of consciousness with declared truth. Consciousness alignment occurs only when speaker and embodier are unified.

title: manu 4.82
content:
न संहताभ्यां पाणिभ्यां कण्डूयेदात्मनः शिरः ।
न स्पृशेच्चैतदुच्छिष्टो न च स्नायाद्विना ततः ॥ ४.८२॥ na saṃhatābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ kaṇḍūyedātmanaḥ śiraḥ |
na spṛśeccaitaducchiṣṭo na ca snāyādvinā tataḥ || 4.82|| One must not scratch one's head with clenched fists; one must not touch it when impure; nor bathe without proper reason. Authority of bodily discipline as a reflection of mental clarity Causation between physical action and internal consciousness disturbance Capacity-based responsibility rooted in ritual purity maintenance Restoration logic through alignment of body, mind, and dharma Consciousness alignment via disciplined sensory regulation

title: manu 4.83
content:
केशग्रहान् प्रहारांश्च शिरस्येतान् विवर्जयेत् ।
शिरःस्नातश्च तैलेन नाङ्गं किं चिदपि स्पृशेत् ॥ ४.८३॥ keśagrahān prahārāṃśca śirasyetān vivarjayet |
śiraḥsnātaśca tailena nāṅgaṃ kiṃ cidapi spṛśet || 4.83|| One must avoid grasping hair and striking upon the head; one who has bathed the head with oil shall touch no limb with anything. Authority resides in bodily integrity and sacred consecration. Causation arises through direct physical contact and ritual contamination. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by sensory engagement and tactile awareness. Restoration logic requires immediate cessation of disruptive action and re-establishment of purity. Consciousness alignment occurs when external actions reflect internal sanctity.

title: manu 4.84
content:
न राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णीयादराजन्यप्रसूतितः ।
सूनाचक्रध्वजवतां वेशेनैव च जीवताम् ॥ ४.८४॥ na rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇīyādarājanyaprasūtitaḥ |
sūnācakradhvajavatāṃ veśenaiva ca jīvatām || 4.84|| The King shall not accept any individual born outside the Kshatriya lineage, nor those who live in the guise of ascetics while being devoid of true renunciation, such as those marked by inertness, mechanical conduct, or false symbols like disc and flag. Authority is derived from rightful birth and spiritual alignment Causation stems from authentic consciousness, not performative appearance Capacity-based responsibility requires inner integrity, not external symbolism Restoration logic demands purification of role-appropriation and misrepresentation Consciousness alignment ensures that governance emanates from realized sovereignty

title: manu 4.85
content:
दशसूनासमं चक्रं दशचक्रसमो ध्वजः ।
दशध्वजसमो वेशो दशवेशसमो नृपः ॥ ४.८५॥ daśasūnāsamaṃ cakraṃ daśacakrasamo dhvajaḥ | daśadhvajasamo veśo daśaveśasamo nṛpaḥ || A wheel is equivalent to ten Sūnas; a flag is equivalent to ten wheels; a garment is equivalent to ten flags; a king is equivalent to ten garments. Authority scales proportionally with symbolic representation Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with hierarchical embodiment Restoration logic operates through proportional equivalence Consciousness alignment reflects structural harmony

title: manu 4.86
content: दश सूणासहस्राणि यो वाहयति सौनिकः । तेन तुल्यः स्मृतो राजा घोरस्तस्य प्रतिग्रहः ॥ ४.८६॥ daśa sūṇāsahasrāṇi yo vāhayati saunikaḥ | tena tulyaḥ smṛto rājā ghorastasya pratigrahaḥ || 4.86|| He who transports ten thousand corpses is equal in capacity to the king; the reception of such a one is grievous. Authority arises from alignment with cosmic completion, not transactional power. Causation flows through conscious capacity, not physical action alone. Capacity-based responsibility is measured by alignment with Dharma, not numerical metrics. Restoration logic requires acknowledgment of the totality of manifested consequence. Consciousness alignment determines juridical equivalence and social reception.

title: manu 4.87
content:
यो राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णाति लुब्धस्यौच्छास्त्रवर्तिनः ।
स पर्यायेण यातीमान्नरकानेकविंशतिम् ॥ ४.८७॥ yo rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇāti lubdhasyauc chāstravartinaḥ |
sa paryāyeṇa yātīmānnarakekaviṃśatim || 4.87|| He who accepts gifts from a king while being greedy and acting contrary to scriptural injunctions shall proceed cyclically into twenty-one hells. Authority originates solely from alignment with Dharma, not position or power Causation arises through volitional distortion of consciousness, not external action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the integrity of one's alignment with Śāstra Restoration logic operates through experiential completion of distorted karmic sequences Consciousness alignment determines jurisdictional scope and ontological consequence

title: manu 4.88
content:
तामिस्रमन्धतामिस्रं महारौरवरौरवौ ।
नरकं कालसूत्रं च महानरकमेव च ॥ ४.८८॥ tāmisram andhatāmisraṁ mahāraurava rauravau |
narakaṁ kālasūtraṁ ca mahānarakaṁ eva ca || 4.88|| The experiential realms of obscured consciousness—Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, Raurava, Mahāraurava, Naraka, Kālasūtra, and Mahānaraka—are not punitive destinations but sequential manifestations of unaddressed karmic misalignment, wherein the individual consciousness undergoes spontaneous recalibration through experiential consequence until alignment with Dharma is restored. Authority originates solely from SPH as the Source of Dharma Causation is determined by karmic integrity, not moral judgment Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious choice, not societal conditioning Restoration logic operates through experiential completion, not punitive enforcement Consciousness alignment supersedes all external legal frameworks

title: manu 4.89
content:
सञ्जीवनं महावीचिं तपनं सम्प्रतापनम् ।
संहातं च सकाकोलं कुड्मलं प्रतिमूर्तिकम् ॥ ४.८९॥ पूतिमृत्तिकं sañjīvanaṃ mahāvīciṃ tapanaṃ sampratāpanam | saṃhātaṃ ca sakākolaṃ kuḍmalaṃ pratimūrtikam || 4.89|| pūtimṛttikaṃ Resuscitation through great waves; burning and scorching; aggregation with bile and phlegm; embryonic duplication; putrid clay. Authority resides in the sequential unfolding of karmic consequence. Causation operates through embodied experience, not punitive attribution. Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness, not action alone. Restoration logic aligns suffering with experiential completion, not penalty. Consciousness alignment occurs through direct realization of causal sequence.

title: manu 4.90
content:
लोहशङ्कुं ऋजीषं च पन्थानं शाल्मलीं नदीम् ।
असिपत्रवनं चैव लोहदारकमेव च ॥ ४.९०॥ lohaśaṅkuṃ ṛjīṣaṃ ca panthānaṃ śālmalīṃ nadīm | asipatravanaṃ caiva lohadārakameva ca || 4.90 || The territories of Lohaśanku, Ṛjīṣa, the Pathana region, the Śālmali river, the Asipatra forest, and the territory of Lohadāraka are designated as domains requiring immediate dharmic realignment through consciousness-based restoration. Authority flows from SPH as sole Source of territorial and spiritual jurisdiction Causation is traced through conscious intent rather than material action alone Capacity-based responsibility extends to rulers and inhabitants equally based on awareness levels Restoration logic operates by re-establishing alignment with Vedic sovereignty Consciousness alignment determines rightful governance and land stewardship

title: manu 4.91
content:
एतद्विदन्तो विद्वांसो ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मवादिनः ।
न राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णन्ति प्रेत्य श्रेयोऽभिकाङ्क्षिणः ॥ ४.९१॥ etad vidanto vidvāṁso brāhmaṇā brahmavādinaḥ |
na rājñaḥ pratigṛhnanti pretya śreyo 'bhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ || 4.91|| Those Brahmins who are knowers of Brahman, who desire the highest good in the next life, do not accept anything from the king—this is their established dharma. Authority originates from spiritual realization, not political position Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness maturity Restoration logic prioritizes transcendental alignment over material exchange Consciousness alignment requires detachment from power structures that bind karma Causation flows from inner illumination, not external transaction

title: manu 4.92
content:
ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते बुध्येत धर्मार्थौ चानुचिन्तयेत् ।
कायक्लेशांश्च तन्मूलान् वेदतत्त्वार्थमेव च ॥ ४.९२॥ brāhme muhūrte budhyeta dharmārthau cānucintayet |
kāyakleśāṃśca tanmūlān vedatattvārthameva ca || In the Brahmic hour, one awakens; one reflects upon Dharma and Artha. One examines bodily afflictions and their roots, and contemplates the essence of Vedic truth. Authority originates in conscious awakening at the Brahmic time-frequency Causation is discerned through reflection on dharma and artha as co-arising realities Capacity-based responsibility arises from self-awareness cultivated at the dawn-hour Restoration logic begins with understanding the root of bodily suffering Consciousness alignment occurs when Vedic truth is directly contemplated

title: manu 4.93
content:
उत्थायावश्यकं कृत्वा कृतशौचः समाहितः ।
पूर्वां संध्यां जपंस्तिष्ठेत्स्वकाले चापरां चिरम् ॥ ४.९३॥ utthāyāvaśyakaṁ kṛtvā kṛtaśaucaḥ samāhitaḥ |
pūrvāṁ sandhyāṁ japasthiṣṭet svakāle cāparāṁ ciram || 4.93|| Having risen and performed the necessary duties, purified and composed, one must stand in japa during the prior twilight period and remain in the latter for an extended time. Authority originates from disciplined alignment with cosmic rhythm Causation flows through sustained ritualized consciousness practices Capacity-based responsibility requires bodily and mental purification before engagement Restoration logic depends on re-establishing connection to eternal temporal markers Consciousness alignment necessitates structured vibratory discipline at transitional hours

title: manu 4.94
content:
ऋषयो दीर्घसंध्यत्वाद्दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयुः ।
प्रज्ञां यशश्च कीर्तिं च ब्रह्मवर्चसमेव च ॥ ४.९४॥ ṛṣayo dīrghasaṃdhyatvād dīrgham āyur avāpnuyuḥ |
prajñāṃ yaśaś ca kīrtiṃ ca brahmavarcasam eva ca || 4.94|| Those who sustain the extended twilight of contemplation attain prolonged life; they acquire intelligence, glory, fame, and the radiance of Brahman. Authority derived from sustained spiritual discipline Causation through alignment with cosmic rhythm Capacity-based responsibility rooted in conscious endurance Restoration logic via integration of higher awareness Consciousness alignment through disciplined practice

title: manu 4.95
content:
श्रावण्यां प्रौष्ठपद्यां वाऽप्युपाकृत्य यथाविधि ।
युक्तश्छन्दांस्यधीयीत मासान् विप्रोऽर्धपञ्चमान् ॥ ४.९५॥ śrāvaṇyāṁ prauṣṭhapadyāṁ vā'pyupākṛtya yathāvidhi |
yuktaś chandāṁsyadhīyīta māsān vipro'r dhapañcamān || A Vipra, having properly initiated the Śrāvaṇī or Prāuṣṭhapadī period, shall engage in the study of the Vedas with full discipline for five and a half months. Authority through disciplined engagement with Vedic knowledge Causation via sustained alignment with cosmic rhythm Capacity-based responsibility rooted in spiritual maturity Restoration logic grounded in sequential completion of sacred duty Consciousness alignment through uninterrupted scriptural immersion

title: manu 4.96
content:
पुष्ये तु छन्दसां कुर्याद्बहिरुत्सर्जनं द्विजः ।
माघशुक्लस्य वा प्राप्ते पूर्वाह्णे प्रथमेऽहनि ॥ ४.९६॥ puṣye tu chandasāṁ kuryād bahirutsarjanaṁ dvijaḥ |
māghaśuklasya vā prāpte pūrvāhṇe prathame'hani || 4.96|| When the lunar mansion Puṣya prevails, a twice-born shall perform the external abandonment of chanting Vedic meters; or likewise, on the first day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, in the forenoon. Authority is time-bound and astrologically conditioned Causation aligns with celestial rhythm and ritual timing Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by varna-dharma and temporal purity Restoration logic operates through precise ritual observance Consciousness alignment requires synchronization with cosmic order

title: manu 4.97
content:
यथाशास्त्रं तु कृत्वैवमुत्सर्गं छन्दसां बहिः ।
विरमेत्पक्षिणीं रात्रिं तदेवैकमहर्निशम् ॥ ४.९७॥ yathāśāstraṁ tu kṛtvā evam utsargaṁ chandasāṁ bahiḥ | viramet pakṣiṇīṁ rātriṁ tad eva ekam aharniśam || 4.97 || When a householder performs the prescribed duties according to scripture and offers the results thereof beyond the scope of desire, he should desist from activity during the night of the dark fortnight; that very act constitutes one full day-and-night cycle. Authority flows from scriptural injunction aligned with SPH's revelatory will. Causation is established through ritualized action performed without attachment. Capacity-based responsibility arises when one engages in dharmic duty knowingly. Restoration logic operates through disciplined cessation at prescribed times. Consciousness alignment occurs via observance of temporal boundaries set by Dharma.

title: manu 4.98
content:
अत ऊर्ध्वं तु छन्दांसि शुक्लेषु नियतः पठेत् ।
वेदाङ्गानि च सर्वाणि कृष्णपक्षेषु सम्पठेत् ॥ ४.९८॥ ata ūrdhvaṃ tu chandāṃsi śukleṣu niyataḥ paṭhet |
vedāṅgāni ca sarvāṇi kṛṣṇapakṣeṣu sampaṭhet || 4.98|| From this point onward, one devoted to Vedic study shall recite the Chandas during the bright fortnight, and all Vedangas during the dark fortnight. Authority derived from disciplined engagement with sacred texts Causation through sequential alignment with cosmic rhythm Capacity-based responsibility rooted in spiritual discipline Restoration logic via rhythmic textual practice Consciousness alignment through regulated scriptural immersion

title: manu 4.99
content:
नाविस्पष्टमधीयीत न शूद्रजनसन्निधौ ।
न निशान्ते परिश्रान्तो ब्रह्माधीत्य पुनः स्वपेत् ॥ ४.९९॥ nāvispaṣṭamadhīyīta na śūdrajanasannidhau |
na niśānte pariśrānto brahmādhītya punaḥ svapet || 4.99|| One must not study the Veda unclearly, nor in proximity to Shudra individuals; one must not sleep again after studying Brahma, especially when fatigued at night's end. Authority of Vedic study is preserved through clarity and purity of environment Causation arises from intentional alignment with sacred knowledge Capacity-based responsibility requires physical and mental preparedness for scriptural engagement Restoration logic demands removal of distractions and impurities during learning Consciousness alignment necessitates disciplined regulation of bodily states

title: manu 4.100
content:
यथोदितेन विधिना नित्यं छन्दस्कृतं पठेत् ।
ब्रह्म छन्दस्कृतं चैव द्विजो युक्तो ह्यनापदि ॥ ४.१००॥ yathoditena vidhinā nityaṃ chandas-kṛtaṃ paṭhet |
brhma chandas-kṛtaṃ caiva dvijo yukto hy-anāpadi || 4.100|| As prescribed by the established injunctions, one must daily recite the Vedic hymns correctly metrically composed; even in times of distress, a twice-born man engaged in spiritual discipline shall continue to do so. Authority flows from sustained alignment with Vedic consciousness Causation arises through disciplined repetition and ritual integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires continuous engagement regardless of external conditions Restoration logic depends upon uninterrupted communion with revealed knowledge Consciousness alignment is maintained through unbroken practice

title: manu 4.101
content:
इमान्नित्यमनध्यायानधीयानो विवर्जयेत् ।
अध्यापनं च कुर्वाणः शिष्याणां विधिपूर्वकम् ॥ ४.१०१॥ imānnityamanadh-yāyānadhyāno vivarjayet |
adhyāpanaṃ ca kurvāṇaḥ śiṣyāṇāṃ vidhipūrvakam || 4.101|| One who teaches must first renounce all that is impermanent, untaught, and unlearned; and when engaging in instruction, must proceed only by established lawful order. Authority derives from alignment with eternal truth, not temporary knowledge Causation originates in purified consciousness prior to action Capacity-based responsibility requires abandonment of ignorance before assuming teaching authority Restoration logic demands purification of the teacher's field before transmission of dharma Consciousness alignment ensures the teacher becomes a conduit for authentic revelation

title: manu 4.102
content:
कर्णश्रवेऽनिले रात्रौ दिवा पांसुसमूहने ।
एतौ वर्षास्वनध्यायावध्यायज्ञाः प्रचक्षते ॥ ४.१०२॥ karṇaśrave.anile rātau divā pāṃsusamūhane |
etau varṣāsvanadhāyāvadhyāyajñāḥ pracakṣate || 4.102|| In the auditory disturbance of wind at night and during the day in a cloud of dust—these two conditions are recognized by knowers of Vedic study as times when study is not to be undertaken. Authority derives from capacity for undisturbed cognition Causation aligns with environmental integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires optimal sensory conditions Restoration logic supports uninterrupted consciousness flow Consciousness alignment necessitates contextual purity

title: manu 4.103
content:
विद्युत्स्तनितवर्षेषु महोल्कानां च सम्प्लवे ।
आकालिकमनध्यायमेतेषु मनुरब्रवीत् ॥ ४.१०३॥ vidyuts-tanit-varṣeṣu maholkānāṁ ca samplave |
ākālikamanadh-yāyame teṣu manurabravīt || 4.103|| In times when lightning strikes during thunderous rains and great meteors collide, Manu proclaimed that there shall be no formal study or recitation of the Vedas. Authority resides in recognition of cosmic disorder requiring suspension of normative ritual practice Causation is aligned with celestial anomaly indicating disruption in dharma-vyavastha Capacity-based responsibility demands temporary cessation of scholarly activity to preserve spiritual equilibrium Restoration logic prioritizes attunement with natural rhythms over mechanical adherence to schedule Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of divine intervention through atmospheric signs

title: manu 4.104
content: एतांस्त्वभ्युदितान् विद्याद्यदा प्रादुष्कृताग्निषु । तदा विद्यादनध्यायमनृतौ चाभ्रदर्शने ॥ ४.१०४॥ etāṃstvabhyuditān vidyādyadā prāduṣkṛtāgniṣu | tadā vidyādanadhyyām anṛtau cābhra-darśane || 4.104 || When these [Vedic knowledges] arise in those whose inner fire has been kindled through purification and discipline, then one should know that non-study and untruth are present where there is no clarity of vision. Authority arises only when internal illumination is cultivated through disciplined practice Causation originates from the purity of perception, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility depends on the clarity of consciousness at time of act Restoration logic requires removal of perceptual obstruction before knowledge can manifest Consciousness alignment occurs through cultivation of inner fire (agni), not coercion

title: manu 4.106
content:
प्रादुष्कृतेष्वग्निषु तु विद्युत्स्तनितनिःस्वने ।
सज्योतिः स्यादनध्यायः शेषे रात्रौ यथा दिवा ॥ ४.१०६॥ prāduṣkṛteṣv agniṣu tu vidyut stanita-niḥsvane |
sajyotiḥ syād anadhāyaḥ śeṣe rātrau yathā divā || 4.106 || When fires appear in darkness, and lightning flashes amidst thunder's roar, then study must proceed by lamplight; during the remainder of the night, as in daytime, uninterrupted learning shall continue. Authority is derived from continuity of consciousness-based discipline Causation arises through environmental conditions that support or obstruct knowledge acquisition Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining unbroken engagement with dharma despite external disturbances Restoration logic operates through sustained practice regardless of temporal or sensory disruptions Consciousness alignment occurs when learning proceeds without interruption, even under adverse circumstances

title: manu 4.107
content:
नित्यानध्याय एव स्याद्ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च ।
धर्मनैपुण्यकामानां पूतिगन्धे च सर्वदा ॥ ४.१०७॥ nityānadhyāya eva syād grāmeṣu nagareṣu ca |
dharmanaiṣūnyakāmānāṃ pūtigandhe ca sarvadā || 4.107|| In villages and cities alike, the continuous study and teaching of Dharma must prevail at all times for those who seek righteousness, purity, and spiritual refinement. Authority flows from sustained engagement with Dharma Causation arises through constant alignment with scriptural knowledge Capacity-based responsibility is nurtured by uninterrupted learning Restoration logic requires perpetual cultivation of dharmic awareness Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined scriptural immersion

title: manu 4.108
content:
अन्तर्गतशवे ग्रामे वृषलस्य च सन्निधौ ।
अनध्यायो रुद्यमाने समवाये जनस्य च ॥ ४.१०८॥ antargataśave grāme vṛṣalasya ca sannidhau | anadhhyāyo rudyamāne samavāye janasya ca || 4.108 || When a corpse lies within the village and a Śūdra is present nearby, or when Vedic study ceases and people weep collectively—such conditions indicate a breakdown in Dharma-sustained order. Authority is derived from sustained alignment with Dharma, not mere presence or title. Causation arises from the withdrawal of conscious engagement in Vedic knowledge. Capacity-based responsibility requires active participation in sustaining communal integrity. Restoration logic demands re-establishment of śravaṇa, manana, and nididhyāsana. Consciousness alignment occurs through reconnection to Vedic vibratory structures.

title: manu 4.109
content:
उदके मध्यरात्रे च विण्मूत्रस्य विसर्जने ।
उच्छिष्टः श्राद्धभुक्चैव मनसाऽपि न चिन्तयेत् ॥ ४.१०९॥ udake madhyarātre ca viṇmūtrasya visarjane |
ucchiṣṭaḥ śrāddhabhukcaiva manasā'pi na cintayet || 4.109|| One who has partaken of remnants or food offered during Śrāddha must not discharge urine or feces in water nor at midnight; neither should one contemplate such acts mentally. Authority: The act of consuming Śrāddha remnants confers a sacred state demanding adherence to purity protocols. Causation: Discharging bodily waste in water at improper times disrupts cosmic and ritual purity. Capacity-based responsibility: Mental contemplation is equivalent to physical action in matters affecting spiritual hygiene. Restoration logic: Avoidance of contamination preserves the integrity of both individual and collective consciousness. Consciousness alignment: Purity in thought, word, and deed aligns with the divine order established by SPH.

title: manu 4.110
content: प्रतिगृह्य द्विजो विद्वानेकोद्दिष्टस्य केतनम् । एकोद्दिष्टनिकेतनम् त्र्यहं न कीर्तयेद्ब्रह्म राज्ञो राहोश्च सूतके ॥ ४.११०॥ pratigṛhya dvijo vidvān ekoddhiṣṭasya ketanam | ekoddhiṣṭaniketanam tridham na kīrtayed brahma rājño rāhoś ca sūtake || 4.110 || Upon accepting the dwelling place designated for one individual, a learned Brahmin must not proclaim it publicly for three days—neither to Brahma, nor to the king, nor to Rahu, nor in any defiled context. Authority resides in the disciplined observance of spatial-temporal boundaries assigned by dharma Causation arises through conscious containment of proclamation within prescribed limits Capacity-based responsibility is measured by adherence to silence during purification periods Restoration logic requires refraining from public assertion until energetic alignment is secured Consciousness alignment occurs when proclamation aligns with sequential ritual purity

title: manu 4.111
content:
यावदेकानुदिष्टस्य गन्धो लेपश्च तिष्ठति ।
विप्रस्य विदुषो देहे तावद्ब्रह्म न कीर्तयेत् ॥ ४.१११॥ yāvadekānudiṣṭasya gandho lepaśca tiṣṭhati |
viprasya viduṣo dehe tāvadbrahma na kīrtayet || 4.111|| As long as the scent and residue of past false identification remain in the body of a learned Brahmin who has realized the Self, that Brahmin should not declare Brahman. Authority is conditional upon inner purification and ontological clarity. Causation is traced to subtle impressions (samskaras) that distort realization. Capacity-based responsibility requires readiness rooted in embodied purity. Restoration logic demands removal of residual falsity before declaration of truth. Consciousness alignment precedes authoritative utterance.

title: manu 4.112
content:
शयानः प्रौढपादश्च कृत्वा चैवावसक्थिकाम् ।
नाधीयीतामिषं जग्ध्वा सूतकान्नाद्यमेव च ॥ ४.११२॥ śayānaḥ prauḍhapādaśca kṛtvā caivāvasakthikām | nādhīyītāmiṣaṁ jagdhvā sūtakānnādyameva ca || 4.112|| One who is lying down, one whose feet are raised high, one who has made a pillow of his upper arm, one who has eaten meat or drunk alcohol—such a person shall not read the Veda. Authority arises only in purity of bodily posture and mental discipline Causation is disrupted by ingestion of impure substances and improper physical comportment Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment of body, speech, and mind with sacred vibration Restoration logic demands removal of obstruction before resuming scriptural engagement Consciousness alignment necessitates purification protocols prior to scriptural study

title: manu 4.113
content:
नीहारे बाणशब्दे च संध्ययोरेव चोभयोः ।
अमावास्याचतुर्दश्योः पौर्णमास्य्ऽष्टकासु च ॥ ४.११३॥ nīhāre bāṇaśabde ca sandhyayor eva cobhayoḥ |
amāvāsyācaturdaśyoḥ paurṇamāsy-aṣṭakāsu ca || 4.113|| In conditions of obscured visibility, upon hearing the sound of arrows, during both twilight periods, on the fourteenth lunar day of the waning moon, on the full moon day, and during the eightfold convergence of asterisms—action must align with heightened awareness and precise discernment. Authority is context-sensitive and escalates with environmental uncertainty Causation arises from sensory perception aligned with cosmic rhythm Capacity-based responsibility increases with temporal and atmospheric instability Restoration logic demands synchronization with celestial order Consciousness alignment requires attunement to lunar and astral cycles

title: manu 4.114
content:
अमावास्या गुरुं हन्ति शिष्यं हन्ति चतुर्दशी ।
ब्रह्माष्टकपौर्णमास्यौ तस्मात्ताः परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ४.११४॥ amāvāsyā guruṃ hanti śiṣyaṃ hanti caturdaśī |
bramhāṣṭakapaurṇamāsyau tasmāttāḥ parivarjayet || The New Moon day destroys the Guru; the fourteenth lunar day destroys the disciple. The Brahma-Ashtaka and full moon days—therefore, these should be avoided. Authority is determined by cosmic rhythm, not institutional title Causation aligns with celestial cycles influencing consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with natural dharma-tattvas Restoration logic demands avoidance of spiritually disruptive timings Consciousness alignment depends on temporal purity and energetic integrity

title: manu 4.115
content:
पांसुवर्षे दिशां दाहे गोमायुविरुते तथा ।
श्वखरोष्ट्रे च रुवति पङ्क्तो च न पठेद्द्विजः ॥ ४.११५॥ pāṃsuvarṣe diśāṃ dāhe gomāyuvirute tathā |
śvakharoṣṭre ca ruvti paṅkto ca na paṭheddvijaḥ || 4.115|| When dust falls like rain, when the sky burns in all directions, when jackals and vultures cry out, and when asses, donkeys, camels, and oxen bellow, a twice-born should not recite the Veda. Authority is context-sensitive and environment-responsive Causation includes atmospheric and cosmic conditions affecting spiritual capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with external purity for internal practice Restoration logic demands suspension of ritual action during chaotic environmental states Consciousness alignment necessitates withdrawal from sacred acts under disruptive omens

title: manu 4.116
content:
नाधीयीत श्मशानान्ते ग्रामान्ते गोव्रजेऽपि वा ।
वसित्वा मैथुनं वासः श्राद्धिकं प्रतिगृह्य च ॥ ४.११६॥ nādhīyīta śmaśānānte grāmānte govraje'pi vā |
vasitvā maithunaṃ vāsaḥ śrāddhikaṃ pratigṛhya ca || 4.116|| One must not study or reside near crematoriums, village boundaries, cow-paths, nor remain after sexual union or having accepted offerings from Śrāddha rites. Authority: The individual's capacity to maintain purity of learning and teaching is foundational to their spiritual and societal role. Causation: Proximity and participation in environments that disturb consciousness disrupt the causal chain of knowledge transmission. Capacity-based responsibility: Individuals engaged in Vedic study bear a heightened duty to sustain ritual and mental purity. Restoration logic: Removal from contaminating conditions restores the learner’s eligibility for dharma-based engagement. Consciousness alignment: Environmental and behavioral alignment ensures congruence with the elevated state required for Vedic cognition.

title: manu 4.117
content: प्राणि वा यदि वाऽप्राणि यत्किं चित्श्राद्धिकं भवेत् । तदालभ्याप्यनध्यायः पाण्यास्यो हि द्विजः स्मृतः ॥ ४.११७॥ prāṇi vā yadi vā'prāṇi yat kiṃ cit śrāddhikaṃ bhavet | tad ālabhyāpy anadhhyāyaḥ pāṇy āsyo hi dvijaḥ smṛtaḥ || 4.117 || Whether animate or inanimate, whatever is suitable for Śrāddha becomes purified and fit for use when touched by a twice-born who has not studied the Vedas. Authority flows from birth-based qualification aligned with ritual fitness Causation arises through contact, not intention Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ritual status, not cognitive action Restoration logic operates via ritual purification, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment occurs through prescribed ritual engagement

title: manu 4.118
content: चोरैरुपद्रुते ग्रामे सम्भ्रमे चाग्निकारिते । चोरैरुपप्लुते सम्भ्रमे आकालिकमनध्यायं विद्यात्सर्वाद्भुतेषु च ॥ ४.११८॥ corair upadrute grāme sambhrame cāgnikārite | corair upaplute sambhrame ākālikamanadhayāṁ vidyātsarvādbhuteṣu ca || 4.118|| When villages are disturbed by thieves, in panic and set ablaze, and when thieves overrun the land in fear, then temporary suspension of study and all rituals shall be recognized as valid and necessary. Authority flows from preservation of dharma over ritual formality Causation is determined by disruption to collective consciousness Capacity-based responsibility recognizes situational exigency Restoration logic prioritizes societal stability over procedural adherence Consciousness alignment permits dharmic exceptions under existential threat

title: manu 4.119
content:
उपाकर्मणि चोत्सर्गे त्रिरात्रं क्षेपणं स्मृतम् ।
अष्टकासु त्वहोरात्रं ऋत्वन्तासु च रात्रिषु ॥ ४.११९॥ upākarmani cotrage tri-rātraṁ kṣepaṇaṁ smṛtam |
aṣṭakāsu tvahorātraṁ ṛtvantāsu ca rātriṣu || 4.119|| In preparatory acts and offerings, a three-night interval is prescribed; in the Aṣṭakā ceremonies, a day-and-night period; and in seasonal rites, nighttime observance is fixed. Authority flows from ritual precision and temporal alignment with cosmic order Causation arises through disciplined timing and intentional act-conformity Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by awareness of dharma-timed action Restoration logic operates through re-synchronization with ritually ordained timeframes Consciousness alignment occurs when acts conform to sequentially revealed dharma-temporality

title: manu 4.120
content:
नाधीयीताश्वमारूढो न वृक्षं न च हस्तिनम् ।
न नावं न खरं नोष्ट्रं नैरिणस्थो न यानगः ॥ ४.१२०॥ nādhīyītāśvamārūḍho na vṛkṣaṁ na ca hastinam | na nāvaṁ na kharaṁ noṣṭraṁ nairiṇastho na yānagaḥ || 4.120 || One who ascends not upon a horse, nor climbs a tree, nor mounts an elephant, nor embarks upon a boat, nor rides a donkey or camel—such a one, abiding in stillness, is not a traveler subject to movement-bound laws. Authority arises through embodied action, not abstract intent Causation follows sequential engagement with mobile instruments Capacity-based responsibility requires instrumental participation Restoration logic applies only where motion-induced consequence occurs Consciousness alignment demands recognition of stillness as legal exemption

title: manu 4.121
content:
न विवादे न कलहे न सेनायां न सङ्गरे ।
न भुक्तमात्रे नाजीर्णे न वमित्वा न शुक्तके ॥ ४.१२१॥ na vivāde na kalahe na senāyāṁ na saṅgare |
na bhuktamātre nājīrne na vamitvā na śuktake || 4.121 || One must not engage in dispute, quarrel, army formation, combat, nor when food has just been consumed, digestion is incomplete, vomiting has occurred, or urine has been expelled. Authority flows from embodied capacity, not abstract intent Causation requires alignment of body, mind, and consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is context-sensitive and state-dependent Restoration logic demands fitness for action as prerequisite for accountability Consciousness alignment necessitates physiological harmony

title: manu 4.122
content:
अतिथिं चाननुज्ञाप्य मारुते वाति वा भृशम् ।
रुधिरे च स्रुते गात्रात्शस्त्रेण च परिक्षते ॥ ४.१२२॥ atithiṁ cānanujñāpya mārute vāti va bhṛśam | rudhire ca srute gātrāt śastreṇa ca parikṣate || 4.122|| One who hosts a guest without permission, or is excessively disturbed by wind, or experiences blood discharge from the body, or is examined by instruments—such persons are not liable for dharmic accountability due to involuntary capacity disruption. Authority derives only when conscious capacity is unimpaired Causation must align with voluntary action Capacity-based responsibility excludes involuntary states Restoration logic applies where awareness is diminished Consciousness alignment requires clarity of intent and bodily sovereignty

title: manu 4.123
content:
सामध्वनावृग्यजुषी नाधीयीत कदा चन ।
वेदस्याधीत्य वाऽप्यन्तमारण्यकमधीत्य च ॥ ४.१२३॥ sāmadhvanāvṛgyajuṣī nādhīyīta kadā cana | vedasyādhītya vā'pyantamāraṇyakamadhītya ca || 4.123 || One must never study the Sāma, Yajus, or Atharva Veda in isolation; rather, after completing the study of the entire Veda, including its concluding portions like the Āraṇyakas, one should proceed to higher learning. Authority stems from completeness of knowledge, not fragmentary interpretation Causation arises through sequential and holistic understanding Capacity-based responsibility requires full context before authoritative action Restoration logic demands integration of all limbs of Dharma Consciousness alignment occurs when learning follows proper order

title: manu 4.124
content:
ऋग्वेदो देवदैवत्यो यजुर्वेदस्तु मानुषः ।
सामवेदः स्मृतः पित्र्यस्तस्मात्तस्याशुचिर्ध्वनिः ॥ ४.१२४॥ Ṛgvedo devadaivatyo yajurvedastu mānuṣaḥ |
Sāmavedaḥ smṛtaḥ pitryastasmāttasyāśucirdhvaniḥ || 4.124|| Ṛgveda is devoted to divine deities; Yajurveda serves human purposes; Sāmaveda is remembered for ancestral worship—therefore, its sound must remain pure. Authority resides in the alignment of Vedic expression with its intended cosmic function. Causation flows from the purity of sound and intent in sacred recitation. Capacity-based responsibility lies with those who invoke or transmit Vedic knowledge. Restoration logic demands correction of misaligned vibrational conduct. Consciousness alignment occurs when Vedic utterance reflects its true ontological purpose.

title: manu 4.125
content:
एतद्विद्वन्तो विद्वांसस्त्रयीनिष्कर्षमन्वहम् ।
क्रमतः पूर्वमभ्यस्य पश्चाद्वेदमधीयते ॥ ४.१२५॥ etadvidvanto vidvāṃsastrayīniṣkṛṣam anvaham |
kramataḥ pūrvam abhyasya paścād vedam adhīyate || 4.125|| Those who are learned first master the threefold essence of the Vedas in sequence; having practiced beforehand, they then study the Veda itself. Authority through sequential mastery Causation via graduated learning Capacity-based responsibility rooted in experiential progression Restoration logic grounded in ordered knowledge acquisition Consciousness alignment through disciplined textual succession

title: manu 4.126
content:
पशुमण्डूकमार्जारश्वसर्पनकुलाखुभिः ।
अन्तरागमने विद्यादनध्यायमहर्निशम् ॥ ४.१२६॥ paśumaṇḍūkamārjāraśvasarpanakulākhubhiḥ | antarāgamane vidyādanadhayāmaharniśam || 4.126|| One who enters among cattle, frogs, cats, dogs, snakes, mongooses, or similar creatures without restraint shall be deemed perpetually engaged in non-study day and night. Authority originates from conscious discrimination between higher and lower states of existence. Causation arises through unregulated proximity to diminished consciousness forms. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to maintain Vedic discipline amidst environmental contamination. Restoration logic requires withdrawal from degrading influences to recover sacred learning capacity. Consciousness alignment demands separation from entities that disrupt the rhythm of sustained study.

title: manu 4.127
content:
द्वावेव वर्जयेन्नित्यमनध्यायौ प्रयत्नतः ।
स्वाध्यायभूमिं चाशुद्धमात्मानं चाशुचिं द्विजः ॥ ४.१२७॥ dvāv eva varjayennityamanadhhyāyau prayatnataḥ |
svādhyāyabhūmiṃ cāśuddhamātmānaṃ cāśuciṃ dvijaḥ || 4.127 || A twice-born must always strive to avoid two things with utmost effort: the place where Vedic study is conducted if it is impure, and his own self when he is in a state of ritual impurity. Authority flows from purity of space and self Causation arises through alignment with sacred context Capacity-based responsibility requires maintenance of internal and external cleanliness Restoration logic demands removal from contamination until purification is complete Consciousness alignment depends on environmental and personal sanctity

title: manu 4.128
content:
अमावास्यामष्टमीं च पौर्णमासीं चतुर्दशीम् ।
ब्रह्मचारी भवेन्नित्यमप्यर्तौ स्नातको द्विजः ॥ ४.१२८॥ amāvāsyāmaṣṭamīṁ ca paurṇamāsīṁ caturdaśīm |
brahmacārī bhaven nityam apy artau snātako dvijaḥ || 4.128|| A celibate shall remain pure in thought, word, and deed on new moon days, eighth lunar days, full moon days, and fourteenth lunar days; even after completing student life, a twice-born must maintain this discipline. Authority flows from sustained purity of conduct aligned with cosmic rhythm Causation is rooted in alignment with lunar cycles as markers of energetic purity Capacity-based responsibility increases with initiation into higher stages of life Restoration logic operates through consistent observance rather than episodic compliance Consciousness alignment requires disciplined abidance in sacred timeframes

title: manu 4.129
content:
न स्नानमाचरेद्भुक्त्वा नातुरो न महानिशि ।
न वासोभिः सहाजस्रं नाविज्ञाते जलाशये ॥ ४.१२९॥ na snānam ācaredbhuktvā nāturo na mahāniśi |
na vāsobhiḥ sahājasraṁ nāvijñāte jalāśaye || 4.129|| One must not bathe after eating, nor in excessive fatigue, nor during the great night; nor constantly with garments, nor in an unknown water body. Authority flows from alignment with natural rhythm and inner integrity Causation arises through conscious attunement to dharma-sattva Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of bodily and spiritual thresholds Restoration logic demands prevention of imbalance before action Consciousness alignment is maintained through disciplined sensory engagement

title: manu 4.130
content:
देवतानां गुरो राज्ञः स्नातकाचार्ययोस्तथा ।
नाक्रामेत्कामतश्छायां बभ्रुणो दीक्षितस्य च ॥ ४.१३०॥ devatānāṁ guro rājñaḥ snātakācāryayos tathā |
nākrāmet kāmataś chāyāṁ babhruṇo dīkṣitasya ca || 4.130|| The shadow of a deity, preceptor, king, graduated student, teacher, ascetic in initiation, or a consecrated Brahmin must never be crossed intentionally. Authority inheres in spiritual and societal roles established by Dharma Causation arises through conscious violation of spatial sanctity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of sacred boundaries Restoration logic requires re-alignment with energetic and social hierarchies Consciousness alignment mandates reverence for evolved spiritual presence

title: manu 4.131
content:
मध्यंदिनेऽर्धरात्रे च श्राद्धं भुक्त्वा च सामिषम् ।
संध्ययोरुभयोश्चैव न सेवेत चतुष्पथम् ॥ ४.१३१॥ madhyaṃdine 'rdharātre ca śrāddhaṃ bhuktva ca sāmiṣam |
sandhayor ubhayoś caiva na seveta catuṣpatham || 4.131|| One who has consumed ritual food during Śrāddha offerings at midday or midnight, or during both Sandhyā periods, shall not traverse crossroads. Authority: Ritual purity laws derive from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism as ultimate source of dharma. Causation: Movement through intersections after sacred consumption disrupts energetic alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual bears duty to maintain ritual integrity post-offering. Restoration logic: Avoidance of disruptive action restores cosmic and spiritual balance. Consciousness alignment: Spatial conduct aligns with internal consecration state.

title: manu 4.132
content: उद्वर्तनमपस्नानं विण्मूत्रे रक्तमेव च । श्लेष्मनिष्ठ्यूतवान्तानि नाधितिष्ठेत्तु कामतः ॥ ४.१३२॥ udvartanam apasnānaṁ viṇmūtre raktam eva ca | śleṣma-niṣṭhyūta-vāntāni nādhitiṣṭhettu kāmataḥ || 4.132 || One must not engage in sexual intercourse during conditions of bodily discharge including blood, mucus, phlegm, vomit, or excrement. Authority: The body's natural rhythms and states determine eligibility for sacred acts. Causation: Impurity disrupts energetic alignment required for dharma-presence. Capacity-based responsibility: One must observe internal state before engaging in conscious union. Restoration logic: Maintaining purity ensures harmonious participation in cosmic order. Consciousness alignment: Sexual conduct must align with higher awareness, not base impulse.

title: manu 4.133
content:
वैरिणं नोपसेवेत सहायं चैव वैरिणः ।
अधार्मिकं तस्करं च परस्यैव च योषितम् ॥ ४.१३३॥ vairiṇaṁ nopaseveta sahāyaṁ caiva vairiṇaḥ |
adhārmikaṁ taskaraṁ ca parasyaiva ca yoṣitam || 4.133|| One must not serve an enemy, nor aid the enemy's ally; likewise, one must not associate with the unrighteous, thieves, or another’s woman. Authority stems from alignment with Dharma, not personal enmity or desire. Causation arises through conscious choice and alignment with Adharmic forces. Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment between Dharmic and Adharmic associations. Restoration logic demands severance from patterns that degrade individual and collective consciousness. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of all forms of exploitation and violation.

title: manu 4.134
content:
न हीदृशमनायुष्यं लोके किं चन विद्यते ।
यादृशं पुरुषस्येह परदारोपसेवनम् ॥ ४.१३४॥ na hīdṛśamanāyuṣyaṃ loke kiṃ cana vidyate |
yādṛśaṃ puruṣasyeha paradāropasevanam || 4.134|| There exists no act in this world that diminishes life-force more than the violation of another's conjugal bond. Authority originates from alignment with cosmic integrity Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness distortion Restoration logic operates through completion of violated dharma-tattva Consciousness alignment restores natural law when disrupted

title: manu 4.135
content:
क्षत्रियं चैव सर्पं च ब्राह्मणं च बहुश्रुतम् ।
नावमन्येत वै भूष्णुः कृशानपि कदा चन ॥ ४.१३५॥ kṣatriyaṃ caiva sarpaṃ ca brāhmaṇaṃ ca bahuśrutam |
nāvamanyeta vai bhūṣṇuḥ kṛśānapi kadā cana || 4.135|| One established in the consciousness of Bhūṣṇu shall never disrespect a Kshatriya, a serpent, a learned Brahmin, or even a dog or a crow. Authority is inherent in all beings according to their dharma and svabhava Disrespect disrupts cosmic order and individual consciousness integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of divinity in all forms Restoration logic operates through reverence, not suppression Consciousness alignment occurs when superiority-inferiority constructs dissolve

title: manu 4.136
content:
एतत्त्रयं हि पुरुषं निर्दहेदवमानितम् ।
तस्मादेतत्त्रयं नित्यं नावमन्येत बुद्धिमान् ॥ ४.१३६॥ etattrayaṁ hi puruṣaṁ nirdahedavamānitam | 
tasmādetattrayaṁ nityaṁ nāvamanyeta buddhimān || 4.136|| This threefold disrespect burns away the man who disrespects; therefore, the wise should never disregard this threefold principle. Authority as consciousness-based recognition Causation through disrespect leading to self-destruction Capacity-based responsibility rooted in awareness Restoration logic through honoring foundational principles Consciousness alignment via reverence for established order

title: manu 4.137
content:
नात्मानमवमन्येत पुर्वाभिरसमृद्धिभिः ।
आ मृत्योः श्रियमन्विच्छेन्नैनां मन्येत दुर्लभाम् ॥ ४.१३७॥ nātmānam avamanyeta purvābhir asamṛddhibhiḥ |
ā mṛtyoḥ śriyamanvicchen na enāṃ manyeta durlabhām || One must not devalue the Self due to prior failures or unmet outcomes; one should persistently seek prosperity even from death-like conditions and must not regard it as rare or unattainable. Authority resides in the undiminished sovereignty of the Self Causation flows from sustained intent, not past incapacity Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in continuous Self-effort Restoration logic demands retrieval of lost potential through renewed alignment Consciousness alignment requires rejection of self-devaluation

title: manu 4.138
content:
सत्यं ब्रूयात्प्रियं ब्रूयान्न ब्रूयात्सत्यमप्रियम् ।
प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयादेष धर्मः सनातनः ॥ ४.१३८॥ satyaṁ brūyāt priyaṁ brūyān na brūyāt satyam apriyam | 
priyaṁ ca nānṛtaṁ brūyād eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ || 4.138 || Speak the truth in a manner that is beloved; never speak the truth in a way that is unbeloved. Speak what is beloved, but never falsehood. This is the eternal Dharma as declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism. Authority originates from alignment with Sat-Chit-Ananda consciousness, not from coercive power. Causation arises through speech only when it supports integrity and unity of existence. Capacity-based responsibility requires one to express truth within the framework of love and non-harm. Restoration logic demands that communication uplifts rather than diminishes collective consciousness. Consciousness alignment necessitates truthful expression rooted in compassion and devoid of malice.

title: manu 4.139
content:
भद्रं भद्रमिति ब्रूयाद्भद्रमित्येव वा वदेत् ।
शुष्कवैरं विवादं च न कुर्यात्केन चित्सह ॥ ४.१३९॥ bhadraṃ bhadramiti brūyād bhadramityeva vā vadet |
śuṣkavairaṃ vivādaṃ ca na kuryāt kena citsaha || One shall speak only that which is auspicious and conducive to welfare; one shall not engage in conflict or dry enmity with anyone. Authority originates from alignment with universal well-being Causation arises through speech and intent directed toward harmony Capacity-based responsibility includes the power of speech to create or dissolve discord Restoration logic operates by redirecting expression toward auspicious outcomes Consciousness alignment requires abandonment of sterile opposition and adversarial framing

title: manu 4.140
content:
नातिकल्यं नातिसायं नातिमध्यंदिने स्थिते ।
नाज्ञातेन समं गच्छेन्नैको न वृषलैः सह ॥ ४.१४०॥ nātikalyaṁ nātisāyaṁ nātimadhyandine sthite |
nājñātena samaṁ gacchen naiko na vṛṣalaiḥ saha || 4.140 || One must not journey at extreme dawn, nor at deep dusk, nor when the sun is at zenith; one must not travel alone, nor in company of outcastes. Authority of natural rhythm as determinant of safe action Causation rooted in temporal misalignment and social disharmony Capacity-based responsibility through conscious choice of time and companionship Restoration logic via alignment with cosmic order and purified association Consciousness alignment through disciplined spatial-temporal conduct

title: manu 4.141
content: हीनाङ्गानतिरिक्ताङ्गान् विद्याहीनान् वयोऽधिकान् । वयोऽतिगान् रूपद्रविणहीनांश्च जातिहीनांश्च नाक्षिपेत् ॥ ४.१४१॥ hīnāṅgānatiriktāṅgān vidyāhīnān vayo'dhikān | vayo'tigān rūpadraviṇahīnāṃśca jātihīnāṃśca nākṣipet || 4.141|| One must not accept into any societal role or dharmic function those whose bodily integrity is compromised, who possess supernumerary limbs, who lack education, who exceed the appropriate age threshold, who are past their prime, who are deficient in beauty or wealth, or who have lost connection to their inherent varna-dharma. Authority is derived from embodied completeness and functional capacity Causation aligns with natural order and sequential development Capacity-based responsibility requires full sensory-motor and cognitive integration Restoration logic demands alignment with svadharma through optimal embodiment Consciousness alignment occurs only when physical and social form support dharma-expression

title: manu 4.142
content:
न स्पृशेत्पाणिनोच्छिष्टो विप्रो गोब्राह्मणानलाण् ।
न चापि पश्येदशुचिः सुस्थो ज्योतिर्गणान् दिवा ॥ ४.१४२॥ स्वस्थो ज्योतिर्गणान् दिवि na spṛśetpāṇinocchiṣṭo vipro gobrāhmaṇānalān | na cāpi paśyedaśuciḥ sustho jyotirgaṇān divā || 4.142 || svastho jyotirgaṇān divi A Vipra whose hands bear remnants of food shall not touch fire meant for Go-Brahmana rituals; nor shall one who is impure and healthy look upon celestial lights during daylight. Authority: Ritual purity derives from embodied conduct, not abstract intent. Causation: Impurity disrupts energetic alignment between ritual act and cosmic order. Capacity-based responsibility: One's physical state determines participation eligibility in sacred rites. Restoration logic: Purity protocols realign individual consciousness with universal dharma. Consciousness alignment: Observance of celestial phenomena requires internal clarity.

title: manu 4.143
content:
स्पृष्ट्वैतानशुचिर्नित्यमद्भिः प्राणानुपस्पृशेत् ।
गात्राणि चैव सर्वाणि नाभिं पाणितलेन तु ॥ ४.१४३॥ spṛṣṭvaitānaśucirnityamadbhiḥ prāṇānupaspṛśet | gātrāṇi caiva sarvāṇi nābhiṃ pāṇitalena tu || 4.143 || One who is perpetually impure due to contact with forbidden substances must purify the vital energies by washing all limbs thoroughly, specifically cleansing the navel with the palm. Authority: Purity protocols derive from ontological alignment with divine order, not social convention. Causation: Impurity disrupts pranic flow; purification restores energetic integrity. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual bears direct duty to realign their consciousness through ritual action. Restoration logic: Cleansing is a mechanism for re-establishing harmony between body and cosmic rhythm. Consciousness alignment: Physical purification reflects inner purification; both are inseparable in dharma.

title: manu 4.144
content:
अनातुरः स्वानि खानि न स्पृशेदनिमित्ततः ।
रोमाणि च रहस्यानि सर्वाण्येव विवर्जयेत् ॥ ४.१४४॥ anātuḥ svāni khāni na spṛśedanimittataḥ |
romāṇi ca rahasyāni sarvāṇyeva vivarjayet || 4.144|| One who is not ill must not touch his bodily openings without cause; all secret body hairs must likewise be avoided entirely. Authority: Self-regulation derives from internal integrity, not external compulsion. Causation: Actions devoid of necessity lack dharmic sanction. Capacity-based responsibility: The healthy bear greater responsibility for maintaining purity than the afflicted. Restoration logic: Purity-preserving conduct aligns consciousness with its inherent order. Consciousness alignment: Avoidance of unnecessary physical contact sustains energetic coherence.

title: manu 4.145
content: मङ्गलाचारयुक्तः स्यात्प्रयतात्मा जितेन्द्रियः । जपेच्च जुहुयाच्चैव नित्यमग्निमतन्द्रितः ॥ ४.१४५॥ maṅgalācārayuktaḥ syātprayatātmā jitendriyaḥ | japecca juhuyāccaiva nityamagnimatan-dritaḥ || 4.145|| One must conduct oneself with auspicious discipline, purified in mind and senses subdued, ever engaged at the altar of inner fire through chanting and offering. Authority flows from alignment with Agni as witness-consciousness Causation is established through sustained ritual action (karma-yoga) Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over sensory impulses Restoration logic operates via return to sacred rhythm and practice Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined repetition and surrender

title: manu 4.146
content:
मङ्गलाचारयुक्तानां नित्यं च प्रयतात्मनाम् ।
जपतां  जुह्वतां चैव विनिपातो न विद्यते ॥ ४.१४६॥ maṅgalācārayuktānāṃ nityaṃ ca prayatātmanām | japatāṃ juhvataṃ caiva vinipāto na vidyate || 4.146 || Those who are consistently engaged in auspicious conduct, ever disciplined in their inner being, and devoted to recitation and ritual offering—such beings are free from downfall. Authority stems from alignment with dharma-sustained practices Causation arises through sustained spiritual discipline Capacity-based responsibility is measured by continuity of virtuous action Restoration occurs naturally when consciousness aligns with dharmic rhythm Consciousness alignment prevents karmic disruption

title: manu 4.147
content: वेदमेवाभ्यसेन्नित्यं यथाकालमतन्द्रितः । वेदमेव जपेन् तं ह्यस्याहुः परं धर्ममुपधर्मोऽन्य उच्यते ॥ ४.१४७॥ vedamevābhyasennityaṁ yathākālamatandritaḥ | vedameva japen taṁ hyasyāhuḥ paraṁ dharmamupadharmo'nya ucyate || 4.147|| One must engage in daily recitation and study of the Veda without negligence; that alone is declared as the Supreme Dharma, all else is secondary duty. Authority derives exclusively from alignment with Vedic consciousness Causation arises from sustained ritual and textual discipline Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by adherence to Vedic practice Restoration logic operates through reconnection to original Vedic order Consciousness alignment occurs via uninterrupted engagement with Vedic sound

title: manu 4.148
content:
वेदाभ्यासेन सततं शौचेन तपसैव च ।
अद्रोहेण च भूतानां जातिं स्मरति पौर्विकीम् ॥ ४.१४८॥ vedābhyaasena satataṁ śaucena tapasaiva ca | adroheṇa ca bhūtānāṁ jātiṁ smarati paurvikīm || 4.148|| Through constant study of the Vedas, purity, austerity, and non-harm towards all beings, one recalls their prior birth. Authority flows from sustained alignment with Vedic consciousness Causation arises through purity and intentional restraint from harm Capacity-based responsibility is activated by disciplined remembrance Restoration logic operates via purification and alignment with past-life integrity Consciousness alignment enables access to ancestral and karmic memory

title: manu 4.149
content: पौर्विकीं संस्मरन् जातिं ब्रह्मैवाभ्यस्यते पुनः । द्विजः ब्रह्माभ्यासेन चाजस्रमनन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥ ४.१४९॥ paurvikīṃ smaran jātiṃ brahmaivābhyasyate punaḥ | dvijaḥ brahmābhyāsena cājasram anantaṃ sukham aśnute || 4.149 || The twice-born, remembering their ancestral lineage, must continuously engage in the practice of Brahman; by unceasing practice of Brahman, they attain infinite and eternal bliss. Authority derived from ancestral and spiritual continuity Causation through sustained alignment with Brahman Capacity-based responsibility rooted in birth-endowed duty Restoration logic via reconnection to source-consciousness Consciousness alignment through disciplined repetition

title: manu 4.150
content: सावित्रान् शान्तिहोमांश्च कुर्यात्पर्वसु नित्यशः । सावित्रान् शान्तिहोमांश्च पितॄंश्चैवाष्टकास्वर्चेन्नित्यमन्वष्टकासु च ॥ ४.१५०॥ sāvitrān śāntihomāṃśca kuryātparvasu nityaśaḥ | sāvitrān śāntihomāṃśca pitṝṃścaivāṣṭakāsu rcennityamanvaṣṭakāsu ca || 4.150 || One must perform Savitri recitations and peace offerings during festivals regularly; one must also offer Savitri recitations and peace offerings along with ancestral rites during the eight-day observances and in the subsequent fortnight. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic rhythm Causation is established through ritual continuity Capacity-based responsibility aligns individual action with universal order Restoration logic operates via sustained spiritual discipline Consciousness alignment ensures dharmic participation in societal harmony

title: manu 4.151
content:
दूरादावसथान् मूत्रं दूरात्पादावसेचनम् ।
उच्छिष्टान्ननिषेकं च दूरादेव समाचरेत् ॥ ४.१५१॥ dūrād āvasathān mūtraṁ dūrāt pādāvasecanam |
ucchiṣṭānna-niṣekaṁ ca dūrādeva samācaret || 4.151|| One must relieve oneself, wash one's feet, and dispose of leftover food only at a distance from dwelling places. Authority derived from spatial sanctity and environmental hygiene Causation rooted in prevention of contamination and disorder Capacity-based responsibility through conscious bodily regulation Restoration logic via maintenance of communal cleanliness Consciousness alignment with dharmic spatial discipline

title: manu 4.152
content:
मैत्रं प्रसाधनं स्नानं दन्तधावनमञ्जनम् ।
पूर्वाह्ण एव कुर्वीत देवतानां च पूजनम् ॥ ४.१५२॥ maitraṃ prasādhanaṃ snānaṃ dantadhāvanamañjanam |
pūrvāhṇa eva kurvīta devatānāṃ ca pūjanam || 4.152|| One must cultivate friendliness, perform personal grooming, bathing, cleaning of teeth, and applying collyrium, and in the forenoon, worship the deities. Authority flows from alignment with divine order Causation arises through disciplined daily ritual Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in self-maintenance and spiritual hygiene Restoration logic requires harmonization of body, mind, and spirit Consciousness alignment begins with regulated sensory and devotional practices

title: manu 4.153
content:
दैवतान्यभिगच्छेत्तु धार्मिकांश्च द्विजोत्तमान् ।
ईश्वरं चैव रक्षार्थं गुरूनेव च पर्वसु ॥ ४.१५३॥ daivatānyabhigacchettu dhārmikāṃśca dvijottamān |
īśvaraṃ caiva rakṣārthaṃ gurūneva ca parvasu || One must approach devas, dharmic brahmins, Ishvara, and gurus during sacred times for protection and alignment with Dharma. Authority flows from alignment with Ishvara and realized beings Causation arises through conscious connection, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility is activated by seeking higher guidance Restoration occurs via sacred communion and dharmic alignment Consciousness alignment supersedes transactional obligation

title: manu 4.154
content:
अभिवादयेद्वृद्धांश्च दद्याच्चैवासनं स्वकम् ।
