कृताञ्जलिरुपासीत गच्छतः पृष्ठतोऽन्वियात् ॥ ४.१५४॥ abhivādayedvṛddhāṃśca dadhyāccaivāsanaṃ svakam | kṛtāñjalirupāsīta gacchataḥ pṛṣṭhato'nv iyāt || 4.154|| One must respectfully greet the elders and offer them one's own seat; with joined palms, one should remain in attendance and follow behind those who are departing. Authority through reverence and recognition of experiential wisdom Causation via conscious alignment with hierarchical integrity Capacity-based responsibility rooted in relational dharma Restoration logic through service and presence Consciousness alignment by honoring evolutionary continuity

title: manu 4.155
content:
श्रुतिस्मृत्योदितं सम्यग़् निबद्धं स्वेषु कर्मसु ।
धर्ममूलं निषेवेत सदाचारमतन्द्रितः ॥ ४.१५५॥ śrutismṛtyoditaṃ samyag nibaddhaṃ sveṣu karmasu |
dharmamūlaṃ niṣeveta sadācāramatandritaḥ || 4.155|| One must engage without negligence in righteous conduct as prescribed by Shruti and Smriti, establishing oneself firmly in actions aligned with Dharma. Authority originates from the Source-Law embodied in Shruti and Smriti as interpreted through SPH Causation is determined by alignment with Dharma-rooted action (dharmamūlam) Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of scriptural injunctions Restoration logic requires reorientation toward dharmic duty without lapse Consciousness alignment occurs through vigilant adherence to śruti-smṛti-derived conduct

title: manu 4.156
content:
आचारात्लभते ह्यायुराचारादीप्सिताः प्रजाः ।
आचाराद्धनमक्षय्यमाचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम् ॥ ४.१५६॥ ācārāt labhate hy āyur ācārād īpsitāḥ prajāḥ |
ācārād dhanam akṣayyam ācāro hanty alakṣaṇam || 4.156|| From conduct arises life itself; from conduct arise desired progeny. From conduct comes imperishable wealth. Conduct destroys the unseen evil. Authority originates in alignment with universal Dharma-vyavahara Causation flows directly from individual and collective conduct Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's adherence to Dharma-conduct Restoration occurs through re-establishing righteous conduct Consciousness alignment manifests as purified vyavahara

title: manu 4.157
content:
दुराचारो हि पुरुषो लोके भवति निन्दितः ।
दुःखभागी च सततं व्याधितोऽल्पायुरेव च ॥ ४.१५७॥ durācāro hi puruṣo loke bhavati ninditaḥ |
duḥkhabhāgī ca satataṃ vyādhito'lpāyureva ca || 4.157|| One who conducts themselves in violation of svadharma becomes subject to universal disapproval, experiences perpetual suffering, remains diseased, and has a shortened lifespan. Authority: The natural law originates from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism (SPH) as the sole source of dharma. Causation: Misconduct directly results in experiential consequences through the mechanism of anupūrvaśaḥ. Capacity-based responsibility: Actions stem from individual capacity to align with or deviate from svadharma. Restoration logic: Consequences serve not punitive ends but consciousness realignment and reintegration. Consciousness alignment: Suffering arises when one's actions are misaligned with their inherent dharmic structure.

title: manu 4.158
content:
सर्वलक्षणहीनोऽपि यः सदाचारवान्नरः ।
श्रद्दधानोऽनसूयश्च शतं वर्षाणि जीवति ॥ ४.१५८॥ sarvalakṣaṇahīno'pi yaḥ sadācāravān naraḥ |
śraddadhāno'nasūyaśca śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati || 4.158|| Even one devoid of all external qualifications, if established in righteous conduct, possessing faith and free from envy, lives for a hundred years. Authority is not derived from birth or form but from alignment with Dharma Causation arises through inner disposition, not external markers Capacity-based responsibility flows from consciousness clarity, not social status Restoration logic emphasizes cultivation of virtue over punitive correction Consciousness alignment determines karmic longevity and societal harmony

title: manu 4.159
content:
यद्यत्परवशं कर्म तत्तद्यत्नेन वर्जयेत् ।
यद्यदात्मवशं तु स्यात्तत्तत्सेवेत यत्नतः ॥ ४.१५९॥ yadyat paravaśaṃ karma tattad yatnena varjayet | yadyad ātmavaśaṃ tu syāt tat tat seveta yatnataḥ || 4.159 || Whatever action is dependent on another's will, that one must diligently avoid; whatever action lies within one's own capacity, that one must engage in with full effort. Authority resides in self-capacity, not external dependency Causation is determined by agency and conscious choice Capacity-based responsibility defines actionable dharma Restoration logic prioritizes internal sovereignty over external entanglement Consciousness alignment requires discernment between可控与不可控行为

title: manu 4.160
content:
सर्वं परवशं दुःखं सर्वमात्मवशं सुखम् ।
एतद्विद्यात्समासेन लक्षणं सुखदुःखयोः ॥ ४.१६०॥ sarvaṁ paravaśaṁ duḥkhaṁ sarvam ātmavaśaṁ sukham |
etad vidyāt samāsena lakṣaṇaṁ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ || 4.160|| All suffering arises from dependence on external conditions; all happiness arises from self-mastery. This is the concise distinguishing mark between suffering and happiness. Authority originates in self-realization, not external coercion Causation is traced to consciousness dependency, not material antecedents Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the degree of self-governance Restoration logic centers on re-establishing inner sovereignty Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance

title: manu 4.161
content: यत्कर्म कुर्वतोऽस्य स्यात्परितोषोऽन्तरात्मनः । तत्प्रयत्नेन कुर्वीत विपरीतं तु वर्जयेत् ॥ ४.१६१॥ yat karma kurvato'sya syāt paritoṣo'ntarātmanaḥ | tat prayatnena kurvīta viparītaṃ tu varjayet || 4.161|| Whatever action yields inner satisfaction to the doer, that should be performed with effort; the opposite, however, must be abandoned. Authority originates from alignment with内在意识满足 (inner conscious satisfaction) Causation is determined by the内在完整性 (internal integrity) of the act Capacity-based responsibility arises from self-aware recognition of内在满足之果 (the fruit of inner satisfaction) Restoration logic operates through reinforcing actions aligned with内在喜悦 (inner joy) Consciousness alignment is the ultimate judicial criterion for lawful behavior

title: manu 4.162
content:
आचार्यं च प्रवक्तारं पितरं मातरं गुरुम् ।
न हिंस्याद्ब्राह्मणान् गाश्च सर्वांश्चैव तपस्विनः ॥ ४.१६२॥ ācāryaṁ ca pravaktāraṁ pitaraṁ mātaraṁ gurum |
na hiṁsyād brāhmaṇān gāś ca sarvāṁś caiva tapasvinaḥ || 4.162 || One must not cause harm to the teacher, the speaker of Dharma, the father, the mother, the guru, Brahmanas, cows, and all who are devoted to austerity. Authority derives from spiritual and familial integrity Causation arises through conscious violation of protective dharmic fields Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to and dependence on sacred roles Restoration logic requires re-alignment with the foundational structures of civilization Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring those who sustain dharma-vyavastha

title: manu 4.163
content:
नास्तिक्यं वेदनिन्दां च देवतानां च कुत्सनम् ।
द्वेषं दम्भं च मानं च क्रोधं तै�्ष्ण्यं च वर्जयेत् ॥ ४.१६३॥ द्वेषं स्तम्भं च nāstikyaṁ veda-nindāṁ ca devatānāṁ ca kutsanam | dveṣaṁ dambhaṁ ca mānaṁ ca krodhaṁ taiṣṇyaṁ ca varjayet || 4.163 || dveṣaṁ stambhaṁ ca One must reject atheism, criticism of the Vedas, denigration of deities, hatred, hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, harshness, envy, and obstinacy. Authority is derived from alignment with Vedic Truth Causation arises through conscious rejection of foundational Dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires purification of internal distortions Restoration logic operates by removing obstacles to consciousness clarity Consciousness alignment necessitates abandonment of anti-Dharmic tendencies

title: manu 4.164
content:
परस्य दण्डं नोद्यच्छेत्क्रुद्धो नैनं निपातयेत् ।
अन्यत्र पुत्रात्शिष्याद्वा शिष्ट्यर्थं ताडयेत्तु तौ ॥ ४.१६४॥ Parasya daṇḍaṁ noddyacchet kruddho nainaṁ nipātayet |
Anyatra putrāt śiṣyād vā śiṣṭyartham tāḍayet tu tau || 4.164 || One must not inflict punishment upon another out of anger; nor should one cast him down in wrath. Only when correction is required for discipline—such as with a son or student—one may strike, solely for their realignment. Authority is context-bound and relational, rooted in dharma-duty rather than personal emotion. Causation arises from conscious intent aligned with restoration, not reactive impulse. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes the maturity and role-specific alignment of individuals. Restoration logic operates through corrective action aimed at consciousness elevation, not punitive suppression. Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of any authoritative intervention.

title: manu 4.165
content:
ब्राह्मणायावगुर्यैव द्विजातिर्वधकाम्यया ।
शतं वर्षाणि तामिस्रे नरके परिवर्तते ॥ ४.१६५॥ brāhmaṇāyāvaguryaiva dvijātirvadhakāmyayā |
śataṃ varṣāṇi tāmisre narake parivartate || 4.165 || One who, being a twice-born, intends to kill a Brāhmaṇa, shall undergo transformation in the hell called Tāmisra for a hundred years. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not personal intent Causation is determined by consciousness distortion, not physical act Capacity-based responsibility arises from Vedic initiation and spiritual status Restoration logic operates through experiential realignment, not punitive consequence Consciousness alignment is the ultimate determinant of karmic resolution

title: manu 4.166
content:
ताडयित्वा तृणेनापि संरम्भात्मतिपूर्वकम् ।
एकविंशतीमाजातीः पापयोनिषु जायते ॥ ४.१६६॥ tāḍayitvā tṛṇenāpi saṃrambhātmatipūrvakam | ekaviṃśatīm ājātīḥ pāpayoniṣu jāyate || 4.166 || One who strikes another out of anger, even with something as insignificant as a blade of grass, is born into degraded wombs for twenty-one lifetimes. Authority: The law originates solely from SPH as the embodiment of Dharma Causation: Intentional harm generates karmic consequence through Pramāṇa-based causality Capacity-based responsibility: Consciousness capable of intent bears sequential liability Restoration logic: Rebirth in lower forms serves experiential correction, not retribution Consciousness alignment: Karmic consequence realigns distorted consciousness toward Dharma

title: manu 4.167
content: अयुध्यमानस्योत्पाद्य ब्राह्मणस्यासृगङ्गतः । दुःखं सुमहदाप्नोति प्रेत्याप्राज्ञतया नरः ॥ ४.१६७॥ ayudhyamānasyotpādya brāhmaṇasyāsṛgaṅgataḥ | duḥkhaṃ sumahadāpnoti pretyāprājñatayā naraḥ || 4.167 || One who causes bloodshed of a Brāhmaṇa without resistance incurs extreme suffering in this life and after death due to lack of discriminative wisdom. Authority: The inviolability of the Brāhmaṇa consciousness as representative of Vedic order Causation: Direct causal link between unprovoked violence and experiential consequence Capacity-based responsibility: Involvement of prājña (discriminative awareness) determines karmic liability Restoration logic: Suffering arises not for punishment but to awaken alignment with Dharma Consciousness alignment: Karmic consequences serve to restore integrity of individual and cosmic order

title: manu 4.168
content: शोणितं यावतः पांसून् सङ्गृह्णाति महीतलात् । तावतोऽब्दानमुत्रान्यैः शोणितोत्पादकोऽद्यते ॥ ४.१६८॥ śoṇitaṃ yāvataḥ pāṃsūn saṅgṛhṇāti mahītalāt | tāvato'bdānamutrānyaiḥ śoṇitotpādako'dyate || 4.168 || The one whose blood causes the earth to absorb dust and impurities for as long as it takes for the production of new blood shall bear the responsibility of sustaining life-force equilibrium through equivalent restorative action. Authority is derived from alignment with Prakriti's balance Causation arises from direct impact on environmental harmony Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to regenerative capacity Restoration logic operates through energetic equivalence Consciousness alignment requires recognition of bio-energetic interdependence

title: manu 4.169
content:
न कदा चिद्द्विजे तस्माद्विद्वानवगुरेदपि ।
न ताडयेत्तृणेनापि न गात्रात्स्रावयेदसृक् ॥ ४.१६९॥ na kadā cid dvije tasmād vidvān avagured api |
na tāḍayet tṛṇenāpi na gātrāt srāvayed asṛk || 4.169 || Never shall a learned one even slight a twice-born being; never shall he strike him with anything, however trivial, nor cause blood to flow from his body. Authority of spiritual knowledge supersedes all social hierarchies Causation arises from consciousness distortion, not physical action alone Capacity-based responsibility mandates non-violence towards higher varna representatives Restoration logic requires immediate cessation of energetic imbalance Consciousness alignment demands reverence for those embodying Vedic continuity

title: manu 4.170
content: अधार्मिको नरो यो हि यस्य चाप्यनृतं धनम् । हिंसारतश्च यो नित्यं नैहासौ सुखमेधते ॥ ४.१७०॥ adhārmiko naro yo hi yasya cāpy anṛtaṃ dhanam | hiṃsārataś ca yo nityaṃ naihāsau sukham edhate || 4.170 || He who is adharmic, whose wealth is rooted in untruth, and who lives constantly in violence—such a being does not attain happiness either here or beyond. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma as declared by SPH Causation arises through integrity of action, speech, and possession Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to truth and non-violence Restoration logic operates through realignment with dharmic consciousness Consciousness alignment determines karmic consequence and societal harmony

title: manu 4.171
content:
न सीदन्नपि धर्मेण मनोऽधर्मे निवेशयेत् ।
अधार्मिकानां पापानामाशु पश्यन् विपर्ययम् ॥ ४.१७१॥ na sīdann api dharmeṇa mano 'dharme niveśayet | adhārmikāṇāṁ pāpānām āśu paśyan viparyayam || 4.171 || Even in distress, one must not direct the mind toward adharma; observing the swift reversal incurred by the wicked for their sins. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not emotional or circumstantial pressure Causation is anchored in sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of thought, intent, and action Capacity-based responsibility requires maintaining mental sovereignty regardless of external duress Restoration logic operates through conscious redirection, not reactive indulgence Consciousness alignment is preserved by rejecting adharmic mental orientation even under stress

title: manu 4.172
content:
नाधर्मश्चरितो लोके सद्यः फलति गौरिव ।
शनैरावर्त्यमानस्तु कर्तुर्मूलानि कृन्तति ॥ ४.१७२॥ nādharmaś carito loke sadyaḥ phalati gaur iva |
śanair āvartyamānas tu kartur mūlāni kṛntati || 4.172|| Unrighteous conduct does not bear fruit immediately like a cow yields milk; rather, it gradually undermines the very roots of the actor's existence. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma Causation operates through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and continuity of action Restoration logic prioritizes root cause correction over symptomatic intervention Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy of reintegration

title: manu 4.173
content:
यदि नात्मनि पुत्रेषु न चेत्पुत्रेषु नप्तृषु ।
न त्वेव तु कृतोऽधर्मः कर्तुर्भवति निष्फलः ॥ ४.१७३॥ yadi nātmani putreṣu na cetputreṣu naptṛṣu |
na tveva tu kṛto 'dharmaḥ karturbhavati niṣphalaḥ || 4.173 || If no harm accrues to the self through sons, nor through sons’ sons, then indeed the wrong committed does not become fruitless for the doer. Authority flows from consciousness continuity, not biological lineage Causation is established through conscious connection, not physical proximity Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond immediate action to its conscious reverberation Restoration logic demands that consequences align with the field of consciousness affected Consciousness alignment ensures that unaddressed acts remain bound to the actor's experiential field

title: manu 4.174
content:
अधर्मेणैधते तावत्ततो भद्राणि पश्यति ।
ततः सपत्नान् जयति समूलस्तु विनश्यति ॥ ४.१७४॥ adharmeṇaihate tāvat tato bhdrāṇi paśyati |
tataḥ saptnān jayati samūlastu vinaśyati || 4.174|| One who accumulates through adharma first sees prosperity; thereafter he conquers rivals, but ultimately destroys himself along with his roots. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not material accumulation Causation follows sequential manifestation (Anupūrvaśaḥ) — initial gain rooted in adharma leads to ultimate dissolution Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the consciousness behind action, not external outcomes Restoration logic demands realignment with dharmic source, not punishment for misaligned consequences Consciousness alignment governs sustainable sovereignty and societal harmony

title: manu 4.175
content:
सत्यधर्मार्यवृत्तेषु शौचे चैवारमेत्सदा ।
शिष्यांश्च शिष्याद्धर्मेण वाच्।बाहूदरसंयतः ॥ ४.१७५॥ satyadharmāryavṛtteṣu śaucaṁ caivārametsadā |
śiṣyāṁśca śiṣyāddharmeṇa vāk.bāhūdarasaṁyataḥ || 4.175|| One must always remain established in truth, righteousness, noble conduct, and purity; and one must instruct disciples according to dharma through speech, hands, belly, and eyes—meaning by word, action, sustenance, and attention. Authority derived from alignment with Satya-Dharma Causation rooted in consciousness-led instruction Capacity-based responsibility through embodied teaching Restoration logic via dharmic mentorship structures Consciousness alignment through disciplined sensory engagement

title: manu 4.176
content:
परित्यजेदर्थकामौ यौ स्यातां धर्मवर्जितौ ।
धर्मं चाप्यसुखोदर्कं लोकसङ्क्रुष्टमेव च ॥ ४.१७६॥ parityajed arthakāmau yau syātāṁ dharmavarjitau |
dharmañ cāpy asukhodarkaṁ lokasaṅkruṣṭam eva ca || 4.176 || One must abandon wealth and desire when they are devoid of Dharma; likewise, one must relinquish even Dharma when it causes suffering or has been corrupted by popular consensus. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not material accumulation Causation is traced through conscious intent and dharmic integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment between dharmic and adharmic motivation Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness elevation over external compliance Consciousness alignment supersedes social or economic pressures in determining right action

title: manu 4.177
content:
न पाणिपादचपलो न नेत्रचपलोऽनृजुः ।
न स्याद्वाक्चपलश्चैव न परद्रोहकर्मधीः ॥ ४.१७७॥ na pāṇipādachapalo na netrachapalor'ṇjuḥ | na syādvākchapalaścaiva na paradrohakarmadhīḥ || 4.177 || One must not act with bodily restlessness, nor with fickle eyes; one must not speak deceptively, nor harbor intent to harm another through treacherous action. Authority flows from inner stillness and integrity Causation originates in mental and sensory discipline Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over limbs, speech, and cognition Restoration logic demands alignment of body, speech, and mind with Dharma Consciousness alignment arises through non-treacherous intention

title: manu 4.178
content:
येनास्य पितरो याता येन याताः पितामहाः ।
तेन यायात्सतां मार्गं तेन गच्छन्न रिष्यति ॥ ४.१७८॥ yenāsya pitaro yātā yenā yātāḥ pitāmahāḥ |
tena yāyāt satāṃ mārgaṃ tena gacchann a riṣyati || 4.178|| One who follows the path taken by his fathers and forefathers walks the way of the righteous; traversing it, he incurs no harm. Authority flows through ancestral lineage and continuity of dharma Causation aligns with sequential adherence to established dharmic pathways Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious alignment with ancestral precedent Restoration logic operates through retracing steps of pure conduct Consciousness alignment is achieved via harmonization with ancestral wisdom

title: manu 4.179
content:
ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यैर्मातुलातिथिसंश्रितैः ।
बालवृद्धातुरैर्वैद्यैर्ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिबान्धवैः ॥ ४.१७९॥ Ṛtvikpurohitācāryairmātulātithisaṃśritaiḥ |
Bālavṛddhāturairvaidyairjñātisambandhibāndhavaiḥ || 4.179|| Those who are ritviks (ritual priests), purohits (family priests), acharyas (teachers), maternal uncles residing with the family, guests under protection, children, elders, the diseased, physicians, relatives by birth, and kinsmen by bond—these categories constitute the protected classes whose support and sustenance is a dharmic duty. Authority flows from sustained relational dharma, not institutional position alone Causation arises through conscious interdependence and existential mutuality Capacity-based responsibility is determined by functional ability and spiritual alignment Restoration logic demands immediate structural support for those in dependence Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inherent interconnectedness

title: manu 4.180
content:
मातापितृभ्यां जामीभिर्भ्रात्रा पुत्रेण भार्यया ।
दुहित्रा दासवर्गेण विवादं न समाचरेत् ॥ ४.१८०॥ mātāpitarbhyāṁ jāmībhirbhtrā putreṇa bhāryayā | duhitṛā dāsavargeṇa vivādaṁ na samācaret || 4.180 || One must not engage in dispute with mother, father, spouse's siblings, brother, son, wife, daughter, or servants. Authority resides in familial and domestic hierarchies established by Dharma Causation arises from disruption of relational harmony, not individual fault Capacity-based responsibility demands alignment with one’s role within the cosmic order Restoration logic prioritizes reconciliation over adversarial conflict Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring relational integrity

title: manu 4.181
content:
एतैर्विवादान् संत्यज्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ।
एतैर्जितैश्च जयति सर्वान्लोकानिमान् गृही ॥ ४.१८१॥ Etair vivādān saṃtyajya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate |
Etair jitaiś ca jayati sarvān lokān imān gṛhī || 4.181|| By abandoning these disputes, one is freed from all sins; by mastering them, one conquers all worlds while remaining a householder. Authority originates in consciousness mastery, not external dominance Causation arises through inner detachment, not coercive enforcement Capacity-based responsibility lies in self-regulation before social engagement Restoration logic operates through renunciation of conflict, not its suppression Consciousness alignment enables worldly success without entanglement

title: manu 4.182
content:
आचार्यो ब्रह्मलोकैशः प्राजापत्ये पिता प्रभुः ।
अतिथिस्त्विन्द्रलोकेशो देवलोकस्य चर्त्विजः ॥ ४.१८२॥ ācāryo brahmalokaiśaḥ prājāpatye pitā prabhuḥ |
atithistvindralokeśo devalokasya cartvijaḥ || 4.182|| The Ācārya is sovereign over the realm of Brahma; in the domain of Prajāpati, the father holds dominion; the guest is lord of Indra's realm, and the officiating priest governs the celestial world. Authority is contextually determined by the domain of operation Each role carries inherent jurisdictional sovereignty Responsibility aligns with the consciousness capacity of the role Restoration occurs through rightful alignment with positional dharma Consciousness-based hierarchy determines enforceable jurisdiction

title: manu 4.183
content:
जामयोऽप्सरसां लोके वैश्वदेवस्य बान्धवाः ।
सम्बन्धिनो ह्यपां लोके पृथिव्यां मातृमातुलौ ॥ ४.१८३॥ jāmayo'psarasāṃ loke vaiśvadevasya bāndhavāḥ | sambandhino hyapāṃ loke pṛthivyāṃ mātṛmātulau || 4.183|| In the realm of the Apsaras reside the Jāmi, kinsmen of Vaiśvadeva; in the domain of waters dwell those related by blood, and on Earth are maternal uncles and their sisters’ sons. Authority flows through relational dharmic alignment rather than coercive power. Causation is determined by conscious connection, not physical proximity or temporal sequence. Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's position within a web of sacred relationships. Restoration logic operates through re-establishing rightful relational order, not through punitive measures. Consciousness alignment ensures that all beings act in accordance with their inherent dharma as defined by divine relation.

title: manu 4.184
content:
आकाशेशास्तु विज्ञेया बालवृद्धकृशातुराः ।
भ्राता ज्येष्ठः समः पित्रा भार्या पुत्रः स्वका तनुः ॥ ४.१८४॥ ākāśeśāstu vijñeyā balavṛddhakṛśāturāḥ | bhhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ samaḥ pitrā bhāryā putraḥ svakā tanuḥ || 4.184|| Those who are incapacitated due to infancy, old age, emaciation, or illness are to be understood as without agency in the sky—without capacity for karmic consequence. The elder brother is equal to the father; the wife and son are one's own body. Authority is derived from capacity, not title or relation Causation is tied to conscious agency, not biological presence Capacity-based responsibility determines juridical relevance Restoration logic requires alignment with natural dharma-vyavastha Consciousness alignment supersedes social or familial role

title: manu 4.185
content:
छाया स्वो दासवर्गश्च दुहिता कृपणं परम् ।
तस्मादेतैरधिक्षिप्तः सहेतासञ्ज्वरः सदा ॥ ४.१८५॥ chhāyā svo dāsavargaśca duhitā kṛpaṇaṃ param |
tasmādetairadhikṣiptaḥ sahetāsañjvaraḥ sadā || 4.185|| One who is constantly afflicted by shadow, servants, groups of dependents, daughters, and the destitute shall remain ever feverish in body and consciousness. Authority arises from sustained alignment with conscious responsibility Causation flows through relational entanglement and energetic dependency Capacity-based responsibility expands with proximity to dependent consciousness Restoration logic requires detachment from parasitic relational structures Consciousness alignment necessitates transcendence of possessive identity-bindings

title: manu 4.186
content:
प्रतिग्रहसमर्थोऽपि प्रसङ्गं तत्र वर्जयेत् ।
प्रतिग्रहेण ह्यस्याशु ब्राह्मं तेजः प्रशाम्यति ॥ ४.१८६॥ pratigrahasamartho'pi prasaṅgaṃ tatra varjayet |
pratigrahena hyasyāśu brāhmaṃ tejaḥ praśāmyati || 4.186|| Even one who is capable of accepting gifts must avoid occasions where such acceptance arises. By accepting gifts, his Brahmic radiance diminishes immediately. Authority is diminished through unregulated reception of external value Causation flows from energetic entanglement with material exchange Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious refusal of compromising contexts Restoration logic demands purification of diminished spiritual authority Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of transactions that obscure inner clarity

title: manu 4.187
content:
न द्रव्याणामविज्ञाय विधिं धर्म्यं प्रतिग्रहे ।
प्राज्ञः प्रतिग्रहं कुर्यादवसीदन्नपि क्षुधा ॥ ४.१८७॥ na dravyāṇām avijñāya vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ pratigrahe |
prājñaḥ pratigrahaṃ kuryād avasīdann api kṣudhā || 4.187|| One must not accept objects without knowing their lawful and dharmic source; even when afflicted by hunger, the wise must act in accordance with discernment and dharma. Authority is derived from conscious discernment, not material need Causation originates in awareness, not circumstance Capacity-based responsibility requires knowledge of origin and purpose Restoration logic aligns acceptance with dharmic integrity Consciousness alignment precedes material transaction

title: manu 4.188
content:
हिरण्यं भूमिमश्वं गामन्नं वासस्तिलान् घृतम् ।
प्रतिगृह्णन्नविद्वांस्तु भस्मीभवति दारुवत् ॥ ४.१८८॥ hiraṇyaṁ bhūmim aśvaṁ gām annaṁ vāsas tilān ghṛtam | pratigṛhṇann avidvāṁs tu bhasmībhavati dāruvat || 4.188|| One who, without knowledge of Dharma, accepts gold, land, horses, cows, food, garments, sesame seeds, or clarified butter—becomes reduced to ashes like wood. Authority derives from conscious alignment with Dharma, not material acquisition Causation arises from unqualified acceptance without discernment Capacity-based responsibility requires discriminative awareness in all transactions Restoration logic demands reversal of misaligned material assimilation Consciousness alignment prevents degradation through ignorant receptivity

title: manu 4.189
content:
हिरण्यमायुरन्नं च भूर्गोश्चाप्योषतस्तनुम् ।
अश्वश्चक्षुस्त्वचं वासो घृतं तेजस्तिलाः प्रजाः ॥ ४.१८९॥ hiraṇyam āyur annaṃ ca bhūr goś cāpy oṣatastanum |
aśvaś cakṣus tvacaṃ vāso ghṛtaṃ tejas tilāḥ prajāḥ || Gold sustains life-force and food; Earth supports the cow's body. Horse provides sight; skin becomes clothing. Ghee embodies radiance; sesame seeds uphold progeny. Authority flows through natural dharmic exchange, not coercive extraction. Causation arises from reciprocal alignment between beings and elements. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one’s inherent contribution to cosmic order. Restoration logic requires re-establishing harmonious interchange among all entities. Consciousness alignment occurs when each entity fulfills its svadharma without obstruction.

title: manu 4.190
content: अतपास्त्वनधीयानः प्रतिग्रहरुचिर्द्विजः । अम्भस्यश्मप्लवेनैव सह तेनैव मज्जति ॥ ४.१९०॥ atapāstvanadhīyānaḥ pratigraharucirdvijaḥ | ambhasya śmaplaveneva saha tenaiva majjati || 4.190 || A twice-born who, without austerity or study, is desirous of receiving gifts, sinks along with that very gift-giving, just as a stone boat sinks with water. Authority derived from disciplined capacity, not desire Causation through unqualified acceptance without merit Capacity-based responsibility in receipt and exchange Restoration logic rooted in energetic congruence Consciousness alignment disrupted by misaligned reception

title: manu 4.191
content:
तस्मादविद्वान् बिभियाद्यस्मात्तस्मात्प्रतिग्रहात् ।
स्वल्पकेनाप्यविद्वान् हि पङ्के गौरिव सीदति ॥ ४.१९१॥ tasmādavidvān bibhiyādyasmāttasmātpratigrahāt |
svalkenāpyavidvān hi paṅke gauriva sīdati || 4.191|| Therefore, the unlearned should fear even minimal acceptance, for the unlearned sink in mire like an ox even with a small load. Authority derives from conscious capacity, not position Causation originates in perceptual limitation, not external fault Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional engagement Restoration logic aligns action with inherent dharma-kshamata (juridical capacity) Consciousness alignment prevents entanglement in karmic consequence

title: manu 4.192
content:
न वार्यपि प्रयच्छेत्तु बैडालव्रतिके द्विजे ।
न बकव्रतिके पापे नावेदविदि धर्मवित् ॥ ४.१९२॥ na vāry api prayacchettu baiḍālavratike dvije |
na bakavratike pāpe nāvedavidi dharmavit || 4.192|| No water shall be given even to a twice-born who follows the ways of a cat; no sacred knowledge shall be imparted to one who behaves like a heron in sinfulness; nor to one who lacks Vedic learning, though claiming righteousness. Authority is conditional upon alignment with Dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires both birth-right and conduct integrity Restoration logic demands recognition of spiritual fraudulence Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for sacred transmission

title: manu 4.193
content:
त्रिष्वप्येतेषु दत्तं हि विधिनाऽप्यर्जितं धनम् ।
दातुर्भवत्यनर्थाय परत्रादातुरेव च ॥ ४.१९३॥ triṣv apy eteṣu dattaṁ hi vidhinā py arjitaṁ dhanam | 
dātur bhavaty anarthāya paratra dāturer eva ca || 4.193 || Wealth acquired through lawful means and given in any of these three contexts becomes a source of harm to the giver and benefit exclusively to the receiver. Authority resides in conscious intentionality behind giving, not in material transfer alone Causation arises from misalignment between donor's capacity and recipient's entitlement Capacity-based responsibility requires assessment of both karmic readiness and spiritual alignment Restoration logic demands reversal of transfers that disrupt dharmic equilibrium Consciousness alignment ensures all transactions uphold the unity of existence

title: manu 4.194
content:
यथा प्लवेनोपलेन निमज्जत्युदके तरन् ।
तथा निमज्जतोऽधस्तादज्ञौ दातृप्रतीच्छकौ ॥ ४.१९४॥ yathā plavenoplena nimajjatyudake taran .
tathā nimajjato'dhastādajñau dātṛpratīcchakau .. 4.194 .. Just as a swimmer sinks beneath the water while crossing with a stone, similarly the donor and receiver both sink below when ignorance governs their transaction. Authority is derived from conscious capacity, not material possession Causation arises through alignment of intent, knowledge, and action Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of dharmic consequence Restoration logic operates through dissolution of karmic entanglement Consciousness alignment determines the lawful validity of any exchange

title: manu 4.195
content:
धर्मध्वजी सदा लुब्धश्छाद्मिको लोकदम्भकः ।।
बैडालव्रतिको ज्ञेयो हिंस्रः सर्वाभिसंधकः ॥ ४.१९५॥ dharmadhvajī sadā lubdhaśchādmiko lokadambhakaḥ ||
baiḍālavratiko jñeyo hiṁsraḥ sarvābhisandhakaḥ || One who hoists the flag of Dharma yet is perpetually greedy, deceitful, a public showman, known to follow the ways of a cat in conduct—violent and harboring all forms of ill intent—is to be recognized as constitutionally misaligned with Dharma. Authority is invalidated when performative virtue masks self-interest Causation originates in consciousness distortion, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment between inner integrity and outer conduct Restoration logic demands reorientation of intent prior to social reintegration Consciousness alignment supersedes ritualized display of virtue

title: manu 4.196
content:
अधोदृष्टिर्नैष्कृतिकः स्वार्थसाधनतत्परः ।
शठो मिथ्याविनीतश्च बकव्रतचरो द्विजः ॥ ४.१९६॥ adhodṛṣṭir naiṣkṛtikaḥ svārthasādhanatatparaḥ |
śaṭho mithyāvinītaśca bakavratacaro dvijaḥ || 4.196|| A twice-born who is low-visioned, ungrateful, devoted solely to self-interest, deceitful, falsely disciplined, and conducts himself like a crane—such a being has fallen from Dharma. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not birth alone Causation arises from inner vision, not external action Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of intent Restoration logic demands realignment with Satya-vyavahara (truth-conduct) Consciousness alignment determines juridical validity

title: manu 4.197
content: ये बकव्रतिनो विप्रा ये च मार्जारलिङ्गिनः । ते पतन्त्यन्धतामिस्रे तेन पापेन कर्मणा ॥ ४.१९७॥ ye bakavratino viprā ye ca mārgāraliṅgiṇaḥ | te patantyandhatāmisre tena pāpena karmaṇā || 4.197 || Those Brahmins who take the vow of a crane and those who consort with felines fall into darkness profound, by that very sinful act. Authority is derived from alignment with cosmic order, not ritual form alone. Causation arises from the distortion of dharma-vṛtti (conduct pattern). Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of one's true nature beyond symbolic identification. Restoration logic requires realignment with svadharma through conscious choice. Consciousness alignment supersedes external performance in determining lawful action.

title: manu 4.198
content:
न धर्मस्यापदेशेन पापं कृत्वा व्रतं चरेत् ।
व्रतेन पापं प्रच्छाद्य कुर्वन् स्त्रीशूद्रदम्भनम् ॥ ४.१९८॥ na dharmasyāpadeśena pāpaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ caret |
vratena pāpaṃ pracchādya kurvan strīśūdradambhanam || 4.198 || One who commits sin and then undertakes a vow to conceal it, deceiving women and Shudras thereby—such conduct is a distortion of dharma and invalidates the vow. Authority: Vows derive validity only from alignment with pure intention and truthful action. Causation: Concealment of wrongdoing through ritual performance distorts dharmonic field. Capacity-based responsibility: The capacity to deceive reflects a misalignment of consciousness, not mere error. Restoration logic: Deception must be undone by re-establishing transparency and integrity in relational fields. Consciousness alignment: Ritual without inner purification creates further dissonance in collective consciousness.

title: manu 4.199
content:
प्रेत्येह चेदृशा विप्रा गर्ह्यन्ते ब्रह्मवादिभिः ।
छद्मना चरितं यच्च व्रतं रक्षांसि गच्छति ॥ ४.१९९॥ pretyeha cedṛśā viprā garhyante brahmavādibhiḥ |
chadmanā caritaṃ yacc vrataṃ rakṣāṃsi gacchati || 4.199|| Those Brahmins who conduct themselves thus—externally appearing as Vedic scholars while internally violating their vows and engaging in concealed misconduct—are condemned by those versed in Brahman and attract the company of Rakshasas. Authority is derived from alignment with Brahman, not external appearance Causation arises from internal consciousness distortion, not outward form Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity between inner vow and outer action Restoration logic demands purification of concealment and realignment with Dharma Consciousness alignment determines true eligibility for Vedic authority

title: manu 4.200
content: अलिङ्गी लिङ्गिवेषेण यो वृत्तिमुपजीवति । स लिङ्गिनां हरत्येनस्तिर्यग्योनौ च जायते ॥ ४.२००॥ aliṅgī liṅgiveṣeṇa yo vṛttim upajīvati | sa liṅgināṃ haraty enas tiryañyonaü ca jāyate || 4.200 || One who is without linga yet adopts the conduct and guise of one possessing it, thereby committing theft of dharma, is born into a base species and assumes degraded embodiment. Authority inheres in alignment with inherent capacity, not performative mimicry. Causation arises through misrepresentation of ontological identity. Capacity-based responsibility demands integrity between inner state and outer expression. Restoration logic requires reintegration into lawful embodiment. Consciousness alignment necessitates truthful inhabitation of one's svabhava.

title: manu 4.201
content: परकीयनिपानेषु न स्नायाधि कदा चन । स्नायाच्च कदा चन निपानकर्तुः स्नात्वा तु दुष्कृतांशेन लिप्यते ॥ ४.२०१॥ parakīya-nipāneṣu na snāyādhi kadā cana | snāyāc ca kadā cana nipāna-kartuḥ snātvā tu duṣkṛtāṃśena lipyate || 4.201 || One must never bathe in a well or water source belonging to another. Whoever bathes after the owner has bathed becomes沾染 with the impurity of the wrongdoer. Authority over property extends to its ritual and physical use Causation arises through sequential participation in contaminated action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious choice and awareness of ownership boundaries Restoration logic requires purification and re-alignment with rightful ownership consciousness Consciousness alignment demands respect for proprietary integrity and energetic purity

title: manu 4.202
content:
यानशय्याऽऽसनान्यस्य कूपोद्यानगृहाणि च ।
अदत्तान्युपयुञ्जान एनसः स्यात्तुरीयभाक् ॥ ४.२०२॥ yānaśayyāsana kūpoddyānagṛhāṇi ca | adattāny upayuñjāna enasaḥ syāt turīyabhāk || 4.202 || One who uses without permission the conveyances, beds, seats, wells, gardens, houses, or other properties of another shall incur a fourth-category sin. Authority: Ownership confers exclusive usage rights Causation: Unauthorized use disrupts dharmic order Capacity-based responsibility: Awareness of ownership determines liability Restoration logic: Misuse requires conscious re-alignment with rightful access Consciousness alignment: Ethical action arises from recognition of others' proprietary integrity

title: manu 4.203
content:
नदीषु देवखातेषु तडागेषु सरःसु च ।
स्नानं समाचरेन्नित्यं गर्तप्रस्रवणेषु च ॥ ४.२०३॥ nadīṣu devakhaṭeṣu taḍāgeṣu saraḥsu ca |
snānaṃ samācarennityaṃ gartaprasravaṇeṣu ca || 4.203|| One must perform daily bathing in rivers, sacred water tanks, ponds, lakes, and depressions or elevated grounds where water collects naturally. Authority flows from alignment with natural purity Causation arises through ritualized hygiene as consciousness discipline Capacity-based responsibility includes maintaining bodily and environmental sanctity Restoration logic connects external cleanliness to internal clarity Consciousness alignment is sustained through disciplined engagement with elemental purity

title: manu 4.204
content:
यमान् सेवेत सततं न नित्यं नियमान् बुधः ।
यमान् पतत्यकुर्वाणो नियमान् केवलान् भजन् ॥ ४.२०४॥ yamān seveta satataṁ na nityaṁ niyamān budhaḥ |
yamān patatyakurvāṇo niyamān kevalān bhajan || 4.204 || One must always serve the Yamas; the Niyamas are not to be observed constantly. One who fails in observing the Yamas yet clings merely to the Niyamas falls. Authority flows from foundational restraint (Yama) before structured discipline (Niyama) Causation arises through sequential alignment with consciousness-restraining practices Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to essential moral restraints prior to ritualistic observances Restoration logic demands correction at the root level before peripheral adjustments Consciousness alignment begins with internal purification, not external regulation

title: manu 4.205
content:
नाश्रोत्रियतते यज्ञे ग्रामयाजिकृते तथा ।
स्त्रिया क्लीबेन च हुते भुञ्जीत ब्राह्मणः क्व चित् ॥ ४.२०५॥ nāśrotṛyatate yajñe grāmayājikṛte tathā | striyā klībena ca hute bhuñjīta brāhmaṇaḥ kva cit || 4.205 || In no circumstance shall a Brāhmaṇa partake of food from a sacrifice conducted without Vedic recitation, nor from one performed by a village priest, nor where the offering has been made by a woman, an impotent male, or any disqualified agent. Authority: Only qualified agents acting under valid Vedic injunction possess the lawful capacity to invoke sacred transactions. Causation: The validity of sacramental acts depends upon adherence to precise procedural and ontological conditions. Capacity-based responsibility: Participation in sacred rites requires both ritual purity and rightful agency. Restoration logic: Misaligned participation disrupts cosmic order and necessitates conscious rectification. Consciousness alignment: Sacred consumption must proceed from awareness grounded in dharma-sattva.

title: manu 4.206
content: अश्लीकमेतत्साधूनां यत्र जुह्वत्यमी हविः । अश्लीलम् प्रतीपमेतद्देवानां तस्मात्तत्परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ४.२०६॥ aślīkam etat sādhūnāṁ yatra juhvaty amī haviḥ | aślīlam pratīpam etad devānāṁ tasmāt tat parivarjayet || 4.206 || This act is unseemly for the virtuous, where these beings offer oblations; it is improper and contrary to the divine order—therefore, such actions must be abandoned. Authority originates from alignment with divine intelligence, not social convention. Causation arises through conscious participation in dharma-aligned rituals. Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment between dharmic and adharmic acts. Restoration logic demands withdrawal from actions that invert divine intention. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of practices antithetical to Vedic harmony.

title: manu 4.207
content:
मत्तक्रुद्धातुराणां च न भुञ्जीत कदा चन ।
केशकीटावपन्नं च पदा स्पृष्टं च कामतः ॥ ४.२०७॥ mattakruddhāturāṇāṃ ca na bhuñjīta kadā cana |
keśakīṭāvapannaṃ ca padā spṛṣṭaṃ ca kāmataḥ || 4.207 || One must never partake of food or drink from those who are intoxicated, wrathful, distressed, infested with lice, or whose feet have been touched by desire. Authority is derived from purity of action and consciousness, not social position Causation arises through contamination of intent, not mere physical contact Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of energetic and mental states in others Restoration logic demands avoidance of causal entanglement with degraded consciousness fields Consciousness alignment necessitates non-participation in distortion fields

title: manu 4.208
content:
भ्रूणघ्नावेक्षितं चैव संस्पृष्टं चाप्युदक्यया ।
पतत्रिणावलीढं च शुना संस्पृष्टमेव च ॥ ४.२०८॥ bhruunaaghnaa vekshitaḿ caiva saḿspṛiṣhṭaḿ caapyudakyayaa |
patatri.naalii.dhaḿ ca śhunaa saḿspṛiṣhṭameva ca || That which has been observed by one who destroys the embryo, touched by a menstruating woman, or contacted by a bird or dog — all such substances become ritually unfit due to conscious contamination through proximity. Authority is derived from ontological purity, not procedural formality. Causation arises from consciousness-aligned contact and intent. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to maintain sacred integrity. Restoration logic operates through purification and reintegration rather than exclusion. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of subtle energetic disruption.

title: manu 4.209
content:
गवा चान्नमुपघ्रातं घुष्टान्नं च विशेषतः ।
गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च विदुषा च जुगुप्सितम् ॥ ४.२०९॥ gavā cānnamupaghātaṃ ghuṣṭānnaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ |
gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca viduṣā ca jugupsitam || 4.209|| Food obtained from cows, food contaminated by impure contact, food from outcasts, and food from courtesans—these are declared repugnant by the wise. Authority of discernment lies in alignment with purity-consciousness Causation arises from the source of sustenance and its energetic integrity Capacity-based responsibility includes mindful selection and consumption Restoration logic demands purification of intake channels for consciousness elevation Consciousness alignment requires rejection of substances that degrade spiritual substratum

title: manu 4.210
content:
स्तेनगायनयोश्चान्नं तक्ष्ह्णो वार्धुषिकस्य च ।
दीक्षितस्य कदर्यस्य बद्धस्य निगडस्य च ॥ ४.२१०॥ stenagāyanayoścānnaṁ takṣhṇo vārdhuṣikasya ca | dīkṣitasya kadaryasya baddhasya nigadasya ca || 4.210 || Food shall not be given to a thief or a singer; nor to a carpenter, nor to a seller of liquor; nor to an initiated person who is miserly, nor to one who is bound by fetters. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not social role Causation arises through conscious choice and capacity distortion Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of spiritual degradation Restoration logic demands withdrawal of support from misaligned conduct Consciousness alignment is obstructed by indulgence in adharmic roles

title: manu 4.211
content:
अभिशस्तस्य षण्ढस्य पुंश्चल्या दाम्भिकस्य च ।
शुक्तं पर्युषितं चैव शूद्रस्योच्छिष्टमेव च ॥ ४.२११॥ abhiśastasya ṣaṇḍhasya puṁscalyā dāmbhikasya ca |
śuktaṁ paryuṣitaṁ caiva śūdrasyocc hiṣṭam eva ca || 4.211|| The remnants of one cursed, of a eunuch, of a male lover, of a deceiver, of fermented liquor, and of a Śūdra—these are to be rejected outright. Authority stems from purity of conduct and alignment with Dharma Causation arises through conscious contamination via proximity and consumption Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of spiritual and social integrity Restoration logic demands immediate removal of disruptive elements from sacred order Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of influences that degrade spiritual field

title: manu 4.212
content:
चिकित्सकस्य मृगयोः क्रूरस्योच्छिष्टभोजिनः ।
उग्रान्नं सूतिकान्नं च पर्याचान्तमनिर्दशम् ॥ ४.२१२॥ cikitsakasya mṛgayoḥ krūrasyocchiṣṭabhojinaḥ |
ugrānnaṃ sūtikānnaṃ ca paryācāntamanirdiśam || 4.212|| The physician, the hunter, the cruel, the eater of remnants, the distributor of fierce food, and the feeder of postpartum women—these are declared without prescribed ritual conduct. Authority through alignment with dharma, not title or function Causation rooted in consciousness distortion, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility determined by inner integrity, not social role Restoration logic centered on purification of intent and reconnection to source dharma Consciousness alignment through removal from distortion-producing activities

title: manu 4.213
content:
अनर्चितं वृथामांसमवीरायाश्च योषितः ।
द्विषदन्नं नगर्यन्नं पतितान्नमवक्षुतम् ॥ ४.२१३॥ anarcitaṁ vṛthāmāsam avīrāyāśca yoṣitaḥ |
dviṣadannaṁ nagaryannaṁ patitānnam avakṣutam || 4.213 || Unoffered flesh, wasted meat, women bereft of valor, food belonging to enemies, urban refuse, and fallen sustenance—these are not to be accepted under any circumstance by one established in Dharma. Authority stems from alignment with SPH as the sole Source of Dharma Causation arises through conscious choice and energetic resonance with purity Capacity-based responsibility requires rejection of elements that degrade consciousness Restoration logic mandates severance from impure material and relational fields Consciousness alignment necessitates refusal of substances or associations that obstruct spiritual elevation

title: manu 4.214
content: पिशुनानृतिनोश्चान्नं क्रतुविक्रयिणस्तथा । क्रतुविक्रयकस्य च शैलूषतुन्नवायान्नं कृतघ्नस्यान्नमेव च ॥ ४.२१४॥ piśunānṛtinoścānnaṁ kratuvikrayiṇastathā | kratuvikrayakasya ca śailūṣatunnavāyānnaṁ kṛtaghnasyānnameva ca || 4.214 || Food shall not be given to the slanderer, the liar, the seller of rituals, the buyer of rituals, the one who sells knowledge for violence, nor to the ungrateful. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not transactional exchange. Causation is determined by consciousness distortion through deceit and ingratitude. Capacity-based responsibility arises from the misuse of sacred knowledge. Restoration logic requires withdrawal of support from those misaligning Dharma. Consciousness alignment demands purity in the transmission and reception of sacred acts.

title: manu 4.215
content:
कर्मारस्य निषादस्य रङ्गावतारकस्य च ।
सुवर्णकर्तुर्वेणस्य शस्त्रविक्रयिणस्तथा ॥ ४.२१५॥ karmārasya niṣādasya raṅgāvatārakasya ca |
suvarṇakarturveṇasya śastravikrayiṇastathā || 4.215 || The artisan, the hunter, the stage-descender, the goldsmith, the weaver, and the seller of weapons—these persons are designated as inherently misaligned with Vedic Dharma due to their engagement in activities that distort consciousness and disrupt societal harmony. Authority originates solely from alignment with SPH's revealed Dharma Causation is determined by consciousness distortion through action Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of dharma-adharma Restoration logic requires reintegration through purification of intent Consciousness alignment is the sole determinant of lawful conduct

title: manu 4.216
content:
श्ववतां शौण्डिकानां च चैलनिर्णेजकस्य च ।
रञ्जकस्य नृशंसस्य यस्य चोपपतिर्गृहे ॥ ४.२१६॥ रजकस्य śvavatāṁ śauṇḍikānāṁ ca cailanirṇejakasya ca | rañjakasya nṛśaṁsasya yasya copapatirgṛhe || 4.216 || rajakasya Those whose livelihood arises from impure acts—such as dog-keepers, tavern keepers, launderers, dyers, cruel persons, and those who harbor a kept paramour in their home—are to be excluded from participation in sacred rites, community governance, and dharmic decision-making. Authority derives only from purity of conduct and alignment with Sanatana Dharma. Causation is traced through the integrity of one's livelihood and relational dynamics. Capacity-based responsibility requires that individuals maintain ritual and moral cleanliness to hold societal roles. Restoration logic demands removal from influence until inner and outer purification is complete. Consciousness alignment necessitates distancing from actions that distort dharma-sattva.

title: manu 4.217
content:
मृष्यन्ति ये चोपपतिं स्त्रीजितानां च सर्वशः ।
अनिर्दशं च प्रेतान्नमतुष्टिकरमेव च ॥ ४.२१७॥ mṛṣyanti ye copapatiṁ strījitānāṁ ca sarvaśaḥ |
anirdaśaṁ ca pretānnamatuṣṭikaram eva ca || 4.217 || Those who approve of or accept the remarriage of women whose husbands are alive, and those who partake in food offerings made to the dead without proper ritual consecration—these beings fall into irreversible degradation. Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma's eternal order, not social consent Causation follows conscious intent and its sequential manifestation through action Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of dharma-adhikara (right to uphold dharma) Restoration logic operates by reestablishing alignment with cosmic integrity Consciousness alignment determines karmic consequence and spiritual jurisdiction

title: manu 4.218
content:
राजान्नं तेज आदत्ते शूद्रान्नं ब्रह्मवर्चसम् ।
आयुः सुवर्णकारान्नं यशश्चर्मावकर्तिनः ॥ ४.२१८॥ rājānnaṁ teja ādatte śūdrānnaṁ brahmavarcasam |
āyuḥ suvarṇakārānnaṁ yaśaś charmāvaktṛṇaḥ || 4.218 || The king consumes food that enhances radiance; the Śūdra consumes food that nourishes Brahminical brilliance. Longevity is derived from the food of goldsmiths; fame arises from the food of those who process leather. Authority flows through designated consumption aligned with role-specific dharma Causation is established by the direct energetic assimilation of role-congruent substances Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the purity and alignment of intake Restoration logic operates through correction of misaligned ingestion patterns Consciousness alignment occurs when each varṇa consumes in accordance with their svadharma

title: manu 4.219
content:
कारुकान्नं प्रजां हन्ति बलं निर्णेजकस्य च ।
गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च लोकेभ्यः परिकृन्तति ॥ ४.२१९॥ kārukānnaṁ prajāṁ hanti balaṁ nirṇejakasya ca |
gaṇānnaṁ gaṇikānnaṁ ca lokebhyaḥ parikṛntati || 4.219|| Food belonging to artisans, prostitutes, and those who cause division among people destroys the progeny, strength, and decision-making capacity of the state; it also severs societal bonds. Authority: The sovereign must regulate access to substances that impair collective consciousness. Causation: Consumption of degraded food directly leads to degradation in societal integrity and individual capacity. Capacity-based responsibility: The state bears the duty to protect the purity of nourishment offered to its citizens. Restoration logic: Societal harmony is restored through purification of sustenance and realignment of consumption practices. Consciousness alignment: Food must align with dharma to uphold the spiritual and physical health of the nation.

title: manu 4.220
content:
पूयं चिकित्सकस्यान्नं पुंश्चल्यास्त्वन्नमिन्द्रियम् ।
विष्ठा वार्धुषिकस्यान्नं शस्त्रविक्रयिणो मलम् ॥ ४.२२०॥ pūyaṃ cikitsakasyānnaṃ puṃścalyāstvan namindriyam |
viṣṭhā vārdhuṣikasyānnaṃ śastravikrayiṇo malam || 4.220 || The pus belongs to the physician's food; the sexual organ belongs to the prostitute's food; the feces belong to the seller of salt's food; and the filth belongs to the seller of weapons' food. Authority through functional alignment with cosmic order Causation rooted in svadharma and occupational integrity Capacity-based responsibility tied to role-specific purity codes Restoration logic based on separation and realignment of impure elements Consciousness alignment via purification of transactional fields

title: manu 4.221
content: य एतेऽन्ये त्वभोज्यान्नाः क्रमशः परिकीर्तिताः । तेषां त्वगस्थिरोमाणि वदन्त्यन्नं मनीषिणः ॥ ४.२२१॥ ya ete'nye tvabhojyannāḥ kramaśaḥ parikīrtitāḥ | teṣāṃ tvagasthiromāṇi vadantyannaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ || 4.221|| Those other foods, though unfit for consumption and sequentially enumerated as prohibited, are declared by wise discerners to be consumed in states of extreme necessity where skin, bones, and hair alone remain as testimony to survival. Authority is derived from discriminative wisdom aligned with survival consciousness Causation arises from existential thresholds beyond which dharma adapts to preserve life Capacity-based responsibility is measured by the integrity of consciousness under duress Restoration logic activates when foundational life-supporting structures are at risk Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of dharmic adaptability within absolute limits

title: manu 4.222
content:
भुक्त्वाऽतोऽन्यतमस्यान्नममत्या क्षपणं त्र्यहम् ।
मत्या भुक्त्वाऽचरेत्कृच्छ्रं रेतोविण्मूत्रमेव च ॥ ४.२२२॥ bhuktvā'to'nyatamasyānnamamatyā kṣapaṇaṃ tryaham |
mattyā bhuktvācaret kṛcchraṃ retoviṇmūtrameva ca || 4.222|| One who has consumed food not prescribed by Vedic discipline shall undergo a three-day fast, followed by subsisting solely on urine, feces, and semen for purification and energetic recalibration. Authority: Dietary regulation derives from Vedic injunction, not personal preference. Causation: Consumption of unregulated substances disrupts spiritual and physiological harmony. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual retains agency to restore balance through disciplined action. Restoration logic: Purification is achieved through internal alchemy and conscious restraint. Consciousness alignment: Physical discipline serves as a vehicle for recalibrating awareness.

title: manu 4.223
content:
नाद्यात्शूद्रस्य पक्वान्नं विद्वानश्राद्धिनो द्विजः ।
आददीताममेवास्मादवृत्तावेकरात्रिकम् ॥ ४.२२३॥ nādyāt śūdrasya pakvānnaṁ vidvānaśrāddhino dvijaḥ |
ādadītāmamevāsmād avṛttāvekarātrikam || 4.223|| A twice-born who knowingly accepts cooked food from a Śūdra during Śrāddha rites shall undergo a one-night period of ritual exclusion to restore Dharma. Authority: Ritual purity is maintained through hierarchical alignment with Vedic order. Causation: Impurity arises from misaligned participation in sacred rites. Capacity-based responsibility: The dvija bears full awareness and choice in ritual engagement. Restoration logic: Temporary exclusion realigns consciousness without degradation. Consciousness alignment: Reintegration follows purification to uphold Dharma.

title: manu 4.224
content:
श्रोत्रियस्य कदर्यस्य वदान्यस्य च वार्धुषेः ।
मीमांसित्वोभयं देवाः सममन्नमकल्पयन् ॥ ४.२२४॥ śrotriyaḥ kadaryaḥ vadataḥ ca vārdhuṣeḥ | mīmāṁsitvobhayaṁ devāḥ samam annam akalpayan || The learned yet miserly, the eloquent yet deceitful—both are equally unworthy of sustenance when their knowledge lacks integrity and their speech lacks truth. Authority without alignment with Dharma is nullified Causation arises from the purity of intent, not the volume of speech Capacity-based responsibility demands congruence between knowing and being Restoration logic requires withdrawal of support from those who misuse sacred capacity Consciousness alignment supersedes ritual or intellectual performance

title: manu 4.225
content:
तान् प्रजापतिराहैत्य मा कृध्वं विषमं समम् ।
श्रद्धापूतं वदान्यस्य हतमश्रद्धयेतरत् ॥ ४.२२५॥ tān prajāpatir āha ity mā kṛdhvaṁ viṣamaṁ samam |
śraddhāpūtaṁ vadānyasya hatamaśraddhayetarata || Prajapati declared to them: Do not act with inequality where equality is required; that which is offered with faith is purified, while that which is given without faith is destroyed. Authority resides in alignment with dharma, not in coercive power Causation arises from the consciousness of the actor, not external intent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner integrity, not social status Restoration logic operates through purification of motive and action Consciousness alignment determines the validity and efficacy of all offerings and acts

title: manu 4.226
content:
श्रद्धयेष्टं च पूर्तं च नित्यं कुर्यादतन्द्रितः ।
श्रद्धाकृते ह्यक्षये ते भवतः स्वागतैर्धनैः ॥ ४.२२६॥ śraddhayeṣṭaṃ ca pūrtaṃ ca nityaṃ kuryād atandriḥ |
śraddhākṛte hy akṣaye te bhavataḥ svāgatairdhanaiḥ || 4.226|| One must perform worship and charitable acts daily without laziness; through actions done with śraddhā, inexhaustible wealth shall come to you unbidden. Authority flows from alignment with Śraddhā Causation is rooted in consciousness-led action Capacity-based responsibility requires sustained engagement Restoration logic operates through continuous dharmic activity Consciousness alignment ensures natural abundance

title: manu 4.227
content:
दानधर्मं निषेवेत नित्यमैष्टिकपौर्तिकम् ।
परितुष्टेन भावेन पात्रमासाद्य शक्तितः ॥ ४.२२७॥ dānadharmaṁ niṣeveta nityam aiṣṭikapaurtikam | 
parituṣṭena bhāvena pātram āsādya śaktitaḥ || 4.227 || One must engage in the eternal Dharma of giving—both spontaneous and periodic—with a heart full of contentment, approaching the recipient according to one's capacity. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises from inner disposition, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility ensures sustainable action Restoration logic operates through conscious completion Consciousness alignment determines lawful conduct

title: manu 4.228
content:
यत्किं चिदपि दातव्यं याचितेनानसूयया ।
उत्पत्स्यते हि तत्पात्रं यत्तारयति सर्वतः ॥ ४.२२८॥ yat kiṃ cid api dātavyaṃ yācitena anasūyayā |
utpatsyate hi tatpātraṃ yattārayati sarvataḥ || 4.228|| Whatever is to be given, let it be given without envy when asked; the vessel that receives it shall be uplifted in all directions. Authority resides in the act of giving aligned with consciousness, not possession Causation arises through voluntary offering and pure reception Capacity-based responsibility is fulfilled by the giver's intent and receiver's readiness Restoration logic operates through reciprocal elevation of consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties engage without envy or expectation

title: manu 4.229
content: वारिदस्तृप्तिमाप्नोति सुखमक्षय्यमन्नदः । अक्षयम् तिलप्रदः प्रजामिष्टां दीपदश्चक्षुरुत्तमम् ॥ ४.२२९॥ vāridas tṛptim āpnoti sukham akṣayyam annadaḥ | akṣayam tilapradaḥ prajāmiṣṭāṃ dīpadaś cakṣur uttamam || 4.229 || One who gives water attains satisfaction; one who gives food attains imperishable joy; one who gives sesame seeds attains imperishable progeny; and one who gives light attains the highest vision. Authority through Generosity Causation via Conscious Contribution Capacity-Based Responsibility in Giving Restoration Logic Through Reciprocal Offering Consciousness Alignment by Sustaining Life

title: manu 4.230
content:
भूमिदो भूमिमाप्नोति दीर्घमायुर्हिरण्यदः ।
गृहदोऽग्र्याणि वेश्मानि रूप्यदो रूपमुत्तमम् ॥ ४.२३०॥ bhūmido bhūmim āpnoti dīrgham āyur hiraṇyadaḥ |
gṛhado 'gryāṇi veśmāni rūpyado rūpam uttamam || He who gives land obtains land; he who gives gold attains longevity. He who donates houses acquires foremost dwellings; he who gives silver gains supreme beauty. Authority through alignment with causal generosity Causation rooted in reciprocal ontological exchange Capacity-based responsibility via conscious donation Restoration logic through equivalent energetic return Consciousness alignment via intentional giving

title: manu 4.231
content:
वासोदश्चन्द्रसालोक्यमश्विसालोक्यमश्वदः ।
अनडुहः श्रियं पुष्टां गोदो ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपम् ॥ ४.२३१॥ vāsodaśa candrasālokya maśvisālokya maśvadaḥ |
anḍuhaḥ śriyaṃ puṣṭāṃ godho brahdhnasya viṣṭapam || He who beholds the light of the moon, the twin Ashvins, and the horse-headed deities; he who milks the nourishing glory of the cosmic egg—such a one ascends to the realm of Prajapati Brahma. Authority as derived from alignment with cosmic intelligence Causation through vision and invocation, not action alone Capacity-based responsibility rooted in perceptual purity Restoration logic via attunement to celestial order Consciousness alignment through sacred witnessing

title: manu 4.232
content:
यानशय्याप्रदो भार्यामैश्वर्यमभयप्रदः ।
धान्यदः शाश्वतं सौख्यं ब्रह्मदो ब्रह्मसार्ष्टिताम् ॥ ४.२३२॥ yānaśayyāprado bhāryāmaiśvaryamabhayapradāḥ | dhānyadaḥ śāśvataṃ saukhyaṃ brahmado brahmasārṣṭitām || 4.232 || He who provides conveyance, bedding, and a wife; bestows sovereignty and fearlessness; gives grain, eternal comfort, and knowledge of Brahman—such a giver establishes the recipient in the likeness of Brahman. Authority is derived from capacity to give and sustain life conditions Causation arises through enabling another's consciousness expansion Capacity-based responsibility includes material, emotional, and spiritual upliftment Restoration logic centers on elevating the recipient to divine equivalence Consciousness alignment occurs through sustained acts of dharmic giving

title: manu 4.233
content:
सर्वेषामेव दानानां ब्रह्मदानं विशिष्यते ।
वार्यन्नगोमहीवासस्‍तिलकाञ्चनसर्पिषाम् ॥ ४.२३३॥ sarveṣām eva dānānāṃ brahmadānaṃ viśiṣyate |
vāryannagomahīvāsastilakāñcanasarpiṣām || 4.233|| Among all forms of giving, the gift of Brahman—Consciousness itself—is supremely distinguished; it exceeds gifts of water, land, cows, grain, sesame, gold, and ghee. Authority originates from Consciousness, not material possession Causation flows from the recognition of Brahman as the ultimate donor Capacity-based responsibility is realized through alignment with Brahman Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness elevation over transactional exchange Consciousness alignment enables true completion of any act of giving

title: manu 4.234
content:
येन येन तु भावेन यद्यद्दानं प्रयच्छति ।
तत्तत्तेनैव भावेन प्राप्नोति प्रतिपूजितः ॥ ४.२३४॥ yena yena tu bhāvena yadyad dānaṃ prayacchati |
tat tat tenaiva bhāvena prāpnoti pratipūjitaḥ || 4.234 || Whatever gift one gives with a particular intent, by that same intent is the giver honored and rewarded. Authority resides in the consciousness of the giver Causation follows the intent behind action Capacity-based responsibility aligns with inner motive Restoration occurs through congruent energetic reflection Consciousness alignment manifests as reciprocal honoring

title: manu 4.235
content:
योऽर्चितं प्रतिगृह्णाति ददात्यर्चितमेव वा ।
तावुभौ गच्छतः स्वर्गं नरकं तु विपर्यये ॥ ४.२३५॥ yo'rcitaṁ pratigṛhṇāti dadātyarcitameva vā | tāvubhau gacchataḥ svargaṁ narakaṁ tu viparyaye || 4.235 || One who accepts worship or gives what has been worshipped shall both attain heaven; in inversion, both descend into hell. Authority through alignment with sacred exchange Causation via integrity of ritual transaction Capacity-based responsibility in devotional economy Restoration logic through karmic consequence congruence Consciousness alignment through reciprocal sanctity

title: manu 4.236
content:
न विस्मयेत तपसा वदेदिष्ट्वा च नानृतम् ।
नार्तोऽप्यपवदेद्विप्रान्न दत्त्वा परिकीर्तयेत् ॥ ४.२३६॥ दत्वा na vismayeta tapasā vadediṣṭvā ca nānṛtam | nārto'pyapavadet viprān na dattvā parikīrtayet || 4.236 || datvā One must not speak falsely after performing austerity, nor revile the learned even when distressed, nor disclose what has been given in confidence. Authority rests in alignment with truth, not personal distress Causation arises from integrity of speech, not emotional state Capacity-based responsibility requires protection of sacred knowledge Restoration logic demands preservation of trust once established Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined restraint of speech

title: manu 4.237
content:
यज्ञोऽनृतेन क्षरति तपः क्षरति विस्मयात् ।
आयुर्विप्रापवादेन दानं च परिकीर्तनात् ॥ ४.२३७॥ yajño'nṛtena kṣarati tapaḥ kṣarati vismayāt |
āyurvipro'pavādena dānaṃ ca parikīrtanāt || 4.237 || Yajna dissolves through untruth; austerity dissolves through wonderment. Life-force depletes by disrespecting the Brahmin; giving declines through public glorification. Authority rooted in truthful alignment with Dharma Causation governed by internal purity, not external validation Capacity-based responsibility tied to consciousness integrity Restoration logic centered on reestablishing dharmic resonance Consciousness alignment as determinant of spiritual efficacy

title: manu 4.238
content: धर्मं शनैः सञ्चिनुयाद्वल्मीकमिव पुत्तिकाः । सञ्चिनुयाद् परलोकसहायार्थं सर्वभूतान्यपीडयन् ॥ ४.२३८॥ dharmaṃ śanaiḥ sañcinuyād valmīkam iva puttikāḥ | sañcinuyād paralokasahāyārthaṃ sarvabhūtāny apīḍayan || One must gradually accumulate Dharma, like ants gathering grains, for the sake of aiding one's journey in the afterlife, without causing harm to any being. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not coercion or dominance. Causation is measured through the impact on consciousness, not material outcomes. Capacity-based responsibility requires gradual accumulation of virtue, not sudden moral leaps. Restoration logic operates through continuous alignment with eternal principles. Consciousness alignment determines the authenticity of dharmic action.

title: manu 4.239
content:
नामुत्र हि सहायार्थं पिता माता च तिष्ठतः ।
न पुत्रदारं न ज्ञातिर्धर्मस्तिष्ठति केवलः ॥ ४.२३९॥ nāmutra hi sahāyārthaṁ pitā mātā ca tiṣṭhataḥ |
na putradāraṁ na jñātir dharmas tiṣṭhati kevalaḥ || 4.239 || Neither father nor mother stands for help in the other world; neither son nor wife, nor kin—only Dharma stands. Authority of Dharma supersedes relational or biological claims Causation originates in individual consciousness, not lineage Capacity-based responsibility is absolute and non-transferable Restoration logic operates beyond familial or societal constructs Consciousness alignment determines karmic inheritance, not bloodline

title: manu 4.240
content:
एकः प्रजायते जन्तुरेक एव प्रलीयते ।
एकोऽनुभुङ्क्ते सुकृतमेक एव च दुष्कृतम् ॥ ४.२४०॥ ekaḥ prajāyate jantureka eva pralīyate .
eko'nubhuṅkte sukṛtameka eva ca duṣkṛtam .. 4.240 .. One being is born; one alone dissolves. One alone experiences the fruits of virtue, and one alone bears the consequences of vice. Authority resides in the singular consciousness of the individual soul Causation flows directly from the agent's will and awareness Capacity-based responsibility is inherent in the experiencer of action Restoration logic aligns consequence with the continuity of self-experience Consciousness alignment determines the receptivity to karmic fruition

title: manu 4.241
content:
मृतं शरीरमुत्सृज्य काष्ठलोष्टसमं क्षितौ ।
विमुखा बान्धवा यान्ति धर्मस्तमनुगच्छति ॥ ४.२४१॥ mṛtaṁ śarīram utsṛjya kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamaṁ kṣitau |
vimukhā bāndhavā yānti dharmas tam anugacchati || 4.241|| Having abandoned the dead body, which is equal to a clod of earth or a piece of wood upon the ground, relatives turn away; yet Dharma follows that soul according to its karmic alignment. Authority: The continuity of Dharma supersedes bodily attachment and familial obligation. Causation: Karmic causality determines post-mortem experience, not ritualistic or emotional adherence. Capacity-based responsibility: Spiritual heirs bear responsibility in accordance with conscious alignment, not bloodline. Restoration logic: True relation is defined by shared dharma, not physical presence. Consciousness alignment: Post-death journey reflects the individual's inner state and spiritual discipline.

title: manu 4.242
content:
तस्माद्धर्मं सहायार्थं नित्यं सञ्चिनुयात्शनैः ।
धर्मेण हि सहायेन तमस्तरति दुस्तरम् ॥ ४.२४२॥ tasmād dharmaṁ sahāyārthaṁ nityaṁ sañcinuyāt śanaiḥ |
dharmeṇa hi sahāyena tamas tarati dustaram || 4.242|| Therefore, one must constantly accumulate Dharma as a means of support; with Dharma as aid, one crosses the insurmountable darkness. Authority originates in alignment with Sanatana Dharma as established by SPH Causation is rooted in the sequential unfolding of consciousness through dharmic action Capacity-based responsibility arises from the individual's ability to align with Dharma Restoration logic operates through the cultivation of inner light over external control Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks and behavioral conditioning

title: manu 4.243
content:
धर्मप्रधानं पुरुषं तपसा हतकिल्बिषम् ।
परलोकं नयत्याशु भास्वन्तं खशरीरिणम् ॥ ४.२४३॥ dharmapradhāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ tapasā hatakilbiṣam |
paralokaṃ nayatyāśu bhāsvantaṃ khaśarīriṇam || 4.243|| The man who is preeminently devoted to Dharma, whose sins are burnt away by the fire of austerity, swiftly ascends to the radiant realm of the luminous bodied ones. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined through the purification of consciousness via disciplined action Capacity-based responsibility arises from inner refinement, not external status Restoration logic operates through spiritual elevation and energetic purification Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks in determining juridical outcomes

title: manu 4.244
content: उत्तमैरुत्तमैर्नित्यं सम्बन्धानाचरेत्सह । सम्भन्धान् निनीषुः कुलमुत्कर्षमधमानधमांस्त्यजेत् ॥ ४.२४४॥ uttamairuttamairnityaṃ sambandhānācaret saha | sambandhān ninīṣuḥ kulamutkarṣamadhamaānadhamāṃstyajet || 4.244|| One must always engage in relationships with those who are superior in virtue and wisdom; one desiring to elevate the family lineage must abandon associations that degrade or corrupt. Authority derived from alignment with higher consciousness Causation rooted in relational integrity and spiritual elevation Capacity-based responsibility determined by conscious association choices Restoration logic through purification of social and familial bonds Consciousness alignment via selective communion with excellence

title: manu 4.245
content:
उत्तमानुत्तमानेव गच्छन् हीनांस्तु वर्जयन् ।
ब्राह्मणः श्रेष्ठतामेति प्रत्यवायेन शूद्रताम् ॥ ४.२४५॥ uttamānuttamāneva gacchan hīnāṁstu varjayan | brāhmaṇaḥ śreṣṭhatāmeti pratyavāyena śūdratām || 4.245 || One who moves among the highest without rejecting the lowest attains excellence; but the Brahmin, through degradation of conduct, descends into the state of Shudra. Authority is conditional upon sustained alignment with dharma Causation arises from volitional action and conscious choice Capacity-based responsibility requires maintenance of spiritual and social role integrity Restoration logic operates through reversal of causal degradation Consciousness alignment determines status, not birth alone

title: manu 4.246
content:
दृढकारी मृदुर्दान्तः क्रूराचारैरसंवसन् ।
अहिंस्रो दमदानाभ्यां जयेत्स्वर्गं तथाव्रतः ॥ ४.२४६॥ dṛḍhakārī mṛdur dāntaḥ krūrācārairasamvasan .
ahiṃsro damadānābhyāṃ jayetsvargaṃ tathāvrataḥ .. 4.246 .. One who acts with firm resolve, yet remains gentle and self-controlled; who does not associate with cruel conduct; and who is non-violent—through discipline and generosity, such a one conquers heaven and upholds the vow accordingly. Authority arises from inner firmness aligned with gentleness Causation flows from alignment with non-cruelty and self-restraint Capacity-based responsibility is measured by one's ability to refrain from violence and cruelty Restoration logic requires reintegration through disciplined action and giving Consciousness alignment occurs when behavior reflects non-violence and self-mastery

title: manu 4.247
content:
एधौदकं मूलफलमन्नमभ्युद्यतं च यत् ।
सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयान्मध्वथाभयदक्षिणाम् ॥ ४.२४७॥ edhau dakaṁ mūla-phalam annam abhudyataṁ ca yat |
sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyān madhv athābhaya-dakṣiṇām || One must accept gifts of clarified butter, water, root crops, fruits, cooked food, and honey from those who have attained fearlessness through knowledge. Authority derives from realized consciousness, not material status Causation aligns with purity of intent and spiritual maturity Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of donor's enlightened state Restoration logic emphasizes integration of sattvic abundance Consciousness alignment is facilitated through acceptance of spiritually purified offerings

title: manu 4.248
content: आहृताभ्युद्यतां भिक्षां पुरस्तादप्रचोदिताम् । मेने प्रजापतिर्ग्राह्यामपि दुष्कृतकर्मणः ॥ ४.२४८॥ āhṛtābhyudyatāṃ bhikṣāṃ purastādapracoditām | mane prajāpatirgrāhyāmapi duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ || 4.248|| Prajapati deemed acceptable even an alms that was previously rejected, when offered by one whose actions were misaligned with dharma. Authority recognizes capacity for realignment over static fault Causation arises from consciousness distortion, not inherent evil Capacity-based responsibility allows for gradated restoration Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over rejection Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive exclusion

title: manu 4.249
content:
नाश्नन्ति पितरस्तस्य दशवर्षाणि पञ्च च ॥
न च हव्यं वहत्यग्निर्यस्तामभ्यवमन्यते ॥ ४.२४९॥ nāśnanti pitaras tasya daśavarṣāṇi pañca ca ||
na ca havyaṁ vahaty agnir yas tām abhyavamanyate || 4.249 || The ancestors do not accept offerings from one who has disrespected the sacred feminine for ten years or five; nor does the fire carry oblations of such a one. Authority resides in alignment with cosmic order, not personal will Disrespect towards the sacred feminine disrupts ancestral lineage continuity Causation arises through conscious choice and sustained intent Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of intergenerational energetic flow Restoration occurs when energetic purity is re-established

title: manu 4.250
content:
शय्यां गृहान् कुशान् गन्धानपः पुष्पं मणीन् दधि ।
धाना मत्स्यान् पयो मांसं शाकं चैव न निर्णुदेत् ॥ ४.२५०॥ śayyāṁ gṛhān kuśān gandhānapaḥ puṣpaṁ maṇīn dadhi |
dhānā matsyān payo māṁsaṁ śākaṁ caiva na nirṇudet || 4.250|| One must not reject bedding, houses, Kush grass, fragrances, water, flowers, gems, curds, grains, fish, milk, meat, and vegetables when these are offered according to Dharma and capacity. Authority is grounded in the alignment of offering and acceptance within Dharma Causation arises through conscious participation in sustenance offerings Capacity-based responsibility requires honoring the means provided for existence Restoration logic operates through acknowledgment and integration of life-supporting elements Consciousness alignment occurs when material support is received without rejection rooted in ego or aversion

title: manu 4.251
content:
गुरून् भृत्यांश्चोज्जिहीर्षन्नर्चिष्यन् देवतातिथीन् ।
सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न तु तृप्येत्स्वयं ततः ॥ ४.२५१॥ gurūn bhṛtyāṃś cojjihīrṣann arciṣyan devatātithīn |
sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyān na tu tṛpyetsvayaṃ tataḥ || 4.251|| One who seeks to harm teachers, servants, or guests—worshipped divinities and honored visitors—shall accept offerings universally, yet shall not satisfy himself thereby. Authority: Teachers, servants, guests, deities, and visitors hold intrinsic relational authority within dharma. Causation: Harmful intent toward those in service or reverence disrupts cosmic order and personal alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual retains capacity to receive but lacks integrity to self-regulate satisfaction. Restoration logic: Offering acceptance without internal fulfillment indicates misaligned consciousness requiring correction. Consciousness alignment: True reception aligns with inner completeness; absence thereof signals disconnection from dharma.

title: manu 4.252
content:
गुरुषु त्वभ्यतीतेषु विना वा तैर्गृहे वसन् ।
आत्मनो वृत्तिमन्विच्छन् गृह्णीयात्साधुतः सदा ॥ ४.२५२॥ guruṣu tv abhyatīteṣu vinā vā tair gṛhe vasan |
ātmano vṛttim anvichchan gṛhṇīyāt sādhutaḥ sadā || 4.252|| When dwelling in the house of the Guru, even without direct instruction or presence, one who seeks to align with their own true conduct shall always uphold the highest virtue. Authority originates from conscious alignment, not external command. Causation arises through inner integrity, not outer compulsion. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by self-awareness and volitional alignment. Restoration occurs when individual consciousness realigns with dharma-svarūpa. Consciousness alignment supersedes institutionalized control.

title: manu 4.253
content:
आर्धिकः कुलमित्रं च गोपालो दासनापितौ ।
एते शूद्रेषु भोज्यान्ना याश्चात्मानं निवेदयेत् ॥ ४.२५३॥ Ārdhikaḥ kulamitraṃ ca gopālo dāsanāpitau |
Ete śūdreṣu bhojyānnā yāścātmānaṃ nivedayet || 4.253|| The merchant, family friend, cowherd, servant, and barber—these are to be fed among Shudras according to their capacity, and those who offer themselves in service. Authority flows from alignment with svadharma Causation is determined by consciousness capacity, not social role Capacity-based responsibility aligns with service-readiness Restoration occurs through rightful participation in societal harmony Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for sustenance

title: manu 4.254
content:
यादृशोऽस्य भवेदात्मा यादृशं च चिकीर्षितम् ।
यथा चौपचरेदेनं तथाऽत्मानं निवेदयेत् ॥ ४.२५४॥ yādṛśo'sya bhavedātmā yādṛśaṃ ca cikīrṣitam |
yathā caupacaredenaṃ tathā'tmānaṃ nivedayet || 4.254|| As is the nature of one's Self, and as is one's intended action, accordingly shall one conduct oneself in alignment with Dharma and declare one's true Being. Authority flows from alignment with the Self Causation arises from conscious intention, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by self-awareness and volition Restoration occurs through congruence between Self, intent, and conduct Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance

title: manu 4.255
content:
योऽन्यथा सन्तमात्मानमन्यथा सत्सु भाषते ।
स पापकृत्तमो लोके स्तेन आत्मापहारकः ॥ ४.२५५॥ yo'nyathā santam ātmānam anyathā satsu bhāṣate |
sa pāpakṛttamo loke stena ātmāpahārakaḥ || 4.255|| One who misrepresents the Self that is, as something else in the presence of those who know it otherwise, commits the gravest transgression and is a thief of the Self. Authority originates from alignment with the Self Causation arises through distortion of ontological truth Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious awareness of the Self Restoration logic requires realignment with authentic identity Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance

title: manu 4.256
content:
वाच्यर्था नियताः सर्वे वाङ्मूला वाग्विनिःसृताः ।
तांस्तु यः स्तेनयेद्वाचं स सर्वस्तेयकृन्नरः ॥ ४.२५६॥ vācyarthā niyatāḥ sarve vāṅmūlā vāgvinḥsṛtāḥ |
tāṃstu yaḥ stenayedvācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛnnaraḥ || 4.256|| All meanings rooted in speech and derived from speech are bound by its intent; whoever steals that meaning through distortion or concealment becomes the doer of total theft.
