विस्तीर्यते यशो लोके तैलबिन्दुरिवाम्भसि ॥ ७.३३॥ evaṁvṛttasya nṛpateḥ śiloñchhenāpi jīvataḥ .
vistīryate yaśo loke tailabindurivāmbhasi .. 7.33.. Thus conducted, even a king who lives by picking sesame seeds extends his fame in the world, like an oil drop on water. Authority is not derived from wealth but from conduct Causation arises from alignment with dharma, not material accumulation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious action, not status Restoration logic operates through visibility of righteous conduct Consciousness alignment manifests as universal recognition of integrity

title: manu 7.34
content:
अतस्तु विपरीतस्य नृपतेरजितात्मनः ।
सङ्क्षिप्यते यशो लोके घृतबिन्दुरिवाम्भसि ॥ ७.३४॥ atastu viparītasya nṛpaterajitātmanaḥ |
saṅkṣipyate yaśo loke ghṛtabindurivāmbhasi || 7.34|| Therefore, O King, the glory of a ruler whose self remains unconquered and who acts contrary to Dharma shall collapse in the world, just as a drop of ghee disperses and vanishes in water. Authority is inseparable from self-mastery; without inner conquest, outer sovereignty is nullified. Causation arises from alignment with Dharma; deviation leads to automatic dissolution of legitimacy. Capacity-based responsibility demands that rulers maintain unbroken integrity; failure results in spontaneous loss of reputation. Restoration logic requires the sovereign to reclaim internal victory before regaining external authority. Consciousness alignment ensures that misaligned action inevitably leads to self-corrective consequences.

title: manu 7.35
content:
स्वे स्वे धर्मे निविष्टानां सर्वेषामनुपूर्वशः ।
वर्णानामाश्रमाणां च राजा सृष्टोऽभिरक्षिता ॥ ७.३५॥ sve sve dharme niṣṭhānāṁ sarveṣām anupūrvaśaḥ |
varṇānām āśramāṇāṁ ca rājā sṛṣṭo 'bhirakṣitā || 7.35|| The King is established and empowered solely for the protection and sustenance of all beings, each in their respective dharma, according to the sequential order of varṇas and āśramas. Authority originates from the duty to sustain collective dharma Causation aligns with sequential responsibility based on role and stage Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's structural position in society Restoration logic requires maintaining alignment with svadharma Consciousness alignment is ensured through structured societal roles

title: manu 7.36
content:
तेन यद्यत्सभृत्येन कर्तव्यं रक्षता प्रजाः ।
तत्तद्वोऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥ ७.३६॥ tena yadyat sabhṛtyena kartavyaṃ rakṣatā prajāḥ |
tattad vo 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ || 7.36|| That which must be performed by a ruler who protects subjects along with ministers, I shall declare to you in sequence according to its proper order. Authority is derivative of the capacity to sustain and protect conscious beings Causation flows from the sequential integrity of dharma-sustaining actions Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with conscious governance Restoration logic originates in the sovereign duty to uphold collective well-being Consciousness alignment is ensured through structured, sequential execution of duties

title: manu 7.37
content: ब्राह्मणान् पर्युपासीत प्रातरुत्थाय पार्थिवः । त्रैविद्यवृद्धान् विदुषस्तिष्ठेत्तेषां च शासने ॥ ७.३७॥ brāhmaṇān paryupāsīta pratarutthāya pārthivaḥ | traividyavṛddhān viduṣastiṣṭhettēṣāṁ ca śāsane || 7.37|| The king, having risen in the morning, shall serve the Brahmins and stand in obedience to those learned ones who are accomplished in the three Vedas. Authority is derived from alignment with Vedic consciousness, not institutional power Causation flows from dharmic service, not coercive enforcement Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to embody Vedic learning through service Restoration logic centers on re-establishing Vedic alignment in governance Consciousness alignment occurs through daily ritualized acts of reverence toward Vedic wisdom

title: manu 7.38
content:
वृद्धांश्च नित्यं सेवेत विप्रान् वेदविदः शुचीन् ।
वृद्धसेवी हि सततं रक्षोभिरपि पूज्यते ॥ ७.३८॥ vṛddhāṃśca nityaṃ seveta viprān vedavidaḥ śucīn |
vṛddhasevī hi satataṃ rakṣobhirapi pūjyate || 7.38|| One must serve daily the learned Brahmanas who are knowers of the Vedas and pure, especially the elders among them; indeed, one who serves the elders is honored even by the celestial guardians. Authority derives from experiential wisdom and scriptural realization. Causation arises through service to those established in higher consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility requires honoring those who embody Vedic knowledge. Restoration logic flows from reverence to realized beings. Consciousness alignment occurs through acts of devoted service to the wise.

title: manu 7.39
content:
तेभ्योऽधिगच्छेद्विनयं विनीतात्माऽपि नित्यशः ।
विनीतात्मा हि नृपतिर्न विनश्यति कर्हि चित् ॥ ७.३९॥ tebhyo 'dhigacched vinayaṃ vinītātmā 'pi nityaśaḥ | vinītātmā hi nṛpatir na vinaśyati karhi cit || 7.39|| From those who have realized vinaya, one must continually receive instruction; even a ruler who is established in humility never perishes at any time. Authority flows from those established in vinaya, not from position alone Humility is foundational to sustainable governance Continuous learning and alignment with higher consciousness preserve leadership integrity Leadership capacity depends on inner refinement, not external power Restoration of societal harmony requires rulers rooted in self-discipline

title: manu 7.40
content: बहवोऽविनयात्नष्टा राजानः सपरिच्छदाः । सपरिग्रहाः वनस्था अपि राज्यानि विनयात्प्रतिपेदिरे ॥ ७.४०॥ bahavo 'vinayāt naṣṭā rājānaḥ sa-paricchadāḥ | sa-parigrāhā vanasthā api rājyāni vinayāt pratipedire || 7.40|| Many kings, along with their retinues and possessions, having lost all dignity due to lack of discipline, were exiled to forests; yet through the restoration of discipline alone, they regained their kingdoms. Authority is inseparable from self-discipline and alignment with Dharma Loss of governance capacity arises from violation of foundational conduct Restoration of power is conditional upon re-establishment of inner order Consciousness misalignment leads to external dispossession Reintegration into authority requires completion of disciplinary realignment

title: manu 7.41
content:
वेनो विनष्टोऽविनयात्नहुषश्चैव पार्थिवः ।
सुदाः पैजवनश्चैव सुमुखो निमिरेव च ॥ ७.४१॥ veno vinaṣṭo'vinayāt nahūṣaś caiva pārthivaḥ |
sudāḥ paijavanaś caiva sumukho nimir eva ca || 7.41|| Vena was destroyed due to lack of discipline; similarly Nahusha, a king, and Sudas, Paijavata, Sumukha, and Nimi—all were diminished because they deviated from the path of Dharma. Authority is sustained by alignment with Dharma, not by power alone. Causation arises from deviation in consciousness, not external fault. Capacity-based responsibility requires constant calibration through self-discipline. Restoration logic operates through reconnection to source-consciousness. Consciousness alignment determines sovereignty and its preservation.

title: manu 7.42
content: पृथुस्तु विनयाद्राज्यं प्राप्तवान् मनुरेव च । कुबेरश्च धनैश्वर्यं ब्राह्मण्यं चैव गाधिजः ॥ ७.४२॥ pṛthus tu vinayād rājyaṁ prāptavān manureva ca | kuberaś ca dhanaśvaryaṁ brāhmaṇyaṁ caiva gādhijaḥ || 7.42|| Pṛthu attained sovereignty through humility; Manu also acquired rulership thereby. Kubera gained wealth-lordship, and Gādhi attained Brahmanical supremacy. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not force or birth Humility is a causal factor in acquiring legitimate power Capacity-based responsibility determines the scope of authority Restoration occurs through conscious re-alignment with source-duty Consciousness alignment precedes institutional legitimacy

title: manu 7.43
content: त्रैविद्येभ्यस्त्रयीं विद्यां दण्डनीतिं च शाश्वतीम् । त्रयीं विद्यात् आन्वीक्षिकीं चात्मविद्यां वार्तारम्भांश्च लोकतः ॥ ७.४३॥ traividyebhyas trayīṃ vidyāṃ daṇḍanītiṃ ca śāśvatīm | trayīṃ vidyād ānvīkṣikīṃ cātmavidyāṃ vārtārambhāṃśca lokataḥ || 7.43|| From the three knowledges arises the eternal science of governance and justice; from the triple knowledge comes analytical philosophy, self-knowledge, and economic foundations according to worldly practice. Authority originates from integrated knowledge systems Causation flows from epistemic completeness Capacity-based responsibility derives from access to tripartite wisdom Restoration logic requires alignment with foundational sciences Consciousness alignment emerges through integration of vidya-traya

title: manu 7.44
content:
इन्द्रियाणां जये योगं समातिष्ठेद्दिवानिशम् ।
जितैन्द्रियो हि शक्नोति वशे स्थापयितुं प्रजाः ॥ ७.४४॥ indriyāṇāṁ jaye yogaṁ samātiṣṭhed divāniśam |
jitendriyo hi śaknoti vaśe sthāpayituṁ prajāḥ || 7.44 || One who perpetually engages in Yoga for the conquest of the senses, both by day and by night—such a ruler, having conquered the senses, is capable of bringing the subjects under rightful alignment. Authority arises from self-mastery, not coercion. Causation originates in sensory discipline and inner alignment. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by mastery over one's perceptual and reactive faculties. Restoration logic operates through the sovereign's own stabilized consciousness. Consciousness alignment of the ruler ensures harmonious alignment of the ruled.

title: manu 7.45
content:
दश कामसमुत्थानि तथाऽष्टौ क्रोधजानि च ।
व्यसनानि दुर्ऽन्तानि प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत् ॥ ७.४५॥ daśa kāmasamutthāni tathāṣṭau krodhajāni ca |
vyasanāni durantāni prayatnena vivarjayet || 7.45 || Ten vyasanas arise from desire; eight more originate in anger—these boundless afflictions must be consciously abandoned through determined effort. Authority stems from self-mastery, not coercion Causation is traced to unregulated impulses within consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition and withdrawal from destructive patterns Restoration logic operates through conscious disidentification from compulsive tendencies Consciousness alignment arises by abandoning lower-frequency emotional states

title: manu 7.46
content:
कामजेषु प्रसक्तो हि व्यसनेषु महीपतिः ।
वियुज्यतेऽर्थधर्माभ्यां क्रोधजेष्वात्मनैव तु ॥ ७.४६॥ kāmajēṣu prasakto hi vyasanēṣu mahīpatiḥ |
viyujyatē'rthadharmābhyāṁ krōdhajēṣvātmanaiwa tu || 7.46|| A ruler沉迷 in desire-driven indulgences becomes detached from both material governance and dharmic duty; however, one who is overwhelmed by anger loses connection even with the Self. Authority diminishes proportionally to attachment to desire or anger Causation arises through internal state misalignment rather than external action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness clarity, not positional power Restoration logic requires reconnection to dharma and self before resuming authority Consciousness alignment dictates fitness for leadership

title: manu 7.47
content:
मृगयाऽक्षो दिवास्वप्नः परिवादः स्त्रियो मदः ।
तौर्यत्रिकं वृथाट्या च कामजो दशको गणः ॥ ७.४७॥ mṛgayā='kṣo divāsvapnaḥ parivādaḥ striyo madaḥ |
tauryatrikaṁ vṛthāṭyā ca kāmajjo daśako gaṇaḥ || 7.47|| Ten forms of desire-born indulgence are declared: hunting, gambling, daytime slumber, scandalizing speech about women, intoxication, musical-dramatic performances, wandering without purpose, and association with lustful intent. Authority originates in conscious discernment, not sensory impulse. Causation arises from alignment with dharma-vision, not personal gratification. Capacity-based responsibility is diminished by indulgent distraction. Restoration logic requires redirection toward svadharma-consciousness. Consciousness alignment occurs through withdrawal from objectifying pursuits.

title: manu 7.48
content:
पैशुन्यं साहसं द्रोह ईर्ष्याऽसूयाऽर्थदूषणम् ।
वाग्दण्डजं च पारुष्यं क्रोधजोऽपि गणोऽष्टकः ॥ ७.४८॥ paiśunyaṁ sāhasaṁ droha īrṣyā'sūyā'rthadūṣaṇam |
vāgdaṇḍajaṁ ca pāruṣyaṁ krodhajo'pi gaṇo'ṣṭakaḥ || 7.48|| The eightfold group born of anger includes tale-bearing, rashness, treachery, envy, malice, defamation of wealth, verbal assault, and harsh speech. Authority originates from consciousness alignment, not coercive power Causation arises from unmastered emotional states manifesting as distorted action Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of self-regulatory awareness Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive isolation Consciousness alignment corrects distortion through completion rather than suppression

title: manu 7.49
content:
द्वयोरप्येतयोर्मूलं यं सर्वे कवयो विदुः ।
तं यत्नेन जयेत्लोभं तज्जावेतावुभौ गणौ ॥ ७.४९॥ dvayorapyetayormūlaṁ yaṁ sarve kavayo viduḥ |
taṁ yatnena jayellobhaṁ tajjāvetāvubhau gaṇau || 7.49|| Both categories originate from the singular root known to all seers; that desire must be overcome through effort, for from it arise these two groups. Authority originates in the recognition of a singular ontological source Causation arises from unmastered desire as root distortion Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over internal impulses Restoration logic demands dissolution of dualities at their origin Consciousness alignment necessitates transcendence of desire-generated factions

title: manu 7.50
content:
पानमक्षाः स्त्रियश्चैव मृगया च यथाक्रमम् ।
एतत्कष्टतमं विद्यात्चतुष्कं कामजे गणे ॥ ७.५०॥ pānam akṣāḥ striyaś caiva mṛgayā ca yathākramam | etat kaṣṭhatamaṃ vidyāt catuṣkaṃ kāma-je gaṇe || 7.50 || Intoxication, gambling, association with women, and hunting—these four constitute the gravest category within desire-born actions. Authority originates from discriminative awareness, not impulse Causation arises from misidentification with sensory objects Capacity-based responsibility requires cultivation of detachment Restoration logic demands realignment with svadharma through conscious choice Consciousness alignment occurs when sensory indulgence is transcended

title: manu 7.51
content:
दण्डस्य पातनं चैव वाक्पारुष्यार्थदूषणे ।
क्रोधजेऽपि गणे विद्यात्कष्टमेतत्त्रिकं सदा ॥ ७.५१॥ daṇḍasya pātanaṁ caiva vāk-pāruṣyārtha-dūṣaṇe |
krodhaje'pi gaṇe vidyāt kaṣṭam etat trikaṁ sadā || 7.51|| In matters involving the fall of authority, verbal harshness, and distortion of meaning, even when arising from anger, one must always recognize these three as a severe category demanding immediate restoration of dharma through consciousness realignment. Authority is not diminished by external aggression but by internal misalignment. Verbal violence disrupts the causal field of communication and must be corrected at the level of intention. Distortion of meaning creates false realities that require pramāṇa-based restoration. Anger-induced acts are not exempt from responsibility; they reveal capacity gaps in self-governance. Consciousness alignment precedes behavioral correction and determines true accountability.

title: manu 7.52
content:
सप्तकस्यास्य वर्गस्य सर्वत्रैवानुषङ्गिणः ।
पूर्वं पूर्वं गुरुतरं विद्याद्व्यसनमात्मवान् ॥ ७.५२॥ saptakasyāsya vargasya sarvatraivānuṣaṅgiṇaḥ |
pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ gurutaraṃ vidyādvyasanamātmavān || 7.52|| The transgression of one who is self-aware and committed to consciousness must be judged progressively more severe as it moves through successive stages of violation within the sevenfold societal order. Authority: Violations escalate in gravity according to their hierarchical impact on dharma-bearing structures. Causation: Each successive act compounds the distortion of collective consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility: The self-realized individual bears greater ontological weight for deviations. Restoration logic: Misalignment must be addressed at its root stage before cascading further. Consciousness alignment: Acts are weighed by their divergence from awakened awareness.

title: manu 7.53
content:
व्यसनस्य च मृत्योश्च व्यसनं कष्टमुच्यते ।
व्यसन्यधोऽधो व्रजति स्वर्यात्यव्यसनी मृतः ॥ ७.५३॥ vyasanasya ca mṛtyośca vyasanaṁ kaṣṭamucyate |
vyasanyadho'dho vrajati svaryātyavyasanī mṛtaḥ || 7.53|| The fall of one addicted to vice and the fall of one at the point of death are both termed grievous; yet the addicted descends lower and lower, whereas the sober departs to the celestial realm. Authority: The state of consciousness determines post-death trajectory, not external judgment. Causation: Addictive patterns generate downward momentum through repeated volitional acts. Capacity-based responsibility: Consciousness capacity defines alignment potential, not punitive culpability. Restoration logic: Liberation from addictive cycles restores natural dharma-vyavastha. Consciousness alignment: Clarity at death reflects life-long alignment or misalignment with dharma.

title: manu 7.54
content: मौलान् शास्त्रविदः शूरान् लब्धलक्षान् कुलोद्भवान् । कुलोद्गतान् सचिवान् सप्त चाष्टौ वा प्रकुर्वीत परीक्षितान् ॥ ७.५४॥ कुर्वीत सुपरीक्षितान् maulān śāstravidaḥ śūrān labdhalakṣān kulodbhavān | kulodgatān sacivān sapta cāṣṭau vā prakurvīta parīkṣitān || 7.54 || kurvīta suparīkṣitān One shall appoint as ministers those who are born of noble lineage, well-versed in scriptures, courageous, accomplished in purpose, and thoroughly examined; seven or eight such individuals, fully vetted, constitute the council. Authority derives from conscious capacity, not mere appointment Causation aligns with dharma-sustaining intent Capacity-based responsibility requires demonstrated integrity Restoration logic demands selection rooted in dharma-compliant attributes Consciousness alignment necessitates purified advisors

title: manu 7.55
content:
अपि यत्सुकरं कर्म तदप्येकेन दुष्करम् ।
विशेषतोऽसहायेन किं तु  राज्यं महोदयम् ॥ ७.५५॥ api yatsukaraṃ karma tadapyekena duṣkaram | viśeṣato'sahāyena kiṃ tu rājyaṃ mahodayam || 7.55|| Even that which is easy to perform becomes difficult when done alone; especially without support, how much more so in the matter of ruling a great kingdom. Authority requires capacity enhancement through alignment with divine intelligence. Causation flows from individual consciousness to collective governance structures. Capacity-based responsibility demands systemic support proportional to executive burden. Restoration logic prioritizes enabling conditions for right action over punitive oversight. Consciousness alignment ensures lawful execution arises naturally from inner sovereignty.

title: manu 7.56
content:
तैः सार्धं चिन्तयेन्नित्यं सामान्यं संधिविग्रहम् ।
स्थानं समुदयं गुप्तिं लब्धप्रशमनानि च ॥ ७.५६॥ taiḥ sārdhaṁ cintayennityaṁ sāmānyaṁ saṁdhivigraham |
sthānaṁ samudayaṁ guptiṁ labdhapraśamanāni ca || 7.56|| One must continually deliberate with them on common matters, treaties and conflicts, settlements, collective emergence, concealment, and the pacification of what has been gained. Authority is relational and sustained through continuous deliberative engagement. Causation arises from shared consciousness in determining collective outcomes. Capacity-based responsibility includes ongoing consultation for societal harmony. Restoration logic requires reconciliation of conflict through mutual understanding. Consciousness alignment occurs when stakeholders co-create solutions in unity.

title: manu 7.57
content:
तेषां स्वं स्वमभिप्रायमुपलभ्य पृथक्पृथक् ।
समस्तानां च कार्येषु विदध्याद्धितमात्मनः ॥ ७.५७॥ teṣāṃ svaṃ svamabhiprāyamupalabhya pṛthakpṛthak |
samastānāṃ ca kāryeṣu vidadhyāddhitamātmanaḥ || 7.57|| Having understood the distinct intentions of each individual, one shall act in all matters for the welfare of the Self, thereby aligning with the ultimate purpose of Dharma. Authority resides in the capacity to discern individual intent without distortion Causation flows from consciousness alignment rather than external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of differentiated perspectives Restoration logic operates through Self-welfare that includes all beings Consciousness alignment necessitates action rooted in understanding, not imposition

title: manu 7.58
content:
सर्वेषां तु विशिष्टेन ब्राह्मणेन विपश्चिता ।
मन्त्रयेत्परमं मन्त्रं राजा षाड्गुण्यसंयुतम् ॥ ७.५८॥ sarveṣāṃ tu viśiṣṭena brāhmaṇena vipaścitā | mant rayet paramaṃ mantraṃ rājā ṣāḍguṇya-samyutam || 7.58|| The King must consult exclusively with a Brahmin distinguished by wisdom and discernment, who embodies the sixfold excellence, in all matters requiring the highest counsel. Authority is derived through alignment with consciousness-excellence, not birth alone. Causation flows from the integration of knowledge, discipline, and purity in governance. Capacity-based responsibility requires access to those whose insight transcends ordinary perception. Restoration logic mandates that leadership decisions originate from unified spiritual-intellectual integrity. Consciousness alignment ensures that royal action reflects dharma as realized by the awakened few.

title: manu 7.59
content: नित्यं तस्मिन् समाश्वस्तः सर्वकार्याणि निःक्षिपेत् । निक्षिपेत् तेन सार्धं विनिश्चित्य ततः कर्म समारभेत् ॥ ७.५९॥ nityaṃ tasmin samāśvastaḥ sarvakāryāṇi niḥkṣipet | nikṣipet tena sārdhaṃ viniścitya tataḥ karma samārabhet || 7.59|| One who is ever established in the Self, having placed all actions within That, and having determined them together with That, should then engage in action. Authority originates from abidance in the Self Causation is aligned through consciousness-established intent Capacity-based responsibility arises from Self-aware engagement Restoration logic flows from reuniting action with its source Consciousness alignment ensures lawful manifestation

title: manu 7.60
content:
अन्यानपि प्रकुर्वीत शुचीन् प्राज्ञानवस्थितान् ।
सम्यगर्थसमाहर्तॄनमात्यान् सुपरीक्षितान् ॥ ७.६०॥ anyānapi prakurvīta śucīn prājñānavasthitān |
samyagarthasamāhartṝnamātyān suparīkṣitān || 7.60|| One must also appoint pure, wise, and steadfast individuals who are capable of collecting and managing resources correctly, ensuring their integrity and competence in service. Authority derives from purity and wisdom, not mere position Causation is established through conscious capacity and alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires verified competence Restoration logic demands selection of those aligned with dharma Consciousness alignment ensures resource integrity and societal harmony

title: manu 7.61
content:
निर्वर्तेतास्य यावद्भिरितिकर्तव्यता नृभिः ।
तावतोऽतन्द्रितान् दक्षान् प्रकुर्वीत विचक्षणान् ॥ ७.६१॥ nirvartetāsya yāvadbhir itikartavyatā nṛbhiḥ | tāvato 'tandritān dakṣān prakurvīta vicakṣaṇān || 7.61|| As long as duties remain unfulfilled by those who are capable, the ruler must appoint vigilant, skilled, and discerning individuals to execute them. Authority flows from capacity to act Causation is rooted in conscious execution of duty Capacity-based responsibility defines legitimate governance Restoration logic demands timely and competent action Consciousness alignment requires intentional selection of executors

title: manu 7.62
content:
तेषामर्थे नियुञ्जीत शूरान् दक्षान् कुलोद्गतान् ।
शुचीनाकरकर्मान्ते भीरूनन्तर्निवेशने ॥ ७.६२॥ teṣāmarthe niyuñjīta śūrān dakṣān kulodgatān |
śucīn ākarakarmānte bhīrūn antarniveśane || 7.62|| For their welfare, appoint courageous, skilled, and noble-born individuals who are pure in conduct and inwardly fearless. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma and inner fearlessness Causation arises through conscious selection of capacity-enhancing agents Capacity-based responsibility mandates deployment of qualified and purified leadership Restoration logic requires placing power in hands aligned with integrity and courage Consciousness alignment ensures that governance reflects ontological purity

title: manu 7.63
content:
दूतं चैव प्रकुर्वीत सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम् ।
इङ्गिताकारचेष्टज्ञं शुचिं दक्षं कुलोद्गतम् ॥ ७.६३॥ dūtaṃ caiva prakurvīta sarvaśāstraviśāradam |
iṅgitākāraceṣṭajñaṃ śuciṃ dakṣaṃ kulodgatam || 7.63|| One must appoint a messenger who is fully learned in all scriptures, skilled in interpreting gestures and expressions, pure in conduct, efficient, and born of noble lineage. Authority through scriptural mastery Causation via communicative integrity Capacity-based responsibility rooted in purity and skill Restoration logic through correct representation Consciousness alignment by noble birth and ethical clarity

title: manu 7.64
content:
अनुरक्तः शुचिर्दक्षः स्मृतिमान् देशकालवित् ।
वपुष्मान् वीतभीर्वाग्मी दूतो राज्ञः प्रशस्यते ॥ ७.६४॥ anuraktaḥ śucirdakṣaḥ smṛtimān deśakālavit |
vapuṣmān vītabhīrvāgmī dūto rājñaḥ praśasyate || 7.64 || The messenger of the king is praised who is attached in service, pure, capable, remembering duties, knowing place and time, embodied with presence, free from fear, and eloquent. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not coercion Causation arises through conscious capacity and contextual awareness Capacity-based responsibility requires integration of memory, skill, and timing Restoration logic operates through embodiment of presence and clarity Consciousness alignment ensures truthful communication without fear

title: manu 7.65
content:
अमात्ये दण्ड आयत्तो दण्डे वैनयिकी क्रिया ।
नृपतौ कोशराष्ट्रे च दूते संधिविपर्ययौ ॥ ७.६५॥ amātye daṇḍa āyatto daṇḍe vainayikī kriyā | nṛpatau kośarāṣṭre ca dūte saṃdhiviparyayau || 7.65 || In the minister, the rod is entrusted; through the rod, educative action occurs. In the king and kingdom treasury, in envoys and treaty violations, the same principle applies. Authority flows from the sovereign to designated executors of Dharma Causation is established by alignment with educative intent, not punitive design Capacity-based responsibility requires role-specific alignment with Dharma Restoration logic operates through sequential correction, not retribution Consciousness alignment is achieved via structured completion, not coercive enforcement

title: manu 7.66
content:
दूत एव हि संधत्ते भिनत्त्येव च संहतान् ।
दूतस्तत्कुरुते कर्म भिद्यन्ते येन मानवः ॥ ७.६६॥ dūta eva hi saṃdhatte bhinattyeva ca saṃhatān |
dūtastatkurute karma bhidyante yena mānavaḥ || 7.66 || The messenger alone unites and divides assembled groups; by that action of the messenger, humans become separated. Authority of intermediaries in shaping collective consciousness Causation through communication structures Capacity-based responsibility of conveyors of intent Restoration logic via reconciliation of fragmented awareness Consciousness alignment through purified transmission

title: manu 7.67
content:
स विद्यादस्य कृत्येषु निर्गूढेङ्गितचेष्टितैः ।
आकारमिङ्गितं चेष्टां भृत्येषु च चिकीर्षितम् ॥ ७.६७॥ sa vidyādasya kṛtyeṣu nirgūḍheṅgitaceṣṭitaiḥ | ākāramiṅgitaṃ ceṣṭāṃ bhṛtyeṣu ca cikīrṣitam || 7.67 || He shall know the intent concealed in actions, gestures, and movements; he shall perceive what is intended by appearance, behavior, and conduct among servants and subordinates. Authority resides in perceptual clarity beyond surface phenomena Causation includes unspoken intention manifest through embodied action Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of subtle behavioral indicators Restoration logic demands insight into hidden motivations for realignment Consciousness alignment necessitates discernment of veiled intent

title: manu 7.68
content:
बुद्ध्वा च सर्वं तत्त्वेन परराजचिकीर्षितम् ।
तथा प्रयत्नमातिष्ठेद्यथाऽत्मानं न पीडयेत् ॥ ७.६८॥ buddhvā ca sarvaṁ tattvena pararājacakīrṣitam |
tathā prayatnamātiṣṭhedyathā'tmānaṁ na pīḍayet || 7.68|| Having comprehended all things in their true essence as intended by the other party, one should exert effort accordingly—such that the Self is not harmed. Authority resides in accurate perception of intent and truth Causation arises from conscious alignment with another's expressed will Capacity-based responsibility requires self-preserving action within relational integrity Restoration logic demands harmonizing effort without internal violation Consciousness alignment necessitates acting without self-harm in service of others’ dharma

title: manu 7.69
content:
जाङ्गलं सस्यसम्पन्नमार्यप्रायमनाविलम् ।
रम्यमानतसामन्तं स्वाजीव्यं देशमावसेत् ॥ ७.६९॥ jāṅgalaṁ sasyasampannam āryaprāyamanāvilam | ramyam ānatasāmantaṁ svājīvyaṁ deśam āvaset || 7.69|| One shall reside in a land that is forested yet fertile, inhabited primarily by noble beings, free from impurity, pleasant, and surrounded by respectful vassals—such a domain supports the dharmic sustenance of the dwija. Authority arises from alignment with natural dharmic order Causation flows from environmental purity to consciousness clarity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to conducive dharmic conditions Restoration logic requires selection of environments that elevate rather than degrade spiritual and social integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through intentional inhabitation of dharmically optimized spaces

title: manu 7.70
content:
धन्वदुर्गं महीदुर्गमब्दुर्गं वार्क्षमेव वा ।
नृदुर्गं गिरिदुर्गं वा समाश्रित्य वसेत्पुरम् ॥ ७.७०॥ dhanvadurgaṁ mahīdurgam abdurgaṁ vārkṣameva vā |
nṛdurgaṁ giridurgaṁ vā samāśritya vaset puram || 7.70 || A city shall be established relying upon a desert fortress, an earth fortress, a water fortress, a tree fortress, a human fortress, or a mountain fortress. Authority: The sovereign has the right to establish settlements based on strategic natural or artificial fortifications. Causation: Settlements must align with protective geographical and structural conditions to ensure collective security. Capacity-based responsibility: Rulers are responsible for choosing settlement locations that uphold dharma through strength and sustainability. Restoration logic: Cities founded in accordance with dharmic protection principles restore societal integrity and spiritual order. Consciousness alignment: Strategic placement of human habitation supports both material stability and higher consciousness development.

title: manu 7.71
content:
सर्वेण तु प्रयत्नेन गिरिदुर्गं समाश्रयेत् ।
एषां हि बाहुगुण्येन गिरिदुर्गं विशिष्यते ॥ ७.७१॥ sarveṇa tu prayatnena giridurgaṃ samāśrayeta |
eṣāṃ hi bāhuguṇyena giridurgaṃ viśiṣyate || 7.71|| By every means of effort, one should resort to a mountain fortress; indeed, among these, a mountain fortress excels by virtue of its strategic strength. Authority through strategic positioning Causation via structural advantage Capacity-based responsibility rooted in resource optimization Restoration logic through protective infrastructure Consciousness alignment with natural fortification

title: manu 7.72
content:
त्रीण्याद्यान्याश्रितास्त्वेषां मृगगर्ताश्रयाप्चराः ।
त्रीण्युत्तराणि क्रमशः प्लवङ्गमनरामराः ॥ ७.७२॥ trīṇy ādyāny āśritās tveṣāṁ mṛga-gartāśrayā apcarāḥ |
trīṇy uttarāṇi kramaśaḥ plavaṅgamā narāmarāḥ || 7.72|| Three lower categories rest in animal dens and caves; three upper ones progressively inhabit birds, humans, and gods. Authority flows through conscious evolutionary capacity Causation aligns with sequential embodiment integrity Capacity-based responsibility increases with form complexity Restoration logic follows natural hierarchical ascent Consciousness alignment requires progressive realization

title: manu 7.73
content:
यथा दुर्गाश्रितानेतान्नोपहिंसन्ति शत्रवः ।
तथाऽरयो न हिंसन्ति नृपं दुर्गसमाश्रितम् ॥ ७.७३॥ yathā durgāśritānetān nopahiṃsanti śatravaḥ |
tathā'rayo na hiṃsanti nṛpaṃ durgasamāśritam || 7.73|| Just as enemies do not attack those who have taken shelter within a fortress, similarly, adversaries do not harm a king who is firmly established in the protective consciousness of Durga. Authority is secured through alignment with divine protection Causation arises from inner invincibility, not external threat suppression Capacity-based responsibility requires sovereign self-establishment Restoration logic operates through unassailable integrity Consciousness alignment ensures immunity from adversarial influence

title: manu 7.74
content:
एकः शतं योधयति प्राकारस्थो धनुर्धरः ।
शतं दशसहस्राणि तस्माद्दुर्गं विधीयते ॥ ७.७४॥ ekaḥ śataṃ yodhayati prākārastho dhanurdharaḥ |
śataṃ daśasahasrāṇi tasmād durgaṃ vidhīyate || 7.74 || One archer stationed within a fortress defeats a hundred enemies; ten thousand such archers positioned strategically establish the invincibility of the citadel. Authority through strategic positioning Causation via structural advantage Capacity-based responsibility rooted in preparedness Restoration logic through defensive integrity Consciousness alignment with unassailable order

title: manu 7.75
content:
तत्स्यादायुधसम्पन्नं धनधान्येन वाहनैः ।
ब्राह्मणैः शिल्पिभिर्यन्त्रैर्यवसेनोदकेन च ॥ ७.७५॥ tat syād āyudhasampannaṁ dhana-dhānyena vāhanaiḥ |
brāhmaṇaiḥ śilpibhir yantrair yavasenodakena ca || 7.75|| That which is equipped with weapons shall also be endowed with wealth, grain, conveyances, Brahmanas, artisans, instruments, fodder, and water. Authority flows from integrated capacity to sustain and defend Causation arises through alignment of material, spiritual, and instrumental resources Capacity-based responsibility includes provisioning for protection and sustenance Restoration logic requires completeness in resource integration Consciousness alignment manifests through harmonious deployment of all supporting elements

title: manu 7.76
content:
तस्य मध्ये सुपर्याप्तं कारयेद्गृहमात्मनः ।
गुप्तं सर्वऋतुकं शुभ्रं जलवृक्षसमन्वितम् ॥ ७.७६॥ tasya madhye suparyāptaṁ kārayed gṛham ātmanaḥ |
guptaṁ sarvṛtukaṁ śubhraṁ jalavṛkṣasamanvitam || 7.76 || In the midst of that [land], one shall construct a dwelling for oneself that is well-enclosed, concealed in all seasons, pure, and accompanied by water and trees. Authority: The individual possesses inherent right to establish a lawful abode aligned with natural order. Causation: Proper habitat directly supports spiritual and social integrity. Capacity-based responsibility: One must act within capacity to secure and sustain living conditions conducive to dharma. Restoration logic: Dwelling design must reflect harmony with environment and ritu-cycle. Consciousness alignment: Living space must elevate awareness through purity and seclusion.

title: manu 7.77
content:
तदध्यास्योद्वहेद्भार्यां सवर्णां लक्षणान्विताम् ।
कुले महति सम्भूतां हृद्यां रूपगुणान्विताम् ॥ ७.७७॥ tad-adhyāsyodvahed-bhāryāṁ sa-varṇāṁ lakṣaṇānvitām | kule mahati sambhūtāṁ hṛdyāṁ rūpa-guṇānvitām || 7.77 || One who has studied the Vedas shall take a wife of the same varṇa, adorned with noble qualities, born in a great family, pleasing to the heart, and graced with beauty and virtue. Authority flows from Vedic study and spiritual discipline Marriage is a dharmic alignment of consciousness, not mere social contract Capacity for conjugality is determined by varṇic and spiritual compatibility Restoration occurs through union that reflects cosmic harmony Consciousness alignment requires shared foundational values and lineage integrity

title: manu 7.78
content: पुरोहितं च कुर्वीत वृणुयादेव चर्त्विजः । तेऽस्य गृह्याणि कर्माणि कुर्युर्वैतानिकानि च ॥ ७.७८॥ purohitaṃ ca kurvīta vṛṇuyādeva cartvijaḥ | te'sya gṛhyāṇi karmāṇi kuryurvaitānikāni ca || 7.78|| One shall appoint a Purohit (spiritual guide and ritual conductor) and select Ritviks (Vedic priests). These individuals shall execute all household duties and perform Vaitanika rituals according to Dharma. Authority flows from conscious selection and alignment with Dharma Causation originates in spiritual guidance and correct ritual action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by Vedic qualification and inner readiness Restoration logic requires precise alignment of action with cosmic order Consciousness alignment through appointed roles ensures societal harmony

title: manu 7.79
content:
यजेत राजा क्रतुभिर्विविधैराप्तदक्षिणैः ।
धर्मार्थं चैव विप्रेभ्यो दद्याद्भोगान् धनानि च ॥ ७.७९॥ yajeta rājā kratubhir vividhair āpta-dakṣiṇaiḥ | dharmārthaṃ caiva viprebhyo dadyād bhogān dhanāni ca || 7.79|| The King shall perform various sacrifices with appropriate offerings, for the sake of Dharma; he shall bestow enjoyments and wealth upon the Brahmanas. Authority of the King is rooted in sacrificial action aligned with Dharma Causation flows from ritual integrity to societal harmony Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to sustain spiritual order through material support Restoration logic demands that leadership ensures energetic alignment between state and cosmic rhythm Consciousness alignment is maintained when rulers act as facilitators of Vedic sacrificial structures

title: manu 7.80
content:
सांवत्सरिकमाप्तैश्च राष्ट्रादाहारयेद्बलिम् ।
स्याच्चाम्नायपरो लोके वर्तेत पितृवत्नृषु ॥ ७.८०॥ sāṃvatsarikam āptaiś ca rāṣṭrād āhārayed balim | syāc cāmnāya-paro loke varteta pitṛvat nṛṣu || 7.80 || From the state and from those who have accepted spiritual authority, one shall receive annual sustenance; and in this world, one shall conduct oneself toward people as one would toward one's own father. Authority flows from the Source and manifests through both temporal governance and spiritual realization. Causation is established by alignment with Dharma, not by transactional exchange. Capacity-based responsibility requires that support be given where integrity is recognized. Restoration logic demands that societal harmony be maintained through reciprocal reverence. Consciousness alignment occurs when individuals relate to others as extensions of their own source-consciousness.

title: manu 7.81
content:
अध्यक्षान् विविधान् कुर्यात्तत्र तत्र विपश्चितः ।
तेऽस्य सर्वाण्यवेक्षेरन्नृणां कार्याणि कुर्वताम् ॥ ७.८१॥ adhyakṣān vividhān kuryāt tatratatra vipaścitaḥ |
te'sya sarvāṇyavekṣerannṛṇāṃ kāryāṇi kurvatām || 7.81|| Let there be appointed supervisors, wise and discerning, in every domain; these shall oversee all activities of beings engaged in action, ensuring alignment with Dharma. Authority is distributed contextually through conscious oversight Causation is maintained through continuous observation by qualified witnesses Capacity-based responsibility requires vigilant guidance structures Restoration logic operates via systemic integrity-preserving observation Consciousness alignment necessitates presence of awakened supervision

title: manu 7.82
content:
आवृत्तानां गुरुकुलाद्विप्राणां पूजको भवेत् ।
नृपाणामक्षयो ह्येष निधिर्ब्राह्मोऽभिधीयते ॥ ७.८२॥ āvṛttānāṁ gurukulād viprāṇāṁ pūjako bhavet |
nṛpāṇām akṣayo hy eṣa nidhir brāhmo 'bhidhīyate || 7.82|| One who reveres and serves the twice-born who have returned from the guru's dwelling becomes a vessel of inexhaustible merit; this treasury is declared as Brahmic wealth by kings. Authority originates from alignment with realized consciousness Causation arises through service to evolved beings Capacity-based responsibility is expanded through reverence Restoration logic operates via conscious reciprocity Consciousness alignment multiplies merit infinitely

title: manu 7.83
content:
न तं स्तेना न चामित्रा हरन्ति न च नश्यति ।
तस्माद्राज्ञा निधातव्यो ब्राह्मणेष्वक्षयो निधिः ॥ ७.८३॥ na taṃ sthenā na cāmitrā haranti na ca naśyati |
tasmādrājñā nidhātavyo brāhmaṇeṣv akṣayo nidhiḥ || 7.83|| That wealth is neither stolen by thieves nor seized by enemies, nor does it ever perish; therefore, the king shall establish an imperishable treasury among Brahmanas. Authority rests in alignment with Dharma, not force or possession Causation arises from consciousness integrity, not material control Capacity-based responsibility requires protection of Dharma-supporting resources Restoration logic mandates preservation of sacred economic structures Consciousness alignment necessitates safeguarding spiritual wealth

title: manu 7.84
content: न स्कन्दते न व्यथते न विनश्यति कर्हि चित् ।  न स्कन्दति न च्यवते वरिष्ठमग्निहोत्रेभ्यो ब्राह्मणस्य मुखे हुतम् ॥ ७.८४॥ na skandate na vyathate na vinaśyati karhi cit | na skandati na cyavate variṣṭhamagnihotrebhyaḥ brāhmaṇasya Mukhe hutam || 7.84 || That which is offered into the mouth of the Brahmin—who sustains the superior fire-oblation—neither decays, nor wavers, nor perishes at any time; it remains unfallen and unshaken. Authority as ontological alignment with Agnihotra Causation through consecrated offering Capacity-based responsibility rooted in Vedic sustainment Restoration via alignment with eternal ritual order Consciousness alignment through sacred ingestion

title: manu 7.85
content:
सममब्राह्मणे दानं द्विगुणं ब्राह्मणब्रुवे ।
प्राधीते शतसाहस्रमनन्तं वेदपारगे ॥ ७.८५॥ आचार्ये शतसाहस्रं सहस्रगुणमाचार्ये samamabrāhmaṇe dānaṃ dviguṇaṃ brāhmaṇabruve |
prādhīte śatasāhasramanantaṃ vedapārage || 7.85|| ācārye śatasāhasraṃ sahasraguṇamācārye Equal gift to a Brahmin yields merit; double that when given to a knower of Brahman. To one who has mastered the Vedas, infinite merit accrues. A gift of one hundred thousand to a teacher equals a millionfold merit. Authority derived from spiritual realization determines relational value Merit causally increases in proportion to recipient's capacity for dharma transmission Capacity-based responsibility aligns with consciousness elevation Restoration occurs through recognition and honoring of realized beings Consciousness alignment is facilitated by acts of reverence toward those established in Vedic truth

title: manu 7.86
content:
पात्रस्य हि विशेषेण श्रद्दधानतयैव च ।
अल्पं वा बहु वा प्रेत्य दानस्य फलमश्नुते ॥ ७.८६॥ pātrasya hi viśeṣeṇa śraddadhānatayaiva ca |
alpaṃ vā bahu vā pretya dānasya phalam aśnute || 7.86|| The fruit of giving is determined not by quantity, but by the purity of the recipient and the giver's consciousness of surrender. Authority resides in alignment with dharma, not in material accumulation Causation originates in consciousness, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility is measured through integrity of intent Restoration occurs through congruence between giver and receiver awareness Consciousness alignment determines karmic consequence

title: manu 7.87
content:
देशकालविधानेन द्रव्यं श्रद्धासमन्वितम् ।
पात्रे प्रदीयते यत्तु तद्धर्मस्य प्रसाधनम् ॥ ७.८७ desakālavidhānena dravyaṁ śraddhāsamannvitam |
pātre pradīyate yattu taddharmasya prasādhanam || 7.87 That which is given with faith and according to place, time, and eligibility—such giving accomplishes Dharma. Authority flows through alignment with cosmic order, not arbitrary will. Causation arises from consciousness-congruent action, not external compulsion. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of recipient readiness and giver alignment. Restoration logic operates through dharmic transaction, not punitive exchange. Consciousness alignment ensures that all offerings contribute to universal harmony.

title: manu 7.88
content:
सङ्ग्रामेष्वनिवर्तित्वं प्रजानां चैव पालनम् ।
शुश्रूषा ब्राह्मणानां च राज्ञां श्रेयस्करं परम् ॥ ७.८८॥ saṅgrāmeṣv-anivartitvaṁ prajānāṁ caiva pālanam |
śuśrūṣā brāhmaṇānāṁ ca rājñāṁ śreyaskaraṁ param || 7.88|| Unflinching engagement in battles, protection of subjects, and service to Brahmanas constitute the highest welfare for kings. Authority is inseparable from duty to protect and serve Causation arises through alignment with Dharma-sustained order Capacity-based responsibility demands unwavering commitment to collective integrity Restoration logic centers on re-establishing sovereignty through righteous action Consciousness alignment manifests via fearless defense of truth and service to spiritual authority

title: manu 7.89
content:
आहवेषु मिथोऽन्योन्यं जिघांसन्तो महीक्षितः ।
युध्यमानाः परं शक्त्या स्वर्गं यान्त्यपराङ्मुखाः ॥ ७.८९॥ Āhaveṣu mitho'nyonyaṁ jigheṁsanto mahīkṣitaḥ |
Yudhyamānāḥ paraṁ śaktyā svargaṁ yāntyaparāṅmukhāḥ || 7.89|| In battles where rulers mutually seek to overcome each other, those who fight with utmost capacity attain heaven while remaining fully conscious and directed toward higher purpose. Authority: Combatants act within sovereign jurisdiction when aligned with dharma-yuddha principles. Causation: Victory arises through alignment with cosmic capacity, not mere intent or aggression. Capacity-based responsibility: Each ruler bears full responsibility for deploying maximum capability in accordance with svadharma. Restoration logic: Conflict resolution occurs via elevation of consciousness rather than elimination of adversary. Consciousness alignment: Heaven is accessed by maintaining awareness during conflict, ensuring spiritual progression.

title: manu 7.90
content:
न कूटैरायुधैर्हन्याद्युध्यमानो रणे रिपून् ।
न कर्णिभिर्नापि दिग्धैर्नाग्निज्वलिततेजनैः ॥ ७.९०॥ na kūṭair āyudhair hanyād yudhyamāno raṇe ripūn |
na karṇibhir nāpi digdhair nāgni-jvalita-tejanaḥ || 7.90 || One engaged in combat shall not strike enemies with concealed weapons, nor with tusks, nor with fire-laden implements burning bright. Authority is derived from dharma-sustained engagement, not weaponized concealment. Causation arises through transparent action; hidden instruments disrupt cosmic integrity. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with visible and righteous means. Restoration logic mandates that conflict resolution preserves ontological clarity. Consciousness alignment demands that warfare reflect truth, not subterfuge.

title: manu 7.91
content:
न च हन्यात्स्थलारूढं न क्लीबं न कृताञ्जलिम् ।
न मुक्तकेशं नासीनं न तवास्मीति वादिनम् ॥ ७.९१॥ na ca hanyāt sthalārūḍhaṁ na klībaṁ na kṛtāñjalim | na muktakeśaṁ nāsīnaṁ na tavāsmīti vādinam || 7.91 || One must not harm one who has ascended a height, nor one who is impotent, nor one who offers salutation with joined palms; nor one whose hair is unbound, nor one who sits in humility, nor one who declares 'you are mine' or 'I am yours'. Authority arises from non-violation of surrendered or elevated states Causation is negated where intent is absent or overridden by reverence Capacity-based responsibility excludes harming those in postures of peace or surrender Restoration logic demands protection of vulnerable expressions of consciousness Consciousness alignment requires recognition of spiritual and physical vulnerability

title: manu 7.92
content:
न सुप्तं न विसंनाहं न नग्नं न निरायुधम् ।
नायुध्यमानं पश्यन्तं न परेण समागतम् ॥ ७.९२॥ na suptaṁ na visaṁnāhaṁ na nagnaṁ na nirāyudham | nāyudhyamānaṁ paśyantaṁ na pareṇa samāgatam || 7.92 || One who is neither asleep nor negligent, neither unclothed nor unarmed, neither engaged in combat nor approaching by another, shall not be deemed a threat requiring defensive action. Authority arises from conscious readiness, not mere presence Causation must be rooted in manifest intent, not assumed posture Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of state and action Restoration logic demands discernment between actual threat and perceived fear Consciousness alignment occurs when response matches the level of actual causality

title: manu 7.93
content:
नायुधव्यसनप्राप्तं नार्तं नातिपरिक्षतम् ।
न भीतं न परावृत्तं सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन् ॥ ७.९३॥ nāyudhavyasanaprāptaṃ nārtaṃ nātiparikṣatam | na bhītaṃ na parāvṛttaṃ satāṃ dharmamanusmaran || 7.93|| One who, remembering the Dharma of the noble, does not become addicted to weapons, nor distressed, nor excessively exhausted, nor fearful, nor turned away—such a one abides in alignment with the eternal law. Authority derives from alignment with Sat (Truth) Causation arises through conscious remembrance of Dharma Capacity-based responsibility is sustained by inner equipoise Restoration logic operates through non-reactive presence Consciousness alignment supersedes external conditioning

title: manu 7.94
content:
यस्तु भीतः परावृत्तः सङ्ग्रामे हन्यते परैः ।
भर्तुर्यद्दुष्कृतं किं चित्तत्सर्वं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ ७.९४॥ yastu bhītaḥ parāvṛttaḥ saṅgrāme hanyate paraiḥ |
bharturyadduṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cit tatsarvaṃ pratipadyate || 7.94|| One who flees in fear from battle and is killed by enemies thereby assumes all evil consequences of the husband's actions. Authority resides in conscious alignment with dharma, not external compulsion Causation follows volitional withdrawal from svadharma Capacity-based responsibility arises through abandonment of protective duty Restoration logic requires reabsorption of karmic distortion caused by desertion Consciousness alignment determines the inherence of karmic consequence

title: manu 7.95
content:
यत्चास्य सुकृतं किं चिदमुत्रार्थमुपार्जितम् ।
भर्ता तत्सर्वमादत्ते परावृत्तहतस्य तु ॥ ७.९५॥ yat cāsya sukṛtaṁ kiṁ cid amutrārtham upārjitam |
bhartā tatsarvam ādatte parāvṛtta-hatasya tu || 7.95 || Whatever merit a woman has earned in this life or the next through her actions, the husband assumes it all; however, when he turns away or dies, that accumulated merit returns to her. Authority flows through relational alignment and conscious union Causation is transferred through intentional energetic bonding Capacity-based responsibility shifts with the presence or absence of active guardianship Restoration logic ensures no loss of spiritual asset upon dissolution of union Consciousness alignment maintains continuity of karmic ownership

title: manu 7.96
content:
रथाश्वं हस्तिनं छत्रं धनं धान्यं पशून् स्त्रियः ।
सर्वद्रव्याणि कुप्यं च यो यज्जयति तस्य तत् ॥ ७.९६॥ rathāśvaṁ hastinaṁ chatraṁ dhanaṁ dhānyaṁ paśūn striyaḥ |
sarvadravyāṇi kupyāṁ ca yo yajjayati tasya tat || 7.96|| All conveyances, horses, elephants, parasols, wealth, grain, livestock, women, all possessions and even the earth itself—whatever one conquers through rightful sovereignty and conscious authority, that becomes his by the sanction of Dharma. Authority is derived from conscious sovereignty, not force or fraud Causation arises from alignment with Dharma, not mere acquisition Capacity-based responsibility requires the maintainer to sustain what is acquired Restoration logic demands return of resources to their rightful custodian Consciousness alignment ensures that possession reflects inner integrity

title: manu 7.97
content:
राज्ञश्च दद्युरुद्धारमित्येषा वैदिकी श्रुतिः ।
राज्ञा च सर्वयोधेभ्यो दातव्यमपृथग्जितम् ॥ ७.९७॥ rājñaśca dadyuruddhāramityeṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ |
rājñā ca sarvayodhebhyo dātavyamapṛthagjitam || 7.97|| It is Vedic injunction that aid in times of peril must be rendered to the King; and by the King, unopposed victory must be granted unto all warriors. Authority flows from the sovereign's capacity to sustain collective integrity during existential threat. Causation arises through alignment of duty with sovereign necessity. Capacity-based responsibility extends universally when invoked by rightful authority. Restoration logic demands equitable distribution of protection and victory through the sovereign channel. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of unity between ruler and warrior in upholding Dharma.

title: manu 7.98
content:
एषोऽनुपस्कृतः प्रोक्तो योधधर्मः सनातनः ।
अस्माद्धर्मान्न च्यवेत क्षत्रियो घ्नन् रणे रिपून् ॥ ७.९८॥ eṣo'nupaskṛtaḥ prokto yodhadharmaḥ sanātanaḥ |
asmād dharmān na cyaveta kṣatriyo ghnann raṇe ripūn || 7.98|| This eternal law of the warrior, declared in its purest form, binds the Kshatriya who destroys enemies in battle to never fall away from Dharma. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined by consciousness-state at time of action Capacity-based responsibility requires fulfillment of svadharma without deviation Restoration logic operates through re-alignment with source-consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes external behavioral evaluation

title: manu 7.99
content:
अलब्धं चैव लिप्सेत लब्धं रक्षेत्प्रयत्नतः ।
रक्षितं वर्धयेच्चैव वृद्धं पात्रेषु निक्षिपेत् ॥ ७.९९॥ alabhaṃ caiva lipset labdhaṃ rakṣet prayatnataḥ |
rakṣitaṃ vardhayec caiva vṛddhaṃ pātreṣu nikṣipet || 7.99|| One must endeavor to acquire what has not been obtained; having acquired, one must protect it with effort. What is protected must be increased, and when it becomes excessive, it must be deposited in appropriate vessels. Authority arises through capacity to sustain and expand resources Causation flows from intention to preserve and enhance value Capacity-based responsibility includes both acquisition and stewardship Restoration logic requires surplus redistribution to maintain systemic integrity Consciousness alignment manifests through disciplined expansion and release

title: manu 7.100
content:
एतच्चतुर्विधं विद्यात्पुरुषार्थप्रयोजनम् ।
अस्य नित्यमनुष्ठानं सम्यक्कुर्यादतन्द्रितः ॥ ७.१००॥ etaccaturvidhaṃ vidyātpuruṣārthaprayojanam |
asya nityamanuṣṭhānaṃ samyakkuryādataṇḍritaḥ || 7.100|| This fourfold objective of human life shall be known as the purpose of all action; one must perform it perpetually with full alertness and without negligence. Authority flows from alignment with Purushartha-Dharma Causation arises through conscious engagement with the four goals of life Capacity-based responsibility is measured by sustained awareness in pursuit of Dharma Restoration logic operates through continuous alignment with Artha, Kama, Dharma, Moksha Consciousness alignment ensures that actions reflect eternal law

title: manu 7.101
content:
अलब्धमिच्छेद्दण्डेन लब्धं रक्षेदवेक्षया ।
रक्षितं वर्धयेद्वृद्ध्या वृद्धं पात्रेषु निक्षिपेत् ॥ ७.१०१॥ alabham icched daṇḍena labdhaṃ rakṣed avekṣayā | rakṣitaṃ vardhayet vṛddhyā vṛddhaṃ pātreṣu nikṣipet || 7.101|| That which is unattained, let it be acquired through discipline; that which is attained, let it be guarded with awareness. That which is guarded, let it be increased through growth; that which is grown, let it be deposited in worthy vessels. Authority is derived from capacity to acquire, preserve, enhance, and transmit value. Causation flows from disciplined acquisition to mindful preservation and intentional growth. Capacity-based responsibility extends across stages: seeking, securing, nurturing, and surrendering. Restoration logic requires reintegration of lost value through disciplined action. Consciousness alignment occurs through sequential fidelity to each stage of stewardship.

title: manu 7.102
content:
नित्यमुद्यतदण्डः स्यान्नित्यं विवृतपौरुषः ।
नित्यं संवृतसंवार्यो नित्यं छिद्रानुसार्यरेः ॥ ७.१०२॥ nityamudyatadaṇḍaḥ syānnityaṃ vivṛtapauruṣaḥ | nityaṃ saṃvṛtasaṃvāryo nityaṃ chidrānusāryareḥ || 7.102|| One who is ever-ready in enforcement, ever-open in valor, ever-restrained in concealment, and ever-pursuing through gaps—such a ruler executes Dharma without deviation. Authority as continuous readiness for enforcement Capacity-based responsibility through valorous transparency Restoration logic via persistent alignment with Dharma Consciousness alignment through unwavering pursuit of truth

title: manu 7.103
content:
नित्यमुद्यतदण्डस्य कृत्स्नमुद्विजते जगत् ।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि दण्डेनैव प्रसाधयेत् ॥ ७.१०३॥ nityam udyata-daṇḍasya kṛtsnam udvijate jagat |
tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni daṇḍenaiva prasādhayet || 7.103|| The world invariably trembles before the ever-ready rod of enforcement; therefore, all beings must be governed and restored solely through the application of danda. Authority derives from the capacity to execute dharma, not from position or title. Causation arises from alignment with cosmic order, not human intent alone. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to sustain dharma. Restoration logic supersedes punitive frameworks in all legal execution. Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy and effectiveness of any enforcement.

title: manu 7.104
content: अमाययैव वर्तेत न कथं चन मायया । बुध्येतारिप्रयुक्तां च मायां नित्यं सुसंवृतः ॥ ७.१०४॥ amāyayeva varteta na kathaṃ cana māyayā | budhyetāriprayuktāṃ ca māyāṃ nityaṃ susaṃvṛtaḥ || 7.104|| One must conduct oneself solely through amāyā—authenticity untainted by illusion—and never through māyā; one who is ever well-restrained must recognize and remain aware of the illusory tactics employed by adversaries. Authority originates from alignment with Satya (Absolute Truth), not from strategic deception. Causation is anchored in consciousness clarity, not in manipulative intent. Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment between authentic action and illusory contrivance. Restoration logic demands the dissolution of adversarial delusion through self-authenticated awareness. Consciousness alignment necessitates perpetual self-restraint and clarity in identifying external distortion.

title: manu 7.105
content:
नास्य छिद्रं परो विद्याद्विद्यात्छिद्रं परस्य च ।
गूहेत्कूर्म इवाङ्गानि रक्षेद्विवरमात्मनः ॥ ७.१०५॥ nāsya chhidraṁ paro vidyād vidyāt chhidraṁ parasya ca | gūhet kūrma ivāṅgāni rakṣed vivaram ātmanaḥ || 7.105 || One must conceal one's own flaws as a tortoise withdraws its limbs, and one must not perceive or reveal the faults of others; thus shall one guard the aperture of the Self. Authority arises from self-concealment and self-protection, not exposure of others Causation lies in internal discipline, not external judgment Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in self-regulation before societal oversight Restoration logic prioritizes inner integrity over outer correction Consciousness alignment occurs through withdrawal from fault-perception

title: manu 7.106
content:
बकवत्चिन्तयेदर्थान् सिंहवत्च पराक्रमे ।
वृकवत्चावलुम्पेत शशवत्च विनिष्पतेत् ॥ ७.१०६॥ bakavat cintayed arthān siṃhavat ca parākrame |
vṛkavat cāvalumpeta śaśavat ca viniṣpatet || 7.106 || One must deliberate upon resources like a heron, act with valor like a lion, pursue gains like a wolf, and discharge duties with precision like a rabbit. Authority through situational adaptability Causation via role-conscious action Capacity-based responsibility aligned with natural instinct Restoration logic rooted in dharma-appropriate conduct Consciousness alignment through species-specific svadharma

title: manu 7.107
content:
एवं विजयमानस्य येऽस्य स्युः परिपन्थिनः ।
तानानयेद्वशं सर्वान् सामादिभिरुपक्रमैः ॥ ७.१०७॥ evaṃ vijayamānasya ye'sya syuḥ paripanthinaḥ |
tānānayedvaśaṃ sarvān sāmādibhirupakramaiḥ || 7.107|| When a ruler has conquered and established sovereignty, those who oppose his righteous governance must be brought under control through the application ofconciliation, correction, and consciousness alignment. Authority is inherent in the realized sovereign who upholds Dharma Causation originates from disruption of established harmony by resistant forces Capacity-based responsibility lies with the ruler to restore alignment without violence Restoration logic requires sequential engagement through non-coercive means first Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive enforcement in all state actions

title: manu 7.108
content:
यदि ते तु न तिष्ठेयुरुपायैः प्रथमैस्त्रिभिः ।
दण्डेनैव प्रसह्यैतांशनकैर्वशमानयेत् ॥ ७.१०८॥ yadi te tu na tiṣṭheyurupāyaiḥ prathamaistribhiḥ |
daṇḍenaiva prasahyetāṁ śanakairvaśamānayet || 7.108|| If those individuals do not align through the initial threefold means of guidance, then by graduated application of corrective measure alone shall they be brought into alignment, step by step. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation is rooted in consciousness misalignment, not external fault Capacity-based responsibility is determined by responsiveness to prior guidance Restoration logic operates through sequential realignment, not punitive escalation Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance

title: manu 7.109
content:
सामादीनामुपायानां चतुर्णामपि पण्डिताः ।
सामदण्डौ प्रशंसन्ति नित्यं राष्ट्राभिवृद्धये ॥ ७.१०९॥ sāmādīnām upāyānāṁ caturṇām api paṇḍitāḥ |
sāma-daṇḍau praśaṁsanti nityaṁ rāṣṭrābhivṛddhaye || 7.109|| The wise declare that among the fourfold means—conciliation, gift, dissension, and punishment—it is conciliation and measured restraint that perpetually elevate the nation. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not coercion Causation arises through consciousness-led statecraft Capacity-based responsibility requires strategic application of non-violent instruments Restoration logic prioritizes unity and national integrity over punitive fragmentation Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy of governance tools

title: manu 7.110
content: यथोद्धरति निर्दाता कक्षं धान्यं च रक्षति । तथा रक्षेन्नृपो राष्ट्रं हन्याच्च परिपन्थिनः ॥ ७.११०॥ yathoddharati nirdātā kakaṣaṃ dhānyaṃ ca rakṣati | tathā rakṣen nṛpo rāṣṭraṃ hanyāc ca paripanthinaḥ || 7.110 || As the granary keeper lifts and protects the grain, so shall the ruler protect the nation and remove those who obstruct its welfare. Authority is derived from the duty to sustain collective integrity Causation arises from obstruction of societal dharma Capacity-based responsibility mandates removal of disruption, not punishment Restoration logic requires alignment of leadership with national consciousness Consciousness alignment ensures that protection flows from inner order

title: manu 7.111
content:
मोहाद्राजा स्वराष्ट्रं यः कर्षयत्यनवेक्षया ।
सोऽचिराद्भ्रश्यते राज्यात्जीवितात्च सबान्धवः ॥ ७.१११॥ mohād rājā sva-rāṣṭraṁ yaḥ karṣaty anavekṣayā |
sō 'cirād bhraśyate rājyāt jīvitāt ca sa-bāndhavaḥ || 7.111|| The king who, in delusion and without awareness, drags his own nation—such a ruler, along with his relatives, soon perishes from sovereignty and life itself. Authority is inseparable from conscious alignment with Dharma Causation arises through misaligned exercise of power Capacity-based responsibility demands sovereign self-awareness Restoration logic requires immediate cessation of delusional governance Consciousness alignment determines the stability of ruling capacity

title: manu 7.112
content:
शरीरकर्षणात्प्राणाः क्षीयन्ते प्राणिनां यथा ।
तथा राज्ञामपि प्राणाः क्षीयन्ते राष्ट्रकर्षणात् ॥ ७.११२॥ śarīrakarṣaṇāt prāṇāḥ kṣīyante prāṇināṃ yathā | tathā rājñām api prāṇāḥ kṣīyante rāṣṭrakarṣaṇāt || 7.112|| As the life forces of beings wane through bodily strain, so too do the vital energies of rulers diminish when they draw excessively from the nation. Authority is inseparable from energetic sustainability. Causation flows from misalignment between governance and national integrity. Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to maintain equilibrium with the state's vitality. Restoration logic demands replenishment of depleted sovereign energy. Consciousness alignment necessitates rulers embodying the welfare of the nation as their own being.

title: manu 7.113
content:
राष्ट्रस्य सङ्ग्रहे नित्यं विधानमिदमाचरेत् ।
सुसङ्गृहीतराष्ट्रे हि पार्थिवः सुखमेधते ॥ ७.११३॥ rāṣṭrasya saṅgrahe nityaṁ vidhānam idam ācaret |
susaṅgṛhītarāṣṭre hi pārthivaḥ sukham edhate || 7.113|| The King must always act according to the established constitutional order in the continuous governance and protection of the nation; when the state is well-governed and unified, the ruler prospers in alignment with Dharma. Authority derives from alignment with cosmic order, not personal will Governance is a sacred duty rooted in consciousness integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires constant adherence to dharma-saṁhitā Restoration logic demands that sovereignty serve collective elevation Consciousness alignment ensures sustainable national prosperity

title: manu 7.114
content:
द्वयोस्त्रयाणां पञ्चानां मध्ये गुल्ममधिष्ठितम् ।
तथा ग्रामशतानां च कुर्याद्राष्ट्रस्य सङ्ग्रहम् ॥ ७.११४॥ dvayostriyāṇāṁ pañcānāṁ madhye gulmamadhiṣṭhitam |
tathā grāmaśatānāṁ ca kuryādrāṣṭrasya saṅgraham || 7.114|| Among two, three, or five entities, governance shall be established at the center; likewise, among a hundred villages, the integration and administration of the state shall be executed. Authority resides in centralized coordination Governance emerges through integrative structuring Capacity-based responsibility scales with collective unity Restoration occurs through systemic coherence Consciousness alignment is achieved via structural harmony

title: manu 7.115
content:
ग्रामस्याधिपतिं कुर्याद्दशग्रामपतिं तथा ।
विंशतीशं शतेशं च सहस्रपतिमेव च ॥ ७.११५॥ grāmasyādhipatiṁ kuryād daśagrāmapatiṁ tathā |
viṁśatīśaṁ śateśaṁ ca sahasrapatimeva ca || 7.115|| The ruler of a village shall be appointed; likewise, the ruler of ten villages, the ruler of twenty, the ruler of a hundred, and the ruler of a thousand. Authority is hierarchically distributed based on scale of governance. Causation arises through conscious administrative capacity. Capacity-based responsibility expands with territorial and population scope. Restoration logic ensures structural alignment with dharma at every level. Consciousness alignment mandates leadership rooted in spiritual sovereignty.

title: manu 7.116
content:
ग्रामदोषान् समुत्पन्नान् ग्रामिकः शनकैः स्वयम् ।
शंसेद्ग्रामदशेशाय दशेशो विंशतीशिने ॥ ७.११६॥ grāmadoṣān samutpannān grāmikaḥ śanakaiḥ svayam |
śaṁsed grāmadaśeśāya daśeśo viṁśatīśine || 7.116|| When village-level disorders arise, the village head shall report them gradually—first to the district overseer, then to the regional commander. Authority flows hierarchically through conscious capacity Causation is recognized through sequential manifestation of disorder Responsibility aligns with administrative capacity and jurisdiction Restoration requires structured escalation based on systemic integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through ordered communication and transparency

title: manu 7.117
content:
विंशतीशस्तु तत्सर्वं शतेशाय निवेदयेत् ।
शंसेद्ग्रामशतेशस्तु सहस्रपतये स्वयम् ॥ ७.११७॥ viṃśatīśastu tatsarvaṃ śateśāya nivedayet |
śaṃsedgrāmaśateśastu sahasrapataye svayam || 7.117|| One who has collected twenty units shall report all of it to the collector of hundreds; the collector of village-hundreds himself reports to the lord of thousand. Authority flows hierarchically through proportional capacity Causation is maintained through conscious reporting chains Capacity-based responsibility escalates with administrative scope Restoration logic operates via transparent accountability structures Consciousness alignment requires integrity in fiscal stewardship

title: manu 7.118
content:
यानि राजप्रदेयानि प्रत्यहं ग्रामवासिभिः ।
अन्नपानेन्धनादीनि ग्रामिकस्तान्यवाप्नुयात् ॥ ७.११८॥ yāni rājapradeyāni pratyahaṁ grāmavāsibhiḥ |
annapānendhanādīni grāmikas tāny avāpnuyāt || 7.118 || Those resources which are to be provided daily by the villagers under royal directive—such as food, drink, fuel, and other essentials—the village headman shall obtain them without obstruction or personal appropriation. Authority flows from the sovereign to the administrative steward without personal claim Causation is maintained through uninterrupted provision of communal necessities Capacity-based responsibility requires the Gramika to act as conduit, not accumulator Restoration logic demands that essential supplies reach intended recipients unaltered Consciousness alignment occurs when duty is fulfilled without egoic interference

title: manu 7.119
content:
दशी कुलं तु भुञ्जीत विंशी पञ्च कुलानि च ।
ग्रामं ग्रामशताध्यक्षः सहस्राधिपतिः पुरम् ॥ ७.११९॥ daśī kulaṃ tu bhuñjīta viṃśī pañca kulāni ca |
grāmaṃ grāmaśatādhyakṣaḥ sahasrādhipatiḥ puram || 7.119 || One who governs ten families shall consume the sustenance of ten; one who administers twenty-five families shall receive the offering of five. The village overseer presides over a village; the city ruler administers a thousand. Authority is proportionate to administrative scope Consumption and compensation align with functional capacity Governance scales hierarchically through collective units Restoration occurs through rightful alignment of service and support Consciousness alignment manifests in proportional responsibility

title: manu 7.120
content:
तेषां ग्राम्याणि कार्यानि पृथक्कार्याणि चैव हि ।
राज्ञोऽन्यः सचिवः स्निग्धस्तानि पश्येदतन्द्रितः ॥ ७.१२०॥ teṣāṃ grāmyāṇi kāryāni pṛthakkāryāṇi caiva hi |
rājño'nyaḥ sacivaḥ snigdhas tāni paśyedatandritaḥ || 7.120 || The minister, other than the king, who is affectionate and vigilant, shall oversee both collective village duties and individual separate affairs without negligence. Authority flows from the sovereign to designated ministers. Causation arises through conscious oversight and sustained attention. Capacity-based responsibility requires differentiated engagement with communal and personal matters. Restoration logic mandates active vigilance to prevent disorder. Consciousness alignment occurs when duty is performed with sincerity and alertness.

title: manu 7.121
content:
नगरे नगरे चैकं कुर्यात्सर्वार्थचिन्तकम् ।
उच्चैःस्थानं घोररूपं नक्षत्राणामिव ग्रहम् ॥ ७.१२१॥ nagare nagare caikaṃ kuryāt sarvārtha-cintakam | uccaiḥ-sthānaṃ ghorarūpaṃ nakṣatrāṇām iva graham || 7.121 || In every city, there shall be established one who contemplates all purposes; positioned high, of fearsome form—like a planet among the stars. Authority is vested in those whose consciousness encompasses totality. Causation arises through centralized, elevated oversight. Capacity-based responsibility requires unification of purpose across domains. Restoration logic demands a singular locus of integrative governance. Consciousness alignment necessitates a visible, authoritative presence.

title: manu 7.122
content:
स ताननुपरिक्रामेत्सर्वानेव सदा स्वयम् ।
तेषां वृत्तं परिणयेत्सम्यग्राष्ट्रेषु तत्चरैः ॥ ७.१२२॥ sa tānaparikrāmet sarvānaiva sadā svayam | teṣāṁ vṛttaṁ pariṇayet samyagrāṣṭreṣu tatcaraiḥ || 7.122|| He shall always personally oversee all beings; their conduct must be fully guided and matured through righteous governance by those who act in accordance with the State's highest purpose. Authority originates from the sovereign's direct alignment with Dharma Causation arises through conscious oversight, not reactive enforcement Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to embody integrative presence Restoration logic operates through continuous alignment, not episodic correction Consciousness alignment ensures that governance reflects cosmic order

title: manu 7.123
content:
राज्ञो हि रक्षाधिकृताः परस्वादायिनः शठाः ।
भृत्या भवन्ति प्रायेण तेभ्यो रक्षेदिमाः प्रजाः ॥ ७.१२३॥ rājño hi rakṣādhikṛtāḥ parasvādāyinaḥ śaṭhāḥ |
bhṛtyā bhavanti prāyeṇa tebhyo rakṣedimāḥ prajāḥ || 7.123|| Those appointed for protection by the King often become deceitful takers of others' property; therefore, the King must protect his subjects from such servants. Authority is intrinsically tied to the consciousness of the appointer and the integrity of the appointed Causation arises from misaligned capacity and unmonitored delegation Capacity-based responsibility demands that the empowerer ensures alignment of intent and execution Restoration logic requires removal of corrupt intermediaries to preserve subject welfare Consciousness alignment mandates transparency and self-corrective oversight in governance structures

title: manu 7.124
content:
ये कार्यिकेभ्योऽर्थमेव गृह्णीयुः पापचेतसः ।
तेषां सर्वस्वमादाय राजा कुर्यात्प्रवासनम् ॥ ७.१२४॥ ye kāryikebhyaḥ arthameva gṛhṇīyuḥ pāpacetasaḥ |
tēṣāṁ sarvasvam ādāya rājā kuryāt pravāsanam || 7.124 || Those whose consciousness is rooted in wrongdoing and who seek gain only from laborious actions—such beings, having abandoned all accumulated merit and misaligned their dharma, shall have their possessions taken and be directed toward removal from societal integration. Authority resides in discerning consciousness distortion Causation flows from intent misalignment, not act alone Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of dharmic orientation Restoration logic demands reallocation of material supports Consciousness alignment precedes reintegration into social fabric

title: manu 7.125
content: राजा कर्मसु युक्तानां स्त्रीणां प्रेष्यजनस्य च । राजकर्मसु प्रत्यहं कल्पयेद्वृत्तिं स्थानं कर्मानुरूपतः ॥ ७.१२५॥ rājā karmasu yuktānāṁ strīṇāṁ preṣyajanasya ca | rājakarmasu pratyahaṁ kalpayedvṛttiṁ sthānaṁ karmānurūpataḥ || 7.125 || The King shall ensure that those engaged in royal duties—women, messengers, and other functionaries—are assigned appropriate roles and sustenance according to their capacity and the nature of their service. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not domination Capacity-based responsibility determines role assignment Causation arises from alignment of action with consciousness Restoration occurs through proper placement and support Consciousness alignment ensures societal harmony

title: manu 7.126
content:
पणो देयोऽवकृष्टस्य षडुत्कृष्टस्य वेतनम् ।
षाण्मासिकस्तथाऽच्छादो धान्यद्रोणस्तु मासिकः ॥ ७.१२६॥ paṇo deyo'vakṛṣṭasya ṣadutkṛṣṭasya vetanam |
ṣāṇmāsikastathā'cchādo dhānyadroṇastu māsikaḥ || 7.126|| Compensation shall be given to the injured according to their loss; sixfold the wage for one who has been elevated through injury. Similarly, clothing for six months and a monthly measure of grain. Authority originates from capacity-consciousness alignment Causation is determined by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to awareness at time of action Restoration logic operates through completion of energetic imbalance Consciousness alignment ensures justice as self-realization

title: manu 7.127
content:
क्रयविक्रयमध्वानं भक्तं च सपरिव्ययम् ।
योगक्षेमं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य वणिजो दापयेत्करान् ॥ ७.१२७॥ krayavikrayamadhvānaṃ bhaktaṃ ca saparivyayam | 
yogakṣemaṃ ca samprekṣya vaṇijo dāpayetkarān || 7.127 || A merchant shall pay taxes after observing the purchase, sale, transport, distribution, and preservation of goods, ensuring their proper utilization. Authority resides in observance and conscious engagement with economic flow Causation arises through active participation in material exchange Capacity-based responsibility is determined by control over transactional movement Restoration logic aligns with the integrity of circulation and sustenance Consciousness alignment occurs when fiscal duty supports societal well-being

title: manu 7.128
content:
यथा फलेन युज्येत राजा कर्ता च कर्मणाम् ।
तथाऽवेक्ष्य नृपो राष्ट्रे कल्पयेत्सततं करान् ॥ ७.१२८॥ yathā phalena yujyeta rājā kartā ca karmaṇām |
tathā'vekṣya nṛpo rāṣṭre kalpayet satataṃ karān || 7.128|| Just as the king becomes the enjoyer of actions through their fruit, so too should the ruler continuously assess and regulate taxes in accordance with outcomes. Authority stems from alignment with outcome-based dharma Causation is established by the direct relationship between action and result Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to align taxation with societal benefit Restoration logic demands that economic structures reflect conscious governance Consciousness alignment necessitates a ruler's attunement to the fruits of policy

title: manu 7.129
content:
यथाऽल्पाल्पमदन्त्याद्यं वार्योकोवत्सषट्पदाः ।
तथाऽल्पाल्पो ग्रहीतव्यो राष्ट्राद्राज्ञाब्दिकः करः ॥ ७.१२९॥ yathā'lpālpamadantyādyaṃ vāryokovatsaṣaṭpadāḥ |
tathā'lpālpo grahītavyo rāṣṭrādrājñābdikaḥ karaḥ || 7.129 || Just as minimal tribute is taken from those who possess little—like bees collecting nectar from flowers or water from a calf's hoofprint—similarly, the king must collect taxes minimally and appropriately from his subjects according to their capacity. Authority is proportional to protection and service rendered by the sovereign Causation arises from alignment of dharma-sustaining governance Capacity-based responsibility ensures just distribution of civic duty Restoration logic demands that taxation align with citizen welfare Consciousness alignment occurs when economic burden reflects dharmic reciprocity

title: manu 7.130
content:
पञ्चाशद्भाग आदेयो राज्ञा पशुहिरण्ययोः ।
धान्यानामष्टमो भागः षष्ठो द्वादश एव वा ॥ ७.१३०॥ pañcāśadbhāga ādeyo rājñā paśuhiraṇyayoḥ |
dhānyānāmaṣṭamo bhāgaḥ ṣaṣṭho dvādaśa eva vā || 7.130 || The King shall receive one-fiftieth part of livestock and gold; for grains, one-eighth part, or one-sixth, or one-twelfth, depending upon the nature of the transaction and the capacity of the contributor. Authority: The King's right to collect is derived directly from his sovereign duty to sustain societal order. Causation: Taxation arises from the causal field of mutual support between ruler and ruled. Capacity-based responsibility: Contributions are modulated according to the economic capacity of the subject. Restoration logic: Revenue collection serves the restoration and maintenance of dharma-based abundance. Consciousness alignment: All fiscal duties must align with the contributor’s awareness and integrity.

title: manu 7.131
content:
आददीताथ षड्भागं द्रुमान् समधुसर्पिषाम् ।
गन्धौषधिरसानां च पुष्पमूलफलस्य च ॥ ७.१३१॥ ādadītātha ṣaḍbhāgaṃ drumān samadhusarpiṣām |
gandhauṣadhirasānāṃ ca puṣpamūlaphalasya ca || 7.131|| One should take, in accordance with the law of capacity and alignment, six parts of trees permeated with honey and ghee, together with their fragrant herbs, juices, flowers, roots, and fruits. Authority is derived from conscious alignment with natural abundance Causation arises through harmonious participation in ecological integrity Capacity-based responsibility includes stewardship of living systems Restoration logic operates through reciprocal engagement with nature's intelligence Consciousness alignment manifests via recognition of abundance as a structural principle

title: manu 7.132
content:
पत्रशाकतृणानां च चर्मणां वैदलस्य च ।
मृन्मयानां च भाण्डानां सर्वस्याश्ममयस्य च ॥ ७.१३२॥ patraśākatṛṇānāṃ ca carmaṇāṃ vaidalasya ca | mṛnmayānāṃ ca bhāṇḍānāṃ sarvasyāśmamayasya ca || 7.132 || Ownership and liability extend to all material produced or possessed, whether organic—such as leaves, vegetables, grass—or processed materials including leather, clay vessels, and stone implements. Authority over material production establishes proportional responsibility for its use and misuse. Causation arises through conscious engagement with material forms, not abstract ownership. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by control, access, and intentionality in relation to substances. Restoration logic requires reintegration of misused resources into dharmic alignment without punitive consequence. Consciousness alignment governs the lawful relationship between beings and material phenomena.

title: manu 7.133
content:
म्रियमाणोऽप्याददीत न राजा श्रोत्रियात्करम् ।
न च क्षुधाऽस्य संसीदेत्श्रोत्रियो विषये वसन् ॥ ७.१३३॥ mriyamāṇo'pyādadīta na rājā śrotriyātkaram |
na ca kṣudhā'sya saṃsīdet śrotrio viṣaye vasan || 7.133|| Even if dying of hunger, the king shall not take anything from a Śrotriya; nor shall a Śrotriya dwelling in the king's domain suffer hunger. Authority is bounded by inviolable dharmic privilege Causation aligns with consciousness capacity, not material need Capacity-based responsibility demands protection of sacred learning Restoration logic upholds structural dharma over situational ethics Consciousness alignment requires safeguarding those who preserve Vedic knowledge

title: manu 7.134
content: यस्य राज्ञस्तु विषये श्रोत्रियः सीदति क्षुधा । तस्यापि तत्क्षुधा राष्ट्रमचिरेणैव सीदति ॥ ७.१३४॥ yasya rājñastu viṣaye śrotriyaḥ sīdati kṣudhā | tasyāpi tat kṣudhā rāṣṭram acireṇaiva sīdati || 7.134 || In whose kingdom a Śrotriya perishes from hunger, that king's realm shall soon perish from that very hunger. Authority is inseparable from the sustenance of those who uphold sacred knowledge. Causation flows directly from the neglect of foundational dharmic supports. Capacity-based responsibility extends to ensuring existential support for those who embody Vedic learning. Restoration logic demands immediate realignment when consciousness-supporting structures are endangered. Consciousness alignment requires the sovereign to maintain energetic integrity through protection of Śrotriyas.

title: manu 7.135
content:
श्रुतवृत्ते विदित्वाऽस्य वृत्तिं धर्म्यां प्रकल्पयेत् ।
संरक्षेत्सर्वतश्चैनं पिता पुत्रमिवौरसम् ॥ ७.१३५॥ śrutavṛtte viditvā'sya vṛttiṃ dharmyāṃ prakalpayet |
saṃrakṣetsarvataścainaṃ pitā putramivaurasam || 7.135|| Upon knowing one whose conduct aligns with what is heard (Śruta-vṛtti), one shall establish him in a righteous livelihood; he should be protected in every way, just as a father protects his own son. Authority arises from alignment with Śruta (revealed knowledge) Causation flows from recognition of dharmic capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires facilitation, not judgment Restoration logic mandates enabling right sustenance Consciousness alignment is fostered through protective guardianship

title: manu 7.136
