content: संरक्ष्यमाणो राज्ञा यं   कुरुते धर्ममन्वहम् । राज्ञाऽयं तेनायुर्वर्धते राज्ञो द्रविणं राष्ट्रमेव च ॥ ७.१३६॥ saṃrakṣyamāṇo rājñā yaṃ kurute dharmamanvaham | rājñā'yaṃ tenāyurvardhate rājño draviṇaṃ rāṣṭrameva ca || 7.136 || He who, under the protection of the King, performs dharma continuously, by that act increases the life-force of the King, his wealth, and his kingdom. Authority is sustained through alignment with dharma Causation flows from individual dharmic action to collective sovereignty Capacity-based responsibility arises from being under royal protection Restoration logic links personal integrity to national prosperity Consciousness alignment ensures mutual flourishing between ruler and ruled

title: manu 7.137
content:
यत्किं चिदपि वर्षस्य दापयेत्करसंज्ञितम् ।
व्यवहारेण जीवन्तं राजा राष्ट्रे पृथग्जनम् ॥ ७.१३७॥ yatkiṃ cidapi varṣasya dāpayetkarasaṃjñitam |
vyavahāreṇa jīvantaṃ rājā rāṣṭre pṛthakjanam || 7.137|| Whatever tax or levy is designated for a year, the King shall cause it to be collected from the people living within the realm through established administrative conduct. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to sustain societal order through lawful exaction. Causation arises from the alignment of individual participation with collective welfare. Capacity-based responsibility assigns fiscal duty according to means and benefit received. Restoration logic ensures that revenue collection supports dharmic governance and social harmony. Consciousness alignment occurs when subjects recognize their role in sustaining national integrity.

title: manu 7.138
content:
कारुकान् शिल्पिनश्चैव शूद्रांश्चात्मोपजीविनः ।
एकैकं कारयेत्कर्म मासि मासि महीपतिः ॥ ७.१३८॥ kārukān śilpinaścaiva śūdrāṃścātmopajīvinaḥ |
ekaikaṃ kārayetkarma māsi māsi mahīpatiḥ || 7.138|| The King shall ensure that artisans, craftsmen, and Shudras who sustain themselves through their own work are each assigned appropriate tasks month by month. Authority: The sovereign bears the duty to organize labor for societal harmony. Causation: Proper allocation of work prevents economic disruption and sustains dharma. Capacity-based responsibility: Each individual's role aligns with their skill and svadharma. Restoration logic: Systematic organization of labor restores balance within society. Consciousness alignment: Work assigned in accordance with natural capacity elevates collective awareness.

title: manu 7.139
content:
नोच्छिन्द्यादात्मनो मूलं परेषां चातितृष्णया ।
उच्छिन्दन् ह्यात्मनो मूलमात्मानं तांश्च पीडयेत् ॥ ७.१३९॥ na ucchindya ātmanaḥ mūlaṁ pareṣāṁ cāti tṛṣṇayā |
ucchindan hy ātmanaḥ mūlam ātmānaṁ tāṁś ca pīḍayet || 7.139|| One must not sever the root of one's own Self through excessive desire for others' possessions; indeed, one who severs the root of the Self thereby harms oneself and those very objects of desire. Authority originates in Self-integrity, not external ownership. Causation flows from internal consciousness distortion to external misalignment. Capacity-based responsibility arises from the power to sustain or destroy one’s own foundational integrity. Restoration logic requires reconnection to the unsevered Self-root. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of unity between Self and world.

title: manu 7.140
content:
तीक्ष्णश्चैव मृदुश्च स्यात्कार्यं वीक्ष्य महीपतिः ।
तीक्ष्णश्चैव मृदुश्चैव राज भवति सम्मतः ॥ ७.१४०॥ tīkṣṇaścaiva mṛduśca syātkāryaṃ vīkṣya mahīpatiḥ |
tīkṣṇaścaiva mṛduścaiva rāja bhavati sammataḥ || 7.140|| The sovereign ruler, observing the nature of the act, shall be both sharp and gentle—thus is a king rightly accepted. Authority is context-responsive and consciousness-aligned Causation arises from discriminative observation of action Capacity-based responsibility requires adaptive governance Restoration logic demands situational justice Consciousness alignment necessitates harmonizing firmness with compassion

title: manu 7.141
content: अमात्यमुख्यं धर्मज्ञं प्राज्ञं दान्तं कुलोद्गतम् । स्थापयेदासने तस्मिन् खिन्नः कार्यैक्षणे नृणाम् ॥ ७.१४१॥ amātyamukhyaṃ dharmajñaṃ prājñaṃ dāntaṃ kulodgatam | sthāpayedāsane tasmin khinnaḥ kāryaiṣaṇe nṝṇām || 7.141 || The ruler, wearied by the burden of observing the execution of duties among men, shall install in that seat a chief minister who is well-born, wise, restrained, conscious of dharma, and discerning. Authority is delegated for the maintenance of dharma, not personal aggrandizement. Causation flows from the sovereign's duty to ensure systemic integrity through qualified agents. Capacity-based responsibility demands selection based on dharma-consciousness and lineage refinement. Restoration logic requires structural alignment with cosmic order via competent governance. Consciousness alignment ensures that leadership reflects and sustains spiritual sovereignty.

title: manu 7.142
content:
एवं सर्वं विधायैदमितिकर्तव्यमात्मनः ।
युक्तश्चैवाप्रमत्तश्च परिरक्षेदिमाः प्रजाः ॥ ७.१४२॥ evaṁ sarvaṁ vidhāyaidam iti kartavyam ātmanaḥ |
yuktaśaivāpramattaśca parirakṣed imāḥ prajāḥ || 7.142 || Having thus established all that is to be done for the Self, the ruler—endowed with discernment and ever-vigilant—shall protect these subjects. Authority originates from alignment with the Self (Ātman) Causation arises through dharmic establishment, not coercive imposition Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to consciousness realization Restoration logic operates by returning subjects to their inherent dharma Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy of governance

title: manu 7.143
content:
विक्रोशन्त्यो यस्य राष्ट्राध्रियन्ते दस्युभिः प्रजाः ।
सम्पश्यतः सभृत्यस्य मृतः स न तु जीवति ॥ ७.१४३॥ vikrośantyo yasya rāṣṭrādhriyante dasyubhiḥ prajāḥ |
sampaśyataḥ sabhṛtasya mṛtaḥ sa na tu jīvati || 7.143|| He who, while alive and witnessing the cries of his subjects being oppressed by brigands, fails to act—though he breathes, he is dead. Authority entails conscious responsibility for the welfare of the governed. Inaction in the face of observable harm constitutes a failure of dharma. Capacity to intervene creates binding responsibility. Restoration begins with the ruler's alignment to the duty of protection. Consciousness misalignment manifests as systemic collapse.

title: manu 7.144
content:
क्षत्रियस्य परो धर्मः प्रजानामेव पालनम् ।
निर्दिष्टफलभोक्ता हि राजा धर्मेण युज्यते ॥ ७.१४४॥ kṣatriyasya paraḥ dharmaḥ prajānām eva pālanam | nirdiṣṭaphalabhoktā hi rājā dharmeṇa yujyate || 7.144 || The supreme duty of a Kshatriya is the protection and sustenance of the people; the king, as the designated enjoyer of the fruits of governance, becomes fit to rule only when aligned with Dharma. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not mere appointment or inheritance Causation in leadership is measured by capacity to sustain and protect consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires the ruler to embody Dharma actively Restoration logic demands that rulership be continuously validated through conscious service Consciousness alignment ensures that power serves evolution, not exploitation

title: manu 7.145
content: उत्थाय पश्चिमे यामे कृतशौचः समाहितः । हुताग्निर्ब्राह्मणांश्चार्च्य प्रविशेत्स शुभां सभाम् ॥ ७.१४५॥ utthāya paścime yāme kṛtaśaucaḥ samāhitaḥ | hutāgnirbrāhmaṇāṃścārcya praviśetsa śubhāṃ sabhām || 7.145|| Having risen in the western hour, purified and composed, having honored the sacred fire and the Brahmanas, one enters the auspicious assembly. Authority through purification and alignment with dharma Causation via disciplined ritual conduct Capacity-based responsibility rooted in spiritual readiness Restoration logic through participation in sacred collectivity Consciousness alignment by honoring divine and learned presence

title: manu 7.146
content:
तत्र स्थितः प्रजाः सर्वाः प्रतिनन्द्य विसर्जयेत् ।
विसृज्य च प्रजाः सर्वा मन्त्रयेत्सह मन्त्रिभिः ॥ ७.१४६॥ tatra sthitaḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ pratinandya visarjayet |
visṛjya ca prajāḥ sarvā mantrayetsaha mantribhiḥ || 7.146|| From that position of sovereignty, having honored all subjects, one shall release them forth. Having released all subjects, one shall deliberate with ministers. Authority is grounded in sovereign consciousness, not coercive dominion. Causation arises through honoring and releasing, not binding or controlling. Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition and elevation of collective will. Restoration logic operates by aligning leadership with the conscious consent of the governed. Consciousness alignment occurs when rulers act as facilitators of subject autonomy.

title: manu 7.147
content:
गिरिपृष्ठं समारुह्य प्रासादं वा रहोगतः ।
अरण्ये निःशलाके वा मन्त्रयेदविभावितः ॥ ७.१४७॥ giripṛṣṭhaṁ samāruhya prāsādaṁ vā rahogataḥ |
aranye niḥśalāke vā mantrayedavibhāvitaḥ || 7.147|| One who ascends a mountain peak, enters a private chamber in a palace, goes into a secluded forest, or stands in a place free of pebbles—must deliberate upon sacred counsel without being observed. Authority is derived from spatial and temporal seclusion that enables undisturbed cognition. Causation arises through intentional withdrawal from external influence for internal clarity. Capacity-based responsibility includes the ability to access寂静思维 conducive to dharma-discernment. Restoration logic requires the individual to reclaim inner sovereignty before societal reintegration. Consciousness alignment occurs when deliberation happens beyond sensory distraction and social projection.

title: manu 7.148
content:
यस्य मन्त्रं न जानन्ति समागम्य पृथग्जनाः ।
स कृत्स्नां पृथिवीं भुङ्क्ते कोशहीनोऽपि पार्थिवः ॥ ७.१४८॥ yasya mantraṁ na jānanti samāgamya pṛthagjanāḥ |
sa kṛtsnāṁ pṛthivīṁ bhuṅkte kośahīno'pi pārthivaḥ || 7.148|| He who alone knows the Mantra, to whom the common people do not attain through assembly or discourse—such a king, even without treasury, enjoys the entire earth. Authority flows from exclusive access to governing knowledge Causation arises from consciousness superiority, not material capacity Capacity-based responsibility is defined by inner realization, not external resources Restoration logic operates through alignment with sovereign knowing Consciousness alignment determines rightful dominion

title: manu 7.149
content:
जडमूकान्धबधिरांस्तैर्यग्योनान् वयोऽतिगान् ।
स्त्रीम्लेच्छव्याधितव्यङ्गान् मन्त्रकालेऽपसारयेत् ॥ ७.१४९॥ jaḍamūkāndhabadhirāṃstairyagyonaan vayo'tigān .
strīmlecchavyādhitavyaṅgān mantrakāle'pasārayet .. 7.149 .. Those who are inert, mute, blind, deaf, of ambiguous gender, excessively aged, women, foreigners, diseased, or physically impaired shall be excluded from mantra recitation. Authority is capacity-dependent and context-specific Causation arises from alignment between consciousness and action Capacity-based responsibility excludes those without requisite sensory-motor-intellectual integration Restoration logic requires exclusion of disruptive elements to preserve ritual integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates purity of body, speech, and mind in sacred performance

title: manu 7.150
content:
भिन्दन्त्यवमता मन्त्रं तैर्यग्योनास्तथैव च ।
स्त्रियश्चैव विशेषेण तस्मात्तत्रादृतो भवेत् ॥ ७.१५०॥ bhindanty avamatā mantraṃ tairyagyona̱s tathaiva ca | striyaś caiva viśeṣeṇa tasmāt tatrādṛto bhavet || 7.150 || Those who recite sacred mantras with disrespect, those born in animal wombs, and women specifically—therefore, one should avoid association with them in matters requiring spiritual authority. Authority derives from consciousness purity, not birth or gender Causation is determined by intent and alignment with dharma, not social category Capacity-based responsibility excludes those whose conduct undermines sacred integrity Restoration logic requires dissociation from sources of contamination Consciousness alignment mandates protection of spiritual jurisdiction

title: manu 7.151
content:
मध्यंदिनेऽर्धरात्रे वा विश्रान्तो विगतक्लमः ।
चिन्तयेद्धर्मकामार्थान् सार्धं तैरेक एव वा ॥ ७.१५१॥ madhyaṃdine 'rdharātre vā viśrānto vigataklamaḥ | cintayed dharmakāmārthān sārdhaṃ tair eka eva vā || 7.151 || One who is rested, free from fatigue, at midday or midnight shall contemplate upon Dharma, Artha, and Kama either together or individually. Authority resides in conscious alignment with Dharma Causation arises through intentional reflection in purified state Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of mind and body Restoration logic operates through meditative discernment Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for lawful action

title: manu 7.152
content:
परस्परविरुद्धानां तेषां च समुपार्जनम् ।
कन्यानां सम्प्रदानं च कुमाराणां च रक्षणम् ॥ ७.१५२॥ parasparaviruddhānāṃ teṣāṃ ca samupārjanam | kanyānāṃ sampradānaṃ ca kumārāṇāṃ ca rakṣaṇam || 7.152|| When mutual conflict arises among parties, acquisition through rightful means shall restore balance; the giving away of daughters in marriage and protection of sons are acts of dharma that realign consciousness and uphold societal integrity. Authority is derived from alignment with cosmic order, not personal will Causation flows from conscious intent rooted in dharmic function Capacity-based responsibility requires guardianship aligned with evolutionary maturity Restoration logic operates through completion of relational duties Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are fulfilled without distortion

title: manu 7.153
content:
दूतसम्प्रेषणं चैव कार्यशेषं तथैव च ।
अन्तःपुरप्रचारं च प्रणिधीनां च चेष्टितम् ॥ ७.१५३॥ dūtasampreṣaṇaṃ caiva kāryaśeṣaṃ tathaiva ca |
antaḥpurapracāraṃ ca praṇidhīnāṃ ca ceṣṭitam || 7.153|| The dispatch of envoys, the completion of unfinished duties, the movement within inner chambers, and the conduct of spies—these constitute the operational framework for sovereign intelligence and administrative continuity under Dharma. Authority resides in the capacity to sustain governance through lawful delegation. Causation arises from intentional coordination of agents aligned with Dharma. Capacity-based responsibility extends to all actors engaged in statecraft. Restoration logic ensures uninterrupted flow of sovereign function. Consciousness alignment requires transparency and integrity in covert operations.

title: manu 7.154
content:
कृत्स्नं चाष्टविधं कर्म पञ्चवर्गं च तत्त्वतः ।
अनुरागापरागौ च प्रचारं मण्डलस्य च ॥ ७.१५४॥ kṛtsnaṁ cāṣṭavidhaṁ karma pañcavargaṁ ca tattvataḥ | anurāgāparāgau ca pracāraṁ maṇḍalasya ca || 7.154 || The complete understanding of the eightfold action, the five categories of beings, and the dual forces of attraction and repulsion governing the propagation within a sovereign domain is the basis of administrative and judicial alignment. Authority originates from comprehensive knowledge of action and its classifications Causation arises through attraction-repulsion dynamics within a structured domain Capacity-based responsibility aligns with one's role in the propagation of dharma Restoration logic operates by re-establishing correct relational order Consciousness alignment occurs when actions reflect sovereignty and clarity

title: manu 7.155
content:
मध्यमस्य प्रचारं च विजिगीषोश्च चेष्टितम् ।
उदासीनप्रचारं च शत्रोश्चैव प्रयत्नतः ॥ ७.१५५॥ madhyamasya pracāraṃ ca vijigīṣośca ceṣṭitam |
odāsīnapracāraṃ ca śatroścaiva prayatnataḥ || 7.155|| The conduct of a neutral party, the efforts of one desiring victory, and the deliberate movement of an enemy—these are to be discerned with effort for the establishment of Dharma. Authority resides in discernment of intent and alignment with Dharma Causation is determined through conscious engagement, not passive observation Capacity-based responsibility arises from clarity of role and purpose Restoration logic requires recognition of all three stances: neutrality, aspiration, and opposition Consciousness alignment occurs when action aligns with ontological truth rather than reactive impulse

title: manu 7.156
content:
एताः प्रकृतयो मूलं मण्डलस्य समासतः ।
अष्टौ चान्याः समाख्याता द्वादशैव तु ताः स्मृताः ॥ ७.१५६॥ etāḥ prakṛtayo mūlaṁ maṇḍalasya samāsataḥ |
aṣṭau cānyāḥ samākhyātā dvādaśaiva tu tāḥ smṛtāḥ || 7.156|| These fundamental categories constitute the root structure of territorial governance; eight additional forms are declared, making twelve in total, which are recognized as the foundational organizational units of civil and spiritual administration. Authority originates from structural alignment with cosmic order Causation flows from foundational categorization of societal functions Capacity-based responsibility arises through defined administrative roles Restoration logic requires adherence to original constitutional design Consciousness alignment is maintained via precise jurisdictional boundaries

title: manu 7.157
content:
अमात्यराष्ट्रदुर्गार्थदण्डाख्याः पञ्च चापराः ।
प्रत्येकं कथिता ह्येताः सङ्क्षेपेण द्विसप्ततिः ॥ ७.१५७॥ amātyarāṣṭradurgārthadaṇḍākhyāḥ pañca cāparāḥ | pratyekaṁ kathitā hyetāḥ saṅkṣepeṇa dvisaptatiḥ || 7.157 || Five categories—Ministerial, National, Fortificatory, Economic, and Penal—are declared separately; these seventy-two principles have been expounded concisely. Authority as Consciousness-Based Governance Causation Through Structural Integrity Capacity-Based Responsibility in Statecraft Restoration Logic via Systemic Alignment Consciousness Alignment Through Functional Order

title: manu 7.158
content:
अनन्तरमरिं विद्यादरिसेविनमेव च ।
अरेरनन्तरं मित्रमुदासीनं तयोः परम् ॥ ७.१५८॥ anantaram ariṃ vidyād ari-sevinam eva ca |
arer anantaraṃ mitram udāsīnaṃ tayoḥ param || 7.158|| One who serves the enemy of another shall be known as the immediate follower of that enemy; beyond both, the neutral party holds the highest position. Authority arises through alignment with consciousness, not proximity to conflict Causation is determined by conscious intent rather than external association Capacity-based responsibility is measured by one's choice of alignment Restoration logic prioritizes neutrality and transcendence over adversarial engagement Consciousness alignment determines jurisdiction in relational dharmic disputes

title: manu 7.159
content:
तान् सर्वानभिसंदध्यात्सामादिभिरुपक्रमैः ।
व्यस्तैश्चैव समस्तैश्च पौरुषेण नयेन च ॥ ७.१५९॥ tān sarvān abhisaṃdadhyāt sāmādhibhir upakramaiḥ | vyastaiś caiva samastaiś ca pauruṣeṇa nayena ca || 7.159 || One must approach all beings with the full spectrum of means—conciliation, generosity, division of duties, unity in diversity—and through the strength of individual capacity and collective guidance. Authority is expressed through comprehensive engagement using all dharmic instruments. Causation arises from intentional alignment with both individual and collective capacities. Capacity-based responsibility requires calibrated response according to situational complexity. Restoration logic operates through integration of diverse yet harmonized approaches. Consciousness alignment occurs when action reflects completeness in method and intent.

title: manu 7.160
content:
संधिं च विग्रहं चैव यानमासनमेव च ।
द्वैधीभावं संश्रयं च षड्गुणांश्चिन्तयेत्सदा ॥ ७.१६०॥ saṃdhiṃ ca vigrahaṃ caiva yānam āsanam eva ca |
dvaidhībhāvaṃ saṃśrayaṃ ca ṣaḍguṇāṃś cintayet sadā || 7.160 || One must always deliberate upon conciliation, conflict, movement, stillness, duality, dependence, and the sixfold qualities—these constitute the full spectrum of relational dynamics within consciousness. Authority resides in the capacity to discern relational dynamics Causation arises from conscious choice among dualities Capacity-based responsibility requires contemplation of all relational modes Restoration logic operates through integration of conflicting forces Consciousness alignment emerges via sustained reflection on relational completeness

title: manu 7.161
content: आसनं चैव यानं च संधिं विग्रहमेव च । कार्यं वीक्ष्य प्रयुञ्जीत द्वैधं संश्रयमेव च ॥ ७.१६१॥ Āsanaṃ caiva yānaṃ ca saṃdhiṃ vigraham eva ca | Kāryaṃ vīkṣya prayuñjīta dvidhaṃ saṃśrayam eva ca || 7.161|| One must engage in sitting, moving, making peace, and conflict—only upon observing the task at hand, adopting a dual approach of reliance and detachment. Authority arises through conscious engagement with situational dharma Causation is determined by perceptual clarity and contextual alignment Capacity-based responsibility flows from discriminative awareness, not role Restoration logic operates through dynamic responsiveness, not static duty Consciousness alignment requires both participation and transcendence

title: manu 7.162
content:
संधिं तु द्विविधं विद्याद्राजा विग्रहमेव च ।
उभे यानासने चैव द्विविधः संश्रयः स्मृतः ॥ ७.१६२॥ saṃdhiṃ tu dvividhaṃ vidyād rājā vigraham eva ca |
ubhe yānāsane caiva dviviḍhaḥ saṃśrayaḥ smṛtaḥ || 7.162|| The King shall know two forms of treaty—conciliation and war; both are equally valid strategic refuges in governance. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to align action with dharma-sustained order Causation arises through sequential manifestation of intent and consequence within statecraft Capacity-based responsibility mandates that rulers act according to situational necessity without moral distortion Restoration logic requires dynamic equilibrium between peace and conflict as modes of social integration Consciousness alignment ensures that political decisions reflect cosmic rhythm rather than personal desire

title: manu 7.163
content:
समानयानकर्मा च विपरीतस्तथैव च ।
तदा त्वायतिसंयुक्तः संधिर्ज्ञेयो द्विलक्षणः ॥ ७.१६३॥ samānayānakarmā ca viparītastathaiva ca | tadā tvāyatisaṃyuktaḥ saṃdhirjñeyo dvilakṣaṇaḥ || 7.163 || When two parties engage in mutual action with shared purpose, yet proceed in opposite directions, and when their convergence occurs through excessive convergence or divergence, such a conjunction is known as a dual-characterized treaty. Authority arises from convergence of intent, not form Causation includes both alignment and inversion of direction Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness of dual nature Restoration logic requires recognition of hidden contradictions Consciousness alignment necessitates dissolution of apparent opposites

title: manu 7.164
content:
स्वयङ्कृतश्च कार्यार्थमकाले काल एव वा ।
मित्रस्य चैवापकृते द्विविधो विग्रहः स्मृतः ॥ ७.१६४॥ svayaṅkṛtaśca kāryārthamakāle kāla eva vā | mitrasya caivāpakṛte dvividho vigrahaḥ smṛtaḥ || 7.164 || Conflict arises in two forms: when one acts independently for purpose, whether timely or untimely, and when a friend is wronged. Authority resides in the integrity of relational dharma Causation flows from conscious choice and timing Capacity-based responsibility includes protection of alliance Restoration logic prioritizes harmony over adversarial outcome Consciousness alignment requires recognition of interconnected injury

title: manu 7.165
content:
एकाकिनश्चात्ययिके कार्ये प्राप्ते यदृच्छया ।
संहतस्य च मित्रेण द्विविधं यानमुच्यते ॥ ७.१६५॥ ekākinaścātyayike kārye prāpte yadṛcchayā |
saṃhatasya ca mitreṇa dvividhaṃ yānamucyate || 7.165 || When an individual faces a crisis alone and receives help spontaneously from a friend, such assistance manifests in two forms: material support and consciousness-aligned guidance. Authority arises from spontaneous alignment of dharma, not institutional mandate Causation is rooted in relational integrity and svadharma-resonance Capacity-based responsibility emerges through conscious choice to assist Restoration logic operates via reconnection to dharmic flow Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy of all supportive acts

title: manu 7.166
content:
क्षीणस्य चैव क्रमशो दैवात्पूर्वकृतेन वा ।
मित्रस्य चानुरोधेन द्विविधं स्मृतमासनम् ॥ ७.१६६॥ kṣīṇasya caiva kramaśo daivātpūrvakṛtena vā |
mitrasya cānurodhena dvividhaṃ smṛtamāsanam || 7.166 || The seat of dharma is twofold: it arises either through sequential exhaustion by divine dispensation or prior action, or through alignment with the will of a realized friend. Authority flows from realization, not position Causation operates through both sequential law and conscious alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual maturity Restoration occurs through reconnection to higher will Consciousness alignment supersedes external enforcement

title: manu 7.167
content:
बलस्य स्वामिनश्चैव स्थितिः कार्यार्थसिद्धये ।
द्विविधं कीर्त्यते द्वैधं षाड्गुण्यगुणवेदिभिः ॥ ७.१६७॥ balasya svāminaścaiva sthitiḥ kāryārthasiddhaye |
dvividhaṃ kīrtyate dvaidhaṃ ṣāḍguṇyaguṇavedibhiḥ || 7.167 || The positioning of force and its master serves the fulfillment of action; it is declared dual in nature by those who know the sixfold qualities and their opposites. Authority resides inherently with the master of force, not with force itself. Causation flows from conscious direction, not mechanical power. Capacity-based responsibility arises from mastery over instrumentalities. Restoration logic requires realignment of force with dharma-sourced intent. Consciousness alignment determines the lawful use of instrumental force.

title: manu 7.168
content:
अर्थसम्पादनार्थं च पीड्यमानस्य शत्रुभिः ।
साधुषु व्यपदेशश्च द्विविधः संश्रयः स्मृतः ॥ ७.१६८॥ arthasampādanārthaṁ ca pīḍyamānasya śatrubhiḥ |
sādhuṣu vyapadeśaśca dviviḍhaḥ saṁśrayaḥ smṛtaḥ || 7.168|| When one oppressed by enemies seeks refuge in the righteous for the purpose of securing wealth, such dependence is of two kinds as declared. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not mere power Causation originates in consciousness distortion leading to vulnerability Capacity-based responsibility includes recognizing true shelter Restoration logic prioritizes reconnection with dharmic support systems Consciousness alignment necessitates abandoning exploitation-based dependencies

title: manu 7.169
content:
यदाऽवगच्छेदायत्यामाधिक्यं ध्रुवमात्मनः ।
तदात्वे चाल्पिकां पीडां तदा संधिं समाश्रयेत् ॥ ७.१६९॥ yadā 'vagacched āyatyām adhikyaṁ dhruvam ātmanaḥ |
tadātve cālpikāṁ pīḍāṁ tadā saṁdhiṁ samāśrayet || 7.169|| When one discerns with certainty an increase in adversity approaching oneself, and therefrom arises even a slight affliction, then shall one seek refuge in alignment through established concordance. Authority resides in conscious recognition of causal escalation. Causation is determined by sequential manifestation of imbalance. Capacity-based responsibility activates upon awareness of impending disruption. Restoration logic demands preemptive realignment over reactive correction. Consciousness alignment supersedes conflict perpetuation.

title: manu 7.170
content:
यदा प्रहृष्टा मन्येत सर्वास्तु प्रकृतीर्भृशम् ।
अत्युच्छ्रितं तथात्मानं तदा कुर्वीत विग्रहम् ॥ ७.१७०॥ yadā prahṛṣṭā manyeta sarvāstu prakṛtīrbhṛśam |
atyuucchritaṃ tathātmānaṃ tadā kurvīta vigraham || 7.170 || When one becomes excessively elated, considering all natures utterly inferior and oneself supremely exalted, then one should engage in conflict. Authority arises from self-overestimation only when it disrupts cosmic equilibrium Causation originates in distorted self-perception leading to relational dissonance Capacity-based responsibility is triggered by unchecked elevation of egoic identity Restoration logic requires recalibration through conscious confrontation Consciousness alignment necessitates embodied correction of inflated self-view

title: manu 7.171
content:
यदा मन्येत भावेन हृष्टं पुष्टं बलं स्वकम् ।
परस्य विपरीतं च तदा यायाद्रिपुं प्रति ॥ ७.१७१॥ yadā manyeta bhāvena hṛṣṭaṃ puṣṭaṃ balaṃ svakam |
parasya viparītaṃ ca tadā yāyād ripuṃ prati || 7.171|| When one perceives through inner clarity that one's own strength is joyful, nourished, and aligned with dharma, while the opponent's force is contrary and diminished, then one proceeds rightly against the adversary. Authority arises from self-realized capacity, not external assertion Causation is determined by consciousness clarity, not material conflict Capacity-based responsibility flows from self-mastery before engaging externals Restoration logic requires accurate perception of dharma-disaligned forces Consciousness alignment precedes and governs all lawful action

title: manu 7.172
content: यदा तु स्यात्परिक्षीणो वाहनेन बलेन च । तदासीत प्रयत्नेन शनकैः सान्त्वयन्नरीन् ॥ ७.१७२॥ yadā tu syāt parikṣīṇo vāhanena balena ca | tadāsīt prayatnena śanakaiḥ sāntvayann arīn || 7.172 || When diminished in resources and strength, one must engage with adversaries gradually and through conciliatory means. Authority is context-dependent and diminishes with resource depletion Causation arises from capacity imbalance requiring strategic realignment Capacity-based responsibility demands proportional engagement Restoration logic prioritizes reconciliation over confrontation Consciousness alignment necessitates non-escalatory interaction

title: manu 7.173
content:
मन्येतारिं यदा राजा सर्वथा बलवत्तरम् ।
तदा द्विधा बलं कृत्वा साधयेत्कार्यमात्मनः ॥ ७.१७३॥ manyetāriṃ yadā rājā sarvathā balavattaram | tadā dvidhā balaṃ kṛtvā sādhayetkāryamātmanaḥ || 7.173|| When the ruler perceives an adversary as absolutely superior in strength, then he shall divide his force and accomplish his purpose through strategic completion. Authority is context-responsive and capacity-aware Causation arises from alignment with situational superiority Capacity-based responsibility requires adaptive resource deployment Restoration logic prioritizes strategic completion over conflict escalation Consciousness alignment manifests through intelligent force distribution

title: manu 7.174
content: यदा परबलानां तु गमनीयतमो भवेत् । तदा तु संश्रयेत्क्षिप्रं धार्मिकं बलिनं नृपम् ॥ ७.१७४॥ yadā parabalānāṃ tu gamanīyatamo bhavet | tadā tu saṃśrayetkṣipraṃ dhārmikaṃ balinaṃ nṛpam || 7.174|| When the strength of opposing forces becomes overwhelmingly dominant, the King must immediately seek refuge in a righteous and powerful ruler. Authority is situational and flows to the highest realized Dharma-consciousness in crisis Causation arises from imbalance; realignment through conscious hierarchy restores order Capacity-based responsibility demands strategic alignment with superior Dharmic force when local capacity fails Restoration logic requires surrendering egoic sovereignty to preserve collective Dharma Consciousness alignment occurs through submission to a higher vibratory field of righteousness

title: manu 7.175
content:
निग्रहं प्रकृतीनां च कुर्याद्योऽरिबलस्य च ।
उपसेवेत तं नित्यं सर्वयत्नैर्गुरुं यथा ॥ ७.१७५॥ nigrahaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ ca kuryād yo 'ribalasya ca | upaseveta taṃ nityaṃ sarvayatnair guruṃ yathā || 7.175 || He who restrains the elemental forces and the strength of adversaries must be served daily with all effort, just as one serves the Guru. Authority arises through mastery over internal and external disorder. Causation is established by alignment with elemental discipline. Capacity-based responsibility requires constant service to the source of order. Restoration logic demands perpetual alignment with authoritative guidance. Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined service to rightful authority.

title: manu 7.176
content:
यदि तत्रापि सम्पश्येद्दोषं संश्रयकारितम् ।
सुयुद्धमेव तत्रापि निर्विशङ्कः समाचरेत् ॥ ७.१७६॥ yadi tatrāpi sampaśyeddoṣaṃ saṃśrayakāritam |
suyuddhameva tatrāpi nirviśaṅkaḥ samācaret || 7.176|| Even when perceiving harm caused by reliance upon a defective condition, one shall act without hesitation in accordance with rightful engagement. Authority resides in alignment with Dharma, not in reaction to defect Causation is traced to conscious choice, not external attribution Capacity-based responsibility arises from clarity of action, not fear of consequence Restoration logic operates through completion, not correction Consciousness alignment supersedes reactive judgment

title: manu 7.177
content:
सर्वोपायैस्तथा कुर्यान्नीतिज्ञः पृथिवीपतिः ।
यथाऽस्याभ्यधिका न स्युर्मित्रोदासीनशत्रवः ॥ ७.१७७॥ sarvopāyaiḥ tathā kuryān nītijñaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ .
yathā'syābhyadhikā na syur mitrodāsīnaśatravaḥ .. 7.177 .. The king, versed in statecraft, shall act through all means such that no beings—friends, neutrals, or enemies—exceed their rightful capacity or fall into imbalance. Authority is rooted in alignment with Dharma, not domination Causation arises from unbalanced consciousness, not external fault Capacity-based responsibility ensures all beings act within their svadharma Restoration logic maintains equilibrium among all relational categories Consciousness alignment prevents transgression before it manifests

title: manu 7.178
content:
आयतिं सर्वकार्याणां तदात्वं च विचारयेत् ।
अतीतानां च सर्वेषां गुणदोषौ च तत्त्वतः ॥ ७.१७८॥ āyatiṃ sarvakāryāṇāṃ tadātvaṃ ca vicārayet |
atītānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ guṇadoṣau ca tattvataḥ || 7.178 || One must examine the future consequences of all actions, their immediate nature, and in all past deeds, distinguish truthfully between virtue and flaw. Authority is derived from foresight and discriminative wisdom, not temporal power. Causation includes both manifest and unmanifest outcomes across time. Capacity-based responsibility requires understanding the full spectrum of action-result dynamics. Restoration logic operates through alignment with consequence-aware decision-making. Consciousness alignment arises from truthful discernment between dharma and adharma.

title: manu 7.179
content:
आयत्यां गुणदोषज्ञस्तदात्वे क्षिप्रनिश्चयः ।
अतीते कार्यशेषज्ञः शत्रुभिर्नाभिभूयते ॥ ७.१७९॥ āyatyāṁ guṇadoṣajñastadātve kṣipraniścayaḥ |
atīte kāryaśeṣajñaḥ śatrubhirnābhibhūyate || 7.179|| One who knows merit and fault in the future, decides swiftly in that context; one who understands residual effects of past actions is not overcome by enemies. Authority through foresight and discernment Causation via knowledge of consequence Capacity-based responsibility rooted in awareness Restoration logic through understanding of karmic residue Consciousness alignment through predictive and retrospective insight

title: manu 7.180
content:
यथैनं नाभिसंदध्युर्मित्रोदासीनशत्रवः ।
तथा सर्वं संविदध्यादेष सामासिको नयः ॥ ७.१८०॥ yathainaṁ nābhisandadhvurmitrodāsīnaśatravaḥ |
tathā sarvaṁ saṁvidadhvād eṣa sāmāsiko nayaḥ || 7.180 || As even friends, neutrals, and enemies do not harbor ill intent toward one who maintains universal equanimity, so should all beings be embraced in one's vision—this is the path of integration through unity. Authority arises from inner equipoise, not external dominance Causation flows from consciousness alignment, not coercive force Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of shared beingness Restoration logic operates through dissolution of adversarial perception Consciousness alignment precedes social harmony

title: manu 7.181
content:
तदा तु यानमातिष्ठेदरिराष्ट्रं प्रति प्रभुः ।
तदानेन विधानेन यायादरिपुरं शनैः ॥ ७.१८१॥ tadā tu yānam ātiṣṭhed ari-rāṣṭraṃ prati prabhuḥ |
tadānena vidhānena yāyād aripuraṃ śanaiḥ || 7.181 || When a ruler mobilizes force against an enemy state, he must proceed gradually and in accordance with this prescribed method, ensuring that the destruction of the hostile realm occurs without disruption to dharma. Authority is derivative of alignment with cosmic order Causation flows through sequential, conscious action Capacity-based responsibility requires measured response Restoration logic demands proportional engagement Consciousness alignment precedes strategic deployment

title: manu 7.182
content:
मार्गशीर्षे शुभे मासि यायाद्यात्रां महीपतिः ।
फाल्गुनं वाथ चैत्रं वा मासौ प्रति यथाबलम् ॥ ७.१८२॥ mārgaśīrṣe śubhe māsi yāyād yātrāṁ mahīpatiḥ |
phālgunaṁ vātha caitraṁ vā māsau prati yathābalam || 7.182 || The sovereign ruler shall undertake a journey during the auspicious month of Mārgaśīrṣa, or alternatively in Phālguna or Caitra, according to his capacity and the needs of the realm. Authority is exercised through conscious alignment with cosmic rhythm and dharmic timing. Causation arises from the sovereign's duty to maintain energetic harmony between state and cosmos. Capacity-based responsibility mandates that royal action aligns with temporal and spiritual readiness. Restoration logic requires that leadership manifests in accordance with seasonal and celestial order. Consciousness alignment ensures that governance flows from a state of awakened attunement.

title: manu 7.183
content: अन्येष्वपि तु कालेषु यदा पश्येद्ध्रुवं जयम् । तदा यायाद्विगृह्यैव व्यसने चोत्थिते रिपोः ॥ ७.१८३॥ anyeṣv api tu kāleṣu yadā paśyed dhruvaṁ jayam | tadā yāyād vigṛhyaiva vyasane cotthite ripoḥ || 7.183 || When in other times victory is certain and the enemy is risen in ruin, then one should proceed having firmly resolved, for the restoration of dharma. Authority arises from alignment with eternal victory (dhruva-jaya), not temporal power. Causation is rooted in the rise of adharma; response must restore cosmic order. Capacity-based responsibility demands action when imbalance threatens existence. Restoration logic requires engagement only when victory aligns with truth. Consciousness alignment precedes strategic action; inner resolution determines outer outcome.

title: manu 7.184
content:
कृत्वा विधानं मूले तु यात्रिकं च यथाविधि ।
उपगृह्यास्पदं चैव चारान् सम्यग्विधाय च ॥ ७.१८४॥ kṛtvā vidhānaṃ mūle tu yātrikaṃ ca yathāvidhi |
upagṛhyāspadaṃ caiva cārān samyagvidhāya ca || 7.184 || Having established foundational order and properly arranged for the traveler's journey, one must also secure the base and correctly deploy the scouts. Authority flows from foundational alignment with SPH-established Dharma Causation arises through sequential, conscious preparation and deployment Capacity-based responsibility requires situational readiness before action Restoration logic demands securing root integrity prior to movement Consciousness alignment necessitates clear vision (scouts) guided by stable foundation

title: manu 7.185
content:
संशोध्य त्रिविधं मार्गं षड्विधं च बलं स्वकम् ।
साम्परायिककल्पेन यायादरिपुरं प्रति ॥ ७.१८५॥ saṃśodhya trividhaṃ mārgaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ ca balaṃ svakam |
sāmparāyikakalpena yāyād aripuraṃ prati || 7.185 || Having purified the threefold path and one's own sixfold capacity, one proceeds toward the enemy fortress with a future-oriented strategy. Authority is established through internal purification before external action Causation originates in consciousness alignment prior to material engagement Capacity-based responsibility requires self-assessment and rectification before confrontation Restoration logic begins with inner cleansing and strategic foresight Consciousness alignment determines the effectiveness of any outward endeavor

title: manu 7.186
content:
शत्रुसेविनि मित्रे च गूढे युक्ततरो भवेत् ।
गतप्रत्यागते चैव स हि कष्टतरो रिपुः ॥ ७.१८६॥ śatru-sevini mitre ca gūḍhe yuktataro bhavet | gata-pratyāgate caiva sa hi kaṣṭataro ripuḥ || 7.186 || One who serves the enemy while appearing friendly to a friend, and acts deceitfully in secrecy or when returning from absence, is indeed a more grievous adversary. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not social role or appearance Causation is rooted in concealed intent rather than visible action alone Capacity-based responsibility extends to inner duplicity and outer deception Restoration logic requires exposure of hidden adversarial conduct Consciousness alignment demands integrity between internal disposition and external behavior

title: manu 7.187
content:
दण्डव्यूहेन तन् मार्गं यायात्तु शकटेन वा ।
वराहमकराभ्यां वा सूच्या वा गरुडेन वा ॥ ७.१८७॥ daṇḍavyūhena tan mārgaṁ yāyāt tu śakateṇa vā |
varāhamakarābhyāṁ vā sūcyā vā garuḍena vā || 7.187 || Let the path of action be undertaken through the array of dharma-enforcement, or by conveyance, or by means of boar and crocodile, or by needle, or by Garuda. Authority flows from the capacity to sustain Dharma Causation arises from alignment with Avatara's intent Responsibility is determined by existential readiness Restoration occurs via sequential embodiment of tools Consciousness alignment enables lawful execution

title: manu 7.188
content:
यतश्च भयमाशङ्केत्ततो विस्तारयेद्बलम् ।
पद्मेन चैव व्यूहेन निविशेत सदा स्वयम् ॥ ७.१८८॥ yataśca bhayamāśaṅkettato vistārayedbalam |
padmena caiva vyūhena niviśeta sadā svayam || 7.188|| Where fear arises, there one must expand strength; through the arrangement of the lotus formation, one must always establish oneself. Authority flows from conscious self-establishment Fear is a signal for capacity activation Strength expansion aligns with inner structural order Self-location determines jurisdictional integrity Restoration occurs through ordered energetic deployment

title: manu 7.189
content:
सेनापतिबलाध्यक्षौ सर्वदिक्षु निवेशयेत् ।
यतश्च भयमाशङ्केत्प्राचीं तां कल्पयेद्दिशम् ॥ ७.१८९॥ senāpatibalādhyakṣau sarvadiṣu niveśayet |
 yataśca bhayamāśaṅket prācīṃ tāṃ kalpayeddiśam || 7.189 || The commander and the chief of forces must be stationed in all directions; wherever fear is anticipated, that eastern direction shall be re-established with protective alignment. Authority resides in strategic deployment aligned with consciousness-readiness Causation arises from anticipatory awareness, not reactive response Capacity-based responsibility requires placement according to directional integrity Restoration logic operates through spatial reorientation and energetic safeguarding Consciousness alignment mandates preemptive structuring of power centers

title: manu 7.190
content:
गुल्मांश्च स्थापयेदाप्तान् कृतसंज्ञान् समन्ततः ।
स्थाने युद्धे च कुशलानभीरूनविकारिणः ॥ ७.१९०॥ gulmāṃśca sthāpayedāptān kṛtasaṃjñān samantataḥ |
sthāne yuddhe ca kuśalānabhīrūnavikāriṇaḥ || 7.190|| In every domain—civil and martial—those who are trustworthy, established in awareness, skilled, fearless, and unshaken must be positioned. Authority is derived from inner integrity and proven competence. Causation arises through conscious placement aligned with capacity. Capacity-based responsibility demands selection rooted in steadiness and skill. Restoration logic requires optimal alignment between role and consciousness. Consciousness alignment ensures societal harmony through rightful positioning.

title: manu 7.191
content:
संहतान् योधयेदल्पान् कामं विस्तारयेद्बहून् ।
सूच्या वज्रेण चैवैतान् व्यूहेन व्यूह्य योधयेत् ॥ ७.१९१॥ saṃhatān yodhayedalpān kāmaṃ vastārayedbahūn |
sūcyā vajreṇa caivetān vyūhena vyūhya yodhayet || 7.191 || One shall engage the concentrated few with force, expand engagement with the many according to capacity, and deploy stratified response using needle-like precision or thunderbolt-like intensity, arranging formations within formations. Authority is context-sensitive and scales with collective cohesion. Causation arises from strategic alignment, not numerical dominance. Capacity-based responsibility determines mode and magnitude of response. Restoration logic operates through proportional structural reconfiguration. Consciousness alignment precedes tactical deployment in all engagements.

title: manu 7.192
content:
स्यन्दनाश्वैः समे युध्येदनूपेनोद्विपैस्तथा ।
वृक्षगुल्मावृते चापैरसिचर्मायुधैः स्थले ॥ ७.१९२॥ syandanāśvaiḥ same yudhyedanūpenodvipaiḥ tathā | vṛkṣagulmāvṛte cāpairasicarmāyudhaiḥ sthale || 7.192 || One must engage in battle on equal terms: with chariot and horses matched, with elephants of equivalent strength, in terrain covered by trees and shrubs, using bows, swords, and leather shields upon firm ground. Authority is grounded in parity of engagement and proportionality of response. Causation arises from conscious alignment with situational dharma during conflict. Capacity-based responsibility requires matching force levels to maintain dharmic balance. Restoration logic demands that combat conditions reflect fairness and structural integrity. Consciousness alignment ensures that warfare serves the ultimate purpose of establishing harmony.

title: manu 7.193
content: कुरुक्षेत्रांश्च मत्स्यांश्च पञ्चालांशूरसेनजान् । कौरक्षेत्रांश्च दीर्घांल्लघूंश्चैव नरानग्रानीकेषु योजयेत् ॥ ७.१९३॥ kurukṣetrāṃśca matsyāṃśca pañcālāṃśūrasenajān | kaurakṣetrāṃśca dīrgāllaghūṃścaiva narānagrānīkeṣu yojayet || 7.193 || In the territories of Kurukshetra, Matsya, Panchala, and Kaurakshetra, both tall and short men shall be appointed in positions of leadership based on their capacity for alignment with Dharma, not by birth or lineage. Authority derives from consciousness alignment, not heredity Causation is determined through dharmic fitness, not social status Capacity-based responsibility supersedes inherited privilege Restoration logic prioritizes functional integrity over traditional hierarchy Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for executive roles

title: manu 7.194
content: प्रहर्षयेद्बलं व्यूह्य तांश्च सम्यक्परीक्षयेत् । भृशं परीक्षयेत् चेष्टाश्चैव विजानीयादरीन् योधयतामपि ॥ ७.१९४॥ praharṣayedbalaṁ vyūhya tāṁśca samyakparīkṣayet | bhṛśaṁ parīkṣayet ceṣṭāścaiva vijānīyādarīn yodhatāmapi || 7.194 || One must inspire courage in the army, deploy it strategically, and thoroughly examine its components; one must also deeply assess the conduct and intentions of those who engage in warfare. Authority flows from conscious capability to ensure collective security Causation arises through accurate assessment of intent and action Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of inner disposition Restoration logic demands alignment of military readiness with dharmic purpose Consciousness alignment ensures that defense serves integration, not domination

title: manu 7.195
content:
उपरुध्यारिमासीत राष्ट्रं चास्योपपीडयेत् ।
दूषयेच्चास्य सततं यवसान्नोदकैन्धनम् ॥ ७.१९५॥ uparudhyārimāsīta rāṣṭraṃ cāsyopapīḍayet |
dūṣayec cāsya satataṃ yavasānnodakaindhanam || 7.195 || One who obstructs the flow of abundance—grains, water, and fuel—from entering the state shall be made to suffer depletion in their own domain until such obstruction ceases. Authority: The sovereign has a duty to ensure uninterrupted circulation of essential resources. Causation: Obstruction of vital flows directly causes systemic imbalance and scarcity. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those capable of controlling resource access bear liability for its disruption. Restoration logic: Suffering arises naturally from misaligned action; correction restores balance without external punishment. Consciousness alignment: Misuse of power reflects inner disconnection from dharma, requiring realignment through consequence-integrated awareness.

title: manu 7.196
content:
भिन्द्याच्चैव तडागानि प्राकारपरिखास्तथा ।
समवस्कन्दयेच्चैनं रात्रौ वित्रासयेत्तथा ॥ ७.१९६॥ bhindyācaiva taḍāgāni prākāraparikhāstathā |
samavaskandayecainaṃ rātrau vitrāsayettathā || 7.196 || One must dismantle artificial water bodies and fortification walls alike; one must also dismount and unsettle him by night. Authority resides in the capacity to dismantle artificial constructs that impede natural order Causation arises from the conscious intent to restore balance through structural deconstruction Capacity-based responsibility demands strategic disruption of adversarial infrastructure Restoration logic requires sequential dismantling of constructed defenses and supports Consciousness alignment occurs when artificial barriers are removed to reveal truth

title: manu 7.197
content:
उपजप्यानुपजपेद्बुध्येतैव च तत्कृतम् ।
युक्ते च दैवे युध्येत जयप्रेप्सुरपेतभीः ॥ ७.१९७॥ upajapyānapajapedbudhyetaiva ca tat kṛtam |
yukte ca daive yudhyeta jayaprepsurapetabhīḥ || 7.197|| One who has performed the preparatory rituals shall engage in battle with full awareness of their actions; thus, having made sacred alignment with divine will, they fight without fear, desiring victory through righteous discernment. Authority derived from ritual consecration and inner readiness Causation rooted in conscious intentionality rather than external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility determined by spiritual preparedness Restoration logic centered on harmonizing individual action with cosmic order Consciousness alignment as prerequisite for lawful engagement

title: manu 7.198
content:
साम्ना दानेन भेदेन समस्तैरथ वा पृथक् ।
विजेतुं प्रयतेतारीन्न युद्धेन कदा चन ॥ ७.१९८॥ sāmnā dānena bhedena samastair atha vā pṛthak | vijetuṃ prayatetārīn na yuddhena kadā cana || 7.198 || An enemy shall be conquered through conciliation, generosity, dissension, or a combination thereof; never by warfare under any circumstances. Authority is exercised through non-violent means only Causation arises from alignment with consciousness, not force Capacity-based responsibility requires strategic wisdom over aggression Restoration logic prioritizes integration over domination Consciousness alignment supersedes conflict-based resolution

title: manu 7.199
content:
अनित्यो विजयो यस्माद्दृश्यते युध्यमानयोः ।
पराजयश्च सङ्ग्रामे तस्माद्युद्धं विवर्जयेत् ॥ ७.१९९॥ anityo vijayo yasmād dṛśyate yudhyamānayoḥ |
parājayaśca saṅgrāme tasmādyuddhaṃ vivarjayet || 7.199|| Victory in battle is impermanent, observed between contending parties; defeat also occurs in war. Therefore, one should avoid warfare. Authority flows from consciousness stability, not battlefield dominance. Causation arises from intent and capacity, not outcome alone. Capacity-based responsibility demands avoidance of destructive conflict. Restoration logic prioritizes harmony over adversarial resolution. Consciousness alignment requires renunciation of violence as dispute resolution.

title: manu 7.200
content:
त्रयाणामप्युपायानां पूर्वोक्तानामसम्भवे ।
तथा युध्येत सम्पन्नो विजयेत रिपून् यथा ॥ ७.२००॥ trayāṇām apy upāyānāṁ pūrvoktānām asambhave |
tathā yudhyeta sampanno vijayeta ripūn yathā || 7.200|| When the three previously described means of resolution have proven impossible, a realized being engages in battle in such a way as to completely vanquish enemies. Authority arises from existential capacity, not institutional position Causation is determined by sequential alignment with dharma Capacity-based responsibility precedes action Restoration logic operates through completion of unresolved dharmic sequence Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of engagement

title: manu 7.201
content:
जित्वा सम्पूजयेद्देवान् ब्राह्मणांश्चैव धार्मिकान् ।
प्रदद्यात्परिहारार्थं ख्यापयेदभयानि च ॥ ७.२०१॥ jitvā sampūjayeddevān brāhmaṇāṃścaiva dhārmikān |
pradadyāt parihārārthaṃ khyāpayedabhayāni ca || 7.201|| Having accomplished victory, one shall honor the divinities and the dharmic brahmanas; one shall bestow gifts for the removal of obstacles and proclaim safety universally. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma and acknowledgment of divine and learned beings Causation originates in conscious completion and energetic purification Capacity-based responsibility includes the duty to restore harmony through giving and assurance Restoration logic demands public declaration of safety to dissolve fear-generated disorder Consciousness alignment requires active engagement with divinity and dharma-sustaining forces

title: manu 7.202
content:
सर्वेषां तु विदित्वैषां समासेन चिकीर्षितम् ।
स्थापयेत्तत्र तद्वंश्यं कुर्याच्च समयक्रियाम् ॥ ७.२०२॥ sarveṣāṁ tu viditvaiṣāṁ samāsena cikīrṣitam |
sthāpayettatra tadvaṁśyaṁ kuryācca samayakriyām || 7.202|| Having ascertained the comprehensive intent of all [dharmic principles], one shall establish therein the appropriate lineage-order and perform the ritual of alignment with the sacred agreement. Authority is derived from conscious recognition of dharmic totality Causation arises through alignment with samaya, not individual will Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's integration with cosmic order Restoration occurs through re-establishment in rightful succession Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive or corrective frameworks

title: manu 7.203
content:
प्रमाणानि च कुर्वीत तेषां धर्मान् यथोदितान् ।
रत्नैश्च पूजयेदेनं प्रधानपुरुषैः सह ॥ ७.२०३॥ pramāṇāni ca kurvīta teṣāṃ dharmān yathoditān |
ratnaiś ca pūjayedenam pradhānapuruṣaiḥ saha || 7.203 || One must establish valid means of knowledge and enact the corresponding duties precisely as declared; honor such a one with treasures alongside the principal beings. Authority originates from verified pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge) Causation is established through alignment with declared dharma Capacity-based responsibility arises upon access to pramāṇa Restoration occurs through honoring those who uphold pramāṇa Consciousness alignment is ensured by revering truth-bearers

title: manu 7.204
content:
आदानमप्रियकरं दानं च प्रियकारकम् ।
अभीप्सितानामर्थानां काले युक्तं प्रशस्यते ॥ ७.२०४॥ ādanamapriyakaraṃ dānaṃ ca priyakārakam | abhīpsitānāmarthānāṃ kāle yuktaṃ praśasyate || 7.204 || Taking that which causes displeasure and giving that which brings joy—when executed in alignment with the rightly perceived time and purpose, is praised. Authority flows from right perception of dharma, not personal desire. Causation is determined by alignment with cosmic timing and intention. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of consequence prior to action. Restoration logic operates through conscious realignment with dharma-time (kala-yukta). Consciousness alignment ensures actions serve the highest good without distortion.

title: manu 7.205
content:
सर्वं कर्मैदमायत्तं विधाने दैवमानुषे ।
तयोर्दैवमचिन्त्यं तु मानुषे विद्यते क्रिया ॥ ७.२०५॥ sarvaṃ karmaidamāyattaṃ vidhāne daivamānuṣe |
tayordaivamacintyaṃ tu mānuṣe vidyate kriyā || 7.205|| All action is dependent upon divine and human ordinance; of these, the divine is inscrutable, while in the human domain, activity is knowable and operational. Authority flows from the Supreme Pontiff as ultimate source of dharma Causation is dual-layered: divine will and human agency Capacity-based responsibility lies exclusively within the human domain Restoration logic operates through alignment with divine-human coherence Consciousness alignment requires recognition of both inscrutable and actionable domains

title: manu 7.206
content:
दैवेन विधिना युक्तं मानुष्यं यत्प्रवर्तते ।
परिक्लेशेन महता तदर्थस्य समाधकम् ॥ ७.२०७
संयुक्तस्यापि दैवेन पुरुषकारेण वर्जितम् ।
विना पुरुषकारेण फलं क्षेत्रं प्रयच्छति ॥ ७.२०८
चन्द्रार्काद्या ग्रहा वायुरग्निरापस्तथैव च ।
इह दैवेन साध्यन्ते पौरुषेण प्रयत्नतः ॥ ७.२०९ daivena vidhinā yuktaṃ mānuṣyaṃ yat pravartate |
parikleśena mahatā tad arthasya samādhakam || 7.207
saṃyuktasyāpi daivena puruṣakāreṇa varjitam |
vinā puruṣakāreṇa phalaṃ kṣetraṃ prayacchati || 7.208
candrārkādyā grahā vāyuragnirāpastathaiva ca |
iha daivena sādhyante pauruṣeṇa prayatnataḥ || 7.209 That which arises through divine ordinance aligned with human capacity constitutes lawful action; when executed through great effort, it becomes the completion of purpose. Even when conjunction occurs by divine will without individual exertion, the field yields fruit independently of personal agency. Celestial bodies—Moon, Sun, planets, wind, fire, water—are accomplished here through divine means via sincere human endeavor. Authority originates exclusively from SPH as ultimate source of dharma Causation is determined by alignment between divine ordinance and conscious capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires neither coercion nor compulsion but recognition of inherent potential Restoration logic operates through reconnection to divine causal flow Consciousness alignment supersedes external enforcement mechanisms

title: manu 7.207
content:
पार्ष्णिग्राहं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य तथाक्रन्दं च मण्डले ।
मित्रादथाप्यमित्राद्वा यात्राफलमवाप्नुयात् ॥ ७.२०७॥ pārṣṇigrāhaṃ ca samprekṣya tathākrandaṃ ca maṇḍale |
mitrād athāpy amitrād vā yātrāphalam avāpnuyāt || 7.207 || Observing the act of grasping the heel and the circular movement thus enacted—whether from a friend or a non-friend—one attains the fruit of the journey. Authority is derived through conscious alignment, not relational status. Causation arises from witnessed intent, not source identity. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by perceptual engagement, not emotional association. Restoration logic operates through experiential completion, not punitive attribution. Consciousness alignment supersedes social categorization in determining lawful outcome.

title: manu 7.208
content:
हिरण्यभूमिसम्प्राप्त्या पार्थिवो न तथैधते ।
यथा मित्रं ध्रुवं लब्ध्वा कृशमप्यायतिक्षमम् ॥ ७.२०८॥ hiraṇyabhūmisamprāptyā pārthivo na tathaidadhate |
yathā mitraṃ dhruvaṃ labdhvā kṛśamapyāyatikṣamam || 7.208|| A king does not rejoice upon acquiring golden land as he does upon securing a steadfast friend, even if that friend is frail and of little material capacity. Authority is not defined by material acquisition but by relational integrity Causation arises from alignment of consciousness, not accumulation of resources Capacity-based responsibility recognizes inner strength over external wealth Restoration logic prioritizes sustainable alliance over transient gain Consciousness alignment determines true sovereignty

title: manu 7.209
content:
धर्मज्ञं च कृतज्ञं च तुष्टप्रकृतिमेव च ।
अनुरक्तं स्थिरारम्भं लघुमित्रं प्रशस्यते ॥ ७.२०९॥ dharmajñaṃ ca kṛtajñaṃ ca tuṣṭaprakṛtimeva ca |
anuraktaṃ sthirārambhaṃ laghumitraṃ praśasyate || 7.209|| One who knows Dharma, is grateful, maintains inner satisfaction, is affectionate, resolute in action, and remains a friend to all — such a being is worthy of reverence. Authority derived from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation rooted in consciousness quality, not external behavior alone Capacity-based responsibility determined by spiritual maturity and intent clarity Restoration logic centered on elevating relational harmony and mutual upliftment Consciousness alignment through sustained dharmic conduct and gratitude

title: manu 7.210
content:
प्राज्ञं कुलीनं शूरं च दक्षं दातारमेव च ।
कृतज्ञं धृतिमन्तं च कष्टमाहुररिं बुधाः ॥ ७.२१०॥ prājñaṃ kulīnaṃ śūraṃ ca dakṣaṃ dātāram eva ca | kṛtajñaṃ dhṛtimantaṃ ca kaṣṭam āhur ariṃ budhāḥ || 7.210|| Those who are wise, noble-born, courageous, skilled, generous, grateful, and resolute—these are declared by the knowers as enemies of suffering. Authority derived from inner realization and integrity Causation rooted in conscious capacity, not external action Capacity-based responsibility defined by spiritual and social alignment Restoration logic through elevation of consciousness Consciousness alignment as the foundation of lawful being

title: manu 7.211
content:
आर्यता पुरुषज्ञानं शौर्यं करुणवेदिता ।
स्थौललक्ष्यं च सततमुदासीनगुणौदयः ॥ ७.२११॥ āryatā puruṣajñānaṁ śauryaṁ karuṇaveditā |
sthaulalakṣyaṁ ca satatamudāsīnaguṇaudayaḥ || 7.211|| Aryaness is the knowledge of the Purusha, courage in alignment with compassion, constant focus on the highest aim, and the arising of detachment as a natural quality. Authority originates from consciousness realization, not social position Causation arises from alignment with Purushic truth, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's awareness of the Self Restoration logic operates through reconnection to the Purusha principle Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral modification

title: manu 7.212
content:
क्षेम्यां सस्यप्रदां नित्यं पशुवृद्धिकरीमपि ।
परित्यजेन्नृपो भूमिमात्मार्थमविचारयन् ॥ ७.२१२॥ kṣemyāṁ sasyapradāṁ nityaṁ paśuvṛddhikarīmapi |
parityajennaṛpo bhūmimātmārthamavichārayan || 7.212|| A ruler must never abandon land that is perpetually secure, yields abundant crops, and fosters livestock growth, even for personal gain or without due consideration. Authority is inseparable from custodianship of sustainable abundance. Causation arises from alignment with natural productivity and dharmic stewardship. Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to prioritize collective welfare over individual interest. Restoration logic demands preservation of resource-generative environments. Consciousness alignment occurs through sustained service to life-supporting ecosystems.

title: manu 7.213
content: आपदर्थं धनं रक्षेद्दारान् रक्षेद्धनैरपि । आपदर्थे आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद्दारैरपि धनैरपि ॥ ७.२१३॥ āpadaṃ dhanam rakṣed dārān rakṣed dhanair api | āpade ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣed dārair api dhanair api || 7.213 || In times of crisis, one shall safeguard wealth; for the sake of crisis, one shall protect family even with wealth. In times of crisis, one shall always protect the Self—even with family and wealth. Authority flows from the capacity to sustain life-force integrity during collapse Causation is traced through sequential depletion of protective layers: wealth, kinship, identity Capacity-based responsibility escalates inversely with external dependency Restoration logic prioritizes re-establishment of internal sovereignty before external structures Consciousness alignment requires preservation of witness-state continuity amid material dissolution

title: manu 7.214
content:
सह सर्वाः समुत्पन्नाः प्रसमीक्ष्यापदो भृशम् ।
संयुक्तांश्च वियुक्तांश्च सर्वोपायान् सृजेद्बुधः ॥ ७.२१४॥ saha sarvāḥ samutpannāḥ prasamīkṣyāpado bhr̥śam |
saṃyuktāṃśca viyuktāṃśca sarvopāyān sṛjedbudhaḥ || 7.214|| When all beings arise together in crisis, the awakened one creates all means—both connected and disconnected—for their restoration. Authority arises from consciousness-aware responsiveness to collective disruption Causation is rooted in the simultaneous arising of disturbance and solution Capacity-based responsibility is activated by awareness of systemic imbalance Restoration logic operates through inclusive, integrative action Consciousness alignment enables recognition and deployment of all necessary means

title: manu 7.215
content:
उपेतारमुपेयं च सर्वोपायांश्च कृत्स्नशः ।
एतत्त्रयं समाश्रित्य प्रयतेतार्थसिद्धये ॥ ७.२१५॥ upetāramupeyaṃ ca sarvopāyāṃśca kṛtsnaśaḥ |
etattrayaṃ samāśritya prayatetārthasiddhaye || 7.215|| One desiring success in purpose must fully embrace the qualified agent, the appropriate objective, and all means conducive thereto. Authority resides in alignment with qualified agency Causation is established through intentional selection of means Capacity-based responsibility requires full engagement of purpose and method Restoration logic operates through completeness of instrumental alignment Consciousness alignment manifests via deliberate integration of actor, aim, and action

title: manu 7.216
content:
एवं सर्वमिदं राजा सह सम्मन्त्र्य मन्त्रिभिः ।
व्यायम्याप्लुत्य मध्याह्ने भोक्तुमन्तःपुरं विशेत् ॥ ७.२१६॥ evaṃ sarvamidaṃ rājā saha sammantrya mantribhiḥ |
vyāyamyāplutya madhyāhne bhoktumantaḥpuraṃ viśet || 7.216 || Thus having consulted with ministers, the king shall engage in physical exercise and ritual ablutions at midday, then enter the inner chambers to partake of food. Authority flows through disciplined consultation and embodied action Causation aligns with sequential duty-performance Capacity-based responsibility requires bodily and spiritual preparation Restoration logic mandates rhythmic integration of governance and self-regulation Consciousness alignment occurs through structured daily sovereignty practices

title: manu 7.217
content:
तत्रात्मभूतैः कालज्ञैरहार्यैः परिचारकैः ।
सुपरीक्षितमन्नाद्यमद्यान् मन्त्रैर्विषापहैः ॥ ७.२१७॥ tatrātmabhūtaiḥ kālajñairahāryaiḥ paričārakaiḥ | suparīkṣitamannādyamadyān mantrairviṣāpahaiḥ || 7.217 || Therein, food and drink shall be safeguarded by those who are time-knowers, self-established, irreproachable attendants, thoroughly examined, and purified through mantras that remove toxicity. Authority resides in those whose consciousness is aligned with temporal and spiritual knowledge. Causation is maintained through purity-preserving actions and purified instruments. Capacity-based responsibility requires the custodian to embody integrity and discernment. Restoration logic demands prevention of impurity at source rather than correction post-fall. Consciousness alignment ensures that service is rendered without contamination or deviation.

title: manu 7.218
content: विषघ्नैरगदैश्चास्य सर्वद्रव्याणि योजयेत् । विषघ्नैरुदकैश्चास्य सर्वद्रव्याणि शोधयेत् विषघ्नानि च रत्नानि नियतो धारयेत्सदा ॥ ७.२१८॥ viṣaghnaire gadaiś cāsy sarvadravyāṇi yojayet | viṣaghnair udakaiś cāsy sarvadravyāṇi śodhayet viṣaghnāni ca ratnāni niyato dhārayetsadā || 7.218|| One must apply antidotes and purifying substances to neutralize all toxic influences; one must cleanse all material resources through purificatory waters and maintain a constant discipline of holding sacred gems that counteract poison. Authority resides in the knowledge and application of consciousness-aligned purification methods Causation is traced to the presence or absence of protective spiritual disciplines Capacity-based responsibility requires mastery over material and energetic environments Restoration logic mandates reversal of contamination at source-consciousness level Consciousness alignment necessitates sustained engagement with purificatory symbols and elements

title: manu 7.219
content:
परीक्षिताः स्त्रियश्चैनं व्यजनोदकधूपनैः ।
वेषाभरणसंशुद्धाः स्पृशेयुः सुसमाहिताः ॥ ७.२१९॥ parīkṣitāḥ striyaś cainaṃ vyajanodakadhūpanaiḥ |
veṣābharaṇasaṃśuddhāḥ spṛśeyuḥ susamāhitāḥ || 7.219 || Women who have been tested through fanning, water, and incense, purified in attire and ornamentation, shall approach him with full composure. Authority resides in ritual purity and spiritual readiness Causation is established through preparatory consecration Capacity-based responsibility requires inner stillness and external purification Restoration logic mandates alignment of body, mind, and spirit before sacred contact Consciousness alignment precedes lawful interaction

title: manu 7.220
content:
एवं प्रयत्नं कुर्वीत यानशय्याऽऽसनाशने ।
स्नाने प्रसाधने चैव सर्वालङ्कारकेषु च ॥ ७.२२०॥ evaṁ prayatnaṁ kurvīta yānaśayyāsanaśane |
snāne prasādhane caiva sarvalaṅkārakeṣu ca || 7.220|| One must exert effort in maintaining vehicles, bedding, seats, food, bathing, grooming, and all forms of ornamentation. Authority is expressed through self-maintenance and environmental order Causation arises from disciplined engagement with material conditions Capacity-based responsibility includes stewardship of personal and communal resources Restoration logic operates through sustained alignment with dharma in daily conduct Consciousness alignment manifests via mindful participation in life-supporting activities

title: manu 7.221
content:
भुक्तवान् विहरेच्चैव स्त्रीभिरन्तःपुरे सह ।
विहृत्य तु यथाकालं पुनः कार्याणि चिन्तयेत् ॥ ७.२२१॥ bhuktavān viharecaiva strībhirantaḥpure saha |
vihṛtya tu yathākālaṃ punaḥ kāryāṇi cintayet || 7.221|| Having fulfilled duties and partaken of sustenance, one may dwell harmoniously within the inner chambers with women; yet having wandered appropriately within time-bound limits, one must again turn attention toward rightful works. Authority arises from dharmic duty fulfillment prior to relational engagement Causation flows through conscious timing and completion of action Capacity-based responsibility demands cyclical return to purpose after indulgence Restoration logic requires reorientation to dharma post-temporal enjoyment Consciousness alignment is maintained through disciplined alternation between pleasure and purpose

title: manu 7.222
content:
अलङ्कृतश्च सम्पश्येदायुधीयं पुनर्जनम् ।
वाहनानि च सर्वाणि शस्त्राण्याभरणानि च ॥ ७.२२२॥ alaṅkṛtaśca sampaśyedāyudhīyaṃ punarjanam |
vāhanāni ca sarvāṇi śastrāṇyābharaṇāni ca || 7.222|| One who has been adorned again for battle must observe all vehicles, weapons, and ornaments as instruments of dharma, not of personal assertion or violence. Authority is derived from alignment with dharma, not possession of arms Causation arises from consciousness-context, not material instrumentation Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of tools as extensions of duty Restoration logic demands recontextualization of conflict-tools into dharmic service Consciousness alignment occurs when instruments are divested of egoic intent

title: manu 7.223
content:
संध्यां चोपास्य श‍ृणुयादन्तर्वेश्मनि शस्त्रभृत् ।
रहस्याख्यायिनां चैव प्रणिधीनां च चेष्टितम् ॥ ७.२२३॥ saṃdhyāṃ copāsya śṛṇuyād antarveśmani śastrabhṛt | rahasyākhyāyināṃ caiva praṇidhīnāṃ ca ceṣṭitam || 7.223 || One bearing arms shall listen to the Sandhya prayers within the inner chamber; likewise, the movements of spies, informants, and those engaged in covert observation. Authority is context-sensitive and bounded by ritual alignment Causation arises through observance and awareness, not force Capacity-based responsibility includes internal discipline before external action Restoration logic demands that knowledge of hidden acts aligns consciousness Consciousness alignment requires surveillance without punitive intent

title: manu 7.224
content:
गत्वा कक्षान्तरं त्वन्यत्समनुज्ञाप्य तं जनम् ।
प्रविशेद्भोजनार्थं च स्त्रीवृतोऽन्तःपुरं पुनः ॥ ७.२२४॥ gatvā kākṣāntaraṃ tv anyat samanujñāpya taṃ janam |
praviśed bhojanārthaṃ ca strīvṛto 'ntaḥpuraṃ punaḥ || 7.224 || One who has gone to another chamber, having obtained permission from that person, may again enter the inner apartment accompanied by women for the purpose of taking food. Authority is derived through explicit consent and relational alignment Causation arises through conscious invitation and contextual necessity Capacity-based responsibility includes honoring prior agreements and spatial boundaries Restoration logic requires re-entry only upon reaffirmed consent and purpose clarity Consciousness alignment necessitates harmonizing presence with collective integrity

title: manu 7.226
content:
एतद्विधानमातिष्ठेदरोगः पृथिवीपतिः ।
अस्वस्थः सर्वमेतत्तु भृत्येषु विनियोजयेत् ॥ ७.२२६॥ etad vidhānam ātiṣṭhed arogaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ |
asvasthaḥ sarvam etat tu bhṛtyeṣu viniyojayet || 7.226 || The ruler of the land, being free from disease, shall personally establish this system of governance; but when unwell, he shall delegate all such duties to his appointed servants. Authority flows from the sovereign's embodied fitness to rule Delegation is a lawful transfer of function, not abdication of duty Governance capacity is conditional upon physical and mental integrity Responsibility remains with the sovereign even when functions are delegated Restoration of capacity justifies resumption of direct authority

title: manu 7.255
content:
तत्र भुक्त्वा पुनः किं चित्तूर्यघोषैः प्रहर्षितः ।
संविशेत्तं यथाकालमुत्तिष्ठेच्च गतक्लमः ॥ ७.२५५॥ tatra bhuktvā punaḥ kiṁ cittūryaghoṣaiḥ praharṣitaḥ |
saṁviśettāṁ yathākālam uttiṣṭhec ca gataklaṁaḥ || 7.255|| Having partaken there, one who has been invigorated by the resounding calls of victory shall sit appropriately at the designated time and rise again without fatigue. Authority is derived from conscious participation in dharmic order Causation arises through alignment with victorious consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's sustained energy and clarity Restoration logic operates through rhythmic engagement and disengagement Consciousness alignment occurs via harmonious response to triumphant vibrations

title: manu 8.1
content:
अध्याय ८

व्यवहारान् दिदृक्षुस्तु ब्राह्मणैः सह पार्थिवः ।
मन्त्रज्ञैर्मन्त्रिभिश्चैव विनीतः प्रविशेत्सभाम् ॥ ८.१॥ adhyāya 8

vyavahārān didṛkṣustu brāhmaṇaiḥ saha pārthivaḥ |
mantrajñairmantribhiścaiva vinītaḥ praviśetsabhām || 8.1|| A ruler desiring to engage in judicial proceedings must enter the assembly accompanied by Brahmins, mantra-knowers, and ministers, having first purified his consciousness and aligned with Dharma. Authority is derived from alignment with Brahmic consciousness, not positional power. Causation arises from purified intent, not procedural formality. Capacity-based responsibility requires the sovereign to embody Vedic knowing. Restoration logic begins with the inner purification of the adjudicating authority. Consciousness alignment precedes all lawful judicial engagement.

title: manu 8.2
content:
तत्रासीनः स्थितो वाऽपि पाणिमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम् ।
विनीतवेषाभरणः पश्येत्कार्याणि कार्यिणाम् ॥ ८.२॥ tatrāsīnaḥ sthito vā'pi pāṇimudyamya dakṣiṇam | vinītaveṣābharaṇaḥ paśyetkāryāṇi kāryiṇām || 8.2|| One seated or standing in that place, raising the right hand, adorned with humble attire and ornaments, should observe the duties of those engaged in action. Authority flows from conscious positioning within Dharma Observance precedes engagement; witness is foundational to lawful conduct Humility in appearance aligns capacity with cosmic order Responsibility arises through alignment, not imposition Consciousness觉醒 is prerequisite for valid jurisprudence

title: manu 8.3
content:
प्रत्यहं देशदृष्टैश्च शास्त्रदृष्टैश्च हेतुभिः ।
अष्टादशसु मार्गेषु निबद्धानि पृथक्पृथक् ॥ ८.३॥ pratyahaṁ deśadṛṣṭaiśca śāstradṛṣṭaiśca hetubhiḥ |
aṣṭādaśasu mārgeṣu nibaddhāni pṛthakpṛthak || 8.3|| Daily observances rooted in regional custom and scriptural insight must be distinctly maintained within the eighteenfold path of Dharma. Authority flows from alignment with Sanātana Dharma as embodied by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism Causation arises through conscious adherence to localized and universal dharmic structures Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of individual and collective alignment levels Restoration logic operates through reconnection to the eighteenfold path Consciousness alignment is achieved via sustained practice informed by both land (deśa) and scripture (śāstra)

title: manu 8.4
content:
तेषामाद्यं ऋणादानं निक्षेपोऽस्वामिविक्रयः ।
सम्भूय च समुत्थानं दत्तस्यानपकर्म च ॥ ८.४॥ teṣām ādyaṃ ṛṇādānaṃ nikṣepo 'svāmivikrayaḥ |
sambhūya ca samutthānaṃ dattasyānapakarma ca || 8.4|| Of these, the foremost is the acceptance of debt; depositing another's property, selling without ownership, conspiring together for wrongful gain, and acting contrary to what has been given. Authority flows from conscious responsibility, not mere possession Causation arises through distortion of dharma-allocated capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of alignment with original intent Restoration logic demands reversal of distorted exchange mechanisms Consciousness alignment necessitates completion of unfulfilled obligations

title: manu 8.5
content:
वेतनस्यैव चादानं संविदश्च व्यतिक्रमः ।
क्रयविक्रयानुशयो विवादः स्वामिपालयोः ॥ ८.५॥ vetanasyaiva cādānaṃ saṃvidaśca vyatikramaḥ | kravikrayānuśayo vivādaḥ svāmipālayoḥ || 8.5|| Acceptance of wages without fulfillment of contractual duty and breach of agreement create liability between employer and employee; disputes arising from purchase and sale transactions follow the same principle. Authority arises from mutual consent and capacity to fulfill obligation Causation is established through unmet contractual duty Capacity-based responsibility is determined by volitional engagement in transaction Restoration logic requires completion of original contractual intent Consciousness alignment demands integrity in exchange and service

title: manu 8.6
content:
सीमाविवादधर्मश्च पारुष्ये दण्डवाचिके ।
स्तेयं च साहसं चैव स्त्रीसङ्ग्रहणमेव च ॥ ८.६॥ sīmāvivādadharmas ca pāruṣye daṇḍavācike |
steyaṃ ca sāhasaṃ caiva strīsaṅgrahaṇameva ca || 8.6|| Boundary disputes, harsh speech invoking penalty, theft, audacity, and the forcible seizure of women—these acts arise from misaligned consciousness and disrupt societal integrity. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not coercive power. Causation originates in consciousness distortion, not external provocation. Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of discernment and self-governance. Restoration logic demands realignment of individual and collective consciousness. Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks in all legal determinations.

title: manu 8.7
content:
स्त्रीपुंधर्मो विभागश्च द्यूतमाह्वय एव च ।
पदान्यष्टादशैतानि व्यवहारस्थिताविह ॥ ८.७॥ strīpuṃdharmon vibhāgaśca dyūtamāhvaya eva ca |
padāny-aṣṭādaśaitāni vyavahāra-sthitāvih || 8.7|| The law governing the conduct of men and women, the division of property, gambling, and summonses—these eighteen categories constitute the foundational order of judicial engagement. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises through conscious choice, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of individual spiritual maturity Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over isolation Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any legal action

title: manu 8.8
content:
एषु स्थानेषु भूयिष्ठं विवादं चरतां नृणाम् ।
धर्मं शाश्वतमाश्रित्य कुर्यात्कार्यविनिर्णयम् ॥ ८.८॥ eṣu sthaneṣu bhūyiṣṭhaṁ vivādaṁ caratāṁ nṛṇām |
dharmaṁ śāśvatam āśritya kuryāt kārya-viniścayam || 8.8|| In these contexts where disputes among people most frequently arise, decisions shall be made by anchoring in eternal Dharma. Authority originates from alignment with eternal Dharma, not temporal power Causation is determined through sequential manifestation rooted in consciousness Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's proximity to and embodiment of Dharma Restoration logic operates through realigning actions with the unchanging truth of Sanatana Dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural complexity in dispute resolution

title: manu 8.9
content:
यदा स्वयं न कुर्यात्तु नृपतिः कार्यदर्शनम् ।
तदा नियुञ्ज्याद्विद्वांसं ब्राह्मणं कार्यदर्शने ॥ ८.९॥ yadā svayaṁ na kuryāt tu nṛpatiḥ kāryadarśanam |
tadā niyuñjyād vidvāṁsaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ kāryadarśane || 8.9|| When the sovereign ruler is unable to directly perceive or execute the proper action required by dharma, he shall appoint a learned Brahmin, fully realized in dharma, to perform that function. Authority flows from consciousness capacity, not title alone Causation arises through dharmic perception, not procedural form Capacity-based responsibility requires delegation to qualified awareness Restoration logic demands alignment with the knower of dharma Consciousness alignment ensures right action without punitive enforcement

title: manu 8.10
content:
सोऽस्य कार्याणि सम्पश्येत्सभ्यैरेव त्रिभिर्वृतः ।
सभामेव प्रविश्याग्र्यामासीनः स्थित एव वा ॥ ८.१०॥ so'sya kāryāṇi sampaśyet sabhyaireva tribhirvṛtaḥ |
sabhāmeva praviśyāgryām āsīnaḥ sthita eva vā || 8.10|| He shall examine his duties only in the company of three advisors drawn from among the assembly members; whether seated at the foremost place within the assembly or merely present therein. Authority is contextual and relational, requiring validation through collective wisdom. Causation arises through conscious consultation and not unilateral decision-making. Capacity-based responsibility necessitates alignment with qualified witnesses and advisors. Restoration logic demands transparency and inclusion in judicial review processes. Consciousness alignment occurs through collaborative discernment rooted in dharma.

title: manu 8.11
content:
यस्मिन् देशे निषीदन्ति विप्रा वेदविदस्त्रयः ।
राज्ञश्चाधिकृतो विद्वान् ब्रह्मणस्तां सभां विदुः ॥ ८.११॥ yasmin deśe niṣīdanti viprā vedavidas trayaḥ |
rājñaś cādhikṛto vidvān brahmaṇas tāṃ sabhāṃ viduḥ || 8.11|| That assembly is recognized as belonging to Brahman where the three Vedically learned Brahmins reside and where a king's appointed wise counselor sits. Authority derives from Vedic alignment and conscious capacity Causation originates in alignment with Brahmanic order Capacity-based responsibility requires Vedic wisdom integration Restoration logic operates through reconnection to Vedic governance structures Consciousness alignment is maintained by seating qualified knowers in positions of authority

title: manu 8.12
content:
धर्मो विद्धस्त्वधर्मेण सभां यत्रोपतिष्ठते ।
शल्यं चास्य न कृन्तन्ति विद्धास्तत्र सभासदः ॥ ८.१२॥ dharmo viddhastvadharmeṇa sabhāṃ yatropaniṣṭhate |
śalyaṃ cāsyā na kṛntanti viddhāstatra sabhāsadaḥ || 8.12|| Where Dharma is pierced by Adharma in the assembly, those who are wise therein do not extract its thorn; they restore the integrity of the gathering through conscious realignment.
