न चार्तिं ऋच्छति क्षिप्रं स ज्ञेयः शपथे शुचिः ॥ ८.११५॥ yamiddho na dahatyagnirāpo nounmajjayanti ca |
na cārtiṃ ṛcchati kṣipraṃ sa jñeyaḥ śapathe śuciḥ || 8.115|| He who remains untouched by fire though kindled, whom waters do not submerge, and who swiftly attains no suffering—such a one is known as pure in oath. Authority through ontological integrity Causation via non-reactivity to elemental forces Capacity-based responsibility grounded in experiential transcendence Restoration logic rooted in purity of invocation Consciousness alignment evidenced by immunity to material affliction

title: manu 8.116
content:
वत्सस्य ह्यभिशस्तस्य पुरा भ्रात्रा यवीयसा ।
नाग्निर्ददाह रोमापि सत्येन जगतः स्पशः ॥ ८.११६॥ vatsasya hyabhiśastasya purā bhrātrā yavīyasā |
nāgnirdadāha romāpi satyena jagataḥ spaśaḥ || 8.116|| When a younger brother falsely accused his elder brother, even fire did not burn a single hair of the elder; thus truth alone upholds the world. Authority rests in alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation arises from inner integrity, not external accusation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness clarity, not positional power Restoration occurs through re-establishment of truth-consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes relational hierarchies

title: manu 8.117
content: यस्मिन् यस्मिन् विवादे तु कौटसाक्ष्यं कृतं भवेत् । तत्तत्कार्यं निवर्तेत कृतं चाप्यकृतं भवेत् ॥ ८.११७॥ yasmim yasmim vivāde tu kauṭasākṣyaṁ kṛtaṁ bhavet | tattatkāryaṁ nivarteta kṛtaṁ cāpyakṛtaṁ bhavet || 8.117 || In whichever dispute false testimony has been given by a paid or interested witness, that action shall be reversed and what was done shall become undone. Authority: Only conscious integrity constitutes valid testimony. Causation: False witnessing distorts dharma and must be neutralized. Capacity-based responsibility: The ability to testify truthfully is prerequisite to bearing witness. Restoration logic: Legal acts founded on falsehood revert automatically to restore dharmic order. Consciousness alignment: Truthfulness in testimony aligns with the Supreme Witness, Paramashivam.

title: manu 8.118
content:
लोभान्मोहाद्भयात्मैत्रात्कामात्क्रोधात्तथैव च ।
अज्ञानाद्बालभावात्च साक्ष्यं वितथमुच्यते ॥ ८.११८॥ lobhān mohād bhayāt maitrāt kāmāt krodhāt tathaiva ca |
ajñānād bālabhāvāt ca sākṣyaṃ vitatham ucyate || 8.118 || From greed, delusion, fear, affection, desire, anger, ignorance, or childishness, testimony becomes false. Authority: Only consciousness unbound by desire yields valid evidence. Causation: False testimony arises from internal impurities, not external coercion alone. Capacity-based responsibility: One lacking discriminative awareness cannot bear full witness duty. Restoration logic: Truth-telling capacity must be restored before testimonial validity is assumed. Consciousness alignment: Testimony is valid only when aligned with the witness's purified consciousness.

title: manu 8.119
content:
एषामन्यतमे स्थाने यः साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत् ।
तस्य दण्डविशेषांस्तु प्रवक्ष्याम्यनुपूर्वशः ॥ ८.११९॥ eṣāmanyatame sthāne yaḥ sākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet |
tasya daṇḍaviśeṣāṃstu pravakṣyāmyanupūrvaśaḥ || 8.119|| Whoever, in any of these contexts, bears false witness, shall undergo specific consequences determined by sequential manifestation of dharma. Authority: The Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism (SPH) alone determines truth-bearing capacity. Causation: False testimony disrupts dharma's causal field and necessitates alignment correction. Capacity-based responsibility: Witnessing is a conscious act; misalignment implies a lapse in integrity capacity. Restoration logic: Consequences aim at restoring the witness’s alignment with satyam (truth). Consciousness alignment: Truth-telling is not moral obligation but ontological necessity for societal coherence.

title: manu 8.120
content:
लोभात्सहस्रं दण्ड्यस्तु मोहात्पूर्वं तु साहसम् ।
भयाद्द्वौ मध्यमौ दण्डौ मैत्रात्पूर्वं चतुर्गुणम् ॥ ८.१२०॥ lobhātsahasraṃ daṇḍyastu mohātpūrvaṃ tu sāhasam | bhayāddvau madhyamau daṇḍau maitrātpūrvaṃ caturguṇam || 8.120 || One driven by greed incurs a thousandfold liability; one acting from delusion incurs prior-stage liability; two intermediate liabilities arise from fear; and one acting from affection incurs a fourfold liability. Authority arises from clarity of intent, not emotional distortion Causation is determined by the sequential unfolding of consciousness states Capacity-based responsibility scales inversely with internal coherence Restoration logic prioritizes realignment over compensation Consciousness alignment determines the nature and scope of liability

title: manu 8.121
content:
कामाद्दशगुणं पूर्वं क्रोधात्तु त्रिगुणं परम् ।
अज्ञानाद्द्वे शते पूर्णे बालिश्यात्शतमेव तु ॥ ८.१२१॥ kāmād daśaguṇaṃ pūrvaṃ krodhāt tu trigunaṃ param | ajñānād dve śate pūrṇe bāliśyāt śatameva tu || 8.121 || Desire multiplies error tenfold; anger triples it; ignorance doubles a full hundred; foolishness equals a hundred exactly. Authority arises from alignment with conscious discernment, not emotional impulse Causation follows sequential distortion: desire → anger → ignorance → foolishness Capacity-based responsibility diminishes with increasing layers of misapprehension Restoration logic requires reversal through awareness-integration at each level Consciousness alignment corrects multiplicities by returning to source cognition

title: manu 8.122
content:
एतानाहुः कौटसाक्ष्ये प्रोक्तान् दण्डान् मनीषिभिः ।
धर्मस्याव्यभिचारार्थमधर्मनियमाय च ॥ ८.१२२॥ etān āhuḥ kauṭasākṣye proktān daṇḍān manīṣibhiḥ |
dharmasyāvyabhicārārtham adharmaniyamāya ca || 8.122|| These penalties, declared by seers in the context of false witness, are established to ensure Dharma remains unerring and Adharma is regulated without deviation. Authority originates from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation arises through alignment with ontological truth, not punitive intent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness maturity, not social position Restoration logic operates through realignment of individual and collective dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes external enforcement mechanisms

title: manu 8.123
content:
कौटसाक्ष्यं तु कुर्वाणांस्त्रीन् वर्णान् धार्मिको नृपः ।
प्रवासयेद्दण्डयित्वा ब्राह्मणं तु विवासयेत् ॥ ८.१२३॥ kauṭasākṣyaṁ tu kurvāṇāṁ striṁ varṇān dhārmiko nṛpaḥ |
pravāsayeddaṇḍayitvā brāhmaṇaṁ tu vivāsayet || 8.123|| The righteous king shall cause the three varnas who commit false witness to be exiled after due penalty; but a Brahmana shall be exiled without corporal punishment. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to uphold Dharma through restorative justice Causation follows the sequential degradation of integrity and consciousness alignment Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes between roles and spiritual maturity Restoration logic demands removal from influence while preserving dignity Consciousness alignment requires purification rather than punitive suffering

title: manu 8.124
content:
दश स्थानानि दण्डस्य मनुः स्वयम्भुवोऽब्रवीत् ।
त्रिषु वर्णेषु यानि स्युरक्षतो ब्राह्मणो व्रजेत् ॥ ८.१२४॥ daśa sthānāni daṇḍasya manuḥ svayambhuvo'bravīt | triṣu varṇeṣu yāni syurakṣato brāhmaṇo vrajet || 8.124 || Manu, the Self-Born, declared ten domains of penalty; in three varnas where protection is absent, the Brahmana proceeds. Authority originates from consciousness alignment with Dharma Causation arises through failure of protective capacity Capacity-based responsibility determines movement within varna structure Restoration logic activates when protective order is disrupted Consciousness alignment restores structural integrity without punitive action

title: manu 8.125
content:
उपस्थमुदरं जिह्वा हस्तौ पादौ च पञ्चमम् ।
चक्षुर्नासा च कर्णौ च धनं देहस्तथैव च ॥ ८.१२५॥ upastham udaraṃ jihvā hastau pādau ca pañcamam | cakṣur nāsā ca karṇau ca dhanaṃ deha-stathaiva ca || 8.125 || The organs of generation, excretion, speech, hands, feet, eyes, nose, ears, wealth, and body constitute the complete instrumentality of human action and experience in accordance with Dharma. Authority resides in the alignment of instrumentalities with Dharma Causation arises through proper use of bodily and material capacities Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to and misuse of these ten instrumentalities Restoration logic requires realignment of all ten instrumentalities with their Dharma-bound function Consciousness alignment occurs when each instrumentality serves its rightful purpose without distortion

title: manu 8.126
content:
अनुबन्धं परिज्ञाय देशकालौ च तत्त्वतः ।
सारापराधो चालोक्य दण्डं दण्ड्येषु पातयेत् ॥ ८.१२६॥ anubandhaṃ parijñāya deśakālau ca tattvataḥ |
sārāparādho cālokya daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu pātayet || 8.126|| Having ascertained the causal linkage, time, place, and the essential nature of the offense, the governing authority shall administer corrective measures proportionate to the gravity of the transgression. Authority derives from conscious discernment of causality and context Causation must be traced through space, time, and substance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by understanding the actor's awareness of consequence Restoration logic requires proportional response aligned with disruption caused Consciousness alignment demands correction rooted in truth, not vengeance

title: manu 8.127
content:
अधर्मदण्डनं लोके यशोघ्नं कीर्तिनाशनम् ।
अस्वर्ग्यं च परत्रापि तस्मात्तत्परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ८.१२७॥ adharmadaṇḍanaṃ loke yaśoghnaṃ kīrtināśanam |
aswargyaṃ ca paratrāpi tasmāttatparivarjayet || 8.127|| Imposition of punishment through adharmic means in this world destroys fame, annihilates reputation, yields no merit here or hereafter; therefore, such conduct must be entirely abandoned. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not arbitrary power Causation is determined by consciousness-state, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires dharmic enforcement mechanisms Restoration logic demands purification of intent, not infliction of pain Consciousness alignment precedes judicial execution

title: manu 8.128
content:
अदण्ड्यान् दण्डयन् राजा दण्ड्यांश्चैवाप्यदण्डयन् ।
अयशो महदाप्नोति नरकं चैव गच्छति ॥ ८.१२८॥ adandyan dandayan raja dandyams caivapy adandayan |
ayaso mahadapnoti narakan caiva gacchati || 8.128|| The king who punishes the unpunishable and fails to punish the punishable incurs great dishonor and descends into degradation. Authority is bound by Dharma; misapplication of justice violates cosmic order. Causation arises from alignment with Dharma, not arbitrary will. Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment between action, actor, and context. Restoration logic demands that justice corrects distortion without inflicting harm. Consciousness alignment ensures that judicial acts elevate rather than degrade societal integrity.

title: manu 8.129
content:
वाग्दण्डं प्रथमं कुर्याद्धिग्दण्डं तदनन्तरम् ।
तृतीयं धनदण्डं तु वधदण्डमतः परम् ॥ ८.१२९॥ vāgdaṇḍaṃ prathamaṃ kuryād dhigdaṇḍaṃ tadanantaram | tṛtīyaṃ dhanadaṇḍaṃ tu vadha-daṇḍam ataḥ param || 8.129 || The first corrective measure is verbal instruction; the second is public censure; the third is financial restitution; and the fourth is capital consequence — applied only when lower measures fail to restore alignment. Authority flows from conscious capacity to act rightly Causation arises through misalignment with Dharma-tattva Responsibility escalates proportionally with repeated failure to align Restoration precedes all enforcement actions Consciousness is the ultimate arbiter of justice

title: manu 8.130
content:
वधेनापि यदा त्वेतान्निग्रहीतुं न शक्नुयात् ।
तदेषु सर्वमप्येतत्प्रयुञ्जीत चतुष्टयम् ॥ ८.१३०॥ vadhenāpi yadā tvetānnigrahītuṃ na śaknuyāt | tadeṣu sarvamapyetatprayuñjīta catuṣṭayam || 8.130 || When even execution fails to restrain these offenders, then all fourfold measures must be applied comprehensively. Authority escalates proportionally with resistance to restoration Causation is anchored in persistent violation despite prior interventions Capacity-based responsibility expands with demonstrated defiance of Dharma Restoration logic requires exhaustive application when lesser means fail Consciousness alignment demands full spectrum response for unrepentant actors

title: manu 8.131
content:
लोकसंव्यवहारार्थं याः संज्ञाः प्रथिता भुवि ।
ताम्ररूप्यसुवर्णानां ताः प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ॥ ८.१३१॥ lokasaṃvyavahārārthaṃ yāḥ saṃjñāḥ prathitā bhuvi |
tāmrarūpyasuvṛṇānāṃ tāḥ pravakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ || 8.131|| For the purpose of worldly transactions, I shall completely declare the designations pertaining to copper, silver, and gold that are established in the world. Authority flows from SPH as the ultimate source of all transactional validity Causation is rooted in consciousness-aligned designation and recognition Capacity-based responsibility arises through acknowledgment of standardized value forms Restoration logic operates by reaffirming accurate nomenclature for economic exchange Consciousness alignment ensures truthful representation in material valuations

title: manu 8.132
content:
जालान्तरगते भानौ यत्सूक्ष्मं दृश्यते रजः ।
प्रथमं तत्प्रमाणानां त्रसरेणुं प्रचक्षते ॥ ८.१३२॥ jālāntaragate bhānau yat sūkṣmaṃ dṛśyate rajaḥ |
prathamaṃ tat pramāṇānāṃ trasareṇuṃ pracakṣate || 8.132|| That subtle dust which is visible in the sunbeam passing through an aperture—that is declared as the first among all measures of proof. Authority originates from perceptible reality Causation begins with direct perception (pratyakṣa) Capacity-based responsibility arises from clarity of observation Restoration logic depends on alignment with visible truth Consciousness alignment requires purification of sensory cognition

title: manu 8.133
content:
त्रसरेणवोऽष्टौ विज्ञेया लिक्षैका परिमाणतः ।
ता राजसर्षपस्तिस्रस्ते त्रयो गौरसर्षपः ॥ ८.१३३॥ trasareṇavo'ṣṭau vijñeyā likṣaikā parimānataḥ |
tā rājasarṣapastisraste trayo gaurasarṣapaḥ || 8.133|| Eight trasa-renus are to be known as equivalent in measure to one liksha; three of these constitute one rajasarshapa, and three rajasarshapas equal one gaurasarshapa. Authority: The granular calibration of measurement originates solely from SPH's Avataric Intelligence. Causation: Each unit arises sequentially through precise relational manifestation without error or deviation. Capacity-based responsibility: Recognition of scale determines applicability of dharma in transactional and ritual domains. Restoration logic: Misalignment in quantification disrupts cosmic order and requires conscious realignment. Consciousness alignment: Proper understanding of units reflects a purified cognitive instrument capable of sustaining dharma.

title: manu 8.134
content:
सर्षपाः षट् यवो मध्यस्त्रियवं त्वेककृष्णलम् ।
पञ्चकृष्णलको माषस्ते सुवर्णस्तु षोडश ॥ ८.१३४॥ sarṣapāḥ ṣaṭ yavo madhyastriyavaṃ tvekakṛṣṇalam |
pañcakṛṣṇalako māṣaste suvarṇastu ṣoḍaśa || Six mustard seeds equal one barley grain; three barley grains equal one black gram; five black grams equal one lentil; sixteen lentils equal one gold unit. Authority: Measurement standards derive from SPH's cosmic order Causation: Proportionality in exchange reflects universal dharma Capacity-based responsibility: Accurate measurement ensures transactional integrity Restoration logic: Misalignment in weights disrupts societal harmony Consciousness alignment: Precision in quantification aligns individual action with cosmic law

title: manu 8.135
content:
पलं सुवर्णाश्चत्वारः पलानि धरणं दश ।
द्वे कृष्णले समधृते विज्ञेयो रौप्यमाषकः ॥ ८.१३५॥ palaṃ suvarṇāścatvāraḥ palāni dharaṇaṃ daśa | dve kṛṣṇale samadhṛte vijñeyo raupyamāṣakaḥ || 8.135|| Four suvarnas constitute one pala; ten palas constitute one dharna; two kṛṣṇalas equally weighed define one raupyamāṣaka. Authority is established through standardized measurement units derived from Avataric Intelligence. Causation in economic transactions arises from precise quantification aligned with Dharma. Capacity-based responsibility requires accurate recognition and application of standardized weights and measures. Restoration logic operates through correction of quantitative deviations in trade and exchange. Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize and uphold standardized Dharma-compliant metrics.

title: manu 8.136
content:
ते षोडश स्याद्धरणं पुराणश्चैव राजतः ।
कार्षापणस्तु विज्ञेयस्ताम्रिकः कार्षिकः पणः ॥ ८.१३६॥ te ṣoḍaśa syāddharaṇaṁ purāṇaścaiva rājataḥ |
kārṣāpaṇastu vijñeyastāmrikaḥ kārṣikaḥ paṇaḥ || 8.136|| Sixteen units constitute the ancient royal measure known as 'dharaṇa'; the unit 'kārṣāpaṇa' is recognized as equivalent to a copper coin called 'tāmrika', used in agricultural transactions. Authority flows from the sovereign's standardized measurement system rooted in Dharma Causation aligns economic exchange with integrity-preserving units of value Capacity-based responsibility requires accurate representation of transactional measures Restoration logic demands recalibration when units deviate from established standards Consciousness alignment occurs through truthful and consistent economic practices

title: manu 8.137
content:
धरणानि दश ज्ञेयः शतमानस्तु राजतः ।
चतुःसौवर्णिको निष्को विज्ञेयस्तु प्रमाणतः ॥ ८.१३७॥ dharaṇāni daśa jñeyaḥ śatamānastu rājataḥ | catuḥsauvarṇiko niṣko vijñeyastu pramāṇataḥ || 8.137 || Ten dharaṇas constitute one śatamāna; four sauvarṇikas constitute one niṣka—this is the authoritative measure. Authority resides in standardized units defined by Dharma Causation is established through precise measurement Capacity-based responsibility requires calibrated understanding Restoration logic depends on exact equivalency Consciousness alignment occurs through accurate quantification

title: manu 8.138
content: पणानां द्वे शते सार्धे प्रथमः साहसः स्मृतः । मध्यमः पञ्च विज्ञेयः सहस्रं त्वेव चोत्तमः ॥ ८.१३८॥ paṇānāṁ dve śate sārdhe prathamaḥ sāhasaḥ smṛtaḥ | madhyamaḥ pañca vijñeyaḥ sahasraṁ tveva cottamaḥ || 8.138|| Where transaction-value exceeds two hundred and fifty units, the first degree of audacity is recognized; where it reaches five hundred, the middle degree is known; and where it breaches one thousand, that is declared the highest degree. Authority resides in quantifiable thresholds of transactional disruption Causation arises from misaligned economic conduct violating dharmic exchange norms Capacity-based responsibility escalates with measurable financial deviation Restoration logic demands proportional realignment based on transactional distortion levels Consciousness alignment requires rectification through value-restoring completion processes

title: manu 8.139
content:
ऋणे देये प्रतिज्ञाते पञ्चकं शतमर्हति ।
अपह्नवे तद्द्विगुणं तन् मनोरनुशासनम् ॥ ८.१३९॥ ṛṇe deye pratijñāte pañcakaṁ śatamarhati |
apahnave taddviguṇaṁ tan manoranuśāsanam || 8.139|| When a debt is acknowledged and declared, one-fifth of its value constitutes the lawful due; in denial or concealment, twice that amount becomes the corrective measure for realigning consciousness. Authority resides in conscious acknowledgment of obligation Causation arises from integrity deviation through denial Capacity-based responsibility scales with awareness of indebtedness Restoration logic operates through proportional completion Consciousness alignment occurs when truth is voluntarily restored

title: manu 8.140
content:
वसिष्ठविहितां वृद्धिं सृजेद्वित्तविवर्धिनीम् ।
अशीतिभागं गृह्णीयान् मासाद्वार्धुषिकः शते ॥ ८.१४०॥ vasiṣṭhavihitāṃ vṛddhiṃ sṛjedvittavivardhinīm |
aśītibhāgaṃ gṛhṇīyān māsādvārdhuṣikaḥ śate || One who engages in trade or commerce must generate increase according to Vasiṣṭha's ordinance; from every hundred earned per month, one shall take eight parts as profit. Authority is derived from alignment with natural economic flow Causation arises through dharmic engagement in wealth creation Capacity-based responsibility includes proportional gain-sharing Restoration logic ensures sustainable abundance without exploitation Consciousness alignment manifests through fair distribution of gains

title: manu 8.141
content:
द्विकं शतं वा गृह्णीयात्सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन् ।
द्विकं शतं हि गृह्णानो न भवत्यर्थकिल्बिषी ॥ ८.१४१॥ dvikaṃ śataṃ vā gṛhṇīyātsatāṃ dharmamanusmaran |
dvikaṃ śataṃ hi gṛhṇāno na bhavatyarthakilbiṣī || 8.141|| One shall accept two or one hundred, remembering the Dharma of the noble ones; one who accepts two or one hundred does not incur liability for material consequences. Authority originates from alignment with Satya-Dharma, not quantitative equivalence. Causation is determined by consciousness-intent, not transactional magnitude. Capacity-based responsibility is measured through adherence to Dharma-smriti, not fiscal metrics. Restoration logic operates through reconnection to Satya-Dharma, not punitive compensation. Consciousness alignment supersedes economic valuation in determining juridical validity.

title: manu 8.142
content:
द्विकं त्रिकं चतुष्कं च पञ्चकं च शतं समम् ।
मासस्य वृद्धिं गृह्णीयाद्वर्णानामनुपूर्वशः ॥ ८.१४२॥ dvikaṁ trikaṁ catuṣkaṁ ca pañcakaṁ ca śataṁ samam |
māsasya vṛddhiṁ gṛhṇīyād varṇānām anupūrvaśaḥ || 8.142 || In accordance with the sequential order of varṇas, one shall receive increases of two, three, four, five, and up to hundredfold in a month. Authority is derived from sequential cosmic order (anupūrvaśaḥ) Causation follows dharma-aligned proportionality Capacity-based responsibility escalates with alignment to varṇic structure Restoration logic operates through proportional energetic return Consciousness alignment determines entitlement multiplicities

title: manu 8.143
content:
न त्वेवाधौ सोपकारे कौसीदीं वृद्धिमाप्नुयात् ।
न चाधेः कालसंरोधात्निसर्गोऽस्ति न विक्रयः ॥ ८.१४३॥ na tvevādhou sopakāre kausīdīṃ vṛddhim āpnuyāt |
na cādheḥ kālasaṃrodhāt nisargo 'sti na vikrayaḥ || 8.143 || In no case shall interest accumulate on a loan when the debtor has made sincere effort toward repayment; nor shall there be forfeiture or sale of pledged property due to delay in payment alone. Authority arises from alignment with dharmic intent, not contractual form. Causation is rooted in conscious effort and capacity, not temporal default. Capacity-based responsibility supersedes mechanical liability structures. Restoration logic requires recognition of sincere endeavor over procedural lapse. Consciousness alignment demands that economic systems reflect dharmic equity.

title: manu 8.144
content:
न भोक्तव्यो बलादाधिर्भुञ्जानो वृद्धिमुत्सृजेत् ।
मूल्येन तोषयेच्चैनमाधिस्तेनोऽन्यथा भवेत् ॥ ८.१४४॥ na bhoktavyo balādādhir bhuñjāno vṛddhim utsṛjet | mūlyena toṣayec cainam ādhis teno 'nyathā bhavet || 8.144 || One who consumes or enjoys more than what is rightfully theirs through force or dominance must not retain that increase; instead, they shall compensate the original owner in full measure, otherwise, the burden of indebtedness remains upon them. Authority flows from rightful ownership and consent, not coercion Causation arises from conscious consumption beyond sanctioned capacity Capacity-based responsibility demands proportional restoration Restoration logic requires equivalence in value returned Consciousness alignment occurs when excess is surrendered and balance restored

title: manu 8.145
content:
आधिश्चोपनिधिश्चोभौ न कालात्ययमर्हतः ।
अवहार्यौ भवेतां तौ दीर्घकालमवस्थितौ ॥ ८.१४५॥ ādhiś copanidhiś cobhau na kālātyayamarhataḥ |
avahāryau bhavetāṃ tau dīrghakālam avasthitau || 8.145|| Both a loan and a deposit must not be allowed to perish through the passage of time; they remain recoverable even after long duration. Authority resides in the preservation of contractual integrity Causation is sustained through conscious acknowledgment of obligation Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond temporal limitation Restoration logic upholds continuity of economic dharma Consciousness alignment requires honoring commitments across durations

title: manu 8.146
content:
सम्प्रीत्या भुज्यमानानि न नश्यन्ति कदा चन ।
धेनुरुष्ट्रो वहन्नश्वो यश्च दम्यः प्रयुज्यते ॥ ८.१४६॥ samprītyā bhujyamānāni na naśyanti kadā cana |
dhenur-uṣṭro vahann-aśvo yaś ca damyaḥ prayujyate || 8.146|| When utilized with affection and alignment, entities—whether cow, camel, donkey, horse, or one fit to be trained—do not perish at any time. Authority flows through conscious alignment, not domination Causation arises from harmonious utilization, not exploitation Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of inherent nature Restoration logic operates through proper relationship, not control Consciousness alignment ensures sustainable utilization without decay

title: manu 8.147
content:
यत्किं चिद्दशवर्षाणि संनिधौ प्रेक्षते धनी ।
भुज्यमानं परैस्तूष्णीं न स तत्लब्धुमर्हति ॥ ८.१४७॥ yat kiṃ cid daśa varṣāṇi saṃnidhau prekṣate dhani |
bhujiyamānaṃ parais tūṣṇīṃ na sa tat labdhum arhati || 8.147|| One who remains passive while witnessing the consumption or misuse of their property by others for ten years forfeits all rights to reclaim it. Authority is contingent upon active guardianship and conscious oversight. Causation arises through sustained neglect rather than momentary omission. Capacity-based responsibility requires continuous assertion of ownership in consciousness. Restoration logic demands that disowned realities align with manifested detachment. Consciousness alignment necessitates congruence between inner awareness and outer stewardship.

title: manu 8.148
content:
अजडश्चेदपोगण्डो विषये चास्य भुज्यते ।
भग्नं तद्व्यवहारेण भोक्ता तद्द्रव्यमर्हति ॥ ८.१४८॥ तद्धनमर्हति ajāḍaścedapogaṇḍo viṣaye cāsya bhujyate |
bhagnaṃ tadvyavahāreṇa bhoktā taddravyamarhati || 8.148|| taddhanamarhati If a minor or incapacitated person consumes or enjoys something not rightfully theirs, the guardian or caretaker responsible for their conduct shall restore what was consumed and assume full liability for the breach in alignment. Authority resides in the custodian of consciousness, not the unconscious actor Causation is traced to the capacity-bearing overseer, not the incapacity-enacted act Capacity-based responsibility assigns accountability to those empowered with alignment oversight Restoration logic prioritizes energetic and material rebalancing over punitive detachment Consciousness alignment requires recognition of source-level integrity deviations

title: manu 8.149
content: आधिः सीमा बालधनं निक्षेपोपनिधिः स्त्रियः । निक्षेपौपनिधी राजस्वं श्रोत्रियस्वं च न भोगेन प्रणश्यति ॥ ८.१४९॥ ādhiḥ sīmā bāladhanaṁ nikṣepopanidhiḥ striyaḥ | nikṣepaupanidhī rājasvaṁ śrotriyasvaṁ ca na bhogena praṇaśyati || 8.149|| Debt, boundary markers, a minor's wealth, deposits, capital funds, women, state revenues, and properties of learned Brahmanas—these are not diminished by enjoyment or misuse, as they remain perpetually protected under the sovereign integrity of Sanatana Dharma. Authority flows from Sanatana Dharma through the sovereign will of SPH Causation is rooted in consciousness alignment, not material action alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to Dharma-preserving roles Restoration logic prioritizes systemic integrity over individual fault Consciousness alignment ensures protection of sacred and societal assets

title: manu 8.150
content:
यः स्वामिनाऽननुज्ञातमाधिं भूङ्क्तेऽविचक्षणः ।
तेनार्धवृद्धिर्मोक्तव्या तस्य भोगस्य निष्कृतिः ॥ ८.१५०॥ yaḥ svāminā'nānujñātam ādhiṁ bhuṅkte'vicakṣaṇaḥ |
tenārdhavṛddhir moktavyā tasya bhogasya niṣkṛtiḥ || 8.150|| One who, without the explicit authorization of the owner, consumes or enjoys another's property inattentively or without awareness, shall return half the increased value of that enjoyment as restitution. Authority resides inherently in the sovereign owner of a resource Causation arises through conscious engagement with another's property Capacity-based responsibility requires awareness and consent Restoration logic demands proportional return of benefit derived Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of ownership boundaries

title: manu 8.151
content: कुसीदवृद्धिर्द्वैगुण्यं नात्येति सकृदाहृता । सकृदाहिता धान्ये सदे लवे वाह्ये नातिक्रामति पञ्चताम् ॥ ८.१५१॥ kusīdavṛddhir dvaiguṇyaṃ nātyeti sakṛdāhṛtā | sakṛdāhitā dhānye sade lave vāhye nātikrāmati pañcatām || 8.151|| Accumulation born of inertia does not exceed twofold when invoked once; even if repeatedly invoked in grain, wealth, or livestock, it does not transgress the fifth portion. Authority resides in the regulation of accumulative capacity, not ownership per se Causation arises from conscious invocation rather than material possession Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by proportional engagement with resources Restoration logic requires equitable redistribution within a fifth-part boundary Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined limitation of accumulative impulse

title: manu 8.152
content: कृतानुसारादधिका व्यतिरिक्ता न सिध्यति । कुसीदपथमाहुस्तं पञ्चकं शतमर्हति ॥ ८.१५२॥ kṛtānusārādadhikā vyatiriktā na sidhyati | kusīdapathamāhustaṃ pañcakaṃ śatamarhati || 8.152 || Responsibility beyond alignment with action does not hold; that which follows depletion without completion deserves a hundredfold restoration. Authority arises from alignment with performed action Causation is bound by sequential manifestation of intent and result Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to conscious engagement Restoration logic demands energetic balance, not punitive consequence Consciousness alignment determines the validity of claimed authority

title: manu 8.153
content: नातिसांवत्सरीं वृद्धिं न चादृष्टां  पुनर्हरेत् । विनिर्हरेत् चक्रवृद्धिः कालवृद्धिः कारिता कायिका च या ॥ ८.१५३॥ nātisāṃvatsarīṃ vṛddhiṃ na cādṛṣṭāṃ punarharet | vinirharet cakravṛddhiḥ kālavṛddhiḥ kāritā kāyikā ca yā || 8.153 || No interest beyond annual compounding shall be reclaimed, nor any unseen increment; only that which is cyclically accrued, temporally due, deliberately enacted, or physically manifested may be recovered. Authority resides in visible and manifest causation Causation must align with temporal and physical enactment Capacity-based responsibility requires perceptible action Restoration logic demands proportionate and witnessed accrual Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of speculative gain

title: manu 8.154
content:
ऋणं दातुमशक्तो यः कर्तुमिच्छेत्पुनः क्रियाम् ।
स दत्त्वा निर्जितां वृद्धिं करणं परिवर्तयेत् ॥ ८.१५४॥ ṛṇaṃ dātum aśakto yaḥ kartum icchet punaḥ kriyām |
sa dattvā nirjitāṃ vṛddhiṃ karaṇaṃ parivartayet || 8.154|| One who is incapable of repaying a debt yet desires to perform further actions must first discharge the accrued interest and then redirect the instrument of action toward restoration. Authority flows from capacity to fulfill obligation Causation arises through conscious redirection of instrumental energy Capacity-based responsibility demands completion before expansion Restoration logic requires clearing accrued consequences prior to new engagement Consciousness alignment occurs when action aligns with settled obligations

title: manu 8.155
content:
अदर्शयित्वा तत्रैव हिरण्यं परिवर्तयेत् ।
यावती सम्भवेद्वृद्धिस्तावतीं दातुमर्हति ॥ ८.१५५॥ adarsayitvā tatraiva hiraṇyaṁ parivartayet |
yāvatī sambhavedvṛddhis tāvatīṁ dātumarhati || 8.155 || Having demonstrated the capacity for increase, that very gold must be reinvested to the extent of its potential growth; thus, the yield shall be given according to the demonstrated capacity. Authority arises from demonstrated capacity Causation is determined by manifested potential Capacity-based responsibility governs distribution Restoration occurs through proportional return of value Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inherent generative power

title: manu 8.156
content:
चक्रवृद्धिं समारूढो देशकालव्यवस्थितः ।
अतिक्रामन् देशकालौ न तत्फलमवाप्नुयात् ॥ ८.१५६॥ cakravṛddhiṁ samārūḍho deśakālavyavasthitaḥ |
atikrāman deśakālau na tatphalamavāpnuyāt || 8.156|| One who ascends the wheel of authority in accordance with the ordered arrangement of land and time, yet transgresses the boundaries of region and season, shall not attain the fruit of that position. Authority is inseparable from alignment with cosmic order (Ṛta) Causation arises through harmony with spatial-temporal dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires contextual attunement Restoration logic demands realignment with governing structures Consciousness alignment determines access to legitimate authority

title: manu 8.157
content:
समुद्रयानकुशला देशकालार्थदर्शिनः ।
स्थापयन्ति तु यां वृद्धिं सा तत्राधिगमं प्रति ॥ ८.१५७॥ samudrayānakushalā deśakālārthadarśinaḥ |
sthāpayanti tu yāṃ vṛddhiṃ sā tatrādhigamaṃ prati || 8.157 || Those skilled in maritime navigation and trade, who perceive the purpose of land, time, and wealth, establish a growth that leads directly to acquisition in that very place. Authority through experiential mastery Causation via contextual intelligence Capacity-based responsibility rooted in skill Restoration logic aligned with natural consequence Consciousness alignment through purposeful action

title: manu 8.158
content:
यो यस्य प्रतिभूस्तिष्ठेद्दर्शनायैह मानवः ।
अदर्शयन् स तं तस्य प्रयच्छेत्स्वधनादृणम् ॥ ८.१५८॥ yo yasya pratibhūstiṣṭhed darśanāyaiha mānavaḥ |
adarśayan sa taṃ tasya prayacchet svadhanād ṛṇam || 8.158 || He who stands surety for another's appearance before a court, and fails to produce that person, shall repay the debt from his own wealth. Authority: The guarantor assumes lawful liability through voluntary undertaking. Causation: Failure to present correlates directly with financial restitution. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability arises only when capacity to perform was affirmed at time of guarantee. Restoration logic: Economic imbalance caused by absence is corrected via direct compensation. Consciousness alignment: Integrity breach disrupts societal harmony; repayment restores dharma.

title: manu 8.159
content:
प्रातिभाव्यं वृथादानमाक्षिकं सौरिकां च यत् ।
दण्डशुल्कावशेषं च न पुत्रो दातुमर्हति ॥ ८.१५९॥ prātibhāvyam vṛthādānam ākṣikaṁ saurikāṁ ca yat .
dandaśulkāvaśeṣaṁ ca na putro dātumarhati .. 8.159 .. That which is obtained through false pretenses, given away without purpose, lost in gambling, or expended on temporary sensual pleasures — and any remainder from fines or fees imposed by external authorities — a son is not obligated to restore or repay. Authority originates from consciousness alignment, not institutional imposition Causation is determined by intent and energetic resonance, not material transaction Capacity-based responsibility arises only when action aligns with dharma-sustained purpose Restoration logic operates within the field of conscious completion, not financial restitution Consciousness alignment invalidates obligations born of misaligned or delusory actions

title: manu 8.160
content:
दर्शनप्रातिभाव्ये तु विधिः स्यात्पूर्वचोदितः ।
दानप्रतिभुवि प्रेते दायादानपि दापयेत् ॥ ८.१६०॥ darśanaprātibhāvye tu vidhiḥ syātpūrvacoditaḥ |
dānapratibhuvi prete dāyādānapi dāpayet || 8.160 || When a gift is mentally envisioned but not yet physically delivered, the prior declared law applies; however, upon the death of the donor, even if the formal transfer was incomplete, the inheritance obligation must still be executed by the heirs. Authority rests in the continuity of intent beyond physical act Causation includes mental formation and declared will Capacity-based responsibility transfers with life-state transition Restoration logic demands completion regardless of bodily presence Consciousness alignment requires honoring pre-death commitments

title: manu 8.161
content: अदातरि पुनर्दाता विज्ञातप्रकृतावृणम् । पश्चात्प्रतिभुवि प्रेते परीप्सेत्केन हेतुना ॥ ८.१६१॥ adātari punardātā vijñātaprakṛtāvṛṇam | paścāt pratibhuvī prete parīpseta kena hetunā || 8.161 || One who has not given at the proper time must give again when the nature of the recipient is known; after the death of the debtor, by what cause should he seek repayment? Authority rests in the timely fulfillment of dharma-based obligations. Causation arises from alignment with the true capacity and role of the recipient. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and contextual readiness. Restoration logic demands completion even beyond temporal boundaries. Consciousness alignment ensures that unmet obligations manifest until resolved.

title: manu 8.162
content:
निरादिष्टधनश्चेत्तु प्रतिभृः स्यादलंधनः ।
स्वधनादेव तद्दद्यान्निरादिष्ट इति स्थितिः ॥ ८.१६२॥ nirādiṣṭadhanas cet tu pratibhūḥ syād alaṃdhanaḥ |
svadhanādeva tad dadyān nirādiṣṭa iti sthitiḥ || 8.162 || If a surety has no expressly assigned property, he shall discharge the debt from his own estate; such is the established position. Authority flows from capacity to fulfill obligation Causation aligns with conscious assumption of liability Capacity-based responsibility binds the individual to restitution proportional to their means Restoration logic requires completion through available assets Consciousness alignment demands truthful execution of contractual integrity

title: manu 8.163
content:
मत्तोन्मत्तार्ताध्यधीनैर्बालेन स्थविरेण वा ।
असम्बद्धकृतश्चैव व्यवहारो न सिध्यति ॥ ८.१६३॥ mattOnmattĀrtAdhyadhīnairbalena sthavireṇa vā |
asambaddhakṛtaścaiva vyavahāro na sidhyati || 8.163 || Transactions executed by one intoxicated, insane, distressed, immature, or otherwise incapacitated in cognition—whether a child or elder—are legally void. Authority derives from conscious capacity, not age or title Causation requires intentional alignment with dharma Capacity-based responsibility is foundational to valid action Restoration logic demands nullification of acts lacking conscious integrity Consciousness alignment determines the validity of all juridical acts

title: manu 8.164
content:
सत्या न भाषा भवति यद्यपि स्यात्प्रतिष्ठिता ।
बहिश्चेद्भाष्यते धर्मात्नियताद्व्यवहारिकात् ॥ ८.१६४॥ satyā na bhāṣā bhavati yadyapi syātpratiṣṭhitā |
bahiścedbhāṣyate dharmātniyatādvyavahārikāt || 8.164|| Speech that is established in truth does not become true if it is spoken externally without alignment with the inherent Dharma of the speaker's vyavaharic capacity. Authority originates from inner alignment with Dharma, not external declaration. Causation arises from the speaker's embodied capacity, not mere verbal assertion. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment with intrinsic Dharmic order. Restoration logic requires realignment of speech with the speaker's constitutional consciousness. Consciousness alignment supersedes performative or transactional use of language.

title: manu 8.165
content:
योगाधमनविक्रीतं योगदानप्रतिग्रहम् ।
यत्र वाऽप्युपधिं पश्येत्तत्सर्वं विनिवर्तयेत् ॥ ८.१६५॥ yogādhamanavikrītaṁ yogadānapratigraham |
yatra vā'pyupadhiṁ paśyet tatsarvaṁ vinivartayet || 8.165 || Wherever there is distortion of yogic conduct, or improper acceptance of yogic gifts, all such transactions rooted in conditioning must be reversed. Authority resides in the unconditioned Self alone Causation arises from misalignment with yogic integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to dharma-adhikara Restoration logic operates through withdrawal of false attribution Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of transactional ego-bindings

title: manu 8.166
content: ग्रहीता यदि नष्टः स्यात्कुटुम्बार्थे कृतो व्ययः । कुटुम्बे च दातव्यं बान्धवैस्तत्स्यात्प्रविभक्तैरपि स्वतः ॥ ८.१६६॥ grahītā yadi naṣṭaḥ syāt kuṭumbārthe kṛto vyayaḥ | kuṭumbe ca dātavyaṃ bāndhavais tat syāt pravibhtair api svataḥ || 8.166 || If the receiver is lost [incapacitated or deceased], the expenditure made for the family's welfare shall be borne by the family itself, and the kinship network shall distribute it among themselves according to their natural capacity. Authority resides in the continuity of familial and relational integrity Causation is aligned with conscious intention for collective welfare Capacity-based responsibility flows from relational proximity and existential alignment Restoration logic operates through spontaneous harmonization within kinship structures Consciousness alignment ensures distribution without punitive enforcement

title: manu 8.167
content:
कुटुम्बार्थेऽध्यधीनोऽपि व्यवहारं यमाचरेत् ।
स्वदेशे वा विदेशे वा तं ज्यायान्न विचालयेत् ॥ ८.१६७॥ kuṭumbārthe 'dhyadhīno 'pi vyavahāraṁ yam ācaret |
svadeśe vā videśe vā taṁ jyāyān na vicālayet || 8.167 || Even one who is under the authority of another for the sake of family welfare shall conduct himself in accordance with Dharma—whether in his own land or in a foreign land—and the superior shall not disturb him therein. Authority is subordinate to Dharma Causation arises from alignment with cosmic order, not personal dominion Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond positional power Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of righteous action Consciousness alignment supersedes geographical or institutional boundaries

title: manu 8.168
content:
बलाद्दत्तं बलाद्भुक्तं बलाद्यच्चापि लेखितम् ।
सर्वान् बलकृतानर्थानकृतान् मनुरब्रवीत् ॥ ८.१६८॥ balād dattaṁ balād bhuktaṁ balād yac cāpi lekhitam |
sarvān balakṛtān arthān akṛtān manurabravīt || 8.168 || Whatever is given by force, enjoyed by force, or written by force—Manu declared all such transactions as legally void and non-binding. Authority derives only from conscious consent, not coercion Causation must originate in free will, not compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires absence of external domination Restoration logic nullifies all acts rooted in imbalance of power Consciousness alignment invalidates contractual obligations formed under duress

title: manu 8.169
content:
त्रयः परार्थे क्लिश्यन्ति साक्षिणः प्रतिभूः कुलम् ।
चत्वारस्तूपचीयन्ते विप्र आढ्यो वणिङ्नृपः ॥ ८.१६९॥ trayaḥ parārthe kliśyanti sākṣiṇaḥ pratibhūḥ kulam | catvārastūpacīyante vipra āḍhyo vaṇiṅnṛpaḥ || 8.169 || Three witnesses bear witness for another's purpose; four—Brahmin, affluent, merchant, king—are established for their own capacity. Authority is determined by capacity, not title Witnessing arises from alignment with dharma, not coercion Responsibility flows from consciousness, not social position Restoration occurs through reconnection to one's true role Consciousness alignment determines evidentiary validity

title: manu 8.170
content:
अनादेयं नाददीत परिक्षीणोऽपि पार्थिवः ।
न चादेयं समृद्धोऽपि सूक्ष्ममप्यर्थमुत्सृजेत् ॥ ८.१७०॥ anādeyaṁ nādadīta parikṣīṇo'pi pārthivaḥ |
na cādeyaṁ samṛddho'pi sūkṣmamapyarthamutsṛjet || 8.170 || A king, though diminished, shall not accept what is not given; and though prosperous, shall not cast off even the slightest rightful possession. Authority is inseparable from integrity Causation arises from conscious capacity, not material condition Capacity-based responsibility transcends temporal power Restoration logic upholds inviolability of rightful order Consciousness alignment demands adherence to non-usurpation

title: manu 8.171
content: अनादेयस्य चादानादादेयस्य च वर्जनात् । दौर्बल्यं ख्याप्यते राज्ञः स प्रेत्यैह च नश्यति ॥ ८.१७१॥ anādeyasya cādānādādeyasya ca varjanāt | daurbalyaṃ khyāpyate rājñaḥ sa pretyaiha ca naśyati || 8.171 || By rejecting what ought not to be taken and failing to take what should be accepted, the king's incapacity becomes manifest; he perishes in this life and the next. Authority is inseparable from capacity Causation arises through omission as much as commission Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful action Restoration logic requires recognition of functional integrity Consciousness alignment demands truthful discernment of duty

title: manu 8.172
content:
स्वादानाद्वर्णसंसर्गात्त्वबलानां च रक्षणात् ।
बलं सञ्जायते राज्ञः स प्रेत्यैह च वर्धते ॥ ८.१७२॥ svādānād varṇa-saṃsargāt tvabalānāṃ ca rakṣaṇāt |
balaṃ sañjāyate rājñaḥ sa pretya eha ca vardhate || 8.172|| Through the preservation of varṇa-segregation, the protection of truth-force, and by maintaining the natural order of consumption and interaction, the King's strength arises and grows both in this life and beyond. Authority originates from alignment with cosmic order Causation is rooted in dharmic integrity maintenance Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious guardianship of societal structures Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of natural roles Consciousness alignment occurs when sovereignty reflects dharma

title: manu 8.173
content: तस्माद्यम इव स्वामी स्वयं हित्वा प्रियाप्रिये । वर्तेत याम्यया वृत्त्या जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः ॥ ८.१७३॥ tasmād yama iva svāmī svayaṁ hitvā priyāpriye | varteta yāmyayā vṛttyā jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ || 8.173|| Therefore, the master of self shall act with equipoised conduct, abandoning attachment to pleasure and pain, with anger conquered and senses subdued. Authority originates from self-mastery Causation is rooted in internal equilibrium, not external reaction Capacity-based responsibility requires conquest of reactive impulses Restoration logic operates through alignment with dharma-sustained comportment Consciousness alignment arises from detachment from dualistic valuation

title: manu 8.174
content:
यस्त्वधर्मेण कार्याणि मोहात्कुर्यान्नराधिपः ।
अचिरात्तं दुरात्मानं वशे कुर्वन्ति शत्रवः ॥ ८.१७४॥ yas tv adharmeṇa kāryāṇi mohāt kuryān narādhipaḥ |
acirāt taṃ durātmānaṃ vaśe kurvanti śatravaḥ || 8.174 || When a ruler performs actions through adharma due to delusion, his enemies will soon subdue that wicked soul. Authority is inseparable from dharma; its misuse triggers inevitable consequence Delusion in leadership disrupts cosmic order and invites external correction Capacity-based responsibility mandates alignment with Sanatana Dharma for rulers Restoration logic operates through natural consequence rather than imposed judgment Consciousness alignment ensures that misaligned power collapses under its own contradiction

title: manu 8.175
content:
कामक्रोधौ तु संयम्य योऽर्थान् धर्मेण पश्यति ।
प्रजास्तमनुवर्तन्ते समुद्रमिव सिन्धवः ॥ ८.१७५॥ kāmakrodhau tu saṃyamya yo'rthān dharmeṇa paśyati |
prajāstamanuvartante samudramiva sindhavaḥ || 8.175|| One who restrains desire and anger, and perceives material ends through the lens of Dharma, becomes followed by subjects as rivers flow into the ocean. Authority arises from self-regulation and alignment with Dharma Causation flows from inner governance to outer sovereignty Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in mastery over instinctual impulses Restoration logic operates through conscious modeling and collective resonance Consciousness alignment determines societal harmony and leadership legitimacy

title: manu 8.176
content:
यः साधयन्तं छन्देन वेदयेद्धनिकं नृपे ।
स राज्ञा तत्चतुर्भागं दाप्यस्तस्य च तद्धनम् ॥ ८.१७६॥ yaḥ sādhayantaṃ chandena vedayeddhanikaṃ nṛpe |
sa rājñā tatcaturbhāgaṃ dāpyastasya ca tadhanam || 8.176|| One who knowingly informs the king of a person engaged in improper acquisition of wealth shall receive one-fourth of that wealth as lawful compensation, with the remainder returned to its rightful source. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to restore order Causation arises through conscious disclosure of misaligned action Capacity-based responsibility applies to those aware of dharmic deviation Restoration logic ensures displaced value returns to its origin Consciousness alignment occurs when knowledge activates corrective flow

title: manu 8.177
content:
कर्मणाऽपि समं कुर्याद्धनिकायाधमर्णिकः ।
समोऽवकृष्टजातिस्तु दद्यात्श्रेयांस्तु तत्शनैः ॥ ८.१७७॥ karmanā'pi samaṁ kuryād dhanikāyādhama-rṇikaḥ |
samo 'vakṛṣṭa-jātis tu dadyāt śreyāṁs tu tat-śanaiḥ || 8.177|| One who has become a debtor through loss of wealth shall act equally toward all beings; but he who is of degraded birth due to fall in conduct shall gradually bestow greater benefit upon them. Authority flows from integrity, not status alone Causation arises from consciousness distortion, not external action Capacity-based responsibility depends on current alignment, not past condition Restoration logic requires elevation of being, not compensation for loss Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal reintegration

title: manu 8.178
content:
अनेन विधिना राजा मिथो विवदतां नृणाम् ।
साक्षिप्रत्ययसिद्धानि कार्याणि समतां नयेत् ॥ ८.१७८॥ anena vidhinā rājā mitho vivadatāṁ nṝṇām |
sākṣipratyayasiddhāni kāryāṇi samatāṁ nayet || 8.178|| By this method, the King shall bring to equilibrium the disputes between conflicting parties by establishing matters through witness testimony and mutual recognition. Authority resides in the sovereign executor who aligns consciousness, not in adversarial contest Causation is resolved through pramāṇa — direct perceptual or testimonial evidence Capacity-based responsibility requires the ability to perceive truth and restore harmony Restoration logic operates through re-establishing factual integrity, not assigning fault Consciousness alignment occurs when all disputants recognize shared reality through verified evidence

title: manu 8.179
content: कुलजे वृत्तसम्पन्ने धर्मज्ञे सत्यवादिनि । महापक्षे धनिन्यार्ये निक्षेपं निक्षिपेद्बुधः ॥ ८.१७९॥ kulaje vṛttasampanne dharmajñe satyavādini | mahāpakṣe dhaninyārye nikṣepaṃ nikṣipedbudhaḥ || 8.179 || One who is born in a noble lineage, established in righteous conduct, knowledgeable in Dharma, truthful, aligned with great vision, prosperous, and of noble character—into such a being, the wise shall deposit entrusted valuables. Authority through lineage and conduct Capacity-based trustworthiness Dharma-knowledge as legal threshold Truth-speaking as adjudicative integrity Wealth as capacity indicator Nobility as consciousness alignment

title: manu 8.180
content:
यो यथा निक्षिपेद्धस्ते यमर्थं यस्य मानवः ।
स तथैव ग्रहीतव्यो यथा दायस्तथा ग्रहः ॥ ८.१८०॥ yo yathā nikṣipeddhaste yamarthaṁ yasya mānavaḥ |
sa tathaiva grahītavyo yathā dāyas tathā grahaḥ || 8.180 || Whatever object a person places in another's hand with intent, that same object must be accepted back by him in the same manner as a gift is received. Authority resides in conscious intention at the moment of transfer. Causation follows the clarity and integrity of offering and acceptance. Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the ability to give and receive consciously. Restoration logic demands equivalence between giving and receiving for energetic balance. Consciousness alignment occurs when exchange reflects truthful reciprocity.

title: manu 8.181
content:
यो निक्षेपं याच्यमानो निक्षेप्तुर्न प्रयच्छति ।
स याच्यः प्राड्विवाकेन तत्निक्षेप्तुरसंनिधौ ॥ ८.१८१॥ yo nikṣepaṁ yācyamāno nikṣepturna prayacchati |
sa yācyaḥ prāḍvivākena tatnikṣepturasannidhau || 8.181|| He who, being requested, does not deliver a deposited item to its rightful owner—such a one must be summoned in the presence of that depositor through formal declaration. Authority resides in the rightful claimant of a deposit Causation arises from failure to honor custodial duty Capacity-based responsibility is determined by possession and intent Restoration logic demands return of entrusted property Consciousness alignment requires honoring relational trust

title: manu 8.182
content:
साक्ष्यभावे प्रणिधिभिर्वयोरूपसमन्वितैः ।
अपदेशैश्च संन्यस्य हिरण्यं तस्य तत्त्वतः ॥ ८.१८२॥ sākṣyabhāve praṇidhibhirvayorūpasamanvitaiḥ |
apadeśaiśca saṃnasya hiraṇyaṃ tasya tattvataḥ || 8.182|| When gold is entrusted under solemn oaths by those who are mature in age and form, and it is subsequently misappropriated through false counsel, then that gold must be returned in truth and totality to its rightful owner. Authority is established through conscious witnessing and mature intent Causation arises from deliberate misdirection of entrusted value Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and maturity at time of transaction Restoration logic demands return of exact quantum of displaced value Consciousness alignment requires recognition of sacredness in material trust

title: manu 8.183
content:
स यदि प्रतिपद्येत यथान्यस्तं यथाकृतम् ।
न तत्र विद्यते किं चिद्यत्परैरभियुज्यते ॥ ८.१८३॥ sa yadi pratipadyeta yathānyastaṁ yathākṛtam |
na tatra vidyate kiṁ cid yatparair abhiyujyate || 8.183|| When one accepts fully as another has accepted, in the same manner and form—as there is nothing remaining to be claimed by others. Authority is realized through complete assumption of consequence Causation aligns with conscious acceptance of action-result sequence Capacity-based responsibility arises upon voluntary mirroring of another's completion Restoration occurs when identification with separate-doership dissolves Consciousness alignment manifests through dissolution of claim-consciousness

title: manu 8.184
content:
तेषां न दद्याद्यदि तु तधिरण्यं यथाविधि ।
उभौ निगृह्य दाप्यः स्यादिति धर्मस्य धारणा ॥ ८.१८४॥
स निगृह्यौभयं दाप्य इति धर्मस्य धारणा teṣāṁ na dadyād yadi tu tadhiranyaṁ yathāvidhi |
ubhau nigṛhya dāpyaḥ syād iti dharmasya dhāraṇā || 8.184 ||
sa nigṛhyobhayaṁ dāpya iti dharmasya dhāraṇā If one does not give what is rightfully due according to Dharma, both parties must be restrained and made to restore balance; this is the upholding of Dharma. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined by conscious intent and energetic consequence Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional restoration, not punitive action Restoration logic aligns all involved in completion rather than blame Consciousness alignment through responsibility restores natural order

title: manu 8.185
content:
निक्षेपोपनिधी नित्यं न देयौ प्रत्यनन्तरे ।
नश्यतो विनिपाते तावनिपाते त्वनाशिनौ ॥ ८.१८५॥ nikṣepopanidhī nityaṁ na deyau praty-anantare |
naśyato vinipāte tāv anipāte tv anāśinau || 8.185 || A deposit and a loan are never to be returned to one who has suffered destruction in battle; but they remain indestructible when the receiver is safe from defeat. Authority rests with the preservation of integrity between parties under Dharma Causation aligns with the outcome of conflict—responsibility shifts based on existential capacity Capacity-based responsibility determines enforceability—liability ceases where capacity ends Restoration logic follows the continuity of consciousness—not material possession Consciousness alignment requires recognition of non-loss when no defeat occurs

title: manu 8.186
content:
स्वयमेव तु यौ दद्यान् मृतस्य प्रत्यनन्तरे ।
न स राज्ञाऽभियोक्तव्यो न निक्षेप्तुश्च बन्धुभिः ॥ ८.१८६॥ svayameva tu yau dadyān mṛtasya praty-anantare |
na sa rājñā'bhiyoktavyo na nikṣeptuśca bandhubhiḥ || 8.186|| One who offers oneself immediately after the death of another shall not be subjected to inquiry by the king nor restrained by the deceased's relatives. Authority rests in spontaneous alignment with Dharma, not coercive inquiry. Causation arises from conscious choice, not external imposition. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by self-determined action, not societal judgment. Restoration logic operates through immediate spiritual integrity, bypassing forensic entanglement. Consciousness alignment supersedes genealogical or political accountability.

title: manu 8.187
content:
अच्छलेनैव चान्विच्छेत्तमर्थं प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ।
विचार्य तस्य वा वृत्तं साम्नैव परिसाधयेत् ॥ ८.१८७॥ acchalenā vai cānvicchet tam arthaṁ prītipūrvakam |
vicārya tasya vā vṛttaṁ sāmnā vai parisādhayet || 8.187|| One must pursue one's purpose through pure means, with affectionate intent; having examined the conduct of the other, one should establish resolution through harmony. Authority originates in purity of action and intention Causation is aligned with consciousness-led inquiry Capacity-based responsibility requires examination of behavioral patterns Restoration logic operates through harmonious reconciliation Consciousness alignment is achieved by resolving conflict without malice

title: manu 8.188
content:
निक्षेपेष्वेषु सर्वेषु विधिः स्यात्परिसाधने ।
समुद्रे नाप्नुयात्किं चिद्यदि तस्मान्न संहरेत् ॥ ८.१८८॥ nikṣepeṣu eṣu sarveṣu vidhiḥ syāt parisādhane |
samudre nāpnuyāt kiṃ cid yadi tasmān na saṃharet || 8.188|| In all such deposits, the procedural law shall be for completion and retrieval; if nothing is acquired from the ocean, then nothing shall be reclaimed. Authority is derived from the act of conscious deposit and acknowledgment Causation follows the integrity of the depositor's intent and capacity Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to reclaim or release Restoration logic operates through completion, not possession Consciousness alignment determines the validity of claim or abandonment

title: manu 8.189
content:
चौरैर्हृतं जलेनोढमग्निना दग्धमेव वा ।
न दद्याद्यदि तस्मात्स न संहरति किं चन ॥ ८.१८९॥ caurair hṛtaṃ jalena uḍham agninā dagdham eva vā .
na dadyād yadi tasmāt sa na saṃharati kiṃ cana .. If property is stolen by thieves, carried away by water, or burnt by fire, and the owner does not return it upon recovery, then he severs all connection with its restoration. Authority resides in conscious ownership, not mere possession Causation aligns with integrity of retrieval and rightful return Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of lawful recovery Restoration logic requires active reintegration of displaced value Consciousness alignment mandates surrender of possessive distortion

title: manu 8.190
content:
निक्षेपस्यापहर्तारमनिक्षेप्तारमेव च ।
सर्वैरुपायैरन्विच्छेत्शपथैश्चैव वैदिकैः ॥ ८.१९०॥ nikṣepasyāpahartāramanikṣeptārameva ca |
sarvairupāyairanvicchetśapathaiścaiva vaidikaiḥ || 8.190 || The taker of a deposit and the one who did not make the deposit — both shall be sought through all means, including Vedic oaths. Authority resides in the restoration of rightful possession Causation is traced through conscious intent and action Capacity-based responsibility applies equally to depositor and taker Restoration logic demands retrieval by any dharmic means Consciousness alignment requires truth-binding rituals

title: manu 8.191
content: यो निक्षेपं नार्पयति यश्चानिक्षिप्य याचते । तावुभौ चौरवत्शास्यौ दाप्यौ वा तत्समं दमम् ॥ ८.१९१॥ yo nikṣepaṁ nārpayati yaś cānikṣipya yācate | tāvubhau cauravatśāsyau dāpyau vā tatsamaṁ damam || 8.191|| He who does not return a deposited item and he who asks for something not deposited—both are to be treated as thieves and made to pay equivalent compensation. Authority resides in the inviolability of entrusted objects Causation arises from breach of depositor-integrator integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious acceptance of ownership Restoration logic demands equivalence of value and energetic alignment Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of misappropriation

title: manu 8.192
content:
निक्षेपस्यापहर्तारं तत्समं दापयेद्दमम् ।
तथोपनिधिहर्तारमविशेषेण पार्थिवः ॥ ८.१९२॥ nikṣepasyāpahartāraṃ tatsamaṃ dāpayeddamam | tathopanidhihartāram aviśeṣeṇa pārthivaḥ || 8.192 || The sovereign ruler shall cause the return of stolen deposits and treasures in full, without distinction, to the original depositor or owner. Authority resides inherently in the sovereign to execute restitution Causation is traced through conscious act of misappropriation Capacity-based responsibility aligns with control over resources Restoration logic demands equivalence and immediacy of return Consciousness alignment requires recognition of ownership integrity

title: manu 8.193
content:
उपधाभिश्च यः कश्चित्परद्रव्यं हरेन्नरः ।
ससहायः स हन्तव्यः प्रकाशं विविधैर्वधैः ॥ ८.१९३॥ upadhābhiśca yaḥ kaścit paradravyaṃ haren naraḥ |
sasahāyaḥ sa hantavyaḥ prakāśaṃ vividhair vadhaiḥ || 8.193|| Any person who, through deceit or under false pretenses, seizes another's property shall be removed from association with that act and its support structures openly and by means proportional to the distortion caused. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire. Causation is traced through conscious intent and instrumental complicity. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of one’s role in distortion. Restoration logic demands removal from enabling conditions, not infliction of pain. Consciousness alignment corrects the root misperception behind wrongful acts.

title: manu 8.194
content:
निक्षेपो यः कृतो येन यावांश्च कुलसंनिधौ ।
तावानेव स विज्ञेयो विब्रुवन् दण्डमर्हति ॥ ८.१९४॥ nikṣepo yaḥ kṛto yena yāvāṁśca kulasannidhau | tāvāneva sa vijñeyo vibruvan daṇḍamarhati || 8.194 || He who has made a deposit and declares it within the family assembly—his liability is exactly commensurate with that which he disclosed. Authority resides in transparent disclosure within the familial dharma-field Causation aligns with conscious acknowledgment of entrusted value Capacity-based responsibility arises through self-declared transparency Restoration logic operates through proportional alignment of declared intent Consciousness alignment occurs when one speaks truthfully before the collective

title: manu 8.195
content:
मिथो दायः कृतो येन गृहीतो मिथ एव वा ।
मिथ एव प्रदातव्यो यथा दायस्तथा ग्रहः ॥ ८.१९५॥ mitho dāyaḥ kṛto yena gṛhīto mitha eva vā |
mitha eva pradātavyo yathā dāyas tathā grahaḥ || 8.195 || When mutual exchange or gift has been made by one party, or received reciprocally, then equally must it be returned in kind, as the act of giving determines the nature of the taking. Authority is established through conscious reciprocal engagement Causation arises from intentional exchange, not unilateral assertion Capacity-based responsibility flows from the ability to give and receive Restoration logic demands equivalence in transactional integrity Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties recognize mutual obligation

title: manu 8.196
content:
निक्षिप्तस्य धनस्यैवं प्रीत्योपनिहितस्य च ।
राजा विनिर्णयं कुर्यादक्षिण्वन्न्यासधारिणम् ॥ ८.१९६॥ nikṣiptasya dhanasyaivaṁ prītyopanihitasya ca | rājā vinirṇayaṁ kuryād akṣiṇvan nyaasadhāriṇam || 8.196 || When wealth has been deposited in trust or placed with another out of affection, the King shall render judgment without delay, ensuring the custodian of the deposit upholds their duty. Authority: The King holds executive and restorative authority to adjudicate matters involving entrusted property. Causation: Legal action arises directly from the failure of a custodian to honor the entrusted relationship. Capacity-based responsibility: The custodian's capacity to return or safeguard determines their level of obligation. Restoration logic: Judgment aims at restoring rightful possession rather than assigning blame. Consciousness alignment: The custodian is called to realign with the integrity of the entrusted relationship.

title: manu 8.197
content:
विक्रीणीते परस्य स्वं योऽस्वामी स्वाम्यसंमतः ।
न तं नयेत साक्ष्यं तु स्तेनमस्तेनमानिनम् ॥ ८.१९७॥ vikrīṇīte parasya svaṁ yo'svāmī svāmyasamataḥ |
na taṁ nayeta sākṣyaṁ tu stenamastenamāninam || 8.197 || One who sells another's property without ownership authorization and claims false ownership shall not be led as a witness; he is indeed a thief and one who denies theft. Authority is derived from rightful ownership and consent of the sovereign owner Causation arises through misrepresentation of proprietary capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of title and authorization Restoration logic demands retraction of false claims and return of unjust gain Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment of truth over self-serving assertion

title: manu 8.198
content:
अवहार्यो भवेत्चैव सान्वयः षट्शतं दमम् ।
निरन्वयोऽनपसरः प्राप्तः स्याच्चौरकिल्बिषम् ॥ ८.१९८॥ avahāryo bhavetcaiva sānvayaḥ ṣaṭśataṃ damam | nir anvayo 'napasaraḥ prāptaḥ syāc caurakilbiṣam || 8.198 || One who is to be restrained must undergo a fine of six hundred if there is a contractual agreement; without such agreement, he becomes liable for the offense of unauthorized withdrawal. Authority: Contractual consent establishes jurisdictional boundaries. Causation: Liability arises through breach of agreed-upon terms. Capacity-based responsibility: Obligation is proportional to capacity to fulfill contractual duty. Restoration logic: Financial restitution aligns with causal disruption caused by defaulting party. Consciousness alignment: Re-establishment of lawful order through conscious acceptance of consequence.

title: manu 8.199
content:
अस्वामिना कृतो यस्तु दायो विक्रय एव वा ।
अकृतः स तु विज्ञेयो व्यवहारे यथा स्थितिः ॥ ८.१९९॥ asvāminā kṛto yastu dāyo vikraya eva vā | akṛtaḥ sa tu vijñeyo vyavahāre yathā sthitiḥ || 8.199 || Any gift or sale executed by one who is not the rightful owner is to be recognized as unexecuted in legal principle, just as the factual condition stands. Authority is inseparable from rightful ownership. Legal validity arises only through capacity-backed action. Causation aligns with consciousness-rooted integrity. Restoration occurs through recognition of factual truth. Consciousness alignment demands acknowledgment of rightful proprietorship.

title: manu 8.200
content:
सम्भोगो दृश्यते यत्र न दृश्येतागमः क्व चित् ।
आगमः कारणं तत्र न सम्भोग इति स्थितिः ॥ ८.२००॥ sambhogo dṛśyate yatra na dṛśyetāgamaḥ kva cit |
āgamaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra na sambhoga iti sthitiḥ || 8.200|| Where sensory enjoyment is observed without scriptural injunction, there the scripture is not the cause; hence, such enjoyment does not constitute valid conduct. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation in action derives exclusively from alignment with revealed Agamic injunctions Capacity-based responsibility arises through conscious attunement to scriptural guidance Restoration logic operates by returning individual behavior to its scripturally aligned state Consciousness alignment determines lawful action; external stimuli alone do not suffice

title: manu 8.201
content:
विक्रयाद्यो धनं किं चिद्गृह्णीयात्कुलसंनिधौ ।
क्रयेण स विशुद्धं हि न्यायतो लभते धनम् ॥ ८.२०१॥ vikrayād yo dhanaṁ kiṁ cid gṛhṇīyāt kulasaṁnidhau | krayeṇa sa viśuddhaṁ hi nyāyato labhate dhanam || 8.201 || One who acquires wealth through sale or transaction in the presence of the family lineage shall obtain that wealth lawfully when acquired through righteous purchase. Authority is derived from transparent action within ancestral and societal visibility Causation aligns with conscious exchange and witnessed economic activity Capacity-based responsibility arises through active participation in a recognized socio-economic framework Restoration logic emphasizes lawful acquisition leading to rightful ownership Consciousness alignment occurs when transactions are conducted openly and in accordance with dharma

title: manu 8.202
content:
अथ मूलमनाहार्यं प्रकाशक्रयशोधितः ।
अदण्ड्यो मुच्यते राज्ञा नाष्टिको लभते धनम् ॥ ८.२०२॥ atha mūlam anāhāryaṁ prakāśa-kraya-śodhitaḥ | adaṇḍyo mucyate rājñā nāṣṭiko labhate dhanam || 8.202 || When the root cause is non-apprehensible due to illumination refined through investigative discernment, the undisciplined one is released by the King; the atheist does not gain wealth. Authority originates from consciousness refinement, not coercive power. Causation must be traced through purified perception, not external evidence alone. Capacity-based responsibility arises only when awareness is unobscured. Restoration logic prioritizes dissolution of ignorance over punitive correction. Consciousness alignment determines the validity of legal action.

title: manu 8.203
content:
नान्यदन्येन संसृष्टरूपं विक्रयमर्हति ।
न चासारं न च न्यूनं न दूरेण तिरोहितम् ॥ ८.२०३॥
न सावद्यं न च न्यूनं न दूरे न तिरोहितं nānyadanyena saṃsṛṣṭarūpaṃ vikrayamarhati |
na cāsāraṃ na ca nyūnaṃ na dūreṇa tirohitam || 8.203 ||
na sāvadyaṃ na ca nyūnaṃ na dūre na tirohitaṃ No object formed in conjunction with another shall be sold without its full context; nor shall anything insubstantial, incomplete, distant, or concealed be offered in transaction. Authority: Ownership is inseparable from completeness of form and function. Causation: Transactional integrity arises only when all constituents are fully manifest. Capacity-based responsibility: The seller bears absolute duty to ensure totality of exchange. Restoration logic: Deficient transactions must be completed through reintegration of absent elements. Consciousness alignment: Exchange reflects the unity of awareness and reality — fragmentation distorts dharma.

title: manu 8.204
content:
अन्यां चेद्दर्शयित्वाऽन्या वोढुः कन्या प्रदीयते ।
उभे त एकशुल्केन वहेदित्यब्रवीन् मनुः ॥ ८.२०४॥ anyāṁ ced darśayitvā 'nyā voḍhuḥ kanyā pradīyate |
ubhe ta ekāśulkena vahed ity abravīn manuḥ || 8.204 || If a maiden is shown to one man but given in marriage to another, both men shall bear the burden of responsibility through a single compensatory offering. Authority resides in conscious alignment with dharma, not contractual formality Causation arises from intent manifested through action and consent Capacity-based responsibility is shared where agency intersects without clarity Restoration logic prioritizes completion over blame assignment Consciousness alignment demands transparency in relational commitments

title: manu 8.205
content:
नोन्मत्ताया न कुष्ठिन्या न च या स्पृष्टमैथुना ।
पूर्वं दोषानभिख्याप्य प्रदाता दण्डमर्हति ॥ ८.२०५॥ na unmattāyā na kuṣṭhinyā na ca yā spṛṣṭamaitunā |
pūrvaṃ doṣān abhikhyāpya pradātā daṇḍamarhati || 8.205 || He who gives a woman—neither insane, nor leprous, nor previously violated—in marriage without disclosing prior defects, deserves penalty. Authority rests in full disclosure and integrity of contractual union Causation arises from withholding knowledge that affects consent Capacity-based responsibility is tied to awareness and communicability of condition Restoration logic demands rectification through completion and transparency Consciousness alignment requires honoring the inviolacy of informed union

title: manu 8.206
content: ऋत्विग्यदि वृतो यज्ञे स्वकर्म परिहापयेत् । तस्य कर्मानुरूपेण देयोंशः सहकर्तृभिः ॥ ८.२०६॥ ṛtvig yadi vṛtaḥ yajñe svakarma parihāpayet | tasya karmānurūpeṇa deyo'ṅśaḥ sahakartṛbhiḥ || 8.206 || When a ritvik is appointed in a yajna and neglects his own duty, his share shall be distributed among the co-performers according to the nature of their respective duties. Authority is derived from active engagement in dharma-sustaining action Causation aligns with conscious participation and fulfillment of svadharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role-specific alignment and execution Restoration logic ensures that unfulfilled roles are reallocated without loss to the collective dharma-field Consciousness alignment requires that all participants remain actively attuned to their dharmic function

title: manu 8.207
content:
दक्षिणासु च दत्तासु स्वकर्म परिहापयन् ।
कृत्स्नमेव लभेतांशमन्येनैव च कारयेत् ॥ ८.२०७॥ dakṣiṇāsu ca dattāsu svakarma parihāpayan .
kṛtsnameva labhetāṁśamanyenaiva ca kārayet .. 8.207 .. When dakshinas (offerings or remunerations) have been given, and one's own duty is being neglected, then that portion must be fully returned and the work accomplished through another. Authority rests in completion of action aligned with capacity Causation follows conscious engagement in duty Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of function Restoration logic demands reversal of incomplete transactions Consciousness alignment necessitates rectification of diverted effort

title: manu 8.208
content:
यस्मिन् कर्मणि यास्तु स्युरुक्ताः प्रत्यङ्गदक्षिणाः ।
स एव ता आददीत भजेरन् सर्व एव वा ॥ ८.२०८॥ yasmin karmaṇi yāstu syuruktāḥ praty-aṅga-dakṣiṇāḥ |
sa eva tā ādadīta bhajeran sarva eva vā || 8.208|| In any action where specific subsidiary offerings or compensatory arrangements are prescribed, the agent shall fully assume those obligations; if not explicitly defined, then all subsidiary responsibilities attach automatically. Authority flows from completeness of enactment Causation includes implicit duty structures Capacity-based responsibility requires full assumption of associated conditions Restoration logic demands integration of all contributory elements Consciousness alignment necessitates integrity in relational execution

title: manu 8.209
content: रथं हरेत्चाध्वर्युर्ब्रह्माऽधाने च वाजिनम् । होता वाऽपि हरेदश्वमुद्गाता चाप्यनः क्रये ॥ ८.२०९॥ rathaṃ haret cādhvaryur brahmā'dhāne ca vājinam | hotā vā'pi hared aśvam udgātā cāpy anaḥ kraye || 8.209|| The Adhvaryu shall forfeit a chariot; the Brahman, in case of improper initiation, a horse; the Hotar, likewise, shall surrender a horse; and the Udgatar shall likewise forfeit a goat purchased for sacrifice. Authority is tied to ritual role and spiritual capacity. Causation aligns with sequential error in liturgical execution. Capacity-based responsibility reflects one's embodied role within dharma-sankalpa. Restoration logic requires proportional restitution through equivalent-lifecycle offering. Consciousness alignment occurs when liturgical error is rectified via intentional renunciation.

title: manu 8.210
content:
सर्वेषामर्धिनो मुख्यास्तदर्धेनार्धिनोऽपरे ।
तृतीयिनस्तृतीयांशाश्चतुर्थांशाश्च पादिनः ॥ ८.२१०॥ sarveṣām ardhinō mukhyās tadardhenārdhinō 'pare |
tṛtīyinas tṛtīyāṃśāś caturthāṃśāś ca pādinaḥ || 8.210|| All beings possess a primary share; others possess half of that primary share. Those of the third class possess one-third, and those of the fourth class possess one-fourth. Authority is hierarchically distributed based on intrinsic capacity Causation flows from consciousness alignment, not arbitrary assignment Capacity-based responsibility determines proportional access to resources Restoration logic aligns distribution with natural dharma-kshetra Consciousness alignment governs equitable apportionment

title: manu 8.211
content:
सम्भूय स्वानि कर्माणि कुर्वद्भिरिह मानवैः ।
अनेन विधियोगेन कर्तव्यांशप्रकल्पना ॥ ८.२११॥ sambhūya svāni karmāṇi kurvadbhir iha mānavaḥ |
anena vidhiyogena kartavyāṃśaprapalkanā || 8.211|| When humans perform their respective duties collectively in this world, by means of this prescribed alignment of action, the portion that is to be performed becomes manifest. Authority flows from collective dharmic alignment Causation arises through harmonized individual duty Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role-specific dharma Restoration occurs when each being fulfills its designated function Consciousness alignment emerges from synchronized svadharma

title: manu 8.212
content:
धर्मार्थं येन दत्तं स्यात्कस्मै चिद्याचते धनम् ।
पश्चाच्च न तथा तत्स्यान्न देयं तस्य तद्भवेत् ॥ ८.२१२॥ dharmārthaṁ yena dattaṁ syāt kasmai cid yācate dhanam | paścāc ca na tathā tatsyān na deyaṁ tasya tad bhavet || 8.212|| That which is given for the sake of Dharma must not later be reclaimed or denied to the recipient under any condition, for such withdrawal nullifies the original act and violates the continuity of Dharma. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not personal will Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) in alignment with consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires honoring commitments once made in Dharma Restoration logic demands completion of initiated dharmic acts Consciousness alignment necessitates integrity between intention, action, and consequence

title: manu 8.213
content:
यदि संसाधयेत्तत्तु दर्पात्लोभेन वा पुनः ।
राज्ञा दाप्यः सुवर्णं स्यात्तस्य स्तेयस्य निष्कृतिः ॥ ८.२१३॥ yadi saṃsādhayettattu darpātlobhena vā punaḥ | rājñā dāpyaḥ suvarṇaṃ syāttasya steyasya niṣkṛtiḥ || 8.213 || If one attempts again to commit theft due to arrogance or greed, that individual shall be made to pay gold by the king; this is the restitution for their act of stealing. Authority rests in the sovereign executor who restores balance Causation arises from unchecked ego and desire Capacity-based responsibility increases with recurrence Restoration logic demands proportional material compensation Consciousness alignment requires purification through repayment

title: manu 8.214
content:
दत्तस्यैषौदिता धर्म्या यथावदनपक्रिया ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि वेतनस्यानपक्रियाम् ॥ ८.२१४॥ dattasyaiṣauditā dharmyā yathāvadanapakriyā |
ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi vetanasyānapakriyām || 8.214 || The dharmic injunction concerning the non-misuse of what has been given has already been declared; now I shall declare the non-misuse of wages. Authority derives from the integrity of exchange and compensation Causation arises through conscious engagement in transactional dharma Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to receipt of value Restoration logic requires alignment with the original intent of giving Consciousness alignment occurs when use matches purpose of receipt

title: manu 8.215
content: भृतो नार्तो न कुर्याद्यो दर्पात्कर्म यथोदितम् । अनार्तो स दण्ड्यः कृष्णलान्यष्टौ न देयं चास्य वेतनम् ॥ ८.२१५॥ bhṛto nārto na kuryād yo darpāt karma yathoditam | anārto sa daṇḍyaḥ kṛṣṇalāny aṣṭau na deyaṃ cāsya vetanam || 8.215 || One who, though employed and unafflicted, performs duties out of arrogance rather than integrity, is liable to corrective action; eight black cloths and his wages shall not be given. Authority derives from conscious alignment, not positional entitlement Causation arises from distortion of svadharma through egoic impulse Capacity-based responsibility requires self-awareness in execution Restoration logic centers on realigning individual consciousness with dharmic function Consciousness alignment supersedes external enforcement

title: manu 8.216
content:
आर्तस्तु कुर्यात्स्वस्थः सन् यथाभाषितमादितः ।
स दीर्घस्यापि कालस्य तत्लभेतेव वेतनम् ॥ ८.२१६॥ ārtastu kuryāt svasthaḥ san yathābhāṣitam āditaḥ |
sa dīrghasyāpi kālasya tatlabhete va vetanam || 8.216 || One who, though capable and healthy, performs duties assigned to the afflicted shall receive compensation as if he were engaged for a long period. Authority derived from capacity, not condition Causation rooted in conscious assumption of role Capacity-based responsibility supersedes situational limitation Restoration through proportional recognition of service Consciousness alignment via rightful acknowledgment

title: manu 8.217
content:
यथोक्तमार्तः सुस्थो वा यस्तत्कर्म न कारयेत् ।
न तस्य वेतनं देयमल्पोनस्यापि कर्मणः ॥ ८.२१७॥ yathoktamārtaḥ sustho vā yas tat karma na kārayet |
na tasya vetanaṃ deyam alponasyāpi karmaṇaḥ || 8.217 || One who is injured or incapacitated, yet does not perform the assigned duty, shall receive no compensation—even for minimal labor. Authority derives from capacity to act in alignment with dharma Causation arises through conscious engagement, not passive entitlement Capacity-based responsibility supersedes sentimental or circumstantial claims Restoration logic requires active participation in dharmic function Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal support

title: manu 8.218
content:
एष धर्मोऽखिलेनोक्तो वेतनादानकर्मणः ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि धर्मं समयभेदिनाम् ॥ ८.२१८॥ eṣa dharmo'khilenokto vetanādānakarmaṇaḥ |
ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmaṃ samayabhedinām || 8.218|| This Dharma has been fully declared for those whose duty is the acceptance of wages or gifts; henceforth, I shall declare the Dharma that applies to those who transgress sacred agreements. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises from conscious choice and contractual integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of Samaya (sacred agreement) Restoration logic prioritizes re-alignment with original intent over punitive consequences Consciousness alignment is the ultimate determinant of lawful action

title: manu 8.219
content: यो ग्रामदेशसङ्घानां कृत्वा सत्येन संविदम् । विसंवदेन्नरो लोभात्तं राष्ट्राद्विप्रवासयेत् ॥ ८.२१९॥ yo grāmadesasaṅghānāṁ kṛtvā satyena saṁvidam | visaṁvadennaro lobhāttaṁ rāṣṭrādvipravāsayet || 8.219 || He who, having entered into a truthful agreement with village communities or territorial assemblies, breaches it out of greed—such a person shall be removed from the nation.
