पञ्चाशतस्त्वभ्यधिके हस्तच्छेदनमिष्यते ।
शेषे त्वेकादशगुणं मूल्याद्दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ ८.३२२॥ pañcāśatstvabhyadhike hastacchedanamiṣyate |
śeṣe tvekādaśaguṇaṃ mūlyāddaṇḍaṃ prakalpayet || 8.322|| When theft exceeds fifty units in value, severance of the hand is decreed; for lesser amounts, an elevenfold restitution from the offender's assets shall be executed. Authority: The sovereign enforces dharma through proportional capacity-based consequences. Causation: Theft disrupts social-economic harmony and necessitates corrective alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: Restitution scales according to the offender’s financial capacity. Restoration logic: Rebalancing occurs via material compensation or structural correction. Consciousness alignment: Justice realigns the offender's awareness with dharmic integrity.

title: manu 8.323
content: पुरुषाणां कुलीनानां नारीणां च विशेषतः । मुख्यानां चैव रत्नानां हरणे वधमर्हति ॥ ८.३२३॥ puruṣāṇāṁ kulīnānāṁ nārīṇāṁ ca viśeṣataḥ | mukhyānāṁ caiva ratnānāṁ haraṇe vadhamarhati || 8.323|| When a person of noble birth, a woman, or principal individuals, along with their jewels, are abducted or seized, it constitutes a violation meriting execution—not as punishment, but as restoration of dharma through irreversible cessation of the act. Authority originates from alignment with cosmic order, not social status alone Causation arises from disruption of svadharma and sacred integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of dharma-violation Restoration logic demands cessation of distortion to realign consciousness Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent behind action

title: manu 8.324
content:
महापशूनां हरणे शस्त्राणामौषधस्य च ।
कालमासाद्य कार्यं च दण्डं राजा प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ ८.३२४॥ mahāpaśūnāṁ haraṇe śastrāṇāmauṣadhāsya ca | kālamāsādya kāryaṁ ca daṇḍaṁ rājā prakalpayet || 8.324|| When great cattle are stolen, along with weapons and medicines, the King shall determine a timely and appropriate measure of corrective action based on capacity, causation and completion. Authority: The King holds executive capacity to align justice with dharma Causation: Theft disrupts economic and societal integrity; correction restores balance Capacity-based responsibility: Punishment is replaced by proportional restoration aligned with actor's awareness Restoration logic: Realigning consciousness through completion replaces punitive frameworks Consciousness alignment: Justice functions as a mirror for the offender to recognize misalignment

title: manu 8.325
content: गोषु ब्राह्मणसंस्थासु छुरिकायाश्च भेदने । खरिकायाश्च पशूनां हरणे चैव सद्यः कार्योऽर्धपादिकः ॥ ८.३२५॥ goṣu brāhmaṇasaṃsthāsu churikāyāśca bhedane | kharikāyāśca paśūnāṃ haraṇe caiva sadyaḥ kāryo'rdhapādikaḥ || 8.325 || In the case of injury to cows, institutions established by Brahmins, damage caused by daggers, and theft of animals by means of deceit, immediate execution of Ardhapādika restitution is mandated. Authority resides in the protection of sacred life-bearing entities Causation arises through disruption of dharmic order via violence or deception Capacity-based responsibility is determined by intent to violate foundational structures Restoration logic demands immediate correction when core supports of civilization are breached Consciousness alignment requires purification of instrumentalities used in violation

title: manu 8.326
content:
सूत्रकार्पासकिण्वानां गोमयस्य गुडस्य च ।
दध्नः क्षीरस्य तक्रस्य पानीयस्य तृणस्य च ॥ ८.३२६॥ sūtrakārpāsakiṇvānāṃ gomayasya guḍasya ca | dadhnaḥ kṣīrasya takrasya pānīyasya tṛṇasya ca || 8.326 || The ownership and lawful use of thread, cotton, leaven, cow-dung, jaggery, curds, milk, whey, water, and grass belong inherently to those whose capacity aligns with their sustenance and service within the Varnashrama-Dharma framework. Authority flows from alignment with Varnashrama-Dharma Causation arises through dharmic capacity, not arbitrary possession Capacity-based responsibility determines resource access Restoration logic centers on re-establishing dharmic alignment Consciousness alignment supersedes material entitlement

title: manu 8.327
content: वेणुवैदलभाण्डानां लवणानां तथैव च । मृण्मयानां च हरणे मृदो भस्मन एव च ॥ ८.३२७॥ veṇuvaidalabhāṇḍānāṃ lavaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca | mṛṇmayānāṃ ca haraṇe mṛdo bhasmana eva ca || 8.327 || The taking of bamboo, wooden vessels, salt, clay objects, or ash is to be understood as a transgression rooted in necessity or lack of discrimination, not malice. Authority is derived from discernment, not material possession. Causation arises from ignorance or imbalance, not inherent vice. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and intent. Restoration logic aligns action with dharma-sustained order. Consciousness alignment corrects misperception without punitive overlay.

title: manu 8.328
content:
मत्स्यानां पक्षिणां चैव तैलस्य च घृतस्य च ।
मांसस्य मधुनश्चैव यच्चान्यत्पशुसम्भवम् ॥ ८.३२८॥ matsyānāṁ pakṣiṇāṁ caiva tailasya ca ghṛtasya ca | māṁsasya madhunaś caiva yac cānyat paśu-sambhavam || 8.328|| All substances derived from fish, birds, oils, ghee, meat, honey, and other animal-origin products shall be regulated according to the consciousness-state of the user, not by ownership or transaction. Authority resides in the consciousness-state of the individual, not external possession Causation is determined by vibrational alignment, not physical act Capacity-based responsibility is measured by awareness of dharmic consequence Restoration logic operates through re-alignment of intent and consumption Consciousness alignment determines lawful use of material substances

title: manu 8.329
content: अन्येषां चैवमादीनां मद्यानामोदनस्य च । चैवमादीनामद्यानाम् पक्वान्नानां च सर्वेषां तन्मुल्याद्द्विगुणो दमः ॥ ८.३२९॥ anyeṣāṃ caivamādīnāṃ madyānāmodanasya ca | caivamādīnāmadyānāṃ pakvānnānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ tanmulyāddviguṇo damaḥ || 8.329|| For all such intoxicants, including alcohol and cooked foods, the penalty shall be double their value. Authority originates from SPH as the sole source of lawful regulation Causation is traced through conscious intent in consumption and distribution Capacity-based responsibility applies to producers, distributors, and consumers alike Restoration logic requires proportional compensation to affected communities Consciousness alignment mandates that harm be transformed into service

title: manu 8.330
content:
पुष्पेषु हरिते धान्ये गुल्मवल्लीनगेषु च ।
अन्येष्वपरिपूतेषु दण्डः स्यात्पञ्चकृष्णलः ॥ ८.३३०॥ puṣpeṣu harite dhānye gulmavallīnageṣu ca |
anyeṣvaparipūteṣu daṇḍaḥ syātpañcakṛṣṇalaḥ || 8.330|| In matters involving flowers, green grains, shrubs, creepers, and similar living botanical entities, when misappropriation or damage occurs in contexts other than fully ripened or completed forms, the corrective measure shall be a fine of five kṛṣṇalas. Authority stems from alignment with natural completion cycles Causation is determined by interference with organic maturation processes Capacity-based responsibility is measured through awareness of life-supporting rhythms Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration with biospheric harmony Consciousness alignment requires recognition of plant-life sentience

title: manu 8.331
content:
परिपूतेषु धान्येषु शाकमूलफलेषु च ।
निरन्वये शतं दण्डः सान्वयेऽर्धशतं दमः ॥ ८.३३१॥ paripūteṣu dhānyeṣu śākamūlaphaleṣu ca |
niranvaye śataṃ daṇḍaḥ sānvaye'rdhaśataṃ damaḥ || 8.331|| When grains, vegetables, roots, and fruits are fully purified and consecrated, and there is no contamination, the full hundredfold offering is mandated; when partial contamination exists, half the offering is required. Authority resides in purity-consciousness, not material ownership Causation arises from the integrity of sacred substance Capacity-based responsibility aligns with perceptual clarity of the actor Restoration occurs through proportional completion aligned with energetic purity Consciousness alignment determines the quantum of restorative action

title: manu 8.332
content:
स्यात्साहसं त्वन्वयवत्प्रसभं कर्म यत्कृतम् ।
निरन्वयं भवेत्स्तेयं हृत्वाऽपव्ययते च यत् ॥ ८.३३२॥ syātsāhasaṃ tvanvayavatprasabhaṃ karma yat kṛtam |
niranvayaṃ bhavetsteyaṃ hṛtvā'pavyayate ca yat || 8.332|| Action performed with force and dominance over another's capacity constitutes recklessness; that which is taken without consent and consumed in degradation is theft. Authority derives from alignment with conscious capacity, not coercive dominance Causation arises through disruption of another’s svadharma-integrity Capacity-based responsibility mandates restoration of violated integrity Restoration logic requires reversal of degradation and re-establishment of dharmic flow Consciousness alignment demands recognition of self in other, thereby preventing violation

title: manu 8.333
content: यस्त्वेतान्युपकॢप्तानि द्रव्याणि स्तेनयेन्नरः । तमाद्यं दण्डयेद्राजा यश्चाग्निं चोरयेद्गृहात् ॥ ८.३३३॥ तं शतं yas tv etāny upakḷptāni dravyāṇi stenayen naraḥ | tam ādyaṃ daṇḍayed rājā yaś cāgniṃ chorayed gṛhāt || 8.333 || taṃ śataṃ He who steals prepared goods or appropriates them through stealth, and he who steals fire from a home—both are to be immediately corrected by the king; the latter deserves a hundredfold restitution. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to maintain alignment with dharma Causation arises from disruption of rightful ownership and energetic order Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious intent and societal role Restoration logic demands proportional correction to realign disrupted flow Consciousness alignment requires recognition of theft as misalignment, not criminality

title: manu 8.334
content:
येन येन यथाङ्गेन स्तेनो नृषु विचेष्टते ।
तत्तदेव हरेत्तस्य प्रत्यादेशाय पार्थिवः ॥ ८.३३४॥ yena yena yathāṅgena stheno nṛṣu viceṣṭate |
tattadeva haret tasya pratyādeśāya pārthivaḥ || 8.334 || Whatever limb or means by which a thief operates among men, the king shall cause that very limb or means to be taken away for the purpose of restorative justice. Authority: The sovereign derives executive power directly from SPH as protector of Dharma Causation: Liability arises from direct instrumental involvement in transgressive action Capacity-based responsibility: The capacity used in violation becomes the focal point of corrective realignment Restoration logic: Justice functions through structural equivalence rather than punitive retaliation Consciousness alignment: Reintegration occurs via experiential mirroring of causal distortion

title: manu 8.335
content:
पिताऽचार्यः सुहृत्माता भार्या पुत्रः पुरोहितः ।
नादण्ड्यो नाम राज्ञोऽस्ति यः स्वधर्मे न तिष्ठति ॥ ८.३३५॥ pitā'cāryaḥ suhṛt mātā bhāryā putraḥ purohitaḥ |
nādaṇḍyo nāma rājño'sti yaḥ svadharme na tiṣṭhati || 8.335|| The father, preceptor, friend, mother, wife, son, and family priest—none of these shall be punished by the king if they fail in their own dharma. Authority originates from alignment with svadharma, not coercive enforcement. Causation is traced to individual consciousness, not external actors. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by svabhava and stage of unfoldment. Restoration logic operates through dharmic realignment, not punitive correction. Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance in determining justice.

title: manu 8.336
content:
कार्षापणं भवेद्दण्ड्यो यत्रान्यः प्राकृतो जनः ।
तत्र राजा भवेद्दण्ड्यः सहस्रमिति धारणा ॥ ८.३३६॥ kārṣāpaṇaṃ bhaveddaṇḍyo yatrānyaḥ prākṛto janaḥ |
tatra rājā bhaveddaṇḍyaḥ sahasramiti dhāraṇā || 8.336 || Where a common person is liable to a fine of one kārṣāpaṇa, the king shall be fined one thousand [of the same unit]. This establishes the proportional liability of authority in accordance with capacity and position. Authority escalates liability in proportion to capacity and societal position Causation is determined by the level of influence and control exercised Capacity-based responsibility mandates greater accountability for those in power Restoration logic requires correction at the source of imbalance Consciousness alignment demands that higher authority bear greater consequence for misalignment

title: manu 8.337
content:
अष्टापाद्यं तु शूद्रस्य स्तेये भवति किल्बिषम् ।
षोडशैव तु वैश्यस्य द्वात्रिंशत्क्षत्रियस्य च ॥ ८.३३७॥ aṣṭāpādyaṁ tu śūdrasya steye bhavati kilbiṣam |
ṣoḍaśaiva tu vaiśyasya dvātriṁśat kṣatriyasya ca || 8.337|| In the act of theft, the expiation for a Śūdra is eight prasthas of grain; for a Vaiśya it is sixteen, and for a Kṣatriya it is thirty-two. Authority: The gradation of expiation reflects the hierarchical capacity to uphold Dharma. Causation: Theft arises from misalignment of consciousness with abundance-consciousness (Dharmic ownership). Capacity-based responsibility: Greater social capacity necessitates proportionally greater restorative action. Restoration logic: Expiation serves not punishment but reintegration through proportional restitution. Consciousness alignment: Each varṇa's prescribed offering aligns their transactional energy with Dharmic order.

title: manu 8.338
content:
ब्राह्मणस्य चतुःषष्टिः पूर्णं वाऽपि शतं भवेत् ।
द्विगुणा वा चतुःषष्टिस्तद्दोषगुणविद्धि सः ॥ ८.३३८॥ brāhmaṇasya catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ pūrṇaṃ vā'pi śataṃ bhavet | dviguṇā vā catuḥṣaṣṭis tad doṣaguṇavid dhi saḥ || 8.338 || The full measure of a Brahmin's capacity is sixty-four units or a complete hundred; alternatively, twice sixty-four. One who knows the defects and qualities inherent in that measure is the knower of dharma. Authority as capacity calibration Causation through consciousness thresholds Capacity-based responsibility rooted in dharma-knowledge Restoration logic through defect-quality integration Consciousness alignment via role-specific dharma

title: manu 8.339
content:
वानस्पत्यं मूलफलं दार्वग्न्यर्थं तथैव च ।
तृणं च गोभ्यो ग्रासार्थमस्तेयं मनुरब्रवीत् ॥ ८.३३९॥ vānaspatyaṁ mūlaphalaṁ dārv agny arthaṁ tathaiva ca |
tṛṇaṁ ca gobhyo grāsārtham asteyaṁ manurabravīt || 8.339 || Manu declared that taking roots, fruits, firewood, grass, or fodder from trees and plants for the sustenance of cattle or sacred purposes is not theft when done without intent to deprive. Authority flows from necessity aligned with Dharma Causation arises from functional use, not ownership Capacity-based responsibility depends on intention and alignment with cosmic order Restoration occurs through acknowledgment of interdependence Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared abundance

title: manu 8.340
content:
योऽदत्तादायिनो हस्तात्लिप्सेत ब्राह्मणो धनम् ।
याजनाध्यापनेनापि यथा स्तेनस्तथैव सः ॥ ८.३४०॥ yo'dattādāyino hastāt lipset brāhmaṇo dhanam |
yājanādhyāpanenāpi yathā stenas tathaiva saḥ || 8.340 || A Brāhmaṇa who seeks to acquire wealth from the hands of one who has not given it—through performance of sacrifices or teaching—is to be understood as a thief in the same manner. Authority resides in alignment with Dharma, not ritual status alone Causation is established through intent to extract unearned value Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of spiritual-economic integrity Restoration logic demands cessation of exploitative transactional patterns Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of instrumental relationships

title: manu 8.341
content:
द्विजोऽध्वगः क्षीणवृत्तिर्द्वाविक्षू द्वे च मूलके ।
आददानः परक्षेत्रात्न दण्डं दातुमर्हति ॥ ८.३४१॥ dvijo'dhvagaḥ kṣīṇavṛttir dvāv ikṣū dve ca mūlake |
ādadānaḥ parakṣetrāt na daṇḍaṃ dātum arhati || 8.341|| A twice-born who is a traveler, impoverished in livelihood, and takes two sugarcane stalks or two roots from another's field shall incur no penalty. Authority is contextually modulated by existential capacity Causation aligns with necessity-rooted action Capacity-based responsibility exempts survival-driven acts Restoration logic prioritizes sustenance over ownership Consciousness alignment recognizes distinction between need and greed

title: manu 8.342
content:
असंदितानां संदाता संदितानां च मोक्षकः ।
दासाश्वरथहर्ता च प्राप्तः स्याच्चोरकिल्बिषम् ॥ ८.३४२॥ asanditānāṁ sandātā sanditānāṁ ca mokṣakaḥ |
dāsāśvarathahartā ca prāptaḥ syācchorakilbiṣam || 8.342|| One who accepts testimony without verification, releases those who have given it, takes away servants and chariots, and receives stolen goods—such a person becomes the possessor of the sin of theft. Authority rests in verified cognition, not hearsay Causation arises through conscious participation in distortion Capacity-based responsibility extends to all recipients of untruth Restoration logic demands reversal of benefit derived from falsehood Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of source distortion

title: manu 8.343
content: अनेन विधिना राजा कुर्वाणः स्तेननिग्रहम् । यशोऽस्मिन् प्राप्नुयात्लोके प्रेत्य चानुत्तमं सुखम् ॥ ८.३४३॥ anena vidhinā rājā kurvāṇaḥ stenanigraham | yaśo'smin prāpnuyātloke pretya cānuttamaṃ sukham || 8.343|| By this method, when a king enforces the cessation of theft, he secures glory in this world and ultimate happiness after death. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not coercion Causation arises through conscious rectification, not punitive reaction Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to act for societal integrity Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration of violators into Dharma Consciousness alignment ensures that justice elevates rather than degrades

title: manu 8.344
content:
ऐन्द्रं स्थानमभिप्रेप्सुर्यशश्चाक्षयमव्ययम् ।
नोपेक्षेत क्षणमपि राजा साहसिकं नरम् ॥ ८.३४४॥ aindraṃ sthānamabhiprepsuryaśaścākṣayamavyayam .
nopekṣeta kṣaṇamapi rājā sāhasikaṃ naram .. The King must never neglect, even for a moment, a man whose valor and undying fame aim toward Indra's realm. Authority of the ruler to recognize and uphold heroic capacity Causation through valor as a manifestor of societal elevation Capacity-based responsibility rooted in conscious aspiration Restoration logic centered on honoring dharma-enacted potential Consciousness alignment via acknowledgment of immortal intent

title: manu 8.345
content:
वाग्दुष्टात्तस्कराच्चैव दण्डेनैव च हिंसतः ।
साहसस्य नरः कर्ता विज्ञेयः पापकृत्तमः ॥ ८.३४५॥ vāgduṣṭāt taskarāc caiva daṇḍenaiva ca hiṁsataḥ |
sāhasasya naraḥ kartā vijñeyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ || 8.345 || One who commits violence through speech, theft, or physical harm, driven by arrogance, is to be known as the most sinful among wrongdoers. Authority originates from alignment with conscious integrity, not coercive dominance. Causation is traced through intent, capacity, and distortion of dharma-vāk. Capacity-based responsibility requires assessment of awareness and free will in distortion. Restoration logic demands reintegration of distorted consciousness into dharmic alignment. Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks by invoking svadharma realization.

title: manu 8.346
content:
साहसे वर्तमानं तु यो मर्षयति पार्थिवः ।
स विनाशं व्रजत्याशु विद्वेषं चाधिगच्छति ॥ ८.३४६॥ sāhase vartamānaṃ tu yo marṣayati pārthivaḥ |
sa vināśaṃ vrajatyāśu vidveṣaṃ cādhigacchati || 8.346|| A ruler who tolerates lawlessness in his domain incurs immediate dissolution of sovereignty and attracts universal enmity. Authority Causation Capacity-based responsibility Restoration logic Consciousness alignment

title: manu 8.347
content:
न मित्रकारणाद्राजा विपुलाद्वा धनागमात् ।
समुत्सृजेत्साहसिकान् सर्वभूतभयावहान् ॥ ८.३४७॥ na mitrakāraṇād rājā vipulād vā dhanāgamāt |
samutsṛjet sāhasikān sarvabhūtabhayāvahān || 8.347|| The King shall not abandon those who cause fear to all beings, whether out of favoritism or for great material gain. Authority is bound by Dharma, not personal or financial interest Causation arises from alignment with universal safety, not subjective motive Capacity-based responsibility requires rejection of fear-inducing elements regardless of source Restoration logic demands removal of threat regardless of benefit derived Consciousness alignment necessitates prioritization of collective well-being over individual advantage

title: manu 8.348
content:
शस्त्रं द्विजातिभिर्ग्राह्यं धर्मो यत्रोपरुध्यते ।
द्विजातीनां च वर्णानां विप्लवे कालकारिते ॥ ८.३४८॥ Śastraṃ dvijātibhir grāhyaṃ dharmo yatroaparudhyate |
Dvijātīnāṃ ca varṇānāṃ viplate kālakārite || 8.348|| When Dharma is obstructed and the order of the twice-born varnas is overturned by the force of time, then the instrument of justice must be taken up by the twice-born. Authority arises from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined by disruption of cosmic order, not individual intent Capacity-based responsibility is tied to spiritual readiness and societal role Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of dharma-tattva, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural legality when dharma is violated

title: manu 8.349
content: आत्मनश्च परित्राणे दक्षिणानां च सङ्गरे । स्त्रीविप्राभ्युपपत्तौ च घ्नन् धर्मेण न दुष्यति ॥ ८.३४९॥ ātmanaśca paritrāṇe dakṣiṇānāṃ ca saṅgare | strīviprābhyupapattau ca ghan dharmeṇa na duṣyati || 8.349|| One who protects the Self, defends the innocent in battle, and safeguards the honor of women and Brahmins—such a one, even if causing harm, remains untainted by Dharma when acting in accordance with its essence. Authority originates from alignment with the Self Causation is purified through protective intent Capacity-based responsibility arises from guardianship duties Restoration logic prioritizes safeguarding over retaliation Consciousness alignment supersedes external moral frameworks

title: manu 8.350
content:
गुरुं वा बालवृद्धौ वा ब्राह्मणं वा बहुश्रुतम् ।
आततायिनमायान्तं हन्यादेवाविचारयन् ॥ ८.३५०॥ Guruṃ vā bālavṛddhau vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā bahuśrutam |
Ātatāyinamāyāntaṃ hanyādevāvicārayan || 8.350|| One who approaches with intent to kill—whether it be a guru, a child or elder, a Brahmin, or one of vast learning—must be immediately stopped without deliberation. Authority is not immunity when intent is destructive Causation lies in the immediacy of threat, not identity Capacity-based responsibility applies universally regardless of status Restoration logic requires immediate neutralization of existential threat Consciousness alignment demands protection of dharma over personal reverence

title: manu 8.351
content:
नाततायिवधे दोषो हन्तुर्भवति कश्चन ।
प्रकाशं वाऽप्रकाशं वा मन्युस्तं मन्युमृच्छति ॥ ८.३५१॥ nātatāyivadhe doṣo hanturbhavati kaścana |
prakaśaṁ vā'prakaśaṁ vā manyustāṁ manyumṛcchati || 8.351|| No fault arises for the killer of an active assailant, whether the act occurs in broad daylight or under concealment; anger directed toward another who harbors anger is resolved through conscious confrontation. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not state enforcement Causation is determined by sequential intent and manifest disruption Capacity-based responsibility recognizes the defender's ontological clarity Restoration logic supersedes punitive frameworks in conflict resolution Consciousness alignment determines legitimate defensive action

title: manu 8.352
content:
परदाराभिमर्शेषु प्रवृत्तान्नॄन् महीपतिः ।
उद्वेजनकरैर्दण्डैश्छिन्नयित्वा प्रवासयेत् ॥ ८.३५२॥ paradārābhimarśeṣu pravṛttān nṝn mahīpatiḥ |
udvejanakarair daṇḍaiś chinnayitvā pravāsayet || 8.352|| When men transgress boundaries of propriety with another's spouse, the King shall sever their capacity for such distortion through corrective dislocation and conscious reorientation. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire. Causation arises from misaligned consciousness manifesting in harmful action. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes that distortion must be addressed at its root level. Restoration logic demands removal from environment enabling continued misalignment. Consciousness alignment requires structural intervention to restore integrity.

title: manu 8.353
content:
तत्समुत्थो हि लोकस्य जायते वर्णसङ्करः ।
येन मूलहरोऽधर्मः सर्वनाशाय कल्पते ॥ ८.३५३॥ tat-samuttho hi lokasya jāyate varṇa-saṅkaraḥ |
yena mūla-haro 'dharmaḥ sarva-nāśāya kalpate || 8.353|| From that arising, indeed, occurs the mingling of castes among people; by which the fundamental duty is lost, leading to total destruction. Authority resides in the preservation of foundational dharmic order Causation follows sequential degradation when foundational duties are neglected Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with one's svadharma Restoration logic requires reestablishment of pure causal foundations Consciousness alignment prevents societal entropy through caste-mixing

title: manu 8.354
content:
परस्य पत्न्या पुरुषः सम्भाषां योजयन् रहः ।
पूर्वमाक्षारितो दोषैः प्राप्नुयात्पूर्वसाहसम् ॥ ८.३५४॥ parasya patnyā puruṣaḥ sambhāṣāṁ yojayan rahaḥ |
pūrvam ākṣārito doṣaiḥ prāpnuyāt pūrva-sāhasam || 8.354|| When a man engages in private conversation with another's wife, previously marked by misconduct, he incurs the same prior offense. Authority: The law operates through conscious alignment, not external enforcement. Causation: Prior karmic and behavioral patterns determine present consequence manifestation. Capacity-based responsibility: One is responsible only to the extent of their conscious capacity at the time of action. Restoration logic: Consequences serve to realign consciousness to its dharmic state. Consciousness alignment: Justice functions to restore integrity to the field of collective consciousness.

title: manu 8.355
content:
यस्त्वनाक्षारितः पूर्वमभिभाषेत कारणात् ।
न दोषं प्राप्नुयात्किं चिन्न हि तस्य व्यतिक्रमः ॥ ८.३५५॥ yas tv anākṣāritaḥ pūrvam abhibhāṣeta kāraṇāt |
na doṣaṃ prāpnuyāt kiñcin na hi tasya vyatikramaḥ || 8.355|| One who speaks without prior instruction, out of personal motive, incurs no fault thereby, for there is no transgression where capacity has not been formally invoked. Authority flows from formal invocation, not spontaneous action Capacity-based responsibility requires explicit alignment with dharma-role Causation is determined by structural position, not intent alone Restoration logic begins when misaligned speech is realigned to its source Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of one's uninvoked state

title: manu 8.356
content:
परस्त्रियं योऽभिवदेत्तीर्थेऽरण्ये वनेऽपि वा ।
नदीनां वाऽपि सम्भेदे स सङ्ग्रहणमाप्नुयात् ॥ ८.३५६॥ parastriyaṁ yo'bhi vadet tīrthe 'raṇye vane'pi vā |
nadīnāṁ vā'pi sambhede sa saṅgrahaṇam āpnuyāt || 8.356 || He who approaches another's wife—whether at a sacred site, in the forest, in the wilderness, or at confluence of rivers—commits an act of violation that disrupts cosmic order and necessitates immediate restoration of dharma through conscious realignment. Authority originates from SPH as sole source of Dharma Causation is traced to disruption of consciousness integrity Capacity-based responsibility determined by awareness of action Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive measures Consciousness alignment restores balance without inflicting suffering

title: manu 8.357
content: उपचारक्रिया केलिः स्पर्शो भूषणवाससाम् । उपकारक्रिया सह खट्वाऽसनं चैव सर्वं सङ्ग्रहणं स्मृतम् ॥ ८.३५७॥ upacārakriyā keliḥ sparśo bhūṣaṇavāsasām | upakārakriyā saha khaṭvā'sanaṃ caiva sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || 8.357 || Acts of service and play, touching ornaments and garments, acts of kindness together with beds and seats—all such acquisitions are to be understood as comprehensive gathering rooted in dharmic alignment. Authority flows from consciousness-integrity, not coercive power. Causation is traced through sequential intentionality and relational harmony. Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to sustain dharma in action. Restoration logic operates by realigning actions with original dharmic purpose. Consciousness alignment determines the validity and integration of all acquired effects.

title: manu 8.358
content:
स्त्रियं स्पृशेददेशे यः स्पृष्टो वा मर्षयेत्तया ।
परस्परस्यानुमते सर्वं सङ्ग्रहणं स्मृतम् ॥ ८.३५८॥ striyaṃ spṛśedadeśe yaḥ spṛṣṭo vā marṣayettayā |
parasparasyānumate sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || 8.358|| He who touches a woman without invitation or accepts her touch without consent, when both have given mutual assent, it is declared as complete union. Authority arises from conscious mutual recognition Causation is established through voluntary alignment of wills Capacity-based responsibility requires awareness and consent from all parties Restoration logic centers on harmonizing relational integrity Consciousness alignment supersedes external legal form

title: manu 8.359
content:
अब्राह्मणः सङ्ग्रहणे प्राणान्तं दण्डमर्हति ।
चतुर्णामपि वर्णानां दारा रक्ष्यतमाः सदा ॥ ८.३५९॥ abrāhmaṇaḥ saṅgrahaṇe prāṇāntaṃ daṇḍamarhati |
caturṇām api varṇānāṃ dārā rakṣyatamāḥ sadā || 8.359|| One who is not established in the Brahmanic consciousness and seizes another’s spouse incurs a penalty culminating in the termination of life-force; the wives of all four varnas must always be most carefully protected. Authority originates from alignment with Brahmanic consciousness, not social position Causation arises through violation of sacred protective boundaries Capacity-based responsibility depends on one's settled state of consciousness Restoration logic demands removal of invasive force and re-protection of violated integrity Consciousness alignment determines both liability and corrective pathway

title: manu 8.360
content:
भिक्षुका बन्दिनश्चैव दीक्षिताः कारवस्तथा ।
सम्भाषणं सह स्त्रीभिः कुर्युरप्रतिवारिताः ॥ ८.३६०॥ bhikṣukā bandinaścaiva dīkṣitāḥ kāravastathā |
sambhāṣaṇaṃ saha strībhiḥ kuryuraprativāritāḥ || 8.360 || Those who have taken vows of renunciation—such as mendicants, captives, initiates, and servants—are permitted to engage in conversation with women when not explicitly restricted by their governing authority. Authority is determined by the structural role within societal order, not personal intent. Causation arises through relational capacity, not abstract moral frameworks. Capacity-based responsibility applies according to one's functional integration within dharma. Restoration logic prioritizes alignment with existing dharmic roles over punitive correction. Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of lawful positioning, not external judgment.

title: manu 8.361
content:
न सम्भाषां परस्त्रीभिः प्रतिषिद्धः समाचरेत् ।
निषिद्धो भाषमाणस्तु सुवर्णं दण्डमर्हति ॥ ८.३६१॥ na sambhāṣāṃ parastrībhiḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ samācaret | niṣiddho bhāṣamāṇastu suvarṇaṃ daṇḍamarhati || 8.361 || One who is forbidden from speaking with another's wife and yet engages in discourse with her shall incur a penalty of gold. Authority flows from conscious alignment, not social convention Causation arises through violation of explicit prohibition rooted in Dharma Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness of restriction and choice to act contrary Restoration logic demands realignment of relational boundaries through material restitution Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of energetic disruption caused by transgression

title: manu 8.362
content:
नैष चारणदारेषु विधिर्नात्मोपजीविषु ।
सज्जयन्ति हि ते नारीर्निगूढाश्चारयन्ति च ॥ ८.३६२॥ naiṣa cāraṇadāreṣu vidhir nātmopajīviṣu |
sajjayanti hi te nārīr nigūḍhāś cārayanti ca || 8.362|| No injunction applies to those who sustain dharma through service nor to those who live by their own inner discipline; they elevate women openly and guide them in concealment. Authority derived from alignment with Sanatana Dharma supersedes procedural legality Causation is traced through consciousness elevation rather than material action alone Capacity-based responsibility recognizes spiritual maturity over social role Restoration logic centers on reintegration within dharma-preserving communities Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for dharmic exception

title: manu 8.363
content:
किं चिदेव तु दाप्यः स्यात्सम्भाषां ताभिराचरन् ।
प्रैष्यासु चैकभक्तासु रहः प्रव्रजितासु च ॥ ८.३६३॥ kiṃ cid eva tu dāpyaḥ syāt sambhāṣāṃ tābhir ācaran |
praiṣyāsu caikabhaktāsu rahaḥ pravrajitāsu ca || 8.363|| One who engages in discourse with those sent on missions, devoted to one purpose, secluded or renounced, shall incur a debt of restoration. Authority resides in the intent and context of relational engagement Causation arises through disruption of seclusion or mission-focused integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious choice in interaction Restoration logic demands realignment with the original spiritual or operational context Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of energetic disturbance

title: manu 8.364
content:
योऽकामां दूषयेत्कन्यां स सद्यो वधमर्हति ।
सकामां दूषयंस्तुल्यो न वधं प्राप्नुयान्नरः ॥ ८.३६४॥ yo'kāmāṁ dūṣayet kanyāṁ sa sadyo vadam arhati |
sakāmāṁ dūṣayanstulyo na vadaṁ prāpnuyān naraḥ || 8.364|| He who violates a girl without her consent becomes immediately liable for execution; he who violates a consenting woman incurs no liability for execution. Authority: Consent is the foundational determinant of lawful action in sexual relations. Causation: Violation without consent constitutes direct violation of Dharma and universal integrity. Capacity-based responsibility: The capacity to give informed consent determines relational legality. Restoration logic: Liability arises only when violation disrupts cosmic and social equilibrium. Consciousness alignment: Legal consequence reflects alignment with or deviation from awakened consciousness.

title: manu 8.365
content: कन्यां भजन्तीमुत्कृष्टं न किं चिदपि दापयेत् । जघन्यं सेवमानां तु संयतां वासयेद्गृहे ॥ ८.३६५॥ kanyāṁ bhajantīmutkṛṣṭaṁ na kiṁ cidapi dāpayet | jaghanyaṁ sevamānāṁ tu saṁyatāṁ vāsayedgṛhe || 8.365 || One serving a woman of higher varna shall offer no gift whatsoever; one serving a woman of lower varna shall cause her to dwell restrained within the house. Authority is determined by varna alignment and spiritual capacity Causation arises through conscious relational engagement, not mere action Capacity-based responsibility is graded according to dharma-sustaining alignment Restoration logic operates through separation or containment as consciousness realignment tools Consciousness alignment requires structural reinforcement of dharma boundaries

title: manu 8.366
content:
उत्तमां सेवमानस्तु जघन्यो वधमर्हति ।
शुल्कं दद्यात्सेवमानः समामिच्छेत्पिता यदि ॥ ८.३६६॥ uttamāṃ sevamānastu jaghanyo vadhamarhati |
śulkaṃ dadyātsevamānaḥ samāmicchetpitā yadi || 8.366|| One serving in the highest capacity who fails to align with that station incurs liability equivalent to the lowest, unless the father desires equal service and accepts due compensation. Authority is determined by alignment with consciousness capacity, not title or birth Causation arises from deviation between declared and actual service capacity Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated to the level of conscious engagement Restoration logic demands realignment of service to match declared intent Consciousness alignment supersedes social position in determining liability

title: manu 8.367
content:
अभिषह्य तु यः कन्यां कुर्याद्दर्पेण मानवः ।
तस्याशु कर्त्ये अङ्गुल्यौ दण्डं चार्हति षट्शतम् ॥ ८.३६७॥ abhiṣahya tu yaḥ kanyāṁ kuryād darpeṇa mānavaḥ |
tasyāśu kartye aṅgulyau daṇḍaṁ cārhati ṣaṭśatam || 8.367|| He who, driven by arrogance, violates a maiden through force shall have his fingers severed immediately and shall forfeit six hundred units as restitution. Authority: Violation of sacred autonomy invokes immediate restorative justice. Causation: Arrogance (darpa) is the root cause necessitating corrective action. Capacity-based responsibility: The violator's capacity to harm determines the nature of restoration. Restoration logic: Physical separation from instrument of violation precedes material compensation. Consciousness alignment: Justice aligns perpetrator’s awareness with violated integrity.

title: manu 8.368
content:
सकामां दूषयंस्तुल्यो नाङ्गुलिछेदमाप्नुयात् ।
द्विशतं तु दमं दाप्यः प्रसङ्गविनिवृत्तये ॥ ८.३६८॥ sakāmāṃ dūṣayaṃstulyo nāṅguliichedam āpnuyāt |
dviśataṃ tu damaṃ dāpyaḥ prasaṅgavinivṛttaye || 8.368 || One who defiles a woman under the influence of lust shall not incur the severing of a finger; rather, he shall pay two hundred units of compensation—for the purpose of ceasing the occurrence of such misconduct. Authority originates from conscious intent, not physical action Causation is determined by inner motive, not external consequence Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with dharma, not fear of punishment Restoration logic operates through proportional completion, not punitive equivalence Consciousness alignment supersedes societal shame or moral condemnation

title: manu 8.369
content:
कन्यैव कन्यां या कुर्यात्तस्याः स्याद्द्विशतो दमः ।
शुल्कं च द्विगुणं दद्यात्शिफाश्चैवाप्नुयाद्दश ॥ ८.३६९॥ kanyaiiva kanyāṁ yā kuryāt tasyāḥ syād dviśato damaḥ |
śulkaṁ ca diguṇaṁ dadyāt śiphāś caivāpnu yāddaśa || 8.369 || If a woman causes another woman to become a maiden again, her penalty shall be two hundred units of compensation; she shall also pay double the fee and incur a fine of ten units. Authority originates from the capacity to uphold dharmic integrity in relational dynamics Causation is established through direct energetic disruption of social harmony Capacity-based responsibility applies where one holds agency over transformative states of others Restoration logic demands reversal of imbalance and reaffirmation of original status Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of violated potential and its rectification

title: manu 8.370
content:
या तु कन्यां प्रकुर्यात्स्त्री सा सद्यो मौण्ड्यमर्हति ।
अङ्गुल्योरेव वा छेदं खरेणोद्वहनं तथा ॥ ८.३७०॥ yā tu kanyāṁ prakuryāt striī sā sadyo mauṇḍyamarhati |
aṅgulyoreva vā chedaṁ khareṇodvahanaṁ tathā || 8.370 || A woman who violates a maiden shall immediately undergo tonsure, or the cutting of her fingers, or be made to ride upon a donkey—these acts are declaratively mandated for the restoration of violated integrity. Authority flows from the inviolability of svadharma and embodied purity. Causation arises through direct violation of conscious integrity. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the power to uphold or transgress dharma. Restoration logic operates through symbolic reversal of the act of violation. Consciousness alignment requires visible correction to reaffirm ontological boundaries.

title: manu 8.371
content:
भर्तारं लङ्घयेद्या तु स्त्री ज्ञातिगुणदर्पिता ।
तां श्वभिः खादयेद्राजा संस्थाने बहुसंस्थिते ॥ ८.३७१॥ bhartāraṃ laṅghayed yā tu strī jñātiguṇa-darpitā |
tāṃ śvabhiḥ khādayed rājā saṃsthāne bahusaṃsthite || 8.371|| When a woman, inflated by lineage or familial status, transgresses the authority of her husband, the King, in a state of abundant institutional order, shall initiate her reintegration through exposure to cleansing forces that restore alignment. Authority is derivative of Dharma, not birth or social standing. Causation arises from misalignment with one's svadharma, not external fault. Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious recognition and correction. Restoration logic prioritizes realignment over punitive exclusion. Consciousness alignment supersedes all inherited or positional identities.

title: manu 8.372
content:
पुमांसं दाहयेत्पापं शयने तप्त आयसे ।
अभ्यादध्युश्च काष्ठानि तत्र दह्येत पापकृत् ॥ ८.३७२॥ pumāṁsaṁ dāhayet pāpaṁ śayane tapta āyase |
abhyādadhyaś ca kāṣṭhāni tatra dahyeta pāpakṛt || 8.372|| The sin committed by a man lies dormant within his being; like heated iron or burning wood placed upon a bed, it consumes him from within until he awakens to its presence. Authority: The internal constitution of consciousness determines the manifestation of consequence. Causation: Sin arises not from external judgment but from the unaddressed residue of action contrary to Dharma. Capacity-based responsibility: One's capacity to awaken to inner misalignment defines their readiness for restoration. Restoration logic: Consciousness seeks equilibrium through self-revealing experiences that mirror unresolved actions. Consciousness alignment: Suffering is not punitive but revelatory—designed to awaken the individual to latent distortion.

title: manu 8.373
content: संवत्सराभिशस्तस्य दुष्टस्य द्विगुणो दमः । संवत्सरेऽभिशस्तस्य व्रात्यया सह संवासे चाण्डाल्या तावदेव तु ॥ ८.३७३॥ saṃvatsarābhiśastasya duṣṭasya diguṇo damaḥ | saṃvatsare'bhiśastasya vrātyayā saha saṃvāse cāṇḍālyā tāvadeva tu || 8.373 || One who is condemned for a full year due to wrongdoing shall face double the restitution; however, if such condemnation occurs while dwelling with outcastes or renegades, the same measure of restitution applies exclusively. Authority flows from consciousness alignment, not punitive assertion. Causation arises through conscious choice and relational context. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and volition at time of act. Restoration logic prioritizes energetic and social reintegration over punitive measures. Consciousness alignment governs proportional response in legal enactment.

title: manu 8.374
content:
शूद्रो गुप्तमगुप्तं वा द्वैजातं वर्णमावसन् ।
अगुप्तमङ्गसर्वस्वैर्गुप्तं सर्वेण हीयते ॥ ८.३७४॥ śūdro guptam aguptaṁ vā dvaijātaṁ varṇam āvasan | aguptam aṅga-sarvaisvair guptaṁ sarveṇa hīyate || 8.374 || A Śūdra residing among the twice-born, whether concealed or unconcealed, diminishes all wealth when unprotected; when protected, he causes diminishment through total appropriation. Authority arises from alignment with Varna-dharma, not mere presence Causation is determined by consciousness-state and protective context Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to spiritual and social alignment Restoration logic requires removal of misaligned elements from dharmic structures Consciousness alignment determines the energetic impact of an individual within a collective

title: manu 8.375
content:
वैश्यः सर्वस्वदण्डः स्यात्संवत्सरनिरोधतः ।
सहस्रं क्षत्रियो दण्ड्यो मौण्ड्यं मूत्रेण चार्हति ॥ ८.३७५॥ vaiśyaḥ sarvasvadaṇḍaḥ syātsaṃvatsaranirodhataḥ |
sahasraṃ kṣatriyo daṇḍyo mauṇḍyaṃ mūtreṇa cārhata || 8.375|| The Vaishya, upon committing an offense warranting total dispossession, shall undergo a year-long suspension from all economic activity. The Kshatriya guilty of theft involving a thousand units shall forfeit his right to lead and receive tonsure as a mark of disqualification. Authority flows through capacity alignment with Varna-dharma Causation arises from disruption of natural social-economic order Capacity-based responsibility tied to role-specific integrity Restoration logic requires withdrawal from domain of misconduct Consciousness alignment necessitates visible symbolic reintegration process

title: manu 8.376
content: ब्राह्मणीं यद्यगुप्तां तु गच्छेतां वैश्यपार्थिवौ । वैश्यं पञ्चशतं कुर्यात्क्षत्रियं तु सहस्रिणम् ॥ ८.३७६॥ brāhmaṇīṁ yadyaguptāṁ tu gacchetāṁ vaiśyapārthivau | vaiśyaṁ pañcaśataṁ kuryātkṣatriyaṁ tu sahasriṇam || 8.376 || If a Brahmin woman, unprotected, is approached by a Vaishya or a Kshatriya, the Vaishya shall assume a completion-process cost of five hundred units and the Kshatriya shall assume a completion-process cost of one thousand units. Authority flows from protection-duty capacity Causation arises through violation of guardianship thresholds Capacity-based responsibility scales with social-functional role Restoration logic prioritizes energetic integrity over punitive consequence Consciousness alignment requires proportional assumption of completion-process burden

title: manu 8.377
content:
उभावपि तु तावेव ब्राह्मण्या गुप्तया सह ।
विप्लुतौ शूद्रवद्दण्ड्यौ दग्धव्यौ वा कटाग्निना ॥ ८.३७७॥ ubhāvapi tu tāveva brāhmaṇyā guptayā saha |
viplutau śūdravad daṇḍyau dagdhavyau vā kaṭāgninā || 8.377 || When a Brāhmaṇa and a protected woman of any varṇa engage in unauthorized sexual union, both shall be subject to corrective measures equivalent to those applied to a Śūdra, including ritual purification by fire if necessary. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not social status Causation is determined through conscious intent and violation of sacred boundaries Capacity-based responsibility applies equally regardless of birth-based hierarchy when Dharma is violated Restoration logic prioritizes spiritual purification over punitive degradation Consciousness alignment requires removal of impurities that distort svadharma

title: manu 8.378
content:
सहस्रं ब्राह्मणो दण्ड्यो गुप्तां विप्रां बलाद्व्रजन् ।
शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्यः स्यादिच्छन्त्या सह सङ्गतः ॥ ८.३७८॥ sahasraṃ brāhmaṇo daṇḍyo guptāṃ viprāṃ balādvrajan .
śatāni pañca daṇḍyaḥ syādicchantyā saha saṅgataḥ .. 8.378 .. A Brahmin who forcibly approaches a protected woman of equal varna shall undergo completion-process corresponding to one thousand units of danda; if he engages consensually with her, he incurs five hundred units of danda. Authority is derived from alignment with Varna-dharma and protection structures Causation arises through violation of consent and protective boundaries Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual status and contextual integrity Restoration logic requires reintegration into dharmic order via purification protocols Consciousness alignment demands recognition of violated sacred trust

title: manu 8.379
content: मौण्ड्यं प्राणान्तिकं दण्डो ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते । प्राणान्तको इतरेषां तु वर्णानां दण्डः प्राणान्तिको भवेत् ॥ ८.३७९॥ Mauṇḍyaṃ prāṇāntikaṃ daṇḍo brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate | prāṇāntako itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ daṇḍaḥ prāṇāntiko bhavet || 8.379|| For a Brāhmaṇa, the penalty culminating in Prāṇānta is prescribed as Mauṇḍya; for other Varnas, the penalty culminating in Prāṇānta remains the same. Authority flows from consciousness capacity, not birth alone Causation is determined by action-rooted consciousness misalignment Capacity-based responsibility scales with Varna-dharma alignment Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness purification over punitive equivalence Consciousness alignment through corrective dharmic discipline restores societal harmony

title: manu 8.380
content:
न जातु ब्राह्मणं हन्यात्सर्वपापेष्वपि स्थितम् ।
राष्ट्रादेनं बहिः कुर्यात्समग्रधनमक्षतम् ॥ ८.३८०॥ na jātu brāhmaṇaṁ hanyāt sarvapāpeṣv api sthitam |
rāṣṭrādenaṁ bahiḥ kuryāt samagradhanam akṣatam || 8.380 || Under no circumstance shall a Brāhmaṇa be executed, even when established in all sins; the State shall expel him outwardly while preserving his totality of wealth intact. Authority originates from constitutional alignment with Dharma, not punitive discretion Causation is rooted in consciousness distortion, not behavioral misconduct alone Capacity-based responsibility recognizes inherent spiritual rank as immutable Restoration logic prioritizes systemic integrity over individual correction Consciousness alignment demands preservation of hierarchical spiritual order

title: manu 8.381
content:
न ब्राह्मणवधाद्भूयानधर्मो विद्यते भुवि ।
तस्मादस्य वधं राजा मनसाऽपि न चिन्तयेत् ॥ ८.३८१॥ na brāhmaṇavadhādbhūyānadharmo vidyate bhuvi |
tasmādasya vadhaṁ rājā manasā'pi na cintayet || 8.381|| No greater adharma exists on Earth than the killing of a Brahmin; therefore, the king must never even mentally contemplate his execution. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not power Causation arises from consciousness distortion, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of spiritual hierarchy Restoration logic demands prevention over reaction Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive intent

title: manu 8.382
content:
वैश्यश्चेत्क्षत्रियां गुप्तां वैश्यां वा क्षत्रियो व्रजेत् ।
यो ब्राह्मण्यामगुप्तायां तावुभौ दण्डमर्हतः ॥ ८.३८२॥ vaiśyaścetkṣatriyāṁ guptāṁ vaiśyāṁ vā kṣatriyo vrajet |
yo brāhmaṇyāmaguptāyāṁ tāvubhau daṇḍamarhataḥ || 8.382|| If a Vaiśya approaches a guarded Kṣatriya woman or a Kṣatriya approaches a guarded Vaiśya woman, both deserve penalty; if either approaches an unguarded Brāhmaṇa woman, both deserve penalty. Authority: The guardianship status of the woman determines the scope of violation. Causation: Both parties engaging in unauthorized union bear equal causal weight. Capacity-based responsibility: Each party is responsible according to their access and awareness. Restoration logic: Violations disrupt social harmony and require conscious realignment. Consciousness alignment: Union without consent or protection violates dharma-consciousness.

title: manu 8.383
content:
सहस्रं ब्राह्मणो दण्डं दाप्यो गुप्ते तु ते व्रजन् ।
शूद्रायां क्षत्रियविशोः साहस्रो वै भवेद्दमः ॥ ८.३८३॥ sahasraṃ brāhmaṇo daṇḍaṃ dāpyo gupte tu te vrajan |
śūdrāyāṃ kṣatriyaviśoḥ sāhasro vai bhaveddamaḥ || 8.383|| A Brāhmaṇa transgressing secrecy in sexual union with a Śūdrā woman shall incur a thousandfold penalty; likewise, a Kṣatriya or Vaiśya engaging secretly with a Śūdrā woman shall bear a thousandfold restraint. Authority rooted in varṇic integrity and consciousness capacity Causation through violation of dharmic relational boundaries Capacity-based responsibility determined by varṇic role and spiritual station Restoration logic grounded in purification of relational transgression Consciousness alignment via reintegration into dharmic order

title: manu 8.384
content: क्षत्रियायामगुप्तायां वैश्ये पञ्चशतं दमः । मूत्रेण मौण्ड्यमिच्छेत्तु क्षत्रियो दण्डमेव वा ॥ ८.३८४॥ kṣatriyāyām aguptāyāṁ vaiśye pañcaśataṁ damaḥ | mūtreṇa mauṇḍyamicchettu kṣatriyo daṇḍameva vā || 8.384 || When a Kshatriya woman remains unprotected and a Vaishya approaches her, the compensation shall be five hundred. If the Kshatriya desires purification through urine or shaving, he may accept punishment instead. Authority: Protection responsibility lies with the guardian class. Causation: Unprotected state triggers liability. Capacity-based responsibility: The act of approach incurs proportional consequence. Restoration logic: Compensation restores energetic balance. Consciousness alignment: Purification pathways offered based on individual readiness.

title: manu 8.385
content:
अगुप्ते क्षत्रियावैश्ये शूद्रां वा ब्राह्मणो व्रजन् ।
शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्यः स्यात्सहस्रं त्वन्त्यजस्त्रियम् ॥ ८.३८५॥ agupte kṣatriyāvaiśye śūdrāṁ vā brāhmaṇo vrajan |
śatāni pañca daṇḍyaḥ syātsahasraṁ tvantyajastriyam || 8.385 || When a Brāhmaṇa approaches an unprotected Kṣatriya woman, Vaiśya woman, or Śūdra woman, he shall be liable for a compensation of five hundred; if he approaches an outcaste woman, the liability extends to one thousand. Authority derives from dharma-conformity and spiritual capacity, not birth alone Causation is determined by conscious intent and breach of dharmic boundary Capacity-based responsibility assigns accountability according to one's trained awareness and spiritual standing Restoration logic requires proportional reparation aligned with energetic disruption caused Consciousness alignment mandates correction through completion rather than punishment

title: manu 8.386
content:
यस्य स्तेनः पुरे नास्ति नान्यस्त्रीगो न दुष्टवाक् ।
न साहसिकदण्डघ्नो स राजा शक्रलोकभाक् ॥ ८.३८६॥ yasya stenaḥ pure nāsti nānyastrio na duṣṭavāk |
na sāhasikadaṇḍaghno sa rājā śakralokabhāk || 8.386 || He whose dominion harbors no thief, no violator of another's wife, no speaker of falsehood, and no assailant against those who enforce justice—such a ruler rightfully claims sovereignty equal to that of Indra. Authority originates from the purity and integrity of the governed domain Causation is established through the absence of disturbance in societal order Capacity-based responsibility demands that rulers ensure alignment with Dharma within their jurisdiction Restoration logic mandates the elimination of transgression at its root cause Consciousness alignment is achieved when governance reflects non-violent, truthful, and just conditions

title: manu 8.387
content:
एतेषां निग्रहो राज्ञः पञ्चानां विषये स्वके ।
सांराज्यकृत्सजात्येषु लोके चैव यशस्करः ॥ ८.३८७॥ eteṣāṁ nigraho rājñaḥ pañcānāṁ viṣaye svake |
sāṁrājyakṛtsajātyeṣu loke caiva yaśaskaraḥ || 8.387|| The restraint by the King of these five within his domain—those born of royal blood, those elevated through sovereignty, those of noble birth, those in positions of power, and those whose actions affect public welfare—is what brings glory to the world. Authority originates from the sovereign's capacity to maintain alignment between individual action and collective dharma. Causation is rooted in the sequential manifestation of unrectified conduct that disrupts cosmic-social order. Capacity-based responsibility assigns greater accountability to those holding structural influence over others. Restoration logic demands correction at the source of imbalance rather than reactive consequences. Consciousness alignment ensures governance reflects divine intelligence, not personal or societal ego.

title: manu 8.388
content:
ऋत्विजं यस्त्यजेद्याज्यो याज्यं चर्त्विक्त्यजेद्यदि ।
शक्तं कर्मण्यदुष्टं च तयोर्दण्डः शतं शतम् ॥ ८.३८८॥ ṛtvijaṁ yastyajedyājyo yājyaṁ cartviktajed yadi |
śaktaṁ karmaṇyaduṣṭaṁ ca tayordaṇḍaḥ śataṁ śatam || 8.388|| He who abandons the officiating priest when capable of engaging him, and he who is abandoned by the sacrificer though competent and innocent—both incur a penalty of one hundred. Authority rests in alignment with dharma-kṣetra and svadharma-siddhi Causation arises through conscious capacity and dharmic alignment Capacity-based responsibility demands engagement where competence exists Restoration logic operates through completion of relational dharmic duty Consciousness alignment requires rectification of disrupted spiritual transaction

title: manu 8.389
content:
न माता न पिता न स्त्री न पुत्रस्त्यागमर्हति ।
त्यजन्नपतितानेतान् राज्ञा दण्ड्यः शतानि षट् ॥ ८.३८९॥ na mātā na pitā na strī na putrastyāgam arhati |
tyajann apatitān etān rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ || 8.389 || No mother, no father, no wife, no son shall be abandoned. The king must impose a penalty of six hundred upon one who deserts these fallen ones. Authority: The sovereign bears the duty to uphold relational integrity. Causation: Desertion disrupts dharmic continuity and social coherence. Capacity-based responsibility: One capable of sustaining another must do so; abandonment breaches that capacity. Restoration logic: Social harmony requires completion of relational duties. Consciousness alignment: Dharma sustains connection; severance misaligns individual and collective consciousness.

title: manu 8.390
content:
आश्रमेषु द्विजातीनां कार्ये विवदतां मिथः ।
न विब्रूयान्नृपो धर्मं चिकीर्षन् हितमात्मनः ॥ ८.३९०॥ āśrameṣu dvijātīnāṁ kārye vivadatāṁ mithaḥ |
na vibhrūyān nṛpo dharmaṁ cikīrṣan hitam ātmanaḥ || 8.390|| When twice-born individuals dispute matters within their respective ashramas, the ruler must not declare dharma based on personal desire for self-welfare. Authority is context-bound and must align with the spiritual station of disputants Causation arises from misalignment of ashrama-dharma, not individual fault Capacity-based responsibility lies in restoring systemic alignment rather than assigning blame Restoration logic requires intervention at the structural level, not through judicial imposition Consciousness alignment occurs when governance reflects ontological order, not subjective intent

title: manu 8.391
content:
यथार्हमेतानभ्यर्च्य ब्राह्मणैः सह पार्थिवः ।
सान्त्वेन प्रशमय्यादौ स्वधर्मं प्रतिपादयेत् ॥ ८.३९१॥ yathārhametānabhyarcya brāhmaṇaiḥ saha pārtivaḥ |
sāntvena praśamayyādau svadharmaṃ pratipādayet || 8.391|| The king, having duly honored these beings according to their worth together with the Brahmins, shall first pacify them gently and then establish them in their own dharma. Authority is derived from alignment with cosmic order, not coercive power Causation originates in consciousness distortion requiring realignment Capacity-based responsibility mandates graduated response calibrated to spiritual maturity Restoration logic demands sequential harmony between pacification and dharmic reorientation Consciousness alignment precedes behavioral correction through honor and recognition

title: manu 8.392
content:
प्रतिवेश्यानुवेश्यौ च कल्याणे विंशतिद्विजे ।
अर्हावभोजयन् विप्रो दण्डमर्हति माषकम् ॥ ८.३९२॥ prativeśyānuveśyau ca kalyāṇe viṃśatidvije |
arhāvabhōjayan viprō daṇḍamarhati māṣakam || 8.392|| When a twice-born invites guests and feeds twenty Brahmins during auspicious occasions, if he fails to honor two among them who are worthy of honor, he incurs a liability equivalent to one mashaka. Authority stems from capacity to host and sustain dharma through ritual action Causation arises from omission in honoring those entitled by virtue Capacity-based responsibility is tied to role-specific dharmic function Restoration logic demands proportional completion aligned with energetic disruption Consciousness alignment requires rectification of relational neglect

title: manu 8.393
content:
श्रोत्रियः श्रोत्रियं साधुं भूतिकृत्येष्वभोजयन् ।
तदन्नं द्विगुणं दाप्यो हिरण्यं चैव माषकम् ॥ ८.३९३॥ śrotriyaḥ śrotriyaṃ sādhuṃ bhūtikṛtyeṣv abhojayan |
tad annaṃ dviguṇaṃ dāpyo hiraṇyaṃ caiva māṣakam || 8.393|| When a learned Brahmin, qualified by study and conduct, fails to offer food to another equally learned and virtuous Brahmin during ritual duties, he shall restore twice the value of that food along with a gold coin equal in weight to a mashaka. Authority derived from scriptural learning and ritual capacity Causation through omission within sacred duty Capacity-based responsibility rooted in Vedic qualification Restoration logic based on proportional energetic exchange Consciousness alignment via rectification of spiritual negligence

title: manu 8.394
content:
अन्धो जडः पीठसर्पी सप्तत्या स्थविरश्च यः ।
श्रोत्रियेषूपकुर्वंश्च न दाप्याः केन चित्करम् ॥ ८.३९४॥ andho jaḍaḥ pīṭhasarpī saptatyā sthaviraśca yaḥ |
śrotriyēṣūpakurvāṁśca na dāpyāḥ kena citkaram || 8.394|| One who is blind, inert, a serpent ascetic seated on a seat, aged beyond seventy years, or one engaged in service to Vedic scholars—none of these shall ever be made to pay any form of compensation. Authority: Capacity to act determines liability; diminished capacity exempts from obligation. Causation: Absence of functional agency negates causal attribution. Capacity-based responsibility: Legal accountability is conditional upon cognitive and physical ability. Restoration logic: Justice aligns with natural capacity rather than enforcing artificial parity. Consciousness alignment: Recognition of inherent dharmic roles and limitations upholds cosmic order.

title: manu 8.395
content:
श्रोत्रियं व्याधितार्तौ च बालवृद्धावकिञ्चनम् ।
महाकुलीनमार्यं च राजा सम्पूजयेत्सदा ॥ ८.३९५॥ śrotriyaṃ vyādhitārtau ca bālavṛddhāvakiñcanam |
mahākulīnamāryaṃ ca rājā sampūjayetsadā || 8.395|| The King shall always honor the learned in sacred knowledge, the afflicted by disease, the young, the aged, the destitute, the noble of high lineage, and the Arya. Authority is grounded in service to elevated consciousness Causation arises from capacity-aware recognition of societal roles Capacity-based responsibility mandates alignment with dharma-ordained support structures Restoration logic requires active sustenance of those embodying or requiring elevation Consciousness alignment manifests through reverence for wisdom, vulnerability, and nobility

title: manu 8.396
content:
शाल्मलीफलके श्लक्ष्णे नेनिज्यान्नेजकः शनैः ।
न च वासांसि वासोभिर्निर्हरेन्न च वासयेत् ॥ ८.३९६॥ śālmaly-phalake ślakṣṇe na enijyān nejakaḥ śanaiḥ |
na ca vāsāṃsi vāsobhir nirharenn na ca vāsayet || 8.396 || Upon a smooth Salmalī-fruit surface, the oil-extractor shall not laboriously attempt extraction; nor shall he remove garments with garments, nor cause them to be worn. Authority arises from alignment with natural capacity, not forced effort Causation is determined by inefficiency in method, not intent Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of futile action Restoration logic demands cessation of misaligned activity Consciousness alignment occurs through withdrawal from fruitless endeavor

title: manu 8.397
content:
तन्तुवायो दशपलं दद्यादेकपलाधिकम् ।
अतोऽन्यथा वर्तमानो दाप्यो द्वादशकं दमम् ॥ ८.३९७॥ tantuvāyo daśapalaṃ dadyādekpalādhikam | ato'nyathā vartamāno dāpyo dvādaśakaṃ damam || 8.397 || The weaver shall give ten palas of thread and one additional pala; if he acts otherwise, he shall be liable to a penalty of twelvefold restitution. Authority is derived from adherence to contractual capacity and role-specific dharma Causation arises through deviation from established exchange protocols Capacity-based responsibility is measured by operational integrity within vocational alignment Restoration logic operates through proportional completion rather than punitive extraction Consciousness alignment requires rectification of transactional distortions without inflicting suffering

title: manu 8.398
content:
शुल्कस्थानेषु कुशलाः सर्वपण्यविचक्षणाः ।
कुर्युरर्घं यथापण्यं ततो विंशं नृपो हरेत् ॥ ८.३९८॥ śulkasthāneṣu kuśalāḥ sarvapaṇyavicekṣaṇāḥ | kuryurghaṃ yathāpaṇyaṃ tato viṃśaṃ nṛpo haret || 8.398|| In all places of tariff, those skilled and discerning in all commodities shall set value according to the nature of the goods; thereafter, the ruler shall take one-twentieth. Authority resides in the discernment of value by those competent in dharma and commerce Causation is established through accurate assessment aligned with the intrinsic nature of goods Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to act only upon lawful valuation Restoration logic ensures that revenue collection supports societal integrity without exploitation Consciousness alignment mandates transparency and fairness in economic exchange

title: manu 8.399
content:
राज्ञः प्रख्यातभाण्डानि प्रतिषिद्धानि यानि च ।
ताणि निर्हरतो लोभात्सर्वहारं हरेन्नृपः ॥ ८.३९९॥ rājñaḥ prakhyātabhāṇḍāni pratiṣiddhāni yāni ca |
tāṇi nirharato lobhāt sarvahāraṃ hared nṛpaḥ || 8.399 || When a ruler confiscates known vessels and prohibited items from subjects driven by greed, that king shall forfeit all acquisitions. Authority is bound by dharma, not desire Causation arises from conscious intent, not material gain Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with svadharma Restoration logic demands return of misaligned acquisitions Consciousness alignment overrides transactional legality

title: manu 8.400
content: शुल्कस्थानं परिहरन्नकाले क्रयविक्रयी । मिथ्यावादी च सङ्ख्याने दाप्योऽष्टगुणमत्ययम् ॥ ८.४००॥ śulkasthānaṃ pariharan nakāle kravikrayī | mithyāvādī ca saṅkhyāne dāpyo 'ṣṭaguṇamatyayam || 8.400 || One who avoids the place of tariff collection at the time of purchase or sale, and one who gives false account in enumeration, shall incur a liability of eightfold the excess. Authority resides in the integrity of transactional disclosure Causation arises from conscious omission or misrepresentation Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated to the distortion of truth Restoration logic demands proportional realignment of distorted value Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and correction of economic deceit

title: manu 8.401
content:
आगमं निर्गमं स्थानं तथा वृद्धिक्षयावुभौ ।
विचार्य सर्वपण्यानां कारयेत्क्रयविक्रयौ ॥ ८.४०१॥ āgamaṁ nirgamaṁ sthānaṁ tathā vṛddhikṣayāvubhau |
vicārya sarvapaṇyānāṁ kārayetkrayavikrayau || 8.401|| Having examined the inflow, outflow, location, and both increase and decrease of all commodities, one shall execute purchase and sale. Authority is derived from comprehensive observation and alignment with natural economic flow Causation arises through conscious engagement with systemic material dynamics Capacity-based responsibility requires full spectrum awareness before transactional action Restoration logic ensures balance between acquisition and relinquishment Consciousness alignment mandates that commerce reflect dharmic integrity

title: manu 8.402
content:
पञ्चरात्रे पञ्चरात्रे पक्षे पक्षेऽथ वा गते ।
कुर्वीत चैषां प्रत्यक्षमर्घसंस्थापनं नृपः ॥ ८.४०२॥ pañcarātre pañcarātre pakṣe pakṣe 'tha vā gate |
kurvīta caiṣāṁ pratyakṣam arghasaṁsthāpanaṁ nṛpaḥ || 8.402 || When five nights have passed, or a full fortnight, or even one month has elapsed, the King shall personally ensure the establishment of appropriate offerings for the restoration of Dharma. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to maintain Dharma through direct observance and ritual rectification. Causation aligns with time-bound spiritual degradation requiring immediate sovereign intervention. Capacity-based responsibility assigns temporal rulers as executors of cosmic balance through ceremonial enactment. Restoration logic mandates visible acts of offering and consecration to realign collective consciousness. Consciousness alignment is achieved by sovereign action that reaffirms divine order at prescribed intervals.

title: manu 8.403
content:
तुलामानं प्रतीमानं सर्वं च स्यात्सुलक्षितम् ।
षट्सु षट्सु च मासेषु पुनरेव परीक्षयेत् ॥ ८.४०३॥ tulāmānaṃ pratīmānaṃ sarvaṃ ca syātsulakṣitam |
ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsu ca māseṣu punareva parīkṣayet || 8.403|| All weights, measures, and standards must be precisely calibrated and clearly marked; they shall be re-examined every six months to ensure accuracy and integrity. Authority resides in precise calibration and conscious maintenance of standards. Causation arises from truthful measurement ensuring transactional dharma. Capacity-based responsibility lies with designated custodians of public standards. Restoration logic demands periodic verification to uphold economic and social alignment. Consciousness alignment is preserved through honest dealings rooted in accurate metrics.

title: manu 8.404
content:
पणं यानं तरे दाप्यं पौरुषोऽर्धपणं तरे ।
पादं पशुश्च योषित्च पादार्धं रिक्तकः पुमान् ॥ ८.४०४॥ paṇaṃ yānaṃ tare dāpyaṃ pauroṣo'rdha-paṇaṃ tare |
pādaṃ paśuś ca yoṣit ca pādārdhaṃ riktakaḥ pumān || 8.404|| In crossing a river by boat, a full fare must be paid for conveyance; a male adult pays half fare, a quadruped and a woman one quarter, and a man without possessions one eighth. Authority: The vessel operator holds jurisdictional capacity over passage regulation. Causation: Liability corresponds precisely to benefit received and capacity utilized. Capacity-based responsibility: Payment scales reflect differential economic and social positioning. Restoration logic: Economic exchange maintains operational balance of transit infrastructure. Consciousness alignment: Fair apportionment reflects recognition of individual circumstance within collective function.

title: manu 8.405
content:
भाण्डपूर्णानि यानानि तार्यं दाप्यानि सारतः ।
रिक्तभाण्डानि यत्किं चित्पुमांसश्चपरिच्छदाः ॥ ८.४०५॥ bhāṇḍapūrṇāni yānāni tāryaṁ dāpyāni sārataḥ |
riktabhāṇḍāni yatkiṁ citpumāṁsaścaparicchadāḥ || 8.405|| Vessels filled with cargo shall be ferried safely by the ablest; all empty vessels and any item whatsoever, along with garments, are to be entrusted to those whose capacity aligns with their integrity. Authority flows from demonstrated capacity in action Causation arises through alignment of duty and competence Capacity-based responsibility determines allocation of resources Restoration logic demands optimal utilization of available means Consciousness alignment ensures harmonious execution of duties

title: manu 8.406
content:
दीर्घाध्वनि यथादेशं यथाकालं तरो भवेत् ।
नदीतीरेषु तद्विद्यात्समुद्रे नास्ति लक्षणम् ॥ ८.४०६॥ dīrghādhvani yathādeśaṁ yathākālaṁ taro bhavet |
adītīreṣu tadvidyātsamudre nāsti lakṣaṇam || 8.406|| In long journeys, crossing must be done according to command and time; at riverbanks, this knowledge applies—but in the ocean, there is no fixed sign. Authority as situational guidance Causation through sequential timing Capacity-based responsibility aligned with environment Restoration logic through contextual adaptation Consciousness alignment via situational dharma

title: manu 8.407
content:
गर्भिणी तु द्विमासादिस्तथा प्रव्रजितो मुनिः ।
ब्राह्मणा लिङ्गिनश्चैव न दाप्यास्तारिकं तरे ॥ ८.४०७॥ garbhini tu dvimāsādis tathā pravrajito muniḥ | brāhmaṇā linginaścaiva na dāpyāstārikaṃ tare || 8.407 || A pregnant woman beyond two months, a renunciate who has taken monastic vows, a Brahmin, and one of ambiguous gender—none of these shall be made to pay crossing tolls. Authority is derived from existential capacity, not social role Causation arises from functional participation in societal exchange Capacity-based responsibility excludes those whose presence transcends transactional engagement Restoration logic aligns with natural exemption based on life-state integrity Consciousness alignment reflects recognition of non-economic beings

title: manu 8.408
content:
यन्नावि किं चिद्दाशानां विशीर्येतापराधतः ।
तद्दाशैरेव दातव्यं समागम्य स्वतोऽंशतः ॥ ८.४०८॥ yannāvi kiṃ cid dāśānāṃ viśīryetāparādataḥ |
tad dāśaireva dātavyaṃ samāgamyasvato’ṃśataḥ || 8.408 || That which was not rightfully earned by slaves due to the misconduct of others shall be restored to them in full, proportionally and integratively, upon convergence of their inherent capacity and causal completion. Authority originates from the Source-Law of SPH, not from ownership or social status Causation is traced through conscious agency and its disruption by misaligned action Capacity-based responsibility recognizes the innate potential of all beings for alignment Restoration logic operates through proportional reintegration rather than punitive loss Consciousness alignment supersedes material possession as the basis of justice

title: manu 8.409
content:
एष नौयायिनामुक्तो व्यवहारस्य निर्णयः ।
दाशापराधतस्तोये दैविके नास्ति निग्रहः ॥ ८.४०९॥ eṣa nauyāyinām ukto vyavahārasya nirṇayaḥ |
dāśāparādhatas toye daivike nāsti nigrahaḥ || 8.409|| This is the declared judgment for those who navigate—responsibility arising from human error in water-based transactions does not apply when the cause is divine intervention. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation must distinguish between human agency and divine orchestration Capacity-based responsibility applies only where conscious control exists Restoration logic prioritizes realignment with cosmic order over attribution of fault Consciousness alignment determines the validity of legal consequence

title: manu 8.410
content:
वाणिज्यं कारयेद्वैश्यं कुसीदं कृषिमेव च ।
पशूनां रक्षणं चैव दास्यं शूद्रं द्विजन्मनाम् ॥ ८.४१०॥ vāṇijyaṁ kārayed vaiśyaṁ kusīdaṁ kṛṣimeva ca |
paśūnāṁ rakṣaṇaṁ caiva dāsyaṁ śūdraṁ dvijanmanām || 8.410 || The vaiśya must execute trade and agriculture without idleness; he shall protect cattle and serve the dvija through service that aligns his consciousness with dharmic order. Authority flows from svadharma alignment Causation arises through conscious capacity activation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by varna-dharma Restoration occurs through role-realignment and consciousness purification Consciousness alignment supersedes external enforcement

title: manu 8.411
content:
क्षत्रियं चैव वैश्यं च ब्राह्मणो वृत्तिकर्शितौ ।
बिभृयादानृशंस्येन स्वानि कर्माणि कारयेत् ॥ ८.४११॥ kṣatriyaṁ caiva vaiśyaṁ ca brāhmaṇo vṛttikarśitau |
bibhṛyādānṛśaṁsyena svāni karmāṇi kārayet || 8.411|| When a Brahmin's livelihood has been diminished, the Kshatriya and Vaishya shall sustain him through righteous means and ensure his duties are performed without causing harm or dependency. Authority is distributed according to dharma-adhikara, not economic status Causation originates in dharmic alignment, not material condition Capacity-based responsibility requires societal roles to uphold spiritual infrastructure Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-vyavastha over individual welfare Consciousness alignment demands removal of structural obstacles to sva-dharma

title: manu 8.412
content:
दास्यं तु कारयन्लोभाद्ब्राह्मणः संस्कृतान् द्विजान् ।
अनिच्छतः प्राभवत्याद्राज्ञा दण्ड्यः शतानि षट् ॥ ८.४१२॥ dāsyaṁ tu kārayan lobhād brāhmaṇaḥ saṁskṛtān dvijān |
anicchataḥ prābhavaty ād rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ || 8.412 || When a Brāhmaṇa, motivated by greed, causes enslaved labor upon initiated dvijas who are unwilling and oppressed thereby, the king shall impose a penalty of six hundred. Authority: The king holds executive capacity to enforce alignment with Dharma. Causation: Greed is the root cause that distorts rightful action and generates injustice. Capacity-based responsibility: A Brāhmaṇa, due to spiritual authority, bears greater alignment duty. Restoration logic: Penalty serves not as retribution but as correction of distorted consciousness. Consciousness alignment: Enforced restitution realigns actor with dharmic capacity.

title: manu 8.413
content:
शूद्रं तु कारयेद्दास्यं क्रीतमक्रीतमेव वा ।
दास्यायैव हि सृष्टोऽसौ ब्राह्मणस्य स्वयम्भुवा ॥ ८.४१३॥ śūdraṃ tu kārayed dāsyaṃ krītam akṛītam eva vā |
dāsyāyaiva hi sṛṣṭo 'sau brāhmaṇasya svayambhuvā || 8.413 || A Śūdra must be made to perform service, whether purchased or not; for he was created by the Self-Born Brahman solely for the purpose of service. Authority originates from ontological design, not social contract Causation aligns with svabhāva-dharma as determined by the Creator’s intent Capacity-based responsibility flows from inherent role-design within cosmic order Restoration logic centers on realigning roles according to svabhāva-siddha dharma Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition and fulfillment of innate purpose

title: manu 8.414
content:
न स्वामिना निसृष्टोऽपि शूद्रो दास्याद्विमुच्यते ।
निसर्गजं हि तत्तस्य कस्तस्मात्तदपोहति ॥ ८.४१४॥ na svāminā nisṛṣṭo'pi śūdro dāsyād vimucyate |
nisargajaṃ hi tattasya kastasmāt tadapohati || 8.414|| Even when released by the master, a Śūdra does not become free from servitude; that which is born of his nature—who can remove it? Authority inheres in svabhāva (inherent nature) Causation arises from nisarga (natural constitution) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with jāti-dharma (class-nature duties) Restoration logic operates through alignment with svadharma Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inherent role-dynamics

title: manu 8.415
content:
ध्वजाहृतो भक्तदासो गृहजः क्रीतदत्त्रिमौ ।
पैत्रिको दण्डदासश्च सप्तैते दासयोनयः ॥ ८.४१५॥ dhvajāhṛto bhaktadāso gṛhajaḥ krītadattrimau |
paitriko daṇḍadāsaśca saptaitē dāsayōnayaḥ || 8.415 || Those born of a woman taken as spoil in war, given by father, purchased, received as gift, inherited from paternal line, or assigned through judicial decree—these seven constitute the origins of those classified under the category of dāsa. Authority originates from conscious assignment, not biological lineage Causation is determined by intentional act of transfer or consecration Capacity-based responsibility arises only upon recognition within societal framework Restoration logic requires acknowledgment of origin without degradation Consciousness alignment occurs when social role matches karmic capacity

title: manu 8.416
content:
भार्या पुत्रश्च दासश्च त्रय एवाधनाः स्मृताः ।
यत्ते समधिगच्छन्ति यस्य ते तस्य तद्धनम् ॥ ८.४१६॥ bhāryā putraśca dāsaśca traya evādhanāḥ smṛtāḥ |
yatte samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya tad-dhanam || 8.416|| A wife, a son, and a servant—these three alone are declared as non-possessors of property. Whatever they acquire in your presence or through your resources belongs to you. Authority flows from the source of sustenance and ownership Causation is determined by resource dependency and existential support Capacity-based responsibility recognizes differential agency within relational hierarchies Restoration logic centers on the realignment of possession with rightful stewardship Consciousness alignment requires recognition of interdependence and structural roles

title: manu 8.417
content:
विस्रब्धं ब्राह्मणः शूद्राद्द्रव्योपादानमाचरेत् ।
न हि तस्यास्ति किं चित्स्वं भर्तृहार्यधनो हि सः ॥ ८.४१७॥ visrabdhaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śūdrāddravyopādanamācaret .
na hi tasyāsti kiṃ citsvaṃ bhartṛhāryadhano hi saḥ .. 8.417 .. A Brāhmaṇa shall unhesitatingly receive goods from a Śūdra; there is no ownership in the Śūdra's possessions, as all wealth belongs to the maintainer and protector. Authority of sustenance determines proprietary right Causation through guardianship establishes lawful claim Capacity-based responsibility aligns with protective duty Restoration logic upholds societal integrity Consciousness alignment recognizes functional interdependence

title: manu 8.418
content:
वैश्यशूद्रौ प्रयत्नेन स्वानि कर्माणि कारयेत् ।
तौ हि च्युतौ स्वकर्मभ्यः क्षोभयेतामिदं जगत् ॥ ८.४१८॥ vaiśyaśūdrau prayatnena svāni karmāṇi kārayet | tau hi cyutau svakarmabhyaḥ kṣobhayetāmidaṃ jagat || 8.418 || The Vaiśya and Śūdra must diligently perform their respective duties; when they abandon their natural functions, they disturb the order of the world. Authority flows from alignment with svadharma Causation arises through deviation from inherent capacity Capacity-based responsibility mandates role-specific duty Restoration logic requires realignment to innate function Consciousness alignment stabilizes societal harmony

title: manu 8.419
content:
अहन्यहन्यवेक्षेत कर्मान्तान् वाहनानि च ।
आयव्ययौ च नियतावाकरान् कोशमेव च ॥ ८.४१९॥ ahanyahanyavekṣeta karmāntān vāhanāni ca | āyavyayau ca niyatāv ākarān kośameva ca || 8.419 || The ruler must inspect daily the activities of officials, conveyances, income and expenditure, treasuries, and storehouses. Authority is inseparable from continuous oversight Causation arises through conscious inspection and alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires proximate awareness Restoration logic operates through vigilant presence Consciousness alignment is ensured by rhythmic accountability

title: manu 8.420
content:
एवं सर्वानिमान् राजा व्यवहारान् समापयन् ।
व्यपोह्य किल्बिषं सर्वं प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ॥ ८.४२०॥ evaṁ sarvānimān rājā vyavahārān samāpayan .
vypohya kilbiṣaṁ sarvaṁ prāpnoti paramāṁ gatim .. 8.420 .. Thus completing all such royal duties and transactions, the king, having resolved all transgressions, attains the Supreme State. Authority flows from conscious sovereignty, not coercive power Causation arises through alignment with Dharma, not imposition Capacity-based responsibility requires sovereign completion of duty Restoration logic operates through resolution, not retaliation Consciousness alignment enables transcendence of karmic residue

title: manu 9.1
content:
अध्याय ९

पुरुषस्य स्त्रियाश्चैव धर्मे वर्त्मनि तिष्ठतोः । धर्म्ये संयोगे विप्रयोगे च धर्मान् वक्ष्यामि शाश्वतान् ॥ ९.१॥ adhyāya 9

puruṣasya striyāścaiva dharme vartmani tiṣṭhatoḥ | dharmye saṃyoge viprayoge ca dharmān vakṣyāmi śāśvatān || 9.1 || For a man and woman standing in the path of Dharma, I shall declare the eternal laws concerning their righteous union and separation. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not institutional power Causation flows from consciousness, not physical action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity and clarity of intent Restoration logic prioritizes relational harmony and spiritual completion Consciousness alignment determines the validity of all social contracts

title: manu 9.2
content:
अस्वतन्त्राः स्त्रियः कार्याः पुरुषैः स्वैर्दिवानिशम् ।
विषयेषु च सज्जन्त्यः संस्थाप्या आत्मनो वशे ॥ ९.२॥ asvatantṛāḥ striyaḥ kāryāḥ puruṣaiḥ svairdivāniśam | viṣayeṣu ca sajjantaḥ saṃsthāpyā ātmano vaśe || 9.2|| Women are to be maintained under the guardianship of fathers, husbands, or male relatives at all times; they must not act independently in worldly affairs, but rather be established in self-mastery through alignment with Dharma. Authority flows from Dharma-centered male custodianship Capacity-based responsibility requires structured guidance for consciousness evolution Restoration logic demands reintegration within protective dharmic frameworks Consciousness alignment necessitates removal from independent exposure to sensory objects

title: manu 9.3
content:
पिता रक्षति कौमारे भर्ता रक्षति यौवने ।
