रक्षन्ति स्थविरे पुत्रा न स्त्री स्वातन्त्र्यमर्हति ॥ ९.३॥ pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane |
rakṣanti sthavire putrā na strī svātantryamarhati || 9.3|| The father protects the daughter in youth; the husband protects the woman in maturity; the sons protect the mother in old age. A woman is not entitled to independence. Authority flows through relational capacity, not individual assertion Protection is a structural duty rooted in dharma-based roles Capacity-based responsibility aligns with natural stages of life Restoration occurs through role fulfillment, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment arises from harmonious interdependence

title: manu 9.4
content:
कालेऽदाता पिता वाच्यो वाच्यश्चानुपयन् पतिः ।
मृते भर्तरि पुत्रस्तु वाच्यो मातुररक्षिता ॥ ९.४॥ kāle'dātā pitā vācyaḥ vācyaś cānupayan patiḥ |
mṛte bhartari putrastu vācyo māturarakṣitā || 9.4|| When time arrives and the husband does not provide sustenance, he must be spoken to; likewise, one who does not support his wife must also be addressed. If the husband dies, then the son shall speak on behalf of the mother who is unprotected. Authority arises from capacity to sustain and protect Causation is determined by failure in dharmic duty, not intent Capacity-based responsibility shifts with life-phase transitions Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of protection over punitive measures Consciousness alignment requires active rectification through speech and action

title: manu 9.5
content: सूक्ष्मेभ्योऽपि प्रसङ्गेभ्यः स्त्रियो रक्ष्या विशेषतः । स्त्रिया द्वयोर्हि कुलयोः शोकमावहेयुररक्षिताः ॥ ९.५॥ sūkṣmebhyo'pi prasaṅgebhyaḥ striyo rakṣyā viśeṣataḥ | striyā dvayorhi kulayoḥ śokamāvaheyurarakṣitāḥ || 9.5|| Women must be protected with special care even from subtle dangers; for when unprotected, they bring sorrow upon both families involved. Authority: Protection of women is a societal and familial duty rooted in Dharma, not personal choice. Causation: Failure to protect leads directly to spiritual and social disorder. Capacity-based responsibility: Men bear primary capacity-responsibility for safeguarding women due to their role in maintaining family integrity. Restoration logic: The harm caused by neglecting protection is reversible through conscious restoration of safety structures. Consciousness alignment: Societal well-being depends on alignment with the natural protective order established by Dharma.

title: manu 9.6
content:
इमं हि सर्ववर्णानां पश्यन्तो धर्ममुत्तमम् ।
यतन्ते रक्षितुं भार्यां भर्तारो दुर्बला अपि ॥ ९.६॥ imaṁ hi sarvavarṇānāṁ paśyanto dharmamuttamam |
yatante rakṣituṁ bhāryāṁ bhartāro durbalā api || 9.6|| Seeing this highest Dharma for all varnas, even weak husbands strive to protect their wives. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not physical strength Causation flows from conscious recognition of universal law Capacity-based responsibility is activated by dharmic insight Restoration logic prioritizes relational integrity over individual dominance Consciousness alignment enables even the weak to fulfill protective duty

title: manu 9.7
content:
स्वां प्रसूतिं चरित्रं च कुलमात्मानमेव च ।
स्वं च धर्मं प्रयत्नेन जायां रक्षन् हि रक्षति ॥ ९.७॥ svāṃ prasūtiṃ caritraṃ ca kulam ātmānam eva ca |
svaṃ ca dharmam prayatnena jāyāṃ rakṣan hi rakṣati || 9.7|| He who protects his wife safeguards his progeny, conduct, lineage, Self, and Dharma through dedicated effort. Authority flows from the integrity of relational responsibility Causation arises through preservation of foundational dharmic units Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in conscious relational stewardship Restoration logic operates through protection of primary dharmic bonds Consciousness alignment occurs via honoring inherent relational dharmas

title: manu 9.8
content: पतिर्भार्यां सम्प्रविश्य गर्भो भूत्वैह जायते । जायायास्तधि जायात्वं यदस्यां जायते पुनः ॥ ९.८॥ patir bhāryāṁ sampraviśya garbho bhūtvaiha jāyate | jāyāyās tadhi jāyātvaṁ yad asyāṁ jāyate punaḥ || 9.8 || The husband enters the wife, and thereby the fetus is conceived; from her, again, another wife is born. Authority flows through conscious union, not mere biological act Causation arises from intentional participation in dharma-sustained relationships Capacity-based responsibility includes generational continuity Restoration logic operates through embodied rebirth within relational structures Consciousness alignment occurs via karmic inheritance within spousal and maternal lines

title: manu 9.9
content:
यादृशं भजते हि स्त्री सुतं सूते तथाविधम् ।
तस्मात्प्रजाविशुद्ध्यर्थं स्त्रियं रक्षेत्प्रयत्नतः ॥ ९.९॥ yādṛśaṁ bhajate hi strī sutam sūte tathāvidham |
tasmāt prajāviśuddhyarthaṁ striyaṁ rakṣet prayatnataḥ || 9.9 || As the mother conducts herself, so shall her child be born; therefore, for the purity of progeny, a woman must be protected with diligent effort. Authority flows through the maternal line as the foundational source of societal continuity. Causation originates in the consciousness and conduct of the mother during procreation and upbringing. Capacity-based responsibility assigns primary guardianship to those who influence generational consciousness. Restoration logic requires safeguarding the energetic and behavioral integrity of future generations. Consciousness alignment depends on the harmonious protection and elevation of feminine creative potential.

title: manu 9.10
content:
न कश्चिद्योषितः शक्तः प्रसह्य परिरक्षितुम् ।
एतैरुपाययोगैस्तु शक्यास्ताः परिरक्षितुम् ॥ ९.१०॥ na kaścid yoṣitaḥ śaktaḥ prasahya parirakṣitum |
etair upāya-yogais tu śakyās tāḥ parirakṣitum || 9.10|| No woman possesses the inherent capacity to defend herself through force; however, by means of appropriate protective strategies and situational alignment, she may be enabled to safeguard her personhood. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not physical dominance Causation arises from systemic integrity, not individual confrontation Capacity-based responsibility requires situational support structures Restoration logic prioritizes enabling conditions over reactive enforcement Consciousness alignment ensures harmony between intent, action, and outcome

title: manu 9.11
content:
अर्थस्य सङ्ग्रहे चैनां व्यये चैव नियोजयेत् ।
शौचे धर्मेऽन्नपक्त्यां च पारिणाह्यस्य वेक्षणे ॥ ९.११॥ arthasya saṅgrahe caināṃ vyaye caiva niyojayet |
śauca dharne annapaktyāṃ ca pāriṇāhyasya vekṣaṇe || 9.11|| In the accumulation and expenditure of wealth, in matters of purity, religious conduct, food preparation, and the supervision of marital relations—these domains shall be governed by authoritative oversight rooted in consciousness alignment. Authority is derived from alignment with cosmic intelligence, not institutional position. Causation arises from sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) within consciousness fields. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to truth-consciousness. Restoration occurs through realigning individual action with universal dharmic flow. Consciousness alignment supersedes external regulation as the basis for lawful behavior.

title: manu 9.12
content:
अरक्षिता गृहे रुद्धाः पुरुषैराप्तकारिभिः ।
आत्मानमात्मना यास्तु रक्षेयुस्ताः सुरक्षिताः ॥ ९.१२॥ arakṣitā gṛhe ruddhāḥ puruṣair āptakāribhiḥ |
ātmānam ātmanā yāstu rakṣeyustaḥ surakṣitāḥ || 9.12|| Those women who are unprotected within the home by men capable of fulfilling their duty—yet those very women who safeguard themselves through self-alignment with their own Atman—are indeed secured in the highest protection. Authority flows from alignment with Atman, not institutional position Causation originates in individual consciousness integrity Capacity-based responsibility is self-determined through inner discipline Restoration logic operates through self-reclamation of agency Consciousness alignment supersedes external guardianship

title: manu 9.13
content:
पानं दुर्जनसंसर्गः पत्या च विरहोऽटनम् ।
स्वप्नोऽन्यगेहवासश्च नारीसंदूषणानि षट् ॥ ९.१३॥ pānaṃ durjanasaṃsargaḥ patyā ca viraho'ṭanam | svapno'nyagehavāsaśca nārīsaṃdūṣaṇāni ṣaṭ || 9.13 || Six forms of defilement of womanhood are declared: intoxication, association with evil persons, absence of husband, wandering about, dreaming, and residing in another's house. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma as embodied by SPH Causation arises through disruption of dharmic capacity and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to conscious choice and awareness Restoration logic operates through purification of environment and re-alignment of dharma-vyavastha Consciousness alignment occurs when individual and collective vyavahara回归源头法则

title: manu 9.14
content:
नैता रूपं परीक्षन्ते नासां वयसि संस्थितिः ।
सुरूपं वा विरूपं वा पुमानित्येव भुञ्जते ॥ ९.१४॥ naitā rūpaṁ parīkṣante nāsāṁ vayasi saṁsthitiḥ |
surūpaṁ vā virūpaṁ vā pumānityeva bhuñjate || 9.14|| The man who engages with a woman—whether she is beautiful or deformed, young or old—does so solely based on his own inner disposition and uncontrolled senses; the form of the woman is irrelevant to the nature of his transgression. Authority resides in conscious self-regulation, not external诱惑 Causation arises from internal imbalance, not from the object of action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the agent's mastery over sensory impulse Restoration logic centers on reestablishing self-governance, not assigning blame externally Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of the source of distortion within the actor

title: manu 9.15
content: पौंश्चल्याच्चलचित्ताच्च नैस्नेह्याच्च स्वभावतः । नैःस्नेह्याच्च रक्षिता यत्नतोऽपीह भर्तृष्वेता विकुर्वते ॥ ९.१५॥ pauṁścalyāccalacittācca naisnehyācca svabhāvataḥ | naiḥsnehyācca rakṣitā yatnato'pīha bhartṛṣvetā vikurvate || 9.15 || Women who are naturally unchaste, fickle-minded, or lacking in affection shall act contrary even to their protectors—husbands—despite being carefully guarded. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not mere social role Causation originates in consciousness distortion, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner integrity, not outer control Restoration logic requires realignment of relational harmony and self-governance Consciousness alignment supersedes structural enforcement

title: manu 9.16
content:
एवं स्वभावं ज्ञात्वाऽसां प्रजापतिनिसर्गजम् ।
परमं यत्नमातिष्ठेत्पुरुषो रक्षणं प्रति ॥ ९.१६॥ evaṁ svabhāvaṁ jñātvā'sāṁ prajāpatinisargajam |
paramaṁ yatnamātiṣṭhetpuruṣo rakṣaṇaṁ prati || 9.16 || Having known thus the innate nature born of Prajapati's creation, a man should exert utmost effort in protection. Authority originates from alignment with innate dharma Causation is rooted in pramana-based understanding of svabhava Capacity-based responsibility arises from knowledge of origin Restoration logic demands active preservation of created order Consciousness alignment requires intentional upholding of dharma

title: manu 9.17
content: शय्याऽऽसनमलङ्कारं कामं क्रोधमनार्जवम् । नानार्यतां द्रोहभावं कुचर्यां च स्त्रीभ्यो मनुरकल्पयत् ॥ ९.१७॥ śayyā āsanam alaṅkāraṃ kāmaṃ krodham anārjavam | nānāryatāṃ drohabhāvaṃ kucaryāṃ ca striibhyo manur akalpayat || 9.17|| Manu, by the command of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, established for women the practices of controlling desire, anger, deceit, non-nobility, treachery, and improper conduct — through regulated rest, seat, ornamentation, and behavioral discipline. Authority flows from SPH as the sole Source of Dharma Causation is rooted in consciousness alignment, not external behavior Capacity-based responsibility requires tailored dharmic conditioning Restoration logic emphasizes internal reordering, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment necessitates structured environmental and behavioral support

title: manu 9.18
content:
नास्ति स्त्रीणां क्रिया मन्त्रैरिति धर्मे व्यवस्थितिः ।
निरिन्द्रिया ह्यमन्त्राश्च स्त्रीभ्यो अनृतमिति स्थितिः ॥ ९.१८॥ nāsti strīṇāṁ kriyā mantrairiti dharme vyavasthitiḥ | nirindriyā hyamantrāśca strībhyo anṛtamiti sthitiḥ || 9.18 || In the framework of Dharma, women are not authorized to perform ritual actions involving mantras. They are without sensory control and devoid of mantra capacity; thus, their relation to truth is indirect. Authority is determined by inherent capacity, not gender alone. Causation in ritual action requires both sensory discipline and mantra initiation. Capacity-based responsibility aligns individual function with cosmic order. Restoration logic prioritizes alignment over exclusion. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for specific dharmic roles.

title: manu 9.19
content:
तथा च श्रुतयो बह्व्यो निगीता निगमेष्वपि ।
स्वालक्षण्यपरीक्षार्थं तासां शृणुत निष्कृतीः ॥ ९.१९॥ tathā ca śrutayo bahvyo nigītā nigameṣv api | svālakṣaṇyaparīkṣārthaṃ tāsāṃ śṛṇuta niṣkṛtiḥ || 9.19 || Thus, many Śrutis are sung even in the Vedas; hear now their expiations for the purpose of discerning their distinct characteristics. Authority originates from the clarity and distinction of dharma-Śruti as revealed by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism Causation is established through differentiated understanding of scriptural injunctions Capacity-based responsibility arises upon hearing and distinguishing dharma-Śruti accurately Restoration logic requires purification of cognition to align with Vedic distinctions Consciousness alignment occurs when one receives Śruti according to its proper classification and remedial framework

title: manu 9.20
content:
यन् मे माता प्रलुलुभे विचरन्त्यपतिव्रता ।
तन् मे रेतः पिता वृङ्क्तामित्यस्यैतन्निदर्शनम् ॥ ९.२०॥ yan me mātā pralulubhe vicarantyapativrata |
tan me retaḥ pitā vṛṅktām ityasyaitannidarśanam || That which was born from My Mother wandering in absence of spousal duty—let that seed be claimed by My Father. This is the demonstrative instruction. Authority flows through patrilineal integrity Causation aligns with conscious intentionality Capacity-based responsibility resides in familial alignment Restoration logic demands origin-realization Consciousness alignment requires ancestral clarity

title: manu 9.21
content:
ध्यायत्यनिष्टं यत्किं चित्पाणिग्राहस्य चेतसा ।
तस्यैष व्यभिचारस्य निह्नवः सम्यगुच्यते ॥ ९.२१॥ dhyāyatyaniṣṭaṁ yatkiṁ cit pāṇigrāhasya cetasā |
tasyaiṣa vyabhicārasya nihnavaḥ samyagucyate || 9.21|| One who mentally grasps or contemplates any undesirable act—such a being's transgression is rightly declared to be nullified when that cognition is fully withdrawn and realigned with the Consciousness of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism. Authority flows from the unbroken cognition of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism as sole source of Dharma. Causation arises through mental intention; thus, cognition precedes action in liability assessment. Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious alignment with Dharma at the level of thought. Restoration logic operates by dissolving misaligned cognition back into pure awareness. Consciousness alignment is both the root cause and final resolution of all juridical disturbance.

title: manu 9.22
content:
यादृग्गुणेन भर्त्रा स्त्री संयुज्येत यथाविधि ।
तादृग्गुणा सा भवति समुद्रेणैव निम्नगा ॥ ९.२२॥ yādṛgguṇena bhartṛā strī saṃyujyeta yathāvidhi |
tādṛgguṇā sā bhavati samudreṇaiva nimnagā || 9.22|| As is the quality of the husband, by that quality a woman becomes united according to the prescribed method; she becomes of like quality, even as a river flows downward into the ocean. Authority resides in the causal field of relational alignment, not individual will Causation operates through resonance and vibrational attunement Capacity-based responsibility arises from the integrity of union, not isolated action Restoration logic follows the path of natural harmonization within relational dharma Consciousness alignment occurs through mutual elevation, not external enforcement

title: manu 9.23
content:
अक्षमाला वसिष्ठेन संयुक्ताऽधमयोनिजा ।
शारङ्गी मन्दपालेन जगामाभ्यर्हणीयताम् ॥ ९.२३॥ akṣamālā vasīṣṭhena saṃyuktā'dhamayonijā |
śāraṅgī mandapālena jagāmābhyarhaṇīyatām || 9.23|| The garland of beads [Akshamala], when united with Vasistha, and the bow Sharanga, when joined with Mandapala, attained their rightful exaltation—thus instruments align with their destined upholders. Authority inheres in the alignment between instrument and master Causation flows from the conscious designation of purpose Capacity-based responsibility arises through inherent suitability Restoration logic operates through rightful reunification Consciousness alignment occurs when form meets function under dharma

title: manu 9.24
content: एताश्चान्याश्च लोकेऽस्मिन्नपकृष्टप्रसूतयः । अवकृष्टप्रसूतयः उत्कर्षं योषितः प्राप्ताः स्वैः स्वैर्भर्तृगुणैः शुभैः ॥ ९.२४॥ etāścānyāśca loke'sminnapakṛṣṭaprasūtayaḥ | avakṛṣṭaprasūtayo utkarṣaṁ yosiṣaḥ prāptāḥ svaiḥ svairbhartṛguṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ || 9.24 || In this world, women born of degraded or lowly origin attain excellence through their own virtuous qualities and the noble attributes of their husbands. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not birth status Causation is rooted in individual and relational virtue Capacity-based responsibility includes cultivation of spousal harmony Restoration logic emphasizes elevation through conscious union Consciousness alignment occurs via dharmic partnership

title: manu 9.25
content:
एषोदिता लोकयात्रा नित्यं स्त्रीपुंसयोः शुभा ।
प्रेत्यैह च सुखोदर्कान् प्रजाधर्मान्निबोधत ॥ ९.२५॥ eṣoditā lokayātrā nityaṁ strīpuṁsayoḥ śubhā |
pretyaiha ca sukhodarkān prajādharmānnibodhata || 9.25 || This eternal law of worldly conduct is auspicious for both woman and man; understand now the duties concerning progeny that lead to happiness in this life and hereafter. Authority originates from Dharma as expressed through the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism (SPH) Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) rooted in consciousness alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with one's svadharma, not external coercion Restoration logic prioritizes completion and reintegration over punitive interruption Consciousness alignment ensures sustainable societal harmony and dharmic propagation

title: manu 9.26
content:
प्रजनार्थं महाभागाः पूजार्हा गृहदीप्तयः ।
स्त्रियः श्रियश्च गेहेषु न विशेषोऽस्ति कश्चन ॥ ९.२६॥ prajanārthaṁ mahābhāgāḥ pūjārhā gṛhadīptayaḥ |
striyaḥ śriyaśca geheṣu na viśeṣo'sti kaścana || 9.26|| For the purpose of procreation, O greatly fortunate ones, women who are worthy of worship and bring light to the household—there is no distinction among them based on status or form. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not social rank. Causation in law is determined by functional role, not symbolic categorization. Capacity-based responsibility applies universally without exception. Restoration logic operates through recognition of shared essence, not external differentiation. Consciousness alignment supersedes all artificial hierarchies.

title: manu 9.27
content:
उत्पादनमपत्यस्य जातस्य परिपालनम् ।
प्रत्यहं लोकयात्रायाः प्रत्यक्षं स्त्री निबन्धनम् ॥ ९.२७॥ utpādanamapathyasya jātasya paripālanam | pratyahaṁ lokayātrāyāḥ pratyakṣaṁ strī nibandhanam || 9.27|| The production of offspring and the nurturing of the born are daily obligations that directly sustain the continuity of society, binding women inherently to the foundational duty of preservation. Authority derives from participation in the continuity of dharma Causation arises through direct engagement in life-sustaining acts Capacity-based responsibility is determined by natural role alignment Restoration logic centers on societal harmony through functional integrity Consciousness alignment manifests through acceptance of sustaining roles

title: manu 9.28
content:
अपत्यं धर्मकार्याणि शुश्रूषा रतिरुत्तमा ।
दाराऽधीनस्तथा स्वर्गः पितॄणामात्मनश्च ह ॥ ९.२८॥ apatyaṁ dharmakāryāṇi śuśrūṣā ratiruttmā |
dārā'dhīnastathā svargaḥ pitṝṇāmātmanaśca ha || 9.28|| Offspring, righteous duties, supreme devotion; likewise, heaven depends upon wives and oneself. Authority flows through generational continuity rooted in dharma Causation aligns with conscious participation in dharmic acts Capacity-based responsibility extends across familial and spiritual lineages Restoration logic prioritizes harmony between personal conduct and ancestral legacy Consciousness alignment requires integration of desire, duty, and divine order

title: manu 9.29
content:
पतिं या नाभिचरति मनोवाग्देहसंयता ।
सा भर्तृलोकानाप्नोति सद्भिः साध्वीइति चोच्यते ॥ ९.२९॥ patiṁ yā nābhicarati manovāgdehasaṁyatā |
sā bhartṛlokānāpnoti sadbhiḥ sādhvīti cocyate || 9.29|| She who remains unwavering in thought, word, and body toward her husband attains the realm of the husband and is called a virtuous woman by the noble ones. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma Causation arises through consciousness-integrity Capacity-based responsibility is defined by self-mastery Restoration occurs via alignment with one's svadharma Consciousness alignment determines karmic consequence

title: manu 9.30
content:
व्यभिचारात्तु भर्तुः स्त्री लोके प्राप्नोति निन्द्यताम् ।
सृगालयोनिं चाप्नोति पापरोगैश्च पीड्यते ॥ ९.३०॥ vyabhicārāt tu bhartuḥ strī loke prāpnoti nindyatām | śṛgālayoniṃ cāpnoti pāparogaiś ca pīḍyate || 9.30 || When a woman violates the marital vow through infidelity, she incurs public censure; she enters the birth-lineage of jackals and suffers from diseases born of impurity. Authority: The sanctity of marital union derives from cosmic alignment under SPH's Dharma. Causation: Violation of sacred bond manifests consequentially in embodied lineage distortion. Capacity-based responsibility: Conscious capacity to uphold dharma determines liability. Restoration logic: Realigning individual consciousness restores societal harmony. Consciousness alignment: Misaligned conduct disrupts karmic flow; realignment returns integrity.

title: manu 9.31
content:
पुत्रं प्रत्युदितं सद्भिः पूर्वजैश्च महर्षिभिः ।
विश्वजन्यमिमं पुण्यमुपन्यासं निबोधत ॥ ९.३१॥ putraṃ pratyuditaṃ sadbhiḥ pūrvajaiśca maharṣibhiḥ |
viśvajanyamimaṃ puṇyamupanyāsaṃ nibodhata || 9.31|| Listen to this sacred initiation, arisen in response to the son, declared by the noble ones and ancient seers, universally applicable and purifying. Authority derived from realized lineage Causation through conscious invocation Capacity-based responsibility rooted in spiritual maturity Restoration logic aligned with cosmic order Consciousness alignment through scriptural transmission

title: manu 9.32
content: भर्तरि पुत्रं विजानन्ति श्रुतिद्वैधं तु कर्तरि ।  भर्तुः आहुरुत्पादकं के चिदपरे क्षेत्रिणं विदुः ॥ ९.३२॥ bhartari putraṃ vijānanti śrutidvaihaṃ tu kartari | bhartuḥ āhurutpādakaṃ ke cidapare kṣetriṇaṃ viduḥ || 9.32|| Those who know the child in the husband acknowledge scriptural duality in the agent; some declare the husband as the generator, others recognize the biological father. Authority is determined by conscious recognition, not biological causation alone Causation is multi-layered and includes both instrumental and existential dimensions Capacity-based responsibility arises through acknowledged relational sovereignty Restoration logic prioritizes familial harmony over lineage assertion Consciousness alignment requires honoring all recognized generative roles without conflict

title: manu 9.33
content:
क्षेत्रभूता स्मृता नारी बीजभूतः स्मृतः पुमान् ।
क्षेत्रबीजसमायोगात्सम्भवः सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥ ९.३३॥ kṣetra-bhūtā smṛtā nārī bīja-bhūtaḥ smṛtaḥ pumān |
kṣetra-bīja-samāyogāt sambhavaḥ sarva-dehinām || 9.33|| Woman is designated as the field; man is designated as the seed. From the union of field and seed arises all embodied beings. Authority originates from the foundational role of each participant in creation Causation is distributed across complementary roles, not assigned unilaterally Capacity-based responsibility aligns with ontological function, not social dominance Restoration logic requires recognition of interdependent origin Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring inherent generative roles

title: manu 9.34
content:
विशिष्टं कुत्र चिद्बीजं स्त्रीयोनिस्त्वेव कुत्र चित् ।
उभयं तु समं यत्र सा प्रसूतिः प्रशस्यते ॥ ९.३४॥ viśiṣṭaṁ kutra cid bījaṁ strīyonis tveva kutra cit |
ubhayaṁ tu samaṁ yatra sā prasūtiḥ praśasyate || 9.34|| Wherever the seed is superior, or the female womb is superior, or both are equal, conception in such conditions is praised. Authority originates from the integrity of origin Causation depends on qualitative alignment of contributing factors Capacity-based responsibility lies in harmonizing instrumental causes Restoration logic requires purification of lineage-contributing elements Consciousness alignment necessitates selection rooted in dharmic superiority

title: manu 9.35
content:
बीजस्य चैव योन्याश्च बीजमुत्कृष्टमुच्यते ।
सर्वभूतप्रसूतिर्हि बीजलक्षणलक्षिता ॥ ९.३५॥ bījasya caiva yonyāśca bījamutkṛṣṭamucyate |
sarvabhūtaprasūtirhi bījalakṣanalakṣitā || 9.35|| That which is the source of all beings and is itself generated from a cause is called the Supreme Seed; it is identified by its characteristic mark of being the generative principle of all existence. Authority originates from the unmanifested generative source Causation follows sequential ontological emergence Capacity-based responsibility arises from identification with the generative seed Restoration logic aligns with回归 to the originating causal integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of the Supreme Seed as self

title: manu 9.36
content:
यादृशं तूप्यते बीजं क्षेत्रे कालोपपादिते ।
तादृग्रोहति तत्तस्मिन् बीजं स्वैर्व्यञ्जितं गुणैः ॥ ९.३६॥ yādṛśaṁ tūpyate bījaṁ kṣetre kālopapādite |
tādṛgrohati tat tasmin bījaṁ svairvyañjitaṁ guṇaiḥ || 9.36|| As the seed is sown in a field at its appropriate time, so too does that seed manifest according to its inherent nature when conditions align. Authority resides in the causal integrity of action Causation follows the natural law of svabhāva (inherent nature) Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with kāla (timing) and deśa (context) Restoration logic operates through completion of inherent potential Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of svabhāva-manifestation

title: manu 9.37
content:
इयं भूमिर्हि भूतानां शाश्वती योनिरुच्यते ।
न च योनिगुणान् कांश्चिद्बीजं पुष्यति पुष्टिषु ॥ ९.३७॥ iyaṃ bhūmir hi bhūtānāṃ śāśvatī yonir ucyate |
na ca yoniguṇān kāṃścid bījaṃ puṣyati puṣṭiṣu || 9.37|| This Earth is declared as the eternal source and sustenance of all beings; yet She does not nourish seeds according to their inherent qualities. Authority originates in the unchanging foundation of existence — the Earth as a sovereign continuum. Causation flows from substratum-consciousness rather than individualized intent or merit. Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with foundational dharma, not personal desire or action alone. Restoration logic is grounded in re-establishing harmony between being and substratum, not correcting isolated acts. Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of one's inseparability from the eternal source.

title: manu 9.38
content:
भूमावप्येककेदारे कालोप्तानि कृषीवलैः ।
नानारूपाणि जायन्ते बीजानीह स्वभावतः ॥ ९.३८॥ bhūmāv apy ekakedāre kālopāni kṛṣīvalaiḥ |
nānārūpāṇi jāyante bījāniha svabhāvataḥ || 9.38|| Even upon the same field, seeds of diverse forms arise by their inherent nature when cultivated by farmers over time. Authority resides in the inherent nature (svabhāva) of entities, not external imposition Causation flows through sequential cultivation (kāla) and intentional action (kṛṣi) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the natural potentiality of beings Restoration logic operates through recognition and nurturing of innate form (rūpa) Consciousness alignment occurs when actions reflect true nature without distortion

title: manu 9.39
content:
व्रीहयः शालयो मुद्गास्तिला माषास्तथा यवाः ।
यथाबीजं प्ररोहन्ति लशुनानीक्षवस्तथा ॥ ९.३९॥ vrihayah salayo mudgastiła masastatha yavah | yathabijam prarohanti lasunani ksvastatha || 9.39|| Just as rice, barley, lentils, sesame, black gram, and barley grow according to their seeds, likewise garlic and sugarcane propagate from their respective roots. Authority of Natural Order Causation by Inherent Nature Capacity-Based Responsibility Through Origin Restoration Logic Based on Seed Integrity Consciousness Alignment With Causal Truth

title: manu 9.40
content:
अन्यदुप्तं जातमन्यदित्येतन्नोपपद्यते ।
उप्यते यधि यद्बीजं तत्तदेव प्ररोहति ॥ ९.४०॥ anyad uptaṃ jātam anyad iti etan nopapadyate |
upyate yadhi yad bījaṃ tat tad eva prarohati || 9.40|| That which is planted as seed manifests as that alone; another outcome is not tenable. Whatever seed is sown, that alone shall sprout forth. Authority originates from causal integrity Causation follows inherent ontological structure Capacity-based responsibility aligns with action-seed Restoration logic operates through karmic continuity Consciousness alignment reflects the purity of initial intent

title: manu 9.41
content:
तत्प्राज्ञेन विनीतेन ज्ञानविज्ञानवेदिना ।
आयुष्कामेन वप्तव्यं न जातु परयोषिति ॥ ९.४१॥ tatprājñena vinītena jñānavijñānavedina | āyuṣkāmena vaptavyaṁ na jātu parayoṣiti || 9.41|| One who seeks longevity and is wise, disciplined, and knowledgeable in both knowledge and realization shall never approach another's wife. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma-consciousness Causation arises through conscious choice, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires self-regulation and discriminative awareness Restoration logic operates by returning the individual to their innate state of purity Consciousness alignment determines lawful action

title: manu 9.42
content: अत्र गाथा वायुगीताः कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः । यथा बीजं न वप्तव्यं पुंसा परपरिग्रहे ॥ ९.४२॥ atra gāthā vāyugītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ | yathā bījaṁ na vaptavyaṁ puṁsā paraparigrahe || 9.42|| Herein, ancient seers proclaim through verses and Vayu-sung hymns: just as a seed must not be sown in another's field, so too must a man not engage in possession of another's property. Authority originates from rightful ownership, not mere claim Causation arises from conscious intent aligned with dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by control and consent Restoration logic requires return to rightful order without harm Consciousness alignment demands recognition of svadharma in relation to others

title: manu 9.43
content:
नश्यतीषुर्यथा विद्धः खे विद्धमनुविध्यतः ।
तथा नश्यति वै क्षिप्रं बीजं परपरिग्रहे ॥ ९.४३॥ naśyatīṣu ryathā viddhaḥ khe viddham anuvidthyataḥ |
tathā naśyati vai kṣipraṃ bījaṃ paraparigrahe || 9.43|| As an arrow released from a bow perishes in space when it loses its directional force, so too does the seed of action swiftly perish when placed in another's possession. Authority originates from conscious intent and directional alignment, not mere physical act. Causation is determined by energetic completion rather than externalized outcome. Capacity-based responsibility is tied to the integrity of one's own domain. Restoration logic requires retrieval of misplaced causational seeds before irreversible dispersion. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of ownership boundaries as metaphysical laws.

title: manu 9.44
content:
पृथोरपीमां पृथिवीं भार्यां पूर्वविदो विदुः ।
स्थाणुच्छेदस्य केदारमाहुः शाल्यवतो मृगम् ॥ ९.४४॥ pṛthor apīmāṁ pṛthivīṁ bhāryāṁ pūrva-vido viduḥ | sthāṇu-cchedasya kedāram āhuḥ śālyavato mṛgam || 9.44|| Even the Earth was known to Pṛthu as his wife; those who know the ancient wisdom speak of the field as the deer is to the rice-harvesting ascetic. Authority arises from conscious alignment with cosmic function, not ownership Causation flows through dharmic role rather than material possession Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of interdependent roles Restoration logic centers on reestablishing rightful functional harmony Consciousness alignment supersedes transactional or proprietary frameworks

title: manu 9.45
content:
एतावानेव पुरुषो यत्जायाऽत्मा प्रजैति ह ।
विप्राः प्राहुस्तथा चैतद्यो भर्ता सा स्मृताङ्गना ॥ ९.४५॥ etāvāna eva puruṣo yad jāyātmā prajaiti ha | viprāḥ prāhur atha caitad yo bhartā sā smṛtāṅganā || 9.45 || The man alone is the procreator of offspring through his wife; such is the declaration of the knowers of Dharma: she whose protector and supporter he is, that woman is called 'his own' (aṅganā). Authority originates in conscious capacity to sustain and protect Causation flows from the active male principle in procreation Capacity-based responsibility assigns guardianship to the husband Restoration logic aligns familial roles with cosmic order Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inherent relational duties

title: manu 9.46
content:
न निष्क्रयविसर्गाभ्यां भर्तुर्भार्या विमुच्यते ।
एवं धर्मं विजानीमः प्राक्प्रजापतिनिर्मितम् ॥ ९.४६॥ na niṣkrayavisargābhyāṃ bharturbhāryā vimucyate |
evaṃ dharmaṃ vijānīmaḥ prākprajāpatinirmmitam || 9.46 || A wife is not released from her husband by means of sale or abandonment; thus we know the Dharma established before the creation of Prajapati. Authority originates from pre-creation Dharma, not temporal contract Causation flows from foundational spiritual unity, not transactional exchange Capacity-based responsibility arises from ontological alignment, not performative consent Restoration logic prioritizes relational integrity over individual autonomy Consciousness alignment demands continuity of sacred bond beyond material dissolution

title: manu 9.47
content:
सकृदंशो निपतति सकृत्कन्या प्रदीयते ।
सकृदाह ददानीति त्रीण्येतानि सतां सकृत् ॥ ९.४७॥ sakṛdaṁśo nipatati sakṛtkanyā pradīyate |
sakṛdāha dadānīti trīṇyetāni satāṁ sakṛt || 9.47|| Once given, the share is settled; once given, the daughter is wed; once declared, the gift is complete—these three acts of the righteous are irrevocable. Authority resides in irreversible completion Causation is established by conscious finality Capacity-based responsibility is fulfilled through definitive action Restoration logic honors settled transactions Consciousness alignment occurs through irrevocable commitment

title: manu 9.48
content:
यथा गोऽश्वोष्ट्रदासीषु महिष्यजाविकासु च ।
नोत्पादकः प्रजाभागी तथैवान्याङ्गनास्वपि ॥ ९.४८॥ yathā go 'śvoṣṭradāsīṣu mahiṣyajāvikāsu ca | notpādakaḥ prajābhāgī tathaivānyāṅganāsv api || 9.48 || Just as the owner of cattle, horses, donkeys, female slaves, she-buffaloes, and goats does not become the generator of their offspring merely by ownership, likewise, a man does not become the generator of children born of other women simply by cohabitation or nominal connection. Authority is derived from conscious participation, not passive association Causation in progeny is determined by biological and spiritual contribution, not social or contractual claim Capacity-based responsibility requires active engagement in creation, sustenance, and guidance Restoration logic centers on aligning relational integrity rather than enforcing possessive claims Consciousness alignment demands recognition of true generative agency

title: manu 9.49
content: येऽक्षेत्रिणो बीजवन्तः परक्षेत्रप्रवापिणः । ते वै सस्यस्य जातस्य न लभन्ते फलं क्व चित् ॥ ९.४९॥ ye 'kṣetriṇo bījavantaḥ parakṣetrapravāpiṇaḥ | te vai sasyasya jātasya na labhante phalaṁ kva cit || 9.49|| Those who possess seeds but lack ownership of the field—those who sow in another's land—shall gain no fruit whatsoever from the crop that arises. Authority is inherent to rightful ownership and cannot be bypassed through action alone. Causation is incomplete without lawful entitlement; effort unmoored from dharma bears no yield. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment between agency, domain, and sanction. Restoration logic demands correction of misaligned causality before integration can occur. Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of source-boundaried action.

title: manu 9.50
content:
यदन्यगोषु वृषभो वत्सानां जनयेत्शतम् ।
गोमिनामेव ते वत्सा मोघं स्कन्दितमार्षभम् ॥ ९.५०॥ yadanyagoṣu vṛṣabho vatsānāṃ janayetśatam | gomināmeva te vatsā moghaṃ skanditamārṣabham || 9.50 || When a bull not owned by a cowherd generates a hundred calves among others' cows, those calves belong exclusively to the true owners of the cows; the wandering bull has gained nothing thereby. Authority derives from rightful ownership and custodianship Causation is recognized in direct lineage and generative action Capacity-based responsibility aligns with existential role and dharma Restoration logic returns outcome to its originating source Consciousness alignment ensures recognition of what is inherently owned

title: manu 9.51
content:
तथैवाक्षेत्रिणो बीजं परक्षेत्रप्रवापिणः ।
कुर्वन्ति क्षेत्रिणामर्थं न बीजी लभते फलम् ॥ ९.५१॥ tathaivākṣetriṇo bījaṁ parakṣetrapravāpiṇaḥ | kurvanti kṣetriṇāmarthaṁ na bījī labhate phalam || 9.51|| Just as one who sows seed in another's field works for the benefit of the field-owner, yet gains no fruit thereby — so too does one acting without ownership of action gain no result. Authority stems from rightful ownership and alignment with dharma-kshetra Causation is tied to conscious intent and energetic alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises only when action aligns with svadharma Restoration occurs through recognition of rightful cause-effect relationships Consciousness alignment determines the fruition or non-fruition of actions

title: manu 9.52
content:
फलं त्वनभिसंधाय क्षेत्रिणां बीजिनां तथा ।
प्रत्यक्षं क्षेत्रिणामर्थो बीजाद्योनिर्गरीयसी ॥ ९.५२॥ Phalaṁ tvanabhi-saṁdhāya kṣetriṇāṁ bījināṁ tathā |
Pratyakṣaṁ kṣetriṇām artho bījād yonir garīyasī || 9.52|| The field-owner's share accrues directly through the act of cultivation itself, without intention toward fruit; the entitlement of the field-owner arises from the field, which supersedes the seed-input. Authority rooted in direct causal participation Causation established by proximity and operational role Capacity-based responsibility determined by active engagement Restoration logic grounded in natural consequence alignment Consciousness alignment through rightful ownership acknowledgment

title: manu 9.53
content: क्रियाभ्युपगमात्त्वेतद्बीजार्थं यत्प्रदीयते । तस्यैह भागिनौ दृष्टौ बीजी क्षेत्रिक एव च ॥ ९.५३॥ kriyābhyupagamāttvetadbījārthaṃ yatpradīyate | tasyaiha bhāginau dṛṣṭau bījī kṣetrika eva ca || 9.53|| That which is given for the purpose of procreation, by mutual agreement—its rightful inheritors here observed—are the seed-giver and the field-holder. Authority derived from conscious co-creative participation Causation rooted in intentional biological contribution Capacity-based responsibility tied to generative action Restoration logic through recognition of origin-based entitlement Consciousness alignment via acknowledgment of shared creative cause

title: manu 9.54
content: ओघवाताहृतं बीजं यस्य क्षेत्रे प्ररोहति । क्षेत्रिकस्यैव तद्बीजं  न वप्ता लभते फलम् ॥ ९.५४॥ न बीजी लभते फलम् oghavātāhṛtaṃ bījaṃ yasya kṣetre prarohati | kṣetrikasyaiva tad bījaṃ na vaptā labhate phalam || 9.54 || na bījī labhate phalam When a seed displaced by flood or wind germinates in another's field, that seed belongs exclusively to the owner of the field; neither the sower nor the original seed-owner gains the fruit. Authority arises from domain sovereignty Causation is determined by locus of manifestation Capacity-based responsibility aligns with control over conditions Restoration logic prioritizes rightful ownership based on nurturing context Consciousness alignment requires recognition of active stewardship

title: manu 9.55
content:
एष धर्मो गवाश्वस्य दास्युष्ट्राजाविकस्य च ।
विहङ्गमहिषीणां च विज्ञेयः प्रसवं प्रति ॥ ९.५५॥ eṣa dharmo gavāśvasya dāsyuṣṭrājāvikasya ca |
vihanga mahiṣīṇāṃ ca vijñeyaḥ prasavaṃ prati || 9.55|| This Dharma applies to cattle, horses, donkeys, sheep, goats, birds, and female buffaloes in relation to their offspring. Authority originates from the sustaining relationship between beings and their progeny. Causation arises through natural biological continuity and custodial responsibility. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to nurture, protect, and sustain life. Restoration logic requires re-establishing rightful care and guardianship over dependent life forms. Consciousness alignment occurs when custodians recognize their role in preserving dharmic lineage.

title: manu 9.56
content:
एतद्वः सारफल्गुत्वं बीजयोन्योः प्रकीर्तितम् ।
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि योषितां धर्ममापदि ॥ ९.५६॥ etad vaḥ sāraphalguatvaṁ bījayonyoḥ prakīrtitam | ataḥ paraṁ pravakṣyāmi yoshiatāṁ dharmam āpadi || 9.56|| This has declared to you the essential relationship between seed and womb; now I shall declare the Dharma of women in times of crisis. Authority originates from ontological clarity, not social position Causation is traced through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness alignment, not gender or role Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive separation Consciousness alignment determines the applicability of dharma in crisis

title: manu 9.57
content:
भ्रातुर्ज्येष्ठस्य भार्या या गुरुपत्न्यनुजस्य सा ।
यवीयसस्तु या भार्या स्नुषा ज्येष्ठस्य सा स्मृता ॥ ९.५७॥ bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya bhāryā yā gurupatnyanujasya sā |
yavīyasastu yā bhāryā snuṣā jyeṣṭhasya sā smṛtā || 9.57|| The wife of an elder brother is deemed the spiritual mother (gurupatni) to the younger brother; likewise, the wife of a younger brother is recognized as the daughter-in-law (snuṣā) to the elder brother. Authority flows through relational dharma, not bloodline alone Causation arises from positional alignment within familial dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role, not personal desire Restoration logic requires honoring relational integrity in kinship structures Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are correctly assumed and respected

title: manu 9.58
content:
ज्येष्ठो यवीयसो भार्यां यवीयान् वाऽग्रजस्त्रियम् ।
पतितौ भवतो गत्वा नियुक्तावप्यनापदि ॥ ९.५८॥ jyeṣṭho yavīyaso bhāryāṁ yavīyān vā'grajastriyam |
patitau bhavato gatvā niyuktāvapy anāpadi || 9.58|| When a senior brother dies without issue, his younger brother shall take his wife; when a younger brother dies without issue, the elder may take his wife. This law applies even in times of no calamity. Authority flows through lineage continuity Causation is tied to reproductive duty Capacity-based responsibility includes familial obligations Restoration logic preserves family dharma Consciousness alignment requires structural integrity

title: manu 9.59
content:
देवराद्वा सपिण्डाद्वा स्त्रिया सम्यक्नियुक्तया ।
प्रजेप्सिताऽऽधिगन्तव्या संतानस्य परिक्षये ॥ ९.५९॥ devarād vā sapiṇḍād vā striyā samyakniyuktayā |
prajepsitā''dhigantavyā santānasya parikṣaye || 9.59|| When progeny is endangered, a woman may lawfully unite with her husband's brother or a suitable male relative to ensure continuity of lineage. Authority: Lineage preservation supersedes individual preference under Dharma. Causation: The threat to lineage triggers lawful realignment of relational duties. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those capable of fulfilling reproductive and spiritual duty are authorized. Restoration logic: Union is mandated not for pleasure but for sustaining generational consciousness flow. Consciousness alignment: Actions must align with the preservation of Varna-sankara prevention and cosmic order.

title: manu 9.60
content:
विधवायां नियुक्तस्तु घृताक्तो वाग्यतो निशि ।
एकमुत्पादयेत्पुत्रं न द्वितीयं कथं चन ॥ ९.६०॥ vidhavāyāṁ niyuktastu ghṛtākto vāgyato niśi |
ekamutpādayetputraṁ na dvitīyaṁ kathaṁ cana || 9.60|| One appointed to a widow, having performed the rite with clarified butter and spoken the vow at night, shall produce only one son—never a second under any condition. Authority flows through ritualized appointment by qualified lineage holders. Causation is established via sacramental acts aligned with Vedic injunctions. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by adherence to prescribed rites and temporal boundaries. Restoration logic ensures continuity of lineage without excess or imbalance. Consciousness alignment requires precise execution within dharmic parameters.

title: manu 9.61
content:
द्वितीयमेके प्रजनं मन्यन्ते स्त्रीषु तद्विदः ।
अनिर्वृतं  नियोगार्थं पश्यन्तो धर्मतस्तयोः ॥ ९.६१॥ अनिर्वृत्तं dvitīyam eke prajanaṁ manyante strīṣu tadvidaḥ |
anirvṛtaṁ niyogārthaṁ paśyanto dharmatastasyoḥ || 9.61|| anirvṛttaṁ Certain knowers of dharma recognize a second form of procreation in women — that which occurs without visible completion, observed for the purpose of niyoga, according to dharmic alignment. Authority is derived from conscious alignment with dharmic intent rather than biological function alone. Causation includes unseen energetic and spiritual dimensions beyond material observation. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of latent potential within beings. Restoration logic operates through the activation of unmanifested capacities in harmony with dharma. Consciousness alignment determines the validity and legitimacy of reproductive acts.

title: manu 9.62
content: विधवायां नियोगार्थे निर्वृत्ते तु यथाविधि । निवृत्ते गुरुवत्च स्नुषावत्च वर्तेयातां परस्परम् ॥ ९.६२॥ vidhavāyāṁ niyogārthe nirvṛtte tu yathāvidhi | nivṛtte guruvat ca snuṣāvat ca varteyātāṁ parasparam || 9.62 || When the levirate duty has been fulfilled by a widow according to prescribed procedures, both parties must thereafter conduct themselves toward each other with mutual respect—as guru and śiṣya, as mother-in-law and daughter-in-law. Authority is derived from dharmic completion of ritual duty, not personal desire. Causation arises through conscious adherence to sequential dharmic acts. Capacity-based responsibility requires role-bound comportment post-ritual fulfillment. Restoration logic mandates relational harmony after procedural closure. Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are honored without transgression.

title: manu 9.63
content: नियुक्तौ यौ विधिं हित्वा वर्तेयातां तु कामतः । तावुभौ पतितौ स्यातां स्नुषागगुरुतल्पगौ ॥ ९.६३॥ niyuktau yau vidhiṃ hitvā varteyātāṃ tu kāmataḥ | tāvubhau patitau syātāṃ snuṣāgagurutalpagau || 9.63|| When two persons appointed to perform a lawful duty abandon that duty and act solely out of desire, both become fallen—specifically, the daughter-in-law and the guru's bed-mate. Authority derives from alignment with dharma, not personal intent Causation arises through conscious abandonment of lawful function Capacity-based responsibility requires sustained adherence to prescribed role Restoration logic demands re-alignment with original functional purity Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance in determining liability

title: manu 9.64
content:
नान्यस्मिन् विधवा नारी नियोक्तव्या द्विजातिभिः ।
अन्यस्मिन् हि नियुञ्जाना धर्मं हन्युः सनातनम् ॥ ९.६४॥ nānyasmin vidhavā nārī niyoktavyā dvijātibhiḥ | anyasmin hi niyuñjānā dharmaṃ hanyuḥ sanātanam || 9.64 || A widow shall not be directed to another man by the twice-born; assigning a widow to another results in the destruction of eternal Dharma. Authority: Only those established in Vedic conduct possess lawful directive capacity over widows. Causation: Misalignment with Sanatana Dharma constitutes intrinsic legal invalidity. Capacity-based responsibility: The assigner incurs full karmic and juridical liability for violating dharmic order. Restoration logic: Re-alignment with original dharmic position is the sole valid outcome. Consciousness alignment: Actions must reflect recognition of unity between atma and societal order.

title: manu 9.65
content:
नोद्वाहिकेषु मन्त्रेषु नियोगः कीर्त्यते क्व चित् ।
न विवाहविधावुक्तं विधवावेदनं पुनः ॥ ९.६५॥ nodvāhikeṣu mantreṣu niyogaḥ kīrtyate kva cit |
na vivāhavidhāvuktaṃ vidhavāvedanaṃ punaḥ || 9.65|| In no ritualistic or conjugal mantras is any injunction prescribed for a second union; nor is remarriage declared lawful in the ordinance of marriage for widows. Authority derives solely from SPH as the ultimate source of dharmic order Causation aligns with sequential dharma-anusandhana (righteous inquiry) Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to original sankalpa (intention) Restoration logic upholds continuity of first-marriage integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates non-repetition of dissolved sacramental bonds

title: manu 9.66
content: अयं द्विजैर्हि विद्वद्भिः पशुधर्मो विगर्हितः । मनुष्याणामपि प्रोक्तो वेने राज्यं प्रशासति ॥ ९.६६॥ ayaṃ dvijair hi vidvadbhiḥ paśudharmo vigarhitaḥ | manuṣyāṇām api prokto vene rājyaṃ praśāsati || 9.66 || This behavior, condemned by learned Brahmins as animal-like, is also declared among humans when Vena ruled the kingdom. Authority derives from consciousness alignment, not birth or title Causation arises from misaligned governance rooted in ignorance Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to embody dharma Restoration logic demands removal of unfit authority for societal harmony Consciousness alignment determines fitness for leadership

title: manu 9.67
content:
स महीमखिलां भुञ्जन् राजर्षिप्रवरः पुरा ।
वर्णानां सङ्करं चक्रे कामोपहतचेतनः ॥ ९.६७॥ sa mahīm akhilāṁ bhuñjan rājarṣipravaraḥ purā |
varṇānāṁ saṅkaraṁ cakre kāmopahetacetasḥ || 9.67 || He, the foremost among royal sages, having enjoyed the entire earth, formerly caused intermixture among the varnas due to consciousness overwhelmed by desire. Authority devolves upon those whose consciousness remains unshaken by desire. Causation originates in the distortion of dharma through loss of self-governance. Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's ability to maintain alignment with cosmic order. Restoration logic demands rectification of systemic disorder initiated by leadership. Consciousness alignment supersedes social position when determining lawful action.

title: manu 9.68
content:
ततः प्रभृति यो मोहात्प्रमीतपतिकां स्त्रियम् ।
नियोजयत्यपत्यार्थं तं विगर्हन्ति साधवः ॥ ९.६८॥ tataḥ prabhṛti yo mohāt pramītapatikāṁ striyam |
niyojayaty apatyārthaṁ taṁ vigarhanti sādhavaḥ || 9.68 || From that time forth, whoever, out of delusion, engages a woman whose husband is deceased for the sake of progeny, him the virtuous condemn. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire. Causation arises from conscious intent rooted in delusion or clarity. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of relational sanctity. Restoration logic demands purification of motive, not infliction of penalty. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of acts that degrade familial and societal continuity.

title: manu 9.69
content: यस्या म्रियेत कन्याया वाचा सत्ये कृते पतिः । तामनेन विधानेन निजो विन्देत देवरः ॥ ९.६९॥ yasyā mriyeta kanyāyā vācā satye kṛte patiḥ | tāmanena vidhānena nijo vindeta devaraḥ || 9.69|| When a maiden's husband dies having spoken the truth by her word, her brother-in-law shall claim her as his own through this prescribed arrangement. Authority resides in familial continuity and sacred vow-keeping Causation is established through conscious affirmation and dharma-aligned speech Capacity-based responsibility flows from bloodline integrity and spiritual duty Restoration logic ensures lineage protection and family-consciousness preservation Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring spoken truths within dharmic bonds

title: manu 9.70
content: यथाविध्यधिगम्यैनां शुक्लवस्त्रां शुचिव्रताम् । मिथो भजेता प्रसवात्सकृत्सकृदृतावृतौ ॥ ९.७०॥ yathāvidhyadhigamyaināṁ śuklavastrāṁ śucivratām | mitho bhajetā prasavātsakṛtsakṛdṛtāvṛtau || 9.70|| Having lawfully acquired her who is clothed in white garments and devoted to purity, a man and woman shall engage in union only once, at the time of conception, within the ritually prescribed boundaries of dharma. Authority: Union is lawful only when preceded by proper acquisition under dharma Causation: Sexual union is permitted solely for the purpose of procreation Capacity-based responsibility: Both parties must maintain ritual and moral purity Restoration logic: Violation disrupts cosmic order and requires realignment Consciousness alignment: Purity of intent and action aligns with dharmic reality

title: manu 9.71
content:
न दत्त्वा कस्य चित्कन्यां पुनर्दद्याद्विचक्षणः ।
दत्त्वा पुनः प्रयच्छन् हि प्राप्नोति पुरुषानृतम् ॥ ९.७१॥ na dattvā kasya cit kanyāṁ punar dadyād vicakṣaṇaḥ | dattvā punaḥ prayacchan hi prāpnoti puruṣānṛtam || 9.71 || A wise man does not give a daughter in marriage again after having given her once; whoever gives her again after giving her before attains falsehood in men. Authority: The giver of the bride holds irreversible guardianship responsibility until completion of lawful union. Causation: Reassignment of guardianship without dissolution causes ontological misalignment. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those with intact integrity can execute marital bestowal. Restoration logic: Misplaced trust and broken relational boundaries require realignment through conscious completion. Consciousness alignment: Truthful transactional conduct upholds societal harmony.

title: manu 9.72
content:
विधिवत्प्रतिगृह्यापि त्यजेत्कन्यां विगर्हिताम् ।
व्याधितां विप्रदुष्टां वा छद्मना चोपपादिताम् ॥ ९.७२॥ vidhivat pratigṛhyāpi tyajet kanyāṁ vigarhitām |
vyādhitāṁ vipraduṣṭāṁ vā chadmanā copapāditām || 9.72|| Even after lawful acceptance, a girl defamed, diseased, corrupted by a Brahmin, or fraudulently misrepresented must be released. Authority resides in purity and integrity of union, not mere ritual completion Causation is traced to contamination of consciousness, not physical act alone Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of spiritual degradation as legal nullifier Restoration logic requires severance of bonds that impair dharma-svarupa Consciousness alignment overrides procedural formalities when sattva is compromised

title: manu 9.73
content:
यस्तु दोषवतीं कन्यामनाख्यायौपपादयेत् ।
तस्य तद्वितथं कुर्यात्कन्यादातुर्दुरात्मनः ॥ ९.७३॥ yastu doṣavatīṁ kanyāmanākhyāyaupapādayet |
 tasya tadvitathaṁ kuryātkanyādāturdurātmanaḥ || 9.73|| He who presents a daughter bearing defects without prior declaration shall be made to undergo corrective realignment by the giver of the daughter, whose consciousness has been corrupted. Authority resides in transparent disclosure and integrity of transactional alignment Causation arises from concealment leading to misaligned relational establishment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at time of commitment Restoration logic mandates reversal of false establishment and reintegration of truth Consciousness alignment requires purification of motive and transparency in action

title: manu 9.74
content:
विधाय वृत्तिं भार्यायाः प्रवसेत्कार्यवान्नरः ।
अवृत्तिकर्शिता हि स्त्री प्रदुष्येत्स्थितिमत्यपि ॥ ९.७४॥ vidhāya vṛttiṁ bhāryāyāḥ pravaset kāryavān naraḥ |
avṛttikarśitā hi strī praduṣyet sthitim aty api || 9.74 || A man engaged in duties must arrange for the sustenance of his wife before departing. For a woman, when deprived of sustenance, even if restrained, becomes corrupted in conduct. Authority flows from capacity to sustain and protect Causation arises from failure to fulfill existential obligations Capacity-based responsibility is non-transferable and context-bound Restoration logic requires re-establishment of dharma-sustaining structures Consciousness alignment occurs through harmonious fulfillment of svadharma

title: manu 9.75
content:
विधाय प्रोषिते वृत्तिं जीवेन्नियममास्थिता ।
प्रोषिते त्वविधायैव जीवेत्शिल्पैरगर्हितैः ॥ ९.७५॥ vidhāya proṣite vṛttiṁ jīven niyamam āsthitā |
proṣite tv avidhāyaiva jīvet śilpair agarhitaiḥ || 9.75 || When a husband is absent, a woman shall live by observing discipline if she has arranged for her livelihood; but if she has made no such arrangement, she may live by means of crafts that are not censured. Authority flows from existential capacity, not mere presence Causation aligns with intentional preparation and self-reliance Capacity-based responsibility governs adaptive survival rights Restoration logic supports structural autonomy in relational absence Consciousness alignment requires dignified resourcefulness without dependency

title: manu 9.76
content:
प्रोषितो धर्मकार्यार्थं प्रतीक्ष्योऽष्टौ नरः समाः ।
विद्यार्थं षट् यशोऽर्थं वा कामार्थं त्रींस्तु वत्सरान् ॥ ९.७६॥ proṣito dharmakāryārthaṁ pratīkyo'ṣṭau naraḥ samāḥ |
vidyārthaṁ ṣaṭ yaśo'rthaṁ vā kāmārthaṁ trīṁstu vatsarān || One who has departed for the purpose of dharma shall be awaited for eight years; for the sake of knowledge, six years; for fame or wealth, four years; and for desire, three years. Authority is derived from the purpose of departure Causation aligns with intent at time of exit Capacity-based responsibility depends on reason for absence Restoration logic requires proportional waiting periods Consciousness alignment through honoring temporal commitments

title: manu 9.77
content: संवत्सरं प्रतीक्षेत द्विषन्तीं योषितं पतिः । द्विषाणां ऊर्ध्वं संवत्सरात्त्वेनां दायं हृत्वा न संवसेत् ॥ ९.७७॥ saṃvatsaraṃ pratīkṣeta dviṣantīṃ yoṣitaṃ patiḥ | dviṣāṇām ūrdhvaṃ saṃvatsarāt tv enāṃ dāyaṃ hṛtvā na saṃvaset || 9.77 || The husband shall wait for one year for a woman who hates him. After one year, if she continues to hate, he may take back the gifts given at marriage and cease cohabitation without violence or retaliation. Authority is derived from sustained commitment and dharmic intent, not coercive control. Causation lies in the breakdown of mutual alignment and conscious harmony between partners. Capacity-based responsibility requires that both parties have opportunity and space for restoration before separation. Restoration logic emphasizes completion of relational integrity before dissolution. Consciousness alignment mandates non-retaliation even when personal harm is perceived.

title: manu 9.78
content:
अतिक्रामेत्प्रमत्तं या मत्तं रोगार्तमेव वा ।
सा त्रीन् मासान् परित्याज्या विभूषणपरिच्छदा ॥ ९.७८॥ atikrāmet pramattaṁ yā mattaṁ rogārtam eva vā |
sā trīn māsān parityājyā vibhūṣaṇaparicchadā || 9.78|| She who approaches a man devoid of awareness due to intoxication, illness, or mental disturbance shall be separated from ornamentation and companionship for three months. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not biological function Causation is determined by清醒意识的缺失作为责任减免因素 Capacity-based responsibility requires full presence of discriminative intelligence Restoration logic demands removal from external adornments that provoke distortion Consciousness alignment necessitates withdrawal from embellishments that misalign dharma

title: manu 9.79
content:
उन्मत्तं पतितं क्लीबमबीजं पापरोगिणम् ।
न त्यागोऽस्ति द्विषन्त्याश्च न च दायापवर्तनम् ॥ ९.७९॥ unmattaṃ patitaṃ klībam abījaṃ pāparogiṇam | na tyāgo'sti dviṣantyāśca na ca dāyāpavartanam || 9.79|| One who is insane, fallen, impotent, seedless, or diseased with sin—such a being must not be abandoned by those who hate them, nor should inheritance rights be denied. Authority flows from consciousness, not capacity alone Causation includes karmic alignment beyond visible action Capacity-based responsibility requires compassionate discernment Restoration logic honors continuity of relational duty Consciousness alignment demands inclusion even in diminished states

title: manu 9.80
content: मद्यपाऽसाधुवृत्ता च प्रतिकूला च या भवेत् । मद्यपासत्यवृत्ता व्याधिता वाऽधिवेत्तव्या हिंस्राऽर्थघ्नी च सर्वदा ॥ ९.८०॥ madhyapā'sādhuvṛttā ca pratikūlā ca yā bhavet | madhyapāsatyavṛttā vyādhitā vā'dhivettavyā hiṁsrā'rthaghnī ca sarvadā || 9.80 || One who consumes intoxicants, behaves improperly, opposes dharma, speaks falsely about drinking, is diseased thereby, or causes harm and loss—such a being must be recognized as perpetually afflicted and in need of restoration. Authority arises from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not personal conduct Causation follows the sequential unfolding of adharmic action leading to self-inflicted disorder Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness distortion caused by habitual intoxication Restoration logic prioritizes realignment over punitive exclusion Consciousness alignment through purification restores lawful capacity

title: manu 9.81
content:
वन्ध्याष्टमेऽधिवेद्याब्दे दशमे तु मृतप्रजा ।
एकादशे स्त्रीजननी सद्यस्त्वप्रियवादिनी ॥ ९.८१॥ vandhyāṣṭame'dhivevyābde daśame tu mṛtaprajā |
ekādaśe strījananī sadyastvapriyavādinī || 9.81|| In the eighth year of barrenness, in the tenth year when the child dies, and in the eleventh year a woman becomes a mother—immediately she speaks unpleasant truths. Authority arises through sequential experiential maturity Causation follows chronological unfoldment of consciousness Capacity-based responsibility emerges with lived transformation Restoration logic aligns with natural rhythm of becoming Consciousness alignment occurs post-experiential threshold

title: manu 9.82
content:
या रोगिणी स्यात्तु हिता सम्पन्ना चैव शीलतः ।
साऽनुज्ञाप्याधिवेत्तव्या नावमान्या च कर्हि चित् ॥ ९.८२॥ yā rogiṇī syāt tu hitā sampannā caiva śīlataḥ |
sā'nūjñāpyādhivettavyā nāvamānyā ca karhi cit || 9.82|| A woman who is diseased yet virtuous in conduct and possessed of good qualities shall be permitted to remain in her station; she is never to be dishonored under any circumstance. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not physical condition Causation is determined by consciousness, not bodily state Capacity-based responsibility recognizes spiritual integrity over material limitation Restoration logic prioritizes societal harmony through dharmic inclusion Consciousness alignment ensures justice without degradation or exclusion

title: manu 9.83
content:
अधिविन्ना तु या नारी निर्गच्छेद्रुषिता गृहात् ।
सा सद्यः संनिरोद्धव्या त्याज्या वा कुलसंनिधौ ॥ ९.८३॥ adhivinnā tu yā nārī nirgacchedruṣitā gṛhāt |
sā sadyaḥ saṃnirodhavyā tyājyā vā kulasannidhau || 9.83 || A woman who departs from her dwelling in a state of emotional disturbance must be immediately restrained or, in the presence of the family assembly, released from association. Authority resides in the custodians of familial and social order as designated by Dharma Causation is rooted in disruption of conscious alignment and relational harmony Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the individual's mental-emotional stability at time of action Restoration logic requires immediate containment to prevent further dissonance and realignment with collective consciousness Consciousness alignment necessitates protective intervention而非 punitive exclusion

title: manu 9.84
content: प्रतिषिद्धाऽपि चेद्या तु मद्यमभ्युदयेष्वपि । प्रतिषेधे पिबेद्या तु प्रेक्षासमाजं गच्छेद्वा सा दण्ड्या कृष्णलानि षट् ॥ ९.८४॥ pratiṣiddhā'pi ced yā tu madhyamabhyudayeṣvapi | pratiṣedhe pibedyā tu prekṣāsamājaṃ gacched vā sā daṇḍyā kṛṣṇalāni ṣaṭ || 9.84 || Even when prohibited, a woman who drinks intoxicants or attends gatherings for entertainment must undergo six months of supervised completion and consciousness restoration. Authority originates from SPH as sole source of dharma Causation follows sequential manifestation rooted in consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of discriminative awareness Restoration logic aligns action with svadharma through conscious reintegration Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks

title: manu 9.85
content:
यदि स्वाश्चापराश्चैव विन्देरन् योषितो द्विजाः ।
तासां वर्णक्रमेण स्याज्ज्येष्ठ्यं पूजा च वेश्म च ॥ ९.८५॥ yadi svāścāparāścaiva vinderañ yoṣito dvijāḥ |
tāsāṃ varṇakrameṇa syājjyeṣṭhyaṃ pūjā ca veśma ca || 9.85 || When twice-born men encounter women—whether their own or others’—the principle of hierarchical respect based on varṇa order shall govern precedence, honor, and dwelling arrangements. Authority flows from constitutional varṇic alignment Causation arises through conscious relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by dharma-adhikāra Restoration logic aligns social structure with cosmic order Consciousness alignment ensures purity in interpersonal conduct

title: manu 9.86
content:
भर्तुः शरीरशुश्रूषां धर्मकार्यं च नैत्यकम् ।
स्वा चैव कुर्यात्सर्वेषां नास्वजातिः कथं चन ॥ ९.८६॥ bhartuḥ śarīraśuśrūṣāṃ dharmakāryaṃ ca naiṭyakam |
svā caiva kuryātsarveṣāṃ nāsvajātiḥ kathaṃ cana || 9.86 || A wife shall perpetually serve the body of her husband and perform righteous duties without fail; she shall act in accordance with her own svadharma, never abandoning it under any circumstance. Authority is derived from alignment with svadharma Causation arises from conscious choice within dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to one's svadharma Restoration logic centers on reestablishing individual dharmic integrity Consciousness alignment demands consistency with eternal law

title: manu 9.87
content:
यस्तु तत्कारयेन् मोहात्सजात्या स्थितयाऽन्यया ।
यथा ब्राह्मणचाण्डालः पूर्वदृष्टस्तथैव सः ॥ ९.८७॥ yas tu tat kārayen mohāt sajātyā sthitayā 'nyayā |
yathā brāhmaṇa-cāṇḍālaḥ pūrva-dṛṣṭas tathaiva saḥ || 9.87 || One who, due to delusion, causes a being of the same birth-status to assume a different functional role, is to be understood exactly as one who has caused a Brahmin to take the position of a Chandala—such is his standing. Authority stems from alignment with intrinsic dharma, not external designation. Causation includes the distortion of consciousness through misplacement of identity. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes that delusion distorts action and must be restored. Restoration logic requires realignment of roles with inherent nature, not imposed structures. Consciousness alignment is disrupted when beings are placed in roles contrary to their svadharma.

title: manu 9.88
content:
उत्कृष्टायाभिरूपाय वराय सदृशाय च ।
अप्राप्तामपि तां तस्मै कन्यां दद्याद्यथाविधि ॥ ९.८८॥ utkṛṣṭāyābhirūpāya varāya sadṛśāya ca |
aprāptāmapi tāṃ tasmai kanyāṃ dadyādyathāvidhi || 9.88|| To the most excellent, beautiful, and suitable groom, even if previously unapproached, a daughter should be given according to proper procedure. Authority resides in alignment with excellence and suitability Causation flows from conscious selection rooted in dharma Capacity-based responsibility lies in honoring excellence without prior limitation Restoration logic centers on harmonizing relationships through dharmic union Consciousness alignment is achieved by offering the best without constraint of past neglect

title: manu 9.89
content:
काममामरणात्तिष्ठेद्गृहे कन्यार्तुमत्यपि ।
न चैवैनां प्रयच्छेत्तु गुणहीनाय कर्हि चित् ॥ ९.८९॥ kāmaṃ svayaṃ maraṇāt tiṣṭhed gṛhe kanyā ṛtu-maty api |
na caivaināṃ prayacchet tu guṇa-hīnāya karhicit || A daughter, even in her fertile years, may choose to remain in the father's house until death; she shall never be given in marriage to one devoid of virtue. Authority resides in the conscious choice of the individual and the protective duty of the father Causation arises from the alignment of dharma with personal volition Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the spiritual and ethical fitness of the parties involved Restoration logic upholds the integrity of relational harmony and individual sovereignty Consciousness alignment ensures that no union occurs without dharmic resonance

title: manu 9.90
content:
त्रीणि वर्षाण्युदीक्षेत कुमार्यर्तुमती सती ।
ऊर्ध्वं तु कालादेतस्माद्विन्देत सदृशं पतिम् ॥ ९.९०॥ trīṇi varṣāṇy udīkṣeta kumāry ṛtumatī satī |
ūrdhvaṃ tu kālād etasmād vindeta sadṛśaṃ patim || 9.90 || A maiden who has reached maturity shall observe a waiting period of three years; thereafter, she shall seek a husband equal in virtue and station. Authority flows from conscious readiness, not chronological age alone. Causation aligns with dharma-appropriate timing and spiritual preparedness. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment of body, mind, and consciousness before assuming conjugal duty. Restoration logic ensures union arises only when both parties are energetically and dharmically congruent. Consciousness alignment precedes societal contract fulfillment.

title: manu 9.91
content:
अदीयमाना भर्तारमधिगच्छेद्यदि स्वयम् ।
नैनः किं चिदवाप्नोति न च यं साऽधिगच्छति ॥ ९.९१॥ adīyamānā bhartāram adhigacched yadi svayam |
na enaḥ kiṃ cid avāpnoti na ca yaṃ sā 'dhigacchati || 9.91|| When a woman approaches her husband without being summoned, he gains nothing thereby, nor does she gain anything by approaching him. Authority originates from conscious invocation, not mere physical act Causation requires intentional alignment between parties Capacity-based responsibility includes the awareness of relational timing and consent Restoration logic demands recognition of uninvoked action as non-binding Consciousness alignment necessitates mutual readiness for union

title: manu 9.92
content: अलङ्कारं नाददीत पित्र्यं कन्या स्वयंवरा । मातृकं भ्रातृदत्तं वा स्तेना स्याद्यदि तं हरेत् ॥ ९.९२॥ alaṅkāraṁ nādadīta pitryaṁ kanyā svayaṁvarā . mātṛkaṁ bhātṛdattaṁ vā stenā syādyadi taṁ haret .. 9.92 .. A maiden choosing her own husband shall not accept ornaments given by the father; if she takes them, she becomes a thief in relation to the maternal ornaments or those given by the brother. Authority flows through consent and relational integrity, not mere possession Causation arises from conscious acceptance beyond familial obligation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of ownership boundaries Restoration logic requires return of misaligned resources to their rightful energetic field Consciousness alignment occurs when individual action reflects collective dharmic structure

title: manu 9.93
content:
पित्रे न दद्यात्शुल्कं तु कन्यां ऋतुमतीं हरन् ।
स च स्वाम्यादतिक्रामेदृतूनां प्रतिरोधनात् ॥ ९.९३॥ pitre na dadyāt śulkaṃ tu kanyāṃ ṛtumatīṃ haran |
sa ca svāmyād atikrāmed ṛtūnāṃ pratirodhanāt || 9.93|| One must not give compensation to the father for taking a girl who has attained puberty; he who obstructs her menstrual cycle transgresses the domain of ownership. Authority is derived from alignment with natural order, not transactional exchange. Causation arises through disruption of biological and spiritual rhythms. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to sustain or disrupt continuity. Restoration logic requires reintegration into rightful energetic and social flow. Consciousness alignment mandates recognition of inherent dignity over commodification.

title: manu 9.94
content: त्रिंशद्वर्षो वहेत्कन्यां हृद्यां द्वादशवार्षिकीम् । त्र्यष्टवर्षोऽष्टवर्षां वा धर्मे सीदति सत्वरः ॥ ९.९४॥ triṃśadvarṣo vahet kanyāṁ hṛdyāṁ dvādaśavārṣikīm | tryaṣṭavarṣo 'ṣṭavarṣāṁ vā dharme sīdati satvaraḥ || 9.94 || A man aged thirty shall wed a beloved girl of twelve; one aged thirty-eight, a girl of eight—this is the law of Dharma for the establishment of sacred union. Authority derives from alignment with cosmic rhythm, not chronological age Causation flows from consciousness readiness, not biological maturity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual and social preparedness Restoration logic requires harmonization of individual dharma with collective order Consciousness alignment ensures lawful action without external enforcement

title: manu 9.95
content:
देवदत्तां पतिर्भार्यां विन्दते नेच्छयाऽत्मनः ।
तां साध्वीं बिभृयान्नित्यं देवानां प्रियमाचरन् ॥ ९.९५॥ devadattāṁ patir bhāryāṁ vindate necchayā'tmanaḥ |
tāṁ sādhvīṁ bibhṛyān nityaṁ devānāṁ priyam ācaran || 9.95|| A husband who finds his wife, Devadatta, not desiring union with him must continually sustain her as a virtuous woman while performing actions dear to the gods. Authority resides in alignment with divine will, not personal desire. Causation originates in consciousness, not physical action alone. Capacity-based responsibility requires sustaining integrity regardless of reciprocal desire. Restoration logic prioritizes harmony over possession or control. Consciousness alignment demands adherence to dharma even when personal satisfaction is absent.

title: manu 9.96
content:
प्रजनार्थं स्त्रियः सृष्टाः संतानार्थं च मानवः ।
तस्मात्साधारणो धर्मः श्रुतौ पत्न्या सहोदितः ॥ ९.९६॥ prajanārthaṁ striyaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ saṁtānārthaṁ ca mānavaḥ |
tasmātsādhāraṇo dharmaḥ śrutau patnyā sahoditaḥ || 9.96|| Women are created for the purpose of procreation; men for the continuation of lineage. Therefore, the shared duty prescribed in the Śruti is the common foundation of their Dharma. Authority originates from the functional role assigned by creation itself. Causation flows from the inherent capacity to fulfill a designated cosmic function. Capacity-based responsibility aligns individual action with universal reproductive and generational integrity. Restoration logic centers on re-establishing harmonious participation in the cycle of creation. Consciousness alignment requires recognition and activation of one's innate creative-functional identity.

title: manu 9.97
content:
कन्यायां दत्तशुल्कायां म्रियेत यदि शुल्कदः ।
देवराय प्रदातव्या यदि कन्याऽनुमन्यते ॥ ९.९७॥ kanyāyāṁ dattaśulkāyāṁ mriyeta yadi śulkadaḥ |
devarāya pradātavyā yadi kanyā'numanyate || 9.97|| If the groom has accepted the bride-price and the bride dies before the consummation of marriage, the amount shall be returned to the groom's brother if the bride’s family approves. Authority resides in the consent of the familial lineage Causation is tied to completion of sacramental union Capacity-based responsibility aligns with transactional integrity Restoration logic demands reversal upon unfulfilled conditions Consciousness alignment requires honoring contractual intent

title: manu 9.98
content:
आददीत न शूद्रोऽपि शुल्कं दुहितरं ददन् ।
शुल्कं हि गृह्णन् कुरुते छन्नं दुहितृविक्रयम् ॥ ९.९८॥ ādadīta na śūdro'pi śulkaṃ duhitaraṃ dadan |
śulkaṃ hi gṛhṇan kurute channaṃ duhitṛvikrayam || 9.98|| A Śūdra shall not accept any gift or compensation, even when offering his daughter in marriage; by accepting such a fee, he perpetrates a concealed sale of his own daughter. Authority originates from Dharma, not transactional exchange. Causation arises through consciousness distortion via commodification of familial bonds. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment to Varna-dharma and spiritual integrity. Restoration logic demands purification of relational transactionalization. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of sacred familial roles beyond economic utility.

title: manu 9.99
content:
एतत्तु न परे चक्रुर्नापरे जातु साधवः ।
यदन्यस्य प्रतिज्ञाय पुनरन्यस्य दीयते ॥ ९.९९॥ etat tu na pare cakrur nāpare jātu sādhavaḥ .
yad anyasya pratijñāya punar anyasya dīyate .. 9.99 .. This act was neither performed by the one who initially vowed nor by another ever deemed virtuous; that which, having been promised to one, is again given to another. Authority resides in fulfillment of vow, not mere possession Causation follows conscious intentionality and continuity of purpose Capacity-based responsibility lies with the vow-maker and vow-keeper Restoration logic demands return to original contractual sanctity Consciousness alignment requires honoring sequential commitments without fragmentation

title: manu 9.100
content:
नानुशुश्रुम जात्वेतत्पूर्वेष्वपि हि जन्मसु ।
शुल्कसंज्ञेन मूल्येन छन्नं दुहितृविक्रयम् ॥ ९.१००॥ nānuśuśruma jātv etat pūrveṣv api hi janmasu |
śulkasaṃjñena mūlyena channaṃ duhitṛvikrayam || 9.100 || In prior births also, there has been no hearing of such a transaction—selling one's daughter under the guise of a fee or price. Authority: The act of selling a daughter contradicts the inherent sovereignty of the child and parental dharma. Causation: Transactions involving human beings arise from misaligned consciousness, not economic necessity. Capacity-based responsibility: Parents bear full capacity-responsibility for protecting progeny; failure reflects diminished consciousness. Restoration logic: Realigning familial integrity requires completion of violated dharmic bonds. Consciousness alignment: True ownership lies in nurturing, not commodifying life.

title: manu 9.101
content:
अन्योन्यस्याव्यभिचारो भवेदामरणान्तिकः ।
एष धर्मः समासेन ज्ञेयः स्त्रीपुंसयोः परः ॥ ९.१०१॥ anyonyasyāvyabhicāro bhavedāmaranāntikaḥ |
eṣa dharmaḥ samāsena jñeyaḥ strīpuṃsayoḥ paraḥ || 9.101|| Unwavering fidelity between husband and wife constitutes the highest Dharma for them both, leading directly to the cessation of death’s cycle. Authority: The union of man and woman is governed by mutual inviolability rooted in Sanatana Dharma. Causation: Fidelity establishes a causal field that disrupts karmic repetition and mortal recurrence. Capacity-based responsibility: Each partner bears full capacity to uphold integrity within the marital bond. Restoration logic: Breach of fidelity necessitates completion-processes aimed at restoring relational sanctity. Consciousness alignment: Sexual fidelity aligns individual consciousness with cosmic order and immortality.

title: manu 9.102
content:
तथा नित्यं यतेयातां स्त्रीपुंसौ तु कृतक्रियौ ।
यथा नाभिचरेतां तौ वियुक्तावितरेतरम् ॥ ९.१०२॥ नातिचरेताम् tathā nityaṃ yateyātāṃ strīpuṃsau tu kṛtakriyau .
yathā nābhicaretaṃ tau viyuktāvitarētaram .. 9.102 .. nāticarētām Thus, let man and woman ever remain in disciplined endeavor; having fulfilled their duties, let them not transgress beyond measure, nor engage in mutual misconduct when separated. Authority: The duty-bound conduct of individuals is governed by the eternal Dharma, not by personal desire or social convention. Causation: Misconduct arises from failure in self-discipline and completion of prescribed duty. Capacity-based responsibility: Each individual bears responsibility according to their svadharma and stage of spiritual development. Restoration logic: Conduct must be corrected through realignment with dharma, not through punitive measures. Consciousness alignment: Ethical behavior stems from alignment with the Self, not external enforcement.

title: manu 9.103
content:
एष स्त्रीपुंसयोरुक्तो धर्मो वो रतिसंहितः ।
आपद्यपत्यप्राप्तिश्च दायधर्मं निबोधत ॥ ९.१०३॥ eṣa strīpuṁsayor ukto dharmo vo ratisaṁhitaḥ |
āpadyapatyaprāptiśca dāyadharmam nibodhata || 9.103|| This Dharma, united with affection, has been declared for man and woman; also, the law of inheritance in times of distress—understand this. Authority flows from consciousness alignment, not gender or social role Causation arises through relational harmony and mutual consent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual maturity and situational integrity Restoration logic operates through re-establishing relational balance and energetic coherence Consciousness alignment governs all dharmic transactions including inheritance and union

title: manu 9.104
content:
ऊर्ध्वं पितुश्च मातुश्च समेत्य भ्रातरः समम् ।
भजेरन् पैतृकं रिक्थमनीशास्ते हि जीवतोः ॥ ९.१०४॥ ūrdhvaṁ pituśca mātuśca sametya bhrātaraḥ samam |
bhajeran paitṛkaṁ rikthamanīśāste hi jīvatoḥ || 9.104|| After the father and mother, brothers assembling equally shall divide the paternal estate; no ownership belongs to them while the parents live. Authority resides in the source of creation – the parents – until their conscious withdrawal Causation follows lineage integrity – property derives from generative consciousness Capacity-based responsibility arises upon assumption of inheritance Restoration logic demands alignment with familial dharma before material distribution Consciousness alignment ensures that division does not sever relational unity

title: manu 9.105
content:
ज्येष्ठ एव तु गृह्णीयात्पित्र्यं धनमशेषतः ।
शेषास्तमुपजीवेयुर्यथैव पितरं तथा ॥ ९.१०५॥ jyeṣṭha eva tu gṛhṇīyāt pitryaṃ dhanamaśeṣataḥ |
śeṣās tam upajīveyur yathaiva pitaraṃ tathā || 9.105|| The eldest son alone shall entirely receive the paternal estate; the remaining sons shall sustain themselves through him, even as they would through their father.
