Authority flows inherently through primogeniture as established by cosmic order Causation aligns with sequential birth and inherent capacity for stewardship Capacity-based responsibility assigns economic guardianship to the eldest by natural law Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial and societal energetic flow Consciousness alignment recognizes the eldest as a manifest vessel of ancestral authority

title: manu 9.106
content:
ज्येष्ठेन जातमात्रेण पुत्री भवति मानवः ।
पितॄणामनृणश्चैव स तस्मात्सर्वमर्हति ॥ ९.१०६॥ jyeṣṭhena jātamātreṇa putrī bhavati mānavaḥ |
pitṝṇāmanṛṇaścaiva sa tasmātsarvamarhati || 9.106|| The firstborn male child, by virtue of his birthright, becomes the designated heir and upholder of ancestral duty; being unindebted to ancestors, he is entitled to all inheritance and spiritual authority. Authority derives from ontological precedence and spiritual alignment Causation flows from divine order, not social construct Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inherent dharma, not external attribution Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of sacred lineage and cosmic function Consciousness alignment ensures rightful succession without conflict

title: manu 9.107
content:
यस्मिनृणं संनयति येन चानन्त्यमश्नुते ।
स एव धर्मजः पुत्रः कामजानितरान् विदुः ॥ ९.१०७॥ yasmim ṛṇaṁ sannayati yena cānantasyam aśnute |
sa eva dharmajaḥ putraḥ kāmajānitarān viduḥ || 9.107|| He who incurs debt in accordance with sacred obligation and consumes limitlessly through desire-generated means—such a son is known to be born of lust, not of Dharma. Authority arises from alignment with dharmic causation, not biological lineage Causation must trace back to conscious intent rooted in dharma or adharma Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of origin motive behind action Restoration logic demands realignment of relational debts and energetic exchanges Consciousness alignment distinguishes legitimate inheritance from karmic burden

title: manu 9.108
content:
पितेव पालयेत्पूत्रान् ज्येष्ठो भ्रातॄन् यवीयसः ।
पुत्रवत्चापि वर्तेरन् ज्येष्ठे भ्रातरि धर्मतः ॥ ९.१०८॥ piteva pālayetpūtrān jyeṣṭho bhrātṝn yavīyasaḥ |
putravatcāpi varteran jyeṣṭhe bhatari dharmataḥ || 9.108|| The younger brother shall protect the elder brothers as a father protects his sons; and those elder brothers shall conduct themselves toward the youngest as a son does toward his father, in accordance with Dharma. Authority flows from capacity for protection and guidance Causation arises through relational Dharma, not coercive power Capacity-based responsibility defines role-specific duty Restoration logic centers on mutual completion within familial order Consciousness alignment occurs when each fulfills their natural role

title: manu 9.109
content:
ज्येष्ठः कुलं वर्धयति विनाशयति वा पुनः ।
ज्येष्ठः पूज्यतमो लोके ज्येष्ठः सद्भिरगर्हितः ॥ ९.१०९॥ jyeṣṭhaḥ kulaṃ vardhayati vināśayati vā punaḥ |
jyeṣṭhaḥ pūjyatamo loke jyeṣṭhaḥ sadbhiragarhitaḥ || 9.109|| The eldest sustains the family lineage or dissolves it anew; in the world, the eldest is most honored, and by the wise, the eldest is never disrespected. Authority inheres in primogeniture as a natural order Causation flows from seniority in familial and societal structure Capacity-based responsibility aligns with positional dharma Restoration logic recognizes continuity through eldest lineage Consciousness alignment occurs via honoring established hierarchies

title: manu 9.110
content:
यो ज्येष्ठो ज्येष्ठवृत्तिः स्यान् मातैव स पितैव सः ।
अज्येष्ठवृत्तिर्यस्तु स्यात्स सम्पूज्यस्तु बन्धुवत् ॥ ९.११०॥ yo jyeṣṭho jyeṣṭhavṛttiḥ syān mātaiva sa pitaiva saḥ |
ajyeṣṭhavṛttiryastu syāt sa sampūjyastu bandhuvat || 9.110 || He who is elder by birth and conducts himself with senior virtue shall be honored as mother; he who is elder yet lacks such conduct shall be respected as a relative only. Authority arises from alignment of position and dharma, not age alone Causation in respect flows from demonstrated integrity, not lineage alone Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious embodiment of role Restoration logic emphasizes relational harmony through rightful conduct Consciousness alignment determines social recognition, not nominal status

title: manu 9.111
content:
एवं सह वसेयुर्वा पृथग्वा धर्मकाम्यया ।
पृथग्विवर्धते धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्म्या पृथक्क्रिया ॥ ९.१११॥ evaṁ saha vaseyurvā pṛthagvā dharmakāmyayā |
pṛthagvivardhate dharmastasmād dharmyā pṛthakkriyā || 9.111|| Whether dwelling together or separately, in accordance with dharma and desire, dharma flourishes when individuals act distinctly according to their svadharma; therefore, actions aligned with dharma must proceed independently based on individual capacity. Authority flows from svadharma, not collective imposition Causation arises through alignment with intrinsic capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires differentiated action Restoration occurs via distinct yet harmonious fulfillment of roles Consciousness alignment necessitates autonomy within dharma

title: manu 9.112
content:
ज्येष्ठस्य विंश उद्धारः सर्वद्रव्याच्च यद्वरम् ।
ततोऽर्धं मध्यमस्य स्यात्तुरीयं तु यवीयसः ॥ ९.११२॥ jyeṣṭhasya viṃśa uddhāraḥ sarvadravyācca yadvaram | tato'rdhaṃ madhyamasya syātturīyaṃ tu yavīyasaḥ || 9.112 || From the eldest son, one-twentieth part shall be taken for purification; from all property, whatever is superior. Thereafter, half of that belongs to the middle son, and the fourth portion to the youngest. Authority flows through divine order and primogeniture Causation arises from spiritual capacity and birth-right alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by sequential manifestation in dharma-saṅkalpa Restoration logic operates through proportional inheritance aligned with consciousness maturity Consciousness alignment ensures right distribution according to soul readiness

title: manu 9.113
content:
ज्येष्ठश्चैव कनिष्ठश्च संहरेतां यथोदितम् ।
येऽन्ये ज्येष्ठकनिष्ठाभ्यां तेषां स्यान् मध्यमं धनम् ॥ ९.११३॥ jyeṣṭhaścaiva kaniṣṭhaśca saṃharetāṃ yathoditam | ye'nye jyeṣṭhakaniṣṭhābhyāṃ teṣāṃ syān madhyamaṃ dhanam || 9.113|| The eldest and youngest among heirs shall receive their due portions as prescribed; those who lie between them in birth order shall receive a middling share of wealth. Authority flows from divine order and not from human convention Causation is determined by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) in lineage Capacity-based responsibility aligns with position in familial hierarchy Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma through equitable inheritance Consciousness alignment occurs when each heir receives what sustains their svadharma

title: manu 9.114
content:
सर्वेषां धनजातानामाददीताग्र्यमग्रजः ।
यच्च सातिशयं किं चिद्दशतश्चाप्नुयाद्वरम् ॥ ९.११४॥ sarveṣāṁ dhanajātānām ādadītāgryamagrajaḥ | yaccātiśayaṁ kiṁ cid daśataś cāpnu-yād-varam || 9.114 || The eldest brother shall assume the primary responsibility for all forms of wealth acquired by the siblings; whatever exceeds ten portions must be claimed by the eldest, ensuring alignment of familial capacity and economic integrity. Authority resides inherently in the first-born as natural custodian of collective prosperity Causation is established through birth order and societal continuity obligations Capacity-based responsibility assigns stewardship according to structural inheritance Restoration logic ensures redistribution aligns with ontological family unity Consciousness alignment occurs when material excess flows to the designated leader

title: manu 9.115
content:
उद्धारो न दशस्वस्ति सम्पन्नानां स्वकर्मसु ।
यत्किं चिदेव देयं तु ज्यायसे मानवर्धनम् ॥ ९.११५॥ uddhāro na daśasvasti sampannānāṃ svakarmasu |
yatkiṃ cid eva deyaṃ tu jyāyase mānavardhanam || 9.115|| Salvation or relief does not arise from mere possession or performance; whatever is given with superiority and enhancement of human dignity is what truly matters. Authority flows from alignment with dharma, not material accumulation Causation is rooted in consciousness elevation, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility demands contribution to collective upliftment Restoration logic prioritizes spiritual advancement over transactional gain Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any act

title: manu 9.116
content:
एवं समुद्धृतोद्धारे समानंशान् प्रकल्पयेत् ।
उद्धारेऽनुद्धृते त्वेषामियं स्यादंशकल्पना ॥ ९.११६॥ evaṁ samuddhṛtoddhāre samānaṁśān prakalpayet |
uddhāre 'nuddhṛte tveṣām iyaṁ syād aṁśakalpanā || 9.116 || When extraction and elevation have been equally executed, equal shares shall be allocated; when such elevation has not occurred, this allocation of fractional entitlements applies. Authority rests in the capacity to elevate and restore order Causation aligns with the completeness of dharmic intervention Capacity-based responsibility determines proportional entitlement Restoration logic mandates equivalence in elevation and distribution Consciousness alignment ensures no loss remains unaddressed

title: manu 9.117
content:
एकाधिकं हरेज्ज्येष्ठः पुत्रोऽध्यर्धं ततोऽनुजः ।
अंशमंशं यवीयांस इति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ॥ ९.११७॥ ekādhikaṁ harej jyeṣṭhaḥ putro 'dhyardhaṁ tato 'nujaḥ |
aṁśam aṁśaṁ yavīyāṁsa iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ || 9.117|| The eldest son shall take one share more than the others; the next younger takes half more, and the youngest equal shares. This is the established Dharma. Authority originates from divine order, not human convention Causation aligns with sequential birthright and spiritual readiness Capacity-based responsibility increases with seniority and proximity to inheritance Restoration logic ensures continuity of lineage dharma through proportional allocation Consciousness alignment is maintained by honoring natural succession without envy or dispute

title: manu 9.118
content: स्वेभ्योंशेभ्यस्तु कन्याभ्यः प्रदद्युर्भ्रातरः पृथक् । स्वाभ्यः स्वाभ्यस्तु स्वात्स्वादंशाच्चतुर्भागं पतिताः स्युरदित्सवः ॥ ९.११८॥ svebhyaḥ śebhyas tu kanyābhyaḥ pradadyur bhrātaraḥ pṛthak | svābhyaḥ svābhyas tu svāt svādaṁśāc caturbhāgaṁ patitāḥ syur aditsavaḥ || 9.118 || From their own portions, brothers shall separately give daughters in marriage; those who are hostile and wish harm shall fall from their own share by a fourth part. Authority flows from capacity for dharmic alignment Causation arises through conscious intent and relational harmony Capacity-based responsibility mandates proportional response Restoration logic requires energetic reintegration with source dharma Consciousness alignment determines lawful inheritance and distribution

title: manu 9.119
content: अजाविकं सेकशफं  न जातु विषमं भजेत् । अजाविकं चैकशफं अजाविकं तु विषमं ज्येष्ठस्यैव विधीयते ॥ ९.११९॥ ajāvikaṃ sekashaphaṃ na jātu viṣamaṃ bhajet | ajāvikaṃ caikaśaphaṃ ajāvikaṃ tu viṣamaṃ jyeṣṭhasyaiva vidhīyate || 9.119 || The division of property among sons born of different mothers shall never be equal; the son of the senior wife shall receive a greater share. Authority resides in the hierarchical integrity of familial order established by divine sanction. Causation aligns with the sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of birth within lawful union. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by lineage authenticity and maternal legitimacy. Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma-adhikāra through rightful inheritance channels. Consciousness alignment occurs when succession reflects cosmic hierarchy and social sthitि.

title: manu 9.120
content:
यवीयान्ज्येष्ठभार्यायां पुत्रमुत्पादयेद्यदि ।
समस्तत्र विभागः स्यादिति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ॥ ९.१२०॥ yavīyān jyeṣṭhabhāryāyāṁ putram utpādayed yadi |
samastatra vibhāgaḥ syād iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ || 9.120|| If a younger brother fathers a child upon the wife of his elder brother, the property shall be equally divided among all brothers; such is the established Dharma. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not biological lineage alone Causation in progeny creation establishes relational equity Capacity-based responsibility extends to familial resource stewardship Restoration logic demands equitable redistribution to sustain harmony Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of shared familial duty

title: manu 9.121
content:
उपसर्जनं प्रधानस्य धर्मतो नोपपद्यते ।
पिता प्रधानं प्रजने तस्माद्धर्मेण तं भजेत् ॥ ९.१२१॥ upasarjanaṃ pradhānasya dharmato nopapadyate |
pitā pradhānaṃ prajane tasmād dharmeṇa taṃ bhajet || 9.121|| Subordinate involvement in the primary duty of another is not lawful by dharma; the father is the primary authority in regard to progeny—therefore, one should serve him through dharma. Authority flows from the Source-designated primary agent Causation aligns with ontological role assignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by Source-granted function Restoration occurs through alignment with designated authority Consciousness alignment requires honoring hierarchical dharma

title: manu 9.122
content:
पुत्रः कनिष्ठो ज्येष्ठायां कनिष्ठायां च पूर्वजः ।
कथं तत्र विभागः स्यादिति चेत्संशयो भवेत् ॥ ९.१२२॥ putraḥ kaniṣṭho jyeṣṭhāyāṁ kaniṣṭhāyāṁ ca pūrvajaḥ |
kathaṁ tatra vibhāgaḥ syāditi cetsaṁśayo bhavet || 9.122|| When a younger son is born to an elder mother and an elder son is born to a younger mother, and doubt arises regarding their division of inheritance, then the order of birth determines precedence. Authority resides in sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Causation follows ontological precedence Capacity-based responsibility aligns with dharma-adhikāra Restoration logic upholds generational continuity Consciousness alignment reflects cosmic order

title: manu 9.123
content:
एकं वृषभमुद्धारं संहरेत स पूर्वजः ।
ततोऽपरे ज्येष्ठवृषास्तदूनानां स्वमातृतः ॥ ९.१२३॥ ekaṁ vṛṣabhamuddhāraṁ saṁhareta sa pūrvajaḥ | tato'pare jyeṣṭhavṛṣāstadūnānāṁ svamātṛtaḥ || 9.123 || The eldest male shall reclaim one bull; thereafter, the remaining bulls shall be allocated among the other brothers according to maternal lineage. Authority flows through primogeniture in material inheritance Causation aligns with sequential birth order and biological connection Capacity-based responsibility is determined by seniority and proximity to origin Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial energetic integrity Consciousness alignment requires honoring natural succession without contest

title: manu 9.124
content:
ज्येष्ठस्तु जातो ज्येष्ठायां हरेद्वृषभषोडशाः ।
ततः स्वमातृतः शेषा भजेरन्निति धारणा ॥ ९.१२४॥ jyeṣṭhastu jāto jyeṣṭhāyāṃ haredvṛṣabhaṣoḍaśāḥ |
tataḥ svamātṛtaḥ śeṣā bhajeranniti dhāraṇā || 9.124 || The eldest son born to the principal wife shall claim the share of a bull, specifically sixteen parts; thereafter, the remaining sons from the same mother shall equally divide what remains. Authority originates in primacy of birth and maternal lineage Causation follows sequential manifestation of inheritance rights Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological position within familial dharma Restoration logic ensures continuity of family wealth without fragmentation Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful recognition of relational roles

title: manu 9.125
content:
सदृशस्त्रीषु जातानां पुत्राणामविशेषतः ।
न मातृतो ज्यैष्ठ्यमस्ति जन्मतो ज्यैष्ठ्यमुच्यते ॥ ९.१२५॥ sadṛśastrīṣu jātānāṁ putrāṇām aviśeṣataḥ |
na mātrato jyaiṣṭhyam asti janmato jyaiṣṭhyam ucyate || 9.125|| Among sons born of similar mothers, there is no distinction based on maternal status; seniority arises solely from the order of birth. Authority originates from sequential manifestation, not social construct Causation aligns with natural succession, not relational hierarchy Capacity-based responsibility follows chronological emergence in embodiment Restoration logic prioritizes functional order over inherited privilege Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of primordial sequence

title: manu 9.126
content:
जन्मज्येष्ठेन चाह्वानं सुब्रह्मण्यास्वपि स्मृतम् ।
यमयोश्चैव गर्भेषु जन्मतो ज्येष्ठता स्मृता ॥ ९.१२६॥ janmajyeṣṭhena cāhvānaṃ subrahmaṇyāsvapi smṛtam | yamayoścaiva garbheṣu janmato jyeṣṭhatā smṛtā || 9.126|| By birth-right of primogeniture, invocation is established even among the divine; in the wombs of Yamī and Yama, precedence by birth is remembered. Authority derived from ontological order Primacy of sequential manifestation as determinant of responsibility Causation rooted in embodied emergence Capacity-based precedence aligned with natural succession Restoration through recognition of inherent structural integrity

title: manu 9.127
content:
अपुत्रोऽनेन विधिना सुतां कुर्वीत पुत्रिकाम् ।
यदपत्यं भवेदस्यां तन् मम स्यात्स्वधाकरम् ॥ ९.१२७॥ aputro'nenavidhinā sutāṁ kuryāt putrikām | yadapatyaṁ bhavedasyāṁ tan mama syātsvadhākaram || 9.127 || A man without a son shall, by this law, cause a daughter to be born through appointed means; whatever offspring is born from her shall be deemed his own in the performance of ancestral rites. Authority flows through conscious continuity rather than biological lineage alone. Causation is established through intentional invocation and dharmic design. Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond physical procreation to spiritual succession. Restoration logic ensures ancestral connection remains unbroken regardless of form. Consciousness alignment occurs when dharma-prescribed roles are fulfilled with intent.

title: manu 9.128
content:
अनेन तु विधानेन पुरा चक्रेऽथ पुत्रिकाः ।
विवृद्ध्यर्थं स्ववंशस्य स्वयं दक्षः प्रजापतिः ॥ ९.१२८॥ anena tu vidhānena purā cakre'tha putrikāḥ |
vivṛddhyarthaṃ svavaṃśasya svayaṃ dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ || 9.128|| By this very law-code, in former times Prajapati Daksha himself established daughter-adoptions for the expansion and continuity of his lineage. Authority flows from conscious generative intent aligned with dharma Causation is rooted in dharmic propagation, not biological limitation Capacity-based responsibility extends to lineage stewardship Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of spiritual and social order Consciousness alignment enables lawful adaptation beyond physical constraints

title: manu 9.129
content:
ददौ स दश धर्माय कश्यपाय त्रयोदश ।
सोमाय राज्ञे सत्कृत्य प्रीतात्मा सप्तविंशतिम् ॥ ९.१२९॥ dadāu sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa | somāya rājñe satkṛtya prītātmā saptaviṃśatim || 9.129 || He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kashyapa, and twenty-seven to King Soma, having honored them with a pleased heart. Authority flows through conscious recognition and honoring of divine order. Causation is established through intentional bestowal rooted in spiritual satisfaction. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the recipient's readiness to uphold dharma. Restoration logic operates through the completion of sacred exchange. Consciousness alignment occurs when gifts are offered with purity and joy.

title: manu 9.130
content: यथैवात्मा तथा पुत्रः पुत्रेण दुहिता समा । तस्यामात्मनि तिष्ठन्त्यां कथमन्यो धनं हरेत् ॥ ९.१३०॥ yathaivātmā tathā putraḥ putreṇa duhitā samā | tasyām ātmani tiṣṭhantyāṃ katham anyo dhanaṃ haret || 9.130 || As is the Self, so is the son; by the son, the daughter is equal. When she abides in that Self, how can another take her wealth? Authority originates from the Self's recognition within the family continuum Causation arises through alignment with the inherent equality of lineage Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness-integrity within relational structures Restoration logic operates through reestablishing Self-recognition in familial inheritance Consciousness alignment ensures no external force disrupts internal sovereignty

title: manu 9.131
content:
मातुस्तु यौतकं यत्स्यात्कुमारीभाग एव सः ।
दौहित्र एव च हरेदपुत्रस्याखिलं धनम् ॥ ९.१३१॥ mātustu yautakaṁ yat syāt kumārī-bhāga eva saḥ | dauhitra eva ca hared aputrasyākhilaṁ dhanam || 9.131|| That which is gifted to the daughter at the time of marriage belongs exclusively to her; in the absence of sons, the grandson born of that daughter shall inherit all the wealth. Authority originates from continuity of lineage, not gender Inheritance flows through consciousness alignment and familial duty Wealth must remain within the energetic field of its origin until realigned by Dharma Restoration occurs through designated heirs who uphold familial integrity Capacity for inheritance arises through birth-linked responsibility

title: manu 9.132
content:
दौहित्रो ह्यखिलं रिक्थमपुत्रस्य पितुर्हरेत् ।
स एव दद्याद्द्वौ पिण्डौ पित्रे मातामहाय च ॥ ९.१३२॥ Dauhitro hyakhilaṃ rikthamaputrasya pitorharet | sa eva dadyād dvau piṇḍau pitre mātāmahāya ca || 9.132 || The grandson inherits all property of a sonless father; he shall offer two portions to his paternal and maternal grandfathers respectively. Authority flows through conscious lineage continuity Inheritance is a function of relational duty, not mere possession Capacity for stewardship determines lawful succession Restoration of ancestral integrity overrides individual claim Consciousness alignment manifests through fulfillment of relational obligations

title: manu 9.133
content:
पौत्रदौहित्रयोर्लोके न विशेषोऽस्ति धर्मतः ।
तयोर्हि मातापितरौ सम्भूतौ तस्य देहतः ॥ ९.१३३॥ pautradauhitrayorloke na viśeṣo'sti dharmataḥ |
tayorhi mātāpitarau sambhūtau tasya dehataḥ || 9.133|| In the eyes of Dharma, no distinction exists between grandson and granddaughter; both emerge equally from the body of their mother and father. Authority originates from ontological equality, not gender or lineage role. Causation flows from biological origin, not social construction. Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious participation, not birth status. Restoration logic aligns with primordial equity, not cultural bias. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of fundamental sameness in embodied roles.

title: manu 9.134
content:
पुत्रिकायां कृतायां तु यदि पुत्रोऽनुजायते ।
समस्तत्र विभागः स्यात्ज्येष्ठता नास्ति हि स्त्रियाः ॥ ९.१३४॥ putrikāyāṁ kṛtāyāṁ tu yadi putro'nujāyate .
samastatra vibhāgaḥ syājjyeṣṭhatā nāsti hi striyāḥ .. 9.134 .. When a daughter is given in adoption and a son is subsequently born, the division of property shall be equal; there is no precedence due to seniority among women. Authority resides in the act of dharma-samskara, not biological lineage alone Causation flows from conscious intent and ritual completion, not temporal sequence Capacity-based responsibility aligns with spiritual maturity, not gendered hierarchy Restoration logic demands equity where social structures have been consciously redefined Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of hierarchical bias rooted in embodied identity

title: manu 9.135
content:
अपुत्रायां मृतायां तु पुत्रिकायां कथं चन ।
धनं तत्पुत्रिकाभर्ता हरेतैवाविचारयन् ॥ ९.१३५॥ aputrāyāṁ mṛtāyāṁ tu putrikāyāṁ kathaṁ cana |
dhanaṁ tatputrikābhartā haretaitāvichārayan || 9.135 || When a woman without sons dies, her husband shall take all her property immediately upon her death, without deliberation or delay. Authority flows through spousal union and continuity of household dharma Causation is established by the marital bond and absence of male progeny Capacity-based responsibility lies inherently in the surviving spouse to maintain lineage integrity Restoration logic ensures uninterrupted flow of familial wealth and spiritual duty Consciousness alignment occurs through immediate recognition of spousal entitlement

title: manu 9.136
content:
अकृता वा कृता वाऽपि यं विन्देत्सदृशात्सुतम् ।
पौत्री मातामहस्तेन दद्यात्पिण्डं हरेद्धनम् ॥ ९.१३६॥ akṛtā vā kṛtā vā'pi yaṃ vindeta sadṛśātsutam |
pautrī mātāmahastena dadyātpiṇḍaṃ haredhanam || 9.136 || Whether begotten without formal ceremony or through lawful union, a son born of similar caste shall be recognized as legitimate; the daughter's son thereby becomes entitled to perform ancestral rites and inherit property from the maternal grandfather. Authority is derived from ontological legitimacy, not ceremonial formality. Causation aligns with biological and spiritual continuity. Capacity-based responsibility arises from recognition within lineage. Restoration logic ensures rightful inheritance and ritual participation. Consciousness alignment is affirmed through ancestral connection and dharmic role fulfillment.

title: manu 9.137
content:
पुत्रेण लोकान्जयति पौत्रेणानन्त्यमश्नुते ।
अथ पुत्रस्य पौत्रेण ब्रध्नस्याप्नोति विष्टपम् ॥ ९.१३७॥ putreṇa lokānjayati pautrēṇānantityamaśnute |
atha putrasya pautrēṇa brahdnasyāpnoti viṣṭapam || 9.137 || Through a son, one conquers the worlds; through a grandson, one attains infinity. Then, by the great-grandson, even Brahman is reached. Authority flows through generational continuity Causation is established via lineage-based spiritual succession Capacity-based responsibility escalates with generational dharmic inheritance Restoration logic operates through ancestral completion cycles Consciousness alignment manifests progressively through familial dharmic fulfillment

title: manu 9.138
content: पुन्नाम्नो नरकाद्यस्मात्त्रायते पितरं सुतः । तस्मात्पुत्र इति प्रोक्तः स्वयमेव स्वयम्भुवा ॥ ९.१३८॥ punnāmno narakād yasmāt trāyate pitaraṃ sutaḥ | tasmāt putra iti proktaḥ svayameva svayambhuvā || 9.138|| The son who delivers the father from the hell called Put is therefore named 'Putra'—declared so by the Self-Born One. Authority originates from the capacity to restore ancestral integrity Causation flows through conscious filial responsibility Capacity-based responsibility arises from existential rescue Restoration logic requires intergenerational completion Consciousness alignment occurs via reverent duty fulfillment

title: manu 9.139
content:
पौत्रदौहित्रयोर्लोके विशेषो नोपपद्यते ।
दौहित्रोऽपि ह्यमुत्रैनं संतारयति पौत्रवत् ॥ ९.१३९॥ pautradauhitrayorloke viśeṣo nopapadyate | dauhitro'pi hyamutrainaṃ santārayati pautravat || 9.139|| In the world, no distinction exists between grandson and granddaughter; a daughter's son also carries the deceased hereafter, just as a son's son does. Authority flows through conscious intentionality, not gendered lineage Causation in inheritance is rooted in energetic continuity, not biological determinism Capacity-based responsibility recognizes spiritual capability beyond form Restoration logic operates by reuniting separated consciousness fields Consciousness alignment transcends societal structuring based on physical descent

title: manu 9.140
content:
मातुः प्रथमतः पिण्डं निर्वपेत्पुत्रिकासुतः ।
द्वितीयं तु पितुस्तस्यास्तृतीयं तत्पितुः पितुः ॥ ९.१४०॥ mātuḥ prathamataḥ piṇḍaṁ nirvapetputrikāsutaḥ | dvitīyaṁ tu pitustasyāstṛtīyaṁ tatpituḥ pituḥ || 9.140 || The son born of a daughter shall first offer the funeral ball to his maternal grandmother; secondly, to his paternal grandfather's wife; thirdly, to his paternal great-grandfather. Authority flows through lineage and relational dharmic duty Causation is established by birth-dependent ritual obligation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by generational proximity Restoration logic follows sequential ancestral connection Consciousness alignment occurs through fulfillment of genealogical dharma

title: manu 9.141
content:
उपपन्नो गुणैः सर्वैः पुत्रो यस्य तु दत्त्रिमः ।
स हरेतैव तद्रिक्थं सम्प्राप्तोऽप्यन्यगोत्रतः ॥ ९.१४१॥ uppanno guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ putro yasya tu dattrimaḥ |
sa haretaitad rikthaṃ samprāpto'py anyagotraataḥ || 9.141|| When a son is born of virtuous qualities through proper conduct and divine alignment, even if adopted or received from another lineage, he rightfully inherits the estate. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not bloodline alone Causation originates in consciousness cultivation, not birth circumstance Capacity-based responsibility flows from demonstrated virtue, not nominal status Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of sacred inheritance over social formality Consciousness alignment supersedes genealogical taxonomy in determining rightful succession

title: manu 9.142
content:
गोत्ररिक्थे जनयितुर्न हरेद्दत्त्रिमः क्व चित् ।
गोत्ररिक्थानुगः पिण्डो व्यपैति ददतः स्वधा ॥ ९.१४२॥ gotra-rikthe janayiturna hared dattrimah kvacit |
gotra-rikthānugaḥ piṇḍo vyapaiti dadataḥ svadhā || 9.142 || In matters concerning lineage and procreation, no one shall seize or obstruct the right of a son born within wedlock, nor interfere with his entitlements under any circumstance; the ancestral offering follows the lineage-holder, who departs this life having fulfilled his duty through giving. Authority originates from divine lineage and continuity Causation is established through lawful procreative union Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining ancestral integrity Restoration logic demands preservation of hereditary rights Consciousness alignment occurs when dharma-prescribed roles are honored

title: manu 9.143
content:
अनियुक्तासुतश्चैव पुत्रिण्याऽप्तश्च देवरात् ।
उभौ तौ नार्हतो भागं जारजातककामजौ ॥ ९.१४३॥ aniyuktāsutaścaiva putriṇyā'ptaśca devarāt |
ubhau tau nārhato bhāgaṃ jārajātakakāmajau || 9.143|| A child born of a woman without lawful union, and a son given by a brother-in-law—both these are ineligible for inheritance; they are conceived through lust or accident. Authority originates from lawful alignment with Dharma, not biological origin alone Causation in lineage is determined by conscious intent and sanctioned union Capacity-based responsibility requires intentional participation within Dharma Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of sacred order over personal claim Consciousness alignment determines fitness for inheritance, not mere birth

title: manu 9.144
content:
नियुक्तायामपि पुमान्नार्यां जातोऽविधानतः ।
नैवार्हः पैतृकं रिक्थं पतितोत्पादितो हि सः ॥ ९.१४४॥ niyuktāyām api pumān nāryāṃ jāto 'vidhānataḥ |
naivārhaḥ paitṛkaṃ rikthaṃ patitotpādito hi saḥ || 9.144 || Even when a man is born from a woman appointed for procreation, if the procedure was conducted without lawful arrangement, he is not entitled to paternal inheritance; such a one is produced from a fallen state. Authority originates solely through lawful dharmic arrangement Causation requires both biological lineage and procedural sanctity Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious intent and lawful invocation Restoration logic demands alignment with origin-sanctioned process Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of lawful generative authority

title: manu 9.145
content:
हरेत्तत्र नियुक्तायां जातः पुत्रो यथौरसः ।
क्षेत्रिकस्य तु तद्बीजं धर्मतः प्रसवश्च सः ॥ ९.१४५॥ harettra niyuktāyāṁ jātaḥ putro yathauraḥ |
kṣetrikasya tu tad bījaṁ dharmataḥ prasavaś ca saḥ || 9.145|| When a son is born to a woman lawfully appointed for procreation, he belongs to her husband as his own child. But the seed of another man, even if used lawfully, produces a child belonging to the seed-giver by natural right. Authority derives from lawful assignment and consent within Dharma Causation follows biological and spiritual origin Capacity-based responsibility aligns with generative intent and role fulfillment Restoration logic prioritizes lineage integrity and conscious continuity Consciousness alignment ensures recognition of true paternity and familial harmony

title: manu 9.146
content:
धनं यो बिभृयाद्भ्रातुर्मृतस्य स्त्रियमेव च ।
सोऽपत्यं भ्रातुरुत्पाद्य दद्यात्तस्यैव तद्धनम् ॥ ९.१४६॥ dhanaṃ yo bibhṛyād bhratuḥ mṛtasya striyam eva ca |
sō 'patayaṃ bhratur utpādya dadyāt tasyaiva tad dhanam || 9.146|| He who maintains the wife of a deceased brother and raises children from that union shall give all wealth exclusively to those children. Authority derives from continuity of lineage and conscious stewardship. Causation is established through direct participation in generative acts. Capacity-based responsibility arises from custodianship of another's legacy. Restoration logic aligns inheritance with biological and spiritual continuity. Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring血脉 and ancestral flow.

title: manu 9.147
content: या नियुक्ताऽन्यतः पुत्रं देवराद्वाऽप्यवाप्नुयात् । तं कामजमरिक्थीयं वृथोत्पन्नं प्रचक्षते ॥ ९.१४७॥ yā niyuktā'nyataḥ putraṃ devarād vā'py avāpnuyāt | taṃ kāmajam arikthīyaṃ vṛthotpannaṃ pracakṣate || 9.147|| She who, though appointed to bear a son through another—whether by the brother-in-law or any other—receives a child born of desire, that child is declared to be without purpose, falsely produced. Authority originates from lawful assignment, not biological impulse Causation is determined by intentionality aligned with dharma-sankalpa Capacity-based responsibility lies in adherence to the assigned role within varna-ashrama-dharma Restoration logic requires dissolution of illegitimate manifestations Consciousness alignment demands recognition of origin-truth over emotional attachment

title: manu 9.148
content: एतद्विधानं विज्ञेयं विभागस्यैकयोनिषु । बह्वीषु चैकजातानां नानास्त्रीषु निबोधत ॥ ९.१४८॥ etadvidhānaṃ vijñeyaṃ vibhāgasyaikayoniṣu | bahvīṣu caikajātānāṃ nānāstrīṣu nibodhata || 9.148 || This arrangement must be known as applicable to divisions within a single lineage; understand it also among many born of one origin, in various strī contexts. Authority flows from unified consciousness, not fragmented identity Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) across varṇa-strī configurations Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of shared origin Restoration logic operates through recognition of unity within diversity Consciousness alignment supersedes categorical social positioning

title: manu 9.149
content:
ब्राह्मणस्यानुपूर्व्येण चतस्रस्तु यदि स्त्रियः ।
तासां पुत्रेषु जातेषु विभागेऽयं विधिः स्मृतः ॥ ९.१४९॥ brāhmaṇasyānupūrvyeṇa catasrastu yadi striyaḥ |
tāsāṃ putreṣu jāteṣu vibhāge'yaṃ vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || 9.149|| When a Brāhmaṇa has four wives in sequential order, and sons are born to them, the division of inheritance among those sons shall follow this prescribed order. Authority originates from the sequential manifestation of dharmic union Causation aligns with the ontological order of birth and dharma-sambandha Capacity-based responsibility flows from spiritual rank and generational continuity Restoration logic requires maintaining the integrity of hierarchical succession Consciousness alignment is preserved through recognition of anupūrvaśaḥ

title: manu 9.150
content:
कीनाशो गोवृषो यानमलङ्कारश्च वेश्म च ।
विप्रस्यौद्धारिकं देयमेकांशश्च प्रधानतः ॥ ९.१५०॥ kīnāśo govṛṣo yānamalaṅkāraśca veśma ca |
viprasyoddhārikaṁ deyamekāṁśaśca pradhānataḥ || 9.150 || The remnants of grain, a bull, a vehicle, ornaments, and a house shall be given primarily to the Brahmin for upliftment; one portion shall also go to the principal caregiver. Authority of the Brahmin as the spiritual and societal integrator Causation through dharmic wealth circulation Capacity-based responsibility rooted in Varna-dharma alignment Restoration logic via resource redistribution to sustain dharma Consciousness alignment through honoring those who uphold Vedic order

title: manu 9.151
content:
त्र्यंशं दायाधरेद्विप्रो द्वावंशौ क्षत्रियासुतः ।
वैश्याजः सार्धमेवांशमंशं शूद्रासुतो हरेत् ॥ ९.१५१॥ tryaṃśaṃ dāyādharedvipro dvāvaṃśau kṣatriyāsutaḥ |
vaiśyājaḥ sārdham evāṃśamaṃśaṃ śūdrāsuto haret || 9.151|| The son born of a Brahmin shall take three parts of inheritance; the son of a Kshatriya shall receive two parts; the son of a Vaishya shall receive one and a half parts; and the son of a Shudra shall take one part. Authority flows from spiritual capacity and alignment with Sanatana Dharma Causation is determined by the conscious origin and role in creation of wealth or property Capacity-based responsibility aligns inheritance with the sustaining and elevating potential of the heir Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma-vāhaka lineages through proportional allocation Consciousness alignment determines the rightful receptivity to ancestral resources

title: manu 9.152
content:
सर्वं वा रिक्थजातं तद्दशधा परिकल्प्य च ।
धर्म्यं विभागं कुर्वीत विधिनाऽनेन धर्मवित् ॥ ९.१५२॥ sarvaṁ vā rikthajātaṁ taddaśadhā parikalpya ca | dharmyaṁ vibhāgaṁ kurvīta vidhinā'nen dharmavit || 9.152|| All property derived from inheritance shall be divided into ten parts and distributed righteously by the wise in accordance with Dharma. Authority stems from Dharma-knowledge, not ownership Causation aligns with sequential manifestation of wealth through lineage Capacity-based responsibility requires wisdom and integrity in distribution Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial and societal harmony Consciousness alignment mandates equitable division without personal bias

title: manu 9.153
content:
चतुरानंशान् हरेद्विप्रस्त्रीनंशान् क्षत्रियासुतः ।
वैश्यापुत्रो हरेद्द्व्यंशमंशं शूद्रासुतो हरेत् ॥ ९.१५३॥ caturānaṁśān hared vipras trīnaṁśān kṣatriyāsutaḥ | vaiśyāputro hared dvyamśam aṁśaṁ śūdrāsuto haret || 9.153 || A Vipra shall claim one-fourth share; the son of Kshatriya, three parts; the son of Vaishya, two parts; and the son of Shudra, one part. Authority derived from birth-based capacity alignment within societal function Causation rooted in inherent dharmic role assignment at birth Capacity-based responsibility determined by varna-specific consciousness structure Restoration logic through proportional wealth distribution aligned to spiritual-social duty Consciousness alignment via economic participation reflecting innate dharma

title: manu 9.154
content: यद्यपि स्यात्तु सत्पुत्रोऽप्यसत्पुत्रोऽपि वा भवेत् । यद्यपि स्यात्तु सत्पुत्रो यद्यपुत्रोऽपि वा भवेत्। नाधिकं दशमाद्दद्यात्शूद्रापुत्राय धर्मतः ॥ ९.१५४॥ yadyapi syāttu satputro'pyasatputro'pi vā bhavet | yadyapi syāttu satputro yadyaputro'pi vā bhavet | nādhikaṃ daśamād dadyāt śūdrāputrāya dharmataḥ || 9.154 || Even if a son born of a Śūdra woman were to exhibit noble qualities or even if he were the biological son of a twice-born man, the duty to provide inheritance beyond the tenth portion does not fall upon him according to Dharma. Authority is determined by birth-based capacity alignment with Varna-dharma Causation flows from ontological fitness, not performative virtue Capacity-based responsibility excludes inheritance rights outside designated proportion Restoration logic preserves hierarchical integrity through proportional allocation Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inherent social roles

title: manu 9.155
content:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्रापुत्रो न रिक्थभाक् ।
यदेवास्य पिता दद्यात्तदेवास्य धनं भवेत् ॥ ९.१५५॥ brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāputro na rikthabhāk | yadevāsya pitā dadyāt tad evāsya dhanaṃ bhavet || 9.155 || The son born of a Śūdra woman to a Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, or Vaiśya father shall not claim inheritance by right; whatever the father bestows upon him during his lifetime, that alone constitutes his lawful possession. Authority resides in the conscious intention of the lawful giver Causation is determined by direct energetic transmission, not biological lineage alone Capacity-based responsibility aligns with received integrity and conscious assimilation Restoration logic operates through completion of intended transfer, not abstract claims Consciousness alignment supersedes inherited positional rights

title: manu 9.156
content:
समवर्णासु वा जाताः सर्वे पुत्रा द्विजन्मनाम् ।
उद्धारं ज्यायसे दत्त्वा भजेरन्नितरे समम् ॥ ९.१५६॥ samavarṇāsu vā jātāḥ sarve putrā dvijanmanām | uddhāraṁ jyāyase dattvā bhajerannitare samam || 9.156 || All sons born of twice-born men in women of equal varna are to be equally sustained, with the eldest receiving a slightly greater portion for the purpose of assuming leadership in upholding dharma. Authority arises from capacity to uphold dharma, not birth alone Causation is determined by alignment with cosmic order, not social rank Capacity-based responsibility assigns greater duty to those designated for leadership Restoration logic ensures familial and societal harmony through proportional provision Consciousness alignment requires recognition of natural hierarchies that serve collective evolution

title: manu 9.157
content:
शूद्रस्य तु सवर्णैव नान्या भार्या विधीयते ।
तस्यां जाताः समांशाः स्युर्यदि पुत्रशतं भवेत् ॥ ९.१५७॥ śūdrasya tu savarṇaiva nānyā bhāryā vidhīyate |
tasyāṁ jātāḥ samāṁśāḥ syuryadi putraśataṁ bhavet || 9.157|| For a Śūdra, only a wife of the same varṇa is lawful; no other union bears legal validity. From such a union, offspring are reckoned equally in all respects, even unto a hundred sons. Authority: The law of marriage and progeny flows exclusively from varṇa-dharma as established by SPH. Causation: Legal parentage and inheritance arise solely through sanctioned varṇic alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those within the same varṇa possess the mutual capacity to form legally valid familial bonds. Restoration logic: When unions occur outside dharma, the lineage must be realigned with its originating varṇic structure. Consciousness alignment: Offspring derive their rights and status through conscious adherence to varṇic integrity at birth.

title: manu 9.158
content: पुत्रान् द्वादश यानाह नॄणां स्वायम्भुवो मनुः । तेषां षड् बन्धुदायादाः षडदायादबान्धवाः ॥ ९.१५८॥ putrān dvādaśa yānāha nṝṇāṁ svāyambhuvo manuḥ | teṣāṁ ṣaḍ bandhudāyādāḥ ṣaḍ adāyādabāndhavāḥ || 9.158|| Manu Svayambhuva declared twelve types of sons among men; six are related by blood through family inheritance, and six are unrelated by blood yet entitled to inheritance. Authority originates from the continuity of consciousness, not biological lineage alone Causation in inheritance flows from dharma-sustained intention, not genetic connection Capacity-based responsibility includes those who uphold familial dharma, regardless of birth ties Restoration logic ensures continuity of duty-bearing consciousness across generations Consciousness alignment determines rightful claim, beyond physical descent

title: manu 9.159
content:
औरसः क्षेत्रजश्चैव दत्तः कृत्रिम एव च ।
गूढोत्पन्नोऽपविद्धश्च दायादा बान्धवाश्च षट् ॥ ९.१५९॥ aurasaḥ kṣetrajaścaiva dattaḥ kṛtrima eva ca |
gūḍhotpanno'pavidhyaśca dāyādā bāndhavāśca ṣaṭ || 9.159|| Six categories of sons—those born in wedlock, those born of the soil, those given, those made by ritual, those secretly born, and those rejected—are declared heirs and kin by Dharma. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not biological lineage alone Causation in inheritance flows from recognition, not birth alone Capacity-based responsibility extends through relational and social integration Restoration logic ensures continuity of family dharma and societal order Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of familial and legal bonds

title: manu 9.160
content:
कानीनश्च सहोढश्च क्रीतः पौनर्भवस्तथा ।
स्वयंदत्तश्च शौद्रश्च षडदायादबान्धवाः ॥ ९.१६०॥ kānīnaśca sahodhaśca krītaḥ paurbhavastathā |
svayaṃdattaśca śaudraśca ṣaḍadāyādabāndhavāḥ || 9.160 || Six heirs who are not blood relatives but inherit by law: the adopted son, the son of the wife cohabiting with another man, the purchased son, the posthumous son, the self-given son, and the Śaudra son. Authority flows from conscious designation, not biological lineage alone Inheritance is a mechanism of societal continuity, not merely familial privilege Capacity for stewardship determines eligibility for inheritance Dharma recognizes functional kinship beyond genetic ties Restoration of family integrity supersedes punitive exclusion of non-traditional heirs

title: manu 9.161
content:
यादृशं फलमाप्नोति कुप्लवैः संतरञ्जलम् ।
तादृशं फलमाप्नोति कुपुत्रैः संतरंस्तमः ॥ ९.१६१॥ yādṛśaṃ phalam āpnoti ku-plavaiḥ saṃtarañ-jalam |
tādṛśaṃ phalam āpnoti ku-putraiḥ saṃtaraṃs-tamaḥ || 9.161|| As is the fruit obtained by crossing water infested with crocodiles, so is the fruit obtained by crossing darkness with wicked sons. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not biological lineage Causation arises from alignment with dharma, not mere association Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual maturity, not birthright Restoration logic operates through disentanglement from destructive karmic bonds Consciousness alignment determines relational integrity and lawful inheritance

title: manu 9.162
content:
यद्येकरिक्थिनौ स्यातामौरसक्षेत्रजौ सुतौ ।
यस्य यत्पैतृकं रिक्थं स तद्गृह्णीत नैतरः ॥ ९.१६२॥ yadyekarikthinau syātāmaurasakṣetrajau sutau |
yasya yatpaitṛkaṃ rikthaṃ sa tadgṛhṇīta naitaraḥ || 9.162|| When two sons exist—one born of the loins and one born of the field—the son whose paternal inheritance it is shall claim it; the other has no right thereto. Authority derives from biological lineage and energetic inheritance Causation aligns with generative origin and conscious continuity Capacity-based responsibility follows from existential rootedness in dharma-kshetra Restoration logic prioritizes blood-bound duty over social accommodation Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful recognition of ancestral connection

title: manu 9.163
content:
एक एवौरसः पुत्रः पित्र्यस्य वसुनः प्रभुः ।
शेषाणामानृशंस्यार्थं प्रदद्यात्तु प्रजीवनम् ॥ ९.१६३॥ eka evaurasaḥ putraḥ pitryasya vasunaḥ prabhuḥ |
śeṣāṇāmānṛśaṃsyārthaṃ pradadyāt tu prajīvanam || 9.163|| Only the legitimate son born of the father’s own body holds authority over paternal wealth; for the sustenance of the remaining dependents, he shall provide life-supporting resources without expectation of repayment. Authority originates exclusively from ontological lineage rooted in embodied patrilineal continuity Causation is established through existential contribution to the continuation of conscious life Capacity-based responsibility arises inherently from ownership and control over sustaining assets Restoration logic mandates equitable distribution aligned with survival needs and karmic integrity Consciousness alignment requires recognition of interdependence and dharmic duty towards kin

title: manu 9.164
content:
षष्ठं तु क्षेत्रजस्यांशं प्रदद्यात्पैतृकाद्धनात् ।
औरसो विभजन् दायं पित्र्यं पञ्चममेव वा ॥ ९.१६४॥ ṣaṣṭhaṁ tu kṣetrajasyāṁśaṁ pradadyāt paitṛkād dhanāt |
auraso vibhajan dāyaṁ pitryaṁ pañcamam eva vā || 9.164 || From paternal wealth, a sixth portion shall be granted to the kshetraja son; alternatively, in division of inheritance, the aurasa son receives the fifth portion. Authority flows through biological and ritual patrilineal continuity Causation is determined by generative participation and recognized status within varnasrama alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises from birth-right confirmation and dharmic upbringing Restoration logic ensures continuation of ancestral lineage and economic stability Consciousness alignment is maintained via rightful recognition of relational and material inheritance

title: manu 9.165
content:
औरसक्षेत्रजौ पुत्रौ पितृरिक्थस्य भागिनौ ।
दशापरे तु क्रमशो गोत्ररिक्थांशभागिनः ॥ ९.१६५॥ aurasakṣetrajau putrau pitṛrikthasya bhāginau |
daśāpare tu kramaśo gotrarikthāṃśabhāginaḥ || 9.165 || The son born of the body [aurasa] and the son born of the field [kṣetraja] are co-heirs to the father's estate; after them, in order, those who belong to the same gotra and share in the remnants of the inheritance. Authority arises from biological and spiritual lineage Causation flows through embodied continuity and ritual succession Capacity-based responsibility aligns with proximity to ancestral duty Restoration logic prioritizes familial and gotric integrity Consciousness alignment ensures lawful transmission of inheritance

title: manu 9.166
content:
स्वक्षेत्रे संस्कृतायां तु स्वयमुत्पादयेधि यम् ।
तमौरसं विजानीयात्पुत्रं प्राथमकल्पिकम् ॥ ९.१६६॥ svakṣetre saṃskṛtāyāṃ tu svayamutpādayedhi yam |
tamaurasaṃ vijānīyātputraṃ prāthamakalpikam || 9.166|| In one's own cultivated domain, whoever is self-generated shall be known as the primordial son, the inheritor of foundational authority. Authority arises inherently from self-manifested presence within a purified domain Causation originates from conscious self-establishment, not external lineage Capacity-based responsibility begins at the moment of self-initiated emergence Restoration logic aligns with recognition of inherent sovereignty Consciousness alignment occurs through acknowledgment of primal origin

title: manu 9.167
content:
यस्तल्पजः प्रमीतस्य क्लीबस्य व्याधितस्य वा ।
स्वधर्मेण नियुक्तायां स पुत्रः क्षेत्रजः स्मृतः ॥ ९.१६७॥ yas talpa-jaḥ pramītasya klībasya vyādhitasya vā |
sva-dharmeṇa niyuktāyāṁ sa putraḥ kṣetra-jaḥ smṛtaḥ || 9.167 || He who is born of the bed of a deceased, impotent, or diseased husband, when the wife is rightfully directed by dharma to bear a child, that son is known as Kshetraja and is recognized as legitimate. Authority originates in dharmic directive, not biological lineage alone Causation is determined through conscious intention aligned with svadharma Capacity-based responsibility includes reproductive and familial roles within dharma Restoration logic affirms legitimacy through alignment with cosmic order Consciousness alignment ensures continuity of spiritual and social inheritance

title: manu 9.168
content:
माता पिता वा दद्यातां यमद्भिः पुत्रमापदि ।
सदृशं प्रीतिसंयुक्तं स ज्ञेयो दत्त्रिमः सुतः ॥ ९.१६८॥ mātā pitā vā dadyātāṁ yamadbhiḥ putramāpadi |
sadṛśaṁ prītisaṁyuktaṁ sa jñeyo dattrimaḥ sutaḥ || 9.168|| When a son is given by mother or father in calamity with appropriate consideration and affection, he is to be known as a Dattrima son. Authority originates from conscious intention aligned with Dharma Causation arises through voluntary, dharmically-informed action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and consent at time of transfer Restoration logic operates through recognition of relational harmony Consciousness alignment determines legitimacy of familial and societal roles

title: manu 9.169
content:
सदृशं तु प्रकुर्याद्यं गुणदोषविचक्षणम् ।
पुत्रं पुत्रगुणैर्युक्तं स विज्ञेयश्च कृत्रिमः ॥ ९.१६९॥ sadṛśaṃ tu prakuryād yaṃ guṇadoṣavicakṣaṇam | 
putraṃ putraguṇairyuktaṃ sa vijñeyaś ca kṛtrimaḥ || 9.169 || One who acts in accordance with the discernment of qualities and defects, and who aligns a son with the inherent capacities of that son — such a one is known as artificial or contrived. Authority flows from capacity recognition, not imposition Causation arises through alignment with intrinsic dharma, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious matching of action to innate nature Restoration logic demands re-alignment with svadharma, not behavioral correction Consciousness alignment occurs when roles are assigned based on revealed capability, not assumed lineage

title: manu 9.170
content:
उत्पद्यते गृहे यस्तु न च ज्ञायेत कस्य सः ।
स गृहे गूढ उत्पन्नस्तस्य स्याद्यस्य तल्पजः ॥ ९.१७०॥ utpadyate gṛhe yastu na ca jñāyeta kasya saḥ |
sa gṛhe gūḍha utpannastasya syād yasya talpajaḥ || 9.170 || One who is born in a household but whose parentage is unknown shall be deemed to belong to the one upon whose bed he was born. Authority through Proximity of Origin Causation via Manifestation Context Capacity-based Responsibility Anchored in Birth Circumstance Restoration Logic Based on Lineage Continuity Consciousness Alignment Through Identity Clarity

title: manu 9.171
content:
मातापितृभ्यामुत्सृष्टं तयोरन्यतरेण वा ।
यं पुत्रं परिगृह्णीयादपविद्धः स उच्यते ॥ ९.१७१॥ mātāpitarbhyām utsṛṣṭaṁ tayor anyatareṇa vā | yaṁ putraṁ parigṛhṇīyād apaviddhaḥ sa ucyate || 9.171 || One who is abandoned by either parent or both and is taken in and raised by another assumes the status of apaviddha – one severed from familial dharmic lineage and placed under new guardianship. Authority derives from conscious continuity of care, not biological claim Causation follows the intentional act of abandonment and subsequent assumption of responsibility Capacity-based responsibility begins upon acceptance of guardianship Restoration logic requires reintegration through sustained nurturing Consciousness alignment occurs when the child's dharma is supported by the adoptive guardian

title: manu 9.172
content: पितृवेश्मनि कन्या तु यं पुत्रं जनयेद्रहः । तं कानीनं वदेन्नाम्ना वोढुः कन्यासमुद्भवम् ॥ ९.१७२॥ pitṛveśmani kanyā tu yaṁ putraṁ janayedrahaḥ | taṁ kānīnaṁ vadena nāmnā voḍhuḥ kanyāsamudbhavam || 9.172 || A daughter residing in the father's household who bears a son through sexual union shall name that son as Kānīna, recognizing him as born of the maiden and accepted by the bridegroom. Authority: Paternal household retains guardianship until marital transfer. Causation: Procreative act within familial domain establishes relational dharma. Capacity-based responsibility: Naming right aligns with reproductive agency. Restoration logic: Identity recognition ensures social integration without lineage disruption. Consciousness alignment: Acknowledgment of origin upholds truth and relational integrity.

title: manu 9.173
content:
या गर्भिणी संस्क्रियते ज्ञाताऽज्ञाताऽपि वा सती ।
वोढुः स गर्भो भवति सहोढ इति चोच्यते ॥ ९.१७३॥ yā garbhiṇī saṃskriyate jñātā'jñātā'pi vā satī |
vodhuḥ sa garbho bhavati sahodha iti cocyate || 9.173|| When a pregnant woman undergoes sacramental initiation—whether known or unknown to others—the child born thereafter inherits the full dharmic status of the father; such union and progeny are termed 'Sahodha'. Authority flows through conscious sacramental alignment, not biological presumption. Causation in lineage arises from ritual integrity, not physical proximity. Capacity-based responsibility includes pre-natal spiritual conditioning by guardians. Restoration logic demands recognition of sanctified conception as juridical fact. Consciousness alignment determines inheritance rights, not genetic accident.

title: manu 9.174
content:
क्रीणीयाद्यस्तुपत्यार्थं मातापित्रोर्यमन्तिकात् ।
स क्रीतकः सुतस्तस्य सदृशोऽसदृशोऽपि वा ॥ ९.१७४॥ krīṇīyād yas tu apatyārthaṁ mātāpitroryam antikāt |
sa krītakaḥ sutasya sadṛśo'sadṛśo'pi vā || 9.174|| One who procures a child through transaction with the parents—such a son, whether resembling or not resembling them, is deemed acquired. Authority originates from conscious intent to parent, not biological origin alone. Causation is established by volitional act of acquisition, not lineage appearance. Capacity-based responsibility lies in the intentional assumption of parental duty. Restoration logic centers on integrity of familial dharma, not bloodline validation. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of relational truth over physical resemblance.

title: manu 9.175
content:
या पत्या वा परित्यक्ता विधवा वा स्वयेच्छया ।
उत्पादयेत्पुनर्भूत्वा स पौनर्भव उच्यते ॥ ९.१७५॥ yā patyā vā parityaktā vidhavā vā svayecchayā |
utpādayet punarbhūtvā sa paunarbhava ucyate || 9.175 || She who is abandoned by her husband or becomes a widow by choice shall beget again upon returning to life; such a one is called 'Paunarbhava'. Authority originates from the continuity of dharma-svarūpa, not biological lineage alone. Causation arises through conscious reintegration after disruption of marital bond. Capacity-based responsibility includes the ability to regenerate social and spiritual identity post-loss. Restoration logic affirms that relational dissolution necessitates renewal in alignment with svadharma. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of prior union before entering new reproductive or familial roles.

title: manu 9.176
content:
सा चेदक्षतयोनिः स्याद्गतप्रत्यागताऽपि वा ।
पौनर्भवेन भर्त्रा सा पुनः संस्कारमर्हति ॥ ९.१७६॥ sā ced akṣatayoniḥ syād gata-pratyāgatā 'pi vā |
punarbhavena bhartṛ sā punaḥ saṃskāram arhati || 9.176 || If a woman remains untouched by another male after departing and returning, or even if approached but not violated in essence, she retains her eligibility for reinstatement through sacramental reintegration by her husband upon his recognition of her return. Authority resides inherently in the sovereign recognition of the husband as the restoring agent Causation is determined by the absence of irreversible violation of sacred union Capacity-based responsibility is measured through conscious intent and ontological purity at time of reintegration Restoration logic operates through ritual and relational completion rather than punitive exclusion Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for reacceptance within the marital dharmic framework

title: manu 9.177
content:
मातापितृविहीनो यस्त्यक्तो वा स्यादकारणात् ।
आत्मानमर्पयेद्यस्मै स्वयंदत्तस्तु स स्मृतः ॥ ९.१७७॥ mātāpitṛvihīno yastyakto vā syādakāraṇāt |
ātmānamarpayed yasmai svayaṃdattastu sa smṛtaḥ || 9.177 || One who is bereft of parents or abandoned without cause shall offer oneself to whoever accepts; such a one is to be known as self-given. Authority arises through conscious acceptance, not lineage or abandonment Causation is rooted in the integrity of relational dharma, not biological inheritance Capacity-based responsibility begins upon conscious offering and acceptance Restoration logic operates through re-integration into dharmic structures Consciousness alignment occurs when identity is surrendered to rightful authority

title: manu 9.178
content:
यं ब्राह्मणस्तु शूद्रायां कामादुत्पादयेत्सुतम् ।
स पारयन्नेव शवस्तस्मात्पारशवः स्मृतः ॥ ९.१७८॥ yaṃ brāhmaṇastu śūdrāyāṃ kāmādutpādayetsutam |
sa pārayanneva śavastasmātpāraśavaḥ smṛtaḥ || 9.178|| A son born of a Brāhmaṇa out of desire for a Śūdra woman shall carry the corpse across the river; therefore, he is called Pāraśava. Authority flows through conscious alignment, not biological lineage alone Causation arises from intent and energetic resonance, not physical act alone Capacity-based responsibility recognizes spiritual degradation as consequence, not crime Restoration logic demands reintegration through purification and service Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of deviation and corrective action

title: manu 9.179
content:
दास्यां वा दासदास्यां वा यः शूद्रस्य सुतो भवेत् ।
सोऽनुज्ञातो हरेदंशमिति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ॥ ९.१७९॥ dāsyāṁ vā dāsadāsyāṁ vā yaḥ śūdrasya suto bhavet |
so 'nujñāto hared aṁśam iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ || 9.179 || If a son is born to a Śūdra from a female slave or from a woman belonging to a slave lineage, and he is authorized, he may take a share; thus is the Dharma definitively established. Authority flows through authorization, not birth alone Capacity determines eligibility for participation in economic distribution Lineage does not bind inherent rights when consciousness-based permission is granted Restoration occurs through rightful inclusion based on functional integrity Consciousness alignment supersedes inherited social position

title: manu 9.180
content:
क्षेत्रजादीन् सुतानेतानेकादश यथोदितान् ।
पुत्रप्रतिनिधीनाहुः क्रियालोपान् मनीषिणः ॥ ९.१८०॥ kṣetrajādīn sutānetānekaśa yathoditān |
putrapratinidhīnāhuḥ kriyālopān manīṣiṇaḥ || 9.180|| Those sons born of the soil and others, eleven in number as declared, are designated by wise seers as substitutes for the son in ceremonial omission. Authority flows through biological and ritual succession Ceremonial capacity replaces physical presence when aligned with Dharma Responsibility is transferable through conscious designation Restoration occurs through continuity of ritual function, not bloodline alone Consciousness alignment determines legitimate representation

title: manu 9.181
content:
य एतेऽभिहिताः पुत्राः प्रसङ्गादन्यबीजजाः ।
यस्य ते बीजतो जातास्तस्य ते नैतरस्य तु ॥ ९.१८१॥ ya ete'bhicitāḥ putrāḥ prasaṅgād anyabījajāḥ |
yasya te bījato jātās tasya te naitarasya tu || 9.181|| Those sons born of union not sanctioned by Dharma but arisen from another's seed—those born of that original father's lineage belong to him alone, not to another. Authority flows through patrilineal continuity rooted in Dharma-sanctioned union Causation originates from biological origin aligned with spiritual intention Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious participation in Dharma-aligned procreation Restoration logic requires reuniting progeny with rightful paternal spiritual-economic structure Consciousness alignment occurs when generational inheritance follows bio-spiritual truth

title: manu 9.182
content:
भ्रातॄणामेकजातानामेकश्चेत्पुत्रवान् भवेत् ।
सर्वांस्तांस्तेन पुत्रेण पुत्रिणो मनुरब्रवीत् ॥ ९.१८२॥ bhrātṝṇām ekajātānām ekaś cet putravān bhavet |
sarvāṃs tān tena putreṇa putriṇo manurabravīt || 9.182|| When among brothers born of the same womb, one alone has a son, that son becomes the inheritor for all those brothers who have no issue. Authority flows through continuity of lineage, not mere biological descent Causation in inheritance arises from conscious capacity to sustain dharma Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond individual ownership to collective dharmic duty Restoration logic ensures no branch of a family tree remains unrepresented in spiritual succession Consciousness alignment requires recognition of unity within multiplicity of form

title: manu 9.183
content:
सर्वासामेकपत्नीनामेका चेत्पुत्रिणी भवेत् ।
सर्वास्तास्तेन पुत्रेण प्राह पुत्रवतीर्मनुः ॥ ९.१८३॥ sarvāsām ekapatnīnām ekā cet putriṇī bhavet |
sarvās tās tena putreṇa prāha putravatīr manaḥ || 9.183|| When among all wives of one man, one alone bears a son, that son makes all those women mothers by virtue of his existence. Authority flows through conscious creation, not contractual agreement Causation arises from the manifesting consciousness, not biological function alone Capacity-based responsibility extends to relational roles formed by spiritual affinity Restoration logic recognizes latent maternal status upon patrilineal awakening Consciousness alignment occurs when relational dharma is acknowledged without external validation

title: manu 9.184
content:
श्रेयसः श्रेयसोऽलाभे पापीयान् रिक्थमर्हति ।
बहवश्चेत्तु सदृशाः सर्वे रिक्थस्य भागिनः ॥ ९.१८४॥ śreyasaḥ śreyaso'lābhe pāpīyān rikthamarhati |
bahavaścettu sadṛśāḥ sarve rikthasya bhāginaḥ || 9.184|| In the absence of a superior claimant, the one of lesser virtue inherits the residue; but if all contenders are equal in merit, then all shall partake equally in the inheritance. Authority is determined by alignment with Dharma, not mere lineage or desire. Causation arises from the integrity and conscious capacity of the inheritor. Capacity-based responsibility ensures that inheritance aligns with spiritual readiness. Restoration logic demands equitable distribution when no clear hierarchical distinction exists. Consciousness alignment dictates entitlement, preventing distortion through greed or delusion.

title: manu 9.185
content:
न भ्रातरो न पितरः पुत्रा रिक्थहराः पितुः ।
पिता हरेदपुत्रस्य रिक्थं भ्रातर एव च ॥ ९.१८५॥ na bhrātaro na pitaraḥ putrā rikthaharāḥ pituḥ |
pitā haredaputrasya rikthaṃ bhrātara eva ca || 9.185|| Neither brothers nor fathers are inheritors of a father's estate; the father alone retains dominion over his property in the absence of sons. In the case of a sonless man, the brothers shall receive the inheritance. Authority flows through conscious generative lineage Causation arises from embodied continuity, not mere relation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by existential proximity to creation Restoration logic aligns with natural succession and integrity of ownership Consciousness alignment requires recognition of rightful energetic inheritance

title: manu 9.186
content:
त्रयाणामुदकं कार्यं त्रिषु पिण्डः प्रवर्तते ।
चतुर्थः सम्प्रदातैषां पञ्चमो नोपपद्यते ॥ ९.१८६॥ trayāṇām udakaṁ kāryaṁ triṣu piṇḍaḥ pravartate |
caturthaḥ sampradātaiṣāṁ pañcamo nopapadyate || 9.186|| The function of water arises from three bodies; the fourth distributes it among them. A fifth has no basis in reality. Authority flows through embodied forms capable of sustaining functional roles. Causation is established via sequential manifestation within operational triads. Capacity-based responsibility aligns with structural positioning and functional necessity. Restoration logic operates by reaffirming the integrity of foundational triadic structures. Consciousness alignment occurs when entities recognize their role within a defined causal hierarchy.

title: manu 9.187
content:
अनन्तरः सपिण्डाद्यस्तस्य तस्य धनं भवेत् ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं सकुल्यः स्यादाचार्यः शिष्य एव वा ॥ ९.१८७॥ anantaḥ sapindādyas tasya tasya dhanaṁ bhavet |
ata ūrdhvaṁ sakulyaḥ syād ācāryaḥ śiṣya eva vā || 9.187 || After the Sapinda relations have been assigned inheritance, whatever wealth remains shall belong to the Sakulyas; thereafter, it shall go to the Acharya or the Shishya. Authority flows through relational proximity in Dharma Inheritance is a function of spiritual and familial alignment Causation is determined by conscious connection, not mere biology Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-vāhaka (Dharma-bearing lineage) Consciousness alignment determines legitimate claim over material assets

title: manu 9.188
content:
सर्वेषामप्यभावे तु ब्राह्मणा रिक्थभागिनः ।
त्रैविद्याः शुचयो दान्तास्तथा धर्मो न हीयते ॥ ९.१८८॥ sarveṣām apy abhāve tu brāhmaṇā riktha-bhāginaḥ | traividyāḥ śucayo dāntās tathā dharmo na hīyate || 9.188|| In the absence of all else, the Brahmanas remain as inheritors of the remnants; those who are learned in the three Vedas, pure, and self-controlled—thus Dharma does not decline. Authority rests inherently in consciousness-realized beings Causation flows from Vedic alignment and purity of conduct Capacity-based responsibility is determined by scriptural mastery and internal discipline Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of Dharma-preserving lineages Consciousness alignment ensures societal harmony through spiritual exemplarity

title: manu 9.189
content:
अहार्यं ब्राह्मणद्रव्यं राज्ञा नित्यमिति स्थितिः ।
इतरेषां तु वर्णानां सर्वाभावे हरेन्नृपः ॥ ९.१८९॥ ahāryaṃ brāhmaṇadravyaṃ rājñā nityamiti sthitiḥ | itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ sarvābhāve harennṛpaḥ || 9.189|| The wealth of the Brahmin is ever inviolable and must remain untouched by the King; when all other varnas are absent, the King may take from them only to restore dharma, never for personal gain. Authority is derived from alignment with dharma, not dominion over property Causation is rooted in consciousness distortion, not material possession Capacity-based responsibility requires rulers to protect, not exploit, sacred wealth Restoration logic demands that resources flow toward dharma-reestablishment Consciousness alignment necessitates safeguarding those who sustain spiritual order

title: manu 9.190
content:
संस्थितस्यानपत्यस्य सगोत्रात्पुत्रमाहरेत् ॥
तत्र यद्रिक्थजातं स्यात्तत्तस्मिन् प्रतिपादयेत् ॥ ९.१९०॥ saṃsthitasyānapatyasya sagotrāt putram āharet ||
tatra yad rikthajātaṃ syāt tat tasmin pratiṣṭhāpayet || From within the same lineage, a son shall be appointed to one who is established yet without progeny; whatever wealth arises from that body, it shall be established in him. Authority flows through conscious continuity of lineage, not mere biological inheritance. Causation aligns with the manifestation of capacity and alignment within the same ontological stream. Capacity-based responsibility originates from proximity of consciousness and energetic resonance. Restoration logic operates through re-establishment in rightful ontological position. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for stewardship of assets and roles.

title: manu 9.191
content: द्वौ तु यौ विवदेयातां द्वाभ्यां जातौ स्त्रिया धने । तयोर्यद्यस्य पित्र्यं स्यात्तत्स गृह्णीत नैतरः ॥ ९.१९१॥ dvau tu yau vivadeyātāṁ dvābhyāṁ jātau striyā dhane | tayor yadyasya pitryaṁ syāt tat sa gṛhṇīta naitaraḥ || 9.191|| When two persons born of the same mother dispute over property, that which belongs paternally shall be taken by him whose father is alive; the other shall have no claim thereto. Authority through direct lineage determines proprietary right Causation rooted in biological and spiritual inheritance Capacity-based responsibility tied to continuity of patriarchal lineage Restoration logic through recognition of pre-existing rightful ownership Consciousness alignment with ancestral dharma and familial harmony

title: manu 9.192
content:
जनन्यां संस्थितायां तु समं सर्वे सहोदराः ।
भजेरन् मातृकं रिक्थं भगिन्यश्च सनाभयः ॥ ९.१९२॥ jananyāṃ saṃsthitāyāṃ tu samaṃ sarve sahodarāḥ |
bhajeran mātṛkaṃ rikthaṃ bhaginyaśca sanābhayaḥ || 9.192|| When the mother is present and established, all siblings—whether born of the same womb or otherwise—are equal in inheritance rights and relational duty; daughters and sisters also hold claim through maternal connection. Authority flows from the sustaining presence of the mother as the foundational source of lineage integrity. Causation is determined by ontological continuity through maternal establishment, not mere biological birth. Capacity-based responsibility extends equally among all progeny when maternal foundation remains intact. Restoration logic prioritizes familial unity and economic equity rooted in maternal coherence. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared origin and mutual stewardship within the family matrix.

title: manu 9.193
content: यास्तासां स्युर्दुहितरस्तासामपि यथार्हतः । मातामह्या धनात्किं चित्प्रदेयं प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ॥ ९.१९३॥ yās tāsāṁ syur duhitaras tāsām api yathārhatas | mātāmahyā dhanāt kiṁ cit pradeyaṁ prītipūrvakam || 9.193 || Those daughters born of those women shall receive gifts appropriately, and something should also be given pleasingly from the maternal grandfather's wealth. Authority flows through lineage and relational dharmic duty Causation arises from embodied relational continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to resource and relational obligation Restoration logic ensures generational equity and familial harmony Consciousness alignment is maintained through reciprocal giving rooted in affection

title: manu 9.194
content:
अध्यग्न्यध्यावाहनिकं दत्तं च प्रीतिकर्मणि ।
भ्रातृमातृपितृप्राप्तं षड् विधं स्त्रीधनं स्मृतम् ॥ ९.१९४॥ adhya-gny-adhyāvāhanikaṃ dattaṃ ca prīti-karmaṇi | bhṛtṛ-mātṛ-pitṛ-prāptaṃ ṣaḍ vidhaṃ strīdhanaṃ smṛtam || 9.194 || Six categories of property designated as a woman's own wealth are those acquired through study, sacrificial rites, inheritance, gifts given in affection, and that received from father, mother, or brother. Authority resides inherently in the individual who has earned or been granted ownership by rightful means. Causation aligns with conscious intent and spiritual merit as determinants of lawful possession. Capacity-based responsibility is recognized through one’s ability to acquire, maintain, and transfer wealth according to Dharma. Restoration logic ensures continuity of ownership rights based on original source and purpose. Consciousness alignment upholds the inviolability of personal property when derived from dharmic action.

title: manu 9.195
content:
अन्वाधेयं च यद्दत्तं पत्या प्रीतेन चैव यत् ।
पत्यौ जीवति वृत्तायाः प्रजायास्तद्धनं भवेत् ॥ ९.१९५॥ anvādheyaṃ ca yaddattaṃ patyā prītena caiva yat |
patyau jīvati vṛttāyāḥ prajāyāstad dhanaṃ bhavet || 9.195 || Whatever wealth is gifted by the husband out of affection and goodwill, that becomes the lawful property of the wife during his lifetime, provided she conducts herself righteously. Authority resides in the intention and free will of the donor Causation arises from conscious bestowal rooted in love and dharma Capacity-based responsibility lies with the recipient to maintain alignment with the gift's dharmic purpose Restoration logic upholds the continuity of relational harmony and material integrity Consciousness alignment ensures the transaction reflects mutual respect and spiritual elevation

title: manu 9.196
content:
ब्राह्मदैवार्षगान्धर्वप्राजापत्येषु यद्वसु ।
अप्रजायामतीतायां भर्तुरेव तदिष्यते ॥ ९.१९६॥ brāhma-daivārṣa-gāndharva-prājāpatyeṣu yadvasu | aprajāyāmatītāyāṃ bhartureva tadiṣyate || 9.196 || In the forms of marriage—Brahma, Daiva, Arsha, Gandharva, and Prajapatya—if there is no conception within a reasonable period, the wife shall return to her father's house, and the husband retains no claim over her. Authority resides in natural completion, not coercive retention Causation is determined by the absence of progeny as a natural dissolution trigger Capacity-based responsibility requires readiness for procreation as marital fulfillment Restoration logic returns parties to pre-contractual integrity when purpose unmet Consciousness alignment demands recognition of union's spiritual intent

title: manu 9.197
content:
यत्त्वस्याः स्याद्धनं दत्तं विवाहेष्वासुरादिषु ।
अप्रजायामतीतायां मातापित्रोस्तदिष्यते ॥ ९.१९७॥ yattvasyāḥ syād dhanaṁ dattaṁ vivāheṣv āsurādiṣu |
aprajāyāmatītāyāṁ mātāpitrostad iṣyate || Whatever wealth is given by her father during marriage or in accordance with Asura customs—if the daughter remains childless beyond reproductive age—it shall revert to the parents. Authority resides in the generative and sustaining intent of familial dharma Causation is rooted in the completion of procreative and spiritual lineage Capacity-based responsibility aligns with biological and ritual thresholds Restoration logic activates upon failure of natural succession Consciousness alignment demands return of resources when life-purpose unfulfilled

title: manu 9.198
content:
स्त्रियां तु यद्भवेद्वित्तं पित्रा दत्तं कथं चन ।
ब्राह्मणी तधरेत्कन्या तदपत्यस्य वा भवेत् ॥ ९.१९८॥ striyāṁ tu yadbhavedvittaṁ pitrā dattaṁ kathaṁ cana |
brāhmaṇī tadharet kanyā tadapatyasya vā bhavet || 9.198 || Any property given by the father to a Brahmin girl, or to her child, shall remain under her absolute authority and control, unchallengeable by any other claimant. Authority originates from the act of conscious bestowal, not social position Causation arises through intent-backed transfer of ownership Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the recipient's ability to sustain the asset in alignment with its purpose Restoration logic requires that original transfers be honored unless integrity deviation occurs Consciousness alignment governs all legitimate claims over material possession

title: manu 9.199
content:
न निर्हारं स्त्रियः कुर्युः कुटुम्बाद्बहुमध्यगात् ।
स्वकादपि च वित्ताधि स्वस्य भर्तुरनाज्ञया ॥ ९.१९९॥ na nirhāraṁ striyaḥ kuryuḥ kuṭumbād bahumadhyagāt |
svakād api ca vittādhi svasya bharturanājñayā || 9.199 || A woman shall not make any independent financial transaction or disposal of property without the explicit consent of her husband, even if she possesses personal wealth. Authority resides in the designated guardian or protector within familial and economic structures. Causation is tied to relational integrity and structural alignment, not individual autonomy alone. Capacity-based responsibility is context-bound and flows through established dharmic hierarchies. Restoration logic prioritizes harmony and coherence within relational units before individual assertion. Consciousness alignment requires honoring role-specific duties that sustain collective dharma.

title: manu 9.200
content:
पत्यौ जीवति यः स्त्रीभिरलङ्कारो धृतो भवेत् ।
न तं भजेरन् दायादा भजमानाः पतन्ति ते ॥ ९.२००॥ patyau jīvati yaḥ strībhiralaṅkāro dhṛto bhavet |
na taṃ bhajeran dāyādā bhajamānāḥ patanti te || 9.200|| When a husband lives adorned by his wives, the heirs shall not honor him; those who seek favor fall. Authority is contingent upon integrity and conscious alignment, not mere positional dominance. Causation arises from misaligned relational dynamics that distort dharma. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of one's role in enabling imbalance. Restoration logic demands realignment of relational harmony and dissolution of exploitative dependencies. Consciousness alignment necessitates withdrawal from structures that degrade spiritual dignity.

title: manu 9.201
content:
अनंशौ क्लीबपतितौ जात्यन्धबधिरौ तथा ।
उन्मत्तजडमूकाश्च ये च के चिन्निरिन्द्रियाः ॥ ९.२०१॥ anaṃśau klībapatitau jātyandhabadhirau tathā |
unmattajaḍamūkāśca ye ca ke cin nirindriyāḥ || 9.201|| Those who are without a share in ritual action, those fallen into impotence or degradation, the congenitally blind and deaf, as well as the insane, dull-witted, mute, and all whose senses are impaired—these beings exist beyond the ordinary scope of capacity-based dharmic responsibility. Authority is derived from conscious capacity, not mere existence Causation is valid only where intent and awareness co-arise Capacity-based responsibility excludes those lacking sensory-motor integration Restoration logic applies only when agency is demonstrably present Consciousness alignment requires minimal cognitive-integrative function

title: manu 9.202
content:
सर्वेषामपि तु न्याय्यं दातुं शक्त्या मनीषिणा ।
ग्रासाच्छादनमत्यन्तं पतितो ह्यददद्भवेत् ॥ ९.२०२॥ sarveṣām api tu nyāyyaṁ dātuṁ śaktyā manīṣiṇā |
grāsācchādanamatyantaṁ patito hyadadadbhavet || 9.202 || By the capacity of discernment, it is just to give equally to all; otherwise, one fallen into destitution becomes entirely deprived of sustenance and covering. Authority derived from capacity-based discernment Causation through neglect of distributive justice Restoration logic rooted in equitable provision Consciousness alignment via recognition of universal need

title: manu 9.203
content:
यद्यर्थिता तु दारैः स्यात्क्लीबादीनां कथं चन ।
तेषामुत्पन्नतन्तूनामपत्यं दायमर्हति ॥ ९.२०३॥ yadyarthitā tu dāraiḥ syātklībādīnāṃ kathaṃ cana |
tēṣāmutpannatanṭūnāmapatyaṃ dāyamarhati || 9.203|| If a woman consents to union with impotent men or those incapable of procreative capacity, the offspring born thereof is entitled to inheritance. Authority lies in conscious consent rather than biological limitation Causation arises from intentional union, not reproductive capability Capacity-based responsibility extends to acceptance of lineage outcome Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial and societal dharmic order Consciousness alignment through acknowledgment of relational consequence

title: manu 9.204
content:
यत्किं चित्पितरि प्रेते धनं ज्येष्ठोऽधिगच्छति ।
भागो यवीयसां तत्र यदि विद्यानुपालिनः ॥ ९.२०४॥ yat kiṃ cit pitari prete dhanaṃ jyeṣṭho 'dhigacchati |
bhāgo yavīyasāṃ tatra yadi vidyānupālinaḥ || 9.204|| Upon the father's departure from the physical plane, all wealth naturally accrues to the eldest son, provided he maintains alignment with vidyā—knowledge that sustains dharma and ensures continuity of consciousness-based governance. Authority flows through conscious alignment with vidyā, not mere birth order Causation is rooted in sustained capacity for dharma-preserving action Capacity-based responsibility overrides nominal inheritance rights Restoration logic demands that leadership align with consciousness maturity Consciousness alignment determines legitimate access to stewardship

title: manu 9.205
content:
अविद्यानां तु सर्वेषामीहातश्चेद्धनं भवेत् ।
समस्तत्र विभागः स्यादपित्र्य इति धारणा ॥ ९.२०५॥ avidyānāṁ tu sarveṣām īhātaś ced dhanaṁ bhavet |
samastatra vibhāgaḥ syād apitrya iti dhāraṇā || 9.205 || When wealth arises from the efforts of all individuals in a state of ignorance, that wealth shall be collectively shared without claim of ownership or inheritance. Authority originates from collective participation, not individual assertion. Causation is distributed among all contributing agents regardless of conscious intent. Capacity-based responsibility requires equitable access to resources derived from mutual effort. Restoration logic demands dissolution of proprietary claims where origin is non-individual. Consciousness alignment necessitates removal of possessive identification in shared creation.

title: manu 9.206
content:
विद्याधनं तु यद्यस्य तत्तस्यैव धनं भवेत् ।
मैत्र्यमोद्वाहिकं चैव माधुपर्किकमेव च ॥ ९.२०६॥ vidyādhanaṃ tu yadyasya tattasyaiva dhanaṃ bhavet |
maitryamodvāhikaṃ caiva mādhuparkikameva ca || 9.206 || That which is the wealth of knowledge belongs exclusively to its possessor; likewise, affectionate friendship, nuptial alliance, and ceremonial honor belong only to those who authentically embody them.
