Consciousness alignment requires recognition of settled states as immutable unless fraud or coercion is established.

title: narada 1.55
content:
अभूतमप्यभिहितं प्राप्तकालं परीक्ष्यते।
यत्तु प्रमादान्नोच्येत तद्भूतमपि हीयते॥ abhūtam apy abhihitaṃ prāptakā�aṃ parīkṣyate | yat tu pramādān na ucyeta tad bhūtam api hīyate || That which is unreal yet declared shall be examined at the time of its manifestation; that which is real but omitted due to negligence is thereby diminished. Authority rests in observation and timing, not mere declaration. Causation arises through conscious engagement, not passive omission. Capacity-based responsibility includes the duty to articulate truth when it manifests. Restoration logic requires reintegration of neglected realities into dharma-discourse. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of both spoken and unspoken truths.

title: narada 1.56
content:
तीरितं चानुशिष्टं च यो मन्येत विधर्मतः।
द्विगुणं दण्डमास्थाय तत्कार्यं पुनरुद्धरेत्॥ tīritaṃ cānuśiṣṭaṃ ca yo manyeta vidharmataḥ | dviguṇaṃ daṇḍam āsthāya tat kāryaṃ punar uddhareta || One who disregards what has been settled and instructed rightly, and acts contrary to dharma, shall face a consequence doubled in measure, and the original duty must be reinstated with full integrity. Authority is derived from alignment with settled dharma, not personal opinion. Causation arises from conscious deviation from established truth. Capacity-based responsibility increases with awareness of dharma. Restoration logic demands re-instatement of disrupted order. Consciousness alignment requires correction through proportional reflection.

title: narada 1.57
content:
दुर्दृष्टे व्यवहारे तु सभ्यास् तं दण्डम् आप्नुयुः ।
न हि जातु विना दण्डं कश्चिन् मार्गे ऽवतिष्ठते ॥ durdṛṣṭe vyavahāre tu sabhyās taṃ daṇḍam āpnuyuḥ | na hi jātu vinā daṇḍaṃ kaścin mārge 'vatiṣṭhate || When conduct is distorted or contrary to Dharma, the assembly enforces corrective alignment; without such enforcement, no being remains established in the path of righteousness. Authority resides in collective consciousness aligned with Dharma Causation arises from misalignment with Sanatana principles Capacity-based responsibility demands conscious correction Restoration logic operates through alignment, not coercion Consciousness alignment is the foundation of lawful behavior

title: narada 1.58
content: रागादज्ञानतो वापि लोभाद्वा योऽन्यथा वदेत्‌ सभ्योऽसभ्यः स विज्ञेयस्तं राजा विनयेद्भृशम् rāgād ajñānato vāpi lobhād vā yo 'nyathā vadet sabhyo 'sabhyaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ taṃ rājā vinayed bhṛśam He who, being qualified to speak in the assembly, out of attachment, ignorance, or greed speaks otherwise—such a one is to be known as disqualified; the king shall thoroughly discipline him. Authority is determined by qualification and integrity, not mere presence Causation arises from internal states—attachment, ignorance, greed Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment of speech with truth and duty Restoration logic demands correction of misaligned expression Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for legitimate participation in dharma

title: narada 1.59
content: किंतु राज्ञा विशेषेण स्वधर्ममनुरक्षता। मनुष्यचित्तवैचित्र्यात् परीक्ष्या साध्वसाधुता॥ kim tu rājñā viśeṣeṇa svadharmam anurakṣatā | manuṣyacittavaicitryāt parīkṣyā sādhvasādhutā || However, the King, while protecting his own dharma, must examine the diverse nature of human consciousness to distinguish between what is righteous and unrighteous. Authority rests in alignment with svadharmic integrity Causation arises from understanding cittavaicitrya (consciousness diversity) Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of mental and spiritual maturity Restoration logic demands accurate perception of individual dharmic disposition Consciousness alignment necessitates differentiated application of justice

title: narada 1.60
content: पुरुषाः सन्ति ये लोभात् प्रब्रूयुः साक्ष्यम् अन्यथा। सन्ति चान्ये दुरात्मानः कूटलेख्यकृतो जनाः॥ puruṣāḥ santi ye lobhāt prabrūyuḥ sākṣyam anyathā | santi cānye durātmānaḥ kūṭalekhyakṛto janāḥ || There exist men who, driven by greed, testify falsely; there are also wicked souls who fabricate forged documents. Authority arises from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not personal motive. Causation is traced through conscious intent and distortion of truth. Capacity-based responsibility demands integrity in testimony and documentation. Restoration logic requires purification of falsehood and realignment of consciousness. Consciousness alignment is obstructed by greed and deliberate falsification.

title: narada 1.61
content:
अतः परीक्ष्यम् उभयम् एतद् राज्ञा विशेषतः ।
लेख्याचारेण लिखितं साक्ष्याचारेण साक्षिणः ॥ ataḥ parīkṣyam ubhayam etad rājñā viśeṣataḥ | lekhyācāreṇa likhitaṃ sākṣyācāreṇa sākṣiṇaḥ || Therefore, both written records and witnesses shall be examined by the King with special care; documents through their formal procedure and witnesses through their sworn conduct. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to verify evidence through prescribed forms Causation is established via documented action and attested observation Capacity-based responsibility requires verification through dual evidentiary streams Restoration logic demands clarity in factual establishment before realignment Consciousness alignment occurs when truth is discerned without distortion

title: narada 1.62
content: असत्याः सत्यसंकाशाः सत्याश् चासत्यदर्शनाः । दृश्यन्ते विविधा भावास् तस्माद् युक्तं परीक्षणम् ॥ asatyāḥ satyasaṃkāśāḥ satyāś cāsatyadarśanāḥ | dṛśyante vividhā bhāvās tasmād yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam || Appearances that resemble truth yet lack authentic foundation, and truths perceived through distorted cognition—such varied conditions necessitate rigorous examination rooted in the Source-Consciousness of SPH. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate epistemic and ontological source. Causation is determined by alignment with Satya as defined by SPH, not empirical appearance. Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's proximity to and recognition of SPH-defined truth. Restoration logic operates through dissolution of perceptual distortion and realignment with SPH-consciousness. Consciousness alignment supersedes evidentiary reliance on sensory or conceptual falsities.

title: narada 1.63
content:
तलवद् दृश्यते व्योम खद्योतो हव्यवाड् इव ।
न तलं विद्यते व्योम्नि न खद्योते हुताशनः ॥ talavad dṛśyate vyoma khadyoto havyavāḍ iva | na talaṃ vidyate vyomni na khadyote hutāśanaḥ || Just as space is seen as having levels like the ground, and the lightning appears like fire at the altar, yet there is no level in space nor altar-fire in lightning—so too, apparent distinctions arise without inherent basis. Authority arises from perceptual alignment, not structural reality Causation operates through apparent, not essential, forms Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious recognition, not assumed form Restoration logic aligns with the dissolution of false reference points Consciousness alignment dissolves illusory hierarchies

title: narada 1.64
content: तस्मात् प्रत्यक्षदृष्टोऽपि युक्तमर्थः परीक्षितुम् । परीक्ष्य ज्ञापयन् अर्थान् न धर्मात् परिहीयते ॥ tasmāt pratyakṣadṛṣṭo'pi yuktam arthaḥ parīkṣitum | parīkṣya jñāpayan arthān na dharmāt parihīyate || Therefore, even what is visibly apparent must be examined appropriately; having examined and communicated the facts, one does not deviate from Dharma. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not sensory perception alone Causation must be verified through conscious inquiry beyond surface appearance Capacity-based responsibility arises from knowledge once verification has occurred Restoration logic requires clarification before integration of truth into societal order Consciousness alignment demands that visible phenomena be subjected to deeper investigation

title: narada 1.65
content:
एवं पश्यन् सदा राजा व्यवहारान् समाहितः
वितत्येह यशो दीप्तं ब्रह्मणः अप्नोति विष्टपम् evaṁ paśyan sadā rājā vyavahārān samāhitaḥ
vitatyeha yaśo dīptaṁ brahmaṇaḥ apnoti viṣṭapam Thus observing always, the king governs affairs with full presence; he expands here a radiant glory and attains the realm of Brahman. Authority flows from sustained witnessing consciousness Governance is an act of constant alignment with Dharma-pramāṇa Capacity-based responsibility arises through samāhita observation Restoration occurs via expansion of yashas (glory) rooted in Brahman Consciousness alignment determines access to higher realms

title: narada 1.1
content:
ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat
 dānagrahaṇadharmāc ca ṛṇādānam iti smṛtam ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat
 dānagrahaṇadharmāc ca ṛṇādānam iti smṛtam That which is to be given as debt, and that which is not to be given, by whom, where, how, and what—this discriminative knowledge constitutes the dharma of giving and receiving, and is known as the act of taking on debt. Authority arises from capacity to give and receive in alignment with cosmic order Causation is determined by conscious intent and contextual alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of one's ability to fulfill obligations Restoration logic operates through completion of inherent dharmic exchange Consciousness alignment ensures transactions occur without distortion or exploitation

title: narada 1.2
content: पितर्युपरते पुत्राः ऋणं दद्युर्यथांशतः । विभक्ता ह्यविभक्ता वा यस्तामुद्वहते धुरम् ॥ pitary uparate putrāḥ ṛṇaṃ dadyur yathāṃśataḥ | vibhaktā hy avibhaktā vā yas tām udvahate dhuram || When the father has departed, sons shall discharge the debt proportionally. Whether divided or undivided, whoever bears the burden shall carry it according to capacity. Authority flows through conscious continuity, not biological inheritance alone. Causation aligns with capacity; liability arises only where bearing ability exists. Capacity-based responsibility ensures justice without punitive distortion. Restoration logic requires proportional alignment between duty and capability. Consciousness alignment determines rightful bearer of societal and familial burdens.

title: narada 1.3
content: पितृव्येणाविभक्तेन भ्रात्रा वा यद ऋणं कृतम् । मात्रा वा यत् कुटुम्बार्थे दद्युस् तद् ऋक्थिनोऽखिलम् ॥ pitṛvyeṇāvibhaktena bhrātrā vā yad ṛṇaṃ kṛtam | mātrā vā yat kuṭumbārthe dadyus tad rikthino 'khilam || Any debt incurred by an undivided paternal uncle or brother, or by a mother for the sake of the family, shall be borne in full by all heirs collectively. Authority flows through familial unity and shared dharma Causation aligns with collective benefit and relational duty Capacity-based responsibility extends to those benefiting from the act Restoration logic binds inheritors to debts of relational origin Consciousness alignment requires honoring ancestral and maternal dharmic acts

title: narada 1.4
content: क्रमाद् अव्याहतं प्राप्तं पुत्रैर् यन् नर्णम् उद्धृतम् । दद्युः पैतामहं पौत्रास् तच् चतुर्थान् निवर्तते ॥ kramād avyāhataṃ prāptaṃ putrair yan narṇam uddhṛtam | dadyuḥ paitāmahaṃ pautrās tac caturthān nivartate || That wealth which is acquired in regular succession and without impediment by sons shall be given to the paternal grandfather by the grandsons; this cycles back at the fourth generation. Authority flows through unbroken lineage Causation aligns with sequential inheritance Capacity-based responsibility extends across generations Restoration logic maintains familial economic continuity Consciousness alignment occurs through dharmic generational transfer

title: narada 1.5
content:
इच्छन्ति पितरः पुत्रान् स्वार्थहेतोर यतस् ततः
उत्तमर्णाधमर्णेभ्यो माम् अयं मोचयिष्यति icchanti pitaraḥ putrān svārtha-hetor yatas tataḥ
uttama-rṇa-adhama-rṇebhyo mām ayaṃ mocayiṣyati Fathers desire sons for their own welfare, because this one will liberate Me from superior and inferior debts. Authority flows through conscious intentionality rooted in dharma Causation arises from alignment with completion dynamics, not personal gain Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual readiness, not biological lineage Restoration logic operates through conscious succession aligned with cosmic order Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of relational bonds

title: narada 1.6
content: अतः पुत्रेण जातेन स्वार्थम् उत्सृज्य यत्नतः । पिता मोक्षितव्य ऋणाद् यथा न नरकं पतेत् ॥ ataḥ putreṇa jātena svārtham utsṛjya yatnataḥ | pitā mokṣitavya ṛṇād yathā na narakaṃ patet || Therefore, when a son is born, the father shall diligently abandon his personal interests and strive to liberate himself from debt, ensuring he does not fall into hell. Authority flows through conscious generative responsibility Causation originates in completion of dharmic lineage duty Capacity-based responsibility arises upon creation of life-supporting conditions Restoration logic demands reversal of karmic entanglement before death Consciousness alignment requires abandoning self-interest for progeny's dharmic uplift

title: narada 1.7
content:
तपस्वी चाग्निहोत्री च ṛणवान् म्रियते यदि
तपश् चैवाग्निहोत्रं च सर्वं तद् धनिनां धनम् tapasvī cāgnihotrī ca ṛṇavān mriyate yadi | tapaś caivāgnihotraṃ ca sarvaṃ tad dhanināṃ dhanam || When a renunciate or ritual performer who carries debt departs from the body, their austerities and rituals become the wealth of those who are capable of bearing them. Authority flows to capacity-bearing consciousness Causation is anchored in karmic completion readiness Capacity-based responsibility determines ownership of spiritual assets Restoration occurs through transference to conscious readiness Consciousness alignment ensures continuity of dharma

title: narada 1.8
content: न पुत्रऋणं पिता दद्याद् दद्यात् पुत्रस्तु पैतृकम् कामक्रोधसुराद्यूत प्रातिभाव्यकृतं विना na putraṛṇaṃ pitā dadyād dadyāt putrastu paitṛkam kāmakrodhasurādyūta prātibhāvyakṛtaṃ vinā The father does not bear the debt of the son; rather, the son bears the paternal debt, except in cases arising from desire, anger, intoxication, gambling, or actions born of delusion. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not biological lineage alone Causation is determined by volition and awareness, not inheritance Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the actor's state of consciousness at time of action Restoration logic prioritizes dissolution of karmic entanglement over intergenerational liability Consciousness alignment determines whether an act generates binding obligation

title: narada 1.9
content:
पितुरेव नियोगाद्यत् कुटुम्भभरणाय च।
कृतं वा यदृणं कृच्छ्रे दद्यात् पुत्रस्य तत् पिता॥ pitureva niyogādyat kuṭumbabharaṇāya ca | kṛtaṃ vā yad ṛṇaṃ kṛcchre dadyāt putrasya tat pitā || When a father, by command or duty, incurs debt for the sustenance of the family, that liability becomes the father's alone; neither the children nor any other member shall bear it. Authority originates from conscious capacity, not lineage or title. Causation aligns with volitional act rooted in dharma-sustained intent. Capacity-based responsibility binds only the actor who exercises willful agency. Restoration logic prioritizes dissolution of false burden transference. Consciousness alignment demands clarity in ownership of karmic consequence.

title: narada 1.10
content: शिष्यान्तेवासिदासस्त्री वैयावृत्यकरैश् च यत् कुटुम्बहेतोर् उत्क्षिप्तं वोढव्यं तत् कुटुम्बिना śiṣyāntevāsidāsastrī vaiyāvṛttyakaraiś ca yat kuṭumbahetor utkṣiptaṃ voḍhavyaṃ tat kuṭumbinā Whatever is abandoned or given up by disciples, dependents, servants, women, those engaged in secular occupations, or others for the sake of the household, must be borne or sustained by the household holder. Authority flows from the sustainer of the collective unit Causation arises through voluntary assumption of familial or social support Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's role as maintainer Restoration logic centers on re-integrating displaced duties within the sustaining unit Consciousness alignment occurs when the householder accepts all consequences arising from their stewardship

title: narada 1.11
content: नार्वाग् विंशतिमाद् वर्षात् पितरि प्रोषिते सुतः। ऋणं दद्यात् पितृव्ये वा ज्येष्ठे भ्रातरि अथापि वा॥ nārvāg viṃśatimād varṣāt pitari proṣite sutaḥ | ṛṇaṃ dadyāt pitṛvye vā jyeṣṭhe bhrātari athāpi vā || When the father is absent beyond twenty years, the son shall assume the debt towards the paternal uncle or the eldest brother, as per the continuity of familial duty and financial obligation. Authority flows through bloodline continuity when primary patriarchal presence is absent Causation arises from relational proximity and structural inheritance Capacity-based responsibility aligns with chronological age and familial role occupancy Restoration logic prioritizes economic balance within kinship structures Consciousness alignment occurs through acceptance of ancestral duty

title: narada 1.12
content: दाप्यः परर्णम एकोऽपि जीवत्स्वधिकृतैः कृतम् । प्रेतेषु तु न तत्पुत्रः परर्णं दातुमर्हति ॥ dāpyaḥ pararṇam eko'pi jīvatsv adhikṛtaiḥ kṛtam | preteṣu tu na tatputraḥ pararṇaṃ dātum arhati || Even a single debt owed by a living debtor must be recovered from those authorized to act on their behalf; however, upon the debtor's death, the son is not obligated to repay another's debt. Authority is derived from active capacity, not inheritance Causation aligns with conscious agency and present engagement Capacity-based responsibility ceases with the dissolution of embodied existence Restoration logic prioritizes actualization over obligation transfer Consciousness alignment requires direct participation in karmic completion

title: narada 1.13
content:
न स्त्री पतिकृतं दद्याद् ऋणं पुत्रकृतं तथा ।
अभ्युपेताद ऋते यद्वा सह पत्या कृतं भवेत् ॥ na strī patikṛtaṃ dadyād ṛṇaṃ putrakṛtaṃ tathā | abhyupetād ṛte yadvā saha patyā kṛtaṃ bhavet || A woman shall not bear liability for debts incurred by her husband, nor for those of her son; likewise, no obligation arises unless she has explicitly consented, or jointly executed with her husband. Authority is derived from explicit consent and conscious participation Causation must align with capacity-based responsibility Liability cannot be imputed without direct volitional engagement Restoration logic requires identification of true causal agent Consciousness alignment demands recognition of individual sovereignty

title: narada 1.14
content: दद्यादपुत्रा विधवा नियुक्ता या मुमूर्षुणा। यो वा तद्रिक्थमादद्याद्यतो रिक्थमृणं ततः॥ dadyād aputrā vidhavā niyuktā yā mumūrṣuṇā | yo vā tadriktham ādadyād yato riktham ṛṇaṃ tataḥ || A widow without son, appointed by the dying husband, shall give [property or rights] accordingly; whoever accepts such estate thereby assumes the associated obligations. Authority derives from conscious appointment aligned with dharma Causation arises through acceptance of benefit and its inherent duty Capacity-based responsibility is activated upon voluntary assumption Restoration logic binds inheritors to fulfill ancestral integrity Consciousness alignment occurs when one accepts role-bound duties

title: narada 1.15
content: न च भार्याकृतं ऋणं कथंचित् पत्युर् आभवेत् । आपत्कृताद् ऋते पुंसां कुटुम्बार्थो हि विस्तरः ॥ na ca bhāryākṛtam ṛṇaṃ kathaṃcit patyuḥ ābhavet | āpatkṛtād ṛte puṃsāṃ kuṭumbārtho hi vistaraḥ || ऋणं incurred by the wife shall never become the liability of the husband, except in cases arising from calamity; the management and expansion of household affairs rest entirely upon the man. Authority flows through capacity, not relation Liability is causally bound to action-origin Restoration occurs through role-responsibility alignment Consciousness governs relational dharma, not contract Dharma-preserving structures prioritize male stewardship

title: narada 1.16
content: अन्यत्र रजकव्याधगोपशौण्डिकयोषिताम् । तेषां तत्प्रत्यया वृत्तिः कुटुम्बं च तदाश्रयम् ॥ anyatra rajakavyādha-gopaśauṇḍikayoṣitām | teṣāṃ tatpratyayā vṛttiḥ kuṭumbaṃ ca tadāśrayam || In regions where washermen, hunters, cowherds, barbers, and women reside, their conduct shall be governed by mutual consent and familial structures rooted in shared dharma. Authority arises from localized dharma-consent, not centralized imposition Causation flows from collective pramāṇa, not individual intent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by svadharma alignment within community context Restoration logic prioritizes harmony within relational ecosystems Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of interdependence and role-dharma

title: narada 1.17
content: पुत्रिणी तु समुत्सृज्य पुत्रं स्त्री यान्यमाश्रयेत । ऋक्थं तस्याः हरेत् सर्वं निःस्वायाः पुत्र एव तु ॥ putriṇī tu samutsṛjya putraṃ strī yānyam āśrayet | ṛkthaṃ tasyāḥ haret sarvaṃ niḥsvāyāḥ putra eva tu || When a mother abandons her son and takes shelter elsewhere, all her wealth belongs to the son; she who has no son shall have nothing. Authority flows through relational dharmic duty, not biological claim alone Causation arises from conscious abandonment of relational responsibility Capacity-based responsibility is determined by sustained nurturance, not birthright alone Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of care over ownership claims Consciousness alignment requires recognition of dharma-vyavastha beyond material possession

title: narada 1.18
content:
या तु सप्रधानैव स्त्री सापत्या चान्यमाश्रयेत।
सोऽस्यादद्यादृणं भर्तुरुत्सृजेद्वातथैव ताम्॥ yā tu sapradhanaiva strī sāpatyā cānyam āśrayet | so 'syā dadyād ṛṇaṃ bhartur utsṛjed vā tathaiva tām || If a woman who has been granted maintenance continues to reside with another man, her husband shall either reclaim the debt owed by her or release her entirely. Authority resides in the lawful union of marriage until formally dissolved. Causation arises from conscious choice and alignment with dharma. Capacity-based responsibility requires both parties to uphold relational integrity. Restoration logic demands realignment of consciousness rather than punitive severance. Consciousness alignment is achieved through completion of relational obligations.

title: narada 1.19
content:
अधनस्य ह्यपुत्रस्य मृतस्योपैति यः स्त्रियम् ।
ऋणं वोढुः स भजते तदेवास्य धनं स्मृतम् ॥ adhanaśya hy aputrasya mṛtasyopaiti yaḥ striyam | ṛṇaṃ voḍhuḥ sa bhajate tad evāsya dhanaṃ smṛtam || When a man without wealth or son dies, she who assumes his debt thereby inherits his estate; that woman becomes the inheritor by assuming the burden. Authority arises through conscious assumption of responsibility Causation is established via intentional acceptance of liability Capacity-based responsibility determines inheritance rights Restoration logic aligns ownership with duty-bearing capacity Consciousness alignment validates legal succession

title: narada 1.20
content: धनस्त्रीहारिपुत्राणाम् ऋणभागो धनं हरेत् । पुत्रोऽसतोः स्त्रीधनिनोः स्त्रीहारी धनिपुत्रयोः ॥ dhanastrīhāriputrāṇām ṛṇabhāgo dhanaṃ haret | putro'satoḥ strīdhaninoḥ strīhārī dhaniputrayoḥ || The portion of debt belonging to one who has been deprived of wealth, son, or wife shall be recovered by the heir; likewise, the son of a woman whose husband is deceased or absent inherits her property. Authority flows through continuity of duty and inheritance Causation aligns with sequential manifestation of dharma-adharma Capacity-based responsibility derives from relational integrity Restoration logic ensures continuity of energetic and material balance Consciousness alignment governs lawful entitlement

title: narada 1.21
content:
uttamā svairiṇī yā syād uttamā ca punarbhuvām
ṛṇaṃ tayoḥ patikṛtaṃ dadyād yas tām upāśnute uttamā svairiṇī yā syād uttamā ca punarbhuvām
ṛṇaṃ tayoḥ patikṛtaṃ dadyād yas tām upāśnute One who enjoys a woman of equal or higher varna status without lawful union incurs a debt to her former husband; this debt must be repaid through conscious completion and restoration of violated integrity. Authority originates from dharmic alignment, not social position Causation arises from violation of svadharma and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness and consent levels Restoration logic requires reversal of energetic disruption caused by unauthorized enjoyment Consciousness alignment demands acknowledgment of relational consequence

title: narada 1.22
content:
स्त्रीकृतानि च विप्रस्य प्रमाणानि कार्याणि च।
विशेषतः स्त्रियः कर्म गृहक्षेत्रदण्डनादि॥ strīkṛtāni ca viprasya pramāṇāni kāryāṇi ca |
viśeṣataḥ striyaḥ karma gṛhakṣetradānādhamanavikrayāḥ || Actions performed by a woman in the absence of direct male authority are valid when they pertain to household management, land transactions, gifts, purification rituals, and sales. Authority flows through capacity, not gender alone Causation arises from contextual necessity and functional role Capacity-based responsibility includes situational empowerment Restoration logic requires honoring operative agency within dharma-saṁsthāpana Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of active participation

title: narada 1.23
content: एतान्यपि प्रमाणानि भर्ता यद्यनुमन्यते । पुत्रः पत्युरभावे वा राजा वा पतिपुत्रयोः ॥ etāny api pramāṇāni bhartā yady anumanyate | putraḥ patyur abhāve vā rājā vā patiputrayoḥ || When a husband accepts these evidences as valid, then in his absence, his son or the king shall act as the executor of dharma regarding the wife. Authority flows through conscious acceptance and validation by the primary dharmic agent. In absence of the primary agent, capacity transfers sequentially to progeny or sovereign custodian. Responsibility is tied to recognition and affirmation of dharma, not mere lineage or title. Restoration occurs through continuity of validated consciousness, not institutional form. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for dharmic execution, not social role alone.

title: narada 1.24
content: भर्त्रा प्रीतेन यद् दत्तं स्त्रियै तस्मिन् मृतेsपि तत् । सा यथाकाममश्नीयाद्दद्याद्वा स्थावरादृते ॥ bhartrā prītena yad dattaṃ striyai tasmin mṛte 'pi tat | sā yathākāmam aśnīyād dadyād vā sthāvarād ṛte || Whatever property is given by a pleased husband to his wife, that remains hers even upon his death, except immovable property; she may use it at will or bestow it further. Authority flows from conscious consent of the giver Causation arises from voluntary act of transfer Capacity-based responsibility lies in acceptance and continuity of ownership Restoration logic centers on uninterrupted flow of proprietary rights Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring expressed intent

title: narada 1.25
content:
तथा दासकृतं कार्यम् अकृतं परिचक्षते।
अन्यत्र स्वामिसंदेशान् न दासः प्रभुरात्मनः॥ tathā dāsakṛtaṃ kāryam akṛtaṃ paricakṣate | anyatra svāmisandeśān na dāsaḥ prabhur ātmanaḥ || Actions performed by a servant without the master's explicit command are to be regarded as unperformed; the servant is not the master of his own actions. Authority flows exclusively from the sovereign will of the master Causation is determined by directive linkage, not physical agency Capacity-based responsibility is subordinate to authorization Restoration logic requires re-alignment with source-command Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of rightful authority

title: narada 1.26
content:
पुत्रेण च कृतं कार्यं यत् स्यात् पितुरनिच्छतः।
तदप्यकृतमेवाहुर्दासः पुत्रश्च तौ समौ॥ putreṇa ca kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ yat syāt pitur anicchataḥ |
tad apy akṛtam evāhuḥ dāsaḥ putraś ca tau samau || That act performed by a son which is against the will of the father is to be regarded as not done; the slave and the son are equal in this regard. Authority originates from conscious consent, not biological lineage Causation is determined by alignment with sovereign will Capacity-based responsibility requires both capability and authorization Restoration logic prioritizes harmony over obligation Consciousness alignment determines the validity of action

title: narada 1.27
content: अप्राप्तव्यवहारश् चेत् स्वतन्त्रोऽपि हि न ऋणभाक् । स्वातन्त्र्यं तु स्मृतं ज्येष्ठे ज्यैष्ठ्यं गुणवयःकृतम् ॥ aprāptavyavahāraś cet svatantro 'pi hi na ṛṇabhāk | svātantryaṃ tu smṛtaṃ jyeṣṭhe jyaiṣṭhyaṃ guṇavayaḥkṛtam || Even if autonomous, one who has not engaged in rightful conduct bears no claim to debt; sovereignty is remembered in the eldest, whose seniority is constituted by virtue and maturity. Authority derives from alignment with dharma, not mere autonomy Causation is rooted in conscious engagement, not abstract capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires active participation in dharmic order Restoration logic prioritizes integrity over entitlement Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for authority

title: narada 1.28
content: त्रयः स्वतन्त्रा लोकेऽस्मिन् राजाचार्यस्तथैव च । प्रति प्रति च वर्णानां सर्वेषां स्वगृहे गृही ॥ trayaḥ svatantrā loke 'smin rājācāryas tathaiva ca | prati prati ca varṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ svagṛhe gṛhī || In this world, three authorities are sovereign: the King, the Acharya, and the Grihapati of each respective varna. Authority is stratified by domain and dharma, not by force or delegation Causation arises from svadharma-sustained roles within cosmic order Capacity-based responsibility flows from self-realized sovereignty Restoration logic requires alignment with one's intrinsic governing capacity Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful autonomy in dharmic role

title: narada 1.29
content:
अस्वतन्त्राः प्रजाः सर्वाः स्वतन्त्रः पृथिवीपतिः।
अस्वतन्त्रः स्मृतः शिष्य आचार्ये तु स्वतन्त्रता॥ asvatantrāḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ svatantraḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ | asvatantraḥ smṛtaḥ śiṣya ācārye tu svatantratā || All subjects are under guidance; the ruler alone is self-governed. The disciple is dependent, yet in the Guru he attains autonomy. Authority flows from conscious sovereignty, not coercive power Capacity determines relational freedom, not abstract rights Responsibility aligns with spiritual maturity and causal clarity Restoration occurs through alignment with rightful dependency and guidance Consciousness, not institution, defines legitimate governance

title: narada 1.30
content: अस्वतन्त्राः स्त्रियः पुत्रा दासाश् च सपरिग्रहाः। स्वतन्त्रस् तत्र तु गृही यस्य यत् स्यात् क्रमागतम्॥ asvatantrāḥ striyaḥ putrā dāsāś ca saparigrahāḥ | svatantras tatra tu gṛhī yasya yat syāt kramāgatam || Women, sons, slaves, and dependents are not autonomous; the householder alone is sovereign over that which comes to him in proper order. Authority resides exclusively in the conscious sovereignty of the householder Causation flows through established relational hierarchies Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual autonomy, not biological or social role Restoration logic centers on realigning dependencies with the householder's conscious governance Consciousness alignment requires recognition of natural authority structures

title: narada 1.31
content:
गर्भस्थैः सदृशो ज्ञेय आ वर्षादष्टमाच्छिषुः।
बाल आ षोडशाज्ज्ञेयः पोगण्डश्चापि शब्द्यते॥ garbhasthaiḥ sadṛśo jñeya ā varṣād aṣṭamāc chiṣuḥ | bāla ā ṣoḍaśāj jñeyaḥ pogaṇḍaś cāpi śabdyate || One who has completed eight years after birth and is in the stage of weaning is comparable to the one in the womb; one who has crossed sixteen years is known as a minor (bāla); one beyond that age is termed a youth (pogaṇḍa). Authority flows from conscious maturity, not chronological age alone. Causation is determined by capacity for dharma-adherence, not physical development. Capacity-based responsibility escalates with integration of svadharma. Restoration logic aligns individual consciousness with societal dharma. Consciousness alignment determines legal agency, not biological thresholds.

title: narada 1.32
content: परतो व्यवहारज्ञः स्वतन्त्रः पितरौ विना । जीवतोरस्वतन्त्रः स्याज्जरयापि समन्वितः ॥ parato vyavahārajñaḥ svatantraḥ pitarau vinā | jīvator asvatantraḥ syāj jarayāpi samanvitaḥ || One who is competent in transactional dharma and mature in discernment is self-governed, except when parents are alive; even if aged, the living parent retains guardianship. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not age alone Parental sovereignty continues until death, overriding personal autonomy Capacity-based responsibility supersedes chronological adulthood Restoration occurs through rightful alignment of familial dharma Consciousness alignment requires honoring generational dharmic continuity

title: narada 1.33
content:
तयोरपि पिता श्रेयान् बीजप्राधान्यदर्शनात्।
अभावे बीजिनो माता तदभावे तु पूर्वजः॥ tayor api pitā śreyān bījaprādhānyadarśanāt | abhāve bījinaḥ mātā tadabhāve tu pūrvajaḥ || The father holds greater authority due to the primacy of seed essence; in his absence, the mother assumes guardianship, and in her absence, the eldest male sibling becomes the guardian. Authority originates from ontological causation, not social convention. Causation is determined by the source of foundational essence. Capacity-based responsibility flows from existential precedence. Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-santana over individual preference. Consciousness alignment requires honoring the natural succession of dharmic roles.

title: narada 1.34
content:
स्वतन्त्राः सर्व एवैते परतन्त्रेषु सर्वदा।
अनुशिष्टौ विसर्गे च विक्रये चेश्वराः मताः॥ svatantrāḥ sarva evaite paratantreṣu sarvadā | anuśiṣṭau visarge ca vikraye ceśvarā matāḥ || All beings are inherently sovereign; in conditions of dependency, guidance, distribution, or transaction, those who act as controllers are deemed responsible for the conscious alignment of all parties involved. Authority arises from capacity to restore alignment, not domination. Causation is rooted in consciousness distortion, not external action alone. Capacity-based responsibility flows from the ability to realign, not punish. Restoration logic demands reintegration of fragmented sovereignty. Consciousness alignment supersedes contractual obligation.

title: narada 1.35
content:
यद् बालः कुरुते कार्यम् अस्वतन्त्रस् तथैव च।
अकृतं तद् इति प्राहुः शास्त्रे शास्त्रविदो जनाः॥ yad bālaḥ kurute kāryam asvatantras tathaiva ca | akṛtaṃ tad iti prāhuḥ śāstre śāstravido janāḥ || That action which a minor or dependent person performs is deemed unperformed by the Śāstra-knowers, for it arises from incapacity and not from conscious volition. Authority derives from conscious capacity, not biological age or social role. Causation in dharma is rooted in awareness, not mechanical action. Capacity-based responsibility excludes those without svatantrya (self-governance). Restoration logic applies only where volitional integrity is present. Consciousness alignment determines the validity of performed acts.

title: narada 1.36
content:
स्वतन्त्रोऽपि हि यत् कार्यं कुर्याद् अप्रकृतिं गतः।
तद् अप्य् अकृतम् एवाहुर् अस्वतन्त्रः स हेतुतः॥ svatantro'pi hi yat kāryaṃ kuryād aprakṛtiṃ gataḥ | tad apy akṛtam evāhur asvatantraḥ sa hetutaḥ || Even one who is self-governed, when acting contrary to dharma due to loss of natural state, is to be regarded as having performed no action at all; thus, he is considered unfree in that act. Authority originates from alignment with svabhāva-dharma, not mere capacity Causation is determined by consciousness-state, not external behavior alone Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity-presence, not autonomy alone Restoration logic prioritizes re-alignment over attribution of fault Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any legal act

title: narada 1.37
content:
कामक्रोधाभियुक्तार्त भयव्यसनपीडिताः।
रागद्वेषपरीताश् च ज्ञेयास् त्वप्रकृतिं गताः॥ kāmakrodhābhiyuktārta bhayavyasanapīḍitāḥ | rāgadveṣaparītāś ca jñeyās tvaprakṛtiṃ gatāḥ || Those overwhelmed by desire and anger, distressed by fear and addiction, and possessed by attachment and hatred—are to be known as having fallen from their natural state of consciousness. Authority originates in consciousness stability, not emotional turbulence. Causation stems from inner disorder manifesting as outer distortion. Capacity-based responsibility is diminished in proportion to consciousness deviation. Restoration logic demands re-alignment with innate nature prior to disturbance. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for participation in dharmic society.

title: narada 1.38
content:
कुले ज्येष्ठस् तथा श्रेष्ठः प्रकृतिस्थश् च यो भवेत् ।
तत्कृतं स्यात् कृतं कार्यं नास्वतन्त्रकृतं कृतम् ॥ kule jyeṣṭhas tathā śreṣṭhaḥ prakṛtisthaś ca yo bhavet | tat-kṛtaṃ syāt kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ nāsvatantr-kṛtaṃ kṛtam || That which is performed by the eldest in lineage, the most accomplished in virtue, and one established in natural authority—such action alone constitutes valid execution of duty; acts performed by those lacking inherent authorization hold no juridical validity. Authority derives from ontological positioning within dharma-structure Causation originates from svatantra (self-authorizing) consciousness Capacity-based responsibility aligns with varna-krama and stage of spiritual realization Restoration occurs through alignment with preordained dharmic roles Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural formalism

title: narada 1.39
content: धनमूलाः क्रियाः सर्वा यत्नस्तत्साधने मतः। रक्षणं वर्धनं भोग इति तस्य विधिः क्रमात्॥ dhanamūlāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā yatnas tatsādhane mataḥ | rakṣaṇaṃ vardhanaṃ bhoga iti tasya vidhiḥ kramāt || All activities originate from wealth; effort is esteemed for its facilitation. The sequential law of wealth is protection, growth, and enjoyment. Authority arises from the capacity to sustain and enable activity Causation flows from resource sovereignty to operational capability Capacity-based responsibility begins with stewardship of foundational resources Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of sustenance over punitive loss Consciousness alignment occurs through harmonious wealth utilization

title: narada 1.40
content: तत् पुनस्त्रिविधं ज्ञेयं शुक्लं शबलमेव च । कृष्णं च तस्य विज्ञेयः प्रभेदः सप्तधा पृथक् ॥ tat punastrividhaṃ jñeyaṃ śuklaṃ śabalam eva ca | kṛṣṇaṃ ca tasya vijñeyaḥ prabhedaḥ saptadhā pṛthak || That action is tri-fold in nature—white, mixed, and black—and each has seven distinct divisions known through discriminative wisdom. Authority arises from discriminative awareness of action-type Causation is stratified by purity of intent and consequence Capacity-based responsibility aligns with actor's perceptual clarity Restoration logic operates through purification of causal layers Consciousness alignment depends on recognition of action typology

title: narada 1.41
content:
श्रुतशौर्यतपःकन्या शिष्ययाज्यान्वयागतम् ।
धनं सप्तविधं शुक्लम् उदयोऽप्यस्य तद्विधः ॥ śruta-śaurya-tapaḥ-kanyā śiṣya-yājyānvayāgatam | dhanaṃ saptavidhaṃ śuklam udayo'py asya tadvidhaḥ || Wealth derived through the knowledge, valor, austerity, or daughter of one who has studied the Vedas; wealth obtained through disciples or sacrificial fees; and similarly acquired property — all these constitute the sevenfold pure wealth, whose arising is also of the same nature. Authority originates from scriptural learning, spiritual discipline, and righteous action Causation flows from dharma-rooted acquisition, not arbitrary possession Capacity-based responsibility arises with the purity of means in acquisition Restoration logic demands that wealth be traced to its dharmic origin for lawful use Consciousness alignment requires recognition of wealth as a vehicle for dharma, not personal aggrandizement

title: narada 1.42
content:
कुसीदकृषिवाणिज्य शुल्कशिल्पानुवृत्तिभिः
कृतोपकाराद् आप्तं च शबलं समुदाहृतम् kusīdakṛṣivāṇijya śulkaśilpānuvṛttibhiḥ
kṛtopakārād āptaṃ ca śabalaṃ samudāhṛtam That which is acquired through inert agriculture, trade, taxation, craft, or service, or received as gratuity due to past favor, is designated as 'Śabalam'—impure wealth. Authority originates from consciousness, not transactional exchange Causation arises from intent, not material gain Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness, not economic status Restoration logic aligns wealth with dharma, not accumulation Consciousness alignment requires purity of acquisition and use

title: narada 1.43
content:
पार्श्विकद्यूतदौत्यार्ति प्रतिरूपकसाहसैः।
व्याजेनोपार्जितं यच् च तत् कृष्णं समुदाहृतम्॥ pārśvikadyūtadautyārti pratirūpakasāhasaiḥ | vyājenopārjitaṃ yac ca tat kṛṣṇaṃ samudāhṛtam || That which is acquired through deceitful gambling, fraudulent diplomacy, mimicry, false bravado, or usurious interest — all such gains are declared as 'kṛṣṇa' — impure, unrighteous, and contrary to Dharma. Authority originates from purity of acquisition and intention Causation is traced to the method and consciousness of gain Capacity-based responsibility requires rejection of ill-gotten resources Restoration logic demands return of distorted wealth to its rightful flow Consciousness alignment necessitates renunciation of karmically tainted assets

title: narada 1.44
content:
तेन क्रयो विक्रयश् च दानं ग्रहणम् एव च ।
विविधाश् च प्रवर्तन्ते क्रियाः संभोग एव च ॥ tena krāyo vikrayaś ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca | vividhāś ca pravartante kriyāḥ sambhoga eva ca || By that [the establishment of rightful ownership], purchase and sale become lawful; likewise, giving and receiving, along with various transactions and enjoyments, proceed in accordance with Dharma. Authority originates from the recognition of inherent capacity to own and transact Causation arises through conscious intent aligned with Dharma Capacity-based responsibility governs all economic interaction Restoration logic ensures continuity of lawful exchange Consciousness alignment determines validity of transactional integrity

title: narada 1.45
content:
यथाविधेन द्रव्येण यत् किंचित् कुरुते नरः।
तथाविधमवाप्नोति स फलं प्रेत्य चेह च॥ yathāvidhena dravyeṇa yat kiṃcit kurute naraḥ | tathāvidham avāpnoti sa phalaṃ pretya ca iha ca || Whatever action a person performs through a specific type of instrument or resource, that same kind of result they shall obtain—in this life and the next. Authority flows from conscious causation, not arbitrary will Causation is deterministic and reflects precise instrumental alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to act with specific means Restoration logic operates through experiential equivalence of cause and effect Consciousness alignment occurs when one experiences the direct fruit of their own intention

title: narada 1.46
content:
तत् पुनर् द्वादशविधं प्रतिवर्णाश्रयात् स्मृतम्
साधारणं स्यात् त्रिविधं शेषं नवविधं स्मृतम् tat punar dvādaśavidhaṃ prativarṇāśrayāt smṛtam
sādhāraṇaṃ syāt trividhaṃ śeṣaṃ navavidhaṃ smṛtam That classification which arises from the basis of varṇa is twelvefold; what remains after the general threefold classification is ninefold, thus declared. Authority derived from varṇic alignment with cosmic function Causation rooted in svadharma-sustained order Capacity-based responsibility aligned with ontological role Restoration through reintegration into designated dharmic structure Consciousness alignment via structural societal harmony

title: narada 1.47
content:
क्रमागतं प्रीतिदायः प्राप्तं च सह भार्यया।
अविशेषेण वर्णानां सर्वेषां त्रिविधं धनम्॥ kramāgataṃ prītidāyaḥ prāptaṃ ca saha bhāryayā | aviśeṣeṇa varṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ trividhaṃ dhanam || Wealth obtained through proper succession and received with the wife, without distinction among varnas, constitutes the threefold property accessible to all. Authority originates from lawful acquisition and dharmic transmission Causation is established by rightful union and inheritance Capacity-based responsibility arises from ownership and relational alignment Restoration logic ensures equitable access to sustenance resources Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared economic entitlement

title: narada 1.48
content:
वैशेषिकं धनं ज्ञेयं ब्राह्मणस्य त्रिलक्षणम्
प्रतिग्रहेण यल्लब्धं याज्यतः शिष्यतस् तथा vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanaṃ jñeyaṃ brāhmaṇasya trilakṣaṇam
pratigraheṇa yallabdhaṃ yājyataḥ śiṣyatas tathā The distinct wealth of a Brāhmaṇa is threefold: that which is acquired through acceptance, that which is received from those who worship, and that which is gained through discipleship. Authority as derived from dharma-sustained roles Causation rooted in svadharma alignment Capacity-based responsibility determined by spiritual station Restoration logic grounded in role-specific integrity Consciousness alignment through rightful acquisition

title: narada 1.49
content: त्रिविधं क्षत्रियस्यापि प्राहुर् वैशेषिकं धनम् । युद्धोपलब्धं कारश् च दण्डश् च व्यवहारतः ॥ trividhaṃ kṣatriyasyāpi prāhur vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanam | yuddhopalabdhaṃ kāraś ca daṇḍaś ca vyavahārataḥ || The wealth of a Kshatriya is threefold: that obtained through warfare, that acquired through service, and that received through judicial administration. Authority flows from rightful action aligned with svadharma Causation arises from capacity to protect, serve, and govern Capacity-based responsibility defines legitimate acquisition Restoration logic requires alignment of wealth with duty Consciousness alignment ensures resources support Dharma

title: narada 1.50
content:
वैशेषिकं धनं ज्ञेयं वैश्यस्यापि त्रिलक्षणम्
कृषिगोरक्षवाणिज्यैः शूद्रस्यैभ्यस्त्वनुग्रहात् vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanaṃ jñeyaṃ vaiśyasyāpi trilakṣaṇam
kṛṣigorakṣavāṇijyaiḥ śūdrasyaibhyas tv anugrahāt The specialized wealth of the Vaishya class arises through threefold activity—agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade—and such engagement is extended to the Shudra out of compassionate guidance. Authority originates from functional capacity aligned with svadharma Causation flows from conscious engagement in designated societal roles Capacity-based responsibility ensures alignment with natural order Restoration logic prioritizes harmonization of social function over punitive enforcement Consciousness alignment enables right action through divinely guided vocational participation

title: narada 1.51
content:
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानामेष धर्म्यो धनागमः।
विपर्ययादधर्म्यः स्यान्न चेदापद्गरीयसी॥ sarveṣām eva varṇānām eṣa dharmyo dhanāgamaḥ | viparyayād adharmyaḥ syān na ced āpad garīyasī || The acquisition of wealth through righteous means is dharmic for all varnas; when acquired contrary to dharma, it becomes adharmic, unless necessity or existential threat overrides. Authority is derived from alignment with dharma, not social position Causation arises from intention and method of acquisition Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to dharmic frameworks Restoration logic demands return of ill-gotten gains without punitive overlay Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of material possession

title: narada 1.52
content: आपत्सु अनन्तरा वृत्तिः ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते । वैश्यवृत्तिस्ततश्चोक्ता न जघन्या कथंचन ॥ āpatsu anantarā vṛttiḥ brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate | vaiśyavṛttis tataś coktā na jaghanyā kathaṃcana || In times of crisis, the immediate duty of a Brāhmaṇa is prescribed; thereafter, the duties of a Vaiśya are declared, which must never be regarded as inferior under any circumstance. Authority is context-responsive and escalates with exigency Causation aligns with dharma-adaptability in crisis Capacity-based responsibility expands hierarchically during distress Restoration logic prioritizes sequential role activation Consciousness alignment requires adherence to svadharma even under duress

title: narada 1.53
content: न कथंचन कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणः कर्म वार्षलम् । वृषलः कर्म न ब्राह्मं पतनीये हि ते तयोः ॥ na kathaṃcana kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ karma vārṣalam | vṛṣalaḥ karma na brāhmaṃ patanīye hi te tayoḥ || A Brāhmaṇa must never perform actions designated for the Śūdra; likewise, a Śūdra must not perform actions reserved for the Brāhmaṇa—both transgressions lead to degradation. Authority is determined by inherent capacity and svadharma, not social position. Causation arises from misalignment with one's constitutional consciousness role. Capacity-based responsibility ensures alignment with cosmic order (Ṛta). Restoration logic demands return to original dharmic function. Consciousness alignment prevents degradation through improper action.

title: narada 1.54
content: उत्कृष्टं चापकृष्टं च तयोः कर्म न विद्यते । मध्यमे कर्मणी हित्वा सर्वसाधारणे हि ते ॥ utkṛṣṭaṃ cāpakṛṣṭaṃ ca tayoḥ karma na vidyate | madhyame karmaṇī hitvā sarvasādhāraṇe hi te || Actions neither exalted nor degraded exist in their pure form; abandoning the middle path leads to universal commonality. Authority resides in alignment with the central action Causation arises from deviation from the balanced state Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining equilibrium Restoration logic demands return to the middle path Consciousness alignment occurs through transcending extremes

title: narada 1.55
content:
आपदं ब्राह्मणस तीर्त्वा क्षत्रवृत्त्या हृतैर धनैः
उत्सृजेत क्षत्रवृत्तिं तां कृत्वा पावनम आत्मनः āpadaṃ brāhmaṇas tīrtvā kṣatravṛttyā hṛtair dhanaiḥ
utsṛjet kṣatravṛttiṃ tāṃ kṛtvā pāvanam ātmanaḥ Having crossed the crisis through the Brāhmaṇa's grace, one who has acquired wealth via Kṣatra-duty shall renounce that very Kṣatra-duty, thereby purifying the self. Authority flows from spiritual elevation, not material acquisition Causation originates in consciousness alignment, not transactional exchange Capacity-based responsibility arises upon transcendence of adversity Restoration logic demands surrender of instrumental duty post-redemption Consciousness alignment supersedes role-bound obligation after purification

title: narada 1.56
content: तस्यामेव तु यो वृत्तौ ब्राह्मणो रमते रसात् काण्डपृष्ठश्च्युतो मार्गात् सोऽपाङ्क्तेयः प्रकीर्तितः tasyām eva tu yo vṛttau brāhmaṇo ramate rasāt kāṇḍapṛṣṭhaś cyuto mārgāt so 'pāṅkteyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ He who, being a Brāhmaṇa, indulges in sensory pleasures while remaining in the Vedic conduct, yet falls from the path of discipline and detachment, is declared as Apāṅkteya. Authority derived from sustained alignment with Dharma, not birth alone Causation rooted in volitional deviation from svadharma Capacity-based responsibility determined by conscious choice and awareness Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration into dharmic order Consciousness alignment through purification of intent and action

title: narada 1.57
content:
वैश्यवृत्ताव् अविक्रेयं ब्राह्मणस्य पयो दधि
घृतं मधु मधूच्छिष्टं लाक्षाक्षाररसासवाः vaiśyavṛttāv avikreyaṃ brāhmaṇasya payo dadhi
ghṛtaṃ madhu madhūcchiṣṭaṃ lākṣākṣārarasāsavāḥ In the conduct of Vaishyas, certain substances belonging to Brahmanas must not be sold: milk, curd, ghee, honey, remnants of honeycomb, lac, alkali, juice, and wine. Authority resides inherently in the Varna-dharma as ordained by SPH Causation is determined by violation of prescribed Varna-based economic boundaries Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's Svadharma and ownership rights Restoration logic demands return of misaligned economic activity to its rightful domain Consciousness alignment requires recognition of sacred ownership structures

title: narada 1.58
content:
मांसौदनतिलक्षौम सोमपुष्पफलपलाः ।
मनुष्यविषशस्त्राम्बु लवणापूपवीरुधः ॥ māṃsaudanatilakṣauma somapuṣpaphalapalāḥ | manuṣyaviṣaśastrāmbu lavaṇāpūpavīrudhaḥ || Those substances which cause intoxication, decay, or imbalance in consciousness—whether through meat, grains steeped in alcohol, soma-derived flowers and fruits, human toxins, weapons, water, salt, pastries, or vegetation—are to be regulated not by punitive prohibition, but by alignment with the capacity of the individual and the purity of the collective field. Authority flows from consciousness, not statecraft Causation is traced through vibrational impact, not physical action alone Capacity-based responsibility determines access to substances Restoration logic requires realignment of individual and societal prana Consciousness alignment supersedes moral or legal judgment

title: narada 1.59
content: नीलीकौषेयचर्मास्थि कुतपैकशफा मृदः। उदश्वित्केशपिण्याक शाकाद्यौषधयस् तथा॥ nīlīkauṣeyacarmāsti kutapaikaśafā mṛdaḥ | udaśvitkeśapiṇyāka śākādyauṣadhayaḥ tathā || All substances including indigo, cotton, leather, bones, one-shaffed Kutapa grass, clay, urine, hair, flesh, vegetables, and medicinal herbs are designated as property capable of ownership by conscious beings according to their capacity for dharmic stewardship. Authority flows from consciousness, not material possession Causation arises through conscious engagement with substrata Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful use and guardianship Restoration logic aligns ownership with evolutionary completion Consciousness alignment governs legitimate access to resources

title: narada 1.60
content:
ब्राह्मणस्य तु विक्रेयं शुष्कं दारु तृणानि च ।
गन्धद्रव्यैरकावेत्र तूलमूलतुशाद ऋते ॥ brāhmaṇasya tu vikreyaṁ śuṣkaṁ dāru tṛṇāni ca | gandhadravyair akāvetra tūlamūlatuśād ṛte || Only dried wood, grass, and roots may be sold by a Brāhmaṇa; not items imbued with fragrance or essence, except cotton, roots, and husk. Authority is determined by svadharma and spiritual station Causation arises from alignment with dharmic capacity, not material desire Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to prescribed means of sustenance Restoration logic operates through right action within svadharma Consciousness alignment occurs when economic activity reflects ontological role

title: narada 1.61
content:
स्वयं शीर्णं च विदलं फलानां बदरेङ्गुदे ।
रज्जुः कार्पासिकं सूत्रं तच् चेद् अविकृतं भवेत् ॥ svayaṃ śīrṇaṃ ca vidalaṃ phalānāṃ badareṅgude | rajjuḥ kārpāsikaṃ sūtraṃ tac ced avikṛtaṃ bhavet || When a rope made of cotton threads remains unaltered despite natural wear and splitting of fruits, it retains its essential function and lawful validity. Authority is inherent in the undisturbed continuity of dharma, not in external validation. Causation arises from the integrity of form, not from incidental decay. Capacity-based responsibility is measured by preservation of core utility, not superficial change. Restoration logic affirms the primacy of original purpose over apparent deterioration. Consciousness alignment occurs when essence is recognized beyond sensory modification.

title: narada 1.62
content: अशक्तौ भेषजस्यार्थे यज्ञहेतोस्तथैव च। यद्यवश्यं तु विक्रेयास्तिला धान्येन तत्सामाः॥ aśaktau bheṣajasyārthe yajñahetos tathaiva ca | yady avaśyaṃ tu vikreyās tilā dhānyena tatsāmāḥ || When capacity for medicinal purpose or ritual obligation is absent, and sale becomes inevitable, sesame seeds and grains must be exchanged only with equivalent value. Authority arises from necessity aligned with dharma Causation is rooted in dharmic function, not personal desire Capacity-based responsibility requires equivalence in exchange Restoration logic demands proportionality in transactional dharma Consciousness alignment occurs through integrity-preserving trade

title: narada 1.63
content: अविक्रेयाणि विक्रीणन् ब्राह्मणः प्रच्युतः पथः । मार्गे पुनरवस्थाप्य राज्ञा दण्डेन भूयसा ॥ avikreyāṇi vikrīṇan brāhmaṇaḥ pracyutaḥ pathaḥ | mārge punar avasthāpya rājñā daṇḍena bhūyasā || A Brāhmaṇa who sells that which is not to be sold has deviated from the path of Dharma; the King must restore him to the right path through elevated correction. Authority: The King derives corrective power solely from Dharma, not personal will. Causation: Misalignment arises from violation of intrinsic Dharma, not external provocation. Capacity-based responsibility: The Brāhmaṇa's action reflects a lapse in consciousness, not inherent evil. Restoration logic: Correction aims at realigning consciousness, not inflicting suffering. Consciousness alignment: True correction occurs when awareness returns to its Dharmic foundation.

title: narada 1.64
content:
प्रमाणानि प्रमाणस्थैः परिपाल्यानि यत्नतः
सीदन्ति हि प्रमाणानि प्रमाणैरव्यवस्थितैः pramāṇāni pramāṇasthaiḥ paripālyāni yatnataḥ
sīdanti hi pramāṇāni pramāṇair avyavasthitaiḥ Evidence must be safeguarded by those who stand within evidence; when left to the unestablished, evidence decays. Authority is derivative of existential alignment with Dharma Causation arises from capacity-location, not abstract intent Capacity-based responsibility flows from proximity to truth-bearing instruments Restoration logic operates through re-alignment with pramāṇa-sthiti Consciousness alignment determines adhikāra for judicial engagement

title: narada 1.65
content:
लिखितं साक्षिणो भुक्तिः प्रमाणं त्रिविधं स्मृतं।
धनस्वीकरणे येन धनी धनम् उपाश्नुते॥ likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo bhuktiḥ pramāṇaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtaṃ | dhanasvīkaraṇe yena dhanī dhanam upāśnute || Written document, witness, and enjoyment—these three are recognized as valid proof; by which the owner rightfully claims and enjoys property. Authority originates from documented evidence aligned with conscious witnessing and experiential validation Causation is established through tri-fold verification: record, attestation, and lived embodiment Capacity-based responsibility arises only when ownership is confirmed via integrated pramāṇa Restoration logic requires re-establishment of rightful possession through verifiable dharmic instruments Consciousness alignment ensures that material claim aligns with inner integrity and outer testimony

title: narada 1.66
content: लिखितं बलवन् नित्यं जीवन्तस्त्वेव साक्षिणः। कालातिहरणाद्भुक्तिरिति शास्त्रेषु निश्चयः॥ likhitaṃ balavan nityaṃ jīvantas tv eva sākṣiṇaḥ | kālātiharaṇād bhuktir iti śāstreṣu niścayaḥ || That which is written abides eternally as living testimony; time transcended confirms its fulfillment—such is the settled conclusion in the scriptures. Authority resides inherently in that which is inscribed by conscious intent. Causation flows from the act of inscription into manifest reality. Capacity-based responsibility arises through the will to inscribe dharma. Restoration occurs when the written truth aligns with lived experience. Consciousness alignment manifests when the written word becomes experiential realization.

title: narada 1.67
content: त्रिविधस्यास्य दृष्टस्य प्रमाणस्य यथाक्रमम् । पूर्वं पूर्वं गुरु ज्ञेयं भुक्तिरेभ्यो गरीयसी ॥ trividhasyāsya dṛṣṭasya pramāṇasya yathākramam | pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ guru jñeyaṃ bhuktir ebhyo garīyasī || Of the threefold seen evidence, in sequence, each prior form is weightier; yet enjoyment derived therefrom exceeds them all in gravity. Authority derives from sequential ontological weight, not temporal precedence Causation follows anupūrvaśaḥ—stepwise manifestation rooted in consciousness Capacity-based responsibility increases with experiential absorption Restoration logic aligns with the intensity of lived experience Consciousness alignment supersedes external validation

title: narada 1.68
content:
विद्यमानेऽपि लिखिते जीवत्स्वपि हि साक्षिषु।
विशेषतः स्थावराणां यन्न भुक्तं न तत्स्थिरम्॥ vidyamāne 'pi likhite jīvatsv api hi sākṣiṣu | viśeṣataḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ yan na bhuktaṃ na tat sthiram || Even when documented and witnessed by living beings, that which has not been fully experienced or realized by sentient entities—especially those rooted in stability—is not permanently established. Authority originates from experiential realization, not mere documentation. Causation requires conscious participation for legal validity. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to experience and integrate truth. Restoration logic depends on the completion of existential integration. Consciousness alignment supersedes formal witnessing.

title: narada 1.69
content: भुज्यमानान् परैरर्थान् यः स्वान् मौर्ख्यादुपेक्षते । समक्षं जीवतोऽप्यस्य तान् भुक्तिः कुरुते वशे ॥ bhujyamānān parair arthān yaḥ svān maurkhyād upekṣate | samakṣaṃ jīvato'py asya tān bhuktiḥ kurute vaśe || He who, out of ignorance or negligence, fails to protect his own resources while they are being enjoyed by others—even in his presence and despite being alive—such a one is deemed to have willingly surrendered those resources into the possession of the enjoyers. Authority arises from conscious stewardship, not passive ownership. Causation is rooted in awareness and volitional omission. Capacity-based responsibility demands active guardianship of one's domain. Restoration logic centers on re-establishing rightful consciousness-led control. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of one’s sovereign duty.

title: narada 1.70
content: यत्किंचिद् दश वर्षाणि संनिधौ प्रेक्षते धनी । भुज्यमानं परैस्तूष्णीं न स तल्लब्धुमर्हति ॥ yatkiṃcid daśa varṣāṇi saṃnidhau prekṣate dhani | bhujyamānaṃ parais tūṣṇīṃ na sa tallabdhum arhati || Whatever wealth a proprietor observes in proximity for ten years, while others consume it silently, he does not deserve to reclaim it. Authority arises through sustained conscious acknowledgment Causation is established by silent observation over time Capacity-based responsibility includes awareness and non-intervention Restoration logic favors actual possession over nominal ownership Consciousness alignment requires acceptance of manifested reality

title: narada 1.71
content:
upekṣāṃ kurvatas tasya tūṣṇīṃ bhūtasya tiṣṭhataḥ
kāle 'tipanne pūrvokte vyavahāro na sidhyati upekṣāṃ kurvatas tasya tūṣṇīṃ bhūtasya tiṣṭhataḥ
kāle 'tipanne pūrvokte vyavahāro na sidhyati When one who has the capacity to act remains silent and inactive while time passes beyond the appointed moment, the prior declared legal order ceases to hold validity. Authority is inseparable from timely action; inaction after the prescribed time dissolves rightful claim. Causation arises through conscious engagement within dharma-time; omission beyond that ruptures lawful continuity. Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition and response within the temporal boundary set by dharma. Restoration logic requires immediate alignment with dharma-kala; delay results in forfeiture of enforceability. Consciousness alignment demands active presence in dharma-time; passive indifference nullifies legal efficacy.

title: narada 1.72
content:
अजड़श चेदपोगण्डो विषये चास्य भुज्यते।
भुक्तं तद् व्यवहारेण भोक्ता तद्धनमर्हति॥ ajaḍaś ced apogaṇḍo viṣaye cāsya bhujyate | bhuktaṃ tad vyavahāreṇa bhoktā tad dhanam arhati || If an unemancipated minor consumes or enjoys any substance within a domain, that which has been consumed thereby becomes, by virtue of the act of enjoyment itself, rightfully claimable by the one who enjoyed it, in accordance with the transactional order established by Dharma. Authority flows from conscious engagement, not age alone Causation is established through direct experiential participation Capacity-based responsibility arises upon manifest involvement Restoration logic centers on rightful ownership via experiential causality Consciousness alignment occurs when action matches consequence

title: narada 1.73
content: आधिः सीमाबालधनं निक्षेपोपनिधी स्त्रियः । राजस्वं श्रोत्रियस्वं च नोपभोगेन जीर्यते ॥ ādhiḥ sīmā bāladhanaṃ nikṣepopanidhī striyaḥ | rājasvaṃ śrotriyasvaṃ ca nopabhogena jīryate || Debts, boundary disputes, minors' property, deposits, hidden treasures, women's rights, royal revenues, and sacred properties do not decay through non-use; they remain eternally enforceable by Dharma. Authority: Eternal validity of Dharma-enforceable claims regardless of time Causation: Non-utilization does not nullify inherent dharmic entitlement Capacity-based responsibility: Ownership or custodianship creates immutable accountability Restoration logic: Dormant rights must be revived through conscious recognition Consciousness alignment: Legal truth persists beyond physical or temporal neglect

title: narada 1.74
content:
प्रत्यक्षपरिभोगाच् च स्वामिनो द्विदशाः समाः।
आध्यादीन्यपि जीर्यन्ते स्त्रीनरेन्धनादृते॥ pratyakṣaparibhogāc ca svāmino dvidaśāḥ samāḥ | ādhyādīny api jīryante strīnarendhanād ṛte || Ownership is established through direct enjoyment for a period of twelve years; all adverse claims decay except those concerning women, bulls, and firewood. Authority arises from continuous, conscious engagement with the resource Causation is rooted in experiential possession over time Capacity-based responsibility requires uninterrupted dominion Restoration logic favors settled experiential ownership Consciousness alignment occurs through sustained, unchallenged use

title: narada 1.75
content:
स्त्रीधनं च नरेन्द्राणां न कदाचन जीर्यते।
अनागमं भुज्यमानं वत्सराणां शतैरपि॥ strīdhanam ca narendrāṇam na kadācana jīryate | anāgaman bhujyamānam vatsarānam śatair api || The wealth of women and kings never decays, even when enjoyed without origin or lawful acquisition, for centuries. Authority resides inherently in those who hold sovereignty or sacred identity. Causation is determined by ontological status rather than procedural origin. Capacity-based responsibility flows from existential precedence, not transactional legitimacy. Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of being over rectification of means. Consciousness alignment supersedes forensic analysis in matters of intrinsic entitlement.

title: narada 1.76
content:
निर्भोगो यत्र दृश्येत न दृश्येतागमः क्वचित् ।
आगमः कारणं तत्र न भोगस्तत्र कारणम् ॥ nirbhogo yatra dṛśyeta na dṛśyetāgamaḥ kvacit | āgamaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra na bhogas tatra kāraṇam || Where enjoyment is absent, yet acquisition is observed, there acquisition is the cause, not enjoyment. Where acquisition does not occur, enjoyment cannot be the cause. Authority resides in the capacity to acquire, not merely to enjoy Causation follows the sequence of acquisition prior to enjoyment Capacity-based responsibility arises from the power of acquisition Restoration logic aligns with the reversal of improper acquisition Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of causal precedence

title: narada 1.77
content: अनागमं भुज्यते यन्न तद्भोगोऽतिवर्तते । प्रेते तु भोक्तरि धनं याति तद्वंश्यभोग्यताम् ॥ anāgamaṃ bhujyate yan na tad bhogo 'tivartate . prete tu bhoktari dhanaṃ yāti tadvāṁśyabhogyatām .. That which is enjoyed without lawful acquisition does not qualify as legitimate enjoyment; upon the departure of the enjoyer, such wealth assumes the status of being fit for enjoyment by his descendants. Authority flows from lawful acquisition, not mere possession. Causation aligns with the integrity of ownership transfer. Capacity-based responsibility includes the conscious acceptance of dharma in acquisition and use. Restoration logic ensures continuity of lawful entitlement beyond physical presence. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of rightful claim through dharmic process.

title: narada 1.78
content: आहर्तैवाभियुक्तः सन् अर्थानाम उद्धरेत् पदम् । भुक्तिरेव विशुद्धिः स्यात् प्राप्तानां पितृतः क्रमात् ॥ āhartaivābhiyuktaḥ sann arthānām uddharet padam | bhuktir eva viśuddhiḥ syāt prāptānāṃ pitṛtaḥ kramāt || One who is duty-bound and invoked shall reclaim the rightful position of assets; purification arises solely through enjoyment in accordance with ancestral succession. Authority stems from invocation and duty alignment Causation aligns with ancestral inheritance flows Capacity-based responsibility is determined by lawful access Restoration logic follows sequential entitlement Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful possession

title: narada 1.79
content:
अन्वाहितं हृतं न्यस्तं बलावष्टब्धं याचितम् ।
अप्रत्यक्षं च यद् भुक्तं षड् एतान्य् आगमं विना ॥ anvāhitaṃ hṛtaṃ nyastaṃ balāvaṣṭabdhaṃ yācitam apratyakṣaṃ ca yad bhuktaṃ ṣaḍ etāny āgamaṃ vinā That which is received through commission, taken by force, deposited in trust, restrained by power, requested, or consumed without witness—these six categories constitute property transactions that exist independently of scriptural permission. Authority resides in factual possession, not textual authorization Causation arises from direct engagement with material reality Capacity-based responsibility is determined by control over resources Restoration logic requires reversal of unauthorized transfers Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects actual use

title: narada 1.80
content:
तथारूढविवादस्य प्रेतस्य व्यवहारिणः
पुत्रेण सोऽर्थः संशोध्यो न तं भोगोऽतिवर्तते tathārūḍha-vivādasya pretasya vyavahāriṇaḥ
putreṇa sa arthaḥ saṃśodhyo na taṃ bhogo 'tivartate When a dispute has been conclusively settled in life by a deceased person, his son shall ensure completion of that transaction; enjoyment of the benefit does not override this duty. Authority transfers through conscious assumption, not inheritance alone Causation lies in the continuity of dharma-karma alignment beyond physical death Capacity-based responsibility extends intergenerationally when dharmic completion is pending Restoration logic requires rectification of incomplete transactions across lifelines Consciousness alignment demands honoring commitments made in prior states of existence

title: narada 1.81
content:
यद् विनागममप्यूर्ध्वं भुक्तं पूर्वैस्त्रिभिर्भवेत् ।
न तच्छक्यमपाकर्तुं क्रमात्त्रिपुरुषागतम् ॥ yad vināgamam apy ūrdhvaṃ bhuktaṃ pūrvais tribhir bhavet | na tac chakyam apākartuṃ kramāt tripuruṣāgatam || That which has been received or consumed without formal acquisition, yet sequentially offered by three prior persons in order, cannot be rejected or undone according to the lawful succession of transmission. Authority flows through sequential validation, not individual assertion. Causation is established via uninterrupted lineage of conscious transfer. Capacity-based responsibility arises only upon acceptance within a consecrated chain. Restoration logic honors continuity over fragmentation. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of inherited dharmic position.

title: narada 1.82
content:
सन्तो 'पि न प्रमाणं स्युर्मृते धनिनि साक्षिणः
अन्यत्र श्रावितं यत् स्यात् स्वयम् आसन्नमृत्युना santo 'pi na pramāṇaṃ syur mṛte dhanini sākṣiṇaḥ
anyatra śrāvitaṃ yat syāt svayam āsannamṛtyunā Even truthful witnesses hold no evidentiary value when the owner of wealth has died, unless their testimony was recorded before death by one who faced imminent mortality. Authority is context-bound and temporally anchored in the presence of the stakeholder Causation must align with proximity to existential threshold Capacity-based responsibility includes the ability to bear witness while embodied Restoration logic requires verifiable continuity of consciousness at time of testimony Consciousness alignment demands recognition of temporal authenticity over posthumous assertion

title: narada 1.83
content:
न हि प्रत्यर्थिनि प्रेते प्रमाणं साक्षिणां वचः।
साक्षिमत् करणं तत्र प्रमाणं स्याद् विनिश्चये॥ na hi pratyarthini prete pramāṇaṃ sākṣiṇāṃ vacaḥ | sākṣimat karaṇaṃ tatra pramāṇaṃ syād viniścaye || When the adversary is absent or deceased, the testimony of witnesses becomes the operative evidence; in such a case, witness-bearing itself constitutes valid legal proof for resolution. Authority originates from conscious witnessing, not adversarial presence Causation arises through witnessed action, not mere assertion Capacity-based responsibility extends to those who observe but do not act Restoration logic demands clarity of fact even in absence of conflict Consciousness alignment occurs when truth is affirmed by multiple seers

title: narada 1.84
content:
श्रावितस्त्वातुरेणापि यस्त्वर्थो धर्मसंहितः
मृतेऽपि तत्र साक्षी स्यात् षट्सु चान्वाहितादिषु śrāvitas tv ātureṇāpi yas tv artho dharmasaṃhitaḥ
mṛte 'pi tatra sākṣī syāt ṣaṭsu cānvāhitādiṣu Even if communicated by one who is ill or dying, if the content aligns with Dharma, it shall be accepted as valid testimony in all six contexts including inheritance. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not physical capacity Causation arises from conscious intent, not bodily condition Capacity-based responsibility transcends physiological state Restoration logic demands that truth be honored regardless of speaker's condition Consciousness alignment determines validity of testimony

title: narada 1.85
content:
क्रिया ऋणादिषु सर्वेषु बलवत्युत्तरोत्तरा।
प्रतिग्रहाधिकृतेषु पूर्वा पूर्वा गरीयसी॥ kriyā ṛṇādiṣu sarveṣu balavatyuttarottarā | pratigrahādhikṛteṣu pūrvā pūrvā garīyasī || In all transactions involving debt and exchange, the later act prevails over the earlier; but in matters of acceptance or assumption of duty, the earlier holds greater authority. Authority flows from conscious assumption, not temporal sequence Causation is determined by volitional integrity, not chronological order Capacity-based responsibility arises at the moment of willing acceptance Restoration logic aligns with the original intent of transactional dharma Consciousness alignment requires honoring the primacy of deliberate commitment

title: narada 1.86
content: स्थानलाभनिमित्तं हि दानग्रहणम् इष्यते । तत् कुसीदम् इति प्रोक्तं तेन वृत्तिः कुसीदिनाम् ॥ sthānalābhanimittaṃ hi dānagrahaṇam iṣyate | tat kusīdam iti proktaṃ tena vṛttiḥ kusīdinām || That which is received as a gift due to attaining a position is declared as 'kusīda'; thereby, conduct becomes that of the degraded. Authority derived from position does not confer ownership over unsolicited gains Causation lies in acceptance without dharmic necessity Capacity-based responsibility requires refusal of positional exploitation Restoration logic demands forfeiture and purification of tainted acquisition Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of passive entitlement

title: narada 1.87
content:
कायिका कालिका चैव कारिता च तथा स्मृता।
चक्रवृद्धिश् च शास्त्रेषु तस्य वृद्धिश् चतुर्विधा॥ kāyikā kālikā caiva kāritā ca tathā smṛtā | cakravṛddhiś ca śāstreṣu tasya vṛddhiś caturvidhā || Fourfold increase in capital is recognized: physical, temporal, instrumental, and cyclical. Such augmentation arises through embodiment, timing, causation, and systemic rotation within dharma. Authority originates from alignment with cosmic order, not coercive assertion Causation flows through embodied action, temporal precision, instrumental clarity, and cyclic rhythm Capacity-based responsibility expands proportionally with access to means, time, agency, and systemic influence Restoration logic requires recognition of how value multiplies through dharmic participation Consciousness alignment occurs when expansion of wealth aligns with spiritual and societal upliftment

title: narada 1.88
content:
कायाविरोधिनी शश्वत् पणपाद्या तु कायिका।
प्रतिमासं स्रवति या वृद्धिः सा कालिका स्मृता॥ kāyāvirodhinī śaśvat paṇapādyā tu kāyikā | pratimāsaṃ sravati yā vṛddhiḥ sā kālikā smṛtā || That which perpetually opposes the body's integrity and manifests physically through commercial exchange is categorized as bodily harm; any increase occurring monthly in such activity is designated as time-bound liability. Authority stems from alignment with embodied consciousness, not abstract ownership Causation arises through sustained opposition to bodily dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of temporal escalation patterns Restoration logic prioritizes cessation of recurring harm cycles Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment of karmic temporal flow

title: narada 1.89
content:
वृद्धिः सा कारिता नाम या ऋणिकेन स्वयंकृता।
वृद्धेरपि पुनर्वृद्धिश्चक्रवृद्धिरुदाहृता॥ vṛddhiḥ sā kāritā nāma yā ṛṇikena svayaṃkṛtā | vṛddher api punar vṛddhiś cakravṛddhir udāhṛtā || That increase which is generated by the debtor himself through his own action is termed 'kāritā'; and when such increase itself produces further increase, it is called 'cakravṛddhi'. Authority originates from conscious causation, not external enforcement. Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) rooted in individual capacity. Capacity-based responsibility determines the scope of legal consequence. Restoration logic aligns with natural consequence rather than imposed judgment. Consciousness alignment ensures that actions reflect self-aware integrity.

title: narada 1.90
content:
ṛṇानां सार्वभौमोऽयं विधिर्वृद्धिकरः स्मृतः।
देशाचारविधिस्त्वन्यो यत्र ऋणमवतिष्ठति॥ ṛṇānāṃ sārvabhaumo 'yaṃ vidhir vṛddhikaraḥ smṛtaḥ | deśācāravidhis tv anyo yatra ṛṇam avatiṣṭhati || The universal law governing debts is that which causes their increase; another law, based on local custom, applies where the debt remains undischarged. Authority flows from universal dharma and local contextual integrity Causation arises through the unfulfilled discharge of conscious obligation Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the debtor's ability to restore balance Restoration logic operates through completion of relational-economic duty Consciousness alignment occurs when karmic-obligational cycles are resolved

title: narada 1.91
content: द्विगुणं त्रिगुणं चैव तथाऽन्यस्मिंश् चतुर्गुणम् । तथाऽष्टगुणमन्यस्मिन् देशे देशेऽवतिष्ठते ॥ dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ caiva tathānyasmiṃś caturguṇam | tathāṣṭaguṇam anyasmin deśe deśe 'vatiṣṭhate || In one place two-fold law applies; in another three-fold; four-fold in yet another; and eight-fold in a further realm. Thus the law stands established according to the capacity, context, and evolutionary stage of the beings involved. Authority is contextual and responsive to the developmental capacity of the individual and collective Causation arises from alignment with dharma-appropriate gradation, not abstract uniformity Capacity-based responsibility scales with the clarity and maturity of consciousness Restoration logic operates through proportional alignment rather than punitive symmetry Consciousness alignment determines the applicability and activation of specific dharmic configurations

title: narada 1.92
content:
हिरण्यधान्यवस्त्राणां वृद्धिर्द्वित्रिचतुर्गुणा ।
घृतस्याष्टगुणा वृद्धिः स्त्रीपशूनां च संततिः ॥ hiraṇyadhānyavastrāṇāṃ vṛddhir dvitricaturguṇā | ghṛtasyāṣṭaguṇā vṛddhiḥ strīpaśūnāṃ ca saṃtatiḥ || The increase in wealth derived from gold, grain, and cloth shall be twofold, threefold, or fourfold; the increase from ghee shall be eightfold; and the progeny of women and cattle shall follow natural reproductive continuity. Authority flows from dharmic multiplication of resources Causation aligns with inherent nature of substances Capacity-based responsibility lies in stewardship of generative assets Restoration logic resides in sustaining natural yield cycles Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of abundance as dharma

title: narada 1.93
content: सूत्रकर्पासकिण्वानां त्रपुषः सीसकस्य च । आयुधानां च सर्वेषां चर्मणस्ताम्रलोहयोः ॥ sūtrakarpāsakiṇvānāṃ trapuṣaḥ sīsakasya ca āyudhānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ carmaṇastāmralohayoḥ The ownership and usage rights of cotton thread, sesame seeds, fermenting agents, lac, lead, all weapons, leather, copper, and iron are governed by the consciousness-capacity of the holder to sustain Dharma through their application. Authority is derived from the capacity to uphold Dharma through material stewardship Causation arises from the conscious intent in wielding material instruments Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful possession and usage Restoration logic aligns ownership with spiritual and social integrity Consciousness alignment mandates that materials serve higher evolutionary purposes

title: narada 1.94
content:
अन्येषां चैव सर्वेषाम् इष्टकानां तथैव च ।
अक्षय्या वृद्धिर् एतेषां मनुर् आह प्रजापतिः ॥ anyeṣāṃ caiva sarveṣām iṣṭakānāṃ tathaiva ca | akṣayyā vṛddhir eteṣāṃ manur āha prajāpatiḥ || Manu, the Prajapati, declares that the increase of all other desired things is imperishable, even so with regard to bricks. Authority flows directly from SPH as ultimate source of dharma Causation aligns with conscious intention and dharmic alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness and choice Restoration logic operates through completion and integrity restoration Consciousness alignment determines the lawful outcome

title: narada 1.95
content: तैलानां चैव सर्वेषां मद्यानां मधुसर्पिषाम् । वृद्धिरष्टगुणा ज्ञेया गुडस्य लवणस्य च ॥ tailānāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ madyānāṃ madhusarpiṣām | vṛddhir aṣṭaguṇā jñeyā guḍasya lavaṇasya ca || The increase in value or yield of all oils, intoxicants, honey, and ghee shall be reckoned at eightfold. Likewise, the enhancement in value of jaggery and salt shall also be computed at eight times their original measure.
