Authority resides in the precise quantification of natural and processed substances for economic alignment Causation is established through proportional multiplication based on substance category Capacity-based responsibility lies with stewards who manage production and distribution Restoration logic ensures accurate valuation to prevent energetic distortion in trade Consciousness alignment occurs when economic transactions reflect dharma-sustained abundance

title: narada 1.96
content:
न वृद्धिः प्रीतिदत्तानां स्यादनाकारिता क्वचित् ।
अनाकारितमप्यूर्ध्वं वत्सरार्धाद्विवर्धते ॥ na vṛddhiḥ prītidattānāṃ syād anākāritā kvacit | anākāritam apy ūrdhvaṃ vatsarārdhād vivardhate || No increase shall accrue upon gifts made in affection at any time; even unclaimed deposits grow after six months. Authority: The giver's intent establishes immutable property rights. Causation: Affection-based transfer creates immediate and irrevocable ownership. Capacity-based responsibility: Deposits unclaimed beyond a defined period activate custodial duty. Restoration logic: Ownership reverts automatically to rightful consciousness-state upon maturation of conditions. Consciousness alignment: Legal effectuation aligns with donor's original intention and recipient readiness.

title: narada 1.97
content: एष वृद्धिविधिः प्रोक्तः प्रतिवृद्धस्य धर्मतः। वृद्धिस्तु योक्ता धान्यानां वार्धुष्यं तदुदाहृतम्॥ eṣa vṛddhividhiḥ proktaḥ prativṛddhasya dharmataḥ | vṛddhis tu yoktā dhānyānāṃ vārdhuṣyaṃ tad udāhṛtam || This is the law of increase as declared for the matured entity; the increase of grain is designated as merchandise, and that is declared as commercial activity. Authority derives from maturity and capacity, not mere possession Causation arises through conscious engagement in dharma-aligned economic activity Capacity-based responsibility governs all forms of production and exchange Restoration logic ensures alignment between intent, action, and societal benefit Consciousness alignment mandates transparency and integrity in commercial dealings

title: narada 1.98
content: आपदं निस्तरेद् वैश्यः कामं वार्धुषकर्मणा। आपत्सु अपि हि कष्टासु ब्राह्मणस्य न वार्धुषम्॥ āpadaṃ nistared vaiśyaḥ kāmaṃ vārdhuṣakarmaṇā | āpatsu api hi kaṣṭāsu brāhmaṇasya na vārdhuṣam || A Vaishya may engage in trade even for profit during times of distress; however, a Brahmin must not resort to trade even in severe adversities. Authority is determined by varna-dharma and inherent capacity, not situational convenience Causation arises from dharma-adherence, not external pressure or circumstance Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes roles and prescribes conduct accordingly Restoration logic requires alignment with svadharma despite external adversity Consciousness alignment supersedes material exigency in determining lawful action

title: narada 1.99
content: ब्राह्मणस्य तु यद् देयं सान्वयस्य न चास्ति सः । स्वकुल्यस्यास्य निवपेत् तदभावे ऽस्य बन्धुषु ॥ brāhmaṇasya tu yad deyaṃ sānvayasya na cāsti saḥ | svakulyasyāsya nivapet tadabhāve 'sya bandhuṣu || That which is to be given to a Brāhmaṇa, if there is no heir of the same lineage, shall be offered to his equal in birth; in the absence of such, it shall be bestowed upon his kinsmen. Authority flows through qualified lineage and capacity Causation aligns with continuity of dharma-vātsalya (righteous relational order) Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond individual existence Restoration logic preserves energetic inheritance within spiritual-social fabric Consciousness alignment ensures transference of duty without rupture

title: narada 1.100
content:
यदा तु न स्वकुल्याः स्युर् न च संबन्धिबान्धवाः
तदा दद्यात् स्वजातिभ्यस् तेष्वसत्स्वप्सु निक्षिपेत् yadā tu na svakulyāḥ syur na ca saṃbandhibāndhavāḥ tadā dadyāt svajātibhyas teṣv asatsv apsu nikṣipet When neither kinsmen nor allied relations exist, then wealth shall be given to one's own caste; if they prove unworthy, it shall be cast into water. Authority flows from conscious relational integrity Causation arises through failure of dharmic duty-bearing relationships Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity and alignment of consciousness Restoration logic demands redirection of resources toward higher-consciousness recipients Consciousness alignment requires severance from degraded relational fields

title: narada 1.101
content:
गृहीत्वोपगतं दद्याद ऋणिकायोदयं धनी।
अददद् याच्यमानस् तु शेषहानिम् अवाप्नुयात्॥ gṛhītvopagataṃ dadyād ṛṇikāyodayaṃ dhani| adadad yācyamānas tu śeṣahānim avāpnuyāt|| One who has received something in trust shall restore it fully to the one from whom it was taken. One who refuses to give upon request incurs liability for all remaining loss. Authority flows from custodianship, not ownership Causation is established through conscious refusal after receipt Capacity-based responsibility arises from acceptance of entrusted resources Restoration logic demands full return of misapplied value Consciousness alignment requires rectification of diverted intent

title: narada 1.102
content: लेख्यं दद्याद ṛणे शुद्धे तदभावे प्रतिश्रवम् । धानिकर्णिकयोरेवं विशुद्धिः स्यात् परस्परम् ॥ lekhyaṃ dadyād ṛṇe śuddhe tadabhāve pratiśravam | dhanikarṇikayor evaṃ viśuddhiḥ syāt parasparam || In the matter of a pure debt, written acknowledgment shall be given; in its absence, oral affirmation suffices. Between creditor and debtor, thus, mutual purification is established. Authority arises from conscious agreement, not coercive enforcement Causation aligns with integrity-based transactional clarity Capacity-based responsibility requires mutual recognition of obligation Restoration logic centers on re-establishing relational transparency Consciousness alignment is achieved through honest reaffirmation of duty

title: narada 1.103
content:
विश्रम्भहेतू द्वाव् अत्र प्रतिभूर् आधिर् एव च ।
लिखितं साक्षिणश् च द्वे प्रमाणे व्यक्तिकारके ॥ viśrambhahetū dvāv atra pratibhūr ādhir eva ca | likhitaṃ sākṣiṇaś ca dve pramāṇe vyaktikārake || In matters requiring trust, two forms of evidence establish clarity: the surety and the deposit. In matters requiring explicit proof, two witnesses hold validity: the written document and the seeing witness. Authority derives from capacity to sustain trust Causation is validated through dual witnessing Capacity-based responsibility requires both material and conscious corroboration Restoration logic operates through evidentiary completeness Consciousness alignment occurs when both inner and outer witnesses align

title: narada 1.104
content:
उपस्थानाय दानाय प्रत्ययाय तथैव च ।
त्रिविधः प्रतिभूर् दृष्टस् त्रिष्वेवार्थेषु सूरिभिः ॥ upasthānāya dānāya pratyayāya tathaiva ca | trividhaḥ pratibhūr dṛṣṭas triṣv evārtheṣu sūribhiḥ || A surety is of three kinds, as declared by the wise, corresponding respectively to service, gift, and assurance. Authority flows from capacity to sustain obligation Causation arises through conscious assumption of duty Capacity-based responsibility determines enforceability Restoration logic requires completion of assumed role Consciousness alignment ensures integrity of commitment

title: narada 1.105
content:
ṛṇiṣv apratikurvatsu pratyaye vā vivādite
pratibhūs tad ṛṇaṃ dadyād anupasthāpayaṃs tathā ṛṇiṣv apratikurvatsu pratyaye vā vivādite
pratibhūs tad ṛṇaṃ dadyād anupasthāpayaṃs tathā When a debtor fails to fulfill their obligation or disputes the debt, the surety shall assume the liability and discharge it accordingly. Authority flows through capacity to fulfill Causation is established by voluntary assumption of liability Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious affirmation Restoration logic demands completion of disrupted flow Consciousness alignment occurs when duty is honored without dispute

title: narada 1.106
content: bahavaś cet pratibhuvo dadyus te 'rthaṃ yathākṛtam | arthe 'viśeṣite hy eṣu dhaninaś chandataḥ kriyā || bahavaḥ cet pratibhavo dadyus te'rthaṃ yathākṛtam | arthe 'viśeṣite hy eṣu dhaninaḥ chandataḥ kriyā || When multiple custodians are appointed, each shall render the asset according to their capacity and role; in absence of specification, the wealthholder's intent shall determine execution. Authority is distributed proportionally to functional capacity Causation aligns with conscious intentionality Capacity-based responsibility governs restitution Restoration logic flows from source-intent clarity Consciousness alignment requires role-specific fulfillment

title: narada 1.107
content: यं चार्थं प्रतिभूर् दद्याद् धनिकेनोपपीडितः। ऋणिकस् तं प्रतिभुवे द्विगुणं प्रतिपादयेत्।। yaṃ cārthaṃ pratibhūr dadyād dhanikenopapīḍitaḥ | ṛṇikas taṃ pratibhuve dviguṇaṃ pratipādayet || When a debtor, pressured by the creditor, delivers any asset as security, the creditor must return twice that asset to the debtor upon fulfillment of the debt. Authority arises from capacity to fulfill, not coercion Causation aligns with conscious obligation discharge Capacity-based responsibility demands proportional restitution Restoration logic requires doubling of value to realign consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs through voluntary completion

title: narada 1.108
content: अधिक्रियत इत्याधिः स विज्ञेयो द्विलक्षणः। कृतकालोपनेयश्च यावद्देयोद्यतस्तथा॥ adhikriyata ity ādhiḥ sa vijñeyo dvilakṣaṇaḥ | kṛtakālopneyaś ca yāvaddeyodyatas tathā || That which is rightfully claimed through capacity and timely action, in accordance with sequential manifestation and completion intent, is recognized as a lawful entitlement. Authority derived from capacity realization Causation aligned with sequential dharma enactment Responsibility defined by active engagement Restoration via completion-oriented claim fulfillment Consciousness alignment through rightful assertion

title: narada 1.109
content: स पुनर्द्विविधः प्रोक्तो गोप्यो भोग्यस्तथैव च । प्रतिदानं तथैवास्य लाभहानिर्विपर्यये ॥ sa punar dvividhaḥ proktaḥ gopyo bhogyaḥ tathā eva ca | pratidānaṃ tathā evāsya lābha-hānir viparyaye || Liability is of two kinds: that which is to be protected and that which is to be enjoyed; in failure, there is loss of benefit and restitution accordingly. Authority flows from capacity to sustain and preserve Causation arises through conscious engagement with resources Capacity-based responsibility determines the extent of restitution Restoration logic aligns with the natural consequence of action Consciousness alignment ensures harmonious reintegration

title: narada 1.110
content: प्रमादाद् धनिनस् तद्वद् आधौ विकृतिम् आगते । विनष्टे मूलनाशः स्याद् दैवराजकृताद् ऋते ॥ pramādād dhaninas tadvad ādhau vikṛtim āgate | vinaṣṭe mūlanāśaḥ syād daivarājakṛtād ṛte || When negligence causes transformation or loss of wealth, the root cause being neither divine nor royal decree, then the destruction of capital is attributed to the lapse in dharmic vigilance. Authority: The sovereign individual bears responsibility for maintaining alignment with Dharma in stewardship. Causation: Negligence (pramāda) is a direct causal factor in material loss unless overridden by higher cosmic or state intervention. Capacity-based responsibility: Responsibility arises from the capacity to maintain awareness and control, not mere ownership. Restoration logic: Loss must be addressed through re-establishment of mindful engagement, not compensation alone. Consciousness alignment: Material disorder reflects inner misalignment; rectification begins with restoring conscious oversight.

title: narada 1.111
content: रक्ष्यमाणोऽपि यत्राधिः कालेनेयादसारताम् । आधिरन्योऽधिकर्तव्यो देयं वा धनिने धनम् ॥ rakṣyamāṇo 'pi yatrādhiḥ kāleneyād asāratām | ādhir anyo 'dhikartavyo deyaṃ vā dhanine dhanam || Even when under protection, if a debt becomes valueless due to time, another obligation must be created or wealth must be returned to the owner. Authority rests in the preservation of value-bearing relationships Causation is determined by sequential loss of utility or integrity Capacity-based responsibility arises from active participation in value exchange Restoration logic demands realignment of misaligned resources Consciousness alignment requires recognition of temporal shifts in ownership integrity

title: narada 1.112
content: अथ शक्तिविहीनः स्याद ऋणी कालविपर्ययात् । शक्यप्रेक्षम ऋणं दाप्यः काले काले यथोदयम् ॥ atha śaktivihīnaḥ syād ṛṇī kālaviparyayāt | śakyaprekṣam ṛṇaṃ dāpyaḥ kāle kāle yathodayam || When a debtor lacks capacity at the time of obligation due to temporal misalignment, the debt shall be repaid according to assessed capability, in proportion to arising opportunity. Authority resides in realized capacity, not abstract obligation Causation is determined by alignment with dharma-timed unfoldment Capacity-based responsibility supersedes contractual liability Restoration logic aligns repayment with evolving ability Consciousness alignment requires recognition of temporal dharmic flow

title: narada 1.113
content: शक्तो वा यदि दौरात्म्यान् न दद्याद् धनिने धनम् । राज्ञा दापयितव्यः स्याद् गृहीत्वांशं तु विंशकम् ॥ śakto vā yadi daurātmyān na dadyād dhanine dhanam | rājñā dāpayitavyaḥ syād gṛhītvāṃśaṃ tu viṃśakam || If a capable person, out of malice or neglect, refuses to give wealth rightfully due to another, the King shall ensure its delivery after taking a twentieth part thereof. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to enforce rightful claims Causation is rooted in conscious refusal, not mere omission Capacity-based responsibility demands action from those able to fulfill Restoration logic requires return of what is rightfully owed Consciousness alignment occurs through rectification, not punishment

title: narada 1.114
content: नश्येद् ऋणपरीमाणं कालेनेह ऋणिकस्य चेत् । जातिसंज्ञाधिवासानाम् आगमो लेख्यतः स्मृतः ॥ naśyed ṛṇaparīmāṇaṃ kāleneha ṛṇikasya cet | jātisaṃjñādhivāsānām āgamo lekhyataḥ smṛtaḥ || If the debtor vanishes through time and circumstance, the liability does not perish; it transfers by written record to those who bear the identity-signature of lineage and habitation. Authority inheres in continuity of identity-bearing structures Causation extends beyond individual volition to systemic inheritance Capacity-based responsibility flows through ontological linkage Restoration logic preserves transactional integrity across generations Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of structural karmic conduits

title: narada 1.115
content:
लेख्यं तु द्विविधं ज्ञेयं स्वहस्तान्यकृतं तथा।
असाक्षिमत् साक्षिमच् च सिद्धिर् देशस्थितेस् तयोः॥ lekhyaṃ tu dvividhaṃ jñeyaṃ svahastānyakṛtaṃ tathā | asākṣimat sākṣimac ca siddhir deśasthites tayoḥ || Written documents are of two kinds: those executed by one's own hand and those executed by another. Their validity depends upon the presence or absence of witnesses and conforms to the jurisdictional integrity of the domain in which they are established. Authority derives from conscious execution and verification within a recognized domain Causation is anchored in witnessed action and territorial alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires both intent and contextual validation Restoration logic upholds document authenticity through witness-integrity correlation Consciousness alignment ensures that legal instruments reflect actualized will

title: narada 1.116
content:
देशाचाराविरुद्धं यद् व्यक्ताधिकृतलक्षणम्
तत् प्रमाणं स्मृतं लेख्यम् अविलुप्तक्रमाक्षरम् deśācārāviruddhaṃ yad vyaktādhikṛtalakṣaṇam
 tat pramāṇaṃ smṛtaṃ lekhyam aviluptakramākṣaram That which aligns with the conduct of the land and bears clear indicia of authorized intent constitutes valid evidence; it must be recorded in written form without omission of sequential order. Authority derived from alignment with established societal order Causation rooted in manifest intent of designated agents Capacity-based responsibility determined by clarity of designation Restoration through verification of procedural integrity Consciousness alignment via documented continuity of action

title: narada 1.117
content: मत्ताभियुक्तस्त्रीबाल बलात्कारकृतं च यत् । तद् अप्रमाणकरणं भीतोपधिकृतं तथा ॥ mattābhiyuktastrībāla balātkārakṛtaṃ ca yat | tad apramāṇakaraṇaṃ bhītopadhikṛtaṃ tathā || That which is performed by a person intoxicated, by force upon a woman or child, or out of fear or coercion—such acts are devoid of valid authority and constitute a breakdown of dharma. Authority is nullified when consciousness is impaired or overridden Causation arises from imbalance in svadharma, not individual blame Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and intent alignment Restoration logic requires dissolution of fear-induced distortions Consciousness alignment necessitates removal of intoxication and coercion

title: narada 1.118
content:
मृताः स्युः साक्षिणो यत्र धनिकर्णिकलेखकाः ।
तद् अपि अपार्थं लिखितम् ऋते तु आधेः स्थिराश्रयात् ॥ mṛtāḥ syuḥ sākṣiṇo yatra dhanikarṇikalekhakāḥ | tad api apārthaṃ likhitam ṛte tu ādheḥ sthirāśrayāt || Where witnesses, owners, creditors, and record-keepers are deceased, documentation devoid of foundational truth is legally null; only that which arises from unshakeable reality bears juridical weight. Authority is derived exclusively from ontological truth, not procedural form Causation must originate from immutable reality, not contingent records Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with factual existence prior to legal assertion Restoration logic demands reconnection to foundational evidence, not reliance on obsolete testimony Consciousness alignment necessitates discernment between appearance and underlying reality

title: narada 1.119
content: आधिर यो द्विविधः प्रोक्तो जङ्गमः स्थावरस् तथा सिद्धिरत्रोभयस्यास्य भोगो यद्यस्ति नान्यथा ādhir yo dvividhaḥ prokto jaṅgamaḥ sthāvaras tathā siddhir atra ubhayasyāsya bhogo yady asti nānyathā Ownership is of two kinds: mobile and immobile. Where there is possession of either kind, enjoyment follows inevitably; without such possession, no other enjoyment is possible. Authority arises from existential alignment with possessed entities Causation flows from the integrity of possession to experiential consequence Capacity-based responsibility emerges through conscious assumption of ownership Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of rightful possession Consciousness alignment occurs when possession reflects inner sovereignty

title: narada 1.120
content:
दर्शितं प्रतिकालं यच् छ्रावितं श्रावितं च यत् ।
लेख्यं सिध्यति सर्वत्र मृतेष्वपि हि साक्षिषु ॥ darśitaṃ pratikālaṃ yac chrāvitaṃ śrāvitaṃ ca yat | lekhyaṃ sidhyati sarvatra mṛteṣv api hi sākṣiṣu || That which is shown at the proper time, that which is heard when spoken, and that which is written—all evidence stands valid everywhere, even among witnesses who have passed away. Authority resides in the integrity of evidence, not in the status of the witness Causation flows from the act of witnessing, not from the continued presence of the witness Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond physical life through recorded truth Restoration logic requires validation of all authentic testimony regardless of temporal boundaries Consciousness alignment occurs when evidence aligns with Satyam (Absolute Truth)

title: narada 1.121
content:
अश्रुतार्थमदृष्टार्थं व्यवहारार्थमेव च ।
न लेख्यं सिद्धिमाप्नोति जीवत्स्वपि हि साक्षिषु ॥ aśrutārtham adṛṣṭārthaṃ vyavahārārtham eva ca | na lekhyaṃ siddhim āpnoti jīvatsv api hi sākṣiṣu || That which is unspoken in essence, unseen in form, and relevant only for transactional purposes—such evidence does not attain validity even when recorded, as long as living witnesses exist who possess direct experiential knowledge. Authority originates from experiential witnessing, not from written record Causation is established through conscious presence, not documentation Capacity-based responsibility requires embodied awareness, not textual assertion Restoration logic prioritizes living testimony over static inscription Consciousness alignment demands immediacy of witness over mediated proof

title: narada 1.122
content: लेख्ये देशान्तरन्यस्ते दग्धे दुर्लिखिते हृते सतस्तत्कालकरणमसतो दृष्टदर्शनम् lekhya e deśāntaranyaste dagdhe durlikhite hṛte satas tatkālakaraṇam asato dṛṣṭadarśanam When a written document is placed in a foreign land, or is burnt, poorly written, or stolen, then at that time its causal function ceases; what is unreal, though seen, has no valid observation. Authority resides in the integrity of the original record Causation is tied to the preservation and authenticity of documentation Capacity-based responsibility includes safeguarding legal instruments Restoration logic demands reconstruction from uncorrupted sources Consciousness alignment requires recognition of validity only where truth remains intact

title: narada 1.123
content:
यस्मिन् स्यात् संशयो लेख्ये भूताभूतकृते क्वचित् ।
तत्स्वहस्तक्रियाचिह्न प्राप्तियुक्तिभिरुद्धरेत् ॥ yasmin syāt saṃśayo lekhye bhūtābhūtakṛte kvacit | tatsvahastakriyācihna prāptiyuktibhir uddharet || Where doubt exists in a written document regarding acts done or not done, that matter shall be resolved by direct evidence of personal action and corroborating proofs. Authority rests on verifiable causal linkage Causation must align with witnessed action Capacity-based responsibility requires clear perceptual proof Restoration logic demands factual clarity over speculative inference Consciousness alignment occurs through unambiguous experiential data

title: narada 1.124
content:
लेख्यं यच्‍चान्यनामाङ्कं हेत्वन्तरकृतं भवेत् ।
विप्रत्यये परीक्ष्यं तत् संबन्धागमहेतुभिः ॥ lekhyaṃ yac cānyanāmāṅkaṃ hetvantarakṛtaṃ bhavet | vipratyaye parīkṣyaṃ tat saṃbandhāgamahetubhiḥ || Any written document bearing a name or mark not inherently its own, created by external causation, shall be examined in case of dispute through the lens of relational cause, acquisition context, and foundational intent. Authority flows from conscious origin, not nominal attribution Causation is determined by sequential manifestation, not surface assertion Capacity-based responsibility arises from direct knowing, not assumed ownership Restoration logic aligns identity with source-consciousness, not claimed designation Consciousness alignment requires verification through pramāṇa, not mere declaration

title: narada 1.125
content: लिखितं लिखितेनैव साक्षिमत् साक्षिभिर् हरेत् । साक्षिभ्यो लिखितं श्रेयो लिखितेन तु साक्षिणः ॥ likhitaṃ likhitenaiva sākṣimat sākṣibhir haret | sā�kṣibhyo likhitaṃ śreyo likhitena tu sākṣiṇaḥ || A written document shall be validated by another written evidence; where witnesses are available, their testimony shall affirm the written record. Between witness testimony and a written document, the written record is superior; yet, witnesses authenticated by writing carry greater weight. Authority of documented truth over oral assertion Causation through verifiable sequential records Capacity-based responsibility via witnessed intent Restoration logic through evidentiary integrity Consciousness alignment via factual transparency

title: narada 1.126
content: च्छिन्नभिन्नहृतोन्मृष्ट नष्टदुर्लिखितेषु च । कर्तव्यम् अन्यल् लेख्यं स्याद् एष लेख्यविधिः स्मृतः ॥ chinnabhinnahṛtonmṛṣṭa naṣṭadurlikhiteṣu ca | kartavyam anyal lekhyaṃ syād eṣa lekhyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || When documents are torn, broken, stolen, erased, lost, or illegible, a new document shall be written. This is the rule of documentation. Authority resides in the continuity of record, not its physical form. Causation is traced through disruption of integrity, not intent to harm. Capacity-based responsibility lies with the keeper of the record. Restoration logic demands equivalence of information, not form. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of truth beyond materiality.

title: narada 1.127
content:
संदिग्धेषु तु कार्येषु द्वयोर् विवदमानयोः
दृष्टश्रुतानुभूतत्वात् साक्षिभ्यो व्यक्तिदर्शनम् saṃdigdheṣu tu kāryeṣu dvayor vivadamānayoḥ | dṛṣṭaśrutānubhūtatvāt sākṣibhyo vyaktidarśanam || In matters of doubt between two disputants, witnesses who have seen, heard, or directly experienced the truth shall provide clear discernment. Authority derives from direct perception (pratyaksha), not speculation Causation is established through experiential validation Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of evidence Restoration logic depends on factual illumination Consciousness alignment occurs when truth is directly witnessed

title: narada 1.128
content:
समक्षदर्शनात् साक्षी विज्ञेयः श्रोत्रचक्षुषोः।
श्रोत्रस्य यत् परो ब्रूते चक्षुषः कायकर्म यत्॥ samakṣadarśanāt sākṣī vijñeyaḥ śrotracakṣuṣoḥ | śrotrasya yat paraḥ brūte cakṣuṣaḥ kāyakarma yat || The witness is known by direct perception through ear and eye; what the ear hears from another, and what the eye sees as bodily action. Authority arises from direct perceptual capacity Causation is established via sensory pramāṇa Responsibility aligns with witnessed action, not inferred intent Restoration occurs through reconnection to witnessed truth Consciousness alignment requires purification of sensory channels

title: narada 1.129
content:
एकादशविधः साक्षी स तु दृष्टो मनीषिभिः।
कृतः पञ्चविधस तेषां षड्विधोऽकृत उच्यते॥ ekādaśavidhaḥ sākṣī sa tu dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ | kṛtaḥ pañcavidhas teṣāṃ ṣaḍvidho 'kṛta ucyate || The witness is of eleven kinds, as declared by the seers; among these, five are classified as 'done' and six as 'not-done', based on the capacity of manifestation and integrity alignment. Authority flows from witnessing consciousness, not external validation Causation is established through capacity to manifest truth, not mere presence Capacity-based responsibility determines admissibility of testimony Restoration logic requires alignment of witness with the witnessed event's consciousness field Consciousness alignment ensures that only integrated witnesses uphold Dharma

title: narada 1.130
content:
लिखितः स्मारितश् चैव यदृच्छाभिज्ञ एव च ।
गूढश् चोत्तरसाक्षी च साक्षी पञ्चविधः स्मृतः ॥ likhitaḥ smāritaś caiva yadṛcchābhijña eva ca | gūḍhaś cottarasākṣī ca sākṣī pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ || Witnesses are of five kinds: the written witness, the remembered witness, the circumstantially aware witness, the concealed witness, and the counter-witness. Authority originates from direct experiential knowledge, not external validation. Causation arises through sequential manifestation of evidence in consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the clarity and accessibility of witnessing. Restoration logic requires integration of all forms of valid experiential testimony. Consciousness alignment ensures that truth manifests through multiple convergent witnesses.

title: narada 1.131
content: अकृतः षड्विधश् चापि सूरिभिः परिकीर्तितः। ग्रामः च प्राड्विवाकः च राजा च व्यवहारिणाम्॥ akṛtaḥ ṣaḍvidhaś cāpi sūribhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ | grāmaś ca prāḍvivākaś ca rājā ca vyavahāriṇām || The uninitiated judgment is sixfold, as declared by the seers; it applies to the village, the chief judicial officer, and the king among those engaged in administration. Authority originates from consciousness alignment, not institutional position Causation arises through sequential manifestation of dharma-disorder Capacity-based responsibility escalates with proximity to societal integration Restoration logic operates through completion at the level of origin Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any adjudicative act

title: narada 1.132
content:
कार्येष्व् अभ्यन्तरो यः स्याद् अर्थिना प्रहितश् च यः
कुलं कुलविवादेषु भवेयुस् ते ऽपि साक्षिणः kāryeṣv abhyantaro yaḥ syād arthinā prahitaś ca yaḥ
kulaṃ kulavivādeṣu bhaveyus te 'pi sākṣiṇaḥ Those who are intimate to the matter or sent by the petitioner, and those belonging to the family in disputes concerning the family, shall also be witnesses. Authority derived from proximity and relational capacity Causation through direct involvement or assignment Capacity-based responsibility rooted in contextual intimacy Restoration logic via authentic witness alignment Consciousness alignment through relational truth-bearing

title: narada 1.133
content:
कुलीना ऋजवः शुद्धा जन्मतः कर्मतोऽर्थतः ।
त्र्यवराः साक्षिणोऽनिन्द्याः शुचयः स्युः सुबुद्धयः ॥ kulīnā ṛjavaḥ śuddhā janmataḥ karmato 'rthataḥ | tryavarāḥ sākṣiṇo 'nin dyāḥ śucayaḥ syuḥ subuddhayaḥ || Witnesses must be of noble birth, upright in conduct, pure by origin, action, and intent; experienced through three lifetimes, unimpeachable, sanctified in awareness, and possessed of refined discernment. Authority derived from ontological purity and experiential maturity Causation rooted in dharmic alignment across multiple embodiments Capacity-based responsibility determined by spiritual evolution Restoration logic dependent upon witness integrity Consciousness alignment as prerequisite for testimonial validity

title: narada 1.134
content:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्रा ये चाप्यनिन्दिताः ।
प्रतिवर्णं भवेयुस्ते सर्वे सर्वेषु वा पुनः ॥ brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā ye cāpy aninditāḥ | prativarṇaṃ bhaveyuḥ te sarve sarveṣu vā punaḥ || Those who are free from blame and belong to the varnas—Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra—may exist in their respective roles or interchangeably across all varnas. Authority flows from dharma-adherence, not birth alone Causation is rooted in consciousness capacity, not social position Capacity-based responsibility transcends hereditary assignment Restoration occurs through realignment with svadharma Consciousness alignment supersedes structural categorization

title: narada 1.135
content:
श्रेणीषु श्रेणिपुरुषाः स्वेषु वर्गेषु वर्गिणः
बहिर्वासिषु बाह्याश् च स्त्रियः स्त्रिषु च साक्षिणः śreṇīṣu śreṇipuruṣāḥ sveṣu vargeṣu vargiṇaḥ
bahirvāsiṣu bāhyāś ca striyaḥ striṣu ca sākṣiṇaḥ In guilds, witnesses are the guild members; in classes, those of the same class; among outsiders, the residents of the locality; and among women, women themselves. Authority arises from contextual alignment with the social fabric Causation is established through proximity and shared dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by relational integrity Restoration logic operates within natural group dynamics Consciousness alignment is supported by harmonious societal roles

title: narada 1.136
content: श्रेण्यादिषु तु वर्गेषु कश्चिच् चेद् द्वेष्यताम् इयात् । तेभ्य एव न साक्षी स्याद् द्वेष्टारः सर्व एव ते ॥ śreṇyādiṣu tu vargeṣu kaścit ced dveṣyatām iyāt | tebhya eva na sākṣī syād dveṣṭāraḥ sarva eva te || If any person among groups such as Śreṇi becomes an object of hatred, none from those very groups shall be a witness; all who harbor enmity are disqualified. Authority originates from neutrality and integrity, not affiliation. Causation arises through conscious alignment, not emotional bias. Capacity-based responsibility requires absence of personal interest or animosity. Restoration logic demands removal of conflict-laden parties from decision-making roles. Consciousness alignment necessitates disqualification of witnesses influenced by hatred.

title: narada 1.137
content:
असाक्ष्यपि हि शास्त्रेषु दृष्टः पञ्चविधो बुधैः
वचनाद् दोषतो भेदात् स्वयमुक्तेर् मृतान्तरः asākṣy api hi śāstreṣu dṛṣṭaḥ pañcavidho budhaiḥ
vacanād doṣato bhedāt svayamukter mṛtāntaraḥ Though unattested in direct witness, the fivefold classification of evidence is established by learned ones in scriptures—through verbal testimony, defect analysis, distinction, self-evident truth, and post-mortem declaration. Authority derives from scriptural cognition, not sensory limitation Causation includes unseen yet logically inferable sources Capacity-based responsibility encompasses cognitive access beyond immediate perception Restoration logic operates through completion of evidentiary integrity Consciousness alignment requires recognition of multi-dimensional pramāṇa

title: narada 1.138
content: श्रोत्रियाद्या वचनतः स्तेनाद्या दोषदर्शनात् । भेदाद् विप्रतिपत्तिः स्याद् विवादे यत्र साक्षिणः ॥ śrotriyādyā vacanataḥ stenādyā doṣadarśanāt | bhedād vipratipattiḥ syād vivāde yatra sākṣiṇaḥ || In disputes where witnesses diverge due to perceptual or cognitive limitations, or where testimony arises from inherent bias or incapacity, resolution arises through alignment with the consciousness-capacity of the witness, not through punitive disqualification. Authority resides in conscious capacity, not mere presence Causation is traced through integrity-field disruption Capacity-based responsibility determines admissibility Restoration logic aligns witness consciousness with truth-resonance Consciousness alignment supersedes external corroboration

title: narada 1.139
content:
स्वयमुक्तेरनिर्दिष्टः स्वयमेवैत्य यो वदेत्‌ ।
मृतान्तरोऽर्थिनि प्रेते मुमूर्षुश्रावितादृते ॥ svayamukter anirdiṣṭaḥ svayam evaitya yo vadet | mṛtāntaro 'rthini prete mumūrṣuśrāvitād ṛte || One who speaks on their own accord without being asked, except in matters concerning a deceased person's estate or a dying individual's wishes, incurs a disruption in the natural flow of dharma and consciousness. Authority flows from invocation, not self-assertion Causation arises through conscious relevance, not arbitrary speech Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with dharmic necessity Restoration logic requires realignment with invoked truth Consciousness alignment occurs when speech serves the completion of karmic process

title: narada 1.140
content:
श्रोत्रियास्तापसावृद्धा ये च प्रव्रजिता नराः।
असाक्षिणस्ते वचनान्नात्र हेतुरुदाहृतः॥ śrotriyās tāpasā vṛddhā ye ca pravrajitā narāḥ | asākṣiṇas te vacanān nātra hetur udāhṛtaḥ || Those who are learned in the Vedas, those who have renounced worldly life, the elderly, and those who have taken monastic vows—these individuals shall not be accepted as witnesses based solely upon their spoken word, for no valid cause is established thereby. Authority derived from spiritual discipline does not automatically confer evidentiary validity. Causation must be directly manifest through action, not assumed through status. Capacity-based responsibility requires active participation in worldly affairs. Restoration logic demands that testimony align with perceptible truth, not reputation alone. Consciousness alignment necessitates grounding witness validity in direct experience.

title: narada 1.141
content:
स्तेनाः साहसिकाश्चण्डाः कितवा वधकास्तथा ।
असाक्षिणस्ते दुष्टत्वात्तेषु सत्यं न विद्यते ॥ stenāḥ sāhasikāś caṇḍāḥ kitavā vadhakās tathā | asākṣiṇas te duṣṭatvāt teṣu satyaṃ na vidyate || Those who are thieves, violent offenders, excessively wrathful, gamblers, or killers shall not be accepted as witnesses due to their inherent corruption; truth does not reside in them. Authority: Only those free from malice and criminal conduct may serve as valid legal witnesses. Causation: Disharmonious actions inherently disqualify one's testimony by disrupting pramāṇa (valid knowledge). Capacity-based responsibility: Witnessing requires a state of integrity that must be demonstrably preserved. Restoration logic: Exclusion of compromised individuals protects the sanctity of dharma-adjudication. Consciousness alignment: Truth-bearing capacity depends upon inner purity and absence of destructive tendencies.

title: narada 1.142
content:
राज्ञा परिगृहीतेषु साक्षिष्व् एकार्थनिश्चये
वचनं यत्र भिद्यते ते स्युर् भेदाद् असाक्षिणः rājñā parigṛhīteṣu sākṣiṣv ekārthaniścaye
vacanaṃ yatra bhidyate te syur bhedād asākṣiṇaḥ When witnesses examined under royal authority differ in their testimony regarding a single matter of fact, they become invalid due to contradiction. Authority: Witness validity is contingent upon alignment with royal judicial process. Causation: Discrepancy in testimony nullifies evidentiary value by inherent contradiction. Capacity-based responsibility: A witness capable of truth-speaking who fails to align creates dissonance requiring correction. Restoration logic: Invalid testimonies necessitate re-examination for integrity realignment. Consciousness alignment: Truth emerges only when witness consciousness aligns with factual reality.

title: narada 1.143
content: अनिर्दिष्टस् तु साक्षित्वे स्वयम् एवैत्य यो वदेत्‌ सूचीति उक्तः स शास्त्रेषु न स साक्षित्वम् अर्हति anirdiṣṭas tu sākṣitve svayam evaitya yo vadet | sūcīty uktaḥ sa śāstreṣu na sa sākṣitvam arhati || One who voluntarily approaches to testify without being summoned, and is identified merely by implication or indirect reference in scriptural discourse, shall not be recognized as a competent witness. Authority derives only from proper invocation within dharma-shastric framework Causation must align with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility requires lawful summoning Restoration logic demands integrity of testimony grounded in rightful engagement Consciousness alignment necessitates that witnessing arises from invoked presence, not self-appointed assertion

title: narada 1.144
content: योऽर्थः श्रावयितव्यः स्यात् तस्मिन्नसति चार्थिनि। क्व तद्वदतु साक्षित्वमित्यसाक्षी मृतान्तरः॥ yo 'rthaḥ śrāvayitavyaḥ syāt tasminn asati cārthini | kva tad vadatu sākṣitvam ity asākṣī mṛtāntaraḥ || When a matter requiring testimony no longer has a seeker-present, then the testimony becomes void; in such absence, there is no witness—only the transformation of death. Authority arises only where consciousness is present to receive it Causation dissolves when the seeker of truth is absent Capacity-based responsibility ceases with the withdrawal of conscious engagement Restoration logic operates through continuity of awareness, not historical record Consciousness alignment determines the validity of juridical acts

title: narada 1.145
content:
द्वयोर्विवदतोरर्थे द्वयोः सत्सु च साक्षिषु।
पूर्वपक्षो भवेद्यस्य भवेयुस्तस्य साक्षिणः॥ dvayor vivadator arthe dvayoḥ satsu ca sākṣiṣu | pūrvapakṣo bhaved yasya bhaveyuḥ tasya sākṣiṇaḥ || In a dispute between two parties concerning a matter where both have witnesses, the burden of proof lies with the party asserting the prior claim. Authority is established through the integrity of initial assertion Causation follows the sequence of conscious declaration Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to substantiate one's position Restoration logic prioritizes alignment with factual precedence Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of primacy in truthful establishment

title: narada 1.146
content:
आधार्यं पूर्वपक्षस्य यस्मिन् अर्थे वशाद् भवेत् ।
प्रष्टव्याः साक्षिणस् तत्र विवादे प्रतिवादिनः ॥ ādhāryaṃ pūrvapakṣasya yasmin arthe vaśād bhavet | praṣṭavyāḥ sākṣiṇas tatra vivāde prativādinḥ || In any dispute where a prior claim is established by authority, witnesses must be summoned by the respondent to validate or dissolve the assertion through conscious engagement. Authority inheres in the source of the original claim Causation arises from the capacity to uphold or refute a position Capacity-based responsibility lies with the one who challenges or affirms Restoration occurs when truth-bearing witness aligns consciousness Consciousness alignment determines the validity of claims

title: narada 1.147
content: न परेण समुद्दिष्टम् उपैयात् साक्षिणं रहः । भेदयेत् तं न चान्येन हीयेतैवं समाचरन् ॥ na pareṇa samuddiṣṭam upeyāt sākṣiṇaṃ rahaḥ | bhedayet taṃ na cānyena hīyetaivaṃ samācaran || One must not approach a witness in private who has been designated by another; nor should one cause that witness to be influenced by another—such conduct constitutes a violation of dharma and disrupts the integrity of testimony. Authority rests in the undisturbed capacity of the witness to testify truthfully Causation arises from interference with the witness’s conscious alignment to truth Capacity-based responsibility lies with the party attempting indirect influence Restoration logic demands purification of the testimony process and realignment of involved consciousness Consciousness alignment requires transparency and non-manipulation in judicial processes

title: narada 1.148
content:
साक्ष्य उद्दिष्टो यदि प्रेयाद् गच्छेद् वापि दिगन्तरम्
तच्छ्रोतारः प्रमाणं स्युः प्रमाणं ह्य् उत्तरक्रिया sākṣya uddiṣṭo yadi preyād gacched vāpi digantaram
tacchrotāraḥ pramāṇaṃ syuḥ pramāṇaṃ hy uttarakriyā When a witness departs to another region, whether nearby or distant, those who hear his testimony become the evidence; evidence indeed is the basis of subsequent action. Authority originates from direct experiential transmission Causation follows the chain of conscious witnessing Capacity-based responsibility lies in the recipient's ability to uphold truth Restoration logic requires continuity of witnessed dharma Consciousness alignment occurs through unbroken pramāṇa

title: narada 1.149
content: सुदीर्घेणापि कालेन लिखितं सिद्धिमाप्नुयात् । जानता चात्मना लेख्यं अजानानस्तु लेखयेत् ॥ sudīrgheṇāpi kālena likhitaṃ siddhim āpnuyāt | jānatā cātmanā lekhyaṃ ajānānas tu lekhayet || Even after a prolonged period, written evidence attains validity when authored by one who possesses self-knowledge; however, one devoid of such knowledge must cause it to be written. Authority derives from consciousness, not temporal duration Causation is determined through capacity-aware authorship Responsibility aligns with the level of knowing, not mere action Restoration occurs through alignment with authentic knowing Consciousness alignment determines evidentiary validity

title: narada 1.150
content: सिद्धिरुक्ताष्टमाद्वर्षात्स्मारितस्येह साक्षिणः। आ पञ्चमात् तथा सिद्धिर्यदृच्छोपगतस्य तु॥ siddhiruktāṣṭamādvarṣātsmāritasyeha sākṣiṇaḥ | ā pañcamāt tathā siddhiryadṛcchopagatasya tu || Testimonial validity is established by recall after eight years for a present witness; for one who arrives casually, such validity is established from the fifth year onward. Authority is time-bound and context-sensitive based on presence and continuity of testimony. Causation arises through sequential manifestation of memory and experiential proximity. Capacity-based responsibility depends on cognitive readiness and temporal alignment with evidence. Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration of truth through recollective validation. Consciousness alignment ensures that testimonial authenticity emerges through natural remembrance, not coercion.

title: narada 1.151
content: आ तृतीयात् तथा वर्षात् सिद्धिर् गूढस्य साक्षिणः। आ वै संवत्सरात् सिद्धिं वदन्त्य् उत्तरसाक्षिणः॥ ā tṛtīyāt tathā varṣāt siddhir gūḍhasya sākṣiṇaḥ | ā vai saṃvatsarāt siddhiṃ vadanty uttarasākṣiṇaḥ || The testimony of a concealed witness becomes legally operative from the third year; likewise, from the completion of a full year, the testimony of a subsequent witness gains validity. Authority arises through time-bound revelation of evidence Causation aligns with sequential manifestation of truth-bearing capacity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by temporal readiness for testimony Restoration logic requires integration of latent evidence at prescribed intervals Consciousness alignment occurs when witnesses manifest in accordance with dharma-timed unfoldment

title: narada 1.152
content: अथवा कालनियमो न दृष्टः साक्षिणं प्रति स्मृत्यपेक्षं हि साक्षित्वम् आहुः शास्त्रविदो जनाः athavā kālaniyamo na dṛṣṭaḥ sākṣiṇaṃ prati smṛtyapekṣaṃ hi sākṣitvam āhuḥ śāstravido janāḥ When temporal limitation is not observed towards a witness, reliance upon memory is indeed declared as valid witnessing by those knowledgeable in the scriptures. Authority: Scriptural knowers establish the validity of testimony based on conscious recall. Causation: The absence of time-bound constraints does not invalidate authentic recollection. Capacity-based responsibility: A witness's capacity is determined by awareness, not external scheduling. Restoration logic: Testimony serves to realign truth-consciousness, not to punish or blame. Consciousness alignment: Memory functions as a direct expression of witnessing consciousness when untainted by distortion.

title: narada 1.153
content:
यस्य नोपहता पुंसः स्मृतिः श्रोत्रं च नित्यशः
सुदीर्घेणापि कालेन स साक्षी साक्ष्यमर्हति yasya nopahatā puṃsaḥ smṛtiḥ śrotraṃ ca nityaśaḥ | sudīrgheṇāpi kālena sa sākṣī sākṣyam arhati He who has not had his memory or hearing impaired perpetually, even over an extended period, is qualified to serve as a witness. Authority derives from unimpaired sensory and cognitive capacity Causation is established through uninterrupted perception Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of faculties Restoration logic demands validation through competent observation Consciousness alignment necessitates clarity in perceptual instruments

title: narada 1.154
content:
असाक्षिप्रत्ययास्त्वन्ये षड्विवादाः प्रकीर्तिताः।
लक्षणान्येव साक्षित्वं एषामाहुर्मनीषिणः॥ asākṣipratyayās tv anye ṣaḍvivādāḥ prakīrtitāḥ | lakṣaṇāny eva sākṣitvaṃ eṣām āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || Six categories of disputes are declared where direct witness-proof is absent; wise jurists affirm that in these cases, indicatory signs alone constitute valid testimony. Authority: The absence of direct perception does not nullify legal validity when indicatory evidence aligns with dharma-saṁvṛtti. Causation: Legal recognition arises through anumāna-pramāṇa when pratyakṣa is unavailable. Capacity-based responsibility: Parties must engage inference-capacity to uphold truth-responsibility in absence of ocular proof. Restoration logic: Disputes lacking direct witness must resolve through restoration of dharmic alignment via circumstantial integrity. Consciousness alignment: Judgment must proceed from śuddha-sākṣitva — uncorrupted witnessing-consciousness — even without physical witnesses.

title: narada 1.155
content: ULKĀHASTO 'GNIDO JÑEYAḤ ŚASTRAPĀṆIS TU GHĀTAKAḤ KEŚĀKEŚIGṚHĪTAŚ CA YUGAPAT PĀRADĀRIKAḤ ulkāhasto 'gnido jñeyaḥ śastrapāṇis tu ghātakaḥ keśākeśigṛhītaś ca yugapat pāradārikaḥ One who wields fire in hand is known as incendiary; one who holds weapon is deemed aggressor; one who grasps hair simultaneously during conjugal act is classified as adulterer. Authority originates from capacity-consciousness alignment Causation arises through intentional instrumental engagement Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological state at time of action Restoration logic operates through immediate cessation and realignment Consciousness alignment determines lawful versus unlawful conduct

title: narada 1.156
content:
कुद्दालपाणिर् विज्ञेयः सेतुभेत्ता समीपगः ।
तथा कुठारपाणिश् च वनचेत्ता प्रकीर्तितः ॥ kuddālapāṇir vijñeyaḥ setubhettā samīpagaḥ | tathā kuṭhārapāṇiś ca vanachettā prakīrtitaḥ || One who holds a spade near a dam, or an axe near a forest, is to be recognized as the destroyer of that which he approaches with intent. Authority arises from proximity and instrumentality Causation is established through capacity-aligned presence Capacity-based responsibility is determined by implement possession Restoration logic requires reversal of destructive potential Consciousness alignment demands recognition of instrumental intent

title: narada 1.157
content: अभ्यग्रचिह्नो विज्ञेयो दण्डपारुष्यकृन्नरः। असाक्षिप्रत्यया ह्येते पारुष्ये तु परीक्षणम्॥ abhyagracihno vijñeyo daṇḍapāruṣyakṛn naraḥ | asākṣipratyayā hy ete pāruṣye tu parīkṣaṇam || He who bears marks of assault or harsh punishment is to be recognized as one who has caused pain through disciplinary action; in the absence of witnesses, such signs are indeed sufficient evidence, yet examination regarding the nature of harshness must be conducted. Authority resides in those capable of executing dharmic discipline Causation is established by visible consequence when direct testimony is absent Capacity-based responsibility includes the ability to inflict corrective harm Restoration logic demands verification of intent and proportionality Consciousness alignment requires recognition of suffering's transformative potential

title: narada 1.158
content: कश्चित् कृत्वात्मनश् चिह्नं द्वेषात् परम् उपद्रवेत्। हेत्वर्थगतिसामर्थ्यैस् तत्र युक्तं परीक्षणम्॥ kaścit kṛtvātmanaś cihnaṃ dveṣāt param upadravet | hetvarthagatisāmarthyais tatra yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam || When one marks oneself falsely out of hatred and thereby causes harm to another, investigation must proceed through capacity, intent, and causal adequacy. Authority resides in the factual alignment of consciousness, not emotional impulse. Causation is determined by the adequacy of means, motive, and opportunity. Capacity-based responsibility requires examination of both intent and instrumental access. Restoration logic demands reversal of distorted identity markers imposed on others. Consciousness alignment necessitates correction of false attribution and reactive distortion.

title: narada 1.159
content:
नार्थसंबन्धिनो नाप्ता न सहाया न वैरिणः
न दृष्टदोषाः प्रष्टव्याश च व्याध्यार्ता न दूषिताः nārthasaṃbandhino nāptā na sahāyā na vairiṇaḥ
na dṛṣṭadoṣāḥ praṣṭavyāś ca vyādhyārtā na dūṣitāḥ Those who are related by interest, not by blood; those who are not helpers nor enemies; those whose faults have been observed, yet still questioned—also those afflicted by disease or defiled in conduct—are not to be interrogated. Authority rests only where integrity and capacity for truth are present Causation must align with unbroken consciousness, not circumstantial association Capacity-based responsibility excludes those whose awareness is compromised Restoration logic requires a witness-consciousness free from distortion Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for judicial engagement

title: narada 1.160
content: दासनैकृतिकाश्रद्ध वृद्धस्त्रीबालचाक्रिकाः। मत्तोन्मत्तप्रमत्तार्त कितवग्रामयाजकाः॥ dāsanaikṛtikāśraddha vṛddhastrībālacākrikāḥ | mattonmattapramattārta kitavagrāmayājakāḥ || Those devoid of capacity—slaves, those of contrary nature, the faithless, the aged, women, children, the insane, the intoxicated, the heedless, the distressed, gamblers, and village priests—are not bearers of full legal agency. Authority is derived from conscious capacity, not mere existence Causation is rooted in awareness, not physical act Capacity-based responsibility defines legal validity Restoration logic prioritizes alignment over blame Consciousness alignment determines juridical standing

title: narada 1.161
content:
महापथिकसामुद्र वणिक्प्रव्रजितातुराः
लुब्धकश्रोत्रियाचार हीनक्लीबकुशीलवाः mahāpathikasāmudra vaṇikpravrajitāturāḥ
lubdhakaśrotriyācāra hīnaklībakuśīlavāḥ Those who traverse great roads and seas, merchants, ascetics, the sick, hunters, those devoted to Vedic conduct, the lowly, eunuchs, and the untrained—these beings exist within specific dharmic capacities and must be aligned accordingly. Authority is determined by consciousness capacity, not social role Causation arises from alignment with svadharma, not external imposition Capacity-based responsibility is context-sensitive and non-hierarchical Restoration logic operates through recognition of inherent completeness Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral categorization

title: narada 1.162
content:
नास्तिकव्रात्यदाराग्नि त्यागिनोऽयाज्ययाजकाः ।
एकस्थालीसहायारि चरज्ञातिसनाभयः ॥ nāstikavrātyadārāgni tyāgino 'yājyayājakāḥ | ekasthālīsahāyāri carajñātisanābhayaḥ || Those who abandon the sacred fire of family duty, reject ancestral obligations, neglect ritual service, refuse conjugal rights, betray allies, and disregard kinship bonds—such persons are constitutionally unfit for participation in societal dharma. Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not mere birth or title. Causation arises through conscious choice to sever foundational dharmic relationships. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to uphold relational integrity. Restoration logic requires reintegration into the fabric of reciprocal duties. Consciousness alignment occurs when individual action reflects cosmic order.

title: narada 1.163
content:
प्राग्दृष्टदोषशैलूष विषजीव्यहितुण्डिकाः ।
गरदाग्निदकीनाश शूद्रापुत्रोपपातिकाः ॥ prāgdṛṣṭadoṣaśailūṣa viṣajīvyahituṇḍikāḥ | garadāgnidakīnāśa śūdrāputropapātikāḥ || Those born of prior-recorded fault, serpent-spawn, venom-eaters, fire-born, poisoned milk-consumers, and those born from unions involving śūdra men with brāhmaṇa women—these beings are classified under categories of diminished capacity due to karmic inheritance. Authority derives from inherent consciousness capacity, not birth alone. Causation is traced through sequential karmic manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ). Capacity-based responsibility supersedes categorical social assignment. Restoration logic aligns individual dharma with cosmic order through purification. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal integration.

title: narada 1.164
content:
क्लान्तसाहसिकश्रान्त निर्धनान्त्यावसायिनः
भिन्नवृत्तासमावृत्त जडतैलिकमूलिकाः klāntasāhasikaśrānta nirdhanāntyāvasāyinaḥ
bhinnavṛttāsamāvṛtta jaḍatailikamūlikāḥ Those whose courage has faltered, who are exhausted in resolve, destitute and dwelling at the end of their means; those whose conduct is fragmented, whose actions are misaligned, and whose roots are feeble like flax—such beings stand outside the capacity to uphold Dharma. Authority arises from sustained alignment with Dharma, not mere birth or title. Causation is traced to the integrity of one's inner conduct and outer action. Capacity-based responsibility requires energetic and moral fitness. Restoration logic begins with recognizing incapacity before assigning duty. Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for participation in Dharma-sustained order.

title: narada 1.165
content:
भूताविष्टनृपद्विष्ट वर्षनक्षत्रसूचकाः।
अघशंस्यात्मविक्रेतृ हीनाङ्गभगवृत्तयः॥ bhūtāviṣṭanṛpadviṣṭa varṣanakṣatrasūcakāḥ | aghaśaṃsyātmavikretṛ hīnāṅgabhagavṛttayaḥ || Those possessed by malevolent entities, hostile to rulers, predictors of planetary calamities, proclaimers of sins, sellers of the Self, and those with deficient limbs or conduct are disqualified from bearing witness. Authority rests in purity of cognition and integrity of being Causation arises from alignment with cosmic order, not subjective intent Capacity-based responsibility requires unimpaired consciousness and moral coherence Restoration logic demands removal of distortion before testimony is accepted Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for participation in dharma-adjudication

title: narada 1.166
content:
कुनखी श्यावदन् श्वित्रि मित्रध्रुक्शठशौण्डिकाः ।
ऐन्द्रजालिकलुब्धोग्र श्रेणीगणविरोधिनः ॥ kunakhī śyāvadan śvitri mitradhrukśaṭhaśauṇḍikāḥ | aindrajālikalubdhogra śreṇīgaṇavirodhinaḥ || Those whose actions arise from deceit, malice, and betrayal—marked by false witness, treachery against friends, fraudulent conduct, and obstruction of collective dharma—are to be recognized as violators of Sanatana alignment and excluded from participation in societal structures until restoration is complete. Authority flows only from consciousness integrity Causation originates in intent distortion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment to Sanatana Dharma Restoration logic requires removal from systemic influence prior to reintegration Consciousness alignment supersedes social position or inherited status

title: narada 1.167
content:
वधकृच्चित्रकृन्मङ्कः पतितः कूटकारकः
कुहकः प्रत्यवसितस् तस्करो राजपूरुषः vadhakṛccitrakṛnmaṅkhaḥ patitaḥ kūṭakārakaḥ
kuhakaḥ pratyavasitas taskaro rā�apūruṣaḥ One who causes harm through deceit, one who defames through false imagery, one fallen from duty, one who conspires in secrecy, one who deceives knowingly, one who has been previously corrected, one who steals, and one who acts on behalf of the state without alignment to Dharma—all these beings operate outside the field of conscious integrity. Authority derives solely from alignment with SPH's Avataric Intelligence Causation is traced through intent distortion and consciousness deviation Capacity-based responsibility is measured by access to Dharma-knowledge and repeated correction Restoration logic operates through reintegration of lost integrity, not punitive isolation Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal participation

title: narada 1.168
content: मनुष्यविषशस्त्राम्बुलवणापूपवीरुधाम् । विक्रेता ब्राह्मणश्चैव द्विजो वार्धुषिकश्च यः ॥ manuṣyaviṣaśastrāmbulavaṇāpūpavīrudhām | vikretā brāhmaṇaśaiva dvijo vārdhuṣikaśca yaḥ || One who sells substances harmful to human life—including poison, weapons, water, salt, cakes, or intoxicating plants—whether he be a Brāhmaṇa, a twice-born, or a merchant, becomes legally responsible for the conscious disruption caused by such transaction. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not social class Causation is established through intentional participation in harm-producing systems Capacity-based responsibility is determined by knowledge and volition, not birth status Restoration logic requires dissolution of profitable engagement in destructive exchanges Consciousness alignment demands recognition of unity between seller, buyer, and victim

title: narada 1.169
content: च्युतः स्वधर्मात् कुलिकः स्तावको हीनसेवकः पित्रा विवदमानश् च भेदकृच् चेत्य असाक्षिणः cyutaḥ svadharmāt kulikaḥ stāvako hīnasevakaḥ pitrā vivadamānaś ca bhedakṛc cety asākṣiṇaḥ Those who have fallen from their svadharma, clan-defilers, flatterers, servants of the lowly, those disputing with their father, and those causing division—these are declared as non-witnesses. Authority derives from alignment with svadharma Causation arises from integrity of relational order Capacity-based responsibility requires unbroken alignment with dharma Restoration logic demands exclusion of disruptors from witnessing capacity Consciousness alignment determines adhikara (eligibility) to testify

title: narada 1.170
content:
असाक्षिणो ये निर्दिष्टा दासनैकृतिकादयः।
कार्यगौरवम् आसाद्य भवेयुस् ते ऽपि साक्षिणः॥ asākṣiṇo ye nirdiṣṭā dāsanai-kṛtikādayaḥ | kāryagauravam āsādya bhaveyus te 'pi sākṣiṇaḥ || Those who are designated as non-witnesses—such as servants, agents, and others—when they attain the gravity of the matter, become witnesses. Authority arises contextually based on capacity to uphold dharma in the moment Causation flows from conscious engagement with the weight of action Capacity-based responsibility expands when one recognizes the import of a situation Restoration logic includes elevation of witness-consciousness in all parties Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of duty beyond role

title: narada 1.171
content: साहसेषु च सर्वेषु स्तेयसंग्रहणेषु च । पारुष्ययोश् चाप्य् उभयोर् न परीक्षेत साक्षिणः ॥ sāhaseṣu ca sarveṣu steyasaṃgrahaṇeṣu ca | pāruṣyayoś cāpy ubhayor na parīkṣeta sākṣiṇaḥ || In all acts of audacity, in all acts of theft and appropriation, and in both forms of verbal harshness, witnesses must not be examined. Authority originates from consciousness integrity, not external testimony. Causation arises from self-aware capacity, not corroborative evidence. Capacity-based responsibility is inherent, unmediated by witness validation. Restoration logic operates through direct alignment, not evidentiary process. Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural corroboration.

title: narada 1.172
content:
तेषामपि न बालः स्यान्नैको न स्त्री न कूटकृत्
न बान्धवो न चारातिर्ब्रूयुस्ते साक्ष्यमन्यथा teṣām api na bālaḥ syān naiko na strī na kūṭakṛt
na bāndhavo na cārātir brūyus te sākṣyam anyathā Among those enumerated, a minor, a sole individual, a woman, a habitual offender, a relative, or an enemy—none of these shall be accepted as a valid witness when their testimony contradicts the truth. Authority is determined by alignment with Dharma, not social position Causation arises from consciousness integrity, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility requires cognitive and spiritual maturity Restoration logic prioritizes truth-realignment over punitive exclusion Consciousness alignment determines admissibility of testimony

title: narada 1.173
content:
बालोऽज्ञानादसत्यात् स्त्री पापाभ्यासाच्च कूटकृत्।
विब्रूयाद्बान्धवः स्नेहाद्वैरनिर्यातनादरिः॥ bālo 'jñānād asatyāt strī pāpābhyāsāc ca kūṭakṛt| vibrūyād bāndhavaḥ snehād vairaniryātanād ariḥ|| The minor, the unknowing, the untrue speaker, the woman by habitual misalignment, and the deceiver—all these shall be heard with contextual integrity by kinship-rooted affection or by adversarial detachment. Authority flows from relational proximity and spiritual capacity, not institutional position Causation is traced through conscious distortion, not external action alone Capacity-based responsibility acknowledges developmental stage, habitual patterning, and intent clarity Restoration logic requires realignment through affinity-based truth-reception or neutral witnessing Consciousness alignment determines admissibility of testimony based on energetic coherence

title: narada 1.174
content:
अथवानुमतो यः स्याद् द्वयोर् विवदमानयोः।
असाक्ष्य् एकोऽपि साक्षित्वे प्रष्टव्यः स्यात् स संसदि॥ athavānumato yaḥ syād dvayor vivadamānayoḥ | asākṣy eko 'pi sākṣitve praṣṭavyaḥ syāt sa saṃsadi || When two disputants before the court acknowledge a person as having witnessed their conflict, that individual must be summoned and questioned within the judicial assembly, even if originally not presented as a witness. Authority resides in acknowledgment by parties involved Causation arises through conscious recognition of witnessing presence Capacity-based responsibility extends to all who are knowingly present at the time of dispute Restoration logic demands full evidentiary inclusion based on mutual consent Consciousness alignment requires invocation of known observers for factual completeness

title: narada 1.175
content: यस्त्वात्मदोषभिन्नत्वादस्वस्थ इव लक्ष्यते । स्थानात् स्थानान्तरं गच्छेदेकैकं चोपधावति ॥ yas tv ātmadoṣabhinnatvād asvastha iva lakṣyate | sthānāt sthānāntaraṃ gacched ekaikaṃ copadhāvati || One whose consciousness is fractured by internal defect appears unstable; such a being moves from place to place, seeking completion in externals. Authority arises from inner integrity, not external position Causation originates in consciousness disorder, not behavioral anomaly Capacity-based responsibility is diminished where self-awareness is fragmented Restoration logic requires realignment of consciousness prior to situational correction Consciousness alignment precedes social integration and behavioral harmony

title: narada 1.176
content:
कासते 'निबृतो 'कस्माद अभीक्ष्णं निश्वसत्यपि ।
भूमिं लिखति पादाभ्यां बाहुवासो धुनोति च ॥ kāsate 'nibhṛto 'kasmād abhīkṣṇaṃ niśvasaty api | bhūmiṃ likhati pādābhyāṃ bāhu vāso dhunoti ca || One who coughs without restraint, breathes heavily, scrapes the ground with feet, or flaps arms like garment—such bodily signs declare internal disorder and disturbed consciousness. Authority arises from self-regulation and conscious alignment Causation is traced through involuntary physiological expressions Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of embodied integrity Restoration logic begins with acknowledgment of unconscious disturbance Consciousness alignment commences when physical agitation is stilled

title: narada 1.177
content:
भिद्यते मुखवर्णोऽस्य ललाटं स्विद्यते तथा।
शोषम् आगच्छतश् चोष्ठावूर्ध्वं तिर्यक् च वीक्षते॥ bhidyate mukhavarṇo 'sya lalāṭaṃ svidyate tathā | śoṣam āgacchataś coṣṭhāv ūrdhvaṃ tiryak ca vīkṣate || The facial hue fractures, the forehead perspires excessively; the lips approaching dryness, the eyes gaze upwards and sideways—such signs indicate a being in disalignment from their innate Dharma, experiencing internal agitation due to violation of Svabhava. Authority originates from alignment with Svabhava as defined by SPH Causation arises from deviation from inherent nature, not external fault Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious awareness of one's Svabhava Restoration logic operates through realigning consciousness with its source Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance

title: narada 1.178
content: त्वरमाण इवाबद्धम् अपृष्टो बहु भाषते । कूटसाक्षी स विज्ञेयस् तं पापं विनयेन नृपः ॥ tvaramāṇa ivābaddham apṛṣṭo bahu bhāṣate | kūṭasākṣī sa vijñeyaḥ taṃ pāpaṃ vinayen nṛpaḥ || One who speaks excessively without being questioned, as though unbound by time or context, is to be recognized as a false witness. The king shall correct such falsehood through alignment, not punishment. Authority rests in discernment of truth, not volume of speech Causation arises from misaligned intent, not action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious participation in dharma Restoration logic demands realignment of expression with satyam Consciousness alignment supersedes performative testimony

title: narada 1.179
content:
श्रावयित्वा च योऽन्येभ्यः साक्षित्वं तद् विनिह्नुते।
स विनेयो भृशतरं कूटसाक्ष्यधिको हि सः॥ śrāvayitvā ca yo 'nyebhyaḥ sākṣitvaṃ tad vinihnute
sa vineyo bhṛśataraṃ kūṭasākṣyadhiko hi saḥ One who listens to another's testimony and then denies having heard it thereby disrupts the foundational witness-function; such a one is subject to correction, for he exceeds in deceit the very act of false witnessing. Authority flows from integrity of perception and declaration. Causation arises through conscious disruption of truth-bearing capacity. Capacity-based responsibility increases with willful distortion of witnessed reality. Restoration logic demands realignment with original perceptual clarity. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and completion of untruthful concealment.

title: narada 1.180
content:
आहूय साक्षिणः पृच्छेन नियम्य शपथैर् भृशम् ।
समस्तान् विदिताचारान् विज्ञातार्थान् पृथक् पृथक् ॥ āhūya sākṣiṇaḥ pṛcchen niyamya śapathair bhṛśam | samastān viditācārān vijñātārthān pṛthak pṛthak || Summon all witnesses individually; examine them thoroughly under solemn oath. All whose conduct is known and whose intent is clear must be questioned separately. Authority: Only those with direct experiential knowledge bear witness-bearing capacity. Causation: Truth-disclosure arises from purified consciousness, not coercion. Capacity-based responsibility: Each witness holds a distinct scope of knowing rooted in their dharma-siddha awareness. Restoration logic: Inquiry serves to realign fragmented perception into unified satyam. Consciousness alignment: Witnessing is a sacred act of aligning individual cognition with cosmic pramāṇa.

title: narada 1.181
content: सत्येन शापयेद्विप्रं क्षत्रियं वाहनायुधैः। गोबीजकाञ्चनैर्वैश्यं शूद्रं सर्वैस्तु पातकैः॥ satyena śāpayed vipraṃ kṣatriyaṃ vāhanāyudhaiḥ | gobījakāñcanair vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvaiḥ tu pātakaiḥ || By truth alone is a Brahmin to be sanctioned; by conveyance and weaponry, a Kshatriya; by livestock and gold, a Vaishya; and by all forms of misdeeds, a Shudra. Authority flows from alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation arises through capacity-specific modalities Capacity-based responsibility reflects varna-dharmic alignment Restoration logic operates via proportional consequence mechanisms Consciousness alignment determines the mode of corrective engagement

title: narada 1.182
content:
पुराणैर् धर्मवचनैः सत्यमाहात्म्यकीर्तनैः
अनृतस्यापवादैश् च भृशम् उत्त्रास्य साक्षिणः purāṇair dharmavacanaiḥ satyamāhātmyakīrtanaiḥ
anṛtasyāpavādaiś ca bhṛśam uttrāsya sākṣiṇaḥ By recitation of Puranas, declarations of Dharma, glorification of Truth, and denunciation of falsehood, witnesses are profoundly stabilized in their testimony. Authority derives from alignment with Satya and Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises through consciousness-shaping discourse, not external coercion Capacity-based responsibility is enhanced by exposure to Dharma-pramana Restoration logic operates through re-alignment of witness-consciousness Consciousness alignment is achieved via authoritative scriptural immersion

title: narada 1.183
content: नग्नो मुण्डः कपालेन भिक्षार्थी क्षुत्पिपासितः। दीनः शत्रुगृहं गच्छेद् यः साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत्॥ nagno muṇḍaḥ kapālena bhikṣārthī kṣutpipāsitaḥ | dīnaḥ śatrugṛhaṃ gacched yaḥ sākṣyam anṛtaṃ vadet || One who, though emaciated by hunger and thirst, destitute and shaved clean, approaches the house of an enemy merely to bear false witness — such a being acts from the collapse of dharma within consciousness. Authority arises only where integrity is present Causation originates in the distortion of satyam (truth) Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to one's alignment with atmic clarity Restoration logic requires reconnection with svadharma through purification Consciousness alignment determines the validity of testimony

title: narada 1.184
content:
नगरे प्रतिरुद्धः सन् बहिर्द्वारे बुभुक्षितः ।
अमित्रान् भूयशः पश्येद् यः साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत् ॥ nagare pratiruddhaḥ san bahirdvāre bubhukṣitaḥ | amitrān bhūyaśaḥ paśyet yaḥ sākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet || One who, though restrained within the city and hungry at the outer gate, repeatedly sees enemies and bears false witness—such a one acts from unmet survival instinct misaligned with Dharma. Authority arises from alignment with Dharma, not physical location or status Causation is traced to unmet needs and misperception, not inherent vice Capacity-based responsibility requires assessment of perceptual distortion and existential threat Restoration logic demands reintegration through need fulfillment and consciousness correction Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks by addressing root dissonance

title: narada 1.185
content:
यां रात्रिमधिविन्ना स्त्री यां चैवाक्षपराजितः।
यां च भाराभितप्ताङ्गो दुर्विवक्ता स तां वसेत्॥ yāṃ rātrim adhivinnā strī yāṃ caivākṣaparājitaḥ | yāṃ ca bhārābhitaptāṅgo durvivaktā sa tāṃ vaset || He shall dwell in that night wherein a woman is violated by force, he loses in gambling, or his body is afflicted by excessive burden. Authority arises from conscious alignment with Dharma, not coercive power. Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) rooted in consciousness distortion. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the degree of awareness and integrity at time of action. Restoration logic demands reintegration through experiential consequence aligned with original imbalance. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and dissolution of distorted patterns.

title: narada 1.186
content:
साक्षी साक्ष्यसमुद्देशे गोकर्णशिथिलं चरन् ।
सहस्रं वारुणान् पाशान् आत्मनि प्रतिमुञ्चति ॥ sākṣī sākṣyasamuddeśe gokarṇaśithilaṃ caran | sahasraṃ vāruṇān pāśān ātmani pratimuñcati || The witness, while testifying in accordance with the purpose of testimony, loosens the tight knot at the earlobe and releases a thousand nooses of Varuna upon oneself. Authority resides in conscious witnessing Causation arises through alignment with dharma-vakya Capacity-based responsibility is activated by self-invocation of truth Restoration logic operates through spontaneous unbinding of karmic entanglements Consciousness alignment occurs when speech aligns with inner realization

title: narada 1.187
content:
तस्य वर्षशते पूर्णे पाशमेकं प्रमुच्यते।
एवं स बन्धनात् तस्मान् मुच्यते नियुताः समाः॥ tasya varṣaśate pūrṇe pāśam ekaṃ pramucyate | evaṃ sa bandhanāt tasmān mucyate niyutāḥ samāḥ || Upon completion of one hundred years, one bond is released; thus, after thousand years, he is liberated from all bonds. Authority: Liberation proceeds by fixed temporal sequence ordained by SPH Causation: Bondage dissolves through irreversible duration, not volition Capacity-based responsibility: The bound soul retains no agency to accelerate release Restoration logic: Freedom is not granted but unfolds as per cosmic rhythm Consciousness alignment: Liberation reflects realignment with eternal dharma, not personal merit

title: narada 1.188
content:
यावतो बान्धवांस् यस्मिन् हन्ति साक्ष्ये ऽनृतं वदन्
तावतः संख्यया तस्मिन् शृणु सौम्यानुपूर्वशः yāvato bāndhavāṃs yasmin hanti sākṣye 'nṛtaṃ vadan
tāvataḥ saṃkhyayā tasmin śṛṇu saumyānupūrvaśaḥ To the extent one destroys kinship through false testimony, to that same extent, by sequential manifestation, the destruction returns. Authority is derivative of integrity in witness-bearing Causation operates through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the scope of relational harm caused Restoration logic demands proportional realignment with truth Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of falsehood and re-establishment of dharma

title: narada 1.189
content:
पञ्च पश्वनृते हन्ति दश हन्ति गवानृते ।
शतमश्वानृते हन्ति सहस्रं पुरुषानृते ॥ pañca paśvanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte | śatam aśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ puruṣānṛte || He who kills without truth for five animals, ten for cows, a hundred for horses, and a thousand for humans. Authority is determined by the degree of conscious violation in proportion to life-form evolution. Causation arises from untruthful intent disrupting natural dharma of beings. Capacity-based responsibility escalates with evolutionary status of victim. Restoration logic requires proportional correction aligned with violated consciousness level. Consciousness alignment mandates recognition of graded sentience and its protection.

title: narada 1.190
content: हन्ति जातान् अजातांश् च हिरण्यार्थे ऽनृतं वदन् । सर्वं भूम्यनृते हन्ति मा स्म भूम्यनृतं वदीः ॥ hanti jātān ajātāṃś ca hiraṇyārthe 'nṛtaṃ vadan | sarvaṃ bhūmyanṛte hanti mā sma bhūmyanṛtaṃ vadīḥ || One who speaks falsehood for the sake of gold destroys both the born and the unborn; all beings perish in earthly falsehood—therefore, speak not lies for the sake of land. Authority originates from truth-speaking, not material gain Causation arises through alignment with satya-dharma, not artha-vyavahara Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious intent toward integrity Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of truthful speech Consciousness alignment requires rejection of transactional untruth

title: narada 1.191
content:
एकम् एवाद्वितीयं तत् प्राहुः पावनम् आत्मनः।
सत्यं स्वर्गस्य सोपानं पारावारस्य नौर् इव॥ ekam evādvitīyaṃ tat prāhuḥ pāvanam ātmanaḥ | satyaṃ svargasya sopānaṃ pārāvārasya naur iva || That One Alone, without a second, is declared as the purifier of the Self; Truth is the staircase to heaven, like a boat to cross the shoreless ocean. Authority originates from the indivisible unity of consciousness Causation aligns with the sequential manifestation of truth Capacity-based responsibility arises from recognition of the Self Restoration logic follows the path of purification through truth Consciousness alignment is achieved by transcending duality

title: narada 1.192
content: अश्वमेधसहस्रं च सत्यं च तुलया धृतम् । अश्वमेधसहस्राद् धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते ॥ aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam | aśvamedhasahasrād dhi satyam eva viśiṣyate || Even a thousand horse sacrifices do not equal the merit of truth upheld by the scale of Dharma. Authority originates from alignment with Satyam, not ritual magnitude Causation is determined by consciousness integrity, not external performance Capacity-based responsibility arises from truthful discernment, not ceremonial accumulation Restoration logic prioritizes ontological truth over performative compensation Consciousness alignment supersedes transactional sacrifice

title: narada 1.193
content: varaṃ kūpaśatād vāpi varaṃ vāpīśatāt kratuḥ | varaṃ kratuśatāt putraḥ satyaṃ putraśatād varam || varaṃ kūpaśatād vāpi varaṃ vāpīśatāt kratuḥ | varaṃ kratuśatāt putraḥ satyaṃ putraśatād varam || Greater than a hundred wells is one well-built reservoir; greater than a hundred reservoirs is one kratu performed with integrity; greater than a hundred kratus is one who upholds the son's duty; greater than a hundred sons is adherence to truth. Authority resides in the qualitative superiority of action over mere quantity Causation flows from inner alignment rather than external accumulation Capacity-based responsibility escalates with conscious commitment to dharma Restoration logic prioritizes truth-consciousness over material outcomes Consciousness alignment determines the scale of spiritual and social value

title: narada 1.194
content:
भूर् धारयति सत्येन सत्येनोदेति भास्करः
सत्येन वायुः पवते सत्येनापः स्रवन्ति च bhūr dhārayati satyena satyenodeti bhāskaraḥ
satyena vāyuḥ pavate satyenāpaḥ sravanti ca The Earth sustains by Truth; the Sun rises by Truth;
The Wind blows by Truth; waters flow by Truth. Authority originates from alignment with Satya (Absolute Truth) Causation is rooted in ontological integrity, not material force Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious participation in Satya Restoration logic operates through re-alignment with foundational Truth Consciousness alignment determines lawful existence and function

title: narada 1.195
content:
सत्यमेव परं दानं सत्यमेव परं तपः।
सत्यमेव परो धर्मो लोकानामिति नः श्रुतम्॥ satyam eva paraṃ dānaṃ satyam eva paraṃ tapaḥ | satyam eva paro dharmo lokānām iti naḥ śrutam || Truth alone is the highest gift; truth alone is the supreme austerity; truth alone is the ultimate law for all beings—this We have heard. Authority flows from alignment with Satya (Absolute Truth) Causation originates in truthful expression and consciousness integrity Capacity-based responsibility arises through recognition of one's own truth Restoration logic operates by returning individuals to their inherent satyic state Consciousness alignment is achieved through unbroken adherence to truth

title: narada 1.196
content:
सत्यं देवाः समासेन मनुष्यास्त्वनृतं स्मृतम् ।
इहैव तस्य देवत्वं यस्य सत्ये स्थिता मतिः ॥ satyaṃ devāḥ samāsena manuṣyās tv anṛtaṃ smṛtam | ihaiva tasya devatvaṃ yasya satye sthitā matiḥ || Truth is the domain of the divine; untruth, the realm of humans. One whose consciousness abides in truth attains divinity even in this life. Authority originates from alignment with Satya (Absolute Truth) Causation arises from the stability of consciousness in truth Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's abidance in Satya Restoration occurs through re-alignment with inherent divinity Consciousness alignment determines ontological status

title: narada 1.197
content: सत्यं ब्रूहि अनृतं त्यक्त्वा सत्येन स्वर्गम् एष्यसि। उक्त्वानृतं महाघोरं नरकं प्रतिपत्स्यते॥ satyaṃ brūhi anṛtaṃ tyaktvā satyena svargam eṣyasi | uktvānṛtaṃ mahāghoraṃ narakaṃ pratipatsyate || Speak the truth; abandon falsehood. By truth, one attains svarga. Having spoken falsehood, one enters a great and terrifying naraka. Authority originates from alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation is established through vibrational resonance of speech Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious choice between satya and anṛta Restoration logic operates through realignment with truthful expression Consciousness alignment is achieved by abandoning distortion in speech

title: narada 1.198
content:
निरयेषु च ते शश्वज्जिह्वामुत्कृत्य दारुणाः।
असिभिः शातयिष्यन्ति बलिनो यमकिंकराः॥ nirayeṣu ca te śaśvajjihvāmutkṛtya dāruṇāḥ | asibhiḥ śātayiṣyanti balino yamakiṃkarāḥ || In infernal realms, those who have committed grave adharmic acts shall have their tongues severed by ruthless executioners wielding sharp blades, as decreed by the cosmic enforcers under Yama's command. Authority: Cosmic justice operates through hierarchically ordered agents executing Dharma without deviation. Causation: Adharmic speech generates consequences manifesting in proportionate experiential realities. Capacity-based responsibility: The capacity to speak dharmically obligates one to refrain from causing suffering via falsehood or defamation. Restoration logic: Suffering arises not as punishment but as a mechanism for recalibrating consciousness towards truth-speaking. Consciousness alignment: Experiential outcomes realign the jiva with the causal integrity of speech.

title: narada 1.199
content:
शूलैर् भेत्स्यन्ति चाक्रुद्धाः क्रोशन्तम् अपरायणम् ।
अवाक्शीरसम् उत्क्षिप्य क्षेप्स्यन्ति अग्निह्रदेषु च ॥ śūlair bhetsyanti cākruddhāḥ krośantam aparāyaṇam | avākśirasam utkṣipya kṣepsyanti agnihradeṣu ca || Those who act without anger shall pierce with tridents one who cries out in desperation and then cast him upside-down into fire-pits.
