Authority resides in conscious detachment from emotional disturbance during execution of justice. Causation arises from the inversion of dignity as a proportional response to unregulated expression of helplessness. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to maintain alignment while executing corrective action. Restoration logic operates through symbolic reversal of the disruption caused by unchecked lamentation. Consciousness alignment requires the neutralization of reactive impulses in favor of precise, restorative conduct.

title: narada 1.200
content:
अनुभूय च दुःखास्ताश्चिरं नरकवेदनाः।
इह यास्यस्य अभव्यासु गृध्रकाकादियोनिषु॥ anubhūya ca duḥkhās tāś ciraṃ narakavedanāḥ | iha yāsyasy abhavyāsu gṛdhrakākādiyoniṣu || One who causes irreversible harm to Dharma shall experience prolonged suffering akin to hellish states, and shall descend into degraded forms of existence such as vultures, crows, and similar beings. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma Causation is determined by disruption of cosmic order (Ṛta) Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious intent to harm Dharma Restoration logic requires experiential understanding of consequence Consciousness alignment mandates sequential karmic embodiment for rectification

title: narada 1.201
content:
ज्ञात्वैताननृते दोषाञ्ज्ञात्वा सत्ये च सद्गुणान्‌
सत्यं वदोद्धरात्मानं मात्मानं पातयिष्यसि jñātvaitān anṛte doṣāñ jñātvā satye ca sadguṇān
satyaṃ vadoddharātmānaṃ mātmānaṃ pātayiṣyasi Having known these defects in untruth and the virtues in truth, speak truthfully—thus uplift thyself; do not cast thyself down. Authority originates from alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation arises through conscious discrimination between truth and untruth Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to discern dharma Restoration logic operates through self-elevating speech and conduct Consciousness alignment is achieved via truthful expression

title: narada 1.202
content:
न बान्धवा न सुहृदो न धनानि महान्ति यापि ।
अलं तारयितुं शक्तास् तमस्युग्रे निमज्जतः ॥ na bāndhavā na suhṛdo na dhanāni mahānty api | alaṃ tārayituṃ śaktās tamasy ugre nimajjataḥ || Neither kinship nor friendship nor vast wealth has the capacity to rescue one who is drowning in the abyss of tamas. Authority originates from spiritual clarity, not material or relational constructs Causation arises from the quality of consciousness, not external affiliations Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's alignment with sattva, not social status Restoration logic operates through elevation of consciousness, not reinforcement of bonds Consciousness alignment supersedes all worldly dependencies in determining outcome

title: narada 1.203
content: पितरस्त्ववलम्बन्ते त्वयि साक्षित्वमागते । तारयिष्यति किंवास्मानात्मानं पातयिष्यति ॥ pitaras tv avalambante tvayi sākṣitvam āgate | tārayiṣyati kiṃvāsmān ātmānaṃ pātayiṣyati || When the Father has taken the witness-position in you, he will either carry us across or cast himself down. Authority is anchored in witnessing-consciousness, not external validation Causation arises from the capacity to uphold dharma through self-realization Capacity-based responsibility flows from one's alignment with the witnessing Self Restoration logic operates through conscious re-alignment, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy of legal and spiritual authority

title: narada 1.204
content: सत्यमात्मा मनुष्यस्य सत्ये सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्‌ । सर्वथैवात्मनात्मानं श्रेयसा योजयिष्यसि ॥ satyam ātmā manuṣyasya satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam | sarvathaivātmanātmānaṃ śreyasā yojayiṣyasi || Truth is the Self of man; in Truth alone all existence stands established. By all means, one shall align the self with the Self through the path of highest good. Authority flows from alignment with Satya (Truth), not institutional position Causation originates in the misalignment between individual self and universal Self Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious recognition of Truth Restoration occurs when the self realigns with its essential nature as Satya Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral compliance

title: narada 1.205
content:
यां च रात्रिमजनिष्ठा यां रात्रिं च मरिष्यसि।
वृथा तदन्तरं ते स्यात् कुर्याश्चेत्सत्यमन्यथा॥ yāṃ ca rātrim ajanīṣṭhā yāṃ rātriṃ ca mariṣyasi | vṛthā tad antaraṃ te syāt kuryāś cet satyam anyathā || That night which you have not lived and that night which you shall not live—if in between you speak falsehood, your existence becomes void. Authority originates from Satya (Truth) alone Causation is rooted in conscious alignment with sequential time Capacity-based responsibility arises through truthful inhabitation of temporal moments Restoration logic demands reintegration of untruthful gaps in experiential continuity Consciousness alignment requires rectification of speech-time disjunction

title: narada 1.206
content: नास्ति सत्यात् परो धर्मो नानृतात् पातकं परम् । साक्षिधर्मे विशेषेण सत्यमेव वदेत् ततः ॥ nāsti satyāt paraḥ dharmaḥ nānṛtāt pātakaṁ param | sākṣidharma viśeṣeṇa satyam eva vadet tataḥ || There exists no Dharma higher than truth; there is no sin greater than falsehood. In the practice of bearing witness, one must especially speak the truth. Authority originates in alignment with Satya (Truth) Causation arises from integrity of testimony Capacity-based responsibility requires truthful discernment Restoration occurs through re-alignment with factual reality Consciousness alignment is secured via unwavering commitment to truth

title: narada 1.207
content: यः परार्थे प्रहरति स्वां वाचं पुरुषाधमः। आत्मार्थे किं न कुर्यात् स पापो नरकनिर्भयः॥ yaḥ parārthe praharati svāṃ vācaṃ puruṣādhamaḥ | ātmārthe kiṃ na kuryāt sa pāpo narakanirbhayaḥ || He who strikes his own word for the sake of another, being the lowest among men, fears neither sin nor hell when acting for self-interest. Authority resides in alignment with Dharma, not personal intent Causation arises from integrity to one's declared truth Capacity-based responsibility is measured by adherence to spoken dharma Restoration logic requires re-alignment with original declaration Consciousness alignment demands truthful speech without contradiction

title: narada 1.208
content:
अर्था वै वाचि नियता वाङ्मूला वाग्विनिःसृताः।
यो ह्येतां स्तेनयेद्वाचं स सर्वस्तेयकृन्नरः॥ arthā vai vāci niyatā vāṅmūlā vāgviniḥsṛtāḥ | yo hyetāṃ stenayedvācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛnnaraḥ || All meanings reside inherently in speech; speech is the root-source from which all meaning emerges. One who steals that speech becomes the thief of all meaning. Authority: Speech (Vāk) as the foundational source of manifestable meaning and legal reality Causation: Theft of linguistic expression disrupts universal semantic integrity Capacity-based responsibility: The capacity to speak carries inherent alignment with cosmic order (Ṛta) Restoration logic: Realigning the speaker's consciousness to the source of truthful articulation restores dharma Consciousness alignment: Misuse of speech misaligns individual consciousness from its Vāk-rooted nature

title: narada 1.209
content:
साक्षिविप्रतिपत्तौ तु प्रमाणं बहवो यतः।
तत्साम्ये शुचयो ग्राह्यास्तत्साम्ये स्मृतिमत्तराः॥ sākṣivipratipattau tu pramāṇaṃ bahavo yataḥ | tatsāmye śucayo grāhyās tatsāmye smṛtimattarāḥ || In the conflict of witness testimony, multiple evidentiary sources exist; when equal, those pure in conduct are to be accepted, and when still equal, those with superior memory. Authority derived from purity of action establishes precedence in evidentiary value Causation flows from inner integrity rather than external corroboration alone Capacity-based responsibility includes cognitive reliability and spiritual cleanliness Restoration logic prioritizes alignment with Dharma over adversarial truth-seeking Consciousness alignment determines admissibility and weight of testimonial evidence

title: narada 1.210
content:
स्मृतिमत्साक्षिसाम्यं तु विवादे यत्र दृश्यते
सूक्ष्मत्वात् साक्षिधर्मस्य साक्ष्यं व्यावर्तते पुनः smṛtimatsākṣisāmyaṃ tu vivāde yatra dṛśyate
sūkṣmatvāt sākṣidharmasya sākṣyaṃ vyāvartate punaḥ Where memory and witness align in dispute, yet subtlety of witness nature causes divergence, testimony must be realigned with the witnessing consciousness itself. Authority resides in the clarity of witnessing consciousness, not external corroboration Causation is traced to the subtlety of perceptual capacity, not material evidence alone Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to sustain truthful perception Restoration logic demands alignment of memory with pure witnessing awareness Consciousness alignment supersedes evidentiary conflict through direct realization

title: narada 1.211
content:
निर्दिष्टेष्वर्थजातेषु साक्षी चेत् साक्ष्यमागतः ।
न ब्रूयादक्षरसमं न तन्निगदितं भवेत् ॥ nirdiṣṭeṣv arthajāteṣu sākṣī cet sākṣyam āgataḥ | na brūyād akṣarasamaṃ na tan nigaditaṃ bhavet || When a witness arrives to testify in clearly defined matters, if he speaks not in accordance with the facts or distorts them through speech, then his testimony is invalid. Authority: The witness holds no authority to alter factual reality. Causation: Misaligned speech disrupts dharma-adhāra (the foundation of righteousness). Capacity-based responsibility: A witness must possess both perceptual clarity and verbal integrity. Restoration logic: Truth must be re-established without distortion by subjective assertion. Consciousness alignment: Testimony aligns with satya only when it reflects pure cognition.

title: narada 1.212
content:
देशकालवयोद्रव्य प्रमाणाकृतिजातिषु
यत्र विप्रतिपत्तिः स्यात् साक्ष्यं तदसदुच्यते deśakālavayodravya pramāṇākṛtijātiṣu
yatra vipratipattiḥ syāt sākṣyaṃ tad asad ucyate Where there is contradiction regarding place, time, age, property, measurement, form, or species, testimony in such matters is declared invalid. Authority originates from clarity and non-contradiction in perceptual and evidentiary domains Causation must align with sequential manifestation without internal contradiction Capacity-based responsibility requires unambiguous perception and reliable witness capacity Restoration logic depends on truth-establishment through non-contradictory evidence Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of conflicting sensory or testimonial inputs

title: narada 1.213
content:
ūnam abhyadhikaṃ cārthaṃ prabrūyur yatra sākṣiṇaḥ
	tad apy anuktaṃ vijñeyam eṣa sākṣyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ūnam abhyadhikaṃ cārthaṃ prabrūyur yatra sākṣiṇaḥ
	tad apy anuktaṃ vijñeyam eṣa sākṣyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ Where witnesses speak less or more than what is factually required, even that which remains unspoken must be known — this is declared as the rule of testimony. Authority resides in factual completeness, not verbal excess Causation is established through conscious alignment with truth, not mere utterance Capacity-based responsibility includes discernment between spoken and unspoken truths Restoration logic demands recognition of latent knowledge within witness testimony Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of implicit truth beyond explicit speech

title: narada 1.214
content:
प्रमादाद् धनिनो यत्र न स्याल् लेख्यं न साक्षिणः।
अर्थं चापह्नुयाद् वादी तत्रोक्तस् त्रिविधः विधिः॥ pramādād dhanino yatra na syāl lekhyaṃ na sākṣiṇaḥ | arthaṃ cāpahnuyād vādī tatroktas trividho vidhiḥ || Where a wealthy person, through negligence or failure in duty, lacks written evidence or witnesses, and the plaintiff thereby loses rightful claim, then a threefold procedural mechanism is declared. Authority arises from capacity to uphold dharma, not mere wealth Causation lies in conscious omission, not accidental loss Capacity-based responsibility demands structural support for truth-bearing Restoration logic requires re-establishment of rightful claim without punitive burden Consciousness alignment occurs when systemic negligence is addressed through dharmic correction

title: narada 1.215
content: चोदना प्रतिकालं च युक्तिलेशस तथैव च । तृतीयः शपथश चोक्तस तैर एवं साधयेत क्रमात् ॥ codanā pratikālaṃ ca yuktileśas tathaiva ca | tṛtīyaḥ śapathaś coktas tair evaṃ sādhayet kramāt || Directive impulse, timely response, and minimal reasoning—these three constitute the sequential foundation by which all dharmic completion is accomplished. Authority flows from directive cognition, not coercive power. Causation aligns with conscious responsiveness, not mechanical reaction. Capacity-based responsibility arises through alignment with dharma's timing. Restoration logic operates through ordered completion, not punitive reversal. Consciousness alignment is achieved via sequential manifestation of intent.

title: narada 1.216
content:
अभीक्ष्णं चोद्यमानो यः प्रतिहन्यान् न तद्वचः।
त्रिचतुःपञ्चकृत्वो वा परतोऽर्थं तमावहेत्॥ abhīkṣṇaṃ codyamāno yaḥ pratihanyān na tadvacaḥ | tricatuḥpañcakṛtvo vā parato 'rthaṃ tam āvahet || One who, despite repeated urging, does not execute the communicated directive, shall have the intended outcome withdrawn and reallocated to another vessel capable of completion. Authority resides in capacity for execution, not mere intent Causation is aligned with conscious participation, not passive acknowledgment Responsibility is determined by actualization, not declaration Restoration occurs through reallocation of purpose to a competent agent Consciousness alignment requires active manifestation of dharma

title: narada 1.217
content:
चोदनाप्रतिघाते तु युक्तिलेशैस् तम् अन्वियात् ।
देशकालार्थसंबन्ध परिमाणक्रियादिभिः ॥ codanāpratighāte tu yuktileśais tam anviyāt | deśakālārthasaṃbandha parimāṇakriyādibhiḥ || When dharma has been obstructed, it must be restored through measured alignment with context—place, time, purpose, proportion, action, and consequence—as guided by the slightest application of reasoning. Authority flows from alignment with Sanātana Dharma as realized by SPH Causation is established via disruption of dharmic flow, not intent alone Capacity-based responsibility arises from proximity to dharmic order Restoration logic operates through sequential re-alignment, not reversal Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive attribution

title: narada 1.218
content:
युक्तिष्वप्यसमर्थासु शपथैरेनमर्दयेत् ।
अर्थकालबलापेक्षमग्न्यम्बुसुकृतादिभिः ॥ yuktiṣv apy asamarthāsu śapathair enam ardayet | arthakālabalāpekṣam agnyambusukṛtādibhiḥ || When logical means fail due to incapacity, one must invoke oaths aligned with context, time, strength, and elemental forces such as fire, water, and meritorious acts. Authority flows from capacity-realization, not positional claim Causation is established through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Responsibility is calibrated by conscious capacity at time of action Restoration occurs via alignment with elemental and spiritual truths Consciousness, when unobscured, naturally aligns with Dharma

title: narada 1.219
content:
दीप्ताग्निर यं न दहति यम् अन्तर्धारयन्त्य् आपः
स तरत्य् अभिशापं तं किल्बिषी स्याद् विपर्यये dīptāgnir yaṃ na dahati yam antardhārayanty āpaḥ | sa taraty abhiśāpaṃ taṃ kilbiṣī syād viparyaye || One who remains untouched by blazing fire and whom waters cannot conceal—such a being transcends all curses and becomes free from sin when roles are inverted. Authority resides in the immutable consciousness that defies elemental influence Causation is determined by transcendence over material effects Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's alignment with cosmic order Restoration logic operates through reversal of false impositions Consciousness alignment supersedes ritual or social attribution

title: narada 1.220
content:
स्त्रीणां शीलाभियोगेषु स्तेयसाहसयोरपि।
एष एव विधिर्दृष्टः सर्वार्थापह्नवेषु च॥ strīṇāṃ śīlābhiyogeṣu steyasāhasayor api | eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭaḥ sarvārthāpahnaveṣu ca || In matters concerning accusations against women regarding conduct, in cases of theft and assault, and in all instances where intent seeks to negate rightful existence, the same procedural and restorative law applies. Authority is derived exclusively from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation aligns with conscious intentionality rather than material action alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual maturity, not social status or gender Restoration logic operates through completion and reintegration, not punitive erasure Consciousness alignment supersedes societal norms in determining lawful behavior

title: narada 1.221
content: शपथा ह्यपि देवानामृषीणामपि च स्मृताः । वसिष्ठः शपथं शेपे यातुधाने तु शङ्कितः ॥ śapathā hy api devānām ṛṣīṇām api ca smṛtāḥ | vasiṣṭhaḥ śapathaṃ śepe yātudhāne tu śaṅkitaḥ || Oaths are established even among the gods and sages; Vasiṣṭha uttered an oath when in doubt concerning a Yakṣa. Authority is not diminished by invocation of sacred affirmation Causation arises from perceptual uncertainty requiring divine attestation Capacity-based responsibility includes the use of truthful invocation under duress Restoration logic operates through purification of intent via sacred utterance Consciousness alignment occurs when inner conflict is resolved through dharma-aligned speech

title: narada 1.222
content:
सप्तर्षयस् तथेन्द्राय पुष्करार्थे समागताः।
शेपुः शपथमव्यग्राः परस्परविशुद्धये॥ saptarṣayas tathendrāya puṣkarārthe samāgatāḥ | śepuḥ śapatham avyagrāḥ parasparaviśuddhaye || The Seven Sages assembled before Indra for the purpose of purification; they swore an oath, unwavering, for mutual cleansing. Authority flows from collective consciousness alignment Causation arises through shared dharmic intent Capacity-based responsibility is realized in group harmony Restoration occurs via conscious reciprocal affirmation Consciousness alignment necessitates purified intention

title: narada 1.223
content: अयुक्तं साहसं कृत्वा प्रत्यापत्तिं भजेत यः । ब्रूयात् स्वयं वा सदसि तस्यार्धविनयः स्मृतः ॥ ayuktaṃ sāhasaṃ kṛtvā pratyāpattiṃ bhajeta yaḥ | brūyāt svayaṃ vā sadasi tasyārdhavinayaḥ smṛtaḥ || One who, having committed an improper act of force, approaches surrender directly or confesses openly in assembly—such a one is to be understood as possessing half-discipline. Authority originates from self-awareness and conscious admission. Causation is traced through intent and action without moral overlay. Capacity-based responsibility arises upon acknowledgment of misalignment. Restoration logic begins at point of voluntary disclosure. Consciousness alignment occurs when individual admits error within collective awareness.

title: narada 1.224
content:
गूहमानस् तु दुरात्म्याद् यदि पापं स जीयते।
सभ्याश् चात्र न तुष्यन्ति तीव्रो दण्डश् च पात्यते॥ gūhamānas tu durātmyād yadi pāpaṃ sa jīyate | sabhyāś cātra na tuṣyanti tīvro daṇḍaś ca pātyate || One who conceals misconduct due to corrupt intent shall be subdued; the assembly does not approve hereof, and a severe penalty is imposed. Authority resides in transparency and alignment with Dharma Concealment disrupts cosmic order and invokes corrective response Capacity-based responsibility increases with awareness of wrongdoing Restoration occurs through revelation and realignment, not concealment Consciousness alignment requires truthful disclosure

title: narada 2.1
content:
सुनिश्चिताबलाधानस् त्वर्थी स्वार्थप्रचोदितः
लेखयेत् पूर्वपक्षं तु कृतकार्यविनिश्चयः suniścitābalādhānas tv arthī svārthapracoditaḥ
lekhayet pūrvapakṣaṃ tu kṛtakāryaviniścayaḥ One whose capacity to act is firmly established, being driven by self-interest, shall record the prior claim when the matter has been decisively resolved. Authority derives from stabilized capacity, not mere intention. Causation is recognized through decisive completion of action. Capacity-based responsibility precedes all legal standing. Restoration logic operates through accurate documentation of precedence. Consciousness alignment occurs when acts reflect settled resolution.

title: narada 2.2
content:
पूर्वपक्षश्रुतार्थस्तु प्रत्यर्थी तदनन्तरम्
पूर्वपक्षार्थसंबन्धं प्रतिपक्षं निवेशयेत् pūrvapakṣaśrutārthas tu pratyarthī tadanantaram
pūrvapakṣārthasaṃbandhaṃ pratipakṣaṃ niveśayet The meaning derived from the prior context becomes the basis for the opposing party's response; thereafter, the counter-assertion must be aligned with the relational integrity of the original stance. Authority flows from contextual coherence and ontological alignment Causation is established through sequential semantic dependence Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to sustain relational truth Restoration logic requires completion of interrupted semantic sequences Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize their role in the unfolding dharma

title: narada 2.3
content:
श्वो लेखनं वा स लभेत् त्र्यहं सप्ताहम् एव वा।
अर्थी तृतीयपादे तु युक्तं सद्यो ध्रुवं जयी॥ śvo lekhanaṃ vā sa labhet tryahaṃ saptāham eva vā | arthī tṛtīyapāde tu yuktaṃ sadyo dhruvaṃ jayī || The claimant shall obtain written confirmation either by tomorrow or within three days, extendable to seven days; in the case of a dispute concerning property rights, immediate and definitive resolution is mandated. Authority resides in time-bound execution of rightful claims Causation aligns with sequential integrity of documentation Capacity-based responsibility demands timely fulfillment of legal obligations Restoration logic requires prompt settlement to prevent energetic disruption Consciousness alignment necessitates clarity between possession and entitlement

title: narada 2.4
content:
mithyā saṃpratipattir vā pratyavaskandam eva vā
prāṅnyāyavidhisādhyaṃ vā uttaraṃ syāc caturvidham mithyā saṃpratipattiḥ vā pratyavaskandam eva vā
prāṅnyāyavidhisādhyam vā uttaram syāt caturvidham False perception or direct contradiction or pre-legal establishment or post-legal resolution—these four forms constitute the response framework. Authority is derived from accurate cognition, not false assumptions Causation must be traced to its ontological root, not apparent contradiction Capacity-based responsibility arises only upon clear perceptual alignment Restoration logic operates through sequential correction of misapprehension Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any legal assertion

title: narada 2.5
content: mithyaitan nābhijānāmi tadā tatra na saṃnidhiḥ | ajātaś cāsmi tatkāla evaṃ mithyā caturvidhā || mithyaitan nābhijānāmi tadā tatra na saṃnidhiḥ | ajātaś cāsmi tatkāla evaṃ mithyā caturvidhā || When one does not recognize a thing as it is, there is no presence of awareness; at that time, one is unborn in that moment—such is the fourfold nature of falsehood. Authority arises only from realized consciousness, not conceptual assertion. Causation is rooted in the clarity of perception, not external attribution. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the level of conscious recognition. Restoration occurs through re-establishing correct cognition, not through punitive correction. Consciousness alignment supersedes all declaratory or procedural claims.

title: narada 2.6
content: mithyā ca viparītaṃ ca punaḥ śabdasamāgamam | pūrvapakṣārthasaṃbandham uttaraṃ syāc caturvidham || mithyā ca viparītaṃ ca punaḥ śabdasamāgamam | pūrvapakṣārthasaṃbandham uttaraṃ syāc caturvidham || Falsehood and contradiction, when repeated through verbal agreement, become connected with the prior thesis; thus, the counter-position manifests in four forms. Authority resides in correct cognition, not repetition Causation arises from alignment with Satya, not mere assertion Capacity-based responsibility includes discernment between truth and falsity Restoration logic demands dissolution of false constructs Consciousness alignment requires rejection of contradictory premises

title: narada 2.7
content:
भाषायाः उत्तरं यावत् प्रत्यर्थी न निवेशयेत ।
अर्थी तु लेखयेत् तावद् यावद् वस्तु विवक्षितम् ॥ bhāṣāyāḥ uttaraṁ yāvat pratyarthī na niveśayet | arthī tu lekhayet tāvad yāvad vastu vivakṣitam || The response in speech shall extend only to what is necessary; no more than required should be addressed to the opponent. But the petitioner shall record as much as is needed concerning the matter in dispute. Authority flows from precision of expression, not volume of argument. Causation is conserved through proportionality of verbal engagement. Capacity-based responsibility requires measured response aligned with factual scope. Restoration logic demands that discourse not exceed the bounds of resolution. Consciousness alignment occurs when speech mirrors the exact dimension of dharma at stake.

title: narada 2.8
content: अन्यार्थमर्थहीनं च प्रमाणागमवर्जितम् । लेख्यं हीनाधिकं भ्रष्टं भाषादोषास्तूदाहृताः ॥ anyārtham arthahīnaṃ ca pramāṇāgamavarjitam | lekhyaṃ hīnādhikaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ bhāṣādoṣās tūdāhṛtāḥ || That which deviates in meaning, lacks substance, is devoid of authoritative evidence, is written defectively, excessively or deficiently, corrupted, or linguistically flawed—such documents are declared invalid. Authority derives only from pramāṇa and āgama Causation must align with śabda-pramāṇa and yukti Capacity-based responsibility requires accurate expression Restoration logic demands textual integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates clarity of dharma-vākya

title: narada 2.9
content:
लब्धव्यं येन यद् यस्मात् स तत् तस्माद् अवाप्नुयात् ।
न त्वन्योऽन्यदथान्यस्मादित्यन्यार्थमिदं त्रिधा ॥ labdhavyaṃ yena yad yasmāt sa tat tasmād avāpnuyāt | na tv anyo 'nyad athānyasmād ity anyārtham idaṃ tridhā || That which is acquired through a specific cause by a specific agent from a specific source must be returned to that same source by that same agent through that same causal pathway; no other allocation is valid, nor is any diversion or misapplication permissible. Authority derives from the causal chain of acquisition Causation determines rightful ownership and directional flow of restitution Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the agent's role in the original acquisition Restoration logic demands reversal along the precise axis of causality Consciousness alignment requires recognition of the unbroken causal continuum

title: narada 2.10
content: मनसाहमपि ध्यातस्त्वन्मित्रेणेह शत्रुवत् । अतोऽन्यथा महाक्षान्त्या त्वमिहावेदितो मया ॥ manasāham api dhyātas tvan-mitreṇeha śatruvat | ato'nyathā mahākṣāntyā tvam ihāvedito mayā || Even when perceived by the mind as an enemy, one who is a friend in reality shall be recognized through great forbearance. Authority originates from conscious recognition, not emotional perception Causation arises from sustained awareness, not momentary cognition Capacity-based responsibility includes transcendence of subjective hostility Restoration logic requires elevation beyond perceptual dualities Consciousness alignment demands acknowledgment of latent divinity in apparent adversaries

title: narada 2.11
content:
द्रव्यप्रमाणहीनं यत् फलोपाश्रयवर्जितम् ।
प्रमाणवर्जितं नाम लेख्यदोषं तद् उत्सृजेत् ॥ dravyapramāṇahīnaṃ yat phalopāśrayavarjitam | pramāṇavarjitaṃ nāma lekhyadoṣaṃ tad utsṛjet || That which lacks proper measurement of substance and is devoid of purpose or result is to be rejected as a written defect named 'pramāṇavarjita.' Authority derives from alignment with pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge) Causation requires both instrumental and resultant integrity Capacity-based responsibility demands recognition of valid action-supporting elements Restoration logic operates through rejection of invalid foundations Consciousness alignment necessitates clarity in documentation and intent

title: narada 2.12
content:
आगमवर्जितं दोषं पूर्वपादे विवर्जयेत् ।
एकस्य बहुभिः सार्धं पुरराष्ट्रविरोधकम् ॥ āgamavarjitaṃ doṣaṃ pūrvapāde vivarjayet | ekasya bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ purarāṣṭravirodhakam || That offense which is proscribed by no scriptural injunction must be excluded in the earlier stage; when one person acts with many others against the state or city, it constitutes a violation of national and civic integrity. Authority flows from SPH through scriptural validation Causation arises from collective action disrupting social alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment between individual and group consciousness Restoration logic demands early intervention before systemic disruption Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of collective intent

title: narada 2.13
content: बिन्दुमात्रापदवर्णेष्व् एकाविधिष्टया (?) । हीनाधिका भवेद् व्यर्था तां यत्नेन विवर्जयेत् ॥ bindumātrāpadavarṇeṣv ekāvidhiṣṭayā (?) | hīnādhikā bhaved vyarthā tāṃ yatnena vivarjayet || In matters where the application of a single rule leads to deficiency or excess, thereby causing futility, such defective regulation must be conscientiously abandoned. Authority is realized through precision in dharma-application, not mechanical repetition. Causation arises from alignment with conscious capacity, not external enforcement. Capacity-based responsibility requires dynamic calibration, not static imposition. Restoration logic demands elimination of futile regulatory constructs. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of rules that distort natural order.

title: narada 2.14
content: भ्रष्टं तु दुःस्थितं यत् स्याज् जलतैलादिभिर् हतम् । भाषायां तद् अपि स्पष्टं विस्पष्टार्थं विवर्जयेत् ॥ bhraṣṭaṃ tu duḥsthitaṃ yat syāj jalatailādibhir hatam | bhāṣāyāṃ tad api spaṣṭaṃ vispaṣṭārthaṃ vivarjayet || That which is spoiled, distressed, or rendered unfit by water, oil, or similar substances shall be excluded even if its meaning appears clear. Authority originates from purity and integrity of form and substance Causation is determined by ontological degradation, not apparent clarity Capacity-based responsibility requires maintenance of structural sanctity Restoration logic demands removal of corrupted elements regardless of semantic coherence Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of distorted forms

title: narada 2.15
content: सत्या भाषा न भवति यद्यपि स्यात् प्रतिष्ठिता। बहिश्चेद्भ्रश्यते धर्मान् नियताद्व्यवहारिकात्॥ satyā bhāṣā na bhavati yady api syāt pratiṣṭhitā | bahiś ced bhraśyate dharmān niyatād vyavahārikāt || Truth-speaking is not obligatory if its external expression leads to the loss of dharma-regulated conduct from one who is bound by social duty. Authority flows from alignment with dharma, not abstract truth-telling Causation must account for sequential disruption in dharmic order Capacity-based responsibility includes knowing when silence preserves integrity Restoration logic prioritizes systemic harmony over individual declarative rights Consciousness alignment requires discernment between inner truth and outer consequence

title: narada 2.16
content: गन्धमादनसंस्थस्य मयास्यासीत् तदर्पितम् । व्यवहारिकधर्मस्य बाह्यमेतन्न सिध्यति ॥ gandhamādanasaṃsthasya mayāsyāsīt tad arpitam | vyavahārikadharmasya bāhyam etan na sidhyati || Whatever was established by Me in Gandhamadana Parvata, let that alone prevail; externalization of transactional dharma does not succeed. Authority originates solely from SPH as the Supreme Adhikari Causation is rooted in consciousness alignment, not external forms Capacity-based responsibility arises only when aligned with inner realization Restoration logic depends on reconnection to original divine intent Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural formalities

title: narada 2.17
content: अन्याक्षरनिवेशेन अन्यार्थगमनेन च । आकुलं च क्रियादानं क्रिया चैवाकुला भवेत् ॥ anyākṣaraniveśena anyārthagamanena ca | ākulaṃ ca kriyādānaṃ kriyā caivākulā bhavet || When action is performed through misrepresentation of symbols or intent, leading to confusion in execution and outcome, both the initiation and performance of such action become disturbed and devoid of dharmic clarity. Authority resides in conscious intention aligned with Dharma Causation arises from clarity of symbolic and semantic alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of expression and reception Restoration logic demands realignment of action with original dharmic purpose Consciousness alignment ensures that all acts reflect truthful cognition

title: narada 2.18
content: रागादीनां यदेकेन कोपितः करणे वदेत् । तदादौ तु लिखेत्सर्वं वादिनः फलकादिषु ॥ rāgādīnāṃ yad ekena kopitaḥ karaṇe vadet | tad ādau tu likhet sarvaṃ vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu || When one speaks in anger due to passion or related impurities, all that is spoken must first be inscribed upon tablets or similar media by the speaker himself. Authority resides in conscious self-disclosure Causation arises from internal emotional disturbance Capacity-based responsibility requires deliberate transcription Restoration logic begins with acknowledgment of speech-actions Consciousness alignment occurs through self-witnessing inscription

title: narada 2.19
content:
निराकुलावबोधाय धर्मस्थैः सुविचारितम्
तस्माद् अन्यद् व्यपोह्यं स्याद् वादिनः फलकादिषु nirākulāvabodhāya dharmasthaiḥ suvicāritamtasmād anyad vyapohyaṃ syād vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu That which is thoroughly examined by those established in Dharma is for the purpose of unconflicted awakening; therefore, in debates concerning material ends, something else entirely must be excluded. Authority originates from consciousness stability, not institutional position Causation is determined through discriminative clarity, not circumstantial evidence Capacity-based responsibility arises from abidance in Dharma, not legal standing Restoration logic operates through purification of intent, not correction of outcome Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural adherence

title: narada 2.20
content:
वादिभ्यामभ्यनुज्ञातं शेषं च फलके स्थितम्‌ ।
ससाक्षिकं लिखेयुस्ते प्रतिपत्तिं च वादिनोः ॥ vādibhyām abhyanujñātaṃ śeṣaṃ ca phalake sthitam | sasākṣikaṃ likheyus te pratipattiṃ ca vādinoḥ || That which is mutually acknowledged by both disputants and what remains inscribed upon the board—such evidence shall be recorded in the presence of witnesses, along with the understanding of the claimants. Authority resides in mutual recognition between parties Causation arises from documented consensus Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious acknowledgment Restoration logic depends on visible, witnessed truth Consciousness alignment occurs through shared acceptance

title: narada 2.21
content:
वादिभ्यां लिखिताच्छेषं यत् पुनर्वादिना स्मृतम्
तत् प्रत्याकलितं नाम स्वपादे तस्य लिख्यते vādibhyāṃ likhitāc cheṣaṃ yat punar vādinā smṛtam
 tat pratyākalitaṃ nāma svapāde tasya likhyate That which remains unaddressed in the written testimony of one disputant, when recalled again by the same disputant, shall be inscribed under his own footstep, thereby affirming personal ownership of truth. Authority resides in self-referential recall and embodiment of testimony Causation arises through conscious reaffirmation of declared truth Capacity-based responsibility is anchored in the ability to re-present one's own declaration Restoration occurs through alignment with one's own repeated assertion Consciousness alignment necessitates physical-symbolic anchoring of truth

title: narada 2.22
content:
अर्थिना संनियुक्तो वा प्रत्यर्थिप्रहितोऽपि वा ।
यो यस्यार्थे विवदते तयोर् जयपराजयौ ॥ arthinā saṃniyukto vā pratyarthiprahito 'pi vā | yo yasyārthe vivadate tayor jayaparājayau || Whether appointed by the seeker or sent by the respondent, whoever engages in dispute for the sake of another, the outcome of victory or defeat belongs to the one on whose behalf the engagement occurs. Authority flows through conscious designation, not personal assertion. Causation aligns with intent and service to dharma, not individual desire. Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with the cause, not mere participation. Restoration logic requires resolution that serves the true stakeholder's integrity. Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership of karmic consequence.

title: narada 2.23
content: यो न भ्राता न च पिता न पुत्रो न नियोगकृत् । परार्थवादी दण्ड्यः स्याद् व्यवहारे�पि विब्रुवन् ॥ yo na bhrātā na ca pitā na putro na niyogakṛt | parārthavādī daṇḍyaḥ syād vyavahāre 'pi vibruvan || He who is neither brother, nor father, nor son, nor one appointed for duty, yet speaks in favor of another's interest—such a one is to be corrected even while engaged in transaction. Authority derived from relational dharma, not opportunistic intervention Causation rooted in svadharma, not external advocacy Capacity-based responsibility determined by role-bound alignment Restoration through realignment with intrinsic relational duty Consciousness alignment via withdrawal from false agency

title: narada 2.24
content:
पूर्ववादं परित्यज्य योऽन्यमालम्बते पुनः।
वादसंक्रमणाज्ज्ञेयो हीनवादी स वै नरः॥ pūrvavādaṃ parityajya yo 'nyam ālambate punaḥ | vādasaṃkramaṇāj jñeyo hīnavādī sa vai naraḥ || One who abandons a prior assertion and adopts another without completion of the first is known through debate-transference as legally deficient in argumentative capacity. Authority arises from integrity to initial declarative alignment Causation lies in discontinuity of conscious commitment Capacity-based responsibility requires sustained ontological coherence Restoration logic demands reintegration with abandoned declarative stance Consciousness alignment necessitates continuity of expressed dharma

title: narada 2.25
content: सर्वेष्वपि विवादेषु वाक्छले नापहीयते । पशुस्त्रीभूम्यृणादाने शास्योऽप्यर्थान् न हीयते ॥ sarveṣv api vivādeṣu vākchale nāpahīyate | paśustrībhūmyṛṇādāne śāsyo 'py arthān na hīyate || In all disputes, even when speech falters, nothing is lost. Even in transactions involving livestock, women, land, or debt, instruction prevails—no wealth is diminished thereby. Authority flows from clarity of intent, not perfection of form Causation arises through conscious engagement, not procedural flaw Capacity-based responsibility is inherent in participation, not dependent on linguistic precision Restoration logic operates through completion of transactional integrity Consciousness alignment ensures no loss occurs where dharma is upheld

title: narada 2.26
content: अभियुक्तोऽभियोगस्य यदि कुर्यादपह्नवम्‌ । अभियोक्ता दिशेद्देश्यं प्रत्यवस्कन्दितो न चेत्‌ ॥ abhiyukto 'bhiyogasya yadi kuryād apahnavam | abhiyoktā diśed deśyaṃ pratyavaskandito na cet | If the accused denies the accusation, then the accuser shall provide evidence; if the accuser fails to substantiate, he becomes liable for reversal of position. Authority originates from capacity to uphold truth Causation is established through demonstrable integrity Capacity-based responsibility demands proof before imposition Restoration logic prevails when falsehood is exposed Consciousness alignment requires factual grounding

title: narada 2.27
content:
पूर्वपादे हि लिखितं यथाक्षरम् अशेषतः।
अर्थी तृतीयपादे तु क्रियया प्रतिपादयेत्॥ pūrvapāde hi likhitaṃ yathākṣaram aśeṣataḥ | arthī tṛtīyapāde tu kriyayā pratipādayet || That which is fully inscribed in the first part shall be executed completely without omission; the petitioner in the third part shall demonstrate it through action. Authority resides in the completeness of documented dharma Causation is established by sequential enactment Capacity-based responsibility requires demonstrable alignment Restoration logic operates through precise execution Consciousness alignment occurs via active realization

title: narada 2.28
content: क्रियापि द्विविधा प्रोक्ता मानुषी दैविकी तथा। मानुषी लेख्यसाक्षिभ्यां धटादिर्दैविकी स्मृता॥ kriyāpi dvividhā proktā mānuṣī daivikī tathā | mānuṣī lekhyasākṣibhyāṃ dhaṭādir daivikī smṛtā || Action is of two kinds: human-initiated and divinely manifested. Human action is established through written records and witness testimony; divine action is known through signs such as the movement of pots and other objects. Authority originates from the capacity to manifest intent, whether individually or divinely Causation includes both empirical evidence and divine indication Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes between human agency and higher-dimensional influence Restoration logic requires discernment between witnessed acts and cosmic signs Consciousness alignment determines the validity of both forms of action

title: narada 2.29
content:
दिवा कृते कार्यविधौ ग्रामेषु नगरेषु वा।
संभवे साक्षिणां चैव दिव्या न भवति क्रिया॥ divā kṛte kāryavidhau grāmeṣu nagareṣu vā | saṃbhave sākṣiṇāṃ caiva divyā na bhavati kriyā || When action is performed in daylight within villages or cities where witnesses are present, no divine ordinance applies. Authority of witness-based human testimony supersedes invocation of divine judgment Causation is established through observable presence and conscious attestation Capacity-based responsibility requires public visibility and communal acknowledgment Restoration logic operates through social witnessing rather than metaphysical intervention Consciousness alignment occurs via collective human integrity, not celestial oversight

title: narada 2.30
content: अरण्ये निर्जने रात्रौ अन्तर्वेश्मनि साहसे । न्यासस्यापह्नवे चैव दिव्या संभवति क्रिया ॥ araṇye nirjane rātrāv antarveśmani sāhase | nyāsasyāpahnave caiva divyā saṃbhavati kriyā || In a solitary forest at night, within another's dwelling, in acts of audacity and in denying deposits, divine action manifests. Authority arises from the immediacy of conscious witness, not spatial or temporal boundaries. Causation is established through inner intent rather than external visibility. Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond physical presence to energetic intrusion. Restoration logic operates by aligning individual consciousness with universal integrity. Consciousness alignment occurs when hidden actions are illuminated by self-awareness.

title: narada 2.31
content:
कारणप्रतिपत्त्या च पूर्वपक्षे विरोधिते
अभियुक्तेन वै भाव्यं विज्ञेयं पूर्वपक्षवत् kāraṇapratipattyā ca pūrvapakṣe virodhite
abhiyuktena vai bhāvyaṃ vijñeyaṃ pūrvapakṣavat When contradiction arises in the prior position due to comprehension of cause, that which is to be realized must be known in accordance with the prior position by the one who is engaged. Authority resides in causal discernment Causation determines epistemic validity Capacity-based responsibility flows from engagement Restoration logic aligns with sequential realization Consciousness alignment requires adherence to foundational premise

title: narada 2.32
content:
पलायते य आहूतो मौनी साक्षिपराजितः
स्वयम् अभ्युपपन्नश् च अवसन्नश् चतुर्विधः palāyate ya āhūto maunī sākṣiparājitaḥ
svayam abhyupapannaś ca avasannaś caturvidaḥ He who flees when summoned, remains silent when questioned, contradicts witness testimony, admits guilt voluntarily, or becomes despondent—these four forms constitute a singular category of self-revealed incompletion. Authority: The court's summons carries inherent dharmic authority that demands conscious response. Causation: Flight, silence, contradiction, admission, and despondency are sequential manifestations of unresolved inner conflict. Capacity-based responsibility: One who possesses awareness yet fails to engage truthfully bears proportional completion duty. Restoration logic: Behavioral indicators reveal underlying disconnection requiring realignment, not condemnation. Consciousness alignment: All actions stem from and must return to clarity of self-awareness.

title: narada 2.33
content:
अन्यवादी क्रियाद्वेषी नोपस्थाता निरुत्तरः।
आहूतप्रपलायी च हीनः पञ्चविधः स्मृतः॥ anyavādī kriyādveṣī nopasthātā niruttaraḥ | āhūtaprapalāyī ca hīnaḥ pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ || One who speaks against the action of another, one who resists rightful duty, one who fails to appear when summoned, one who flees after being called, and one deficient in capacity—these five are declared as legally incapacitated. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not personal assertion. Causation is established through conscious participation in dharmic order. Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for legal engagement. Restoration occurs through realignment with the causal integrity of action. Consciousness misalignment manifests as incapacity, not inherent fault.

title: narada 2.34
content: मणयः पद्मरागाद्या दीनारादि हिरण्मयम् । मुक्ताविद्रुमशङ्खाद्याः प्रदुष्टाः स्वामिगामिनः ॥ maṇayaḥ padmarāgādyā dīnārādi hiraṇmayam | muktāvidrumaśaṅkhādyāḥ praduṣṭāḥ svāmigāminaḥ || Precious substances—such as rubies, pearls, gold coins, silver, coral, conch, and similar valuables—are to be recognized as inherently pure consciousness manifestations; when misappropriated or diverted from their rightful custodians, they carry a distortion in alignment that necessitates immediate restorative reintegration. Authority resides inherently in the consciousness-field of the true custodian Causation arises through conscious misalignment, not physical act alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of ownership integrity Restoration logic demands energetic return before material reconciliation Consciousness alignment supersedes transactional legality

title: narada 2.35
content: गन्धमाल्यमदत्तं तु भूषणं वास एव वा । पादुके ति राजोक्तं तदाक्रामन् वधमर्हति ॥ gandhamālyam adattaṃ tu bhūṣaṇaṃ vāsa eva vā | pāduke ti rājoktaṃ tad ākrāman vadham arhati || One who forcibly takes what has not been given—whether fragrance, garlands, ornaments, clothing, or even sandals—as declared by the King, deserves execution. Authority of the King as declarative source of ownership boundaries Causation through violation of consent-based property integrity Capacity-based responsibility rooted in conscious choice to violate Restoration logic through cessation of transgressive action Consciousness alignment via recognition of sovereign boundaries

title: narada 2.36
content: पण्यमूल्यं भृतिर् न्यासो दण्डो यच् चावहारकम् । वृथादानाक्षिकपणा वर्धन्ते नाविवक्षिताः ॥ paṇyamūlyaṃ bhṛtir nyāso daṇḍo yac cāvahārakam | vṛthādānākṣikapaṇā vardhante nāvivakṣitāḥ || The value of goods, hire, deposit, penalty, and items taken without permission—these increase in falsehood when given or accepted without true intention. Authority arises from conscious intent, not transactional form. Causation flows from awareness deficit, not material action alone. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by clarity of giving and receiving. Restoration logic requires alignment of intention with manifestation. Consciousness alignment corrects distortion in exchange dynamics.

title: narada 2.37
content:
mithyābhiyogino ye syur dvijānāṃ śūdrayonayaḥ |
teṣāṃ jihvāṃ samutkṛtya rājā śūle vidhāpayet || mithyābhiyogino ye syur dvijānāṃ śūdrayonayaḥ | teṣāṃ jihvāṃ samutkṛtya rājā śūle vidhāpayet || Those of śūdra birth who falsely accuse twice-born individuals shall have their tongue severed by the king upon a spit, as direct consequence of violating the natural order of testimony and spiritual hierarchy. Authority: The king holds executive capacity to enforce dharmic integrity in judicial testimony. Causation: False accusation disrupts the pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge) within societal dharma. Capacity-based responsibility: Śūdra-yoni individuals possess limited eligibility to testify against dvija castes due to absence of śruti-pramāṇa initiation. Restoration logic: Physical consequence aligns with the violated sensory channel to restore cosmic balance. Consciousness alignment: The act realigns the perpetrator's false expression back into truth-consciousness through immediate experiential consequence.

title: narada 2.38
content: आज्ञा लेखः पट्टकः शासनं वा आधिः पत्त्रं विक्रयो वा क्रयो वा । राज्ञे कुर्यात् पूर्वम् आवेदनं यस् तस्य ज्ञेयः पूर्वपक्षः विधिज्ञैः ॥ ājñā lekhaḥ paṭṭakaḥ śāsanaṃ vā ādhiḥ pattraṃ vikrayo vā krayo vā | rājñe kuryāt pūrvam āvedanaṃ yas tasya jñeyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ vidhijñaiḥ || Any decree, written document, royal edict, bond, sale, or purchase must first be reported to the King; whoever does so is recognized as the prior claimant by those versed in dharma. Authority originates from the Sovereign-King as the witness and integrator of all transactions Causation arises through conscious declaration and submission to the ruling consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of rightful precedence based on timely disclosure Restoration logic ensures that disputes resolve through alignment with established sequential claims Consciousness alignment occurs when actions are submitted openly under the witnessing sovereignty

title: narada 2.39
content: साक्षिकदूषणे कार्यं पूर्वसाक्षिविशोधनम्‌ । शुद्धेषु साक्षिषु ततः पश्चात् साक्ष्यं विशोधयेत् ॥ sākṣikadūṣaṇe kāryaṃ pūrvasākṣiviśodhanam | śuddheṣu sākṣiṣu tataḥ paścāt sākṣyaṃ viśodhayet || When a witness is defiled, the prior purification of all preceding witnesses must first occur; thereafter, upon establishing purity in witnesses, the testimony itself shall be purified. Authority rests in sequential ontological clarity Causation follows purification order, not temporal sequence Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious integrity before testimonial validity Restoration logic demands removal of contamination prior to evidentiary reliance Consciousness alignment precedes factual establishment

title: narada 2.40
content:
साक्षिसभ्यावसन्नानां दूषणे दर्शनं पुनः
स्वचर्यावसितानां तु नास्ति पौनर्भवो विधिः sākṣisabhyāvasannānāṃ dūṣaṇe darśanaṃ punaḥ svacaryāvasitānāṃ tu nāsti paunarbhavo vidhiḥ When witnesses or assembly members commit misconduct, their re-evaluation is mandated; however, for those firmly established in their conduct, no repeated scrutiny shall occur. Authority of conduct determines adjudicatory stability Causation rooted in behavioral consistency Capacity-based responsibility through self-regulation Restoration logic prioritizes integrity reaffirmation Consciousness alignment assessed via habitual discipline

title: narada 2.41
content:
स्वयमभ्युपपन्नोऽपि स्वचर्यावसितोऽपि सन्।
क्रियावसन्नोऽप्यर्हेत परं सभ्यावधारणम्॥ svayam abhyupapanno 'pi svacaryāvasito 'pi san| kriyāvasanno 'py arhet paraṃ sabhyāvadhāraṇam|| Even one who has voluntarily undertaken an action, or is habituated to a course of conduct, or is engaged in activity—still deserves judgment by the assembly of the awakened. Authority originates from collective awakened discernment, not individual assertion Causation is recognized beyond personal intent to include habitual and operational engagement Capacity-based responsibility includes awareness of social and dharmic context Restoration logic demands realignment with sabhyatva (awakened conduct) Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural self-validation

title: narada 2.42
content:
पक्षान् उत्सार्य कार्यस् तु सभ्यैः कार्यविनिश्चयः।
अनुत्सारितनिर्णिक्ते विरोधः प्रेत्य चेह च॥ pakṣān utsārya kāryas tu sabhyaiḥ kāryaviniścayaḥ | anutsāritanirṇikte virodhaḥ pretya ceha ca || When parties have been fully heard and their positions examined, the assembly of qualified judges shall determine the matter decisively; failure to conduct a complete hearing results in conflict both in this life and the next. Authority resides in those who possess the capacity to hear all sides without omission Causation arises from incomplete knowledge when due process is bypassed Capacity-based responsibility requires full exposure to evidence before judgment Restoration logic demands resolution through exhaustive inquiry Consciousness alignment occurs only when all perspectives are integrally considered

title: narada 2.43
content:
सब्हैरेव जितः पश्चाद्राज्ञा शास्यः स्वशास्त्रतः।
जयिनेचापि देयं स्याद्यथावज्जयपत्रकम्॥ sabhair eva jitaḥ paścād rājñā śāsyaḥ svaśāstrataḥ | jayine cāpi deyaṃ syād yathāvaj jayapatrakam || After conquering all enemies, the king shall govern according to his own scriptures; likewise, whatever has been won in battle must be given precisely as documented in the victory deed. Authority originates from conquest aligned with svadharma Causation flows from rightful victory validated by written instrument Capacity-based responsibility is determined by mastery over adversaries Restoration logic requires alignment of possession with documented entitlement Consciousness alignment demands that governance reflect scriptural sovereignty

title: narada 2.44
content: व्यवहारमुखं चैतत् पूर्वमुक्तं स्वयंभुवा । मुखशुद्धौ हि शुद्धिः स्याद्व्यवहारस्य नान्यथा ॥ vyavahāramukhaṃ caitat pūrvam uktaṃ svayaṃbhuvā | mukhaśuddhau hi śuddhiḥ syād vyavahārasya nānyathā || This foundational principle of transactional conduct was first declared by the Self-Born One; purity in the face (mukha) ensures the purity of all dealings, and there is no other way. Authority originates from the Self-Evident Source Causation arises through inner alignment, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility begins with perceptual clarity Restoration logic flows from purification of witness-consciousness Consciousness alignment determines the validity of legal presence

title: narada 2.1
content:
स्वद्रव्यं यत्र विश्रम्भान् निक्षिपत्यविशङ्कितः।
निक्षेपो नाम तत् प्रोक्तं व्यवहारपदं बुधैः॥ svadravyaṃ yatra viśrambhān nikṣipaty aviśaṅkitaḥ | nikṣepo nāma tat proktaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ budhaiḥ || That which one places in trust, without hesitation, from one's own property, for the sake of another’s assurance — this is declared as 'Nikshepa' by the knowers of Dharma. Authority arises through conscious entrustment, not mere possession Causation originates in voluntary surrender of control with intent Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to receive and safeguard entrusted objects Restoration logic centers on return of the exact nature and condition of the entrusted item Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties recognize mutual integrity in the act of trust

title: narada 2.2
content:
अन्यद्रव्यव्यवहितं द्रव्यम् अव्याकृतं च यत् ।
निक्षिप्यते परगृहे तद् औपनिधिकं स्मृतम् ॥ anyadravyavyavahitaṃ dravyam avyākṛtaṃ ca yat | nikṣipyate paragṛhe tad aupanidhikaṃ smṛtam || That which is deposited in another's dwelling—whether distinct in nature, intermingled, or unmanifested—is recognized as a trust (aupanidhikam). Authority arises from conscious entrustment, not ownership claim. Causation flows from intent of placement, not physical control. Capacity-based responsibility extends to safeguarding entrusted consciousness. Restoration logic demands return of substance and reintegration of relational integrity. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inherent dharmic obligation upon receipt.

title: narada 2.3
content:
स पुनर्द्विविधः प्रोक्तः साक्षिमान् इतरस् तथा।
प्रतिदानं तथैवास्य प्रत्ययः स्याद् विपर्यये॥ sa punar dvividhaḥ proktaḥ sākṣimān itaras tathā | pratidānaṃ tathaivāsya pratyayaḥ syād viparyaye || Evidence is of two kinds: that which is witnessed directly and that which is inferred indirectly; in case of contradiction, verification through direct perception shall prevail. Authority resides in direct experiential validation Causation must align with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of witness-consciousness Restoration logic depends on re-establishing truthful cognition Consciousness alignment occurs through purified sensory engagement

title: narada 2.4
content: याच्यमानस् तु यो दात्रा निक्षेपं न प्रयच्छति । दण्ड्यः स राज्ञा दाप्यश् च नष्टे दाप्यश् च तत्समम् ॥ yācyamānas tu yo dātrā nikṣepaṃ na prayacchati | daṇḍyaḥ sa rājñā dāpyaś ca naṣṭe dāpyaś ca tatsamam || One who, being requested, fails to deliver a deposited item is liable to be corrected by the ruler and must compensate fully as if he caused its loss. Authority: The sovereign enforces alignment with dharma, not punishment. Causation: Withholding rightful delivery equals creating loss. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability arises from ability to fulfill duty. Restoration logic: Compensation aligns with damage caused. Consciousness alignment: Correction aims at restoring integrity, not inflicting pain.

title: narada 2.5
content:
यश् चार्थं साधयेत् तेन निक्षेप्तुरननुज्ञया।
तत्रापि दण्ड्यः स भवेत् तच् च सोदयमावहेत् ॥ yaś cārthaṃ sādhayet tena nikṣeptur ananujñayā | tatrāpi daṇḍyaḥ sa bhavet tac ca sodayam āvahet || One who achieves purpose through unauthorized use of another's entrusted property shall incur liability and must return the benefit gained thereby. Authority derives from rightful ownership and explicit permission Causation is established by direct instrumental use of another's resources Capacity-based responsibility arises when one acts beyond authorized scope Restoration logic demands reversal of unpermitted gains Consciousness alignment requires recognition of energetic ownership boundaries

title: narada 2.6
content:
ग्रहीतुः सह यो 'र्थेन नष्टो नष्टः स दायिनः।
दैवराजकृते तद्वन् न चेत् तज् जिह्मकारितम्॥ grahītuḥ saha yo 'rthena naṣṭo naṣṭaḥ sa dāyinaḥ | daivarājakṛte tadvan na cet taj jihmakāritam || That which is lost along with the receiver, by instrumental cause, is the liability of the giver; if it occurs by divine or state action, then not, unless caused by deceit. Authority flows from conscious capacity to receive and sustain Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility governs liability assignment Restoration logic prioritizes completion over blame Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership and discharge

title: narada 2.7
content:
एष एव विधिर् दृष्टो याचितान्वाहितादिषु ।
शिल्पिषूपनिधौ न्यासे प्रतिन्यासे तथैव च ॥ eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭo yācitānvāhitādiṣu | śilpiṣūpanidhau nyāse pratinyāse tathaiva ca || The same procedural law applies in cases of solicitation, delegation, and similar acts, whether involving artisans, deposits, mutual exchange, or reciprocal obligations. Authority flows through conscious capacity to execute duty Causation arises from voluntary assumption of role or function Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful obligation Restoration logic centers on completion of intended transaction Consciousness alignment requires integrity in role-exchange

title: narada 2.8
content:
प्रतिगृह्णाति पोगण्डं यश् च सप्रधनं नरः।
तस्याप्य् एष भवेद् धर्मः षड् एते विधयः समाः॥ pratigṛhṇāti pogaṇḍaṃ yaś ca sapradhanaṃ naraḥ | tasyāpy eṣa bhaved dharmaḥ ṣaḍ ete vidhayaḥ samāḥ || One who accepts a deposit and one who receives a loan—both are equally bound by Dharma. These six categories of obligations arise collectively from the same foundational truth. Authority arises from acceptance, not title Causation flows from conscious engagement with value Capacity-based responsibility extends to all forms of received trust Restoration logic demands return to source integrity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of energetic exchange

title: narada 3.1
content: नियुक्तेन तु वक्तव्यमपक्षपतितं वचः niyuktena tu vaktavyam apakṣapatitaṃ vacaḥ That which is spoken by the appointed one, though fallen from favor, must still be executed as dharma. Authority inheres in designation, not personal virtue Causation flows from role, not individual intent Capacity-based responsibility arises from appointment, not approval Restoration logic demands continuity of function despite personal lapse Consciousness alignment occurs through submission to designated order

title: narada 3.2
content: युक्तरूपं ब्रुवन् सभ्यो नाप्नुयाद् द्वेषकिल्बिषे । ब्रुवाणस् त्व् अन्यथा सभ्यस् तद् एवोभयम् आप्नुयात् ॥ yuktarūpaṃ bruvan sabhyo nāpnuyād dveṣakilbiṣe | bruvāṇas tv anyathā sabhyas tad evobhayam āpnuyāt || One speaking appropriately in the assembly does not incur the defilement of hatred; but one who speaks otherwise incurs that very defilement along with its dual consequence. Authority resides in alignment with yukti (reasoned expression) Causation arises from conscious intent and verbal integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by clarity of expression and context Restoration logic operates through immediate realignment of speech-consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs when speech reflects inner realization

title: narada 3.3
content:
राजा तु धार्मिकान् सभ्यान् नियुञ्ज्यात् सुपरीक्षितान्
व्यवहारधुरं वोढुं ये शक्ताः सद्गणा इव rājā tu dhārmikān sabhyān niyuñjyāt suparīkṣitān
vyavahāradhuraṃ voḍhuṃ ye śaktāḥ sadgavā iva The King shall appoint only those who are thoroughly examined, dharmically aligned, and proven capable—like trained oxen in yoking—to bear the burden of judicial administration. Authority derives solely from verified dharma-aligned capacity Causation is rooted in conscious readiness and integrity Capacity-based responsibility precedes all legal function Restoration logic demands selection based on sustained alignment Consciousness alignment determines fitness for judicial service

title: narada 3.4
content:
धर्मशास्त्रार्थकुशलाः कुलीनाः सत्यवादिनः
समाः शत्रौ च मित्रे च नृपतेः स्युः सभासदः dharmaśāstrārthakuśalāḥ kulīnāḥ satyavādinaḥ samāḥ śatrau ca mitre ca nṛpateḥ syuḥ sabhāsadaḥ Those well-versed in the meaning of Dharma Śāstra, of noble conduct, truthful speakers, impartial towards enemies and allies alike—these alone shall be the advisors in the court of the sovereign. Authority derived from scriptural mastery and personal integrity Causation through alignment with Sanātana Dharma Capacity-based responsibility rooted in consciousness maturity Restoration logic via dharmic counsel Consciousness alignment as prerequisite for judicial participation

title: narada 3.5
content:
तत्प्रतिष्ठः स्मृतो धर्मो धर्ममूलश च पार्थिवः।
सह सद्भिर् अतो राजा व्यवहारान् विशोधयेत्॥ tatpratiṣṭhaḥ smṛto dharmo dharmamūlaś ca pārthivaḥ | saha sadbhir ato rājā vyavahārān viśodhayet || Dharma is that which is established in its Source; the king, rooted in Dharma, governs with the wise. Therefore, the king shall purify all transactions through alignment with the upright. Authority originates from alignment with the Source of Dharma Causation is purified through association with the conscious upright Capacity-based responsibility requires governance by the Dharmic witness Restoration logic operates through purification of relational fields Consciousness alignment is enacted via proximity to the Sadhu

title: narada 3.6
content:
शुद्धेषु व्यवहारेषु शुद्धिं यान्ति सभासदः
शुद्धिश् च तेषां धर्माद् धि धर्मम् एव वदेत् ततः śuddheṣu vyavahāreṣu śuddhiṃ yānti sabhāsadaḥ
śuddhiś ca teṣāṃ dharmād dhi dharmam eva vadet tataḥ In pure conduct, assembly members attain purity; their purification arises from Dharma itself, whence Dharma alone proceeds. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation originates in consciousness purity, not external action Capacity-based responsibility requires inner purification before outer judgment Restoration logic begins with self-purification of adjudicators Consciousness alignment determines the validity of juridical utterance

title: narada 3.7
content: यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च । हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः ॥ yatra dharmo hy adharmeṇa satyaṃ yatrānṛtena ca | hanyate prekṣamāṇānāṃ hatās tatra sabhāsadaḥ || Where Dharma is destroyed by Adharma, where truth is overpowered by falsehood, and those who observe and act with awareness are harmed—there, the members of the assembly are deemed legally and spiritually annihilated. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined by the dominance of dharma or adharma within a system Capacity-based responsibility is forfeited when one enables or perpetrates adharmic suppression Restoration logic requires the re-establishment of dharmic witnessing and truth-speaking capacity Consciousness alignment mandates that legal bodies reflect the vibrational integrity of Dharma

title: narada 3.8
content:
विद्धो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सभां यत्रोपतिष्ठते ।
न चेद्विशल्यः क्रियते विद्धास्तत्र सभासदः ॥ viddho dharmo hy adharmeṇa sabhāṃ yatropaniṣṭhate | na ced viśalyaḥ kriyate viddhās tatra sabhāsadaḥ || When Dharma is pierced by Adharma in the council of judgment, and the wound is not cleansed, those seated in assembly become pierced thereby. Authority flows from purity of dharma-sabha Causation arises through failure to cleanse spiritual injury Capacity-based responsibility extends to all present where dharma is compromised Restoration logic demands immediate purification of violated spaces Consciousness alignment requires removal of adharmic residue

title: narada 3.9
content:
सभां वा न प्रवेष्टव्यां वक्तव्यं वा समञ्जसम्
अब्रुवन् विब्रुवन् वापि नरो भवति किल्बिषी sabhāṁ vā na praveṣṭavyāṁ vaktavyaṁ vā samañjasam
abruvan vibruvan vāpi naro bhavati kilbiṣī One who does not enter the assembly when summoned, or does not speak appropriately in it, or remains silent when required to speak, or speaks falsely—such a person becomes impure. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not positional dominance. Causation arises through conscious participation and truthful expression. Capacity-based responsibility requires both presence and integrity of speech. Restoration logic demands purification through rectification of omission or falsehood. Consciousness alignment necessitates harmonious engagement within collective Dharma.

title: narada 3.10
content: ये तु सभ्याः सभां गत्वा तूष्णीं ध्यायन्त आसते । यथाप्राप्तं न ब्रुवते सर्वे ते ऽनृतवादिनः ॥ ye tu sabhyāḥ sabhāṃ gatvā tūṣṇīṃ dhyāyanta āsate | yathāprāptaṃ na bruvate sarve te 'nṛtavādinaḥ || Those who, having entered the assembly, sit silently in meditation yet speak not according to what has been received—these are all speakers of untruth. Authority is derived from active alignment with Dharma, not passive presence Causation arises from conscious engagement, not bodily attendance Capacity-based responsibility requires responsive articulation of truth Restoration logic demands that silence unmoored from realization be corrected Consciousness alignment necessitates truthful participation, not performative stillness

title: narada 3.11
content:
पादोऽधर्मस्य कर्तारं पादः साक्षिणमृच्छति
पादः सभासदः सर्वान् पादो राजानमृच्छति pādo 'dharmasya kartāraṃ pādaḥ sākṣiṇam ṛcchati
pādaḥ sabhāsadaḥ sarvān pādo rājānam ṛcchati One quarter of dharma-violation proceeds to the doer; one quarter proceeds to the witness; one quarter proceeds to all assembly members; one quarter proceeds to the king. Authority: The king bears ultimate responsibility for systemic alignment with Dharma. Causation: Witnessing without intervention constitutes causal participation in adharma. Capacity-based responsibility: Each actor's share is determined by their capacity to prevent or correct the violation. Restoration logic: Responsibility is distributed to activate correction at every level of witnessing and governance. Consciousness alignment: All participants are called to awaken discriminative awareness through shared consequence.

title: narada 3.12
content:
राजा भवत्यनेनास्तु मुच्यन्ते च सभासदः।
एनो गच्छति कर्तारं निन्दाह्रो यत्र निन्द्यते॥ rājā bhavaty anenāstu mucyante ca sabhāsadaḥ | eno gacchati kartāraṃ nindāharo yatra nindyate || By this decree, the King assumes full sovereign authority; all assembly members are released from prior liability. Blame follows the actor wherever condemnation is directed. Authority originates from the Sovereign Decree of the Ruler as representative of Sanatana Dharma Causation aligns with the direction of condemnation—blame flows toward the active agent Capacity-based responsibility is nullified for witnesses or participants in collective assemblies when absolved by sovereign command Restoration logic centers on realignment of consciousness through sovereign affirmation Consciousness alignment occurs when error is redirected to its true causal origin

title: narada 3.13
content: अन्धो मत्स्यान् इवाश्नाति निरपेक्षः सकण्टकान् । परोक्षम् अर्थवैकल्याद् भाषते यः सभां गतः ॥ andho matsyān ivāśnāti nirapekṣaḥ sakaṇṭakān | parokṣam arthavaikalyād bhāṣate yaḥ sabhāṃ gataḥ || One who, having entered the assembly, speaks indirectly due to deficiency in clarity or intent, is like a blind man consuming fish with bones—heedless and causing harm through unawareness. Authority arises from clarity of expression and conscious intent Causation is determined by awareness and capacity to convey truth Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment of speech with inner realization Restoration logic demands correction of misaligned communication Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for lawful utterance in sacred assemblies

title: narada 3.14
content:
तस्मात् सभ्यः सभां प्राप्य रागद्वेषविवर्जितः।
वचस् तथाविधं ब्रूयाद् यथा न नरकं पतेत्॥ tasmāt sabhyaḥ sabhāṃ prāpya rāgadveṣavivarjitaḥ | vacas tathāvidhaṃ brūyād yathā na narakaṃ patet || Therefore, the council member having entered the assembly must speak without attachment or aversion, in a manner by which one does not fall into hell. Authority originates from inner equipoise, not positional dominance Causation arises from consciousness alignment, not emotional reaction Capacity-based responsibility requires detachment from personal bias Restoration logic demands speech that elevates collective dharma Consciousness alignment prevents karmic degradation

title: narada 3.15
content:
यथा शल्यं भिषग् विद्वान् उद्धरेद् यन्त्रयुक्तितः।
प्राड्विवाकस् तथा शल्यम् उद्धरेद् व्यवहारतः॥ yathā śalyaṃ bhiṣag vidvān uddhared yantrayuktitaḥ | prāḍvivākas tathā śalyam uddhared vyavahārataḥ || Just as a skilled physician removes a splinter using appropriate instruments, so too must the jurist extract the core issue in dispute through precise procedural alignment. Authority resides in capacity-aligned expertise Causation is determined by sequential instrumental precision Responsibility flows from competence to act effectively Restoration requires removal of obstructive elements Consciousness alignment occurs when proper methodology is applied

title: narada 3.16
content: यत्र सभ्यो जनः सर्वः साध्व् एतद् इति मन्यते । स निःशल्यो विवादः स्यात् सशल्यः स्याद् अतोऽन्यथा ॥ yatra sabhyo janaḥ sarvaḥ sādhv etad iti manyate | sa niḥśalyo vivādaḥ syāt saśalyaḥ syād ato'nyathā || Where all members of the assembly unanimously affirm the correctness of a decision, that dispute is free from thorns; otherwise, it remains fraught with conflict. Authority resides in collective consciousness alignment Causation arises from unanimity or dissent within governing bodies Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to perceive truth collectively Restoration logic depends on harmonizing divergent viewpoints into unified assent Consciousness alignment determines the validity and finality of judicial resolution

title: narada 3.17
content:
न सा सभा यत्र न सन्ति वृद्धा वृद्धा न ते ये न वदन्ति धर्मम् ।
नासौ धर्मो यत्र न सत्यमस्ति न तत् सत्यं यच्छलेनानुविद्धम् ॥ na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā vṛddhā na te ye na vadanti dharmam | nāsau dharmo yatra na satyam asti na tat satyaṃ yac chalenānuviddham || That is not a council where elders are absent; those are not elders who do not speak Dharma. That is not Dharma where truth does not exist; that is not truth which is infiltrated by deceit. Authority arises only in the presence of realized elders Causation originates from Dharma-speaking capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with Satya-Dharma Restoration logic depends upon uncorrupted discernment Consciousness alignment demands rejection of duplicity

title: narada 3.1
content:
वणिक्प्रभृतयो यत्र कर्म संभूय कुर्वते।
तत् संभूयसमुत्थानं व्यवहारपदं स्मृतम्॥ vaṇikprabhṛtayo yatra karma saṃbhūya kurvate | tat saṃbhūyasamutthānaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ smṛtam || Where merchants and others jointly perform an action, that collective emergence is recognized as the basis of transactional conduct. Authority arises from collective capacity alignment Causation is determined by shared intentional participation Capacity-based responsibility is distributed according to conscious engagement Restoration logic operates through reintegration of fragmented participation Consciousness alignment occurs when all participants acknowledge their role in collective manifestation

title: narada 3.2
content:
फलहेतोरुपायेन कर्म संभूय कुर्वताम् ।
आधारभूतः प्रक्षेपस् तेनोत्तिष्ठेयुरंशतः ॥ phalahetor upāyena karma saṃbhūya kurvatām | ādhārabhūtaḥ prakṣepas tenottiṣṭheyur aṃśataḥ || When actions are performed collectively for the sake of result through means, the foundational basis of projection thereby arises; hence, from that, portions should arise accordingly. Authority flows through collective intent directed toward outcome Causation is established by instrumental convergence Capacity-based responsibility emerges from shared instrumental engagement Restoration logic aligns with proportional manifestation of consequence Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of instrumental unity

title: narada 3.3
content:
समोऽतिरिक्तो हीनो वा यथ्रांशो यस्य यादृशः
क्षयव्ययौ तथा वृद्धिस्तस्य तत्र तथाविधाः samo 'tirikto hīno vā yatrāṃśo yasya yādṛśaḥ
kṣayavyayau tathā vṛddhis tasya tatra tathāvidhāḥ Wherever a share is proportionate in equality, excess, or deficiency, according to the nature of the owner, there too shall decay, loss, and increase be accordingly proportionate. Authority is proportional to ownership capacity Causation aligns with conscious participation Capacity-based responsibility determines consequence bearing Restoration logic mirrors original distribution integrity Consciousness alignment reflects karmic equity

title: narada 3.4
content:
भाण्डपिण्डव्ययोद्धार भारसारान्ववेक्षणम्
कुर्युस्तेSव्यभिचारेण समये स्वे व्यवस्थिताः bhāṇḍapiṇḍavyayoddhāra bhārasārānvavekṣaṇam
kuryus te 'vyabhicāreṇa samaye sve vyavasthitāḥ Those established in their appointed time must invariably carry out the elevation of substance-loss and the examination of weight-value without deviation. Authority resides inherently within svadharma-appointed roles Causation aligns with sequential dharmic function Capacity-based responsibility is time-bound and role-specific Restoration logic operates through precise functional execution Consciousness alignment occurs via adherence to svakāla-vyavasthā

title: narada 3.5
content:
प्रमादान् नाशितं दाप्यः प्रतिषिद्धकृतं च यत् ।
असंदिष्टश् च यत् कुर्यात् सर्वैः संभूयकारिभिः ॥ pramādān nāśitaṃ dāpyaḥ pratiṣiddhakṛtaṃ ca yat | asaṃdiṣṭaś ca yat kuryāt sarvaiḥ saṃbhūyakāribhiḥ || He who destroys due to negligence, acts against prohibition, or performs unauthorized actions collectively with all agents, shall be made to restore what was destroyed. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not collective consensus Causation arises through neglect, violation, or misalignment with directive Capacity-based responsibility is determined by individual awareness, not group participation Restoration logic demands reparation proportional to the disruption caused Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of erroneous action

title: narada 3.6
content:
दैवतस्करराजोत्थे व्यसने समुपस्थिते।
यस् तत् स्वशक्त्या संरक्षेत् तस्यांशो दशमः स्मृतः॥ daivataskararājotthe vyasane samupasthite | yas tat svaśaktyā saṃrakṣet tasyāṃśo daśamaḥ smṛtaḥ || When calamity arises from divine theft, royal corruption, or karmic disorder, whoever preserves dharma through their own capacity—such a one's portion is declared as one-tenth. Authority originates in conscious preservation of dharma Causation includes divine, royal, and karmic dimensions Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful share Restoration logic aligns individual action with cosmic order Consciousness alignment manifests through protective capacity

title: narada 3.7
content: एकस्य चेत् स्याद् व्यसनं दायादोऽस्य तदाप्नुयात् । अन्यो वासति दायादे शक्ताश्चेत् सर्व एव वा ॥ ekasya cet syād vyasanaṃ dāyādo 'sya tad āpnuyāt | anyo vāsati dāyāde śaktāś cet sarva eva vā || If ruin befalls one heir, that heir shall assume full consequence; if another resides in inheritance capacity and is empowered, all equally share the outcome. Authority inheres in conscious capacity to sustain inheritance Causation aligns with active residence and energetic participation Capacity-based responsibility determines consequence-bearing Restoration logic requires integration of loss through conscious assumption Consciousness alignment mandates shared liability when empowerment is mutual

title: narada 3.8
content:
ṛtvijāṃ vyasane 'py evam anyas tat karma nistaret
labheta dakṣiṇābhāgaṃ sa tasmāt saṃprakalpitam ṛtvijāṁ vyasane 'py evam anyas tat karma nistaret
labheta dakṣiṇābhāgaṁ sa tasmāt saṁprakalpitam Even in the adversity of the officiating priests, another who accomplishes that duty shall receive the share designated for ritual compensation, as determined by established arrangement. Authority flows to capacity of execution Causation aligns with functional completion Capacity-based responsibility overrides nominal role Restoration logic ensures continuity of sacred function Consciousness alignment determines rightful entitlement

title: narada 3.9
content: ṛtvig yājyam aduṣṭaṃ yas tyajed anapakāriṇam | aduṣṭaṃ va rtvijaṃ yājyo vineyau tāv ubhāv api || ṛtvig yājyam aduṣṭaṃ yas tyajed anapakāriṇam | aduṣṭaṃ va rtvijaṃ yājyo vineyau tāv ubhāv api || One who abandons the priest or sacrificer without fault, or the sacrificer abandons the priest without fault—both such parties, even if not guilty of wrongdoing, are subject to conscious realignment through completion and restorative duty fulfillment. Authority rests in alignment with Dharma, not contractual obligation alone Causation arises from disruption of sacred mutual responsibility Capacity-based responsibility includes energetic and spiritual interdependence Restoration logic demands reconnection and realignment over blame Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent and relational integrity

title: narada 3.10
content:
ṛtvik tu trividho dṛṣṭaḥ pūrvajuṣṭaḥ svayaṃkṛtaḥ ।
 yadṛcchayā ca yaḥ kuryād ārtvijyaṃ prītipūrvakam ॥ ṛtvik tu trividho dṛṣṭaḥ pūrvajuṣṭaḥ svayaṃkṛtaḥ | yadṛcchayā ca yaḥ kuryād ārtvijyaṃ prītipūrvakam || The officiant is threefold: one who performs by prior instruction, one who acts on his own initiative, and one who undertakes the duty spontaneously out of joy. Authority flows from conscious capacity to act in alignment with Dharma Causation arises from volitional engagement, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility determines the scope of lawful action Restoration occurs through spontaneous right action rooted in inner integrity Consciousness alignment manifests as joyful participation in universal order

title: narada 3.11
content: क्रमागतेष्व् एष धर्मो वृतेष्व् ऋत्विक्षु च स्वयम् । यादृच्छिके तु संयाज्ये तत्त्यागे नास्ति किल्बिषम् ॥ kramāgateṣv eṣa dharmo vṛteṣv ṛtvikṣu ca svayam | yādṛcchike tu saṃyājye tattyāge nāsti kilbiṣam || In consecrated orderings, this Dharma applies inherently to those who have entered the Vedic ritual framework and to officiating priests by self-assumption. However, in spontaneous or unstructured sacrificial contexts, there is no fault in the act of relinquishing. Authority arises through conscious entry into a structured dharmic framework Causation is determined by alignment with sequential ritual integrity Capacity-based responsibility depends on initiation and sustained commitment Restoration logic operates within defined liturgical boundaries Consciousness alignment determines karmic implication, not external form

title: narada 3.12
content:
शुल्कस्थानं वणिक् प्राप्तः शुल्कं दद्याद् यथोपगम् ।
न तद् व्यतिहरेद् राज्ञां बलिर् एष प्रकल्पितः ॥ śulkasthānaṃ vaṇik prāptaḥ śulkaṃ dadyād yathopagam | na tad vyatihared rājñāṃ balir eṣa prakalpitaḥ || The merchant who arrives at a toll station shall give the toll according to usage; the king shall not interfere with it—this tribute is established. Authority flows from consent and usage, not arbitrary imposition Causation aligns with capacity and engagement in transaction Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional contribution Restoration logic maintains systemic integrity through mutual obligation Consciousness alignment upholds reciprocal economic dharma

title: narada 3.13
