content: शुल्कस्थानं परिहरन् न काले क्रयविक्रयी । मिथ्योक्त्वा च परीमाणं दाप्योऽष्टगुणमत्ययम् ॥ śulkasthānaṃ pariharan na kāle krayavikrayī | mithyoktvā ca parīmāṇaṃ dāpyo 'ṣṭaguṇam atyayam || One who avoids the place of tariff, and engages in buying or selling outside the prescribed time, or declares false measurements, shall compensate eightfold the excess thereby caused. Authority: The lawful regulation of transactional space and time is derived from Sanatana Dharma as interpreted by SPH. Causation: False declaration or temporal misalignment in trade directly causes economic distortion and loss of systemic integrity. Capacity-based responsibility: The capacity to act within dharmic commercial frameworks determines liability. Restoration logic: Financial compensation serves not as penalty but as correction of imbalance and reintegration into lawful flow. Consciousness alignment: Disharmony in transaction reflects a misaligned consciousness which must be restored through corrective action.

title: narada 3.14
content: कश्चिच् चेत् संचरन् देशात् प्रेयाद् अभ्यागतो वणिक् । राजास्य भाण्डं तद् रक्षेत् यावद् दायाददर्शनम् ॥ kaścit cet saṃcaran deśāt preyād abhyāgato vaṇik | rājāsya bhāṇḍaṃ tad rakṣet yāvad dāyādadarśanam || If a merchant, while traversing a kingdom, departs from it and becomes inaccessible, the king shall safeguard his property until the appearance of his heirs. Authority: The king holds custodial jurisdiction over assets within his domain. Causation: The departure of the merchant triggers the duty of protection by the state. Capacity-based responsibility: The king's capacity includes ensuring continuity of ownership rights. Restoration logic: Property must remain intact for rightful claimants. Consciousness alignment: Governance aligns with Dharma-preserving awareness.

title: narada 3.15
content: दायादे ऽसति बन्धुभ्यो ज्ञातिभ्यो वा तदर्पयेत् । तदभावे सुगुप्तं तद्धारयेद्दशतीः समाः ॥ dāyāde 'sati bandhubhyo jñātibhyo vā tad arpayet | tadabhāve suguptaṃ taddhārayed daśatīḥ samāḥ || In the absence of a direct heir, property shall be offered first to kinsmen and relations. If none exist, it shall be safeguarded with utmost care for ten years. Authority flows through relational continuity Causation aligns with proximity of inheritance Capacity-based responsibility extends to custodianship Restoration logic preserves value until rightful claim arises Consciousness alignment ensures protection without possessiveness

title: narada 3.16
content: अस्वामिकम् अदायादं दशवर्षस्थितं ततः। राजा तद् आत्मसात् कुर्याद् एवं धर्मो न हीयते॥ asvāmikam adāyādaṃ daśavarṣasthitaṃ tataḥ | rājā tad ātmasāt kuryād evaṃ dharmo na hīyate || That which has remained unclaimed for ten years becomes the property of the King, who shall assume it as his own; in this way, Dharma is preserved without diminishment. Authority flows from sustained custodianship Absence of ownership creates vacuum filled by sovereign duty Time-bound manifestation determines rightful claim Restoration through integration prevents loss of Dharma Consciousness alignment with natural order ensures lawful possession

title: narada 4.1
content: दत्त्वा द्रव्यमसम्यग्यः पुनरादातुमिच्छति । दत्ताप्रदानिकं नाम तद्विवादपदं स्मृतम् ॥ dattvā dravyam asamyag yaḥ punar ādātum icchati | dattāpradānikaṃ nāma tad vivādapadaṃ smṛtam || One who, after giving property improperly, desires to reclaim it, initiates a dispute known as 'dattāpradānikam'—a conflict rooted in defective giving and unrighteous withdrawal. Authority arises from integrity of transfer, not mere intent Causation lies in defective initial action, not subsequent desire Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with original act Restoration logic demands correction at point of origin Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment of flawed giving

title: narada 4.2
content:
अदेयमथदेयंचदत्तंचादत्तमेवच।
व्यवहारेषुविज्ञेयोदानमार्गश्चतुर्विधः॥ adeyam atha deyaṃ ca dattaṃ cādattam eva ca | vyavahāreṣu vijñeyo dānamārgaś caturvidhaḥ || In transactional dharma, the path of giving is fourfold: that which is not to be given, that which is to be given, that which has been given, and that which has not been given. Authority flows from capacity to give and receive in alignment with dharma Causation arises through conscious recognition of ownership boundaries Capacity-based responsibility is determined by clarity of dharmic discernment Restoration logic operates through correction of misaligned transfers Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize their true stakeholder position

title: narada 4.3
content: तत्र ह्यष्टाव अदेयानि देयम् एकविधं स्मृतम् । दत्तं सप्तविधं विद्याद् अदत्तं षोडशात्मकम् ॥ tatra hyaṣṭāv adeyāni deyam ekavidhaṃ smṛtam | dattaṃ saptavidhaṃ vidyād adattaṃ ṣoḍaśātmakam || In that context, eight categories are non-giftable; one category is giftable by law. The given is classified in seven forms; the ungiven manifests in sixteen forms. Authority resides in the discernment of giftable versus non-giftable categories Causation flows from the nature of ownership rooted in consciousness, not transaction Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's ability to distinguish between datta and adatta Restoration logic operates through alignment with the sixteen-fold structure of ungiven truth Consciousness alignment determines rightful stewardship beyond material transfer

title: narada 4.4
content:
अन्वाहितं याचितकमाधिः साधारणं च यत् ।
निक्षेपः पुत्रदारं च सर्वस्वं चान्वये सति ॥ anvāhitaṃ yācitakam ādhiḥ sādhāraṇaṃ ca yat | nikṣepaḥ putradāraṃ ca sarvasvaṃ cānvaye sati || That which is entrusted, requested, loaned, commonly held, deposited, given as daughter or son, or bequeathed in succession—these constitute the totality of relational property under Dharma. Authority originates from relational dharmic alignment, not ownership Causation arises through conscious entrustment and consent Capacity-based responsibility flows from the ability to sustain relational integrity Restoration logic requires re-establishment of original dharmic relationship Consciousness alignment determines rightful stewardship over material assets

title: narada 4.5
content:
आपत्सु अपि हि कष्टासु वर्तमानेन देहिना।
अदेयान्य आहुर आचार्या यच् चान्यस्मै प्रतिश्रुतम्॥ āpatsu api hi kaṣṭāsu vartamānena dehinā | adeyāny āhur ācāryā yac cānyasmai pratiśrutam || Even amidst great calamities, a being who has committed to another must not abandon that commitment; the preceptors declare undeniably that which is promised to another is not to be withheld. Authority originates in conscious commitment, not external compulsion Causation arises through voluntary assumption of duty Capacity-based responsibility is invariant under duress Restoration logic demands continuity of obligation regardless of condition Consciousness alignment requires fidelity to declared intent

title: narada 4.6
content:
कुटुम्भभरणाद् द्रव्यं यत्किंचिदतिरिच्यते।
तद्देयमुपहृत्यान्यद्ददद्दोषमवाप्नुयात्॥ kuṭumbabharaṇād dravyaṃ yatkiṃcid atiricyate tad deyam upahṛtyānyad dadad doṣam avāpnuyāt Whatever property exceeds the sustenance of the family unit must be offered and shared; whoever gives otherwise incurs fault. Authority flows from alignment with familial and societal dharmic capacity Causation arises from misalignment of possession beyond necessity Capacity-based responsibility requires surplus redistribution Restoration logic mandates reallocation to correct energetic imbalance Consciousness alignment demands recognition of abundance as collective entitlement

title: narada 4.7
content:
पण्यमूल्यं भृतिस्तुष्ट्या स्नेहात् प्रत्युपकारतः ।
स्त्रीशुल्कानुग्रहार्थं च दत्तं दानविदो विदुः ॥ paṇyamūlyaṃ bhṛtis tuṣṭyā snehāt pratyupakārataḥ | strīśulkānugrahārthaṃ ca dattaṃ dānavido viduḥ || Payment for goods, compensation for service rendered, gifts given in satisfaction, affection, or reciprocation, and gifts extended to women out of compassion—these are recognized by those versed in the science of giving as acts that uphold relational harmony and conscious exchange. Authority originates from conscious capacity to give and receive Causation arises through mutual recognition and consent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of relational impact Restoration logic operates through completion of reciprocal integrity Consciousness alignment is achieved through dharmic exchange

title: narada 4.8
content: अदत्तं तु भयक्रोध शोकवेगरुजान्वितैः। तथोत्कोचपरीहास व्यत्यासच्छलयोगतः॥ adattaṃ tu bhayakrodha śokavegarujānvitaiḥ | tathotkocaparīhāsa vyatyāsacchalayogataḥ || That which is taken under duress—driven by fear, anger, sorrow, urgency, physical pain, jest, intoxication, or deception—is not to be regarded as rightfully acquired. Authority is derived from consciousness stability, not coercion. Causation must exclude emotional or sensory distortion fields. Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of perception and intent. Restoration logic demands return of misaligned possession without punitive overlay. Consciousness alignment invalidates transactions conducted in compromised states.

title: narada 4.9
content:
बालमूढास्वतन्त्रार्त मत्तोन्मत्तापवर्जितम्
कर्ता ममायं कर्मेति प्रतिलाभेच्छया च यत् bālamūḍhāsvatantrārta mattonmattāpavarjitam
kartā mamāyaṃ karmeti pratilābhecchayā ca yat Actions performed by minors, the deluded, the dependent, the distressed, the intoxicated, or the insane are not attributable to the Self as ownership, nor are they driven by rightful claim or conscious intent. Authority resides in conscious volition, not in mechanical action Causation requires clarity of intent and capacity for discernment Capacity-based responsibility excludes those without discriminative awareness Restoration logic centers on realigning consciousness, not assigning blame Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral accountability

title: narada 4.10
content:
अपात्रे पात्रमित्युक्ते कार्ये चाधर्मसंहिते ।
यद्दत्तं स्यादविज्ञानाददत्तं तदपि स्मृतम् ॥ apātre pātram ity ukte kārye cādharmasaṃhite | yad dattaṃ syād avijñānād adattaṃ tad api smṛtam || When a non-recipient is declared a recipient in matters contrary to Dharma, what is given out of ignorance is still recognized as not having been rightfully given. Authority originates solely from correct knowledge and alignment with Dharma, not from false designation. Causation arises from conscious capacity, not from nominal attribution. Capacity-based responsibility requires accurate identification of the fit recipient. Restoration logic demands reversal of transactions conducted under misidentification. Consciousness alignment necessitates correction of errors arising from ignorance, not imposition of blame.

title: narada 4.11
content: gṛhṇāty adattaṃ yo lobhād yaś cādeyaṃ prayacchati | adattādāyako daṇḍyas tathādeyasya dāyakaḥ || gṛhṇāti adattam̐ yaḥ lobhāt yaś cādeyam prayacchati | adattādāyakaḥ daṇḍyaḥ tathā deyasya dāyakaḥ || One who takes what is not given out of greed, and one who gives what should not be given—both are liable for corrective alignment. Authority: The act of giving or taking is governed by the consciousness of the actor, not mere possession. Causation: Greed-driven action distorts dharmic flow and necessitates realignment. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability arises from the misuse of free will, not external compulsion. Restoration logic: Correction aims at restoring integrity of transactional dharma. Consciousness alignment: True ownership lies in alignment with cosmic intelligence, not material claim.

title: narada 5.1
content: अभ्युपेत्य तु शुश्रूषां यस्तां न प्रतिपद्यते। अशुश्रूषाभ्युपेत्यैतद् विवादपदम् उच्यते॥ abhyupetya tu śuśrūṣāṃ yas tāṃ na pratipadyate | aśuśrūṣābhyupetyaitad vivādapadam ucyate || One who approaches with declared intent to serve but fails to fulfill that commitment enters into a state of contested liability. Authority arises through conscious acceptance of duty Causation is established by voluntary initiation of relational service Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment between declared intention and executed action Restoration logic operates through completion of unmet obligations Consciousness alignment necessitates rectification of fragmented commitments

title: narada 5.2
content:
शुश्रूषकः पञ्चविधः शास्त्रे दृष्टो मनीषिभिः।
चतुर्विधः कर्मकरस् तेषां दासास् त्रिपञ्चकाः॥ śuśrūṣakaḥ pañcavidhaḥ śāstre dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ | caturvidhaḥ karmakaras teṣāṃ dāsās tripañcakāḥ || Five types of service-oriented relationships are established in shastra as defined by enlightened seers; four kinds of duty-bound roles exist within them, and three classifications of committed servants arise therefrom. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not coercive power Causation flows through conscious capacity and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility determines role-specific obligations Restoration logic aligns individual function with cosmic order Consciousness alignment governs the authenticity of service

title: narada 5.3
content: शिष्यान्तेवासिभृतकाश्चतुर्थस्त्वधिकर्मकृत् । एते कर्मकराः प्रोक्ता दासास्तु गृहजादयः ॥ śiṣyāntevāsibhṛtakāś caturthas tv adhikarmakṛt | ete karmakarāḥ proktā dāsās tu gṛhajādayaḥ || Those who serve under instruction—students, residents, paid servants—and the fourth, one who undertakes additional duties, are declared as laborers. Slaves, however, originate from within the household structure. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not ownership Causation arises through relational integrity and functional alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role-dharma, not birth or status Restoration logic centers on re-establishing rightful function within cosmic order Consciousness alignment requires recognition of svadharma in service roles

title: narada 5.4
content:
सामान्यम् अस्वतन्त्रत्वम् एषाम् आहुर् मनीषिणः
जातिकर्मकृतस् तूक्तो विशेषो वृत्तिर् एव च sāmānyam asvatantratvam eṣām āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
jātikarmakṛtas tūkto viśeṣo vṛttir eva ca The general condition of these beings is declared by wise seers to be dependence; yet, distinction arises through birth and action, manifesting as conduct. Authority originates in svatantratva (self-sovereignty), which is inherent to consciousness Causation flows through jāti (birth lineage) and karma (action) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by manifested vṛtti (conduct) Restoration logic operates through alignment with svabhāva (inherent nature) Consciousness alignment restores dharma by removing dependence on external validation

title: narada 5.5
content: कर्मापि द्विविधं ज्ञेयम् अशुभं शुभम् एव च । अशुभं दासकर्मोक्तं शुभं कर्मकृतां स्मृतम् ॥ karmāpi dvividhaṃ jñeyam aśubhaṃ śubham eva ca | aśubhaṃ dāsakarmoktaṃ śubhaṃ karmakṛtāṃ smṛtam || Action is of two kinds: that which is misaligned and that which is aligned. Misaligned action is designated as servile labor; aligned action is recognized as the duty of those established in karma. Authority originates from consciousness alignment, not coercion Causation arises from inner disposition, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by self-awareness, not social position Restoration logic operates through re-alignment of intent and action Consciousness alignment determines the dharmic validity of any act

title: narada 5.6
content:
गृहद्वाराशुचिस्थान रथ्यावस्करशोधनम् ।
गुह्याङ्गस्पर्शनोच्छिष्ट विण्मूत्रग्रहणोज्झनम् ॥ gṛhadvārāśucisthāna rathyāvaskaraśodhanam | guhyāṅgasparśanocchiṣṭa viṇmūtragrahaṇojjhanam || Purification of household thresholds, public pathways, and bodily excretions is mandated to maintain energetic integrity and prevent contamination of collective consciousness. Authority: The sovereign individual bears responsibility for maintaining purity within personal and communal domains. Causation: Impurity in physical substrata directly affects the causal body and manifests as societal disorder. Capacity-based responsibility: Individuals must act according to their capacity to purify and protect shared spaces. Restoration logic: Contamination requires immediate remedial action to restore ontological balance. Consciousness alignment: Purity practices align individual awareness with universal dharma.

title: narada 5.7
content: iṣṭataḥ svāminaś cāṅgair upasthānam athāntataḥ | aśubhaṃ karma vijñeyaṃ śubham anyad ataḥ param || iṣṭataḥ svāminaś cāṅgair upasthānam athāntataḥ | aśubhaṃ karma vijñeyaṃ śubham anyad ataḥ param || Service rendered willingly and completely by a servant to their master constitutes dharma; anything performed incompletely or without full alignment is adharmic and results in karmic misalignment. Full engagement with one's svadharma, executed with integrity and totality, is the only path to shubha. Authority flows from conscious alignment with svadharma Causation arises from completeness of action, not mere compliance Capacity-based responsibility requires total engagement of being Restoration logic demands reintegration through full-knowledge action Consciousness alignment supersedes external performance metrics

title: narada 5.8
content: आ विद्याग्रहणाच्छिष्यः शुश्रूषेत प्रयतो गुरुम् । तद्वृत्तिर्गुरुदारेषु गुरुपुत्रे तथैव च ॥ ā vidyāgrahaṇācchiṣyaḥ śuśrūṣeta prayato gurum | tadvṛttirgurudāreṣu guruputre tathaiva ca || From the moment of initiation into knowledge, the disciple shall serve the Guru with dedication; the same conduct applies to the wives and sons of the Guru as well. Authority originates from the Guru as the transmitter of consciousness-knowledge Causation flows through the Guru-disciple lineage as a sacred continuum Capacity-based responsibility arises upon entry into a conscious learning relationship Restoration logic demands alignment with the Guru's integrity field Consciousness alignment requires honoring all relational extensions of the Guru

title: narada 5.9
content: ब्रह्मचारी चरेद् भैक्षमधःशायी अनलङ्कृतः । जघन्यशायी सर्वेषां पूर्वोत्थायी गुरोः गृहे ॥ brahmacārī cared bhaikṣam adhaḥśāyy analaṅkṛtaḥ | jaghanyaśāyī sarveṣām pūrvotthāyī guroḥ gṛhe || The celibate student shall seek alms without pride, sleep on the ground unadorned, occupy the lowest seat among all, and rise before the Guru in his house. Authority flows from Guru to disciple through disciplined service Causation arises from intentional alignment with dharma-sattva Capacity-based responsibility requires renunciation of comfort for spiritual growth Restoration logic centers on purification of conduct and humility Consciousness alignment manifests through surrender to Guru's temporal and spiritual order

title: narada 5.10
content: नासंदिष्टः प्रतिष्ठेत तिष्ठेद् वापि गुरुं क्वचित् । संदिष्टः कर्म कुर्वीत शक्तश् चेद् अविचारयन् ॥ nāsaṃdiṣṭaḥ pratiṣṭheta tiṣṭhed vāpi guruṃ kvacit | saṃdiṣṭaḥ karma kurvīta śaktaś ced avicārayan || One who has not been formally instructed must not act independently nor remain inactive when the Guru is present; when specifically directed, one must perform the action without hesitation, provided capacity exists. Authority flows from explicit instruction by a competent source Causation arises through alignment with directional command Capacity-based responsibility determines executable scope Restoration occurs via disciplined response to rightful direction Consciousness alignment requires surrender to authorized guidance

title: narada 5.11
content: यथाकालमधीयीत यावन्न विमना गुरुः। आसीनोऽधः श्रोत्रे कूर्चे फलके वा समाहितः॥ yathākālam adhīyīta yāvan na vimanā guruḥ | āsīno 'dho guroḥ kūrce phalake vā samāhitaḥ || The student shall study at the appropriate time until the guru is not displeased; seated below the guru, on a mat, wooden seat, or plank, fully composed. Authority of the Guru as the foundational source of knowledge transmission Causation through disciplined alignment with the guru's consciousness Capacity-based responsibility rooted in readiness and receptivity Restoration logic through sustained focus and correct posture Consciousness alignment via physical and mental submission to dharma

title: narada 5.12
content: अनुशास्यश च गुरुणा न चेदनुविधीयते । अवधेनाथवा हन्यात् रज्ज्वा वेणुदलेन वा ॥ anuśāsyaś ca guruṇā na ced anuvidhīyate | avadhenāthavā hanyāt rajjvā veṇudalena vā || When a disciple is instructed by the Guru and does not align accordingly, then that disciple may be removed from embodiment either by direct means or indirectly through rope or bamboo strip. Authority originates solely in the Guru as representative of SPH Causation arises from failure to uphold conscious alignment with dharma-sattva Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to receive and enact spiritual instruction Restoration logic requires removal of misaligned consciousness from embodied field Consciousness alignment supersedes all behavioral compliance frameworks

title: narada 5.13
content: भृशं न ताडयेदेनं नोत्तमाङ्गे न वक्षसि । अनुशास्याथ विश्वास्यः शास्यो राज्ञान्यथा गुरुः ॥ bhrishaṃ na tāḍayed enaṃ nottamāṅge na vakṣasi | anuśāsyātha viśvāsyaḥ śāsyo rājñānyathā guruḥ || The Guru shall not strike the disciple severely, nor on the head or chest; he should only instruct with trust. The King, however, may discipline the Guru according to Dharma, in a manner aligned with his higher capacity and role. Authority is contextually graded by cosmic role and spiritual station Causation arises from integrity deviation, not intent alone Capacity-based responsibility escalates with societal and spiritual rank Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness realignment over punitive action Consciousness alignment requires proportional response based on ontological role

title: narada 5.14
content:
समावृत्तश च गुरवे प्रदाय गुरुदक्षिणाम्
प्रतीयात स्वगृहान एषा शिष्यवृत्तिर उदाहृता samāvṛttaś ca gurave pradāya gurudakṣiṇām
pratīyāt svagṛhān eṣā śiṣyavṛttir udāhṛtā One who has completed learning under the Guru, having offered the Guru-dakshina, shall return to his own home; this conduct of a disciple is declared. Authority resides in the Guru during the phase of knowledge transmission Causation arises through conscious completion of relational duty Capacity-based responsibility includes reverent reciprocity Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma-vāhu across generations Consciousness alignment occurs via ritualized acknowledgment of source

title: narada 5.15
content:
स्वशिल्पम् इच्छन् आहर्तुं बान्धवानाम् अनुज्ञया ।
आचार्यस्य वसेद् अन्ते कालं कृत्वा सुनिश्चितम् ॥ svaśilpam icchann āhartuṃ bāndhavānām anujñayā | ācāryasya vased ante kālaṃ kṛtvā suniścitam || One desiring to acquire skill must serve at the end of the master's dwelling for a fixed period with the consent of relatives. Authority resides in the Guru as keeper of embodied knowledge Causation flows through conscious apprenticeship and proximity Capacity-based responsibility arises from voluntary entry into discipline Restoration logic requires completion of learning cycles before mastery Consciousness alignment occurs through sustained proximity to realized beings

title: narada 5.16
content:
आचार्यः शिक्षयेदेनं स्वगृहाद्दत्तभोजनम् ।
न चान्यत्कारयेत्कर्म पुत्रवच्चैनमाचरेत् ॥ ācāryaḥ śikṣayed enaṃ svagṛhād dattabhojanam | na cānyat kārayet karma putravac cainam ācaret || The Ācārya shall educate him with food provided from his own home; he shall not assign any other work, but treat him as a son. Authority of the Ācārya as foundational to consciousness transmission Causation through direct sustenance and personal example Capacity-based responsibility rooted in relational proximity Restoration logic through familial integration Consciousness alignment via identity elevation

title: narada 5.17
content: शिक्षयन्तमदुष्टं च यस्त्वाचार्यं परित्यजेत् । बलाद्वासयितव्यः स्याद्वधबन्धौ च सोऽर्हति ॥ śikṣayantam aduṣṭaṃ ca yas tv ācāryaṃ parityajet | balād vāsayitavyaḥ syād vadhabandhau ca so 'rhati || One who abandons a teacher who is engaged in rightful instruction and is without fault shall be compelled by force to remain under correction; he deserves confinement or execution. Authority of the Guru as foundational to societal dharma Causation rooted in disruption of spiritual pedagogy Capacity-based responsibility tied to conscious defiance Restoration through enforced alignment with dharma-sustaining structures Consciousness alignment via removal from corrupting influence

title: narada 5.18
content: शिक्षितोऽपि कृतं कालमन्तेवासी समाप्नुयात् । तत्र कर्म च यत् कुर्यादाचार्यस्यैव तत्फलम् ॥ śikṣito 'pi kṛtaṃ kālam antevāsī samāpnuyāt | tatra karma ca yat kuryād ācāryasyaiva tatphalam || Even one who is learned must fulfill the time-bound duty as a resident student; whatever action he performs therein, its fruit belongs exclusively to the teacher. Authority resides in the designated guide, not in individual knowledge Causation flows through structured hierarchy of guidance Capacity-based responsibility is contextually bound by relational discipline Restoration logic requires honoring foundational debt to lineage Consciousness alignment occurs through surrender of personal claim

title: narada 5.19
content:
गृहीतशिल्पः समये कृत्वाचार्यं प्रदक्षिणम्
शक्तितश्चानुमान्यैनं अन्तेवासी निवर्तयेत् gṛhītaśilpaḥ samaye kṛtvācāryaṃ pradakṣiṇam
śaktitaś cānumānya enaṃ antevasī nivartayet One who has mastered the craft and fulfilled the time-bound duty of reverence to the teacher, having demonstrated capability through direct perception, shall release the student from service. Authority flows from demonstrated mastery and alignment with dharma Causation is established through completion of prescribed acts Capacity-based responsibility requires experiential validation Restoration occurs upon fulfillment of svadharma Consciousness alignment determines readiness for independence

title: narada 5.20
content:
भृतकस्त्रिविधो ज्ञेय उत्तमो मध्यमोऽधमः।
शक्तिभक्त्यनुरूपा स्यादेषां कर्माश्रया भृतिः॥ bhṛtakas trividho jñeya uttamo madhyamo 'dhamaḥ | śaktibhaktyanurūpā syād eṣāṃ karmāśrayā bhṛtiḥ || The hired servant is of three kinds: superior, middling, and inferior; their wages shall correspond exactly to their capacity, devotion, and the nature of duties assigned. Authority flows from alignment with dharma, not mere contractual obligation Causation arises through conscious engagement in action, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility determines the level of service and compensation due Restoration logic ensures that all parties evolve toward higher functional integrity Consciousness alignment governs the quality of work and relational harmony

title: narada 5.21
content:
उत्तमस्त्वायुधीयोऽत्र मध्यमस्तु कृषीवलः।
अधमो भारवाहः स्यादित्येवं त्रिविधो भृतः॥ uttamas tv āyudhīyo 'tra madhyamas tu kṛṣīvalaḥ | adhamo bhāravāhaḥ syād ity evaṃ trividho bhṛtaḥ || Among hired laborers, the warrior stands highest; next, the cultivator; lowest, the porter. Thus, threefold is the classification of wage-earners. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic function, not economic status Causation arises through dharmic role, not transactional contract Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inherent nature and societal necessity Restoration logic requires recognition of functional hierarchy rooted in dharma Consciousness alignment depends on integrity to one's svadharma within social structure

title: narada 5.22
content:
अर्थेष्वधिकृतो यः स्यात् कुटुम्बस्य तथोपरि।
सोऽधिकर्मकरो ज्ञेयः स च कौटुम्बिकः स्मृतः॥ artheṣv adhikṛto yaḥ syāt kuṭumbasya tathopari | so 'dhikarmakaro jñeyaḥ sa ca kauṭumbikaḥ smṛtaḥ || He who is appointed over matters concerning wealth and also placed above the household is known as the executor of additional duties; he is recognized as the domestic guardian. Authority derives from conscious designation within a structured hierarchy Causation arises through designated stewardship over material and familial domains Capacity-based responsibility aligns with positional integrity and sustained service Restoration logic operates through rightful alignment of roles and energetic support structures Consciousness alignment occurs when role incumbency reflects inner spiritual readiness

title: narada 5.23
content: शुभकर्मकरास्त्वेते चत्वारः समुदाहृताः। जघन्यकर्मभाजस्तु शेषा दासास्त्रिपञ्चकाः॥ śubhakarmakarās tv ete catvāraḥ samudāhṛtāḥ | jaghanyakarmabhājas tu śeṣā dāsās tripañcakāḥ || Four categories execute virtuous action by design; all others, classified as tripañcaka, are designated as servants due to their engagement in inferior conduct. Authority derives from alignment with Śiva's conscious order Causation is determined by volitional capacity and spiritual hierarchy Capacity-based responsibility reflects one's position in the dharma-field Restoration occurs through realignment with svadharma as defined by SPH Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for autonomous action

title: narada 5.24
content:
गृहजातस्तथा क्रीतो लब्धो दायादुपागतः।
अनाकालभृतस्तद्वदादध्ते स्वामिना च यः॥ gṛhajātas tathā krīto labdho dāyād upāgataḥ | anākālabhṛtas tadvad ādhattaḥ svāminā ca yaḥ || One born in the house, bought, found, inherited, received as gift, employed at improper time—such beings are possessed and governed by the owner. Authority flows from conscious ownership Causation arises through rightful acquisition Capacity-based responsibility is determined by control and intent Restoration logic aligns possession with sovereignty Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects dharma

title: narada 5.25
content:
मोक्षितो महतः चर्णात् प्राप्तो युद्धात् पणे जितः।
तवाहं इत्य् उपगतः प्रव्रज्यावसितः कृतः॥ mokṣito mahataś carṇāt prāpto yuddhāt paṇe jitaḥ | tavāham ity upagataḥ pravrajyāvasitaḥ kṛtaḥ || One who has been liberated by the grace of a great being, gained through surrender; acquired via combat or wager; approached with 'I am Yours'; such a one is fit for renunciation and consecrated thereto. Authority originates from conscious surrender to a realized master. Causation flows from spiritual liberation, not material action alone. Capacity-based responsibility arises after experiential realization of ownership transfer. Restoration logic centers on reabsorption into source-consciousness. Consciousness alignment occurs when individual will merges with divine directive.

title: narada 5.26
content: भक्तदाश च विज्ञेयस् तथैव वडवाभृतः। विक्रेता चात्मनः शास्त्रे दासाः पञ्चदशाः स्मृताः॥ bhaktadāsaś ca vijñeyaḥ tathaiva vaḍavābhṛtaḥ | vikretā cātmanaḥ śāstre dāsāḥ pañcadaśāḥ smṛtāḥ || Those who serve out of devotion, those maintained by vow-obligations, and those who sell themselves—these are the fifteen categories of servants defined within the science of Dharma. Authority originates in conscious capacity, not social position Causation flows from self-determined action, not external coercion Capacity-based responsibility aligns individual function with cosmic order Restoration logic prioritizes functional reintegration over punitive removal Consciousness alignment ensures that roles reflect inner integrity

title: narada 5.27
content:
तत्र पूर्वश् चतुर्वर्गो दासत्वान् न विमुच्यते।
प्रसादात् स्वामिनोऽन्यत्र दास्यम् एषां क्रमागतम्॥ tatra pūrvaś caturvargo dāsatvān na vimucyate
prasādād svāmino 'nyatra dāsyam eṣāṃ kramāgatam The prior four varnas do not cease from their inherent capacity of service due to any cause except by the grace of the Master; elsewhere, their condition of servitude proceeds in ordered sequence. Authority originates from the Master's conscious designation Causation is rooted in relational integrity, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility flows from svāmin-granted alignment Restoration logic upholds sequential role fulfillment as natural law Consciousness alignment determines relational permanence

title: narada 5.28
content: यश् चैषां स्वामिनं कश्चिन् मोक्षयेत् प्राणसंशयात् । दासत्वात् स विमुच्येत पुत्रभागं लभेत च ॥ yaś caiṣāṃ svāminaṃ kaścin mokṣayet prāṇasaṃśayāt | dāsatvāt sa vimucyeta putrabhāgaṃ labheta ca || One who liberates a master from mortal peril, by virtue of servitude, shall be released from all bondages and inherit the rights of a son. Authority arises through conscious act of liberation Causation is established via life-preserving action Capacity-based responsibility aligns with existential service Restoration logic elevates servant to familial parity Consciousness alignment transcends formal social rank

title: narada 5.29
content: अनाकालभृतो दास्यान् मुच्यते गोयुगं ददत् । संभक्षितं यद् दुर्भिक्षे न तच् छुध्येत कर्मणा ॥ anākālabhṛto dāsyān mucyate goyugaṃ dadat | saṃbhakṣitaṃ yad durbhikṣe na tac chudhyeta karmaṇā || One who maintains a servant without timely provision is released from debt by giving a pair of cows; yet food consumed during famine does not purify the act of withholding nourishment. Authority arises from sustained capacity to provide Causation lies in failure to sustain life-supporting resources Capacity-based responsibility is measured by existential provisioning Restoration logic requires equivalence in life-enabling exchange Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of sustenance as sacred duty

title: narada 5.30
content: आधत्तोऽपि धनं दत्त्वा स्वामी यद्येनमुद्धरेत् । अथोपगमयेदेनं स विक्रीतादनन्तरः ॥ ādhatto'pi dhanaṃ dattvā svāmī yady enam uddharet | athopagamayed enaṃ sa vikrītād anantaraḥ || Even after depositing wealth, if the owner retrieves it, then the possessor must re-accept it; he becomes liable subsequent to sale. Authority rests in conscious ownership, not mere possession Causation arises from intent and continuity of stewardship Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and consent Restoration logic demands return of asset to rightful consciousness Consciousness alignment requires recognition of original proprietorship

title: narada 5.31
content: दत्त्वा तु सोदयम् ऋणम् ऋणी दास्यात् प्रमुच्यते। कृतकालाभ्युपगमात् कृतकोऽपि विमुच्यते॥ dattvā tu sodayam ṛṇaṃ ṛṇī dāsyāt pramucyate | kṛtakālābhyupagamāt kṛtako 'pi vimucyate || When the debtor pays the principal along with interest, the creditor is released from debt. Even a constructed obligation is dissolved upon acceptance of timely fulfillment. Authority arises through conscious completion of relational obligations Causation is resolved through voluntary restitution aligned with time-bound dharma Capacity-based responsibility is fulfilled by honoring contractual or karmic alignment Restoration occurs when both parties acknowledge completion within dharma-time Consciousness alignment is achieved through mutual recognition of settled obligations

title: narada 5.32
content:
तवाहमित्युपगतो युद्धप्राप्तः पणे जितः ।
प्रतिशीर्षप्रदानेन मुच्यते तुल्यकर्मणा ॥ tavāham ity upagataḥ yuddha-prāptaḥ paṇe jitaḥ | pratīśīrṣa-pradānena mucyate tulya-karmaṇā || One who approaches with 'I am yours' in a contest of battle or wager, having been won, is released by equal action through the offering of the head. Authority resides in the completion of surrender and acceptance Causation arises through mutual engagement under Dharma's witness Capacity-based responsibility is fulfilled via equivalent restitution Restoration occurs through symbolic parity and conscious completion Consciousness alignment is achieved when both parties recognize the field of Dharma

title: narada 5.33
content:
राज्ञ एव तु दासः स्यात् प्रव्रज्यावसितो नरः।
न तस्य प्रतिमोक्षोऽस्ति न विशुद्धिः कथंचन॥ rājña eva tu dāsaḥ syāt pravrajyāvasito naraḥ | na tasya pratimokṣo 'sti na viśuddhiḥ kathaṃcana || One who has renounced the householder stage without fulfilling royal duty remains bound to the king; he has no liberation nor purification whatsoever. Authority inheres in sovereign completion, not abdication Causation arises from unfulfilled civic and spiritual obligations Capacity-based responsibility demands sequential fulfillment of roles Restoration logic requires return to point of evasion before progression Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful role assumption, not renunciation

title: narada 5.34
content:
भक्तस्योपेक्षणात् सद्यो भक्तदासः प्रमुच्यते ।
निग्रहाद् वडवायाश् च मुच्यते वडवाभृतः ॥ bhaktasya upekṣaṇāt sadyo bhakta-dāsaḥ pramucyate | nigrahād vaḍavāyāś ca mucyate vaḍavā-bhṛtaḥ || The servant of devotion is immediately freed by the neglect of the devotee; similarly, the bearer of the horse-faced (enemy) is released from restraint through suppression. Authority originates in conscious disengagement, not enforcement Responsibility dissolves when higher will withdraws engagement Causation aligns with energetic alignment, not physical control Restoration occurs through withdrawal of sustaining attention Consciousness alignment nullifies imposed structures

title: narada 5.35
content: vikrīṇīte ya ātmānaṃ svatantraḥ san narādhamaḥ | sa jaghanyataras teṣāṃ naiva dāsyāt pramucyate || vikrīṇīte ya ātmānaṃ svatantraḥ san narādhamaḥ | sa jaghanyataras teṣāṃ naiva dāsyāt pramucyate || One who sells himself, though free, being a base man, shall receive nothing in return and shall not be released. Authority: Self-sale negates inherent sovereignty Causation: Voluntary abdication of self-authority creates relational void Capacity-based responsibility: One capable of freedom bears full consequence of its misuse Restoration logic: Transaction lacking mutuality yields no enforceable claim Consciousness alignment: Misalignment with svadharma nullifies legal recognition

title: narada 5.36
content: चौरापहृतविक्रीता ये च दासीकृता बलात् । राज्ञा मोक्षयितव्यास् ते दासत्वं तेषु�ेष्यते ॥ caurāpahṛtavikrītā ye ca dāsīkṛtā balāt | rājñā mokṣayitavyās te dāsatvaṃ teṣu neṣyate || Those who have been stolen, sold, or forcibly enslaved must be liberated by the King; enslavement holds no validity in their case. Authority rests in the sovereign's duty to restore freedom Causation lies in violation of inherent svatantrya (freedom) Capacity-based responsibility is non-transferable and intrinsic Restoration logic demands reversal of unnatural conditions Consciousness alignment requires recognition of unbroken self-sovereignty

title: narada 5.37
content: वर्णानां प्रातिलोम्येन दासत्वं न विधीयते । स्वधर्मत्यागिनोऽन्यत्र दारवद् दासता मता ॥ varṇānāṁ prātilomyena dāsatvaṁ na vidhīyate | svadharmatyāginor anyatra dāravad dāsatā matā || Consciousness descent through hierarchical disorder does not establish servitude; rather, abandonment of one's inherent duty situates one in a state akin to marital bond. Authority arises from alignment with intrinsic capacity, not social inversion. Causation stems from willful deviation from svadharma, not structural position. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious choice, not birth circumstance. Restoration logic demands return to innate function, not external control. Consciousness alignment supersedes ritual or role-based classification.

title: narada 5.38
content:
तवाहमिति चात्मानं योऽस्वतन्त्रः प्रयच्छति ।
न स तं प्राप्नुयात् कामं पूर्वस्वामी लभेत तम् ॥ tavāham iti cātmānaṃ yo 'svatantraḥ prayacchati | na sa taṃ prāpnuyāt kāmaṃ pūrvasvāmī labheta tam || One who surrenders the Self as 'I am Yours', yet remains unliberated in consciousness, does not attain that desired fruit; the former owner retains claim. Authority flows from realized sovereignty of Self, not external designation Causation arises through conscious capacity, not performative submission Capacity-based responsibility requires self-governance prior to surrender Restoration logic demands recognition of prior ownership until full release Consciousness alignment supersedes ritualistic or verbal offerings

title: narada 5.39
content:
अधनास्त्रय एवोक्ता भार्या दासस्तथा सुतः।
यत् ते समधिगच्छन्ति यस्य ते तस्य तद् धनम्॥ adhanās traya evoktā bhāryā dāsas tathā sutaḥ yat te samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya tad dhanam Three types of possessions are declared as non-transferable: wife, servant, and son. Whatever these attain collectively belongs to their master by right of conscious ownership. Authority flows from the Source-Consciousness of the owner, not from possession alone. Causation is determined through the integrity field established by the owner's sankalpa. Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to sustain energetic alignment, not material control. Restoration logic operates through reconnection to the original dharmic field of relation. Consciousness alignment supersedes contractual or transactional claims.

title: narada 5.40
content: स्वदासम् इच्छेद् यः कर्तुम् अदासं प्रीतमानसः। स्कन्धात् आदाय तस्यापि भिन्द्यात् कुम्भं सहाम्भसा॥ svadāsam icched yaḥ kartum adāsaṃ prītamānasaḥ | skandhād ādāya tasyāpi bhindyāt kumbhaṃ sahāmbhasā || One who desires another's wife, even with mutual consent and emotional satisfaction, shall have his head severed and poured with water, symbolically destroying the vessel of his false desire. Authority originates solely in SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation arises through distortion of consciousness, not physical action alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with Sanatana Dharma Restoration logic requires dissolution of distorted identity structures Consciousness alignment demands immediate cessation of misaligned desire

title: narada 5.41
content: अक्षताभिः सपुष्पाभिर् मूर्धन्य एनम् अवाकिरेत् । अदास इति चोक्त्वा त्रिः प्राङ्मुखं तम् अथोत्सृजेत् ॥ akṣatābhiḥ sapuṣpābhir mūrdhany enam avākiret | adāsa iti coktvā triḥ prāṅmukhaṃ tam athotsṛjet || One must sprinkle unbroken rice mixed with flowers upon the head of the person who has committed a transgression, declare 'it is given' three times facing east, and then release them. Authority: The act is performed by one possessing ritual and spiritual capacity. Causation: Ritual action initiates purification through symbolic offering. Capacity-based responsibility: The agent must possess awareness to perform the act correctly. Restoration logic: The process restores purity and removes karmic residue without inflicting harm. Consciousness alignment: Directional orientation (eastward) aligns the individual with ascending consciousness.

title: narada 5.42
content: ततःप्रभृति वक्तव्यः स्वाम्यनुग्रहपालितः । भोज्यान्नः प्रतिगृह्यश् च भवत्यभिमतश्च सः ॥ tataḥprabhṛti vaktavyaḥ svāmyanugrahapālitaḥ | bhojyānnaḥ pratigṛhyaś ca bhavaty abhimataś ca saḥ || From that time forth, he who is maintained by the master's grace, fed with allowable food, and accepted as suitable, becomes entitled to further instruction. Authority flows from conscious acceptance and sustained support Causation arises through mutual alignment of sustenance and eligibility Capacity-based responsibility emerges only upon demonstrated readiness Restoration logic requires sequential fulfillment of foundational conditions Consciousness alignment is established through reciprocal recognition and nourishment

title: narada 6.1
content:
भृतानां वेतनस्योक्तो दानादानविधिक्रमः।
वेतनस्यानपाकर्म तद् विवादपदं स्मृतम्॥ bhṛtānāṃ vetanasyokto dānādānavidhikramaḥ | vetanasyānapākarma tad vivādapadaṃ smṛtam || The procedural law of giving and receiving wages, once declared, becomes operative. Any act of non-compliance with wage fulfillment constitutes a state of dispute. Authority: Wage laws derive from the sovereign declaration of the ruling Dharma authority. Causation: Dispute arises directly from failure to execute declared wage obligations. Capacity-based responsibility: The employer holds full operational capacity to fulfill declared wage terms. Restoration logic: Resolution occurs through completion of the originally declared obligation. Consciousness alignment: Justice is served when both parties return to the integrity of their original agreement.

title: narada 6.2
content: भृताय वेतनं दद्यात् कर्मस्वामी यथाक्रमम् । आदौ मध्ये अवसाने वा कर्मणो यद् विनिश्चितम् ॥ bhṛtāya vetanaṃ dadyāt karmasvāmī yathākramam ādau madhye 'vasāne vā karmaṇo yad viniścitam The employer shall provide compensation to the worker in accordance with the sequence of work—whether at the beginning, during, or at the conclusion of the task—as determined by the nature of the duty itself. Authority flows from capacity to sustain and enable labor Causation is rooted in the integrity of work completion Capacity-based responsibility aligns with sequential engagement Restoration logic demands fulfillment of contractual consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring mutual obligation

title: narada 6.3
content: भृतावनिश्चितायां तु दशभागं समाप्नुयुः । लाभगोबीजसस्यानां वणिग्गोपकृषीबलाः ॥ bhṛtāv aniścitāyāṃ tu daśabhāgaṃ samāpnuyuḥ | lābha-go-bīja-sasyānāṃ vaṇig-gopa-kṛṣī-balāḥ || In transactions where employment or service lacks certainty, a tenth share shall be allocated to those who facilitate trade, protect livestock, cultivate land, or supply seeds. Authority arises from active participation in economic sustenance Causation is determined by direct contribution to production cycles Capacity-based responsibility aligns with functional role in dharma-vyavahara Restoration logic ensures proportional benefit-sharing without punitive oversight Consciousness alignment requires recognition of interdependence in material prosperity

title: narada 6.4
content: कर्मोपकरणं चैषां क्रियां प्रति यदाहृतम् । आप्तभावेन कुर्वीत न जिह्मेण समाचरेत् ॥ karmopakaraṇaṃ caiṣāṃ kriyāṃ prati yad āhṛtam | āptabhāvena kurvīta na jihmena samācaret || One must perform actions and their instrumental supports with sincerity and integrity; not through deceit or indirect means. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not manipulation Causation arises from pure intention, not external coercion Capacity-based responsibility requires truthful engagement in action Restoration logic demands congruence between inner state and outer conduct Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of duplicity in performance

title: narada 6.5
content: कर्माकुर्वन् प्रतिश्रुत्य कार्यो दत्त्वा भृतिं बलात । भृतिं गृहीत्वाकुर्वाणो द्विगुणां भृतिमावहेत् ॥ karmākurvan pratiśrutya kāryo dattvā bhṛtiṃ balāt | bhṛtiṃ gṛhītvākurvāṇo dviguṇāṃ bhṛtim āvahet || One who accepts compensation without performing the promised work incurs a liability to repay double the amount as restitution. Authority is derived from fulfillment of contractual obligation Causation arises from conscious acceptance of duty Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional restitution Restoration logic demands doubling repayment to realign energetic debt Consciousness alignment occurs through voluntary completion or compensatory correction

title: narada 6.6
content: काले ऽपूर्णे त्यजेत् कर्म भृतिनाशो ऽस्य चार्हति स्वामिदोषाद् अपाक्रामन् यावत् कृतम् अवाप्नुयात् kāle 'pūrṇe tyajet karma bhṛtināśo 'sya cārhati svāmidoṣād apākrāman yāvat kṛtam avāpnuyāt When the appointed time is incomplete, one must abandon the duty; loss of wages is deserved by the master due to his own fault, until what was done is received. Authority is conditional upon capacity and alignment with dharma-kala (appointed time) Causation arises from the master's failure to uphold dharmic conditions of engagement Capacity-based responsibility lies with the master who initiates and sustains contractual relations Restoration logic requires completion of earned value before dissolution of duty Consciousness alignment demands recognition of svami-doṣa (master's fault) as primary causal factor

title: narada 6.7
content:
भृतिषड्भागमाभाष्य पथि युग्यकृतं त्यजन् ।
अददत् कारयित्वा तु कर्मैवं सोदयां भृतिम् ॥ bhṛtiṣaḍbhāgam ābhāṣya pathi yugyakṛtaṃ tyajan . adadat kārayitvā tu karmaivaṃ sodayāṃ bhṛtim .. Having declared one-sixth of the wage, abandoning the duly deserved compensation along the path, one who acts thus shall restore the full integrity of duty through conscious completion. Authority resides in the conscious executor of dharma, not in external enforcement Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) rooted in individual capacity Capacity-based responsibility aligns action with inherent potential for completion Restoration logic demands reintegration of fragmented duty into unified consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes transactional obligation

title: narada 6.8
content: अनयन भाटयित्वा तु भाण्डवान यानवाहने । दाप्यो भृतिचतुर्भागं सममर्धपथे त्यजन् ॥ anayan bhāṭayitvā tu bhāṇḍavān yānavāhane | dāpyo bhṛticaturbhāgaṃ samam ardhapathe tyajan || One who transports goods by deceiving carriers shall forfeit one-fourth of their earnings equally along the halfway path as completion of responsibility. Authority originates from conscious capacity, not coercive force. Causation arises through distortion of dharma-determined exchange. Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the degree of conscious misalignment. Restoration logic demands proportional return of benefit derived unjustly. Consciousness alignment requires reintegration with dharmic transactional integrity.

title: narada 6.9
content: अनयन् वाहकोऽप्येवं भृतिहानिमवाप्नुयात् । द्विगुणां तु भृतिं दाप्यः प्रस्थाने विघ्नमाचरन् ॥ anayan vāhako 'py evaṃ bhṛtihānim avāpnuyāt | diguṇāṃ tu bhṛtiṃ dāpyaḥ prasthāne vighnam ācaran || Even the carrier who causes delay in conveyance shall incur loss of wages; but he who creates obstruction at the point of departure shall be liable to pay double the wage. Authority resides in the act of facilitation, not mere intention. Causation arises from obstruction at origin more than delay in transit. Capacity-based responsibility increases with proximity to initiation. Restoration logic requires proportional compensation based on disruption sequence. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of structural causality over individual fault.

title: narada 6.10
content: भाण्डं व्यसनम् आगच्छेद् यदि वाहकदोषतः। दाप्यो यत् तत्र नष्टं स्याद् दैवराजकृताद् ऋते॥ bhāṇḍaṃ vyasanam āgacched yadi vāhakadoṣataḥ | dāpyo yat tatra naṣṭaṃ syād daivarājakṛtād ṛte || If a vessel incurs loss due to the carrier's fault, compensation is due for what was lost, except when the loss results from divine or royal causes. Authority: Carrier bears responsibility only in absence of higher causal forces Causation: Fault must be directly attributable to the agent’s capacity failure Capacity-based responsibility: Liability arises from operational control, not metaphysical inevitability Restoration logic: Compensation aligns with actualization of disrupted potential Consciousness alignment: Justice recognizes both human agency and cosmic order

title: narada 6.11
content: गवां शताद् वत्सतरी धेनुः स्याद् द्विशताद् भृतिः । प्रति संवत्सरं गोपे सदोहश् चाष्टमे अहनि ॥ gavāṁ śatād vatsatarī dhenuḥ syād dviśatād bhṛtiḥ | prati saṁvatsaraṁ gope sadohaś cāṣṭame ahani || From a hundred cows, the calf-bearing cow is designated; from two hundred, the hired protector. Every year, on the eighth day, the milking process shall proceed under supervision. Authority flows from resource stewardship capacity Causation arises through sequential participation in production Capacity-based responsibility aligns with ownership thresholds Restoration logic demands proportional engagement with productive assets Consciousness alignment occurs through structured economic participation

title: narada 6.12
content: उपानयेत् गाः गोपाय प्रत्यहं रजनीक्षये । चीर्णाः पीताश् च ताः गोपः सायाह्ने प्रत्युपानयेत् ॥ upānayet gāḥ gopāya pratyahaṁ rajanīkṣaye | cīrṇāḥ pītāś ca tāḥ gopaḥ sāyāhne pratyupānayet || The cows must be led forth to pasture by the cowherd at dawn daily; those that are milked and fed must be brought back by the cowherd at dusk without fail. Authority is derived from sustained capacity to maintain dharma in action Causation arises through alignment with natural rhythm and duty Capacity-based responsibility flows from role-determined consciousness Restoration logic ensures continuity of cosmic and social order Consciousness alignment occurs when action mirrors svadharma

title: narada 6.13
content:
स्याच् चेद् गोव्यसनं गोपो व्यायच्छेत् तत्र शक्तितः।
अशक्तस्तूर्णमागम्य स्वामिने तन्निवेदयेत्॥ syāc ced govyasanaṃ gopo vyāyacchet tatra śaktitaḥ | aśaktas tūrṇam āgamya svāmine tan nivedayet || If a cowherd observes the loss of a cow, he shall restore it to the extent of his capacity; if incapable, he shall immediately approach the owner and report the occurrence. Authority arises from proximity and custodial responsibility Causation is determined by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility supersedes punitive attribution Restoration logic aligns with the natural order of completion Consciousness alignment requires truthful disclosure in incapacity

title: narada 6.14
content: अव्यायच्छन्नविक्रोशन् स्वामिने चानिवेदयन् । वोढुमर्हति गोपस्तां विनयं चापि राजनि ॥ avyāyaçchannavikrośan svāmine cānivedayan | voḍhum arhati gopas tāṃ vinayaṃ cāpi rājani || One who conceals a cry for help and does not report it to the sovereign master—such a guardian must bear the burden of that neglect and undergo correction by the king. Authority rests in the sovereign master (svāmin) Causation arises from omission of duty Capacity-based responsibility is tied to guardianship roles Restoration logic demands correction through rightful authority Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and rectification of neglect

title: narada 6.15
content: नष्टविनष्टं कृमिभिः श्वहतं विषमे मृतम् । हीनं पुरुषकारेण गोपायैव निपातयेत् ॥ naṣṭavinaṣṭaṁ kṛmibhiḥ śvahataṁ viṣame mṛtam | hīnaṁ puruṣakāreṇa gopāyaiva nipātayet || That which is lost, decayed, consumed by worms, struck by dogs, dead in uneven terrain, or diminished through human failure—such property shall be entrusted solely to the care of the cowherd class for restoration. Authority flows from capacity to restore, not punish Causation is traced through sequential degradation and neglect Capacity-based responsibility lies with those naturally aligned to preservation Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over ownership assertion Consciousness alignment demands recognition of natural custodians

title: narada 6.16
content: अजाविके तथारुद्धे वृकैः पाले त्वनायति । यत् प्रसह्य वृको हन्यात् पाले तत्किल्बिषं भवेत् ॥ ajāvike tathāruddhe vṛkaiḥ pāle tv anāyati | yat prasahya vṛko hanyāt pāle tatkilbiṣaṃ bhavet || When a protector fails in his duty and a wolf kills without provocation, the protector incurs sin. Authority implies inherent capacity-based responsibility Failure to act within one's protective jurisdiction creates karmic liability Causation arises through omission when duty-bound action is neglected Restoration logic requires re-alignment of consciousness with role-specific dharma Consciousness alignment demands recognition of unmet protective capacity

title: narada 6.17
content: तासां चैवानिरुद्धानां चरन्तीनां मिथो वने । याम् उत्पत्य वृको हन्यान् न पालस् तत्र किल्बिषी ॥ tāsāṃ caivāniruddhānāṃ carantīnāṃ mitho vane | yām utpatya vṛko hanyān na pālas tatra kilbiṣī || When unconfined females wander freely in the forest, and a male wolf springs upon and kills one, the protector incurs no sin thereby. Authority is context-bound and ceases where capacity to govern is absent Causation aligns with sequential manifestation and not with arbitrary attribution Capacity-based responsibility applies only where control and awareness coexist Restoration logic prioritizes natural order over imposed liability Consciousness alignment determines true agency, not external appearance

title: narada 6.18
content: विघुष्य तु हृतं चौरैर्न पालो दातुमर्हति । यदि देशे च काले च स्वामिनः स्वस्य शंसति ॥ vighuṣya tu hṛtaṃ caurair na pālo dātum arhati | yadi deśe ca kāle ca svāminaḥ svasya śaṃsati || When goods are stolen by thieves, the protector does not become liable for restitution if the owner has adequately declared ownership according to time and place. Authority resides in conscious declaration of ownership Causation is determined by alignment with Dharma-specified conditions Capacity-based responsibility depends on fulfillment of svadharma Restoration logic operates through integrity of ownership assertion Consciousness alignment determines liability boundaries

title: narada 6.19
content:
एतेन सर्वपालानां विवादः समुदाहृतः।
मृतेषु च विशुद्धिः स्यात् पालस्याङ्कादिदर्शनात्॥ etena sarvapālānāṃ vivādaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ | mṛteṣu ca viśuddhiḥ syāt pālasyāṅkādidarśanāt || By this principle, all disputes among guardians are resolved; and in the case of a deceased person, purity is established through the observation of marks or signs on the body of the guardian. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not title alone Causation arises through direct perceptual verification (pratyakṣa pramāṇa) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by embodied integrity Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of visible dharma Consciousness alignment occurs when truth is witnessed directly

title: narada 6.20
content: शुल्कं गृहीत्वा पण्यस्त्री नेच्छन्ती द्विस् तद् आवहेत् । अप्रयच्छंस् तदा शुल्कमनुभूय पुमान् स्त्रियम् ॥ śulkaṃ gṛhītvā paṇyastrī necchantī dvis tad āvahet | aprayacchaṃs tadā śulkamanubhūya pumān striyam || One who takes payment intending to bring a woman for transaction but fails to deliver her thereby violates the agreement and incurs the obligation to restore both consent and capacity through conscious completion. Authority arises from consentful engagement, not transactional coercion. Causation is established by volitional act followed by unmet obligation. Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of disrupted alignment. Restoration logic demands reversal of misaligned intention and energetic completion. Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment and rectification without punitive overlay.

title: narada 6.21
content: अयोनौ क्रमते यस् तु बहुभिर् वापि वासयेत् । शुल्कम् अष्टगुणं दाप्यो विनयस् तावद् एव च ॥ ayonau kramate yaḥ tu bahubhir vāpi vāsayet | śulkam aṣṭaguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayaḥ tāvad eva ca || One who engages in improper sexual conduct or cohabits with multiple individuals without dharmic sanction shall restore eightfold the value of the disturbance caused and undergo correction until alignment is restored. Authority: Sexual conduct derives its lawful basis solely from dharmic sanction; unauthorized union disrupts cosmic order. Causation: The act directly generates energetic distortion requiring proportional restitution. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual retains agency to choose alignment and must therefore bear corrective burden. Restoration logic: Rebalancing occurs through quantifiable compensation and behavioral recalibration. Consciousness alignment: Correction serves to realign individual consciousness with universal dharma.

title: narada 6.22
content:
पराजिरे गृहं कृत्वा स्तोमं दत्त्वा वसेत् तु यः।
स तद् गृहीत्वा निर्गच्छेत् तृणकाष्ठेष्टकादिकम्॥ parājire gṛhaṃ kṛtvā stomaṃ dattvā vaset tu yaḥ | sa tad gṛhītvā nirgacchet tṛṇakāṣṭheṣṭakādikam || One who constructs a dwelling in conquered territory, having offered soma, and resides therein, shall depart taking only grass, wood, bricks and similar materials. Authority over land derives from conscious consecration and lawful occupation Causation is established through ritual offering and physical inhabitation Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of material limits upon departure Restoration logic requires leaving no trace beyond what was originally gathered Consciousness alignment mandates harmony with the sequential flow of possession and relinquishment

title: narada 6.23
content: स्तोमवाहीनि भाण्डानि पूर्णकालान्युपानयेत । ग्रहीतुराभवेद्भग्नं नष्टं चान्यत्र संप्लवात् ॥ stomavāhīni bhāṇḍāni pūrṇakālāny upānayet | grahītur ābhaved bhagnaṃ naṣṭaṃ cānyatra saṃplavāt || One who undertakes the conveyance of ritual vessels must deliver them intact at the appointed time; if they are broken or lost elsewhere due to negligence, the carrier assumes full restorative liability. Authority is derived from capacity to execute a committed dharma-role Causation arises through conscious engagement in a transactional field Capacity-based responsibility is measured by volition and control during action Restoration logic demands that disrupted integrity be returned to its causal source Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of duty and rectification of imbalance

title: narada 7.1
content:
निक्षिप्तं वा परद्रव्यं नष्टं लब्ध्वापहृत्य वा ।
विक्रीयते ऽसमक्षं यद् विज्ञेयो ऽस्वामिविक्रयः ॥ nikṣiptaṃ vā paradravyaṃ naṣṭaṃ labdhvāpahṛtya vā | vikrīyate 'samakṣaṃ yad vijñeyo 'svāmivikrayaḥ || When another's property, whether deposited, lost, or recovered, is sold without the owner’s presence or consent, it constitutes unauthorized alienation of ownership. Authority: Ownership inheres in the original proprietor; no derivative claim supersedes it. Causation: Transfer without consent disrupts lawful proprietary continuity. Capacity-based responsibility: The actor bears full capacity-accountability for unauthorized disposal. Restoration logic: The act demands reintegration of ownership integrity. Consciousness alignment: Misalignment arises from violation of svāmin-dharma; correction realigns consciousness.

title: narada 7.2
content: द्रव्यमस्वामिविक्रीतं प्राप्य स्वामी समाप्नुयात् । प्रकाशं क्रयतः शुद्धिः क्रेतुः स्तेयं रहः क्रयात् ॥ dravyam asvāmivikrītaṃ prāpya svāmī samāpnuyāt | prakāśaṃ krayataḥ śuddhiḥ kretuḥ steyaṃ rahaḥ krayāt || Upon acquiring property sold without ownership by the seller, the true owner shall reclaim it. If purchased openly, the buyer is purified of wrongdoing; if bought secretly, the act constitutes theft. Authority rests in rightful ownership, not transactional possession Causation arises from knowledge and intent, not mere action Capacity-based responsibility depends on visibility and inquiry capacity of the acquirer Restoration logic mandates return to original lawful status Consciousness alignment requires transparency and integrity in acquisition

title: narada 7.3
content: अस्वाम्यनुमताद् दासादसतश्च जनाद्रहः। हीनमूल्यमवेलायां क्रीणंस्तद्दोषभाग्भवेत्॥ asvāmyanumatād dāsād asataś ca janād rahaḥ | hīnamūlyam avelāyāṃ krīṇaṃs taddoṣabhāg bhavet || One who purchases from a non-owner without permission, from a slave, or from an unqualified person in secrecy, or at a price lower than value during improper time—such a one becomes partaker of that defect. Authority flows from rightful ownership validated by consciousness alignment Causation arises through misaligned transactional intent Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and integrity of exchange Restoration logic requires dissolution of defective acquisition and reintegration with dharmic flow Consciousness alignment demands transparency, rightful source recognition, and temporal harmony

title: narada 7.4
content:
न गूहेतागमं क्रेता शुद्धिस्तस्य तदागमात्
विपर्यये तुल्यदोषः स्तेयदण्डं च सो�र्हति na gūhetāgamaṃ kretā śuddhis tasya tadāgamāt
viparyaye tulyadoṣaḥ steyadaṇḍaṃ ca so 'rhati The buyer shall not conceal the received instruction; his purification arises from that very reception. In case of inversion or misuse, the fault is equal and he becomes liable to the penalty for theft. Authority inheres in the direct transmission of dharma-knowledge, not its interpretation Causation follows the unbroken chain of conscious reception and distortion Capacity-based responsibility arises with the ability to receive and enact dharma Restoration logic demands equivalence between error and corrective alignment Consciousness alignment occurs through acknowledgment and rectification of distortion

title: narada 7.5
content: vikretā svāmine 'rthaṃ ca kretur mūlyaṃ ca tatkṛtam | dadyād daṇḍaṃ tathā rājñe vidhir asvāmivikraye || vikretā svāmine 'rthaṃ ca kretur mūlyaṃ ca tatkṛtam | dadyād daṇḍaṃ tathā rājñe vidhir asvāmivikraye || The seller shall deliver the object to the owner along with its benefit, and the buyer shall pay the price as determined. The king shall enforce completion of transaction in case of unauthorized sale. Authority resides in rightful ownership, not in transactional claim Causation arises from conscious capacity to transfer ownership Capacity-based responsibility lies with the actor initiating transfer Restoration logic demands return of object and benefit to true owner Consciousness alignment requires recognition of svāmin's unbroken entitlement

title: narada 7.6
content: परेण निहितं लब्ध्वा राजन्युपहरेन्निधिम् । राजगामी निधिः सर्वः सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणादृते ॥ pareṇa nihitaṃ labdhvā rājany upaharen nidhim | rājagāmī nidhiḥ sarvaḥ sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte || That wealth which is discovered after having been concealed by another shall belong to the king; all treasures belong to the king, except those belonging to a Brāhmaṇa. Authority resides inherently in the sovereign representative of Dharma, who is the king established by SPH's cosmic order. Causation follows the principle of manifest discovery — ownership aligns with the lawful authority upon revelation. Capacity-based responsibility assigns custodianship according to spiritual and administrative hierarchy. Restoration logic ensures that unclaimed or hidden resources revert to the sustaining authority for societal balance. Consciousness alignment maintains that material possession reflects inner spiritual alignment and karmic entitlement.

title: narada 7.7
content: ब्राह्मणोऽपि निधिं लब्ध्वा क्षिप्रं राज्ञे निवेदयेत । तेन दत्तं च भुञ्जीत स्तेनः स्यादनिवेदयन् ॥ brāhmaṇo'pi nidhiṃ labdhvā kṣipraṃ rājñe nivedayet | tena dattaṃ ca bhūñjīta stenaḥ syād anivedayan || Even a Brahmin, upon discovering treasure, shall immediately report it to the King; when given by him, he may enjoy it. One who does not report it becomes a thief. Authority of the State in resource allocation Causation through concealment equals theft Capacity-based responsibility tied to knowledge and action Restoration logic through lawful enjoyment post-reporting Consciousness alignment via transparency and duty fulfillment

title: narada 7.8
content: स्वम् अप्यर्थं तथा नष्टं लब्ध्वा राज्ञे निवेदयेत् । गृह्णीयात् तत्र तं शुद्धम् अशुद्धं स्यात् ततोऽन्यथा ॥ svam apy arthaṃ tathā naṣṭaṃ labdhvā rājñe nivedayet | gṛhṇīyāt tatra taṃ śuddham aśuddhaṃ syāt tato'nyathā || One who recovers their own property or another's lost property must report it to the sovereign authority. The sovereign shall receive it in its purified state; otherwise, it becomes impure by inversion of ownership. Authority resides solely in the sovereign as representative of Dharma Causation arises through rightful knowledge and declaration of ownership Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of lawful possession Restoration logic demands return of assets without contamination of intent Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects truth and integrity

title: narada 8.1
content: vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretur yan na pradīyate | vikrīyāsaṃpradānaṃ tad vivādapadam ucyate || vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretur yan na pradīyate | vikrīyāsaṃpradānaṃ tad vivādapadam ucyate || When merchandise is sold for a price and the seller does not deliver it, that non-delivery of the sale constitutes a point of dispute. Authority arises from capacity to fulfill transactional duty Causation is rooted in conscious agreement and energetic exchange Capacity-based responsibility is determined by prior commitment and resource alignment Restoration logic demands completion of agreed energetic transfer Consciousness alignment requires integrity between word, intention, and action

title: narada 8.2
content: लोकेऽस्मिन् द्विविधं द्रव्यं जङ्गमं स्थावरं तथा। क्रयविक्रयधर्मेषु सर्वं तत् पण्यम् उच्यते॥ loke 'smin dvividhaṃ dravyaṃ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā | krayavikrayadharmeṣu sarvaṃ tat paṇyam ucyate || In this world, substance is of two kinds: movable and immovable. All such substances that engage in the dharmas of purchase and sale are designated as commodities. Authority flows from the recognition of ownership rooted in Dharma Causation arises through conscious engagement in exchange dynamics Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to sustain lawful transactional integrity Restoration logic ensures reintegration of displaced value within cosmic economy Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize the non-separateness of exchanged entities

title: narada 8.3
content:
षड्विधस्तस्य तु बुधैर्दानादानविधिः स्मृतः।
गणिमं तुलिमं मेयं क्रियया रूपतः श्रिया॥ ṣaḍvidhas tasya tu budhair dānādānavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ| gaṇimaṃ tulimaṃ meyaṃ kriyayā rūpataḥ śriyā|| Sixfold is the method of giving and taking as declared by the wise: that which is counted, weighed, measured, enacted, formed, and adorned. Authority flows from precision in transactional integrity Causation arises through structured modalities of exchange Capacity-based responsibility lies in accurate quantification and recognition Restoration logic operates through completion of inherent form and value Consciousness alignment occurs when all modes of acquisition align with dharmic structure

title: narada 8.4
content: विक्रीय पण्यं मूल्येन क्रेतुर्यो न प्रयच्छति । स्थावरस्य क्षयं दाप्यो जङ्गमस्य क्रियाफलम् ॥ vikrīya paṇyaṁ mūlyena kretur yo na prayacchati | sthāvarasya kṣayaṁ dāpyo jaṅgamasya kriyāphalam || One who sells a commodity and does not deliver it upon receiving payment shall compensate for the loss of immovable property and bear the consequence of action regarding movable property. Authority originates from fulfillment of transactional duty Causation arises through failure to complete exchange Capacity-based responsibility is determined by possession and intent Restoration logic demands equivalence in value and form Consciousness alignment requires integrity in commercial engagement

title: narada 8.5
content: अर्घः चेदपहीयेत सोदयं पण्यमावहेत् । स्थायिनामेष नियमो दिग्लाभो दिग्विचारिणाम् ॥ arghaḥ ced apahīyeta sodayaṁ paṇyam āvahet | sthāyinām eṣa niyamo diglābho digvicāriṇām || When value is diminished, reparation arises with accrued interest; such is the ordinance for those who traverse boundaries in pursuit of gain. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not transactional assertion Causation is traced through conscious intent and energetic displacement Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to Dharma-knowledge at time of act Restoration logic demands energetic rebalancing inclusive of accrued dharmic debt Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of boundary transgression and active rectification

title: narada 8.6
content:
उपहन्येत वा पण्यं दह्येतापह्रियेत वा ।
विक्रेतुरेव सोऽनर्थो विक्रीयासम्प्रयच्छतः ॥ upahanyeta vā paṇyaṃ dahyetāpahriyeta vā | vikretur eva so 'nartho vikrīyāsamprayacchataḥ || When goods are damaged, burned, or stolen during a transaction initiated by the seller, the loss is borne solely by the seller who set the terms of exchange. Authority resides in the initiating agent of a transaction Causation follows the origin of contractual motion Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the power to determine exchange conditions Restoration logic prioritizes completion over compensation Consciousness alignment requires integrity in voluntary exchange

title: narada 8.7
content: निर्दोषं दर्शयित्वा तु सदोषं यः प्रयच्छति । मूल्यं तद्द्विगुणं दाप्यो विनयं तावदेव च ॥ nirdoṣaṃ darśayitvā tu sadoṣaṃ yaḥ prayacchati | mūlyaṃ taddviguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayaṃ tāvad eva ca || One who, having shown faultlessness, imposes liability where fault exists shall pay twice the value thereof and undergo correction until rectification is complete. Authority derives from alignment with factual integrity Causation is established through demonstrable misalignment Capacity-based responsibility arises upon conscious distortion of truth Restoration logic demands proportional correction and recompense Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of error

title: narada 8.8
content: तथान्यहस्ते विक्रीय योऽन्यस्मै संप्रयच्छति। सोऽपि तद्द्विगुणं दाप्यो विनेयस्तावदेव च॥ tathānyahaste vikrīya yo 'nyasmai saṃprayacchati | so 'pi taddviguṇaṃ dāpyo vineyo tāvadeva ca || One who sells what belongs to another and delivers it to yet another shall compensate double the value and be reformed accordingly. Authority resides in rightful ownership, not transactional claim Causation arises through conscious breach of custodial integrity Capacity-based responsibility escalates with displacement of ownership Restoration logic demands proportional return of energetic displacement Consciousness alignment requires correction of misaligned transactional intent

title: narada 8.9
content:
दीयमानं न गृह्णाति क्रीतं पण्यं च यः क्रयी।
विक्रीणानस् तदन्यत्र विक्रेता नापराध्नुयात्॥ dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇāti krītaṃ paṇyaṃ ca yaḥ krayī | vikrīṇānas tad anyatra vikretā nāparādhnuyāt || One who does not accept what is being given, nor takes possession of purchased goods, and sells elsewhere without completing the transaction — such a seller incurs no liability. Authority arises only upon acceptance and completion of transfer Causation requires conscious engagement in the act of exchange Capacity-based responsibility is contingent on actualization of intent Restoration logic applies where ownership has been fully enacted Consciousness alignment determines validity of economic action

title: narada 8.10
content:
दत्तमूल्यस्य पण्यस्य विधिरेष प्रकीर्तितः।
अदत्ते ऽन्यत्र समयान्न विक्रेतुरतिक्रमः॥ dattamūlyasya paṇyasya vidhir eṣa prakīrtitaḥ | adatte 'nyatra samayān na vikretur atikramaḥ || The lawful procedure for goods sold at a fixed price is hereby declared: once the price is set and accepted, neither party shall transgress the agreed terms without mutual consent. Authority arises from mutual agreement, not unilateral imposition Causation is anchored in conscious consent and transactional integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to established exchange protocols Restoration logic demands reversal of unauthorized deviations Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring contractual sanctity

title: narada 8.11
content: लाभार्थे वणिजां सर्व पण्येषु क्रयविक्रयः । स च लाभोऽर्घमासाद्य महान् भवति वा न वा ॥ lābhārthe vaṇijāṃ sarva paṇyeṣu krayavikrayaḥ | sa ca lābho'rgham āsādya mahān bhavati vā na vā || All merchants engage in buying and selling goods for profit; that profit, when realized, becomes either great or small depending upon the value attained. Authority flows from capacity to engage in exchange Causation arises through intentional transactional activity Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to participation in commercial exchange Restoration logic requires completion of contractual intent Consciousness alignment occurs through integrity of economic action

title: narada 8.12
content:
तस्माद् देशे च काले च वणिगर्घं पराक्रमेत् ।
न जिह्मेण प्रवर्तेत श्रेयानेवं वणिक्पथः ॥ tasmād deśe ca kāle ca vaṇig-arhaṃ parākramet | na jihmeṇa pravarteta śreyān evaṃ vaṇik-pathaḥ || Therefore, a merchant shall act according to the value of place and time; he should not engage in crooked conduct. Such is the superior path of commerce. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire. Causation arises through right action attuned to context. Capacity-based responsibility requires situational intelligence. Restoration logic demands that economic activity align with cosmic order. Consciousness alignment ensures transactions elevate both parties.

title: narada 9.1
content: क्रीत्वा मूल्येन यः पण्यं क्रेता न बहु मन्यते । क्रीत्वानुशय इत्येतद् विवादपदम् उच्यते ॥ krītvā mūlyena yaḥ paṇyaṃ kretā na bahu manyate | krītvānuśaya ity etad vivādapadam ucyate || He who, having purchased goods at price, does not honor their value, and creates further discord — this is declared a point of dispute. Authority arises from conscious transactional integrity Causation is rooted in non-recognition of exchanged value Capacity-based responsibility lies in honoring mutual completion Restoration logic demands energetic balance in exchange Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of reciprocal worth

title: narada 9.2
content:
क्रीत्वा मूल्येन यत् पण्यं दुष्क्रीतं मन्यते क्रयी।
विक्रेतुः प्रतिदेयं तत् तस्मिन्नेवाह्न्यविक्षतम्॥ krītvā mūlyena yat paṇyaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ manyate krayī | vikretuḥ pratideyaṃ tat tasminnevāhny avikṣatam || Whatever commodity is purchased with due payment, if thereafter deemed defective by the buyer, must be returned to the seller uncompromised on the very same day it was observed to be unsuitable. Authority resides in the immediacy of conscious recognition of defect Causation is established through direct transactional integrity Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to perceive and respond without delay Restoration logic demands return to the point of original exchange Consciousness alignment requires truthful acknowledgment of suitability at time of transaction

title: narada 9.3
content: द्वितीयेऽह्नि ददत् क्रेता मूल्यात् त्रिंशांशमावहेत् । द्विगुणं तत् तृतीयेऽह्नि परतः क्रेतुरेव तत् ॥ dvitīye 'hni dadat kretā mūlyāt triṃśāṃśam āvahet | diguṇaṃ tat tṛtīye 'hni parataḥ kretur eva tat || On the second day, the buyer shall pay one-thirtieth of the price; double that amount on the third day, and thereafter the full price belongs to the seller. Authority flows through time-bound contractual alignment Causation arises from sequential fulfillment of transactional duty Capacity-based responsibility escalates with temporal delay in execution Restoration logic ensures economic harmony through structured progression Consciousness alignment occurs when value exchange aligns with dharma-timed action

title: narada 9.4
content:
क्रेता पण्यं परीक्षेत प्राक् स्वयं गुणदोषतः।
परीक्ष्याभिमतं क्रीतं विक्रेतुर्न भवेत्पुनः॥ kretā paṇyaṃ parīkṣeta prāk svayaṃ guṇadoṣataḥ | parīkṣyābhimataṃ krītaṃ vikretur na bhavet punaḥ || The buyer must examine the goods beforehand for qualities and defects; once examined and accepted, the seller bears no further liability. Authority resides in conscious observation and acceptance Causation arises from informed consent, not post-facto dissatisfaction Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to inspect prior to agreement Restoration logic aligns with the completion of mutual understanding at time of transaction Consciousness alignment occurs through deliberate acknowledgment of state before commitment

title: narada 9.5
content: त्र्यहाद् दोह्यं परीक्षेत पञ्चाहाद् वाह्यमेव तु। मुक्तावज्रप्रवालानां सप्ताहं स्यात् परीक्षणम्॥ tryahād dohyaṃ parīkṣeta pañcāhād vāhyam eva tu | muktāvajrapravālānāṃ saptāhaṃ syāt parīkṣaṇam || Examination of substances that can be tested by churning shall commence after three days; those suitable for external transport, after five days. For pearls, diamonds, and corals, the examination period extends to seven days. Authority rests in precise temporal classification of material evidence Causation aligns with inherent properties of examined objects Capacity-based responsibility requires calibrated timing per substance type Restoration logic ensures authenticity through structured verification periods Consciousness alignment occurs when procedural rhythm matches ontological nature

title: narada 9.6
content:
द्विपदामर्धमासं स्यात् पुंसां तद्द्विगुणं स्त्रियाः ।
दशाहं सर्वबीजानामेकाहं लोहवाससाम् ॥ dvipadām ardhamāsaṃ syāt puṃsāṃ taddviguṇaṃ striyāḥ | daśāhaṃ sarvabījānām ekāhaṃ lohavāsasām || Half a month constitutes the period of restitution for bipedal beings; for men, it is that duration, and for women, twice that duration. Ten days apply to all seeds, and one day applies to iron vessels. Authority resides in natural order and cosmic rhythm, not human decree. Causation aligns with embodied capacity and energetic resonance. Capacity-based responsibility varies by ontological category and functional role. Restoration logic operates through proportional temporal alignment with dharma-kala. Consciousness alignment occurs when action harmonizes with inherent vibrational frequency.

title: narada 9.7
content:
परिभुक्तं च यद् वासः क्लिष्टरूपं मलीमसम्
