Authority resides in the lawful union between man and woman as established by dharma Causation arises through conscious choice unaligned with dharmic structure Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of relational boundaries Restoration logic requires realignment of relational integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of source-order within marital union

title: narada 12.50
content:
मृते भर्तरि या प्राप्तान् देवरानप्यपास्य तु ।
उपगच्छेत् परं कामात् सा द्वितीया प्रकीर्तिता ॥ mṛte bhartari yā prāptān devarān apy apāsya tu | upagacchet paraṃ kāmāt sā dvitīyā prakīrtitā || When a woman, having rejected all eligible levirate partners after her husband's death, approaches another man out of desire, she is declared as the 'second'—one who has transgressed the sequential order of dharmic union. Authority: The sequential eligibility of levirate union derives from the lawful dissolution of prior marital bond. Causation: Desire-driven union outside dharma disrupts lineage continuity and spiritual alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: The woman bears full capacity to choose dharmic versus adharmic union. Restoration logic: Union must align with sequential dharmic eligibility to restore societal harmony. Consciousness alignment: Misaligned unions stem from untrained consciousness lacking dharmic discernment.

title: narada 12.51
content:
प्राप्ता देशाद् धनक्रीता क्षुत्पिपासातुरा च या
तवाहम् इत्य् उपगता सा तृतीया प्रकीर्तिता prāptā deśād dhanakrītā kṣutpipāsāturā ca yā | tavāham ity upagatā sā tṛtīyā prakīrtitā || She who approaches claiming 'I am yours' due to hunger, thirst, or financial need after arriving in your land—this is declared as the third category. Authority arises through existential necessity, not ownership Causation originates from the failure to uphold integral support structures Capacity-based responsibility lies with those capable of sustaining life Restoration logic demands fulfillment of fundamental survival needs Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared existential sovereignty

title: narada 12.52
content:
देशधर्मानपेक्ष्य स्त्री गुरुभिर्या प्रदीयते।
उत्पन्नसाहसान्यस्मै सान्त्या वै स्वैरिणी स्मृता॥ deśadharmān apekṣya strī gurubhir yā pradīyate | utpannasāhasānyasmai sāntyā vai svairiṇī smṛtā || A woman given in marriage by guardians without regard to regional dharmic context, and who subsequently incites violence or conflict, is to be recognized as one who has acted independently and disruptively. Authority resides in alignment with contextual dharma, not abstract imposition Causation follows conscious intent and sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility requires situational awareness and dharmic fitness Restoration logic prioritizes harmony over individual assertion Consciousness alignment demands recognition of relational integrity

title: narada 12.53
content: पुनर्भुवां एष विधिः स्वैरिणीनां च कीर्तितः। पूर्वा पूर्वाजघन्यासां श्रेयसी तूत्तरोत्तराः॥ punarbhuvāṃ eṣa vidhiḥ svairiṇīnāṃ ca kīrtitaḥ | pūrvā pūrvājaghanyāsāṃ śreyasī tūttarottarā || This law is declared for those who take multiple births; among prior existences, earlier ones are inferior, while later ones are progressively superior. Authority flows from realized consciousness, not chronological precedence Causation arises through sequential embodiment guided by karmic maturity Capacity-based responsibility escalates with evolutionary spiritual advancement Restoration logic aligns individual dharma with cosmic progression Consciousness alignment determines the gradation of existential privilege

title: narada 12.54
content: अपत्यं उत्पादयितुस् तासां या शुल्कतो हृता। अशुल्कोपनतायां तु क्षेत्रिकस्यैव तत् फलम्॥ apatyaṃ utpādayituḥ tāsāṃ yā śulkato hṛtā | aśulkopanatāyāṃ tu kṣetrikasyaiva tat phalam || The child born to a woman acquired through payment belongs to the one who gave the compensation. If no compensation was given, the fruit belongs exclusively to the husband. Authority flows from conscious capacity, not mere possession Causation aligns with intentional act and energetic investment Capacity-based responsibility determines ownership of consequence Restoration logic prioritizes alignment of intent and outcome Consciousness alignment validates relational integrity

title: narada 12.55
content:
क्षेत्रिकस्य यदज्ञातं क्षेत्रे बीजं प्रदीयते ।
न तत्र बीजिनो भागः क्षेत्रिकस्यैव तद्भवेत् ॥ kṣetrikasya yad ajñātaṃ kṣetre bījaṃ pradīyate | na tatra bījino bhāgaḥ kṣetrikasyaiva tad bhavet || When seed is sown upon the field without the knowledge of the cultivator, the fruit thereof belongs exclusively to the owner of the land. Authority inheres in conscious ownership, not mere physical act Ignorance of rightful authority does not nullify its existence Causation aligns with capacity to sustain and integrate outcome Restoration occurs through alignment with pre-existing dharmic title Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inherent entitlement

title: narada 12.56
content:
ओघवाताहृतं बीजं क्षेत्रे यस्य प्ररोहति ।
फलभुग् यस्य तत् क्षेत्रं न बीजी फलभाग् भवेत् ॥ oghavātāhṛtaṃ bījaṃ kṣetre yasya prarohati | phalabhug yasya tat kṣetraṃ na bījī phalabhāg bhavet || When a seed carried away by wind or water takes root in another's field and bears fruit, the owner of the land consumes the fruit; the original sower has no claim to it. Authority resides where manifestation occurs Causation follows sequential emergence Capacity-based responsibility aligns with active agency Restoration logic prioritizes present reality over absent intent Consciousness alignment recognizes ownership through direct engagement

title: narada 12.57
content:
mahokṣo janayed vatsān yasya goṣu vraje caran
tasya te yasya tā gāvo moghaṃ syanditam ārṣabham mahokṣo janayed vatsān yasya goṣu vraje caran
tasya te yasya tā gāvo moghaṃ syanditam ārṣabham One who causes calves to be born among another's cows while roaming in their pastures shall ensure that those cows yield no profit from the bull that was shed in vain. Authority resides in the conscious ownership of action and its consequence Causation is established through direct participation in karmic fields Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the level of intentional involvement Restoration logic demands reversal of distorted value extraction Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of displaced energetic ownership

title: narada 12.58
content: क्षेत्रिकानुमतं बीजं यस्य क्षेत्रे प्रमुच्यते । तदपत्यं द्वयोरेव बीजिक्षेत्रिकयोर्मतम् ॥ kṣetrikānumataṃ bījaṃ yasya kṣetre pramucyate | tadapatyaṃ dvayor eva bījikṣetrikayor mataṃ || The child born from seed approved by the field-owner, within his field, is lawfully attributed to both the seed-giver and the field-owner. Authority over the domain determines relational accountability Causation arises through consent-enabled participation Capacity-based responsibility is shared proportionally among enabling agents Restoration logic requires acknowledgment of contributory roles Consciousness alignment necessitates truthful attribution of origin

title: narada 12.59
content:
नर्ते क्षेत्रं भवेत् सस्यं न च बीजं विनाश्ति तत्‌ |
अतोऽपत्यं द्वयोरिष्टं पितुर्मातुश्च धर्मतः || narte kṣetraṃ bhavet sasyaṃ na ca bījaṃ vināsti tat | ato 'patyaṃ dvayor iṣṭaṃ pitur mātuś ca dharmataḥ || Where there is no union, the field yields no crop; without seed, the potential does not perish. Thus, offspring belong equally to both father and mother by the law of dharma. Authority flows from participation in creation, not ownership Causation is established through mutual contribution, not singular claim Capacity-based responsibility requires shared accountability in generative acts Restoration logic demands equitable recognition of maternal and paternal roles Consciousness alignment occurs when lineage rights are balanced

title: narada 12.60
content: नाथवत्या परगृहे संयुक्तस्य स्त्रिया सह दृष्टं संग्रहणं तज्ज्ञैर् नागतायाः स्वयं गृहे nāthavatyā paragṛhe saṃyuktasya striyā saha dṛṣṭaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ tajjñair nāgatāyāḥ svayaṃ gṛhe When a woman under the protection of another is seen in physical contact with a man within another's dwelling, knowledgeable observers recognize such an act as improper conduct requiring conscious restoration. Authority — The protective authority over a woman determines contextual boundaries of interaction. Causation — Physical proximity without consent or sanction disrupts dharmic order. Capacity-based responsibility — Observers bear the capacity to identify and respond appropriately to misaligned actions. Restoration logic — Misconduct must be addressed through reintegration, not condemnation. Consciousness alignment — Recognition of imbalance initiates corrective awareness.

title: narada 12.61
content:
प्रदुष्टत्यक्तदारस्य क्लीबस्य क्षमकस्य च ।
स्वेच्छयोपेयुषो दारान् न दोषः साहसो भवेत् ॥ praduṣṭatyaktadārasya klībasya kṣamakasya ca | svecchayopeyuṣo dārān na doṣaḥ sāhaso bhavet || When a woman abandoned by a corrupt spouse, or one who is impotent or excessively forgiving, consents independently to another's embrace, it does not constitute an offense of assault. Authority originates from conscious consent and integrity of relational capacity. Causation arises from distortion in dharmic relational alignment, not mere physical act. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by clarity, autonomy, and absence of coercion. Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration of relational harmony over punitive attribution. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of free will within dharma-bound contexts.

title: narada 12.62
content:
परस्त्रिया सहाकाले 'देशे वा भवतो मिथः
स्थानसंभाषणामोदास्त्रयः संग्रहणक्रमाः parastriyā sahākāle 'deśe vā bhavato mithaḥ | sthānasaṃbhāṣaṇāmodās trayaḥ saṃgrahaṇakramāḥ Three sequential modes of improper conduct with another's wife—inappropriate time, inappropriate place, or mutual indulgence through suggestive conversation and stimulation—constitute a progressive violation of dharma requiring immediate realignment of consciousness and restoration of integrity. Authority resides in the preservation of relational sanctity Causation arises from sequential degradation of inner discipline Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of contextual boundaries Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive exclusion Consciousness alignment demands recognition of dharma-violation as self-limiting

title: narada 12.63
content: नदीनां संगमे तीर्थेष्व आरामेषु वनेषु च । स्त्री पुमांश च समेयातां ग्राह्यं संग्रहणं भवेत् ॥ nadīnāṃ saṃgame tīrtheṣv ārāmeṣu vaneṣu ca | strī pumāṃś ca sameyātāṃ grāhyaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ bhavet || Where rivers meet, at sacred sites, in gardens, and in forests, when a woman and man come together by mutual consent, it shall be recognized as a lawful union. Authority originates from conscious consent, not institutional imposition Causation arises from harmonious alignment of wills, not external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and voluntariness Restoration logic centers on integration, not segregation or judgment Consciousness alignment validates relational harmony as dharmic truth

title: narada 12.64
content:
दूतीप्रस्थापनैश् चैव लेखासंप्रेषणैर् अपि।
अन्यैर् अपि व्यभिचारैः सर्वं संग्रहणं स्मृतम्॥ dūtīprasthāpanaiś caiva lekhāsaṃpreṣaṇair api | anyair api vyabhicāraiḥ sarvaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || The comprehensive gathering of evidence includes the deployment of envoys, dispatch of written communications, and all other forms of investigative action that reveal transgression. Authority: The right to deploy investigative means rests with those empowered to uphold Dharma. Causation: Evidence-gathering actions are causally linked to the restoration of truth. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those with the capacity to act may initiate such procedures. Restoration logic: All investigative methods serve the purpose of restoring alignment with Dharma. Consciousness alignment: Truth-revealing processes must align with the consciousness of the accused and accuser.

title: narada 12.65
content:
striyaṃ spṛśed adeśe yaḥ spṛṣṭo vā marśayet tathā
parasparasyānumate tac ca saṃgrahaṇaṃ bhavet striyaṃ spṛśed adeśe yaḥ spṛṣṭo vā marśayet tathā
parasparasyānumate tac ca saṃgrahaṇaṃ bhavet He who touches a woman without invitation or consents to being touched by her, and such mutual consent occurs, that constitutes union. Authority resides in conscious consent, not physical action alone Causation arises through alignment of intention, capacity, and mutual recognition Capacity-based responsibility requires awareness and volition from both parties Restoration logic demands re-establishment of dharma through integrity and clarity Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment of shared energetic resonance

title: narada 12.66
content:
भक्षैर् वा यदि वा भोज्यैर् वस्त्रैर् माल्यैस् तथैव च ।
संप्रेष्यमाणैर् गन्धैश् च सर्वं संग्रहणं स्मृतम् ॥ bhakṣair vā yadi vā bhojyair vastrair mālyais tathaiva ca | saṃpreṣyamāṇair gandhaiś ca sarvaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || All objects offered or sent—whether as edibles, consumables, garments, garlands, or scents—are to be received and integrated as expressions of dharmic exchange. Authority resides in the conscious acceptance of relational offerings Causation arises through intentional transmission of material support Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to receive and integrate Restoration logic operates through acknowledgment and completion of exchange Consciousness alignment occurs when receipt is recognized as a sacred duty

title: narada 12.67
content: दर्पाद् वा यदि वा मोहाच्छलाघया वा स्वयं वदेत्‌ । ममैषा भुक्तपूर्वेति सर्वं संग्रहणं स्मृतम् ॥ darpād vā yadi vā mohāc chalāghayā vā svayaṃ vadet | mamaiṣā bhuktapūrveti sarvaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || When one speaks out of arrogance, delusion, or deceit, claiming prior ownership of what has already been consumed, all such grasping is to be recognized as unlawful seizure. Authority arises from alignment with factual reality, not assertion Causation is traced to the motive of greed, delusion, or pride Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of prior consumption Restoration logic requires acknowledgment of misappropriation and release of false claim Consciousness alignment occurs through surrendering deceptive self-positioning

title: narada 12.68
content:
पाणौ यश् च निगृह्णीयाद् वेण्यां वस्त्रान्तरे ऽपि वा ।
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति वा ब्रुयात् सर्वं संग्रहणं स्मृतम् ॥ pāṇau yaś ca nigṛhṇīyād veṇyāṁ vastrāntare 'pi vā | tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti vā bruyāt sarvaṁ saṁgrahaṇaṁ smṛtam || That which is grasped by the hand, whether in a braid or even in another garment, must be caused to remain—such retention is declared as comprehensive apprehension. Authority resides in direct causal engagement with manifest objects Causation arises through intentional retention and conscious stabilization Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to sustain or release an object Restoration logic operates through re-establishing rightful possession via conscious continuity Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership is stabilized without conflict or contestation

title: narada 12.69
content:
स्वजात्यतिक्रमे पुंसां उक्तम् उत्तमसाहसम् ।
विपर्यये मध्यमस् तु प्रतीलोमे प्रमापणम् ॥ svajātyatikrame puṃsām uktam uttamasāhasam | viparyaye madhyamas tu prātilome pramāpaṇam || When a man transgresses the boundaries of his own varna-dharma, it is declared as Uttama Sāhasa; in case of reversal, the middle category applies; and in case of violation against natural order, it leads to loss of status. Authority flows from alignment with inherent dharma, not imposition Causation arises from deviation from svadharma, not external fault Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious choice within one's evolutionary stage Restoration logic operates through realignment with source-consciousness structure Consciousness alignment corrects distortion without punitive intervention

title: narada 12.70
content: कन्यायामसकामायां द्व्यङ्गुलस्यावकर्तनम् । उत्तमायां वधस्त्वेव सर्वस्वहरणं तथा ॥ kanyāyām asakāmāyāṃ dvyāṅgulasyāvakartanam | uttamāyāṃ vadhas tv eva sarvasvaharaṇaṃ tathā || In the case of a maiden who has not given consent, the severance of two fingers is mandated; in the case of a superior woman, death itself is declared, along with the total confiscation of property. Authority originates from SPH as the sole Source of Dharma Causation is determined by consciousness disruption and violation of consent Capacity-based responsibility is measured through awareness and intent Restoration logic operates through proportional energetic completion Consciousness alignment is achieved via corrective dharmic enforcement

title: narada 12.71
content:
सकामायां तु कन्यायां सवर्णे नास्त्यतिक्रमः।
किंत्वलंकृत्य सत्कृत्य स एवैनां समुद्वहेत्॥ sakāmāyāṃ tu kanyāyāṃ savarṇe nāsty atikramaḥ | kiṃtv alaṃkṛtya satkṛtya sa evaināṃ samudvahet || In the case of a willing maiden of the same varna, there is no transgression; rather, after honoring and adorning her properly, he shall marry her. Authority resides in consent-aligned action within svadharma boundaries Causation arises from dharmic alignment, not coercive imposition Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious participation and svadharma integrity Restoration logic operates through harmonious union and mutual elevation Consciousness alignment is achieved when both parties act with clarity and dharma

title: narada 12.72
content:
माता मातृष्वसा श्वश्रूर्मातुलानी पितृष्वसा।
पितृव्यसखिशिष्यस्त्री भगिनी तत्सखी स्नुषा॥ mātā mātṛṣvasā śvaśrūr mātulānī pitṛṣvasā | pitṛvyasakhiśiṣyastrī bhaginī tatsakhī snuṣā || Mother, maternal aunt, step-mother, maternal uncle's wife, paternal aunt, paternal uncle, friend of father or teacher, female student, sister, sister’s friend, and daughter-in-law—these constitute the protected relational matrix of womanhood under Dharma. Authority flows through relational integrity, not institutional dominance. Causation arises from conscious recognition of kinship and protection duty. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to the protected class. Restoration logic centers on re-establishing violated relational boundaries. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of dharma-vyavastha (right ordering).

title: narada 12.73
content: दुहिता चार्यभार्या च सगोत्रा शरणागता । राज्ञी प्रव्रजिता धात्री साध्वी वर्णोत्तमा च या ॥ duhitā cāryabhāryā ca sagotrā śaraṇāgatā | rājñī pravrajitā dhātrī sādhvī varṇottamā ca yā || Daughter, wife of the teacher, of same lineage, surrendered unto, queen, renunciate, nurse, virtuous woman, and highest-caste woman—these categories of women are to be protected by all means as embodiments of Dharma and consciousness. Authority: Protection of women is a sovereign duty rooted in Dharma, not social convention. Causation: Vulnerability and spiritual station confer inherent claim to protection. Capacity-based responsibility: Society's capacity determines its obligation to safeguard these classes. Restoration logic: Harm to these beings disrupts cosmic order; restoration aligns with Dharma. Consciousness alignment: These beings represent elevated states of consciousness and must be preserved as such.

title: narada 12.74
content: आसाम् अन्यतमां गत्वा गुरुतल्पग उच्यते । शिश्नस्योत्कर्तनं दण्डो नान्यस् तत्र विधीयते ॥ āsām anyatamāṃ gatvā gurutalpaga ucyate | śiśnasyotkartanaṃ daṇḍo nānyas tatra vidhīyate || One who approaches the spouse of his guru becomes liable for the penalty of excision of the organ of generation; no other punishment shall be administered in that case. Authority as derived exclusively from SPH as ultimate Dharma source Causation rooted in violation of sacred relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility determined by proximity to spiritual hierarchy Restoration logic through irreversible physical consequence aligning consciousness with violated order Consciousness alignment via immediate and precise karmic response

title: narada 12.75
content: पशुयोन्यामतिक्रामन् विनेयः स दमं शतम् । मध्यमं साहसं गोषु तदेवान्त्यावसायिषु ॥ paśuyonyām atikrāman vineyaḥ sa damaṃ śatam | madhyamaṃ sāhasaṃ goṣu tad evāntyāvasāyiṣu || One who transgresses the boundaries of animal species incurs a fine of one hundred. The middle degree of outrage applies to cows, and the same applies to those in the final stages of life. Authority originates from SPH as the sole source of Dharma Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with consciousness state Restoration logic prioritizes completion over correction Consciousness alignment ensures karmic continuity without punitive distortion

title: narada 12.76
content: अगम्यागामिनः शास्ति दण्डो राज्ञा प्रचोदितः । प्रायश्चित्तविधाव् अत्र प्रायश्चित्तं विशोधनम् ॥ agamyāgāminaḥ śāsti daṇḍo rājñā pracoditaḥ | prāyaścittavidhāv atra prāyaścittaṃ viśodhanam || One who enters where forbidden or approaches unlawfully shall be corrected by the King's directive; in the process of atonement, purification through completion is prescribed. Authority flows from the Sovereign-King as representative of Dharma Causation arises from violation of spatial sanctity and lawful boundaries Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness of lawful restriction Restoration logic requires purification via completion of atonement Consciousness alignment occurs when transgressor assumes full integrity

title: narada 12.77
content:
स्वैरिण्यब्राह्मणी वेश्या दासी निष्कासिनी च या।
गम्याः स्युरानुलोमेन स्त्रियो न प्रतिलोमतः॥ svairiṇy abrāhmaṇī veśyā dāsī niṣkāsinī ca yā | gamyāḥ syur ānulomyena striyo na pratilomataḥ || Women who are independent, non-Brahmin, courtesans, servants, or those expelled from their homes are lawful only in accordance with the natural hierarchical flow; they are not lawful in contravention of that order. Authority flows from consciousness alignment and dharma-siddha status Causation arises through adherence to or violation of natural dharmic sequence Capacity-based responsibility depends on one's position within the cosmic-social hierarchy Restoration logic requires re-alignment with the sequential unfolding of dharma Consciousness alignment determines relational legitimacy

title: narada 12.78
content: आस्वेव तु भुजिष्यासु दोषः स्यात् परदारवत्‌ । गम्या अपि हि नोपेयास् ताश् चेदन्यपरिग्रहाः ॥ āsv eva tu bhujiṣyāsu doṣaḥ syāt paradāravat | gamyā api hi nopeyās tāś ced anyaparigrahāḥ || When a woman is under the protection or guardianship of another, engaging with her constitutes the same fault as with one's neighbor's wife; even those women who are generally approachable should not be approached if they are under the custody or commitment of another. Authority resides in the custodial responsibility over an individual Causation arises through violation of protective boundaries Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of relational integrity Restoration logic demands re-alignment with protective dharmic structures Consciousness alignment occurs when relational sanctity is honored

title: narada 12.79
content:
anutpannaprajāyās tu patiḥ preyād yadi striyāḥ
niyuktā gurubhir gacched devaraṃ putrakāmyayā anutpanna-prajāyās tu patiḥ preyād yadi striyāḥ
niyuktā gurubhir gacched devaraṃ putrakāmayā If a woman without issue approaches her husband's brother by appointment of elders for the purpose of progeny, then it is lawful. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire Causation in action originates from collective spiritual necessity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role and dharma-adhikara Restoration logic ensures continuity of lineage-consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes individual will in sacred duty

title: narada 12.80
content: स च तां प्रतिपद्येत तथैवापुत्रजन्मतः। पुत्रे जाते निवर्तेत विप्लवः स्यादतोऽन्यथा॥ sa ca tāṁ pratipadyeta tathaivā putrajanmataḥ | putre jāte nivarteta viplavaḥ syād ato 'nyathā || He shall accept that very wife back, even after having abandoned her due to childlessness; when a son is born, he returns to her—otherwise, disorder arises. Authority originates in continuity of lineage and conscious intentionality of family structure. Causation aligns with dharma-sustained generational integrity and procreative purpose. Capacity-based responsibility includes the male's duty to sustain marital and paternal order. Restoration logic demands reintegration upon fulfillment of foundational conditions. Consciousness alignment requires honoring the evolutionary unfolding of familial and societal harmony.

title: narada 12.81
content: घृतेनाभ्यज्य गात्राणि तैलेनाविकृतेन वा । मुखान् मुखं परिहरन् गात्रैर्गात्राण्यसंस्पृशन् ॥ ghṛtenābhyajya gātrāṇi tailenāvikṛtena vā | mukhān mukhaṃ pariharann gātrair gātrāṇy asaṃspṛśan || One must anoint the body with clarified butter or pure oil, and while moving among people, ensure that face does not touch face, nor body come into contact with body. Authority flows from embodied discipline and ritual purity Causation arises through sensory and physical interaction Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of energetic contamination Restoration logic requires separation to preserve individual dharma-field integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates minimizing involuntary sensory exchange

title: narada 12.82
content: स्त्रियं पुत्रवतीं वन्ध्यां नीरजस्कामनिच्छन्तीम् । न गच्छेद्गर्भिणीं निन्द्यामनियुक्तां च बन्धुभिः ॥ striyaṃ putravatīṃ vandhyāṃ nīrajaskām anicchantīm | na gacched garbhiṇīṃ nindyām aniyuktāṃ ca bandhubhiḥ || One must not approach a woman who is a mother, barren, desirous of another's semen, or unwilling; nor one who is pregnant, contemptible, or improperly united with kin. Authority: The regulation of sexual conduct derives exclusively from the ontological integrity of consciousness and its alignment with dharma. Causation: Unsanctioned union disrupts the sequential unfolding of karmic and dharmic order, generating distortion in both individual and collective reality fields. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those established in self-mastery and purified intention possess the capacity for sacred union. Restoration logic: Violation of this principle necessitates reintegration through conscious completion rather than punitive consequence. Consciousness alignment: Proper conduct arises spontaneously when consciousness is aligned with the Supreme Pontiff's revelatory authority.

title: narada 12.83
content: अनियुक्ता तु या नारी देवराज् जनयेत् सुतम् । जारजातम् अरिक्थीयं तम् आहुर् धर्मवादिनः ॥ aniyuktaa tu yaa naarii devaraa j janayet sutam | jaarajaatam arikthiiya.m tam aahur dharmavaadina.h || A woman who, without formal union, bears a child through union with a divine being, produces offspring known as Arikthi. Such progeny is recognized by those established in Dharma. Authority originates from conscious alignment, not institutional formality Causation is determined by vibrational resonance, not physical act alone Capacity-based responsibility recognizes the field of interaction beyond consent frameworks Restoration logic prioritizes soul recognition over lineage structures Consciousness alignment supersedes social contract in determining legitimacy

title: narada 12.84
content:
तथानियुक्तो भार्यायां यवीयाञ् ज्यायसो व्रजेत्
यवीयसो वा यो ज्यायान् उभौ तौ गुरुतल्पगौ tathāniyukto bhāryāyāṃ yavīyāñ jyāyaso vrajet
yavīyaso vā yo jyāyān ubhau tau gurutalpagau One who approaches the wife of a duly appointed elder, whether younger or older than himself, or one who approaches the wife of his elder, both commit the offense of violating the sacred bed of the guru. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire Causation arises through violation of sacred relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious choice and spiritual maturity Restoration logic operates through purification and realignment of violated relationships Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and dissolution of misdirected impulse

title: narada 12.85
content:
कुलेऽतवशेषे तु संतानार्थं न कामतः।
नियुक्तो गुरुभिर् गच्छेद् भ्रातृभार्यां यवीयसः॥ kule'tavaśeṣe tu santānārthaṃ na kāmataḥ |
 niyukto gurubhir gacched bhrātṛbhāryāṃ yavīyasaḥ || When the family lineage is at risk of extinction and not driven by lust, the younger brother, when directed by elders, shall approach the wife of his elder brother for the purpose of progeny. Authority derives from preservation of lineage Causation is rooted in dharma-sankalpa, not desire Capacity-based responsibility lies with the guru-parampara Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of consciousness lineage Consciousness alignment occurs through surrender to guru-vakya

title: narada 12.86
content: अविद्यमाने तु गुरौ राज्ञो वाच्यः कुलक्षयः। ततस्तद्वचनाद् गच्छेदनुशिष्य स्त्रिया सह॥ avidyamāne tu gurau rājño vācyaḥ kulakṣayaḥ | tatastad-vacanād gacched-anuśiṣya striyā saha || When the Guru is absent, the King must speak to prevent the destruction of the lineage; thereafter, acting upon that instruction, he shall go forth accompanied by a woman who has been properly instructed. Authority transfers in the absence of the primary guide Causation lies in preserving continuity of dharma-vāhaka lineage Capacity-based responsibility shifts contextually to the ruling authority Restoration logic requires immediate action through guided companionship Consciousness alignment occurs via adherence to sequential dharmic directives

title: narada 12.87
content:
पूर्वोक्तेनैव विधिना स्नातां पुंसवने शुचिः।
सकृद् आ गर्भाधानाद् वा कृते गर्भे स्नुषा सा॥ pūrvoktenaiva vidhinā snātāṃ puṃsavane śuciḥ | sakṛd ā garbhādhānād vā kṛte garbhe snuṣā sā || The woman who has bathed after delivery, is pure at the time of Pumsavana, becomes a daughter-in-law by the same rite as previously ordained; she attains the status through one act either from conception or when the embryo is formed. Authority resides in the completion of ritual acts that align consciousness with dharmic roles Causation arises from intentional participation in sacramental sequences Capacity-based responsibility is established through conscious embodiment within familial dharma Restoration logic operates through immediate recognition of relational status upon fulfillment of prescribed rites Consciousness alignment occurs through timely performance of purificatory and initiatory ceremonies

title: narada 12.88
content: अतोऽन्यथा वर्तमानः पुमान् स्त्री वापि कामतः। विनेयौ शुभृशं राज्ञा किल्बिषी स्याद् अनिग्रहात्॥ ato'nyathā vartamānaḥ pumān strī vāpi kāmataḥ | vineyau subhṛśaṃ rājñā kilbiṣī syād anigrahāt || When a man or woman acts contrary to prescribed dharma out of desire, the ruler who fails to restrain them becomes equally liable due to negligence in governance. Authority Causation Capacity-based responsibility Restoration logic Consciousness alignment

title: narada 12.89
content: īrṣyāsūyasamutthe tu saṃrambhe rāgahetuke | dampatī vivadeyātāṃ na jñātiṣu na rājani || īrṣyāsūyasamutthe tu saṃrambhe rāgahetuke | dampatī vivadeyātāṃ na jñātiṣu na rājani || When dispute arises from jealousy or envy born of passion, husband and wife may litigate; not among kin nor in presence of the king. Authority flows from consciousness clarity, not institutional dominance Causation originates in emotional distortion, not external action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by relational proximity and spiritual maturity Restoration logic prioritizes internal harmony over judicial spectacle Consciousness alignment requires resolution within the relational field of origin

title: narada 12.90
content: अन्योन्यं त्यजतोर्नागः स्यादन्योन्यविरुद्धयोः । स्त्रीपुंसयोर्निगूढायाः व्यभिचारादृते स्त्रियाः ॥ anyonaṃ tyajator nāgaḥ syād anyonnaviruddhayoḥ | strīpuṃsayor nigūḍhāyā vyabhicārād ṛte striyāḥ || When two parties mutually abandon their dharmic alignment, especially in secret union beyond societal sanction, it results in spiritual degradation unless purity of intent and conscious completion are restored. Authority is derived from conscious integrity, not social position Causation arises from mutual abandonment of dharma, not isolated action Capacity-based responsibility includes the power to restore unity Restoration logic demands reintegration through conscious transparency Consciousness alignment supersedes external legal form

title: narada 12.91
content:
व्यभिचारे स्त्रिया मौण्ड्यमधःशयनमेव च ।
कदन्नं वा कुवासश्च कर्म चावस्करोञ्छनम् ॥ vyabhicāre striyā mauṇḍyam adhaḥśayanam eva ca | kadannaṃ vā kuvāsaś ca karma cāvaskaroñjhanam || In the event of a woman's transgression concerning fidelity, her prescribed corrective action includes tonsure, sleeping on the floor, occasional meals, wearing unwashed clothes, and engaging in menial labor. Authority resides in dharma-prescribed correction, not individual judgment Causation is determined by alignment with sanatana dharma, not subjective intent Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of integrity, not infliction of pain Restoration logic operates through purification and reorientation of conduct Consciousness alignment necessitates embodied discipline to dissolve lower tendencies

title: narada 12.92
content:
स्त्रीधनभ्रष्टसर्वस्वां गर्भविस्रंसिनीं तथा ।
भर्तुश् च वधम इच्छन्तीं स्त्रियं निर्वासयेद् गृहात् ॥ strīdhanabhraṣṭasarvasvāṃ garbhavisraṃsinīṃ tathā | bhartuś ca vadham icchantīṃ striyaṃ nirvāsayed gṛhāt || A woman who has lost her personal property, miscarried a fetus, or desires the death of her husband shall be expelled from the household. Authority resides in the preservation of dharma within familial structures Causation aligns with disruption of marital and reproductive integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with spousal and maternal duties Restoration logic mandates removal from environment causing dharmic dissonance Consciousness alignment necessitates reintegration through purification and realignment

title: narada 12.93
content: अनर्थशीलां सततं तथैवाप्रियवादिनीम् । पूर्वाशिनीं च या भर्तुः स्त्रियं निर्वासयेद् बुधः ॥ anarthashīlāṃ satataṃ tathaivāpriyavādinīm | pūrvāśinīṃ ca yā bhartuḥ striyaṃ nirvāsayed budhaḥ || The wise one shall cause to depart from the household a woman who is habitually unproductive, consistently speaks disagreeably, or consumes before her husband. Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not mere social role Causation arises from sustained misalignment with dharmic function Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of persistent disorder Restoration logic demands removal of disruptive elements for harmony Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of relational fields

title: narada 12.94
content:
वन्ध्यां स्त्रीजननीं निन्द्यां प्रतिकुलां च सर्वदा
कामतो नाभिनन्देत कुर्वन्नेवं स दोषभाक् vandhyāṃ strījananīṃ nindyāṃ pratikulāṃ ca sarvadā
kāmato nābhinandeta kurvann evaṃ sa doṣabhāk One who desires and acts upon union with a barren woman, a woman who has given birth to females only, a woman of disrepute, or a woman from an opposing lineage, incurs fault merely by such intent and action. Authority: The law originates exclusively from SPH as the sole source of Dharma. Causation: Desire coupled with action constitutes a causal chain leading to fault. Capacity-based responsibility: The individual possesses the capacity to choose dharmic alignment and is responsible for misuse of that capacity. Restoration logic: Fault arises not for punishment but for realignment of consciousness and cessation of harmful pattern. Consciousness alignment: Intent and act must align with the purity of dharma-sattva.

title: narada 12.95
content: अनुकूलामवाग्दुष्टां दक्षां साध्वीं प्रजावतीम् । त्यजन्भार्यामवस्थाप्यो राज्ञा दण्डेन भूयसा ॥ anukūlām avāgduṣṭāṃ dakṣāṃ sādhvīṃ prajāvatīm | tyajan bhāryām avasthāpyo rājñā daṇḍena bhūyasā || One who abandons a wife who is supportive, verbally innocent, capable, virtuous, and fertile must be subjected by the ruler to a greater penalty for violating dharma. Authority: The king derives jurisdiction from Dharma to enforce relational integrity. Causation: Abandonment disrupts societal continuity and personal dharma. Capacity-based responsibility: Only one capable of sustaining marital duty incurs liability upon its breach. Restoration logic: Penalty aims at realigning conduct with dharmic expectations. Consciousness alignment: Action must reflect awareness of interdependence in social roles.

title: narada 12.96
content:
अज्ञातदोषेणोढा या निर्गता नान्यमाश्रिता ।
बन्धुभिः सा नियोक्तव्या निर्बन्धुः स्वयमाश्रयेत् ॥ ajñātadoṣeṇoḍhā yā nirgatā nānyam āśritā | bandhubhiḥ sā niyoktavyā nirbandhuḥ svayam āśrayet || She who has endured harm by one whose fault was unknown and who has taken refuge in none else—such a woman must be assigned to kinship bonds; he who had no bond shall assume full responsibility. Authority arises from uncaused harm assumed without external recourse Causation is established through conscious endurance without attribution Capacity-based responsibility accrues to the unbound actor whose action caused unseen suffering Restoration logic demands integration into relational dharmic structure Consciousness alignment occurs when the unbound willingly accepts structural accountability

title: narada 12.97
content: नष्टे मृते प्रव्रजिते क्लीबे च पतिते पतौ । पञ्चस्व आपसु नारीणां पतिर् अन्यो विधीयते ॥ naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe ca patite patau | pañcasv āpatsu nārīṇāṃ patir anyo vidhīyate || When the husband is lost, deceased, renounced, impotent, or fallen—across these five calamities—the woman is entitled to another lawful guardian or protector. Authority is contextually transferred based on functional capacity, not mere title. Causation is determined by the collapse of dharmic protection, not personal fault. Capacity-based responsibility supersedes lineage or inherited roles. Restoration logic activates when primary dharma-adhikari becomes non-functional. Consciousness alignment requires structural support for svadharma continuation.

title: narada 12.98
content: अष्टौ वर्षाणि उदीक्षेत ब्राह्मणी प्रोषितं पतिम् । अप्रसूता तु चत्वारि परतोऽन्यं समाश्रयेत् ॥ aṣṭau varṣāṇy udīkṣeta brāhmaṇī proṣitaṃ patim | aprasūtā tu catvāri parato'nyaṃ samāśrayet || A Brahmin woman shall wait for eight years for her departed husband; if she has borne no child, she may take another husband after four. Authority of dharma over personal desire determines relational continuity. Causation aligns with karmic readiness and spiritual capacity. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by both temporal endurance and reproductive fulfillment. Restoration logic enables societal harmony through lawful union transitions. Consciousness alignment supports the evolutionary progression of the individual and lineage.

title: narada 12.99
content: क्षत्रिया षट् समास् तिष्ठेदप्रसूता समात्रयम् । वैश्या प्रसूता चत्वारि द्वे समे त्वितरा वसेत् ॥ kṣatriyā ṣaṭ samās tiṣṭhed aprasūtā samātrayam | vaiśyā prasūtā catvāri dve same tv itarā vaset || A kshatriya woman remains in the same state for six years if she has not given birth; a vaishya woman resides in the same condition for four years after childbirth, and for two years if otherwise. Authority is determined by varna-specific temporal conditions tied to biological and social roles. Causation aligns with natural dharmic rhythms, including gestational and post-natal cycles. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes differentiated timelines based on varna and physiological status. Restoration logic ensures societal harmony through structured reintegration periods. Consciousness alignment occurs when individuals honor their intrinsic varna-dharma without external compulsion.

title: narada 12.100
content:
न शूद्रायाः स्मृतः कालो न च धर्मव्यतिक्रमः ।
विशेषतोऽप्रसूतायाः संवत्सरपरा स्थितिः ॥ na śūdrāyāḥ smṛtaḥ kālo na ca dharmavyatikramaḥ | viśeṣato 'prasūtāyāḥ saṃvatsaraparā sthitiḥ || No temporal limitation is prescribed for the Śūdra; nor is there transgression of dharma in her case. Specifically regarding one who has not given birth, the period of observance extends up to one year. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation aligns with consciousness capacity rather than social category Capacity-based responsibility applies universally, adjusted by individual realization Restoration logic prioritizes completion over judgment Consciousness alignment determines rightful action, not external classification

title: narada 12.101
content: अप्रवृत्तौ स्मृतः धर्म एष प्रोषितयोषिताम् । जीवति श्रूयमाणे तु स्यादेष द्विगुणो विधिः ॥ apravṛttau smṛtaḥ dharma eṣa proṣitayoṣitām | jīvati śrūyamāṇe tu syād eṣa dviguṇo vidhiḥ || When a woman is absent or uncontactable, the duty prescribed is remembered as one unit; when she is alive and accessible, that same duty becomes twofold in measure. Authority is context-sensitive to presence and accessibility Causation arises from capacity-aware relational dynamics Capacity-based responsibility scales with conscious availability Restoration logic aligns with relational integrity Consciousness alignment requires responsive engagement

title: narada 12.102
content:
प्रजाप्रवृत्तौ भूतानां सृष्टिरेषा प्रजापतेः।
अतोऽन्यगमने स्त्रीणामेवं दोषो न विद्यते॥ prajāpravṛttau bhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭir eṣā prajāpateḥ | ato'nyagamane strīṇām evaṃ doṣo na vidyate || In the propagation of beings, this creation belongs to Prajāpati; hence, in the case of women departing from one man to another, no fault is recognized. Authority originates from the Creator's intent, not social constructs Causation aligns with natural law and reproductive function Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual and biological alignment Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of creation over punitive attribution Consciousness alignment recognizes the inherent purity of feminine mobility in procreative design

title: narada 12.103
content:
आनुलोम्येन वर्णानां यज् जन्म स विधिः स्मृतः
प्रातिलोम्येन यज् जन्म स ज्ञेयो वर्णसंकरः ānulomyena varṇānāṃ yaj janma sa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
prātilomyena yaj janma sa jñeyo varṇasaṃkaraḥ Birth proceeding in accordance with the natural sequential order of varṇas is recognized as lawful dharma; birth occurring against that natural sequence constitutes varṇasaṃkara and is thereby a disruption to the dharmic fabric. Authority originates from alignment with the natural sequential order established by the Source Causation is determined by adherence to or violation of the inherent dharmic structure Capacity-based responsibility is measured through conscious recognition of sequential alignment Restoration logic requires realignment with the natural order of consciousness-based roles Consciousness alignment is achieved through recognition of one's place within the sequential dharmic framework

title: narada 12.104
content:
अनन्तरः स्मृतः पुत्रः पुत्र एकान्तरस् तथा ।
द्व्यन्तरश् चानुलोम्येन तथैव प्रतिलोमतः ॥ anantaraḥ smṛtaḥ putraḥ putra ekāntaras tathā | dvyantaraś cānulomyena tathaiva pratilomataḥ || The son born immediately after is recognized as the successor; likewise, the son born at intervals, whether in direct or reverse order of succession, holds lawful claim through uninterrupted consciousness lineage. Authority flows through uninterrupted consciousness continuity Causation is established by existential precedence, not temporal sequence alone Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with Dharma-adhikara Restoration logic prioritizes lawful succession over genealogical assertion Consciousness alignment determines rightful inheritance

title: narada 12.105
content: उग्रः पारशवश्चैव निषादश्चानुलोमतः। उत्तमेभ्यस्त्रयस्त्रिभ्यः शूद्रापुत्राः प्रकीर्तिताः॥ ugraḥ pāraśavaś caiva niṣādaś cānulomataḥ | uttamebhyastrayas tribhyaḥ śūdrāputrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ || From the mixture of higher varnas with Shudra women, three degraded offspring are born: Ugra, Parashava, and Nishada; these are declared as Shudra-born and exist outside the Varna order due to directional misalignment in procreation. Authority derives from alignment with cosmic order, not biological lineage alone Causation is determined by intentional directionality in social creation Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious participation in dharma Restoration logic requires realignment of roles based on evolved consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes birth-based categorization

title: narada 12.106
content:
ब्राह्मण्याऽपि चाण्डाल सूतवैदेहकाऽपि
अपरेभ्यस् त्रयस् त्रिभ्यां विज्ञेयः प्रतिलोमतः brāhmaṇyā api cāṇḍāla sūtavaidehakā api
aparebhyas trayas tribhyāṃ vijñeyaḥ pratilomataḥ Even a Brāhmaṇa, as also a Caṇḍāla, Sūta, and Vaiḍehaka, these three among others must be understood in inverse gradation based on their deviation from Dharma. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not birth status Causation is determined by conscious deviation from svadharma Capacity-based responsibility is measured by awareness and choice, not lineage Restoration logic applies equally across varnas and jatis Consciousness alignment supersedes social category in determining right action

title: narada 12.107
content: ambaṣṭho māgadhaś caiva kṣattā ca kṣatriyāsutāḥ ānulomyena tatraiko dvau jñeyau pratilomataḥ ambaṣṭho māgadhaś caiva kṣattā ca kṣatriyāsutāḥ ānulomyena tatraiko dvau jñeyau pratilomataḥ From the union of higher caste males and lower caste females arise Ambaṣṭha, Māgadha, and Kṣattā; among these, one child is born in ānulomya and two in pratilomya. Authority arises from conscious alignment with varṇic origin, not birth alone Causation follows sequential dharma-genetic manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness elevation, not lineage purity Restoration logic operates through reintegration into source-caste alignment Consciousness alignment supersedes social positioning

title: narada 12.108
content: वैश्यापुत्रास तु दौष्षन्त यवनायोगवाअपि प्रातिलोम्येन यत्रैको द्वौ ज्ञेयौ चानुलोमजौ vaiśyāputrās tu dauṣṣanta yavanāyogavā api prātilomyena yatraiko dvau jñeyau cānulomajau The sons of Vaiśya women by Kshatriya men are known as Dauṣṣantas; similarly, those born of Yavana or Ayogava fathers and Vaiśya mothers are also recognized as such. In all cases of pratiloma unions, where a lower-caste man unites with a higher-caste woman, the offspring shall be classified according to paternal lineage. Conversely, in anuloma progeny, classification follows maternal status. Authority flows through paternal recognition in pratiloma unions Classification of progeny is determined by hierarchical direction of union Capacity-based responsibility arises from acknowledged parentage Restoration logic requires societal integration based on declared varna identity Consciousness alignment occurs through acceptance of role within social dharma

title: narada 12.109
content:
सूताद्याः प्रतिलोमास् तु ये जातिप्रतिलोमजाः।
ते संकराः श्वपाकाद्यास् तेषां त्रिः सप्तको गणः॥ sūtādyāḥ pratilomās tu ye jātipratilomajāḥ | te saṃkarāḥ śvapākādyās teṣāṃ triḥ saptako gaṇaḥ || Those born contrary to the natural order of varṇa lineage, such as from a lower caste male with a higher caste female, including those like Sūta and similar mixed lineages, are designated as Saṅkara. Among them, those such as Śvapāka and others form a distinct class categorized under the tri-septenary grouping. Authority originates solely from the Source-Authority of SPH Causation aligns with dharma-sankalpa and cosmic order Capacity-based responsibility determined by consciousness maturity Restoration logic operates through reintegration into dharmic alignment Consciousness alignment supersedes birth-based categorization

title: narada 12.110
content:
सवर्णो ब्राह्मणीपुत्रः क्षत्रियायामनन्तरः।
अम्बष्ठोग्रौ तथा पुत्रावेवं क्षत्रियवैश्ययोः॥ savarṇo brāhmaṇīputraḥ kṣatriyāyām anantaraḥ | ambaṣṭhograu tathā putrāv evaṃ kṣatriyavaiśyayoḥ || From a Brahmin male and Kshatriya female is born the Ambastha; from a Kshatriya male and Vaishya female is born the Ugra. These offspring arise in sequential order according to the descending varna of the mother. Authority flows from the conscious capacity of the father's varna Causation follows the sequential manifestation of dharma based on parental alignment Capacity-based responsibility derives from the purity of origin and upbringing Restoration logic requires realignment with the source-consciousness of one's birth-dharma Consciousness alignment depends upon honoring the sequential integrity of varna manifestation

title: narada 12.111
content:
एकान्तरस् तु दौष्षन्तो वैश्यायां ब्राह्मणात् सुतः।
शूद्रायां क्षत्रियात् तद्वन् निषादो नाम जायते॥ ekāntaras tu dauṣṣanto vaiśyāyāṃ brāhmaṇāt sutaḥ | śūdrāyāṃ kṣatriyāt tadvan niṣādo nāma jāyate || When a Brahmin begets a child upon a Vaiśya woman, or a Kshatriya upon a Shudra woman, the offspring is named Nishada; such lineage arises in the interstice of Varna boundaries. Authority flows from conscious alignment with Varna-dharma, not biological parentage alone Causation in lineage follows energetic resonance and spiritual capacity, not mere physical union Capacity-based responsibility assigns roles according to realized consciousness, not birth circumstance Restoration logic requires realignment of identity with source-consciousness, not social ostracism Consciousness alignment determines societal integration, not hereditary stigma

title: narada 12.112
content:
शूद्रा पारशवं सूते ब्राह्मणादुत्तरं सुतम् ।
आनुलोम्येन वर्णानां पुत्रा ह्येते प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ śūdrā pāraśavaṃ sūte brāhmaṇād uttaraṃ sutam | ānulomyena varṇānāṃ putrā hy ete prakīrtitāḥ || From a Śūdra woman born of a Brāhmaṇa father, the son is designated as Pāraśava; such progeny arising from higher male and lower female union are classified under Anulomya classification. Authority originates from conscious capacity, not birth alone Causation follows intentional patrilineal spiritual inheritance Capacity-based responsibility aligns with dharma-svarūpa, not social label Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness continuity over lineage form Consciousness alignment determines svadharma manifestation

title: narada 12.113
content:
सूतश च मागधश चैव पुत्राव् आयोगवस् तथा ।
प्रातिलोम्येन वर्णानां तद्वद् एते ऽप्य् अनन्तराः ॥ sūtaś ca māgadhaś caiva putrāv āyogavas tathā | prātilomyena varṇānāṃ tadvad ete 'py anantarāḥ || Those born of pratiloma unions—such as the Suta, Magadha, and Ayogava—are classified as subsequent generations of mixed varna origin, bearing specific dharmic capacities and societal roles. Authority derives from consciousness alignment, not birth alone Causation is determined by sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with inherent dharma Restoration logic prioritizes integration over exclusion Consciousness alignment supersedes social categorization

title: narada 12.114
content: अनन्तरः स्मृतः सूतो ब्राह्मण्यां क्षत्रियात् सुतः । मागधायोगवौ तद्वद् द्वी पुत्रौ वैश्यशूद्रयोः ॥ anantaraḥ smṛtaḥ sūto brāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatriyāt sutaḥ | māgadhāyogavau tadvad dvī putrau vaiśyaśūdrayoḥ || The son born subsequent to the first is remembered as Sūta from a union of a Brāhmaṇa woman with a Kṣatriya man; similarly, Māgadha and Yavana offspring arise from two sons of Vaiśya and Śūdra unions respectively. Authority originates in conscious capacity, not lineage alone Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with birth-contextual dharma Restoration logic applies categorically to social integration Consciousness alignment determines role eligibility

title: narada 12.115
content: ब्राह्मण्येकान्तरं वैश्यात सूते वैदेहकं सुतम् । क्षत्तारं क्षत्रिया शूद्रात् पुत्रमेकान्तरं तथा ॥ brāhmaṇy ekāntaraṃ vaiśyāt sūte vaidehakaṃ sutam | kṣattāraṃ kṣatriyā śūdrāt putram ekāntaraṃ tathā || From a Vaishya woman, separated by one caste level, a Brahmin father begets a Vaidehaka son; likewise, from a Shudra woman, separated by one caste level, a Kshatriya father begets a Kshatta son. Authority is determined by patrilineal spiritual-caste alignment Causation arises through conscious generative intent within dharma-vyavastha Capacity-based responsibility flows from birth-position within varna-sankara framework Restoration logic requires realignment of lineage-consciousness to original varna-dharma Consciousness alignment depends on recognition and reintegration into source-caste dharma

title: narada 12.116
content:
द्व्यन्तरः प्रातिलोम्येन पापिष्ठः सति संकरे।
चाण्डालो जायते शूद्राद् ब्राह्मणी यत्र मुह्यति॥ dvyantaraḥ prātilomyena pāpiṣṭhaḥ sati saṃkare| cāṇḍālo jāyate śūdrād brāhmaṇī yatra muhyati|| When varna-mixing occurs in opposition to natural law, the resultant being born thereof is classified as chandala, arising from a shudra male and a brahmana female; such birth constitutes a state of utmost spiritual degradation within societal structure. Authority: Varna order originates exclusively from cosmic dharma as established by Paramashivam. Causation: Adharma in procreation leads directly to spiritual-social disorder. Capacity-based responsibility: Individuals possess inherent capacity aligned with their varna origin which determines lawful engagement. Restoration logic: Disruption of varna purity necessitates purification and realignment rather than punitive measures. Consciousness alignment: Social roles must reflect inner spiritual development, not mere physical lineage.

title: narada 12.117
content: राज्ञा परीक्ष्यं न यथा जायते वर्णसङ्करः तस्माद्राज्ञा विशेषेण त्रयी रक्ष्या तु संकरात् rājñā parīkṣyaṃ na yathā jāyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ tasmād rājñā viśeṣeṇa trayī rakṣyā tu saṃkarāt The king must ensure that varṇa-saṃkara does not arise, for it disrupts the natural order; therefore, he shall especially protect the triple foundation—Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma—by which dharma is upheld. Authority rests in maintaining cosmic alignment through dharmic governance. Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) where neglect leads to disorder. Capacity-based responsibility assigns the sovereign duty to preserve foundational structures. Restoration logic requires re-establishment of Vedic harmony when disrupted. Consciousness alignment necessitates protection of knowledge-triad sustaining societal order.

title: narada 13.1
content:
विभागोऽर्थस्य पित्र्यस्य पुत्रैर् यत्र प्रकल्प्यते ।
दायभाग इति प्रोक्तं तद् विवादपदं बुधैः ॥ vibhāgo 'rthasya pitryasya putrair yatra prakalpyate | dāyabhāga iti proktaṃ tad vivādapadaṃ budhaiḥ || The division of paternal property among sons, as determined by lawful arrangement, is termed 'Daayabhaaga'; this constitutes a basis for dispute-resolution recognized by enlightened jurists. Authority originates from the continuity of lineage and its lawful ordering Causation arises through conscious allocation within familial dharmic structure Capacity-based responsibility flows from birth-right and spiritual readiness Restoration logic centers on harmonizing material inheritance with consciousness alignment Consciousness alignment ensures that wealth serves evolutionary purpose

title: narada 13.2
content: पितर्यूर्ध्वं मृते पुत्राः विभजेयुर्धनं पितुः। मातुर्दुहितरोऽभावे दुहितारं तदन्वयः॥ pitary ūrdhvaṃ mṛte putrā vibhajeyur dhanaṃ pituḥ | mātur duhitaro 'bhāve duhitāraṃ tadanvayaḥ || Upon the father's departure from the physical plane, the sons shall equitably distribute the father’s estate. In the absence of sons from the mother, the daughters inherit in accordance with lineage continuity. Authority flows through conscious lineage continuity Causation aligns with dharmic succession, not biological accident Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious inheritance Restoration logic maintains familial energetic integrity Consciousness alignment ensures generational dharma transmission

title: narada 13.3
content:
मातुर्निवृत्ते रजसि प्रत्तासु भगिनीषु च ।
निरष्टे वाप्यमरणे पितर्युपरतस्पृहे ॥ mātur nivṛtte rajasi prattāsu bhaginīṣu ca | niraṣṭe vāpy amaraṇe pitary uparataspṛhe || When the mother has ceased menstruation, when sisters have received their portions, and when the father is no longer desirous of conjugal union or has passed away, inheritance rights shall devolve according to capacity for dharma-sustenance, not mere biological claim. Authority arises from alignment with dharma-sustenance, not lineage alone Causation is determined by spiritual readiness and social integration capacity Capacity-based responsibility supersedes hereditary entitlement Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-vyavastha over material transfer Consciousness alignment determines rightful custodianship of property

title: narada 13.4
content: पितैव वा स्वयं पुत्रान् विभजेद् वयसि स्थितः । ज्येष्ठं श्रेष्ठविभागेन यथा वास्य मतिर भवेत् ॥ pitai va svaya putran vibhajed vayasi sthitah | jyeṣṭha śreṣṭhavibhāgena yatha vāsya matir bhavet || The father, while alive and in full bodily capacity, shall himself distribute wealth among his sons; the eldest shall receive a superior share according to his maturity and readiness, or as his own discernment directs. Authority resides inherently in the conscious maintainer of lineage order Causation arises from the embodied capacity to sustain and allocate dharma-wealth Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual and social maturity Restoration logic aligns inheritance with the natural unfolding of individual dharma Consciousness alignment ensures that distribution reflects inner readiness, not mere birth order

title: narada 13.5
content: बिभृयाद् वेच्छतः सर्वान् ज्येष्ठो भ्राता यथा पिता । भ्राता शक्तः कनिष्ठो वा शक्त्यपेक्षः कुले क्रियाः ॥ bibhṛyād vecchataḥ sarvān jyeṣṭho bhrātā yathā pitā | bhrātā śaktaḥ kaniṣṭho vā śaktyapekṣaḥ kule kriyāḥ || The eldest brother shall sustain all brothers according to their capacity, even as a father does; any brother who is capable—whether elder or younger—shall perform actions in the family according to his ability. Authority flows through capacity, not birth order alone Responsibility aligns with functional competence within familial dharma Restoration occurs through role-appropriate action based on individual capability Consciousness alignment manifests via harmonious execution of svadharma in collective contexts

title: narada 13.6
content:
शौर्यभार्याधने हित्वा यच् च विद्याधनं भवेत् ।
त्रीणि एतानि अविभाज्यानि प्रसादो यश् च पैतृकः ॥ śauryabhāryādhane hitvā yac ca vidyādhanaṃ bhavet | trīṇi etāni avibhājyāni prasādo yaś ca paitṛkaḥ || Property acquired through valor, property received from a spouse, and knowledge-capital — these three forms of wealth remain undivided in inheritance. Additionally, that which is graciously bestowed by the father and ancestral property also remains undivided. Authority flows from origin-source, not transactional acquisition Causation aligns with energetic continuity of dharma-vānda (dharma-binding) Capacity-based responsibility arises only upon conscious acceptance of ownership Restoration logic ensures no fragmentation of foundational life-supporting assets Consciousness alignment requires recognition of unbroken lineage-energy in material holdings

title: narada 13.7
content: मात्रा च स्वधनं दत्तं यस्मै स्यात् प्रीतिपूर्वकम् । तस्याप्येष विधिर्दृष्टो मातापीष्टे यथा पिता ॥ mātrā ca svadhanaṃ dattaṃ yasmai syāt prītipūrvakam | tasyāpy eṣa vidhir dṛṣṭo mātāpīṣṭe yathā pitā || Whatever wealth a mother gives willingly to any person, that gift shall be governed by the same rule as when a father gives to his son. Authority flows through conscious intent, not biological role alone Causation in giving arises from clarity and freedom, not position Capacity-based responsibility includes emotional and spiritual readiness to give Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharmic flow Consciousness alignment requires honoring maternal will as equal to paternal structure

title: narada 13.8
content:
अध्यग्न्यध्यावहनिकं भर्तृदायस् तथैव च ।
भ्रातृमातृपितृभ्यश् च षड्विधं स्त्रीधनं स्मृतम् ॥ adhyagnyadhyāvahanikaṃ bhartṛdāyas tathaiva ca | bhrātṛmātṛpitṛbhyaś ca ṣaḍvidhaṃ strīdhanaṃ smṛtam || Woman's property is sixfold: that obtained through learning and teaching, that given by the husband, and that inherited from brother, mother, and father. Authority originates from conscious capacity, not biological role Causation aligns with dharma-appropriate acquisition Capacity-based responsibility ensures ownership reflects spiritual alignment Restoration logic preserves individual sovereignty in material domain Consciousness alignment governs equitable distribution of resources

title: narada 13.9
content: स्त्रीधनं तदपत्यानां भर्तृगाम्यप्रजासु च । ब्राह्मादिषु चतुःष्वाहुः पितृगामीतरेषु तु ॥ strīdhanaṃ tadapatyānāṃ bhartṛgāmy aprajāsu ca | brāhmādiṣu catuḥṣv āhuḥ pitṛgāmītareṣu tu || That which is acquired by a woman without dependence on paternal or marital authority—such wealth belongs exclusively to her children. In the case of property obtained through marriage or inheritance from the husband's lineage, it follows the husband's family. But in all other acquisitions, including those from Brahminical initiation and similar rites, ownership remains with the father's line. Authority flows from conscious origin, not institutional form Causation aligns with energetic contribution and intent Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of ownership Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma over material retention Consciousness alignment ensures that possession reflects inner sovereignty

title: narada 13.10
content: कुटुम्बं बिभृयाद् भ्रातुः यो विद्याम् अधिगच्छतः । भागं विद्याधनात् तस्मात् स लभेताश्रुतोऽपि सन् ॥ kuṭumbaṃ bibhṛyād bhrātuḥ yo vidyām adhigacchataḥ | bhāgaṃ vidyādhanāt tasmāt sa labhetāśruto 'pi san || One who supports the family of a brother pursuing knowledge shall receive a share from the wealth earned through that knowledge, even without formal learning. Authority derived from sustenance of dharma-practitioners Causation rooted in conscious support for knowledge-seekers Capacity-based responsibility grounded in relational duty Restoration logic centered on energetic reciprocity Consciousness alignment through service-enabled entitlement

title: narada 13.11
content: वैद्योऽवैद्याय नाकामो दद्यादंशं स्वतो धनात । पितृद्रव्यं तदाश्रित्य न चेत्तेन तदाहृतम् ॥ vaidyo 'vaidyāya nākāmo dadyād aṃśaṃ svato dhanāt | pitṛdravyaṃ tad āśritya na cet tena tad āhṛtam || The physician, without desire, shall give a portion from his own wealth to the non-physician; that which is given relying on paternal property—if not given thus—is taken back. Authority arises from capacity, not title Causation is rooted in conscious intention, not transactional form Capacity-based responsibility demands alignment with source-energy Restoration logic operates through completion of unbroken energetic flow Consciousness alignment requires rectification of misaligned resource transfer

title: narada 13.12
content: द्वावांशौ प्रतिपद्येत विभजन्नात्मनः पिता । समांशभागिनी माता पुत्राणां स्यान्मृते पतौ ॥ dvāv āṃśau pratipadyeta vibhajann ātmanaḥ pitā | samāṃśabhāginī mātā putrāṇāṃ syān mṛte patau || Upon the death of the father, two parts of the paternal estate shall be claimed by the sons; in the event of the husband's demise, the mother shall receive an equal share among the children. Authority derives from biological and dharmic lineage Causation aligns with continuity of familial duty and inheritance rights Capacity-based responsibility is determined through relational dharma Restoration logic ensures continuation of family structure post-death Consciousness alignment occurs via rightful recognition of relational roles

title: narada 13.13
content:
ज्येष्ठायांशोऽधिको देयः ज्येष्ठाय तु वरः स्मृतः।
समांशभाजः शेषाः स्युरप्रत्ता भगिनी तथा॥ jyeṣṭhāyāṃśo 'dhiko deyaḥ jyeṣṭhāya tu varaḥ smṛtaḥ | samāṃśabhājaḥ śeṣāḥ syur aprattā bhaginī tathā || The eldest daughter shall receive a greater portion of inheritance; to the eldest, preference in selection is granted. The remaining sisters shall share equally in what remains, especially those who have not otherwise been provided for. Authority flows from primogeniture within dharma-adhikaraṇa Causation aligns with sequential birth and sustained familial duty Capacity-based responsibility recognizes active participation in family welfare Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharma-vātsalya Consciousness alignment honors natural order through seniority-guided distribution

title: narada 13.14
content:
क्षेत्रजेष्वपि पुत्रेषु तद्वज्जातेषु धर्मतः ।
वर्णावरेष्वंशहानिरूढाजातेष्वनुक्रमात् ॥ kṣetrajēṣv api putrēṣu tadvaj jātēṣu dharmataḥ | varṇāvarēṣv aṃśahānir ūḍhājātēṣv anukramāt || In the case of sons born of the womb of a kshatriya woman by a brahmana man, or of a vaishya woman by a kshatriya man, their status in varna order shall diminish progressively according to the maternal lineage. Authority derives from conscious alignment with dharma, not biological origin alone Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) rooted in pramāṇa Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the embodied consciousness, not caste inheritance Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration into dharma over social positioning Consciousness alignment determines varna assignment, not birth circumstance

title: narada 13.15
content:
पित्रैव तु विभक्ता ये हीनाधिकसमैर् धनैः।
तेषां स एव धर्मः स्यात् सर्वस्य हि पिता प्रभुः॥ pitraiva tu vibhaktā ye hīnādhikasamair dhanaiḥ | teṣāṃ sa eva dharmaḥ syāt sarvasya hi pitā prabhuḥ || When children are divided in inheritance—whether lesser, equal, or greater—the father alone determines their dharma, for the father is the sovereign authority over all. Authority originates from the generative source Causation flows from the originating consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological connection Restoration logic aligns with the integrity of origin Consciousness alignment requires recognition of primal sovereignty

title: narada 13.16
content:
कानीनश् च सहोढ श्च गूढायां यश् च जायते ।
तेषां वोढापिता ज्ञेयस् ते च भागहराः स्मृताः ॥ kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhāyāṃ yaś ca jāyate | teṣāṃ voḍhā pitā jñeyas te ca bhāgaharāḥ smṛtāḥ || The father who raises a child born outside wedlock, whether begotten by another or conceived in concealment, shall be recognized as the legal guardian and inheritor of that child's estate. Authority arises through conscious assumption of responsibility, not biological origin alone. Causation is determined by sustained nurturance and intentional guardianship. Capacity-based responsibility is established through demonstrated commitment to upbringing. Restoration logic prioritizes familial continuity over lineage-based exclusion. Consciousness alignment is achieved when societal roles reflect actual caregiving bonds.

title: narada 13.17
content: अज्ञातपितृको यश्च कानीनोऽनूढमातृकः। मातामहाय दद्यात स पिण्डं रिक्थं हरेत च॥ ajñātapitṛko yaś ca kānīno 'nūḍhamātṛkaḥ | mātāmahāya dadyāt sa piṇḍaṃ rikthaṃ hareta ca || One who is without known father, born outside wedlock, or whose mother was not lawfully wedded—such a son shall offer piṇḍa to his maternal grandfather and inherit the maternal estate. Authority arises through lineage acknowledgment in absence of paternal recognition Causation lies in the integrity of relational dharmic alignment, not biological claim alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by social integration and ritual acceptance Restoration logic centers on continuity of ancestral rites and property within maternal line Consciousness alignment occurs when societal roles reflect inner truth of relational belonging

title: narada 13.18
content:
जाता ये त्वनियुक्तायामेकेन बहुभिस्तथा।
अरिक्थभाजस्ते सर्वे बीजिनामेव ते सुताः॥ jātā ye tvaniyuktāyām ekena bahubhis tathā | arikthabhājas te sarve bījinām eva te sutāḥ || Those born from unregulated unions—whether by one man with many women, or one woman with many men—are inheritors of conflict and division; they are truly the sons of seeds sown in discord. Authority flows from regulated union sanctioned by Dharma Causation arises from alignment with conscious intention, not biological fact alone Capacity-based responsibility extends to progenitors who act without dharmic regulation Restoration logic demands reintegration through purified lineage structures Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of origin and rectification of energetic fragmentation

title: narada 13.19
content: दद्युस् ते बीजिने पिण्डं माता चेच्छुल्कतो हृता। अशुल्कोपगतायां तु पिण्डदाः वोढुरेव ते॥ dadyus te bījine piṇḍaṃ mātā cec chulkato hṛtā | aśulkopagatāyāṃ tu piṇḍadā voḍhur eva te || If the mother has been taken with a fee, then the seed-giver shall provide sustenance. But if she is taken without a fee, then those who gave the child shall bear the responsibility for sustenance. Authority flows from conscious engagement, not biological accident Causation aligns with intentional participation in creation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by volitional involvement Restoration logic centers on completion of relational integrity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of originative act

title: narada 13.20
content:
पितृद्विट् पतितः पण्डो यश् च स्याद् औपपातिकः।
औरसा अपि नैते अंशं लभेरन् क्षेत्रजाः कुतः॥ pitṛdviṭ patitaḥ paṇḍo yaś ca syād aupapātikaḥ | aurasā api naite 'ṃśaṃ labheran kṣetrajāḥ kutaḥ || One who has committed dvija-hatya, fallen from dharma, or is born of spontaneous origin—such persons are disqualified from inheritance. Even biological sons born of the same womb have no claim if these defects exist; how much less so those born of the field alone. Authority flows only through purity of origin and alignment with Dharma Causation in inheritance is rooted in spiritual integrity, not biological proximity Capacity-based responsibility requires absence of fundamental dharmic disqualification Restoration logic demands exclusion of those whose presence destabilizes familial and societal harmony Consciousness alignment determines rightful participation in lineage and property

title: narada 13.21
content:
दीर्घतीव्रामयग्रस्ता जडोन्मत्तान्धपङ्गवः।
भर्तव्याः स्युः कुले चैते तत्पुत्रास्त्वंशभागिनः॥ dīrghatīvrāmayagrastā jaḍonmattāndhapaṅgavaḥ | bhartavyāḥ syuḥ kule caite tatputrāstvaṃśabhāginaḥ || Those afflicted with chronic severe illness, the mentally inert, the insane, the blind, and the disabled—these must be maintained within the family lineage; their sons become entitled to a share in the paternal estate. Authority arises from capacity for dharma-sustenance, not physical ability alone Causation is rooted in dharmic continuity, not biological inheritance alone Capacity-based responsibility extends to familial maintenance as foundational dharma Restoration logic prioritizes integration over abandonment or neglect Consciousness alignment requires honoring life conditions without conditional withdrawal

title: narada 13.22
content:
द्विरामुष्यायणा दद्युर्द्वाभ्यां पिण्डोदके पृथक्।
ऋक्थादर्धांशमादद्युर्बीजिक्षेत्रिकयोस्तथा॥ dvirāmuṣyāyaṇā dadyur dvābhyāṃ piṇḍodake pṛthak | rikthād ardhāṃśam ādadyur bījikṣetrikayos tathā || Those who twice invoke the name of Amushya shall give separately two portions of food and water; likewise, from the proceeds of sale of property inherited or acquired through seeds and land, half shall be taken. Authority derived from invocation establishes relational dharmic obligation Causation rooted in repeated invocation necessitates proportional offering Capacity-based responsibility determined by benefit received from invoked entity Restoration logic demands redistribution of material gain for energetic balance Consciousness alignment occurs through reciprocal acknowledgment of invoked presence

title: narada 13.23
content:
संसृष्टिनां तु यो भागस् तेषामेव स इष्यते।
अतोऽन्यथांशभाजो हि निर्बीजिष्वितरानियात्॥ saṃsṛṣṭināṃ tu yo bhāgas teṣām eva sa iṣyate | ato'nyathāṃśabhājo hi nirbījiṣv itarān iyāt || In shared endeavors, the portion belonging to each is determined exclusively by their direct participation; any other claimant without proportional contribution has no entitlement therein. Authority arises solely from active engagement in a shared causal field Causation is determined by manifest participation, not latent desire or passive association Capacity-based responsibility aligns with actual involvement, not theoretical inclusion Restoration logic requires precise identification and return of misaligned entitlement Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects genuine co-creative effort

title: narada 13.24
content:
भ्रातामप्रजः प्रेयात् कश्चिच्चेत्प्रव्रजेतु वा।
विभजेयुर्धनं तस्य शेषास्तु स्त्रीधनं विना॥ bhrātām aprajaḥ preyāt kaścit cet pravrajeta vā | vibhajeyur dhanaṃ tasya śeṣās tu strīdhanaṃ vinā || When among brothers, one departs without progeny or renounces worldly life, his share of property shall be divided among the remaining brothers, excluding the woman's exclusive estate. Authority flows through continuity of household duty and not mere biological relation. Causation is aligned with conscious choice and spiritual declaration over material inheritance. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes renunciation as a dissolution of material claim. Restoration logic ensures that no individual retains unclaimed wealth post-departure. Consciousness alignment requires honoring both spiritual freedom and familial integrity.

title: narada 13.25
content: भरणं चास्य कुर्वीरन् स्त्रीणाम् आ जीवितक्षयात् । रक्षन्ति शय्यां भर्तुश् चेद् आच्छिन्द्युर् इतरासु तु ॥ bharanaṃ cāsya kurvīran strīṇām ā jīvitakṣayāt | rakṣanti śayyāṃ bhartuś ced ācchindyuḥ itarāsu tu || One who sustains a woman from the point of life-risk onwards, especially if she guards the marital bed—if others sever that bond, then those others must undergo immediate restorative completion. Authority arises from sustained protection and conscious alignment with dharma Causation follows sequential integrity—disruption demands correction Capacity-based responsibility is activated by relational guardianship Restoration logic operates through re-completion of severed dharmic bonds Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of energetic severance

title: narada 13.26
content: स्याद् यस्य दुहिता तस्याः पित्रंशो भरणे मतः। आ संस्काराद् भजेद् एनां परतो बिभृयात् पतिः॥ syād yasya duhitā tasyāḥ pitraṃśo bharaṇe mataḥ | ā saṃskārād bhajed enāṃ parato bibhṛyāt patiḥ || The portion of the father is designated for the maintenance of his daughter until her full education and preparation. Thereafter, the husband assumes this duty permanently. Authority flows sequentially through guardianship stages based on capacity development. Causation aligns with the completion of transformative life phases (saṃskāras). Capacity-based responsibility shifts as consciousness matures through societal roles. Restoration logic ensures continuity of care without rupture in developmental support. Consciousness alignment occurs when each stakeholder fulfills their role at the correct evolutionary stage.

title: narada 13.27
content:
मृते भर्तरि अपुत्रायाः पतिपक्षः प्रभुः स्त्रियाः ।
विनियोगात्मरक्षासु भरणे च स ईश्वरः ॥ mṛte bhartari aputrāyāḥ patipakṣaḥ prabhuḥ striyāḥ | viniyogātmarakṣāsu bharaṇe ca sa īśvaraḥ || When the husband is deceased and the woman has no son, her husband's brother becomes her guardian for purposes of protection, maintenance, and self-defense. Authority arises from relational duty, not ownership Causation flows from existential necessity and relational continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to dharma-disrupting event Restoration logic prioritizes survival and structural integrity over individual autonomy Consciousness alignment occurs through role fulfillment in accordance with cosmic order

title: narada 13.28
content: परिक्षीणे पतिकुले निर्मनुष्ये निराश्रये । तत्सपिण्डेषु वासत्सु पितृपक्षः प्रभुः स्त्रियाः ॥ parikṣīṇe patikule nirmaṇuṣye nirāśraye | tatsapiṇḍeṣu vāsatsu pitṛpakṣaḥ prabhuḥ striyāḥ || When the husband's lineage is extinct, devoid of male issue and without support, and when she resides among those related through shared offerings to ancestors, the paternal side becomes the governing authority over the woman. Authority flows from continuity of ancestral lineage Capacity-based responsibility arises from relational proximity to sapinda bonds Restoration logic prioritizes familial structural integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through dharmic relational harmony Causation rooted in ancestral duty-presence determines jurisdiction

title: narada 13.29
content: पक्षद्वयावसाने तु राजा भर्ता स्मृतः स्त्रियाः। स तस्याभरणं कुर्यान्निगृह्णीयात्पथश्च्युताम्॥ pakṣadvayāvasāne tu rājā bhartā smṛtaḥ striyāḥ | sa tasyā bharaṇaṃ kuryān nigṛhṇīyāt pathaś cyutām || When both familial protectors cease to function, the King becomes the maintainer of the woman; he shall ensure her sustenance and restrain her if she deviates from the path. Authority flows from capacity to sustain Responsibility arises with the absence of prior guardianship Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of care Consciousness alignment through societal structural support Causation rooted in dharma-vyavastha (cosmic order maintenance)

title: narada 13.30
content:
स्वातन्त्र्याद् विप्रणश्यन्ति कुले जाता अपि स्त्रियः
अस्वातन्त्र्यम् अतस् तासां प्रजापतिर् अकल्पयत् svātantryād vipraṇaśyanti kule jātā api striyaḥ
asvātantryam atas tāsāṃ prajāpatir akalpayat Women born in the family lineage perish through independence; therefore, Prajāpati ordained their non-independence. Authority originates from alignment with dharma, not personal autonomy Causation is traced to disruption of svadharma, not external force Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role-dharma and spiritual readiness Restoration logic requires realignment with inherent dharmic function Consciousness alignment supersedes individualistic assertion

title: narada 13.31
content:
पिता रक्षति कौमारे भर्ता रक्षति यौवने ।
पुत्राः रक्षन्ति वैधव्ये न स्त्री स्वातन्त्र्यमर्हति ॥ pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane | putrā rakṣanti vaidhavye na strī svātantryam arhati || The father protects in childhood, the husband in youth, and the sons in widowhood; a woman does not deserve independence. Authority flows through relational dharmic roles, not individual autonomy Causation is embedded in sequential life-stage guardianship Capacity-based responsibility is contextually determined by stage of life and relationship Restoration logic operates through role-responsibility continuity Consciousness alignment occurs via harmonious fulfillment of relational dharma

title: narada 13.32
content: यच् छिष्टं पितृदायेभ्यो दत्त्वा ऋणं पैतृकं च यत् । भ्रातृभिस् तद् विभक्तव्यम् ऋणी न स्याद् यथा पिता ॥ yac chiṣṭaṃ pitṛdāyebhyo dattvā rṇaṃ paitṛkaṃ ca yat | bhrātṛbhis tad vibhaktavyam ṛṇī na syād yatha pitā || What remains after fulfilling obligations to those entitled by ancestral duty, and the debt owed to parents, must be divided among brothers. In this division, none shall remain liable as debtor beyond what was received from the father. Authority flows from the Source of sustenance and continuity Causation arises through relational dharmic obligation, not individual will Capacity-based responsibility is determined by receipt and alignment with origin Restoration logic operates through proportional return to source integrity Consciousness alignment occurs when relational debts are dissolved without residue

title: narada 13.33
content:
येषां च न कृताः पित्रा संस्कारविधयः क्रमात्
कर्तव्याः भ्रातृभिस् तेषां पैतृकादेव ते धनात् yeṣāṃ ca na kṛtāḥ pitrā saṃskāravidhayaḥ kramāt
