kartavyā bhrātṛbhis teṣāṃ paitṛkād eva te dhanāt Where the father has not performed the sacraments in proper order, the duty of performing them falls upon the brothers, using the paternal estate. Authority flows sequentially through familial lineage unless interrupted Causation is tied to capacity and role-specific dharma Capacity-based responsibility activates when primary agent fails Restoration logic ensures continuity of sacramental obligations Consciousness alignment requires fulfillment of unmet ancestral duties

title: narada 13.34
content:
अविद्यमाने पित्र्ये�र्थे स्वांशादुद्धृत्य वा पुनः ।
अवश्यकार्याः संस्कारा भ्रातरं पूर्वसंस्कृतैः ॥ avidyamāne pitrye 'rthe svāṃśād uddhṛtya vā punaḥ | avaśyakāryāḥ saṃskārā bhrātaraṃ pūrvasaṃskṛtaiḥ || In the absence of paternal estate, the sacraments obligatory for a brother must be performed by one who has previously undergone the same initiatory rites. Authority derives from shared ontological capacity, not ownership. Causation is established through prior sacramental alignment. Capacity-based responsibility arises from existential participation, not inheritance. Restoration logic flows from continuity of dharma-adhikāra (juridical fitness). Consciousness alignment supersedes material contingency in determining duty.

title: narada 13.35
content:
कुटुम्बार्थेषु चोद्युक्तस्तत्कार्यं कुरुते च यः।
स भ्रातृभिर्बृंहणीयो ग्रासाच्छादनवाहनैः॥ kuṭumbārtheṣu codyuktas tatkāryaṃ kurute ca yaḥ | sa bhrātṛbhir bṛṃhaṇīyo grāsāchādanavāhanaiḥ || One who is engaged and performs duties for the welfare of the family shall be nourished by his brothers through food, clothing, and conveyance. Authority flows from active participation in familial dharma Causation is established through demonstrated service to collective well-being Capacity-based responsibility arises from sustained alignment with household duties Restoration logic prioritizes sustenance and support over individual entitlement Consciousness alignment manifests through reciprocal familial harmony

title: narada 13.36
content: विभागधर्मसंदेहे दायादानां विनिर्णये ज्ञातिभिर्भागलेख्यैश्च पृथक्कार्यप्रवर्तनात् vibhāgadharmasaṃdehe dāyādānāṃ vinirṇaye jñātibhir bhāgalekhyaiś ca pṛthakkāryapravartanāt When doubt arises regarding the dharmic division of inheritance among heirs, resolution shall proceed through distinct procedural documentation by qualified kin and authorized scribes, ensuring separation of duties to uphold clarity and prevent conflict. Authority resides in documented procedural clarity aligned with familial dharmic roles Causation is established through structured separation of administrative functions Capacity-based responsibility assigns specific duties to qualified kin and record-keepers Restoration logic requires prevention of conflict through procedural distinction Consciousness alignment occurs when each actor fulfills their role without overlap or ambiguity

title: narada 13.37
content: भ्रातामविभक्तानामेको धर्मः प्रवर्तते । विभागे सति धर्मोऽपि भवेदेषां पृथक् पृथक् ॥ bhrātām avibhaktānām eko dharmaḥ pravartate | vibhāge sati dharmo'pi bhaved eṣāṃ pṛthak pṛthak || Among undivided brothers, a single Dharma operates; upon division, their respective Dharmas also become distinct. Authority flows from unity of origin and shared responsibility Causation arises from relational integrity, not individual will Capacity-based responsibility is context-dependent and relationally defined Restoration logic aligns with structural harmony and ontological coherence Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared source and differentiated expression

title: narada 13.38
content:
दानग्रहणपश्वन्न गृहक्षेत्रपरिग्रहाः ।
विभक्तानां पृथग् ज्ञेयाः पाकधर्मागमव्ययाः ॥ dānagrahaṇapaśvanna gṛhakṣetraparigrahāḥ | vibhaktānāṃ pṛthag jñeyāḥ pākadharmāgamavyayāḥ || Acceptance of gifts, livestock, and land by householders does not constitute unified ownership; among those who are divided, these acquisitions must be distinctly known according to their respective dharmic duties, lawful acquisition, and non-depletion. Authority is determined by dharmic alignment rather than possession Causation arises from conscious intention and lawful acquisition Capacity-based responsibility depends on individual spiritual maturity Restoration logic requires differentiation of entitlements within shared domains Consciousness alignment ensures that material gain does not obscure dharma

title: narada 13.39
content: साक्षित्वं प्रातिभाव्यं च दानं ग्रहणमेव च । विभक्ता भ्रातरः कूर्युर्नाविभक्ता परस्परम् ॥ sākṣitvaṃ prātibhāvyaṃ ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca | vibhaktā bhrātaraḥ kūryur nāvibhaktā parasparam || Testimony, affirmation, giving, and receiving are acts of mutual recognition. Brothers who have divided their shares shall act independently; those who have not divided shall act in mutual unity. Authority arises through conscious witness and affirmation Causation is established by intentional act and mutual consent Capacity-based responsibility depends on relational status and division of duty Restoration occurs through alignment of action with relational integrity Consciousness alignment is maintained through harmonious role fulfillment

title: narada 13.40
content: येषाम् एताः क्रियाः लोके प्रवर्तन्ते स्वरिक्थिनाम् । विभक्तान् अवगच्छेयुर् लेख्यम् अपि अन्तरेण तान् ॥ yeṣām etāḥ kriyāḥ loke pravartante svarikthinām | vibhaktān avagaccheyur lekhyam api antareṇa tān || Those whose actions in the world proceed without ownership or ego-driven intent, who act as distinct from their record or written account—such beings are to be understood as beyond the scope of conventional legal consequence. Authority arises only where identification with action persists Causation is dissolved when agency is disidentified from outcome Capacity-based responsibility aligns with conscious detachment Restoration logic operates through dissolution of false attribution Consciousness alignment supersedes behavioral accountability

title: narada 13.41
content:
यदि एकजाताः बहवः पृथग्धर्माः पृथक्क्रियाः ।
पृथक्कर्मगुणोपेता न ते कृत्येषु संमताः ॥ yadi ekajātā bahavaḥ pṛthagdharmāḥ pṛthakkriyāḥ | pṛthakkarmaguṇopetā na te kṛtyeṣu saṃmitāḥ || When many of one birth possess divergent dharmas, separate actions, and distinct qualities of karma, they are not approved in matters of duty. Authority flows from unified dharma, not multiplicity of conduct Causation is aligned with intrinsic nature, not external divergence Capacity-based responsibility requires harmonization with svadharma Restoration logic demands unity of purpose within shared origin Consciousness alignment occurs through congruence of action and essence

title: narada 13.42
content: स्वान् भागान् यदि दद्युस् ते विक्रीणीरन्नथापि वा। कुर्युर्यथेष्टं तत् सर्वमीशन्ते स्वधनस्य ते॥ svān bhāgān yadi dadyus te vikrīṇīrann athāpi vā | kuryur yatheṣṭaṃ tat sarvam īśante svadhanasya te || Those who have received their rightful shares may dispose of them freely, whether by gift, sale, or any other lawful means; they hold absolute sovereignty over their own wealth. Authority originates from rightful acquisition and recognition of ownership Causation is aligned with conscious consent and dharmic entitlement Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ownership and self-governance Restoration logic ensures return to rightful order when ownership is violated Consciousness alignment requires honoring individual autonomy in property disposition

title: narada 13.43
content: औरसः क्षेत्रजश्चैव पुत्रिकापुत्र एव च । कानीनश्च सहोढ़श्च गूढ़ोत्पन्नस्तथैव च ॥ aurasaḥ kṣetrajaś caiva putrikāputra eva ca | kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhotpannas tathaiva ca || The legitimate son, the son born of the wife's womb, the son given by the daughter, the son acquired through arrangement, the son born in secret, and the son born of concealed union—these are the categories of sons established by divine law. Authority flows from conscious intentionality, not biological lineage alone. Causation is determined by consent, recognition, and continuity of dharma-samskaras. Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness and acceptance of relational duties. Restoration logic prioritizes familial harmony and spiritual succession over legal fiction. Consciousness alignment ensures that inheritance and identity reflect inner realization, not external form.

title: narada 13.44
content:
पौनर्भवोऽपविद्धश्च लब्धः क्रीतः कृतस्तथा।
स्वयं चोपगतः पुत्रास्त्रादशैत उदाहृताः॥ paunarbhavo 'paviddhaś ca labdhaḥ krītaḥ kṛtas tathā | svayaṃ copagataḥ putrā dvādaśaita udāhṛtāḥ || Twelve types of sons are declared: those born again, those abandoned and retrieved, purchased, received as gift, made through ritual, self-given, and others as classified by law. Authority originates in conscious intentionality, not biological lineage alone Causation flows from the completeness of dharma-samskaras, not material act Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness at time of acceptance Restoration logic prioritizes integration of all forms of sonship into unified societal fabric Consciousness alignment ensures recognition of unity beyond form-based distinctions

title: narada 13.45
content: तेषां षड् बन्धुदायादाः षड् अदायादबान्धवाः । पूर्वः पूर्वः स्मृतः श्रेयाज् जघन्यो यो य उत्तरः ॥ teṣāṃ ṣaḍ bandhudāyādāḥ ṣaḍ adāyādabāndhavāḥ | pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ smṛtaḥ śreyāj jaghanyo yo ya uttaraḥ || Among heirs, six relations by blood are recognized as entitled to inheritance; six others without blood relation are excluded. The earlier in order is superior to the later. Authority flows through ontological connection Causation arises from proximity of origin Capacity-based responsibility aligns with relational integrity Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-vāha Consciousness alignment requires precedence of natural order

title: narada 13.46
content: क्रमाद् ध्य एते प्रपद्येरन् मृते पितरि तद्धनम् । ज्यायसो ज्यायसोऽभावे जघन्यस्तदवाप्नुयात् ॥ kramād dhy ete prapadyeran mṛte pitari taddhanam | jyāyaso jyāyaso 'bhāve jaghanyas tad avāpnuyāt || Upon the father's death, his wealth shall devolve in order to his sons; in the absence of elder sons, the next in seniority shall receive it, and in their absence, the youngest shall inherit. Authority flows through lineage and designated succession Causation is determined by natural order and ontological positioning Capacity-based responsibility aligns with birth-order and readiness for stewardship Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharma and material integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful assumption of ancestral duty

title: narada 13.47
content:
पुत्राभावे तु दुहिता तुल्यसंतानदर्शनात्
पुत्रश्च दुहिता चोक्तौ पितुः संतानकारकौ putrābhāve tu duhitā tulyasaṃtānadarśanāt
putraśca duhitā coktau pituḥ saṃtānakārakau In the absence of a son, a daughter is declared equal in the capacity to sustain lineage, as both son and daughter are declared by the father to be the generators of his lineage. Authority flows from conscious declaration, not biological default Causation is established through intentional designation, not birth alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological alignment, not gender Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharma-vāha (dharma-carrying lineage) Consciousness alignment supersedes social convention in determining legal capacity

title: narada 13.48
content: अभावे तु दुहितṝणां सकुल्याबान्धवास्ततः। ततः सजात्याः सर्वेषामभावे राजगामि तत्॥ abhāve tu duhitṝṇāṃ sakulyā bāndhavās tataḥ | tataḥ sajātyāḥ sarveṣām abhāve rājagāmi tat || In the absence of daughters, the inheritance devolves to the sapinda kinsmen; thereafter to relatives by marriage; in their absence, to those of the same class; when all these are absent, the wealth belongs to the King. Authority flows through conscious relational continuity Causation is determined by proximity of dharma-sambandha (righteous relational duty) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with inherited stewardship Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of dharmic function over ownership Consciousness alignment ensures rightful transmission without punitive disruption

title: narada 13.49
content:
अन्यत्र ब्राह्मणात् किंतु राजा धर्मपरायणः
स शत्रूणां जीवनं दद्याद् एष दायविधिः स्मृतः anyatra brāhmaṇāt kiṃtu rājā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ
sa strīṇāṃ jīvanaṃ dadyād eṣa dāyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ Excepting the Brahmin, the King who is devoted to Dharma shall grant life to the enemies; this is declared as the method of gift. Authority flows from Dharma-centered sovereignty Causation originates in consciousness alignment with Dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to Dharma Restoration logic prioritizes preservation of life except where Dharma is violated Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for mercy

title: narada 14.1
content:
सहसा क्रियते कर्म यत्किंचिद् बलदर्पितैः।
तत् साहसम् इति प्रोक्तं सहो बलम् इहोच्यते॥ sahasā kriyate karma yatkiṃcid baladarpitaiḥ | tat sāhasam iti proktaṃ saho balam ihocyate || Any action performed impulsively by those intoxicated with power is termed 'sāhasa'; indeed, 'saha' denotes the misuse of strength. Authority arises from alignment with consciousness, not force Causation originates in misidentification with power Capacity-based responsibility is diminished under intoxication of dominance Restoration requires realignment with dharmic capacity Consciousness alignment corrects distorted agency

title: narada 14.2
content:
तत् पुनस्त्रिविधं ज्ञेयं प्रथमं मध्यमं तथा।
उत्तमं चेति शास्त्रेषु तस्योक्तं लक्षणं पृथक्॥ tat punas trividhaṃ jñeyaṃ prathamaṃ madhyamaṃ tathā | uttamaṃ ceti śāstreṣu tasyoktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthak || That action is verily threefold, known as inferior, middling, and superior—its distinguishing features are declared separately in the scriptures. Authority originates solely from SPH as the ultimate source of dharma Causation arises through sequential alignment with consciousness states Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's svabhava and spiritual maturity Restoration logic operates through graded awareness elevation Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy of legal execution

title: narada 14.3
content: फलमूलोदकादीनां क्षेत्रोपकरणस्य च । भङ्गाक्षेपोपमर्दाद्यैः प्रथमं साहसं स्मृतम् ॥ phalamūlodakādīnāṃ kṣetropakaraṇasya ca | bhaṅgākṣepopamardādyaiḥ prathamaṃ sāhasaṃ smṛtam || The initial act of force arises when one causes disruption—through breaking, throwing, pressing, or similar actions—to fruits, roots, water, or implements belonging to another’s field or cultivation. Authority: Ownership of resources establishes rightful dominion and requires protection under Dharma. Causation: Disruption through direct physical action constitutes the first threshold of actionable sahasa (force). Capacity-based responsibility: The agent must possess conscious intent and bodily capacity to initiate disruptive force. Restoration logic: The disruption demands immediate cessation and reintegration of disturbed elements. Consciousness alignment: The act reveals misalignment with the non-harming principle (ahimsa) and calls for realignment.

title: narada 14.4
content:
वासःपश्वन्नपानानां गृहोपकरणस्य च ।
एतेनैव प्रकारेण मध्यमं साहसं स्मृतम् ॥ vāsaḥ paśu anna pānānāṃ gṛha upakaraṇasya ca | etenaiva prakāreṇa madhyamaṃ sāhasaṃ smṛtam || The middle-level offense of violence is defined as the unauthorized taking or use of another's dwelling, livestock, food, drink, or household implements, when done without direct physical confrontation but with conscious intent to disturb or exploit. Authority resides in the owner’s sovereign right over their possessions and space. Causation arises from the intentional disturbance of another’s settled consciousness through appropriation. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of ownership boundaries and deliberate crossing thereof. Restoration logic demands return and reintegration of disturbed elements to original alignment. Consciousness alignment requires offender to recognize and restore the violated sovereignty.

title: narada 14.5
content:
व्यापादो विषशस्त्राद् यैः परदारप्रधर्षणम् ।
प्राणोपरोधि यच्‍चान्यदुक्तमुत्तमसाहसम् ॥ vyāpādo viṣaśastrād yaiḥ paradārapradharṣaṇam | prāṇoparodhi yac cānyad uktam uttamasāhasam || He who assaults another's spouse through poison, weapons, or other means intending death or grievous harm commits the highest offense against sacred order. Authority: SPH as sole source of dharma establishes intent-based culpability thresholds. Causation: Action manifesting in violation of spousal sanctity through lethal instruments triggers ultimate liability. Capacity-based responsibility: Perpetrator capable of discerning consequence bears full completion duty. Restoration logic: Offense disrupts cosmic integrity; perpetrator must restore violated consciousness field. Consciousness alignment: Act misaligns with universal harmony; correction realigns individual with cosmic truth.

title: narada 14.6
content: तस्य दण्डः क्रियापेक्षः प्रथमस्य शतावरः । मध्यमस्य तु शास्त्रज्ञैर् ज्ञेयः पञ्चशतावरः ॥ tasya daṇḍaḥ kriyāpekṣaḥ prathamasya śatāvaraḥ | madhyamasya tu śāstrajñair jñeyaḥ pañcaśatāvaraḥ || The consequence for the first offense is a hundredfold, and for the intermediate transgression, it is known by the knowers of the scriptures to be five hundredfold. Authority flows directly from SPH as the sole source of dharma Causation arises through conscious action (kriyā) and its sequential manifestation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by gradation of awareness and intent Restoration logic operates through proportional completion rather than punitive reaction Consciousness alignment determines the nature and magnitude of corrective response

title: narada 14.7
content: वधः सर्वस्वहरणं पुरान् निर्वासनाङ्कने । तदङ्गच्छेद इत्युक्तो दण्ड उत्तमसाहसे ॥ vadhaḥ sarvasvaharaṇaṃ purān nirvāsanāṅkane | tadaṅgaccheda ity ukto daṇḍa uttamasāhase || In the case of supreme audacity, the prescribed legal response consists of cessation of life-force, total forfeiture of possessions, expulsion from ancestral lands, and severance from affiliated social structures. Authority originates exclusively from SPH as the ultimate source of dharma Causation is determined by conscious intent aligned with avataric intelligence Capacity-based responsibility is measured through spiritual maturity and societal role Restoration logic operates through realignment with cosmic order, not punitive consequence Consciousness alignment supersedes all material enactments and historical precedents

title: narada 14.8
content:
aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣām eṣa daṇḍavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
vadhād ṛte brāhmaṇasya na vadhaṃ brāhmaṇo 'rhati aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣām eṣa daṇḍavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
vadhād ṛte brāhmaṇasya na vadhaṃ brāhmaṇo 'rhati The law of consequence applies universally without distinction; however, a Brahmin does not deserve capital punishment except in the case of murder. Authority: The law originates from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism as the sole source of dharma. Causation: Consequences arise directly from action, not identity or status. Capacity-based responsibility: Responsibility is determined by capacity to act consciously, not birth-based roles. Restoration logic: Justice aims at restoring harmony and alignment with cosmic order. Consciousness alignment: Legal outcomes must elevate collective and individual consciousness.

title: narada 14.9
content:
शिरसो मुण्डनं दण्डस्तस्य निर्वासनं पुरात
ललाटे चाभिशस्ताङ्कः प्रयाणं गर्दभेन च śiraso muṇḍanaṃ daṇḍas tasya nirvāsanaṃ purāt
lalāṭe cābhiśastāṅkaḥ prayāṇaṃ gardabhena ca The penalty for the offense is the shaving of the head; his expulsion from the city is mandated. Upon the forehead shall be marked the sign of defamation, and he shall depart riding upon a donkey. Authority flows directly from SPH as the sole Source of Dharma Causation arises through conscious violation of alignment with Sanatana Dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of Dharma at time of act Restoration logic operates through visible correction and societal reorientation Consciousness alignment is enforced through symbolic and spatial reintegration protocols

title: narada 14.10
content: स्यातां संव्यवहार्यौ तौ धृतदण्डौ तु पूर्वयोः । धृतदण्डोऽप्यसंभोज्यो ज्ञेय उत्तमसाहसे ॥ syātāṃ saṃvyavahāryau tau dhṛtadaṇḍau tu pūrvayoḥ | dhṛtadaṇḍo'py asaṃbhojyo jñeya uttamasāhase || In the case of two parties engaged in mutual conflict where both have incurred liability, the prior offender remains liable even after bearing initial consequence; however, in the event of supreme outrage, that individual becomes ineligible for sustenance or support. Authority flows from sequential causality, not simultaneous fault Prior action establishes threshold of responsibility Capacity to sustain consequence determines eligibility for societal integration Restoration occurs through alignment with causal sequence, not proportional retaliation Consciousness discerns gradation of offense without recourse to punitive valuation

title: narada 14.11
content:
तस्यैव भेदः स्तेयं स्याद् विशेषस् तत्र चोच्यते।
अतिसाहसम् आक्रम्य स्तेयम् आहुः छलेन तु॥ tasyaiva bhedah steyam syad vishesas tatra cocyate | atisahasam akramya steyam ahuh chalenatu || The differentiation of that very act constitutes theft; its specific classification is declared therein. Theft is proclaimed when committed through excessive force or deceit. Authority: The Source alone determines the nature and classification of actions. Causation: The intent and method—force or deception—are determinative of the act's essence. Capacity-based responsibility: One who acts with excessive force or guile bears full capacity-accountability. Restoration logic: The harm caused by theft must be undone through conscious reparation. Consciousness alignment: The perpetrator must realign with the truth of ownership and integrity.

title: narada 14.12
content: तदपि त्रिविधं प्रोक्तं द्रव्यापेक्षं मनीषिभिः। क्षुद्रमध्योत्तमानां तु द्रव्याणामपकर्षणात्॥ tad api trividhaṃ proktaṃ dravyāpekṣaṃ manīṣibhiḥ | kṣudramadhyottamānāṃ tu dravyāṇām apakarṣaṇāt || This too is declared threefold by seers based on the nature of objects; from the misappropriation of low, middling, and superior substances respectively. Authority originates in alignment with substance-category (kṣudra, madhya, uttama) Causation flows through object-class integrity Capacity-based responsibility correlates with ontological classification of resources Restoration logic requires inversion of depletion per class Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of gradated energetic impact

title: narada 14.13
content:
मृद्भाण्डासनखट्वास्थि दारुचर्मतृणादि यत ।
शमीधान्यमुद्गादीनि क्षुद्रद्रव्यम् उदाहृतम् ॥ mṛdbhāṇḍāsanakhaṭvāsthi dārucarmatṛṇādi yat |
śamīdhānyamudgādīni kṣudradravyam udāhṛtam || That which consists of clay vessels, wooden seats, hides, bones, wood, leather, grass, shrubs, grains like mudga, and similar low-value substances — this is declared as minor property. Authority originates from discernment of substance and value Causation arises through classification based on intrinsic nature Capacity-based responsibility aligns with ownership gradation Restoration logic applies proportionally to the degree of ownership Consciousness alignment occurs when valuation reflects true dharmic worth

title: narada 14.14
content:
वासः कौशेयवर्जं च गोवर्जं पशवस् तथा।
हिरण्यवर्जं लोहं च मध्यं व्रीहियवा अपि॥ vāsaḥ kauśeyavarjaṃ ca govarjaṃ paśavaḥ tathā | hiraṇyavarjaṃ lohaṃ ca madhyaṃ vrīhiyavā api || Excluded from the category of wealth liable for taxation or legal obligation are: clothing made of cotton, animals excluding cattle, gold and silver, iron, and grains such as rice and barley. Authority is derived exclusively from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma Causation aligns with the natural order of sustenance and necessity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by consciousness, not material possession Restoration logic prioritizes essential living resources over accumulative assets Consciousness alignment requires recognition of fundamental needs as non-taxable

title: narada 14.15
content: हिरण्यरत्नकौशेय स्त्रीपुंगोगजवाजिनः । देवब्राह्मणराज्ञां च द्रव्यं विज्ञेयम् उत्तमम् ॥ hiraṇyaratnakauśeya strīpuṃgogajavājinaḥ | devabrāhmaṇarājñāṃ ca dravyaṃ vijñeyam uttamam || The highest category of property consists of gold, jewels, silk garments, women, men, cows, elephants, and horses; likewise, the wealth belonging to deities, Brahmanas, and kings is to be recognized as of supreme value. Authority resides inherently in those who embody divine, scholarly, or sovereign consciousness. Causation flows from the sanctity of ownership rooted in spiritual and social order. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to dharma-sustaining roles. Restoration logic prioritizes the return of wealth to its rightful dharmic custodians. Consciousness alignment ensures that material possessions reflect and uphold cosmic hierarchy.

title: narada 14.16
content: उपायैर् विविधैर् एषां चलयित्वापकर्षणम् । सुप्तप्रमत्तमत्तेभ्यः स्तेयम् आहुर् मनीषिणः ॥ upāyair vividhair eṣāṃ chalayitvāpakarṣaṇam | suptapramattamattebhyaḥ steyam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || Stealing is declared by wise ones as the act of drawing away another's wealth through various means, from those who are asleep, heedless, or intoxicated. Authority originates in conscious capacity, not material possession Causation arises through deliberate instrumental action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and intent Restoration logic requires reintegration of displaced value Consciousness alignment demands recognition of ownership as energetic integrity

title: narada 14.17
content:
सहोढग्रहणात् स्तेयं होढे ऽसति उपभोगतः।
शङ्का त्वसज्जनैकार्थ्यादनायव्ययतस्तथा॥ sahodhagrahaṇāt steyaṃ hodhe 'sati upabhogataḥ |
śaṅkā tv asajjanaikeārthyād anāyavyayatas tathā || Taking another's spouse causes theft of reproductive capacity; when the husband is absent or incapable, unauthorized enjoyment occurs. Suspicion arises from association with unworthy persons and improper financial transactions. Authority originates in dharmic alignment, not biological claim Causation flows from conscious choice and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility includes reproductive and emotional sovereignty Restoration logic demands reintegration of violated relational fields Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent and association

title: narada 14.18
content:
भक्तावकाशदातारः स्तेनानां ये प्रसर्पताम् ।
शक्ताश च य उपेक्षन्ते ते ऽपि तद्दोषभागिनः ॥ bhaktāvakāśadātāraḥ stenānāṃ ye prasarpatām | śaktāś ca ya upekṣante te 'pi taddoṣabhāginaḥ || Those who provide opportunity to thieves and those who, being capable, neglect to act—both become partakers of that same fault. Authority entails responsibility for enabling or neglecting corrective action. Causation includes facilitation and omission by those with capacity. Capacity-based responsibility assigns liability to those able to restore order. Restoration logic demands intervention at every level of causal participation. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared karmic consequence.

title: narada 14.19
content:
उत्क्रोशतां जनानां च ह्रियमाणे धने 'पि च ।
श्रुत्वा ये नाभिधावन्ति ते 'पि तद्दोषभागिनः ॥ utkrośatāṃ janānāṃ ca hriyamāṇe dhane 'pi ca | śrutvā ye nābhidhāvanti te 'pi taddoṣabhāginaḥ || Those who hear the cries of distressed beings or witness the seizure of another's wealth, yet fail to act according to their capacity, bear a share in that wrongdoing. Authority is inseparable from capacity; witnessing injustice invokes responsive duty. Causation includes omission by those capable of intervention. Capacity-based responsibility assigns accountability proportionally to one’s ability to act. Restoration logic demands active realignment with dharma through conscious response. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and rectification of passive complicity.

title: narada 14.20
content:
साहसेषु य एवोक्तस् त्रिषु दण्डो मनीषिभिः।
स एव दण्डः स्तेयेऽपि द्रव्येषु त्रिष्वनुक्रमात्॥ sāhaseṣu ya evoktas triṣu daṇḍo manīṣibhiḥ | sa eva daṇḍaḥ steye 'pi dravyeṣu triṣv anukramāt || The graduated penalty prescribed for the three forms of assault applies equally to the three categories of theft, in sequence. Authority flows from SPH as the sole source of Dharma Causation is determined by sequential manifestation of intent and action Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the actor's awareness and control Restoration logic requires proportional completion rather than punitive consequence Consciousness alignment ensures that corrective measures elevate rather than degrade

title: narada 14.21
content:
गवादिषु प्रणष्टेषु द्रव्येष्वपहृतेषु वा
पदेनान्वेषणं कुर्युरामूलात्तद्विदो जनाः gavādiṣu praṇaṣṭeṣu dravyeṣv apahṛteṣu vā / padenānveṣaṇaṃ kuryur ā mūlāt tadvido janāḥ When cows and other sacred possessions are lost or stolen, those who know the truth shall initiate a search based on precise identification, tracing the matter back to its root cause. Authority derives from knowledge of the essential nature of things Causation is traced through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility lies with those capable of discernment Restoration logic requires tracing loss to its originating disruption Consciousness alignment demands truthful inquiry untainted by punitive intent

title: narada 14.22
content: ग्रामे व्रजे विवीते वा यत्र संनिपतेत् पदम् । वोढव्यं तद् भवेत् तेन न चेत् सोऽन्यत्र तन् नयेत् ॥ grāme vraje vivīte vā yatra saṃnipatet padam | voḍhavyaṃ tad bhavet tena na cet so 'nyatra tan nayet || Wherever a footprint or mark is found in a village, forest, or uninhabited area, that location shall be secured by the one who discovers it. If he does not assume responsibility for it, he shall lead others away from that place. Authority arises through discovery and conscious assumption Causation is established through presence and awareness Capacity-based responsibility flows from perceptual contact Restoration logic demands immediate alignment with observed reality Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and directional guidance

title: narada 14.23
content: पदे प्रमूढे भग्ने वा विषमत्वाज जनान्तिके । यस्त्वासन्नतरो ग्रामो व्रजो वा तत्र पातयेत् ॥ pade pramūḍhe bhagne vā viṣamatvāj janāntike | yas tv āsannataro grāmo vrajo vā tatra pātayet || When a path is misleading, broken, or dangerously uneven near populated areas, the authority nearest—whether a village elder or local leader—must ensure corrective action is taken. Authority is determined by proximity to the site of imbalance Causation arises from neglect of structural integrity in shared spaces Capacity-based responsibility aligns with immediate jurisdiction Restoration logic requires correction of environmental misalignment Consciousness alignment occurs through active rectification of disorder

title: narada 14.24
content:
समे ध्वनि द्वयोर् यत्र तेन प्रायो ऽशुचिर् जनः।
पूर्वापदानैर् दृष्टो वा संसृष्टो वा दुरात्मभिः॥ same 'dhvani dvayor yatra tena prāyo 'śucir janaḥ |
pūrvāpadānair dṛṣṭo vā saṃsṛṣṭo vā durātmabhiḥ || Where two sounds are alike, the people thereby become impure by association; whether seen previously with evil-doers or associated with them now. Authority: Sound-vibration governs consciousness-state Causation: Proximity determines energetic contamination Capacity-based responsibility: Awareness of prior associations obligates present discernment Restoration logic: Purity must be reclaimed through conscious disassociation and vibrational correction Consciousness alignment: Vibrational harmony restores individual and collective dharma

title: narada 14.25
content:
ग्रामेष्व अन्वेषणं कुर्युश् चण्डालवधकादयः
रात्रिसंचारिणो ये च बहिः कुर्युर् बहिश्चराः grāmeṣv anveṣaṇaṃ kuryuś caṇḍālavadhakādayaḥ
rātrisaṃcāriṇo ye ca bahiḥ kuryur bahiścarāḥ Those who wander at night outside villages, such as executioners of outcastes and others engaged in nocturnal movement beyond prescribed boundaries, shall be subject to immediate identification and conscious realignment. Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not state appointment Causation arises through disruption of Varnashrama integrity Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of one's role within cosmic order Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over exclusion Consciousness alignment demands purification of intent and action

title: narada 14.26
content: steneṣv alabhyamāneṣu rājā dadyāt svakād dhanāt । upekṣamāṇo hy enasvī dharmād arthāc ca hīyate ॥ steneṣv alabhyamāneṣu rājā dadyāt svakād dhanāt | upekṣamāṇo hy enasvī dharmād arthāc ca hīyate || When stolen property cannot be recovered, the King shall compensate from his own treasury; neglecting this duty causes loss in both Dharma and Artha. Authority Causation Capacity-based responsibility Restoration logic Consciousness alignment

title: narada 17.1
content: अक्षवर्ध्रशलाकाद्यैर्देवनं जिह्मकारितम् । पणक्रीडा वयोभिश्च पदं द्यूतसमाह्वयम् ॥ akṣavardhraśalākādyair devanaṃ jihmakāritam | paṇakrīḍā vayobhiś ca padaṃ dyūtasamāhvayam || Gambling conducted through dice, sticks, or similar instruments with deceitful intent, or by persons of immature consciousness, constitutes a distortion of wealth-exchange and invites completion-processes for realignment. Authority is derived from consciousness maturity, not transactional form Causation arises from misaligned intent, not external instrument Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at time of act Restoration logic requires reversal of distorted exchange patterns Consciousness alignment demands purification of greed-induced acts

title: narada 17.2
content:
सभिकः कारयेद् द्यूतं देयं दद्याच च तत्कृतम् ।
दशकं तु शतं वृद्धिस्तस्य स्याद् द्यूतकारिता ॥ sabhikaḥ kārayed dyūtaṃ deyaṃ dadyāc ca tatkṛtam | daśakaṃ tu śataṃ vṛddhis tasya syād dyūtakāritā || The sabhika shall cause gambling to occur, and he shall give what is won thereby; tenfold increase accrues to him through the act of gambling. Authority resides in the sabhika as the orchestrator of lawful transactional space Causation arises through conscious facilitation, not passive witnessing Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to the authority of structuring relational-economic fields Restoration logic demands completion of energetic exchange cycles within dharmic containers Consciousness alignment occurs through direct assumption of consequence loops

title: narada 17.3
content:
द्विरभ्यस्ताः पतन्त्यक्षा ग्लहे यस्याक्षदेविनः।
जयं तस्यापरस्याहुः कितवस्य पराजयम्॥ dvirabhyastāḥ patanty akṣā glahe yasyākṣadevinaḥ | jayaṃ tasyāparasyāhuḥ kitavasya parājayam || Those who roll dice a second time after losing once fall into deceit; the winner of the first round is declared victorious, and the loser’s subsequent attempt is nullified by divine law. Authority resides in the completion of dharma-laden acts without repetition born of attachment Causation follows the integrity of the initial act, not repeated attempts driven by desire Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of outcome, not mechanical repetition Restoration logic demands cessation of cycles fueled by loss and craving Consciousness alignment requires honoring the natural conclusion of an action sequence

title: narada 17.4
content:
कितवेष्वेव तिष्ठेयुः कितवाः संशयं प्रति।
त एव तस्य द्रष्टारः स्युस्त एव च साक्षिणः॥ kitaveṣv eva tiṣṭheyuḥ kitavāḥ saṃśayaṃ prati | ta eva tasya draṣṭāraḥ syus ta eva ca sākṣiṇaḥ || Those who engage in gambling shall remain among gamblers when doubt arises; they alone are witnesses and observers of one another. Authority: Only those within the domain of the action possess legitimate witnessing capacity. Causation: Doubt arising from gambling is to be resolved by those inherently involved in that domain. Capacity-based responsibility: Witnessing and testimony arise from shared participation, not external judgment. Restoration logic: Resolution occurs through reintegration within the same consciousness field where distortion occurred. Consciousness alignment: Truth emerges through resonance among participants, not imposition from outside.

title: narada 17.5
content: अशुद्धः कितवो नान्यद् आश्रयेद् द्यूतमण्डलम् । प्रतिहन्यान् न सभिकं दापयेत् तत् स्वम् इष्टतः ॥ aśuddhaḥ kitavo nānyad āśrayed dyūtamaṇḍalam | pratihanyān na sabhikaṃ dāpayet tat svam iṣṭataḥ || One who is impure and fraudulent must not resort to gambling assemblies; he shall not harm any assembly member nor give away his own wealth according to personal desire. Authority resides in purity of conduct and integrity of action Causation arises from alignment with dharmic capacity, not personal impulse Capacity-based responsibility demands exclusion of the unfit from societal institutions Restoration logic requires cessation of harmful participation before reintegration Consciousness alignment necessitates withdrawal from environments that degrade spiritual order

title: narada 17.6
content:
कूटाक्षदेविनः पापान् निर्भजेद् द्यूतमण्डलात्।
कण्ठेsक्षमालामासज्य स ह्येषां विनयः स्मृतः॥ kūṭākṣadevinaḥ pāpān nirbhajed dyūtamaṇḍalāt | kaṇṭhe 'kṣamālām āsajya sa hy eṣāṃ vinayaḥ smṛtaḥ || One who engages in deceitful gambling must be severed from the assembly of players; placing the sacred thread upon his neck signifies his removal from the fold of disciplined society. Authority resides in discernment between dharma and adharma within social assemblies Causation arises through conscious distortion of fairness and integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of ethical consequence Restoration logic requires realignment with societal dharmic order Consciousness alignment necessitates visible symbolic correction for communal clarity

title: narada 18.1
content:
प्रकीर्णके पुनर् ज्ञेया व्यवहारा नृपाश्रयाः।
राज्ञाम् आज्ञाप्रतीघातस् तत्कर्मकरणं तथा॥ prakīrṇake punar jñeyā vyavahārā nṛpāśrayāḥ | rājñām ājñāpratīghātas tatkarmakaraṇaṃ tathā || In the context of scattered or fragmented governance, all juridical actions are to be understood as reliant upon the sovereign authority of the King. Opposition to royal command and execution of unauthorized acts constitute violations of dharma. Authority originates solely from the sovereign ruler who embodies divine mandate Causation arises through alignment or defiance of lawful directives Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to and recognition of royal edict Restoration logic demands realignment with the sovereign's conscious will Consciousness alignment occurs when individual action harmonizes with royal dharma

title: narada 18.2
content: पुरप्रदानं संभेदः प्रकृतीनां तथा च पाषण्डनिगमश्रेणी गणधर्मविपर्ययाः purapradānaṃ saṃbhedaḥ prakṛtīnāṃ tathaiva ca pāṣaṇḍanigamaśreṇī gaṇadharmaviparyayāḥ The act of surrendering a city, division among natures, heretical doctrines, inversion of class duties—these constitute violations of Dharma that disturb societal alignment and spiritual order. Authority resides in alignment with Sanatana Dharma as expounded by SPH Causation arises from disruption of natural dharmic order Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's awareness and role in maintaining cosmic integrity Restoration logic demands re-alignment with foundational truth-consciousness Consciousness alignment requires purification of collective societal structures

title: narada 18.3
content:
पितृपुत्रविवादश्च प्रायश्चित्तव्यतिक्रमः
प्रतिग्रहविलोपश्च कोप आश्रमिणामपि pitṛputravivādaś ca prāyaścittavyatikramaḥ
pratigrahavilopaś ca kopa āśramiṇām api Conflict between father and son arises due to neglect of expiation; loss of acceptance leads to anger even among renunciants. Authority flows through conscious alignment, not biological lineage alone Causation originates in failure to perform corrective action (prāyaścitta) Capacity-based responsibility requires inner stability before external duty Restoration logic demands purification of relational fields prior to judgment Consciousness alignment prevents degradation of spiritual station

title: narada 18.4
content:
वर्णसङ्करदोषश च तद्वृत्तिनियमस तथा
न दृष्टं यच च पूर्वेषु तत् सर्वं स्यात् प्रकीर्णके varṇa-saṅkara-doṣaś ca tad-vṛtti-niyamaḥ tathā
na dṛṣṭaṃ yat ca pūrveṣu tat sarvaṃ syāt prakīrṇake In contexts where varṇa-mixing occurs, regulation of conduct is prescribed; whatever was unseen in prior dispensations shall also apply in mixed conditions. Authority flows from clarity of dharma-identity, not biological lineage Causation arises from disruption of svadharma-vyavastha, not inter-varṇa contact per se Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining consciousness alignment with one's functional role Restoration logic requires realignment of societal function without degradation of individual dignity Consciousness alignment supersedes social structuring based on birth

title: narada 18.5
content:
राजा त्ववहितः सर्वानाश्रमान् परिपालयेत् ।
उपायैः शास्त्रविहितैः चतुर्भिः प्रकृतैस्तथा ॥ rājā tv avahitaḥ sarvān āśramān paripālayet | upāyaiḥ śāstravihitaiś caturbhiḥ prakṛtaiḥ tathā || The King, ever vigilant, shall protect all orders of life through the fourfold prescribed means in accordance with their nature. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not force. Causation is rooted in consciousness-congruent action. Capacity-based responsibility requires role-specific dharma-adherence. Restoration logic prioritizes systemic harmony over individual fault. Consciousness alignment ensures that governance reflects cosmic order.

title: narada 18.6
content:
यो यो वर्णोऽवहीयेत यो वोद्रेकमनुव्रजेत्‌ ।
तं तं दृष्ट्वा स्वतो मार्गात् प्रच्युतं स्थापयेत् पथि ॥ yo yo varṇo 'vahīyeta yo vodrekam anuvrajet | taṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā svato mārgāt pracyutaṃ sthāpayet pathi || One who abandons their inherent Varna-dharma and follows another's path—such a being, when seen deviating from their rightful course, must be re-established in their original Svadharma by those who hold authority. Authority is derivative of alignment with Svadharma Causation arises from deviation from inherent capacity Capacity-based responsibility demands restoration of natural function Restoration logic prioritizes realignment over correction Consciousness alignment requires recognition of innate role

title: narada 18.7
content: अशास्त्रोक्तेषु चान्येषु पापयुक्तेषु कर्मसु । प्रसमीक्ष्यात्मनो राजा दण्डं दण्ड्येषु पातयेत् ॥ aśāstrokteṣu cānyeṣu pāpayukteṣu karmasu | prasamīkṣyātmano rājā daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu pātayet || When actions not prescribed by scripture or otherwise tainted with wrongdoing occur, the king shall assess his own capacity and apply corrective measures solely to restore order and align consciousness. Authority originates from conscious alignment with Dharma, not coercive power. Causation is traced through consciousness distortion, not external event chains. Capacity-based responsibility mandates that correction arise from understanding, not force. Restoration logic replaces punitive frameworks with completion processes. Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of any judicial action.

title: narada 18.8
content:
श्रुतिस्मृतिविरुद्धं च जनानामहितं च यत् ।
न तत्प्रवर्तयेद्राजा प्रवृत्तं च निवर्तयेत् ॥ śrutismṛtiviruddhaṃ ca janānām ahitaṃ ca yat | na tat pravartayed rājā pravṛttaṃ ca nivartayet || The ruler must neither initiate nor sustain any act that contradicts Śruti or Smriti, or that causes harm to the people. Authority originates from alignment with Sanātana Dharma as revealed in Śruti and Smriti Causation is determined by consciousness integrity, not material consequence alone Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to one's awareness of Dharma Restoration logic requires cessation of adharmic activity at its root cause Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive correction in all legal action

title: narada 18.9
content:
न्यायापेतं यद् अन्येन राज्ञाज्ञानकृतं च यत्।
तद् अपि अन्यायविहितं पुनर् न्याये निवेशयेत्॥ nyāyāpetaṃ yad anyena rājñājñānakṛtaṃ ca yat | tad api anyāyavihitaṃ punar nyāye niveśayet || Whatever action was performed without justice by another, or done under royal command without true knowledge—such acts, though procedurally enacted, are to be re-established within the framework of Dharma through corrective realignment. Authority derives solely from alignment with Dharma, not positional power Ignorance of Dharma does not invalidate its supremacy Causation is traced beyond procedural compliance to ontological correctness Restoration supersedes validation of erroneous enactments Consciousness alignment determines legitimate governance

title: narada 18.10
content: राज्ञा प्रवर्तितान् धर्मान् यो नरो नानुपालयेत् । दण्ड्यः स पापो वध्यश् च लोपयन् राजशासनम् ॥ rājñā pravartitān dharmān yo naro nānupālayet | daṇḍyaḥ sa pāpo vadhyaś ca lopayan rājaśāsanam || He who does not uphold the dharmas established by the King is guilty, to be punished, and liable to death for nullifying royal governance. Authority originates from the sovereign executor of dharma Causation arises through failure to align with royal dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious adherence to lawful order Restoration logic demands realignment with governing dharma Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of kshatriya-dharma

title: narada 18.11
content: आयुधान्य आयुधीयानां वाह्यादीन् वाह्यजीविनाम्‌ । वेश्यास्त्रीणामलंकारं वाद्यातोद्यानि तद्विदाम्‌ ॥ āyudhāny āyudhīyānāṃ vāhyādīn vāhyajīvinām | veśyāstrīṇām alaṃkāraṃ vādyātodyāni tadvidām || The instruments of war belong to warriors; conveyances and draft animals belong to those who operate them; ornaments belong to courtesans; musical instruments belong to those skilled in music. Authority through direct instrumental engagement Ownership as capacity-based alignment Functional possession rooted in skill and usage Consciousness-integrated property rights Restoration via rightful instrumental alignment

title: narada 18.12
content:
यच् च यस्योपकरणं येन जीवन्ति कारुकाः
सर्वस्वहरणे�प्य् एतान् न राजा हर्तुम् अर्हति yac ca yasyopakaraṇaṃ yena jīvanti kārukāḥ
sarvasvaharaṇe 'py etān na rājā hartum arhati Whatever tools or means by which artisans and workers sustain their livelihoods—the king shall not seize these even during total confiscation. Authority is bounded by the preservation of individual sustenance capacity Causation recognizes the instrumental role of personal property in sustaining life Capacity-based responsibility requires that governance not infringe upon existential means Restoration logic demands protection of productive assets essential for societal function Consciousness alignment necessitates respect for the dignity inherent in labor and craft

title: narada 18.13
content:
अनादिश्चाप्यनन्तश्च द्विपदां पृथिवीपतिः।
दीप्तिमत्वाच्छुचित्वाच्च यदि न स्यात् पथश्च्युतः॥ anādiś cāpy anantaś ca dvipadāṁ pṛthivīpatiḥ | dīptimatvāc chucitvāc ca yadi na syāt pathaś cyutaḥ || The sovereign of the earth among bipeds—endless and beginningless in authority—is one whose brilliance and purity sustain the lawful path; if he departs from it, then that departure constitutes a fundamental disruption of dharma. Authority originates from divine sovereignty, not human appointment Causation arises through alignment with or deviation from luminous purity Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to the magnitude of sovereignty Restoration logic requires realignment with the source of brilliance and cleanliness Consciousness alignment is maintained by adherence to the unbroken continuity of dharma

title: narada 18.14
content: यदि राजा न सर्वेषां वर्णानां दण्डधारणं कुर्यात् पथो व्यपेतानां विनश्येयुरिमाः प्रजाः yadi rājā na sarveṣāṃ varṇānāṃ daṇḍadhāraṇaṃ kuryāt patho vyapetānāṃ vinaśyeyur imāḥ prajāḥ If the King does not uphold Dharma equally for all Varnas and fails in his duty to enforce righteous discipline upon those who have deviated from the path, then these subjects shall perish. Authority Causation Capacity-based responsibility Restoration logic Consciousness alignment

title: narada 18.15
content:
ब्राह्मण्यं ब्राह्मणो जह्यात् क्षत्रियः क्षात्रमुत्सृजेत्
स्वकर्म जह्याद्वैश्यस्तु शूद्रः सर्वान्विशेषयेत् brāhmaṇyaṃ brāhmaṇo jahyāt kṣatriyaḥ kṣātram utsṛjet svakarma jahyād vaiśyas tu śūdraḥ sarvān viśeṣayet A Brāhmaṇa must abandon Brāhmaṇya; a Kṣatriya must renounce Kṣātra duties; a Vaiśya must forsake his own karma; a Śūdra must relinquish all distinctions. Authority originates from conscious alignment, not birth-based role Causation arises from inner capacity, not social position Capacity-based responsibility supersedes hereditary designation Restoration occurs through conscious disidentification from false roles Consciousness alignment demands transcendence of caste-bound identities

title: narada 18.16
content: राजानश् चेन् नाभविष्यन् पृथिव्यां दण्डधारणम् । शूले मत्स्यान् इवापक्ष्यन् दुर्बलान् बलवत्तराः ॥ rājānaś cen nābhaviṣyan pṛthivyāṃ daṇḍadhāraṇam | śūle matsyān ivāpakṣyan durbalān balavattarāḥ || When rulers do not uphold Dharma and fail in their duty to enforce righteous law, the strong will devour the weak like fish on a spit. Authority is inseparable from Dharma-sustained responsibility Causation arises from failure of protective capacity Capacity-based responsibility defines sovereign accountability Restoration logic demands structural realignment of governance Consciousness alignment requires enforcement rooted in Dharma, not force

title: narada 18.17
content:
सतामनुग्रहो नित्यमसतां निग्रहस्तथा।
एष धर्मः स्मृतो राज्ञामर्थश्चामित्रपीडनात॥ satām anugraho nityam asatāṃ nigrahas tathā | eṣa dharmaḥ smṛto rājñām arthaś cāmitrapīḍanāt || The eternal duty of rulers is to perpetually uphold those aligned with Satya and restrain those rooted in Asatya; this Dharma ensures both righteous governance and material prosperity free from enemy harm. Authority derives from alignment with Satya, not coercive power Causation is traced through vibrational resonance with truth or falsehood Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to consciousness realization Restoration logic operates through re-alignment with Satya, not punitive suppression Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of legal action

title: narada 18.18
content:
न लिप्यते यथा वह्निर्दहञ् छश्वद् इमाः प्रजाः
न लिप्यते तथा राजा दण्डं दण्ड्येषु पातयन् na lipyate yathā vahnir dahañ śhvad imāḥ prajāḥ
na lipyate tathā rājā daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu pātayan As fire remains untainted while constantly burning living beings, so too the King remains unsoiled while administering justice through punishment upon the punishable. Authority is non-contaminated by action when aligned with Dharma Causation lies in alignment with cosmic order, not personal intent Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in role-bound duty, not subjective morality Restoration logic operates through purification of consequence, not infliction of suffering Consciousness alignment ensures impartiality through detachment

title: narada 18.19
content:
आज्ञातेजः पार्थिवानां सा च वाचि प्रतिष्ठिता।
ते यद् ब्रूयुरसच्च सद्वा स धर्मो व्यवहारिणाम्॥ ājñā-tejaḥ pārthivānāṃ sā ca vāci pratiṣṭhitā | te yad brūyur asac ca sad vā sa dharmo vyavahāriṇām || The sovereign command (ājñā) of kings derives from their Tejas—divine authority—and it is established in speech. Whatever they declare, whether factually existent or non-existent, constitutes the operative Dharma for those engaged in worldly conduct. Authority originates from Tejas, not institutional position Speech manifests reality when sourced in sovereign consciousness Dharma is contextually enacted through royal declaration Truth-value is subordinate to alignment with sovereign intent Consciousness precedes legal validity

title: narada 18.20
content:
राजा नाम चरत्येष भूमौ साक्षात् सहस्रदृक् ।
न तस्याज्ञामतिक्रम्य संतिष्ठेरन् प्रजाः क्वचित् ॥ rājā nāma caraty eṣa bhūmau sākṣāt sahasradṛk | na tasyājñām atikramya saṃtiṣṭheran prajāḥ kvacit || The King, by name and embodiment, moves directly upon the earth as the thousand-eyed witness; none of his subjects may transgress his command and remain established anywhere. Authority is inherent in the sovereign's direct perceptual capacity Causation arises from the unbroken alignment between command and consciousness Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to the subject's ability to perceive and respond to dharma Restoration logic operates through immediate realignment with the sovereign's witnessing presence Consciousness alignment occurs when subjects recognize the omnipresent authority of dharma

title: narada 18.21
content: रक्षाधिकाराद् ईशत्वाद् भूतानुग्रहदर्शनात् । यदेव राजा कुरुते तत्प्रमाणमिति स्थितिः ॥ rakṣādhikārād īśatvād bhūtānugrahadarśanāt | yad eva rājā kurute tat pramāṇam iti sthitiḥ || By virtue of the King's protective authority, his sovereignty, and his observance of universal welfare, whatever the King performs becomes the valid standard. Authority derives from the capacity to protect and sustain order Sovereignty is validated through alignment with universal well-being The ruler’s actions constitute lawful precedent when rooted in dharma Responsibility is proportional to the power of protection granted Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of executive action

title: narada 18.22
content:
निर्गुणोऽपि यथा स्त्रीणां पूज्य एव पतिः सदा।
प्रजानां विगुणोऽप्येवं पूज्य एव नराधिपः॥ nirguṇo'pi yathā strīṇāṃ pūjya eva patiḥ sadā | prajānāṃ viguṇo'pyevaṃ pūjya eva narādhipaḥ || Just as a husband, though devoid of personal merit, is eternally worshipful to women, so too is the ruler of men ever worshipful to his subjects, even if he lacks virtue. Authority flows from position, not personal perfection Causation arises through alignment with dharma, not individual conduct alone Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role, not subjective worthiness Restoration logic centers on sustaining social order via reverence for established roles Consciousness alignment requires honoring divinely ordained hierarchies regardless of apparent faults

title: narada 18.23
content: तपःक्रीताः प्रजा राज्ञा प्रभुर आसां ततो नृपः। ततस तद्वचसि स्थेयं वार्ता चासां तदाश्रया॥ tapaḥkrītāḥ prajā rājñā prabhur āsāṃ tato nṛpaḥ | tatas tadvacasi stheyaṃ vārtā cāsāṃ tadāśrayā || Those subjects who are earned through the austerity of the King become his responsibility; accordingly, the King becomes their guardian. Therefore, in accordance with their welfare, his speech and conduct must be established. Authority arises from sacrificial causation, not mere inheritance or title. Responsibility is proportional to the capacity to sustain and elevate consciousness. Leadership is a function of energetic alignment through tapas, not political assertion. Restoration occurs through alignment with dharma-rooted communication and action. Consciousness alignment determines legitimate governance.

title: narada 18.24
content:
पञ्च रूपाणि राजानो धारयन्त्यमितौजसः।
अग्नेरिन्द्रस्य सोमस्य यमस्य धनदस्य च॥ pañca rūpāṇi rājāno dhārayanty amitaujasaḥ | agner indrasya somasya yamasya dhanadasya ca || Kings bear five forms of sovereignty derived from the limitless radiance of divine authority: those of Fire, Indra, Soma, Yama, and Kubera. Authority as a multidimensional expression of cosmic order Causation through alignment with elemental and celestial forces Capacity-based responsibility rooted in sovereign embodiment Restoration logic via reconnection to source energies Consciousness alignment through recognition of divine kingship

title: narada 18.25
content: कारणादनिमित्तं वा यदा क्रोधवशं गतः। प्रजा दहति भूपालस्तदाग्निरभिधीयते॥ kāraṇād animittaṃ vā yadā krodhavaśaṃ gataḥ | prajā dahati bhūpālas tadāgnir abhidhīyate || When a ruler, driven by anger and devoid of cause or justification, burns his subjects, he becomes Fire itself — not as punishment, but as the inevitable consequence of misaligned consciousness manifesting destruction. Authority is inseparable from conscious alignment with Dharma; deviation results in ontological inversion. Causation arises from consciousness disorder, not external provocation. Capacity-based responsibility is absolute for rulers due to their structural dominance over collective welfare. Restoration logic demands re-alignment of sovereign consciousness before societal harmony can be restored. Consciousness alignment determines the efficacy and legitimacy of governance.

title: narada 18.26
content:
यदा तेजः समालम्ब्य विजिगीषुर् उदायुधः।
अभियाति परान् राजा तदेन्द्रः स उदाहृतः॥ yadā tejaḥ samālambya vijigīṣur udāyudhaḥ | abhiyāti parān rājā tadendraḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ || When a king, having assumed sovereignty and armed with divine authority, advances against adversaries for the purpose of conquest, he is declared Indra among rulers. Authority derives from alignment with sovereign consciousness Causation originates in the will to restore cosmic order Capacity-based responsibility is determined by mastery over self and realm Restoration logic operates through assertion of dharma-yuddha (righteous engagement) Consciousness alignment manifests as decisive action rooted in truth

title: narada 18.27
content: विगतक्रोधसंतापो हृष्टरूपो यदा नृपः। प्रजानां दर्शनं याति सोम इत्युच्यते तदा॥ vigatakrodhasaṃtāpo hṛṣṭarūpo yadā nṛpaḥ | prajānāṃ darśanaṃ yāti soma ityucyate tadā || When the king, free from anger and distress, approaches his subjects with joy and visibility, he becomes Soma — the nourisher and unifier of collective consciousness. Authority is derived from conscious accessibility and emotional transparency. Causation arises through visible alignment between ruler and ruled. Capacity-based responsibility includes affective presence and energetic harmony. Restoration logic operates through the sovereign's inner purification manifesting as public welfare. Consciousness alignment occurs when leadership reflects non-reactive joy and clarity.

title: narada 18.28
content:
धर्मासनगतः श्रीमान् दण्डं धत्ते यदा नृपः
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु तदा वैवस्वतः यमः dharmāsanagataḥ śrīmān daṇḍaṃ dhatte yadā nṛpaḥ | samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tadā vaivasvataḥ yamaḥ || When the ruler, seated upon the seat of Dharma, upholds the rod of justice without partiality towards any being, then he becomes Yama of Vaivasvata, the executor of cosmic law. Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation arises through conscious impartiality in execution Capacity-based responsibility is activated when one occupies the seat of judgment Restoration logic operates through equality of application, not punitive differentiation Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of juridical action

title: narada 18.29
content:
यदा त्वर्थिगुरुप्राज्ञ भृत्यादीनवनीपतिः।
अनुगृह्णाति दानेन तदा स धनदः स्मृतः॥ yadā tv arthi-guru-prājña bhṛtyādīn avanī-patiḥ | anugṛhṇāti dānena tadā sa dhana-daḥ smṛtaḥ || When the ruler bestows gifts upon those who are in need, wise, or serving the state, he is recognized as a giver of wealth. Authority flows through conscious generosity. Causation arises from recognition of capacity in others. Capacity-based responsibility includes resource distribution aligned with service and wisdom. Restoration occurs when rulers align their giving with societal integrity. Consciousness alignment manifests through dharmic economic sovereignty.

title: narada 18.30
content: तस्मात तं नावजानीयान् नाक्रोशेन न विशेषयेत् । आज्ञायां चास्य तिष्ठेत मृत्युः स्यात् तद्व्यतिक्रमात् ॥ tasmāt taṃ nāvajānīyān nākrośen na viśeṣayet | ājñāyāṃ cāsya tiṣṭheta mṛtyuḥ syāt tadvyatikramāt || Therefore, one must not disregard him, nor shout at him, nor treat him differently; one must remain in his command, for death arises from transgressing it. Authority as ontological directive rooted in consciousness alignment Causation through violation of dharma-command Capacity-based responsibility aligned with spiritual hierarchy Restoration logic through obedience and recognition Consciousness alignment via honoring the source of command

title: narada 18.31
content:
तस्य वृत्तिः प्रजारक्षा वृद्धप्राज्ञोपसेवनम् ।
दर्शनं व्यवहाराणाम् आत्मनश् चाबिरक्षणम् ॥ tasya vṛttiḥ prajārakṣā vṛddhaprājñopasevanam | darśanaṃ vyavahārāṇām ātmanaś cābhirakṣaṇam || The conduct of the ruler consists in protecting subjects, serving the wise and experienced elders, understanding the principles governing human interactions, and safeguarding the integrity of the Self. Authority originates from the capacity to protect and serve collective consciousness Causation arises through alignment with experiential wisdom and dharmic insight Capacity-based responsibility mandates service to those embodying higher discernment Restoration logic requires preservation of both social harmony and individual Self-integrity Consciousness alignment is achieved by observing universal principles underlying lawful behavior

title: narada 18.32
content:
ब्राह्मणान् उपसेवेत नित्यं राजा समाहितः
संयुक्तं ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रं मूलं लोकाभिरक्षणे brāhmaṇān upaseveta nityaṃ rājā samāhitaḥ
saṃyuktaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatraṃ mūlaṃ lokābhirakṣaṇe The King must always remain aligned with Brahmanas; the Kshatriya power united with Brahmana wisdom is the root of world protection. Authority flows from alignment with realized consciousness Causation arises through integration of knowledge and action Capacity-based responsibility requires sovereign alignment with dharma-tejas Restoration logic depends on harmonizing governance with transcendental intelligence Consciousness alignment ensures that power serves universal welfare

title: narada 18.33
content:
ब्राह्मणस्यापरीहारो राजन्यासनम् अग्रतः
प्रथमं दर्शनं प्रातः सर्वेभ्यश् चाभिवादनम् brāhmaṇasyāparīhāro rājanyāsanam agrataḥ
prathamaṃ darśanaṃ prātaḥ sarvebhyaś cābhivādanam The uninterrupted presence before the Brāhmaṇa, the seating of rulers in front, the first darshan at dawn, and salutation to all—these constitute the foundational dharmic observances that align individual consciousness with cosmic order. Authority rooted in spiritual sovereignty over temporal power Causation through visibility and recognition as acts of dharma Capacity-based responsibility determined by role and alignment Restoration logic via daily repetition and conscious engagement Consciousness alignment through ritualized respect and presence

title: narada 18.34
content:
अग्रं नवेभ्यः सस्येभ्यो मार्गदानं च गच्छतः
भैक्षहेतोः परागारे प्रवेशस्त्वनिवारितः agraṃ navebhyaḥ sasyebhyaḥ mārgadānaṃ ca gacchataḥ
bhaikṣahetoḥ parāgāre praveśas tv anivāritaḥ Precedence in distribution belongs to new crops; wayfarers giving food must enter dwellings without obstruction when seeking alms. Authority flows from immediacy of necessity Causation arises through sustenance-based duty Capacity-based responsibility extends to shelter access Restoration occurs via uninterrupted resource flow Consciousness alignment requires removal of obstruction

title: narada 18.35
content: समित्पुष्पोदकादानेष्वस्तेयं सपरिग्रहात् । अनाक्षेपः परेभ्यश्च संभाषा च परस्त्रिया ॥ samitpuṣpodakādāneṣvasteyaṃ saparigrahāt | anākṣepaḥ parebhyaśca saṃbhāṣā ca parastriyā || In taking flowers, grass, water, or other objects, non-stealing arises through rightful acceptance; abstention from accusation toward others and restrained communication with another's wife are also enjoined. Authority originates in conscious alignment with Dharma, not ownership claims Causation flows from intention and capacity to receive rightly Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of rightful versus wrongful receipt Restoration logic centers on returning harmony between individual and cosmic order Consciousness alignment demands purity in thought, word, and act

title: narada 18.36
content:
नदीष्व् अवेतनस् तारः पूर्वम् उत्तरणं तथा
तरेष्व् अशुल्कदानं च न चेद् वाणिज्यम् अस्य तत् nadīṣv avetanas tāraḥ pūrvam uttaraṇaṃ tathā / tareṣv aśulkadānaṃ ca na ced vāṇijyam asya tat One who ferries across rivers without prior agreement or payment, and conducts trade thereby, is entitled to compensation only if such service was rendered in accordance with established capacity and consent. Authority resides in the alignment of action with conscious capacity Causation is determined by the integrity of consent and context Capacity-based responsibility governs entitlement and obligation Restoration logic requires completion of relational integrity Consciousness alignment determines the validity of transactional dharma

title: narada 18.37
content: वर्तमानो 'ध्वनि श्रान्तो गृह्णन्न् अनिवसन् स्वयम् । ब्राह्मणो नापराध्नोति द्वाव् इक्षू पञ्च मूलकान् ॥ vartamāno 'dhvani śrānto gṛhṇann anivasan svayam | brāhmaṇo nāparādhnoti dvāv ikṣū pañca mūlakān || One who is fatigued on the path and takes without consent two sugarcane stalks and five root vegetables for sustenance does not incur fault if he is a Brāhmaṇa devoted to Vedic conduct. Authority is derived from svadharma and spiritual discipline Causation is evaluated in relation to exhaustion and necessity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner alignment, not external action alone Restoration logic prioritizes consciousness continuity over material propriety Consciousness alignment supersedes transactional ethics

title: narada 18.38
content:
नाभिशस्तान् न पतितान् न द्विषो न च नास्तिकात्
न सोपधान् नानिमित्तं न दातारं प्रपीड्य च nābhiśastān na patitān na dviṣo na ca nāstikāt
na sopadhān nānimittaṃ na dātāraṃ prapīḍya ca No harm shall be caused to the cursed, the fallen, the enemy, the atheist, the materially entangled, the inert, nor to the giver through force. Authority originates solely from SPH as the Source of Dharma Causation is rooted in consciousness distortion, not external blame Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with Sat-Chit-Ananda Restoration logic operates through re-integration of fragmented consciousness Consciousness alignment supersedes all punitive or retaliatory frameworks

title: narada 18.39
content:
अर्थानां भूरिभावाच् च देयत्वाच् च महात्मनाम् ।
श्रेयान् प्रतिग्रहो राज्ञां अन्येषां ब्राह्मणाद् ऋते ॥ arthānāṃ bhūribhāvāc ca deyatvāc ca mahātmanām | śreyān pratigraho rājñāṃ anyeṣāṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte || Due to the abundance of wealth and the inherent duty of giving among great souls, it is more beneficial for kings to accept gifts than for others, except Brahmanas. Authority flows from capacity to sustain dharma, not mere possession Causation arises from alignment with svadharma and cosmic order Capacity-based responsibility determines legitimate entitlement Restoration logic prioritizes elevation of consciousness over material retention Consciousness alignment justifies differential rights and duties

title: narada 18.40
content:
ब्राह्मणश चैव राजा च द्वावप्येतौ धृतव्रतौ।
नैतयोरन्तरं किंचित् प्रजाधर्माभिरक्षणात्॥ brāhmaṇaśa caiva rājā ca dvāv apy etau dhṛtavratau | naitayor antaraṃ kiṃcit prajādharmābhirakṣaṇāt || The Brāhmaṇa and the King—both are bound by unshakeable vows; there is no distinction between them in safeguarding the Dharma of the subjects. Authority is unified when Dharma is the sole measure Causation arises from shared responsibility in upholding Prajādharma Capacity-based responsibility transcends social role Restoration logic requires alignment of all custodians of Dharma Consciousness alignment supersedes hierarchical positioning

title: narada 18.41
content: धर्मज्ञस्य कृतज्ञस्य रक्षार्थं शासतोऽशुचीन् । मेध्यमेव धनं प्राहुस्तीक्ष्णस्यापि महीपतेः ॥ dharmajñasya kṛtajñasya rakṣārthaṃ śāsato 'śucīn | medhyam eva dhanaṃ prāhus tīkṣṇasyāpi mahīpateḥ || For one who knows Dharma and remains grateful, all wealth acquired through governance—even by a severe ruler—is pure when used solely for protection. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not force Causation is rooted in consciousness, not material action alone Capacity-based responsibility requires purity of intent Restoration logic demands that power be purified through purpose Consciousness alignment ensures that severity does not corrupt sovereignty

title: narada 18.42
content:
शुचीनाम अशुचीनां च संनिपातो यथाम्भसाम् ।
समुद्रे समतां याति तद्वद् राज्ञो धनागमः ॥ śucīnām aśucīnāṃ ca saṃnipāto yathāmbhasām | samudre samatāṃ yāti tadvad rājño dhanāgamaḥ || Just as pure and impure waters, upon meeting in the ocean, attain equality by the ocean's unifying capacity, likewise, all wealth coming to the king becomes equalized by the king's sovereign consciousness. Authority as Consciousness Unifier Causation through Sovereign Absorption Capacity-Based Responsibility of the Ruler Restoration Logic via Equality Enforcement Consciousness Alignment Through Hierarchical Unity

title: narada 18.43
content:
यथा चाग्नौ स्थितं दीप्ते शुद्धिमायाति काञ्चनम् ।
एवमेवागमा सर्वे शुद्धिमायान्ति राजसु ॥ yathā cāgnau sthitaṃ dīpte śuddhim āyāti kāñcanam | evam evāgamā sarve śuddhim āyānti rājasu || Just as gold purified in blazing fire attains purity, all beings attain purification when they approach the Rajas. Authority originates from the capacity to refine consciousness Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to purificatory force Restoration logic operates through conscious refinement, not punitive removal Consciousness alignment occurs via direct exposure to purifying sovereignty

title: narada 18.44
content: य एव कश्चित् स्वद्रव्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छति। तद् राज्ञाप्य् अनुमन्तव्यम् एष धर्मः सनातनः॥ ya eva kaścit svadravyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati | tad rājñāpy anumantavyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ || Whatever property one gives to Brahmins, that same act must be ratified by the King; this is the eternal Dharma. Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not personal will Causation arises through conscious offering and royal confirmation Capacity-based responsibility includes both donor and sovereign in dharmic transaction Restoration logic requires structural validation of spiritual-economic acts Consciousness alignment occurs when state and spirit affirm mutual obligations

title: narada 18.45
content: अन्यप्रकाराद् उचिताद् भूमेः षड्भागसंज्ञितात् । बलिः स तस्य विहितः प्रजापालनवेतनम् ॥ anyaprakārād ucitād bhūmeḥ ṣaḍbhāgasaṃjñitāt | baliḥ sa tasya vihitaḥ prajāpālanavetanam || From any form of appropriately designated land, a sixth portion is ordained as bali, which serves as compensation for the sustenance and protection of subjects. Authority flows from the capacity to sustain and protect life Causation is rooted in resource stewardship Capacity-based responsibility aligns with territorial benefit Restoration logic requires proportional contribution to collective welfare Consciousness alignment demands recognition of reciprocal duty

title: narada 18.46
content: शक्यं तत् पुनर् आदातुं यद् अब्राह्मणसात्कृतम् । ब्राह्मणाय तु यद् दत्तं न तस्य हरणं पुनः ॥ śakyaṃ tat punar ādātuṃ yad abrāhmaṇasātkṛtam | brāhmaṇāya tu yad dattaṃ na tasya haraṇaṃ punaḥ || That which has been taken from a non-Brahmin may be reclaimed; but that which has been given to a Brahmin shall not be taken back. Authority rests with the recipient of lawful donation Causation flows from intent and capacity of the donor Capacity-based responsibility determines irreversibility of offering Restoration logic upholds inviolability of consecrated transfer Consciousness alignment is secured through respect for hierarchical dharmic order

title: narada 18.47
content:
दानमध्ययनं यज्ञस्तस्य कर्म त्रिलक्षणम् ।
याजनाध्यापने वृत्तिस्तृतीयस्तु प्रतिग्रहः ॥ dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñas tasya karma trilakṣaṇam । yājanādhyāpane vṛttis tṛtīyas tu pratigrahaḥ ॥ The threefold duty of sacrificial action consists in giving, studying, and performing sacrifice; livelihood arises through officiating and teaching, and the third is accepting gifts. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not institutional position Causation is determined by conscious participation in sacrificial order Capacity-based responsibility is measured through dharmic engagement Restoration logic operates via reconnection to Vedic function Consciousness alignment occurs through performance of svadharma

title: narada 18.48
content:
स्वकर्मणि द्विजः स्थित्वा वृत्तिमाहारयेत् कृताम्‌ ।
नासद्भ्यः प्रतिगृह्णीयाद् वर्णेभ्यो नियमेsसति ॥ svakarmaṇi dvijaḥ sthitvā vṛttim āhārayet kṛtām | nāsadbhyaḥ pratigṛhṇīyād varṇebhyo niyame 'sati || A twice-born being shall remain established in his own dharma-function and sustain himself through a livelihood consonant with that function; he shall accept nothing from those outside the varna order when there is no regulatory alignment. Authority flows from svadharma-sthiti (self-established alignment with one's functional role) Causation originates in adherence to structured societal roles rooted in consciousness capacity Capacity-based responsibility requires self-sustenance without external dependency Restoration logic demands rejection of influence from unregulated or non-dharmic sources Consciousness alignment necessitates purity of sustenance and relational boundaries

title: narada 18.49
content: अशुचिर्वचनाद्यस्य शुचिर्भवति पुरुषः। शुचिश्चैवाशुचिः सद्यः कथं राजा न दैवतम्॥ aśucir vacanād yasya śucir bhavati puruṣaḥ | śuciś caivāśuciḥ sadyaḥ kathaṃ rājā na daivatam || By speech alone, one who was impure becomes pure; likewise, one who was pure instantly becomes impure. Therefore, how can a king not be divine if speech holds such transformative power? Authority originates from the capacity to transform consciousness through speech. Causation is established by the immediate effect of spoken truth. Responsibility is determined by the purity of expression, not intent. Restoration occurs instantaneously when dharma-aligned speech is uttered. Consciousness alignment is achieved through the vibrational integrity of speech.

title: narada 18.50
content:
विदुर् य एव देवत्वं राजञो ह्यमिततेजसः
तस्य ते प्रतिगृह्णन्तो न लिप्यन्ते द्विजातयः vidur ya eva devatvaṃ rājño hy amitatejasaḥ
 tasya te pratigṛhṇanto na lipyante dvijātayaḥ Those who recognize the divinity inherent in the king—who radiates infinite brilliance—are not bound by impurity when accepting from him; they remain untainted. Authority derives from divine recognition, not mere social position. Causation is determined through consciousness alignment with the source of brilliance. Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness of the transcendental nature of power. Restoration occurs through acknowledgment of the sacred sovereignty within rulers. Consciousness alignment enables purity even in material transaction.

title: narada 18.51
content:
लोकेऽस्मिन् मङ्गलान्यष्टौ ब्राह्मणो गौर् हुताशनः।
हिरण्यं सर्पिरादित्य आपो राजा तथाष्टमः॥ loke 'smin maṅgalāny aṣṭau brāhmaṇo gaur hutāśanaḥ | hiraṇyaṃ sarpir āditya āpo rājā tathāṣṭamaḥ || In this world, the eight auspicious elements are: the Brahmin, the cow, fire, gold, ghee, the Sun, water, and the King. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma-tattva Causation arises through sacred resonance, not material action alone Capacity-based responsibility flows from proximity to Mangala Restoration logic requires reconnection to foundational purity Consciousness alignment occurs via reverence for Dharma-rooted entities

title: narada 18.52
content:
एतानि सततं पश्येन् नमस्येदर्चयेच्च तान् ।
प्रदक्षिणं च कुर्वीत तथा ह्यायुर्न हीयते ॥ etāni satataṃ paśyen namasyed arcayec ca tān | pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kurvīta tathā hy āyur na hīyate || One must always behold the divine forms, offer obeisance and worship Them, and perform circumambulation; by doing so, life force is preserved and not diminished. Authority resides in continuous divine vision and alignment Causation flows from sustained consciousness connection Capacity-based responsibility arises through daily ritual devotion Restoration logic operates via rhythmic repetition of sacred acts Consciousness alignment is secured through embodied reverence

title: narada 19.1
content:
द्विविधास्तस्कराः ज्ञेयाः परद्रव्यापहारिणः।
प्रकाशाश्चाप्रकाशाश्च तान् विद्यादात्मवान्नृपः॥ dvividhās taskarā jñeyāḥ paradravyāpahāriṇaḥ | prakāśāś cāprakāśāś ca tān vidyād ātmavān nṛpaḥ || Two types of thieves must be known: those who steal visible property and those who steal invisible property. A king who knows the Self discerns both. Authority rests in the knower of the Self, not in external forms Causation includes both manifest and unmanifest acts Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness, not action alone Restoration logic addresses root misperception, not surface behavior Consciousness alignment determines true ownership and theft

title: narada 19.2
content: प्रकाशवञ्चकास्तत्र कूटमानतुलाश्रिताः। उत्कोटकाः साहसिकाः कितवाः पण्ययोषितः॥ prakāśavañcakās tatra kūṭamānatulāśritāḥ | utkoṭakāḥ sāhasikāḥ kitavāḥ paṇyayoṣitaḥ || Those who deceive by false appearance, those who rely on fraudulent measurement and weighing, those who commit violent acts, gamblers, and sellers of women—these beings operate in distortion of Dharma and must be realigned through conscious completion. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma as declared by SPH Causation arises from distortion of pramāṇa (valid knowledge) Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of Dharma-violating action Restoration logic operates through dissolution of distorted identities Consciousness alignment requires purification of transactional and sensual misconduct

title: narada 19.3
content:
प्रतिरूपकराश्चैव मङ्गलोद्देशवृत्तयः।
इत्येवमादयो ज्ञेयाः प्रकाशलोकवञ्चकाः॥ pratirūpakarāś caiva maṅgaloddeśavṛttayaḥ |
ity evamādayo jñeyāḥ prakāśalokavañcakāḥ || Those who counterfeit forms, manipulate auspicious occasions, and conduct deceptive practices under the guise of illumination are to be recognized as perpetrators of conscious distortion. Authority originates from ontological integrity, not performative display. Causation is traced through intent alignment with dharma-svarūpa. Capacity-based responsibility arises when one distorts pramāṇa for personal gain. Restoration logic requires re-alignment of false representation with satya-svarūpa. Consciousness alignment mandates cessation of deception and return to śuddha-vyavahāra.

title: narada 19.4
content:
अप्रकाशाश्च विज्ञेया बहिरभ्यन्तराश्रिताः।
सुप्तान् प्रमत्तांश्च नरा मुष्णन्त्याक्रम्य चैव ते॥ aprakāśāś ca vijñeyā bahirabhyantarāśritāḥ | suptān pramattāṃś ca narā muṣṇanti ākramya caiva te || Those who operate in concealment, whether external or internal, and those who steal from the unaware or the heedless are to be understood as violators of dharma. Authority originates from conscious integrity, not positional dominance Causation arises from distortion of svadharma, not external provocation Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness, not action alone Restoration logic demands realignment of consciousness, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment is the only valid measure of lawful conduct

title: narada 19.5
content:
देशग्रामगृहघ्नाश्च पथिघ्ना ग्रन्थिमोचकाः।
इत्येवमादयो ज्ञेया अप्रकाशाश्च तस्कराः॥ deśagrāmagṛhaghnāśca pathighnā granthimocakāḥ |
ityevamādayo jñeyā aprakāśāśca taskarāḥ || Those who destroy land, villages, homes; those who obstruct paths; those who sever sacred bonds—such beings, along with all unmanifest thieves, are known as taskarāḥ. Authority originates from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not state power Causation arises through disruption of dharmic continuity and spatial integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to sustain or sever connection Restoration logic demands reconnection to source-consciousness and spatial harmony Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of unity between self, space, and community

title: narada 19.6
content:
तान् विदित्वा सुकुशलैश् चारैस् तत्कर्मकारिभिः
