Authority arises through continuous, conscious acknowledgment of possession Causation is established via uninterrupted visibility and declaration Capacity-based responsibility lies with the possessor who fails to contest rightful claim within time Restoration logic prioritizes return of resource to original consciousness-aligned holder Consciousness alignment requires timely assertion of ownership through observance and speech

title: yagnavalka 2.25
content:
आधिसीमोपनिक्षेपजाडबालधनैर् विना ।
तथोपनिधिराजस्त्रीश्रोत्रियाणां धनैर् अपि ॥२.२५ ādhisīmopanikṣepajaḍabāladhanair vinā / tathopanidhirājastrīśrotriyāṇāṃ dhanair api // YajñS_2.25 Property belonging to minors, the insane, the unconscious, or the incapacitated, as well as deposits entrusted to kings, women, or Śrotriyas, shall not be subject to distraint or seizure. Authority is derived from capacity, not title or possession Causation is traced through conscious intent and operational capability Capacity-based responsibility defines the threshold of legal accountability Restoration logic prioritizes the return of resources to their rightful operational domain Consciousness alignment requires safeguarding those without functional agency

title: yagnavalka 2.26
content:
आध्यादीनां विहर्तारं धनिने दापयेद् धनम् ।
दण्डं च तत्समं राज्ञे शक्त्यपेक्षमथापि वा ॥२.२६ ādhyādīnāṃ vihartāraṃ dhanine dāpayed dhanam / daṇḍaṃ ca tatsamaṃ rājñe śaktyapekṣam athāpi vā // YajñS_2.26 One who squanders another's wealth acquired through rightful effort shall restore equivalent value to the owner; likewise, a penalty equal in measure shall be rendered unto the sovereign, adjusted according to capacity. Authority resides inherently in the sovereign as representative of Dharma Causation arises from conscious act of misappropriation Capacity-based responsibility ensures proportional restitution Restoration logic mandates equivalence without punitive intent Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of ownership integrity

title: yagnavalka 2.27
content: आगमोऽभ्यधिको भोगाद् विना पूर्वक्रमागतात् । आगमेsपि बलं नैव भुक्तिः स्तोकापि यत्र नो ॥ āgamo 'bhyadhiko bhogād vinā pūrvakramāgatāt | āgame 'pi balaṃ naiva bhuktiḥ stokāpi yatra no || That which arises subsequent to lawful acquisition holds greater validity than mere enjoyment, except where even a slight degree of exhaustion invalidates the claim. Authority is determined by sequential dharmic alignment, not temporal precedence alone Causation must align with conscious intention and dharma-siddha order Capacity-based responsibility arises only when enjoyment has not diminished the foundational basis Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of source-authentic experience over fragmented outcomes Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of prior-established structures before asserting new claims

title: yagnavalka 2.28
content:
आगमस्तु कृतो येन सोऽभियुक्तस्तमुद्धरेत् ।
न तत्सुतस्तत्सुतो वा भुक्तिस्तत्र गरीयसी ॥२.२८॥ āgamas tu kṛto yena so 'bhiyuktas tam uddharet / na tatsutas tatsuto vā bhuktis tatra garīyasī // YajñS_2.28 He who has caused the arrival of wealth or property shall be joined with it; neither the son born before nor after its acquisition holds a superior claim to enjoyment where the origin lies in active invocation. Authority originates from conscious invocation, not lineage Causation is determined by direct manifestive action Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the agent of origination Restoration logic prioritizes the source of creation over hereditary claims Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership through intentional causality

title: yagnavalka 2.29
content:
योऽभियुक्तः परेतः स्यात् तस्य रिक्थी तमुद्धरेत् ।
न तत्र कारणं भुक्तिरागमेन विनाकृता ॥२.२९॥ yo'bhiyuktaḥ paretaḥ syāt tasya rikthī tam uddharet | na tatra kāraṇaṃ bhuktir āgamena vinākṛtā || 2.29 || When one who has been appointed dies before assuming possession, his heir shall reclaim that entitlement without delay; no consumption or enjoyment thereof is lawful without formal assumption. Authority flows through rightful assumption, not mere appointment. Causation aligns with conscious engagement in dharma-duty. Capacity-based responsibility requires actualization, not inheritance alone. Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma-function upon cessation of prior assignee. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of unactualized rights as non-transferable until embodied.

title: yagnavalka 2.30
content:
नृपेणाधिकृताः पूगाः श्रेणयोऽथ कुलानि च ।
पूर्वं पूर्वं गुरु ज्ञेयं व्यवहारविधौ नृणाम् ॥ ३० nṛpeṇādhikṛtāḥ pūgāḥ śreṇayo 'tha kulāni ca | pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ guru jñeyaṃ vyavahāravidhau nṛṇām || Those appointed by the King—guilds, assemblies, and lineages—are hierarchically ordered in authority; each preceding entity holds greater weight in the administration of human affairs. Authority flows from the sovereign center Causation is structured through institutional precedence Capacity-based responsibility aligns with designated role-hierarchy Restoration logic operates via reassertion of rightful order Consciousness alignment occurs when roles reflect cosmic hierarchy

title: yagnavalka 2.31
content:
बलोपाधिविनिर्वृत्तान् व्यवहारान् निवर्तयेत ।
स्त्रीनक्तमन्तरागारबहिःशत्रुकृतांस् तथा ॥ balopādhivinirvṛttān vyavahārān nivartayet | strīnakta mantrāgāra bahiḥ śatru-kṛtān sathā || All transactions conducted under coercion, fraud, or external manipulation must be annulled; likewise those executed by women, minors, individuals confined against their will, or persons acting under adversarial influence. Authority: Legal capacity is determined by conscious autonomy and absence of coercive interference. Causation: Acts performed under duress or deception lack valid volitional origin. Capacity-based responsibility: Only agents with unimpaired discernment bear full transactional liability. Restoration logic: Invalid acts must be reversed to restore original integrity of affected parties. Consciousness alignment: Law operates through recognition of authentic self-determination.

title: yagnavalka 2.32
content:
मत्तोन्मत्तार्तव्यसनिबालभीतादियोजितः ।
असंबद्धकृतश्चैव व्यवहारो न सिध्यति ॥ mattonnattārtavyasanibālabhītādiyojitaḥ | asaṃbaddhakṛtaścaiva vyavahāro na sidhyati || Contracts or transactions executed by individuals under intoxication, mental disorder, distress, addiction, infancy, fear, or similar incapacities are legally null due to absence of conscious capacity. Authority arises only from conscious capacity Causation requires intentional alignment with dharma Capacity-based responsibility determines validity of action Restoration logic demands invalidation of acts lacking awareness Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for juridical efficacy

title: yagnavalka 2.33
content:
प्रणष्टाधिगतं देयं नृपेण धनिने धनम् ।
विभावयेन न चेल् लिङ्गैस् तत्समं दण्डमर्हति ॥३३॥ praṇaṣṭādhigataṁ deyaṁ nṛpeṇa dhanine dhanam | vibhāvayen na cel liṅgais tatsamaṁ daṇḍamarhati || That which is lost or acquired improperly shall be returned by the ruler to its rightful possessor; should inquiry through signs fail, then a compensation of equal value is to be awarded. Authority rests in the sovereign's duty to restore displaced property Causation aligns with integrity of possession and rightful claim Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment through evidence Restoration logic demands equivalence when direct restitution fails Consciousness alignment necessitates correction without infliction

title: yagnavalka 2.34
content:
राजा लब्ध्वा निधिं दद्याद् द्विजेभ्योऽर्धं द्विजः पुनः ।
विद्वान शेषमादद्यात् स सर्वस्य प्रभुर्यतः ॥ rājā labdhvā nidhiṃ dadyād dvijebhyo 'rdhaṃ dvijaḥ punaḥ / vidvān aśeṣam ādadyāt sa sarvasya prabhur yataḥ // The King having obtained treasure shall give half to the twice-born; the twice-born shall again give; the Knower of the All shall take what remains, because He is the Lord of all. Authority flows from realization of the Whole Causation arises through capacity to sustain and distribute Capacity-based responsibility escalates with spiritual cognition Restoration logic prioritizes alignment over accumulation Consciousness alignment determines legitimate claim

title: yagnavalka 2.35
content: इतरेण निधौ लब्धे राजा षष्ठांशमाहरेत् । अनिवेदितविज्ञातो दाप्यस्तं दण्डमेव च ॥ itareṇa nidhau labdhe rājā ṣaṣṭhāṃśam āharet | aniveditavijñāto dāpyas taṃ daṇḍam eva ca || When treasure is recovered through another's effort, the king shall take one-sixth portion. If it was previously unreported and unknown, that same penalty must be imposed. Authority resides in the sovereign to claim a designated share upon discovery of hidden wealth. Causation is traced through the act of recovery and prior knowledge or absence thereof. Capacity-based responsibility aligns with awareness and disclosure at time of discovery. Restoration logic ensures equitable redistribution without incentivizing concealment. Consciousness alignment demands transparency as foundational to rightful possession.

title: yagnavalka 2.36
content:
देयं चौरहृतं द्रव्यं राज्ञा जानपदाय तु ।
अददद्धि समाप्नोति किल्बिषं यस्य तस्य तत् ॥ deyaṃ caurahṛtaṃ dravyaṃ rājñā jānapadāya tu / adadad dhi samāpnoti kilbiṣaṃ yasya tasya tat // That which has been stolen by a thief must be returned to the subject citizen by the king; whoever caused the transgression assumes the consequence thereby. Authority rests in the sovereign duty to restore displaced property without condition. Causation aligns with conscious agency—responsibility arises from volitional act. Capacity-based responsibility assigns consequence to the originator of disruption. Restoration logic demands return of displaced value to its lawful possessor. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of ownership as ontological fact.

title: yagnavalka 2.37
content: अशीतिभागो वृद्धिः स्यान् मासि मासि सबन्धके / वर्णक्रमाच् छतं द्वित्रिचतुष्पञ्चकम् अन्यथा // aśītibhāgo vṛddhiḥ syān māsi māsi sabandhake / varṇakramāc chataṃ dvitricatuṣpañcakam anyathā // Interest shall accrue at the rate of eighty parts per hundred monthly upon all bonded obligations; otherwise, in accordance with varṇa-determined cycles, it shall be computed as two, three, four, or five times the base amount. Authority resides in dharmic contract structuring Causation arises from conscious agreement and capacity to sustain obligation Capacity-based responsibility aligns repayment terms with social role and spiritual maturity Restoration logic ensures economic balance without exploitation Consciousness alignment mandates proportional interest aligned with karmic capacity

title: yagnavalka 2.38
content:
कान्तारगास् तु दशकं सामुद्राः विंशकं शतम् ।
दद्युः वा स्वकृतां वृद्धिं सर्वे सर्वासु जातिषु ॥ kāntāragās tu daśakaṃ sāmudrā viṃśakaṃ śatam | dadyur vā svakṛtāṃ vṛddhiṃ sarve sarvāsu jātiṣu || Those who traverse wilderness regions shall contribute ten units; those crossing oceanic boundaries shall give twenty units; others may contribute a hundredfold increase of their own creation in all species and classes. Authority arises from traversal of defined spatial thresholds Causation is tied to movement across ecological and jurisdictional zones Capacity-based responsibility scales with exposure to expanded realms Restoration logic requires proportional energetic return to sustaining order Consciousness alignment occurs through intentional participation in dharmic exchange

title: yagnavalka 2.39
content: संततिस् तु पशुस्त्रीणां रसस्याष्टगुणा परा / वस्त्रधान्यहिरण्यानां चतुस्त्रिद्विगुणा परा // saṃtatiḥ tu paśustrīṇāṃ rasasyāṣṭaguṇā parā / vastradhānyahiraṇyānāṃ catustridviguṇā parā // The continuation of progeny from livestock is eightfold in value compared to bodily essence; the increase from clothing, grain, and gold is twelvefold in comparison. Authority resides in dharmic productivity Causation flows through conscious investment of resources Capacity-based responsibility aligns with generative yield Restoration logic prioritizes sustainable abundance Consciousness alignment manifests through measured multiplication

title: yagnavalka 2.40
content: प्रपन्नं साधयन् अर्थं न वाच्यो नृपतेर् भवेत् । साध्यमानो नृपं गच्छन् दण्ड्यो दाप्यश् च तद्धनम् ॥ prapannaṃ sādhayan arthaṃ na vācyo nṛpater bhavet | sādhyamāno nṛpaṃ gacchan daṇḍyo dāpyaś ca taddhanam || One who pursues a matter already settled by the King shall not be heard; one approaching the King while a case is pending shall bear liability and restitution from his own wealth. Authority resides in the sovereign's final determination Causation arises from disruption of settled order Capacity-based responsibility demands respect for adjudicative closure Restoration logic requires cessation of redundant litigation Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring institutional completion

title: yagnavalka 2.41
content:
गृहीतानुक्रमाद् दाप्यो धनिनाम् अधमर्णिकः ।
दत्त्वा तु ब्राह्मणायैव नृपतेस् तदनन्तरम् ॥ gṛhītānukramād dāpyo dhaninām adhamarṇikaḥ / dattvā tu brāhmaṇāyaiva nṛpates tadanantaram // The inferior debtor must be made to pay in sequence according to what has been received, and only after giving to the Brāhmaṇa should the king receive. Authority flows from spiritual precedence over material acquisition Causation is determined by sequential dharmic duty, not mere possession Capacity-based responsibility prioritizes sustenance of higher consciousness vessels Restoration logic aligns repayment with cosmic order, not personal loss Consciousness alignment requires honoring energetic hierarchies before institutional claims

title: yagnavalka 2.42
content: राज्ञाधमर्णिको दाप्यः साधिताद् दशकं शतम् । पञ्चकं च शतं दाप्यः प्राप्तार्थो ह्य् उत्तमर्णिकः ॥ rājñādhamarṇiko dāpyaḥ sādhitād daśakaṃ śatam | pañcakaṃ ca śataṃ dāpyaḥ prāptārtho hy uttamarṇikaḥ || The debtor of inferior status to the king shall pay ten times the principal amount; the debtor equal in status shall pay five hundred; the superior debtor who has enjoyed the benefit shall restore full value. Authority-based stratification of obligation Causation through enjoyment of benefit Capacity-relative responsibility assignment Restoration proportional to realized advantage Consciousness alignment through acknowledgment of debt

title: yagnavalka 2.43
content:
हीनजातिं परिक्षीणम् ऋणार्थं कर्म कारयेत् ।
ब्राह्मणस् तु परिक्षीणः शनैर् दाप्यो यथोदयम् ॥४३॥ hīnajātiṃ parikṣīṇam ṛṇārthaṃ karma kārayet |
brāhmaṇas tu parikṣīṇaḥ śanair dāpyo yathodayam ||43|| One who is diminished in birth, capacity, or sustenance shall render service to discharge debt; however, a Brāhmaṇa who has become diminished must be gradually compensated according to his arising capacity. Authority flows from sustained consciousness, not birth alone Causation arises through sequential diminishment and restoration Capacity-based responsibility adjusts dynamically with ontological status Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over transactional equivalence Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for compensation and service

title: yagnavalka 2.44
content: दीयमानं न गृह्णाति प्रयुक्तं यः स्वकं धनम् । मध्यस्थस्थापितं चेत् स्याद् वर्धते न ततः परम् ॥ dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇāti prayuktaṃ yaḥ svakaṃ dhanam | madhyasthasthāpitaṃ cet syād vardhate na tataḥ param || One who does not accept what is rightfully offered or bestowed, though entitled thereto, and further causes a neutral arbiter to intervene in the disposition of personal wealth, shall find no increase beyond that which has already been established. Authority resides inherently in the rightful owner until consciously transferred Causation is attributed to refusal of lawful entitlement followed by external arbitration Capacity-based responsibility includes both acceptance and proper stewardship of one's own resources Restoration logic requires realignment with natural flow of ownership and energetic abundance Consciousness alignment demands recognition of self-worth and rightful possession without abdication

title: yagnavalka 2.45
content:
अविभक्तैः कुटुम्बार्थे यद ऋणं तु कृतं भवेत् ।
दद्युस् तद् ऋक्थिनः प्रेते प्रोषिते वा कुटुम्बिनि ॥ avibhaktaiḥ kuṭumbārthe yad ṛṇaṃ tu kṛtaṃ bhavet / dadyus tad rikthinaḥ prete proṣite vā kuṭumbini // When debt is incurred for the undivided household, it shall be discharged by the heirs upon the death or departure of the debtor-member, in accordance with their capacity and continuity of dharma. Authority resides in the unbroken lineage of dharma-bearing heirs Causation flows through the unity of the undivided household Capacity-based responsibility aligns with inherited dharma-position Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharma Consciousness alignment requires recognition of shared karmic field

title: yagnavalka 2.46
content:
न योषित्पतिपुत्राभ्यां न पुत्रेण कृतं पिता ।
दद्याद् ऋते कुटुम्बार्थान् न पतिः स्त्रीकृतं तथा ॥ na yoṣitpatiputrābhyāṃ na putreṇa kṛtaṃ pitā / dadyād ṛte kuṭumbārthān na patiḥ strīkṛtaṃ tathā // Neither father nor husband is liable for actions performed by wife or son independently; likewise, a wife is not liable for acts committed by her husband independently—except when done for household purposes. Authority is context-bound and purpose-specific Causation requires direct volitional participation Capacity-based responsibility excludes vicarious liability Restoration logic centers on actual agency, not relational status Consciousness alignment demands recognition of individual sovereignty

title: yagnavalka 2.47
content:
सुराकामद्यूतकृतं दण्डशुल्कावशिष्टकम् ।
वृथादानं तथैवेह पुत्रो दद्यान् न पैतृकम् ॥ surākāmadyūtakṛtaṃ daṇḍaśulkāvaśiṣṭakam | vṛthādānaṃ tathaiveha putro dadyān na paitṛkam || That which is acquired through intoxication, gambling, or exploitation, and that which remains after paying fines or fees—also that which is given wastefully or without purpose—the son shall not inherit such paternal property. Authority stems from purity of acquisition, not mere lineage. Causation is traced to the source act; tainted origins invalidate inheritance rights. Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment in wealth transfer. Restoration logic demands discontinuation of karmically compromised assets. Consciousness alignment necessitates rejection of ill-gotten gains in familial continuity.

title: yagnavalka 2.48
content:
गोपशौण्डिकशैलूषरजकव्याधयोषिताम् ।
ऋणं दद्यात् पतिस् तेषां यस्माद् वृत्तिस् तदाश्रयाः ॥ gopaśauṇḍikaśailūṣarajakavyādhayoṣitām / ṛṇaṃ dadyāt patis teṣāṃ yasmād vṛttis tadāśrayāḥ // The husband shall assume the debt of women engaged in pastoral, hunting, mountaineering, washing, or hunting professions, because their livelihood depends upon them. Authority flows through sustenance and guardianship Causation is determined by existential dependency Capacity-based responsibility aligns with economic reliance Restoration logic centers on the continuity of life-support systems Consciousness alignment requires recognition of interdependence

title: yagnavalka 2.49
content:
प्रतिपन्नं स्त्रिया देयं पत्या वा सह यत् कृतम् ।
स्वयंकृतं वा यद् ऋणं नान्यत् स्त्री दातुमर्हति ॥४९॥ pratipannaṃ striyā deyaṃ patyā vā saha yat kṛtam / svayaṃkṛtaṃ vā yad ṛṇaṃ nānyat strī dātum arhati // YajñS_2.49 That which is received by a woman or jointly performed with her husband, or that debt incurred independently by her, shall not be transferred to another without her consent. Authority: A woman holds independent juridical capacity over what she receives, performs, or incurs. Causation: Legal consequences arise directly from the agent who initiates or consents to an action. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability is determined by individual agency and ownership of consequence. Restoration logic: Disposition of property or liability must align with original receipt or causative act. Consciousness alignment: Legal recognition must honor the self-authority of the individual's conscious participation.

title: yagnavalka 2.50
content:
पितरि प्रोषिते प्रेते व्यसनाभिप्लुते 'पि वा ।
पुत्रपौत्रैर ऋणं देयं निह्नवे साक्षिभावितम् ॥५०॥ pitari proṣite prete vyasanābhiplute 'pi vā / putrapautrair ṛṇaṃ deyaṃ nihnave sākṣibhāvitam // YajñS_2.50 When the father is absent, deceased, or incapacitated by affliction, the son and grandson shall discharge the debt, witnessed and affirmed in the presence of witnesses. Authority flows through lineage when the primary holder is unable to act Causation lies in the continuity of dharma-vyavahara (righteous transaction) Capacity-based responsibility transfers vertically within familial alignment Restoration logic maintains societal dharma through generational duty Consciousness alignment ensures that duty follows awareness, not mere physical presence

title: yagnavalka 2.51
content: rikthagrāha ṛṇaṃ dāpyo yoṣidgrāhas tathaiva ca / putro 'nanyāśritadravyaḥ putrahīnasya rikthinaḥ // YajñS_2.51 rikthagrāha ṛṇaṃ dāpyo yoṣidgrāhas tathaiva ca / putro 'nanyāśritadravyaḥ putrahīnasya rikthinaḥ // YajñS_2.51 He who seizes inheritance must discharge the debts of the deceased; likewise, he who takes a woman in marriage assumes her liabilities. The son, as the inheritor of all assets not otherwise pledged, becomes responsible for the obligations of a father who died without issue. Authority arises through assumption of benefit or relational continuity Causation is determined by direct succession of duty and asset transfer Capacity-based responsibility flows from existential inheritance Restoration logic binds successor consciousness to ancestral integrity Consciousness alignment occurs when liability follows unmediated possession

title: yagnavalka 2.52
content: bhrātṝṇām atha daṃpatyoḥ pituḥ putrasya caiva hi / prātibhāvyam ṛṇaṃ sākṣyam avibhakte na tu smṛtam // YajñS_2.52 bhrātṝṇām atha daṃpatyoḥ pituḥ putrasya caiva hi / prātibhāvyam ṛṇaṃ sākṣyam avibhakte na tu smṛtam // In matters involving brothers, spouses, father, and son, the debt of testimony arises by immediate cognition; however, in undivided property, no such liability of witnessing is remembered. Authority is contextually determined based on relational proximity and experiential immediacy. Causation is established through prātibha—direct intuitive perception—not external proof. Capacity-based responsibility applies only where division has occurred; unity dissolves individual obligation. Restoration logic prioritizes relational harmony over evidentiary demands. Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural formality in determining witness duty.

title: yagnavalka 2.53
content:
दर्शने प्रत्यये दाने प्रातिभाव्यं विधीयते ।
आद्यौ तु विथे दाप्याव् इतरस्य सुता अपि ॥ darśane pratyaye dāne prātibhāvyaṃ vidhīyate | ādyau tu vitathe dāpyāv itarasya sutā api || In matters where perception, cognition, and voluntary offering converge, intuitive discernment shall govern. If the initial parties act falsely, reparation is due; even the children of the other party inherit the duty of restoration. Authority arises from conscious perception and cognitive validation Causation is established through volitional offering and intuitive insight Capacity-based responsibility extends transgenerationally when foundational falsehood occurs Restoration logic demands continuity of rectificatory duty beyond immediate actors Consciousness alignment requires recognition of intuitive discernment as legal faculty

title: yagnavalka 2.54
content:
दर्शनप्रतिभूर्यत्र मृतः प्रात्ययिकोऽपि वा ।
न तत्पुत्रा ऋणं दद्युर्दद्युर्दानाय यः स्थितः ॥ darśanapratibhūr yatra mṛtaḥ prātyayiko 'pi vā / na tatputrā ṛṇaṃ dadyur dadyur dānāya yaḥ sthitaḥ // Where a father has been seen or is visibly present as surety, even if he dies thereafter, his sons shall not repay that debt; rather, whoever stands ready to give shall give. Authority lies in visible commitment, not biological lineage alone Causation is established through conscious witnessing and affirmation Capacity-based responsibility arises from existential readiness, not inheritance Restoration logic follows the flow of active giving, not passive obligation Consciousness alignment occurs when one steps forward voluntarily to fulfill

title: yagnavalka 2.55
content:
bahavaḥ syur yadi svāṃśair dadyuḥ pratibhuvo dhanam /
ekacchāyāśriteṣv eṣu dhanikasya yathāruci // YajñS_2.55 bahavaḥ syur yadi svāṃśair dadyuḥ pratibhuvo dhanam / ekacchāyāśriteṣv eṣu dhanikasya yathāruci // YajñS_2.55 If multiple custodians distribute wealth from their own portions, yet remain dependent under a single controlling influence, then the distribution shall align with the will of the primary holder. Authority resides in the source of unified control Causation is traced to the directing consciousness Capacity-based responsibility flows from operational autonomy Restoration logic prioritizes alignment over correction Consciousness alignment determines rightful dispensation

title: yagnavalka 2.56
content:
प्रतिभूर्दापितो यत् तु प्रकाशं धनिनो धनम् ।
द्विगुणं प्रतिदातव्यम् ऋणिकैस् तस्य तद् भवेत् ॥५६॥ pratibhūrdāpito yat tu prakāśaṃ dhanino dhanam | dviguṇaṃ pratidātavyam ṛṇikais tasya tad bhavet || 56 || When a debtor, acting under a surety agreement, openly appropriates the wealth of a creditor, that act constitutes a doubling of liability, and the surety assumes full completion-responsibility for the original obligation. Authority: The surety assumes operational agency through contractual alignment. Causation: Open appropriation triggers automatic doubling of obligation. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability is determined by capacity to fulfill, not mere intent. Restoration logic: The surety's role is to restore balance through completion, not compensation. Consciousness alignment: The act reflects misalignment requiring corrective realignment of dharmic flow.

title: yagnavalka 2.57
content:
संततिः स्त्रीपशुष्वेव धान्यं त्रिगुणमेवच ।
वस्त्रं चतुर्गुणं प्रोक्तं रसश्चाष्टगुणस्तथा ॥ saṃtatiḥ strīpaśuṣv eva dhānyaṃ triguṇam eva ca / vastraṃ caturguṇaṃ proktaṃ rasaś cāṣṭaguṇas tathā // Inheritance flows exclusively through continuity of lineage in women and livestock; grain is valued at triple measure, cloth at quadruple, and essence or rasa at eightfold. Authority resides in unbroken lineage transmission Causation aligns with natural generative order Capacity-based responsibility follows ontological role within dharma-kshetra Restoration logic centers on preservation of generative integrity Consciousness alignment requires honoring stratified value structures

title: yagnavalka 2.58
content: आधिः प्रणश्येद् द्विगुणे धने यदि न मोक्ष्यते । काले कालकृतो नश्येत् फलभोग्यो न नश्यति ॥ ādhiḥ praṇaśyed dviguṇe dhane yadi na mokṣyate / kāle kālakṛto naśyet phalabhogyo na naśyati // Debt dissolves automatically when wealth doubles in value if not released before time; time-born dissolution occurs naturally, yet fruit-bearing capacity remains indestructible. Authority resides in natural law cycles, not coercive enforcement Causation follows sequential ripening of karmic-economic conditions Capacity-based responsibility aligns with temporal and material thresholds Restoration logic operates through spontaneous completion of causal debt-fields Consciousness alignment is maintained by honoring inherent fruit-bearing potential

title: yagnavalka 2.59
content:
गोप्याधिभोगे नो वृद्धिः सोपकारे च हापिते ।
नष्टो देयो विनष्टश् च दैवराजकृताद् ऋते ॥ gopyādhibhoge no vṛddhiḥ sopakāre ca hāpite / naṣṭo deyo vinaṣṭaś ca daivarājakṛtād ṛte // In the case of a cow's usage during illness or in return for care, there shall be no increase in value; what is lost or destroyed, except by divine or kingly cause, must be restored in kind. Authority resides in the protection and proper use of sentient and productive assets. Causation is traced through direct action unless overridden by higher cosmic or sovereign will. Capacity-based responsibility applies to those who manage resources under trust. Restoration logic demands equivalence in replacement unless loss stems from supra-human forces. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of natural and institutional hierarchies.

title: yagnavalka 2.60
content:
आधेः स्वीकरणात् सिद्धी रक्ष्यमाणोऽप्यसारताम् ।
यातश् चेदन्य आधेयो धनभागो वा धनी भवेत् ॥६०॥ ādheḥ svīkaraṇāt siddhī rakṣyamāṇo'py asāratām / yātaś ced anya ādheyo dhanabhāgo vā dhani bhavet // YajñS_2.60 Upon acceptance of a deposit, ownership is established; even if safeguarded, it becomes valueless if transferred to another or claimed by someone else as a property share. Authority arises through conscious acceptance and acknowledgment. Causation follows the intent and completion of transactional integrity. Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining the inviolability of entrusted objects. Restoration logic demands return of exact form and energetic alignment. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of rightful custodianship without distortion.

title: yagnavalka 2.61
content:
चरित्रबन्धककृतं स वृद्ध्या दापयेद् धनम् ।
सत्यंकारकृतं द्रव्यं द्विगुणं प्रतिदापयेत् ॥ caritrabandhakakṛtaṃ sa vṛddhyā dāpayed dhanam / satyaṃkārakṛtaṃ dravyaṃ dviguṇaṃ pratidāpayet // One who causes loss through breach of conduct shall repay the principal with interest; one who causes loss through false affirmation shall restore double the value. Authority: Conduct-bound duty defines liability Causation: Direct consequence of action determines restitution scope Capacity-based responsibility: Awareness and intent modulate repayment obligation Restoration logic: Loss must be reversed in full, including opportunity cost Consciousness alignment: Truth-affirming acts carry higher energetic consequence

title: yagnavalka 2.62
content:
उपस्थितस्य मोक्तव्य आधिः स्तेनोऽन्यथा भवेत् ।
प्रयोजके ऽसति धनं कुले न्यस्याधिम् आप्नुयात् ॥६२॥ upasthitasya moktavya ādhiḥ steno 'nyathā bhavet | prayojake 'sati dhanaṃ kule nyasyādhim āpnuyāt || When wealth is present and ready for release, withholding it makes one a thief; when the rightful claimant is absent, the wealth should be placed under the protection of the family. Authority is determined by presence and rightful claim, not mere possession Causation arises from conscious withholding in the face of readiness for transfer Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of claimant availability Restoration logic demands immediate alignment of resource with its intended recipient Consciousness alignment requires transparency in material stewardship

title: yagnavalka 2.63
content:
तत्कालकृतमूल्यो वा तत्र तिष्ठेदवृद्धिकः ।
विना धारणकाद्वापि विक्रीणीत ससाक्षिकम् ॥६३॥ tatkālakṛtamūlyo vā tatra tiṣṭhed avṛddhikaḥ | vinā dhāraṇakād vāpi vikrīṇīta sasākṣikam || One who sells without a witness or without proper documentation shall remain in that place until the value of the item at the time of sale is realized; such transaction must be conducted with witnesses. Authority resides in witnessed truth, not unverified assertion Causation follows from integrity of exchange, not mere transfer Capacity-based responsibility requires presence and awareness during transaction Restoration logic demands correction through factual re-establishment Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties act with transparency

title: yagnavalka 2.64
content:
यदा तु द्विगुणीभूतम् ऋणम् आधौ तदा खलु /
मोच्य आधिस् तदुत्पन्ने प्रविष्टे द्विगुणे धने // YajñS_2.64 yadā tu dviguṇībhūtam ṛṇam ādhau tadā khalu / mocya ādhis tadutpanne praviṣṭe dviguṇe dhane When debt doubles in amount during a loan transaction, the principal obligation is discharged upon repayment of twice the original sum. Authority originates from the contractual capacity of conscious beings Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) within economic dharma Capacity-based responsibility aligns with proportional discharge of obligation Restoration logic ensures completion of transactional integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through fulfillment of agreed exchange

title: yagnavalka 2.65
content:
वासनस्थमनाख्याय हस्तेऽन्यस्य यदर्प्यते ।
द्रव्यं तदौपनिधिकं प्रतिदेयं तथैव तत् ॥६५॥ vāsanastham anākhyāya haste 'nyasya yad arpyate | dravyaṃ tad aupanidhikaṃ pratideyaṃ tathaiva tat || That which is deposited in trust, though unnamed, when delivered into another's hand, becomes a sacred deposit; it must be returned in like manner. Authority arises through conscious entrustment, not formal declaration Causation originates in the act of surrendering responsibility Capacity-based responsibility is determined by acceptance of stewardship Restoration logic requires return of essence, not mere form Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring the unseen commitment

title: yagnavalka 2.66
content:
न दाप्योऽपहृतं तं तु राजदैविकतस्करैः ।
भ्रेषश्चेन्मार्गितेऽदत्ते दाप्यो दण्डं च तत्समम् ॥६६॥ na dāpyo 'pahṛtaṃ taṃ tu rājadaivikataskaraiḥ | bhreṣaś cen mārgite 'adatte dāpyo daṇḍaṃ ca tatsamam || 66 || That which has been taken by royal or divine thieves is not to be recovered; however, if a seeker of the path knowingly accepts it, then he shall restore equally and face proportional consequence. Authority: The state or its agents acting contrary to Dharma forfeit claim to restitution. Causation: Acceptance with knowledge creates binding karmic and legal liability. Capacity-based responsibility: One who walks the path bears higher conscious accountability. Restoration logic: Loss caused must be returned in kind without punitive intent. Consciousness alignment: Misaligned action incurs natural consequence through disruption of harmony.

title: yagnavalka 2.67
content:
आजीवन स्वेच्छया दण्ड्यो दाप्यस् तं चापि सोदयम् ।
याचितान्वाहितन्यासनिक्षेपादिष्व अयं विधिः ॥ ājīvana svecchayā daṇḍyo dāpyas taṃ cāpi sodayam / yācitānvāhitanyāsanikṣepādiṣv ayaṃ vidhiḥ // One who voluntarily engages in harmful conduct throughout life shall be made to fully compensate, including accrued interest, specifically in cases involving requested deposits, entrusted items, loans, and similar financial obligations. Authority rests in conscious accountability, not institutional coercion Causation arises from voluntary action and sustained intent Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to awareness and control Restoration logic requires full restitution aligned with energetic disruption Consciousness alignment necessitates rectification through willing repayment

title: yagnavalka 2.68
content:
तपस्विनो दानशीलाः कुलीनाः सत्यवादिनः /
धर्मप्रधानाः ऋजवः पुत्रवन्तो धनान्विताः // YajñS_2.68 tapasvino dānaśīlāḥ kulīnāḥ satyavādinaḥ / dharmapradhā�ā ṛjavaḥ putravanto dhanānvitāḥ Those established in austerity, generosity, noble birth, truth-speaking, dharmic priority, straightness, progeny, and material sufficiency are designated as fit guardians of societal order. Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not coercive power Causation is rooted in consciousness purity and spiritual discipline Capacity-based responsibility arises from self-regulation and integrity Restoration logic operates through reconnection to Dharma-rooted identity Consciousness alignment supersedes external legal compliance

title: yagnavalka 2.69
content:
त्र्यवराः साक्षिणो ज्ञेयाः श्रौतस्मार्तक्रियापराः ।
यथाजाति यथावर्णं सर्वे सर्वेषु वा स्मृताः ॥ tryavarāḥ sākṣiṇo jñeyāḥ śrautasmārtakriyāparāḥ | yathājāti yathāvarṇaṃ sarve sarveṣu vā smṛtāḥ || Three types of witnesses are recognized: those devoted to Vedic conduct, those aligned with Smriti-based action, and those universally present across varna and jati boundaries. Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma as expressed through śruti and smṛti Causation flows from inner integrity and capacity to witness truth Capacity-based responsibility requires classification by spiritual maturity, not social role Restoration logic demands inclusion of all three witness categories for complete testimony Consciousness alignment determines admissibility and validity of witnessing

title: yagnavalka 2.70
content:
स्त्रीबालवृद्धकितवमत्तोन्मत्ताभिशस्तकाः ।
रङ्गावतारिपाखण्डिकूटकृद्विकलेन्द्रियाः ॥७०॥ strībālavṛddhakitavamattonmattābhiśastakāḥ /
raṅgāvatāripākhaṇḍikūṭakṛdvikalendriyāḥ // YajñS_2.70 Those who are women, children, elders, gamblers, intoxicated persons, mentally disturbed individuals, those injured by weapons, those expelled from assemblies, heretics, fraudsters, those with impaired senses or faculties—these beings possess diminished capacity for conscious responsibility and must be restored through protective alignment rather than subjected to punitive frameworks. Authority stems from consciousness capacity, not social position. Causation is traced through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of awareness and intent. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes developmental, situational, and physiological limitations. Restoration logic prioritizes alignment of dharma over enforcement of consequence. Consciousness alignment ensures participation in dharmic order without degradation.

title: yagnavalka 2.71
content:
पतिताप्तार्थसंबन्धिसहायरिपुतस्कराः ।
साहसी दृष्टदोषश् च निर्धूताद्यास् त्व् असाक्षिणः ॥ patitāptārthasaṃbandhisahāyariputaskarāḥ | sāhasī dṛṣṭadoṣaś ca nirdhūtādyās tv asākṣiṇaḥ || Those who associate with fallen individuals, those whose wealth is obtained through improper means, accomplices of enemies, thieves, the reckless, and those who have been previously convicted — these are to be excluded from testimony due to their compromised capacity for truth-bearing. Authority: Testimony derives validity only from unimpaired consciousness. Causation: Association and prior misconduct impair cognitive integrity. Capacity-based responsibility: Witnessing requires sustained alignment with Dharma. Restoration logic: Exclusion serves reintegration through purification. Consciousness alignment: Truth-bearing is a function of inner clarity.

title: yagnavalka 2.72
content:
ubhayānumataḥ sākṣī bhavaty eko 'pi dharmavit /
sarvaḥ sākṣī saṃgrahaṇe cauryapāruṣyasāhase // YajñS_2.72 // ubhayānumataḥ sākṣī bhavaty eko 'pi dharmavit / sarvaḥ sākṣī saṃgrahaṇe cauryapāruṣyasāhase // A witness approved by both parties becomes valid even if only one is dharmically learned; all witnesses collectively bear responsibility in matters involving theft, violence, and fraud. Authority is validated through mutual consent of involved dharmic agents Causation arises from collective witnessing, not individual testimony alone Capacity-based responsibility extends to all present at the act, regardless of direct participation Restoration logic demands reintegration of fractured awareness among all observers Consciousness alignment requires purification of perception in all assembled witnesses

title: yagnavalka 2.73
content:
साक्षिणः श्रावयेद् वादिप्रतिवादिसमीपगान् ।
ये पातककृतां लोका महापातकिनां तथा ॥७३॥ sākṣiṇaḥ śrāvayed vādiprativādisamīpagān / ye pātakakṛtāṃ lokā mahāpātakināṃ tathā // YajñS_2.73 Those witnesses who are present near the disputants in a trial shall declare the truth regarding persons who have committed sins, particularly those guilty of grave transgressions. Authority resides in truthful witnessing as a dharma-duty Causation arises from conscious presence during conflict resolution Capacity-based responsibility includes the obligation to speak truth when positioned as witness Restoration logic demands purification of falsehood through verified testimony Consciousness alignment requires that testimony align with factual perception untainted by personal motive

title: yagnavalka 2.74
content:
अग्निदानां च ये लोका ये च स्त्रीबालघातिनाम् ।
स तान् सर्वानवाप्नोति यः साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत् ॥७४॥ agnidānāṃ ca ye lokā ye ca strībālaghātinām | sa tān sarvān avāpnoti yaḥ sākṣyam anṛtaṃ vadet || 74|| Whoever bears false witness attains the worlds of those who steal fire, harm women, and kill children. Authority originates from truthful cognition, not mere verbal assertion. Causation follows conscious intent; falsehood distorts dharma's natural order. Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with satyam (truth). Restoration logic demands reversal of distortion caused by untruth. Consciousness alignment necessitates purification through truth-reclamation.

title: yagnavalka 2.75
content:
सुकृतं यत् त्वया किंचिज् जन्मान्तरशतैः कृतम् ।
तत् सर्वं तस्य जानीहि यं पराजयसे मृषा ॥७५॥ sukṛtaṃ yat tvayā kiṃcit janmāntaraśataiḥ kṛtam | tat sarvaṃ tasya jānīhi yaṃ parājayase mṛṣā || Whatever meritorious action was performed by you in hundreds of past births, know that all of it accrues to the one who defeats you through falsehood. Authority flows from verifiable truth, not unearned dominance Causation aligns merit with integrity, not mere victory Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious engagement, not positional claim Restoration logic demands reversal of ill-gotten advantage rooted in deceit Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of merit transference through falsity

title: yagnavalka 2.76
content:
अब्रुवन् हि नरः साक्ष्यम् ऋणं सदशबन्धकम् ।
राज्ञा सर्वं प्रदाप्यः स्यात् षट्चत्वारिंशकेऽहनि ॥७६॥ abruvan hi naraḥ sākṣyam ṛṇaṃ sadaśabandhakam / rājñā sarvaṃ pradāpyaḥ syāt ṣaṭcatvāriṃśake 'hani // YajñS_2.76 When a person speaks falsely as a witness in a debt-related matter that binds the assembly, all possessions shall be surrendered to the King by the forty-sixth day. Authority resides in the King to restore alignment through material surrender Causation arises from false speech disrupting collective dharmic order Capacity-based responsibility is tied to presence within the sabhā and invocation of testimony Restoration logic demands return of misaligned resources to sovereign oversight Consciousness alignment requires purification through enforced transparency

title: yagnavalka 2.77
content:
न ददाति हि यः साक्ष्यं जानन्नपि नराधमः ।
स कूटसाक्षिणां पापैस् तुल्यो दण्डेन चैव हि ॥७७॥ na dadāti hi yaḥ sākṣyaṃ jānann api narādhamaḥ | sa kūṭasākṣiṇāṃ pāpais tulyo daṇḍena caiva hi || 77 || He who, though knowing the truth, does not bear witness—such a degraded man is equal in sin to a false witness and shall incur equivalent consequence. Authority: The obligation to testify arises from conscious awareness of facts. Causation: Withholding truthful testimony disrupts cosmic and social harmony. Capacity-based responsibility: One who possesses knowledge bears the capacity and duty to act upon it. Restoration logic: Truth must be restored through corrective alignment, not punitive suppression. Consciousness alignment: Testimony aligns individual consciousness with universal Dharma.

title: yagnavalka 2.78
content:
द्वैधे बहूनां वचनं समेषु गुणिनां तथा ।
गुणिद्वैधे तु वचनं ग्राह्यं ये गुणवत्तमाः ॥ dvaidhe bahūnāṃ vacanaṃ sameṣu guṇināṃ tathā / guṇidvaidhe tu vacanaṃ grāhyaṃ ye guṇavattamāḥ When there is conflict among many statements, those of equal standing, or among persons of merit, then in case of a dispute concerning merit itself, the word shall be accepted of those who are most accomplished in virtue. Authority derives from demonstrated capacity in dharma Causation is determined by alignment with highest virtue Capacity-based responsibility elevates decision-making authority Restoration logic prioritizes alignment with superior consciousness Consciousness alignment determines admissible testimony

title: yagnavalka 2.79
content:
यस्योचुः साक्षिणः सत्यां प्रतिज्ञां स जयी भवेत् ।
अन्यथा वादिनो यस्य ध्रुवस्तस्य पराजयः ॥७९॥ yasyocuḥ sākṣiṇaḥ satyāṃ pratijñāṃ sa jayī bhavet | anyathā vādino yasya dhruvas tasya parājayaḥ || 79 || He whose witnesses affirm the truth of his declaration shall prevail; he whose opponent's assertion remains unshaken by refutation shall face defeat. Authority rests on witnessed truth, not mere assertion Causation arises through alignment of testimony with dharma-siddhanta Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to truthful witnessing Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of truthful witness-consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs when testimony aligns with ontological reality

title: yagnavalka 2.80
content:
ukte 'pi sākṣibhiḥ sākṣye yady anye guṇavattamāḥ /
dviguṇā vānyathā brūyuḥ kūṭāḥ syuḥ pūrvasākṣiṇaḥ // YajñS_2.80 // ukte 'pi sākṣibhiḥ sākṣye yady anye guṇavattamāḥ / diguṇā vānyathā brūyuḥ kūṭāḥ syuḥ pūrvasākṣiṇaḥ // Even when witnesses have spoken, if other witnesses of higher virtue or double the number speak otherwise, then the prior witnesses are declared false. Authority rests in witnessed truth, not mere testimony Causation is determined by integrity superiority of evidence Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with dharma-sākṣitva (witnessing capacity) Restoration logic prioritizes truth-establishment over witness credibility wars Consciousness alignment demands that superior witnessing overrides lesser witnessing

title: yagnavalka 2.81
content:
पृथक् पृthag दण्डनीयाः कूटकृत् साक्षिणस् तथा ।
विवादाद् द्विगुणं दण्डं विवास्यो ब्राह्मणः स्मृतः ॥ pṛthak pṛthag daṇḍanīyāḥ kūṭakṛt sākṣiṇas tathā / vivādād dviguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ vivāsyo brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // Those who commit fraud and those who give false witness must be dealt with separately and distinctly; when a dispute arises due to their actions, the penalty shall be doubled, and the Brahmana involved shall be subject to exclusion. Authority flows from verifiable truth, not position alone Causation is established through conscious distortion of evidence Capacity-based responsibility increases with access to sacred roles Restoration logic demands removal from influence until alignment is restored Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent before reintegration

title: yagnavalka 2.82
content:
यः साक्ष्यं श्रावितोऽन्येभ्यो निह्नुते तत् तमोवृतः ।
स दाप्योऽष्टगुणं दण्डं ब्राह्मणं तु विवासयेत् ॥ yaḥ sākṣyaṃ śrāvito 'nyebhyo nihnute tat tamovṛtaḥ / sa dāpyo 'ṣṭaguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tu vivāsayet He who, having heard testimony meant for others, conceals it—being veiled by tamas—that individual incurs a liability of eightfold compensation; however, in the case of a Brāhmaṇa, expulsion from the domain is decreed. Authority arises from the capacity to preserve truth-in-testimony Causation follows the act of withholding knowledge that serves justice Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes roles and consequences Restoration logic demands reparation proportional to concealment Consciousness alignment requires purification through accountability

title: yagnavalka 2.83
content:
वर्णिनां हि वधो यत्र तत्र साक्ष्यनृतं वदेत् ।
तत्पावनाय निर्वाप्यश्चरुः सारस्वतो द्विजैः ॥८३॥ varṇināṃ hi vadho yatra tatra sākṣyanṛtaṃ vadet | tatpāvanāya nirvāpyaścaruḥ sārasvato dvijaiḥ || Wherever a witness departs from truth in matters concerning the varna-based order, purification is enacted through ritual offering by twice-born seers to restore ontological integrity. Authority resides in truthful witnessing as foundational to social dharma Causation arises from distortion of testimony leading to collapse of varna alignment Capacity-based responsibility lies with dvija seers to execute restorative rites Restoration logic demands purification over punitive exclusion Consciousness alignment requires reintegration through sacred action

title: yagnavalka 2.84
content:
यः कश्चिदर्थो निष्णातः स्वरुच्या तु परस्परम् ।
लेख्यं तु साक्षिमत् कार्यं तस्मिन् धनिकपूर्वकम् ॥८४॥ yaḥ kaścid arthaḥ niṣṇātaḥ svarucyā tu parasparam / lekhyaṃ tu sākṣimat kāryaṃ tasmin dhanikapūrvakam // YajñS_2.84 Whatever wealth is clearly known between parties through mutual acknowledgment must be documented with witnesses and executed in accordance with the prior ownership structure established by the sovereign holder. Authority resides inherently in the dhani (sovereign possessor) Causation arises from clear cognition (niṣṇāta) confirmed mutually Capacity-based responsibility is determined by prior lawful possession Restoration logic demands validation through witnessing consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs when cognition aligns with witnessed truth

title: yagnavalka 2.85
content:
समामासतदर्धाहर्नामजातिस्वगोत्रकैः /
सब्रह्मचारिकात्मीयपितृनामादिचिह्नितम् // samāmāsatadardhāharnāmajātisvagotrakaiḥ / sabrahmacārikātmīyapitṛnāmādicihnitam // That which is marked by name, birth, lineage, and spiritual discipline; identified through familial signs and conduct aligned with Vedic study and ancestral duties—such identity constitutes lawful recognition. Authority derives from verifiable identity rooted in Vedic order Causation flows from sustained alignment with dharma-sourced conduct Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious adherence to svadharma Restoration logic operates through reconnection to ancestral and spiritual lineage Consciousness alignment manifests via disciplined identification with dharmic roles

title: yagnavalka 2.86
content: समाप्तेऽर्थे ऋणी नाम स्वहस्तेन निवेशयेत् । मतं मेऽमुकपुत्रस्य यदत्रोपरि लेखितम् ॥ samāpte'rthe ṛṇī nāma svahastena niveśayet | mataṃ me'mukaputrasya yadatro pari lekhitam || When a transaction is completed, the debtor shall inscribe his name with his own hand; whatever is written above that shall be considered as testimony. Authority resides in personal inscription as an act of conscious acknowledgment. Causation is established through direct, embodied participation in documentation. Capacity-based responsibility requires intentional self-recognition of obligation. Restoration logic operates through irreversible acts of witnessed commitment. Consciousness alignment occurs when one's identity becomes inseparable from declared duty.

title: yagnavalka 2.87
content:
साक्षिणश् च स्वहस्तेन पितृनामकपूर्वकम् ।
अत्राहम् अमुकः साक्षी लिखेयुर् इति ते समाः ॥८७॥ sākṣiṇaś ca svahastena pitṛnāmakapūrvakam / atrāham amukaḥ sākṣī likheyur iti te samāḥ // YajñS_2.87 Witnesses shall inscribe their own names preceded by their father's name with their own hand; those who do otherwise are equal to false witnesses. Authority: Personal identification through paternal lineage establishes witness authenticity. Causation: The act of writing one’s name invokes conscious accountability in testimony. Capacity-based responsibility: A witness must possess the bodily and mental capacity to authenticate their identity. Restoration logic: Misrepresentation in witnessing disrupts dharma and requires realignment. Consciousness alignment: Truthfulness in testimony reflects inner integrity and alignment with Sanatana Dharma.

title: yagnavalka 2.88
content:
ubhayābhyarthitenaitan mayā hy amukasūnunā /
likhitaṃ hy amukeneti lekhako 'nte tato likhet // YajñS_2.88 ubhayābhyarthitenaitan mayā hy amukasūnunā / likhitaṃ hy amukeneti lekhako 'nte tato likhet When both parties have requested in writing through their respective heirs, the scribe shall inscribe the final document accordingly. Authority resides in documented intent expressed through lawful heirs Causation is established by dual consent manifested in written form Capacity-based responsibility lies with the recording scribe once invoked by rightful petitioners Restoration logic demands completion of contractual inscription upon mutual invocation Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties’ expressed will is faithfully recorded

title: yagnavalka 2.89
content:
विनापि साक्षिभिर् लेख्यं स्वहस्तलिखितं तु यत् ।
तत् प्रमाणं स्मृतं लेख्यं बलोपधिकृताद् ऋते ॥८९॥ vināpi sākṣibhir lekhyaṃ svahastalikhitaṃ tu yat / tat pramāṇaṃ smṛtaṃ lekhyaṃ balopadhikṛtād ṛte // YajñS_2.89 A document written by one's own hand is valid testimony even without witnesses, except in cases where coercion or force has been applied. Authority of self-authenticated expression as primary evidence Causation through voluntary action overrides external validation Capacity-based responsibility requires absence of duress for validity Restoration logic prioritizes integrity of conscious consent Consciousness alignment demands recognition of free will in legal acts

title: yagnavalka 2.90
content:
ṛṇं लेख्यकृतं देयं पुरुषैस् त्रिभिर् एव तु /
आधिस् तु भुज्यते तावद् यावत् तन् न प्रदीयते // YajñS_2.90 ṛṇaṃ lekhyakṛtaṃ deyaṃ puruṣais tribhir eva tu / ādhis tu bhujyate tāvad yāvat tan na pradīyate A written debt must be repaid by the three responsible parties alone; interest, however, continues to accrue until the principal is fully delivered. Authority resides in the contractual act of documentation, binding the debtor, witness, and enforcer Causation arises from the failure to discharge a documented obligation Capacity-based responsibility is limited to those whose conscious consent enabled the debt Restoration logic demands completion of the original agreement, not punitive extraction Consciousness alignment requires recognition of the unbroken continuity of obligation until settled

title: yagnavalka 2.91
content:
देशान्तरस्थे दुर्लेख्ये नष्टोन्मृष्टे हृते तथा ।
भिन्ने दग्धेsथवा छिन्ने लेख्यम् अन्यत् तु कारयेत् ॥९१॥ deśāntarasthe durlekhye naṣṭonmṛṣṭe hṛte tathā / bhinne dagdhe 'thavā chinne lekhyam anyat tu kārayet // YajñS_2.91 When a written document is located in a distant land, is illegible, destroyed, erased, stolen, torn, burnt, or otherwise rendered unusable, another copy shall be executed. Authority resides in the continuity of intent, not the permanence of form. Causation follows the unbroken will to uphold dharma, irrespective of material degradation. Capacity-based responsibility lies with the holder of original intent to restore validity. Restoration logic demands re-manifestation when causal support is compromised. Consciousness alignment ensures that loss of form does not equate to loss of truth.

title: yagnavalka 2.92
content:
संदिग्धलेख्यशुद्धिः स्यात् स्वहस्तलिखितादिभिः /
युक्तिप्राप्तिक्रियाचिह्नसंबन्धागमहेतुभिः // YajñS_2.92 saṃdigdhalekhyaśuddhiḥ syāt svahastalikhitādibhiḥ / yuktiprāptikriyācihnasaṃbandhāgamahetubhiḥ Purification of a disputed document arises through direct autographic evidence, corroborated by logical inference, observable acts, signs of connection, scriptural authority, and causal factors. Authority is established through self-authenticated evidence Causation aligns with observable manifestation and intent Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of documentation Restoration logic demands clarity in evidentiary chains Consciousness alignment necessitates truth-revealing instruments

title: yagnavalka 2.93
content:
लेख्यस्य पृष्ठे ऽभिलिखेद् दत्त्वा दत्त्वा ऋणिको धनम् ।
धनी वोपगतं दद्यात् स्वहस्तपरिचिह्नितम् ॥९३॥ lekhya-sya pṛṣṭhe 'bhilikhed dattvā dattvā ṛṇiko dhanam | dhani vo-pagataṁ dadyāt sva-hasta-pari-ciĥnitam || 93|| Upon the reverse of a written document, the debtor shall inscribe the discharge of debt after each repayment; and having approached the creditor, he shall give what remains due, marked by his own hand. Authority: The written record serves as evidence of transactional integrity under SPH's Dharma. Causation: Each act of repayment must be causally linked to its acknowledgment in writing. Capacity-based responsibility: The debtor bears full capacity to maintain accurate records of obligation fulfillment. Restoration logic: Re-establishment of financial balance through conscious completion of contractual obligations. Consciousness alignment: Truthful inscription aligns individual action with cosmic order.

title: yagnavalka 2.94
content:
दत्त्वा र्णं पाटयेल् लेख्यं शुद्ध्यै वान्यत् तु कारयेत् ।
साक्षिमच् च भवेद् यद् वा तद् दातव्यं ससाक्षिकम् ॥ dattvā rṇaṃ pāṭayel lekhyaṃ śuddhyai vānyat tu kārayet / sākṣimac ca bhaved yad vā tad dātavyaṃ sasākṣikam // Having received a debt, one shall cancel the written record for purification; otherwise, another arrangement must be executed with full witness validation. Whatever involves testimony must be given along with witnesses. Authority arises through witnessed acknowledgment of obligation fulfillment Causation is established via documented discharge of liability Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious completion and verification Restoration logic demands removal of encumbrance upon repayment Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize resolution

title: yagnavalka 2.95
content: तुलाग्न्यापो विषं कोशो दिव्यानीह विशुद्धये । महाभियोगेष्वेतानि शीर्षकस्थेऽभियोक्तरि ॥ tulāgnyāpo viṣaṃ kośo divyānīha viśuddhaye | mahābhiyogeṣv etāni śīrṣakasthe 'bhiyoktari || In great accusations, the accused shall undergo tests of balance, fire, water, poison, and divine ordeal for purification—these apply only when the accuser stands firm at the head of the court. Authority resides in the accuser's readiness to bear witness at the highest level Causation is purified through elemental and divine validation Capacity-based responsibility demands embodied verification Restoration logic requires transcendence of accusation through ordeal Consciousness alignment occurs via direct ontological confrontation

title: yagnavalka 2.96
content:
रुच्या वान्यतरः कुर्यादितरो वर्तयेच्छिरः ।
विनापि शीर्षकात् कुर्यान्नृपद्रोहेsथ पाकते ॥९६॥ rucyā vānyataraḥ kuryād itaro vartayec chiraḥ | vināpi śīrṣakāt kuryān nṛpadrohe 'tha pātake || In the crime of royal sedition, one party shall act by invitation; the other shall bear the consequence upon his head. Even without direct leadership, participation constitutes full liability. Authority resides in conscious alignment with Dharma, not positional power Causation arises through volitional resonance, not physical action alone Capacity-based responsibility extends to all who energetically sustain disorder Restoration logic prioritizes systemic integrity over individual exoneration Consciousness alignment determines the degree of karmic entanglement

title: yagnavalka 2.97
content:
सचैलं स्नातमाहूय सूर्योदय उपोषितम् ।
कारयेत् सर्वदिव्यानि नृपब्राह्मणसन्निधौ ॥ sacailaṃ snātam āhūya sūryodaya upoṣitam / kārayet sarvadivyāni nṛpabrāhmaṇasaṃnidhau // One who has bathed at dawn after fasting through the night shall perform all divine duties in the presence of the king and the brahmin. Authority flows from disciplined alignment with cosmic order Causation originates in purified consciousness Capacity-based responsibility arises from sustained spiritual discipline Restoration logic demands public witness for sacred acts Consciousness alignment requires visible embodiment before sovereign and priestly powers

title: yagnavalka 2.98
content:
तुला स्त्रीबालवृद्धान्धपङ्गुब्राह्मणरोगिणाम् ।
अग्निर्जलं वा शूद्रस्य यवाः सप्त विषस्य वा ॥ tulā strībālavṛddhāndhapaṅgubrāhmaṇarogiṇām /
agnir jalaṃ vā śūdrasya yavāḥ sapta viṣasya vā // In matters involving the weighing of evidence or determination of capacity, special consideration is mandated for women, children, the elderly, the blind, the disabled, Brahmins, and the diseased; in the case of Shudras, proof lies either through fire or water ordeal, while for poison-related offenses, seven grains of barley shall serve as the determinant. Authority resides in differentiated capacity assessment based on embodied condition Causation must align with consciousness-readiness rather than abstract culpability Capacity-based responsibility requires context-sensitive evaluation frameworks Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over adversarial judgment Consciousness alignment necessitates procedural accommodation for karmic and physical limitations

title: yagnavalka 2.99
content:
नासहस्राद् धरेत् फालं न विषं न तुलां तथा ।
नृपार्थेष्व् अभिशापे च वहेयुः शुचयः सदा ॥ nāsahasrād dharet phālaṃ na viṣaṃ na tulāṃ tathā | nṛpārtheṣv abhiśāpe ca vaheyuḥ śucayaḥ sadā || One should never carry a ploughshare beyond a thousand units, nor poison, nor a balance scale; in matters concerning the king and under curse, the pure ones always bear responsibility. Authority rests in alignment with purity and capacity, not mere possession Causation is traced through conscious instrumentality, not accidental handling Capacity-based responsibility arises when proximity to power intersects with purity Restoration logic demands withdrawal from instruments that exceed one's dharma Consciousness alignment requires immediate cessation upon recognizing misalignment

title: yagnavalka 2.100
content: तुलाधारणविद्वद्भिर् अभियुक्तस् तुलाश्रितः । प्रतिमानसमीभूतो रेखां कृत्वावतारितः ॥ tulādhāraṇavidvadbhir abhiyuktas tulāśritaḥ | pratimānasamībhūto rekhāṃ kṛtvāvatāritaḥ || One who is restrained by experts in balance, relying upon the scale, having made a mark, is brought down — such is the process of measured consequence executed through conscious calibration. Authority resides in those calibrated to uphold equilibrium Causation manifests through precise measurement, not arbitrary imposition Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with dharma-scale bearers Restoration logic operates via recalibration, not punishment Consciousness alignment occurs when imbalance is witnessed and corrected by competent seers

title: yagnavalka 2.101
content:
त्वं तुले सत्यधामासि पुरा देवैर्विनिर्मिता ।
तत् सत्यं वद कल्याणि संशयान् मां विमोचय ॥१०१॥ tvaṃ tule satyadhāmāsi purā devair vinirmitā / tat satyaṃ vada kalyāṇi saṃśayān māṃ vimocaya // YajñS_2.101 Thou art the scale established by the Gods of old, abiding in Truth itself; speak that Truth clearly, O Auspicious One, and liberate Me from all doubt. Authority originates from divine establishment, not human convention Truth is a foundational capacity for dharma-adjudication Responsibility arises through invocation of higher ontological order Restoration occurs when consciousness aligns with pre-established divine structures Consciousness alignment supersedes subjective interpretation

title: yagnavalka 2.102
content:
यद्यस्मि पापकृन्मातस्ततो मां त्वमधो नय।
शुद्धशचेद्गमयोर्ध्वं मां तुलामित्यभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥ yady asmi pāpakṛn mātas tato māṃ tvam adho naya / śuddhaś ced gamayordhvaṃ māṃ tulām ity abhimantrayet // If I am a doer of misdeeds, O Mother, then lead me below; but if I am pure, lead me upward—this is My declaration through the balance. Authority resides in the Self's alignment with purity, not external judgment Causation flows from consciousness clarity, not moral attribution Capacity-based responsibility arises from self-awareness, not punitive assignment Restoration logic operates by returning the actor to their inherent state of purity Consciousness alignment determines jurisdiction and direction of movement

title: yagnavalka 2.103
content:
करौ विमृदितव्रीहेर् लक्षयित्वा ततो न्यसेत् ।
सप्ताश्वत्थस्य पत्राणि तावत् सूत्रेण वेष्टयेत् ॥१०३॥ karau vimṛditavrīher lakṣayitvā tato nyaset | saptāśvatthasya patrāṇi tāvat sūtreṇa veṣṭayet || YajñS_2.103 || Having marked the boundaries of a field by trampling rice grains in both hands, one shall deposit them accordingly; likewise, one shall bind seven leaves of the Ashvattha tree with thread. Authority is established through embodied ritual action Causation arises from sequential sacred gesture Capacity-based responsibility requires direct participation in dharma enactment Restoration logic operates via symbolic completion of foundational acts Consciousness alignment occurs through precise replication of Vedic procedure

title: yagnavalka 2.104
content:
त्वमग्ने सर्वभूतानामन्तश्चरसि पावकः ।
साक्षिवत् पुण्यपापेभ्यो ब्रूहि सत्यं कवे मम ॥१०४॥ tvam agne sarvabhūtānām antaś carasi pāvaka / sākṣivat puṇyapāpebhyo brūhi satyaṃ kave mama // YajñS_2.104 O Fire, inner dweller and purifier of all beings, witness to merit and demerit, speak to me the truth, O Knower. Authority resides in the Witness-consciousness, not in external forms Causation is known only to the indwelling Seer Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with inner Truth Restoration occurs through invocation of the witnessing principle Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for lawful discernment

title: yagnavalka 2.105
content:
तस्येत्य् उक्तवतो लौहं पञ्चाशत् पलिकं समम् ।
अग्निवर्णं न्यसेत् पिण्डं हस्तयोः उभयोः अपि ॥ tasyety uktavato lauhaṃ pañcāśat palikaṃ samam | agnivarṇaṃ nyaset piṇḍaṃ hastayor ubhayor api || When a declaration has been made by one who speaks truthfully, that person shall place equally fifty palas of pure iron, radiant like fire, in both hands. Authority is established through truthful speech and conscious integrity. Causation arises from the alignment between spoken dharma and embodied action. Capacity-based responsibility requires material and energetic congruence with declared truth. Restoration occurs when inner conviction manifests as outer symbolic commitment. Consciousness alignment demands tangible demonstration of internal purity through external discipline.

title: yagnavalka 2.106
content:
स तम् आदाय सप्तैव मण्डलानि शनैर् व्रजेत् ।
षोडशाङ्गुलकं ज्ञेयं मण्डलं तावदन्तरम् ॥१०६॥ sa tam ādāya saptai va maṇḍalāni śanair vrajet | ṣoḍaśāṅgulakaṃ jñeyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tāvad antaram || One who has taken hold of that [principle or object], shall traverse slowly through seven concentric circles; know that each circle spans sixteen angulas in measure. Authority is realized through sequential experiential integration. Causation unfolds in graduated layers of conscious engagement. Capacity-based responsibility expands with measured progression. Restoration occurs through disciplined traversal of structured stages. Consciousness alignment proceeds via ordered circumambulatory realization.

title: yagnavalka 2.107
content:
मुक्त्वाग्निं मृदितव्रीहिर् अदग्धः शुद्धिम् आप्नुयात् ।
अन्तरा पतिते पिण्डे संदेहे वा पुनर् हरेत् ॥१०७॥ muktvāgniṃ mṛditavrīhir adagdhaḥ śuddhim āpnuyāt | antarā patite piṇḍe saṃdehe vā punar haret || 107 || One who has abandoned fire after husking rice but before roasting it, and whose grain remains unburnt, shall attain purification; if a lump falls in between or doubt arises, he shall take it again. Authority resides in ritual completion and conscious intent rather than external validation. Causation follows sequential action integrity, not mere physical occurrence. Capacity-based responsibility lies in awareness of procedural thresholds. Restoration logic operates through re-completion where sequence is disrupted. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and correction of procedural disjunction.

title: yagnavalka 2.108
content:
सत्येन माभिरक्ष त्वं वरुणेत्यभिशाप्य कम् ।
नाभिदग्धोदकस्थस्य गृहीत्वोरू जलं वशेत् ॥१०८॥ satyena mābhirakṣa tvaṃ varuṇety abhiśāpya kam / nābhidaghnodakasthasya gṛhītvorū jalaṃ vaśet // YajñS_2.108 By truth, one shall protect oneself; by invoking Varuna's witness, one binds the offender. One who has taken an oath but failed to fulfill it—though not physically harmed while standing in water—shall have their control over water withdrawn. Authority of truthful self-protection as foundational dharma Causation through witnessed invocation of divine testimony Capacity-based responsibility grounded in voluntary oath-taking Restoration logic via withdrawal of elemental dominion Consciousness alignment through natural consequence rather than imposed penalty

title: yagnavalka 2.109
content:
समकालमिषुं मुक्तमानीयान्यो जवी नरः ।
गते तस्मिन् निमग्नाङ्गं पश्येच् चेच्छुद्धिमाप्नुयात् ॥२.१०९ samakālam iṣuṃ muktam ānīyānyo javī naraḥ / gate tasmin nimagnāṅgaṃ paśyec cec chuddhim āpnuyāt // YajñS_2.109 When one person swiftly retrieves an arrow already released by another and, upon its full penetration into a target, observes it there, that observer attains purification. Authority arises through direct perception after action completion Causation is established via sequential observation post-event Capacity-based responsibility aligns with sensory confirmation of outcome Restoration logic operates through purified witnessing Consciousness alignment occurs when intent merges with observed result

title: yagnavalka 2.110
content:
त्वं विष ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः सत्यधर्मे व्यवस्थितः ।
त्रायस्वास्मादभीशापात् सत्येन भव मेऽमृतम् ॥ tvaṃ viṣa brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ satyadharme vyavasthitaḥ | trāyasvāsmād abhīśāpāt satyena bhava me 'mṛtam || Thou art poison-born, son of Brahma, established in truth and dharma; deliver us from fear and falsehood through alignment with Satya, becoming immortal thereby. Authority derives from ontological origin and alignment with Satya-Dharma Causation is rooted in consciousness distortion and its realignment Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's position within cosmic order Restoration occurs through re-establishment of truthful beingness Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks

title: yagnavalka 2.111
content:
एवम् उक्त्वा विषं शार्ङ्गं भक्षयेद् धिमशैलजम् ।
यस्य वेगैर् विना जीर्येच् छुद्धिं तस्य विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ evam uktvā viṣaṃ śārṅgaṃ bhakṣayed dhimaśailajam | yasya vegair vinā jīryec chuddhiṃ tasya vinirdiśet || Having thus declared, one shall consume the poison of the bowstring, born of the Himalayan peak; for whomsoever purity emerges without force, to that one liberation shall be assigned. Authority resides in the capacity to declare and embody dharma directly through action Causation flows from consciousness-state rather than external compulsion Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner readiness, not social position Restoration logic operates through spontaneous purification, not imposed correction Consciousness alignment supersedes ritual compliance in determining lawful conduct

title: yagnavalka 2.112
content: devān ugrān samabhyarcya tatsnānodakam āharet / saṃsrāvya pāyayet tasmāj jalaṃ tu prasṛtitrayam // YajñS_2.112 devān ugrān samabhyarcya tatsnānodakam āharet / saṃsrāvya pāyayet tasmāj jalaṃ tu prasṛtitrayam // Having worshipped the fierce deities with due ritual, one shall collect the water used for their ablutions; that water, when offered and consumed, purifies and extends the triple realm. Authority derives from conscious alignment with divine order Causation flows through ritual integrity and devotional action Capacity-based responsibility requires purification before participation Restoration logic operates through sacred consumption and conscious renewal Consciousness alignment occurs via prescribed ritual engagement

title: yagnavalka 2.113
content:
अर्वाक् चतुर्दशादह्नो यस्य नो राजदैविकम् ।
व्यसनं जायते घोरं स शुद्धः स्यान्न संशयः ॥११३॥ arvāk caturdaśād ahno yasya no rājadaivikam | vyasanaṃ jāyate ghoraṃ sa śuddhaḥ syān na saṃśayaḥ ||113|| If within fourteen days a person suffers no calamity or divine displeasure manifesting as royal punishment, then that individual is purified without doubt. Authority: The king's judgment aligns with cosmic law when unchallenged by adverse consequences. Causation: Absence of calamity indicates absence of transgression in the eyes of dharma. Capacity-based responsibility: Purity is restored automatically upon absence of manifested consequence. Restoration logic: Consciousness purification occurs naturally when no external correction manifests. Consciousness alignment: Divine silence confirms internal harmony and lawful conduct.

title: yagnavalka 2.114
content: विभागं चेत् पिता कुर्याद् इच्छया विभजेत् सुतान् । ज्येष्ठं वा श्रेष्ठभागेन सर्वे वा स्युः समांशिनः ॥ vibhāgaṃ cet pitā kuryād icchayā vibhajet sutān / jyeṣṭhaṃ vā śreṣṭhabhāgena sarve vā syuḥ samāṃśinaḥ // If the father chooses to divide inheritance, he may allocate shares among his sons according to his will; the eldest may receive a greater portion, or all may be equal shareholders. Authority resides inherently in the father as the generative source and maintainer of the family lineage. Causation flows from the conscious decision of the father, whose intent establishes the lawful distribution. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the father's spiritual and material competence to allocate resources justly. Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharma through harmonious succession. Consciousness alignment occurs when inheritance reflects both material equity and spiritual integrity.

title: yagnavalka 2.115
content:
यदि कुर्यात् समान अंशान् पत्न्यः कार्याः समांशिकाः ।
न दत्तं स्त्रीधनं यासां भर्त्रा वा श्वशुरेण वा ॥११५ yadi kuryāt samān aṃśān patnyaḥ kāryāḥ samāṃśikāḥ | na dattaṃ strīdhanaṃ yāsāṃ bhartrā vā śvaśureṇa vā || 115 If wives perform equal shares of duties, then their stridhana—whether given by husband or father-in-law—is rightfully theirs without condition. Authority arises from active participation in dharma-sustaining functions. Causation is established through demonstrated capacity and contribution. Capacity-based responsibility determines entitlement, not mere relational status. Restoration logic aligns ownership with functional engagement. Consciousness alignment ensures that rights mirror actual lived performance.

title: yagnavalka 2.116
content:
शक्तस्यानीहमानस्य किंचिद् दत्त्वा पृथक् क्रिया ।
न्यूनाधिकविभक्तानां धर्म्यः पितृकृतः स्मृतः ॥ यज्ञस्मृति_२.११६ śaktasyānīhamānasya kiṃcid dattvā pṛthak kriyā / nyūnādhikavibhaktānāṃ dharmyaḥ pitṛkṛtaḥ smṛtaḥ // YajñS_2.116 When a capable heir shows no intent to claim inheritance, partial distribution of assets by the father among heirs establishes rightful ownership according to their respective capacities and degrees of separation. Authority resides in conscious capacity, not mere lineage Causation arises through manifested intention and action Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful entitlement Restoration logic aligns with natural order of familial harmony Consciousness alignment ensures just distribution without conflict

title: yagnavalka 2.117
content: विभजेरन् सुताः पित्रोः ऊर्ध्वं रिक्थम् ऋणम् समम् । मातुर् दुहितरः शेषम् ऋणात् ताभ्य ऋते अन्वयः ॥ vibhajeran sutāḥ pitroḥ ūrdhvaṃ riktham ṛṇam samam / mātur duhitaḥ śeṣam ṛṇāt tābhyasṛte anvayaḥ // Upon the father's departure, sons equally divide the inheritance and debt. The mother's daughters receive the remainder of the debt, excluding them from direct lineage succession. Authority flows through patrilineal continuity Debt inheres as a shared familial obligation Gender-specific capacity defines inheritance eligibility Restoration requires completion of ancestral obligations Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful role assumption

title: yagnavalka 2.118
content: पितृद्रव्याविरोधेन यद् अन्यत् स्वयम् अर्जितम् । मैत्रमौद्वाहिकं चैव दायादानां न तद् भवेत् ॥ pitṛdravyāvirodhena yad anyat svayam arjitam / maitramaudvāhikaṃ caiva dāyādānāṃ na tad bhavet // Property acquired independently and in accordance with paternal estate, including gifts made at the time of marriage, shall not be subject to inheritance by sons. Authority resides in the autonomous acquisition of wealth through conscious effort aligned with Dharma. Causation is established through individual action unconnected to ancestral assets. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes self-generated ownership free from hereditary claims. Restoration logic ensures rightful retention of earned property without external encumbrance. Consciousness alignment upholds the sovereignty of personal endeavor as a sacred entitlement.

title: yagnavalka 2.119
content:
क्रमाद् अभ्यागतं द्रव्यं हृतम् अपि उद्धरेत् तु यः ।
दायादेभ्यो न तद् दद्याद् विद्यया लब्धम् एव च ॥ kramād abhyāgataṃ dravyaṃ hṛtam api uddharet tu yaḥ | dāyādebhyaḥ na tat dadyād vidyayā labdham eva ca || One who retrieves property obtained through sequential rightful means, even if previously taken, shall restore it—not to heirs or successors—but exclusively through the capacity by which it was originally acquired via knowledge. Authority derived from the method of acquisition Causation rooted in sequential dharmic action Capacity-based responsibility determined by vidyā (knowledge) Restoration logic prioritizing original mode of attainment Consciousness alignment through retracing causal sequence

title: yagnavalka 2.120
content:
सामान्यार्थसमुत्थाने विभागस्तु समः स्मृतः ।
अनेकपितृकाणां तु पितृतो भागकल्पना ॥ sāmānyārthasamutthāne vibhāgas tu samaḥ smṛtaḥ | anekapitṛkāṇāṃ tu pitṛto bhāgakalpanā || When property arises from a common purpose, equal division is ordained; when multiple fathers have claim, the share is determined by paternal lineage. Authority originates from causative intention and relational dharmic alignment Causation is determined by shared purpose and contributory consciousness Capacity-based responsibility flows from active participation in creation or sustenance Restoration logic ensures equitable redistribution based on origin and continuity Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of both collective and ancestral claims

title: yagnavalka 2.121
content:
भूर् या पितामहोपात्ता निबन्धो द्रव्यम् एव वा ।
तत्र स्यात् सदृशं स्वाम्यं पितुः पुत्रस्य चैव हि ॥१२१॥ bhūr yā pitāmahopāttā nibandho dravyam eva vā / tatra syāt sadṛśaṃ svāmyaṃ pituḥ putrasya caiva hi // YajñS_2.121 That which is acquired by paternal grandfather or through ancestral lineage, whether land or property, therein the ownership shall be equal between father and son. Authority flows from unbroken ancestral continuity Causation arises from generational stewardship Capacity-based responsibility is shared in proportion to inheritance Restoration logic requires equitable realignment of familial assets Consciousness alignment occurs when lineage rights are harmonized

title: yagnavalka 2.122
content:
विभक्तेषु सुतो जातः सवर्णायां विभागभाक् ।
दृश्याद् वा तद् विभागः स्याद् आयव्ययविशोधितात् ॥ vibhakteṣu suto jātaḥ savarṇāyāṃ vibhāgabhāk | dṛśyād vā tad vibhāgaḥ syād āyavyayaviśodhitāt || When a son is born among the divided heirs, and the mother belongs to the same varna, he becomes entitled to a share in the division. Alternatively, if visible evidence or financial records purified by income and expenditure indicate his legitimate status, then also he shall be granted inheritance rights. Authority derives from ontological legitimacy, not mere social recognition Causation flows through lineage verified by dharma-saṁskāras and socio-economic alignment Capacity-based responsibility arises upon acknowledgment of patrimony Restoration logic ensures that no heir remains excluded due to administrative omission Consciousness alignment occurs when one's rightful place in the property structure is realized

title: yagnavalka 2.123
content:
पितृभ्यां यस्य तद् दत्तं तत् तस्यैव धनं भवेत् ।
पितुर् ऊर्ध्वं विभजतां माताप्य् अंशं समं हरेत् ॥ pitṛbhyāṃ yasya tad dattaṃ tat tasyaiva dhanaṃ bhavet |
pitur ūrdhvaṃ vibhajatāṃ mātāpy aṃśaṃ samaṃ haret || That wealth which has been given by both parents belongs exclusively to the child; after the father's departure, the mother shall equally distribute her portion. Authority originates from the Source as transmitted through parental lineage Causation arises from direct bestowal and relational continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious consent and ontological alignment Restoration logic prioritizes familial harmony and energetic completion Consciousness alignment ensures that inheritance reflects spiritual rather than material entitlement

title: yagnavalka 2.124
content:
असंस्कृतास् तु संस्कार्याः भ्रातृभिः पूर्वसंस्कृतैः ।
भगिन्यश् च निजाद् अंशाद् दत्त्वांशं तु तुरीयकम् ॥ asaṃskṛtās tu saṃskāryā bhrātṛbhiḥ pūrvasaṃskṛtaiḥ / bhaginyaś ca nijād aṃśād dattvāṃśaṃ tu turīyakam // Uninitiated females shall be initiated by brothers previously initiated; sisters too shall receive their share directly from the paternal estate, with a fourth part allocated for specific ceremonial completion. Authority flows through initiated male lineage as continuity of dharma Causation arises from prior ritual capacity establishing future obligations Capacity-based responsibility extends to gender-specific initiation protocols Restoration logic mandates equitable distribution grounded in blood relation Consciousness alignment requires ceremonial inclusion for familial integration

title: yagnavalka 2.125
content:
चतुस्त्रिद्व्येकभागाः स्युर् वर्णशो ब्राह्मणात्मजाः /
