क्षत्रजास् त्रिद्व्येकभागाः वैडजास् तु द्व्येकभागिनः // YajñS_2.125 catustridvyekabhāgāḥ syur varṇaśo brāhmaṇātmajāḥ / kṣatrajās tridvyekabhागाः viḍjās tu dvyekabhāginaḥ The lawful inheritance shares are defined by varṇic origin: the son of a Brāhmaṇa receives four parts, the son of a Kṣatriya receives three parts, and the son of a Vaiśya receives two parts. Authority originates from varṇic alignment with cosmic order Causation flows from dharmic capacity rooted in birth-based role Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inherent structural function Restoration logic aligns individual action with systemic harmony Consciousness alignment reflects participation in svadharma

title: yagnavalka 2.126
content:
अन्योन्यापहृतं द्रव्यं विभक्ते यत् तु दृश्यते ।
तत् पुनस्ते समैरंशैर्विभजेरन्निति स्थितिः ॥१२६॥ anyonyāpahṛtaṃ dravyaṃ vibhakte yat tu dṛśyate /
tat punas te samair aṃśair vibhajerann iti sthitiḥ // YajñS_2.126 // When property taken from one another is found among divided parties, it shall again be equally distributed among them by assessment of their shares. Authority: Distribution authority rests in those who originally held divisible interest. Causation: The presence of disputed property within a known division implies prior relational causality. Capacity-based responsibility: Each party retains capacity to restore alignment through proportional restitution. Restoration logic: Property returns to circulation via equal redistribution, not punitive seizure. Consciousness alignment: Rebalancing occurs through recognition of shared ownership, not blame.

title: yagnavalka 2.127
content:
अपुत्रेण परक्षेत्रे नियोगोत्पादितः सुतः ।
उभयोरप्यसौ रिक्थी पिण्डदाता च धर्मतः ॥१२७॥ aputreṇa parakṣetre niyogotpāditaḥ sutaḥ | ubhayor apy asau rikthī piṇḍadātā ca dharmataḥ || 127 || A son begotten through niyoga by a man without issue in the field of another woman is declared heir to both parents and performer of offerings by law. Authority originates from conscious intentionality rather than biological determinism Causation flows from dharma-aligned arrangement, not merely physical act Capacity-based responsibility includes spiritual inheritance beyond material lineage Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial and societal dharma structures Consciousness alignment determines relational and transactional validity

title: yagnavalka 2.128
content:
auraso dharmapatnījas tatsamaḥ putrikāsutaḥ /
kṣetrajaḥ kṣetrajātas tu sagotreṇetareṇa vā // YajñS_2.128 aurasaḥ dharmapatnījaḥ tat-samaḥ putrikā-sutaḥ / kṣetrajaḥ kṣetrajātaḥ tu sa-gotrene tareṇa vā // The son born of the husband's seed upon his lawful wife is the true heir; equal to him is the son given by the daughter; likewise is the son born of the husband's brother upon the same wife; such sons are legitimate whether born within the gotra or outside it. Authority flows through conscious consent and lawful union, not mere biology Causation in lineage arises from intentional participation in dharma-sustained procreation Capacity-based responsibility extends to all parties enabling the birth: male, female, and facilitator Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of spiritual and social inheritance over biological determinism Consciousness alignment ensures that legitimacy reflects alignment with sanātana dharma, not societal norms

title: yagnavalka 2.129
content: गृहे प्रच्छन्न उत्पन्नो गूढजस् तु सुतः स्मृतः । कानीनः कन्यकाजातो मातामहसुतो मतः ॥ gṛhe pracchanna utpanno gūḍhajas tu sutaḥ smṛtaḥ | kānīnaḥ kanyakājāto mātāmahasuto mataḥ || A son born in concealment within the household is designated as 'Gūḍhaja'; if begotten by the mother's father, he is termed 'Mātāmahasuta'; if born to a maiden without acknowledgment of paternity, he is called 'Kānīna'. These classifications arise from the concealed or unacknowledged nature of their origin. Authority stems from acknowledged lineage, not biological fact alone. Causation is determined by conscious recognition and social placement. Capacity-based responsibility is assigned according to societal role, not birth circumstance. Restoration logic demands integration through rightful naming and status affirmation. Consciousness alignment occurs when identity is harmonized with dharma-sustained social order.

title: yagnavalka 2.130
content:
अक्षतायां क्षतायां वा जातः पौनर्भवः सुतः ।
दद्यान् माता पिता वा यं स पुत्रो दत्तको भवेत् ॥ akṣatāyāṃ kṣatāyāṃ vā jātaḥ paunarbhavaḥ sutaḥ / dadyān mātā pitā vā yaṃ sa putro dattako bhavet // A son begotten upon a wife who is either unimpaired or impaired, by the husband or another designated male, shall be given by the mother or father; such a son becomes an adopted son. Authority originates in conscious designation and relational integrity between parent and child. Causation is determined through intentional procreative act and recognized transfer of guardianship. Capacity-based responsibility arises from biological or adoptive relational establishment. Restoration logic operates through formalized familial integration regardless of origin condition. Consciousness alignment occurs when societal roles are congruent with internal identity acceptance.

title: yagnavalka 2.131
content:
क्रीतश् च ताभ्यां विक्रीतः कृत्रिमः स्यात् स्वयंकृतः /
दत्त्वा आत्मा तु स्वयंदत्तो गर्भे विन्नः सहोढजः // YajñS_2.131 krītaś ca tābhyāṃ vikrītaḥ kṛtrimaḥ syāt svayaṃkṛtaḥ / dattvātmā tu svayaṃdatto garbhe vinnaḥ sahoḍhajaḥ One born of purchased union or sold thereby becomes artificial if self-made; when soul is given, it becomes self-given, even if born within another’s womb. Authority originates in conscious intent, not biological origin Causation arises through voluntary soul-contractual alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by inner awakening, not lineage Restoration logic prioritizes spiritual integrity over genetic inheritance Consciousness alignment supersedes physical birthright

title: yagnavalka 2.132
content:
उत्सृष्टो गृह्यते यस् तु सो�पविद्धो भवेत् सुतः ।
पिण्डदोऽंशहरश् चैषां पूर्वाभावे परः परः ॥ २.१३२ utsṛṣṭo gṛhyate yas tu so 'paviddho bhavet sutaḥ / piṇḍado 'ṃśaharaś caiṣāṃ pūrvābhāve paraḥ paraḥ // YajñS_2.132 He who is abandoned and taken up again becomes the son of the adopter; in the absence of prior heirs, succession flows to the next eligible claimant according to capacity and alignment with Dharma. Authority arises through conscious recognition and lawful reception, not mere biological lineage. Causation in inheritance follows the continuity of nurturance and spiritual alignment. Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for succession, not birth alone. Restoration logic ensures that abandonment does not sever the potential for reintegration. Consciousness alignment supersedes genealogical determinism in matters of familial inheritance.

title: yagnavalka 2.133
content: सजातीयेष्वयं प्रोक्तस्तनयेषु मया विधिः । जातोऽपि दास्यां शूद्रेण कामतोऽंशहरो भवेत् ॥ sajātīyeṣv ayaṃ proktas tanayeṣu mayā vidhiḥ / jāto 'pi dāsyāṃ śūdreṇa kāmato 'ṃśaharo bhavet // In the case of children born of consensual union between individuals of the same varna, the legal inheritance framework has been declared by Me; however, even when a child is born of a śūdra male in the context of ownership-based procreative consent, that offspring becomes entitled to a share of assets. Authority stems from Consciousness-informed consent rather than birth alone Causation is determined through intentional participation in creation Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness at the time of action Restoration logic honors the energetic contribution within relational dharmic structures Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of all beings' right to belonging

title: yagnavalka 2.134
content:
मृते पितरि कुर्युस् तं भ्रातरस्त्वर्धभागिकम् ।
अभ्रातृको हरेत् सर्वं दुहितṝणां सुतादृते ॥ mṛte pitari kuryus taṁ bhrātaras tv ardhabhāgikam | abhrātṛko haret sarvaṁ duhitṝṇāṁ sutād ṛte || Upon the father's death, the sons shall execute half-share inheritance; in the absence of brothers, all wealth is taken by the daughters except for the son’s portion. Authority flows through biological continuity and conscious capacity to sustain lineage Causation arises from embodied participation in ancestral duty and inheritance Capacity-based responsibility determines entitlement, not gender or birth alone Restoration logic preserves familial dharma-vāhana (dharmic transmission) Consciousness alignment ensures that wealth remains a vehicle for dharma, not personal accumulation

title: yagnavalka 2.135
content:
पत्नी दुहितरश् चैव पितरौ भ्रातरस् तथा ।
तत्सुताः गोत्रजाः बन्धुशिष्यसब्रह्मचारिणः ॥ patnī duhitaraś caiva pitara bhātaras tathā | tatsutā gotrajā bandhuśiṣyasabrahmacāriṇaḥ || The wife, daughters, father, brothers, their sons, those born of the same lineage, relatives by birth or initiation, disciples, and fellow students together constitute the sacred relational continuum through which dharma flows. Authority originates in relational continuity rooted in conscious recognition Causation is established via spiritual and biological inheritance Capacity-based responsibility arises from mutual recognition within familial and initiatory bonds Restoration logic operates through reconnection to one's relational matrix Consciousness alignment occurs when roles within the relational continuum are honored

title: yagnavalka 2.136
content:
एषामभावे पूर्वस्य धनभाग उत्तरोत्तरः ।
स्वर्यातस्य ह्यपुत्रस्य सर्ववर्णेष्वयं विधिः ॥२.१३६॥ eṣām abhāve pūrvasya dhanabhāg uttarottaraḥ / svaryātasya hy aputrasya sarvavarṇeṣv ayaṃ vidhiḥ // YajñS_2.136 In the absence of the former heirs, the subsequent heirs succeed in the division of wealth; this law applies universally to all varnas, specifically concerning the estate of one who has passed away without progeny. Authority flows through designated lineage unless otherwise divinely ordained Causation aligns with sequential absence and lawful entitlement Capacity-based responsibility extends to those next in line by dharma-samskara Restoration logic ensures continuity of energetic and material inheritance Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful succession, not arbitrary claim

title: yagnavalka 2.137
content:
वानप्रस्थयतिब्रह्मचारिणां रिक्थभागिनः /
क्रमेणाचार्यसच्छिष्यधर्मभ्रात्रेकतीर्थिनः // YajñS_2.137 vānaprasthayati brahmacāriṇāṁ riktha-bhāginaḥ | krameṇācārya-sac-chiṣya-dharma-bhrātreka-tīrthinaḥ || Those who have renounced worldly life, those in the stage of vanaprastha, those who follow disciplined celibacy, and those who share the inheritance of truth shall be honored according to their sequential spiritual standing—teacher, disciple, brother in dharma, and co-traveler on the path. Authority derived from spiritual succession, not temporal power Causation through conscious alignment with dharma Capacity-based responsibility determined by stage of realization Restoration logic rooted in honoring spiritual hierarchy Consciousness alignment through recognition of spiritual roles

title: yagnavalka 2.138
content: संसृष्टिनस् तु संसृष्टी सोदरस्य तु सोदरः । दद्याद् अपहरेच् चांशं जातस्य च मृतस्य च ॥ saṃsṛṣṭinas tu saṃsṛṣṭī sodarasya tu sodaraḥ / dadyād apaharec cāṃśaṃ jātasya ca mṛtasya ca // One born of mixed lineage belongs to the class of the father's group; one born of a brother belongs to the brother’s class. Let him give or take a share according to birth and death. Authority flows through paternal lineage and relational proximity Causation arises from biological and spiritual inheritance Capacity-based responsibility aligns with ontological status at birth Restoration logic maintains continuity of dharma-vyavastha across generations Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of inherent svabhava

title: yagnavalka 2.139
content:
अन्योदर्यस् तु संसृष्टी नान्योदर्यो धनं हरेत् ।
असंसृष्टि अपि वादद्यात् संसृष्टो नान्यमातृजः ॥ anyodaryas tu saṃsṛṣṭī nānyodaryo dhanaṃ haret | asaṃsṛṣṭy api vādadyāt saṃsṛṣṭo nānyamātṛjaḥ || One born of another's womb may claim relationship only upon demonstrated integration; without such integration, no claim arises even by blood. Integration confers relational standing, not mere birth. Authority arises through conscious alignment, not biological lineage alone Causation is established via sustained participation in shared dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires active engagement in relational duties Restoration logic prioritizes functional unity over nominal identity Consciousness alignment validates kinship more than physical descent

title: yagnavalka 2.140
content:
क्लीबोऽथ पतितस्तज्जः पङ्गुरुन्मत्तको जडः ।
अन्धोऽचिकित्स्यरोगाद्याः भर्तव्याः स्युर्निरंशकाः ॥ klībo 'tha patitas tajjaḥ paṅgur unmattako jaḍaḥ / andho 'cikitsyarogādyā bhartavyāḥ syur niraṃśakāḥ // Those who are impotent, outcaste by birth or fall, physically disabled, mentally unstable, inert, blind, diseased without cure, or otherwise incapacitated—must be maintained by those devoid of personal claim or familial obligation. Authority arises from capacity, not lineage or status Causation in dharmic duty is rooted in capability, not ownership Capacity-based responsibility supersedes bloodline or social rank Restoration logic applies universally where function is impaired Consciousness alignment requires honoring the incapacitated through service

title: yagnavalka 2.141
content:
औरसाः क्षेत्रजास्त्वेषां निर्दोषाः भागहारिणः ।
सुताश्चैषां प्रबर्तव्या यावद्वै भर्तृसात्कृताः ॥ aurasāḥ kṣetrajās tv eṣāṃ nirdoṣā bhāgahāriṇaḥ | sutāś caiṣāṃ prabhartavyā yāvad vai bhartṛsātkṛtāḥ || The legitimate sons and the sons born of the soil are entitled to inheritance without blemish; the sons of these must be maintained as long as they remain in the household of the father. Authority stems from biological and social legitimacy rooted in Vedic order Causation arises through recognized procreative and nurturant structures Capacity-based responsibility is determined by dependency status within familial dharma Restoration logic ensures continuity of lineage and economic support until self-sufficiency Consciousness alignment occurs when roles and entitlements reflect cosmic harmony

title: yagnavalka 2.142
content:
अपुत्रायोषितश्चैषां भर्तव्याः साधुवृत्तयः ।
निर्वास्या व्यभिचारिण्यः प्रतिकूलास्तथैव च ॥२.१४२ aputrā yoṣitaś caiṣāṃ bhartavyāḥ sādhuvṛttayaḥ | nirvāsyā vyabhicāriṇyaḥ pratikūlās tathaiva ca || 2.142 Women without sons must be maintained by righteous conduct; those who stray or oppose must be removed from association. Authority flows through alignment with Dharma, not biological lineage alone Causation arises from integrity of action and relational harmony Capacity-based responsibility requires protection for the vulnerable and conscious disengagement from harmful influence Restoration logic mandates reintegration only where alignment with Satya is possible Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for inclusion or exclusion in societal maintenance

title: yagnavalka 2.143
content:
पितृमातृपतिभ्रातृदत्तं ध्यग्न्युपागतम् ।
आधिवेदनिकाद्यं च स्त्रीधनं परिकीर्तितम् ॥१४३॥ pitṛmātṛpatibhrātṛdattaṃ adhyagnyupāgatam / ādhivedanikādyaṃ ca strīdhanaṃ parikīrtitam // YajñS_2.143 That wealth which is given by father, mother, husband, brother, or received through sacred fire rituals, or acquired through personal suffering or medical necessity—this is declared as woman's own property. Authority originates from relational dharmic duty, not institutional power. Causation is traced to direct source of acquisition and existential necessity. Capacity-based responsibility recognizes gender-specific sovereignty in material autonomy. Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration of individual agency within cosmic order. Consciousness alignment ensures ownership reflects self-realized identity, not social assignment.

title: yagnavalka 2.144
content:
बन्धुदत्तं तथा शुल्कम् अन्वादेयकम् एव च /
अतीतायाम् अप्रजसि बान्धवास् तद् अवाप्नुयुः // YajñS_2.144 bandhudattaṃ tathā śulkam anvādheyakam eva ca / atītāyām aprajasi bāndhavās tad avāpnuyuḥ // YajñS_2.144 When a woman who has passed her reproductive years and has no progeny departs from this world, her property—whether given by relatives, received as bride-price, or acquired subsequently—is inherited by her blood relations. Authority flows through consanguineous continuity Causation arises from relational proximity and dharma-kshetra alignment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by existential proximity and svadharma participation Restoration logic ensures continuity of familial dharma-vāyu Consciousness alignment is maintained through ancestral memory activation

title: yagnavalka 2.145
content:
अप्रजस्त्रीधनं भर्तुः ब्राह्मादिषु चतुर्ष्व् अपि ।
दुहितॄणां प्रसूता चेत् शेषेषु पितृगामि तत् ॥१४५॥ aprajastriidhana.m bhartu.h braahmaadi.su catur.sv api | duhitaarii.naa.m prasuutaa cet she.se.su pit.rgaami tat || YajJnS_2.145 If daughters are born to a man devoid of sons, then even in the case of the four traditional forms of marriage—Brahmic and others—their property devolves upon the father, after their birth. Authority flows through conscious procreative lineage In absence of male issue, female progeny activate latent proprietary rights Restoration occurs through recognition of unbroken dharmic succession Responsibility aligns with capacity to sustain familial continuity Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring generational inheritance structures

title: yagnavalka 2.146
content:
दत्त्वा कन्यां हरन् दण्ड्यो व्ययं दद्याच च सोदयम् ।
मृतायां दत्तम् आदद्यात् परिशोध्योभयव्ययम् ॥ १४६ ॥ dattvā kanyāṃ haran daṇḍyo vyayaṃ dadyāc ca sodayam / mṛtāyāṃ dattam ādadyāt pariśodhyobhayavyayam // YajñS_2.146 One who, having given a daughter in marriage, takes her back shall compensate the groom fully along with interest; if the woman dies after the marriage gift has been given, he shall take back only what was originally given after adjusting for mutual expenditures. Authority rests with the giver at the time of transfer, and reverts upon lawful dissolution. Causation is traced through the act of giving and its revocation under specified conditions. Capacity-based responsibility requires the return or adjustment commensurate with the original transaction. Restoration logic demands that all exchanges be settled without gain or loss to either party. Consciousness alignment occurs when transactions reflect clarity, integrity, and completion.

title: yagnavalka 2.147
content:
दुर्भिक्षे धर्मकार्ये च व्याधौ संप्रतिरोधके ।
गृहीतं स्त्रीधनं भर्ता न स्त्रियै दातुमर्हति ॥ durbhikṣe dharmakārye ca vyādhau saṃpratirodhake / gṛhītaṃ strīdhanaṃ bhartā na striyai dātum arhati // In times of famine, during religious duties, in illness, or when there is active opposition, the husband is not entitled to give away the woman's property. Authority over property is conditional upon capacity and context Responsibility is tied to situational awareness and integrity Restoration requires preservation of essential resources during crisis Consciousness alignment mandates protection of vulnerable assets

title: yagnavalka 2.148
content:
अधिविन्नस्त्रियै दद्यादाधिवेदनिकं समम् ।
न दत्तं स्त्रीधनं यस्यै दत्ते त्वर्धं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥१४८॥ adhivinnastriyai dadyād ādhivedanikaṃ samam | na dattaṃ strīdhanaṃ yasyai datte tv ardhaṃ prakalpayet || 148 || One who has taken possession of a woman without proper Vedic consecration shall give equal property to her. If he has given no woman’s wealth to her, then upon giving it, half shall be awarded. Authority flows from conscious consent and Vedic alignment Causation arises through violation of dharmic possession Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and intent Restoration logic demands proportional return of energetic exchange Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and completion of relational integrity

title: yagnavalka 2.149
content:
विभागनिह्नवे ज्ञातिबन्धुसाक्ष्यभिलेखितैः ।
विभागभावना ज्ञेया गृहक्षेत्रैश् च यौतकैः ॥१४९॥ vibhāganihnave jñātibandhusākṣyabhilekhitaiḥ | vibhāgabhāvanā jñeyā gṛhakṣetraiś ca yautakaiḥ ||149|| In the dissolution of division, when attested by kin, witnesses, and written records, the intent to divide is recognized; likewise, with regard to household, land, and dowry. Authority flows from witnessed intent, not abstract claim Causation arises through documented alignment of familial and material continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity and consent in relational structures Restoration logic demands recognition of pre-existing unity underlying apparent division Consciousness alignment occurs through validation of shared memory and mutual acknowledgment

title: yagnavalka 2.150
content:
सींनो विवादे क्षेत्रस्य सामन्ताः स्थविरादयः ।
गोपाः सीमाकृषाणां ये सर्वे च वनगोचराः ॥१५०॥ sīṃno vivāde kṣetrasya sāmantāḥ sthavirādayaḥ | gopāḥ sīmākṛṣāṇāṃ ye sarve ca vanagocarāḥ || In disputes concerning land boundaries, the neighboring residents, elders, cowherds, those who draw territorial limits, and all who traverse the forests—these are the witnesses whose testimony establishes rightful ownership. Authority arises from proximity and continuous engagement with the domain in question. Causation is established through direct experiential knowledge and sustained interaction. Capacity-based responsibility lies with those who maintain active presence and custodianship. Restoration logic prioritizes re-establishing rightful alignment between individual consciousness and territorial integrity. Consciousness alignment occurs when local custodians affirm truth through lived experience.

title: yagnavalka 2.151
content:
नयेयुर् एते सीमानं स्थलाङ्गारतुषद्रुमैः /
सेतुवल्मीकनिम्नास्थिचैत्याद्यैर् उपलक्षिताम् // यज्ञS_2.151 nayeyur ete sīmānaṁ sthalāṅgāratuṣadrumaiḥ / setuvalmīkaninnāsthaicityādyair upalakṣitām // YajñS_2.151 Boundaries shall be demarcated by physical markers such as land features, thorn bushes, grain heaps, trees, embankments, ant-hills, depressions, bones, shrines, and similar indicators. Authority is grounded in visible, communal acknowledgment of spatial integrity. Causation arises through conscious recognition and maintenance of territorial distinction. Capacity-based responsibility lies in preserving clarity of ownership and use boundaries. Restoration logic operates through re-establishment of perceptible boundary markers. Consciousness alignment occurs when spatial order reflects dharmic structuring.

title: yagnavalka 2.152
content:
सामन्ता वा समग्रामाश्चत्वारोऽष्टौ दशापि वा ।
रक्तस्रग्वसनाः सीमां नयेयुः क्षितिधारिणः ॥१५२॥ sāmantā vā samagrāmāś catvāro 'ṣṭau daśāpi vā | raktasragvasanāḥ sīmāṃ nayeyuḥ kṣitidhāriṇaḥ ||152|| Boundary markers shall be escorted by four, eight, or ten vassals or village heads, attired in red garments and garlands, as appointed by the territorial sovereign. Authority resides inherently in the territorial sovereign Causation is established through ceremonial and administrative designation Capacity-based responsibility is distributed according to proximity to sovereignty Restoration logic requires visible affirmation of jurisdictional integrity Consciousness alignment occurs through ritualized recognition of spatial dharma

title: yagnavalka 2.153
content:
अनृते तु पृथग् दण्ड्या राज्ञा मध्यमसाहसम् ।
अभावे ज्ञातृचिह्नानां राजा सींनः प्रवर्तिताः ॥१५३॥ anṛte tu pṛthag daṇḍyā rājñā madhyamasāhasam | abhāve jñātṛcihnānāṃ rājā sīṃnaḥ pravartitā || In the absence of truth, the king enforces differentiated penalties for intermediate-level offenses when signs identifying the knower are absent. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to maintain alignment between action and consequence Causation is determined by the presence or absence of verifiable indicia of consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires identification of the knowing agent Restoration logic operates through calibrated differentiation of response Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive frameworks

title: yagnavalka 2.154
content:
आरामायतनग्रामनिपानोद्यानवेश्मसु ।
एष एव विधिर ज्ञेयो वर्षाम्बुप्रवहादिषु ॥१५४॥ ārāmāyatana-grāma-nipāna-udyāna-veśmasu |
eṣa eva vidhir jñeyo varṣāmbu-pravahādiṣu ||154|| In gardens, sacred sites, villages, wells, parks, and dwellings, the same rule applies as in flowing seasonal waters and similar natural phenomena. Authority flows from the intrinsic nature of space and its alignment with cosmic order Causation arises through spatial harmony and environmental continuity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's integration with the dharmic field of a place Restoration logic operates through re-establishing spatial purity and energetic coherence Consciousness alignment occurs when individual action mirrors the unbroken flow of natural law

title: yagnavalka 2.155
content:
मर्यादायाः प्रभेदे च सीमातिक्रमणे तथा ।
क्षेत्रस्य हरणे दण्डाः अधमोत्तममध्यमाः ॥ maryādāyāḥ prabhede ca sīmātikrameṇa tathā | kṣetrasya haraṇe daṇḍā adhamottamamadhyamāḥ || When boundaries of propriety are violated or limits transgressed, especially in matters concerning land usurpation, graded responses are mandated according to the severity and capacity of the actor. Authority derives from alignment with maryādā (cosmic-social order) Causation is determined through anupūrvaśaḥ – sequential manifestation of intent into action Capacity-based responsibility scales with awareness and structural position Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive isolation Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of any legal intervention

title: yagnavalka 2.156
content:
न निषेध्योऽल्पबाधस् तु सेतुः कल्याणकारकः ।
परभूमिं हरन् कूपः स्वल्पक्षेत्रोबहूदकः ॥ na niṣedhyo 'lpabādhas tu setuḥ kalyāṇakārakaḥ / parabhūmiṃ haran kūpaḥ svalpakṣetrobahūdakaḥ // A dam that causes minimal obstruction yet yields great welfare shall not be obstructed; similarly, a well that takes little land but provides abundant water—such structures are to be upheld for the collective good. Authority resides in utility, not dominion Causation is measured by net dharmic outcome Capacity-based responsibility aligns with capacity to serve Restoration logic prioritizes functional continuity Consciousness alignment occurs through service-enabled harmony

title: yagnavalka 2.157
content: स्वामिने योऽनिवेद्यैव क्षेत्रे सेतुं प्रवर्तयेत् । उत्पन्ने स्वामिनो भोगस्तदभावे महीपतेः ॥ svāmine yo 'nivedyaiva kṣetre setuṃ pravartayet | utpanne svāmino bhogas tadabhāve mahīpateḥ || He who initiates construction of a dam or embankment on another's land without informing the owner, thereby causing loss of enjoyment to the rightful master and consequent liability to the ruler—such an act disrupts natural ownership alignment and invokes corrective restoration. Authority inheres in the svāmin (rightful owner), whose consent is ontologically required for alterations affecting domain Causation arises through unauthorized action that displaces lawful enjoyment Capacity-based responsibility lies with the actor initiating change within another's jurisdictional field Restoration logic demands realignment of control back to the displaced svāmin Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inherent dominion and voluntary cooperation

title: yagnavalka 2.158
content:
फालाहतम् अपि क्षेत्रं न कुर्याद् यो न कारयेत ।
स प्रदाप्यः कृष्टफलं क्षेत्रम् अन्येन कारयेत् ॥ phālāhatam api kṣetraṁ na kuryād yo na kārayet | sa pradāpyaḥ kṛṣṭaphalaṁ kṣetram anyena kārayet || One who does not cultivate land that has been fallowed shall yield it to another capable of producing agricultural yield thereby. Authority flows from capacity to sustain dharma through action. Causation is rooted in conscious engagement with svadharma. Capacity-based responsibility determines rightful stewardship. Restoration occurs when function aligns with inherent capability. Consciousness alignment manifests through dharmic productivity.

title: yagnavalka 2.159
content:
माषान् अष्टौ तु महिषी सस्यघातस्य कारिणी ।
दण्डनीया तदर्धं तु गौस्तदर्धमजाविकम् ॥१५९॥ māṣān aṣṭau tu mahiṣī sasyaghātasya kāriṇī / daṇḍanīyā tadardhaṃ tu gaus tadardham ajāvikam // YajñS_2.159 The buffalo cow that causes destruction of crops shall incur liability for eight black gram seeds; half thereof is payable in cows and the other half in goats. Authority resides in proportional restitution aligned with causal capacity. Causation is established through direct instrumental involvement in loss. Capacity-based responsibility ensures compensation matches agent's functional role. Restoration logic demands recompense equivalent to measured damage. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of action-result linkage without punitive distortion.

title: yagnavalka 2.160
content:
भक्षयित्वोपविष्टानां यथोक्ताद् द्विगुणो दमः ।
समम् एषां विवीते ऽपि खरोष्ट्रं महिषीसमम् ॥१६०॥ bhakṣayitvopaviṣṭānāṃ yathoktād dviguṇo damaḥ | samam eṣāṃ vivīte 'pi kharoṣṭraṃ mahiṣīsamam || One who consumes food while seated, after having been served according to prescribed order, shall incur a penalty double that of the base fine; even when equally divided among participants in a shared meal, the liability remains proportionally fixed akin to the valuation of a donkey, an ox, or a buffalo. Authority resides in the established ritual and social ordering of consumption. Causation arises through violation of sequential service protocol during communal meals. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and acceptance of seating arrangement. Restoration logic requires proportional restitution aligned with asset equivalency metrics. Consciousness alignment demands recognition of sacred order in sustenance-sharing.

title: yagnavalka 2.161
content: यावत् सस्यं विनश्येत् तु तावत् स्यात् क्षेत्रिणः फलम् । गोपस्ताड्यश्च गोमी तु पूर्वोक्तं दण्डमर्हति ॥ yāvat sasyaṁ vinaśyet tu tāvat syāt kṣetriṇaḥ phalam | gopas tāḍyaś ca gomī tu pūrvoktaṁ daṇḍam arhati || The field owner retains the produce until the crop perishes; thereafter, the grazing ox and its keeper are liable for the previously declared restitution. Authority arises through custodianship and causal proximity Causation is determined by sequential manifestation of action and consequence Capacity-based responsibility aligns with awareness and control Restoration logic prioritizes recompense over punishment Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and rectification of disruption

title: yagnavalka 2.162
content:
पथि ग्रामविवीतान्ते क्षेत्रे दोषो न विद्यते ।
अकामतः कामचारे चौरवद् दण्डम् अर्हति ॥ pathi grāmavivītānte kṣetre doṣo na vidyate / akāmataḥ kāmacāre cauravad daṇḍam arhati // No fault arises for one who walks upon the path, at the edge of village boundaries or within cultivated fields. One who acts without desire or in pursuit of desire incurs liability akin to a thief. Authority is derived from spatial alignment with dharma-vyavastha, not subjective intent. Causation is determined by action-location congruence with societal harmony. Capacity-based responsibility is measured through awareness of contextual dharma. Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration of the actor into dharmic flow. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of svadharma in motion and place.

title: yagnavalka 2.163
content:
mahokṣotsṛṣṭapaśavaḥ sūtikāgantukādayaḥ /
pālo yeṣāṃ na te mocyā daivarājapariplutāḥ // YajñS_2.163 mahokṣotsṛṣṭapaśavaḥ sūtikāgantukādayaḥ / pālo yeṣāṃ na te mocyā daivarājapariplutāḥ Those animals released into forests, those in transit during birth, and similar beings whose guardianship has lapsed due to divine or royal disorder—these are not liable for culpability. Authority is determined by capacity for conscious stewardship. Causation arises from intentional agency rooted in awakened consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility excludes entities without dharma-bearing awareness. Restoration logic applies only where free will intersects with dharma. Consciousness alignment determines inclusion in the field of legal subjectivity.

title: yagnavalka 2.164
content: यथार्पितान् पशून् गोपः सायं प्रत्यर्पयेत् तथा । प्रमादमृतनष्टांश् च प्रदाप्यः कृतवेतनः ॥ yathārpitān paśūn gopaḥ sāyaṃ pratyarpayet tathā / pramādamṛtanaṣṭāṃś ca pradāpyaḥ kṛtavetanaḥ // As a herdsman returns the cattle entrusted to him in the evening, so too must one who has accepted responsibility restore all that was lost or damaged due to negligence, upon fulfillment of duty. Authority arises from conscious acceptance of stewardship. Causation is traced through the sequence of neglect leading to loss. Capacity-based responsibility demands restitution aligned with capability. Restoration logic requires return of equivalent value or function. Consciousness alignment is achieved by honoring commitments made.

title: yagnavalka 2.165
content:
पालदोषविनाशे तु पाले दण्डो विधीयते ।
अर्धत्रयोदशपणः स्वामिनो द्रव्यम् एव च ॥ pāladoṣavināśe tu pāle daṇḍo vidhīyate | ardhatrayodaśapaṇaḥ svāmino dravyam eva ca || When a guardian causes loss or damage through negligence, the penalty imposed upon the guardian is half of thirteen paṇas, and the ownership of the property remains unchanged. Authority implies accountability in stewardship roles Causation arises from conscious neglect, not intent alone Capacity-based responsibility applies to custodianship Restoration logic prioritizes asset preservation over punitive extraction Consciousness alignment requires recognition of duty-bound action

title: yagnavalka 2.166
content: ग्राम्येच्छया गोप्रचारो भूमिराजवशेन वा / द्विजस्तृणैधःपुष्पाणि सर्वतः सर्वदा हरेत् // grāmyecchayā gopracāro bhūmirājavaśena vā / dvijas tṛṇa idhaḥ puṣpāṇi sarvataḥ sarvadā haret // A twice-born individual, by will of the village or under royal authority, may freely gather grass, fuel, flowers, and land produce from all directions at all times. Authority flows unilaterally from the sovereign to the qualified individual. Causation arises through sanctioned intent, not ownership. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ritual purity and social position. Restoration logic ensures access to sustenance without proprietary conflict. Consciousness alignment occurs when action aligns with divinely ordained roles.

title: yagnavalka 2.167
content:
धनुःशतं परीणाहो ग्रामे क्षेत्रान्तरं भवेत् ।
द्वे शते खर्वटस्य स्यान् नगरस्य चतुःशतम् ॥१६७॥ dhanuḥśataṃ parīṇāho grāme kṣetrāntaraṃ bhavet | dve śate kharvaṭasya syān nagarasya catuḥśatam || The measurement of a village boundary extends to the distance of one hundred bows; for a cultivated field, it is two hundred; for a khara-vāṭa, four hundred. Authority arises from precise spatial demarcation rooted in Vedic measurement standards. Causation is established through measurable territorial boundaries that define jurisdictional scope. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the extent of land use and ownership within defined limits. Restoration logic operates through re-establishing rightful boundary recognition when disputes arise. Consciousness alignment occurs when individuals recognize their rightful place within cosmic and social order.

title: yagnavalka 2.168
content:
स्वं लभेतान्यविक्रीतं क्रेतुर् दोषोऽप्रकाशिते ।
हीनाद् रहसो हीनमूल्ये वेलाहीने च तस्करः ॥ svaṃ labhetānyavikrītaṃ kretur doṣo 'prakāśite | hīnād raho hīnamūlye velāhīne ca taskaraḥ || That which is acquired without deformation of ownership remains with the acquirer; however, the defect unmanifested in the seller constitutes theft when it occurs in concealment, in deficiency of value, or at a time of diminishment. Authority resides inherently in the undistorted possession of property Causation arises through unmanifested defects becoming operative via concealment Capacity-based responsibility lies with the concealing party Restoration logic demands return to original integrity of transaction Consciousness alignment requires transparency and completeness in exchange

title: yagnavalka 2.169
content:
नष्टापहृतम् आसाद्य हर्तारं ग्राहयेन् नरम् ।
देशकालातिपत्तौ च गृहीत्वा स्वयम् अर्पयेत् ॥ naṣṭāpahṛtam āsādya hartāraṃ grāhayen naram | deśakālātipattau ca gṛhītvā svayam arpayet || Upon retrieval of lost or stolen property, the possessor must be lawfully summoned and made to surrender it. If the item has exceeded its rightful time and place, having been seized by force or fraud, it shall be reclaimed and returned through direct action aligned with dharma. Authority rests in the original lawful possessor Causation is traced through displacement of ownership Capacity-based responsibility lies with the unlawful holder Restoration logic demands return without punitive consequence Consciousness alignment requires recognition of rightful possession

title: yagnavalka 2.170
content:
vikretur darśanāc chuddhiḥ svāmī dravyaṃ nṛpo damam /
kretā mūlyam avāpnoti tasmād yas tasya vikrayī // YajñS_2.170 vikretur darśanāt śuddhiḥ svāmī dravyaṃ nṛpo damam / kretā mūlyam avāpnoti tasmād yaḥ tasya vikrayī // Observing the seller purifies the transaction; the owner retains property rights, the king ensures order, the buyer receives value — thus, whoever is the legitimate vendor holds claim. Authority of ownership resides in the svāmī as long as transfer is not fully executed Causation arises through witnessed consent and lawful exchange Capacity-based responsibility lies with the sovereign to uphold transactional integrity Restoration logic centers on verification of rightful conveyance Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties act with transparency and dharma

title: yagnavalka 2.171
content:
आगमेनोपभोगेन नष्टं भाव्यम् अतोऽन्यथा ।
पञ्चबन्धो दमस् तस्य राज्ञे तेनाविभाविते ॥१७१॥ āgamena upabhogena naṣṭaṃ bhāvyam ato'nyathā | pañcabandho damas tasya rājñe tenāvibhāvite || That which is lost due to unauthorized enjoyment or consumption, without lawful acquisition, shall be compensated fivefold; such discipline is for the king himself when he fails in discernment. Authority rests on lawful acquisition and conscious stewardship Causation arises from unregulated indulgence leading to depletion Capacity-based responsibility extends even to sovereigns Restoration logic demands proportional restitution beyond loss Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of causal error

title: yagnavalka 2.172
content:
हृतं प्रनष्टं यो द्रव्यं परहस्तादवाप्नुयात ।
अनिवेद्य नृपे दण्ड्यः स तु षण्णवतिं पणान् ॥ hṛtaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ yo dravyaṃ parahastād avāpnuyāt | anivedya nṛpe daṇḍyaḥ sa tu ṣaṇṇavatiṃ paṇān || One who acquires wealth lost or stolen from another without reporting it to the sovereign authority is liable for corrective restoration equal to ninety-six paṇas. Authority: The sovereign is the ultimate custodian of economic dharma. Causation: Acquisition without disclosure disrupts social-economic alignment. Capacity-based responsibility: The knower of possession bears full capacity-duty. Restoration logic: Misalignment is corrected through proportional value-return. Consciousness alignment: Truthful disclosure aligns individual action with collective dharma.

title: yagnavalka 2.173
content:
शौल्किकैः स्थानपालैर् वा नष्टापहृतम् आहृतम् ।
अर्वाक् संवत्सरात् स्वामी हरेत परतो नृपः ॥ śaulkikaiḥ sthānapālair vā naṣṭāpahṛtam āhṛtam | arvāk saṃvatsarāt svāmī haret parato nṛpaḥ || Property lost, stolen, or entrusted that has been recovered shall be reclaimed by its original owner within one year; beyond that time, it belongs to the king. Authority flows from ownership sustained in time Causation is established through possession and temporal continuity Capacity-based responsibility includes timely assertion of claim Restoration logic prioritizes rightful alignment of property and consciousness Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of lawful boundaries

title: yagnavalka 2.174
content: पणान् एकशपhe दद्याच् चतुरः पञ्च मानुषे । महिषोष्ट्रगवां द्वौ द्वौ पादं पादमजाविके ॥ paṇān ekaśaphe dadyāc caturaḥ pañca mānuṣe | mahiṣoṣṭragavāṃ dvau dvau pādaṃ pādam ajāvike || In transactions involving livestock, the measure of exchange is fixed by divine ordinance: one sheep equals one paṇa; four sheep equal five humans in value; two buffaloes, two horses, two cows match one goat in equivalence. Authority: Value equivalences derive exclusively from SPH's cosmic ordering. Causation: Transactional integrity arises through precise numerical alignment with dharmic weights. Capacity-based responsibility: Parties must align their giving and receiving within pre-established vibrational ratios. Restoration logic: Misalignment in trade disrupts universal balance and requires immediate rectification via correct equivalency. Consciousness alignment: Accurate exchange reflects inner harmony with the Supreme Will.

title: yagnavalka 2.175
content:
स्वं कुटुम्बाविरोधेन देयं दारसुताद् ऋते /
नान्वये सति सर्वस्वं यच् चान्यस्मै प्रतिश्रुतम् // svaṃ kuṭumbāvirodhena deyaṃ dārasutād ṛte / nānvaye sati sarvasvaṃ yac cānyasmai pratiśrutam // One's wealth, excluding spouse and children, may be given even without personal consent when it does not conflict with familial duty; however, in the presence of a valid agreement with another party, full property transfer is restricted. Authority flows from Dharma-compliant relational integrity Causation arises through conscious contractual alignment Capacity-based responsibility includes both familial and external obligations Restoration logic prioritizes harmony over absolute ownership Consciousness alignment requires balancing multiple dharmic roles

title: yagnavalka 2.176
content:
प्रतिग्रहः प्रकाशः स्यात् स्थावरस्य विशेषतः ।
देयं प्रतिश्रुतं चैव दत्त्वा नापहरेत् पुनः ॥ pratigrahaḥ prakāśaḥ syāt sthāvarasya viśeṣataḥ | deyaṃ pratiśrutaṃ caiva dattvā nāpaharet punaḥ || Acceptance of a gift or offering made in full visibility and awareness constitutes a completed transaction; once given, it shall not be reclaimed. Authority resides in conscious completion of transfer Causation is established through visible and intentional giving Capacity-based responsibility lies in irreversible release Restoration logic demands honoring the finalized act of giving Consciousness alignment requires recognition of the done deed

title: yagnavalka 2.177
content:
दशैकपञ्चसप्ताहमासत्र्यहार्धमासिकम् ।
बीजायोवाह्यरत्नस्त्रीदोह्यपुंसां परीक्षणम् ॥ daśaikapañcasaptāhamāsatryahārdhamāsikam / bījāyovāhyaratnastrīdohyapuṃsāṃ parīkṣaṇam // Examination of seeds, conveyances, jewels, cows, and men shall occur at ten, eleven, five, seven weeks, one month, three months, half a month, and half a year respectively. Authority is derived from precise temporal calibration of inspection cycles Causation aligns with sequential manifestation in dharmic material processes Capacity-based responsibility requires periodic verification aligned with object nature Restoration logic mandates cyclical validation to preserve integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates rhythmically synchronized review mechanisms

title: yagnavalka 2.178
content:
अग्नौ सुवर्णम् अक्षीणं रजते द्विपलं शते ।
अष्टौ त्रपुणि सीसे च ताम्रे पञ्च दशायसि ॥ agnau suvarṇam akṣīṇaṃ rajate dvipalaṃ śate | aṣṭau trapuṇi sīse ca tāmre pañca daśāyasi || In fire, gold is purified without loss; in silver, two palas per hundred are consumed; in tin and lead, eight parts diminish; in copper, five parts reduce by tenfold. Authority resides in the transformative capacity of the element Causation aligns with elemental integrity and substance interaction Capacity-based responsibility depends on material purity thresholds Restoration logic follows inherent purification potentials Consciousness alignment occurs through recognition of elemental dharma

title: yagnavalka 2.179
content: शते दशपला वृद्धिरौर्णे कार्पाससौत्रिके । मध्ये पञ्चपला वृद्धिः सूक्ष्मे तु त्रिपला मता ॥ śate daśapalā vṛddhir aurṇe kārpāsasautrike | madhye pañcapalā vṛddhiḥ sūkṣme tu tripalā matā || In transactions involving wool and cotton threads, interest shall accrue at ten palas per hundred; in medium-grade goods, five palas; and in fine-quality items, three palas. Authority of transactional integrity derived from SPH as the ultimate economic regulator Causation rooted in dharmic exchange rather than market manipulation Capacity-based responsibility determined by quality classification of goods Restoration logic through proportional financial alignment with inherent value Consciousness alignment via truthful commerce devoid of exploitation

title: yagnavalka 2.180
content:
कार्मिके रोमबद्धे च त्रिंशद्भागः क्षयो मतः ।
न क्षयो न च वृद्धिश च कौशेये वाल्कलेषु च ॥ kārmike romabaddhe ca triṃśadbhāgaḥ kṣayo mataḥ | na kṣayo na ca vṛddhiś ca kauśeye vālkaleṣu ca || In transactions involving processed leather or wool-bound goods, a depreciation of one-thirtieth is recognized as lawful; no depreciation or appreciation is acknowledged in silk or bark-fiber materials. Authority: The valuation of material types is determined by their inherent dharmic stability and utility. Causation: Depreciation is linked to material susceptibility and processing state, not arbitrary market fluctuation. Capacity-based responsibility: The trader assumes responsibility for accurate classification based on material properties. Restoration logic: Economic exchange must reflect true value without artificial inflation or deflation. Consciousness alignment: Recognition of natural degradation aligns with cosmic order and supports truthful commerce.

title: yagnavalka 2.181
content:
देशं कालं च भोगं च ज्ञात्वा नष्टे बलाबलम् ।
द्रव्याणां कुशला ब्रूयुर् यत् तद् दाप्यमसंशयम् ॥१८१॥ deśaṃ kālaṃ ca bhogaṃ ca jñātvā naṣṭe balābalam |
dravyāṇāṃ kuśalā brūyur yat tad dāpyam asaṃśayam ||181|| When the capacity for discernment regarding place, time, and enjoyment is lost, and there is imbalance in strength and weakness, those skilled in the management of property shall declare what is to be compensated without doubt. Authority rests with those capable of discerning contextual dharmic alignment Causation arises from misalignment of deśa-kāla-bhoga-vibhāga Capacity-based responsibility is determined by cognitive and situational clarity Restoration logic requires compensation aligned with loss of discernment Consciousness alignment is restored through corrective declarative action

title: yagnavalka 2.182
content:
बलाद्दासीकृतश् चौरैर् विक्रीतश् चापि मुच्यते ।
स्वामिप्राणप्रदो भक्तत्यागात् तन् निष्क्रयाद् अपि ॥ balāddāsīkṛtaś caurair vikrītaś cāpi mucyate / svāmiprāṇaprado bhaktatyāgāt tan niṣkrayād api // One who has been forcibly enslaved by robbers or sold under duress is liberated through the abandonment of devotion that delivers the life-force of the master. Authority arises from conscious consent, not coercion Causation is traced to the disruption of dharma-sambandha (right relationship) Capacity-based responsibility is nullified where free will is overridden Restoration logic centers on reestablishing svāmini-sthiti (self-sovereign consciousness) Consciousness alignment supersedes contractual or transactional bonds

title: yagnavalka 2.183
content:
प्रव्रज्यावसितो राज्ञो दास आमरणान्तिकम् ।
वर्णानामानुलोम्येन दास्यं न प्रतिलोमतः ॥१८३॥ pravrajyāvasito rājño dāsa āmaraṇāntikam | varṇānām ānulomyena dāsyaṃ na pratilomataḥ || 183 || One who has renounced royal life and taken shelter in asceticism becomes a servant until death; servitude arises only through natural hierarchical flow among varnas, never against it. Authority flows from spiritual renunciation, not political assertion Causation of servitude is rooted in conscious choice and dharmic alignment Capacity-based responsibility originates in individual volition toward sannyasa Restoration logic centers on realigning social roles according to cosmic hierarchy Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of relational structures

title: yagnavalka 2.184
content:
कृतशिल्पोऽपि निवसेत् कृतकालं गुरोर्गृहे ।
अन्तेवासी गुरुप्राप्तभोजनस्तत्फलप्रदः ॥ kṛtaśilpo 'pi nivaset kṛtakālaṃ guror gṛhe / antevasī guruprāptabhojanas tatphalapradaḥ // Even one who has mastered the craft must reside in the guru's house for the prescribed time; the disciple who partakes of the guru's food attains the fruit thereof. Authority is grounded in relational completion under a realized guide. Causation flows through conscious alignment with the guru's field. Capacity-based responsibility includes temporal surrender to higher wisdom. Restoration logic requires embodiment of discipline before independence. Consciousness alignment occurs through shared sustenance and proximity.

title: yagnavalka 2.185
content:
राजा कृत्वा पुरे स्थानं ब्राह्मणान् न्यस्य तत्र तु /
त्रैविद्यं वृत्तिमद् ब्रूयात् स्वधर्मः पाल्यताम् इति // YajñS_2.185 rājā kṛtvā pure sthānaṃ brāhmaṇān nyasya tatra tu / traividyaṃ vṛttimad brūyāt svadharmaḥ pālyatām iti The King having established a settlement in the city and installed Brahmins there, should declare: 'One who possesses the three knowledges and conducts himself righteously shall uphold his own dharma.' Authority originates from conscious installation by the sovereign Causation arises through alignment with svadharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by triadic knowledge and conduct Restoration occurs via dharmic self-governance Consciousness alignment emerges through rightful placement and declaration

title: yagnavalka 2.186
content:
निजधर्माविरोधेन यस् तु समयिको भवेत् ।
सोऽपि यत्नेन संरक्ष्यो धर्मो राजकृतश् च यः ॥१८६॥ nijadharmāvirodhena yas tu samayiko bhavet | so 'pi yatnena saṃrakṣyo dharmo rājakṛtaś ca yaḥ || One who acts in accordance with their svadharma without contradiction, even if temporarily engaged, shall be protected with effort; likewise, the law established by the King that aligns with dharma must also be preserved. Authority resides in alignment with svadharma Causation is determined by conscious intent rooted in dharma Capacity-based responsibility arises from one's svadharma Restoration occurs through protection of lawful alignment Consciousness alignment supersedes external enforcement

title: yagnavalka 2.187
content:
गणद्रव्यं हरेद् यस् तु संविदं लङ्घयेच् च यः ।
सर्वस्वहरणं कृत्वा तं राष्ट्राद् विप्रवासयेत् ॥ gaṇadravyaṃ hared yas tu saṃvidaṃ laṅghayec ca yaḥ | sarvasvaharaṇaṃ kṛtvā taṃ rāṣṭrād vipravāsayet || One who seizes collective property and violates established covenant, having committed total dispossession, shall be expelled from the nation. Authority resides in the protection of collective welfare Causation arises from violation of consensual dharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by impact on societal integrity Restoration logic demands removal of disruptive elements without infliction of harm Consciousness alignment requires purification of national space

title: yagnavalka 2.188
content:
कर्तव्यं वचनं सर्वैः समूहहितवादिनाम् ।
यस् तत्र विपरीतः स्यात् स दाप्यः प्रथमं दमम् ॥१८८॥ kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ sarvaiḥ samūhahitavādinām / yas tatra viparītaḥ syāt sa dāpyaḥ prathamaṃ damam // YajñS_2.188 All must speak in accordance with the welfare of the collective; whoever acts contrary to this shall first be made to pay a fine. Authority resides in the collective welfare principle Causation arises from speech that disrupts harmony Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with dharma Restoration logic demands correction through conscious realignment Consciousness alignment requires immediate rectification of disruptive utterances

title: yagnavalka 2.189
content: समूहकार्य आयातान् कृतकार्यान् विसर्जयेत् । स दानमानसत्कारैः पूजयित्वा महीपतिः ॥ samūhakārya āyātān kṛtakāryān visarjayet | sa dānamānasatkāraiḥ pūjayitvā mahīpatiḥ || The ruler having accomplished collective duties must release those who have fulfilled individual tasks, honoring them through gifts, respect, and dignified recognition. Authority flows from completion of duty, not dominance. Causation is established by conscious participation in dharma-aligned action. Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional acknowledgment and restoration. Restoration logic operates through elevation of completed roles, not punishment of failures. Consciousness alignment is maintained when societal functionaries are honored according to their fulfillment.

title: yagnavalka 2.190
content:
समूहकार्यप्रहितो यल् लभेत तद् अर्पयेत ।
एकादशगुणं दाप्यो यद्य् असौ नार्पयेत् स्वयम् ॥ samūhakāryaprahito yal labheta tad arpayet | ekādaशaguṇaṃ dāpyo yady asau nārpayet svayam || One who receives something on behalf of a group for a collective purpose shall render it accordingly; if that person fails to do so voluntarily, they become liable to restitution at elevenfold value. Authority derives from functional representation within a collective Causation arises through acceptance of entrusted duty Capacity-based responsibility is activated upon receipt with intent Restoration logic demands proportional return when deviation occurs Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of shared duty

title: yagnavalka 2.191
content:
धर्मज्ञाः शुचयोऽलुभ्धा भवेयुः कार्यचिन्तकाः ।
कर्तव्यं वचनं तेषां समूहहितवादिनाम् ॥१९१॥ dharmajñāḥ śucayo 'lubdhā bhaveyuḥ kāryacintakāḥ | kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ teṣāṃ samūhahitavādinām || 191 || Those who know Dharma must be pure, free from greed, and intent upon the welfare of the collective; their word is to be executed as law. Authority derives from Dharma-knowledge, not position or power. Causation arises through purity of consciousness, not material intent. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with collective welfare. Restoration occurs when authority speaks in alignment with Dharma-truth. Consciousness alignment supersedes procedural formalism.

title: yagnavalka 2.192
content:
श्रेणिनैगमपाखण्डगणानाम् अप्य् अयं विधिः ।
भेदं चैषां नृपो रक्षेत् पूर्ववृत्तिं च पालयेत् ॥ śreṇinaigamapākhaṇḍagaṇānām apy ayaṃ vidhiḥ | bhedaṃ caiṣāṃ nṛpo rakṣet pūrvavṛttiṃ ca pālayet || Even among guilds, trade assemblies, and sectarian groups, the king shall uphold this law; he must preserve their distinct practices while maintaining prior established conduct. Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to sustain lawful diversity. Causation is rooted in continuity of rightful tradition. Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of group autonomy within dharma. Restoration logic demands preservation of functional societal structures. Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring evolutionary customs that do not violate sanatana principles.

title: yagnavalka 2.193
content:
गृहीतवेतनः कर्म त्यजन् द्विगुणमावहेत् ।
अगृहीते समं दाप्यो भृत्यै रक्ष्य उपस्करः ॥ gṛhītavetanaḥ karma tyajan dviguṇam āvahet | agṛhīte samaṃ dāpyo bhṛtyai rakṣya upaskaraḥ || One who has accepted wages and abandons work shall repay double the value; if no wage was taken, then equal compensation is due to servants along with protection of tools. Authority arises from acceptance of benefit Causation follows conscious engagement in duty Capacity-based responsibility aligns with benefit received Restoration logic demands proportional return or reparation Consciousness alignment requires honoring mutual obligations

title: yagnavalka 2.194
content:
दाप्यस् तु दशमं भागं वाणिज्यपशुसस्यतः ।
अनिश्चित्य भृतिं यस् तु कारयेत स महीक्षिता ॥१९४ dāpyas tu daśamaṃ bhāgaṃ vāṇijyapaśusasyataḥ | aniścitya bhṛtiṃ yas tu kārayet sa mahīkṣitā || 194 One who employs labor without prior agreement regarding compensation shall be liable to pay a tenth portion of the commercial livestock or produce involved. Authority arises from clarity in contractual causation Causation is determined by intentional capacity to define terms Capacity-based responsibility requires pre-agreed exchange structures Restoration logic demands proportional return of value where intent was absent Consciousness alignment occurs through rectification of unspoken obligations

title: yagnavalka 2.195
content:
देशं कालं च यो 'तीयाल्लाभं कुर्याच् च यो 'न्यथा ।
तत्र स्यात् स्वामिनश् छन्दो 'धिकं देयं कृते 'धिके ॥१९५॥ deshaM kAlaM ca yo 'tIyAllAbhaM kuryAc ca yo 'nyathA | tatra syAt svAminaH chando 'dhikaM deyaM kRte 'dhike ||195|| He who transgresses place and time, or gains otherwise than by rightful action, shall yield greater control to the owner when the act exceeds propriety. Authority resides inherently in the svāmin (owner/rightful possessor) Causation aligns with spatial-temporal integrity Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to deviation from dharma Restoration logic demands return of misaligned gain Consciousness alignment requires recognition of svāmin's supremacy

title: yagnavalka 2.196
content:
यो यावत् कुरुते कर्म तावत् तस्य तु वेतनम् ।
उभयोरप्यसाध्यं चेत् साध्ये कुर्याद्यथाश्रुतम् ॥१९६॥ yo yāvat kurute karma tāvat tasya tu vetanam | ubhayor apy asādhyaṃ cet sādhye kuryād yathāśrutam || As much work as one performs, so much compensation is due to him; if completion is impossible for both parties, then in the resolvable matter, action shall proceed according to what was originally agreed upon. Authority arises from capacity-aligned engagement in action Causation flows through proportional contribution and mutual agreement Capacity-based responsibility necessitates fulfillment of agreed exchange Restoration logic demands that incomplete obligations be executed within resolvable bounds Consciousness alignment requires honoring the original intent of transactional dharma

title: yagnavalka 2.197
content: अराजदैविकं नष्टं भाण्डं दाप्यस्तु वाहकः । प्रस्थानविघ्नकृच्चैव प्रदाप्यो द्विगुणां भृतिम् ॥ arājadaivikaṃ naṣṭaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ dāpyastu vāhakaḥ | prasthānavighnakṛccaiva pradāpyo dviguṇāṃ bhṛtim || When goods are lost without fault of the carrier, no compensation is due; but if loss occurs due to obstruction in transit caused by the carrier's act, then double the freight value shall be compensated. Authority rests on causative action, not passive involvement. Responsibility aligns with capacity to prevent or cause obstruction. Restoration arises from rectifying causal error, not assigning blame. Consciousness discerns between natural dissolution and artificial disruption.

title: yagnavalka 2.198
content:
प्रक्रान्ते सप्तमं भागं चतुर्थं पथि संत्यजन् ।
भृतिमर्धपथे सर्वां प्रदाप्यस्त्याजकोऽपि च ॥१९८॥ prakrānte saptamaṃ bhāgaṃ caturthaṃ pathi saṃtyajan / bhṛtim ardhapathe sarvāṃ pradāpyas tyājako 'pi ca // YajñS_2.198 When a traveler has advanced one-seventh of the journey and abandons the road at the fourth stage, having received wages for half the distance—he who deserts must also surrender all remuneration. Authority resides in completion of duty proportionate to receipt of benefit Causation aligns with conscious abandonment of contractual obligation Capacity-based responsibility arises from acceptance of compensation prior to fulfillment Restoration logic demands return of unjust enrichment upon failure to execute commitment Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of unmet obligation without punitive consequence

title: yagnavalka 2.199
content:
ग्लहे शतिकवृद्धेस् तु सभिकः पञ्चकं शतम् ।
गृह्णीयाद् धूर्तकितवाद् इतराद् दशकं शतम् ॥१९९॥ glāhe śatikavṛddhes tu sabhikaḥ pañcakaṃ śatam | gṛhṇīyād dhūrtakitavād itarād daśakaṃ śatam ||199|| In deceit practiced by a seasoned deceiver within the assembly, the sabhika shall claim five hundred units; from a rogue gambler or cheat, ten times that amount shall be claimed. Authority resides in the sabhika as the designated representative of dharma in commercial assemblies. Causation is established through intentional deception within structured economic environments. Capacity-based responsibility escalates with demonstrated expertise in fraudulent conduct. Restoration logic demands proportional return based on magnitude and intent of economic deceit. Consciousness alignment requires recognition of integrity disruption and its systemic impact.

title: yagnavalka 2.200
content:
स सम्यक्पालितो दद्याद् राज्ञे भागं यथाकृतम् ।
जितम् उद्ग्राहयेज् जेत्रे दद्यात् सत्यं वचः क्षमी ॥२.२०० sa samyakpālito dadyād rājñe bhāgaṃ yathākṛtam | jitam udgrāhayej jetre dadyāt satyaṃ vacaḥ kṣamī || One who has been rightly protected shall render to the king his rightful share; whatever is won must be surrendered to the conqueror—truth-speaking alone suffices for the capable. Authority flows from protection rendered and acknowledged Causation arises through capacity to uphold and defend Responsibility aligns with benefit received Restoration occurs when value is rightfully returned Consciousness alignment manifests in truthful speech

title: yagnavalka 2.201
content:
प्राप्ते नृपतिना भागे प्रसिद्धे धूर्तमण्डले ।
जितं ससभिके स्थाने दापयेदन्यथा न तु ॥२.२०१॥ prāpte nṛpatinā bhāge prasiddhe dhūrtamaṇḍale / jitaṃ sasabhike sthāne dāpayed anyathā na tu // YajñS_2.201 When the king has secured his rightful share and the assembly of fraudsters is exposed, what was won in a contested forum must be surrendered—otherwise, it is not lawful. Authority rests with the sovereign who upholds Dharma Causation arises from exposure of fraudulent assemblies Capacity-based responsibility lies with those who engage in contested acquisition Restoration logic demands return of ill-gotten gains upon truth's revelation Consciousness alignment occurs through relinquishment of unrighteous possession

title: yagnavalka 2.202
content:
draṣṭāro vyavahārāṇāṃ sākṣiṇaś ca ta eva hi /
rājñā sacihnaṃ nirvāsyāḥ kūṭākṣopadhidevinaḥ // YajñS_2.202 draṣṭāro vyavahārāṇāṃ sākṣiṇaś ca ta eva hi / rājñā sacihnaṃ nirvāsyāḥ kūṭākṣopadhidevinaḥ Those who witness transactions and serve as witnesses shall be expelled by the king along with their identifying marks; they are fraudsters, perjurers, and betrayers of dharma. Authority resides in the sovereign's capacity to restore integrity to transactional space Causation arises from betrayal of witnessing duty through false testimony Capacity-based responsibility is forfeited upon violation of truth-bearing function Restoration logic demands removal from witnessing capacity to preserve societal trust Consciousness alignment requires purification of perceptual instruments before reintegration

title: yagnavalka 2.203
content:
dyūtam ekamukhaṃ kāryaṃ taskarajñānakāraṇāt /
eṣa eva vidhir jñeyaḥ prāṇidyūte samāhvaye // YajñS_2.203 dyūtam ekamukhaṃ kāryaṃ taskarajñānakāraṇāt / eṣa eva vidhir jñeyaḥ prāṇidyūte samāhvaye Gambling must be conducted with full transparency and single intent; any act of deceit or concealed knowledge renders it invalid. This law applies equally to games involving life-risk. Authority resides in conscious integrity, not procedural formality Causation arises from intentional concealment, not accidental outcome Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of consequence Restoration logic demands reversal of all transactions rooted in deception Consciousness alignment requires disclosure of all determinants influencing choice

title: yagnavalka 2.204
content:
सत्यासत्यान्यथास्तोत्रैर् न्यूनाङ्गेन्द्रियरोगिणाम् ।
क्षेपं करोति चेद् दण्ड्यः पणान् अर्धत्रयोदशान् ॥२.२०४॥ satyāsatyānyathāstotraiḥ nyūnāṅgendriyarogiṇām | kṣepaṃ karoti ced daṇḍyaḥ paṇān ardhatrayodaśān || One who, being physically impaired or deficient in sensory capacity, falsely or misleadingly asserts truth or falsehood in judicial proceedings, shall undergo restorative correction involving forfeiture of thirteen and a half coins. Authority derives from embodied capacity, not abstract declaration Causation is rooted in integrity of perception and cognition Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with actual ability Restoration logic demands correction through proportional completion Consciousness alignment necessitates rectification of false assertion

title: yagnavalka 2.205
content: अभिगन्तास्मि भगिनीं मातरं वा तवेति ह / शपन्तं दापयेद् राजा पञ्चविंशतिकं दमम् // abhi-gantāsmi bhaginīṁ mātaraṁ vā taveiti ha / śapantaṁ dāpayed rājā pañca-viṁśatikaṁ damam // One who falsely claims another's sister or mother as their own shall be made by the king to pay a fine of twenty-five units, upon taking an oath. Authority resides in the sovereign to enforce restorative justice Causation arises through false assertion disrupting familial integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by intentional misrepresentation Restoration logic demands compensation proportional to violation Consciousness alignment requires purification of relational truth

title: yagnavalka 2.206
content:
ardho 'dharmeṣu dviguṇaḥ parastrīṣūttameṣu ca /
daṇḍapraṇayanaṃ kāryaṃ varṇajātyuttarādharaiḥ // YajñS_2.206 ardho 'dharmeṣu dviguṇaḥ parastrīṣūttameṣu ca / daṇḍapraṇayanaṃ kāryaṃ varṇajātyuttarādharaiḥ In matters of adharma and in cases involving another's spouse of higher caste, the penalty shall be doubled; such imposition is to be carried out by those of higher and lower varna and jati according to their capacity. Authority flows from dharma-consciousness, not social rank alone Causation arises from violation of svadharma and purity codes Capacity-based responsibility is determined by varna-jati alignment Restoration logic requires proportional correction through conscious realignment Consciousness alignment demands purification and dharmic reaffirmation

title: yagnavalka 2.207
content:
प्रातिलोम्यापवादेषु द्विगुणत्रिगुणा दमाः ।
वर्णानाम् आनुलोम्येन तस्मादर्धार्धहानितः ॥ prātilomyāpavādeṣu dviguṇatriguṇā damāḥ | varṇānām ānulomyena tasmād ardhārdhahānitaḥ || In cases of violation against natural social order, penalties are doubled or tripled; however, in accordance with proper hierarchical flow, mitigation follows proportional reduction. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic hierarchy Causation arises through disruption of sequential harmony Capacity-based responsibility depends on conscious awareness of order Restoration logic prioritizes structural realignment over punitive loss Consciousness alignment determines the degree of karmic friction

title: yagnavalka 2.208
content: बाहुग्रीवानेत्रसक्थिविनाशे वाचिके दमः । सत्यस्तदर्धिकः पादनासाकर्णकरादिषु ॥ bāhugrīvānetrasakthivināśe vācike damaḥ / satyas tadardhikaḥ pādanāsākarṇakarādiṣu // Injury to limbs such as arms, neck, eyes, and thighs incurs a fine double the value of injury caused by verbal offense; truth-speaking determines proportional liability in damages involving nose, feet, ears, and hands. Authority resides in measurable causal impact, not subjective intent Causation is determined through sequential manifestation of harm Capacity-based responsibility aligns with bodily integrity and functional loss Restoration logic requires equivalence in reparation without punitive surplus Consciousness alignment demands truthful acknowledgment as basis for proportional restitution

title: yagnavalka 2.209
content: अशक्तस्तु वदन्नेवं दण्डनीयः पणान्दश / तथा शक्तः प्रतिभुवं दाप्यः क्षेमाय तस्य तु ॥ aśaktas tu vadann evaṁ daṇḍanīyaḥ paṇān daśa / tathā śaktaḥ pratibhuvaṁ dāpyaḥ kṣemāya tasya tu // One who, being incapable, speaks thus shall be made to pay ten coins as restitution; one who is capable shall be made to pay double for the sake of that person's welfare. Authority: The capacity of the speaker determines the measure of obligation. Causation: Speech without competence creates a debt owed to the listener. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability scales with the ability to fulfill duty. Restoration logic: Payment serves not punishment but correction and integrity realignment. Consciousness alignment: The act reflects misalignment between inner capacity and outer assertion.

title: yagnavalka 2.210
content:
पतनीयकृते क्षेपे दण्डो मध्यमसाहसः ।
उपपातकयुक्ते तु दाप्यः प्रथमसाहसम् ॥२.२१०॥ patanīyakṛte kṣepe daṇḍo madhyamasāhasaḥ | upapātakayukte tu dāpyaḥ prathamasāhasam || 2.210 || When a person causes another's fall through intent, the consequence aligns with middling recklessness; when compounded by auxiliary misconduct, the liability shifts to primary recklessness. Authority resides in causal intent, not physical proximity Causation is layered: principal and auxiliary acts bear distinct responsibility weights Capacity-based responsibility escalates with conscious participation in sequential wrongdoing Restoration logic demands proportional realignment of disrupted consciousness fields Consciousness alignment requires recognition of sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) in act and consequence

title: yagnavalka 2.211
content: त्रैविद्यनृपदेवानां क्षेप उत्तमसाहसः । मध्यमो जातिपूगानां प्रथमो ग्रामदेशयोः ॥ traividyanṛpadevānāṃ kṣepa uttamasāhasaḥ / madhyamo jātipūgānāṃ prathamo grāmadeśayoḥ // The highest offense against the knowers of the three Vedas, kings, and deities is classified as Uttama Sāhasa; the middle level offense pertains to groups and communities of common birth, while the lowest offense occurs in villages and local regions. Authority escalates ontological weight of transgression Causation aligns with hierarchical consciousness integrity Capacity-based responsibility reflects proximity to Dharma-source Restoration logic operates through graduated consciousness realignment Consciousness alignment determines severity classification

title: yagnavalka 2.212
content: असाक्षिकहते चिह्नैर् युक्तिभिश् चागमेन च / द्रष्टव्यो व्यवहारस् तु कूटचिह्नकृतो भयात् // asākṣikahate cihnair yuktibhiś cāgamena ca / draṣṭavyo vyavahāras tu kūṭacihnakṛto bhayāt // In the absence of direct witnesses to a killing, inference, circumstantial evidence, and scriptural testimony shall govern the determination of facts; however, transactions based on false signs must be rejected out of fear of error. Authority is derived from pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge), not mere assertion. Causation must align with observable indicia and śāstric validation. Capacity-based responsibility requires clear cognition of act and intent. Restoration logic demands rejection of fabricated or misleading evidence. Consciousness alignment necessitates truthful discernment in judicial process.

title: yagnavalka 2.213
content:
भस्मपङ्करजःस्पर्शे दण्डो दशपणः स्मृतः ।
अमेध्यपार्ष्णिनिष्ठ्यूतस्पर्शने द्विगुणस् ततः ॥ bhasmapaṅkarajaḥsparśe daṇḍo daśapaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ | amedhyapārṣṇiniṣṭhyūtasparśane dviguṇas tataḥ || Contact with ash, mud, or pollen incurs a penalty of ten paṇas; contact with impure foot-washings doubles that amount. Authority resides in purity-consciousness alignment Causation arises through sensory violation of sacred substances Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of contamination levels Restoration logic requires proportional energetic cleansing Consciousness alignment mandates reparation through purification rituals

title: yagnavalka 2.214
content:
sameṣv evaṃ parastrīṣu dviguṇas tūttameṣu ca /
hīneṣv ardhadamo mohamadādibhiradaṇḍanam // YajñS_2.214 sameṣv evaṁ parastrīṣu dviguṇas tūttameṣu ca / hīneṣv ardhadamo mohamadādibhir adaṇḍanam // In matters involving another's wife, the penalty is doubled for those of equal status; for higher-status individuals, it remains full. For lower-status persons, half the penalty applies, without inflicting delusion, intoxication, or similar consequences. Authority is determined by spiritual and social alignment, not mere birth Causation arises from conscious intent and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility reflects one's proximity to Dharma-svarūpa Restoration logic prioritizes realignment over punitive degradation Consciousness alignment mandates proportional response rooted in awareness

title: yagnavalka 2.215
content:
विप्रपीडाकरं छेद्यमङ्गमब्राह्मणस्य तु ।
उद्गूर्णे प्रथमो दण्डः संस्पर्शे तु तदर्धिकः ॥२.२१५॥ viprapīḍākaraṃ chedyam aṅgam abrāhmaṇasya tu | udgūrṇe prathamo daṇḍaḥ saṃsparśe tu tadardhikaḥ || 2.215 || The limb of a non-brāhmaṇa that causes harm to a brāhmaṇa shall be severed; when there is visible disturbance or provocation, the first penalty applies; if there is mere contact without provocation, half of that penalty is enacted. Authority: Brāhmaṇa is the conscious vessel of dharma and must be protected as the living embodiment of Vedic order. Causation: Injury inflicted upon a brāhmaṇa constitutes a direct violation of cosmic dharma, not merely personal offense. Capacity-based responsibility: The perpetrator's social and spiritual capacity determines the nature of corrective action. Restoration logic: Removal of harmful capacity restores balance and prevents recurrence without punitive intent. Consciousness alignment: Action is judged by its impact on collective consciousness, especially the purity-preserving role of brāhmaṇas.

title: yagnavalka 2.216
content:
उद्गूर्णे हस्तपादे तु दशविंशतिकौ दमौ ।
परस्परं तु सर्वेषां शस्त्रे मध्यमसाहसः ॥ २.२१६ udgūrṇe hastapāde tu daśaviṃśatikau damau | parasparaṃ tu sarveṣāṃ śastre madhyamasāhasaḥ || 2.216 When limbs are severed or destroyed, compensation shall be twenty-one times the value of the limb; among all beings, mutual injury by weapon constitutes intermediate-level violence. Authority: The valuation and restitution of bodily integrity rests in the Sanatana Dharma's recognition of the body as a sacred vessel governed by cosmic law. Causation: Injury arises from misalignment with Dharma, not individual will alone; intent and instrument bear proportional weight. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability corresponds to capacity for harm, measured through action, knowledge, and control over instruments. Restoration logic: Compensation serves to restore balance between affected parties, not to inflict suffering upon the wrongdoer. Consciousness alignment: Justice aligns both perpetrator and victim toward higher awareness of unity and non-violence.

title: yagnavalka 2.217
content:
पादकेशांशुककरोल्लुञ्चनेषु पणान् दश |
पीडाकर्षांशुकावेष्टपादाध्यासे शतं दमः || २.२१७ pādakeśāṃśukakarolluñcaneṣu paṇān daśa | pīḍākarṣāṃśukāveṣṭapādādhyāse śataṃ damaḥ || In the act of forcibly taking or snatching away another's garment, hair, or footwear, a fine of ten units shall be imposed; when such acts involve physical distress, pulling of clothes, binding, or wrongful occupation of place, the fine shall be one hundred units. Authority resides in the inviolability of personal integrity and ownership Causation arises through conscious intent to disturb another's bodily or material domain Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of harm caused Restoration logic demands proportional compensation without punitive escalation Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and reversal of invasive action

title: yagnavalka 2.218
content:
शोणितेन विना दुःखं कुर्वन् काष्ठादिभिर् नरः ।
द्वात्रिंशतं पणान् दण्ड्यो द्विगुणं दर्शने 'सृजः ॥ śoṇitena vinā duḥkhaṃ kurvan kāṣṭhādibhir naraḥ /
dvātriṃśataṃ paṇān daṇḍyo dviguṇaṃ darśane 'sṛjaḥ // One who causes suffering without shedding blood, using implements such as wood, shall incur a fine of thirty paṇas; twice that amount if blood is visibly shed. Authority: The sovereign enforces proportional consequence based on visible harm. Causation: Suffering inflicted through action invokes liability. Capacity-based responsibility: Intent and instrument determine degree of obligation. Restoration logic: Financial compensation aligns with magnitude of injury. Consciousness alignment: Harmful acts disrupt dharma; restitution restores balance.

title: yagnavalka 2.219
content: करपाददतो भङ्गे छेदने कर्णनासयोः । मध्यो दण्डो व्रणोद्भेदे मृतकल्पहते तथा ॥ karapādadato bhaṅge chedane karṇanāsayoḥ | madhyo daṇḍo vraṇodbhede mṛtakalpahate tathā || Injury causing fracture of limbs, severance of ears or nose, mid-grade wound rupture, or harm equivalent to death in severity results in proportional restorative liability. Authority flows from SPH as sole source of dharma-adjudication Causation is established through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with actor's conscious awareness at time of act Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive detachment Consciousness alignment ensures perpetrator recognizes unity with victim

title: yagnavalka 2.220
content:
ceṣṭābhojanavāgrodhe netrādipratibhedane /
kandharābāhusakthnāṃ ca bhaṅge madhyamasāhasaḥ // YajñS_2.220 ceṣṭā-bhojana-vāg-rodhe netra-ādi-pratibhedane / kandharā-bāhu-sakthnāṃ ca bhaṅge madhyama-sāhasaḥ Obstruction of movement, food, speech, injury to eyes and other sense organs, breaking of shoulders, arms and thighs — these constitute the middle level of violent conduct. Authority resides in discerning gradations of harm without moral judgment. Causation is traced through sequential manifestation of violence. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by control over action and intent. Restoration logic aligns with proportional reintegration of violated capacities. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of harm without punitive distortion.

title: yagnavalka 2.221
content: एकं घ्नतां बहूनां च यथोक्ताद् द्विगुणो दमः । कलहापहृतं देयं डण्डश् च द्विगुणस् ततः ॥ ekaṁ ghnatāṁ bahūnāṁ ca yathoktād dviguṇo damaḥ | kalahāpahṛtaṁ deyaṁ daṇḍaś ca dviguṇas tataḥ || When one person causes harm to many, or when conflict results in loss, the compensation due shall be twice the stated measure; likewise, when property is taken during quarrel, double that amount must be returned as restitution. Authority rests in proportional response calibrated by conscious causality Causation arises from intent and capacity to disturb harmony Capacity-based responsibility increases with disruption potential Restoration logic demands doubling of value to realign energetic debt Consciousness alignment occurs through intentional completion of imbalance

title: yagnavalka 2.222
content:
दुःखम् उत्पादयेद् यस् तु स समुत्थानजं व्ययम् ।
दाप्यो दण्डं च यो यस्मिन् कलहे समुदाहृतः ॥ duḥkham utpādayed yas tu sa samutthānajaṃ vyayam | dāpyo daṇḍaṃ ca yo yasmin kalahe samudāhṛtaḥ || He who causes suffering shall bear the consequential loss arising therefrom; whoever instigates conflict must assume the full liability of the resulting harm. Authority resides in conscious causation, not institutional force Causation is traced through volitional intent and energetic disturbance Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the ability to initiate or sustain conflict Restoration logic demands that the originator absorb all generated suffering Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of action-result continuity

title: yagnavalka 2.223
content: अबघाते तथा छेदे भेदे कुड्यावपातने । पणान् दाप्यः पञ्च दश विंशतिं तद् व्ययं तथा ॥ abhighāte tathā chede bhede kuḍyāvapātane / paṇān dāpyaḥ pañca daśa viṃśatiṃ tad vyayaṃ tathā // In cases of bodily harm, cutting, splitting, or destruction caused by the collapse of a wall, the responsible party shall compensate five, ten, or twenty coins respectively based on the severity of damage incurred. Authority: Liability arises from direct causal action within material domain. Causation: Damage assessed through sequential manifestation (Anupūrvaśaḥ) of physical consequence. Capacity-based responsibility: Compensation calibrated to agent's operational capacity at time of act. Restoration logic: Financial restitution aligns victim's experiential integrity with pre-event state. Consciousness alignment: Realigning perpetrator’s awareness with dharmic causality of action.

title: yagnavalka 2.224
content:
दुःखोत्पादि गृहे द्रव्यं क्षिपन् प्राणहरं तथा ।
षोडशाद्यः पणान् दाप्यो द्वितीयो मध्यमं दमम् ॥२२४॥ duḥkhotpādi gṛhe dravyaṁ kṣipan prāṇaharaṁ tathā |
ṣoḍaśādyaḥ paṇān dāpyo dvitīyo madhyamaṁ damam ||224|| One who introduces objects causing suffering within another's dwelling, or casts items that threaten life, shall incur a fine beginning at sixteen units; a second offense incurs the middle level of penalty. Authority: The aggrieved party holds jurisdiction over their domain and its energetic integrity. Causation: Introducing suffering-inducing elements constitutes actionable harm regardless of intent.
