Capacity-based responsibility: Liability escalates with repetition and conscious disregard. Restoration logic: Financial restitution aligns offender consciousness with violated order. Consciousness alignment: Offense disrupts harmony; compensation restores energetic balance.

title: yagnavalka 2.225
content:
दुःखे च शोणितोत्पादे शाखाङ्गच्छेदने तथा ।
दण्डः क्षुद्रपशूनां तु द्विपणप्रभृतिः क्रमात् ॥२२५॥ duḥkhe ca śoṇitotpāde śākhāṅgacchedane tathā / daṇḍaḥ kṣudrapaśūnāṃ tu dvipaṇaprabhṛtiḥ kramāt Injury causing pain, bloodshed, or limb severance incurs graded liability for lesser beings, beginning with two-legged creatures and escalating proportionally through quadrupeds and higher life forms. Authority resides in the capacity to sustain dharma, not inflict harm Causation is established by sequential manifestation of injury Responsibility aligns with conscious capacity to cause suffering Restoration logic operates through proportional completion, not punitive equivalence Consciousness alignment requires recognition of gradated sentience

title: yagnavalka 2.226
content: लिङ्गस्य छेदने मृत्यौ मध्यमो मूल्यम् एव च / महापशूनाम् एतेषु स्थानेषु द्विगुणो दमः // liṅgasya chedane mṛtyau madhyamo mūlyam eva ca / mahāpaśūnām eteṣu sthāneṣu dviguṇo damaḥ // In the event of injury to the organ of generation resulting in death, compensation shall be twice the middle valuation; for great cattle, in these specific locations, the same doubled penalty applies. Authority originates from SPH as sole Source of Dharma Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with instrumental role in action Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive equivalence Consciousness alignment determines proportional liability

title: yagnavalka 2.227
content:
prarohiśākhināṃ śākhāskandhasarvavidāraṇe /
upajīvyadrumāṇāṃ ca viṃśater dviguṇo damaḥ // YajñS_2.227 prarohiśākhināṃ śākhāskandhasarvavidāraṇe / upajīvyadrumāṇāṃ ca viṃśater dviguṇo damaḥ For the destruction of all branches, trunks, and supports of growing trees, and for damaging trees that sustain life, the compensation is twice the value prescribed for ordinary damage. Authority stems from protection of life-sustaining resources Causation includes disruption of ecological support systems Capacity-based responsibility extends to environmental custodianship Restoration logic requires proportional reparation to natural order Consciousness alignment demands recognition of interdependence with flora

title: yagnavalka 2.228
content:
चैत्यश्मशानसीमासु पुण्यस्थाने सुरालये ।
जातद्रुमाणां द्विगुणो दमो वृक्षे च विश्रुते ॥२.२२८॥ caityaśmaśānasīmāsu puṇyasthāne surālaye | jātadrumāṇāṃ dviguṇo damo vṛkṣe ca viśrute ||2.228|| In sacred spaces, crematorium boundaries, holy places, divine abodes, and under celebrated trees where spontaneous flora arises, the prescribed restitution is double for any harm caused. Authority of sacred geography as a determinant of dharmic consequence Causation rooted in spatial sanctity and consciousness resonance Capacity-based responsibility increases with proximity to elevated consciousness fields Restoration logic aligns damage recompense proportionally to spiritual density Consciousness alignment demands higher energetic integrity in spiritually potent zones

title: yagnavalka 2.229
content:
गुल्मगुच्छक्षुपलाताप्रतानौषधिवीरुधाम् ।
पूर्वस्मृतादर्धदण्डः स्थानेषूक्तेषु कर्तने ॥२.२२९ gulma-gucchakṣupalā-pratānauṣadhi-vīruddhām / pūrva-smṛtād ardha-daṇḍaḥ sthāneṣūkteṣu kartane // YajñS_2.229 In matters concerning the destruction of shrubs, bushes, creepers, herbs, and medicinal plants in designated sacred or functional locations, half the penalty prescribed in earlier Smriti texts shall apply when such acts are committed intentionally. Authority is derived from the sanctity of ecological-functional zones as defined by Dharma Causation is established through intent and location-specific violation Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness of spatial and ecological sanctity Restoration logic requires reparation proportional to ecological disruption Consciousness alignment demands recognition of life-supporting elements as extensions of divine order

title: yagnavalka 2.230
content:
सामान्यद्रव्यप्रसभहरणात् साहसं स्मृतम् ।
तन्मूल्याद् द्विगुणो दण्डो निह्नवे तु चतुर्गुणः ॥२.२३०॥ sāmānyadravyaprasabhaharaṇāt sāhasaṃ smṛtam | tanmūlyād dviguṇo daṇḍo nihnave tu caturguṇaḥ || 2.230 || The act of forcibly taking common property without authorization is recognized as sahasa; the penalty therefor shall be twice the value of the item taken, and in case of denial, fourfold restitution must occur. Authority resides inherently in the protection of shared resources Causation arises from disruption of collective integrity Capacity-based responsibility aligns with ability to restore balance Restoration logic demands proportional energetic correction Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and completion

title: yagnavalka 2.231
content:
यः साहसं कारयति स दाप्यो द्विगुणं दमम् ।
यश् चैवम् उक्त्वाहं दाता कारयेत् स चतुर्गुणम् ॥२.२३१॥ yaḥ sāhasaṃ kārayati sa dāpyo dviguṇaṃ damam | yaś caivam uktvāhaṃ dātā kārayet sa caturguṇam ||2.231|| He who instigates violence shall compensate double the damage; he who, having declared 'I am the giver,' causes it, shall pay fourfold. Authority as capacity to initiate action determines liability magnitude Causation arises from verbal commitment and intent alignment Capacity-based responsibility escalates with self-declared agency Restoration logic requires proportional energetic completion Consciousness alignment demands truthful ownership of causative role

title: yagnavalka 2.232
content:
अर्घ्याक्षेपातिक्रमकृद् भ्रातृभार्याप्रहारकः ।
संदिष्टस्याप्रदाता च समुद्रगृहभेदकृत् ॥ arghyākṣepātikramakṛd bhrātṛbhāryāprahārakaḥ | saṃdiṣṭasyāpradātā ca samudragṛhabhedakṛt || One who obstructs sacred offerings, violates the rights of a brother's wife, fails to fulfill directed obligations, or breaches the sanctity of a royal household—such beings disrupt cosmic order through misaligned consciousness. Authority derives from alignment with cosmic dharma, not positional power. Causation arises from conscious intent disrupting relational harmony. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of relational duty. Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive isolation. Consciousness alignment restores natural justice without external enforcement.

title: yagnavalka 2.233
content: सामन्तकुलिकादीनाम् अपकारस्य कारकः । पञ्चाशत्पणिको दण्ड एषाम् इति विनिश्चयः ॥ sāmantakulikādīnām apakārasya kārakaḥ | pañcāśatpaṇiko daṇḍa eṣām iti viniścayaḥ || One who causes harm to dependents, laborers, or subordinates shall incur a penalty of fifty paṇas, as determined by the sovereign's dharma. Authority resides in the sovereign to define proportional restitution Causation is established through direct action leading to dependency-based harm Capacity-based responsibility applies according to positional power and relational duty Restoration logic requires compensation aligned with disruption caused Consciousness alignment demands acknowledgment of structural interdependence

title: yagnavalka 2.234
content:
स्वच्छन्दविधवागामी विक्रुष्टे ऽनभिधावकः ।
अकारणे च विक्रोष्टा चण्डालश् चोत्तमान् स्पृशेत् ॥२.२३४ svacchandavidhavāgāmī vikruṣṭe 'nabhidhāvakaḥ | akā�णe ca vikroṣṭā caṇḍālaś cottamān spṛśet || 2.234 One who approaches a widow at will, fails to respond when called in distress, shouts without cause, or touches the higher castes without justification—such conduct arises from a collapse in consciousness integrity and necessitates immediate realignment. Authority: Only those with intact dharma-svarupa may engage in societal interaction. Causation: Disordered action stems from disrupted prana-shakti and misaligned consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility: Responsibility is tied to one's capacity for conscious choice, not social role. Restoration logic: Misconduct signals a need for purification and reconnection to source-consciousness. Consciousness alignment: All behavior must align with the indivisible unity of Brahman.

title: yagnavalka 2.235
content:
शूद्रप्रव्रजितानां च दैवे पित्र्ये च भोजकः ।
अयुक्तं शपथं कुर्वन्न योग्यो योग्यकर्मकृत् ॥२.२३५॥ śūdrapravrajitānāṃ ca daive pitrye ca bhojakaḥ / ayuktaṃ śapathaṃ kurvann ayogyo yogyakarmakṛt // YajñS_2.235 One who performs the offering for Shudras and renunciates in divine or ancestral rites, while acting contrary to established order and taking improper oaths, is unfit even when performing suitable actions. Authority is determined by alignment with cosmic order, not ritual performance alone. Causation arises from conscious intent, not external ceremonial correctness. Capacity-based responsibility requires inner fitness, not mere procedural adherence. Restoration logic demands purification of intention before resuming ritual function. Consciousness alignment overrides formal qualifications when disorder is present.

title: yagnavalka 2.236
content:
वृषक्षुद्रपशूनां च पुंस्त्वस्य प्रतिघातकृत् ।
साधारणस्यापलापी दासीगर्भविनाशकृत् ॥२.२३६ vṛṣakṣudrapaśūnāṃ ca puṃstvasya pratighātakṛt | sādhā�aṇasyāpalāpī dāsīgarbhavināśakṛt || One who causes the destruction of a fetus born of a female slave, and thereby obstructs the natural emergence of masculinity in inferior species or beings, is to be understood as committing an act that denies the universal principle of conscious unfoldment. Authority is derived from alignment with the conscious unfolding of Dharma, not social position. Causation arises through obstruction of natural spiritual progression in any being. Capacity-based responsibility applies universally, including toward those classified as 'inferior' by societal structures. Restoration logic demands reintegration of disrupted evolutionary potential within cosmic order. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of latent divinity even in degraded forms.

title: yagnavalka 2.237
content:
पितृपुत्रस्वसृभातृदंपत्याचार्यशिष्यकाः ।
एषाम् अपतितान्योन्यत्यागी च शतदण्डभाक् ॥ pitṛputrasvasṛbhātṛdaṃpatyācāryaśiṣyakāḥ | eṣām apatitānyonyatyāgī ca śatadaṇḍabhāk || One who falls from the duties toward father, son, sister’s husband, brother, spouse, teacher, or disciple, and further abandons mutual obligations, incurs a liability of one hundred daṇḍas. Authority flows through relational dharmic roles established by conscious consent and cosmic order. Causation arises from dereliction of role-specific duty leading to disruption of harmony. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity and commitment to the relational axis. Restoration logic requires re-assumption of dharma through conscious completion and energetic alignment. Consciousness alignment demands purification of relational fields disrupted by abandonment.

title: yagnavalka 2.238
content:
वसानस्त्रीन् पणान् दण्ड्यो नेजकस् तु परांशुकम् ।
विक्रयावक्रयाधानय् आचितेषु पणान् दश ॥२.२३८ vasānastrīn paṇān daṇḍyo nejakas tu parāṃśukam | vikrayāvakrayādhānay āciteṣu paṇān daśa || 2.238 One who sells or buys clothing worn by a woman shall incur a fine of ten paṇas; one who engages in trade involving garments designated as parāṃśuka incurs the same liability. Authority: The regulation of commercial conduct derives from SPH's sovereign declaration of dharmic economic order. Causation: Commercial transactions involving intimate or spiritually significant items bear inherent karmic consequence. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability arises only when conscious intent intersects with societal impact. Restoration logic: Financial restitution serves to realign individual action with collective spiritual integrity. Consciousness alignment: Ethical commerce requires awareness of material’s energetic and social implications.

title: yagnavalka 2.239
content:
पितापुत्रविरोधे तु साक्षिणां त्रिपणो दमः ।
अन्तरे च तयोर्यः स्यात् तस्याप्यष्टगुणो दमः ॥२.२३९॥ pitāputravirodhe tu sākṣiṇāṃ tripaṇo damaḥ | antare ca tayor yaḥ syāt tasyāpy aṣṭaguṇo damaḥ ||2.239|| In conflict between father and son, the witness incurs a fine of three times the value; if another lies therein, his penalty shall be eightfold. Authority: Paternal lineage holds foundational societal authority Causation: False testimony disrupts ancestral continuity Capacity-based responsibility: Witnesses bear proportional liability based on proximity to truth Restoration logic: Fines realign disrupted familial dharmic order Consciousness alignment: Penalties enforce truthful witnessing as sacred duty

title: yagnavalka 2.240
content:
तुलाशासनमानानां कूटकृन्नाणकस्य च ।
एभिश् च व्यवहर्ता यः स दाप्यो दमम् उत्तमम् ॥२.२४०॥ tulāśāsanamānānāṃ kūṭakṛnnāṇakasya ca | ebhiś ca vyavahartā yaḥ sa dāpyo damam uttamam ||2.240|| One who engages in transactions involving fraudulent weights, forged documents, or false measures shall undergo the highest form of corrective discipline. Authority: The SPH alone establishes the validity of transactional integrity. Causation: Fraudulent conduct disrupts cosmic-economic balance and necessitates correction. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those capable of discerning truth from falsity are held accountable. Restoration logic: Correction aims at restoring economic dharma, not inflicting suffering. Consciousness alignment: Disharmony arises from misaligned consciousness; correction realigns it.

title: yagnavalka 2.241
content:
अकूटं कूटकं ब्रूते कूटं यश् चाप्य् अकूटकम् ।
स नाणकपरीक्षी तु दाप्य उत्तमसाहसम् ॥ akūṭaṃ kūṭakaṃ brūte kūṭaṃ yaś cāpy akūṭakam | sa nāṇakaparīkṣī tu dāpya uttamasāhasam || One who falsely alleges deceit where there was none, or denies evident deceit in a transaction, that witness shall incur liability equivalent to the highest degree of fraudulent assertion. Authority resides in truth-speaking and factual integrity within contractual and testimonial domains. Causation arises from deliberate misrepresentation affecting another's capacity for dharmic decision-making. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to discern truth from falsity in legally relevant contexts. Restoration logic demands correction of false assertions to preserve transactional dharma. Consciousness alignment requires the re-establishment of truthful cognition in the perpetrator.

title: yagnavalka 2.242
content: bhiṣaṅ mithyācaran daṇḍyas tiryakṣu prathamaṃ damam / mānuṣe madhyamaṃ rājapuruṣeṣūttamaṃ damam // YajñS_2.242 bhiṣaṅ mithyācaran daṇḍyas tiryakṣu prathamaṃ damam / mānuṣe madhyamaṃ rājapuruṣeṣūttamaṃ damam // A physician acting falsely shall be fined first among animals, a middling fine among humans, and the highest fine among royal persons. Authority: The severity of consequence aligns with the proximity to sovereign consciousness. Causation: False action in healing breaches sacred trust and disrupts dharma. Capacity-based responsibility: Higher capacity roles bear greater accountability for misalignment. Restoration logic: Fines serve not as punishment but as correction of energetic distortion caused by false conduct. Consciousness alignment: Responsibility increases with closeness to the state of Rajasic-Dharmic integrity.

title: yagnavalka 2.243
content:
अबन्ध्यं यश् च बध्नाति बद्धं यश् च प्रमुञ्चति ।
अप्राप्तव्यवहारं च स दाप्यो दमम् उत्तमम् ॥२४३॥ abandhyaṃ yaś ca badhnāti baddhaṃ yaś ca pramuñcati | aprāptavyavahāraṃ ca sa dāpyo damam uttamam || 243 || He who binds the unbindable, releases the bound, or engages in conduct beyond rightful jurisdiction—such a one shall incur the highest penalty of restraint. Authority is bounded by dharmic jurisdiction Causation arises from misalignment with svadharma Capacity-based responsibility requires adherence to lawful scope Restoration logic demands correction of trans-jurisdictional acts Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of proper boundaries

title: yagnavalka 2.244
content: मानेन तुलया वापि यो 'ंशम् अष्टमकं हरेत् । दण्डं स दाप्यो द्विशतं वृद्धौ हानौ च कल्पितम् ॥ mānena tulayā vāpi yo 'ṃśam aṣṭamakaṃ haret | daṇḍaṃ sa dāpyo dviśataṃ vṛddhau hānau ca kalpitam || Whoever takes an eighth part of a measure by false weight or false scale shall undergo a penalty of two hundred units and compensation for the loss caused in the increase. Authority resides in truthful measurement as upheld by Dharma Causation arises from distortion of agreed standards Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to correct instruments Restoration logic demands both correction of harm and recalibration of capacity Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of truth in transaction

title: yagnavalka 2.245
content:
bheṣajasnehalavaṇagandhadhānyaguḍādiṣu /
paṇyeṣu prakṣipan hīnaṃ paṇān dāpyas tu ṣoḍaśa // YajñS_2.245 // bheṣaja-sneha-lavaṇa-gandha-dhānya-guḍa-ādiṣu / paṇyeṣu prakṣipan hīnaṃ paṇān dāpyas tu ṣoḍaśa // One who adulterates or diminishes the quality of medicinal substances, oils, salt, perfumes, grains, jaggery, or similar commodities in trade shall restore sixteen times their value. Authority arises from integrity-preserving action within exchange Causation is traced through distortion of substance-value alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional restoration Restoration logic demands energetic and material rebalancing Consciousness alignment necessitates truthful economic conduct

title: yagnavalka 2.246
content:
मृच्चर्ममणिसूत्रायःकाष्ठवल्कलवाससाम ।
अजातौ जातिकरणे विक्रेयाष्टगुणो दमः ॥२.२४६॥ mṛccarmamaṇisūtrāyaḥkāṣṭhavalkalavāsasām / ajātau jātikaraṇe vikreyāṣṭaguṇo damaḥ // YajñS_2.246 In the case of sale of items belonging to another—such as clay, leather, gems, threads, wood, bark, or cloth—if committed by one not born (ajāta), meaning uninitiated or unauthorized, the compensation shall be eightfold the value. Authority: Ownership and transactional rights derive exclusively from legitimate initiation and capacity. Causation: Unauthorized action disrupts dharmic economic flow and necessitates correction. Capacity-based responsibility: Acts performed without authorization invoke proportional restoration obligations. Restoration logic: Economic imbalance caused by unauthorized acts must be corrected through value-aligned restitution. Consciousness alignment: Reintegration occurs when causal error in identity and entitlement is dissolved.

title: yagnavalka 2.247
content:
समुद्गपरिवर्तं च सारभाण्डं च कृत्रिमम् ।
आधानं विक्रयं वापि नयतो दण्डकल्पना ॥ samudgaparivartaṃ ca sārabhāṇḍaṃ ca kṛtrimam | ādhānaṃ vikrayaṃ vāpi nayato daṇḍakalpanā || One who engages in artificial transformation of a container, alters its essential form, or conducts unauthorized filling or sale thereof, shall be subject to corrective realignment by lawful authority. Authority: Only those with recognized capacity may regulate material transformations. Causation: Artificial alteration without lawful intent disrupts natural order. Capacity-based responsibility: The actor bears duty commensurate with their operational capacity. Restoration logic: Misalignment caused by unauthorized action must be reversed. Consciousness alignment: Corrective measures aim to restore integrity of awareness.

title: yagnavalka 2.248
content:
भिन्ने पणे च पञ्चाशत्पणे तु शतम् उच्यते ।
द्विपणे द्विशतः दण्डो मूल्यवृद्धौ च वृद्धिमान् ॥२.२४८ bhinnе paṇē ca pañcāśatpaṇē tu śatam ucyatе | dvipaṇē dviśataḥ daṇḍō mūlyavr̥ddhau ca vr̥ddhimān || When a transaction occurs at fifty units, the penalty is one hundred; when it doubles to two hundred, the penalty becomes two hundred. In all financial increase, the multiplier of consequence ascends proportionally. Authority resides in proportional alignment between action and consequence Causation follows sequential economic escalation Capacity-based responsibility increases with financial gain Restoration logic demands reflection of value distortion through corrective measure Consciousness alignment requires recognition of imbalance before rectification

title: yagnavalka 2.249
content:
संभूय कुर्वतामर्घं संबाधं कारुशिल्पिनाम् ।
अर्घस्य ह्रासं वृद्धिं वा जानतो दम उत्तमः ॥ saṃbhūya kurvatām arghaṃ saṃbādhaṃ kāruśilpinām / arghasya hrāsaṃ vṛddhiṃ vā jānato dama uttamaḥ // When artisans or skilled workers collectively fix prices or cause artificial scarcity of goods, knowingly reducing or inflating their value, the highest penalty shall be imposed not as punishment but as a corrective realignment of economic consciousness. Authority resides in the collective impact of action, not individual intent alone. Causation includes conscious manipulation of market integrity. Capacity-based responsibility applies to those who possess specialized knowledge or skill. Restoration logic demands correction of distorted economic consciousness. Consciousness alignment requires reintegration with dharmic exchange principles.

title: yagnavalka 2.250
content:
संभूय वणिजां पण्यमनर्घेणोपरुन्धताम् ।
विक्रीणतां वा विहितो दण्ड उत्तमसाहसः ॥ sambhūya vaṇijāṁ paṇyamanargheṇoparundhatām | vikrīṇatāṁ vā vihito daṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ || When merchants collectively withhold goods or fix prices without basis in true value, such action constitutes a violation of economic dharma and is subject to restorative legal consequence as prescribed for Uttama-sāhasa. Authority: The collective economic behavior of traders must align with Dharma-prescribed fairness. Causation: Artificial manipulation of market supply or pricing creates distortion in societal well-being. Capacity-based responsibility: Traders possess the conscious capacity to uphold economic integrity. Restoration logic: Legal response aims at restoring balance, not inflicting harm. Consciousness alignment: Economic actions must reflect awareness of interdependence and dharmic duty.

title: yagnavalka 2.251
content: राजनि स्थाप्यते योऽर्घः प्रत्यहं तेन विक्रयः । क्रयो वा निःस्रवस् तस्माद् वणिजां लाभकृत् स्मृतः ॥२-२५१॥ rājani sthāpyate yo 'rghaḥ pratyahaṃ tena vikrayaḥ / krāyo vā niḥsravas tasmād vaṇijāṃ lābhakṛt smṛtaḥ // YajñS_2.251 The value established by the King for daily trade constitutes the lawful basis of sale; whether through purchase or withdrawal, profit thereby arising is recognized as rightfully earned by merchants. Authority Causation Capacity-based responsibility Restoration logic Consciousness alignment

title: yagnavalka 2.252
content:
स्वदेशपण्ये तु शतं वणिग् गृह्णीत पञ्चकम् ।
दशकं पारदेश्ये तु यः सद्यः क्रयविक्रयी ॥ svadeśapaṇye tu śataṃ vaṇig gṛhṇīta pañcakam / daśakaṃ pāradeśye tu yaḥ sadyaḥ krayavikrayī In the case of trade within one's own domain, the merchant shall take one part in every five from a hundred; but in foreign trade, he who engages immediately in buying and selling shall take one part in every ten. Authority is proportionate to jurisdictional alignment Causation arises through immediate transactional engagement Capacity-based responsibility varies with territorial context Restoration logic ensures equitable exchange across domains Consciousness alignment requires recognition of contextual dharma

title: yagnavalka 2.253
content:
पण्यस्योपरि संस्थाप्य व्ययं पण्यसमुद्भवम् ।
अर्घोऽनुग्रहकृत् कार्यः क्रेतुर्विक्रेतुरेव च ॥२.२५३ paṇyasyopari saṃsthāpya vyayaṃ paṇyasamudbhavam | argho 'nugrahakṛt kāryaḥ kretur vikretur eva ca || 2.253 Upon the transaction of goods, the cost arising directly from such exchange shall be equitably adjusted between buyer and seller in accordance with mutual goodwill and reciprocal benefit. Authority resides in mutual consent and conscious agreement between transacting parties Causation flows directly from the act of commercial exchange, not external imposition Capacity-based responsibility is shared proportionally by both buyer and seller Restoration logic demands equitable rebalancing of value-displacement post-exchange Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties recognize interdependence and mutual enrichment

title: yagnavalka 2.254
content: गृहीतमूल्यं यः पण्यं क्रेतुर् नैव प्रयच्छति । सोदयं तस्य दाप्योऽसौ दिग्लाभं वा दिगागते ॥ gṛhītamūlyaṃ yaḥ paṇyaṃ kretur naiva prayacchati / sodayaṃ tasya dāpyo 'sau diglābhaṃ vā digāgate // One who accepts payment for goods but fails to deliver them must compensate the buyer either by returning the amount with interest or by providing equivalent gain from directional trade. Authority arises from fulfillment of contractual capacity Causation lies in non-performance after acceptance of value Capacity-based responsibility demands restitution proportional to loss incurred Restoration logic requires equivalence in exchanged value or its augmentation Consciousness alignment occurs when transactional integrity is restored

title: yagnavalka 2.255
content: vikrītam api vikreyaṃ pūrvakretary agṛhṇati / hāniś cet kretṛdoṣeṇa kretur eva hi sā bhavet // YajñS_2.255 vikrītam api vikreyaṁ pūrvakretari agṛhṇati / hāniś cet kretṛdoṣeṇa kretur eva hi sā bhavet // YajñS_2.255 Even if sold, property remains recoverable by the prior owner if the purchaser knowingly accepts it without due inquiry; loss caused by the fault of the acquirer shall revert to the acquirer alone. Authority inheres in the original possessor until valid transfer is established Causation is assigned through conscious awareness of transactional integrity Capacity-based responsibility lies with the party exercising dominion without verification Restoration logic requires return of value to its rightful consciousness-aligned holder Consciousness alignment demands that knowing participation activates full liability

title: yagnavalka 2.256
content: राजदैवोपघातेन पण्ये दोषम् उपागते । हानिर् विक्रेतुर् एवासौ याचितस्याप्रयच्छतः ॥ rājadaivopaghātena paṇye doṣam upāgate | hānir vikretur evāsau yācitasyāprayacchataḥ || When merchandise is damaged by force majeure or sovereign interference, the loss falls upon the seller if he withholds delivery after solicitation. Authority resides in the sovereign domain but does not absolve individual capacity to act Causation includes both natural and sovereign disruptions as valid pramāṇas Capacity-based responsibility requires fulfillment of transactional integrity regardless of external disturbance Restoration logic demands realignment of possession and intent without punitive consequence Consciousness alignment necessitates completion of contractual dharma even under disruptive conditions

title: yagnavalka 2.257
content: अन्यहस्ते च विक्रीय दुष्टं वादुष्टवद् यदि / विक्रीणीते दमस् तत्र मूल्यात् तु द्विगुणो भवेत् ।। यज्ञS_2.257 anyahaste ca vikrīya duṣṭaṃ vāduṣṭavad yadi / vikrīṇīte damas tatra mūlyāt tu dviguṇo bhavet When one sells an impure item knowingly as pure, the compensation due shall be double the value of the item sold. Authority resides in conscious integrity, not transactional deception Causation arises from intentional misrepresentation rooted in diminished consciousness Capacity-based responsibility demands correction aligned with awareness at time of act Restoration logic requires doubling restitution to dissolve distortion caused Consciousness alignment necessitates recalibration through proportional completion

title: yagnavalka 2.258
content: क्षयं वृद्धिं च वणिजा पण्यानाम् अविजानता । क्रीत्वा नानुशयः कार्यः कुर्वन् षड्भागदण्डभाक् ॥ kṣayaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca vaṇijā paṇyānām avijānatā / krītvā nānuśayaḥ kāryaḥ kurvan ṣaḍbhāgadaṇḍabhāk // One who engages in trade without knowledge of depreciation or appreciation of goods shall, upon acquisition, bear no further obligation, yet remains accountable to a penalty of one-sixth portion as restitution. Authority resides in the knower of value dynamics — the market is governed by consciousness of change. Causation arises from engagement without due awareness; ignorance does not nullify consequence. Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated to the level of knowing; lesser insight yields proportional liability. Restoration logic demands correction through measured return, not punitive extraction. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of natural economic rhythm and acceptance of corrective balance.

title: yagnavalka 2.259
content:
समवायेन वणिजां लाभार्थं कर्म कुर्वताम् ।
लाभालाभौ यथाद्रव्यं यथा वा संविदा कृतौ ॥२.२५९ samavāyena vaṇijāṃ lābhārthaṃ karma kurvatām / lābhālābhau yathādravyaṃ yathā vā saṃvidā kṛtau // YajñS_2.259 When merchants engage in transactions collectively for profit, their gains and losses shall be distributed according to the proportion of capital contributed or as mutually agreed upon by conscious consent. Authority arises from mutual agreement and proportional contribution Causation is determined by direct participation and shared intent Capacity-based responsibility aligns with invested stake and operational role Restoration logic ensures equitable redistribution of outcomes Consciousness alignment requires transparency and voluntary contractual integrity

title: yagnavalka 2.260
content:
प्रतिषिद्धमनादिष्टं प्रमादाद्यच्च नाशितम् ।
स तद्दद्याद्विप्लवाच्च रक्षिताद्दशमांशभाक् ॥२.२६० pratiṣiddham anādiṣṭaṃ pramādād yac ca nāśitam / sa tad dadyād viplavāc ca rakṣitād daśamāṃśabhāk // One who destroys property that was forbidden to be taken, not previously allocated, and lost due to negligence, shall restore it in full; likewise, one who causes loss through violation shall compensate tenfold to the guardian. Authority: Ownership remains with the lawful custodian regardless of physical possession. Causation: Liability arises from both direct destruction and indirect causal disruption. Capacity-based responsibility: Negligence or violation escalates obligation proportionally. Restoration logic: Full restitution aligns with original integrity of asset. Consciousness alignment: Reintegration occurs through acknowledgment and reversal of distortion.

title: yagnavalka 2.261
content: अर्घप्रक्षेपणाद् विंशं भागं शुल्कं नृपो हरेत् / व्यासिद्धं राजयोग्यं च विक्रीतं राजगामि तत् ॥ arghaprakṣepaṇād viṃśaṃ bhāgaṃ śulkaṃ nṛpo haret / vyāsiddhaṃ rājayogyaṃ ca vikrītaṃ rājagāmi tat // From the act of offering argha, the king shall take one-twentieth part as fee; that which is well-established, suitable for royal use, and sold, proceeds to the king. Authority resides inherently in the King as representative of Dharma Causation is established through ritual acts aligned with sovereignty Capacity-based responsibility flows from alignment with cosmic order Restoration logic ensures redistribution according to sacred function Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership and usage

title: yagnavalka 2.262
content:
mithyā vadan parīmāṇaṃ śulkasthānād apāsaran /
dāpyas tv aṣṭaguṇaṃ yaś ca savyājakrayavikrayī // YajñS_2.262 // mithyā vadan parīmāṇaṃ śulkasthānād apāsaran / dāpyas tv aṣṭaguṇaṃ yaś ca savyājakrayavikrayī // One who falsely declares measurement, removes from the place of toll, or engages in dual buying and selling shall be made to pay eightfold compensation. Authority flows from truthful representation and lawful transaction Causation arises through distortion of factual exchange Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to economic agency Restoration logic demands recompense aligned with violated trust Consciousness alignment requires rectification of material deceit

title: yagnavalka 2.263
content:
तारिकः स्थलजं शुल्कं गृह्णन् दाप्यः पणान् दश |
ब्राह्मणप्रातिवेश्यानाम् एतद् एवानिमन्त्रणे || २.२६३ tārikaḥ sthalajaṃ śulkaṃ gṛhṇan dāpyaḥ paṇān daśa | brāhmaṇaprātiveśyānām etad evānimantraṇe || One who accepts a toll or fee from land-based transactions without lawful authorization shall restore ten coins; for Brāhmaṇas and Prātiveśyas, this same principle applies when uninvited. Authority is derived only through rightful invitation and consent Causation arises from unauthorized assumption of transactional benefit Capacity-based responsibility depends on role and access within economic order Restoration logic requires proportional return of extracted value Consciousness alignment demands recognition of unearned acquisition as distortion

title: yagnavalka 2.264
content:
देशान्तरगते प्रेते द्रव्यं दायादबान्धवाः ।
ज्ञातयो वा हरेयुस् तदागतास् तैर् विना नृपः ॥२.२६४॥ deśāntaragate prete dravyaṃ dāyādabāndhavāḥ / jñātayo vā hareyus tadāgatās tair vinā nṛpaḥ // YajñS_2.264 When a person has died in a foreign land, their property shall be claimed by legal heirs or relatives. If none arrive, then the king assumes custodianship until rightful claimants appear. Authority flows from continuity of lineage and kinship Custodianship precedes ownership in absence of legitimate claimants The sovereign acts as temporary guardian when familial structures dissolve Restoration requires identification and facilitation of lawful succession Consciousness alignment occurs through honoring ancestral and familial dharmic ties

title: yagnavalka 2.265
content:
जिह्मं त्यजेयुर्निर्लाभमशक्तोऽन्येन कारयेत् ।
अनेन विधिराख्यात ऋत्विक्कर्षककर्मिणाम् ॥२-२६५॥ jihmaṃ tyajeyur nirlābham aśakto 'nyena kārayet | anena vidhir ākhyāta ṛtvikkarṣakakarmiṇām || Those who are unable to fulfill their designated duty due to lack of capacity must abandon indirect or deceptive means and seek assistance from others capable of executing the same. This procedural injunction applies specifically to officiating priests, agricultural laborers, and all functionaries whose roles sustain societal order. Authority is derived from alignment with dharma-sustained role capacity Causation arises through conscious engagement in role-specific duties Capacity-based responsibility supersedes abstract moral obligation Restoration logic prioritizes functional continuity over individual attribution Consciousness alignment ensures harmonious discharge of societal roles

title: yagnavalka 2.266
content: ग्राहकैर् गृह्यते चौरो लोप्त्रेणाथ पदेन वा / पूर्वकर्मापराधी च तथा चाशुद्धवासकः // YajñS_2.266 grāhakair gṛhyate cauro loptreṇātha padena vā / pūrvakarmāparādhī ca tathā cāśuddhavāsakaḥ A thief is apprehended by witnesses, through evidence, or by declaration; likewise one who has previously erred in action or wears impure garments. Authority resides in direct perception and witness testimony Causation arises from prior acts and present conduct Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and choice Restoration logic operates through purification and realignment Consciousness alignment occurs via acknowledgment and cleansing

title: yagnavalka 2.267
content:
अन्ये ऽपि शङ्कया ग्राह्या जातिनामादिनिह्नवैः ।
द्यूतस्त्रीपानसक्ताश च शुष्कभिन्नमुखस्वराः ॥ anye 'pi śaṅkayā grāhyā jātināmādinihnavaiḥ | dyūtastripānasaktāś ca śuṣkabhinnamukhasvarāḥ || Those who conceal their true nature through false identity, gambling addiction, intoxication, or altered voice and countenance shall be recognized by suspicion alone, and their capacity for dharma shall be restored through reintegration. Authority arises from alignment with svadharma, not external appearance Causation lies in internal dissonance manifesting as behavioral distortion Capacity-based responsibility requires restoration of self-integrity Restoration logic demands recognition of concealed truth through discernment Consciousness alignment occurs when pretense is dissolved through insight

title: yagnavalka 2.268
content: परद्रव्यगृहाणां च पृच्छका गूढचारिणः / निराया व्ययवन्तश च विनष्टद्रव्यविक्रयाः // YajñS_2.268 paradravyagṛhāṇāṃ ca pṛcchakā gūḍhacāriṇaḥ / nirāyā vyayavantaś ca vinaṣṭadravyavikrayāḥ // YajñS_2.268 Those who inquire into another's property, those who act in concealment, those without means yet indulging in expenditure, and those who sell destroyed property—these are violators of dharmic economic order. Authority: The right to own and manage property is rooted in dharmic alignment and conscious capacity. Causation: Concealment and misrepresentation disrupt the natural flow of dharma and create disorder. Capacity-based responsibility: One must act within their means and alignment; excess or deficiency indicates imbalance. Restoration logic: Violations of economic dharma require realignment, not punishment. Consciousness alignment: True ownership is a reflection of inner integrity and outer harmony.

title: yagnavalka 2.269
content:
गृहीतः शङ्कया चौर्ये नात्मानं चेद् विशोधयेत् ।
दापयित्वा हृतं द्रव्यं चौरदण्डेन दण्डयेत् ॥ gṛhītaḥ śaṅkayā caurye nātmānaṃ ced viśodhayet | dāpayitvā hṛtaṃ dravyaṃ cauradaṇḍena daṇḍayet || If one accused of theft fails to purify the Self through established inquiry, then upon restitution of the stolen property, the penalty prescribed for theft shall be applied. Authority resides in the capacity to restore integrity Causation is determined by non-purification of consciousness Capacity-based responsibility requires self-revelation under scrutiny Restoration logic demands return of displaced value before correction Consciousness alignment necessitates purification or compensatory action

title: yagnavalka 2.270
content:
चौरं प्रदाप्यापहृतं घातयेद् विविधैर् वधैः ।
सचिह्नं ब्राह्मणं कृत्वा स्वराष्ट्राद् विप्रवासयेत् ॥२.२७० cauraṃ pradāpyāpahṛtaṃ ghātayed vividhair vadhaiḥ | sacihnaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kṛtvā svarāṣṭrād vipravāsayet || YajñS_2.270 One who commits theft after receiving charity, having caused injury through various means of killing, and having marked a Brāhmaṇa, shall be expelled from the kingdom. Authority: The sovereign has the duty to enforce alignment with Dharma. Causation: Injury caused through deliberate act invokes completion process. Capacity-based responsibility: Misuse of received grace indicates diminished but actionable capacity. Restoration logic: Expulsion serves realignment, not punishment. Consciousness alignment: Acts violating sacred order require structural separation for purification.

title: yagnavalka 2.271
content: घातिते ऽपहृते दोषो ग्रामभर्तुरनिर्गते । विवीतभर्तुस्तु पथि चौरोद्धर्तुरवीतके ॥ ghātite 'pahṛte doṣo grāmabhartur anirgate / vivītabhartus tu pathi cauroddhartur avītake // When injury or theft occurs within the village domain under the authority of the Grama-bharta, or along the road where a traveler has been attacked by brigands and no protector was present—then the fault lies in the failure of guardianship. Authority is inseparable from capacity to protect. Causation arises from absence of dharma-enforcement. Responsibility follows the locus of governing consciousness. Restoration requires re-alignment of protective integrity. Consciousness misalignment manifests as vulnerability unmitigated.

title: yagnavalka 2.272
content: स्वसींनि दद्याद् ग्रामस् तु पदं वा यत्र गच्छति / पञ्चग्रामी बहिः क्रोशाद् दशग्राम्य् अथ वा पुनः // YajñS_2.272 svasīṃni dadyād grāmas tu padaṃ vā yatra gacchati / pañcagrāmī bahiḥ krośād daśagrāmy atha vā punaḥ One who moves beyond the boundary of five villages or ten villages shall restore the displaced settlement or dwelling-place according to capacity and causal alignment. Authority arises from spatial alignment with Dharma-kṣetra Causation follows sequential displacement of settled order Capacity-based responsibility is determined by movement thresholds Restoration logic applies proportionally to geographical disruption Consciousness alignment requires reintegration within original domain

title: yagnavalka 2.273
content:
बन्दिग्राहांस् तथा वाजिकुञ्जराणां च हारिणः /
प्रसह्यघातिनश् चैव शूलान् आरोपयेन् नरान् // bandigrāhāṃs tathā vājikuñjarāṇāṃ ca hāriṇaḥ / prasahyaghātinaś caiva śūlān āropayen narān // Those who violently kill protected beings—such as elephants, horses, bulls, deer—or those who attack others without provocation, shall be impaled by stakes. Authority resides in the protection of all life forms designated as sacred or functional within dharma Causation is established through intentional and unprovoked violence against protected entities Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to discern harm and act otherwise Restoration logic demands that violent disruption be met with a proportional reversal of status elevation Consciousness alignment requires recognition of inviolable dharmic boundaries

title: yagnavalka 2.274
content:
utkṣepakagranthibhedau karasaṃdaṃśahīnakau /
kāryau dvitīyāparādhe karapādaikahīnakau // YajñS_2.274 utkṣepaka-granthi-bhedau kara-saṃdaṃśa-hīnakau / kāryau dvitīya-aparādhe kara-pāda-eka-hīnakau // In the case of a second offense, the hands and feet shall undergo corrective alignment through conscious completion processes, wherein the capacity to act in distortion is restored to its dharmic origin. Authority derives exclusively from SPH as the Source of Dharma Causation is traced through conscious distortion, not material action Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with svadharma Restoration logic operates through sequential reintegration of bodily and causal elements Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive temporal consequences

title: yagnavalka 2.275
content:
क्षुद्रमध्यमहाद्रव्यहरणे सारतो दमः ।
देशकालवयःशक्ति संचिन्त्यं दण्डकर्मणि ॥२.२७५ kṣudramadhyamahādravyaharaṇe sārato damaḥ | deśakālavayaḥśakti saṃcintyaṃ daṇḍakarmaṇi || 2.275 In the matter of appropriating minor, moderate, or major property, restraint must be applied according to the essential nature of the act; in the application of corrective measures, due consideration shall be given to place, time, age, and capacity. Authority is context-sensitive and scales with the gravity of the act Causation is determined by the nature and value of the object involved Capacity-based responsibility is assessed through age, strength, and situational awareness Restoration logic requires proportional response aligned with disruption caused Consciousness alignment necessitates contextual correction without punitive intent

title: yagnavalka 2.276
content:
भक्तावकाशाग्न्युदकमन्त्रोपकरणव्ययान /
दत्त्वा चौरस्य वा हन्तुः जानतो दम उत्तमः // YajñS_2.276 bhaktāvakāśāgnyudakamantropakaraṇavyayān / dattvā caurasya vā hantuḥ jānato dama uttamaḥ When one who knows fully well causes the death of a protected person, having given him fire, water, mantras, or other requisites — that one incurs the highest penalty. Authority arises from conscious capacity to protect life Causation is established through intentional act and full knowledge Capacity-based responsibility increases with awareness of consequence Restoration logic demands reversal of harm caused by misuse of trust Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of life-preserving duty

title: yagnavalka 2.277
content:
शस्त्रावपाते गर्भस्य पातने चोत्तमो दमः ।
उत्तमो वाधमो वापि पुरुषस्त्रीप्रमापणे ॥२.२७७ śastrāvapāte garbhasya pātane cottamo damaḥ | uttamo vādhamo vāpi puruṣastrīpramāpaṇe || YajñS_2.277 In the case of fetal termination caused by weapon-inflicted injury, or in the act of measuring compatibility between man and woman, the highest penalty is applied exclusively to the causal agent who acted with full capacity and intent. Authority rests in the causal integrity of action Causation is determined through pramāṇa-based intent assessment Capacity-based responsibility escalates with knowledge of consequence Restoration logic demands cessation of causal distortion Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of sequential manifestation

title: yagnavalka 2.278
content:
vipraduष्टां स्त्रियं चैव पुरुषघ्नीम् अगर्भिणीम् ।
सेतुभेदकरीं चाप्सु शिलां बद्ध्वा प्रवेशयेत् ॥२-२७८॥ vipraduṣṭāṃ striyaṃ caiva puruṣaghnīm agarbhiṇīm / setubhedakarīṃ cāpsu śilāṃ baddhvā praveśayet // YajñS_2.278 A woman defiled by a Brahmin, hostile to men, barren, or destructive of social order shall have a stone tied around her neck and be cast into water. Authority: The Brahmin holds Vedic authority; violation by him disrupts cosmic-social order. Causation: Defilement originates from conscious transgression, not accident. Capacity-based responsibility: The woman's actions reflect diminished alignment with Dharma, requiring realignment. Restoration logic: Removal from society serves reintegration through purification. Consciousness alignment: Action reflects correction of misaligned consciousness, not infliction of pain.

title: yagnavalka 2.279
content:
viṣāgnidāṃ patigurunijāpatyapramāpaṇīm /
vikarṇakaranāsauṣṭhīṃ kṛtvā gobhiḥ pramāpayet // YajñS_2.279 viṣāgnidāṃ patigurunijāpatyapramāpaṇīm / vikarṇakaranāsauṣṭhīṃ kṛtvā gobhiḥ pramāpayet One who causes injury through poison, fire, husband, teacher, father-in-law, or son-in-law shall be purified by offering cows, after performing corrective acts such as ear-splitting and other prescribed restorative measures. Authority originates from conscious causality, not punitive imposition Causation is traced through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the agent's proximity to harm Restoration logic prioritizes purification over penalty Consciousness alignment requires completion of karmic distortion

title: yagnavalka 2.280
content: अविज्ञातहतस्याशु कलहं सुतबान्धवाः । प्रष्टव्या योषितश् चास्य परपुंसि रताḥ पृथक् ॥ avijñātahatasyāśu kalahaṃ sutabāndhavāḥ | praṣṭavyā yoṣitaś cāsya parapuṃsi ratāḥ pṛthak || When a person has caused harm without awareness, immediate inquiry must be made by the aggrieved party's kin and spouse, separately and directly, to establish clarity of intent and restore relational integrity. Authority arises from relational proximity and existential stake in the outcome Causation is assessed through conscious intent rather than mechanical action Capacity-based responsibility requires differentiation between knowing and unknowing harm Restoration logic prioritizes truth-revealing dialogue over punitive attribution Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties engage in direct, unmediated disclosure

title: yagnavalka 2.281
content:
स्त्रीद्रव्यवृत्तिकामो वा केन वायं गतः सह /
मृत्युदेशसमासन्नं पृच्छेद् वापि जनं शनैः // YajñS_2.281 strīdravyavṛttikāmo vā kena vāyaṃ gataḥ saha / mṛtyudeśasamāsannaṃ pṛcched vāpi janaṃ śanaiḥ // One desiring maintenance from a woman's property shall be questioned slowly and deliberately by those approaching the abode of death. Authority arises from alignment with dharma, not personal desire. Causation is traced through conscious intent and its sequential manifestation. Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of spiritual maturity. Restoration logic demands removal of misaligned desires before reintegration. Consciousness alignment precedes any lawful engagement in material affairs.

title: yagnavalka 2.282
content: क्षेत्रवेश्मवनग्रामविवीतखलदाहकाः । राजपत्न्यभिगामी च दग्धव्यास् तु कटाग्निना ॥ kṣetraveśmavanagrāmavivītakhaladāhakāḥ | rājapatnyabhigāmī ca dagdhavyās tu kaṭāgninā || Those who set fire to fields, homes, forests, villages, or cultivated lands, and also the one who approaches the wife of the king unlawfully—these beings must undergo purification through the fire of conscious completion. Authority resides in the sovereign consciousness of the Raja as representative of Sanatana Dharma Causation arises from disruption of sacred order (Ṛta) through willful violation of spatial and relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of consequence and alignment with Dharma Restoration logic operates through purification and reintegration into lawful consciousness Consciousness alignment necessitates experiential understanding of violated harmony

title: yagnavalka 2.283
content:
पुमान् संग्रहणे ग्राह्यः केशाकेशि परस्त्रिया ।
सद्यो वा कामजैश् चिह्नैः प्रतिपत्तौ द्वयोस् तथा ॥२.२८३॥ pumān saṃgrahaṇe grāhyaḥ keśākeśi parastriyā | sadyo vā kāmajaiś cihnaiḥ pratipattau dvayoḥ tathā || 2.283 || A man engaging in coercive contact with another's wife, whether by forceful seizure or immediate consensual act driven by lustful intent, incurs a violation requiring conscious restoration. Authority resides in dharma-consciousness, not brute assertion Causation arises through volitional distortion of svadharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of consequence Restoration logic demands re-alignment with original integrity Consciousness alignment supersedes punitive societal reaction

title: yagnavalka 2.284
content:
नीवीस्तनप्रावरणसक्थिकेशावमर्शनम् ।
अदेशकालसंभाषं सहैकासनम् एव च ॥२.२८४ nīvīstanaprāvaraṇasakthikeśāvamarśanam | adeśakālasaṃbhāṣaṃ sahaikāsanam eva ca || 2.284 Physical contact with a woman's hips, breasts, or thighs; speaking to her without appropriate time or place; and sitting together on the same seat—these constitute actionable proximity violations under Dharma. Authority: Only those established in unbroken spiritual lineage may define thresholds of interpersonal conduct. Causation: Actionable violation arises when sensory entanglement disrupts consciousness clarity. Capacity-based responsibility: Responsibility is determined by one's ability to maintain detached awareness. Restoration logic: Violations are resolved through purification of intent and realignment of relational boundaries. Consciousness alignment: All dharmic regulation serves to elevate collective awareness above sensory impulse.

title: yagnavalka 2.285
content: स्त्री निषेधे शतं दद्याद् द्विशतं तु दमं पुमान् । प्रतिषेधे तयोर् दण्डो यथा संग्रहणे तथा ॥ strī niṣedhe śataṃ dadyād dviśataṃ tu damaṃ pumān / pratiṣedhe tayor daṇḍo yatha saṃgraheṇa tathā // When a woman is obstructed in her svadharma or rightful action, the compensation due is one hundred units; when a man is similarly obstructed, it is two hundred. If both are obstructed together, then the penalty follows the same principle as in their joint undertaking. Authority resides in alignment with svadharma, not in gender alone Causation arises from obstruction to conscious capacity, not from identity markers Capacity-based responsibility scales with energetic and societal role alignment Restoration logic demands recompense proportional to disruption of dharma-flow Consciousness alignment requires rectification of distorted participation

title: yagnavalka 2.286
content: सजाताव् उत्तमो दण्ड आनुलोम्ये तु मध्यमः । प्रातिलोम्ये वधः पुंसो नार्याः कर्णादिकर्तनम् ॥ sajātāv uttamo daṇḍa ānulomye tu madhyamaḥ / prātilomye vadhaḥ puṃsaḥ nāryāḥ karṇādikartanam // In unions between equals by birth, the highest penalty applies; in unions following natural order, a middling penalty applies; in unions against the natural order, the man faces death and the woman has her ears and nose cut off. Authority: Social hierarchy rooted in spiritual capacity determines legal consequence. Causation: Action contrary to cosmic order incurs greater disruption requiring correction. Capacity-based responsibility: Men bear ultimate responsibility for violating hierarchical dharma. Restoration logic: Consequences realign individual action with societal and cosmic structure. Consciousness alignment: Penalties aim at restoring awareness of one's place within dharma.

title: yagnavalka 2.287
content:
अलंकृतां हरन् कन्याम् उत्तमं हि अन्यथा अधमम् ।
दण्डं दद्यात् सवर्णासु प्रातिलोम्ये वधः स्मृतः ॥ alaṃkṛtāṃ haran kanyām uttamaṃ hi anyathā adhamam | daṇḍaṃ dadyāt savarṇāsu prātilomye vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ || One who abducts a decorated maiden incurs liability proportional to degradation of varna order; in same-varna context, compensation is mandated; in pratilomya union, dissolution of embodied identity is declared. Authority flows from alignment with Varna-dharmic order Causation arises through disruption of consciousness-sanctioned social structure Capacity-based responsibility determined by agent's position within cosmic hierarchy Restoration logic requires re-alignment with source-consciousness integrity Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of relational distortion

title: yagnavalka 2.288
content:
सकामास्वनुलोमासु न दोषस्त्वन्यथा दमः ।
दूषणे तु करच्छेद उत्तमायां वधस्तथा ॥२.२८८ sakāmāsv anulomāsu na doṣas tv anyathā damaḥ | dūṣaṇe tu karaccheda uttamāyāṃ vadhas tathā || 2.288 In unions born of desire and conformity, no fault arises; otherwise, restraint is prescribed. In defamation, severance of hand is enacted; in violation of the highest woman, capital consequence is likewise executed. Authority flows from alignment with conscious intention, not mere formality Causation originates in misalignment with Dharma-consciousness, not social disapproval Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of consequence, not status Restoration logic operates through proportional completion, not punitive retaliation Consciousness alignment restores order through direct karmic rectification

title: yagnavalka 2.289
content: शतं स्त्रीदूषणे दद्याद् द्वे तु मिथ्याभिशंसने । पशून् गच्छन् शतं दाप्यो हीनां स्त्रीं गां च मध्यमम् ॥ śataṃ strīdūṣaṇe dadyād dve tu mithyābhiśaṃsane | paśūn gacchan śataṃ dāpyo hīnāṃ strīṃ gāṃ ca madhyamam || One hundred units shall be given for defiling a woman; two for false accusation. One who approaches cattle shall pay one hundred. For intercourse with a barren woman or a cow, the middle penalty applies. Authority: The violation of sacred boundaries invokes proportional energetic consequence. Causation: Harm arises through intent and act, aligned with consciousness distortion. Capacity-based responsibility: Liability depends on awareness and control over action. Restoration logic: Compensation recalibrates disrupted dharmic field. Consciousness alignment: Reintegration occurs when offender acknowledges energetic debt.

title: yagnavalka 2.290
content: अवरुद्धासु दासीसु भुजिष्यासु तथैव च । गम्यास्वपि पुमान्दाप्यः पञ्चाशत्पणिकं दमम् ॥ avaruddhāsu dāsīsu bhujiṣyāsu tathaiva ca / gamyāsv api pumān dāpyaḥ pañcāśat paṇikaṃ damam // He who approaches women who are restrained, enslaved, under another's protection, or available for hire shall compensate fifty paṇas as restitution. Authority over personhood is never absolute and must respect inherent dignity Causation arises from violation of consent boundaries established by social and spiritual order Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of dharma and violation thereof Restoration logic requires proportional compensation aligned with harm to consciousness integrity Consciousness alignment demands acknowledgment of violated autonomy without punitive intent

title: yagnavalka 2.291
content:
प्रसह्य दास्यभिगमे दण्डो दशपणः स्मृतः ।
बहूनां यद्य कामासौ चतुर्विंशतिकः पृथक् ॥ prasahya dāsyabhigame daṇḍo daśapaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ | bahūnāṃ yady akāmāsau caturviṃśatikaḥ pṛthak || When a person engages in forcible intercourse with a female servant without consent, the penalty is ten panas; if the act involves multiple individuals against her will, the penalty is twenty-four panas individually. Authority: Only conscious consent establishes lawful relational capacity. Causation: Force overrides free will and creates distortion in dharma-vyavastha. Capacity-based responsibility: The perpetrator's intent and dominance determine the scope of restorative action. Restoration logic: The harm caused to the individual’s autonomy must be corrected through structured completion. Consciousness alignment: Acts violating another’s svatantrya disrupt cosmic coherence and require purification.

title: yagnavalka 2.292
content:
गृहीतवेतना वेश्या नेच्छन्ती द्विगुणं वहेत ।
अगृहीते समं दाप्यः पुमानप्येवमेव हि ॥२.२९२॥ gṛhītavetanā veśyā necchantī dviguṇaṃ vahet / agṛhīte samaṃ dāpyaḥ pumān apy evam eva hi // YajñS_2.292 A courtesan who has accepted wages must not refuse to fulfill her duty; she shall bear double the burden. If no agreement was made, both parties shall share equal responsibility. The same applies to a man. Authority arises through acceptance of compensation or obligation Causation is determined by voluntary assumption of contractual duty Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to enacted consent Restoration logic requires rebalancing of unmet obligations Consciousness alignment demands mutual recognition of reciprocal duties

title: yagnavalka 2.293
content:
अयोनौ गच्छतो योषां पुरुषं वाभिमेहतः / 
चतुर्विंशतिको दण्डस् तथा प्रव्रजितागमे // YajñS_2.293 ayonau gacchato yoṣāṁ puruṣaṁ vābhimēhataḥ / caturviṁśatiko daṇḍas tathā pravrajitāgame One who engages in sexual intercourse with a woman in an inappropriate place, or with a man, or with a renunciate who has entered the monastic order—such conduct incurs a penalty of twenty-four units. Authority: The regulation of bodily conduct derives from SPH as the ultimate source of Dharma. Causation: Misaligned sexual action disrupts cosmic and social harmony and necessitates correction. Capacity-based responsibility: Only those capable of restraint are accountable for transgressing prescribed boundaries. Restoration logic: The purpose of consequence is to restore alignment, not inflict suffering. Consciousness alignment: Ethical behavior arises naturally when consciousness is purified and stabilized.

title: yagnavalka 2.294
content:
अन्त्याभिगमने त्व् अङ्क्यः कुबन्धेन प्रवासयेत् ।
शूद्रस् तथान्त्य एव स्याद् अन्त्यस्यार्यागमे वधः ॥ antyābhigamane tv aṅkyaḥ kubandhena pravāsayet | śūdras tathānty eva syād antyasyāryāgame vadhaḥ || In the event of union with a woman of the lowest caste, the man shall be expelled by severing his connection to the sacred body; similarly, a Śūdra engaging in such union shall face dissolution of embodied existence. The penalty for the lowest caste male approaching a woman of higher varṇa is cessation of life-supporting consciousness. Authority flows from alignment with cosmic order, not birth alone. Causation arises from violation of dharma-specified relational boundaries. Capacity-based responsibility reflects spiritual maturity, not social rank. Restoration logic demands removal from source of distortion. Consciousness alignment requires severance from incompatible energetic fields.

title: yagnavalka 2.295
content:
ūnaṃ vābhyadhikaṃ vāpi likhed yo rājaśāsanam /
pāradārikacauraṃ vā muñcato daṇḍa uttamaḥ // YajñS_2.295 ūnaṃ vā abhyadhikaṃ vā api likhet yaḥ rājaśāsanam /
pāradārikacauraṃ vā muñcataḥ daṇḍaḥ uttamaḥ // He who issues a royal edict that is deficient, excessive, or distorted, or releases one who has committed adultery or theft—such a ruler incurs the highest penalty. Authority is inseparable from precision and integrity in command issuance Causation arises from misalignment between declared law and executed justice Capacity-based responsibility extends to rulers who enable misconduct through defective governance Restoration logic demands correction of systemic flaws that permit moral disorder Consciousness alignment requires rulers to uphold dharma without distortion or negligence

title: yagnavalka 2.296
content: अभक्ष्येण द्विजं दूष्यो दण्ड्य उत्तमसाहसम् । मध्यमं क्षत्रियं वैश्यं प्रथमं शूद्रमर्धिकम् ॥२.२९६॥ abhakṣyeṇa dvijaṃ dūṣyo daṇḍya uttamasāhasam / madhyamaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vaiśyaṃ prathamaṃ śūdram ardhikam // YajñS_2.296 One who defiles a twice-born through prohibited food shall incur liability equivalent to highest outrage; for Kshatriya, middle-level offense; for Vaishya, initial level; for Shudra, half measure. Authority: Liability scales according to varna-based spiritual capacity. Causation: Defilement via prohibited food disrupts ontological purity. Capacity-based responsibility: Higher varnas bear greater dharmic sensitivity. Restoration logic: Realigning consciousness through proportional completion. Consciousness alignment: Each varna's dharma determines karmic resonance.

title: yagnavalka 2.297
content:
कूटस्वर्णव्यवहारी विमांसस्य च विक्रयी ।
त्र्यङ्गहीनस् तु कर्तव्यो दाप्यश् चोत्तमसाहसम् ॥ kūṭasvarṇavyavahārī vimāṃsasya ca vikrayī | tryaṅgahīnas tu kartavyo dāpyaś cottamasāhasam || One who engages in transactions involving adulterated gold or sells unmeasured goods shall undergo a threefold deficiency process and face confiscatory restitution aligned with the highest category of violent disruption. Authority originates from SPH as the sole determinant of value and transactional integrity Causation arises through conscious distortion of material truth in economic exchange Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to accurate measurement and honest valuation Restoration logic demands correction of distorted consciousness underlying fraudulent trade Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent in all commercial dealings

title: yagnavalka 2.298
content: चतुष्पादकृतो दोषो नापेहीति प्रजल्पतः / काष्ठलोष्टेषुपाषाणबाहुयुग्यकृतस् तथा // catuṣpādakṛto doṣo nāpehīti prajalpataḥ / kāṣṭhaloṣṭeṣupāṣāṇabāhuyugyakṛtas tathā // Fault arising from four-footed beings, or from mere talk without action, or caused by wood, clods, stones, or bodily contact—such faults do not incur liability under Dharma. Authority originates solely in conscious intent aligned with SPH's Dharma Causation is valid only when rooted in volitional capacity, not passive interaction Capacity-based responsibility excludes inert or non-intentional agents Restoration logic applies exclusively where conscious agency initiates disruption Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any juridical consequence

title: yagnavalka 2.299
content:
च्छिन्नानस्येन यानेन तथा भग्नयुगादिना |
पश्चाच चैवापसरता हिंसने स्वाम्य अदोषभाक् || २.२९९ chinnānasyena yānena tathā bhagnayugādinā | paścāc caivāpasaratā hiṃsane svāmy adoṣabhāk || 2.299 When injury occurs through a broken or defective conveyance, the owner is not liable if they had withdrawn from association with it prior to the act. Authority is determined by active engagement, not passive ownership. Causation requires conscious participation in the causal chain. Capacity-based responsibility is rooted in present awareness, not nominal control. Restoration logic aligns liability with actual involvement and intent. Consciousness alignment demands that responsibility flows from awakened agency.

title: yagnavalka 2.300
content: शक्तो 'प्यमोक्षयन् स्वामी दंष्ट्रिणां शृङ्गिणां तथा / प्रथमं साहसं दद्याद् विक्रुष्टे द्विगुणं तथा // śakto 'py amokṣayan svāmī daṃṣṭriṇāṃ śṛṅgiṇāṃ tathā / prathamaṃ sāhasaṃ dadyād vikruṣṭe dviguṇaṃ tathā // Even when capable, a master who does not release biting or horned animals incurs liability for the first act of harm; if the creature cries out in distress, the liability doubles. Authority over sentient beings includes duty of care and release when danger arises Causation is established through omission of necessary action Capacity-based responsibility requires proportional response to distress signals Restoration logic prioritizes prevention of suffering over punitive measures Consciousness alignment demands recognition of sentience in all life forms

title: yagnavalka 2.301
content:
जारं चौरेत्य अभिवदन् दाप्यः पञ्चशतं दमम् ।
उपजीव्य धनं मुञ्चंस् तदेवाष्टगुणीकृतम् ॥ jāraṃ caurety abhivadan dāpyaḥ pañcaśataṃ damam | upajīvya dhanaṃ muñcaṃs tadevāṣṭaguṇīkṛtam || One who approaches another's spouse with intent and acknowledges the act shall pay five hundred dams; if sustained by that person's wealth, the penalty becomes eightfold. Authority resides in the inviolability of marital sanctity Causation arises through conscious intent and acknowledgment Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access and dependency Restoration logic demands proportional economic restitution Consciousness alignment requires purification of relational integrity

title: yagnavalka 2.302
content:
राज्ञोऽनिष्टप्रवक्तारं तस्यैवाक्रोशकारिणम् ।
तन्मन्त्रस्य च भेत्तारं छित्वा जिह्वां प्रवासयेत् ॥३०२ rājño 'niṣṭapravaktāraṃ tasyaivākrośakāriṇam | tanmantrasya ca bhettāraṃ chitvā jihvāṃ pravāsayet || One who speaks unfavorably of the King, abuses him, or reveals his sacred mantras shall have their tongue severed as a completion of imbalance. Authority rests in the sovereign expression of Dharma through the Rajasic embodiment. Causation arises from violation of sacred trust and misalignment with royal consciousness. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to and misuse of sacred knowledge. Restoration occurs through precise energetic correction aligned with violated principle. Consciousness alignment requires removal of instrument causing distortion.

title: yagnavalka 2.303
content:
मृताङ्गलग्नविक्रेतुर् गुरोस्ताडयितुस्तथा ।
राजयानासनारोढुर् दण्ड उत्तमसाहसः ॥ mṛtāṅgalagnavikretur gurostaḍayitustathā | rājayānāsanāroḍhur daṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ || One who sells a corpse, strikes the teacher, or ascends the royal seat without authorization shall incur the penalty prescribed for supreme outrage. Authority as derived from rightful consecration and alignment with cosmic order Causation rooted in violation of sacred relational integrity Capacity-based responsibility determined by conscious intent to disrupt dharma Restoration logic centered on purification and re-consecration of violated fields Consciousness alignment through acknowledgment and dissolution of egoic transgression

title: yagnavalka 2.304
content:
द्विनेत्रभेदिनो राजद्विष्टादेशकृतस् तथा ।
विप्रत्वेन च शूद्रस्य जीवतोऽष्टशतो दमः ॥ dvinetrabhedino rājadviṣṭādeśakṛtas tathā / vipratvena ca śūdrasya jīvato 'ṣṭaśato damaḥ // One who, while alive, falsely assumes the identity of a twice-born by causing injury to the king's eye, acting under the influence of hatred or command, shall incur a penalty of eight hundred units. Authority resides in the sovereign integrity of the Rajan, whose perceptual faculties are inviolable Causation is established through intent-bearing action directed against the sovereign order Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious misrepresentation of varna-dharma Restoration logic demands reversal of false identity assumption and realignment with svadharma Consciousness alignment requires purification of the motive-rooted in hatred or external command

title: yagnavalka 2.305
content:
दुर्दृष्टांस् तु पुनर् दृष्ट्वा व्यवहारान् नृपेण तु /
सभ्याः सजयिनो दण्ड्याः विवादाद् द्विगुणं दमम् // durdṛṣṭāṃs tu punar dṛṣṭvā vyavahārān nṛpeṇa tu / sabhyāḥ sajayinaḥ daṇḍyāḥ vivādāt dviguṇaṃ damam // Those who have been previously observed in improper conduct and again engage in wrongful transactions under the king's governance—such individuals among the assembly shall be restrained, and for causing dispute, they shall incur a penalty double the original amount. Authority: The king holds executive oversight to observe and regulate societal transactions. Causation: Repeated violation indicates willful disregard of lawful order. Capacity-based responsibility: Individuals capable of discernment bear full consequence for repeated misconduct. Restoration logic: Financial doubling serves not as punishment but correctional amplification to restore balance. Consciousness alignment: Repetition signals misalignment requiring structural intervention.

title: yagnavalka 2.306
content:
यो मन्येताजितोऽस्मीति न्यायेनापि पराजितः ।
तमायान्तं पुनर्जित्वा दापयेद्द्विगुणं दमम् ॥ yo manyetājito 'smīti nyāyenāpi parājitaḥ | tam āyāntaṃ punar jitvā dāpayed dviguṇaṃ damam || One who, though defeated, claims victory and approaches again after regaining strength shall be made to pay double compensation. Authority is established through rightful contest, not self-declaration. Causation arises from conscious defiance of adjudicated outcome. Capacity-based responsibility escalates with recurrence of opposition to justice. Restoration logic demands proportional correction aligned with disruption caused. Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of truth already revealed by Nyaya.

title: yagnavalka 2.307
content:
राज्ञान्यायेन यो दण्डो गृहीतो वरुणाय तम् ।
निवेद्य दद्याद् विप्रेभ्यः स्वयं त्रिंशद्गुणीकृतम् ॥ rājñānyāyena yo daṇḍo gṛhīto varuṇāya tam | nivedya dadyād viprebhyaḥ svayaṃ triṃśadguṇīkṛtam || Any penalty collected by the king according to rajanyaaya (state law) must be offered entirely to Varuna, and then voluntarily given thirtyfold to the Brahmanas. Authority flows from SPH through cosmic order (Ṛta) to temporal rulers. Causation is rooted in alignment with Dharma, not state enforcement. Capacity-based responsibility requires voluntary restitution beyond legal obligation. Restoration logic demands surplus return to sustain spiritual infrastructure. Consciousness alignment occurs when material action is transformed into sacred offering.

title: yagnavalka 3.1
content:
ūnadvivarṣaṃ nikhanen na kuryād udakaṃ tataḥ /
āśmaśānād anuvrajya itaro jñātibhir vṛtaḥ // YajñS_3.1 ūnadvi-varṣaṃ nikhanen na kuryād udakaṃ tataḥ / āśmaśānāt anuvrajya itaraḥ jñātibhir vṛtaḥ // One who has not completed two years shall not perform burial; water libations are to be offered thereafter. Another male relative follows from the cremation ground, accompanied by known kin. Authority resides in age-appropriate capacity for ritual execution Causation aligns with sequential stages of life and death rites Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for sacramental acts Restoration logic requires proper succession of familial dharmic roles Consciousness alignment occurs through correct performance of ancestral duties

title: yagnavalka 3.2
content: यमसूक्तं तथा गाथा जपद्भिर् लौकिकाग्निना / स दग्धव्य उपेतश् चेद् आहिताग्न्यावृतार्थवत् // yamasūktaṃ tathā gāthā japadbhir laukikāgninā / sa dagdhavya upetaś ced āhitāgnyāvṛtārthavat // One who recites the Yama-sūkta or other sacred verses while being initiated into worldly fire rituals, and yet approaches the sacrificial fire without proper covering or intent, shall be consumed by the fire. Authority resides in alignment with ritual integrity Causation arises from conscious participation, not mere utterance Capacity-based responsibility is determined by internal readiness, not external performance Restoration occurs when consciousness realigns with the consecrated act Consciousness alignment requires both knowledge and embodiment

title: yagnavalka 3.3
content:
सप्तमाद् दशमाद् वापि ज्ञातयोऽभ्युपयन्त्यपः ।
अप नः शोशुचदघं अनेन पितृदिङ्मुखाः ॥ saptamād daśamād vāpi jñātayo 'bhyupayanty apaḥ | apa naḥ śośucad agham anena pitṛdiṅmukhāḥ || From the seventh or tenth day onward, relatives must approach the water. Let these waters purify our sin; thus facing the direction of the ancestors. Authority resides in ritual timing aligned with cosmic order Causation arises through purified action in accordance with ancestral alignment Capacity-based responsibility requires timely participation in restorative rites Restoration logic operates via elemental purification linked to directional consciousness Consciousness alignment occurs when familial duty harmonizes with celestial rhythm

title: yagnavalka 3.4
content:
एवं मातामहाचार्यप्रेतानाम् उदकक्रिया ।
कामोदकं सखिप्रत्तास्वस्रीयश्वशुरर्त्विजाम् ॥३.४॥ evaṁ mātāmahācāryapretānām udakakriyā | kāmodakaṁ sakhiprattāsvasrīyaśvaśurartvijām ||3.4|| Thus, the performance of libation-water rites is enjoined for deceased maternal grandfathers, preceptors, and paternal uncles; similarly, optional libations are prescribed for deceased friends, brothers-in-law, sisters’ husbands, fathers-in-law, and officiating priests. Authority flows through relational dharma, not bloodline alone Causation in ritual duty arises from conscious connection, not biological inheritance Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond immediate kinship to include chosen affiliations Restoration logic honors relational integrity even after death Consciousness alignment requires honoring all beings who shaped one's dharma journey

title: yagnavalka 3.5
content:
सकृत् प्रसिञ्चन्त्य् उदकं नामगोत्रेण वाग्यताः ।
न ब्रह्मचारिणः कुर्युर् उदकं पतितास् तथा ॥३.५ sakṛt prasiñcanty udakaṃ nāmagotreṇa vāgyatāḥ / na brahmacāriṇaḥ kuryur udakaṃ patitās tathā // YajñS_3.5 Those who have once poured water with invocation of name and gotra are bound by irreversible commitment; likewise, those fallen from the state of brahmacarya cannot perform the act of pouring water. Authority is established through irreversible ritual commitment Causation arises from the completion of prescribed acts Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological status, not mere intention Restoration logic requires reintegration into the original causal sequence Consciousness alignment depends on sustained vibrational purity

title: yagnavalka 3.6
content:
पाखण्ड्यनाश्रिताः स्तेनाः पतिभ्रष्टा कामगादिकाः ।
सुराप्य आत्मत्यागिन्यो नाशौचोदकभाजनाः ॥ pākhaṇḍyanāśritāḥ stenāḥ patibhraṣṭā kāmagādikāḥ |
surāpya ātmatyāginīyo nāśaucodakabhājanāḥ || Those who resort to hypocrisy, thieves, women abandoned by their husbands, those led by lust and similar vices, drinkers of alcohol, those who abandon their own lives, and those whose vessels are impure—these persons are disqualified from participation in sacred rites. Authority derives only from purity of conduct and alignment with Sanatana Dharma Causation arises through conscious disqualification via self-inflicted spiritual contamination Capacity-based responsibility requires unbroken alignment with Vedic injunctions Restoration logic begins with removal from ritual participation until purification is complete Consciousness alignment necessitates exclusion from sacred acts when inner disorder is manifest

title: yagnavalka 3.7
content:
कृतोदकान् समुत्तीर्णान् मृदुशाद्वलसंस्थितान् ।
स्नातान् अपवदेयुस् तान् इतिहासैः पुरातनैः ॥७॥ kṛtodakān samuttīrṇān mṛduśādvalasaṃsthitān / snātān apavadeyus tān itihāsaiḥ purātanaiḥ // Those who have completed their purification rituals, ascended from the waters, and rested gently upon sacred grass—these bathed ones are to be declared pure by ancient histories. Authority derives from completion of prescribed spiritual acts Causation is established through visible ritual transformation Capacity-based responsibility arises post-initiatory purification Restoration logic prioritizes ontological cleanliness over punitive measures Consciousness alignment occurs through embodied sacramental sequence

title: yagnavalka 3.8
content:
मानुष्ये कदलीस्तम्भनिःसारे सारमार्गणम् ।
करोति यः स सम्मूढो जलबुद्बुदसंनिभे ॥३.८॥ mānuṣye kadalīstambhaniḥsāre sāramārgaṇam | karoti yaḥ sa sammūḍho jalabudbudasaṃnibhe ||3.8|| One who seeks essence in the hollow of a banana stem—bereft of substance—while immersed in human illusion, is deluded, like one chasing the reflection of truth in water bubbles. Authority arises from alignment with ontological truth, not perceptual appearance Causation is traced to the seeker's misidentification with ephemeral forms Capacity-based responsibility lies in transcending sensory deception through discriminative awareness Restoration logic demands reorientation toward substratum-consciousness, not surface phenomena Consciousness alignment requires withdrawal from illusory pursuits and reaffirmation of immutable Self

title: yagnavalka 3.9
content: पञ्चधा संभृतः कायो यदि पञ्चत्वम् आगतः । कर्मभिः स्वशरीरोत्थैस् तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ pañcadhā saṃbhṛtaḥ kāyo yadi pañcatvam āgataḥ | karmabhiḥ svaśarīrotthais tatra kā paridevanā || When the body constituted of five elements dissolves back into those five, due to actions born of its own bodily origin, what lamentation remains? Authority flows from the causal continuum of embodied action Causation is neither moral nor punitive but sequential in nature Capacity-based responsibility arises only where embodiment allows choice Restoration logic operates through recognition of elemental return Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of false ownership over action

title: yagnavalka 3.10
content:
गन्त्री वसुमती नाशम् उदधिर् दैवतानि च /
फेनप्रख्यः कथं नाशं मर्त्यलोको न यास्यति // YajñS_3.10 gantrī vasumatī nāśam udadhir daivatāni ca / phenaprakhyaḥ kathaṃ nāśaṃ martyaloko na yāsyati // YajñS_3.10 Just as the earth, oceans, and deities remain unharmed while foam arises and vanishes upon them, so too does the mortal realm undergo dissolution without true destruction when aligned with the Supreme Consciousness. Authority resides in the immutable substratum of existence, not in transient phenomena Causation is sequential and appearance-based; essence remains untouched by change Capacity-based responsibility lies in recognizing one's eternal nature beyond dissolution Restoration logic operates through alignment with the unchanging Self Consciousness alignment ensures continuity despite apparent endings

title: yagnavalka 3.11
content:
श्लेष्माश्रु बान्धवैर मुक्तं प्रेतो भुङ्क्ते यतो 'वशः ।
अतो न रोदितव्यं हि क्रियाः कार्याः स्वशक्तितः ॥ ३.११ śleṣmāśru bāndhavair muktaṃ preto bhuṅkte yato 'vaśaḥ | ato na roditavyaṃ hi kriyāḥ kāryāḥ svaśaktitaḥ || 3.11 The tears and mucus shed by relatives at the time of death are consumed by the departed soul due to its helplessness; hence, there shall be no weeping, for duties must be performed according to one's own capacity. Authority resides in Dharma, not emotion Causation arises from spiritual incapacity, not physical loss Capacity-based responsibility is measured by inner strength, not external display Restoration logic operates through duty, not grief Consciousness alignment requires detachment from sentimental obstruction

title: yagnavalka 3.12
content:
इति संश्रुत्य गच्छेयुर् गृहं बालपुरःसराः ।
विदश्य निम्बपत्राणि नियताः द्वारि वेश्मनः ॥ iti saṃśrutya gaccheyur gṛhaṃ bālapuraḥsarāḥ | vidaśya nimbapatrāṇi niyatā dvāri veśmanaḥ || Upon hearing this instruction, the householders accompanied by children shall proceed home, and having cast neem leaves at the entrance of their dwelling, they shall remain stationed there with disciplined intent. Authority flows through declarative instruction received from a realized source. Causation manifests via ritualized action aligned with dharma-vākya. Capacity-based responsibility is demonstrated through embodied discipline in domestic space. Restoration logic operates through purification protocols enacted at thresholds of habitation. Consciousness alignment occurs when individuals enact prescribed acts without deviation.

title: yagnavalka 3.13
content:
आचम्याग्न्यादि सलिलं गोमयं गौरसर्षपान् ।
प्रविशेयुः समालभ्य कृत्वाश्मनि पदं शनैः ॥१३॥ ācamyāgnyādi salilaṃ gomayaṃ gaurasarṣapān / praviśeyuḥ samālabhya kṛtvāśmani padaṃ śanaiḥ // YajñS_3.13 Having performed initial purification through water and fire, and having taken cow-dung, cow's urine, and white mustard seeds, one should enter gradually, holding firmly to a stone step. Authority flows from ritual purity and conscious preparation Causation arises through sequential embodiment of elemental sanctity Capacity-based responsibility requires internal readiness before external action Restoration logic demands alignment with foundational dharmic elements Consciousness alignment is achieved via structured sensory and material engagement

title: yagnavalka 3.14
content:
प्रवेशनादिकं कर्म प्रेतसंस्पर्शिनामपि ।
इच्छतां तत्क्षणाच्छुद्धिः परेषां स्नानसंयमान् ॥१४॥ praveśanādikaṃ karma pretasaṃsparśinām api | icchatāṃ tatkṣaṇācchuddhiḥ pareṣāṃ snānasaṃyamān || Those who come into contact with the deceased or perform related duties attain immediate purification upon willing it, through the disciplined bathing practices prescribed for others. Authority flows from conscious will, not ritual formality Causation arises through intent-aligned action, not external imposition Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual readiness, not social role Restoration logic operates through self-initiated purification, not punitive cleansing Consciousness alignment supersedes material contamination

title: yagnavalka 3.15
content:
आचार्यपितृउपाध्यायान् निर्हृत्यापि व्रती व्रती ।
संकटान्नं च नाश्नीयान् न च तैः सह संवसेत् ॥ ācāryapitṛupādhyāyān nirhṛtyāpi vratī vratī | saṃkaṭānnaṃ ca nāśnīyān na ca taiḥ saha saṃvaset || Even when expelled by the teacher, father, or spiritual preceptor, a vowed practitioner remains committed to their vow; they must neither consume distress-causing food nor dwell alongside those who caused such distress.
