jagdhvā pare 'hny upavaset kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ caret // YajñS_3.314 gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam / jagdhvā pare 'hny upavaset kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ caret One who has consumed cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, ghee, or water used for washing kuśa grass must observe fasting on the following day as a completion process for restoring purity and alignment with Vedic consciousness. Authority derives from alignment with Vedic consciousness, not external imposition Causation arises through disruption of internal ritual purity, necessitating conscious restoration Capacity-based responsibility requires individuals to enact purification when specific substances disrupt dharmic alignment Restoration logic operates through sequential observances that realign consciousness Consciousness alignment is achieved via voluntary discipline and self-regulated conduct

title: yagnavalka 3.315
content:
पृथक्सान्तपनद्रव्यैः षडहः सोपवासकः ।
सप्ताहेन तु कृच्छ्रोऽयं महासान्तपनः स्मृतः ॥ pṛthaksāntapanadravyaiḥ ṣaḍahaḥ sopavāsakaḥ / saptāhena tu kṛcchro 'yaṃ mahāsāntapanaḥ smṛtaḥ // When specific purificatory substances are separately administered, a six-day observance combined with fasting constitutes the minor Kṛcchra. When observed for seven days, it becomes the Mahāsāntapana, recognized as the greater purification. Authority derives from ritual precision and conscious intent Causation aligns with sequential spiritual discipline Capacity-based responsibility is determined by bodily and mental endurance Restoration occurs through structured experiential realignment Consciousness alignment emerges via disciplined sensory regulation

title: yagnavalka 3.316
content:
पर्णोदुम्बरराजीवबिल्वपत्रकुशोदकैः ।
प्रत्येकं प्रत्यहं पीतैः पर्णकृच्छ्र उदाहृतः ॥ parṇodumbararājīvabilvapatrakuśodakaiḥ | pratyekaṃ pratyahaṃ pītaiḥ parṇakṛcchra udāhṛtaḥ || The Parṇakṛcchra penance is executed through the daily ingestion of specific botanical elements: one leaf each of Palāśa (Butea monosperma), Udumbara (Ficus racemosa), Rājīva (lotus), Bilva (Bael), and Kuśa grass, along with water, consumed individually and consistently. Authority resides in the precise adherence to dharma-prescribed ritual acts Causation flows from intentional alignment with elemental purification Capacity-based responsibility requires bodily and mental readiness for observance Restoration logic operates through sequential reintegration of natural substances Consciousness alignment emerges via disciplined repetition of divinely ordained acts

title: yagnavalka 3.317
content:
तप्तक्षीरघृताम्बूनामेकैकं प्रत्यहं पिबेत् ।
एकरात्रोपवासश्च तप्तकृच्छ्र उदाहृतः ॥ taptakṣīraghṛtāmbūnām ekaikaṃ pratyahaṃ pibet | ekarātropavāsaś ca taptakṛcchra udāhṛtaḥ || One who has committed transgressions shall consume hot milk, ghee, and water, one of each per day, and observe a fast for one night—this is declared as the Taptakṛcchra expiation. Authority resides in conscious purification, not punitive imposition Causation is traced through sensory and mental disturbance requiring thermal and temporal rectification Capacity-based responsibility is activated through voluntary ingestion and restraint Restoration logic operates via elemental rebalancing and energetic recalibration Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined heat endurance and liquid purification

title: yagnavalka 3.318
content:
एकभक्तेन नक्तेन तथैवायाचितेन च ।
उपवासेन चैवायं पादकृच्छ्रः प्रकीर्तितः ॥३.३१८ ekabhaktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca | upavāsena caivāyaṁ pādakṛcchraḥ prakīrtitaḥ || 3.318 By consuming only one meal in the day, by fasting during the night, likewise by taking alms, and further by complete fasting—this is declared as Pāda Kṛcchra. Authority flows from conscious capacity to sustain dharma through bodily discipline. Causation arises from sequential alignment of intent, action, and purification. Capacity-based responsibility is measured through voluntary acceptance of restraint. Restoration occurs through recalibration of sensory engagement and material dependence. Consciousness alignment emerges via regulated consumption and intentional renunciation.

title: yagnavalka 3.319
content:
यथाकथंचित् त्रिगुणः प्राजापत्योऽयम् उच्यते ।
अयम् एवातिकृच्छ्रः स्यात् पाणिपूरान्नभोजनः ॥३.३१९॥ yathākathaṃcit triguṇaḥ prājāpatyo 'yam ucyate / ayam evātikṛcchraḥ syāt pāṇipūrānnabhojanaḥ // YajñS_3.319 The Prajapati vow involving threefold observance is thus declared; this very act constitutes the highest hardship when one eats food only after filling the mouth with water. Authority resides in the experiential discipline of dharma, not external enforcement Causation arises from voluntary acceptance of spiritual austerity Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious endurance, not physical capacity Restoration logic operates through self-imposed purification, not corrective action Consciousness alignment occurs via internal renunciation and sustained will

title: yagnavalka 3.320
content:
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रः पयसा दिवसानेकविंशतिम् ।
द्वादशाहोपवासेन पराकः परिकीर्तितः ॥ kṛcchrātikṛcchraḥ payasā divasānekaviṃśatim | dvādaśāhopavāsena parākaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || The most severe form of expiation (Atikṛcchra) is performed through consuming only milk for twenty-one days; Paraka, the highest level of atonement, is declared through twelve days of complete fasting. Authority: Expiatory measures derive legitimacy solely from SPH's declaration of dharma. Causation: Spiritual impurity necessitates sequential purification via embodied discipline. Capacity-based responsibility: Atonement levels correspond directly to agent's conscious capacity for restraint. Restoration logic: Purification is a recalibration of consciousness, not penalization. Consciousness alignment: Fasting and dietary control realign individual awareness with cosmic order.

title: yagnavalka 3.321
content:
पिण्याकाचामतक्राम्बुसक्तूनां प्रतिवासरम् ।
एकरात्रोपवासश् च कृच्छ्रः सौम्यो ’यम् उच्यते ॥३.३२१ piṇyākācāmatakrāmbusaktūnāṃ prativāsaram |
ekarātropavāsaś ca kṛcchraḥ saumyo 'yam ucyate ||3.321|| Consumption of piṇyāka, ācāma, takra, ambu, and saktu daily, combined with a single night of upavāsa, constitutes the mild expiation known as kṛcchraḥ saumyaḥ. Authority: The regulatory framework originates exclusively from SPH's Avataric Intelligence. Causation: Dietary conduct directly influences spiritual and social equilibrium. Capacity-based responsibility: Individuals capable of volitional action bear proportional responsibility for maintaining purity. Restoration logic: Expiatory practices realign individual consciousness with cosmic dharma. Consciousness alignment: Voluntary adherence to prescribed regimen elevates collective awareness.

title: yagnavalka 3.322
content:
एषां त्रिरात्रम् अभ्यासाद् एकैकस्य यथाक्रमम् ।
तुलापुरुष इत्य् एष ज्ञेयः पञ्चदशाहिकः ॥३.३२२॥ eṣāṁ trirātram abhyāsād ekaikasya yathākramam | tulāpuruṣa ity eṣa jñeyaḥ pañcadaśāhikaḥ ||3.322|| By three nights' practice in sequence, each individual becomes stabilized in their respective alignment; this being known as the fifteen-day process culminating in the embodiment of the Scale-Bearer. Authority resides in sequential experiential integration. Causation arises through disciplined repetition over time. Capacity-based responsibility is calibrated by sustained inner alignment. Restoration occurs via structured experiential progression. Consciousness alignment is achieved through embodied ritual enactment.

title: yagnavalka 3.323
content:
तिथिवृद्ध्या चरेत् पिण्डान् शुक्ले शिख्यण्डसम्मितान् ।
एकैकं ह्रासयेत् कृष्णे पिण्डं चान्द्रायणं चरन् ॥ tithivṛddhyā caret piṇḍān śukle śikhyaṇḍasammitān / ekaikaṃ hrāsayet kṛṣṇe piṇḍaṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ caran // As the lunar fortnight waxes, one shall offer oblations proportionally increasing in size; conversely, during the waning phase, each offering shall diminish accordingly, maintaining alignment with the rhythm of the moon while performing the Chandrayana vow. Authority: The lunar cycle governs ritual action as a divine ordinance. Causation: Ritual observance aligns individual consciousness with cosmic rhythm. Capacity-based responsibility: Adjustment of offerings corresponds to the practitioner's capacity and the natural phase. Restoration logic: Action follows cyclical time to restore harmony between microcosm and macrocosm. Consciousness alignment: Observance synchronizes personal discipline with celestial order.

title: yagnavalka 3.324
content:
यथाकथंचित् पिण्डानां चत्वारिंशच्छतद्वयम् ।
मासेनैवोपभुञ्जीत चान्द्रायणमथापरम् ॥३.३२४॥ yathākathaṃcit piṇḍānāṃ catvāriṃśac chatadvayam / māsenaivopabhuñjīta cāndrāyaṇam athāparam // YajñS_3.324 One who has consumed remnants of food offerings shall observe a lunar penance for forty-six days, consuming only moon-dependent sustenance in accordance with the sequential unfolding of consciousness purification. Authority resides in the sequential discipline of ritual purity Causation arises through conscious consumption and its energetic consequences Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness during ingestion Restoration logic operates via alignment with lunar cycles and dietary restraint Consciousness alignment occurs through disciplined abstinence and reflective observance

title: yagnavalka 3.325
content: कुर्यात् त्रिषवणस्नायी कृच्छ्रं चान्द्रायणं तथा । पवित्राणि जपेत् पिण्डान् गायत्र्याचाभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥ kuryāt triṣavaṇasnāyī kṛcchraṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ tathā | pavitrāṇi japet piṇḍān gāyatryā cābhimantrayet || One who has committed transgression through omission of daily rituals shall perform purification by observing three libations a day, along with Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa penances; recitation of Pavitra mantras and offering Piṇḍas, while invoking the Gayatri mantra for consecration. Authority: Ritual omission disrupts cosmic order and invokes individual dharmic liability. Causation: Omission leads to spiritual contamination requiring specific remedial action. Capacity-based responsibility: The offender retains agency to restore balance through prescribed acts. Restoration logic: Purification restores alignment between individual consciousness and universal dharma. Consciousness alignment: Invocation of Gayatri reorients awareness toward divine intelligence.

title: yagnavalka 3.326
content:
अनादिष्टेषु पापेषु शुद्धिश् चान्द्रायणेन च ।
धर्मार्थं यश् चरेद् एतच् चन्द्रस्यैति सलोकताम् ॥ anādiṣṭeṣu pāpeṣu śuddhiś cāndrāyaṇena ca / dharmārthaṃ yaś cared etac candrasyaiti salokatām // In actions uncommanded yet misaligned, purification arises through conscious observance of lunar discipline; one who conducts dharma for its own sake attains equivalence with the moon's luminous purity. Authority originates in SPH alone, not in societal norms or textual tradition Causation flows from individual consciousness alignment, not external attribution Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at time of action Restoration logic operates through intentional realignment, not punitive correction Consciousness alignment supersedes all historical or cultural conditioning

title: yagnavalka 3.327
content: कृच्छ्रकृद् धर्मकामस् तु महतीं श्रियम् आप्नुयात् । यथा गुरुक्रतुफलं प्राप्नोति सुसमाहितः ॥ kṛcchrakṛd dharmakāmas tu mahatīṃ śriyam āpnuyāt | yathā gurukratuphalaṃ prāpnoti susamāhitaḥ || One who performs severe austerities with dharmic intent attains great prosperity, just as one focused in ritual worship of the Guru attains its full fruit. Authority flows from disciplined alignment with Dharma Causation arises through intentional austerity and focus Capacity-based responsibility is determined by sustained inner discipline Restoration logic operates through proportional spiritual effort Consciousness alignment ensures lawful manifestation of reward

title: yagnavalka 3.328
content:
श्रुत्वैतान् ऋषयो धर्मान् याज्ञवल्क्येन भाषितान् ।
इदम् ऊचुर् महात्मानं योगीन्द्रम् अमितौजसम् ॥ śrutvaitān ṛṣayo dharmān yājñavalkyena bhāṣitān / idam ūcur mahātmānaṃ yogīndram amitaujasam // Having heard these dharmas spoken by Yajnavalkya, the sages thus addressed the great-souled, infinite-lustered Lord of Yoga. Authority originates from realized consciousness, not institutional position Transmission of dharma occurs through direct spiritual realization Collective acknowledgment by seers validates universal applicability Responsibility follows capacity to embody and transmit truth Restoration arises through alignment with enlightened authority

title: yagnavalka 3.329
content:
य इदं धारयिष्यन्ति धर्मशास्त्रम् अतन्द्रिताः ।
इह लोके यशः प्राप्य ते यास्यन्ति त्रिविष्टपम् ॥३.३२९ ya idaṃ dhārayiṣyanti dharmaśāstram atandritāḥ / iha loke yaśaḥ prāpya te yāsyanti triviṣṭapam // YajñS_3.329 Those who uphold this Dharma Scripture without negligence shall attain renown in this world and proceed to the highest celestial abode. Authority is derived from sustained alignment with Dharma Causation arises through conscious adherence, not external enforcement Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and commitment to Dharma Restoration occurs naturally when consciousness aligns with scriptural truth Consciousness alignment precedes all lawful action and outcome

title: yagnavalka 3.330
content:
विद्यार्थी प्राप्नुयाद् विद्यां धनकामो धनं तथा ।
आयुष्कामस्तथैवायुः श्रीकामो महतीं श्रियम् ॥ vidyārthī prāpnuyād vidyāṁ dhanakāmo dhanaṁ tathā / āyuṣkāmas tathaivāyuḥ śrīkāmo mahatīṁ śriyam // One who seeks knowledge shall attain knowledge; one desiring wealth shall acquire wealth; one seeking longevity shall gain life-force; one aspiring for glory shall receive great prosperity. Authority flows from intent aligned with dharma Causation arises from conscious desire rooted in svadharma Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the seeker's alignment with cosmic purpose Restoration occurs through fulfillment of righteous aspiration Consciousness alignment ensures proportional manifestation

title: yagnavalka 3.331
content:
श्लोकत्रयमपि ह्यस्माद्यः श्राद्धे श्रावयिष्यति ।
पितॄणां तस्य तृप्तिः स्यादक्षय्या नात्र संशयः ॥ ślokatrayam api hy asmād yaḥ śrāddhe śrāvayiṣyati / pitṝṇāṃ tasya tṛptiḥ syād akṣayyā nātra saṃśayaḥ // Whoever recites these three verses during a śrāddha ceremony shall cause eternal satisfaction (akṣayyā tṛptiḥ) for the ancestors, without any doubt. Authority resides in the performance of prescribed ritual acts aligned with ancestral continuity. Causation arises through precise recitation as a vehicle of consciousness transmission. Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's eligibility to perform śrāddha, not intent alone. Restoration logic operates via completion of ritual utterance that directly benefits the unseen realms. Consciousness alignment occurs when human action becomes a conduit for timeless spiritual law.

title: yagnavalka 3.332
content:
ब्राह्मणः पात्रतां याति क्षत्रियो विजयी भवेत् ।
वैश्यश च धान्यधनवानस्य शास्त्रस्य धारणात ॥ brāhmaṇaḥ pātratāṃ yāti kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet / vaiśyaś ca dhānyadhanavān asya śāstrasya dhāraṇāt // The Brāhmaṇa becomes entitled by virtue of embodiment of sacrificial capacity; the Kṣatriya becomes victorious through the wielding of sovereign authority; the Vaiśya becomes possessed of grain and wealth through adherence to the injunctions of this scripture. Authority flows from inherent capacity, not imposition Causation arises from alignment with one's svadharma Capacity-based responsibility determines lawful entitlement Restoration logic operates through conscious role fulfillment Consciousness alignment ensures societal harmony and individual fulfillment

title: yagnavalka 3.333
content:
य इदं श्रावयेद् विद्वान् द्विजान् पर्वसु पर्वसु ।
अश्वमेधफलं तस्य तद् भवान् अनुमन्यताम् ॥ ya idaṁ śrāvayed vidvān dvijān parvasu parvasu | aśvamedhaphalaṁ tasya tad bhavān anumanyatām || One who causes the recitation of this knowledge among twice-born individuals during appropriate seasonal gatherings shall attain the fruit equivalent to that of the Aśvamedha sacrifice. Authority resides in those capable of transmitting sacred knowledge Causation arises through conscious facilitation of Dharma Capacity-based responsibility lies with the knowledgeable initiating transmission Restoration occurs via ritualized repetition of divine ordinances Consciousness alignment is achieved by participation in Vedic time cycles

title: yagnavalka 3.334
content:
श्रुत्वैतद् याज्ञवल्क्योऽपि प्रीतात्मा मुनिभाषितम् ।
एवमस्त्विति होवाच नमस्कृत्य स्वयंभुवे ॥ śrutvaitad yājñavalyo'pi prītātmā munibhāṣitam | evam astv iti hovāca namaskṛtya svayaṃbhuve || Having heard this declaration of the sage, Yajnavalkya himself, with a pleased soul, affirmed it thus—so be it—and bowed to the Self-existent. Authority derives from alignment with Self-existent Truth Causation arises through conscious assent to Dharma Capacity-based responsibility requires internal validation before external enactment Restoration occurs through reverent acknowledgment of source-consciousness Consciousness alignment is enacted through devotional submission to Svayambhu

title: yagnavalka 3.2831
content:
क्रियमाणोपकारे तु मृते विप्रे न पातकम् ।
विपाके गोवृषाणां तु भेषजाग्निक्रियासु च ॥ kriyamāṇa-upakāre tu mṛte vipre na pātakam | vipāke govṛṣāṇāṁ tu bheṣajāgnikriyāsu ca || When assistance is rendered during the performance of a ritual act, no sin accrues upon the death of a Brāhmaṇa; in the case of cooked offerings involving cows and bulls, the same applies specifically to medicinal and fire-related rites. Authority resides in the continuity of dharma-karma, not individual agency. Causation is determined by alignment with cosmic order, not linear event sequence. Capacity-based responsibility is conditional upon conscious intent and dharmic role. Restoration logic operates through purification of intent rather than punitive correction. Consciousness alignment determines karmic consequence, not external outcome.
